top_reviews.content: Worst boba I ever tried. I got the Malda matcha latte and it was nothing like the picture they displayed. No mango puree no just plain green matcha. It was also way too much sweet I can tell there is almost 80grams of sugar. I paid 9.24$ with 1$ tip and it’s not worth the price at all. Unfriendly service might as leave no tip 👎

Horrible bubble tea. As an Asian who has drunk many bubble teas, this is one of the worst. I ordered the classic milk tea with 50% sweetness. It has no tea flavour, very watered down and extremely sweet. The boba was ok. I had bubble tea from Feng Cha Teahouse the other day it was so much better.

I will forever enjoy their Strawberry Matcha with Almond Jelly. It's delicious and such a nostalgia for me. The almond jelly is delicious and is really the star of this place. No matter what competition comes into the area, their almond jelly will always stand out.

I stopped by here as it was in the area and I needed a cool drink. It wasn't busy when I went and was able to put my order in immediately. I didn't want anymore caffeine so I ordered the berry hibiscus with chia seeds. The drink was good and refreshing.

Boba Guys is a must try! One of the best boba shops I’ve tried - and we have tried plenty. They have unique flavors you won’t find elsewhere and I hope someday they’ll span some store to TX! We got the Korean banana milk tea w boba and matcha strawberry milk tea w boba. Very tasty and filling. The drinks were not too sweet and I’ve had matcha + fruit milk teas before that can be overpowering w one flavor but Boba Guys did a great job of balancing this drink; you taste the matcha and lingering sweet strawberry taste afterwards. Delicious! Well worth the wait. We arrived around 12pm and saw that there boba was still be made; unavailable until 1pm. Had a flight to catch but we stuck around the area & I’m so happy we were able to make this our last stop! Heard that the lines can be out the doors sometimes so make sure you order ahead or spare some waiting time in case you get here on a busy day.

reviews_snippets.content: "The staff was super about recommending drinks and they really knew their stuff."

top_reviews.content:
I recently tried two drinks from this place – Plantea and Passion Fruit Tea – and honestly, both were so good!
The Plantea had such a smooth and refreshing taste. You can tell they use good quality ingredients. It wasn’t too heavy or overly sweet, just nicely balanced and super enjoyable.
The Passion Fruit Tea was my favorite though! The sugar level was just perfect – not too sweet, not too bland. It had that fresh, tangy kick that makes you want to keep sipping. They really got the sweetness level right.
What I appreciated even more is their effort to reduce plastic waste here in California. Instead of the usual plastic cups, they served the drinks in reusable glass bottles — and at the same price as a regular cup! That’s such a thoughtful move, and it feels good to support a business that actually cares about the environment.
Great taste, perfect sweetness, and eco-friendly too — definitely coming back again! 😊

Wonderful customer service. Delish drinks. Quick service. They provide their drinks in a glass container which you can save to redeem a new drink at 10% off. If you turn in 10 bottles, you get a free drink. I recommend going. Enough seats for 12 people.

We were craving boba tea late at night and found this spot open until 11 PM! My boyfriend tried a sample of the Thai tea first to make sure it wasn’t too sweet—and it blew our mind. It was perfectly balanced with just the right amount of sweetness, exactly what we always been looking for. Bubble tea can sometimes be way too sugary, but not here. They had run out of tapioca pearls, so my boyfriend went with grass jelly instead, and honestly, it was the most delicious Thai tea I’ve ever had! Definitely will come back here again when we in SF!
I got the Nutella Milk Tea with sea salt sprinkles and… my soul left my body for a few minutes of bliss. Super tasty and affordable!

One of my go to's whenever I'm in the area! Highly recommend their grape fruit tea with sea salt crema (blueberry is my second choice)! The tea flavors here are better than the other boba shops. I still opt for 0% sugar, but y'all may want to go a little bit higher.

Sustainability is one of their core values. They offer glass bottles at the same price. You can get 10% off your drink if you reuse it!

reviews_snippets.content: "Food: 4 Decor: 3 Service: 3 Came here to grab some cold oolong milk tea."
"They offer fresh fruit teas, super friendly staff."

name: Purple Kow

top_reviews.content: Great brewed tea is nice and strong so it's not watered down when milk and/or fruit purees/ juices are added. Tea quality is good. Their price point is very fair and not outrageous like other places with lower quality products. They don't use fruit syrups to sweeten their drinks so lowering the sweetness level doesn't lessen the fruit flavor. Their choco (and regular) pudding is amazing! Purple Kow is still my favorite bubble tea shop.

I ordered my drink with 25% sugar, but they served it at full sweetness. When I brought it to their attention, the staff claimed that their percent options are for "additional" sugar above standard sweetness. That makes zero sense. If you care about customizing your drink or watching your sugar intake, avoid this place.

Must say the chicken here is really tender and delicious, I was very surprised.

I don't rate chicken wings very highly but the nuggets here are really delicious. Soft, juicy and flavorful.

The price here is affordable but the shop is a bit small.

Will come back.

Tried the toffee QQ half sweet with oat milk. Everything was good.  The cups are huge and don’t fit in a cup holder. Might be hard for little hands to hang on to.

Seating available inside.  Parking could be challenging.

We waited 5 minutes, there was no one in-front of us.

Straws look like compostable, hoping it doesn’t get soggy before I finish. I like to take my time and enjoy it all afternoon.

the wait time is atrocious,, but purple kow is a sf staple.

i'd give them a 3.5 if i could, based on nostalgia and taste overall.

with three people working the shop, it's just hard to justify the near 15 minute wait time on a weekday with school still being in session. maybe it's because i ordered food. but i also waited the same amount of time when i went back multiple times back 2021 when i ordered ONLY drinks (usually ordering just one drink every time i went).

usually there's a line but when i got there, there wasn't a line but (3-4) people who've ordered waiting. ordering never takes long at purple kow. it's always the waiting. i think it's because they offer food items--so that really delays the whole process.

it would be awesome if they can figure out a way to separate the food from the drink making station, or completely remove the food and make purple kow solely a boba shop. they can just stand alone as a drink place, they can survive.. maybe? it's so sf staple so,,

the garlic fries is a complete letdown, do not get it at all. the garlic flavor doesn't even stick to the fries so it's just regular,barely salted fries. just don't get it.

my mango green tea was solid. no toppings doesnt delude the flavor, so i'll just keep getting that in the future. pricing is honestly not bad, it works for me, 10$ for fries and boba :')

i'd get purple kow again if i'm ever around the area, but man. the wait time really just turns me off all the time. so who knows frens, who knows.

top_reviews.content:
The matcha latte had a delicate, smooth flavor — creamy, gentle, and perfectly balanced.
The ichigo daifuku was simply delightful: soft, chewy mochi wrapped around a juicy fresh strawberry, with a subtle sweetness that complemented the fruit beautifully.
A lovely combination!

Stopped by to grab a drink and was pleasantly surprised. The milk tea was really good, and the drinks came out fairly quickly. I ordered a matcha milk tea with boba, and the flavors were nicely balanced. The matcha wasn’t too bitter, and the boba had a great chewy texture.
I also picked up a croissant, and it was surprisingly good. Light, flaky, and a nice little treat to go with the drink. It was an easy and enjoyable stop, and I’d definitely come back to try more items on the menu next time.

This tea house is supported by the sale of bubble tea and other tea-family sweet drinks served in plastic disposable cups and straws. The space is cool, but the vibe is ruined by poorly amp'd junk music that is more sound graffiti than music. They would be better off with ambient sounds or no music at all. But invest is speakers first.

I know a thing or two about tea, so I wanted to enjoy some properly brewed Chinese tea while in Downtown Berkeley.  I opted for Da Hong Pao (Great Red Robe), a generally wonderful tea from Fujian. I watched the staff brew it in a small pot; after steeping,  they served it to me in 8 oz ceramic cup. Serving chinese tea to westerners in a way that works in  can be hard. I prefer gongfu places where I can brew myself and get multiple steeps.  Or places devoted only to tea and not tea infused drinks. That said, it wasn't a bad brew. But one doesn't get to linger over the tea, or enjoy the other aspects associated with traditional tea culture here.

I won't come back unless it's empty, the music is off, or something else changes.

If you want a fruit, milk or bubble tea, I would recommend. Head to Blue Willow, Far Leaves, or Teance if you want to drink actual tea.  They could certainly do it here, but they can't do both starbucks-style tea and fine tea at the same time. It's a shame.

Great teas!
Yummy matcha soft serve!
Compostable cups and straws!
Oh my.
And the boba was perfectly cooked (not heavily sugared like most boba places).
We also got daifaiku which they sell from another vendor.
I love that the tea quality wasn’t secondary like many shops.
Staff were friendly too.

I highly recommend this place.

Nice tea house at Berkeley.  They have another location at SF. We stopped by after lunch. Looks like it is a good place to study or work as I see many customers working on the laptop.
I heard this tea house is pretty famous. it has nice interior and high ceiling. They also have one popup store inside when we visit.
There are plenty of teas  and match varieties. They also sell the match powder, tea leaf and Hojicha powder . They also have imperial Matcha powder.  We ordered just cold matcha and it was good.  it was not that strong.  We will stop by next time to try other tea.

top_reviews.content:
Stumbled upon this with my friend, I got the regular iced matcha latte and she got the blood orange matcha latte. The iced matcha latte was perfect~ the blood orange matcha latte was interesting in a good way! You taste both the orange and the matcha, it was a perfect  balance of the two.

It’s a super cute matcha cafe. They sell matcha here and other teas. Service was fast and they were all very helpful.

We stopped here after a recommendation. I love a creamy, umami, nutty, and minimally bitter or astringent matcha. My friend and I both got the plain matcha latte, and we were floored. It was so delicious!! Both one of our favorite matchas ever! I live in Seattle but will come back on my next trip!

Used to be good, the quality is worse and more expensive now. I work nearby and so I have come here often over a long period of time. I used to feel it was worth it paying more than other shops to have quality. But then they started to upcharge everything, even for getting no ice 😂 and they put less matcha every time. This last time it was almost pure milk, so I asked for an extra shot. This is how the color is with a double shot of matcha. So I will sadly drink my last cup of milk from Asha , hopefully they’ll change.
One of the baristas has yet to make my drink to my specifications, so it’s super inconsistent. This is a photo of when I asked for a double shot (after the double shot was poured in). Basically milk
One of the best matcha spots in the city! The matcha is always smooth and high quality, and the boba is delicious with the perfect texture. Definitely one of my favorite places to grab a drink.

I really thought this place was cute, and their menu was amazing with so many delicious options. But when I got my drink, the matcha wasn't very strong, there was a lot of ice (I got light ice), and the Asian pear I got in it was chunky and not very flavorful. The size was also pretty small, and this whole drink cost $8.15!! I also asked for it 'for here,' but it came in the same cup as the 'to-go' cups. Overall, it wasn't that good and I would likely not come again. Maybe their other drinks are better though!

top_reviews.content:
Hey Tea is my most favorite boba spot in Bay no doubt. I could not find a drink that I hate here 🥹 Today I tried their new seasonal drink - pistachio cloud jasmine coconut and I really like it. It tastes super fresh, light and not too sweet at all. Basically just coconut juice with a nutty creamy pistachio foam on top but it went really well together. You can even choose 0 cal sweetener to lower the calories intake, which I did, so I didn’t feel guilty at all drinking the whole thing!
It wasn’t busy when I went, maybe I got lucky, but I got my drink in like 5 mins after ordering. But if you want to save time, you can download the Hey Tea app and order ahead, really convenient if you don’t wanna wait. I don't have enough phone storage for it but I would do that if I can 😂

Our first time at a Heytea store was in New York. We liked it a lot. So we were happily surprised when we came across this place in San Francisco. The teas taste very good and the prices are fair. The store is clean and the workers are hygienic. There were a lot of customers which speaks for itself. We will be back.

It’s always so busy but the staff always had great attitude. Loved the two drinks I got here and downloaded the app and ordered in advance since the wait is about 20-40mins on average especially if they have conferences that day
Amazing fresh tea and signature cheese foam! Real fruit ingredients, customizable sweetness, clean shop and nice service. My go-to bubble tea shop, highly recommend!！
Too busy and waited too long for the order.  I got the four drinks in preorder; but still needed to wait half hour!   Hopefully. the store can smooth out the production process.

top_reviews.content: i’d heard great things about boba guys and never had a chance to try it till now. WORTH the freaking wait! i did my research on yelp and saw lots of people recommend the strawberry matcha. i added boba and mochi and it was the best thing my taste buds have had in a lonnnng time! the strawberry tasted like actual strawberry and not the artificial syrup. the matcha to milk ratio was perfectly balanced. the boba was chewy and soft, with a touch of sweetness. i wish i lived closer so i could experience it all over again! super clean inside too, which is always an added plus! my only complaint is parking is very very limited (not their fault). cannot wait to come back and try something new!

- the store was calm on a Sunday afternoon. Store staff friendly and greeted me when I came in.
- I got a strawberry 🍓 matcha 🍵 with oatmilk! It was fresh and delicious. Maybe next time I’ll get less sweet instead.

Ordered the Thai Milk Tea with boba from here. The boba texture was perfect. The Thai tea was a bit weak as we felt there was maybe a bit too much milk or condensed milk (whichever they use). It didn’t help that 1/3 if the cup was ice which quickly melted, diluting the drink. No option to choose less ice on the ordering kiosk.
Thai  tea boba  and strawberry fields with home made boba and strawberry puree. Yum. Highly recommend  about $7 and quality. Good value

I have been coming to this place almost every day for the past three years and I am writing this review because of one issue that I have repeatedly noticed and find very concerning.
Over time, I have noticed a pattern regarding restroom access. I have observed that customers who appear to be White or Asian are allowed to use the restroom, while customers of other racial backgrounds are 99% of time told that the restroom is "out of order." I have personally witnessed this happen on multiple occasions, and it has made me uncomfortable and concerned about whether all customers are being treated equally.
I understand that there may be legitimate reasons for a restroom to be unavailable at certain times. However, when I repeatedly see some customers being allowed to use it while others are told it is out of order, it raises serious concerns about fairness and equal treatment.
I sincerely hope the manager or owner sees this review and takes the time to look into this matter. I have been a regular customer for three years and I am bringing this up because I would genuinely like to see the situation addressed. Everyone who comes into a business should be treated with the same level of respect and consideration regardless of their race or ethnicity.
Thank you for taking the time to read and consider my concerns.

top_reviews.content: Came here for afternoon tea~ it’s my first time here and we came to celebrate Women’s day (March 8th). I love the cute little smoke salmon sandwiches, the fruits on top are fresh and sweet, the pastries on the second level were okey and slightly to sweet for my taste. Overall, I had a great experience here. All of the waitresses were very kind & helpful. They took the time to answer our questions~

I don't even know where to begin to write how disappointed I am in the service I received yesterday from LoveJoy Tea Room.

I reached out to have LoveJoy Tearoom cater my company's International Women's Day Luncheon because my predecessors used her services the year before. Unfortunately, I could not speak with them or get any reviews on how well the service was, I just remember how beautiful it looked in passing. Well, I'll never let a beautiful aesthetic allow me to make that mistake again.

I requested a full high tea service with tea, dishes, sandwiches, etc. She let me know that she was able to cater for my event. I asked that she give me an itemized payment receipt and her version of an itemized receipt was typing out each individual thing she was bringing and how much it would cost in total on a word document. It is very hard to get that through compliance at my company. I should have known then, I was in trouble.

When she arrived, she complained about finding the parking as if we didn't validate her for parking in our building. Once she got up to the floor she came in and set up the tea which took about 15-20 minutes total. I signed her payment receipt, tipped her and as an avid high tea patron I asked her how long each tea, she brought needed to seep, ALL FOR HER TO TELL ME SHE DOESN'T SUPPLY THE TEA!!!!!!! Excuse me? Why would we cater from a Tearoom that didn't supply tea? The gag was, she provided us with sugar cubes but no tea.

Further, she completed the 'ready for use' set up all for us to notice the cups were dirty. - to the point when washing the cups in our sink, a large spider jumped out of one of them. We wasted 15 tea bags that I am extremely happy we had in our office already because we also notice, only after putting the bags in the pots, that they were dirty as well.

We had to wash the entire rental within 20 minutes before the event began.

Another thing that really bothered me was there were no sandwich description tints letting people know what was in the sandwiches as a food allergy precaution. Not only that, but I’m also more than sure she didn't bring all the sandwich options I requested.

She also charged me $40 for checkerboard cookies (although the invoice says "tea biscuits") that she picked up from Sprouts for $5.99 per box. There were no petit fours, no cream for the "tea biscuits" etc.

This whole experience was a disappointment, and I truly feel ripped off as I paid $919.00 + tip for what I thought was going to be a High Tea experience and ended up being a horrible catering experience. I'll never work with her again and I suggest you don't either.

Had a wonderful time with my son. Delicious finger sandwiches and the scone was spot on.  Magda was attentive and friendly 😊It is best to make reservations if you want to sit inside but the Parklet is just as fine as well since we did not have a reservation.  It was cozy and nice.  We were not forgotten out there.  Would come here again👍👍👍👍👍 prices vary depending what you want expect to pay $20-40 per person

Tea accoutrements so scrumptious I’m fairly certain I ascended to another plane of hedonism. I cannot speak for the petit fours, as we were too full by their arrival, but everything else! Beyond delightful! The scones were heavenly. The jams and curds and marmalades were fresh and flavorful. The salad dressing was perfectly balanced. The teas and tearoom atmosphere themselves were delightful, and our very kind server brought both an extra pot for the table for us to sample a flavor (chestnut, which we ended up purchasing) and an extra dessert for the bride to be. Plan on more time than suggested to savor every morsel, come hungry, and eat your scone warm.

I ordered lovejoy’s for a work catered event and it was amazing! Celine and her team are so helpful, friendly and the food is delicious. We got a selection of sandwiches, quiches, Shepards pie, scones, sausage rolls. All so good. And the bread was fresh! Thank you Celine

Came here today and bought a large Jazmin strawberry boba ice tea no boba
Nice and refreshing.

Came for boba with a group of friends. They allow you to order ahead of time which saves plenty of time! Good value and a lot of boba in the drink which was nice. Employees were very friendly and super quick. Always a good experience!

When I got there, there was already a line and it was between 2 & 3. No restrooms there so had to go to a WholeFoods a couple blocks down. I got a seasonal drink, Rosanthemum, and was heavily disppointed. To me it just tasted like liquefied roses and it was super sweet even though it was "normal" sweetness. Would advise to order it less sweet than normal. Boba was not the best...could have been better. It was a bit hard but not too hard that it was hard to chew. It was not as chewy as I've had it at other places. One thing that was okay was that they were playing music from the Disney movie "The Little Mermaid", so that made the experience comforting. As I've seen in other reviews, it is highly overrated and pricey too.

Simply the best boba drinks on the menu and consistent! Calling out consistency since there have been other places where I have experienced some unintended changes in flavors.
The matcha lattes, non caffeinated,  ube drinks are my go-to options and its fun to try and check-out their seasonal new additions.

Refreshing organic hot and cold milk teas and more with a nice variety. The tapioca are chewy with a hint of honey but not overly sweet. The jelly is made in house. Be prepared for a line but well worth the wait if you are a boba fan.

top_reviews.content:
Came here for Tpumps Tuesday. The way boba prices are going now you really get your bang for your buck at Tpumps. They upgrade your drink to jumbo size for free on Tuesday and I really like that their drinks come with boba already in the price. Tpumps always have soft QQ boba. I wish the service was a little bit better but it doesn’t take away from the drink itself. At tpumps you’re allowed to pick up to three flavors to mix and I also go with the strawberry, mango, lychee. And you have the option to choose if you want to add milk or not; which they have different milk options for you. You also get to choose if you want to add tea or go without the caffeine.

If you’re looking for a quick drink too they always have drinks in their fridge for super cheap but it’s premade to whatever flavors they got in it.

So good. Service was amazing and kind and the free sample is always a fun way to get excited about your boba. Highly recommend coming here if you are in the or if you aren’t. I recommend kiwi, passion fruit, mango if you don’t know what to order.

I love tpumps! It's so nostalgic to me and the boba is one of the best imo! The boba is cooked so perfectly with the right amount of chewiness and it's coated thoroughly with the right amount of sweetness. I do find their drinks to be a bit at times, but the employees are so kind and friendly and always willing to remake drinks and offer suggestions if you don't like it, despite them being tremendously busy at times! Another thing I love about tpumps is their price!!! It's so so affordable and makes me less guilty to spend money on boba. Even after all these years they continue to promote tpumps tues with a free cup upsize on tues. I really appreciate that they didn't change the interior much after all these years, and allow customers to leave mssgs or little notes on their walls. It makes the place so comfy and nostalgic. Tpumps employees are always so friendly and they seem very fun as well! Since it's located on irving, parking can be kinda tough sometimes, but tpumps is my go to sweet treat!

These folk make an interesting drink which is somewhere between a smoothie and boba milk tea. I got a pomegranate black tea with boba and it was an interesting mixture of textures and tastes, but I was quickly into it. I’d definitely come back again. Their default milk is dairy-free.

Drinks were also relatively cheap, for SF prices. On Tuesdays, you can get a large for the price of a medium.

The store is a bit drab and dark. It takes minimalism a degree or two too far, but they sometimes have free tea samples!

Drinks are so so good! Lots of unique and delicious flavors. Very affordable prices and the workers are so sweet! They are always willing to remake drinks if you don’t like it. Would definitely come back again!

reviews_snippets.content: "Pretty good drinks I just wish they had enough seats for people to sit"

Not the best boba but it is cutely decorated and they process drinks so fast! There is never a massive line here, and it is in a quaint alley next to the Cookie Factory. There is also not much seating.

The lychee jelly is standard and good. I got the honey grapefruit boba, which was less sweet than I thought at 25%. The boba itself was watery and kinda not very strongly tea flavored. The grapefruit rind at the bottom was good and flavorful but did not translate to the rest of the drink

Extremely disappointing experience.

I clearly requested no added sugar in my Green Thai Tea. The tea and milk themselves are already unsweetened — I simply asked them not to add extra sugar, which should be a basic and reasonable customization.

The staff told me they “could not do that,” and repeatedly refused to make the drink without added sugar. It is honestly shocking that after paying nearly $10 for a drink, a customer is not even allowed to choose the sweetness level.

What made the situation worse was the attitude. When I asked to speak with a manager or get a contact number, the staff refused to provide any information and showed zero willingness to help or resolve the issue.

A drink shop that cannot accommodate a simple “no sugar” request — and refuses to let customers contact management — clearly does not care about customer experience.

This place is not friendly to anyone who has dietary restrictions, controls sugar intake, or simply prefers less sweet drinks. I will never return to any Little Sweet location, and I strongly recommend others think twice before coming here.

top_reviews.content:
BW is the friendliest, loveliest place to sit and enjoy a tasty drink in Berkeley. Their tea is so consistently delicious and the staff is so knowledgeable and welcoming. Everyone who works here has been so warm and generous in creating a space that truly feels like a community hub that brings the best of all the colorful sides of life that the bay has to offer. I’ve spent hours talking with strangers at the bar about art and poetry and life, and I’ve spent hours reading and writing in peaceful solitude. Blue willow is truly an escape from the stress of daily life.

Their wide range of teas is a testament to the very intentional curation and selection of really special cakes and leaves from around the world. Their in house blends and herbal options are also a treat. But nothing beats their hojicha latte on a cloudy day.

The acupressure + tea tasting I did there in the fall was one of the sweetest little moments of last year. Pairing a grounding puerh with a lesson on acupressure points related to the lungs and grief, giving me a chance to tune into my body and mind in a safe, educating space.

I’m so grateful that such a beautiful place like this exists and is thriving so well, community spaces like this are what allow us to share our lives and selves, and spaces like this are what makes Berkeley and the east bay feel like home.

Thanks BW for offering a sense of place, and a beautiful space to inspire creativity and community.

The establishment is bright and airy, with several intimate spaces creatively designed for Zen like relaxation which encourages one to linger. I’ve never observed a broader selection of quality teas, however, Aly and Niko helped us efficiently navigate choices to match our taste profile. You can even order a flight to sample several teas and from there decide what to purchase for taking home (Blood Orange super tasty). In addition to tea, Blue Willow offers high quality pastries and Japanese cookies as well as tea preparation and serving ware. Happened to hit their 9 year anniversary which elevated the experience. top_reviews.content:
I waited 50 minutes for a drink :|

The sequence of unfortunate events:
[[0 minutes]] Smooth ordering at the kiosk. Very excited for the mochi yingde special!
[[25 minutes]] Waiting and people watching. Overheard another customer asking about an order. It turns out they ran out of mochi and it would take 10 minutes.
[[40 minutes]] The staff were still telling people that the mochi is a "10 minute" wait.
[[45 minutes]] Finally, I saw mochi being scooped into several drinks.
[[50 minutes]] My order # still showed 'in preparation' on the screen, and they never called my #. I approached the staff and said "I wanted to check on my order, because I've waited for 50 minutes". The staff handed me my drinks, which had been sitting on the counter all along and said "have a nice day"
[[finally got my drink]] I inhaled in a few minutes. Tragically, much of the mochi was stuck on the bottom and unreachable by the wide straw. I had to wait until I got home so that I could get a spoon and scoop out the coveted mochi.

Thoughts:
- With all their advanced technology, they could definitely better communicate and handle delays, like when they need to make a new batch of mochi. Plenty of other boba shops alert customers when something will take longer than expected.
- They really need to fix the processing system so that orders are appropriately announced when ready. They have tons of orders, and it's impossible just by looking at the lineup to identify the drinks you got. There's nothing worse than waiting indefinitely because the order never properly scanned at completion.
- Customer service could do something better than "have a nice day" for bloopers causing a 50-minute wait. (This is very long, even for restaurant food standards.) I've had lots of experiences where the business offered some sort of discount or a voucher for a future visit.

Other notes:
- Parking isn't too bad in the large plaza
- Small seating area with a few chairs and standing tables
- The seating area wasn't really the cleanest. One of the tables looked like it had gum stuck to the side (or maybe it's dried-up mochi)
- On the bright side, I do like how all the drinks have little cute motivational quotes and small doodles on the labels
- I also commend the eco-friendly considerations, like the options for cup choices for some drinks and the "unpackaged" option to be bagless (though I think that boba drinks packaged in branded gift bags is a little excessive)

Cute little boba shop tucked away in Berkeley, in the Telegraph district, close to several popular food joints. Parking is super convenient with several reasonably priced garages and plenty of cheap street parking. This place has a small seating area with a few tables and pickup options available. Ordering is efficient through a kiosk and fulfilled quickly.

We ordered a matcha yuzu tea, a strawberry pudding with boba, a taro tea and a signature black tea with boba. All were excellent. They allowed for customizing the ice and sugar levels for all drinks. My favorites were the matcha yuzu and the signature black tea. The matcha yuzu was light, extremely fresh and citrusy. The black tea was strong and very high quality. The strawberry one was on the sweeter side so opting for a lower sugar level is a good idea. The taro one had an overpowering taro flavor.

All in all, highly recommend this for a post meal dessert if you're in the area!

There’s a young guy (who looks Chinese) who is always smiling and even remembers my usual order. Also, the woman who can speak Thai is absolutely wonderful. Both of them go above and beyond, and whenever there’s a hiccup with an order, they handle it so helpfully and with a great attitude. Even the manager is amazing. Super refreshing, the custard went very well with the milk and perfectly cooked boba pearls. The pearls were bouncy and didn’t stick to your teeth, they were also not over saturated in sugar either.

I do have to say that the store itself was uncomfortably hot and humid. I’m not sure what was going on with the ventilation. They even had one of the front doors propped open and it felt like a completely different climate inside the store. Hopefully that gets fixed soon.

The tea had strong flavor, not overly sweet (0% and 30% sweet) and the boba was fresh with the right chew. Drinks were made quickly and the staff was friendly. Clean shop with a simple vibe—no frills, just solid milk tea.

top_reviews.content:
Our first time and not our last!

We enjoyed our experience here. I ordered the Reserve Matcha latte and my partner the oolong tea. Both drinks were fantastic and this cafe did not disappoint. The cashier was very knowledgeable on the menu and the variety. And the employees were working seamlessly on the busy Sunday morning orders.

This may be a tight spaced location for some, but amazing things taste better with patience. Really enjoyed observing the fresh mill grinding as well has their custom tea extractor pulling fresh brews.

Constance Tea & Matcha is an absolute game-changer for the SF Bay Area. They are the first and only tea studio in the area to freshly grind Tencha leaves into matcha in-house using commercial-grade stone mills. Getting to watch the traditional matcha-making process right in front of you is incredibly cool and unique.

The Vibe
The space itself is super clean, beautiful, and radiating calm, Zen vibes. It’s the perfect place to unwind and enjoy a high-quality brew.

The Drinks
We ordered the Reserve Matcha and the Black Matcha. Both drinks were absolutely delicious and packed with that rich, savory umami flavor. Too often, matcha at other shops tastes watered down, but here, the exceptional quality of the tea really shines through. You can taste the freshness in every sip.

The Service
While waiting for our drinks, I had the pleasure of meeting one of the co-founders, Bill, and his lovely wife. They are incredibly passionate about their craft and so knowledgeable! I walked away learning so much about the art of tea just from chatting with them.

Final Verdict: Exceptional quality, beautiful space, and wonderful owners. This is officially my new go-to matcha spot!

What an incredible experience! Today was their soft opening, and this is truly the first store I’ve ever seen serving freshly milled matcha. This is not your typical matcha shop—it’s something completely unique and on another level.

You can actually taste the difference when the matcha is freshly milled. The flavor is richer, smoother, more aromatic, and far more complex than the matcha served at regular cafés. Every drink feels like a premium tea experience rather than just another trendy beverage.

We ordered the Freshly Milled Matcha Latte and the Black Matcha. From what I understand, they may be the first shop serving Black Matcha, which made the experience even more special. The Black Matcha was rich, bold, flavorful, and unlike anything I’ve ever had before. It was easily one of the best tea drinks I’ve ever tasted.

Even on their very first day, people were waiting over an hour for their drinks, which says a lot. Normally, I would never wait that long, but after trying it, I can honestly say it was worth every minute. The quality, craftsmanship, and attention to detail are exceptional and unlike anything else I’ve experienced in the Bay Area.

If you’re a matcha lover, this is a destination worth visiting. A truly one-of-a-kind concept and a refreshing addition to the tea community. Congratulations on the soft opening—I can’t wait to come back and see what’s next! 🍵✨

Checked out the newly opened fresh milled matcha spot in Outer Richmond. Glad I did it.
A wonderful cozy spot. Bench seating along the wall and a small counter.
Many matcha options including fresh milled matcha, stone ground teas, freshly ground teas pulled to order, brewed teas.
Friendly and efficient service.
I chose the classic fresh milled matcha latte and it was perfect. No added sugar to allow me to enjoy the matcha.
Wonderfully made and worth a future visit.
Check this place out.

I wasn’t planning on buying four drinks, but after trying the first one, I ended up ordering four Freshly Milled Reserve Matchas to share with friends and family.

The quality here is on a completely different level from most matcha shops. The matcha is incredibly smooth, naturally sweet, and full of flavor without the harsh bitterness that many places try to cover up with extra sugar. You can actually taste how fresh it is.

What impressed me most is that Constance Tea & Matcha is the first shop in the Bay Area serving freshly milled matcha. Once you’ve tasted freshly milled matcha, it’s hard to go back to the pre-ground powder used by most cafes.

I’ve visited many matcha shops throughout the Bay Area, and this is easily my favorite. If you’re serious about matcha and want to experience what high-quality matcha is supposed to taste like, Constance Tea & Matcha is a must-visit.

The best matcha I’ve had in the Bay Area. I’ll definitely be back for more.

Right out the gate, I knew this would be a place I am not going to frequent. I was waiting for a train and wanted a sweet treat, and HoneyBear was closest.

First, I’ll give my compliments. The tea is strong and high quality, compared to other boba places. It doesn’t just taste like syrup water. They fulfilled my various specifications, such as light sweetness and light ice. I’m glad they allow customizations. The pearls are noticeably sweet, and while I’m not personally a fan, I think others would be. The atmosphere of the place is cute. Those are big compliments, though that is where they end.

Now, my criticisms. The pearl quality was inconsistent, although most of them were too soft. The pearl to tea ratio was not the best (not enough boba to finish the tea). The regular size was NOT proportionate to the price. I ordered a peach black tea, which totalled to $7.25 (with boba). The cup is stubby for $7, especially when you compare what you can get from other places for the same cost. The milk teas and specialty drinks were even more expensive at the base price, and their selection could be broadened. They only take card payments here, and while the place is cute, there was barely any seating.

Overall, HoneyBear Boba is just another boba place, nothing too special about it. I’m glad there’s a boba place around these parts, but that alone is no reason to love it. 3/5.

The Imperial Tea Court restaurant in the Ferry Building has been holding the San Francisco Tea Festival each year. And I didn’t want to miss out this special Spring event - May 2nd & 3rd. As a tea fan, I attended the 1st day - 5/2/26. I enjoyed it so much!
The curated group of vendors from China/Japan/Taiwan/Nepal/India/Europe and USA at this event is always interesting and I usually find a new tea or two.
Asian American purveyors of tea, local pastry treats, tea infused chocolate and tea paraphernalia fill out the show. Attendees got to sample from all vendors. Then, for those teas I liked, I got to purchase the teas! The best: an outstanding Indonesian Ginger tea from a company called NUSA which was started by a young Asian American young man who shifted careers to start his own tea business! Amazing!
I also attended a lecture about Kore tea but there was a later lecture on how to cook with tea - the room was packed…note to myself: arrive early to the lecture room for the next tea lecture of interest!
As an early bird attendee, I received a white tote bag filled with a variety of tea samples and the porcelain sampling teacup cup! What a fun day!

we shared a Beijing Braise pork belly and Dragon Well Dumplings , and both were incredibly delicious 😋 pork belly is usually hit or miss for me but it melted in my mouth. I was so excited to see the large selection of tea they had with detailed descriptions and bought two types to try. The gaiwan teacups are a good price too, which is nice considering the area can be a bit pricey towards tourists. The Hong Kong milk tea was delicious and sweet how I like it! will be stopping by every time I take the ferry now!

p.s. I suggest putting some tea pets out to sell too ! I bet customers would love them!

The staff at the front was super accommodating by making it all vegetarian and made it ready in some minutes. We were running short of time, otherwise we would have dined in. It seemed a good place for dining in or takeout. Good that they have vegetarian options in the menu since there are only a few restaurants in the ferry building serving dishes suitable for 100% vegetarian diet.
Had the pork hand pulled noodles, they were amazing! Lovely spot for lunch and tea.

The layers were on point: creamy matcha up top, sweet strawberry on the bottom, and chewy boba pearls that had a nice texture. Not overly sweet either, which I liked. You get that earthy matcha flavor with a fruity twist. Solid combo.

Food-wise, I went for the spam fried rice, garlic fries, and chicken wings — don’t judge, I was hungry 😅
The spam fried rice was honestly fire. Comfort food vibes, perfectly seasoned, and the spam was cut just right — crispy edges, not too salty. The garlic fries were loaded (in a good way) with garlic and crispy all the way through. And the wings? Crunchy outside, juicy inside, and full of flavor. Kinda addicting, not gonna lie.

The place itself is cute and laid-back, and everything came out pretty quick. Perfect little spot if you’re craving a good drink and some comfort bites. Will definitely be back.

top_reviews.content: Make your reservations TODAY! I absolutely LOVE LOVE LOVE Malaya Tea Room! **credentials: Teahead with a good amount of tea experience in the US, BC, and UK; recently relocated to the Bay and on the hunt for the best tea service locally.**

Kicking off the series here with Malaya, a tribute to British Malayan culture; an unconventional but intriguing pick.

Ambiance: Tea for two on a rainy Saturday afternoon. 1:15 p.m. time slot; full house, too packed for an audible conversation. I’d recommend booking the proper 3 p.m. slot.

Our table was directly in front of the open entrance, so expect some wind and chills.

Tea: Refillable water, non-refillable tea. The Apple Cider lacked apple flavor. The Genmaicha with Coconut was pleasant but weak; I had to ask for a double bag.

Eats: The Southeast Asian–style sardine sandwich was well-seasoned and balanced with cucumbers, absolutely phenomenal!

The Chicken Apple came on brown bread with generous apple chunks.

The Turkey and Smoked Salmon sandwiches were mediocre.

The scone was on the dry side, but the clotted cream was proper. Unsure if the jam was homemade or commercial. Fruits were fresh and sweet. The pandan cake was a nice twist, subtle enough for those unfamiliar with the flavor.

Service: The servers were very polite and kind, with some training in tea knowledge. They kept interactions minimal to avoid disruption. Ring the bell for service.

Amenities: The room was clean and well kept, with a spacious restroom in the back. Non-formal china. Low coffee table. Chairs and tiered stands can be wobbly.

Accessibility: The entrance is ADA-compliant, though the packed seating can pose challenges for wheelchair access. I’d recommend noting your needs during booking to ensure the best seating.

Overall: A cozy neighborhood spot for those seeking a casual outing. A lot of thought and emphasis have been put into showcasing the owner’s Southeast Asian heritage, and I’d highly recommend exploring that when ordering.

top_reviews.content:
What a fantastic experience! Dartealing’s High Tea was truly the best I’ve ever had. The seasonal menu was beautifully curated, with every item fresh, flavorful, and perfectly balanced. The house special Baja fish sandwich was outstanding and absolutely worth the additional $9.

The service was equally impressive. My server, Keith, was attentive, friendly, and helped make the afternoon even more enjoyable. I highly recommend Dartealing to anyone looking for an exceptional tea experience, and I’m already looking forward to my next visit!

Darteeling has absolutely ruined me--I don't think I'll be able to enjoy another tea lounge for a good while. I've been to Rundle Bar in Banff, Courtyard in Boston, Majorelle in NY, and a few other places in DC and as wonderful as those locations were, I always left feeling the savory sandwiches were underwhelming or not really savory/bland and sweets were too sweet with flavor profiles that seemed too unique for my taste.

Dartealing's savory bites this season were balanced, familiar but elevated, had great contrasting textures and genuinely delicious. The sweets were also not too sweet, which I appreciated because I finished my entire portion before my husband finished his (this never happens). I also felt the preset menu was very intentional in how it was composed and loved how there was no silverware (don't know if this was intentional) because that typically takes up so much space on the table.

It was also super cozy inside and felt homey which is my preference. I felt like I could just  sit and enjoy my tea time without worrying about anything else.

I don't live in SF, but would be willing to fly from the opposite coast to come here again!

I spotted Dartealing Lounge several times when riding by on a SF Muni bus going from Caltrain towards downtown. A lover of tea, I was happy to finally try it with a friend this past weekend.
The experience was good. 😊
Ambiance: the lounge is in an old (historic) building on 3rd Street in SOMA. The long room has a cozy feel with the cutest décor (decorative lamps, chintz curtains, a variety of seats and photos). It is spacious compared to another SF (Noe Valley) tea room I’d visited years ago - giving you some privacy.
Food: the Proper Tea service was what the two of us ordered. It is two pots of tea (separate flavors) in gorgeous heavy china teapots and a 3-tiered plated tower with a mix of savory and sweet creations. We happened to be at the lounge while the June menu was « Latin flavor ». My absolute favorite things were the tea sandwiches. The shop makes their own sauces and recipes for these. There were two corn (elote), two chicken salad and two cucumber sandwich triangles per person - basically we each ended up with 1.5 entire full-sized sandwiches on soft white and brown bread.
The acclaimed scone was just okay.
I found having my scone sliced already and a spot of clotted cream and a spot of lemon curd on it (rather than keeping it whole and the toppings in side cups) to be less pleasurable. The scones were small and slightly toasted - they ended up being dry :(
Cutting one small scone in half with a result of two pieces was dainty-looking but not substantial. The puréed black bean (with chunks of bean) empanada was yummy but underbaked and the chorizo roll in puff pastry was nice but there was very little chorizo.
Teas: I chose a black tea (Her Majesty’s Secret Service) and my friend chose a white, fruity tea (Cabana Boy). Both teas had light aromas and tastes. They went well with the food.
Service: Very pleasant. We were asked to wait in the entry lounge for 5 minutes until our official start time of 11:30am commenced. Then right on time, we were escorted to our table - a cute round set up in a corner. The wingback chair I sat in was plush and I sank in. The tea service was clearly explained to us and we placed our orders. We were asked how things were once and had the water in the teapot’s replenished.
Interesting fact: the lounge has been in business for 17 years. That’s some longevity!!!
Overall, Dartealing Lounge provides a nice tea service at a reasonable price. The other patrons (Moms with daughters, Grandmothers with grandkids or just groups of friends) were enjoying the experience. The 90 minutes for this reservation went by so quickly that we had to box some of the food to takeaway. I’m sure others were like me wishing we were given more time to relax.

OMG so much fun. The food was excellent, tea was delicious, and environment was beyond charming. I highly recommend trying this at least once. The flavors were an inventive, global version of high tea. DO make a reservation, they only offer the afternoon tea on weekends. Unless there is a game happening (though it explicitly says no game parking), the side street is good for parking.

P.s. If they have baja fish sandwich, say yes.

This place deserves five stars. We were lucky to dine on the last day of the Asian-inspired menu, and boy oh boy, did I feel pampered. The black sesame scone was the best scone I ever had in my life. All the sandwiches and little bites were unique and flavorful.

We ordered the chestnut oolong milk tea with grass jelly at 50% sweetness, which turned out to be the perfect balance. The drink is made with oat milk and topped with whipped cream and rich chestnut paste, finished with fresh chestnut pieces on top. We also tried one of their cone-style desserts, something we’ve never seen offered elsewhere, which made the visit even more memorable.
Overall, the drink was unique, flavorful, and well-crafted. Prices are comparable to other boba tea shops, making it a great option if you’re looking for something familiar yet a little different. Definitely worth stopping by if you’re in the area.

Sweetheart Cafe, Oakland’s Chinatown

This Sweetheart Cafe location has been here for more than 30 years. It originally sells snacks and tons of candies in different aisles . Later on, they sold dried fruits also. Eventually they sold hot foods like popcorn chicken, curry fish balls and different boba drinks. They have seatings as well.

Their boba drinks had became so popular that they opened locations in Berkeley, San Francisco and Milpitas.

I walked into Plentea around 9:58 PM without realizing they closed at 10. I was looking over the menu while another customer finished ordering. After they left, the woman working the counter started bringing the signs in from outside and closed the door, which is when I realized they were closing.

At that point it was already about 10:01 PM, so I asked if she’d still be willing to make a smoothie, but also told her I completely understood if the answer was no. Instead of acting annoyed or rushing me, she smiled and said she’d be happy to make one.

She took the time (a few mins) to talk with me, gave a few recommendations, and I ended up going with the blueberry smoothie. It was good, although probably not the flavor I’d order again personally. But honestly, the customer service was the standout part of the experience.

One thing I REALLY appreciated was that they offered the choice between a plastic bottle or a glass bottle for the same price. As someone who tries to avoid plastic and live a more non-toxic lifestyle, that immediately stood out to me. Not many places think about details like that anymore.

The employee had a genuinely great attitude the entire time, even though they were already trying to close up for the night. As soon as I got my smoothie, I headed out so they could finish closing.

I’ll definitely be back to try more flavors. If you’re in San Francisco and looking for smoothies, teas, and a spot that actually cares about customer experience (and offers glass bottles!), Plentea is worth checking out.

As I was walking and saw the sign that said "SOPHIE'S CUPPA TEA Not all caffeine is black" I had an immediate reaction.  I love tea and I love to support local mom's and pop's shops, and would have loved to try a cuppa where, according to the website, one doesn't need to put milk and sugar in it.

However, the undertext of the signage didn't sit quite well with me.  I was curious as to why I had such a visceral reaction, so much so that I researched the chemical composition of caffeine.  In my research caffeine is not one color at all, but is comprised of all colors as it comes in a white powdered form.  White is all the colors in the visible light spectrum. I ordered through the app and selected Takeaway. When I received the notification that my drink was ready, I went into the store and was met with a large crowd of people waiting. It wasn’t obvious where the mobile pickup area was. Since the store is quite small, it quickly became crowded. I think adding retractable queue barriers to separate mobile pickups from in-store orders would help keep things more organized and improve the flow.

Another thing I noticed was that my cup had a clear Takeaway label, but none of the staff asked whether I needed a bag, so I had to ask for one myself. At many HEYTEA locations in Asia, staff usually ask if customers need a bag before the customer has to ask. They also often remind customers where to find straws or include one with the order. Here, I noticed both myself and other customers having to look around for the self-service straws, which were located on the left side and partially blocked by people waiting. It made the pickup process a bit inconvenient.

I understand the store has only been open for a few weeks, so the team is probably still ironing things out. I hope these suggestions can help improve the overall experience, as the drinks were definitely worth trying.

top_reviews.content:
I have been wanting to try this place for some months now. Interesting that the grand opening sign is still there after a year or so. The interior is clean. Staff is courteous.

I tried the Hong Kong Silky Classic Milk Tea. It tasted all right. I thought having "Silky" in the name is funny, as Hong Kong milk tea is supposed to be silky. I didn't like that if I wanted no ice, I would have to pay extra. Also, the store charges a 4% processing fee when customers pay with a card. So with the fee, the $6.50 tea with toppings came to a total of about $8.50.

To me, the taste of the tea didn't match up to the price. So it's unlikely I'll come here again for tea.

Stopped by to try some ice cream after lunch. The young man working by himself didn’t greet us even after we had been in the shop for a while. I feel like he could have been friendlier. The dessert was just okay, in my opinion.

Located in the Parkside neighborhood, Milktopia is a small unassuming storefront; however, once you step inside you're greeted with a wide array of tea beverages, snacks and soft serve options - something for everyone!

Inside Milktopia, ordering can be done either with one of their employees or at the kiosk. Seating isn't plentiful in the store, which makes sense given the size; however, there are four bar stool style seating available for those of you wanting to enjoy your selections. Otherwise, most patrons often take their goodies to-go and enjoy them while strolling around the area.

I ordered their mango pomelo sago, the HK silky milk tea, and the salty egg puff. Mango pomelo sago is a personal go-to drink of mine, and I'm happy to share that the one crafted by Milktopia tastes just as good as any of my favorites. The HK silky milk tea was authentic, although I will note they use evaporated milk (as opposed to the usual condensed milk) so the drink is a little less sweet than it normally is, which could be a bonus to some. Their egg puffs are freshly made and take about 10 or so minutes to prepare. Their salty egg puff was a delicious mix of savory and sweet flavors, and they also have other unique egg puff flavors including oreo, boba, and meat floss (which I'll definitely be back to try in the future).

If you're in the Parkside area and are looking for your next best boba stop, then I highly recommend giving Milktopia a try!

Super fresh delicious teas!
The boba soft serve was also amazing!!!
I wish I lived closer but then again I would probably be here everyday!
Can't wait to come back and try all the other drinks!!!

The HK milk tea I had had a very strong tea flavor but it was way too sweet. On top of that, I ordered it with no toppings and the bill came out to over $7, $8 with tip and they also charge a 4% fee for credit card transactions… yes I understand it is hard to do business nowadays but to make your customers pay 4% for using a credit card is absurd especially because I know the merchant fee is not 4%.

This location in the Outer Sunset is my favorite because it’s so close to Golden Gate Park. There are also plenty of great restaurants nearby, making it the perfect place to stop by with friends after a heavy meal.

Overall, an amazing spot with excellent matcha, great service, and a wonderful atmosphere. Highly recommended!

Their matcha tends to be more astringent than some other matcha in the area, so just be warned if that isn't your thing and you prefer a smoother matcha.

I also love their matcha soft serve and parfaits. Sooooo good!

They also have more seating here, which I really appreciate, and a bathroom in the back.

Looking forward to coming back when I'm in the area.

I recently visited Brew Cha - South San Francisco, and I must say, it’s a fantastic spot for tea lovers! The environment is clean, modern, and welcoming, making it a great place to relax or grab a drink to go. The menu offers a wide variety of tea options, from classic black and green teas to unique specialty drinks.

What I appreciate most is the ability to customize drinks to my preference—whether it’s adjusting the sweetness level, ice amount, or adding organic milk options. The quality of the ingredients is evident, and the flavors are well-balanced. My Ceylon Black Tea with organic whole milk was smooth and refreshing, with just the right level of sweetness.

The staff is friendly and efficient, ensuring quick service even during busy hours. If you’re in the area and looking for a high-quality tea shop with plenty of choices, I highly recommend Brew Cha!

top_reviews.content: This small bubble tea place has delicious ice cream and various Asian drink dessert (bubble tea, tapioca, cheese tea, etc.). The place is a small and unassuming, and they don't even have a bathroom there. But the ice cream is delectably fruity and our strawberry flavor ice cream even has real strawberry in it.

This might be a little bit off the beaten path, but it’s definitely not too far from Golden Gate Park. If you turn the corner on 24th Avenue and go towards Lincoln way, you’ll be at Golden Gate Park. Nobody is paying me to write this or telling me to write this, because the prices here are great. I feel like the food and drinks here are great too. Don’t expect to get the world’s best food because that costs a lot of money, and you’re not paying Michelin star prices right? I don’t see enough 5 star reviews here. Any place would be Covid safe(r) if everyone could afford a mask, so maybe if you cared about workers rights people with disabilities who have more money, then more people could access high quality masks, and have paid sick leave too, as they talk about on the “dmv” tv show. It’ll be Covid safe(r) if you take your order to-go. Not everyone has a place to go to that isn’t indoors, so leave the indoor dining to the people who really need it. I feel like people don’t understand culture differences. If they’re looking for a cha chaan teng, that’s a specific kind of business known as a Hong Kong style cafe. There are plenty in San Francisco, and several in the bay area. Any ole’ bubble tea place is not a cha chaan teng so you might get appetizers and snacks at the maximum, but you ain’t gonna be gettin’ a full meal so start steppin’ if you don’t know how to come correct.

I’m pretty picky when it comes to Hong Kong egg puff because it’s surprisingly hard to find a good one. The perfect egg puff should be slightly sweet but not too sweet, crispy on the outside and hollow, pillowy soft, and slightly chewy on the inside. Most of the ones I’ve tried in the States have been stale or lacking texture, but the one here at Hillclub is honestly one of the best I’ve had in SF.

The staff were also incredibly friendly. They gave me complimentary samples and genuinely asked for feedback on some new drinks they were testing, including the hojicha latte and lemon grapefruit tea. Both were delicious, but the lemon grapefruit tea was my favorite. It had a strong tea flavor (which I love), not too sweet, and the real grapefruit added extra depth and made the drink much more interesting.

Overall, great drinks, great food, and great service. I’ll definitely be back to try more things!

top_reviews.content:
If you're looking for a truly unique team-building experience that goes beyond the typical happy hour or offsite activity, I cannot recommend this tea blending workshop enough.

Our company recently partnered with Marlene and her incredible team for a tea blending event, and it was one of the most engaging and well-received employee experiences we've hosted. What made the event so special wasn't just the tea itself, rather it was the way Marlene created an environment that encouraged genuine connection, curiosity, and conversation.

In a workplace where many of our employees spend their days focused in labs, collaborating across teams, or rushing between meetings, this experience gave people an opportunity to slow down, be present, and connect with colleagues in a completely different way. Employees who may have only exchanged a quick greeting in the hallway found themselves sharing stories, learning together, and bonding over the creative process of crafting their own tea blends.

Marlene's warmth, passion, and expertise were evident from the moment we arrived. Her knowledge of tea history, sourcing, flavor profiles, and blending techniques transformed the workshop into both an educational and interactive experience. She has a remarkable ability to make everyone feel welcome, regardless of whether they're a lifelong tea enthusiast or someone who rarely drinks tea at all.

The feedback from our employees was overwhelmingly positive, with many sharing that it was one of the most memorable and meaningful company events they've attended. The experience struck the perfect balance between learning, creativity, and community building.

Whether you're planning a corporate team event, gathering with friends, or simply looking for a wonderful local business to support, I highly encourage you to book a blending experience or stop by the shop. Spend a few minutes talking with the staff and you'll quickly understand why so many folks are drawn to Sips' passion, kindness, and deep appreciation for the art of tea.

Thank you Marlene and team, for creating such a thoughtful and memorable experience for our organization. We left with more than just custom tea blends, we left with stronger connections and lasting memories.

Tea🍵💚

Sips Global Tea has definitely become our go-to tea spot. My wife and I have been coming here for a few months now, and we love trying all the different teas from around the world—Asia, South America, Europe, and Africa. It’s been such a fun experience exploring new flavors together.

The owner is amazing—always so friendly, helpful, and super knowledgeable about the teas. The service is consistently excellent, and the ambiance is just perfect. It’s one of those places where you can truly relax and unwind. Plus, they often have samples available, which makes it even more enjoyable to try something new.

I also noticed they offer classes online, and I’m really thinking about signing up for the matcha-making class—it sounds really interesting!

Right now, I’m drinking the cherry blossom green tea, and it’s so good. Tea has become part of my morning routine, and I love that they have such a wide variety of green teas, along with black and herbal options. If you’re not sure what to get, just ask—they’re always happy to help you find something that fits your taste.

Honestly, my love for tea has grown so much since coming here. Highly recommend checking it out!

We randomly wandered into this tea shop after grocery shopping. and I am so glad we did. From the moment you walk in, you’re surrounded by the most amazing tea flavors from around the world.

Each packet comes with a beautifully detailed description of the ingredients and the benefits, which makes choosing feel thoughtful and personal.

The flavors are outstanding: vanilla cream, mango tropical, and so many others exotic blends from each corner of the world.

There’s also an impressive wellness line that helps with things like congestion, menstrual cramps, and digestion.

The teas are so good that we literally created a tea station at home because we drink them that often.

Marlen ( the owner) is truly the heart of this place. She will spend as much time as you need helping you choose, and it’s obvious how passionate she is about tea. Her knowledge and genuine enthusiasm make the experience even better.

Whether you’re trying to break away from coffee, you’ve always loved tea, or you’re just looking to try something new—this is definitely the place. Highly recommend.

SIPS Global Teas moved its location from 1650 Park Street, Alameda to 2215 S Shore Center on or about May 3, 2025. Their sponsored ad was on Facebook announcing their opening on the above mentioned date.

I went to the new location on June 14, 2025. I did not meet the owner, Marlene Quan, but I met her daughter. The shop has over 85 different teas from Africa, Asia, South America and Germany.

The loose leaf teas are on display in glass bottles. I love this business as I can open the bottles and smell the aroma of the teas.

Of course, I bought two bags of loose leaf teas - butterfly pea flower and Bora Bora. Butterfly pea flower is from Asia. That tea is a popular beverage in Thai restaurants. The tea is blue, but changes color when sliced lemon is added to purple. The Bora Bora is custom made by the owner. It has hibiscus flowers, elderberries, papaya, piece of raspberry and strawberry, etc. It is definitely a fruit tea.

The owner was at an outdoor event occurring several feet from her business. The event was a celebration of Juneteenth.

They also have workshops for people to come in and customize their own tea. Since I did not meet the owner, there will be a future visit. I'm curious as to what is in the gunpowder tea.
Stumbled upon this shop today—such a lovely space and an amazing range of loose leaf teas! Met the owner too, super friendly and passionate. Thrilled to have an independent tea shop nearby.

The San Francisco Museum of Modern Art is one of the best museums in San Francisco, and a must-visit for anyone with even a passing interest in modern and contemporary art. We have visited twice, and both experiences exceeded our expectations.

The museum feels modern from the moment you step inside. The architecture and layout feel intentional and thoughtfully designed, creating a space that is both visually striking and easy to navigate. The collection is varied, and the galleries are arranged in a way that rarely feels overcrowded. This was particularly impressive given that we visited on a Saturday during the summer holiday season, while a special exhibition was also running. The works on display range from familiar names such as Warhol and Lichtenstein to pieces that are provocative, bizarre, and unapologetically avant-garde.

Most recently, we attended the *Matisse’s Femme au chapeau: A Modern Scandal* exhibition, and it was one of the strongest special exhibitions we have seen in San Francisco. My partner and I have visited a number of special exhibitions throughout the city, and while many have been excellent, few have demonstrated the same level of attention to detail. The curators meticulously recreated the original salon gallery where the works debuted, adding valuable historical context and helping visitors better appreciate the controversy and significance surrounding the painting.

The museum café offers a pleasant place to take a break between galleries. The outdoor courtyard is tastefully accented with sculptures and provides impressive views of the surrounding city. The food was surprisingly good, and while the prices were average for the area, they felt reasonable by museum standards. The tart was particularly memorable: fresh, light, and flavorful. It is more of a snack than a meal, but it makes for a nice accompaniment to a coffee and conversation. For budget-conscious visitors, the meal pictured below cost around $15, which felt quite reasonable for a museum café in San Francisco.

To make the most of your visit, purchase your tickets online in advance. They can be added directly to your phone’s wallet, allowing you to bypass the ticket line. If you plan to attend a special exhibition, arrive close to your scheduled entry time, as visitors are generally not admitted early. Afterward, consider spending some time in the Yerba Buena Gardens across the street. It is a peaceful place to relax, reflect on the exhibits, and bring a wonderful day to a close.

top_reviews.content:
Overall, we had a great time at the San Francisco Zoo and really enjoyed our visit. We arrived around 3:00 PM, and I would definitely recommend coming earlier. Even though the zoo closes at 5:00 PM, many attractions and experiences close around 4:00–4:30 PM, so you can easily miss out on some activities if you arrive later. The zoo's official closing time is 5:00 PM, but some experiences end before that.

The zoo has a nice variety of animals and plenty of restrooms throughout the park, which is convenient. However, the restrooms we used were not very clean. The food stands also closed fairly early, although that was understandable since we visited late in the afternoon.

One disappointment was that we couldn't see the kangaroos because the only access was through an area that had already closed. The only other way in was through the play area, which required an additional fee.

Overall, it was a pleasant visit, but if you want to enjoy everything the zoo has to offer, I highly recommend arriving in the morning.

We had a great time at the San Francisco Zoo. The lemurs were definitely a highlight, and it was wonderful to see so many animals up close. The animals appeared well cared for, and there was a wide variety of exhibits to explore and learn from.

The docents were friendly, enthusiastic, and eager to share their knowledge, which made the visit even more enjoyable. There was always something interesting to discover, making it a fun experience for both kids and adults.

The zoo is a beautiful place to spend a day outdoors, though some areas could benefit from a little refresh. A few plants have become overgrown, and some exhibit viewing windows are showing signs of age, making it harder to get a clear view of the animals.

Overall, it was an enjoyable visit with plenty to see and learn, and we look forward to coming back.

My experience at the San Francisco Zoo was excellent from start to finish. One of the standout features was the mobile app, which made navigating the zoo incredibly easy. The interactive map and journey-planning tools were well designed, user-friendly, and helped us make the most of our visit without missing any of the major attractions.
The zoo itself is impressively organized, with animals grouped into themed regions that create a more immersive experience. I particularly enjoyed how areas such as Africa, Australia, South America, and the exotic animal exhibits were clearly separated and thoughtfully designed. Even insects and smaller creatures have their own dedicated area, which shows the attention to detail and educational value that the zoo offers.
There is a great diversity of animals, making it easy to spend an entire day exploring. The habitats appeared well maintained, and the layout encouraged a natural flow from one exhibit to another.
During our visit, one cafeteria was open and serving guests, while the pizza restaurant was temporarily closed. Hopefully it reopens soon, as having both food venues operating would help distribute visitors more evenly and improve the overall dining experience during busy periods.
Overall, this is a fantastic destination for families, couples, tourists, and animal lovers of all ages. The combination of excellent organization, a wide variety of animals, educational exhibits, and a very helpful mobile app made for a memorable day out. I would definitely recommend a visit and look forward to returning in the future.

This has got to be one of the best zoos I’ve ever visited! The animals have so much space, all seem very well taken care of, and the employees were all very nice and helpful. Wandering through the Africa section alone was jaw dropping! My kids especially loved the penguins who seemed to be having the time of their lives! The food at the cafe was really good too! I got chicken strips that were fried to perfection and juicy. My daughter got mac and cheese which was made with cavatappi noodles! We really enjoyed our time and felt like the zoo was a really well thought out, lovely place for animals and education.

One of the best zoos in the Bay Area for families with young children!

Compared with Happy Hollow, Palo Alto Junior Museum & Zoo, and Oakland Zoo, this was my favorite.

The entire zoo is mostly flat, making it very easy to explore with a stroller! 🍼 We were also impressed by how close we could get to many of the animals compared to other local zoos.

We skipped the dinosaur attraction because our 2-year-old found it a little scary, but we still spent a wonderful day here and never felt like we missed out.

Parking was $15, which was reasonable for a full day visit. We’d definitely come back, especially in a different season.

Oakland Zoo is one of the best family attractions in the Bay Area and a place we thoroughly enjoyed visiting. The zoo strikes an excellent balance between conservation, education, and entertainment, making it a great experience for both children and adults. PLEASE BUY TICKETS IN ADVANCE.

One of the highlights is the spacious, well-maintained habitat design. The animals appear to have significantly larger and more natural living environments than many traditional zoos, reflecting the zoo’s strong commitment to animal welfare and conservation. The gondola ride to California Trail is a must-do, offering beautiful panoramic views of the Bay Area while providing access to exhibits featuring native California wildlife such as bears, wolves, bison, and mountain lions.

Families with young children will find plenty to do. The zoo is clean, easy to navigate, stroller-friendly, and offers numerous educational opportunities throughout the park. The staff and volunteers are knowledgeable, friendly, and clearly passionate about the animals and conservation efforts.

What impressed me most is how Oakland Zoo goes beyond simply displaying animals. The organization actively participates in wildlife rescue, rehabilitation, and conservation programs, creating a meaningful educational experience for visitors. The exhibits are thoughtfully designed and provide valuable information about animal habitats, environmental challenges, and species preservation.

The zoo also offers beautiful walking paths, playground areas, and ample opportunities to relax while enjoying the scenery.

Whether you’re a local resident or visiting the Bay Area, Oakland Zoo is absolutely worth the trip. It’s a wonderful destination for families, animal lovers, and anyone interested in conservation. We left with a greater appreciation for wildlife.
