top_reviews.content:
This park is one of my favorites in the city 💚 It’s a steep hike up, but you’re rewarded with incredible views of the bay, the Bay Bridge, the Transamerica Pyramid, Salesforce Tower, Coit Tower, and Chinatown 🌉🏙️.

The nature in this little park is so beautiful: trumpet trees, lots of hummingbirds 🐦, colorful flowers 🌸, and little benches where you can sit and just take in the city views. On the other side of the park, you can see Alcatraz and the bay!

Yes, the climb is steep, but it is so, so worth it. And if you want to keep going, you can cross the street (just be careful, there’s no real crosswalk and cars come up fast). Keep climbing for even more views all the way to the top of Russian Hill. Or walk down one block and walk the Macondray lane (another favorite!).

One of those places that really reminds you how special this city is ✨❤️

As a beautiful place and green space, I give it a nice 5-star review.  However there are a lot of stairs with a high elevation gain/descent.  I can’t imagine anybody with any kind of walking handicap being able to enjoy this greenspace.    It’s pretty but taxing in your body.  Please be comfortable climbing 130 steps. 👍🏼

Ina Coolbrith Park is a forgotten hidden jewel of The City attached with a touching story of legendary American pioneers🫡 and it also has awesome views from Coit Tower, Alcatraz to the Bay Bridge and landmark downtown skyscrapers. The park is situated on 1715 Taylor Street what was once a steep and impassable section of Vallejo Street running downhill towards Chinatown in Russian Hill neighborhood.[*A few houses north from Coolbrith’s original home located at 1604 Taylor street that was destroyed in the 1906 earthquake and fire. It is said that although Coolbrith who is also a “cat lady” 😉escaped alive with her two white Persian cats and a female companion her personal library of over 3000 volumes of valuable books, correspondence, and her nearly finished manuscript on the history of early California literature were lost.😔]
The park is named after Ina Donna Coolbrith (1841-1928)(born Josephine Donna Smith, who was the niece of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints founder Joseph Smith🫡to my friends “Elder Murray” et al. from Utah whom I befriended at Chinatown church on Washington Street), a prominent San Francisco poet who became California's first Poet Laureate in 1915 during the Panama–Pacific International Exposition in San Francisco, who left the Mormon community with her mother (Née Coolbrith) as a child in 1851 after death of both her father and legendary uncle in the midst of prejudice, violence and persecution on a wagon train to Los Angeles, California, where she began to learn and write poetry. Although her personal life is sadly entangled with tragedies and poverty, Coolbrith managed to have published hundreds of works over a span of 50 years. More importantly, in order to support her family (her mother and sister who were sick then died in late 1870s) Coolbrith who was known to (if not admired by) many “big shots” figures including Mark Twain, Bret Harte, Joaquin Miller and John Muir had to work as Oakland’s first public librarian (and female imagine that) who mentored Jack London and Isadora Duncan who also lived or otherwise had ties there when they were teens. [* Note: Ira became an honorary member of the Bohemian Club, a rare feat in the history of that exclusive all-male San Francisco secretive private club that is also located on Taylor Street @ Post Street. "Weaving spiders come not here…"]
The park was dedicated to Ira in 1911 and a memorial plaque was placed in 1947. It's terraces and wooden staircases were carved from the hillside, creating a hidden garden effect similar to Greenwich or Gilbert steps (aka “The mother and daughter steps.”) Suggestion for following walking/hiking routes:❶Muni T-Chinatown, 30 (Stockton), 45 (Union/Stockton), 12 (Folsom/Pacific), 8 (Bayshore), 39 (Coit) walk up on Vallejo Street passing Central police station reach Mason Street climb up stairs to top of the park about 15 floors. {*The OA house (season 2 on Netflix) another City’s historic landmark is situated across the park on 1001 Vallejo Street.} ❷ Muni 30 (Stockton), 28 (19th Avenue) walk/climb up on steep Taylor street alone from North Point cutting through Columbus or Jones and Leavenworth about 25-30 floors. ❸ Muni 19 (Polk/Lombard), 49 (Van Ness/Mission), 30 (Stockton), 28 (19th Avenue) walk/climb up on Lombard then turn on Taylor about 40-45 floors. {If you choose to continue on Lombard it will take you all the way up to Coit Tower through Pioneer Park which would add on an additional 17 to 20 floors. You can then go back to the top of the Coolbrith park southbound on Taylor or via Vallejo at Mason from the bottom.}
Enjoy views of The City while appreciating our history and doing a little workout! 😉
“To its great City of the Seven Hills
And lo! The city bore Saint Francis’ name!”

This deep canyon, visible from the Miraloma area along O'Shaughnessy Boulevard in San Francisco, offers a peaceful retreat into nature. We enjoyed an easy 2.5-mile hike along the well-marked trails. It's an ideal spot for anyone seeking a relaxing walk while immersing themselves in the natural beauty of the park. It’s also a great place to walk your dog, and so far, there have been no coyote warnings. The hillside and trails are adorned with wild yellow flowers (field mustards), poppies, fire thorns, and other native plants that enhance the landscape. Apart from the park, it also has amenities like the recreational center, tennis courts, multi-purpose fields, a nursery Co-op school and playgrounds

The cooler weather makes this an ideal time for hiking, though it’s important to note that some areas might be slippery in colder season. Make sure to wear proper hiking shoes, especially on the higher trails.

The view from the top is beautiful. You can see the bay and San Francisco city and also Golden Gate Bridge. However, I would like to call out a few things that might help folks make their decision as to whether to visit or not - especially if they’re driving from far.

1) This place is basically a large rock that one needs to climb. Once at the top, you get access to this beautiful view. The climb itself is barely 5-10 minutes. There are stairs to do so. If you truly want to “rock climb”, you can take the non-stairs route and climb from one of the other sides. But if you’re not a trained climber and you are going to take the stairs anyway, this is barely a 5-10 minute climb.

2) While the view is beautiful, getting to this place is basically driving for several miles on hilly roads with lots of stops/traffic lights through narrow streets. The distance from wherever you live might not be much but it’ll be a slow drive due to how much you’d have to stop just to get here.

3) There’s no designated parking here as such. This is a residential area and you will have to park on the street. Finding a parking spot itself took us 10-15 mins. It might take more if you come during busy hours. The lanes are VERY narrow and a pain to navigate in a car.

4) The view itself is nice but maybe something that you can sit and enjoy for no more than 15-20 mins perhaps.

Overall, if you live in the area and don’t have to drive a long way to visit this spot or deal with parking, I’d totally recommend this spot. However, if you’re driving from a distance and if you will need a parking spot, it may not be that productive a use of your time and energy.

Tucked away on 16th Street near Castro, this spot elevates Asian-inspired sweets with a modern twist—think Korean, Japanese, and Thai fusion treats like fluffy Japanese cheesecakes, pandan cakes, lychee cheesecake, colorful bingsoo, honey toast, and indulgent lava cakes. The presentation is stunning, and flavors are spot-on—not too sweet, with premium ingredients shining through every bite. We tried the Japanese-style cakes and some savory snacks, and everything was delicious and worth the $15-20 per dessert (taxes and tip included). Staff is super friendly, and it's a staple for SF foodies. Highly recommend for a special treat or date night—pure bliss!

What stood out wasn’t just the flavor, but the contrast—soft, crunchy, creamy, all in one bite. Even the sauces on the side felt intentional, not decorative. It’s the kind of dish that shows restraint, which is rare in desserts trying this hard to impress.

Not just Instagram-pretty. It actually delivers.

top_reviews.content: One of my favorite day trips/side quests from SF I’ve done to date. It’s a short hike down, through a tunnel, to this historic lighthouse. Make sure you get there with enough time to hike out and back (give yourself an hour). There’s great views of the golden gate and the open ocean!

🚪 A Beautiful View Blocked by a Locked Door
Visiting this iconic landmark during the government shutdown was a deeply frustrating experience. While the surrounding Marin Headlands remain some of the most stunning terrain in Northern California, it was incredibly disheartening to hike out toward the point only to find the access restricted. There is something uniquely aggravating about seeing such immense natural beauty lead directly to a locked gate. You can see the lighthouse in the distance, but the shutdown effectively cut off the most meaningful part of the visit.

🚶 The Disappointment of the Trail
The journey out to the point is usually one of the most rewarding short hikes in the Bay Area, but without access to the lighthouse itself, it feels incomplete.

Pointless Hike: You still have to navigate the steep, winding path and the limited parking situation, but instead of the reward of crossing the suspension bridge, you are met with closure signs.

Lack of Information: During the shutdown, there are no rangers or staff on-site to provide updates or information, leaving visitors to guess which parts of the trail are actually open or when things might change.

Wasted Effort: For anyone traveling from San Francisco or further, the time and effort required to get out here—only to be stopped at a tunnel or gate—is a significant investment that ends in a total letdown.

🌊 Scenic Beauty vs. Administrative Hurdles
The scenery remains breathtaking, but it’s hard to enjoy the crashing waves and cliffside views when the primary destination is barred.

The "World's End" Vibe: This spot is often called the "world's end" because of its rugged, isolated feel. During the shutdown, that isolation feels much more literal and unwelcome.

Inaccessibility: The suspension bridge and the tunnel are the highlights of this park, and having them shut down due to administrative lapses makes the entire trip feel like a missed opportunity. It’s a reminder of how fragile our access to these public treasures can be.

🔦 Final Thoughts and Recap
To recap, it was pretty frustrating to find the site closed when I went. While the scenery is undeniably beautiful, the experience of being met with a locked door after the trek out there was a major disappointment. It’s a beautiful place, but the frustration of the government shutdown made the visit feel like a waste. I’ll definitely have to come back when things are fully operational, but for anyone planning a trip during a lapse in funding, be warned that the best parts of the experience will likely be behind a lock and key.

Extremely Disappointing and Unprofessional Experience

I rarely leave negative reviews, but the way my girlfriend and I were treated at this establishment was completely unacceptable.

The situation began when the front-desk employee with long hair told me I needed to throw away my coffee. I calmly explained that I would finish it and would not bring it into the theater. Instead of handling the situation professionally, his attitude became unnecessarily rude, confrontational, and disrespectful.

What made the situation significantly worse was the way he spoke to my girlfriend, including using profanity during the exchange. There is absolutely no reason for an employee dealing with paying customers to speak to them in that manner.

I also want to be careful and clear about this: I cannot know the employee’s intentions, but the way we were singled out and treated left us feeling that the interaction may have been racially motivated. That is a serious concern, and no customer should leave an establishment feeling targeted or discriminated against.

This experience was embarrassing, disrespectful, and completely avoidable. A disagreement over an outside beverage should never escalate into profanity toward a customer’s girlfriend and the customers ultimately being removed after asking management for help.

Based on how this situation was handled from the front-desk employee all the way through management I cannot recommend this establishment. Customers deserve to be treated with basic professionalism, dignity, and respect, especially when they are paying for a service.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Absolute Dessert Heaven in North Beach!

The customisation here is a sugar-lover's dream. I built a sandwich with a Gooey Butter Cake cookie on the bottom and a Cookie Monster cookie on top, stuffed with their signature blue Bear Batter ice cream.
Pro Tip: You must get it hot-pressed. They put the whole sandwich in a press that warms the cookies just enough to make them gooey without completely melting the ice cream. It’s a total game-changer.
Variety: If you're not in the mood for a sandwich, their Bear Bowls (warm cookie or brownie bowls) are equally incredible. They also have solid vegan and gluten-free options.

The Experience:
Vibe: The shop has a fun, trendy atmosphere with cool neon signs and a few tables inside to sit and watch the action on Columbus Ave.
Late Night: It’s one of the best late-night spots in the area, staying open until 2:00 AM on Fridays and Saturdays.

Cafe Strada in Berkeley: Hot Chocolate That Didn't Live Up to the Hype

If you're searching for the cozy cafe to spend a weekend afternoon in Berkeley, Cafe Strada may come up on your radar — but don't get too excited about the hot chocolate. Despite all the hype, it didn’t quite deliver the rich, indulgent experience you might expect from a café with such a strong reputation. The chocolate was decent, but nothing extraordinary.

The café, though, is a bustling hub of activity, especially on weekends. Expect to find it packed with students and those just chilling with friends. The ambiance is laid-back yet vibrant, making it a spot to catch up or get some work done. A friend introduced me to this spot, and while the crowd may be overwhelming at times, the environment has a certain charm. It’s a lively place where you can soak in the energy of the city, but if you're looking for solitude, you might want to come during the quieter hours.

So, if you're in the mood for a bustling atmosphere and a place to hang out, Cafe Strada won’t disappoint. Just maybe skip the hot chocolate and try one of their other drinks instead.

Hey friends! This review is about sustainability only.

I so appreciate your attention to detail when it comes to how folks here can use reusable mugs, and also limit their impact on the environment via plastic pollution.

The real silverware, the real glassware, the real mugs, the real spoon for the bowl of sugar, and the recycled napkins are an excellent touch!

That said, I was a bit disheartened to see how many people were enjoying their coffee to stay, but in to go cups. I understand that these to go cups might be compostable. But a quick glance into the recycling and trash bins shows that there is no delineation between the two. I wonder if there are ways that the barista can work clearly articulate the for-here option, by asking if people are staying to work or meet a friend.

I was also a bit disheartened to see the sale of plastic bottled water here. By 2050, there will be more plastic in the ocean than fish. And over 95% of the plastic that we try to recycle does not actually get recycled. But rather ends up in landfills, oceans, or burned in incinerators.

By now, there are tons of options for at least better water. Maybe aluminum canned?

Thank you for considering my feedback. All in all, I was impressed by your Sustainable offerings. Just would love to see some better communication to folks dining in, who would be able to skip the trash made entirely. Thanks again! Lovely courtyard too.

Seriously, I cannot describe this place, or show enough pictures to make it sound or look any better than it is in person.  I have never, and will never, recommend going to someplace more special than the Blackhawk Museum (and I’ve been to Disneyland)!  It is so special to fully immerse yourself in this museum.  Every area you go to has so many beautifully stunning exhibits, you could spend a full day and still need to go back!  Interactive exhibits, exhibits that literally come to life in a picture.  Cars I have only dreamt of seeing up close and personal and some I never knew existed!   The history from so many regions and time periods is truly unmatched anywhere I’ve ever been before.  The building is HUGE!  It is stroller assessable and has an elevator to go to the 2nd floor.  You can tell they take pride in what they have and these remarkable, priceless artifacts and exhibits give you a sense of awe and inspiration!  Please, if you live near and never been, go!  Please, if you’re far and never been, still go!  I promise you it will NOT disappoint!

Truly one of the finest museums I’ve ever visited anywhere in the world. About 25 minutes from my hotel in San Ramon Ca. What sets it apart is the extraordinary range and quality under one roof. The classic car collection alone is world-class—rare, beautifully restored automobiles displayed like works of art. Then you step into the Spirit of the Old West, the stunning Art of Africa gallery, the immersive Into China exhibit with its Forbidden City model and terracotta warriors, and the incredible World of Nature hall packed with hundreds of meticulously staged animal dioramas.

Everything is presented with exceptional lighting, detail, and storytelling. It’s not just a car museum or a history museum—it’s a complete cultural experience that keeps surprising you around every corner.

I had no idea a museum like this even existed in Danville and honestly it completely surprised me

The classic car collection is incredible. I’m definitely not a car expert, but even I could appreciate how beautiful everything was. The cars are displayed more like pieces of art than a typical museum, and you can tell how much care goes into every exhibit. The museum is especially known for its world-class automobile gallery, but it also has exhibits on the Old West, Africa, China, and nature, so there’s way more to see than I expected.

The best part was watching my kid’s reaction. He was completely obsessed with all the cars and didn’t want to leave. Since it wasn’t crowded, we could take our time, look at everything up close, and actually enjoy the experience without feeling rushed.

If you’re anywhere near the East Bay, it’s absolutely worth the drive. I can’t believe I didn’t know about this place sooner. We’ll definitely be coming back.

At the start of 2025, I took on a 12-hour walk across San Francisco. I began in the Excelsior neighborhood and made Candlestick Point my first destination. By the time I reached the park, I was rewarded with a gorgeous sunrise and captured some of my favorite photos from the entire day.

The park itself was quiet and relaxing, with a restroom available and just one other person around, Jose, who I enjoyed chatting with and watching his dog play. While I wouldn’t recommend walking to this park due to the surrounding abandoned, wasteland-like areas, it’s well worth a visit if you’re already nearby.

Great Park Amenities, Needs some Safety Intervention.

This park offers a truly excellent setting for community use, perfect for day picnics and evening walks, and is equipped with all the expected amenities of a quality public space. It holds significant potential to become a highly frequented local asset.
However, the experience is currently marred by some safety concerns. The presence of unwanted individuals lingering in the parking lot creates an atmosphere that feels unsafe, particularly for families and solo visitors.
This security issue appears to have directly impacted the facilities. The main restrooms are closed, replaced by temporary, makeshift plastic units, presumably due to the unresolved loitering issues.
Local authorities must address these safety and security problems head-on to allow the park to reach its full potential and attract higher foot traffic. Until then, I recommend visiting only in groups and restricting trips to daytime hours.

This was our first experience camping here and it was a blast. Typically I travel hundreds of miles to get away from daily city life. If I only knew it was in my backyard all this time!

This was my son's first camp out and I couldn't ask for a better place.

Great spot to hike or bike.  The campground is closed until next week.  Drive carefully as there are still many downed trees in the roads and some rock piles from small slides which have yet to be removed.  There are plenty of open trails but some have also been closed until maintenance can prioritize the work.  A truly beautiful reservoir with abundant bird song and activity.  There were a number of people but not too crowded for a Sunday.

I liked this hike. I hiked with a group of 10 including an 8 year old boy. Hike is smooth and stable. It is surrounded by mature trees including the redwood trees.

There is a fair number of parking spots at this entrance. We started at 6:30 am and came back around 9:20 am. We made a loop around the trail. To make a complete loop, we had to walk on the side of the road and in residential neighborhood without any issue.

I recommend this hike with friends and family.

It's a great place to walk with family and friends, nice place to walk dogs with water stops around the park. The trees give a nice smell that relaxes everyone as you walk by. The park has many hills and plain Rocky paths. I recommend bringing water and a camera with you, I love walking and taking pictures as I walk by. Overall a great park!

Great camping spot, was lucky to not have a run in with raccoons. Awesome trails with some not being for the faint of heart! Research your trails before you take them! They have bathroom & shower facilities on the campgrounds which is a great help. Dumpsters & recycling bins are nearby too so it makes cleaning up a breeze. AC is also the best campground in Oakland cost wise. Worth spending some time here.

The Irish Times in San Francisco is the kind of spot you go to when you want things easy and unfussy. The vibe is laidback and welcoming—no pretense, just a solid neighborhood bar feel where you can settle in without feeling rushed. It’s comfortable whether you’re stopping in solo or meeting a couple of friends to kick off the evening.

The fish and chips are a standout. The portions are large—properly large—so you won’t leave hungry. The fish comes crisp on the outside, flaky on the inside, and the fries hold their own. It’s the kind of plate that pairs perfectly with a pint and makes you glad you ordered food instead of just grazing on snacks.

The restroom meets basic code standards and gets the job done, but on a packed night it can feel a bit stretched thin. Not a dealbreaker, just something to keep in mind if the place is buzzing.

Overall, it’s a good stop for a quick pint of Guinness before heading somewhere else. The pour is solid, the atmosphere is relaxed, and it’s an easy place to start—or briefly anchor—your night out.

Lorraine, I have to express my absolute gratitude for the amazing experience you provided during the World Cup game. My husband and I were visiting from out of town and they made us feel at home. A decent spot for HK-style cravings in the Bay, but lacks authenticity

Review Content:
Shooting Star Cafe offers a variety of Hong Kong-style dishes that are somewhat hard to find in the Bay Area, but the execution is a bit hit-or-miss.

• Clay Pot Rice: The flavor is good, but if you order takeout, don’t expect that signature crispy rice crust (guoba) at the bottom. It loses its texture in the container.

• Chicken: The meat was very tender and flavorful, though there were quite a lot of small bone fragments to navigate.

• Beef Brisket with Rice Rolls: The taste was acceptable, but the portion of beef was disappointing.

• Sweet and Sour Pork: A bit too sweet for my preference; it becomes a little overwhelming after a few bites.

• French Toast: Disappointing as it lacked the expected crispiness and fragrant buttery taste.

• Coconut Sago: Just average.

Summary:
It’s a convenient spot that captures the "idea" of Hong Kong cafe food, but it still has a way to go before it feels truly authentic or "grounded." Good for a quick fix, but keep your expectations in check.

You need to come here with something in mind or else you’ll get lost in the menu. They have everything and everything is on the menu. If you drove and are on a meter, your meter’s up before you finish reading what to order. With that said, the staff are friendly. The food is on point for a typical Hk cafe. Prices are reasonable so great for a place to catch up with friends or dessert after dinner. Would come again.

This was our first time coming to this venue.   I am handicapped and there were alot of stairs to climb with no directions as to whether there was an elevator available for ADA.  I arrived early, so there were plenty of seats to choose from. In addition to the required 2 drink , per person, minimum (And they stick by that), we ordered the nachos, which were very good. The comedians were also pretty funny and there was really no bad seat.

If I wasn’t required to give a star, this would be 0 stars.

I received an email from Punch Line SF offering two free tickets and confirmed our attendance for Red Richardson on September 19. We hadn’t been to Punch Line in about a month and were looking forward to seeing the show.

I have a disability that requires strict dietary restrictions, and because of medication I had just taken, I could only drink basic tap water. After we were seated, I explained this to a staff member, who said he would notify our server.

When our server, Kat, came to the table, I again explained my situation and asked for tap water. She said she would bring it but that I would still be charged $7 for the Liquid Death water they provide. I explained that I specifically needed basic tap water and was dehydrated. She then told me that I was still required to purchase two drinks for myself and that my boyfriend had to purchase two drinks as well.

I explained that paying was not the issue. My boyfriend was happy to meet the two-drink minimum, but I was not going to pay for tap water that I medically needed. Kat laughed, told me I had to comply, and then said, “Let me get my manager so he can talk with you. I’m sure he will make you leave.”

This entire exchange happened while the MC was on stage, and it was loud enough that people around us were looking over.

The manager, Kim, asked me to step outside the venue so we could discuss the situation. I explained what happened and asked for Kat’s name, which Kim provided. Kim explained the two-drink policy and offered a reasonable accommodation: my boyfriend could purchase two food items and two drinks to satisfy the minimum, while I would not be charged for tap water. I accepted that solution. She also asked whether I was comfortable having Kat continue as our server. I said no, so she arranged for another server.

Unfortunately, when Kim returned inside and told Kat that she had lost our table, I could hear Kat laughing loudly and making racist comments about me. My boyfriend heard them as well. At that point, we decided we could no longer stay.

The replacement server came to take our order. I thanked her and explained why we were leaving. I also told Kim on our way out that we were leaving because of Kat’s behavior. There was no apology or apparent concern. Security also watched my movements as we left, which added to an already uncomfortable experience.

The issue was never about paying. It was about how I was treated when I disclosed a legitimate disability-related need. I understand that businesses have policies, and Kim did ultimately offer a workable accommodation. But the way Kat handled the situation—including laughing at me, refusing to identify herself, threatening that I might be removed, and the racist comments we heard afterward—completely ruined our evening.

The two-drink minimum is also a recurring complaint in the reviews, and I understand why. The prices are extremely high for food and beverages at a comedy club. Whether tickets are complimentary or purchased, requiring customers to spend substantial additional money to satisfy a drink minimum can make an already expensive evening even more costly.

I am an event manager and promoter and operate my own event business. I work with a large professional network, and many of my clients rent entire venues for their events. Because of this experience, I will not recommend Punch Line SF to my clients, use it for my own events, or choose it for my own entertainment.

Punch Line SF: do better.

What I enjoyed most about the show were the acrobatics. I also liked how it incorporates excerpts from poems by local writers, giving the audience a glimpse into San Francisco’s culture and the ideas of some of its most influential thinkers from the early to mid-20th century.

The show begins by referencing the great 1906 earthquake and then moves chronologically through the city’s history, touching on milestones such as the LGBTQ+ rights movement, even featuring trans acrobats as part of the cast. By the end, I felt the production was deeply rooted in San Francisco and created by and for its community. At first, that local focus might make it seem less accessible to visitors, but it actually adds authenticity and charm.

I really liked the concept of blending world-class acrobatics with the city’s history, poetry, and culture. It’s a very unique experience, and I definitely recommend it.

Grand View Park also known as “Turtle Hill,” an aptly named hilltop park in the Sunset has panoramic views stretching from vast Ocean Beach and Pt. Reyes to its west, Golden Gate Park to its north-east, downtown San Francisco and  Lake Merced to its south-east. The park features “a dune plant community atop 140-million-year-old rock called Franciscan chert, which was first formed when the region was part of the ancient sea floor.” Also, it is notable for its remnant dune scrub vegetation and the presence of rare plants like the Franciscan wallflower.

The 4 hiking routes are as follows:
❶ 16th Avenue Tiled Steps & Moraga: take Muni Bus 28 or 28R off Noriega & 19th Ave walk up one block to Moraga hit the colored tile steps [*10 floors] will take you all the way to the park. [*25 floors.]
❷ 16th Avenue Hidden Garden Steps: N Judah & 16th Avenue stop, walk up on 16th Ave one block to Kirkham, climb up the colored steps facing you about 6 floors then follow 15th Avenue circle to climb up wooden steps reach the top of the hill. [*25 floors]
❸ 15th Avenue Hidden Steps: N Judah & 16th Avenue stop, walk up one block on 15th Ave to Kirkham, turn slightly to left to climb up 10 floors of hidden steps (no color tiles) then follow 15th Avenue circle to climb up wooden steps reach the top of the hill. [*25 floors]
❹ Moraga Steps: N Judah & Funston climb up on Funston turn right on Moraga; 6, 43, 44 & 66 (*scenic route goes around inner Sunset) off 9th Avenue & Lawton walk up to Moraga. [*32 floors including hilly streets] Enjoy the workout and the views.😂{Do bring a hooded jacket! 😉 }
❗When visiting Grandview Park, please stay on stairways and established paths to help stopping erosion and protect habitat. 🙏
Until we reached to the top, we knew why it's call grand view! Some stairs nearby are also decorated with pretty mosaic or paining.

I’ve had accommodating experiences at Escape Lounge in the past, especially when flying red-eye to Mexico. I typically arrive a few hours early, and staff have previously made reasonable exceptions to allow entry before closing, which I appreciated.

This recent experience was very different and concerning.

After initially being told to return at a specific time (three hours before my flight), I came back as instructed. At that point, the supervisor, Timm, told me to leave and escalated the situation unnecessarily. He threatened to call the police and proceeded to do so, while also attempting to falsely characterize me as intoxicated simply because he had seen me have a beer at a nearby restaurant earlier.

When the police arrived, they spoke with me and determined there was no issue—no disturbance, no intoxication, and no wrongdoing on my part. No action was taken, which makes the escalation feel unwarranted and inappropriate.

Separately, the denial of entry due to early closing hours—despite the lounge not being busy—highlights inconsistency in how policies are applied. Based on prior visits, there appears to be discretion, but it is not applied consistently.

Additionally, in past late-evening visits, food was not replenished and the lounge was not well maintained, which further detracts from the value for travelers on late-night departures.

Overall, the combination of inconsistent policy enforcement, premature closing relative to flight schedules, and the way this situation was handled makes the experience significantly less worthwhile for late-night travelers.

I would strongly encourage better alignment of lounge hours with departing flights, clearer and more consistent policy enforcement, and improved staff training around de-escalation and customer handling.

I like how the sandwich is prepped with chips sitting at the middle of the silver plate surrounded by sandwich slices.

Overall, the experience is great with many people playing board games. I probably should take one of my friends to play board games for experience and get pizza even when I never play board games for years. It’d be an awesome experience!

It’s also a cool destination for friends visiting from out of town. It’s hard to pass up hanging out at the oldest bar in San Francisco, made partially from parts of a shipwreck! It has that classic, old-timey neighborhood bar feel without feeling overly touristy. The staff is always so nice and welcoming!

The drinks are great (I think I’ve had most of the cocktail menu at this point), and the food is delicious. My favorite cocktail would have to be the Pimm’s Cup, though it’s hard to choose just one. Food-wise, we’ve had the burger (mine with a Beyond patty), the patty melt, chicken mole nachos, quesadilla, chili, clam chowder, and mac & cheese—can you tell we come here a lot? I haven’t personally tried the meats, but the mole sauce on the chicken mole nachos is delicious, almost as good as the mole my parents make. The burger is so good and is my usual go-to, with sweet potato fries. I’d say we’ve tried a good majority of the menu at this point, and we’ve never been disappointed.

I highly recommend it for a chill night with friends or to watch a game. There’s also a small outdoor area that’s great if you’re looking for a quieter evening. We usually only sit outside when we bring our dog (she loves bars—might have a drinking problem).

An absolute gem of the East Bay and within Oakland's crown jewel park. Any plant lover and admirer of nature would enjoy this calm and peaceful slice of Oakland. From the community garden, fragrant garden, succulent garden, palm tree forest, and super cool rock garden- there is a garden for everyone. My favorite garden is like a hidden garden within gardens - The Rhododendron garden is an absolute treasure with rarer garden specialties that are beautiful and very fragrant (Vireya!). The garden and park are well kept given the constraints of budgeting and volunteer maintenance. I can see how some parts of the garden need repair and replacement but you can definitely see the hard work and talent it takes to upkeep the gardens. There are event spaces that seem to open up for plant sales or shows at some point. Overall, a must visit if you like nature and are at Lake Merritt.

These "gardens" need a tremendous amount of work & would benefit highly from some significant donations. The Japanese fountains were strategically designed & still look great. With all the tech money floating around in Berkeley, seems like a few major donors could really help them out & support the dedicated volunteers they have. We did enjoy our visit and found some lovely plants to suggest to local family for landscaping purposes.

top_reviews.content:
I’ve often seen the quirky little Panhandle through the window of a car, but last week, I had the privilege of seeing it on foot and up-close. It was a pleasant experience. As evident on the map, the park is not very wide, but it is long. I took a walk circling the entire park, which lasted maybe 20-30 minutes. I got to people watch and appreciate the nearby architecture while getting some light cardio in. I also enjoyed a quick lunch here on one of the benches.

There’s winding paths around the park for both cyclists and people who are walking, and the majority of the park consists of flat grassy areas and trees. I kind of wish there was more plant and wildlife diversity, however. I also think that the park is quite boxed-in in the neighborhood, with most of the stores and businesses being a couple blocks up the hill. Additionally, what makes this park a little less interesting for me is its lack of a view (which… it’s not on a hill, so I can’t expect that of it, but still).

Overall, I can’t say it’s even in my top 5 or top 10 list of San Francisco parks, but it’s still a great place to be, especially if you want to exercise, picnic, or have something else to see in the Haight-Ashbury area. 4/5.

It's a decent park, it's always good to have parks around, but it's completely overshadowed by golden gate park in my opinion.

My kid has been coming here with their dad for about a year now and they've been raving about the lamb sliders and Brussels sprouts. We finally had a chance to come on a Tuesday night and it was just as charming as they described. We got the lamb sliders and requisite Brussels sprouts, but I misunderstood and thought they said they could polish most of that off by themselves, so I got the fish sandwich (that came with house made chips). Wasn't sure if they meant UK dtyle chips which are what we consider French fries, or if they meant American potato chips, aka crisps.

The portions are generous on all three dishes. I took a bite of my kid's lamb sliders, which was juicy, tender, and the lamb patty cooked perfectly. My fish sandwich had a healthy portion of fried cod, but too much slaw and tartar sauce- made for a super messy, drippy sandwich that sogged out the poor potato roll trying to hold it all together. The Brussels sprouts are a good way to make you believe you're eating healthy (they're vegetables!) when you're gobbling down a plate of deep fried goodness 🤣 good thing they didn't feel greasy or laden with oil.

Next time I'll have to try their sausage roll, Portobello sandwich, and shepherds pie, though they have tough competition with my own versions! Overall Slainté gets my vote for a cozy little place to have some lovely, unpretentious food and soak in a slice of Irish ambiance in Oakland.

top_reviews.content: Absolutely delicious food at the rooftop. And spectacular view of the city. Will definitely return when I come back to town. I had the Lima Roll and the Kaiyo Roll. Both were so fresh and delicious. Oh and the Cesar Salad.... Wowow. The dressing is out of this world.

You guys have an amazing location, a fantastic rooftop view, and a really interesting Japanese-Peruvian concept. That’s exactly why the food was so disappointing. With everything this place has going for it, I expected much more.

I wouldn’t say the food was bad. It wasn’t. We ate, we were full, and overall it was okay. But there was absolutely no wow factor.

We ordered three different rolls — with crab, scallops, shrimp — and somehow they all tasted almost the same. One had a little crunch from the tempura, but other than that, there was surprisingly little difference in flavor. Mostly rice with a hint of seafood. For three different rolls with very different ingredients, that was disappointing.

The wasabi was another strange part. It was dry, almost crumbly, and had practically no flavor or heat. The soy sauce was the opposite — so salty that even a tiny amount completely overpowered the sushi. And the ginger was sweet and mild, without that fresh, slightly sharp bite that normally cleans your palate between pieces.

The frustrating part is that this place has so much going for it. The rooftop is beautiful, the view is fantastic, and the concept sounds exciting. But you can’t rely on the location and the view alone. The food needs to match the setting, and for us, it simply didn’t.

A solid 3 out of 5. Definitely not terrible, but not memorable either. I’m glad we tried it and enjoyed the view, but I don’t think I’d come back for the food.

Staff were kind and attentive but service was slower than anticipated due to the Valentine’s Day weekend. We really appreciated that our waiter didn’t charge us for one of the items we ordered that somehow got missed and we ended up having to wait a while for. Would definitely be back another time!

KAIYŌ Rooftop – Great Drinks, Good Food & a Lively Atmosphere!

We had a really good experience at KAIYŌ Rooftop! The drinks were excellent, and the rooftop had a fun, energetic atmosphere that made it a great place to hang out.

We ordered shrimp and a sushi roll, and both were delicious. The place did get pretty loud as the evening went on, but it actually added to the lively vibe rather than taking away from the experience.

Our server seemed to be juggling quite a few tables and was constantly busy, but he genuinely did his best to take care of us. What stood out was the teamwork — multiple staff members stepped in to help whenever needed, which we appreciated.

The only uncomfortable part came toward the end of our visit. The next party waiting for our table was standing right there while we were still seated, which made us feel a little rushed. I understand that rooftop restaurants have reservations and need to turn tables, but the transition could have been handled more gracefully.

Overall, great cocktails, tasty food, a fun atmosphere, and a hardworking team. Despite a couple of minor hiccups, we enjoyed ourselves and would definitely consider coming back!

Overall: 8/10

top_reviews.content:
Absolute staple of San Francisco. There’s always space to dance, multiple floors of music, and it’s always felt safe. They bring in some of the best headliners in the scene and are loved by the San Francisco music community.

Part of why 1015 is so successful is that Afton is deeply in touch with the local artist scene.

When I first moved here, I went all the time with friends and I knew eventually I wanted to be on stage myself. I started DJing, created a collective, and got into producing. After emailing a few times, I got my first shot opening for one of my favorite artists, Kasbo. It made me actually believe I might have a shot at making it in music.

Afton doesn’t ignore emails. She’s intentional about who gets to open for who, which is part of what made the opportunity feel so special.

I remember when I opened for Kasbo, she specifically asked if I knew any female DJs who could join the lineup too. She goes out of her way to support artists who get overlooked elsewhere, which has made her something of an icon among local DJs.

She understands that local DJs are a huge part of what makes 1015 successful, and she has a way of making them feel special by giving them a chance to play alongside their favorite artists. That’s why 1015 Folsom is so loved by the local community. She’s somehow turned 1015 into a beautiful music community, not just a venue that throws shows.

Great venue with several floors. Different vibe and DJs on each dancefloor. Shout out in particular to events that Afton is involved in. When she is promoting I already know it's going to be fun, well-run, well-attended, and book cool artists.

The staff is really caring and puts their all into each night the doors open. They book high quality headlining artists and work hard to book aligning and talented local support.  So come early you might just find your new favorite local DJ 😉

We loved that you could take as much time as you needed to get through the rooms and weren't stopped at 60 minutes.  The progressive story line was also layered and interesting, and having a live person be part of the experience was so unique and fun!

Absolutely loved The Game Parlour — genuinely one of my favorite places we visited while in San Francisco.

As someone with celiac disease, finding places that are not only safe but also fun and genuinely exciting to eat at can be difficult, and this place absolutely delivered. Everything being gluten-free immediately made it feel more relaxing, but what really surprised me was just how many options they had. It was honestly hard to choose because so much of the menu sounded good.

There were two of us, and we ended up ordering three items to split because we wanted to try multiple things, but the portions were way more filling than we expected. The waffle sandwiches especially were substantial, and combined with fries and drinks, we were struggling to finish everything by the end — definitely not a complaint!

Beyond the food, the whole concept and atmosphere were just great. It’s part board game café, part restaurant, and it created such a fun, welcoming environment. They had board games, cards, games for purchase, and what appeared to be rentable/playable games as well. Even in the middle of the week around lunchtime, there was a nice mix of people there — some working remotely, some grabbing lunch, some hanging out and playing games. It really felt like a community space.

The owners/staff were also incredibly kind and patient while I asked a million questions trying to decide what to order because there were so many things I wanted to try. They were genuinely helpful and welcoming throughout the whole experience.

The space itself was comfortable too, with nice bathrooms and what appeared to be outdoor seating for warmer weather.

Overall, this is exactly the kind of business I love supporting: inclusive, social, community-oriented, and safe for people with dietary restrictions without making the experience feel limited or boring. I truly hope they continue to thrive because I would 1000% go back and already want to return next time I’m in San Francisco.

I visited Ocean Beach Cafe during a short trip to San Francisco and really enjoyed it. It is about a 20 to 25 minute walk from Outer Richmond and close to Ocean Beach, which makes it a great spot for a relaxed breakfast.

I had the Epic Breakfast Sandwich, which was filling and very tasty. I also tried the Golden Chai, a turmeric-based drink, and it was warm and flavorful.

The service was friendly, and I liked their selection of non-alcoholic drinks, including infused options. Overall, it is a cute, laid-back place near the ocean and worth a visit.

One of the drinks we bought was $17 and it was super little and not even tasty. Menu is pretty small with not many good breakfast choices.

Just a minute from the beach, Ocean Beach Cafe feels exactly how a neighborhood spot should feel: welcoming & alive with community energy.

I tried the cortado, made with milk delivered fresh that morning & an iced golden chai that was perfectly balanced & refreshing after a walk by the water. From their thoughtfully curated non-alcoholic bottle shop, I picked up a premium alcohol-free wine from Vienna, Austria, part of a selection that clearly reflects intention & care behind what they stock.

Breakfast did not disappoint. A warm everything bagel with a “secret sauce” I am still thinking about, generous salsa options & homemade pastries that made it hard to choose just one. The staff is young, friendly & fast paced in the best way, attentive without ever making you feel rushed. I noticed pets happily set up with their own treats & water bowls, which adds to the relaxed coastal atmosphere.

What truly makes the place special, though, is the mix of people coming through the door. All ages. Surfers fresh from the beach, families, remote workers, neighbors picking up salads & sandwiches. It feels lived in & real.

And then there is Josh, the owner. When he walks in, the energy subtly shifts. His passion for non-alcoholic beverages, shaped by years behind the bar & now five years building this concept, gives the space a quiet magnetism. Conversations naturally unfold about well-being, mindful drinking & community. You can easily spend hours there, sipping slowly & talking about life.

I also loved the Hawaiian furniture handcrafted by his father, which gives the space a deeply personal & home-like feel.

What elevates Ocean Beach Cafe even further is how it connects daily rituals with something bigger. Every Saturday, the team organizes a local beach cleanup, inviting neighbors & customers to begin their morning with purpose. By removing plastic & marine debris from the shoreline, they contribute directly to Life Below Water (SDG 14) & the protection of coastal ecosystems. These cleanups strengthen community ownership & environmental responsibility. By turning care for public space into a shared ritual, the café contributes to Sustainable Cities & Communities (SDG 11), showing how resilient cities are built through small, consistent collective actions.

(NOTE: I can't actually rate the food becuase we didn't have any!  We stopped in to ask about omelettes and the staff members recommended we head a few doors down to TJ Cafe, which we did, (see separate review).  I just gave it 5 stars becuse everybody else has and I see no need to bring down the rating.)

On the way back to our car from TJ Cafe, i noticed, through the window, that the wall of bottles was actually topped by a big sign saying non-alcholic!  Having been a member of a non-drinking community since 1962, I was fascinated to see such display and dropped in to check it out

We spent some 15 minutes with Josh, an ex-bar tender,  explaining his philosophy on the social need for community life withoug depending on alcohol (See his Youtube channel: "Josh the non-Alcoholic" for more on this).

Josh gave my wife a free cup of coffee since TJ Cafe down the road had no had free refills, and we entered a draw to win a bottle of non-Alcoholic French wine.  Josh surprised us by telling us that the French wine industry is going big on non-alcoholic wines.

I bought a can of Vanua Bliss  - a Mango flavoured Kava drink - vastly different from the Kava served to me during my 3 years stay on Tanna, New Hebrides  (1977 to 1980) which was made by youth chewing the kava in their mouths, spitting it out on to a coconut sheath, then pouring water into it and squeezing it into a half shell of a coconut and cerimoniously handing it to you under the shade of a huge Nambunga tree as the twilight deepened! Such are memories made of.  While Kava is not alcoholic, it does have some muscle relaxant properties and give a weird buzz of the tongue.

I wish him well in his endeavour to allow the teetotaler community to enjoy the social aspects of drinks with their meals, without worring about the alcohol destroying our brain cell and livers!

There’s not a lot you can do besides look at the view. There’s no room to play sports, and even if you did, I’d hope your ball doesn’t fall down the hill. I’d feel bad giving it a 3, even if it was deserving of one based on my criteria. It’s still a memorable experience if you have nothing else to do. Overall, 4/5.

Highest point in the city. Worth a visit, even if it's foggy as it adds to the atmosphere (if you have already seen the views of the city).

The hike is easy though at an incline, there is a massive cross dedicated to the Armenian genocide up top, and I'm sure without the fog there are amazing views as well.

San Francisco offers an exceptional starting point for a day of relaxation from the top of this park, providing an awe-inspiring view of its skyline. The short hike to the summit is not overly challenging, rewarding visitors with a breathtaking panorama. This serene experience is highly recommended for those seeking a leisurely yet fulfilling day.

Mt. Davidson Park is a peaceful and scenic destination that offers one of the best nature experiences in San Francisco. The wooded trails are quiet and relaxing, and the hike to the summit is well worth it. The panoramic views from the top are absolutely stunning, making it a perfect spot for photography, reflection, or simply enjoying the fresh air. It’s a beautiful escape from the city’s hustle and bustle. Highly recommend visiting if you love nature and great views!

Loved my first "hike" on Mount Davidson. Really accessible and easy to do with a toddler and infant in an ergo. Not strenuous, but fantastic views of the city in many directions (no Golden Gate Bridge, though). I have no idea how it took me so long to get here... Half hour drive from mid-peninsula well worth it for an easy trek with multi-million dollar views. This is now a new go-to spot to bring out oft owners who don't want anything too strenuous.

Relatively easy 10 minute hike up to Mt Davidson from the 38 bus stop. Good neighborhood hike for kids and dogs on leash. Sweeping views of SF at the top and large 8 story tall cross in the eucalyptus trees. Watch out for mud in the shaded areas!

I appreciate spending time in Oscar Grant Plaza. It’s a unique open space in the heart of downtown Oakland where community truly comes alive. There’s an open grassy area where people walk their dogs, play music, and gather to connect. You’ll often see folks playing chess, singing, or engaging in deep conversations.

It’s also a powerful place—just steps from the Black Panther museum—and it naturally draws community organizers, activists, and people who come to reflect and express themselves.

🐦 The pigeons gathering here add a quiet beauty
🎶 There’s often live music or spontaneous performance
🗣️ You’ll find space for both joy and deep thought

That said, it’s not ideal for small children—people often smoke here, and sometimes folks play soccer or other ball games in ways that feel a little unsafe in such a shared space. I wish more people were mindful of how their actions impact others.

Solid downtown Oakland coffee stop with good vibes.

The lavender latte and ube latte both get a lot of love from me personally and deliver on flavor without being overly sweet. Espresso drinks are smooth and well made.
Food side is decent. Bagels are one of the stronger points and closer to a proper New York style than most places around here. Avocado toast and simple bagel combos with cream cheese or hummus hold up fine for a casual meal. Pastries like the scones and muffins are solid too.

Awaken Cafe ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

The Vibe & Workflow: Awaken hits all the marks: consistent service, great atmosphere, and serious coffee. If you’re working on a laptop (especially with a glossy screen), you’ll appreciate the thoughtful lighting and tinted windows—no glare here. The charcoal interior is a vibe, and the tables are heavy and stable (no wobbling coffee spills on your tech).

Food & Drink:

Coffee: I haven’t bought the beans, but the drip coffee is easily some of the best around.

Food: A thoughtful mix of bakery items, snack plates, and house-made sandwiches. The portions are surprisingly large.

Logistics:

Location: Smack dab between 12th St and 19th St BART. Easy hop in, hop out.

Parking: Decent amount of metered parking in the surrounding area.

Seating: Great mix, from outdoor Broadway seating to conference tables and bar spots with hooks for your bags.

The Verdict: A no-brainer for coffee, food, or a workspace in the Town. My only knock? I wish they were open later.

We came here for the first time 14 years ago, after we had just met. Our coffees were so good that we sat down and held a 2-hour long conversation while comfortably seated outside. Later 14 years married we've been back since and they still have the same great coffee and atmosphere that helped us on our first date.

As a regular coffee drinker, I’ll be honest—sometimes coffee just doesn’t hit the way you need it to. But this place completely changed that for me. I stopped in on a Monday afternoon needing a real pick-me-up and ordered a cold brew… and wow. It was smooth, bold, and perfectly balanced—honestly, I felt the boost after just a few sips.

You can really taste the quality and care in their coffee. It feels authentic, not rushed or overly processed like some places. I also tried their salted chocolate chip cookie, and it was just as impressive—fresh, flavorful, and definitely a treat worth getting again.

On top of that, the staff was patient, welcoming, and genuinely friendly, which made the whole experience even better. This is the kind of spot you look forward to coming back to—especially when you need that perfect reset during a long day.

top_reviews.content:
I can’t recommend Origin Lab Coffee & Matcha enough. From the moment you walk in, it feels like the kind of place you want to make your regular spot — cozy, clean, and genuinely welcoming. But what really sets it apart is the matcha. It’s some of the best I’ve had anywhere: smooth, high-quality, and clearly made by people who care about getting it right rather than just churning out drinks. If you’ve been let down by watery or overly sweet matcha elsewhere, this is the place that’ll change your mind.

A huge part of what makes this spot special is Ibrahim, the owner. He’s absolutely amazing — friendly, attentive, and the kind of person who makes you feel like a valued guest rather than just another customer. You can tell he takes real pride in what he’s built, and that care comes through in every detail, from the quality of the drinks to the warm atmosphere. It’s rare to find a small business run with this much heart.

Whether you’re grabbing a quick drink or settling in to relax, they’ve got you covered with both indoor and outdoor seating, and the hours are convenient too. Do yourself a favor and stop by — order a matcha, say hi to Ibrahim, and you’ll understand why this place has such a loyal following. I’ll absolutely be back, and I recommend it to anyone without hesitation. Five stars all the way.

This is my 3 times been here this place is great matcha making always ıt’s really dark matcha and so smooth when ı sip ıt’s like made my day. Employees is great very helpful this the best costumer service coffee shop in the downtown. I will definitely came back.

Just tried this new spot in FiDi that opened a couple weeks ago and honestly… it’s a matcha lover’s dream.

The quality of the matcha is on another level—super smooth, vibrant, not bitter at all. You can tell they’re using high-grade stuff, and it actually makes a difference. The drink I got (pictured) had this perfectly creamy foam with a light dusting of matcha on top—simple but really well executed.

This isn’t the place you go for your standard coffee run (there are plenty of those nearby). You come here for the specialty drinks. That’s where they really stand out—creative, well-balanced, and clearly thought through.

Also worth calling out: the vibe. The owner is incredibly warm and welcoming, and the whole staff greets you with genuine smiles. It feels like they actually care, which is rare.

Feels like a hidden gem already. Big upgrade for the neighborhood.

I stopped by Origin Lab on their soft opening day and was seriously impressed. The space feels fresh, lite, thoughtful, and inviting without trying too hard.

The coffee is excellent, smooth, balanced, and clearly made with care. You can tell they’re paying attention to quality and detail. I also tried their matcha, and it was one of the best I’ve had, vibrant, not overly sweet, and really well prepared. It’s rare to find a place that does both coffee and matcha this well.

The owner and team are friendly, welcoming, and genuinely excited to be there making coffee and matcha with expertise, and it was especially cool to see the craft going into it. Highly recommend checking it out!

top_reviews.content: Mountain Lake Park is a peaceful and beautiful place to enjoy the outdoors. Whether you’re looking for a quiet escape or a family-friendly spot to spend time outside, this park is definitely worth a visit. Highly recommended!
We traversed Mountain Lake area as part of an urban hike. Playground looked excellent with bathrooms nearby. Popular for dog walkers. Peaceful path and surrounds. Enjoy.

Outstanding playground, views, and nature:

Mountain Lake Park in San Francisco is a true hidden gem. Tucked away in the Presidio, it’s a perfect spot to escape the city’s hustle and bustle. The park’s highlight is definitely Mountain Lake, which offers beautiful views and a peaceful vibe. Walking around the lake on the well-kept trails is a great way to relax, and you might even spot some cool wildlife like birds and turtles.

For families, the playground is fantastic. It’s safe, fun, and keeps the kids entertained for hours. If you’re into sports, there are tennis courts too. One thing I really appreciate about this park is how clean and well-maintained it is, making every visit pleasant.

I love the tranquility. Despite being in the city, it feels like a quiet retreat. Whether you’re sitting by the lake, exploring the trails, or having a picnic, it’s a great place to unwind and enjoy nature.

natural beauty, good facilities, peaceful atmosphere… This makes it a must-visit in San Francisco. Whether you live nearby or are just visiting, this park is a perfect escape.

This park is really great for everything. It is very easy to access more trails from the park, such as the mountain lake trail if you want to walk there. Also, the lake itself is very pretty, especially around sunset.

DO NOT SIGN UP

The Battery has many luxurious and well-designed spaces, but most of them are CLOSED all the time. And when they are not closed they are mostly empty. Despite The Battery calling itself a "social club", the opportunity to socialize and meet likeminded people is slim to none. The fees are steep and the membership team does not grant any discretionary refunds, "not even in case of death". The Battery lures members in with well-orchestrated open houses during peak hours on Friday afternoons, when the club appears at least somewhat used, but after committing your strictly non-refundable initiation fee, the experience starts lacking very quickly and very heavily.

I visited this club on multiple occasions on various week or weekend days. All but one of the bars have been closed during every single visit. The only bar that remains open at all times can be described at mediocre at best. Both, the bar as well as the restaurant, are quite pricey despite the already steep club fees and are barely visited by any guests. While you encounter the restaurant at roughly 25% capacity some of the time, I found myself sitting in a big empty room with more staff than guests on other days. Some amenities like the rooftop or wine-room remain closed at all times can only be booked for private events against a monumental fee.

During my open house, the hostess leading my tour made various promises about all the great spaces and events and how many great people one can meet when joining the club. In truth, the club is empty most of the week, over 80% of its amenities are closed at all times, and the membership team only cares about collecting initiation fees rather than using feedback to improve the club. This club is not a good place to spend your social time and I honestly feel ripped off.

Some places feel exclusive. The Battery feels intentional.

We’ve spent a lot of time around spaces that promise a certain level of experience, and not all of them deliver. The Battery does—quietly, confidently, without needing to prove anything. From the moment you step inside, there’s a sense that every detail has been considered, not just for aesthetics, but for how people actually move through and enjoy the space.

What stands out most is the consistency. The service is dialed in—attentive without hovering, polished without feeling stiff. It’s the kind of hospitality that understands its audience and meets them exactly where they are. As a business that values experience just as much as product, that level of execution doesn’t go unnoticed.

The food and drink program holds its own, too. Nothing feels like an afterthought. It’s curated, balanced, and reliable in a way that supports the overall atmosphere rather than competing with it. You’re not just there to eat—you’re there to exist in a space that’s been carefully built for connection, conversation, and a certain pace of life.

Places like The Battery don’t happen by accident. It takes vision, discipline, and a clear understanding of what your clientele actually values. From our perspective, it’s a standard worth recognizing—and one that raises the bar for everyone operating in the same ecosystem.

top_reviews.content:
The Twin Peaks Tavern is the first LGBTQ bar in the world to have oversized windows making its patrons visible from the street outside. This happened in 1972 when two local lesbians purchased what had been an Irish Pub since 1935. Historically, gay bars had no windows, to protect the anonymity of the patrons and for safety and security, as gay bars could be a target of vandalism or other violence.

It's saloon days go back to the gay nineties, i.e., the 1890s. It is a designated SF historic landmark at the corner of Castro and 17th street.

One of the best people watching spots in the Castro. You never know what you'll see on Castro Street in front of the bar.

It nearly closed during the Covid Pandemic, but a Gofundme campaign raised over $100,000 to keep it open.

There's a documentary short film, "Through the Windows," about the historic and beautiful bar.

top_reviews.content: The vibrant walls and colorful decor may feel a little overwhelming at first, but the food certainly makes up for it. We had the cheesecake which was dense yet perfectly soft , along with avocado toast and a sandwich. The avocado toast was topped with a thick fluffy layer of egg, and cherry tomatoes. The bacon-and-egg croissant sandwich  had flaky, golden croissant layers, and was filled with fluffy scrambled egg , and generous pieces of crispy bacon. It was buttery, and hearty. There are also plenty of snacks, and little bites to choose from, making it a great spot to linger over a meal.

Food was lovely, i had their chocolate pistachio baklava, turkish delight and a slice of dubai chocolate cake. They were all nice

Mellis Cafe is a bright, welcoming café that makes a good stop for coffee in the Union Square area. I visited before a nearby appointment and ordered a drip coffee, which was strong, flavorful, and served quickly by the friendly staff.

The café has a comfortable layout with seating on both the main level and a raised area toward the back. In addition to coffee, they offer a selection of Turkish sweets, including baklava and Turkish delight. Overall, it has a relaxed atmosphere and is a nice place to enjoy a coffee or take a short break before continuing your day.

I was visiting town for a conference staying at the Hilton Union Square just down the street.

First, I chose this place because my name is Meli, and... Close enough. Second of all, it had good reviews and I love me a good bagel sandwich. Third, it was very conveniently located from the hotel. Glad to report that it did not disappoint!

My husband and I went twice and got two different kinds of breakfast sandwiches; all were delish. I love that you can customize easily.

Bagels are yummy but wish there was more than only plain cream cheese.

Coffee was yummy, too! We had lattes and cappuccinos and were happy all around.

I dig that they have a bunch of random snacks available - some that are not normally available just anywhere...

Not a ton of seating, but we went at like 9:30am on a Saturday and we're easily able to sit, so that was nice.

Staff was sweet and friendly. Would happily return!

top_reviews.content: NLPOA provides a great community service at this park every year for an Easter Extravaganza. The park is a great place for family gatherings. I remember spending so many summers at this historic landmark in West Oakland. It's got a ton of space to just hang out, from a baseball field, skate park, basketball courts, and a recreation center where you can enroll the kids in youth activities. You can even rent out a venue there! There's also a swimming pool, though I'm not sure if it's still open since it's been a really long time since I've swum there. But we had a blast when I was a kid! It's an awesome park with tons to do.

I'm 71 and I played in this park until I was 14. When I was 6 and older there was this thing that kids would hold on to run real fast and jump on it. I would swear it was 50 kids or more...this was in the 50's and early 60's. My siblings and I would go swimming and our great uncle would be near the men at the picnic tables taking a shot and giving us change for the snow cone truck. At 15 no more parks for me and my family lived on 37th and Webster across from Moss wood. I will always love this park . precious family memories. The baseball field is gone. Today so many White People at the Park. When I was growing up all Black hard working folks. Our visit today was for Patricia Lowe..Queen of Line dancing..

An area asset. Historical importance can't be understated. I met in the old house building just yesterday to action against unjust coal plans in Oakland. The legacy of protest is alive, but we should haveadw more progress. Don't forget the history or the struggle.
I was there for an event for Easter by the NLPOA (National Latino Peace Officers of Alameda)

I paid $70 for admission( working hours in Saturday 11:00am- 8:00pm), but less than 12 minutes after we entered (I bought the ticket at 6:54 PM, and the lights went out at 7:06 PM), the staff just went home. They turned off the lights, armed the security alarm, locked the doors, and left me inside with my son without even checking if all the visitors had exited!

We tried the cortado and an iced latte, and both were excellent. You could clearly taste the quality of the coffee beans and the drinks felt very refreshing. They also had a good selection of pastries and sandwiches that looked tempting and worth trying next time.

top_reviews.content:
Starbucks (3801 Bayview Plaza)

I stopped by this location and ordered a medium macchiato with whipped cream and extra drizzle. The experience ended up requiring three separate corrections before the order was finally addressed.

After placing the order, I waited roughly 8–10 minutes. During that time two customers approached the pickup counter because their orders had been made incorrectly. When my drink was handed to me, it was a hot macchiato instead of iced, so I asked for a correction. The replacement drink I received was iced but missing both the whipped cream and the extra drizzle that had been requested. I had to go back a third time to ask for the order to be fixed.

Separately, I asked staff whether I could leave a few flyers. One employee said she would “give them to the manager,” but no clear approval or denial was communicated.

While waiting inside, I noticed that customer traffic appeared relatively low, and a large portion of the people entering seemed to be connected to nearby offices. The location sits adjacent to a CPS/child-welfare office and other publicly funded service providers, and many of the surrounding businesses in the plaza appear tied to government-funded or nonprofit operations.

This broader context is relevant because the surrounding area has limited food access. The recent closure of the Lucky grocery store in Bayview has made the neighborhood more of a food desert, leaving only a small number of nearby options (such as a Subway and a few small restaurants) along with this Starbucks. For a location serving a community with limited alternatives, basic service accuracy and responsiveness become especially important.

Between the repeated order errors, the unclear response to a simple request about community flyers, and the overall setting in a resource-limited area heavily connected to public-service infrastructure, this location would benefit from stronger management oversight and more consistent customer service practices.

I hope corporate leadership reviews how this store is operating within the broader neighborhood ecosystem, because locations like this often function as informal gathering points for residents, service providers, and families navigating nearby institutions.

The only thing that I could not stand was the music in the store. They were blasting music at maximum volume. It was so bad that even the cashier could not hear what I was saying. I was hoping to stay at the store to do work, but had to leave as it was too loud in there. I'd give this place another try, but there are nicer Starbucks out there.

(1) The first thing that irked me big time was the fact that they didn’t have outlets… let alone blocked outlets that you don’t allow guests to use. No wonder that’s why there was such less foot traffic than all other local coffee shops in our area…

Chloe’s Café is one of those rare San Francisco treasures that has managed to keep its heart and charm through the decades. I used to live catty-corner from the restaurant, and my weekend ritual was to peek out the window at the line before heading down — because yes, there’s always a line on weekends (and for good reason!).

It’s a small, cozy spot with only a handful of tables inside, but after COVID they expanded to outdoor seating, which made it even more inviting. Still, expect a bit of a wait — the food is absolutely worth it.

The menu is to die for, but the banana walnut pancakes deserve their own round of applause. Fluffy, perfectly caramelized, and subtly nutty — I’ve never had better pancakes anywhere, period. Add in friendly, efficient service and the charm of being right on the J line at Church and 26th, and it’s easy to see why Chloe’s has been a neighborhood favorite for so many years.

If you’re looking for a classic SF breakfast spot with soul, this is it. 🥞☕

Stopped into Coffee To The People while exploring San Francisco and really enjoyed the vibe.

I just got a chai latte, but overall it was a really comfortable spot to warm up, relax for a bit, and recharge before heading back out to explore. The staff were friendly, the drinks were affordable, and the café had a lot more seating than many of the other coffee shops we visited around the city.

The atmosphere had a lot of personality too. It wasn’t polished or overly cookie-cutter, which honestly made it feel more authentic and welcoming. There were used books, stickers, flyers, community postings, and all kinds of little details that gave the place charm and character.

We were there during the middle of the week, so it wasn’t overly crowded, but there were still people working, hanging out, and enjoying the space, which added to the cozy neighborhood feel.

One small note: the overall aesthetic definitely leans more eclectic/grungy than modern and sleek, which I personally didn’t mind in the main café space because it fit the personality of the place. The bathroom experience wasn’t quite my favorite though. I understand why many city cafés require a key/code for restroom access, but I do tend to prefer bathrooms to feel a bit cleaner and more updated, even in more laid-back spaces.

Overall though, definitely somewhere I’d go back to. It had a relaxed, lived-in kind of atmosphere that just worked.

top_reviews.content:
On Saturday, June 20, 2026, I ate at U :Dessert Story for my birthday.

We went there a little bit after 5 pm. The place wasn't busy at all. There were a few people eating there.

Here's what we ordered. The Salted Egg Yolk Brick Toast, Chocolate Volcano Bingsu 🌋 and Mango Stick Rice Bingsu. The Salted Egg Yolk Brick Toast was hands down one of the best desserts I've ever eaten. The orange Egg custard sauce was delicious and the Brick Toast was warm and soft. The vanilla bean ice cream on top was the perfect addition to this dessert. Hands down the best dessert out of the 3 we ordered and definitely a 5 out of a 5! The Chocolate Volcano Bingsu was good. It wasn't knock your socks off good like the Salted Egg Yolk Brick Toast but good overall. The chocolate flavor was lacking in my opinion. I wanted it to taste more like chocolate and have more of a chocolate pronounced flavor but it didn't. The chocolate flavor was mild at best. There were bananas, cocoa krispies, corn flakes and brownie chunks throughout the chocolate volvcano. I can see why a lot of people order this dessert because the presentation is cool. It's pretty big and it comes out with a dry ice cube on top that makes it look smoky and foggy to simulate a volcano that just erupted. Cool concept. The mango sticky rice Bingsu was my least favorite. The mango chunks weren't ripe and were hard. They didn't taste good or have good flavor. The sticky rice which was green tasted okay but not so great. The condensed milk on the side was super sweet and made the dessert taste somewhat better. But overall the mango sticky rice Bingsu was a failure. I don't recommend ordering this dessert.

Even though the mango sticky rice Bingsu wasn't good, I would still come back and try more desserts. I would try another Brick Toast and some other chocolate desserts that sounded good on the menu.

I came with friends for dessert one evening, but it was a bit disappointing overall.
When we arrived (a little late), all the toast items were already sold out. The staff didn’t inform us beforehand and just let us sit down, which felt quite unprofessional.

The regular cakes were average — nothing special. The shaved ice (bingsu)was less sweet than I expected, which was actually a good thing for me, but it was served in very basic, low-quality dishes that didn’t match the café’s supposed aesthetic or price level.

The biggest disappointment was the Thai Tea Mille Crepe. The sauce was not smooth at all — it had clumps and felt very sweet(looks like curry?). I still finished it, but the next day I suffered from severe diarrhea. I strongly suspect the sauce and cream in the Thai Tea mille crepe were not fresh.

Lesson learned: it’s probably best to avoid dairy-based desserts here in the evening.
Will think twice before returning.

Second time here & the quality of food + service were amazing both times :) I know everyone comes here for the bingsu but don’t sleep on their pastries! They make them all from scratch in-house. The chocolate matcha lava cake is SUPERB. Instead of chocolate oozing out, it’s matcha flavor filling. A bite of the cake, matcha filling, matcha ice cream and cookie crunch… heaven :)
