Honestly, my only hesitation in leaving this review is that it might get so popular I’ll have to start waiting in longer lines!

We found this hidden gem during our Spring Break vacation. We loved it so much we visited multiple times. The owner is so friendly and welcoming, the atmosphere is relaxing; feels like home. I ordered the LOX bagel each time, I couldn’t get enough of it. I wish we had this place back home.

Beautiful local cafe with a huge menu of breakfast, sandwiches, pastries and gelatos. Loved everything we tried and coffee is amazing. No laptops allowed here so you get to have real conversations and nobody be hogging tables.

The doc offers a fresh& thought-provoking take on environmentalism &spirituality within the documentary space, making for a screening unlike any other
The Great Star team was incredibly kind and welcoming throughout the evening.

Saw a Sketchfest event here and excited to check out more here. Seats are just as historic for better or worse: May be a bit small for those who are bigger, your view may be blocked if you're short and are sat behind a tall person, and can be a challenge to get to your assigned seat. Sat closer to the wall and volume got a bit loud, enough to make my ears ring a bit after, so consider ear plugs if you're sensitive. During the show, the stage lighting was randomly cycling through the different lights for a moment and was a little distracting. Little downside of going back to the Central Subway after the show is the hill you have to walk up to get back to Stockton. Still don't regret going to this theater and it won't be my last.

This is definitely becoming one of my favorite spots in the Bay—perfect for taking a breather, getting some work done, or simply soaking in those classic California vibes. Highly recommended.

Live Oak Park is a nice city park with a mix of amenities and spaces for meeting up with friends. There are several distinct areas for different activity types, and this park is especially popular with families.

Between Shattuck and Walnut Streets, there is a green space for groups and families to hang out. There are some nice trees and an idyllic stream where you can catch nature vibes.

Directly south of the lawn and separated by the stream, there is the Live Oak Community Center and Live Oak Theater for community events and performing arts. This side of the park contains playgrounds, basketball courts, and tennis courts. The playground amenities are much better for older children than toddlers. The varuous ball courts are in decent-but-not-amazing condition.

Across the street (between Walnut and Oxford), there is a smaller park "Area 2" with some picnic tables and a grill. There isn't much green space on this side, but you can visit the Berkeley Art Center while here. I recommend stopping by if you are visiting when the Art Center is open (12pm-5pm, Fri-Sun, free admission).

The prices are totally fair.

The people in the bar are friendly, and even if you’re not a local, they’ll welcome you in Like you are.

I understand that new owners took over the place, but it still remains an amazing vibe. They kept the Photo Booth, And all the fixings.

Let’s keep it a SF secret!

The 500 Club bar is a delightful neighborhood spot that effortlessly combines old-school charm with a welcoming, modern atmosphere. From the moment you step inside, you’ll notice its classic neon sign and vintage décor, which give it an inviting, retro vibe. The bartenders are friendly, approachable, and highly skilled, crafting cocktails that range from time-honored favorites to creative twists. Meanwhile, the reasonably priced beer selection caters to those who prefer a no-frills, laid-back experience.

Regular patrons will tell you that the 500 Club is a place where strangers soon become friends, thanks to the bar’s relaxed ambiance and lively conversation. Whether you’re grabbing a quick after-work drink or settling in for a long night of socializing, the space offers comfortable seating and enough room to breathe. On most nights, the jukebox plays an eclectic selection of tunes that appeal to a wide variety of tastes. Throughout the week, you can find local artists and the occasional event, adding an extra layer of entertainment. All in all, the 500 Club delivers a charming slice of neighborhood nightlife that feels refreshingly unpretentious. It’s an ideal destination for anyone looking to unwind, enjoy good company, and savor authentic bar culture.

Aquatic Park, located near the San Francisco Maritime National Historical Park, is a historic waterfront area featuring a sheltered cove, a sandy beach, and a promenade along the northern edge of the city. This is a nifty little museum that packs a surprisingly big punch for its size. The Randall Museum is an absolute gem for families looking for an affordable, engaging outing that combines education with genuine fun. As a free attraction, it stands out as one of the best ways to enjoy quality bonding and learning time with the little ones without worrying about ticket prices or expensive extras.

My kids were completely captivated from the moment we walked in. They especially loved the live reptiles and the insect exhibits, spending a long time watching the snakes, lizards, and various bugs up close. There’s something special about seeing their eyes light up when they get to observe real animals rather than just pictures in a book. Beyond the creatures, the museum offers a thoughtful mix of hands-on science displays, nature-focused exhibits, and interactive stations that encourage curiosity without overwhelming younger visitors.

What makes the experience even better is the relaxed, uncrowded atmosphere. Unlike larger, more hectic museums, the Randall feels intimate and approachable. Kids can move at their own pace, ask questions, and revisit the displays that grab their attention most. Parents will appreciate how easy it is to supervise while still feeling like they’re sharing in the discovery. It’s the kind of place where you leave feeling like you’ve actually connected with your children rather than simply entertained them.

I would definitely recommend setting aside an afternoon to come and enjoy some time here with your kids. Whether you’re looking for a low-pressure educational outing or just a pleasant way to spend a free day together, the Randall Museum delivers. It’s one of those underrated local spots that reminds you great experiences don’t always require a big budget or a long drive—just a little curiosity and some time together.

top_reviews.content:
This staging area is the western edge of Reinhardt Redwood Regional Park, located on Skyline Boulevard in Oakland. The eastern staging area is on Redwood Road and called the "Redwood Staging Area." Us old-timers just call them the Skyline or Redwood Gate. The parking lot is free, there are two toilets with running water to wash hands. A water fountain and faucet to fill water bottles and for dogs.

It's Springtime while I'm writing this review and there are LOADS of ticks. Wear white socks that cover your calf and take boots and socks off before getting back in your car. Check your pants and your dogs, especially collars and tail feathers.

The trail to the left of the lot is a one mile gradual decline to a bench. You choose to either keep going down or turn around. The trail to the right is mostly flat and is 1.25 miles to the Moon Gate.

The parking lot is very crowded on weekends so choose other trailheads such as Waterloo or Moon Gate. Another good tip is to buy an annual pass from the East Bay Regional Parks District Foundation: All lots are free, discounts on water activities like swimming and boating.

Have fun, bring more water than you think you need, and check everyone for ticks!
Great little spot for a nice walk/hike/bike trails with breathtaking views and big redwoods!!!

Overall great start to a hike!

Parking: free lot with plenty of spaces, but it fills up fast! We got here around 8:15am and there were only two spots left
Bathrooms: porta potty style, but there’s sanitizer inside
Trails: area connects to multiple trails of various levels. We went down on the stream trail. Be warned- from this starting point it is quite steep (and muddy)! Lots of cool mushrooms at this time of year.

It's a moderate to difficult hike in some portions. Due to rain the weather was nice but pockets of places where it was slippery. So be careful and wear you hiking and mud boots.
Parking is not enough and street parking has to be done in a way that you don't block the road. Couple of my friends got ticket and fine for $76 (not cheap). So be very careful. Come early and you may find parking.
Overall I enjoyed the hike. It's DOG and CAT friendly so bring them along but also be ready to get mud off of them 😀😀.

Ave Maria! Amazing, it is peaceful and quiet. Don't go by yourself special if you don't know the area because we saw only two couples in our entire hike. My group and I had the park pretty much to ourselves but it is huge. The trees are gorgeous 😍 bring water and snacks because it is a long hike. Dress in layers even if it is 120 at the parking lot because the temperature drops to approximately 50's once you are deep in the park.  Be aware of mountain loins/bobcats, coyotes, ect. Enjoy the peace that the place gives you. Please don't leave garbage or graphite on trees or rocks be respectful of mother nature.

that's how i know a spot has character. a metaphor: this bar shares the name for a soldier in a core unit of the ancient roman army, but when you arrive, you will be greeted by a sign reading "cead míle fáilte", which feels like an ironic juxtaposition, especially for someone like me whose family came from ireland through scotland to the united states. rome never openly attempted to conquer hibernia (their name for ireland), but they did exert a proto-colonial type of influence over the region, primarily through christianity. however, catholicism came to be a defining aspect of irish identity, especially during the troubles. small aspects of gaelic paganism survived even into my own family's traditions by being fully wrapped in a christian coat. now these things are inextricable; culture is messy like that. and in that respect, the name kind of works. that's this bar — it's a lot of things, and they weirdly fit together into being a special little community. the reason i have to withhold a star, even though (in case you haven't figured it out by now) this is my favorite bar is that the drinks... are fine? this is mostly a review of the experience, but drinks are a part of that experience, and they're honestly whatever. they're good enough! it's the memories and fun times that keep me coming back. objectively, it's a four out of five. but subjectively... well, everybody knows it has a perfect score in my heart.

North Beach Playground History

I've lived in North Beach for over two decades. Back then, the playground's official name was "North Beach Playground," and it was a bit behind on maintenance. Then, when the great Joe DiMaggio passed away, the city decided to rename it. The story goes that the Hall of Famer's estate did not take kindly to the fact that his name was associated with a rundown playground. So in 2005, the city completed a $7.5 million renovation and significantly improved the facilities.

The park is a great place for all in the neighborhood. Families can bring their kids and take advantage of the kids' playground. There are tennis, basketball, and Bocce courts, a public pool, and a multi-use community building with table tennis tables available for all.

Many people might not know that Joe DiMaggio grew up in North Beach and played baseball in the very same area where the playground now stands. His legacy and connection to the community made the renaming and renovation even more meaningful. The park is a recreational space and a tribute to the iconic baseball legend who became a local hero.

The playground is also home to some interesting public art pieces, including murals depicting scenes from DiMaggio’s life and career. This adds a unique cultural and historical layer to the park, making it a place for physical activities and a spot for reflection and appreciation of local history.

Moreover, the playground is beautifully integrated into the North Beach community, surrounded by charming cafes, bakeries, and historic landmarks. It's a place where you can feel the vibrant spirit of the neighborhood, whether you're taking a stroll or engaging in a friendly game of Bocce.

The Joe DiMaggio Playground is truly a gem in the heart of North Beach, blending history, culture, and recreation in a way that enriches the lives of all who visit. Whether you're a local or just passing through, it's definitely worth a visit to experience its unique charm and significance.

The cashier was attentive and extremely helpful with their recommendations. Will definitely be back in the future.

Such a delightful and charming café! Worth the long drive for a bite to eat. The atmosphere was warm and inviting, and the vibes were pure comfort. I went with my friend, and we shared our food like old companions on a cozy little adventure. I felt like Bilbo Baggins enjoying a hearty meal in my Hobbit hole, watching the rain sprinkle softly outside as people hurried past on their way to work or the nearby hospital. The only thing missing was my pipe!
The service was absolutely phenomenal. The owners went above and beyond with their hospitality, and I’m still touched by how kind and genuine they were. I truly hope they know how much their efforts were appreciated, and they have my sincerest prayers that their café continues to flourish and bring warmth to those who wander through their doors.

First time visiting this cute little café, and I was pleasantly surprised. The rose cinnamon latte was unique, flavorful, and absolutely delicious. The homemade biscuits were fresh, buttery, and the perfect complement to my drink. The atmosphere was cozy and welcoming, making it a great spot to relax and unwind. The only downside was that parking was a bit difficult to find, but the experience was well worth it. I’ll definitely be back!

We enjoyed the Classic Breakfast after it was recommended witch included eggs, toast, and potatoes. We were also graced with the very tasty banana bread, and fruit bowl featuring nectarines and pears. Our beverages were a cappuccino and a hot chocolate. Everything was very tasty, presented very well, and was very affordable. The restaurant itself was really clean and looked great inside and out. We will definitely be back! The staff was very friendly and helpful!

Great indie cafe find. Operated by some nice folks from Turkey. They offer some unique coffee concoctions (got The Sandman Latte, super food chaga cocoa vanilla cinnamon with oatmilk). And yes, they have Ube Latte with the rootcrop sourced from the Philippines). The only problem was that we arrived at 330PM and they close at 4PM (they open at 7AM), but they were nice enough to allow us to order still and stay until 430PM.

Came in here for the first time today and I’m so glad I did! Their matcha oat latte was soooo yummy and their staff was so accommodating and friendly. The matcha they use is soooo yummy, I’ve had a lot of matcha (as this is my beverage of choice) but I now feel like this earned my top choice for matcha lattes. This is now one of my favorite matcha spots in the city. I intend to buy some matcha next time I stop by. Thank you so much!! 🩵

Highly recommend this spot you won’t regret it!

We’ve been searching San Francisco this week for the best mochas. This place has a line of locals, because it’s obviously really good. A few seats outside, but mainly just to go orders. Guys working are super chill. Love it

Delicious coffee!
I ordered an oat cappuccino and totally loved the texture and flavor of the coffee.

Their coffee is velvety, smooth and balanced. Prices are comparable to local coffee shops in SF area.

Highly recommend this place for a great cup of coffee!

Awarding 3 stars for decent coffee and 4 stars for kind service from a kind young man. Cappuccinos were decent and cortado was good. This establishment sells its marquee beans which they roast and offer to other cafes. That’s a big plus for me and we purchased single origin Sumatra beans to take home. Merchandise for sale effectively promotes their brand. It’s a hole in the wall with no seating to speak of. Didn’t help that 1 hour earlier I visited Coffee Movement on Balboa Street which is a top tier establishment on national scale - and coffee drinks at a lower price point. There are other coffee houses that offer better cups than Snowbird in San Francisco which you can find by reading my reviews.

Snowbird Coffee makes a decent cup of coffee and they also have a small pastry shelf. Nothing outstanding but you get your morning coffee and bite done.  Service is friendly and fast, and there is a spacious parket outside so you can hang around if you would like to.

Cool fun bar on the edge of nob Hill. Very large interior, but very ordinary. Music is good, locals are good, bartenders here are generally great. Mainly go here for big gatherings. But style here is not the main concern. There are some bar games.

Pretty chill bar with good beers on tap. I was staying close-by when travelling solo and dropped in one evening for some beers. I sat at the bar, watched some game on the TV.. The bartender was attentive. It's located across from a Thai restaurant and a Chinese restaurant across the road.

Chill and fun place with a warm atmosphere. Craft beers and a pleasant cocktail menu. They have Skee Ball + Skee Basketball, and a boxing punch game. The staff was friendly and the holiday decorations were fun and thorough. Next time I'll try pool or shuffle board!

The Wreck Room is a classic neighborhood bar with great energy and a really comfortable, welcoming vibe. It’s got that local feel that’s hard to find, laid-back, friendly, and full of good people. Drinks are strong, reasonably priced, and the bartenders are chill and easy to talk to.

There’s plenty to keep you entertained too, pool tables, darts, shuffleboard, and a couple of arcade games, all spread out enough that it never feels cramped or too loud. It’s the perfect kind of spot where you can actually relax, have a few drinks, and hang out without feeling rushed or overwhelmed.

A friend of mine who’s a regular brought me here for the first time a few weeks ago, and I liked it so much that I came back with my boyfriend not long after. Both times we had a great experience. Even though we’re from out of the district, everyone made us feel right at home, like we’d been coming there for years.

Overall, The Wreck Room just gets it right. It’s comfortable, fun, and has that real community feel that keeps you wanting to come back. Not too loud, not too small, just a genuinely great place to spend an evening with friends. Definitely a new favorite.

top_reviews.content: This place is AMAZING!!! I came here to celebrate my 21st and it did NOT disappoint! The queens are GORGEOUS and have such great energy! If your going to SF, add this place to your list!

Inexpensive drag Brunch. Well worth the trip and spend that extra money on the amazing Queens. The staff takes good care of everyone and it is a good time. The wings were pretty darn good.

Bring cash. There is no atm!

The lesbian parade on the Friday of Pride weekend is what brought us here, to hopefully grab a birds eye view of it while having a few beers. Believe it or not, it worked! We ended up with choice seats at the corner outdoor lanai.

ATMOSPHERE:
The bar takes up the entire second floor of a two level building at the corner of 16th & Market, right where the parade passes. Plus, they have a cool but skinny outdoor lanai with a railing counter and bar stools that is excellent for people-watching. The inside has some good square footage but it still can get cramped.

The crowd was a mix. We met all walks of life while here, including a gay-friendly drunk straight girl traveling nurse that wanted to take my gay friend and possibly me home. :-O Thanks anyway, sister lol.

They have a full service bar and great music.

SERVICE:
Though I didn't experience it because all of my beers were purchased for me, my friends returned fairly quickly from the bar, so service was fast despite the busyness.

FUN TIP:
Something that kept me entertained were the ding dong drivers at the intersection of Market, Noe & 16th. Some drivers on Noe that were headed north would stop for some reason in the middle of Market, thus blocking traffic headed east on Market. HONNNNNNNK and me SMH all afternoon long, lol!

OVERALL:
Cool vibe & views, great prices, free street entertainment.

A mainstay in the Castro with a large balcony that overlooks Market st. Usually great music and sometimes a drag show! They have decent bar food which is a plus when wanting something casual while you also have a drink!

New to town, everyone was very friendly. Had a great time talking and having 2 Peach Lemonades to die for. Haven't had a drink this good since I was in Georgia. DJ played fun music for a Sunday afternoon. Loud enough to dance and just quiet enough to chat. Come on out and enjoy a Peach Lemonade!
Really like the refreshed look and the fun vibe.  Bartenders were super friendly and made me feel welcomed.  Will definitely be back!

Loved this!!! Been to plenty back home. Tracy Love and the late Bradly Bogart! Miss him dearly.  The show here was Awesome!!!

top_reviews.content: rader Sam’s is one of those rare San Francisco bars that feels like stepping into a fully realized world rather than just another place to grab a drink. The immersive tiki décor, warm amber lighting, and layers of hand-crafted details give the space a cozy, transportive feel that immediately sets it apart from typical cocktail bars. It’s intimate without feeling cramped, with different pockets of seating that make it work equally well for quiet conversations or casual group outings. While the bar is clearly adult-oriented in terms of drinks, the playful tropical visuals make it approachable and visually engaging even earlier in the evening. The atmosphere leans relaxed and nostalgic rather than loud or chaotic, which makes it a great stop for people who value ambiance as much as cocktails. Accessibility is generally manageable with ground-level seating and open walkways, though tighter areas near the bar may require some navigation

I went there on a Saturday night to check out this old San Francisco Tiki bar hangout.

We got there around 9:30 expecting there to be some form of a crowd. It was rather empty, that should’ve been our first clue. The one thing I will tell you Is that it definitely smells like an old San Francisco bar. But giving it the benefit of the doubt, and the fact that there’s a long history with this bar, we ventured on and order a drink.

My partner and I both ordered a mai tai. We figured this was a tiki bar staple that could be made easily and correctly. The bartender had to look at the menu and some instructions to figure out how to make a mai tai. Frankly, it was really just a pineapple drink with a smidge of booze.

The bar is a very strange tiki bar like setting, but unfortunately has a huge TV, which is a dead giveaway that it’s not a real tiki bar. It’s more like a local tiki bar themed hangout that used to be super cool and now. Is resting on some form of a laurel.

The best part about the place is the sign outside. So maybe stop by for a photo of the sign and go to one of the other many great tiki bars In San Francisco.

Sorry, but this bar has had its day.

Truly nothing like this spot. For an outer Richmond excursion there’s nowhere I’d rather go. Trad’r Sam follows through on good vibes, good drinks, welcoming & friendly staff, and most importantly a sense of community. Beware, if you go once you may just find yourself sat at this bar more often than not. I see tikki drinks in your future!
one of my favorite bars in the city. the drinks are well priced and i haven’t had a drink that i didn’t enjoy. great to go with friends and share a bowl with

Loved my experience here the cocktails tasted ok the Mai Tai wasn’t traditional but was ok I liked the zombie more. They typically blend the zombie but the bartender gave us the choice so we went with it on the rocks. They also take card now but charge a transaction fee.

top_reviews.content:
Bluestone Lane Avery Café in FiDi is one of those polished, modern cafés I had been wanting to try, and overall the food was good. The soft chili scramble toast with salmon stood out. The scrambled eggs tasted fresh and well cooked, and the salmon was nicely balanced and not overly salty, which I really appreciated.

That said, a couple of things felt off. When we walked in, the sign at the entrance said to wait for staff to seat us, but guests who arrived after us were allowed to pick tables on their own. That was confusing and took away a bit from the experience. The granola yogurt bowl was also disappointing. It had an overwhelming amount of granola and barely any yogurt, making it feel very dry, and we ended up leaving a lot of it unfinished. Improving the yogurt to granola ratio would make a big difference.

Overall, it is a solid café with good food, but there is room for improvement in both service flow and a few menu details.

Finding a place that does both a proper latte and a proper breakfast in the United States is like stumbling upon an oasis in the desert.

Couldn’t recommend this place more to anybody who has had to suffer what is labelled a “latte” elsewhere in this country. Thanks guys! 🙏

Bluestone Lane Avery Café is one of my favorite neighborhood spots — the coffee is consistently excellent and the Aussie-inspired menu never disappoints.
The space is bright, welcoming, and perfect for a relaxed breakfast or quick meeting.
Everything feels fresh and thoughtfully done.
Chris runs it with such warmth and pride — you can truly feel it every time you walk in.

My coworker told me about Bluestone so I decided to check them out. The guy who helped me out was very chill. He recommended the Blueberry and peanut butter smoothie, his recommendation was spot on what I was looking for. I also ordered a Bacon Egg and cheese croissant. Safe to say I’ll be back for more. Thanks to Edgar and his team

If you are visiting this hidden SF treasure, please be reminded that parking is scarce.

The whole experience was great both times we went. We went yesterday to have some coffee and ended up staying a while to chat and today we went back for breakfast and coffee and again it was great. The owner/manager was so attentive and created a great feel. Will be back next week visit.

One of the nicest and most unique parks in San Francisco.

There are plenty of spots to sit, there's a grassy area if you'd like to have a picnic, and there are porta-potties if you need to use one. There are great views of the bay and a platform so you can see everything. Also, the area is very clean and you could probably swim in the cove if you wanted.

Not only is it a park, but also a historical site. There are many signs with information about people building ships and some remnants of the equipment. Overall, I highly recommend this park. You could easily spend a whole afternoon here.

Sunny and clean city park with a nice lawn, dog area and a small beach! I passed by the park during a run along the coast and enjoyed a little stop in this beautiful park. There are some picnic tables in the park which is awesome but otherwise there aren't a lot of facilities in the park so I think it has some potentials to be more interesting.
The neighborhood feels modern and urban, has plenty of restaurants and cafes within a short walk.

Absolutely stellar, playful and uniquely situated park in Mission Bay / Dogpatch.  Love the historical structures still standing and the playful silhouette paintings of boats that were build here.  The beach looks like a stellar paddle board / wading area.

It’s a beach in Dogpatch Neighborhood. Bring your kayak, picnic basket or not as there are picnic tables with a grill! Super dog friendly, kids can ride their bikes, scooters, fly a kite, and have fun.

Lovely park for families, dogs, everyone. You can wade in the bay or canoe. The cranes and equipment are fascinating. Lots of care and detail went into this park and it shows. There is a cool restaurant and bar nearby and others within walking distance.

I had a great experience at this Berkeley coffee shop today. My family and I enjoyed coffee and some drinks, and everything was excellent. The service was friendly and attentive, the place was super clean and truly luxurious, and the drinks were incredibly good. Highly recommend.

With so many empty storefronts on Telegraph and businesses without interior guest spaces, I welcome this new place to study while being able to enjoy their coffee and food. The service is very friendly and the owner is a young bipoc local.

Boudin is one of those places that just feels like San Francisco. Every time we visit, it's lively, bustling, and full of energy, and it's become a must-stop for our family.

One of the highlights of this trip was introducing our kids to Boudin for the first time. Watching them experience the famous sourdough bread was so much fun, and they were instantly hooked. The bread really is as good as everyone says it is.

As visitors, there are plenty of places you can eat in San Francisco, but Boudin is one of the few that feels like a true city tradition. Between the delicious food, the iconic sourdough, and the fun atmosphere, it's an experience as much as it is a meal.

If you're visiting San Francisco, put Boudin on your list. It's a classic for a reason.

Small Boudin location with the classic sourdough breads!  We got the long 1.5 lb sourdough and they sliced it on the spot.  The bread was fresh and delicious!  We will be coming back to this location during our stay in Inner Richmond.

Already famous for their sourdough, locals already know the Geary & 10th location is the best spot to get Boudin without dealing with Fisherman's Wharf crowds, but here’s the real insider hidden gem: skip the sourdough and try their focaccia.

I ordered the Ham & Brie on Rosemary Focaccia, and the bread steals the show. It’s incredibly fresh, perfectly oily without being greasy, pillowy soft on the inside, and beautifully seasoned with fragrant rosemary and sea salt. It’s a massive upgrade from a standard sandwich roll and holds up perfectly to the ingredients.

If you think Boudin is a one-trick pony for tourists, order a sandwich on the focaccia or grab a tomato focaccia loaf to go.
It's heavily loaded with blistered, caramelized tomatoes. The edge pieces have this incredible, crispy, oil-fried crunch, but the inside stays completely pillowy and soft. When you bite into it, the sweetness of the roasted tomatoes balances out the rich, savory oil.

It tastes like an artisanal flatbread you’d pay top dollar for at a trendy wine bar, but it’s right here in the Richmond for a fraction of the price.The staff at this location are fast, the parking on Geary is manageable if you time it right, and the baking quality is incredibly consistent. A legacy product doesn't lose its soul just because it expands. The Geary location proves that Boudin is still fundamentally an SF staple for real people.  Highly recommend.

TL;DR: The absolute best spot in the Haight to catch a match—especially during massive tournaments like the World Cup. Insane energy, wall-to-wall screens, and a stellar staff. Just roll up 1–2 hours early if you want a hope of getting inside, and always bring a jacket!

​⚽ The Vibe & The Setup
​This place is a beautiful, high-energy soccer haven. The indoor decor is pure sports nostalgia with flags and memorabilia covering the walls, instantly setting the perfect tone.

​The Layout: It's got a great layout that naturally splits into a lively front bar, a cozy back section, and a few corner tables/bar stools. There’s a pool table too, though it’s understandably blocked off when a big game is on.
​The Screens: They have a ton of TVs positioned everywhere, so you won't miss a single play if you're inside.

​Outdoor Space: There's a sweet outdoor seating area if you want to soak up the atmosphere without staring at a screen—just note there are no TVs outside!

​🍺 Drinks & Logistics
​On Tap: They serve up a great pour of Guinness (around $10.17 a pint) alongside pitchers and solid bar snacks to keep you fueled.

​Restrooms: A huge plus for a packed bar—they actually have three restrooms, which keeps the lines moving.
​🎒 Local Pro-Tips for Match Day

​Arrive Early (No, Seriously): If you roll up right at kickoff, you’re not getting in. It gets so packed that there’s often zero standing room left. Cruise over an hour or two before the whistle blows to claim your spot.

​The Haight Chill: It’s the Haight, so the neighborhood microclimate rules apply. Even if it feels warm when you walk in, pack a heavy jacket or hoodie. By the time you leave after a 2-3 hour match, the evening chill will have rolled in.

​Parking: Parking around Haight Street is notoriously brutal. Arriving early helps, but taking transit or a rideshare is definitely the move here.

​If you want to watch a game surrounded by beautiful, passionate fans and an immaculate crowd vibe, this is the spot.

About 10 different options for nude recreation, consisting of numerous saunas, a steam bath, hot pools, a cold plunge,  a cool temperature pool and a rooftop for laying out and enjoying views of the city. My only real complaints are the price and the cold plunge policy. The cold plunge is intended strictly for quick plunges, and staff will ask you to get out if you stay in for more than a few seconds. The TV room could also use an update, although it rarely seems to be used.

Overall, it's a great experience with excellent amenities, and I'd recommend it to anyone looking for a relaxing spa day.

The spa itself, I give 1 star - it’s pretty crowded, the pools are small. It felt like a gym and less like a spa. Which might be for some people, but it wasn’t for me.

I give 3 extra stars for the cafe 🫶 - it was a really sweet space the hang out. The food is incredible (you have to try the soup dumplings), and there are chess boards to play which, which was really fun for our group.

Overall, this place is a unique and fun experience, especially for a group of friends. Just not the relaxing spa experience I typically strive for.

top_reviews.content: I hope they find a way to make this museum bigger.  I was hoping for something more substantial.  The stuff they have there is powerful and very educational. Great little museum. Super welcoming reception from Micky--thanks for the reminder about masking. Good exhibits about the historical presence of LGBT+ individuals and couples in the region. The Harvey Milk exhibit was powerful as well.

What a deeply thoughtfully curated museum - I, like many others, visited to see the original Gilbert Baker flag on display (a treasure in itself) but the extra exhibits were so lovely! The thought and care the team put into this museum is on par with a much larger institutions. Absolutely worth a visit.

The GLBT Historical Society Museum is a small museum located in the Castro focusing on national GLBT movements with a particular interest in San Francisco gay history. The entry fee was $10, which I was happy to pay to support a very worthwhile cause.

The museum is much, much smaller than I was expecting and is just two rooms. The indoor entrance walkway makes up about a fourth of the space but is basically dead, unused space.

The first room is informational with a timeline of GLBT history and then an exhibit that opened on June 7, 2024 called “Erotic Resistance: Performance, Art, and Activism in San Francisco Strip Clubs 1960s-1990s”, which is a photo collection.

The other room is a standing collection that includes a leather culture display, miscellany, a Harvey Milk collection, and a José Julio Sarria collection. The prize in the collection is part of the original gay pride flag, which was very powerful and meaningful for me to see in person.  That made the visit worth it, but outside of that there wasn’t a big draw for me considering the museum and associated collection is so small.

If you’re already in the Castro, it could be a fun quick stop, but it’s not something I’d travel far to see.

Belmo Café – A Rare Bakery Gem Worth the Journey
At last—we’ve found a truly exceptional bakery. Belmo Café is an absolute treasure, offering baklava of every kind imaginable, each one crafted to perfection with delicate layers, balanced sweetness, and rich, authentic flavor.
Beyond the baklava, their specialty French and Algerian pastries are nothing short of extraordinary. Every item reflects skill, tradition, and care—these are not everyday desserts, but culinary gems you savor slowly and remember long after.
This is the kind of place that’s worth any trip, no matter the distance. If you appreciate genuine craftsmanship, refined flavors, and pastries made the right way, Belmo Café delivers on every level.
I highly recommend giving them a try—you’ll quickly understand why this bakery stands in a class of its own.

The Cheese Board is a co-op that started as a cheese store, but now also has a beloved bakery and pizzeria (next door). If you are visiting Berkeley, you must stop by the Cheese Board.

The bakery is one of the best all-around bakeries in the area -- other places in the East Bay may specialize in a certain type of baked good, but the Cheese Board can make everything well (especially if it has cheese!)

If stopping by for the bakery, you must try the signature cheese roll. Otherwise, there is a rotating selection of breads and pastries, some of which were "invented" in house and have special names (wolverines, zampanos, chocolate things, etc.). The bakery items are continually made throughout the day.

While waiting in line for the bakery, you can also get a selection of cheese and prepared sauces. The $25 Adventure Bag contains a good choice of random cheeses, and the green hot sauce is also tasty as a condiment/dip.

You can buy par-baked pizzas to finish baking at home. The pizzas are always vegetarian and change every day. If you're just visiting, you can get a baked pizza at the pizzeria next door instead. The pizza is the best pizza in Berkeley.

Everything you can buy here is delicious. You can't go wrong with any of the food choices.

---

For first time visitors or a casual stop, I recommend buying a cheese roll, seeded baguette, and any pastry that tickles your fancy.

For a more substantial amount of food to bring home, I recommend a pizza, a 6-pack of English muffins, the green sauce, and a cheese Adventure Bag. The green sauce usually goes well on the pizza.

Staff here are very friendly, knowledgeable and helpful.

A great variety of cheeses are available here, with 3 flavors available to try each week. They offer plentiful amounts of sheep and goat cheeses as well more common cheeses as well.

Service is quick but doesn't feel rushed. Store is very clean and well presented.

Peña Pachamama is definitely a unique experience in San Francisco, especially if you enjoy vegan food, live music, and South American culture. The entire menu is vegan or plant based, and they had a lot more options than I expected, which was great to see.

We ordered the Raw sampler and the Andean sampler. The food itself was good and flavorful, though I’ll admit I was a little surprised by the portion-to-price ratio. In reality, they were more individual-sized entrees with a few different components on the plate. Still good, just a little expensive for what you get.

What really made the night memorable was the atmosphere. They had live music and traditional Peruvian dancing during dinner, which gave the whole place a really warm, cultural vibe. It felt more like an experience than just going out to eat.

Overall, I’m glad we went and I would absolutely come back again. If you’re vegan or plant bases or somply looking for a different kind of dinner spot in San Francisco with live entertainment and Andean-inspired food, Peña Pachamama is worth checking out .

And the quality did not live up to the price either. I was also surprised that there weren’t any appetizers on the menu for one person besides a single empanada and chips. This park offers two playgrounds, a grass area, picnic benches with bbq, basketball, tennis and volleyball court, a small amphitheater, and sidewalks for biking and walking. The grassy area is really sunny as most trees are on the outer rim.

Typical East Bay regional park, complete with classic EBRPD trail layout which go directly up the steepest parts of a hill. I don't know who or if anyone plans these trails, but it sure seems like their motto is "The shortest way from Point A to Point B". We started at the Stonewall-Panoramic trailhead off of Claremont Ave, which has almost no parking, you're fighting with residents and other hikers to find a spot. We got there around 8AM and still had trouble parking. Narrow winding road, parallel parking on steep inclines, cars park 2 inches from your bumper, fun stuff!

The trails we took were nice, again the start was extraordinarily steep, right off the jump you go from resting HR to max effort. The trail network is bracketed by Claremont Ave and Grizzly Peak Blvd. There are nice spots for panoramic vistas of the Bay, and some flatter trails as well. The views are the best reason to visit this park, it's just a bit of a headache to park and the steepness of the trails is annoying. Good wildflower displays in spring.

I love watching the sunset from here, it's amazing. During the day it's excellent to hike for the views alone. I highly recommend visiting at least once and taking a good camera. Lots of incredible views and trails. The trails have numerous steep parts, so bring water and good trail shoes.

Great park with challenging hikes and fantastic views. There are trails here that ascend ~1,500 feet - all the way to the base of Tilden Regional Park. It’s a park I frequent when weather permits (which fairly often) for the hikes.

I’ve seen all manner of wildlife on trails in this park: Coyotes, deer, prairie dogs (or at least that is what I think they are), rabbits, rattle snakes, lizards, etc… but haven’t had any issues.

Gorgeous view of the city and the bay from the preserve! The best view points are close to different trail heads around  Berkeley, the Berkeley Overlook Vista Point and a place marked as Pano. However, those segments of the trail are also the steepest so definitely be prepared for some strenuous climb.
The trail east of Panoramic Way is significantly quieter with much less foot traffic but also you are getting away from the best views and getting into the woods.

Staff is nice and the ambience is great

Finally have chance to visit and try this restaurant.  I was not planning to stop by but when I passed the the restaurant and lunch time , I decided to stop by.
This restaurant serves Asian fusion dishes and it is not that large and bright. The concept kind of like fast food style where you order and pay first.
It was full when we arrived and we had to wait. You cannot get the table until you ordered.
You order at cashier and they will get you a table after you paid.
We ordered bulgogi burrito,  bsnh mi, curry udon with fried chicken , and ginger chicken jook. Our order was ready pretty quickly.
I love the jook. It is korean style chicken porridge. Combine it with chine donut is great.
Curry udon is yummy. It like malaysia laksa or thai red curry meet japanese udon.  The soup is not yoo heavy and the fried chicken was yummy.
Banh mi is kind of same as what you get from vietnamese banh mi shop. Burrito is ok but not special except this one come with bulgogi as the protein. Thus on is Mexican food meet Korean.
Overall it was a nice lunch with my family. Will visit again when I am at neighborhood to try other dishes.

We stopped by this afternoon for lunch during our visit in San Francisco.  At first glance, the restaurant was well organized, clean and filled with great vibes from the customers and their staffs.  We ordered David’s Fried Chicken Sandwich, Wooly Pig Sandwich, Szechuan Chicken/Tufu, Vermicelli Bowl Grilled Pork/Tufu, Taiwanese Pork Cutlet Sandwich and Curry Udon.  Everyone polished their plate and said they loved their dish.  I had their Grilled Pork Curry Udon and I was blown away with how tender the grilled pork was and the flavour of the curry broth was on point.  I hesitate ordering beef or pork now because of my declined in saliva production due to radiation and chemo treatments in 2017.  I was amazed that I actually enjoyed eating grilled pork again.  Thanks Wooly Pig!!!

Overall, our experience with their restaurant/staffs/food superseded our expectation during our food tour in San Francisco.  I highly recommend you visit here during your visit in San Francisco.

June 2025:
First time back since 2021. This place has totally evolved into a legitimate sit down diner type cafe that has some delicious food. I was craving a Vietnamese sandwich and ordered the tofu again. It was super delicious 😋. My wife ordered the breakfast veggie burrito 🌯 and it was delicious too.

The guy at the table next to us had the chicken szechuan rice plate and it looked really good too!

Dinner menu is available on weekdays and I want to try one of their dinner burritos!

Will definitely be back soon for more delicious food!

2-14-21:

top_reviews.content:
The best escape room I have ever been to!

Our group of 8 did “The Attraction” room and it was so immersive! The challenges were diverse, and not repetitive in any way so each piece of the puzzle suited different skills. You really have to work as a group to get out in the 2 hr limit.

Located quite literally in the Palace of Fine Arts building this is a must do group activity!

10/10 recommend!

This was hands down one of the most memorable experiences of our entire California trip.

We came as a family of five with three kids (ages 3, 7 and 10) to celebrate our oldest daughter’s 10th birthday, and choosing the Edison Room turned out to be the perfect birthday gift.

What impressed us most was that every single family member could participate. Even our 3-year-old had little “missions” and felt like an important part of the team. Our 7- and 10-year-olds solved plenty of puzzles, while the adults had enough challenging moments to stay fully engaged. I’d definitely recommend having at least one puzzle-loving adult in the group, but that’s exactly what makes it such a rewarding family experience.

The puzzles are incredibly creative, varied and satisfying. Nothing felt repetitive or cliché. Every new discovery made us smile and made us want to keep exploring.

What made this room truly special, though, was its educational value. It’s much more than an escape room—it’s an immersive journey into the world of Thomas Edison, inventions, electricity, innovation and the spirit of discovery. On our way home we spent another hour talking with our daughters about Edison, his laboratory, the history of electricity and how great inventions changed the world. That’s something we definitely didn’t expect from an escape room!

A huge thank you to the entire Palace Games team for creating such a thoughtful experience. Especially to Andrew for his thoughtful advice which room to choose, and AJ who was incredible hands-on game manager at the place. It was worth every penny and became a birthday our daughter—and all of us—will remember for many years.

We have done 3 rooms here, all of the rooms are the best of the best. "The Attraction," is truly amazing. I doubt I'll ever find an escape room that well designed and elaborate ever again. Can't wait to come back and try the others, kudos to the designers and the very friendly staff.

top_reviews.content:
Final Final has a solid atmosphere, especially if you like a sports bar feel with plenty of screens and a lively crowd. When we went, it was extremely busy, and it seemed pretty likely that the beer festival ending down the street had a lot to do with that. The place definitely had energy, but it also felt a bit like the whole city got funneled through one doorway at once.
Inside, it’s a good-looking bar, and the updated bathrooms stood out in a good way. They’ve been nicely redone with individual genderless stalls and a single sink area outside, which felt modern and efficient. There are also two pool tables, though they really seem to fight for space once the crowd builds up, since people tend to pack in around them. There’s also just one outdoor table, so that is not exactly a big patio situation.
The toughest part of the experience was getting a drink. There’s no real dedicated walk-up space at the bar, so you kind of have to lean in and order over the head of someone already seated there, which is awkward for everybody involved. If you catch it at a quieter time, I could see it being a much smoother hang, but on a packed night it turns into a bit of a contact sport. Still, if you want a buzzy sports-bar vibe in San Francisco, it gets the job done.

Final Final will forever hold a special place in my heart. Was in town with friends visiting from NY and we were thrilled to find a bar that showcased New York sports. We watched the Knicks win their NBA Championship 🏆. The vibes were great, a lot of good energy and fun atmosphere. Was impressed with how the bar tenders handled the huge crowds. They seemed short staffed but you wouldn't know it
Very fun experience

Love the new Final Final (and I’ve lived here since 2005), but these horribly erect chairs have to go.  It’s like a Siberian gulag prison camp to sit in them; no layback whatsoever.  Maybe they want you to not sit in them?

Also, can’t believe they got rid of Trummer, really the only good beer produced in America.

Came several hours early for a little birthday WC action on a Sunday morning after planning many weeks ahead cause they specifically said they didn't take reservations for tables, only to wllk in to the half the tables being reserved.

Ridiculous staff that thought he was amusing said they didn't take reservations, but "money can buy anything". Lol it's not money that's buying your tables if you aren't allowing those willing to pay to reserve buddy - Icky, unreliable place to watch a game.

Awesome spot, sometimes it's a struggle to grab a seat anywhere but they let you chill in the garden area so no biggie. Staff definitely on point, friendly and quick. Weekends are absolute chaos inside but hey, at least it's right around the corner and easy to pop into. The kind of place that's got that buzz for a reason, worth dealing with the crowd. Solid 4.5/5, would happily come back even knowing I'll probably have to fight for a table.

reviews_snippets.content: "Wonderful service and great selection of drinks!"

top_reviews.content:
A grassy field, stage, and benches are present at this park, which seems to be designed for events or occasions.

This is a brief walk away from the Downtown Berkeley BART station and two parking lots. It's directly across from the Berkeley City Hall and near some other government buildings. There are events frequently in the park or near the park. There isn't a playground for kids or restrooms. There are a few works of public art which help to make it look nicer. Some restaurants are nearby and this could be a place to sit if you take your food to go. There is a farmers' market every Saturday on one of the streets that border this park.

The park itself seems to be a place where homeless people congregate during the week. On weekends there are other activities taking place and seems more family friendly. This Saturday we saw a farmers market and on Sunday attended a Lowrider car show on our way to get donuts nearby. An awesome find, we talked to the team from Vajitos Bikes and they were great!

Wide open space in  the central plaza of city government facilities. A bit rundown from near constant occupation since its opening decades ago. But still providing the desired effect of grandure for the municipal complex

Awesome first time experience! The Fried Lobster with Garlic Noodles was out of this world. Mac&Cheese with Lobster was to die for...I am looking forward to next year being bigger and better! Thanks for the memories...
Nice quiet park some lady yelled every 5 minutes but was harmless cool climbing trees nice place for a dog walk

Even after he sliced it and ran it through the toaster. What a great spot!! Thank you for the excellent and friendly service!!

Very good coffee. The cafe roasted their own coffee bean. It is very interesting that cafe opened by non western. Their coffee is one of the best in this area. The chocolate latte is interesting, very similar to mocha, but with chocolate form on top. I can see their coffee bean roasting process in store as well. The begal also very good. This cafe consider medium size. Very quick and friendly service. Majority of tables are clean. Customer had 2 hours limit seating, but very relax cafe. Accessible by public transport.
This place was amazing! Perfect service and coffee. Recommend they add stevia as a condiment though.

Nice cafe shop with good atmosphere. Came hear to work. They limit the tables for 2 hours. It is nice if you want to spend time with your family or friends. But it is not ideal for working. Of course good coffee! And ok pastry options.

top_reviews.content: Classy, elegant and relaxing atmosphere. A memorable experience for sure. The service was so good, and the drinks were perfect. I recommend trying a Vesper here because they absolutely nailed it. Will definitely be coming back next time I’m in town.

We came to The Red Room since we were staying at the hotel for the night. We really enjoyed the atmosphere at firs…the cocktails were great, the bottle of wine was excellent, the smash burgers were delicious, and the live music created a fun vibe.

Unfortunately, the experience took a turn when we noticed a cockroach crawling on the wall directly behind our table. We immediately pointed it out to our server, who simply said, “Okay, I’ll take care of it.” However, nothing was done. The roach continued crawling around behind our table for another 15–20 minutes.

We mentioned it a second time, and the server told us he would “handle it when they close.” That response was honestly shocking. A cockroach in a dining area should be addressed immediately, not left to continue crawling around near guests while they’re eating and drinking. We ended up moving tables but it was still crawling around.

The server did offer us a complimentary drink, which we appreciated, but it didn’t make up for the lack of urgency or concern regarding cleanliness. It’s disappointing because everything else about the evening had been enjoyable. I hope management takes this seriously and addresses both the pest issue and how situations like this are handled in the future.

Fantastic bar that emanates history and class.  High ceilings, rich redwood paneling, original Gustav Klimt paintings, and elegant seating all heighten the experience.  Drinks are excellent, and our waitress was friendly and attentive.  There was a terrific live jazz ensemble when we were there on a Thursday evening.  Definitely worth a visit!

This bar was lovely. The elegant entrance, leading to a high-ceilinged space accented with stunning Klimt-inspired artwork, immediately captivated me. The drinks were excellent, and the burgers and truffle fries were absolutely delicious.

While the service wasn’t the best—requiring effort to get the staff’s attention when needed—they were attentive and helpful once they noticed us. They could intentionally look around for customers' needs instead of chatting with each other. Additionally, the round tables we were seated at by the wall felt rather small for a group; larger tables would have been more comfortable.

Despite these minor issues, I still give it a 5 out of 5 because the overall experience was fantastic.

Hands-down, my favorite bar in San Francisco. Classy, classic, sophisticated, stylish and yet low-key. The bar is something to just simply marvelous. The etched glass, the under lighting just gives it such an cool speakeasy vibe. The drinks are great, the only place that makes a Chocolate Martini that I actually enjoy. The hosts and the bartenders are awesome, and the lobby is just a thrill to be in with incredible furniture.

top_reviews.content: Such a warm and welcoming place! The atmosphere is cozy, the desserts are amazing, and the coffee is absolutely top-notch. They also show World Cup matches for free, which makes it a great spot to enjoy the games with friends. The staff is friendly, and you can really feel the passion behind this place. Highly recommended for anyone looking for great coffee, delicious treats, and a comfortable atmosphere.

Barista Cafe is an absolute gem! The owner and the entire staff are incredibly warm, friendly, and welcoming—they make you feel right at home the moment you walk in. The coffee is outstanding, but you absolutely cannot leave without trying their crepes; they are genuinely amazing and pair perfectly with the drinks. Plus, the location is fantastic and so convenient for a quick walk-in. It’s such a wonderful place with great vibes. You should definitely check it out, you won't regret it!

My favorite breakfast place in Presidio Heights! I go there every opportunity I have. Excellent, especially fresh and flavorful food (avocado toast, breakfast platter) and delicious drinks (cortado, cappuccino with oat milk). Great atmosphere too. I love this coffee shop.

Delicious food.  Not too good costumer service though. Stayed for one hour and the staff got every single order incorrect including mine. They fixed it all with smiles on their faces but too many mistakes made my stay longer than usual.

My family and I come here every few months and love this place. But after our lunch there today I just had to leave a review. Yo! The vegan sando is SO goood!!! I was raving about while eating it. And they offer gf bread options plus you can add a protein. My kids always get the crepes and of course they’re so delicious every time. Oh, be sure to grab a hot drink too. I had the chai soy latte and it was divine. Such a great atmosphere for a casual coffee and bite of food.

top_reviews.content:
When: Tue @9am

I keep hearing about this place and felt I am long overdue to give it a try.  Sadly it was not a great experience for us getting breakfast there.

You line up first to order, then you sit down.  For some reason the cashier did not hear my second order and that made the transaction twice as long.  Here’s what we ordered:

HUEVOS RANCHEROS - $15
2 over easy eggs on fried tortillas, red salsa, beans, potatoes, sour cream.
This has got to be the saddest Huevos Rancheros plate I’ve seen and experienced.  Wish the dallop of scour cream was bigger, and overall this dish was just okay.  It felt unhappy, but the taste was fine, nothing memorable.

BREAKFAST SANDWICH - $8
Egg Cheese, and choice of meat (sausage) and bread (croissant.)
Somehow this was serviced on sourdough, and it’s not worth having them fix this.  It’s also not worth $8, it looks and tastes like something I can easily make at home.

All in all, we were very unhappy with our time and food here, but glad we finally gave it a shot and tried it!

A charming breakfast spot with nice ambiance. Minus a star because it was *so* loud inside due to the frequent running of the juicer + blender + milk steamer and the “background” music being too loud. Could seriously use acoustic foam panels to quiet the space. Second star comes off because our food for 3 people was generally thought to be “just ok,” our dishes came out at very different times, and drinks were served well into our meal.
The omelet was definitely worth the price!

i got the iced latte and a slice of their banana bread, perfect combo for a quick break. they have this nice little patio area out back that's super chill and not crowded. definitely gonna be my new spot to read or just zone out for an hour

The staff are all so polite. The food is REALLY good. French fries 100% perfect. Seasoned perfectly, crunchy on the outside, soft on the inside. I recommend you choose the outdoor seating in the back because it's the most perfect seating area ever. I sat near the fountain, my shoes got wet but I was too focused on the food. First time we sat w/o talking. Went here a second time and the food just wasn't as good as before. Bacon was dry.

This is such a great place. It's design is so cute. Its a train station. It has ample seating for everyone. You always see the locals here. The food and pastries are home made. When visiting I always got moms oatmeal. I tried the chocate croissants and the cheese Danish, amazing. I tried their green monster drink. It is hethy and delicious. Everything is made when ordered so it is very fresh. The service is outstanding, some of the best customer service you can get these days. Overall rating is excellent!!

top_reviews.content: This is the good stuff! We found them as Ippuku was partnering with them for dessert but unfortunately, that’s now concluded. They have unique in house made flavors which change weekly that you won’t find anywhere else!

The best gelato place I've ever been to. They are innovative with their seasonal flavors (which actually taste good and aren't just different), and their usual flavors are also phenomenal. We come almost every week. Our favorites are muscat grape, Arabic coffee, watermelon, and the best, walnut (it blew out minds).

By far my favorite gelato place in the universe! I have visited this place multiple times. The seasonal fruit flavors are always punchy and intensely flavored—for example, the pluot king and watermelon gelatos taste like the best, most condensed versions of the fruits themselves. I found out today that one of the founders graduated from a gelato university in Bologna, which explains a lot.

Tip: you can get two flavors in the regular cup. I always pair a fruity flavor with a darker or creamier one. Pictured here is the strawberry and black sesame; calamansi lime and fiordilatte (background).

Great ice cream, usually super friendly service. Advice to management: be sure to adequately train staff on adjusting speed to meet demand. There did not appear to be any sense of urgency as the line extended out the door and progress remained glacial (pun intended); staff actually appeared oblivious to the wait time. If the staff has limitations making them unable to serve customers that have been waiting patiently since well before closing time, those customers should be given sufficient warning in advance, not after having already waited 20 minutes.
Such good gelato, the best one we tried in Berkeley. They have unique seasonal flavors and they hand make their waffles. We will be coming back for this next time we visit.

top_reviews.content: This was the chillest place to eat a bagel, read a book, and open a pack. I decided decaf but I hear the coffee is swell. Beautiful artwork and an array of desserts, great selection I had to get one later. Lox bagel was stacked.

On my way south out of SF, I was looking for a coffee spot to stop and grab a drink and a bite. Martha & Bros had decent reviews and was in the way. I was pleasantly surprised by the offerings when I arrived. Tons of food options, and a solid selection of flavored lattes too.

Me and my wife got a couple drinks and a brownie. Both of our drinks were quite good. Strong flavor and on the sweeter side (how we like it). The brownie also was surprisingly good. Definitely worth stopping in if you are in the area.

Martha & Brothers (just Martha’s if you’re local :) is one of the best coffee shops in San Francisco. The coffee and espresso is a rich, dark roast blend. We always get Americanos with hot milk and they are really perfection - of course there are mochas and chais and all kinds of specialty drinks but it all starts with the beans. Moreover all the staff are incredibly friendly (where else are you greeted with “hello, love”). The baristas are pro but humble — David is great and remembers your drink, and Giselle gets special mention for her strong Americanos. There is seating indoors and outside on a few tables. Big windows make it a refuge from the daily hustle, comfy place to meet a friend or to bang out a few emails while high on caffeine. There really is a Martha, she’s the owner and a local legend. If you get your coffee early enough you just might meet her and her infectious smile…

Visited Martha’s with a friend who lives in Bernal Heights. In order the Masala Chai hot tea, which I thought would be just hot tea and then found out it is a latte. It was delicious, although it wasn’t what I was expecting! Cute little shop with more seating than one would expect in a small coffee shop.
This is one of the best coffee shops I’ve been to. I’m visiting and so glad I found this early in my trip. It’s fast paced, but so welcoming. Lovely people and great food.

Great study/work spot! Plenty of accessible outlets, comfortable seating, and good lighting. Free wifi! And the food & drink options are also great. I had the grilled salmon lavash wrap and a chunk of cinnamon crumble cake- delicious! It was hard to choose among all the options so I will definitely be coming back to try others. Also generally good vibes and friendly staff :)

Edit- I’ve come back many times since I originally posted and the grilled salmon wrap never disappoints!! This is my go-to spot for this part of the city.

I have loved this cafe since 2003 when I lived on Coleridge St and would have my salmon wrap every weekend. Such a cosy cafe with a beautiful courtyard. I’ve been home in Australia for many years now, but every time I’m in CA, I make an effort to get to Progressive Grounds for my salmon wrap. No one makes it like you do. I can’t even make it the way you do. Beautiful people, great service, and a very atmospheric cafe not like anywhere else on the other side of the world. I’ve been looking. So grateful you are still there. Looking forward to my next salmon wrap!

Marco, the owner, is such a friendly dude!
Very cozy interior with lots of cushy seating.
There's a fun hallway with lanterns that leads to an even quieter room with a fireplace.
And outside, there's a lovely patio!
Definitely coming back here to try more breakfast, lunch, ice cream, and wine/beer options 💚

Came to Progressive Ground for an early breakfast. I wanted to try their wraps but they are only available for lunch...so I went for a bagel with pesto turkey. It turned out that the portion was bigger than I expected (the bagel was cut in half horizontally and each half got its own meat and cheese) and the taste was pretty good, even though it’s simply microwave heated.
There cozy home-style decor isn't my thing but there is a lovely patio in the back with multiple tables well separated and I enjoyed my breakfast with fresh air. Friendly service and Ok price.

As a pinhead, I wanted to share what a cool place this is. Machines were in great shape. Lots of unique pins for the connoisseur. They have all the latest, hard to find machines, with a great collection of EM's that I really enjoyed. Met the owner, who was great. And the staff were solid as well. Big fan overall.

This place is awesome!! I am not a pinball aficionado, but I can't help but feel like any pro would be happy here.

Plays seem to be about $1 across the board with one monthly $0.25 machine and some other non-pinball games.

They also have some snacks and a screen printing service?!

I don't know how to describe this place other than a warehouse of pure, concentrated fun.

Try the old school 2v2 pong. If you've never tried that CRT-analog dial control, it's a very cool sensation if you're only used to digital inputs.

The BEST — play for all ages, incredible selection of pinball and other games, from latest and coolest pinball machines that you never knew about — try the Godzilla! — to old school and retro games that are good clean fun in a retro and playful atmosphere.  No-brainer for any day of the week, or particularly when Carl is in town

Great selection of machines, most in excellent condition. I appreciate that events can be held in the back and silk screening is offered. However, the machines are a bit sensitive to bumping, especially in crowded areas. I chose to play in less congested spots after experiencing that. Overall, it's definitely worth supporting this hidden gem!

I have been wanting to come to this museum since last year. My dad was a pilot for Transocean Airlines. I found out about this museum and their collection of memorabilia from the museum folks at the SFO museum. I thought it was a pleasant experience and the kids that were visiting were obviously very excited about flying. Looks like Father's Day this year will be a terrific day to come visit since they will have a lot of events planned.

Highly recommend and a hidden gem!! Tucked away behind the Oakland airport, this museum should definitely a perfect stop for you and or family or destination. They have a variety of aircraft, great gift shop and courteous staff. Very reasonable priced and they also partner with cool events. Will definitely be back soon, thanks and had an Awesome time!!

Really cool opportunity to see aircraft across the years.  From some scale models to replicas to actual aircraft.  Very low key but enjoyable.  I would've loved to see the inside of the flying boat passenger plane, but that was a separate guided tour we didn't have time to do during our visit.  A couple videos, history of women in aviation, and pieces on Amelia Earhart were a few of the many interesting exhibits

Fun place for anyone who loves fighter jets, and appreciates the history of the older and retired craft.
The president of the Museum was able to give us a tour and was very informative with all the exhibits.
The outdoor portion is home to an F-14 Tomcat!!!
If you love fighter jets, this is a great place to start.

top_reviews.content: First time at Riptide yesterday. It was the perfect beach vibe I was looking for. Beautiful decor and rad people. Live music was perfect to end my Sunday in the city on the beach. I will definitely go again. Thank you! <3

​The Riptide is just a great little spot with excellent vibes, strong drinks, and a perfect setup for live music. I went on a rainy, cold Saturday night around 9 PM to catch the band Middle Dog.

Despite the bad weather in San Francisco, the place was absolutely popping - the whole neighborhood seemed to be out, and the crowd made the atmosphere awesome. It was a great mix of regulars, first-timers like myself, and everyone in between!

​They are drinks-only, but they have a great range of beer and liquor options, and the bartenders definitely don't skimp on the pours. The service was very friendly and efficient, even when busy. Although it was crowded (it got a little hot at peak, but opening the door quickly solved that!), it never felt uncomfortably packed. Once you got inside, great smell of baked goods for sure and packed of people waiting for freshly bake custards since they ran out within A MINUTE. They ran out of most of their goodies so you have a choice of get what they have available or wait for the next patch…we waited and it was aooo soo worth it.  I mean, it’s cheap and greatly good. Oh I also got their HK hot bubble tea, and it just hitting all the right spot.  Thank you.

I absolutely love Cantonese sponge cupcakes! I’ve tried them in major Chinatowns across the U.S., and Flushing in New York and San Francisco Chinatown used to be tied for first place.

However, when I went back to Flushing in 2024 to try them again, I found that the quality had declined. The sponge cake was no longer as soft and fluffy as it used to be. In contrast, Yummy Bakery in San Francisco has now become the top choice!

I stopped by Yummy Bakery & Cafe in Chinatown and tried their egg tarts, and they were absolutely worth it. The crust was flaky, buttery, and light, while the custard filling was smooth, silky, and not overly sweet. It had that perfect balance that makes you want to eat more than one. The bakery itself is a classic Hong Kong–style spot with lots of fresh buns and pastries lined up in the case, and the smell of fresh bread hits you as soon as you walk in. Prices are very reasonable, and everything feels fresh out of the oven. It’s a no-frills place, but that’s the charm—it’s all about the quality of the pastries. If you’re in Chinatown and craving a good egg tart, this is definitely a place to stop by.

Their pineapple butter bun/菠萝油 is TO DIE FOR. They warm up the bread for you then add a slice of butter in the middle, so when you bite on it it’s crispy on outside and chewy on the inside, with warm butter spreading through your mouth. Hands down the pineapple butter bun you could find in bay area.

The workers here speaks Cantonese, Mandarin, and English. They didn’t make me feel unwelcoming like other cantonese shops just because I speak mandarin. Great customer service!

A small but steep hill that offers great views of the city (downtown, as well as Bernal Heights!). There is a dirt trail with stairs in some segments that leads from the end of 30th St to the top, where you can continue to climb to Walter Haas Playground and get even better views.

Whereas other patrons want a place to park themselves and use WiFi for free, I want to be able to get a seat, eat, relax with a beverage, read or people watch. Blue Danube is charming!
It’s not a cookie cutter chain coffee shop.

Francisco Park in San Francisco is a wonderful place to spend time outdoors. The park has two separate areas for dogs, with the lower one covered in artificial grass and the upper one with real grass. There is also a small garden next to the dog park and a playground for kids. The pathways wind through the park, making it fun to explore. It is a lively, welcoming spot to relax and enjoy some fresh air.

From Reservoir to Recreation

Francisco Park is located on the corner of Bay and Hyde Streets in San Francisco. Its interesting history mirrors the city's development and community spirit. Initially, this was the site of the Francisco Reservoir, which was constructed in 1860 and decommissioned in 1940 after the Lombard Street reservoir was established.

The reservoir served as a critical water source for the growing city. However, by 1940, it had become obsolete due to advancements in the city's water infrastructure. Over the following decades, the site remained unused and largely forgotten, becoming an overgrown and fenced-off area entirely contrasting with its vibrant neighborhoods. In the late 1990s and early 2000s, when I worked at the Civic Center, I used to walk home through or along this location and wonder why such a precious piece of real estate was left forgotten and unattended, but that was not the case, of course!

In the early 2000s, residents and civic groups started pushing to turn the forgotten site into a community hangout. After years of planning, fundraising, and battling red tape, Francisco Park opened its doors in 2021. The park's all about lush greenery, walking paths, playgrounds, and killer views of the Bay, Golden Gate Bridge, and Alcatraz. It's a testament to the power of people and the city's willingness to save and reuse its historic spaces for everyone to enjoy.

One of Francisco Park's nice features is the dog playground, a dedicated space where dogs can exercise and socialize off-leash. Designed with both pets and their owners in mind, the playground features secure fencing and shaded seating areas. It provides plenty of room for dogs to run freely and play while promoting responsible pet ownership through well-maintained facilities and clear rules. This addition to the park enhances its appeal as a community hub, encouraging interactions among dog owners and contributing to the overall vibrancy and inclusiveness of Francisco Park.

I have taken our little puppy there a few times, and although he is not the young and energetic fuzzy little guy he was a few years ago, he still enjoys interacting with other dogs, big and small. I have also been fortunate to get acquainted with a few neighbors I would not have met otherwise.

Immaculate park with great views, a picnic area, a children's playground, dog play area, and a variety of plant species.

This reservoir-turned-park (according to the signs throughout it) spans about a block. It can be accessed through four entrances (the dog play area has separate gates). The upper Hyde St. entrance provides the best views, in my opinion. There are also restrooms, bike racks, nearby parking, and a community garden (it wasn't open when I was there). Overall, if you're in the area, you should check out this park. If it's your first time, you can easily spend an hour or two just looking at the views.

Had a great experience at Café du Nord while visiting San Francisco.

First and foremost, huge credit for the artists they bring in. We went to see Amistat, and they were absolutely phenomenal live. Truly talented musicians and incredible songwriters, so the venue already earned major points from me just based on the lineup alone.

That might sound random to point out, but in smaller live music venues — especially darker, more crowded ones — that’s not always the case. The layout also kept the bathroom line from interfering too much with the bar area or the actual show, which was nice.

Overall, it was a really solid venue with a good atmosphere, and I’d absolutely go back for another show if I was in San Francisco and they had artists I wanted to see playing there.

We visited this park during the Día de los Muertos (Day of the Dead) celebration, and it was an incredibly moving and memorable experience. The event was filled with vibrant altars (ofrendas), honoring loved ones who have passed, each adorned with flowers, candles, photos, and offerings. The atmosphere was enriched by spiritual songs, traditional dances, and a deep sense of community and reverence.

Traditionally celebrated on November 1 and 2, Día de los Muertos is a Mexican tradition that blends indigenous practices with Catholic influences, honoring the connection between the living and the dead. What made this celebration even more special was its inclusivity—altars representing Palestinian, Persian, and Chinese cultures were also on display, showcasing how this tradition resonates across different communities.

The sight of people from diverse backgrounds coming together to honor their ancestors was truly powerful. This event was not just a cultural celebration but also a moving reminder of the universal nature of remembrance and love. If you have the chance to attend a Día de los Muertos event, it’s a deeply meaningful experience you won’t forget.
