I had a great experience at this museum. It was free during my visit so I wanted to stop here while exploring San Francisco.

The place itself (including the restrooms) was clean and organized. The artwork and displays were also sophisticated and profound. However, I noticed that most of these artwork (probably all of them in fact) were of Chinese (or other East Asian) origin rather than being international. However, since admission was free, I’ll keep it as a 5-star review. The staff were very kind and helpful in providing information regarding the museum, including a statue that cannot be photographed. Overall, I think it is a nice museum.

This was my favourite art museum in San Francisco, the entrance is a little weird but the upstairs is carefully curated and uses natural light from skylights in some parts. There were very few people in it, the staff seemed bored but were very nice and informative.

I really love Asian art styles so most of my photos are from those exhibits.

The International Art Museum of America is truly a hidden gem in San Francisco. I rarely see it advertised, and I actually discovered the museum because of a special Tibetan thangka exhibition they were hosting.

The staff here are incredibly friendly and welcoming, which made the whole visit even more enjoyable. What surprised me most was the collection—there are some truly remarkable and rare works here, including masterpieces by Zhang Daqian, Qi Baishi, and Fu Baoshi. I honestly did not expect to come across works by artists of this caliber when I first walked in!

I also had the pleasure of meeting the museum director, Mr. Xie, who was extremely approachable, warm, and down-to-earth.

I’m so glad I discovered this museum. If you’re interested in art, especially Chinese and Asian art, I definitely recommend taking the time to visit. It deserves to be much better known in San Francisco!
Amazing free museum with a quiet spot at the entrance. Lovely Asian art including calligraphy. Some very dramatic pieces. We were only in SF for two days and we were so glad we did not miss this.

Very disappointing experience with AMC Metreon. I purchased confirmed tickets for the Aug 26, 6 PM IMAX 70mm screening well in advance. By the time AMC notified us, other IMAX 70mm screenings were already sold out or had very limited seating. A refund and complimentary regular movie ticket don’t really solve that problem — had this showtime not been sold by mistake, I could have purchased another 70mm screening when tickets were available.

I contacted AMC hoping they could simply move us to another IMAX 70mm screening, but their current response time is 7–10 business days, potentially after the event.

If you are looking for a unique, world-class experience for a private event, or a fun night out, look no further than The Magic Patio. We recently hosted a joint 50th birthday party there for 45 guests, and it was amazing.

From the very beginning, Andrew, the owner and magician, was an absolute dream to work with. The planning process was seamless; he was incredibly easy to coordinate with during scheduling and checked in regularly as the day of the event approached.

The night of the event was flawless. Andrew and his staff greeted our guests with such warmth, immediately making everyone feel at home. They manned the bar before the show, setting a perfect, welcoming tone for the evening.

The performance was absolutely amazing. Our guests were completely enthralled from start to finish. Andrew does a great job of incorporating humor and the crowd into the act, making everyone feel like part of the show. After the show ended, Andrew mingled with the crowd, performing up-close magic throughout the room.

Our friends and family haven't stopped talking about it; everyone had the best time and could not have enjoyed the show more. Whether you want to see a public performance or host a private event that your guests will never forget, you absolutely have to go to The Magic Patio. Thank you, Andrew, for making our 50th so special!

One of the most unique and compelling experiences you'll ever have. Andrew is one of the most talented people I know, and his version of magic is one you won't find anywhere else. Bring everyone you know because it'll be the best date night / birthday outing / friend hang / solo treat you've had in a long while!

top_reviews.content: Everything I ordered here was delicious.  The sweet bean jam bun was full of jam, and the bread was pleasantly chewy and bouncy, the perfect counterpoint to the rich bean jam.  The salt bread was equally chewy and delicious, and the salt was an excellent accent, not overpowering.  The entire bottom of the roll was deliciously buttery, and you could enjoy bites that were rich and buttery or pillowy and delicious with just bread.  The chocolate croissant was delicious, but I was little disappointed at the amount of chocolate in the croissant.  I was definitely hoping for more.  The iced caramel macchiato was definitely machine created, but was still delicious, and the volume of the drink was excellent.  The price point for everything is low, so the cost performance at this bakery is amazing, and they’re all over the Bay Area, so you almost always find one.  Looking forward to trying more of their menu.

The staff were super friendly and the place had a good energy—a few people sitting, enjoying their coffee, and just hanging out.

The bakery layout is well thought out and super easy to navigate. The cold case looked really fresh and inviting, too.

I tried a few things and everything was spot on:

Mango Panna Cotta:  Delicious and tasted just as good as it looked.

Mango Milk Bun:  This was a favorite. It had that perfect chewy texture, and the sweetness from the mango was just right—not overpowering at all.

Basque Cheesecake Cup: Really, really good. Definitely worth grabbing.

Taro Mochi Boroh:  It’s huge, almost like a loaf, and has this great crust (the "boroh" part) that pairs perfectly with the soft, chewy mochi and taro filling inside.

Honestly, having a spot like this in downtown San Leandro is a huge plus. It’s a solid, reliable place to grab a treat and a coffee. Definitely recommend checking it out if you’re in the area.

I visited the San Francisco Railroad Museum today, and it was such a delightful experience. The staff were truly amazing—some of the nicest people I’ve encountered in San Francisco. They were kind, attentive, sweet, and incredibly courteous. What really stood out was how they took the time to explain the history behind everything and went above and beyond to help my son have a hands-on experience, making him feel like he was actually conducting a streetcar.

The museum itself is small, but full of charm and history. It’s a really cute space with plenty to see, plus a nice selection of merchandise to browse. Its convenient location makes it an easy and worthwhile stop.

Overall, it may be small, but it’s packed with fun and heart. A wonderful experience that I would definitely recommend, especially for families.

The San Francisco Railway Museum is such a hidden gem! I’ve lived in San Francisco for over 20 years, and I only recently visited for a work event—now I wish I had gone sooner. The museum is incredibly interesting, offering a fascinating look into the history of the city’s iconic rail cars and the evolution of public transportation in SF.

Learning about how the cable car system operates and is maintained was especially eye-opening. It’s one thing to ride the cable cars as a local or a visitor, but it’s completely different to see the mechanics, engineering, and dedication that go into keeping them running. The exhibits are well presented, informative, and filled with great historic photos and artifacts that bring the story of SF transit to life.

Even though the museum isn’t huge, it’s packed with engaging displays and is absolutely worth a visit—whether you’re a longtime resident like me or just exploring the city. A wonderful stop for anyone curious about San Francisco’s history and the charm behind its most iconic form of transportation.

The Docent named Bob was amazing and knew a lot of information. Out of all the museums Ive been to, the people here were the most thorough. They knew a lot, have lived here a long time, and had been volunteering for just as long. A must for anyone who wants to know knowledge and history of the city, and almost exceedingly one of the most important organizations in history preservation. The gift shop, a but gaudy but with a space so small there is only so much you can do, however, regardless of how small the building was the docents there knew so much, and it made for a very personal experience. There is a ton of great things to see here, but for history purposes, drop by The Railway Museum and just ask for a bit of history, they won't mind to much and you'll probably learn way more than if you just read about it. Great building, great place, great knowledge. Also ask about the railcar signs that say Pool, something I definitely didn't know.
It's a great place.

A Hidden Gem Between Chinatown and the Financial District

St. Mary’s Square is one of those places you might pass by numerous times without realizing how interesting it truly is. I did just that for years! I walked by it from different sides many times and never took the opportunity to walk in, look around, and learn more about it.

At first glance, the park appears to be a standard city park, but it’s actually a rooftop plaza, redesigned in the 1950s by landscape architect Robert Royston and built atop an underground parking garage. The square has served as a community gathering place since the mid-1800s, although the atmosphere back then was vastly different from today’s calm lunchtime scene.

In the late 19th century, this area was part of a notoriously rowdy section of San Francisco, filled with saloons, brothels, and opium dens. It became so infamous that the leaders of Old St. Mary’s Cathedral, located directly across the street, carved the phrase “Son, Observe the Time and Fly from Evil” onto the cathedral’s clock tower—clearly intended as a warning to those lingering below. The 1906 earthquake and fires devastated much of the surrounding neighborhood, creating an opportunity to reimagine the space as a public square rather than a problem zone.

Today, the park is notable not only for its location but also for its artwork and historical significance. The most prominent feature is the 14-foot statue of Dr. Sun Yat-sen, the founder of the Republic of China, created by renowned San Francisco sculptor Beniamino Bufano. This tribute is significant; Sun Yat-sen spent considerable time in San Francisco raising funds and support for his revolutionary efforts, and this square was one of the places he frequented during his years in exile.

More recently, the square became home to the Comfort Women Memorial, installed in 2017 to honor the victims of wartime sexual slavery during World War II. This memorial adds another thoughtful and reflective layer to an already meaningful space.

With its layered history, public art, and peaceful setting above the bustling city streets, St. Mary’s Square is an excellent place to grab a coffee, sit for a while, and quietly take in one of San Francisco’s most fascinating corners.

One of my favorite parks to visit in San Francisco. It tends to be quieter and calmer than others, and it’s slightly hidden away from the main Chinatown area (I actually discovered it on accident). That makes it a great place to chill and relax amongst the hustle and bustle of the rest of the city. It is simultaneously on street level and on rooftop level thanks to being on a hill, and harbors views of 555 California Street, 333 Bush Street, the Hartford Building, and the Russ Building. The park is right next to the California St cable car line, which is very convenient. There is also a parking garage underneath the park. Overall, 5/5.

I recently stopped by Ruby Room in downtown Oakland, located along 14th Street in the city’s Uptown district. The area has developed into one of Oakland’s main nightlife corridors, and Ruby Room stands out as a long-running local bar that blends vintage character with a relaxed neighborhood vibe.

The atmosphere feels eclectic and unmistakably retro. The interior décor mixes dim lighting, vintage furniture, and a slightly old-school lounge aesthetic that gives the space a personality very different from more modern cocktail bars. It feels like a place that has evolved over time rather than being designed to follow current trends, which adds to its charm.

The bar program focuses on straightforward cocktails and drinks rather than elaborate mixology. The environment encourages guests to relax, talk, and spend time with friends rather than treat the bar as a formal cocktail destination. The space often attracts a mix of locals, artists, and visitors exploring the Uptown nightlife scene.

Service during the visit felt casual and friendly, fitting the laid-back nature of the venue. The staff maintained an easygoing tone that matches the overall character of the bar.

From a global travel perspective, Ruby Room reminded me of the vintage neighborhood bars I have encountered in cities like Portland, Berlin, and Montreal where personality and atmosphere often matter more than polished design.

top_reviews.content:
If you’re looking to dive into the soul of San Francisco, the Presidio Officers’ Club is an absolute standout. I recently visited, and it’s easily one of the most culturally rich spots in the city.
Why It’s Worth the Trip:
Masterful History Showcase: The historical exhibits are exceptionally well-laid out. Unlike some museums that can feel cluttered, the flow here is intuitive and keeps you engaged from start to finish.
Deeply Interesting Content: The storytelling bridges the gap between the Ohlone heritage, the Spanish colonial era, and the U.S. Army’s long tenure. It manages to be educational without being dry.
Stunning Atmosphere: The building itself is a piece of history. Walking through the renovated halls feels like stepping back in time, yet it’s polished with all the modern comforts you’d want.
The Setting: You can’t beat the location. Being nestled in the heart of the Presidio makes it the perfect anchor for a day of exploring the park.
Whether you're a local history buff or a visitor looking for something more substantial than a typical tourist trap, the Officers’ Club is a class act. It’s a beautifully curated tribute to the many layers of San Francisco’s past.

top_reviews.content:
A must-visit place for anyone living in the area (4/5 Green Stars)
Bring cash! That’s the first rule of Schmidt’s Pub. Maybe it’s the only rule! I’ve been coming here a bit more regularly, lately – more visits in the last year compared to the previous decade, in fact. Now I wonder what I was waiting for.

According to the East Bay Express, Schmidt’s Pub is “basically your living room, but better” – that does sum it up, except that very few of us have living rooms anything like this, with a cozy fireplace surrounded by comfy armchairs and rustic tables beside sunny windows. Not many of us have living rooms with Old Speckled Hen on tap, or populated with an entertaining parade of quirky folk and friendly dogs. If the people and dogs are not entertaining enough then pick up a copy of Calvin and Hobbes or A History of Clay Pipes (okay, I made that one up) and have a little retreat with a pint.

4/5 Green Stars for social and environmental impact, based on these factors:
•	Beer on tap (transported in reusable kegs) has a much lower footprint compared to bottles or cans.
•	Allows you to bring your own food, which is good for folk like vegans who are often more comfortable with BYO.
•	The snacks available at the counter could be a bit more Berkeley (or Albany)! They were mostly from big corps – Lays chips (PepsiCo) and chocolate bars from Mars. Would be nice to see a more imaginative/ethical selection.
•	A great community space with an inclusive atmosphere. Schmidt’s is home to many groups (e.g., knitting) and provides a second family for many, some who send postcards from their trips!
•	Finally, we shouldn’t underestimate the importance of having a place to slow down, reflect and connect with each other a little. In that respect, Schmidt’s Pub is worth its weight in gold.

Schmidt's is a rare anomaly. A cross between an English pub, a bed and breakfast and the living room of cultured intellectual. Where else in the East Bay can you enter a 100+ year old house, choose from a selection of ales, lagers and stouts on draft and in bottles and cans and an assortment of fine tobacco, cigars and smoking accessories, sit down in a chair with a wooden table and read something, including the books on the shelves? Truly a wonder. And if you do purchase a cigar, you can smoke it outside. I wouldn't be surprised if people discuss Proust here. Cheers!

top_reviews.content: My wife and I arrived in San Fran after a long day of flying with little food, so we were hungry and looking for a nice bar to eat and have a drink. The sign out front of The Old Ship Saloon said to visit their other restaurant, Grumpy’s, so we walked a few more blocks and was able to find two seats at the bar at Grumpy’s. The place was crowded, but the two bar tenders were very attentive and quick to take our order. There were several cocktails on the menu, a good selection of beers, mostly local, and a very nice selection of bourbon. We did not have any of the high-end bourbons, but our pour of Knob Creek was very reasonably priced. We started with the spinach and artichoke dip, which was more like a buffalo chicken dip, but with artichokes instead of chicken. The dip had a lot of flavor, but there was almost too much cheese. For dinner, we split the burger, which came with two patties. The burger was cooked perfect, and the fries were basically McDonalds French fries, but fresh. If you are looking for a place that has a local vibe, this is the place, and the prices were reasonable.

Fun place to go for a drink or to, or watch a Super Bowl Game, or dance.

March 22-

Bus Stop keeps the Cow Hollow bar spirit alive with a twist. It’s been around since 1900. The bread is top notch - amazing.

On Saturdays they also have a stand outside in back which can have a shorter line, plus there might be different selection. 🥖

Had the biscuits with fruit filling, sourdough loaf and cheese sourdough.     The biscuit was great and unique in a light flaky biscuit with sweet fruit filling.    The cheese sourdough bread was outstanding!

I was extremely impressed by the quality of their pastries. I ordered apple turnover and it was very fresh and cinnamon-y. The pastry itself was very light, not too sweet at all (which was amazing) and flaky. It was one of the best apple turnovers I’ve ever had if not the best! I also ordered Challah bread and it was DEVINE! The sweetness level was just to perfection and it was light and fresh. I wish I had appetite to order everything from their menu upon my first time!

I’m obsessed with their olive roll and I’m pretty sure their classic sourdough would be equally great. The dough was so fresh, soft, chewy and flavorful, it’s insane. And the little pieces of olives were an awesome little extra. I had to go back and get one more for the road as I was travelling that day.
We also tried the salami sandwich, which was nice, but I wish there was one more ingredient in it. My partner loved it though. Staff was a bit weird cause when we asked for recommendations they drew a blank and couldn’t think of which sandwich is the best - which to me is surprising if you’re selling the good but oh well.
I will be thinking about the olive roll until I visit again, probably only in a few years.

Blue Bottle still prices and presents itself as though it occupies the top tier of specialty coffee. In my experience, it no longer does.

The cafés look polished, the branding remains strong, and the prices are unmistakably premium, but the coffee itself too often lands at the level of merely competent. The espresso is frequently lacking the necessary balance, usually over-extracted, and the cappuccinos and lattes often feel like drinks executed to a broad commercial standard rather than with real technical distinction. For what Blue Bottle charges, that is not a minor shortcoming. It is the central failure.

What makes it worse is that the brand still seems to rely on an older reputation for seriousness that the current product often does not support. The staff no longer consistently seem especially well trained or genuinely coffee-obsessed, and the overall experience feels more like an upscale retail performance than a café built around uncompromising quality.

A recent promotion dispute only confirmed that broader decline. It took far too much time and escalation to resolve a simple issue, and the company only became conciliatory after repeated pressure. Even then, the response was more damage control than accountability. For me, that was the final confirmation that Blue Bottle is no longer operating at the level its branding and prices claim.

There was a time when Blue Bottle felt worth going out of one’s way for. That time appears to have passed.

If you're anywhere near the Golden Gate Bridge, skipping the Round House Café would honestly be a mistake.

This café is one of those rare spots where the location alone is worth the visit, but the experience goes well beyond just the view.

I stopped by recently and was blown away by the unobstructed, postcard-perfect views of the bridge—it’s easily one of the most scenic coffee stops in San Francisco. Whether you’re a tourist or a local, it’s the kind of place that makes you pause and just take it all in.

On the food side, everything hit the mark. The avocado toast was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully plated, and the coffee was equally impressive. I tried the cortado and cappuccino, both crafted with care—smooth, balanced, and exactly what you’d want while soaking in that view.

The energy inside the café is fantastic. It’s bright, airy, and full of life. The baristas clearly enjoy what they do—you can feel it in the atmosphere. Service is quick, friendly, and efficient even when it gets busy, which it often does.

A small heads-up: parking can be tricky. The lots near the bridge are limited and fill up fast, especially on weekends or sunny days. But once you’re there, it’s absolutely worth the effort.

Highly recommend making this a stop when visiting San Francisco or even if you're just passing by the Golden Gate Bridge. Great coffee, delicious food, and one of the best views in the city—hard to beat.

After long time we recalled this place and wanted to go again. We tried searching it but couldn't find. They take cash so there wasn't any credit card transaction to find the name of this place. I tried searching lounges and bars on google but this place name never showed up. Then after few years I decided to drive to SF and search this place. I drove by all near by streets but couldn't find and was disappointed. Then finally I went to one restaurant (from where we searched this lounge previously) and yelped for lounges. I looked at all the nearby lounge pictures and in one of them I saw couches. So I suspected that it should be that lounge only. I drove there and as soon as I entered I was so happy to finally found it. I immediately ordered Gimlet. They have the best Gimlet. I sat on the couch and searched about this place. I found out that its the 2nd oldest lounge in SF since 1893. There was a huge earthquake in 1906 and this place survived it. The Fillmore Sweep: Strategy and Caffeine at Compton’s
The afternoon sun was cutting right through the glass storefront of Compton’s Coffee House on Fillmore, bouncing off the sleek wooden counters like a spotlight. It’s a busy, sharp, independent neighborhood operation—regulars spilling out onto the wooden benches outside with their dogs, while the interior runs on high-efficiency espresso pulls.
The miniature anarchist and I took a spot near the back counter, positioned directly under a rather cubist, geometric oil painting of a solitary pigeon that looked like it was auditing our conversations. She was taking a tactical break from her usual high-grade pastry targets, demanding a sweet afternoon fluid instead.
We laid out our orders to keep the afternoon moving smoothly.
For me, a single shot of decaf espresso in a standard-issue paper cup—clean, robust, and expertly pulled with zero bitter edge. For the anarchist, an iced vanilla latte layered beautifully over thick blocks of ice. The espresso float mingled perfectly with the sweet vanilla cream, providing the exact hit of sugary momentum she required to plan her next neighborhood campaign.
The layout inside is wonderfully clean—towering stacks of pristine paper cups lined up behind the glass case like architectural pillars, shelves stocked with clean chemical pour-over kits, and a team behind the counter that handles the heavy peak-hour rush with smooth, absolute precision.
**The Verdict:** Compton’s is a flawless, five-star neighborhood asset on the Fillmore beat. The coffee quality is premium, the atmosphere balances a bustling neighborhood energy with a cool, artistic edge, and the drinks are crafted with zero technical errors. It's the perfect drop-point to refuel your wits before heading back out into the city fog.
Rating: 5 out of 5 Stars.

Fort Mason Park was once an historic army post located at the edge of the San Francisco Bay. Now, paved accessible trails connect Fort Mason's upper and lower units. In between, the Great Meadow slopes down from upper Fort Mason to the Marina. These grassy hilltops and hollows are great for picnicking, sunbathing, walking, or sports activities. The meadow also offers wonderful views of San Francisco's hilly skyline and the Golden Gate Bridge. Fort Mason served as an Army post for more than 100 years, initially as a coastal defense site and subsequently as a military port facility. During World War II, it was the principal port for the Pacific campaign. Today it is part of the Golden Gate National Recreation Area and the site of several cultural facilities. The entire fort area is listed as a historic district on the National Register of Historic Places.

Fort Mason Park in San Francisco is a historic waterfront park located on the northern edge of the city, overlooking the San Francisco Bay.
The park combines natural beauty with preserved historic architecture, offering panoramic views, walking paths, and public programs that celebrate art, culture, and history.

This is easily one of the most culturally significant buildings in Oakland. Many don’t realize the massive impact the Masons had on designing the Bay Area—from the layouts of our streets to stunning landmarks like the Chapel of the Chimes. The Oakland Scottish Rite Center served as their grand anchor. Regardless of your perspective on Freemasonry, the sheer beauty of the parks and public spaces they influenced across Oakland and San Francisco speaks for itself.
If you get the chance to attend or host an event here, jump at it. Every nook and cranny is meticulously designed, featuring incredible global symbolism and a breathtaking mix of Gothic, Roman, and Greek architecture.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 5 Stars
Delah Coffee on Sansome Street is an absolute gem in the heart of San Francisco’s Financial District. From the moment you walk in, the space feels warm, modern, and welcoming — a perfect balance of sleek city café and rich cultural tradition.
The coffee is truly next-level. Their Yemeni-style offerings have a depth and spice profile you just don’t find at typical coffee shops. The cardamom-infused drinks are beautifully aromatic, smooth, and unforgettable. Even the classic espresso drinks are crafted with precision — bold, balanced, and topped with gorgeous latte art.
What really sets Delah apart is the experience. The staff is friendly, knowledgeable, and genuinely passionate about the coffee they serve. They’re happy to explain the origins and flavor notes, which makes the visit feel personal rather than transactional.
It’s the perfect spot for a morning pick-me-up, a mid-day reset, or a relaxed meeting over something special. If you're anywhere near Sansome Street, this place is a must-visit.
Highly recommend — easily 5 stars. 🌟

Been going to Round 1 for years but never been so disrespected by the staff as I have here. I was visiting last weekend and went to the Stonestown Round 1 to see if they had any good prizes at the exchange since I had ~16,000 tickets saved up over the years and my local Round 1 doesn't have many good prizes.

I chose a locked up prize worth 10,000 tickets and had to fill out some paperwork for the exchange. They swiped my card and the screen showed the purchase. I filled out the paperwork, handed it to the staff and asked if there was anything else I needed to do. The woman behind the counter told me "No, my manager just needs to sign it" and walked away to help someone at a different counter. I stood around for around 30 seconds, not sure if I needed to be present any longer but couldn't get her attention while she was busy. I figured the transaction was complete so I took the prize and walked out to my car— I had an appointment to get to soon, a gift from the family member hosting me while visiting SF.

Just after I got back to my car and started navigating, I got a phone call. It was the manager at Round 1, demanding I return immediately. He said he needed me back to "verify my tickets are legitimate". I explained I was visiting and had an appointment to get to, etc, that they had my member card information if they needed to verify anything like that. That I could email them any more info if they needed something since I really didn't have time to spare. He said that his staff said I swiped the item and took off after she told me I needed to wait for the manager, and he told me that he'd report me for stealing the item if I didn't return.

I reluctantly hurried back and got the counter. I handed my card over to the staff (again) and she swiped it, looking to her screen and pressing something on there to pull up my transaction history. She swore up and down that they'd "tried refreshing it like 6 times" but that it didn't work before. She went to get her manager who did me the kindness of showing up after 4 minutes before proceeding to stare at the screen and scroll through year after year of every time I earned tickets at round 1. He did this for a few more minutes, saying nothing to me, not looking at me, before signing his part of the paperwork and saying "Thank you" to me before walking off.

After all the hassle he'd put me through, the stress of knowing I'd be late to my appointment, that I couldn't do my family the decency of showing up to an appointment on time, after threatening to report me as stealing his merchandise, he can't even look at me and give me a simple apology for the difficulty. For making me trudge back to fix his mistake since he clearly hasn't trained his staff to communicate clearly, all so he could swipe my card again since I guess there must have been something wrong with it on his end the first time. So he could idly look through my years upon years of visits to Round 1 after having insulted me and called me a thief.

I peeked at the screen while he was going through my history. Seems over the years I've spent more than $1200 at Round 1, but no more. Absolutely baffling that someone in his position could lack the most basic semblance of customer service skills, it's no wonder his staff are incompetent.

top_reviews.content:
**A Must-Visit Dive Bar with Character and Cocktails**

Specs is the kind of place that reminds you why dive bars are the heart and soul of a city. Nestled in the bustling streets of San Francisco, this local gem offers a vibrant, eclectic atmosphere that keeps guests coming back.

The cocktails? Simply excellent—crafted with care and never lacking in quality. The bar’s interior is a sight to behold, an unmissable stop for those who appreciate quirky, history-soaked decor. From the walls lined with artifacts to the dim lighting that creates the perfect laid-back vibe, every detail feels intentional.

One of Specs’ standout qualities is its incredibly mixed and diverse crowd, creating a welcoming space for all. And yes, even the bathroom deserves a mention—it’s truly unique in its own way, adding to the charm that makes this dive bar unforgettable.

My coworkers and I spent an afternoon hanging out here recently, and it was nothing short of a fantastic experience. Whether you’re a local or just visiting, Specs is a must for anyone looking to enjoy great drinks, good conversation, and an atmosphere that feels effortlessly cool.

Cheers to Specs! 🍸

---

We just ducked in here to get away from the cold. I had a great old fashioned here that was quick but perfectly done jack daniels mix.

It was just a quick drink but the atmosphere was so good and friendly. The patrons were all ages and did not make old me feel out of place. It was fun.

I have been coming here for over thirty years. And . . . it . . . hasn’t . . . changed. Well, they take cards these days. Otherwise, not much. The floor still flexes when you go back to the Hostel-style bathrooms (where privacy is a foolish notion and sanitation is an open question).

I continue to find some nook or cranny that holds yet another fascinating item I never saw before (or, perhaps, forgot about). Come for the reasonably-poured drinks, friendly conversation, great people watching, and stay for the Saltines and cheese?!?! Yep. It just works.

I get the connection to Vesuvio. But I find that place to often be overly packed and often annoying (not the place, but the tourists who flock in after doing the requisite alley pictures and bookstore noodling). When you can go there and it is not packed? The slightly more affected kissing cousin to Specs’. But, if forced, I will always choose Specs’, even if it, too, can become a humid mess of humanity at peak hours on warmer days. Thing is, it seems to save itself by being tucked away in that little half-alley. Almost like a force-field.

I still have a matchbook that says “Takes No Guff.” I still miss the regulars, now passed, who used to occupy the same seat every time I would infrequently visit, and who would regale you with tales of the old days. But the building feels like it still retains those things in trace form. So, while every visit is a new experience, there is still something that reminds me why I came here the first time, years ago. That’s reason enough for me to already be planning to come back again the next time I am in town.

A rare instance where an ‘institution’ deserves the moniker, likely in multiple senses.
A true Beat dive bar, they used to call it “crossing the river” from Vesuvio to the this place. Don’t come here if you’re looking to be coddled. That’s part of the charm.

Welcome to the “old San Francisco”, a place that  represents how San Francisco used to be. Unique, a little worn, with its own character, a bit corky AND !!! The park is a fairly cosey one. The parking lot is slightly hard to find, but there is plenty of parking on the street, next to the field. There are three levels to the park, connected by slightly steep paved trails. On the lowest level, there is a fairly good sized baseball field. On the second level, there is a second field that is wide open, which is a perfect area for you to bring groups of kids to do activities or your dog to have them run around on a long leash. On the third level, there is a duck pond, play structure, and a picnic area. There is also a basketball court and tennis courts to the side. Nearly everything you need for a good weekend outside with friends and family. Not five starts because people don't take care of it and there is a lot of litter.

TLDR, visit the park with family and your dog, you'll have a good time on a sunny day!

Our friend who was turned away identifies as they/them and without explanation from the staff member, and inconsistent application of rules pertaining to ID, I suspect it might have been a situation where our friend was unfairly discriminated against for their appearance.

Hidden gem with an outstanding beer selection! This bar is a bit tucked away, but absolutely worth finding. The bartender was incredibly friendly and easy to talk to, which made the whole experience even better.

Somehow I ended up back at Maruwu Seicha 😂

I stopped by the Palo Alto location not too long ago, but this one in Japantown honestly felt like a better experience.

The service was noticeably faster, the staff seemed a little more organized, and everything just flowed better. I ordered the matcha soft serve this time and I actually thought it tasted better too. Maybe it was just a good day, but the matcha flavor felt richer and the texture was super smooth.

It’s still not the best matcha I’ve ever had, but it’s a nice stop if you’re walking around Japantown and craving something cold. The location has a good vibe and it was easy to grab something without a long wait.

Funny how I ended up here again… but I’d probably choose this location over the Palo Alto one next time

The matcha here is really consistent. I’ve been several times since they’ve opened and I’ve always been happy with my drink! I especially love their peach matcha latte (seasonal). Their hojicha latte is already pretty good. Their soft serve is also really good and the matcha one has a very strong flavor. The line to order with a cashier tends to be shorter than the kiosk and sometimes peopme don’t realize that there are 2 separate lines. Would definitely recommend!

Stopped by Maruwu Seicha on a Saturday afternoon, and the queue had us confused at first 😅. Pro tip learned: skip the line entirely by ordering via mobile app for pickup!

We loved the rich, smooth matcha soft serve cone 🍦 the bold, authentic matcha paired with the crisp waffle cone was perfect. The ube matcha latte 🟣💚 looked stunning, but it had way too much ice, we finished with still half cup of ice left.

Overall a great Japantown spot! Definitely doing mobile order next time to skip the hassle, and will ask for light ice on the drink!

I ordered the matcha ube latte along with the hokkaido cheese tarts and matcha cheese tarts. The matcha was strong and the ube complements it nicely. Both tarts were great too, slightly crisp but not too sweet, but I still prefer the regular cheese tart. The matcha added some bitterness, and the flavors didn’t blend as smoothly as I expected.

The lines can be quite long but it moves fast.

Wow, and I mean wow.  The matcha green tea was amazing!  I had it hot, and it was one of the best I ever had.

The ice cream was delightful, and my kids enjoyed it.  The cold drinks look really good as well- and I was pleasantly surprised by this shop.

It's a reason why it was really popular- the service was nice and fast.  The barista was really friendly and helpful.  Definitely coming back here if I'm in here.

Try the macha, hojicha, ice cream.  I want to try the matcha/ube next time. Enjoy!!

A massive fire at a warehouse in Boyle Heights.

Right before I'm about to partake in a dinner at a shelter in Skid Row.

The service is top-notch — the staff is friendly, attentive, and always ready to make great recommendations. With plenty of big screens, you won't miss a single moment, whether it's NFL, NBA, or any other sport. It's a great atmosphere for hanging out with friends, enjoying good drinks, and cheering for your favorite teams. Highly recommend!

My wife and I decided to spend her birthday in San Francisco on the weekend of 13-14 December 2025.  We had been planning to drive home (5 hours) early Sunday morning to catch the Bills @ Patriots game, when a search found this particular Bills Backer Bar, and we decided to extend our stay a day.  Well . . .  What an experience!  Our Uber dropped us off across the street and before we had crossed, we were immediately welcomed.  Fortunately, we got there early because the place packed quickly with Bills (and Eagles) fans — it’s also an Eagles Backer Bar.  The next few hours were by far the most fun I’ve had in a bar in at least 35 years.  I felt like I was on a room full of long-term friends.  Staff and customers alike were without exception truly welcoming and wonderful.  The experience was unbelievable.  I’ve been in Bills bars literally all across the US, and this is second to none.  I sent messages and Google Maps pins to everyone I know about how great this place really is.  No lie:  I’d rather drive the 5 hours from my home to see a Bills game here than to fly to Buffalo to see a game.  This place is only missing a good beef-on-weck and great wings (they have no food), but I’m not sure you can find paragon versions of either in San Francisco.  It’s a very small price to pay for an outstanding friendly welcoming experience.  My wife and I both agree, the time spent at NorthStar was the highlight of our whole trip and the most fun we’ve had at a bar in several decades.

We will be back to this establishment, planning a trip around watching a Bills game.

Thanks guys for a wonderful experience!

By the way, the reason for a lot of the money spent was because we tipped extremely well for extremely exceptional service and the experience.  Also, we bought some merch

Ditto all the other positive comments. Plus: They serve scrambled eggs prepared by what I consider the Greatest Of All Times method, which in my 74 years in America have only experienced from my Viennese Mama, her European friends, and one Texan. I cannot even duplicate exactly their deliciousness. Alert: if your taste buds and food feel is stuck on eggs that are heavily beaten, with any of the add ins the myriad "best" eggs recipes espouse before they hit the heat -- you might be disappointed. Or you might prefer that the very small amount of bell pepper and onion they include be omitted. But eggs prepared the Alem/Austrian way are MUCH more egg-flavorful and easier to get the yolk still soft but fully cooked.

The bean stew didn't say there'd be cheese in it, we scooped it out, we omitted the mentioned egg at ordering time. It didn't have much flavor to it. It looks like it would be spicy or smokey in the images so that was somewhat disappointing. However, the bread was really good, we 2 generous baguettes per order. There's a cute little indoor area to sit and eat, but it's a very tight squeeze, so if you have a stroller or wheelchair it may not be accessible.

First time trying shihan ful! Really really tasty, simple but hearty. Deeply flavourful fava beans, with both spices and also fresh peppers, good aromatic olive oil, and a bit of cheese on top. Sop it up with the bread roll!

top_reviews.content: Given how few queer/lesbian spaces there are left in the city, I was excited to spend some time here over Pride weekend. Unfortunately had the most bummer experience - I came in with my wife and a couple of friends, the bar was not very busy around 8 PM. I ordered a martini for my wife, and the bartender loudly scoffed and rolled their eyes and asked if I was serious, then proceeded to make three martinis and had me pay for them all. I was so confused by the experience that I just paid and went straight to the backyard instead of arguing it because it felt like intentional hazing instead of a misunderstanding. Truly don’t understand the point of treating polite, visibly queer people with such contempt in a queer space, especially when the drink order is simple and the bar is slow. I’d think it was a one-off but a regular in the backyard told me that’s typical behavior from that bartender.

I've been here before and never had any issues until today. My mom and I came in just to have a drink. The bartender with glasses and dark hair immediately asked for our IDs without even saying "hello," "hi," or "welcome." It came across as rude and left a bad impression on both of us. I completely understand that identification needs to be checked, but the way it was asked came across as rude and disrespectful, especially with a smirk on her face. A simple greeting and a polite request for our IDs would have made the difference. I've had this bartender before, and she was fine. I've even seen her outside of work where she is friendly. It was surprising to experience a different personality. The way she interacts with customers while working comes across as rude and it's honestly confusing considering how different she is outside of bartending. I noticed a previous Yelp review describing a similar experience with the same bartender, so it doesn't seem like this was an isolated incident. Unfortunately, because of this experience, we won't be coming back. Please keep in mind l've been to many bars throughout the city, both new and old-school. I was born and raised here and not once has a bartender been rude about asking to see our IDs. It's never been the fact that we were asked for identification, it was the way we were treated. I'm not writing this review because I'm "sensitive" or because I have an issue with being asked for identification. I am sharing my experience because customer service matters. After reading other reviews, it's clear that I am not the only customer who has had concerns about this bartender's demeanor.
Oldest lesbian bar in the city with old school duve bar vibes! Great backyard on a beautiful day! Totally recommend if you are in Bernal Heights.

I've lived in the neighborhood for years and this was my first time visiting. Now it's my favorite new bar! The outdoor garden seating is probably the best I've hung out in the whole city. They've created little seating areas for people to group themselves in so there's nice separation from one another. Great drink selections and you're supporting a local business owner. Super supportive of the LGBTQIA community which is great for any establishment.

This place Absolutely Sucks. Don't waste your time going here unless you want to be disappointed. Beautiful backyard garden but unfortunately the staff is extremely rude and can't even make a margarita correctly.

My friend and I wanted to play pool and grab a couple of drinks but instead we were met with hostility immediately. A staff member asked us how we got in there and where we came from. We were asked “So you think you can just walk in here?” The door was wide open and there was no bouncer. We were followed out and harassed up until the door being shut behind us as we left. For some additional context, it was 11:40pm and we did not know they closed at 12am, we assumed it was 2am like most bars and the door was wide open. We are both visibly lesbians and were excited to be in a lesbian bar but will not be coming back. I hate to make a bad review as a lesbian about a lesbian bar but I did not feel welcome at all. It seems like the staff like their regulars and no one else.

Lovely lesbian and everyone bar! Had a delightful time catching a drink and watching a few old movies. They do play sports when a good game is on! Plus they have a pool table and a neat outside chill spot! If you're in the area, stop in!

I am loathe to make a poor review of a lesbian bar as there are so preciously few, but the no laptop at the bar policy is cis-hetty, ableist, and out of touch. I tipped the bartender who agreed it was unnecessary very well, but, being shuffled away to a corner, I spoke to fewer people, bought fewer drinks, and spent less time than I would have otherwise. It's like, if you're neurotypical, you're allowed at the bar to make friends and do what you want, but if you're autistic and need a social crutch, there's a lonely table way off in a dark corner they'd much rather you sit at. It's not even as if laptops at the bar inhibit socialization, as the other bartender had to interrupt me talking with another patron over what I was working on to inform me I had to move. For a place that's supposed to be defined by its inclusivity, this was a remarkably unwelcomed experience. I sincerely hope other lesbian bars aren't like this.

This is not my first time going to this coffee shop — their coffee is excellent. However, I met my girlfriend this morning for coffee and had a very unpleasant experience.
I ordered a simple Americano, asked for some oat milk, and waited and waited and waited. When my coffee was finally ready, I picked up the cup and it was lukewarm, so I asked the barista to steam the Americano. She said sure and, with a snooty attitude, told me to ask for a Cortado next time so she could charge me more. I asked what the difference was, and while she explained, she proceeded to pour a tiny bit of steamed oat milk on top. My coffee continued to be lukewarm, and for $6.75 — by the way, why is an Americano $6.75? For that price, I could have gone anywhere for a cup of coffee without the snooty attitude.

I'm good, there are dozens of amazing coffee spots in San Francisco that I rather support.

I’ve never been here before, but it’s right down the street from where I’m staying. I usually go to Farley’s a couple of blocks away, but I decided to give this place a try since it’s a local neighborhood spot.

It was about 12:45 p.m. when I went in—fairly quiet with just a few customers. The space is clean and very simplistic, with no indoor seating. There are only a few benches outside, so if it’s raining, you won’t have a place to sit.

I ordered an iced Americano with a splash of milk, and they offered honey or sugar cane as sweeteners (I usually bring my own Stevia). The drink came in what looked like a medium size, comparable to national coffee chains, and cost a little over six dollars—which isn’t bad for the area.

The flavor was excellent: smooth, not burnt, and nicely balanced. It’s a great place to stop for a quick espresso or afternoon coffee. Parking is fairly easy in this neighborhood—just keep an eye on the signs, since there’s a two-hour limit on weekdays. On Saturdays, parking is free.

Overall, Linea Coffee Roasting has good vibes, solid coffee, and a convenient location surrounded by other small shops and restaurants. Definitely worth a visit if you’re nearby.

Linea Roastery on Mariposa is my go-to for fresh roasted beans. The beans are always high quality, and their espresso drinks are consistently excellent. They also often have flash sales for 50% off, which is a huge bonus. Really solid spot for both coffee beans and a dependable espresso drink.

The coffee might be good, however, when we paid $9 dollars for one small coffee, we expected more not discrimination! Definitely will not come back.

Cute, inviting atmosphere — this wine bar has a cozy vibe that makes it feel like a great spot to relax. Unfortunately, the service felt extremely rushed. It almost felt like the moment we took our last bite, our plates were cleared and the check was brought over, which took away from what could’ve been a more enjoyable experience.

The food was good, but nothing especially memorable or standout. Overall, a pleasant setting with decent food, but the pacing of service made the visit feel hurried rather than leisurely.

Food options are limited but everything we ordered was tasty. It was a typical cool san francisco night and the dining room was shivering cold even with jackets on (guest at an adjacent table even commented on how cold it was). Of the four wines we tried, two were really good, two were mediocre, disappointing when a 6 oz pour is ~ $20. The servers hustled but always seemed a little off. Bill included one more glass of wine than we ordered. There are better places in the neighborhood to spend $100 per person on dinner with drinks.

InoVino is a disaster. The food is overpriced, and the service is appalling. It doesn’t even compete with the other Italian restaurant in the neighborhood, Bambino’s, which is significantly better.

The food is nothing to write home about, the meatballs were bland, the pasta undercooked, the insalata has no depth. Portions were laughably small for the absurd prices they charge. There was at least a 25 min gap between our appetizers and entrees and the pinsa was served lukewarm.

After receiving our bill, we noticed the “SF Mandates Employee Benefits” junk fee of 5% which is not required by law. We rightly deducted this from the tip, leaving a more than generous total of 17% for the quality of the service and restaurant. Apparently, that wasn’t enough for our server, who decided to confront us, yelling why we left a “10% tip”. Even if you do remove the fee portion, I’m not sure how he arrived upon this number. We calmly explained to him that we subtracted the tip based on the fee he charged us following which he again screamed at us to leave the restaurant and never come back again. Having a difference of opinion is ok, but screaming at your patrons and the toxic behavior which is evident from the replies the owner leaves on others’ reviews, makes me worried for others who visit this despicable restaurant. We’re certainly not missing out on being barred from this substandard place.

I’m sure the owner’s inevitable unhinged reply will only reinforce what a dumpster fire this place truly is.

Earlier this year Shane told me I could return in early 2026; I declined. On this most recent visit, I tried not to make things awkward and agreed to have one drink with my partner. When he ordered, the bartender said they didn’t have what I wanted and added, “Shane’s coming,” then brushed off my follow‑up questions. The message felt clear.
It’s not a terrible bar, but for people I care about, my advice would be: stop in for a quick round, be very low‑key, and don’t expect it to feel especially welcoming unless you fit a certain demographic or are already grandfathered in with the regulars.

Noticed they use fresh-squeezed grapefruits, oranges, lemons, and limes for their cocktails giving them a refreshing taste,  a pleasant surprise, although it also makes service really slow during peak hours.
The covered back patio is a unique perk compared to other bars in this area (heated and dog-friendly in spots), ideal for when the Richmond fog rolls in or on rarer sunny days.

So interesting to read and experience the scents themselves. Even with Covid and being masked, it was interactive and I experienced the scents. The objects were beautiful, funny, serious, thought-provoking. I loved how everything was so different. I brought back to my own graphic design practice the installation design, the fact that it made me think about the way that others experience my work in all senses, and the flow of the exhibit itself.

It was a pretty short visit, I read everything and was pretty paced and detailed, about 40 minutes for me!

TLDR: not worth the price of admission, the design peace exhibit wasn’t very innovative either:

top_reviews.content: Best local Oakland hike that is an unknown to most people. 1.5 hours and your wiped out. Great views, great shade, excellent redwood forest to relax in. It can be dangerous at night if you don’t have a headlamp and it’s got an amazing view at the top during the day. Sometimes you can encounter wildlife and from the top of the trail, you can reach Merritt College! This is a fun spot to reflect and get in a solid workout.
Great experience, highly suggest this place if you are looking for a hike in the Bay Area !

Around six months before we got married in Berkeley in August, we started reaching out to possible welcome party venues for the night before the big day. We wanted to find a place that would allow for outside food at a reasonable cost, provide quality drinks for a fair price, and has a nice access-controlled event space on premises. As someone who has run a number of large events previously, I know well that this task can be somewhere between tough and impossible. The minute one uses the term “wedding” to any vendor, costs can go way up. Or venues can charge exorbitant fees for space reservations, or have minimum spends that are crazy. And, honestly, it is really hard to simply find venues that allow for outside food.

So we started the search, and emailed venues throughout the East Bay area (Oakland, Berkeley, Emeryville, Albany, Alameda), At first, the only possible venues I could find were craft brewing establishments. The one with the best location for us charged a lot for space reservation, and for a space that was not access controlled, and without our own dedicated bar. So, in effect, we would be paying thousands for a craft beer spot to a few “reserved” signs on some random tables for us. Suffice to say, we were starting to get discouraged.

Then, after another internet search, I found a listing for Acme Bar in west Berkeley. Having never been there before (it has been a few years since I have lived in the East Bay), I asked around and realized that it’s a pretty cool bar with good service and great drinks. We checked in out in person, and was pretty impressed with the available event space. But our greatest surprise was when we actually emailed Acme, and got to know the owner of the bar. She must have had a previous life as an event planner or something, cause she was amazing. The prices she quoted were quite fair, and she helped identify possible outside food vendors that met our needs. She helped arrange special drinks for our event, which ended up being really tasty. The beer selection we ended up having was top notch as well, as was the wine selection. We arranged for our own dedicated space on a Friday evening, with our own bar. She helped identify our needs for us, and went out of her way – along with her great staff – to ensure we had a great event.

Some of my friends are quite experienced with events, and others are pretty hard to please, and everyone had a great time. The price quoted was on target, and there were absolutely no surprises, price-wise. I have never been more satisfied with a venue, or had a better event for the price. Working with Acme was, in two words, both fair and fun. We highly recommend working with them – you will not be disappointed.

Cocktails superb. We created a dance floor inside at the end and it was nothing short of perfect. 10/10 — highly recommend this place for any party or event rental

SOHN is a Korean breakfast and brunch cafe in the Dogpatch neighborhood. I have to give them a compliment on their design, this is probably one of the most aesthetic cafe in the Bay Area. The cafe is very spacious with both downstairs and upstairs seating, free wifi, plenty of power outlets, making it a great working space for remote workers (like me) or students.

Their menu has a wide variety of food and drink options, and I really enjoyed everything I ordered. I had hojicha latte and Galbi Patty Melt (their breakfast sandwich).

Hojicha latte was not too sweet so you can focus on the nutty flavor of the drink. And what I like most is that the "hot hojicha" was served at a perfect temperature, warm enough to be comforting but not too hot to burn my mouth.

Their Galbi Patty Melt featured Korean BBQ beef, cheddar cheese, and kimchi slaw on a sesame croissant bun. The croissant was incredibly buttery, which makes me want to come back and try more of their croissants next time.

Overall, I had a great experience. This will definitely be my go-to cafe for working from now on.

This beautifully designed cafe offers a Korean-themed menu. While you may need to wait in line outside for a table, it’s well worth it if the weather allows.

For brunch, I tried the Galbi Patty Melt (cheese-filled + savory burger). I also highly recommend the popcorn chicken, which comes with tteok, rice cakes, and a flavorful gim, seaweed, topping. Paired with the 'Yuza Perilla Espresso Tonic,' it made for a wonderful brunch. I thoroughly enjoyed my visit and would definitely frequent this spot if I lived in the area.

I went to 924 Gilman Street last night for a hardcore show, and it was honestly one of the most beautiful, heartwarming experiences I’ve had in a long time. My partner used to go to Gilman 20 years ago and really wanted me to see it.
All of the bands were indígena, and the energy was just through-the-roof positive. Before the second band started, they played norteño and were like, “We’re proud of who we are and where we’re from. ICE can’t take that from us.” It was so powerful. One moment people were dancing bachata, and the next it turned into hardstyle two-step.
It made me so proud to be Chicano,and so proud of our young ones. You could really feel how important hardcore is. Arms flailing, incredible twirls, cartwheels, roundhouse kicks, playful punching. There’s a kind of radical freedom in hardcore that’s so rare to witness.
When the show ended and we were driving home, I looked at my partner and said, “Wow… that venue has probably saved so many lives.” An all-ages space, no drugs, no booze, shows happening constantly,it’s no wonder it’s such an institution. It creates room for people to safely be themselves.

He saw me with a can of soda and told me that he couldn't let me in if he saw me drinking in front of the venue. On our way to leave the block and get as far away from him as possible while we waited, he shouted at another group that they couldn't stand on the ample sidewalk.

When our party arrived, we got in line to enter. One of my friends accidentally got out his French ID which prompted a different security guard to say he "was really hoping he was gonna get the chance to kick him out" before my friend retrieved his passport.

I organize and run bar events. I get that bar patrons are not always the easiest to work with. I feel silly for never having known this existed right up the street from me, having lived in the area for 6 years.

And not just that, the production is forreal-forreal. Like forereal-forreal.

It gets freezing, so be prepared and bring warm coats and a blanket. There's a cafe that sells snacks like pop-corn, tea and hot chocolate. They take credit cards and cash.

*The only thing I did not appreciate about the venue, nor the promoter who hosts shows in general, is that there was no mention of a parking fee which is $10--to the City of Oakland. (I go to San Joaquin Miller Park and park off of Sanborn often enough), and I never have to pay. So when I saw the map, I never thought there'd a fee. I hardly ever carry cash; couldn't pay for parking. But the parking attendant, bless him, let me through, albeit with harsh judgment eyes.*

Back to the venue/musical: I saw Gypsy on 6/15/23. HIGHLY RECOMMEND! Where do I leave a review about this production and the artists!? OMG...it was AWESOME! I don't even remember getting the playbill, btw. The orchestra, the artists, EVERYTHING made me #verklempt, the power of theater--the dedication of each artist: you could smell it. The props, the stagehands, all the little accoutrement techniques of theater--it's as if I have never seen, known, or appreciated theater before! It carries such a different aura from film, from digital production. I just purchased tickets from TodayTix on a whim, to keep my daughter exposed to live theater...and it was I who was re-blown away. (Wish I had the head-blown emoji here.)

The venue and the act--all of it was incredibly heart warming, even though I was freezing by bones off.

GO WATCH SOME THEATER!

top_reviews.content:
Bake Sum is a must-visit if you're in Oakland. The online ordering process is smooth, though they really need to work on their pickup notifications. I never got the text saying my order was ready, so I just showed up 10 minutes after my scheduled time. Luckily, it was ready when I got there, but the digital alert system is definitely missing the mark.

Logistics-wise, it’s easy. Parking on Grand Avenue was no problem at all on a Sunday morning, and the service was great. The staff were friendly, helpful, and actually asked if I needed anything else before I left—which I appreciated.

The food, however, is on another level. This isn't just your typical neighborhood bakery; they are doing some serious fusion work here that really pays off.

The Okonomiyaki Danish: A genuine masterpiece. I’ve never seen anything like it. If you’re a fan of okonomiyaki, this hits those same savory notes in a totally new way. It’s inventive and the flavors are spot on.

The Green Onion Croissant: Just as good as a high-end green onion pancake, but with that perfect flaky croissant texture.

The Seasonal Croissant: A great test of quality. The passion fruit curd was sharp and bright, but the pastry stayed perfectly crisp.

The Coconut Milk Bun: Light, airy, and the coconut flavor was authentic and not too heavy.

Even the standard croissant was excellent—perfectly flaky and a great match for some simple jam. Bake Sum is a fantastic addition to the Oakland and East Bay food scene. Despite the minor issue with the pickup text, the product itself is top-tier. I’m already planning on going back to see what else they rotate in.

The Yuzu Meringue Bun at Bake Sum on Grand Avenue is ridiculously more decadent than I was prepared for, and it is worth every single bite.I decided to treat myself to a really fancy pastry, and I am so grateful that I did. The cinnamon sugar sprinkled all over the outside gives it a great texture that pairs beautifully with the heavy, rich pastry dough. All of that body is exactly what was needed to balance out the generous amount of yuzu filling inside, which has a light, delightful, and surprising citrus taste. It is perfectly executed and the ultimate way to pamper yourself.

Croissubi ($6.25): A cold croissant and thin piece of spam slapped together. The inside is mostly hollow and there's really nothing special about this at all.

Green Onion Croissant ($5.75): Tasted like a very bad and dense version of green onion pancakes.

Black Sesame Snickerdoodle Cookie ($4.75): Took a few bites to really get into it. If you're a fan of sesame you might enjoy it, but I learned that I much prefer normal snickerdoodles.

I saw this place on the news a few years ago, and was so happy to finally try it!

People had to go out and ask them to start the movie because they couldn’t be bothered to tell anyone waiting that there were issues. We just asked for a refund and left.

In a city brimming with excellent movie theaters, the Presidio is among my top choices! It's small but quaint, has fair prices for food & beverages, it has that classic old school cinema vibe, it's in a beautiful area of the city with some great shops & dining options nearby, and best of all, the theaters offer terrific viewing from virtually ever seat in the house. The slope per row is quite steep, meaning there likely won't be any heads blocking the screen from your view AND you won't strain your neck looking up at a screen for a couple hours - even the lower seats are lined up quite perfectly with the screen.

Tips: the movie started about 10 minutes after its scheduled starting time after a couple trailers meaning you have a bit of wiggle room if you are running late, and (at the time of writing this) tickets on online website such as Fandango are $15, but $14 at the door. There is no reserved seating, but perhaps if you're worried of the theater selling out, that extra dollar might be worth it.

My companion had a custom vegetarian savory crepe.  Many offerings for vegetarians.

Our only disappointment was not having room to share Crepe Suzette for dessert, but we will be back!

Other 1/2 of bagel was face up, not toasted and again no butter.
Not very appetizing presented this way, as if I was to "build my own" breakfast sandwich".

I kept adding salt and pepper myself and again, it was so boring and so tasteless, not worth the price.
The dots of sauce didn't add one thing to this breakfast sandwich.
May you have better luck w/your food.

top_reviews.content: Beautiful simple and delightful cafe in Albany. Stopped for a Boba and Banh Mi and have fully made this one of my regular neighborhood spots. The sandwiches are killer. ❤️ And the owners are amazing. Definitely worth a stop!

When searching for a quick, easy, and filling lunch during my break, I ended up here at this cute little Viet Bagel & Banh Mi shop called Tay Tah Cafe!

When you first enter, you’re guided by arrows that lead you to the ordering tablet, or you can order at the main counter. The shop is small, but has plenty of counter seating and some small tables available as well! In between the front door and ordering, there’s a selection of chips and snacks for you to browse as well.

I was initially looking to order Banh Mi but was a bit intimidated by the $17/banh mi price tag. I opted in for an open face Asiago Bagel with Lox for $13 and placed my order. Breakfast orders that are $10+ get a free house coffee as well, so of course I opted in for it!

There’s a bathroom just around the corner from the ordering kiosk, but while I was making my way over there, the kind staff let me know that they are actually sold out of lox. They offered me a refund or to change what I ordered. I decided to switch to the Asiago Bagel with Ham, Bacon, Egg, and Cheese since it was the same price as the Lox!

My coffee came out first, and the person who gave me my coffee also filled up my cup with ice when I asked! The coffee itself had a nice deep & bitter flavor which I look for in a house coffee.

The sandwich was STUFFED full. I’ve never had a bagel breakfast sandwhich where I’ve quite had to unhinge my jaw like this. My photos did not do the sandwich justice, but I promise it’s so much bigger than you’d expect!

The eggs were perfectly fluffy and smothered in cheese. The ham and bacon were cooked to my personal liking. If you like crispy bacon, maybe mention that to them, because it was perfectly chewy for me. The bagel, was soft, fluffy, yet so bouncy, and I LOVE that there are poppy seeds mixed into their Asiago bagel.

The cost to quantity ratio for the breakfast sandwich was 100% worth it. I’ll definitely be back when I need a hearty sandwich.

Stopped by Tay Tah Café on Solano Ave in Albany for lunch and had the Avocado Tofu Banh Mi—fresh, flavorful, and such a generous portion that I had to take half home. They also serve coffee, tea, boba, and smoothies. A really nice spot, I’d definitely come back.

top_reviews.content:
I have played at both locations and the quality of the Pleasanton rooms is not as great as the Livermore ones. The pricing per person (~$38) is expensive but not bad at all compared to other escape room places. It's just that any profit made is not being reflected on making the rooms higher quality or more immersive. The room decor isn't very good and a lot of it is coated in layers of hot glue instead of being properly repaired or replaced. The worst issue is that the individual rooms don't have ceilings and you can hear everything that is going on outside of the room, as well as the ambiance from the neighboring escape rooms. This is especially horrible with parties or large groups of children. The way the puzzles flow is also pretty random and does not make much sense storytelling-wise.
Employees seem incredibly overworked and the facility understaffed. Often only one Game Master on shift and they're always stressed out. But still providing good service despite that. I made sure to tip.
It's not super bad but there are other places in the bay that are much better for a similar price.

The game master was nice enough, but the actual escape room malfunctioned many time, lights were out, and puzzles and reveals were not working.  Game master had to come in several time to apologize and say that wasn't suppose to happen, and you did solve the puzzle, it is just delayed badly.  Wouldn't recommend for any age group and cant recommend location in good faith.  Giving two starts versus one as kid running it was doing his best given the amount of issues faced.

Pretty poor experience overall. We did the Hidden Temple and some items released early without solving a clue, others didn’t release when we did solve a clue, all after the intro tape wouldn’t start and the game master came in our room 3 separate times to apologize/explain what was going on. We had done Escape Rooms twice before at different locations/brand names with a very positive experience, but we won’t be returning to this one.

The escape room experience was great!  We came here for a team building experience and the guys had a blast.  One team escaped the Forebidden Temple, while the other team in the Tokyo room ran out of time with three of the four items needs found!  The only negativity was the price of the flat bread pizza, $66 for three.  They were extremely small for the price.

We had a great experience in the Forbidden Temple adventure. 4 adults and 6 kids ranging from 8-14 years old. Everyone had fun exploring and solving the mysteries. When we hit a jam, we were able to get a clue, which we took advantage of a few times. There were a few things that made people jump, but nothing too scary for the kids. We had a great time and will likely come back to experience another adventure!

My favorite things about this spot:

The location is excellent - right on Oak Street, with outdoor benches and convenient outlets for charging devices, which can be surprisingly hard to find.

It pains me that I do not live in this city, because if I did, Third Wheel Coffee would be my first stop every morning. The pine bud infused syrup makes the latte very aromatic and adds an herbal note that pairs beautifully with the high quality espresso. It's unique. It's perfect. I will be thinking about it everyday until I return. Don't skip their hot chocolate either! top_reviews.content: Wow. I think I found my favorite coffee shop in Oakland.  It’s quite lovely with its beautiful shiny tiled green panel.  Drinks are served on off white ceramic ware with the crown logo with saucer. I was shocked on my second visit that I had a choice of espresso to be used for my latte. The details and delivered drink here are amazing! This service is best when you are not in a rush and can appreciate execution and an actualized experience.

I’ve been here a few times and the drinks are almost always great. Some of the staff I’ve encountered have been really sweet and welcoming. Today, April 5th around 11am, my husband grabbed the Rosina and Classic lattes while I waited in the car with my sleeping toddler. After tasting them, I went in to ask for a bit more of the specialty syrups that come with those drinks. Instead, the staff pictured told me four times to go add simple syrup myself which isn’t the same thing. The looks and tone I received felt very condescending and dismissive. We paid $15 plus a tip; I don’t think asking for more of the syrup that’s already part of the drink is an unreasonable request.

It’s a really nice cafe for coffee connoisseurs and enthusiasts in Oakland! They offer a variety of beans and pour over flights. The latte is good and is more on the light roast side (which seems to be their preference here). They also host classes. The inside is really nice but the seating is a bit difficult for coworking. They do have tables outside and an outdoor area!

We recently visited a charming coffee house in Oakland, known for its specialty in pour-over coffee. When we arrived in the morning, the place wasn't too busy, and we were pleased to find plenty of comfortable seating areas. The coffee shop offers a variety of coffee beans sourced from different parts of the world, and they even have their own coffee roasting and tasting room. This was the first coffee shop I've ever visited with a coffee brewing lab, which was quite impressive.

We ordered a filtered pour-over (Colombia Edwin Norena), a latte, and an iced coffee, along with two pastries. The pastries were delicious, and the coffees were flavorful, although not overly strong. The pour-over coffee, in particular, stood out for its lack of bitterness. I also noticed another customer ordering an espresso flight, which was presented beautifully. I look forward to trying that next time.

I absolutely love this place! The atmosphere is fantastic—cozy and inviting—though seating is quite limited, especially in the mornings when it gets busy. They have a special Tasting Room that offers stellar coffee service, with diverse counter heights perfect for drinks and light bites. The space also features an impressive 8-tap system and a mobile modular coffee bar called “Naaga,” crafted by Oakland artist Chambers Art & Design.

The aroma of fresh coffee here is incredible. Today, I ordered a 4oz espresso with milk made from the Kenya Kii Peaberry Washed beans, as well as a menu item called Leila by Alisha Rajan. The Leila is mischievous and magical—a sparkling iced Americano with fig and ginger syrup, topped with ume plum coconut whipped cream and garnished with candied ginger. It’s like Leila, the black cat, inviting you to play along. The Leila uses Tanzanian beans and, although the portions are small and prices on the higher side, the quality is absolutely worth it. The coffee is fragrant and intensely flavorful.

If you enjoy fruity coffee blends, Leila is a must-try. The staff explain the coffees in a way that’s easy to understand and really enhances the experience. I’ll definitely be coming back—just wish there were more seats! Parking is street-side with a coin meter, so plan accordingly.

❻Take Aeria Way Steps down to Noriega then Selma Way Steps down back to 12th Avenue. When you reach Judah you are embraced by Muni N (“Ocean Beach”) train going back to downtown or explore the beautiful Ocean Beach.

top_reviews.content: White Rabbit in San Francisco is a high-energy hybrid space that effortlessly blends a stylish cocktail bar, lounge, and late-night club into one immersive experience. The crowd skews social and fashion-forward, making it a great spot for birthdays, group nights out, or starting the evening before heading deeper into the city. Their bar program is solid, offering well-crafted cocktails alongside familiar spirits, so both casual drinkers and cocktail enthusiasts feel catered to. Music is a central part of the experience, with DJs spinning sets that keep the room lively without feeling chaotic or overwhelming. Seating and layout encourage mingling, which adds to the social, party-like atmosphere. Overall, White Rabbit succeeds as a vibrant nightlife destination that feels curated, energetic, and unmistakably San Francisco.

top_reviews.content: Incredible concert venue! Two weeks in a row one day hot the other a bit cool both unforgettable experience. Stern grove concert series is in its 86th season and just getting better.

A friend had tickets for Bob Mould and Patti Smith. We arrived at 1pm for the 2pm show. There were no more seats where you can see the stage unless you went up the hillside. You’d have to sit in uneven grounds on a patch of dirt. (A couple who sat next to us relocated from the hillside as people above them were slid down on them.) Ended up sitting in the meadow to the right of the stage. They had a screen to watch the stage and it’s near the food trucks. Sound is great if you’re ok not seeing the artists.
