There's food service available and in fact this time I heard there were food trucks as well. Restrooms are there and if you have a water bottle you can refill it with water since it's hot. But San Francisco weather is just perfect at this time. So enjoy the music and forget everything. One thing to make sure is that you should register yourself first otherwise entry is not allowed.

I hadn't been to Stern Grove in more than a decade because it stopped programming jazz.  Back then, I found the venue uncomfortable because I sat for two hours on an inclined spot of bare dirt way above the basin floor, with both bad sightlines and awful sound.

This year, I was surprised to see Herbie Hancock and the SFJazz Collective lined up for an enticing Sunday bill. I was very happy to score tickets when they first became available and was looking forward to the concert.

We arrived 45 minutes before the 2pm start of the show, coming in from the 23rd Avenue entrance. On the way in, we passed the grassy meadow where you can't see the stage, so have to watch the show on a big screen TV.  I knew we were in trouble because it already was at standing room only capacity.

We continued into the main basin. The area below the walkway was filled with picnic tables sold for $2500 to $4000 and a largely unoccupied media area. The general admission audience was parked on the side of a tall, bare dirt hill amid large trees that would obscure sightlines. There was absolutely nowhere to sit that we could see. Staff told us that there wasn't anyplace to sit except, maybe, at the top of the hill. As we are 74 and 75 years old, that didn't seem a realistic solution.

The staff member said the only other option was the meadow, where we could watch the show on TV, so we walked back there. There still was nowhere to sit, so I tried a different tack: I have a torn ligament that requires me to wear an ankle brace, so I asked about ADA seating. I was pointed to a taped off strip of bare grass on the meadow, which had no seating at all and in all which the spots already had been claimed.

At that point, we decided to leave. As we were leaving, we saw hundreds of people trying to enter the venue. With half an hour to go before showtime, they weren't stragglers but they weren't going to be able to sit or even stand anywhere.

I know my opinion is unpopular, but I think this the worst venue at which I ever have attempted to enjoy music. Too many tickets distributed, virtually no seating anywhere comfortable, a big portion of the audience seated on an adjoining meadow watching TV, and no ADA accommodation all seem disrespectful of audience and musician alike, at least if you don't spend a small fortune for a reserved table.

I don't see myself retuning, but, obviously, tens of thousands of happy campers fill the basin every Sunday, so I know that others don't see things as I do.  If you do plan to go, it appears essential that you arrive about noon when the doors open.

Came here after prayer and was so grateful to find a cafe open late during Ramadan. It’s a small ma and pa spot with such a cozy, homey atmosphere that makes you feel instantly welcome.

top_reviews.content: Wow wow wow! We were searching all over our town for some tickets to see the new Spider-Man movie, but we weren’t able to find any. I recalled seeing a post online about this cute little movie theater in Tiburon! Man, this place has all you could ever want in a movie theater AND MORE! Movie quality was great, sound was great, and we were so comfortable. Chatted with the guy that was working the counter for a little bit and he might be the nicest dude I’ve ever met. Even though it’s about a 45 minute drive from my house, I can’t wait to come back (and try all of the food on the menu). Couldn’t have dreamed up a better movie theater if I tried.

I was rather disappointed in this venue. They had no record of my tickets. They tried three different ways, and I even had the receipt confirmation. They staff just told us to go sit where we thought we were, and if someone came with a ticket to move to an empty spot. There was one person who was checking people in, and running concession counter. I did not think that it was fair to him. There were no signs to which theater the movie was in, and we spent 5 minutes in the wrong theater. Only found out because I went to the lobby and heard the staff telling someone where the movie we were seeing was. The parking was way too expensive. I thought they would validate the parking, but no. Not sure that I would go back.

A very nice experience in a relaxed and cozy spot to watch major movies and very yummy concessions. Love the decorations in lobby that went with the movies both on and historia.  Really get a feel for those days when you rode your bike with friends and watched movies ate popcorn and laughed riding bikes back before the street lights came on.  Will be back when ever in town

What a fun experience! A little movie theater with extremely comfortable cushioned armchairs and love seats. The theater is decorated with very interesting vintage items, such as a payphone (which I have not seen in decades), etc. A very cute little cinema but also a very comfortable way to experience watching a movie. They have a menu of food and drink items at a reasonable price to enjoy while watching the movie. I highly recommend this family owned movie theater.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
I can’t say enough good things about this incredible theater and the man who runs it.

I was in town from Texas for a business meeting and needed a safe, fun spot for my two kids (ages 11 and 8). The only movie showing that night was Sunset Boulevard — a Hollywood classic, but not exactly what they had in mind. I had thought Fantastic Four was playing, and when I realized my mistake, I didn’t know what to do.

That’s when the real superhero showed up: the owner.

This place is a gem. We’ll never forget it — and we’ll be back anytime we’re in town.

top_reviews.content:
We heard that Piccino Coffee Bar had a new James Beard-recognized pastry chef at the helm, so we had to check it out. We ordered the Strawberry Guava Lemon Danish and the Twice-Baked Almond Croissant, and both were incredible.

The danish had a perfectly caramelized exterior with multiple layers of filling that created a moist, flavorful interior. It’s one of the best guava pastries I’ve had—it immediately reminded me of the famous guava rolls from Rosetta in Mexico City. The almond croissant was equally phenomenal; as a big fan of marzipan, getting two well-executed forms of it in one bite was a real treat. Neither was overly sweet, and both paired perfectly with a classic Americano.

This is a true hole-in-the-wall with no indoor seating. Woods Yard Park is just a block away and has plenty of tables, but your experience will definitely depend on the weather cooperating. Otherwise, plan to take your order to go!

There is a bench right outside if you wish to sit and a park across the road where we ended up sitting. So though it’s take away only you don’t have to leave asap. The venue itself is intimate and vibrant, perfect for enjoying live comedy. The crowd was lively, the vibe was welcoming, and the food and drinks just added to the experience.

If you’re in Oakland or nearby, don’t miss the shows by Comedy Oakland. It’s a perfect mix of laughs, great service, and fun—this is definitely a show I’ll be coming back to.

top_reviews.content: Shotgun Players is a great theater space in Berkeley. I saw a show here yesterday and was impressed by how intimate and inviting the venue feels. The theater is small enough that you feel close to the performance, but still has the production quality and atmosphere of a much larger space. The seating provides a strong view of the stage, the space has a lot of character, and the staff created a welcoming experience from the moment I arrived. I also appreciated how the design of the theater makes live performance feel immediate and engaging. A great local venue for anyone who enjoys live theater. I would absolutely return for another production.

Saw Sondheim’s "Sunday in the Park with George". I’ve been listening to this mesmerizing Broadway cast album for 42 years, There was some part of me that didn’t think the live play experience could live up to the album—even on Broadway.

I need not have worried. The Shotgun Players performance was outstanding in every way: the WHOLE cast- and especially Dot and George-  the musicians, the choice of instruments, and the evident care and thought behind every detail. Sitting in the first row of such an intimate theater made the experience feel especially close and alive.

A true gem—one I hope as many people get to savor as my sister and I did. One of my best Christmas gifts from my sister!
First off the theater is beautiful and staff incredible. The play was thoroughly enjoyable and so well done. I look forward to many many more visits.

I feel like I’m being generous here with these 2 stars. Maybe it should have been less. The black repertory theater - which has way more culture - is within walking distance. That’s my way of saying that y’all might be better off at the black repertory theater, especially since they played “poor magazine”’s “crushing wheelchairs” movie, which is fire. The actors are trained in the style of the Brazilian theater, known as the “theater of the poor.” It’s mesmerizing. However, while the performers at the shotgun players are extremely talented they are limited by the lack of vision, and financing skills, of the shotgun players management team. I could be mistaken, but I think tickets are supposed to be available on a sliding scale, especially for poor people who don’t speak English as their first language. Maybe tickets are supposed to be $24 or less depending on the venue. My goodness, Abeg do your research people, and I’m not even Ghanaian but y’all got me saying, “Abeg.”

I recently visited Laughing Monk Brewing in San Francisco’s Bayview district, and it stands out as one of the more distinctive craft breweries in the city. Located inside an industrial area along Egbert Avenue, the setting feels authentic to the craft brewing culture where many breweries operate inside converted warehouse spaces rather than polished tourist districts.

The taproom has a relaxed, community-oriented atmosphere. Large brewing tanks are visible from the seating area, which gives visitors a direct sense that they are inside a working brewery rather than simply a bar serving beer. The interior is casual and spacious, with communal tables that encourage conversation among guests who are there primarily to explore the beer.

The brewery focuses on a wide range of styles, which keeps the menu interesting for both casual drinkers and dedicated craft beer enthusiasts. Their lineup often includes hazy IPAs, lagers, and Belgian-inspired ales. The beers tend to emphasize balance and drinkability rather than extreme experimental flavors, which makes it easy to sample several options during a visit.

Service is friendly and knowledgeable. Staff are comfortable walking guests through the tap list and explaining different styles, which adds value for visitors who may be unfamiliar with certain brewing techniques or ingredients.

From a global travel perspective, Laughing Monk Brewing reminds me of independent breweries I have visited in places like Portland, Copenhagen, and Melbourne, where craft beer culture thrives in warehouse-style spaces that prioritize community and experimentation.

I worked near Captain’s Chest for about five years, and for a long time it was one of our regular after-work spots. My coworkers and I had countless birthdays, going-away parties, bachelorette parties, and random “we survived the week” drinks there. We knew the regulars, loved the atmosphere, and the bartenders were a huge part of why we kept coming back.

That changed about a year ago when a bartender I’ll call J started working the daytime shift.

I bartended for 15 years, so I understand that everyone has an off day and that bartending can be exhausting. The first time J waited on us, she was standoffish, barely engaged with our group, and despite there only being around eight people in the bar, we repeatedly had to ask for refills or shots. It genuinely felt like she either didn’t want us there or didn’t want to be there.

I gave her the benefit of the doubt and assumed it was just a bad day. We came back the following week and had essentially the same experience. What made it even more noticeable was that she was quick and attentive with the daytime regulars I had gotten to know over the years, while our group seemed to be treated like an inconvenience.

Eventually I stopped going unless there was a specific reason to be there. Over time, most of my coworkers did the same. These are people who work in fields that require an incredible amount of patience with different personalities and behaviors, and even they reached a point where they were tired of feeling dismissed, spoken to rudely, or treated like they were bothering someone simply by ordering drinks.

There were also a few incidents my male coworkers told me about that made them extremely uncomfortable, including being shown explicit photos without being warned what they were about to see. One of them is gay and another was recently married. I have zero issue with anyone having an OnlyFans or doing whatever they want with their own body, but people should be able to choose whether they want to see explicit content.

That is what makes this review frustrating to write, because almost everything else about Captain’s Chest has always been great. The other bartenders have consistently been funny, welcoming, and attentive. The karaoke host is great. The regular clientele is fun. For years, this was genuinely one of our places.

My birthday is next week, and normally my coworkers and I would show up 10 to 20 people deep and spend plenty of money on drinks and tips. This year we’re going somewhere else.

One employee managed to turn a place a whole group of us loved into somewhere we actively avoid, and that really sucks.

That said, I would not write Captain’s Chest off completely. It is a fun little bar with a lot of great people and some genuinely awesome staff. My advice would just be to go later in the day, when one of the other bartenders is working.

top_reviews.content:
Stopped by CoffeeShop for the first time and it was an easy win. The space has that relaxed, neighborhood feel where you immediately feel comfortable, even on a first visit. Staff were friendly, welcoming, and helpful without rushing anything.

I tried the cappuccino and the matcha, and both were genuinely well done. The cappuccino had a smooth, balanced flavor with just the right amount of foam, and the matcha was whisked properly — no clumps, no bitterness, just a clean, steady flavor. You can tell they take their drinks seriously.

For a first‑time visit, everything hit the mark: good drinks, good vibe, and a team that makes you feel like you’ll want to come back.

I’m giving this place two stars. The ambience is lovely and it’s a great corner spot — I hadn’t been here before and was looking forward to it.

After a long bike ride, I decided to stop in for tea (I’m usually a coffee drinker). I ordered an Earl Grey expecting to receive a cup of hot water with the teabag on the side, so I could sit with my partner and decide for myself when the tea was ready to drink.

Instead, my partner received his coffee while I was left waiting, and I was told my tea would be brought out. After several minutes, I went back to check and realized they had prepared the tea for me. That completely missed the point — part of the tea experience is controlling the strength and timing yourself.

When I questioned it, I was told, “that’s how my owner tells me to make it,” which was frustrating. I paid for the tea and expected to enjoy it my way.

In the end, I had to ask for a new cup of hot water and a teabag so I could prepare it myself.

The space is great, but the service experience missed a basic understanding of how tea is typically served and enjoyed. Staff training would make a big difference.

A charming coffee shop with clean Scandinavian decor - trim wooden chairs and a digital mural give it a modern vibe. There’s some outdoor seating too, perfect for sunny days. Their Thai breakfast was healthy and fresh, with the subtle brew rounding out the flavors beautifully. The nutty cookie was crumbly and delicious. The server was all smiles and thoughtfully brought our food to the table. A great spot for a post-work pause in the sun.

CoffeeShop will always have a special place in my heart! Since moving to San Francisco, my boyfriend and I have been coming to this location at least four times a week. It’s such a beautiful place! The baked goods are unbelievable—especially the charcoal salmon croissant (it feels like Christmas whenever I see them being sold). The coffee is absolutely delicious, and once you learn how much care and craftsmanship go into every drink and pastry, you’ll appreciate it even more❕

I’ve been to all three locations, but this one feels so special. Dogpatch is a wonderful area, perfect for a walk. The owners, Olga and Wilson, are such amazing people! I could go on and on, but long story short: try this place, and you’ll always want to come back!

Outstanding coffee—none of that over-sweetened “coffee”. I tried the cherry cruffin which was excellent as well, although I found the powdered sugar to make it a tad too sweet on the first bites. The space itself is inviting and so is the staff.

As a bonus, the person with the aux cord had a great music taste.

Cute and trendy little cocktail bar in the Mission.  Lots of seating, with tables partitioned far enough apart that you can have a bit of privacy. Soft lighting and chill music, so you can have a conversation at regular volume without needing to shout over background noise.

The ID Security person was reading Sylvia Plath’s semi-autobiographical novel “The Bell Jar” with a clip-on-booklight when we handed her our IDs, and that should tell you everything you need to know about this hidden gem. It takes itself seriously as a sophisticated bar with just a hint of pretentiousness that is, admittedly, well-earned: the drinks are good, and they know they’re good.

The dim lighting adds to the swanky mood of a 1960’s Southwestern parlor which was the perfect vibe for our date night. It honestly felt like walking into my trendy older cousin’s first apartment after she graduated college: it was tastefully decorated by someone who finally had the money to execute their vision and to do it right.

The cocktail menu leans towards more mature flavors, so this isn’t the place to go if you’re looking for really fruity or flirty drinks. Instead, these drinks are thoughtfully constructed into something you’ll want to slowly slip throughout conversation.

Ultimately, we asked the bartender for her recommendations, and it was the best thing we could have done — 10/10 for both cocktails (Public Sesame #1 and New Wave Fix).

The Public Sesame #1 scratched my itch for a Negroni, but with an interesting nutty overtone from the sesame flavor. The giant ice cube really elevated the presentation, and I enjoyed seeing it slowly melt as I sipped away at it.

The New Wave Fix is not a bad choice if you want something sweeter and easier to drink, though it is deceptively complex — the sweet and sour pineapple is rounded out with the toasted-coconut liqueur. It tastes foamy and creamy without being heavy at all.

With all the various restaurants, venues, and shops around the area, Dalva is a must-try before or after another event. Will be back for another nightcap soon!

The bartender, Wyatt, was incredibly kind and helpful to my friends and I. I’m relatively new to the world of mixology but Wyatt made it abundantly clear that the drinks at Dalva are not just recipes but actually labors of love and full of thoughtful precision.
Emily and Sienna were very welcoming as well!

Café Angolo was a pleasant first-time stop for me. I went in a few days ago and ordered a cortado and a panini sandwich, and I enjoyed both. When I arrived, there was a short line and just one person behind the counter, which actually gave me a few minutes to look over the menu and decide. Choosing the cortado was easy; picking a sandwich took a little more thought.

When it was my turn, I asked whether they could make an egg sandwich using a panini. The person helping me explained that they only had boiled eggs, which wasn’t quite what I had in mind. I asked for a recommendation instead, and he suggested one of the meat panini options. I wish I remembered the name, but whatever it was, it turned out to be a great choice. After ordering, I paid and was asked to take a seat while the food was prepared.

It was a nice day, so I sat outside, sipped my cortado, and watched the steady flow of people along Columbus Avenue. When my sandwich arrived, it hit the spot. The panini was warm and satisfying, with a well-balanced mix of meat and greens—exactly what I’d been craving. Overall, it was a relaxed and enjoyable experience, and I’d happily stop by again when I’m in the neighborhood.

top_reviews.content: This cute and green location is kind of hard to miss when you walk on 9th. Their fruit sandwiches look great. We picked out a yuzu salmon onigiri which ended up being the best food item.  The chicken filet karage and tonkatsu with pineapple were okay but the meat was not flavorful or seasoned well.  It tasted like there was no salt on the meat.  The tonkatsu sauce was overly sweet.  We got a strawberry cream and pistachio cream matcha which were both good.  We did enjoy taking it to the nearby SF Botanical Garden to eat as this location has a very small seating area.

Ok matcha lattes, welcoming small interior optimized for seating.

Walking by this morning, I saw the door was open. I had heard that their drinks are good, so I stepped inside only to be told they open at 11, so I went back outside to wait for six minutes.

At 11, I went back in, past their sandwiches and onigiri, and asked about the dirty matcha cream latte and was told it has coffee or something, so I decided to just get an iced matcha latte ($6.75).

I was the first customer so I saw the interior looking pristine. They have free infused water and merch for sale. Across from that, there was a long bench attached to the moon wall facing six small tables each with a chair. Other cafes looking to optimize small spaces could take inspiration from this.

My drink was ready in only two minutes. It was a deep, murky green. It wasn't the best matcha I've ever had, but it was the darkest green matcha latte I've ever seen. It didn't taste very high-quality, but like they used a lot of powder. I felt it clinging to my tongue after each sip. Still, I was able to finish the drink.

Overall, it's a nice place but I wouldn't wait in line for their matcha again. I applaud their fast service and would be willing to return for food and a non-matcha drink.

I first heard about this place through an Instagram reel and had been wanting to visit for a while. We finally stopped by on a weekend afternoon, and despite the crowd, we were lucky enough to get a table.

All three of us ordered their kadak chai, and it was definitely the highlight of the visit. This is real Indian-style milk tea with a lovely aroma of green cardamom—not the typical Starbucks-style chai latte. The tea was strong, comforting, and perfectly sweetened, making it ideal for a relaxing afternoon. They also sell their tea blends and masala tea packets if you’d like to take some home.

For snacks, we tried an aloo tikki roll wrapped in paratha. It was decent but nothing particularly memorable. The paratha was a bit too oily and greasy, and overall, it felt slightly overpriced for the portion size. We also tried another pastry with a mango cream cheese filling, which was okay but not outstanding.

The standout food item was definitely the pistachio rose cake slice. It was a generous portion, tasted almost homemade, and had a lovely balance of pistachio and rose flavors without being overly sweet. I would highly recommend trying this one.

Overall, I really enjoyed the authentic chai and cozy atmosphere. While some of the snacks were hit or miss, the tea and desserts made the visit worthwhile. If you’re a fan of real Indian chai, this place is definitely worth a stop.

top_reviews.content:
Parked about a block away in a free spot on the street, though options were relatively limited during the morning window. Upon entering the bakery, the counter clerk offered a warm, welcoming greeting. The physical space is nice, clean, and spacious, presenting a highly relaxed atmosphere that was not busy at all during the transaction. The display cases feature a decent, well-curated selection of both sweet and savory items. Total spend across a five-item menu block came to $35.00.

Structural packaging execution at the counter did unfortunately suffer from standard drift; the morning bun was placed directly on top of and against the traditional croissant inside the box. Due to this inverted nesting layout, some crush damage occurred to the delicate lamination of the croissant, which should have been anchored safely on top of the denser assets.

Everything tasted great across the entire selection. The signature Rebel Within muffin ($9.75) delivered an excellent flavor profile, featuring textures similar to a high-quality biscuit. Heating it up in a 400-degree oven for 7 minutes at home perfectly activated the savory, well-seasoned sausage, green scallion, and asiago-parmesan cake matrix around the runny, soft-boiled egg center, proving it to be a really well-assembled item. Despite the box compression, the traditional croissant ($5.50) delivered a good buttery taste and maintained a medium crunch factor throughout. The triple chocolate croissant ($7.00) was absolutely delicious, showcasing a beautiful presentation topped with cocoa powder and a chocolate drizzle alongside an excellent crunch. The morning bun ($6.25) was one of the better ones in the Bay Area, delivering a nice balance of sweet flavors from the honey, vanilla, and Meyer lemon sugar toss with superb textures. For the seasonal flavor, the coffee custard inside the Coffee Custard Kouign-Amann ($6.50) did expectedly affect the internal architecture of the pastry over time due to its moisture and weight, but the execution remained very good. The exterior still retained a decent amount of the expected crisp croissant crunch beneath its café au lait mini macaron cap, making it a highly enjoyable item that warrants a repeat purchase. This location delivers a reliable baseline of hospitality, space, and product quality.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (4 stars)

top_reviews.content:
If you’re a local, Tony Nik’s is one of those places where you can count on running into familiar faces—neighbors, old friends, or someone you haven’t seen in months who still remembers exactly what you drink. And if you’re a visitor, don’t worry for a second. This North Beach landmark has always welcomed newcomers with the same ease and charm. The bartenders are friendly, skilled, and never rushed, even when the bar is full. Whether you’re ordering a classic cocktail or something simple, the drinks here are consistently well-made.

In a neighborhood where new spots come and go, this bar keeps its timeless feel—dim lighting, a relaxed atmosphere, and that unmistakable sense of history in the walls. It’s the kind of place where you can stop in before dinner, settle in after a long day, or chat with the regulars and feel like you belong. The bone marrow needs more crostinis- I feel like a few more would make the dish really enjoyable. The wines are really pricey as well, so you might be really hurting with the a few wines and the mandatory 20% if the service and snacks are not overly perfect.

Buddy Bar is one of those spots I've become a big fan of. Nestled in the Mission, it's quickly become one of our favorite dining stops whenever we're in the neighborhood. It strikes that rare balance: a casual but well-appointed atmosphere, staff who are not just knowledgeable but clearly enthusiastic about what they do, and food and drinks that are inventive without ever tipping into pretension.

We've now been a few of times, and each visit has been a reminder of why Buddy stands out.

The menu changes quite a bit between visits, which makes going back genuinely exciting. Some staples remain--anchoring the experience--but the new additions have always been fantastic, each one crafted with real thought and flair.  Both times, we've insisted on what has become our go-to move: letting the staff guide us through dealer's choice. It's the best way to experience Buddy, because you don't just get food--you get the perspective and excitement of the team who know it best. Every dish they suggested was a hit.

On one visit, that lineup included Za'atar Pommes Dauphine (crispy potato puffs with labneh and pickles), Yogurt Dumplings with herbs and spiced oil, and Lentils en Papillote served with mushrooms and bright pickled accents. Another night, we had their crisp Fried Chicken, a delicate Kafta Wrap tucked into phyllo with herbs and pickled onion, and the show-stopping Habibi Tiramisu, layered with cold brew, cardamom, orange blossom, pistachio, and topped with a cloud of kataifi.

Each dish felt inventive yet grounded--familiar flavors given new dimension, plated with care but never overproduced.  And while we usually lean toward interesting wine pairings (Buddy has a great list of natural leaning wines), at our visits we embraced the cocktail program.

True to form, we left it to the staff, asking for dealer's choice all the way through. Every single cocktail was spot-on--balanced, creative, and well matched to the food--even if we don't actually know what they were called. That sense of trust, and the payoff it brings, is part of what makes Buddy special.  In the end, Buddy Bar manages to cover the spectrum. It's a fantastic casual stop when you want inventive dishes or a well-made drink. But it also shines as a spot for a date night or a dinner with friends, where the energy of the room, the thought behind the food, and the warmth of the staff come together in just the right way.

For us, it's become one of those Mission places we can't help but keep coming back to.

top_reviews.content: Brought my wife to the Haunted Doll House experience for her Birthday/Halloween. It was far more than we anticipated! Mindbending, joyful, enriching, soulful, amusing, and wonderful. Personal and social at the same time. The expeience lasts long after the actual tour. We can't stop talking about it.

When searching for something unique to surprise my daughter with while we were in San Francisco to celebrate her graduation, I found The Gregangelo Museum and opted for the Mysteries and Meals tour. This includes the garden tour, which is the guided Riddle of the Sphynx experience, followed by a lunch and then a behind the scenes tour of the inside of the house and the Down the Rabbit Hole themed art/riddle experience therein.

That's the summary in a nutshell.

The experience itself...would be like the cracking of a million shells. It's awe-inspiring whimsical art that cracks open your heart from the very start, reminding you what it's like to not only look at the world, but to breathe it in, to ponder it, with childlike wonder. The riddles are entertaining, but also there are thought-provoking questions that your guide (Nick, in our case, and who was just incredible) will ask. There are games that you will play, some maybe you've played last week, maybe you haven't played in decades. It's whimsy. It's wonderful.

Lunch is a gathering where you are invited inside, where piano music fills the space and more guests arrive, just as if you've been welcomed to a potluck or to visit with friends, and perhaps, if you're like me, you'll start to fully recognize that this museum is also a home. The space has not only whimsy, but warmth and a heart.

Gregangelo and other artists welcome you and after enjoying an inspired presentation by a local artist (for us, it was an author presenting on her newest publication on Burning Man - fabulous),  you are welcomed to fill your plate and gather around in the garden and enjoy the company and join in conversations with the artists who work in the museum and also the others who are visiting. It's beautiful community. (And if you're lucky enough to be there when Gregangelo has made chocolate chip cornbread, take seconds and thirds...and maybe one more, if Marcello offers the plate again by the door when you are leaving.)

Marcello, the creative director, was our charming and wonderful host for the behind the scenes tour after lunch. This tour included more moments of introspection and quiet thought, along with times to laugh together and look at the world with a little more curiosity. In the basement, while we marveled at the incredible organization of ribbons and baubles and posters and collections of years and years of organic art and life shimmering and patching itself together, over and over again in this space, we talked a bit about the struggles of the world now (of which, we know there are just so many), and how they impact everyone, even houses of magical whimsy with sphynx's and mosaic pathways that lead to secret gardens.

All this to say -  GO.

It's the furthest thing from what you expect when you hand over money for an experience these days - and I have never been more pleasantly surprised and grateful to be reminded that these people and places and spaces exist.

This place is not for everyone with the simple minded, the price was really expensive, but if you love an art, story telling, this interactive story telling museum for you and it get you to think about your past and future. But the most excited things that make me moved is his mosaic pieces. The work take so much time and its beautiful. Theres a big range of collections inside the house, the people was so nice, they let me and my sis to take more snaps to appreciated the interior of the room.

top_reviews.content:
Went to see Tony & Tina’s Wedding at the Presidio Theatre last weekend and honestly had no idea what I was getting into. The show was wild (in the best way), but the venue itself really impressed me.
First off, the location is perfect tucked away in the Presidio. The building looks beautiful at dusk with the lighting, and there’s something special about seeing theater in a space that feels both intimate and elegant. Way different from the big downtown venues. Inside, the theatre strikes this nice balance between professional and cozy. Good sightlines from every seat I could see, and the acoustics worked well even when the Tony & Tina cast was running around interacting with the audience. The lobby area has this warm, welcoming vibe with local art on the walls and space to actually move around during intermission without feeling cramped. What really got me was how the staff handled everything. Tony & Tina’s Wedding is basically controlled chaos -actors mingling with the audience, food service, the whole interactive experience - and the Presidio crew made it all look effortless. Professional but not stuffy, which matched the show perfectly.

A lovely venue, especially for Opera Parallele productions. Great staff, well run, comfortable seating. And the history of the location and the beauty of the Presidio is a treat.  If you are at all thinking of attending a performance of any sort at this location, go ahead and take the plunge, you won't be disappointed.

We go to a lot of shows all over the Bay Area but this was our first time at this theater. We saw Walter Trout (a favorite guitarist of ours) open for Elvin Bishop. They’ve all been around forever and they’ve all still got it. It’s a beautiful theater, well maintained and with comfortable seating. The sound was great and the theater is well staffed and well managed. We would definitely go back again.

I’ve been attending shows- and volunteering at some of them, since this jewel opened. Let’s see positives; it’s a beautiful, elegant, spacious theatre right in the heart of The Presidio, with an absolutely fantastic, always original lineup of shows and a really top flight, happy staff.
Negatives; maybe you haven’t had the sheer pleasure of attending yet, but that’s fixable!

Clean venue, great acoustics, wonderful staff, awesome lightening, and solid lineup of performances.

For artists:
State of the art theatre with secure and clean loading dock. Green room is awesome and their kitchen is stocked and clean. They have bathroom stage right there’s ample space in the wings to stretch. The back drop is backlit or top lit so very easy to put up projections without interference. They have a clean and modern rehearsal room with full length mirrors. Downstairs they have an entire wood shop, men/woman dressing room with full bathrooms/showers and “star” dressing rooms. They have 1 elevator for staff to use and an easily accessible stairwell. Their outdoor area is beautiful and the presidio in general is very very nice.

a review from @amom2kidsandapark

Memorial Park is the perfect addition to a downtown San Leandro Adventure!
Memorial Park in San Leandro is two blocks from the library and two more blocks from downtown. There is a parking lot, bathroom, two covered picnic areas (one very close to the parking lot the other behind the playground), a small rose garden, walking paths, grassy areas and a memorial honoring the residents of San Leandro who gave the ultimate sacrifice in World War II, Korea, and Vietnam.

There are two separate play areas. One is very large and almost completely gated. Inside is a multi level play structure with steps, two slides, (a straight slide and an s shape slide), various ladders (some I've never seen before), a short tunnel, monkey rings, and learning activities. There is also a balancing log roller activity.

The kiddie play area is in the gated area but then has its own gate around the structure. The structure is shorter with a slide, a short tunnel, steps, and a vehicle looking sitting area. The fence around this kiddie area has activities built into it. Although this is a kiddie area, some of the activities and steps are a tad higher off the ground than normal. Along with the two play structures there is a big swing set with both bucket and standard swings.

The other play area has a smaller structure with two slides (tube and spiral), steps, various ladders, and a big plexiglass wall for looking out to the people below.

The amount of people at this park usually depends on the day of week and the weather.
So many different things for the kids to do!

top_reviews.content:
🫶 Everything feels intentional — from texture to flavor.✅
Arrived around 9:30 am and snagged the last focaccia. Incredibly soft and airy inside, with a slightly crisp, savory top. Layers of pesto, roasted cherry tomatoes, and a rich eggy filling melted into the bread. Subtle coconut aroma from the oil. Crispy bacon bits added the perfect salty crunch. Guava soda with iced coffee was refreshing. Paired with salt bread, it was top-tier. Bring your own bag and clean up. Eco-conscious vibe. Definitely coming back. “Everything feels intentional — from texture to flavor.”

I was really with high hopes. The pandan latte was good. The guava pillow was very underwhelming. We did try their morning bun and the blue corn cookies and those were all great. I think if they would throw out the dead flowers and be a little more attentive the experience may had been better.

5 stars for:
• innovative coffee and tea drinks
• creative pastries
• helpful staff

Tried the Guava Pillow on a staff recommendation and loved every sip. It’s a coffee soda topped with guava foam (light, bubbly, slightly tart, and subtly tropical).

Visually, it’s beautiful too: it literally looks like a cloud floating on coffee.

5/5

Absolutely delightful coffee, matcha, and baked goodies! This adorable little coffee shop always has a giant line, but I can absolutely see why — the coffee is rich and nutty, either on its own, in a classic espresso drink, or mixed with one of their delightful Asian-inspired syrups. They have some of the best matcha beverages in the city, and I am consistently impressed by their selection of classic and Asian-inspired pastries. Everything is available between opening and when they’re sold out, and they definitely run out of the exciting, house-made pastries — like their ube salt bread, kimchi furikake chorizo scones, or sesame toffee chocolate chip cookies — quite quickly, so you have to get there early if you want to indulge. I usually try to arrive within an hour or two of them opening if I want one of their delicious Asian-inspired pastries, but it’s absolutely worth the early morning trek. I especially love their salt bread, which is super buttery and pillowy, and it has a great balance of salty vs. sweet. I also love their more classic pastries that they got from another bakery for later arrivals. The millet muffin is my go-to — it’s not overly sweet, has a great grainy texture and crunch from the millet, and is a nice hearty breakfast. Even though the line looks long and intimidating, it moves quite quickly. The team is really efficient, so I’ve never waited more than 10 minutes to order or more than 5 minutes for my order to be made afterwards, even when the line is out the door.

As a local entertainment spot, it fits right in with Daly City’s mix of simple, community-style hangouts.

Sydney G Walton Square, a Hidden Gem in San Francisco's waterfront

Sydney G Walton Square is a lovely urban park in San Francisco, just a short walk from the Embarcadero and the Ferry Building. It's a peaceful escape from the city's hustle and bustle, with beautifully landscaped grounds, vibrant flower beds, and shady trees. Whether you're looking for a leisurely walk, a peaceful lunch spot, or simply a place to unwind, this park has covered you. It's a testament to San Francisco's commitment to preserving green spaces in the city.

The park is named after Sydney G. Walton, a well-respected figure in San Francisco's business and philanthropic community. Established in the late 20th century as part of the Embarcadero redevelopment, the square pays tribute to Walton's contributions to the city.

The park's creation was part of a project to breathe new life into the waterfront area, a joint effort involving city planners, landscape architects, and community leaders. Since its inception, the square has become integral to the neighborhood, mirroring San Francisco's rich history and modern spirit. Its pleasant blend of natural beauty and public art continues to attract visitors and enrich the city's cultural tapestry.

One of Sydney G Walton Square's standout features is its captivating public art installations, which add a cultural and artistic flair to the space. The park also boasts inviting benches and picnic areas, making it a warm and welcoming place for individuals and families alike.

Its prime location near the Embarcadero and a wealth of dining and shopping options make it a convenient and appealing destination for locals and tourists. In summary, Sydney G Walton Square is a delightful green haven that enriches San Francisco's urban scenery and offers a rejuvenating escape for everyone visiting.

An authentic Victorian Queen Anne house belonging to San Francisco’s late-19th-century merchant class that survived both the 1906 earthquake and the subsequent fire - which already makes it more resilient than most modern real estate narratives.

The house offers a fascinating glimpse into the lives of early merchant families and how they translated commercial success into social legitimacy in a rapidly growing city. In many ways, it’s a time capsule of upward mobility, an immigrant merchant household eager to signal its arrival in San Francisco’s social ranks.

Architecturally, the house embodies classic Victorian aspiration. Like many merchant families of the era, the owners attempted to replicate the visual language of European wealth by painting and treating the wooden façade to resemble stone.

The bathroom is particularly memorable: marble-top grooming table, exposed plumbing, clawfoot tub, early shower, and a bidet - a layered approach that feels refreshingly complex compared to today’s minimalist bathrooms.

After heading out, I saw an advertisement for a $50 for 5 admissions discount card. If you're a regular at this theatre, I recommend buying that. Came here to bring in NYE. It was a very special surprise for my wife because they were showing Purple Rain and Signs of The Times this night. We throughly enjoyed ourselves. They gave us a gift bag, complimentary champagne when 12 am struck, the dropped balloons and they even had someone bring guitars that were one owned by Prince himself. This was more than I expected. She and I had a blast singing and talking with fellow Peince fans

On New Years Eve 2025, exactly one year ago, I was assaulted outside of the Vogue Theater.

I had a rough 2024. Lost my job, Got out of a relationship. Lost my car. Was dealing with the loss of my cat. Ended up cutting myself off and lost friendships. It does not necessarily justify it, but it comes as no surprise that on 12/31/24, I was desperately trying to self medicate. I had gone to the Vogue Theater for a Purple Rain/ Sign ‘O’ The Times double feature. I had been drinking prior to going to the movie theater, and ordered another beer when I arrived. After the countdown, I continued to get drunk off prepoured champagne glasses. At one point, I remember grabbing the entire champagne bottle and stowing away in the bathroom. I am not trying to make excuses for or defend my actions, but at the time, these actions made sense as a coping mechanism. Eventually I was confronted by the owners of the theater, taken outside and asked to leave. I distinctly remember one of the owners bragging about how he knew the local cops and he could ring them right then and now. And for whatever reason, despite the fact that they were two grown men dealing with one drunk unarmed individual who posed ZERO physical threat, they pepper sprayed me at point blank range. Regardless of how much I'd drank, this is absolutely not how you should act as an event host, especially at an NYE party. At no point was I asked if I was okay, nor was I offered water.

After walking from the theater with absolutely no sense of direction, I remember passing out at a bus stop. freezing and no idea how to get home. At some point around 4am, I woke up and saw a driver pull up and offer me a ride claiming to be an Uber driver. Now, normally, one would be more skeptical, but that was proven difficult after I had been pepper sprayed and chased out. I distinctly remember while sitting in the passenger seat, the driver groping my thigh, telling me to stay still. Despite the pepper spray, despite all the drinks, I remember feeling completely paralyzed as the streets started to take shape. I remember yelling at the top of my lungs and screaming my address. When we finally arrived, the driver paused, and then noticed that my roommate was coming home right at that same time as well. If that coincidence hadn't occurred, I have no idea how worse that night could have gone.

I spent New Years Day 2025 in bed, nursing a hangover and a remarkably swollen and burnt face, and put Heat and Moonstruck on the TV. I knew I needed to make a change. Despite the fact that my face still burned and would continue to burn for the next week, I went back to the Vogue Theater to retrieve a hat I'd left near my seat. After giving me back my hat and reprimanding me once more, the same man from the night laughed and asked me “how'd you like that face full of pepper spray?” Tomorrow, New Years Day 2026, will mark one year sober for me. I am very happy to have made this milestone, am incredibly appreciative of the support my friends and family have extended, and above all, am grateful for the clarity and confidence it's given me to speak up about how terribly I was treated by the staff at the Vogue Theater last year, who were too bent on playing cowboy than they were helping a patron.

top_reviews.content:
A notable operational shift has occurred: customers are finally permitted inside the shop floor. On all previous visits, ordering was restricted entirely to the exterior door frame, so being able to step inside the bakery significantly improves the experience. Arriving shortly after the morning opening window yielded easy street parking. This area of San Leandro is fortunate to have an excellent bakery nearby, and I am glad to call it my home bakery.

The morning selection was impressive, with three specific bakes demonstrating great technical execution:

The Cherry Hand Pie: The first item to catch my eye in the display. The flavor profile brings back childhood nostalgia, channeling a classic Hostess fruit pie but re-engineered into an elevated version. The pastry texture is excellent, yielding a clean, flaky dough that holds up perfectly against the fruit filling.

The Blueberry-Walnut Bostock: A great alternative version of a traditional Bostock. Cut thick with a satisfyingly chewy crumb, the blueberries are well-integrated, bursting during the chew to provide just the right amount of natural sweetness alongside the walnuts.

The Traditional Croissant:  A beautiful technical execution of laminated dough. The exterior appearance boasts a uniform golden bake, and bisection reveals a fully developed aeration and an impeccable open honeycomb crumb structure. This is top-tier viennoiserie craftsmanship.

As Kneaded Bakery remains a wonderful neighborhood staple. Between the artisan craftsmanship, excellent pastry rotation, and the welcoming indoor setup, it is easily one of the premier baking programs in the area.

top_reviews.content: I love that you can bring your own food and drinks ($5 charge per person for alcohol). I had the Daft Punk room for 8 people. The folks that check you in are friendly and great customer service. The song selection was great with variety of languages, genres, artists and eras, sound system was good. With the space and bodies in there it can get toasty with the singing, dancing, and drinking. I run very warm so at one point had to step out to get air. This was my first time here and we were celebrating the holidays and the start of a 2 week work break. I am definitely coming back.

I’ve been coming to Fillmore Karaoke for around 15 years now, and it’s been great to see how the system has been updated over the years. They have a really good song selection—we usually sing English, Mandopop, and Cantopop—and they’ve had most of the songs we’ve wanted.

The current system is very easy to use and has some features that I don’t always see at other karaoke places:

* Easily browse top songs of all time or search by artist or song name
* Shuffle songs
* Fast-forward through songs, which is great for songs with long intros
* Add or remove the singer’s voice

We also tried scanning the QR code to use our phones as a remote, but it didn’t work for us. We just took turns sitting near the screen to manage the songs instead.

The song selection is pretty extensive, although we did run into a few songs that showed “Downloading” after selecting them but never actually downloaded. I’d recommend checking that the song was successfully added to the queue before assuming it’s there.

The rooms are clean and spacious, as they have always been in my experience, and we’ve never had an issue with them. If you come during happy hour, rooms are 35% off before 8 p.m., which is a great deal.

A few things to know before you go:

* The front desk will ask how long you plan to use the room. If there are other guests waiting or a reservation after yours, that will determine your end time.
* There is a minimum one-hour charge. After the first hour, you’re charged in 15-minute increments if you don’t use a full additional hour.
* They aren’t always very clear about the exact timing, so I’d recommend noting your start time and setting your own timer so you know when your room time is ending.
* There is a credit card processing fee as well as an additional mandatory fee.

Overall, this has been one of my go-to karaoke spots for years. The rooms are consistently clean and spacious, the song selection is great, and I really like how easy the current system is to use. Just keep an eye on your timing and the extra fees when booking.

top_reviews.content: The shop is super cute, but if you’re wanting a matcha go elsewhere. I paid over $7 for glorified sweet milk. Like just don’t serve matcha if this is what you’re serving.

A serene and peaceful place to be and relax and contemplate life while sipping some coffee or tea. The rustic wood grain tones established and atmosphere of calm in a hip and sophisticated way with some retro leanings. I came here because the trains were delayed for a while on Bart so I sat here in the early morning and sipped a chai latte and wandered around through this quiet spacious area with vintage paraphernalia and quite soft cozy couches. By the time I left, the trains are running normally again, and the log jam of people waiting on the BART platform had dissipated. I would like to recommend the vanilla scones, as the one I had added a little dash of elegance and softness to my already relaxed experience in this little haven with my tea. There is nothing absolutely exceptional about this space, but it is simply a clean and peaceful place to feel the sunlight on your face and drink some tea or coffe and wait for a while. There is a piano and some ornate lamps and lovely pictures on the wall.

My favorite place to come by in the mornings! Staff are super friendly and the coffee is creamy and delicious. The owner is super receptive to feedback and the space is large and welcoming to book or art clubs to utilize the space during business hours.
Little bit pricey. Ambience is old. Staff is in a rush on taking orders. Free wifi
Great local cafe. Plenty of seats. Work friendly (free good wifi and a large table with extension cable) and dog friendly (indoor)! Menu were ok, but the space fitted my needs!

top_reviews.content: This is one of my favorite spots to take in the city view. If you are up for some exercise and maybe even an owl siteing, I recommend taking the Esmeralda steps starting at Coleridge street. You can burn off some of the calories from you Taqueria Cancun Burrito on nearby Mission Street and be rewarded with a fantastic view of the city when you reach the top. This is also a great spot to walk you dog off leash an activity that is very popular with neighbors on Bernal Hill. If you are feeling especially vigorous you can follow up you hilltop experience with a walk down to Cortland Ave where there are many great restaurants and cafes.

Bernal Heights is such a peaceful spot with one of the best panoramic views of San Francisco. It feels a bit more off the beaten path than Twin Peaks, and that’s part of the charm — fewer crowds, more calm.

The view from the top is amazing: downtown, the bay, the bridges, and on a clear day, even out to the ocean. It’s also a great place to just sit and take in the city from above.

It can get a little windy, so a jacket is a good idea, but overall it’s a quiet, beautiful escape right in the city. A hidden gem for sure.

Well maintained park with stunning, panoramic views of the city. Definitely a must-visit for tourists and locals alike. Dog friendly, with a plethora of spots to set up shop to read, picnic, or just take in the view. Note that the main view of the city does require some uphill walking - not fully accessible by car.

Beautiful day to hike at Bernal Heights Park. Never disappoints on days like today. There are many trails to chose from and get of of the beat views of San Francisco skyline,  bay and Peninsula. Great spot to jog, hike or walk you pet or just take in the view or have a picnic. It's closed to traffic around the mountain so very safe for all to enjoy.

I don’t get why this park isn’t talked about more. You get an amazing view not just Downtown San Francisco, but the entire Bay Area. There’s also a fun swing to try out. We brought our pupusas, sisigsilog, and blackberries from Alemany Farmers Market up to the benches to enjoy.

This is one of the cutest coffee spots in the city! The molasses cookie and crumb cake were excellent. I highly recommend either or both. The coffee was also hot, strong, and delish!

I love the inside of this place and their location. You have to go.

Located at Church and 30th st.  Excellent food and cappuccino.   The quiche breakfast is excellent.  Atmosphere is great 👍.   The owners are friendly.  Everything good about XO.  Absolutely recommended and ☆☆☆☆☆ an authentic 5 stars.

A semi-fancy coffee shop, with exquisite decor. It is a good place to work, and you will see many other patrons working. No surprise, with the free wifi and many outlets. The only thing to complain about would be the cold. Speaking of patrons, they betray the coffee shop's Noe Valley location.
The coffee shop seems to have good breakfast and brunch options, and a colorful palette of pastries. However, the lunch options were more limited. Also, prices were toward the posh side.
I had mixed feelings about the staff. Some of them were very courteous, others rather aloof.
Everything considered, I will probably nonetheless come here again one morning.

We went to cafe xo wanting to try a new place in the neighborhood. The experience was very disappointing. We ordered bagel with lox and a Belgian waffle and lemon cake. For the prices the bagel and waffle were just not upto the mark. They were eatable but when you pay 10$ for a bagel you expect it to be a certain standard. Same with the waffle. Cafes around this place have way better food for the same price. The servers were not polite and didn’t care to explain details on the bagel when I asked.

Horrid bagels. top_reviews.content:
DO BELIEVE ABOUT WOULD YOU BELIEVE in 2026!
For whatever reason if you are in the inner Richmond neighborhood at Geary at 11th Avenue, stop by  Would You Believe Bar. This  spot hit the mark when an impromptu occasion arose to watch the World Cup match of Belgium versus United States.

Smiles are part of my sipping experience. Amanda the bartender starts the chain with a smile and a greeting.  More smiles came with  entertaining questions about the beer pours behind the dozen beer handles.  The shelves and the top shelves are intriguing, and the woodwork show how the Would You Beleive owners care about the place.

Other scores include the commentary for the game could be heard. Also, fresh popcorn during the game was another score, and bartender Amanda kept to her promise of delivering it when   The closed captions appearing on the television to assist in having a complete commentary experience was another goal scored.

Finally,   the physical layout excels for creating pockets of places for small groups to gather.  There are a dozen bar stools that are uniquely designed. to belly up to and are a good sit.  The craftmanship is consistent with bar's stylish look.

I am so glad that I took a moment to duck into Would You Believe for a sip off the streets of San Francisco--and to share with others. The WYB Cocktail bottle opener handed off is a pleasant remembrance.

The bartenders are extremely great! I had one of those nights where I’m just gonna drink a mocktail and Randy made a great mix for a cosmo like drink and mannnnn it was so great! It’s the only place I could get a great mocktail here❤️ The cocktails were exquisite as well, I tried, guilty 💕 We got free popcorn too haha!

I almost walked right past Would You Believe? because from the outside it feels like one of those true neighborhood spots that only regulars know about. Ended up stopping in for one drink and stayed way longer than planned. I’m still here 3 years later.

What stood out most was the atmosphere — it’s the right mix of lively, but not enough to overwhelm my social battery. The bartenders Tannyce and Alifa were genuinely welcoming, not the forced “customer service” kind of friendly. They saw what I needed beyond a drink, and kept me coming back for more.

The cocktails were also way more creative than I expected from a dive bar. It wasn’t quite TL vibes, but more like TL adjacent. The  drinks clearly have some thought behind them. The vodka on the rocks was exceptional. Gordon knew to stir not shake, there wasn’t even fries on the side.

I came for the depression, but stayed for the friends.  If you want a spot  that only asks for ID, and come as you are then Would You Beleive, I got a spot for you. 10/10 would frequent again.

such an awesome cocktail bar!!! and their prices are not insane! every interaction i’ve had with the staff has been so lovely, even helped my friend who is new to drinking order something she would like. super nice environment even for new drinkers because you’re not going to be judged for not knowing how to order lol. i stumbled across this bar by chance while walking after getting dinner and i’ve come back since and will definitely return :)
Great bar! Gordon is a great host. I would recommend groups come here. Good billiards table and other games. Great locals vibe.

Merritt Station Cafe has everything I need for remote work. I didn’t want to share this place for a long time to keep it on the low, but honestly the staff is so great I am happy to share.

It’s very non-pretentious. It has all kinds of seating, lots of outlets, reliable wifi. The bathroom could be cleaner but it’s better than most cafe bathrooms.

I have come for the avocado egg and cheese sandwich on a croissant consistently. I also love their peanut butter chocolate smoothie and chai with espresso. It was like God herself answered my prayers when they started serving sushi—which they prep fresh per order! I have also gotten a free roll once for being a regular.

Thank you Merritt Station for being my favorite cafe near Lake Merritt!

I went in today to ask for a misdelivered package that was potentially delivered to this address. The person at the counter was extremely dismissive and rude and simply said no to every question I had without even bothering to check if they received a package. OK good to know that I will never be stopping in to spend my money and I'll tell my community to not too also.

Oh and by the way, every single one of your neighbors were more than helpful and even walked out of their store with me to point me to places where packages consistently get misdelivered to. Every single one of them was more than helpful to me, except for you.

Good luck having this person as a face for you business. 0 stars.

EDIT: I included 1 star in the atmosphere section after the response from the owner. "We don't check or track packages". A neighbor asking for their package that may have been misdelivered to you is not a service, that is human courtesy, but only if you understand what that actually means. Definitely not ever stepping foot in this place.

Incredible experience. The staff were genuinely kind and humble, which made everything feel even more special. You can tell they really care about what they do—the coffee was expertly made, and the sushi was some of the freshest and most flavorful I’ve had. Truly impressed. Highly recommend.

a neighborhood gem!! I absolutely love this place, coffee is great and the food is delicious! super reasonably priced, amazing atmosphere, and run by the most kind people. The owner always remembers my order 🥹
Community spots like these are truly what makes Oakland special.

Merritt Station Cafe is an absolute gem! The coffee here is always on point—smooth, rich, and perfectly brewed every time. Their pastries are fresh and delicious, a sweet treat to pair with your coffee.

And the sushi? Fresh, well-prepared, and a great option when you’re looking for something a little different. It’s rare to find a spot that does coffee, pastries, and sushi all so well, but Merritt Station Cafe nails it.

A well-designed (yet down-to-earth) coffeehouse in Portola. Refined industrial interior, concrete walls and antique barrel wood ceilings. Very well-made coffee beverages.

Cute indoor seating for working, luscious outdoor patio seating next to the noble mission Green Between, an initiative of Portola Garden Club.

Currently, top of the list for unique SF coffeehouses.

The coffee is good. But I see in the reviews a trend that I experienced as well around service. I am friendly and definitely showed up with an upbeat demeanor. I don’t expect everyone to be upbeat. But I do take issue with having a barista act like I don’t deserve to exist as soon as I walk in. I still maintained an upbeat approach hoping that they will eventually meet me with even the slightest tone of friendliness, but that did not happen. When you are being served food by someone who looks at you like they wish that you were dead… it makes you not really want to eat there. Again, the coffee was good. But the service felt like I was being deeply judged and rejected simply for how I present, like a value judgement being instantly passed without knowing anything about who I am and how I move through the world. I was just buying coffee. Is it that hard to make that a pleasant experience? Especially when you charge $8 for it?
The coffee was great, but the atmosphere deserves 10 stars

Very cozy spot with great Turkish coffee and Turkish delights. Came in tonight and ordered a Turkish coffee, a half pistachio/half vanilla latte, and two pistachio Turkish delights, everything was delicious, including the service! Such a warm and inviting atmosphere.

Very cozy Turkish place for work or date (see the first pic!).

We got the pain au chocolate, which was so delicious! The chocolate filling was great and they had a copious amount in the pastry. Finally, we got the jalapeño cheese bagel with garlic herb cream cheese. The cream cheese was scrumptious, but the bagel felt a little stale.

Service was fast for the place’s size, and it smelled delicious inside when we walked in. There is a little seating area but it’s probably better to take your food to go.
Beautiful family place. The helpers behind the counter were very kind and helpful. Highly recommended for an early morning satisfying meal.

(Their hot chocolate run ended with winter but that was also amazing)

Was hoping for more than just 2 vegan ice cream options, and they said none of the cones are vegan. I got the mango sticky rice, which is a great flavor idea, and it was delicious. Very sweet and creamy but the shop is tiny so it was crowded and the spoon was as tiny as possible.

They have 4 flavors that they rotate monthly. Will definitely be back! Great treat after shopping for groceries at the nearby Trader Joe's!

I've been meaning to review the lovely original ice cream they have on offer here but I fell in love with their winter hot chocolate selection and I needed to tell someone immediately. Walking in I was hit with the aroma of warm caramelized marshmallow, the result of a wonderful, rich, house hot chocolate served up with a toasted marshmallow halo on the rim and fluffy whipped cream. Super decadent and lovely addition to their menu.

The ice cream speaks for itself. Beautifully fluffy and unique flavors that are all made in-house. The fruity selections are a highlight, especially the pinkberry and mango sticky rice. They change up their flavors regularly, including their sorbet offering for the vegans, so there is always something new to try. A local gem worth visiting rain or shine.

top_reviews.content: amazing new korean wine bar with INCREDIBLE food. we ordered the pork jowl jeyuk, popcorn chicken, seoul crudo, and beef tartare, and honestly every dish was so good. but the pork jowl jeyuk was definitely our favorite, we ended up ordering a second one. we weren't expecting a wine bar to have such creative and delicious food, but everything exceeded our expectations. the ambience was also amazing, from the cozy lighting inside to the patio. you can tell a lot they put a lot of thoughts went into the design. our server daniel was super friendly and attentive, and the owner was very welcoming too. definitely a spot we'll be coming back to.

One of the most memorable Korean dining experiences I’ve had in San Francisco! What really stood out was the menu. It was so nice to find dishes that aren’t easy to come by, like yukhoe (Korean-style beef tartare) and fresh sashimi. Pairing them with different kinds of makgeolli made the meal even more enjoyable, and the recommendations were spot on.

The space feels thoughtfully designed, and everyone working there was welcoming and attentive. We sat on the patio, which had a great atmosphere, and the gas heaters kept it comfortable even after the sun went down.

If you’re looking for Korean food beyond the usual BBQ or comfort dishes, this place is absolutely worth a visit.

Good:
- The dishes were all super good and came out quickly
- The makgekoli flight tasting was good, though it was a lot less than I thought given how expensive it was. We liked two of them but the other two were pretty sour
- The vodka rigatoni was a standout for me, as well as the korean fried chicken
- The ttekbokki was amazing too - good texture and very chewy
- The place is really cute and good for a date night or casual catchup with friends!

Bad:
- It's pretty expensive for the amount of food you get, very small portions
- It's super packed inside

Overall this was solid Korean food, just pricey and fancy.

Absolutely worth the two-month wait! Every dish exceeded my expectations and incredibly fresh ingredients, amazing flavors, and perfectly balanced sauces. My friends were obsessed, and I’m already planning my next visit. Highly recommend to anyone looking for an exceptional Korean restaurant!

Huge thanks to Hwanghah and the entire Jilli team! My birthday felt so special, from how accommodating and responsive planning the event was to how kind and attentive the team was I am so glad I picked Jilli for my day!

I originally picked Jilli because the vibe felt like Seoul meets NYC. The aesthetic was perfect for what I was looking for.

Hwanghah was really responsive and accommodating in supporting me with planning. She made the process so easy and I was so grateful she was able to seat our larger group indoors.

The food and drink were also phenomenal, my personal favorite was the kimchi pasta. The spice from the pasta and creaminess was perfect and that was by far my number one pick. The group overall really enjoyed the pork jowel, tuna dip, and shrimp toast. If I had to give one critique I’d honestly skip on the popcorn chicken.

The drinks were also fantastic makgeollis, it was nice to hear about how the alcohol was made and where. The staff was really knowledgeable and had good recommendations.

Finally, the staff went above and beyond with making our evening feel special. They helped take photos, changed the colors for the lights, and were a hoot all evening! It was a very memorable evening thanks to the entire team, can’t wait to be back💖

I had low expectations for this park, as before I visited, it seemed like the bulk of it was taken up by the reservoir. However, the park area actually has a lot to offer, like that immaculate view. You can see Marin and the Golden Gate Bridge very clearly to the North, and turning to the West, the Pacific Ocean and some distant island formations. Don’t forget the beautiful and colorful Sunset District houses, which you look down on as you ascend the hill.

I have “beef” with places labelled parks that are really just hills or hiking trails, but this was an exception. The climb up the paved paths were easy and there were a great deal of benches to sit, both at the bottom and the top of the hill, which is unlike some other parks I know (cough, Buena Vista). Most of the park seems like plain grass at first, but when you take the time to walk along the edges of the reservoir you’ll see a more diverse array of plants and trees.

Overall, it’s always a treat to have my expectations succeeded. 4/5.

Small park built on the hillside corner of Sunset Reservoir (now fenced off as a solar field) with a few paved trails. top_reviews.content:
The "Bear vs. Bull" at Alamo Drafthouse in San Francisco refers to a standalone bar located within the New Mission Theater. The bar's name is inspired by a San Francisco historical rumor of animal fights, and the menu reflects this theme with locally sourced ingredients and California-centric selections.
Historical Inspiration:
The bar's name comes from a rumor that the New Mission Theater once hosted animal fights, including a legendary encounter between a bear and a bull.

The building is listed as a San Francisco Designated Landmark since May 27, 2004; and listed as one of the National Register of Historic Places since November 9, 2001.

The building originally designed by the Reid Brothers. It was renovated for the Nasser Brothers Theaters circuit in 1932 by Timothy Pflueger, who transformed it into Art Deco-style. It boasts a 70 foot (21 m) marquee sign that is a local landmark. In its early life, it showed mostly "B" movies.

In the 1960s and 1970s, it specialized in children's fare. The theater closed in 1993 and became a furniture store. It was purchased by the City College of San Francisco, who proposed to raze it and build new campus facilities. But a group called "Save The New Mission Theater", headed by Alfonso Felder, lobbied to stop the college from destroying the theater.

The building was renovated by the Alamo Drafthouse Cinema chain headquartered in Austin, Texas; it re-opened as a movie theater, restaurant, and bar in December 2015, and maintained the name New Mission Theater.

Mt Olympus Park is one of San Francisco's hidden gems! Let's start with the downsides of this location. It isn't easy to get too, isn't remotely handicap accessible, and some of the best views are blocked by trees. However, it is still very much worth visiting if you like exploring San Francisco's hills. On the plus side, you aren't going to be fighting boorish tourists for a place to sit and relax, as this spot is really hard to find, even with a map. It's also something of a hike from Haight or Castro streets. The walk from Haight and Masonic is a little less steep than from Castro and Market, and there are some magnificent houses along the way. There are also some marvelous views from the steps on Upper Terrace just before you get to the park as well. The park has a lovely, old-fashioned garden and several benches to admire the views from. The best view is to the east where you can see Potrero and Candlestick hills and the east bay in the distance. Trees obscure the view to the west toward Cole Valley and the Presidio in the far distance. Sadly, there are building in the way south and north, so you have to take photos of Sutro Tower and the Avenues from Upper Terrace instead.
Very small and low-key, but very quiet and cozy and still offers a nice view.

I’m writing this review because I genuinely want to see this venue and its events do better — especially since the concept for this night was excellent on paper.

I attended “Desmadre: Bachata vs. Cumbia” on 1/31/26, specifically because the event title and promotion clearly suggested a night centered on bachata and cumbia. That was the sole reason my friends and I bought tickets. Unfortunately, the event was not at all what was advertised.

When we arrived, the music being played was general Latin/club music, but neither bachata nor cumbia. We asked other attendees whether those genres had been played earlier, and they said only briefly, if at all. Later, after speaking directly with the DJ and staff, I learned that the DJ only plays vinyl — and that bachata “basically doesn’t exist on vinyl,” which explained why no bachata was played at all during the night.

That raises a serious issue. If an event is marketed around specific genres:

- the DJ should be able to deliver those genres, or

- the event name and promotion should be changed to reflect reality, or

- an exception should be made (digital/CDs/etc.) to honor what was promised to ticket buyers.

None of those things happened here.

Eventually, some cumbia was played, but it was short-lived, and there was no bachata at all. For dancers like me — who don’t dance salsa and were excited to finally attend an event where we wouldn’t have to sit songs out — this was deeply disappointing. Had we known what the music would actually be, we would not have purchased tickets.

This isn’t about taste or preference; it’s about accurate advertising and respect for your audience. A great concept fell flat because execution didn’t match promotion.

I hope the organizers take this feedback seriously, because the idea behind this event was solid — it just wasn’t delivered as promised.

top_reviews.content:
Firebrand Bread was such a wonderful surprise! We stopped in for brunch and were immediately impressed by the warm, welcoming atmosphere. The space is bright and airy, with lots of natural light, and there is plenty of comfortable indoor and outdoor seating, making it a great place to relax.

Everything we tried was delicious. The pastries were fresh and flaky, the bread was outstanding, and the matcha was excellent. You can really taste the quality of the ingredients.
