This is definitely a place I’ll be coming back to. Just to be clear, this is not a sponsored review-I paid for everything myself and simply wanted to share a genuinely great experience. Highly recommended!

Love the space and menu for the converted airplane hangar now trendy and chic coffee house.  Visited on a Sunday afternoon, and was happy to find the pastry case still relatively full of goodies.  The savory scones looked delish, a merging of cheesy goodness and bacon bits, but I went for the blueberry offering instead, opting for a bit more sweetness.  The volume of the scone is formidable, and the flavor is sweet without being overpowering.  There are tons of sweets for any type of sweet tooth, so you’re bound to find something you like.  Gave the original croissant a go, and it was an amazing blend of crispy, flaky crust and soft, chewy inside.  As for drinks, the green smoothie was incredibly tasty and sweet without being too sweet, so I drank it down in a hurry.  The iced mocha was mild and easy to drink, and I love that it had tiny chocolate flakes as the flavoring over the heavy syrups.  The vibe was chill with both inside and outside seating with tons of spaces between the tables for easy navigating.  The staff was kind and efficient, and from ordering to drinking/eating seemed quite fast.  Love this new Alameda cafe feature!

Outdoor seating on picnic tables allows us to bring our dogs. Can get chilly and windy on certain days. Be prepared with a jacket. Great atmosphere. Tasty burgers although we didn't have any this time.

We stumbled upon this place as we were exploring Alameda and we are so happy we did! We tried their tuna melt, ham and cheese croissant, matcha croissant, and vanilla bombolone. Everything was super delicious and fresh! My favorite was the matcha croissant. It was flaky and had a sweet matcha filling. They had indoor and outdoor seating and the service was quick. Everyone was very nice and helpful. We will be back!

Tucked away in a striking, massive industrial hangar on the former Alameda Naval Base, the physical space here is genuinely impressive—a nice, interesting environment to relax and enjoy your treats. Logistics are seamless with highly accessible mid-morning parking, and the counter service is consistently efficient, friendly, and welcoming.

A notable operational friction point lies in the terminal packaging protocol. While staff packages each pastry individually, stacking the entire payload vertically inside a single larger paper bag places excessive weight on the delicate laminated doughs below. This lack of structural protection resulted in noticeable compression damage to both croissants during transit.

Passion Fruit Bomboloni
The Exterior: Absolutely immaculate. The yeast-dough envelope features a flawlessly fried exterior crust that instantly channels the pillowy, sugar-dusted profile of traditional Hawaiian malasadas.

The Filling: Inside, the execution is stellar. The crumb matrix is fully populated by a generous payload of vibrant, perfectly balanced passion fruit curd. This item alone justifies a return deployment.

Classic Butter Croissant
The Crust: The outer shell registers a clean, golden-brown color index with a pleasant, subtle initial crunch.

The Crumb: While the flavor yields a clean, highly satisfying pure butter taste, the inner lamination lacks optimal brittleness. The shatter index is a bit too muted; it needs a more aggressive oven spring to achieve that elite, flaky fragmentation.

Matcha Croissant
The Crust: Visually striking but mechanically compromised. The green bi-color glaze layer is excessively stiff and hard—by far the most difficult pastry to cleanly cut in half that I've encountered yet.

The Crumb: Under the pressure of a knife, the hard topping causes the entire middle to collapse into a compressed layer. While the matcha flavor itself is quite good, the clashing textures—gummy internal compression against an unyielding crust—make it tough to recommend.

Blueberry Kouign-Amann
The Crust: The caramelized sugar glaze delivers a decent, satisfying crunch along the bottom base.

The Crumb: The berry expression and laminated sugars yield pretty good flavors overall. It is a highly respectable execution, but it doesn't quite cross the threshold into greatness—there are simply better bakery options for this specific pastry archetype across the local Bay Area network.

Goat Cheese Pretzel
The Exterior: Downright awful and completely inedible. The heavily blistered, charred skin misses the mark of a proper alkaline bath or lye-dipped pretzel. It features zero traditional snap, resulting in a completely soft, leathery, and gummy exterior texture.

The Filling: A massive thermal mismatch. The coarse, poorly proofed dough surrounds an isolated wedge of goat cheese. Instead of melting into a smooth, savory core, the intense oven heat stripped all moisture from the filling, leaving it completely dry, crumbly, and chalky.

Ultimately, this stop highlights the wide variance that can occur between a bakery’s high-volume wholesale production and its daily retail execution. While the artisan bread line looks exceptionally well-calibrated and the yeast-dough program hits a phenomenal high with the standout passion fruit bomboloni, the laminated pastries struggle under heavy toppings, and the savory program experiences critical execution failures.

For the optimal experience, bypass the complex pastries and the savory pretzels entirely. Deploy a highly targeted strategy: pull a baseline sourdough loaf for your home pantry, grab a box of the exceptional, malasada-style filled doughnuts to enjoy in the unique hangar space, and ensure you request a flat pastry box at check-out to safeguard your items from their vertical bag-packing system.

It is an undeniably cool destination spot to relax, but a highly selective ordering protocol is required to yield maximum culinary utility.

Located in the Sunset District, this family-friendly haven spans over six acres, providing an enchanting escape for locals and visitors alike. Its prime location near Ocean Beach offers breathtaking vistas of the Pacific Ocean, enhancing the playground experience with refreshing sea breezes and stunning sunsets.

The playground caters to children of all ages, boasting a plethora of exciting features and recreational amenities. Little ones can frolic in the colorful play structures, while older kids engage in friendly competition on the basketball courts or soccer fields. The park also showcases well-maintained picnic areas and spacious grassy fields, encouraging families and friends to gather for joyful picnics and outdoor gatherings.

Nature enthusiasts will revel in the lush greenery, as the park harmoniously blends with its coastal surroundings. Walkways meander through the landscape, providing peaceful strolls amidst the native flora. Additionally, fitness enthusiasts can partake in invigorating workouts on the exercise stations spread throughout the park.

With its inclusive ambiance, West Sunset Playground warmly welcomes people of all backgrounds, fostering a strong sense of community. Whether one seeks recreational thrills, natural tranquility, or simply a serene escape from the bustling city, this beloved playground has something to offer for everyone. top_reviews.content: Lovely hole in the wall place! Great flavors executed very well. The Shiro latte is definitely where it’s at. Slightly sweet, slightly salty, perfectly umami. The space is serene. Everything is beautifully put together. Full disclosure parking is horrendous, but the area is really nice. So even if you have to park far and walk, it’s not so bad.

Best specialty coffee shop in the bay area, hands down. For pourover enthusiasts, it doesn't get any better.

Whether you're deep into pourover or need an alt-milk latte, these guys deliver in an uncompromising, intimate setting with a super focused menu. I think you gotta enjoy this now before they blow up and scale up.

They're rotating globally top-tier coffee brands like Tim Wendelboe and Big Sur, while also being a micro-roaster themselves with a specialization in Chinese origin coffee. The curation is second to none, everything is superb.

Pourover and espresso are all faultless. The gear on the bar is all unmatched and cutting-edge, think Dragonfly and Orea drippers and I've actually seen them brew with (not cheap at all) Sibarist Fast filters.

The cups are absolutely dialed in with hyper clarity. These are real-deal pourover gods. The milk drinks are so elegant that you can pick anything and be sure it'll be good.

I could go on and on... but will just say this is the finest specialty coffee experience in the bay right now. Oh, and they're super nice guys.

Finally got to try Yunan coffee again! They are rare to come by in the US (last time I had them was in Kurasu Kyoto), I’m grateful that Masterpiece offers them right here in the Bay Area :)
My barista gracefully shared their recipe with me too. I enjoyed my visit!

I recently got a chance to visit Masterpiece Coffee in Berkeley. They focus on specialty coffee produced in Yunnan, China, with Asian-inspired drinks served at a kiosk. Their specialty is Chinese coffee, slow bar pour over, a minimal menu, and uniquely crafted drinks. Young Sun takes incredible pride in every cup, and my experience was truly heavenly!

Tried Koolfi Creamery today and loved it. The mango lassi flavor was so refreshing and creamy, and the classic malai kulfi with cardamom and saffron was so good - really nailed that flavor and texture.
I normally skip the waffle cone, but decided to try it this time since it's described as not too sweet. Glad I did!The dosa waffle cone was really well balanced, sweet and savory with a nice crunch, which elevated the whole experience.
I'll definitely be back to try more flavors, even though these two might already be my top picks.

Great Indian ice cream spot! I’ve had the filter coffee ice cream before and it was good, this time we tried the karak chai (never heard of this one before) and malai kulfi ice creams. Really good taste, and definitely coming back!

A visit to Koolfi Creamery and Cafe is a must for anyone looking for a unique ice cream experience in SF within Salesforce towers bldg.. This cozy spot offers an incredible array of flavors with an Indian twist that you simply won't find anywhere else.
While all the flavors we tried were delicious—the rich and creamy Alphanso and the classic Koolfi were both fantastic—the real standout was the Mysore Pak. This flavor truly steals the show with its perfect balance of sweetness and texture, capturing the essence of the classic Indian sweet.
We also ordered the koolfi falooda, which was a masterpiece. It was perfectly crafted and absolutely delicious, with a surprise layer of Alphanso ice cream at the bottom that provided an extra, delightful twist. You truly have to try it to experience its exquisite taste!
If you're a fan of unique desserts and want to explore flavors beyond the ordinary, Koolfi Creamery and Cafe is the place to be. You'll be happy you did.

Koolfi is an Indian and LGBTQ+ owned ice cream shop located in one of the Salesforce building. The owners were super friendly and consisted of a lady and her mother. They were so nice, and it was so endearing seeing the mother support her daughter and explaining the flavors and options on the menu.

They have a variety of unique flavors. I had their  gulab jamun sundae with a scoop of the Klassic Koolfi (Malai Kulfi) and one scoope of the jackfruit coconut flavored ice cream.

The gulab jamun sundae consists of two warm, fried balls of dough drenched in a sweet syrup with one scoop of your choice of ice cream on top. This was my favorite! I have had gulab jamun before and always think it pairs well with cold ice cream on top, and I really like the Klassic Koolfi flavor, which had pistachios, walnuts, cardamom, rose water, and saffron.

The jackfruit coconut flavor tasted exactly like its name. As a Viet who loves jackfruit, I really liked it, and it tasted very reminiscent and familiar to many of the cold desserts we have! You can really taste the jackfruit which has a sweet but tart taste.

There is no seating inside, but there is plenty of outdoor seats.

Overall, I would come back to try their other unique flavors and support their small business.

I am an ice cream fiend. No doubts on that! I had eaten Indian ice cream waaay back in an Indian shop on Valencia in the Mission. It was good! Which is why I searched and found Koolfi!
This Vacant-to-Vibrant pop-up of East Bay’s Koolfi Creamery offers delicious Indian Ice cream using Strauss Creamery milk. There are vegan options too.
I got a double scoop with Lotus & Rose and the traditional Masala Koolfi flavors. Clean tasting. No gummy residue on the tongue. Little chewy bits in the Lotis & Rose scoop. Yum!! The Chief Creative Ice Cream Maker used to be a City Engineer! Now she makes ice cream that she reminisces about from home. Best of luck to this women-owned business!

We had such a great experience at this Colombian restaurant! If you are looking for authentic Latin flavors and a true taste of Colombia, this is the place to come. The atmosphere is cozy, family-friendly, and makes you feel right at home. We tried the tamal and a traditional Colombian breakfast, and both dishes were full of flavor, fresh, and absolutely delicious.

What really stood out was the service — everyone was super kind, welcoming, and attentive, which made the whole visit even better. We are staying in downtown and decided to come here, and honestly, it was more than worth the trip. If you’re visiting the area or even if you live nearby, don’t miss the chance to stop by. You’ll leave full, happy, and already planning your next visit!

I was working on the visitation valley area a couple days ago and was thinking what am I going to have for lunch? I looked on my phone and there weren't many choices but came across creative Ideas Cafe. It had really good reviews and a pretty decent size menu. I've never had Colombian food before so I didn't know what to expect. I did a little research online and Instagram and watched a couple videos of food influencers reviewing the place. I decided I would give it a try. I am really happy that I did. I ended up getting the Bandeja Paisa which was really tasty. There was a mix of different dishes in the plate that I've never had before. Everything was flavorful from the Colombian chorizo to the Colombian red beans or the chicharronas or my favorite the cheese arepa with some of their green salsa. OMG that green salsa is the shit hella good. I also wanted to try the Ajiaco which is their corn and potatoe and chicken and soup. The soup had a really nice taste to it very comforting. I also did an order of their chicken and beef empanadas those were out of the park great flavor. The crunch itself was so crispy that also paired well with the green salsa I washed it down with a squirt grapefruit soda. Couldn't have paired better. I definitely want to go back and try some new dishes that I have not tried yet. Their menu is a pretty good size and everything is made to order. If you have a chance to stop by and visit this place, do not think twice you will like it. Keep up the great work!

I was recommended this place by a local business owner in the area and thought I'd give this place a shot. Kept it simple with 3 street tacos that were OK. Carne asada was a bit dry and the tortillas were very dry - almost tasted uncooked or like they'd been out for a while. The stiffness of the tortilla made it a unpleasant to eat overall. I did enjoy the passionfruit agua fresca and do recommend. It tastes very natural with a slight sourness, not overly sweet. Another thing that was unpleasant for me was the customer service by the woman taking my order. I would be in the middle of ordering and she'd cut me off to speak to other customers and then do something else behind the counter repeatedly. Id patiently wait for her to come back and whenever she started taking my order shed go back to ignoring me to do something else. I know businesses can get busy but i found it rude as a customer.

Highly recommend this place and so happy for the neighborhood for adding on a new cuisine! The arepas were authentic that brought back so many good Colombia memories! The beef empanadas was so delicious- thin crust with tasty filling! I can’t wait to try out the other items on the menu. They also have a catering arm of the business. All their stuff look so pretty. I can’t wait to try out more menu items in the coming weeks!

If you’re looking for “REAL” Colombian food in the Bay Area; this spot is excellent. This is a small Colombian and Mexican cafe-turned-restaurant which has some of the most authentic and homemade Colombian food I’ve tried in the area. They even have local Colombian beers and desserts.

While it seems small, there are a few tables inside and outside. This establishment is growing in popularity and does cater. They have a variety of arepas, Colombian breads, and weekly Colombian soups which are just amazing. When we went today; they had ajiaco which I haven’t seen in YEARS. They also had bandeja paisa, pandebono, arepa de queso, and so many other treats.

If you’re not a fan of Colombian food - there is also tons of Mexican food here too. However; I HIGHLY recommend coming for the Colombian dishes which are honestly some of the best in the area if you’re a Colombia fan.

If you’re a sports fan, Splash at Thrive City is an absolute dream! Located just outside the Chase Center, this 30,000-square-foot sports bar is next-level when it comes to watching the game, grabbing great food, and enjoying top-tier drinks.The two-level setup ensures that every seat is a good seat, and the massive TV screens make you feel like you’re right in the action—whether it’s basketball, football, or tennis, you won’t miss a moment. The atmosphere is electric, especially on game days, making it the perfect place to cheer on your team. The food was surprisingly good for a sports bar, and the drink menu had a great selection to keep the energy going. The service was friendly and efficient, even with a packed house. If you’re heading to the Chase Center or just looking for a great spot to watch the game, Splash is the place to be. I’ll definitely be back! Splash at Thrive City – ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (Would Be 10 Stars If I Could)

The drinks matched the quality of the food. The Bloody Mary was bold, balanced, and properly garnished — exactly what you want for brunch. No shortcuts.

Service is where Splash truly stands out. Alonzo took outstanding care of us — attentive without hovering, personable, and fully engaged. I recently attended an event at Lions Den Bar and Lounge in Chinatown with a large group from my organization. The experience was a mixed bag for me, but here’s a breakdown:

Food:
I tried the wings, spring rolls, and chow mein, and all were seasoned pretty well. I’m not sure if the food was made in-house or catered, but it was decent overall. I also had a couple of drinks—Stella and a Gin and Tonic—which were standard but good.

Service:
The staff seemed fine, though I didn’t have much interaction with them beyond ordering drinks. Payment options were a bit limited, as I didn’t notice tap-to-pay, and most people just used their cards.

Ambience:
This is where things were a little hit-or-miss for me. When we arrived around 5:00pm, the place was pretty empty, but it picked up when our event started at 6:00pm. The seating was adequate, though some people in our group had to stand, but it didn’t seem to bother them. The lighting was actually a highlight, with colorful lights adding a nice vibe as the evening went on.

The real fun began when karaoke started—definitely a high point! It really lifted the mood, especially since the Padres vs Dodgers game was also on the screens, adding to the entertainment.

Overall:
If you’re looking for a spot for a group event, this place might do the trick, especially with the added fun of karaoke and a game on TV. However, if I were going solo or with just one other person, I’d probably choose another spot, as the overall vibe just wasn’t for me.

Came here for dinner, first time visiting this place even though I've passed by many times since it opened.  The place was busy, but there were still a good amount of tables to sit in.  I think we only waited a minute, and the waitress sat us down and got us tea all within a couple of minutes.  The decoration and atmosphere is casual with a sense that you are in a Hong Kong style restaurant with a large mural of a Hong Kong street with lots of store front signs and neon lights.  The decoration is eclectic with an Asian theme with lots of little Asian themed toys and knickknacks.

The food menu is extensive with lots of common foods found in street cafes such as toasts, baked rice, and noodles dishes to the more common dishes like fried rice, Chow mien, porridge, etc. Then there is the more oddball and exotic dishes made with intestines, blood, and frogs.

As I wasn't into experimenting into the exotic dishes we decided to order BBQ pork fried rice,  salt & pepper deep fried fish, salt & pepper deep fried tofu, wonton soup, western style overeasy egg in minced beef sauce over rice, and stir-fry beef rib-eye Japan style.

All the dishes came in within the next 10 to 15 minutes.  They looked delicious to my eyes and smelled even better.   The bbq pork unfortunately did not meet my satisfaction.  Yeah, it looked great and smelled good, but the taste was just bland.  There wasn't even a taste of the bbq pork. The pork itself was dry, like the remnants of old bbq pork cuttings that have been sitting for a while.  Fortunately the other dishes were arriving and we had a better experience.

The next dish to come was the wonton soup. The bowl had enough soup and wonton dumplings to serve at least all four of us with a couple extras.  There were also fresh baby bok Choi vegetables in the soup, which was nice to balance all the meat.  The soup was okay,  nothing exciting.  The meat filling in the wonton was okay too... I've had better.

The next dish up was the salt & pepper tofu cubes. These deep-fried morsels were piping hot with a nice outer crunch and very soft interior.  The outside had a really nice seasoning that was savory with a hint of spices. There were also sprinkling of fried jalapeño peppers and garlic.  It was delicious.

The next dish was the salt & pepper deep fried fish.  Just like the tofu,  these fish were battered and deep fried and seasoned with salt, spices,  and that mixture of jalapeños pepper and fried garlic. The fish was delicious with a semi crunchy outer shell and a very nice soft, smooth, almost melty interior. I'm not sure what type of fish they used, but it was really nice and soft.

A minute later, the waitress brought out the rest of our order.  It was the overeasy egg in minced beef and sauce over rice and the stir-fry beef rib-eye Japan style.

The western style egg in minced beef sauce over rice was truly delicious.  It was a mound of rice with a brown gravy sauce with minced beef and shavings of I think it was broccoli stems. In the middle of all that mess was a raw egg cooking in the heat of the dish.  The beef and sauce mixed in with the rice was just great.  I really can't explain the taste, it was like putting gravy into your rice but the gravy is not over powering. It balanced the right amount of saltiness, beef flavor, and umami to go right with the plain white rice.

My favorite dish above all the stir-fry beef ribeye Japan style dish.  The pieces of beef are stir fried in a sweet, savory sauce with a very distinctive flavor I couldn't identify.  Under the beef are pan fried soft tofu rounds that have the sauce dripping on it.  Surrounding the beef and tofu is a bed of fresh broccoli with drippings of sauce on top.  This dish was really exceptionally good.  The beef was so tender and juicy with the addition of the sauce that it was an explosion of flavor and texture in your mouth.

We truly ate really well and had lots of leftover for the next day.  I'll probably visit again and try their other dishes.  Some of the dishes you can't find in regular Chinese restaurants.

Gorgeous historic home and grounds open for tours.  The house was built by Alexander Dunsmuir for his bride in 1899. The house was decorated beautifully for the holiday season and also had lots of holiday photo opportunities outside for children, as well as two bouncy houses. There was a high tea event available, tickets available online and had sold out by our arrival.  Friendly and helpful staff were plentiful.  Parking was $15.  Disability Information:  Disabled parking available on request, with drop off and shuttle available to the house. The lovely walk through the grounds is on a paved but slightly bumpy narrow road that gently ascends to the house, which sits on a small rise.  The road is perhaps 1/8th mile long.  There is a ramp to the back door, but tours enter through the front and people are carefully routed in one direction only.  Some stair climbing is necessary to see the house; I did not see any elevator or disabled access to the second floor.  The restrooms are nearby in another building, but require either ascending a fairly long stair up the hill or using the slightly steep ramp walkway tucked around the back.  Printed information throughout the house offered no Braille.  The movement of foot traffic through the house moved at a fairly good pace, but if one wishes to move at a more leisurely pace most of the time there is room to allow others to pass.  A lovely place to visit and we all very much enjoyed it!

I will visit here next year! My favorite classic (1976) horror movie Burnt Offerings was filmed here and it was the first movie to ever be filmed at this estate. It felt so comfortable to be there that we will be back soon.

top_reviews.content: I got here at 7:30 am on Saturday, and there were hardly anyone was dining. I like to beat the traffic and have a quiet morning, and it was perfect. I had Fluffy chili scramble. It was well executed and put together. My latte was pretty and yummy.

OMG some of the best coffee I had in a long time. The people here are so nice and friendly (great service).
Now to the food the BL Burrito is too die for, ask for less feta unless you like feta. The layers of flavor were amazing.
Highly recommended on all aspects of what a restaurant should deliver (food + service + atmosphere).

We visited the restaurant for breakfast as a group of four. The food was very good and met our expectations in terms of quality and taste.

However, the service left room for improvement. My wife’s order was unfortunately forgotten, and she only received her meal after we asked about it and waited additional time. By then, the rest of us had already finished eating.

This is something that ideally should not happen.

We tried Bluestone Lane for breakfast, when we were staying in the Marina.  Not realizing that our stay was the same morning as the San Francisco Marathon, Bluestone Lane was super busy and packed with people when we arrived.

Nonetheless, after a short wait, a table was set for us.  The restaurant was definitely super short staffed, as a table was set up for us and the server told us they would bring us chairs to finish up the table so we could sit down.  After waiting several minutes for the chairs, a guest at one of the other tables offered up some extra chairs, so we were able to finish setting up the table and sit down.

The menu had lots of nice and smaller options for kids, which was great since we were with my two younger nieces.  One of my nieces got the banana bread with a smashed avocado side, while the other got the blueberry pancakes.  I got the BL burrito and my partner got a side of toast and helped the girls with their meals.

While the prices for the items were pretty reasonable, the portions were also a bit small.  The banana bread in particular was a small portion, with my niece noting that she was still hungry after finishing the plate.  Unfortunately, since the restaurant was really busy, we did not want to order any additional items but instead opted to get her more food after leaving the restaurant.  My younger niece did really enjoy the blueberry pancakes, which was also a more generous portion.

My partner's toast was okay, although not as toasted/crispy as expected.  The BL burrito was just okay; it tasted like a very basic breakfast burrito without a ton of flavor, so I doused it in Cholula to give it a little kick.

Despite being slammed with marathon goers and understaffed, the servers were really nice and tried their best to be attentive.  The food was fairly reasonably priced, but the portions were a bit small.

Great coffee. But also so much seating! Great place to do some remote work from if you are tired of working from work.
Had an interesting coffee specials menu though of my go to cappuccino order which was good.
My friend got a tea and she loved it too.

When asked about it, the lady said the charge was due to a us being with a birthday group (that had their own tabs per individual). We didn’t order any food or catering. It was a meet up spot to have drinks. I’m not sure why they would charge us 18.5% individually. One of our party closed a tab and then opened one later on and was also charged 18.5% again! The total for my tab was $125 (3 shots and 3 mixed drinks) that’s included with the gratuity. If you round it up, that’s a $20.83 charge PER DRINK! top_reviews.content: Adorable quaint little shop near San Jose park,  great spot for a Saturday to grab some ice cream with kids and head over to a nostalgic park! Amazing service, provided samples upon asked. I tried the noose tracks ice cream, a vanilla base with chocolate fudge and peanut butter cups. I would absolutely recommend this flavor to all, but they also offered a lot of other classic flavors (such as vanilla, cookies and cream, cotton candy, birthday cake, etc). They have a whole selection of sherberts as well, with unique flavors such as maui waui and pineapple sherbet. This is a must try place for ice cream, especially with kids!

We got a Mint Chip and one of the coffee flavors. There's something about the texture that I didn't like so I wouldn't try again. My partner thought it was fine though.

I didn't vibe with the name of the available flavors and everything looked bright and artificial - which I think would attract the kids. I actually first asked "what's the best seller?" to the staff and I got a "depends on your taste." Fair. But that doesn't help me decide on something to try - it would have been nice if the staff could have suggested a few flavors people gravitate to since it would let me know that they know their customers and flavors. I ended up with the Mint Chip flavor since it would be one of the safe options.

Service: Staff were courteous and friendly, and I appreciated the nice touch of the US flag with my ice cream to commemorate Fourth of July! Scoop prices are reasonable and they allow single splits without charging extra, which is a plus.

Ice Cream: I was a tad disappointed in my flavors (Pumpkin and Strawberry Cheesecake) on my first visit; both needed more flavor and sweetness. Texture was thick yet slightly icy.

On my second visit, I tried two classic flavors (Cookies & Cream, Green Tea), which were nicely flavored and creamy.

Will definitely go back to try their frozen Greek yogurt!

Final Price: $4.50 Single split scoop

top_reviews.content:
Jack Early Park is a hidden gem in North Beach that you might easily overlook unless you know where to look. Situated at the end of Pfeiffer Street, up a steep hill, it was developed by local resident Jack Early, who, in the early 1960s, transformed a neglected, rocky patch of land into a peaceful garden. He cleared debris, brought in soil, and planted trees, flowers, and shrubs—ultimately gifting the space to the city. This park is a great example of how one person's efforts can create a lasting impact on a neighborhood.

Getting there is part of the experience. You ascend a narrow staircase between buildings, and at the top, you are rewarded with a small concrete terrace that offers one of the best panoramic views in the area. On a clear day, you can see Alcatraz Island, Pier 39, and even the Golden Gate Bridge all in one magnificent view.

While the park isn't large, that adds to its charm. It features a few benches, some greenery, and just enough space to sit down, relax, or enjoy a quiet moment away from the crowds. Whether you're a local or just exploring North Beach, it's a worthwhile stop if you're up for a short climb and want a different perspective of the city.

Top 10 observations and mind-blowing facts about Jack Early Park. (You won't believe number 8!)

1. You probably won't get hit in the head by an errant frisbee

2. Outside Lands or any other music festival is unlikely to book this park for concerts

3. Rarely the scene of any impromptu drum circles

4. No competition for public BBQ grills on Saturday afternoons

5. Closed to auto traffic since 1962 (bikes ok)

6. No public restrooms. Plan accordingly.

7. Your children won't get injured on any playground equipment

8. You can run 50 laps around the perimeter of the park and brag to  friends about your athletic endurance

9. There's very low risk of a sprinkler system coming on while you're making out late at night

10. You won't get lost on the hiking trails.

top_reviews.content:
The Presidio offers a unique blend of natural beauty, rich history, and vibrant culture. Once a military post, this 1,491-acre park has transformed into a haven for locals and visitors alike, providing a serene escape from the city’s hustle and bustle.
A Journey Through Time
Established in 1776 by Spanish settlers, the Presidio began as a military fortification to protect the bay. It later came under Mexican control in 1821 and was eventually taken over by the United States Army in 1846. For over two centuries, it served as a strategic military base before transitioning into a national park site in 1994. Today, the Presidio stands as a testament to the layered history of California, with preserved buildings and landmarks that tell stories of its diverse past.  ￼ ￼ ￼
Nature’s Playground
The Presidio boasts over 24 miles of hiking and biking trails, meandering through eucalyptus groves, coastal bluffs, and scenic overlooks. Crissy Field offers a picturesque waterfront promenade with stunning views of the Golden Gate Bridge, while Baker Beach provides a tranquil spot for sunbathing and picnicking. The recently developed Presidio Tunnel Tops features expansive lawns, gardens, and a nature play area, making it a perfect destination for families.  ￼ ￼
Cultural and Artistic Endeavors
Art enthusiasts will appreciate the Presidio’s commitment to integrating art within its natural landscape. Notably, British artist Andy Goldsworthy’s installations, such as “Wood Line,” seamlessly blend with the environment, inviting contemplation and exploration.  The Presidio Officers’ Club houses exhibitions that delve into the area’s rich history, from its indigenous roots to its military significance, offering visitors a comprehensive understanding of its evolution.  ￼ ￼ ￼
Culinary Delights and Accommodations
After a day of exploration, visitors can indulge in a variety of dining options within the Presidio. From casual cafes to refined restaurants, there’s something to satisfy every palate. For those wishing to extend their stay, the Lodge at the Presidio offers comfortable accommodations with views of the Golden Gate Bridge, blending modern amenities with historical charm.  ￼
Accessibility and Visitor Information
The Presidio is easily accessible via public transportation, with the free PresidiGo Shuttle providing convenient routes throughout the park. The Presidio Visitor Center, open daily from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., serves as an excellent starting point, offering maps, exhibits, and knowledgeable staff to assist with trip planning.  ￼ ￼
Conclusion
The Presidio stands as a remarkable fusion of history, nature, and culture, offering a multifaceted experience for all who visit. Whether you’re a history buff, nature lover, or art enthusiast, this urban oasis provides a refreshing and enriching escape within San Francisco.

top_reviews.content:
My partner and I chose to rent the Temescal Lake Beach House for 8 hours for our wedding and are so happy with our choice! The venue was beautiful and the surroundings are so gorgeous we didn’t bring any flowers at all. The building inside is clean and friendly, big enough to comfortably sit our group of around 55 people (8 round tables of 6 -7 people) as well as a rectangular table each for drinks, the buffet, cake, and gifts. We brought some small decorations for the tables and to hang off the already existing wall hooks, but didn’t need any additional lighting or big decor to make the space feel inviting.
The venue has a list of approved caterers to choose from, and our caterer did all the unlocking and loading in, set-up, and take down so the process was pretty easy for us and a few of our family members who helped with decorating.

The space feels serene and quiet as the courtyard is tucked away in the trees on one side of the lake, so even with families on the beach, the venue felt private.
The pricing felt very reasonable compared to other local venues, and we love support the East Bay Regional Parks!
We would absolutely choose this venue again for its beautiful interior, stunning patio, and surrounding nature.

Parking was easy and the small lot close by was big enough for most of the guests, and the larger parking lot was not too far of a walk away.

Excellent venue for intimate celebrations with close family and friends.

10/10 would highly recommend!

2 rooms, patio, bathrooms and prep area for events. Downstairs has changing rooms for the beach.

Lots of foot traffic in the area from hikers, schoolchildren and nannies with infants.

The view is charming and a walk around the lake is short and pleasant.

We used Culinary Excellence and they were great! There is not a full kitchen on-site though so they were cooking in a tent out in the parking area. This venue allows beer & wine only, no liquor. The interior and exterior are nice enough on their own so we really didn't need to decorate very much to make it look nice. It's a very nice property considering the low cost to rent.
Temescal Beach House is an awesome venue! We're wedding photographers and have had a great experience here. Highly recommend it :).

Come to this restaurant!

We came in without a reservation - so they were a little unsure where to put us at first (hence 4 service stars), but the service and everything else after were excellent!

For 5 people we ordered the larger mazze platter and 2 additional dishes, all three kitchen “main” dishes, and all three desserts. We shared everything family style and it was the perfect amount (if not a little more). 4 of 5 of us got wine experiences, all the wine was unique and went well with the food.

The flavors were incredible!
Our favorites were the platter, the beef kitchen main, and the saffron yogurt dessert. But honestly everything was great! You can’t go wrong, just depends on what you like.
Go and enjoy!

I went to see The Lifespan of a Fact  3 days after seeing Morher Road at the Berkeley Rep… right next door. Mother Road was like Theatre 2.0 while the Aurora Theatre performance was like Theatre 3.0…
theatre elevated!

Everything you want non-musical  live theatre to be (btw Mother Road had a smattering of non memorable music)

But the contrast of the experience made it clear why I left Mother Road at intermission…. And was (in contrast) on the edge of my seat the entire “Lifespan of a Fact” performance

Despite the fact that often the audience is 3 feet from the actors on “stage” at the Aurora …the performances felt real …like you were a fly on the wall …and this was really happening

And like real life…the conflicts don’t get all buttoned up…there is no formula. There are life-like dilemmas with no clear answer… even from the final lines in the final scene

Will I go to a Berkeley rep show again? … prob…
to see a musical…
because there’s a time and place for a feel-good, predictable, formulaic show that teaches a clear inspirational lesson.

But if you want theatre that perks you up and offers a reframing of a society you THINK you understood… stick to the Aurora theatre…and by all means see The Lifespan of a Fact.
Directing, lighting, acting, overall cleverness, realism of script
…and humor under stress!

A+++

Great Notion Brewery: Berkeley's Explosion of Flavor and Innovation

Our insatiable thirst for exciting breweries and unique beers led us to Great Notion Brewery in Berkeley, and let me tell you, it was a revelation. Great Notion truly lives up to its name. Their beers are unlike anything you've ever experienced – bursting with flavor, pushing boundaries, and offering something truly special for every taste bud.

Convenience and Comfort: A Smooth Start to Your Adventure

Finding parking in Berkeley can sometimes be a hassle, but Great Notion makes things easy. They offer decent street parking options, and for those who prefer a contactless experience, pay-by-phone parking is readily available. Once you've secured your spot, head inside for a comfortable and relaxing atmosphere. The seating is described as "decent," suggesting a good mix of tables and chairs to accommodate groups of all sizes.

The MVP Hall of Fame: Electric Headband, Over Ripe Fruit, and More!

Now, let's dive into the main event – the incredible beers!  Great Notion boasts a wide range of styles, but your review highlights a few true champions:

Electric Headband (MVP): I can  describe this beer as "to die for" with its vibrant blue color and surprising blue raspberry flavor. A beer this unique deserves a visit on its own!

Over Ripe Fruit in the Can (MVP): This "mango heaven" sounds like a smoothie lover's dream come true. It's a testament to Great Notion's innovative spirit and their ability to create truly delicious and unexpected flavor combinations.

Munchies: This imperial stout takes the cake for intriguing ingredients. Combining pretzels, potato chips, and peanut butter might seem strange on paper, but a "complex" and "soulful" taste hints at a truly unique and satisfying experience.

GR 75: This red tart ale sounds like a delightful burst of tropical fruit flavors. I can mention notes of guava and raspberry, making it a perfect choice for those who enjoy a refreshing and slightly sour brew.

RIPE: As an IPA lover, my declaration that this is "one of the best IPAs I've ever tasted" is high praise indeed. It suggests a perfectly balanced and flavorful IPA that will leave any hop-head happy.

A Must-Visit for Beer Adventurers and Traditionalists Alike

Great Notion Brewery caters to all palates. Whether you're a seasoned craft beer enthusiast seeking the next boundary-pushing brew, or a casual drinker looking for something unique and delicious, Great Notion has something for you. They even offer non-alcoholic options, like the "Black Cherry Cream Soda" – creamy, different, and perfect for those who want to enjoy the experience without the alcohol.

This place is a true gem, and with so many incredible beers on tap (including the "Beer Has No Name" hazy IPA), it's no surprise id plan to return for more.

google.description: Small 1-room museum in an adult shop tracing the history of the sex toy from the 19th century.

top_reviews.content: So, my friend and I visited this museum for shits and giggles, but honestly, we were not disappointed. This place had one room full of displays and information on the history of the creation of the vibrator, its origins, and its development throughout the centuries. It was clean, organized, and easy to interact with some of the displays. Plus, it's free and open to the public during store hours, so why not? It's a nice little bonus to the adult shop here, and I give the place two thumbs up!

The museum doesn’t have a store front. It’s inside of the Good Vibrations Store. Friendly staff. They will direct you to the room. So educational, and the staff is able to answer questions if you have any. Awesome displays and graphs.

Great experience at the whole location. The museum was a large room at the back of the store that told the history well. Loved having educators running the shop so questions were easy to ask and I was comfortable the whole time. Worth the stop.

2024 EDIT AT END.

Very informative and fun and wild at times. It's a small room in the back of the store, so more of an exhibit than a museum. 20-30 minutes to fully look at everything. Should probably call ahead because it seems like the hours can sometimes be weird.

In order to visit the museum, you need a photo ID (not sure what the age restriction was, though) and you need to be comfortable walking through a store full of sex toys and related merchandise, but if you're thinking of visiting the Antique Vibrator Store, you're probably already there.

EDIT: I've been meaning to edit this for months since I learned that the narrative from Rachel Maines that the museum supports is actually a myth. A lot of the history in the museum is still legit and the vibrators in the museum are certainly real and still very cool, but I hope that the museum provides more clarity on this point (rating switched from 5 to 3 stars for now). As another sex historian Hallie Lieberman notes in a 2020 article for the NY Times,

"The myth can be traced to Rachel Maines’s 1999 book “Technology of Orgasm” (she wrote some earlier articles, but the book is what put this version of the vibrator’s history on the map). Published by Johns Hopkins University Press, “Technology” seemed like a well-researched scholarly book, with 465 citations and a plethora of primary sources, some in Greek and Latin; the problem is that none of them actually supported this story. (Ms. Maines has said she put forth her version as an “interesting hypothesis” and never intended it to be seen as established fact.) Nonetheless, the idea caught on and spread."

Here's a citation for the scholarly article Liberman co-wrote to debunk the myth:

Lieberman, Hallie and Eric Schatzberg, "A Failure of Academic Quality Control: The Technology of
Orgasm." Journal of Positive Sexuality 4, no. 2 (2018): 24-47.

EDIT 2: Sadly we're down to 2 stars till hopefully it's updated. Upon finally editing this review I read the entire academic article from the Journal of Positive Sexuality mentioned above, and it turns out that a lot more of the historical timeline in the museum (which I have pictures of from a year ago) are misleading in the same way that Rachel Maines's use of those "sources" were misleading (the article touches on Galen, Forestus, Highmore, and Taylor). The museum's founder (Joani Blank) is even referenced in the article for her partial critique of the myth.

More importantly, I thought that the account in the academic article about how easily Maines's book was accepted and used in academics, law, and pop culture (not to mention vibrator museums), is far more interesting than the false narrative Maines put forth. I would readily watch that movie over the various films made about this vibrational myth.
Love how this museum is a combination of education and imagination. Learned a lot of interesting information of vibrators🥵

top_reviews.content: We hired Shadelands Ranch for our wedding. Such an incredible venue. Very spacious, naturally beautiful (lots of greenery and flowers on site), good weather, amazing staff (we worked with Christine and she was a pleasure). Such a delightful tour with a lovely gentleman and lady as our guides. I learned so much about Walnut Creek’s history and life in the 1890s–1920s. The display of old-time tools and icons was especially captivating, quiet reminders of how people once lived. A truly worthwhile stop

Having our wedding at Shadelands Historical Ranch and Museum was amazing. The venue itself is gorgeous, with incredible colors from the emerald lawn and giant trees to the explosion of roses around the gazebo! Our wedding was in May and all the flowers were in bloom, it was like a page from a storybook with hummingbirds and butterflies out and about enjoying the day too. Our guests kept raving about how beautiful and picturesque it was.

Christine and Jackie made it a very stress-free experience. We had a morning wedding with a group of about 80 guests, along with a buffet table, mobile barista, DJ and sound system, and plenty of room for our three photographers to easily maneuver to get their shots. (Will update later with some professional photos when those arrive!) The venue provides chairs and various sizes of tables all arranged to your liking, we requested that the lawn seating be set up for the ceremony and for the tables to be set up around the edge of the patio area and they had everything set up exactly how we envisioned, so all we had to do was come in and decorate. Event insurance is required, along with multiple contacts on hand. Contract and rates are very straightforward. While the magnificent trees cover a large portion of the grassy area, would recommend bringing your own canopies with weights if you plan to set up tables within the paved area. Overall a grand experience with the venue and welcoming staff.

The Shadelands Ranch House was the perfect venue for our wedding. After issues with our original venue, and being a little over 2 months out from our wedding, Shadelands luckily had a cancellation for our wedding day and we were able to fully move over and have our wedding there. We worked with Jackie leading up to the wedding. She was so accommodating and helpful with trying to make our vision come to life. She allowed us to come see the venue a few times before the wedding to make sure we knew where everything would be and how it would look day of. They also provided all tables and chairs, and had everything set up before our allotted rental time. The venue itself is beautiful and has many trees, the gazebo, flowers, and the amazing house. The venue is fully outdoors and our wedding day was much hotter than expected for an October wedding. However, they allowed us to set up fans and a portable air conditioner in the bridal suite to help with the heat. They provided a venue coordinator who was there day of to make sure everything was set up correctly and taken down at the end of the night. They also had a pumpkin patch going on in front of the house that they redirected traffic for and gave all the kids at our wedding tickets to go get their own pumpkins. I really liked the idea of this and especially the mission of the non-profit. I thought it was such a cool vibe, shoes off, living room hangout. But the sound just wasn't there.

If those two things were addressed I would definitely be back and be a part of their program.

I really wanted to enjoy the time I spent here listening to Frank Ocean's Channel Orange but felt the listening experience was lackluster overall. The back left speaker was considerably louder than the rest and I did not feel immersed really. I've had better audio experiences in households with modest equipment at best. It basically ended up being less comfortable and less impressive than just listening to the album at home with headphones.

Writing specifically about the EnvelopSF surround audio course for young people - OUTSTANDING. My kid’s only issue was that the course had an end date at all, would’ve happily kept coming indefinitely.

The ambience was very cool, however the sound was extremely disappointing. With all those speakers surrounding the space, I expected to be “enveloped” in sound. However, out of all the speakers they only had one in the back of the room playing. I listened to the same album on my drive back home & it sounded so much better. For $30/ticket, I would expect to have a great listening experience and be surrounded by the sound. The music needs to be louder & all the speakers should be on as was advertised. I could hardly hear it! For any big music or sound enthusiasts, i would not recommend this experience. I was so excited to listen to my favorite album & am so disappointed :(

Really excellent concept and overall a great listening experience - though I have a few hopefully constructive criticisms. I went for the first and so far only time for a listening session: Boards of Canada: Music Has The Right To Children. This is an awesome album with lots of "space" even in the stereo mix, and it was amazing to hear in a dark room with no distractions (I'm reminded of Pauline Oliveros writing on "deep listening" and the legacy of the San Francisco Tape Music Center). I love the meditative vibe and the cash bar including tea, beer, seltzers, etc. - I wasn't bothered by anyone getting up for a refill.

I have a 5.1 setup at home and have listened to a handful of albums mixed for surround sound - and I would love to hear one of these on the Envelop setup. It seems that for albums that do not have a surround sound mix, the Envelop staff/volunteers/artists will create a custom "patch" for spatializing the audio and expanding the sound field to their 32 speaker setup (8 towers with 3 speakers stacked, 4 speakers overhead, and 4 subwoofers). This was pretty effective even though I was sitting towards the perimeter and right next to one of the 8 main towers, I could head things subtly moving around, and felt suitably immersed beyond what I'd expect from a stereo mix. I would recommend that Envelop start adding info about the specific mix to their event pages, for those who care - it would be nice to know if the album being presented was mixed for quadraphonic, 5.1 surround, 7.1, atmos, etc, or if the spatialization is being done by the Envelop folks. (I would love to hear some quad vinyl on this setup!)

Some minor complaints - it's a little crowded in there and the little folding seats are not very comfortable. I'm sure they have the capacity dialed in for the economics of this sort of thing, but I would have preferred beanbag chairs or scattered cushions / foam shapes and about half the number of attendees. And a little more air movement would have been nice (no shoes!) but not if fans would have to compete with the music - a tough problem to solve.

Overall, a great experience and I'm hoping to go back again while on this and future visits to SF!

It was empty when I went in but after ordering, I notice most people picking up their items to go.  So while this place doesn’t seem like a spot to hang out and work out of (even though there are counter seatings facing the window), it seems more of a take out/delivery kind of spot.

I spoke to Russel, who was very helpful with my order, suggest that next time if I wanted any of the pandan drinks, I’d have to order early as they sell out.  Perhaps I should have gotten one right then and there but I needed my caffeine fix, so I got their most popular coffee drink:

HANOI EGG COFFEE - $8
Vietnamese coffee topped with their specialty egg cream.
I rarely see any egg coffee so I knew this was my chance!  Before mixing the egg cream, I appreciate how this literally tastes like iced Vietnamese coffee—bold and strong coffee flavor, with the rich and sweet taste from the condensed milk.  Add that custard-like topping made it even better—yay protein!  I appreciate that this comes as a hot beverage too as an option!

I love that they have a nice selection of unique pastries, but it seems they have already sold out on some items.  So here’s what I got to try:

MOCHI BITES - $4 each
I got both available flavors: BLACK SESAME and THAI TEA.  They both have a wonderful chewy texture that I expect in a mochi muffin, and you really taste the flavors.  I highly recommend!

PANDAN COCONUT CROISSANT - $6
So nice of them to offer to heat it up.  This flaky pastry has a pandan with shredded coconut filling..which if you are like me, I don’t care for anything coconut in shredded form.  But I’m such a sucker for anything with pandan, haha.  Overall not bad though!

UBE POUND CAKE - $5.50
This tiny pound cake didn’t have much of an ube flavor, but it ain’t dry!  It was moist and not too sweet.  It was thoroughly enjoyed!

I really hope to come back and try their other pastries and drink selections.  I love how they decorated their shop, have cool merch to sell, and and appreciate how personal they made my first visit here.  Thanks so much House of Phin, happy 2 year anniversary!

Best Vietnamese coffee we’ve been able to find in Oakland!! Also beats the few we’ve been to in SF. We tried their House of Phin Coffee and Hanoi Egg Coffee and absolutely loved it! :)
Even though it’s in a shady-looking part of town, it’s really nice inside.

This is the best Vietnamese coffee shop that my sister and I have ever tried!! We were visiting our brother and his girlfriend for vacation and this was our favorite coffee stop! Definitely going to visit again!!❤️

Excellent crafted coffees, matchas and teas. The coffees are drip and made to order, the matcha is excellent. Had some pastries and they’re tasty as well but the drinks are the signature. Nice, friendly workers.

The inside is very cute but limited seating, seems like it’s much more of a to-go place. It’s kind of easy to miss outside so look for its yellow awning neighbor.

I usually walk here but did drive once and found parking rather challenging as it’s a tight one lane street. If you see a spot, grab it or park up the street past the shop. But don’t let parking deter you from these fantastic drinks.

Wonderful customer service from start to finish. Everyone was warm, attentive, and made me feel welcome right away. When I ordered my drink, they even asked if I wanted Valentine’s flowers added on top, which was such an adorable and thoughtful touch. I passed, but it made the experience feel personal and kind. My drink was excellent, and the level of care they showed made the whole visit memorable. I’ll happily be back. ❤️

I really enjoyed my time visiting the treasure Island museum. I love the murals on the wall and the art deco lobby. The buildings architecture is beautiful and this place is definitely worth a stop. The museum is great and the goals bar distillery is really nice and very appealing aesthetically. Can’t wait to visit again soon.

The museum presently features a small but interesting display of Treasure Island history. The real attraction is the magnificent building from the 1939/40 fair. A magnificent moderne structure with original statuary from the fair on display out front. The building stood in for the Berlin Airport in Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade. The views of SF are terrific. The island can be easily reached by an 8 minute ferry ride from the Ferry Building for $5. There is a very nice beach near the museum and a good lunch with an incredible view is available from the Mersea restaurant nearby. Well worth a trip out on the bay.

Part of the museum is under renovation.  I hope to return and update my review after it's completed. Their history of Treasure Island exhibit (their only exhibit) takes 15 minutes to 1 hour.
The Art Deco building itself is interesting. As is the large mural. We almost missed the Art Deco sculptures out front.
I didn’t get to see the inside of the museum, so I can’t say much about that — but one thing’s for sure: it’s a night view gem! Great spot for the view!

top_reviews.content: BOMB! The reviews speak for themselves, the food was incredible and Kahlil is a very nice and humble man. Definitely will be coming back🔥

I was around this area for the first time since I was visiting UCSF Pride Hall.

It was around lunch time and I wanted to grab some coffee and Luna’s appeared on the search.

I read on the Google reviews that their chicken teriyaki sandwich was excellent so I made up my mind to see what was the hub bub.

I enter the little cafe and I see it’s small but also quaint with its diner design. I meet one of the owners Khalil and he impressed me with his patience and hospitality.

I ordered the chicken teriyaki sandwich meal with a coffee for a drink.

The coffee was ok. Wasn’t coffee connoisseur levels of excellence but it got my cravings out of the way and it was nice to get oatmilk with it as a complimentary addition.

The fries were EXCELLENT with their flavor and crunch. The texture was crispy on the outside and light and fluffy on the inside. The amount of oil used was just right to give the fries more flavor and not a greasy texture. The addition of salt and pepper added flavor to the fries.

Now for the big moment—chicken teriyaki sandwich. I got it with every complementary sandwich topping Luna’s offers and on a Dutch crunch bread. 1) I like Dutch crunch so I already had a good feeling about it. 2) I would have never guessed the toppings on the sandwich would work so well together with the chicken teriyaki. You either would be tasting the flavors of the toppings or you’d get a nice light chicken teriyaki flavor. Bonus is if you’re into that charred burnt grill end flavor (I am), you will pick up some of those notes.

I left Luna’s that day feeling energized before my walk to work and if I find myself in the area hungry, I’ll be sure to stop by again. Not to mention, it was pretty heartwarming to see regulars in the neighborhood come and go in and out of the cafe. Just shows me that Luna’s has made itself a valuable place in the neighborhood.
Working at Zuckerberg I stopped in for a quick bite they have the cute sandwich boards and a delicious pastrami “made to order perfection!” So glad I came in 🤤

I really wasn’t expecting much from this place when I first walked in. However, the price for coffee is a great deal! yummy food, owners are super nice. good place to sit and watch everyone and everything go by.

top_reviews.content: The Naval Air Museum was a surprising delight; particularly for me in view of my special interest in the pioneering age of flying boats. In fact I had built a balsa model of the China Clipper from scratch without knowing much of the history. And I had no idea the Museum had a special section for the Pan Am clippers, so you can imagine my surprise when I recognised it! The other oustanding features of the museum include aircraft and ship models, and a terrific library with a fascinating section of unique donated photos. Yet it is the eagerness of the staff that makes the difference. And if you have a penchant for clippers it is terrific - the RC China Clipper is priceless!

This is a treasure hidden in plain sight. Knowing history helps make more informed decisions. War isn’t religious or political, it’s power and control that the dark elite seek via corrupt & coercive fear based manipulation.

The people who “work” here are retired members of the public who have a love for the history of the country and more so, for military history.

I met Bob, Ellen and another whose name I didn’t catch. Ellen and I connected deeply in the library, one of my favorite places to hang out. Apparently her favorite place too. She’s written two books, one on the Armenian genocide, taught at the unified school district in SF for over 40 years.

Elders are keepers of knowledge and stories are meant for the masses to digest and make better choices.

A really nice museum about WWI, WWII, and history of the Alameda Naval Air Station. This museum has many nice collections.
This museum is independently run by a group of senior volunteers who previously worked at the Navel Air Station. The volunteers are really nice and knowledgeable. I got the beef empanada, which tasted really hearty and rich. The outside texture was flaky and golden. The accompanying chimichurri sauce paired well with it.

The drink menu is solid. I got the bombom latte is delicious and rich, and just the right amount of sweetness, not too sweet. It was also huge for the price. They have non-dairy alternatives like oat milk and almond milk.

The people working here really care about good food and drinks, and are happy to explain what anything on the menu is (like the orange latte, which is orange juice with a shot of espresso - I'd never had it, though the guy working there said people love it). The pink tree, floral and glitter walls, local art, and whole atmosphere is such a nice vibe. There's free Wi-Fi as well in case you're looking to study or get some work done. There's plenty of good seating.

Note that you get a discount if you pay in cash. Also, parking in the area isn't great because of the proximity to Balboa Park BART. I came on a Sunday and I had to park and walk two blocks.

Latte: The coffee itself was great, but I felt the milk foam wasn’t thick enough. I hope next time I can get more velvety foam!

Overall, this is a nice spot to check out if you’re passing by. It’s a great way to experience Peruvian coffee and appreciate the owner’s unique taste in furniture and decorations!👌🏻

Racist. I'm deeply disappointed by what happened here. I came in, ordered tequila, 2 ciders, paid for it, and closed my tab. I then stepped just outside to sit down finish the last bit of one of the ciders - something I've seen people do countless times in my life all around this city and the world. A few minutes later, when I tried to return to toss it in the trash, I was told by the same white bartender who served me that I had STOLEN the drink and was now banned from the bar.

Let me be clear: I paid for the drink. I was calm and respectful. There was no reason to escalate the situation, and certainly no reason to accuse me of theft. The fact that I, a Black man, was immediately assumed to be stealing despite doing nothing wrong speaks volumes.

To make matters worse, I was on the phone at the time with someone who overheard the entire exchange--and even they commented on how much disrespect and contempt was in her voice when she said it. That kind of condescension and accusatory tone was just unprofessional.

Instead of a simple heads-up about a policy (which, by the way, was never made clear), I was criminalized. Loudly. Publicly in front of someone else. Without hesitation. It was humiliating, infuriating, and heartbreaking to experience this in a city I've called home for 30 years.

To those who run this bar: If your staff can't enforce rules without racial assumptions or power trips, the problem isn't the policy--it's the people.

I won't be back.

Update: The owner’s public response below falsely accuses me of lying, which only proves my point about their hostility and lack of professionalism.

top_reviews.content:
My husband and I just spent two weeks visiting Oakland and we discovered Gelato Firenza (near Grand Lake Theate) one week into our trip. Once we did we made a special trip there every day, and one day even went twice! It’s the best gelato we’ve tasted anywhere, and we’ve been all over.

We first had gelato 40 years ago in Rome and were delighted as it became increasingly popular all over the world. We’ve tried it in many places, but this is our favorite.

We learned that it’s all natural, no additives, and made on the premises daily by the owner, who is so devoted to getting the flavors just right that she often spends four or more days perfecting them.

We love the fact that it’s not overly sweet, so you can really taste the underlying flavors (and feel good about it having less sugar). They’re very generous about allowing you to taste before ordering, and the prices are excellent.

Our favorites were: hazelnut, salted caramel, strawberry and rose (which was so unique and delicious!) Others we tasted and loved included Earl Grey, Matcha, coconut, almond, Dulce de Leche, and cookies and cream, but every flavor we tried was truly delicious.

For reference I have only written two other reviews in my life: one about my dog’s veterinarian, and one about a hotel in Thailand. But this gelato is so special and the owner so delightful I had to pass the word on.

We can’t wait to return to the Bay Area for more.

I always pass by so was tempted to try today just because i am on a gelato spree since the hot weekend.

Would love to come back and try more flavors.

Accessibility****This easy to get to with a wheel chair. Street parking can be difficult but you can park in the Trader Joes parking lot.

Cost***average.

Service**The person behind the mask serving the ice cream felt robotic, and she didn't seem interested in relating to me. She was not friendly.  When I asked about the Gelato, she just pointed to the sign.

top_reviews.content:
One of the nicest indoor pickleball facilities I’ve been to — and I don’t say that lightly.

The moment you walk in, the vibe hits you. It’s artsy, clean, and cozy in a way that lowkey feels like how I’d want my own home to be. Everything feels intentional and well thought out, not just thrown together to be “another court.”

Beyond the courts, the lounge area is a huge plus. Comfy seating, fast Wi-Fi, big-screen TVs, and a game room with classics and board games make it easy to hang around before or after playing. This spot is clearly built for community, not just quick games and dip.

They’ve also got a fitness studio, sauna, and a kitchen + wine bar, which makes it perfect for events, corporate outings, or just a full-on social hang. Located in the heart of Oakland (on the better side), and it was great running into some familiar faces while our team toured the space.

Hours are super convenient (8am–10pm daily), pricing is straightforward for both court bookings and open play, and the overall experience feels premium without being stuffy.

If you’re looking for Oakland’s indoor pickleball social club — this is it. Courts, vibes, and community all in one place. Would 100% come back.

We LOVE this place! It’s become part of our regular routine - rain hail or shine, it’s always happening here. It’s SO great that we can play year round in comfort and it doesn’t cost the earth. The gym is a huge bonus - it’s got everything you need, plus the sauna and a lovely shower room to freshen up when we squeeze in a game or 2 and a workout before work. It’s genius that they have great coffee and breakfast options and loads of secure parking - makes our commute in so easy. We’ve yet to attend one of their wine tastings, but we hear great things from other regulars. We were happy that you don’t have to be a member, especially if you’re meeting friends there for a game or a drink. Great addition to the Oakland PB scene!

I have played at this fabulous location on four occasions. So far, everything to love about this fairly new facility. The people are very nice, friendly, helpful - I saw one hostess make a latte and bring it to the court for the individual. It is very efficient for checking in and signing up online (go to the court reserve app to sign up). You can have memberships with benefits, or in my case, I signed up for the free option, so I have access for rainy days. The decor is very nice and inviting. Several "still working crowd" came and set up their laptops to work between games! They have a yummy kale salad with delicious crispy tofu. They offer a yoga/pilates mix a few mornings a week. I do like that they only have four courts - three for play and one off to the back for lessons and clinics, play when not used. On rainy days, do plan ahead. I liked that they do not overbook - 8 signed up for one court, so we played rally scoring and kept it moving (so plan ahead on rainy days).  Overall, a definite 5 stars from me!

We hosted a team offsite at Pickle Athletics, and the experience was exceptional from start to finish. Pre-event and day of communication with their team was absolutely top-notch, making the planning seamless. From the moment we arrived, they made us feel incredibly welcome. The facility is beautiful, offering amazing courts, a great lounge, and top-tier amenities. It was the perfect blend of activity and relaxation for our group. Highly recommend them for any corporate event!

Have really been enjoying playing here! Both reserved courts and open play have been a blast. The facility is great, the employees and owner are super helpful, and most importantly the players are really friendly and fun to play with.

What Can Improve:

Pro Tips:

top_reviews.content:
Delightful breakfast sandwich spot!! I had never heard of a bakery that specializes in English muffins, but Leadbetters absolutely excels at building the most beautiful English muffin sammies. The muffins themselves are quite large and robust (perhaps 1.5x the size of a standard grocery store English muffin), and they feature your standard white or whole wheat muffins, as well as a ton of options with fun flavors infused. You can get the muffins plain or topped with just a pat of butter or jam, but they also have the most amazing selection of sandwiches. I opted for their avocado toast, which comes with a generous portion of super fresh mashed avocado, pickled onions, and sprouts. I also added on some scrambled eggs for extra protein, and they were great — super creamy, rich, and just the right amount of salt. The overall toast didn’t have a ton of flavor, but they have a few hot sauces available that really leveled up the toast. My partner got their standard breakfast sandwich with bacon, which came with the same beautifully scrambled eggs, a slice of cheddar, and layer of perfectly crispy bacon.

The staff is super friendly and very ready to answer any and all questions about their menu, and I loved the outdoor seating space. The little nooks on the sidewalk balcony were really cute and cozy, and the street was quiet enough that we weren’t disturbed during our meal but hopping enough that there was plenty of good people watching. We loved our brunch here, and I can’t wait to come back!!

Super fresh.  The best English Muffin in the City!  Egg sandwiches are fluffy and delicious but the lox sandwich is also a favorite.  Friendly and kind workers with hot and fresh Andytown coffee. Don’t get me started on how tasty the blueberry banana loaf is. 🤤 I highly recommend this Castro gem!

The peanut butter is fine (who knows if it is homemade or from a jar, though.). The banana is fine. The English Muffin is nice. The chocolate is non-existent. They forgot it! And multiple employees looked at it before they boxed it up. And this is one of their regular on-menu items!! Very disappointing.
Also ordered a cherry chocolate English Muffin with cream cheese. Again, multiple people looked at it before it got boxed up. It's a plain English Muffin and the cream cheese tastes off. There is nothing cherry or chocolate about it!! And I think they put something on it other than cream cheese and then just slathered cream cheese over it.

I would not recommend this place, I'm afraid. There was no one else waiting for orders and they were not busy at all. And they couldn't get a simple order of two English muffins right.

My friend & I have been searching for another sports bar to check out in Oakland; one that'll cover basketball & soccer in particular. There are very few bars we know of that show soccer games, but we decided to take a chance and made a reservation at Mushin to watch the El Clásico. Here is a summary of our experience today:

Ambiance - clean, classy, and feels like a party all at once with the DJ playing music in the background (mixture of 90s-00s hip-hop/R&B). The back area was reserved for a private party, which can be organized separately with staff for future social events. Plenty of TV screens throughout. It was pretty busy when we arrived at 12:45pm on a Sunday, so we were grateful for making the reservation ahead of time.

Drinks - signature cocktails were distinct from each other & delicious. I had the caipirinha & Tap Tap cocktails (only one of which I could show, because the other I lovingly consumed right away), whereas my friend had a few IPAs. Prices are standard Bay Area-wise ($5-6 for beers, $10-15 for cocktails)

Food - good, but limited. They do have a brunch menu which is separate from another I've seen online. Fried chicken & waffles were nice. If you're extremely hungry, I'd recommend eating elsewhere beforehand, as portions are small-medium at best.

Service -  the staff were very amicable and willing to accommodate our needs, whether it be changing the channels to our requested game, making friendly banter, or checking in on us to make sure everything was met despite how busy it was.

Overall, our time here was fantastic! Needless to say, I will be coming back here again and bringing along other friends to share the same experience. But also because I'm awfully curious about this avocado margarita... Cheers!

top_reviews.content: I ordered two croissants here and asked about filling my reusable water bottle, but the cafe does not refill reusable bottles or provide water cups. But the sign framing this as “supporting our small business” felt off to me. For a cafe inside a transit station, it would be much more customer friendly and *environmentally reasonable* to offer tap water to paying customers, even if it is in a limited or self serve way. The croissant was okay, but this sign left a less than positive impression.

BADM has transformed significantly since its inception. Initially, it may not have been a five-star experience – it seemed somewhat limited in size, and children could breeze through the exhibits rather quickly. Fast forward to now, it’s a splendid destination for children, ideally those under 7 or 8 years old, and is particularly wonderful for toddlers. We have maintained our membership for several consecutive years, finding it to be an excellent value; it practically pays for itself after just a couple of visits. My children are 5 and 7, and while we’re undecided on renewing our membership next year, the recent park expansions, new science buildings, and engaging interactive stations continue to captivate them.
