top_reviews.content:
The grand re-opening was Saturday, Sunday, January 17, 18, 2026. Nicely done, we spent 1.5 hours with both 1st and 4th graders engaged in art or exploring exhibits and preschool play area.

This is not open every day so check official web site for times open.

There is excellent information on various aspects of Lake Merritt, as the oldest bird refuge in the U.S.

Most exhibits are "no touch" but items are not inside cases, so keep your kids close and read signs. One rock exhibit invites touch, but sign is flat on high shelf, so not noticeable. The rest of open display cases have signs saying "do not touch" but visually and informationally are very well done.  I imagine this may change, if public does not take care of exhibits, will try to update review next time we visit.

The 1st grader loved the egg comparison display, of eggs from humming bird, up to osterich size. She was drawing eggs and comparing them, or using art supplies on table to color or add details. The burrowing owl exhibit was my favorite.

The various stuffed birds along the top display shelves, representing the Lake Merritt bird population, had a corresponding identity list.  Lots of people stopped to compare and find the birds on display.

They have a baby/preschool program open to public twice a week,at specific times, with a $5.00 supply fee that looks inviting and a great bargain for parents who loves interactive activities to do WITH your little one.

I remember this center from my children and grand children visiting decades ago, it has been updated and refreshed, especially the preschool are which is inviting and well stocked. We peeked in the cloth boxes on the shelves with various toys. Our favorite was the table with chairs, and in the center was built in box of bones & shells to touch, hold, view in the built-in magnifying glasses in table.

My son remembered it as "Tired". It is nicely refreshed and relevant to today's world.

Incredibly poor management of the Bird Yard by Lake Merritt. No fresh water for the migratory birds. There are literally signs posted saying they need the fresh water and Rotary Nature center hasn't done anything to fix the problem.

I reached out to them several times and offered to help and volunteer and never received a response.

People are not doing their jobs we pay out of our taxes for them to do.

It’s really sad how they let things go over the years. There basically is no sanctuary left. All the plants and water have dried up and died. You can tell that they’re not using fountains or sprinklers to keep the sanctuary going, resulting in all the wild life to disappear.  Homeless camps and garbage surround the sides of the center and the center itself isn’t even open for the public to view its mini museum or to buy bird seeds. Not to mention the water levels of lake Merritt have gone down significantly and the islands located on the lake where some birds reside are dried up and dead. It’s a shame with how expensive it is to live in that area that no money is going into the upkeep of that historical area. Shame on Oakland, and shame on its previous and recent mayors for allowing it to get to that point. There’s plenty of money to keep building luxury apartments that no one can afford to live in though.

The Rotary Nature Center is an awesome place to take little kids. It's small and a little rough around the edges, but kids could care less. There's a live snake and tarantula. They also have bees and others stuffed creatures.

They also have different nature programs, some restricted to those 18+, and volunteer opportunities.

The best place to watch the birds in the nature preserve is right next door. The center sells bird food for a dollar.
Very nice to learn about animals and nature

La Boulangerie (formerly La Boulange) has been a Bay Area stable since 1996. The cafe bakery was founded by Pascal Rigo and began on Fillmore Street in San Francisco with the mission to offer delicious food at an affordable price. Fast forward to today, La Boulangerie has multiple locations across San Francisco and the greater Bay Area, offering a selection of breads, sweet and savory croissants, and beverages to the public. This new location is located in the Marina District inside ERIA. It can be a bit challenging to find parking; however, the location is very accessible via public transit.

Looking for a quick bite to eat, I selected their apple chausson and a large iced americano.

I don't pretend to be an expert in French pastry; however, I do remember taking a short introductory French class in seventh grade, where I was introduced to the wonders of laminated pastry. During class, our teacher offered us the opportunity to order some pastries from a local bakery to enjoy in class as part of the cultural immersion. I selected the chausson aux pommes (or apple chausson) and since then I've adored this pastry. For those who don't know, an apple chausson is essentially a French apple turn over made from laminated puff pastry, folded into a half-moon shape, and filled with sweet apple compote.

La Boulangerie certainly lives up to their promise - the apple chausson was delicious. The pastry was light, airy, and flake (just as a good laminated pastry should be), with a delectable apple compote filling. The large americano was a great pick-me-up that I enjoyed as I strolled around the neighborhood on this particularly sunny day (beautiful weather for SF).

If you're already a fan of La Boulangerie, then you'll be pleased to explore this new location of theirs!

google.address: 2337 Derby St, Berkeley, CA 94705, United States

top_reviews.content:
A Diorama Museum for the Commons: Public Art on Derby Street
Tucked along Derby Street in Berkeley, you'll find an extraordinary example of art as civic gift—a collection of handcrafted diorama boxes, each a self-contained world visible through small windows. The "Diorama Museum," as one box announces, presents an astonishing range of tableaux: healthy and bleached coral reefs (complete with didactic labels), prehistoric scenes with dinosaurs browsing among ferns, protest vignettes proclaiming "RESIST NOW!", a glittering proclamation of "THEIA'S FATE," folk art compositions with intricate patterns, and even a rendering of Monterey's Cannery Row viewed through a vintage television frame.
What elevates this beyond mere decoration is the deliberate philosophical stance it embodies. These works aren't gated behind museum admission or gallery exclusivity—they exist in the liminal space between private property and public street, offered freely to anyone who walks by. The artist-family (whom I had the privilege of meeting) maintains these pieces for strangers, for neighbors, for the occasional photographer, asking nothing in return. This is art as democratic practice, as radical generosity.
The craftsmanship reveals hours of labor: layered paper constructions, carefully positioned miniatures, painted backdrops, natural materials, found objects transformed. Each diorama invites sustained looking, rewards attention with detail. They speak to environmental concern, political engagement, local history, natural wonder, and pure aesthetic play.
In an era of increasing privatization and digital atomization, these small wooden boxes mounted on posts represent something increasingly rare: art made deliberately, joyfully, for the commons. They remind us that public space can still be a site of encounter, beauty, and shared humanity—if we choose to make it so.
A delightful little public installation, well worth a stop to add some brightness to your day!

top_reviews.content:
AMAZING SELECTION OF RETRO GAMES! My 6 year old daughter really enjoyed the Pinball machine which made me very proud to have the chance to introduce her to classic games from my childhood.
I’d like to give a special shout out to Evie with the pink hair. She was very kind and helped us fix the Pin Bot game when the ball got stuck. She’s very energetic with the kids and adds more fun into the space. I’ll definitely be coming back!

A couple of weeks ago I had my daughter’s 8th birthday party here! Rick the owner and his staff were wonderful to work with from the start of planning to day of festivities. This is the perfect venue for a small party, I had about 30 guests and it didn’t feel crowded at all. The kids had fun with the 70 minutes of game play before moving into the party room, but I think it was the adults that had the most fun, as these are the arcade games we all grew up with! HA! Once the game play is over, the party like mentioned moves into the party room which is a great size. I had the new Shore Shack restaurant in Rockaway cater the party, which was perfect!

Important things to note:  I did bring everything from balloons, table cloths, party plates and napkins, a cooler for canned beverages. This isn’t a typical party play place where a lot of this stuff is provided for you, but on the day of Rick greeted us at my car with a rolling cart for all the party stuff which was amazing and so helpful. He was able to store the stuff in a back hallway while the other party was happening (I booked the 12:30 time slot)  I was able to do a site visit before I booked Replay and Rick and Atti answered all my questions.

There is a refrigerator and freezer to store cold items and a corner nook with counter space too, it was the perfect spot to store the cake.

Oh and the little outdoor seated patio area was a great hit too! I added some floral decorations on the tables to add some color but that’s just me doing the most. HA!  I’m so happy this place is here in Pacifica!

I was born in 1979. I have dreamed of a place like this opening close to home. I played several games which I remember from back in the day, and two hands full of games which I do not remember. I had a blast.

The prices for daily and monthly use are incredibly fair. There are snack and beverages available. The vibe was all good. I wish this business the very best in health and longevity. The “party room” option is wonderful  and simple—the business “opens” for the party a few hours before regular business resumes.

There is one machine that has 15+ games programmed into it.

Please visit this location and keep Replay active!

Special thank you to the owners for making the dream come true.

Pics to follow soon-I had too much fun playing to snap photos.

Great arcade and excellent event space.

The arcade isn't huge but it's packed with old favorites. There's a comfortable outdoor space between the arcade and event room with cushy seating to enjoy the fresh air. The event room is well-lit and has a small kitchenette with sink, small counter and fridge. The room itself has plenty of armchairs and dining tables that were arranged for the baby shower as one large rectangular table that was could have accommodated about 20 people. There's also a roomy patio with direct access to the parking lot. A hall with bathrooms between the arcade and event room (in case you don't want to walk through the outdoor space) is shared with the UPS store and very clean.

Replay Classic Arcade is an absolute gem! It’s clear how much care and passion goes into keeping these classic games and CRT monitors running in top shape. The game selection brings back all the nostalgic arcade magic, and the atmosphere is unbeatable. Highly recommended to anyone who appreciates classic arcade culture—5 stars!

top_reviews.content: Wow, restoring this historic spot for everyone to visit was such a heroic effort! Stepping inside totally takes you back 180 years, and you can almost hear the happiness and struggles of the people who were here. It's not a huge place, but the docents, Kent and his colleagues, really made it such a rich experience with their amazing, vivid descriptions! Enjoyed every minute of the 100min tour.

We’ve been looking forward to visiting the Moraga Adobe for some time now. So when we saw that tours were available on the website we jumped to reserve a spot. The Adobe is beautifully and thoughtfully restored and filled with period appropriate pieces. The tour guide was very informative and told a story of a lively evening in 1855 with a New Year’s Eve party, dancing, and music that really brought the history to life. I’m glad the community worked so hard to preserve this piece of California’s history
Our family really enjoyed touring the newly opened restored adobe. Guides were knowledgeable and enthused to welcome visitors. Well worth the visit.

In addition to being a California Historical Landmark, the Joaquín Moraga was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1972.

In 1835, Mexico granted 13,326 acres, El Rancho Laguna de los Palos Colorados, to Joaquín Moraga and his cousin Juan Bernal. Six years later, Joaquín built this house, which is the oldest surviving adobe house in Contra Costa County.

The Joaquín Moraga Adobe was photographed in 1922 for the Historical American Building Survey (HABS). It has been restored and remodeled twice since then, first in 1941 and again in 1964 when it was incorporated into a private home.

When we tried to visit the Joaquín Moraga Adobe in 2006, the building was not visible from the public right-of-way. The Friends of the Joaquín Moraga Adobe were working to provide community access to the building and grounds.

This is the oldest adobe structure in Contra Costa County, built in 1841. It's seen better days, but there's an effort to restore it to its original state and to make it a museum, which would be wonderful.

“We Are Not Strangers Here” at the Society of California Pioneers in the Presidio. Though the displays were interesting there was an apparent whitewashing of the history of Black farmers in California – a very Pollyanna view.

There was no reference to the most critical factor Black farmers experienced in farming, not only in California, but throughout the country - the fact that Black farmers have been excluded from farm programs for decades by the US Department of Agriculture. And when the American Rescue Plan was passed to try and remedy this situation in 2021, White farmers rose to block all funding to Black farmers.

In 1920 Blacks were 925,708 - 14 percent of all farmers.

At midcentury, there were 560,000 black farmers or 10 percent of all farmers.

Today, just 1.4 percent of farmers identify as Black or mixed race.

This type of whitewashing history is extremely detrimental to our understanding of what has happened in our world. It’s also dangerous. We need to understand this history to dismantle it. This exhibit simply propagates our misunderstanding of what and how our history is part of today.

Little cafe with hairy sandwiches.

This cafe, located inside the HSS Building at San Francisco State University, is almost never busy and delivers tasty sandwiches for prices comparable to other campus cafes. The sandwich itself was pretty good. I ordered a Milano club, which had tomatoes, onion, pesto, bacon, turkey, and swiss on ciabatta. There are lids, napkins, and sweeteners in the adjacent room. There are also two vending machines, but they aren't well-stocked.

There is no seating, but you can find benches outside the building or somewhere else inside the building. The service was pretty good and it wasn't busy at all, even during lunchtime. If my sandwich didn't have hairs, I would give this place four stars.

top_reviews.content:
Our daughter has taken classes at Kids n Dance (owned & managed by same persons who own & manage Expression Arts). Later she joined Expression Arts & was part of the troupe for 3 years. Circus was a haven for our child who built a community w/the peer troupers & truly enjoyed the art of circus. Over the past two years, we have increasingly heard of concerns by our daughter. While we were receptive, we initially tried to ask that she to trust the program, embrace challenges as opportunities to learn, & to believe in the positive intent of management. But over the past season the concerns and experiences have escalated. Troupers have come forward to raise awareness of troubling experiences. Some concerns raised by troupe members & our daughter:

Unsafe Physical Environment: Inadequate warm-up, inadequate breaks, extended time upside-down, & a persistent culture of pushing through pain & injury. During the lead up to performances, the children are often at practice for 6+ hours. Practice increases in frequency until the final few weeks preceding shows, where practice is nearly every day. During the two weeks of performances, troupers were asked to do 1 show on Friday, 2 shows on Saturday, & 3 shows on Sunday. Each show is ~2.25 hours. It was only after there were serious concerns raised in a parent conference with Kris and Marielle, that the 3rd performance on Sunday was cancelled. The standards, rigorous schedule, & high-risk performance are a dangerous recipe for the safety of the troupe.

Emotional Manipulation & Inappropriate Behavior: Esme drifts between friend & coach w/ the troupe. The relationship is confusing, w/Esme using this bond to instill her values on the children & also playing favorites. Multiple troupe members have noted that Esme can be erratic in her behavior, switching between positive behavior & disparaging & belittling language. In one incident, Esme told our daughter that she must have “ADD” after our daughter offered to help with transitions. Another time, Esme commented on the body figure of a trouper. Also, she told a group that their act was “stupid”. In isolation these incidents may be explainable (Kris & Marielle have attempted to rationalize all of the incidents), but what can’t be explained or rationalized is how widespread & consistent the experiences are amongst the troupe. After a senior troupe member sent a note to the parents about her own traumatic experiences, numerous troupe members came forward & shared consistent & repeated experiences.

What is most concerning is the complete lack of accountability & curiosity to do something about the numerous concerns raised by the troupe & families. We believe Esme, Kris, and Marielle have the best of intent and they want to provide a safe place for children & to cultivate a thriving community. We also believe they are wholly incompetent & untrained in how to create this place. The incompetence can be addressed, there are programs like SafeSport which, coupled with Esme’s passion for the art, could transform the space. But Esme, Kris, & Marielle first need to face the root of the issue & take concerns seriously. After a senior troupe member raised concerns about her own experiences, she was abruptly removed from the troupe & essentially called a liar. Parents then demanded a conference w/management. Esme did not attend. Kris & Marielle spent the bulk of 90 min. deflecting & taking no ownership or corrective measures.

Despite her initial love & passion for circus arts, our daughter has decided to move on. Despite everything we note above, our hope is that Expression Arts & Kids n Dance thrives & can be a safe place for youth to grow & express themselves. For this to happen, two things are needed: 1) Management needs to be curious, vulnerable, & accountable for the harm they are causing to the children. No more deflection. 2) They need to pursue ongoing training to equip themselves to appropriately & safely engage with children & young adults.

top_reviews.content:
Tony’s Pizza definitely lives up to its reputation for quality. The fresh ingredients really stand out, and the New Yorker pizza was outstanding. The crust was perfectly cooked with an incredible crispness that gave every bite great texture without being overdone. You can tell they take pride in using high-quality ingredients.

The service was very friendly, although it was a bit slower than expected. It almost felt like our table was just outside our waitress’s usual service area, so there were a few longer waits than we’d have liked.

The prices are what you’d expect for California, but the quality of the food makes it worthwhile. If you’re looking for exceptional pizza made with fresh ingredients and a perfectly crispy crust, Tony’s is absolutely worth a visit.

Tony’s Pizza Napoletana is absolutely worth the visit. The pizza was outstanding, with fresh ingredients, a perfectly crispy crust, and incredible flavor in every bite. The menu offers a great variety, and everything was served fresh and beautifully prepared. The staff were friendly and attentive, and the atmosphere was warm and welcoming. One of the best pizza experiences I’ve ever had—I’ll definitely be back the next time I’m in San Francisco!

Decided to walk down to Tony's on a Sunday while visiting San Francisco. For whatever reason, I showed up early - and I was glad I did. There was a line 1/2 block long and I arrived 10 minutes early before the place even opened! Soon, the line was practically down the end of the block. I figured - wow 😲 this place must be amazing! I was seated at the bar which was fine. Bartender greeted me pretty quickly and provided me a menu. The menu was pretty extensive. I decided to try the gluten free deep dish Detroit style pizza with sausage. It took over 45 minutes to receive the order. The pizza was very average. I honestly don't think sausage was even on it unless it was so finely ground that it melted into the crust. The crust was dense and chewy and honestly felt overcooked. Overall, I felt it wasn't worth the $27 I spent. I did like the atmosphere; it was very busy with a lot of activity and conversation among patrons. Nonetheless, I would go back next time I'm in SF and try something else to see if my opinion improves.

It was a great pizza restaurant in San Francisco’s little Italy neighborhood. It is rare to find coal-fired wood style pizza these days and they have it.  We had garlic breads and the coal fired wood pepperoni thin crust pizza. It was delicious like New York pizza and the portion was generous. The server was attentive and friendly and the restaurant is warm and vibrant. Please make sure you join their waitlist on line beforehand and check-in with them when you get there.

Tony's Pizza is an icon in the pizza world. They are rated as one of the top pizza spots in the entire country, and for good reason. Instead of focusing on just one style, they feature a wide variety of pizzas to pick from including New York, Detroit, and coal fired options. I'm a sucker for a good New York pie, and I found theirs to be delicious and absolutely massive. The garlic cheese bread was also tasty, and came with a delicious agave dipping sauce that I've never seen before but became a big fan of. The food does take a while to come out, but it's worth the wait. Service was super friendly as well. Also, heads up that they get super busy regardless of the day and time that you visit. I highly recommend getting on the virtual wait-list way before you arrive in order to save yourself potentially well over an hour of waiting for a table.

Had a really good experience at Pier Market Seafood. Everything was amazing overall. The Garlic Parmesan Fries and Fried Calamari were both really good, and the Grilled Chicken Breast was especially nice and flavorful.

The Pier Market Mixed Grill was okay-ish compared to the other dishes, but the Strawberry Lemonade was super refreshing and delicious. Great food, nice atmosphere, and definitely worth visiting while at Pier 39.

I ordered the grilled swordfish, which was $29.95. Considering the location on Pier 39, I thought the price was fairly reasonable. The biggest disappointment was the portion size. The plate came with what looked like only about 2½ ounces of rice and maybe 2 ounces of vegetables. I would have appreciated a more generous serving of both, although I suspect that might have made the very small, thin piece of swordfish look even smaller by comparison.

The food itself tasted good. The swordfish was well seasoned, cooked properly, and served hot. The rice and vegetables, however, were only lukewarm, and some of the zucchini was much softer than other pieces, almost as if additional vegetables had been added to a warmer later in the evening.

Despite those shortcomings, the location is hard to beat. Sitting on Pier 39 with views of the waterfront made the experience enjoyable, and that’s ultimately what made the meal worthwhile.

Jack London Square along the Oakland marina is one of those places that quietly grows on you over time. Years ago, this was part of my regular Capitol Corridor commute — a transfer point between sides of the Bay and just another stop in a busy schedule. Coming back now with a camera in hand, it feels completely different.

The marina has a calming rhythm: boats gently rocking, reflections on the water, and that open Bay light that changes by the minute. It’s a great spot for photography, especially around sunset when the sky and water start to mirror each other. The mix of modern waterfront and historic character gives it personality without trying too hard.

What really stands out for me is the nostalgia. Returning years later brought back memories of those commute days, but in a much more relaxed way. Now it’s a place to slow down, walk the promenade, and enjoy Oakland’s waterfront vibe.

If you’re in the East Bay, it’s worth spending some time here — whether for photos, a stroll, or just to sit by the water and take in the scene.

While all the flavors are fantastic, in my opinion the suffer from trying to make so much food too quickly.
I eat rather quickly and could not eat the burrito before it got too soggy and fell apart.

Finding parking just takes as long as waiting in line and getting your orders out to you. 2 burritos and 2 tacos with 2 drinks is 80 bucks plus a tip and total of hundred bucks. That’s a lot of money just for those! The burrito was ok, seasoned good with guacamole, sour cream, beans. I got the super burrito and with the salsa it was good. It’s not bad 3.5 at best for flavor and the price is a no go for me, and I’m being generous with my star review. The horchata taste they add to much sugar instead of the condensed milk. The melon drink was too chunky and wasn’t strained and didn’t taste milky. Those who know, know what I’m talking about. I just came because there was a line and I thought it was bomb. It’s aight, not for the price.

Messy but worth digging in.

Came on a Friday slightly past noon and there were already about ten groups ahead of us. Skipped the main line and went straight to the separate takeout window and our food was ready in 15 mins.

We got a couple super tacos and a burrito to share. Everything was grilled flawlessly, and our favorite was actually the most basic one (Carne Asada). Lengua and Carnitas didn't come through as flavorful as I'd hoped, and with toppings overflowing everywhere, it got hard to tell them apart.

The tacos were also so huge they layered two tortillas instead of one. We much preferred the crispy shell version over the plain double tortilla. Outer shell crisped up, inner one kept soft. Between the meat juices and the guac, things got soggy fast though.

The burrito was one of the best I've had in a while. No rice inside, and the beans and guac filling that space instead made the proteins feel way more satisfying. Gelatinized starch granules usually bind fat and trap volatile aromatics, so without the rice soaking them up, the meat's aroma came through louder. Also Glutamate (beans) + Inosinate (carne asada) supra-additive chemistry just works great all the time.

OUTSTANDING STEAK BURRITO!  The char-grilled smoke billowing from the top of this restaurant was the first sight and scent that this place was doing something right.  Arrived at 11:45am on a Wed and the line was 25 people long with another 15 waiting for food they ordered to-go, however the line moves quickly.  The restaurant is small, but turnover is relatively high.  We dined in and waited almost 15 min (worth the wait) for a steak burrito that was out of this world.  The meat was perfectly char-grilled, tender, and incredibly tasty!  We got ours “dorado” style, which is some extra flat top grilling for added flavor (do this!).  I have eaten 100s of burritos from several dozen great Mexican restaurants.  Nothing compares to this steak burrito!  Wow!  We wanted to stand up and applaud after we finished!

The burritos were really good. It definitely lived up to the hype. Make sure to make the burrito "super" it adds sour cream,cheese and avocado. And also get it crispy. They crisp the sides of the burrito on the grill making it that much better. The flour tortilla they use for the burrito was insanely good. A little thicker and softer than all the other flour tortillas I've had before, super good. 🙌
All the employees were super nice and the atmosphere was moderately noisy but something to be expected in a restaurant this popular and this historic.
The only down side is the neighborhood is a little sketchy. Be careful where you park and dont leave valuables in your car visible to the public. I hear break in are common, although thankfully nothing happened to our car.
Other than this, this was one of the best burritos I've had in a long time. Definitely a must try if your in the city.

"Service, food, ambience — all 10/10 Mexican restaurant!"
"The taco was served in a crispy tortilla which was wrapped in a soft taco."

top_reviews.content: My friends and I all got the double double animal style burgers and enjoyed them soooo much. As someone who doesn’t live in a city with in n out, I’m still thinking about this burger and am craving another one! We were headed to the airport so I unfortunately couldn’t try the fries. If you’re looking to be in and out (haha) go inside and order for quicker service. Drive thru line was long!

Don't get me wrong, this is not a diner's burger.  However, for the fast food, double-double is very decent.  The fries were seasoned properly also.  They do put you on the spot when they ask to round to the nearest dollar to prevent child abuse.  However, when you tell them no, they don't roll their eyes, or do any weird pauses, etc.

Always good burgers. Depending on the time, there could be a long wait but the staff is typically super efficient. My go to order is double double with grilled onions and pickles. If I'm really hungry, well done fries is included.

I was really disappointed after all the hype about this place.  We went at 730 pm and it was crazy busy.  People everywhere elbow to elbow.  The burger was high quality but it was as thin as a McDonald's burger.  Not much meat at all. The double double had more meat.   And the fries are not crispy.  They taste like freeze dried food.  Service was great!

Came here after Fourth of July fireworks in San Francisco, and while the drive-thru line wrapped around through light cycles of the intersection and the line of pedestrians ran into the parking lot, they still moved people incredibly efficiently. I was able to get my burger and fries in about 15 minutes and was very pleased with the classic, consistent In-N-Out taste. Unfortunately, I really like cheese fries, but they cost the same as Animal Fries ($5) which feels a bit pricey when considering normal fries cost a little over $2. But besides that, prices are very competitive for the quality.

google.name: Scoma's Restaurant

google.description: Spacious waterfront restaurant serving seafood pulled straight off the boat.

top_reviews.content:
Came here after a hike for lunch and waited about 30 minutes for an outdoor table. The waterfront setting made the wait worthwhile and added to the relaxing atmosphere.

Once seated, I was craving oysters, and this place delivered. The calamari was fresh and crispy with just the right amount of batter. The vongole pasta was flavorful, but my favorite was the creamy risotto with perfectly cooked scallops. The cioppino was also delicious, and a glass of wine made the meal even better.

Service was attentive throughout, making for an enjoyable dining experience and giving me another reason to return.

I visited this restaurant over the weekend, and it exceeded my expectations in every respect. Making a reservation was definitely the right choice, as the restaurant was very busy.

The service was exceptional—professional, attentive, and genuinely welcoming throughout the entire evening. The food was equally impressive: every dish was of outstanding quality and fully justified the prices charged. A detail that particularly stood out was being offered the locally caught salmon, as the fishing boat had only returned to the harbor earlier that same day. It doesn’t get much fresher than that.

The location is simply stunning. Watching the sunset over the harbor while enjoying dinner created a truly memorable atmosphere that perfectly complemented the dining experience.

Having traveled the entire West Coast from Seattle to San Diego, I can honestly say that this was the finest restaurant of my trip. The combination of exceptional food, impeccable service, and a breathtaking setting makes this place stand out even among some very strong competition. Highly recommended.

Scoma’s of Sausalito has a beautiful waterfront view and a really nice atmosphere. The service was great and everyone was friendly. We tried the clam chowder, burger, and a few different pastas, and enjoyed everything we ordered. My favorite was definitely the pesto shrimp pasta—it was delicious! Overall, a great place to enjoy good food with an amazing view.

Right off the water, this restaurant is quiet and offers an individual and peaceful dining experience. Feeling more fancy than regular cuisine, we did their lunch special which came with a chowder that was so delectable and creamy, and our main which was pasta and salad. The portions were generous with just enough to have you feeling full without feeling too full. The taste of the food was very fresh and light. It’s more on the expensive side but we found the food to be quality.

Pretty good experience overall. The complementary bread was so-so, but the whipped butter made it better. We started with some clam chowder. The portion wasn't that big, but the soup was creamy. We then had their oysters a la Scoma, with spinage and melted cheese. It's very different from a regular oysters platter, but it was pretty tasty, albeit a bit salty. For main courses we had their pasta diplomatica and the fish and chips. The pasta was quite good. The fish was perfect; the fries were alright. We finished the evening with a torta setteveli (chocolate cake), which was decent.

The ambience is nice, but the service is exceptional. We spent $157 for two people after tax before tip and we were absolutely stuffed, we definitely could and should have ordered less.

reviews_snippets.content: "I ordered three appetizers, calamari, crispy fries, and the beet salad."

name: Super Duper Burgers
address: 721 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94103, United States

top_reviews.content:
Super Duper Burgers is one of the best fast-casual burger spots in San Francisco.

The burger is simple but done right. The beef patty is juicy, well-seasoned, and has a nice char that gives it extra flavor. The bun is soft but holds everything together perfectly, and the fresh toppings make a big difference.

The garlic fries are a must. Crispy, garlicky, and honestly one of the highlights of the meal. Pair it with a milkshake and you’ve got a perfect combo.

The vibe is casual and busy, especially during lunch hours. It’s not a place to relax for long, but great for a quick, satisfying meal.

Prices are a bit higher than typical fast food, but still reasonable for San Francisco.

⚠️ It gets crowded, and seating can be limited during peak times.

Overall, a solid choice if you want a high-quality burger without going to a full restaurant.

👉 Check my profile for more food spots and travel tips.

Stopped by Super Duper Burgers for a casual lunch and ordered their organic egg sandwich along with the signature garlic fries. The sandwich was fresh, satisfying, and packed with flavor, while the garlic fries were definitely the highlight—crispy, cheesy, and incredibly appetizing. The ingredients tasted fresh, and the overall quality stood out from a typical fast-casual burger spot. Great option for a quick bite in San Francisco. Would gladly stop by again! 🍔🍟😋

Delicious fresh handmade burgers and crispy fries ❤️🍔, hypster and modern style spot👍🏼. Very clean! All crew where nice and had rapid service. I would just recommend to lower a lil bit the music. It seemed it was a disco  (glad they had bose sound system because at least it sounded good quality 😬) but i came to have a tranquile meal, not to be pushed to put noise cancelling headphones.

We visited Super Duper Burger with my kids and they loved it! The burgers were crispy, juicy, and full of flavor, with delicious homemade pickles on the side. They enjoyed every bite!

For me, it was a little too rich because I’m not usually a big burger fan, but I can see why this place is popular. Definitely a great spot for burger lovers.

Most amazing and juiciest burgers we’ve ever had! 12/10 experience. The staff are super friendly too. We’re from Canada and this is the first food place we visited over here; overall such a wonderful experience.

top_reviews.content: Good food, but not quite great. It's a solid 4 out of 5, not bad. We love coming here. Wine and liquor selections are minimal but okay. The fried chicken is incredible. The greens are really good. The grits are 8 out of 10. Everything was good. I recommend Brenda's to all.

A different type of French cuisines. The place is unassuming, affordable and has local diners. Good service overall. The fried chicken is good, served hot. The bloody Mary with pickled okra is a bit bitter. The crawfish bignet is tasty, more cheesy than clawfish, worth a try. If you like sausage, you would enjoy andouille, a different kind of sausage like meat. If you like new orlean dish, you would enjoy the French soul food offered here. We like this variation from the most refined French dish.

This is a well-known brunch and breakfast spot in San Francisco. Their food tends to be on the salty side, but their coffee is excellent with a wide variety of options. The atmosphere is enjoyable. I love this place, especially if they used less salt.

Brenda’s French Soul Food delivered a solid dining experience with a few standout dishes and a few that didn’t quite hit the mark. Our party unanimously agreed that the fried chicken was the highlight—crispy, flavorful, and definitely worth the visit. The beignets were also a treat, light and tasty with just the right touch of sweetness.
Some dishes were more middle-of-the-road. The red beans and rice and the biscuits were decent but didn’t stand out in a memorable way. Unfortunately, the shrimp and grits fell short of expectations and didn’t quite come together in flavor.
Overall, it was a good experience with some hits and misses, and we’d rate it a 7 out of 10. Worth trying, especially for the fried chicken and beignets.

Not a bad place to get some fun French/Southern food. If you’re into grits, the shrimp and grits are a favorite. And we also like the chicken sandwich. The beignets are also really good if you’ve got enough room for dessert.

The service here isn’t bad, but it is an amazing. We arrived with a reservation a few minutes early and the restaurant was almost completely empty and they still didn’t see us. But they did see a bunch of walk-ins which was a little weird. And then even before we were done with our meal, they were consistently trying to rush us out of our table, even though there were more open tables, and nobody waiting to be seated.

That being said, that atmosphere is really fun and if you go on Sunday evenings, they have live music being played. Makes for a really fun atmosphere during dinner.

top_reviews.content: Stopped in for lunch, just around the corner of our hotel. This place has both indoor and outdoor seating. We opted for one of their advertised specials, Meatballs Arrabbiata. Big well flavored meatballs in a fantastic slightly spicy marinara. My cheese stuffed ravioli were equally delicious, as was my spouse's bacon wrapped prawns. All very fresh and well made food. Our server, Tim, was friendly and attentive. Nice location at the Wharf. Highly recommend.

Located right at the very heart of Fisherman’s Wharf, Cioppino’s offers both outdoor patio seating and indoor seating they really know how to blend Italian tradition with San Francisco’s seafood. You will find here crab, fresh fish, shrimp, clams, and mussels as well as pasta and pizza and of course the World Famous Cioppino which is a seafood stew with crab legs, clams, mussels, snapper, calamari, and shrimp in a tomato broth.

This was my first time here and will gladly come back again and again, the place has a great Fisherman’s Wharf atmosphere, the staff is really cool and helpful and they made us feel really welcomed, we had the traditional Clam Chowder with the Salad Combo, and it is a great combination, because you get the chowder in a Boudin sourdough bread bowl and a mixed green salad. Don’t make the same mistake I made getting the Cup Clam Chowder because you won’t get the bread bowl, and you will miss the full clam chowder experience.

Our main dishes were the Scampi Linguini that came with jumbo shrimps, scallions, diced tomatoes in a white wine and lemon butter sauce, absolutely delicious and the Penne Pomodoro with Grilled Chicken and Romano Cheese. I liked the Scampi Linguini better; however the Penne Pomodoro was really good as well.

Our server was Salvador and he was really helpful and took care of all our needs.

Considering this place is in the heart of a major tourist area such as Fisherman’s Wharf, they are doing an excellent job. Highly recommended!!!

Visited Cioppino’s for a work dinner and had a really great experience. The restaurant is conveniently located in the North Beach area, which makes it easy to get to and perfect if you’re exploring that part of the city.

The decor and atmosphere give off a classic Italian aesthetic — warm, inviting, and perfect for a nice dinner setting. The staff were amazing throughout the night, attentive and genuinely welcoming.

We had a prix fixe menu for our group and everything was delicious. The pacing was great and it made the whole experience feel seamless for a larger party.

Highly recommend this spot, especially if you’re planning a group dinner or special occasion

food is amazing! pizza and pastas are top notch, heck even the garlic bread and salads were incredible.

staff is super friendly and welcoming.

outdoor patio is perfect when weather is nice! love this place.

This is a great little outdoor dining experience Italian cuisine. Wait staff was very professional. Restrooms very clean. Food moderately priced but worth it every bit. Would recommend their signature dish. It is for two. Very delicious. This is a great experience, I would return  every day if I could.

top_reviews.content:
THIS IS A MUST IN SF!!

When I saw over 4,000 reviews with a 4.9 rating on Google Maps, I was honestly skeptical—so I decided to try it myself. Believe me when I say this place truly deserves all 5 stars.

The food is hands down some of the best we’ve ever had. The service was also excellent—the owner is incredibly friendly and a great host, which makes the whole experience even better.

Everything we ordered was amazing, but the Mesopotamian plate was definitely the best value. The desserts were also really good.

This is not a paid advertisement—I’m just genuinely excited about this place and highly recommend it. Plus, it’s not as crowded as other spots in North Beach, which is a big bonus.

Amazing food & service. We popped in here hungry and left full, happy, and with a bag of leftovers! The portions are large and all the food fresh and flavorful. We ordered the Grilled Branzino and Mesopotamia Kebab for our mains. Our server was very attentive and gave us plenty of things to try while we were here. Great place to stumble upon!

I’d love to leave the best possible review for this restaurant! ❤️ The food was absolutely delicious — everything was fresh, beautifully presented, and clearly prepared with great care. Every dish we ordered was excellent, and it had been a long time since we enjoyed a dinner this much.

I’d also like to mention the wonderful atmosphere and great service. This is definitely the kind of place you want to come back to and happily recommend to friends. Absolutely 5 stars! ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

My husband and I were visiting SF and found this place randomly. As a Turkish person, I really missed service like this in a restaurant.

Abdurrahman was very kind and welcoming. The food was absolutely delicious. The meat was cooked perfectly, and the mezes were amazing. And honestly, I still can’t believe they managed to make dolma better than my grandma’s! Also, you get extra mezes from the house if you order any meat/chicken.

Awesome turkish food, reasonable prices, and great service. We even brought our coworkers the next day! Def recommend!

The food was absolutely amazing from start to finish. The falafel was perfectly crispy on the outside and soft, flavorful, and fresh on the inside. The tzatziki was creamy, refreshing, and complemented every bite beautifully. The fries were golden, crispy, and seasoned just right.

The salad tasted incredibly fresh with crisp vegetables and a well-balanced dressing, while the hummus was smooth, rich, and packed with flavor. Every dish felt freshly prepared and made with quality ingredients.

Overall, a fantastic meal with excellent flavors, freshness, and presentation. I would definitely come back and highly recommend it to anyone looking for delicious Mediterranean food! 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟

top_reviews.content: House of Nanking is an absolute must-visit! The food was fresh, full of flavor, and every dish we ordered was outstanding. The portions were generous, and the service was warm, attentive, and made us feel right at home. You can tell they take pride in both the quality of their food and the experience they provide. If you’re looking for delicious Chinese food with a welcoming atmosphere, this place is definitely worth a visit. I’ll be coming back!

If you're looking for great food with good prices this is the place.
Staff were very friendly and the service was very good. Very busy place with a good atmosphere and history.
Came back a 2nd time for dinner on Sunday
Ordered 3 dishes one chicken, one pork and noodles. Asked the waitress for the chefs choice and we were not disappointed.
Pork Ribs glazed with Zucchini,  Chicken with sweet potatoes and sauce, and last of all noodles with herbs.
The taste was amazing, l would highly recommend trying this.

Best Chinese food I have ever had. Each and every dish was soooo flavorful and delicious.

It’s a small restaurant but it’s very renowned and it’s been featured in several food channels and magazines.

It’s Keanu Reeves’s favorite restaurant as well.

We had such a wonderful experience at House of Nanking.

We arrived just before the dinner rush, and even though there was already a long line forming outside, the staff kept things moving efficiently and had everyone seated surprisingly quickly.

Our kids felt welcome and enjoyed the decor. The walls had articles and awards. Seated close to other tables but comfortable.

What made this visit especially memorable was meeting Chef Peter Fang himself. It was incredibly humbling to watch someone so renowned and successful personally greeting guests, taking orders, and checking on tables. Seeing a chef of his caliber so hands-on and genuinely invested in his customers says a lot about the restaurant and the person behind it. His humility and passion left just as much of an impression on us as the food.

We ordered the short ribs with bok choy, the pork confit, the duck buns, and the House Noodles. Every dish was packed with flavor and thoughtfully prepared. The standout for me was definitely the duck buns - they were absolutely incredible and something I'd order again in a heartbeat. The House Noodles were also delicious, and the short ribs were tender and full of rich, savory flavor.

If you're visiting San Francisco's Chinatown, House of Nanking is absolutely worth the wait. Great food, generous portions, and an unforgettable dining experience made even better by Chef Peter Fang's genuine hospitality.

After hearing from multiple sources this was the best Chinese food in San Francisco, my wife and I were alittle disappointed. Whilst the Sesame Chicken came out very fast and was delicious, the House Noodles took a while to come out. To the point where we had basically finished the chicken, when we had hoped to eat both dishes at the same time. The house noodles were underwhelming, not very flavoursome and tasted over cooked and slightly soggy. Perhaps the restaurant's massive popularity with tourists has resulted in their standards slipping recently.

top_reviews.content:
The staff were friendly and courteous throughout our visit. We arrived around 4:00 PM, well before the typical dinner rush, but still waited over 30 minutes for a table, which shows how popular the restaurant is.
The food was very good, and both pasta dishes were well prepared.
One small disappointment was the bread service. After we finished our bread, we asked if we could have another basket. Our server said they would bring more, but it never arrived. It may have simply been forgotten during a busy service.
If the weather is nice, I would recommend sitting outdoors. The indoor dining room feels quite crowded, and because of the open kitchen, the smell of cooking lingers in the air. By the end of the meal, our clothes noticeably smelled like kitchen smoke.
Overall, we enjoyed the food and the service. With a little improvement to the seating wait and indoor ventilation, the dining experience would be even better.

If you are in San Francisco, you absolutely have to check this place out—you won't regret it! Sotto Mare is located in a great neighborhood, and the vibe inside is incredibly fun and bustling. Even though the place was packed, the staff was super friendly, attentive, and running around making sure everyone was taken care of.
Here is what we tried:
Richie's Marinated Cold Cracked Dungeness Crab: My oh my, this has to be the best crab I have ever had in my life. Absolutely incredible.
Clams on the Half Shell: Nicely fresh, clean, and a perfect appetizing start to the meal.
The World-Famous Cioppino: This was the absolute star of the night. While I haven't tried every single cioppino in the Bay Area, this has to be the best one around. The flavor is outstanding—subtle, mild, and perfectly balanced. The portion size is huge and was more than enough for me and my lady. It is just loaded to the brim with fresh seafood, including mussels, clams, calamari, scallops, and shrimp.
Pro-Tip: Go early right when they are about to open! They don’t take standard small-group reservations, and this place gets really, really busy fast.

Long waits on a Saturday night, but you get a buzzer so you can walk around.

The last time I was here was 2018, and the food is still excellent. I always order the cioppino and although still good, it seems like the recipe has changed a little bit. The oysters are superb as is the cobb salad.

Wines are well priced and service is great. Sitting outside is preferable to inside.

Such amazing Italian food!! Ordered a half dozen of east + west oysters. I personally prefer east cuz it’s sweater. Absolutely favorite is the seafood risotto, so much seafood and fresh. Same with their signature seafood soup(?) forgot the actual name of the dish. But it’s served with so much fresh seafood. Crab, shell, squid, mussel. Seasoning is absolutely spot on. Not too heavy or creamy. Such delicious food for amazing price! Def a 10/10!! Server was so nice. Just be aware they have added a 4% service fee. I didn’t take it out because I feel they deserve that and to better survive in sf as such an amazing Italian restaurant.

Very good, home style seafood!  All our dishes were fresh and favorable.  Service was generally good but the tables were small and you had to navigate putting the dishes on the table.
Highly recommended!

I had the spicy meltburger with fresh jalapenos, lettuce, avocado, and spicy sauce. I also got chicken and bacon Mac n cheese and Parmesan fries. Everything tasted amazing. It was a little pricier than a generic fast food burger place but it was worth it!

Ordered the double BBQ bacon burger with fries and it absolutely hit. The burger was juicy, stacked perfectly, and the BBQ sauce + bacon combo was on point without being overwhelming. Fries were hot, crispy, and fresh.

What really stood out was the customer service—super friendly when I asked questions about the menu, and they were happy to give extra sauce without any attitude. You can tell they actually care about the experience, not just the food.

Definitely a spot I’d come back to when I’m craving a solid burger.

Mushroom Swiss had tender mushrooms and the adding the melt sauce brought all the flavors together!

I had lettuce wrap melt cheeseburger and it was the perfect size!

We didn't see any seats downstairs, but had the balcony all to ourselves! Easy to hear conversations and chill vibes!

Def a great smash burger place to enjoy!

Went there as soon as they opened to get a breakfast sandwich and it did not disappoint!! I was able to customize it the way I wanted to and it turned out amazing. An egg melt with avocado, caramelized onions and mushrooms. Absolutely delicious

Good food and the atmosphere is very relaxed. The wait times can be pretty good but no one really says if your order is ready if you order online. It's difficult to get someone's attention. Other than that the whole place is good.

name: The Grove Restaurant & Bar

google.name: The Grove Restaurant & Bar
google.address: 690 Mission St, San Francisco, CA 94105, United States
google.description: Popular spot for American home cooking in a mountain-lodge-like setting with communal seats.

top_reviews.content:
We stopped here for lunch while visiting SFMOMA. It was peak lunch hour and there was a line outside, but it moved quickly—it was more of an entry line than a wait. Once inside, you order at a kiosk, get a number, find a seat, and the food is brought to your table.

I had the New York-style pastrami sandwich, served with a pickle and a small side of lettuce (chips are also an option). The pastrami was meaty, rich, and quite filling—half the sandwich was enough for me to take the rest home. It was fresh and definitely not bad, although having had some excellent pastrami in New York, I wouldn’t call this exceptional.

My friend had a slice of apple pie and really enjoyed it. She found it fresh and pleasantly, mildly sweet without being overly sugary.

They have a good selection of all-day breakfast items and sandwiches. The restaurant was almost full and clearly popular. Overall, nothing extraordinary that you’ll remember for years, but a solid, reliable spot for a satisfying lunch in the area.

I really enjoyed the vibe here. Perfect for a lunch date. You order your food, pay at the register, and they give you a number, and you can go sit wherever you want. They servers will find you. My lady and I sat upstairs. I ordered the Crisp Oven Fried Chicken Sandwich and my lady ordered the Roadt Chicken Apple Salad. I also was being a fat ass and ordered a huge chocolate chip cookie and a (I think it was a coffee cake or a crumble, my bad.) But it was good. The cookie was alright, I give the cookie a C but everything else was on point. Sit up stairs for the best ambience. We went around 1130 am.

The chairs next to the fireplace are the spot on a rainy day - cozy and warm.

I ordered the avocado toast with poached eggs, which came with a side salad. It was very filling and well-balanced.

***No WiFi *** so plan accordingly. Bring a hotspot if you need to work, or take it as an opportunity to unplug and just enjoy the space.

Overall, a great place to slow down, especially when the weather calls for something warm and relaxed.

Wonderful environment, well situated in the city too. If you're here with a lot of people you're likely to have a good time, but even parties of two or one suffice. The food is scrumptious, and the whole place feels like a cabin you'd eat at before embarking upon a beautiful hike across some snowcapped peaks.

I was a regular at the Grove when living in San Francisco and specifically when there were several locations before the lockdown. My favorites were located on Hayes and in the designer's district. Only this one at Yerba Buena now remains. I still like the food (not cheap) and they offer a very tasty GF bread.

However, I asked for only one instead of two poached eggs with the avocado toast and was told: "it will be the same price"!
"Yes, ok I understand" . However I suggested to comp me the bread since I had to pay extra for the GF bread (which I never understood  why most restaurants charge extra for GF bread in the first place; it is not that much more expensive than regular bread).
The cashier: "Well, I can't; I would need to have a manager do it."

And is it that difficult to call a manager to ask? My thought, that I didn't bother to express because at that point, I was annoyed, especially after learning that the orange juice was more than $9.00. I declined to add the juice to my order!!
My tip was not as generous as usual!
The weather was beautiful so eating outside was nice.

reviews_snippets.content: "Great atmosphere and service with solid food, good portions, and lots of options"
"This Grove offers a small, well curated menu of home cooked meals."
"Fun environment sat upstairs and people watched as we ate!"

name: La Mar Cocina Peruana San Francisco
address: PIER 1 1/2 The Embarcadero N, San Francisco, CA 94111, United States

top_reviews.content:
Top notch venue with patio sitting and a million dollar bay view. The interior design of the restaurant is most impressive and modern. We arrived early and were enjoyed the bar area to see the live telecast of world cup soccer.

Service was excellent and friendly. The Peruvian menu was expertly crafted and executed. Ingredients was fresh and well seasoned.

Highly recommended.

★★★★★

La Mar Cocina Peruana is one of the best dining experiences in San Francisco. The waterfront location on the Embarcadero is stunning, creating the perfect atmosphere for lunch or dinner. Every dish was beautifully presented and packed with fresh, vibrant flavors.

The ceviche was exceptional, the seafood was incredibly fresh, and the cocktails—especially the Pisco Sour—were outstanding. The service was attentive, knowledgeable, and made us feel welcome from the moment we arrived.

Whether you’re celebrating a special occasion or simply looking for an unforgettable meal, La Mar delivers on every level. Amazing food, beautiful views, and impeccable service. I can’t wait to come back.

The food was amazing. The standouts of the night were the nigiri’s and the chocolate cake. The nigiri’s were to die for. The chocolate cake is truly made like they do at the bakeries in Peru. It is super authentic and delicious. I am looking forward to being back and trying the rest of the menu. I mentioned to our lovely waiter that I had a shellfish allergy and he told me they would accommodate the entire menu. He even double checked that things did not have oyster sauce for me. The attention to detail was amazing.

We are vegetarian and had many options to choose from. We especially loved the veggie ceviche and the fresh corn empanadas. For our mains we tried the Veggie Saltado, it was delicious ! It had a nice Asian twist to it. I love that they offer complimentary fresh potato chips with a yummy sauce, complimenting our drinks nicely!👌🏽 Views on the patio were great. Staff was attentive too.This was my second time here and I’ll definitely be coming back. 🙌🏽

We were three people and ordered the Kampachi Experience Menu. The food was exquisite, with every dish prepared from the fish presented to us at the beginning of the meal. The ceviche, sashimi, stir-fried fish, and fried rice were absolutely top-notch.

The service was excellent and perfectly on point. It is definitely very expensive, around $250 per person, but worth every penny for the quality and overall experience.

Highly recommended.

reviews_snippets.content: "Great location, open kitchen, variety of seating options, tasty tapas."
"Main fish of grilled salmon, shrimp with mushrooms , veggies was excellent."
"It's is a bit loud vibrant restaurant with excellent food and service."

name: Golden Boy Pizza
address: 542 Green St, San Francisco, CA 94133, United States

google.name: Golden Boy Pizza
google.address: 542 Green St, San Francisco, CA 94133, United States
google.description: Funky joint specializing in focaccia pizzas with a variety of meat & veggie toppings.

top_reviews.content:
Went here with my family and wow… what a scene. The line was LOOOONG. We waited about 1 hour and 15 minutes for our pizza. With hungry kids, that is basically a survival challenge.
But then we took the first bite… and suddenly nobody was complaining. The pizza was sooo soft, almost like a fluffy cloud, and it just melted in your mouth. The crust was thick but light, crispy on the outside and pillowy inside. Super simple, super good.
Only downside: very limited options if you are vegetarian and nothing for vegans. There was just choice between pesto veggie and cheese. Overall though, totally worth the wait. Next time I am 100% ordering ahead because now I know the pizza is worth it, but my feet cannot handle another hour-long line.

Golden Boy Pizza is a must-visit in San Francisco! The pizza was absolutely delicious, fresh and full of flavour. The crust was perfectly cooked, the toppings were generous, and every slice was outstanding.

The atmosphere was lively, the service was quick, and it is easy to see why this place is so popular with both locals and visitors. Even with a queue, the food was worth the wait.

Decent pizza for the price. Thick crust, generous toppings, efficient gruff service that reminds me of New York. Park nearby to consume your goods at! Take away only. Slices and whole pies available. They heat up your slices so it's a bit of a wait but they stay piping hot for a while. I'd be happy to return if I were in the area again.

The pizza here is amazing. I tried the pepperoni slice and it was genuinely delicious with a very authentic flavor. Even late at night the queue was surprisingly long, which says a lot about how popular the place is.

It’s just a small takeaway counter, so don’t expect a premium atmosphere, more of a classic, local vibe. During peak hours you’ll need to wait in line, and once you reach the front you place your order, pay, and give your name. After that there’s a short wait until they call you, and then you get your pizza.

Overall, great taste and totally worth the wait if you’re craving a quality slice.
How is it possible I didn't find Golden Boy Pizza back in the 80s when I spent a lot of time in this neighborhood? The pizza is fantastic and at an excellent price. The crust is delicious.

reviews_snippets.content: "Best place to grab a whole pie or a slice great food great people"
"It’s a walk-up counter, no inside service, so I can’t rate the “atmosphere.”"
"Their crust, sauce, cheese and ingredients makes their pizza the best in town."

name: Sweet Maple
address: 2101 Sutter St, San Francisco, CA 94115, United States

top_reviews.content:
One of the Best Brunch Spots in San Francisco

Sweet Maple in Pacific Heights was such a great find. Started with the Bloody Mary, which was flavorful, well-balanced, and the perfect way to kick off brunch.

The Millionaire’s Bacon sampler platter was easily one of the highlights — thick, sweet, savory, and ridiculously good. If you like bacon, this is basically mandatory.

I also tried the Pimped Shin Cupbop, and it was a fun twist on the classic Shin Cup. Comfort food with a serious upgrade — flavorful, satisfying, and definitely not your average brunch dish.

The food was so good that I ended up doing something I almost never do at restaurants: I bought both a T-shirt AND a hoodie. 😂 That probably says more about how much I enjoyed the place than anything else.

Great food, fun atmosphere, generous portions, and a place that doesn’t take itself too seriously. Definitely one of my favorite brunch stops in San Francisco and somewhere I’d happily come back to.

Ok Sweet Maple hit THE spot! Yum on yum. I usually don’t order sandwiches at restaurants. However, this breakfast sandwich was delicious. The bread was nice and soft. The bacon was nice and crisp. The fried French toast was another level when I come back. I will definitely be getting that. I got the coconut latte it was pretty good overall five stars.

Really great food and pretty quick to get into even on a Sunday afternoon. I enjoyed my sandwich and others enjoyed their meals. They were quick to get us a high chair for the baby but after that the service slowed up a bit. The food was nice and hot when it came. It was pretty loud with everybody so it made it hard to talk. I’d go back and try some other things.

Sweet Maple was definitely worth the visit and lived up to the hype as a brunch spot in San Francisco. The food was genuinely delicious, the portions were generous, and the overall experience was really enjoyable. Their famous Millionaire’s Bacon absolutely did not disappoint — it was flavorful, perfectly cooked, and easy to see why it’s one of their signature items.

I ordered the Blackstone Benedict, which included the Millionaire’s Bacon, and it was excellent. Everything tasted fresh and well-balanced, and the flavors worked really well together. My fiancé ordered the French toast with added eggs and bacon, and that was equally good. The food quality here definitely stands out.

The service was also very solid. Staff was friendly, attentive, and the restaurant seemed to run efficiently despite how busy it was. One thing to note is that the restaurant gets VERY loud, especially during peak brunch hours, so it was a little difficult at times to hear the person I was with. Still, the energy and popularity of the place make sense once the food arrives.

It is on the pricier side, but for the quality, portions, and overall brunch experience, I can understand why it’s such a popular spot. Also worth mentioning: they had signs warning customers not to leave valuables in their cars due to break-ins in the area, which I appreciated them being upfront about.

Overall, I’d definitely come back and would recommend Sweet Maple to anyone looking for a memorable brunch in SF.

Came with a friend for breakfast. It was super busy but no wait surprisingly. I tried the "Souflegg", fluffy eggs in a skillet and split the millionaire's bacon. The bacon was sweet and candied with a kick of spice, it was so good. The Souflegg was tasty and surprisingly filling. I'd definitely come back for breakfast!

name: Original Joe’s Westlake
address: 11 Glenwood Ave, Daly City, CA 94015, United States

top_reviews.content:
Alberto is the best! My friend and I strolled into Original Joe's Westlake on a Wednesday evening to grab dinner, drinks, dessert, and watch the Mexico vs. Czechia game. Thanks to Alberto and the entire team, we had the best time, food, and overall experience.

Even though the restaurant was incredibly busy—packed with people and with guests constantly walking in throughout the evening—Alberto never made us feel forgotten. He thoughtfully checked in on us, got everything to us in a reasonable amount of time, and was incredibly patient as I asked questions about different menu items. He even let us know that, although he was busy, we should simply flag him down if we needed anything at all.

At establishments like this that have such a high volume of customers, I honestly don't expect service like this. I expect long waits and to spend half the evening trying to find my server. Not Alberto, though. He was kind, professional, helpful, and knowledgeable from beginning to end.

As for the food, I had the Pilsner and Joe's Filet of Sole, my friend had the Golden Ale and Joe's Eggplant Parmigiana, and we shared the butter cake with ice cream for dessert. Everything was chef's kiss, including the bread and butter!

I would absolutely come back just for the service from Alberto. Five stars, always. You can never go wrong with Original Joe's, and Alberto made an already great experience even better!

I can finally check off Original Joe's off my restaurant bucket list and we had a great experience 🎉 I did a walk in for a party of 5, as we weren't able to make reservations that were all taken online - did not want to go somewhere else either and were prepared to wait 30 minutes or so but were pleasantly surprised to be seated in less than 10 minutes. The place was poppin with a full entrance but the lovely hosts did a great job of greeting me and getting us started. Put my number down and get a text when the tables ready while we went out for some fresh air. There was complementary hot bread and butter (I think it was sourdough? It was soo yummy).

We tried the caesar salad and calamari as appetizers, and they were both hits. The caesar salad was crisp and light, and had fresh anchovies. The calamari was a bit crispy and soft at the same time, with tartar sauce and a marinara (I think?) with horseradish for a lil kick. Squeeze that lemon over it, yumms. I like that there were two dip options. Killed it and forgot the pics 😝

For our entrees I got the prime rib special which comes with the sides of mashed potatoes and aus jus and creamed spinach. I got mine medium rare and it was delicious. Just right, and not tooooo salty. Others got the braised short ribs, the ribeye, and pastas spicy rigatoni and carbonara. The rigatoni won over the carbonara in my opinion, and wasn't as spicy as I thought (good for me lol). If others want it spicier I think you could ask 🌶️

Overall we had a lovely time, ambience was good and it was low light, nice vibes, it was lively and our servers were attentive. Prices are up there so it's a special occasion kinda spot for me. They gave my sister a little birthday cake piece and sang. We'll be back and try their desserts next time, I was stuffed 😋

February 2026:
Had a large party here for an early dinner. Service was a bit off this time. We came around the shift change and our first server was rushing us to get our order in. He was very impatient. Once he left, service was better.

I had the eggplant parmigiana. Was pretty good. Would get something different next time.

July 2025:
Came here for an anniversary dinner and was very pleased. I had the lasagna and my wife had the prime rib. Both were very tasty.

Dessert was very tasty too.

This place gets packed. Service is very friendly. Would definitely come back again.

Been coming here since 2013 and the quality of food and service has been impeccable and consistent. Today, got a chance to try the weekday lunch specials and I think we will be back for more weekday lunch.

The chicken pot pie sells out quickly so make sure to plan ahead. Plenty of parking, make reservation because it does get busy during lunch and dinner time.

Just an incredible evening. Fabulous food, I had the Marry Me Farfalle with prawns A++. Dessert was decadent. Great coffee, and even cocktails for those who prefer no liquor but want to celebrate. For me my twin nieces graduation from college. I flew in from green bay, WI. It was so busy that night, but you treated all five of us with care. My experience was even better than when we came after their high school graduation. My dad was there that night; we lost him last summer. But I'll always remember that night at Joes. Ill be there next time im in town! Grazie! Ciao! Muah!

top_reviews.content: This is one of the real jewels for eating well prepared seafood and a beautiful view. I went here recently for my birthday.  The whole experience was wonderful! We started with the market salad with grilled peaches and artichokes. The ceviche with house made chips. AmThe eggplant Katsu.  All were really great but the star of the show was the eggplant katsu! Surprisingly awesome! Our entrees were the grilled swordfish with green papaya and the grilled Dorado with chili braised cabbage. Both were very fresh and well prepared.  The service was excellent and professional! A magical birthday experience!

Best views, beautiful ambiance, and exceptional service from Brian and his colleagues. The food was delicious, and I couldn’t have asked for a better birthday lunch experience. I love that they offer a reservation system, and everyone here is genuinely warm and welcoming. The restaurant itself is a vibe…elegant, inviting, and beautifully designed. The two large fish tanks really elevate the entire dining room and create a unique atmosphere. The martini was also excellent. This is exactly why I keep coming back time and time again.

Lovely bar lounge upon entry with sweeping views of the Bay Bridge.

Top quality seafood, highest levels of freshness. Excellent option for raw bar, with Seafood Tower coming with half dozen oysters and clams, half lobster, shrimp and crab cocktails as well as ceviche served with tostones.

Menu flavors are clean and simple — though notably, not heavy on spice (i.e classically New American)

Perfect for celebrating a special occasion.

Had a great time at Waterbar with some friends a few days ago. The atmosphere was incredible and the view on the terrace was top-tier. Staff was friendly, and a special mention to Pete who was very welcoming and hospitable. All the food we tried, especially the fish and seafood, was phenomenal. It was all cooked to perfection and full of flavor. The dessert was decadent and completed our meal beautifully. No alcohol for me, but the mocktail I had was refreshing and delicious. Definitely a must if you’re visiting San Francisco!

First time in this restaurant. We went to celebrate our 12th Anniversary. The restaurant had an amazing detail leaving us a card with the signature of each employee congratulating us. The atmosphere is very welcome and cozy. The two fish tanks make the place unique. Also, the view to bay bridge make my night. Food exquisite.

name: In-N-Out Burger

top_reviews.content:
In-N-Out Burger is one of those places that feels simple in the best way possible. The menu is short, which honestly makes ordering less stressful, and everything feels intentional. You go there knowing you’re getting burgers, fries, and shakes—no distractions. The burgers are fresh, juicy, and taste like they were actually made when you ordered, not pulled from a heat lamp. The toasted buns and crisp lettuce make everything feel balanced instead of greasy.

The fries are probably the most debated part. On their own, they’re hit or miss since they’re fresh-cut and not super crispy, but ordering them “animal style” changes everything. With cheese, grilled onions, and sauce, they’re way more satisfying. The shakes are thick, classic, and not overly sweet, which makes them easy to finish.

What really stands out is the price and consistency. For how good the food is, it’s surprisingly affordable, especially compared to other fast-food chains. The staff is usually friendly and upbeat, and the restaurant stays pretty clean even when it’s packed. Overall, In-N-Out isn’t trying to be fancy—it just does fast food really well, and that’s why people love it.

Even though this location is usually busy, the staff were friendly, efficient, and kept the service moving smoothly. Drive through line was reaching around the block, so be wary of that. I walked in for takeout and took about 15 minutes for a good amount of food. Solid food, but be prepared to wait if youre doing drive through

I've always been told that if I'm in Cali I need to try IN & OUT burger.  Nice spot. I liked how minimal their menu was. Plus they also have another menu you have to ask about. Loved the idea of free peppers with your burgers. I appreciate that they make a note to say FRESH FRIES! Cause there's really nothing better than that. Pretty reasonable price for a combo for what I've seen from burger joints in Cali..which is a plus to me. Great experience.

We were beyond impressed with the entire operation at In-N-Out from the moment we pulled in to the moment we left. The drive-thru was absolutely packed, and the inside was buzzing with customers, yet everything ran so smoothly. The restaurant was spotless, and the atmosphere felt both welcoming and organized. We were greeted right away, and to our surprise, our order was ready within just a few minutes.

The food exceeded expectations — the burgers were juicy and flavorful with perfectly crisp buns, and the French fries tasted incredibly fresh, cooked to that ideal balance of not too soft and not too hard. What stood out even more was the staff. They kept the place immaculate, cleaning continuously and keeping the kitchen running like a well-oiled machine.

It’s rare to see such efficiency and quality in such a busy setting. This In-N-Out sets the bar high for fast food — highly recommend stopping by!
This is essentially the same experience you get with every In N Out in California, and its a great one. Bonus points for giving me a BUNCH of extra spread
