top_reviews.content:
Had a solid experience at Viks Chaat. The food definitely leans very spicy, so be prepared if you’re sensitive to heat, but there’s still good flavor throughout the menu. The setup is more cafeteria-style than a traditional sit-down restaurant, which gives it a casual, bustling atmosphere that fits the place well.

The portions are generous and overall it’s good value for the money, especially considering Bay Area prices. The lamb biriyani stood out as a particularly good deal — hearty, flavorful, and filling. Pairing it with one of their draught lagers worked really well and balanced the spice nicely.

Not the place for a quiet upscale dining experience, but if you want satisfying Indian comfort food with solid portions and a lively atmosphere, it’s worth checking out.

Viks is a great one stop for groceries and Indian home style food.

The lunch thali is great at the price point with tandoori chicken or lamb, a daal, rice and a roti.

The chole bature is great. The chole has some tamarind chutney for that nice sour tangyness and some raw red onions and mango pickle. The bhatura is always piping hot and fried to order.

The tandoori chicken was nice and juicy but you don't get the smoky taste from a tandoor. Daal was nice and home style with not too much butter/ghee.

The dahi puri was cool and refreshing.

The lamb was nice but I prefer goat.

Not much ambience and service is self service.

I love to get mango lassi from the supermarket.

All in all will be back again and again.

Viks in Berkeley is a cool hybrid cafeteria and market. No tipping, super fast service, and the whole place—from the restrooms to the dining area—is spotless. The food leans mostly sweet and sour. The Mango Lassi is basically the Indian version of Mango Pomelo Sago—mind-blowingly good!
The only downside was the first cashier, who looked completely over life. Turns out they forgot my Mango Lassi, which you're supposed to get right after ordering. I only figured it out while waiting for my food when I saw the next cashier hand a drink to another customer immediately.
Overall verdict: Definitely worth coming back.

Overall okay kind of restaurant. Not bad but not good that one can miss. Self service mess type atmosphere, clean your own table, can be huge lines when peak time, food quality is bringing street side flavor but prices are mid scale restaurant.

An amazing place serving Indian chaat. Can get crowded on the weekends, but still the service is pretty quick. Plenty of seating options both indoors and outdoors. We ordered Chole Bhature, Dahi Batata Puri, Pav Bhaji, Kaathi roll and Samosas. The Samosad were top notch, followed by Dahi Batata Puri, Bhatura was amazing but Chole could have been little more flavorful. Pav Bhajj and Kathi roll were decent but not very amazing. They serve Campa Cola too.

top_reviews.content:
Fantastic food, atmosphere and view. The waitress was horribly inattentive, but the other waitstaff were very helpful.

The (chilled) Dungeness crab was fresh, full and sweet. Delicious! Great presentation too.

Chose a dozen mixed raw oysters. The Sweetwater and Kumamoto were my favs. Well balanced and not too briny.

Ordered some grilled oysters too. Really like the bourbon chipotle. Nice mild smokiness and spice.

Michelin star in 2005. Food exemplified that star on my visit.

Oysters were good, food was good, but the Clam Chowder was the best!!!

We went to a Giants game and came here after, it was crowded from the stadium but they were able to seat us much faster than we expected!

Ordered appetizers only since we ate a lot at the game.

The Clam Chowder was the best and creamiest! It was delicious!

The oysters and clams were fresh!

The soft shelled crab was kind of bland so I added the oyster sauce to it to give it flavor.  The lady we saw who ordered had a huge crab, we got 2 tiny ones in our sandwich.

I've been to Hog Island where you can buy your oysters and shuck them yourself. It's a great outing. BUT my hubby picked me up from the airport and I was craving oysters before we drove back home, so we stopped here for dinner.

We had the oyster bar mix (twice) we split the clamp chowder. Red abalone with salmon roe. And tried the BBQ oysters with Chipotle butter. And got some fries for our toddler.

The abalone was so delicious, it was devoured shortly. My favorite oysters were all from hog island. They did have some from Maryland, which to me weren't sweet and were very bring. Just not my cup of tea, they weren't bad. Just in comparison to the tamales bay oysters, they were no match.

The claim chowder was okay...just a cream and butter base with leeks, with full clams in their shell. Now, while I appreciate have full chunks of clams, I did NOT appreciate having cracked clam shells that I ended up crunching on. (Spuds clam chowder is my favorite. Bold flavor, lots of clams, potatoes, garlic, the whole works). To me this chowder just lacked flavor and needed the clam shells removed.

But the Main reason we were there was because of the oysters. And they were so good we got another dozen. Over all, very good food, service was pretty good for being busy, (they refilled water jugs like ninjas), I would just not suggest the clam chowder.

Very busy at lunchtime on a Saturday - wait time outside was about 20 minutes or so and it was well worth it.  Clam chowder was excellent - very hearty, plenty of clams, and used my bread to insure I was able to get the last drops of broth.  Prices were $$$. Very friendly staff - service was fast.

We had an amazing experience and loved everything. Food, service, prices, ambience.

We had:
• the bread and butter, and you can immediately tell the bread is bakery-made —absolutely delicious.

• oyster bar mix, fresh and flavorful

• the smoked oysters were outstanding as well.

• 🌟mussels, with fries or pasta which both were fantastic. The white wine broth was so rich and delicious that after finishing the mussels, we found ourselves drinking the remaining broth.

• 🌟soft-shell crab sandwich, when it arrived, we were shocked to see a whole crab between the buns, we had never seen that before. At first, we weren’t sure we would like it, but we were completely wrong. The shell is incredibly soft, and once fried, you can barely tell it’s there. The crab was perfectly cooked, well seasoned, and absolutely delicious. We would highly recommend this sandwich to anyone, even if it looks unusual at first.

The service was excellent, the music created a great atmosphere, and we had a wonderful time overall. We can’t wait to come back!

top_reviews.content: The salt&pepper crab was cooked perfectly to retain the sweetness of the fresh crab.  The baked Chilean sea bass was very good though the size was pretty small for the price.  The mixed veggies deluxe was also excellent.  Free hot tea.  The restaurant was extremely busy for a weeknight so reservation was a must.  Call to reserve to get more open slots than reserved on line.

Passed in front of this place so many times, never really giving it any credit. But it’s actually a pretty big spot! It also gets very busy during lunchtime, so get here before 11:30 if you want to skip the line! The menu is robust, they have a lot of dishes to choose from. It’s definitely a bit heavy on the salt side, but might appeal to most people (I avoid salty foods). It’s definitely well seasoned and you can taste it. Everything I ate was good, although nothing blew me away, it is a solid option. I also saw a lot of people eating their crab noodles, which definitely stands out when looking around. Maybe I’ll give it a try next time.

R&G Lounge definitely lived up to its reputation.

When I first walked up, there was a huge crowd gathered outside, and I almost left because I assumed the wait would be an hour or more. Thankfully, I went inside anyway and put my name on the waitlist. Since I was dining solo, I was seated in less than 3 minutes. Most of the people waiting outside were larger groups, so if you're by yourself, don't let the crowd discourage you. Walk-ins are available daily.

The restaurant was busy and full of families, so it was definitely lively and a little noisy, but the service was fast and attentive throughout my meal.

I ordered the Half Peking Duck, Honey Walnut Prawns, and a Guava Juice.

The Peking Duck was excellent. The skin was beautifully crisp, the meat was tender and juicy, and the steamed buns with hoisin sauce and scallions brought everything together perfectly.

The Honey Walnut Prawns were another standout. Large shrimp, perfectly cooked, with a rich creamy sauce balanced by the sweetness and crunch of the candied walnuts.

The guava juice was refreshing and paired well with the meal.

After a disappointing experience at another restaurant earlier in the evening, R&G Lounge completely turned my night around. Great food, quick service, and a restaurant I'd gladly return to the next time I'm craving authentic Cantonese cuisine in San Francisco.

Party of 3 immediately sat on Thursday 8/27 for lunch time

For the most part, enjoyed everything and service was decent! I really appreciated the complimentary hot tea upon being seated. Between the 3 of us, I think we all had just 1-2 notes about each dish but overall, good visit.

Excellent lobster with sticky fried rice and salt & pepper crab. Only complaints are: server did not give a good estimate of what the costs would be so the bill was a surprise, and when I asked if 4 dishes was too much for 3 people he encouraged me to order everything (and it ended up being way too much food), which tells me he was more interested in making money than serving the best interest of the customer and being honest. The food was great so I have no complaints there, but the service needs training

top_reviews.content: Public Market Emeryville was just a hop and a skip from our hotel so we ended up there a couple times. One night we had Japanese tonkatsu to go, and one night we ate in, having Korean bento box! Tuesday is trivia night with teams competing against each other, and although we didn't stay, we could hear the laughter and fun going on over the speaker. Big screen TV was great for the sports enthusiasts watching the world soccer series. Public market was really convenient for us since we were without a car. Easy to walk to, good people, great food!
Second time being here. The first time, there was a live band playing. It's pretty loud for us so we sat farther away. There were folks real close, so some people are fine with it.

There are so many great food options that everyone can find something they like, which makes it perfect for meeting up with friends. I also love that it’s a comfortable place to get some work done if you want a change of scenery. During the World Cup, they had the matches playing on projectors throughout the market, which created such a fun atmosphere and made it feel like a community event.

I haven't been here for many years and I remember back than that there were more restaurants and little eateries, now I only see a few places and a majority of the places close up early.  Came here on a Saturday 6pm and most places were closing up at 8pm. Great market to catch a meal whether you are going solo, with family or a larger group!

top_reviews.content: Great vibes all around. The place feels welcoming the moment you walk in, and the energy is just right lively but not loud. The pizza tasted clean and fresh, which made it super easy to enjoy without feeling heavy afterward. The beer selection was solid too and paired perfectly with the food. Overall, a really good spot. I’d definitely go again.

After recommendations from three locals to try this spot, I couldn't ignore it anymore.

I got the eutropia and the wings. The naming of the pizzas as celestial bodies is quite cute. The eutropia was very good and dare I say it tastes better after reheating as leftovers.

The wings tossed with honey Sriracha were good but the ranch was something special. I asked one of the staff what it was and they told me regular ranch. I felt like I was being gas lit in real time, it didn't look like regular ranch and it for sure tasted better than regular ranch. My waitress came over and I asked her the same question and she let me know it was special house made ranch with dill and other ingredients! Thank you! I would have had crashed out if this flavor came from thousand island or some bottled ranch and re-evaluated my life. Needless to say I took that shit home and dipped my leftover pizza. A+ ranch!

What a hidden gem in Berkeley!
I was in the mood for good, authentic pizza — and as someone from New York, I’m definitely spoiled — but this place really impressed me. The pizza was amazing, and the manager, Sami, went above and beyond to get us a great table and make sure our food and drinks were perfect. I really appreciated his friendliness, and even our server mentioned what a great manager he is. I’ll definitely be coming back — not just for the food, but for the hospitality and the wonderful atmosphere. 🥰

Came in for pizza and beer here because this used to be my husband's favorite place when he was in college at uc berkeley!
We were a large group and took some time to decide on the seating and the menu - and the server was so patient with us🙏
We got four pizzas and they were all so good! If I had to pick a favorite, it would probably be Circe. The outdoor space was heated and wonderful.

Decent pizza, lots of options and a nice restaurant and outdoor patio space. Extensive beer selection but unfortunately they were out of the first three I wanted so I settled for a fourth option. Note that they can't split checks which is not a big deal. Just plan accordingly.

What a treat it was to find an outdoor venue with so many different dining options.
We were at the nearby UCSF hospital for Business & were looking for a casual bite to eat nearby, here in the Mission bay area. We decided on the Parkland gardens side. It had several outdoor seating options. There were couches, wood picnic tables with benches or little cafe 2-tops. They even had 2 Large tee-pee style covered areas with tvs in them. The food truck just inside had an amazing selection of seafood & comfort foods. We were not disappointed at all! Once we finished, we walked around & found the photo booths & mini-golf course. They had several fire pit seating areas, which would be great for a cozy cup of cocoa & s'mores. If you are looking for a great casual outdoor atmosphere with great food options for everyone in your group...this is your place.
We went to during one of the World Cup matches. Ambience was great and lots of options for food as there were many many food trucks. I loved the Cajun grilled chicken salad and boba drink next to it.

We had such a wonderful experience bringing our preschool kids to Spark Social SF for mini golf and outdoor play! The space is safe, fun, and perfect for young children to explore and enjoy themselves. The kids loved the mini golf area, open seating, and playful atmosphere. Staff were friendly, and there was plenty of room for our group to relax and have fun. A fantastic spot for preschool outings and family-friendly activities. We’ll definitely be back!

Was very excited to check out this multi-block project! I'm always looking for ideas to bring back to my community Parks Board and this area did not disappoint. So many amenities packed in one area , truly something for everyone!

Booked The Enclave for our post-wedding lunch and it was such a great decision and our guests keep talking about how it was such a unique wedding lunch.

The Enclave (1 bungalow, 2 cabanas) were very spacious for our 42 guests and for kids to run around in. This was on March 21st at the end of a heat wave so the bungalow did get pretty toasty at noon but it cooled down.

Leading up to the event the organizers sent out very clear emails once we booked our private cabanas. At one point the organizers were very accommodating about a miscommunication involving a discount code.

Pre-paying tickets for our guests ended up being such an easy system. Each ticket is a dollar and you can use them at any food truck. By the end of the lunch everyone was full and trying to find ways to spend all the tickets.

top_reviews.content: A well-oiled machine for distribution of delicious baked goods.  As a newbie to the bakery, I ended up going in the wrong door and found myself at the coffee station, but what I should have done is follow the line of people waiting for their go at the counter to order.  The morning is peak time for buying baked goodies, and the vibe of the bakery is that the crowd were either locals or (many time) repeat customers.  After the quick progression to the counter from entering, I was greeted by a wall of delicious looking bread of all varieties.  The Asiago olive loaf was my first sampling, and I toasted it to add a little crispiness once I got it home.  The mix of slightly baked onions and olives in the sinewy loaf was amazing, the cheese being a lovely accent.  It made me wish I had bought at least one more.  The scones were the real bread all-stars for me.  The corn-cherry scones were so damned hearty.  The corn meal added an even richer texture to the scone, so I loved it even more, but the crown jewel of the scones was the oat-cranberry scone.  The crust was this and crispy, and the inside was perfectly crumbly and soft.  Definitely buying that again on my next visit.   So many things still on the menu that I want to try.  The cost performance of this bakery is incredible.  The only hassle is parking in the area, which being in Berkeley means it’s going to be awful just about all of the time.  The staff was effective as hell and got me through quickly, but the staff seemed willing to step me through examining some of the offerings, but customer speed did seem to be valued as part of the bread buying experience.
Hands down, the best pizza I had in my life. Every day, they prepare only one kind of veggie pizza. There is always line, but moves fast. Don’t miss it, if you are around.

Finally made it to the Cheese Board Pizza Collective in Berkeley — a spot I’ve wanted to try for years.

They serve one style of pizza a day, and when it’s gone, it’s gone. Today’s slice with baby chard and kale, leek, mozzarella, ricotta salata, garlic olive oil, and citrus zest was fresh, unique, and seriously good.

I’m usually a simple pizza guy, but this one delivered. Absolutely worth the wait. A true Berkeley staple.

Popped in on April 30 and tried the mushroom pizza + salad. They do a different vegan pizza every day. As a huge meat lover, I was surprised by how much I liked the mushroom one. The staff were super sweet and even gave me an extra slice! Also, the salad was so fresh, and that green sauce is so good that I bought a small tub to take home.

Love that it’s a worker-owned co-op with a classic Berkeley feel. Their website is actually super helpful too. You can check the daily pizza/bakery menu and live music schedule before you go.
MUST Visit this place especially if you are a strict vegetarian. You CANNOT go wrong with their quality and hygiene. Be ready to wait for 15-20 mins in line to enjoy the pizza

top_reviews.content:
Nice seafood restaurant with a view of the beach and the Bay. It was very busy when we arrived. Getting a parking space was tough because a lot of beachgoers also use this same parking.
Starting with calamari, it was a hit and was everyone’s favorite. Salads were well presented and tasted very good. Short ribs was super tender but personally I’d prefer having more texture/chewiness. Cioppino was at good portion size with lots of seafoods. All tasted very fresh.
Our server worked super hard and was very helpful when making sure he served beyond all our needs.

Beach Chalet is one restaurant that everyone should try. The restaurant itself is historic and has morals all around. The staff is very friendly. You can order appetizers, or full plates. The drinks (alcohol) are also good. The view is the main attraction. But you must reserve the window inorder to seat there. The brussels sprouts, were my favorite of all. The crab cakes was crabby when I tell you. I did not even want to share, but I was in a group setting that was the whole purpose is to share. Would I go back? Yes, I would.

Location, location, location...
I reckon everything comes down to the prime location of Beach Chalet. Get a window seat to watch the coastal views of the bay and enjoy a sunset if possible.

The food was just OK, nothing was good, great or outstanding, including the beer. Also the service is a bit of something to be desired as well. We came here on a whim, we didn't have reservations, so we did expect an long wait and were also OK with sitting at the bar.

We ended up at the bar, the hostess mentioned there was nothing available, but never gave us a wait time. We saw a few spots open at the bar, so we just opted to grab them. There was only one bartender working his tail off. He was very backed up and didn't have any help. We wanted to be as respectful as possible, so we tried bother him as little as possible. We definitely spent a decent amount of  time waiting. Finally some back up arrived; pleasant fellow, but didn't move with much urgency. Took our orders and disappeared for a bit. The wait for the food wasn't actually that bad. The kitchen staff was stacked...

STARTERS:
~ Steamed Mussels - 3.5/5
Simple steamed Mussels. They were just OK. The sauce was nice, if you let the Sourdough bread soak it up. Nothing to rave about.

~ Buttermilk Fried Calamari - 2.5/5
Meh. The Calamari were NOT crispy at all. Actually they were fairly soggy. Flavor was OK.

DINNER:
- SEAFOOD:
~ Crab Carbonara - 2.5/5
Another dish that was just OK. Far to pricey for the amount of Crab they put in there...I think it might have been one leg! I kid you not!! Honestly, I can make this better. I'd go as far as to say, the frozen Carbonara from Trader Joe's is better. Might not be a fair comparison as it actually came from Italy...

~ Chalet Beer Sampler - 2/5
I was curious about the beers when I realized Beach Chalet was also a brewery. I opted for the Beer sampler when I found out all the beers were made in house. Meh. I thought the Blonde was the best one they had. They also ran out of a few beers.

Best thing about our evening was the parking, lol. The ambiance is brilliant, that's about it for me. Can't see myself voluntarily returning...

Eclectic design. Ocean views. I've been here a few times, twice for brunch and once for dinner. It's never overly crowded and I don't know why. The Caesar salad was a work of art, with large romaine leaves topped with an anchovy dressing and shaved Parmesan (also had real anchovies on the salad!)
The clam chowder was fresh & creamy, with large clams.
The ribeye was perfectly cooked, with a lightly charred outside & tender inside. The truffle mac and cheese was a delight. The lobster tail with melted butter was succulent. The seasonal fruit crisp with vanilla ice cream was absolutely divine and a perfect ending to a delicious meal. All with a wonderful and attentive server who made sure our water glasses were never empty. Perfect for a special occasion.

My wife and I stopped by for Sunday brunch.  I made a reservation via Yelp, however, it was unnecessary as there appeared to be plenty of available seating at 11:30 a.m.  The hostess greeted us with a smile and sat us by the window where we had an unobstructed view of the beach and the Pacific Ocean (it was a beautiful day by the beach in the City, which is not a common event).

We ordered the lemon ricotta beignets, which were fine, but a little too dense for our liking.  I chased down the beignets with a Manhattan.  I got the Mahi Mahi served over coconut rice accompanied by string beans.  The presentation was nice and it tasted good.  Nothing necessarily special, but still delicious.  My wife ordered the 1/2 pound burger and fries which she enjoyed.

Our server, Gerald, was friendly and attentive.  My wife and I are fairly simple dining folk ("low maintenance") so we did not require much attention during our meal.  Gerald still kept an eye on us and filled up my water glass without having to ask, cleared our plates when we were done, and provided us with boxes to wrap up some of the beignets and half of my wife's burger.

The drinks, appetizer beignets, and entrees were served at a good pace.  Our drinks came first, promptly followed by the beignets.  As we were finishing with the beignets (we left half to take home), our entrees were delivered.

The view was spectacular from where we sat.  The restaurant seemed clean and neat.  I do wish the windows were cleaner/clearer, but given how windy it gets along the beach and the volume of sand that blows, I can see that it might require daily exterior window cleaning, which would not be financially feasible.  The noise level was fine.  It was slightly loud as there was a table of about 8 or 10 guests sat by us, but the sound level and ambiance were fine.

Although I opine the meal was a bit pricey for what we got, given the spectacular elevated view of the beach and the fact that the restaurant is located in San Francisco, it would be unfair of me to say that the menu was overpriced.  They do charge a SF healthcare tax/fee (I think it was 5% or 6%).

Only in SF will I pay $25 for tacos and not get mad about it. The various meats were delicious, the tortillas fresh, and I’ve never had such flavorful black beans, like really good beans. The restaurant has great vibes and pleasant staff.

Always a fan of mexican cuisine.. but this place was even better.

Everything was exceptional, the birria tacos were melting in my mouth.. and the carne asada ones were almost as food.

but the chile relleno was the surprise of the evening, mildly spicy with so much flavour.

The classic margarita was 10/10, but the other ones were just so sweet, not a fan. Highly recommend the classic one!

One of the best restaurants I’ve ever been to. The atmosphere is on point, the food is a culinary delight, and the drinks are perfect. We are PICKY. Even the chips and salsa are better. Service was great, very attentive. We devoured the meal 🍽️

🍹 Came for One Drink, Stayed for the Vibe

I've been coming to Tropisueño for years, but last night was something special.

The food was amazing as always, and the cocktails were spot on, but the bartenders completely made the night. They were having fun, interacting with everyone at the bar, making killer drinks, and creating the kind of atmosphere that makes you want to stay for "just one more."

You know those rare places where the staff's energy elevates the entire experience? That was exactly what happened. These guys were talented, personable, and genuinely seemed to love what they do. Watching them work together behind the bar was almost as enjoyable as the drinks themselves.

I've had a lot of good experiences at Tropisueño over the years, but this was easily one of the most memorable. It's not often you leave a restaurant talking more about the people than the food, but that's exactly what happened.

Huge thanks to the bartenders for making a great night even better. I'll definitely be back soon.

🍹🌮❤️

top_reviews.content: Z & Y Restaurant was a great Chinatown dining experience. The Peking duck was excellent, with a beautiful smoky flavor and perfectly roasted skin. You can really taste the technique behind it. The shrimp fried rice was also very good, flavorful, well cooked, and satisfying. Overall, the food felt authentically Sichuan, bold, aromatic, and full of character. Definitely worth trying if you’re looking for real Chinese food in San Francisco Chinatown.

Absolutely fantastic food. They do not hold back the spice. Both the food and service were top notch. It does get crowded and the place is small. Make reservations beforehand. They will greet you with Kung fu tea which I found very cool. Overall I loved everything about the restraunt. I will definitely go there again.

The food was delicious and authentic. What was “medium” spicy burned through our throats but tasty nonetheless. The tea-smoked duck was great, but it should be bundled with greens, sauce and wrappers by default cause it makes no sense any other way - it could just be $10 more expensive and come as a package. Other than that the service was good and the overall experience well worth a Michelin Bib-Gourmand.

I was a bit surprised by the comments here, because the actual ratings don’t seem to match my experience, I’m usually hesitant to judge a restaurant, especially when it comes to food from not my background, but for a place associated with the Michelin Guide or positioned in this price range, I think it should at least start with good quality ingredients. I think most people just saying good because Chinese cuisine have a strong fry and good chili oil culture, but that doesn't mean we should just say tasty to every meal that taste like it (referencing the comments).

Unfortunately, many of the reviews here feel driven more by hype, after visiting, I noticed a “leave a comment and get a free dessert” sign, which might help explain the inflated ratings.

The food wasn’t bad, but in this area there are definitely better and more affordable options, I just want to say, I didn’t try every item on the menu, but I’m not willing to spend $100+ just to fully evaluate the place.

I wouldn’t normally be this critical, but the experience was frustrating, especially with waitress asking for the tip and being mad not receiving, added service charge with a table that didn’t even have basic items like salt or napkins.

Don't think that I'm mad, this is just a objective review in the end.

This restaurant in Chinatown is a perfect 10/10. The food is incredible with so many amazing choices. Service is great and although you may have to wait, it’s well worth it! Michelin star, served multiple international heads of state - the door has more prestigious awards than I thought possible… if you go to one place in China town, Z & Y won’t disappoint!

reviews_snippets.content: "This place def give hole in a wall vibes and staff was very friendly and kind."

name: Taqueria El Paisa
address: 4610 International Blvd, Oakland, CA 94601, United States

google.address: 4610 International Blvd, Oakland, CA 94601, United States
services: Does not have assistive hearing loop
google.description: No-frills neighborhood spot serving up informal Mexican grub such as tacos, burritos & tortas.

top_reviews.content:
Getting here right after opening is the best move if you want to beat the massive rush this place gets later in the day. Plus, I managed to snag free street parking right around the corner.

There was practically no line when I arrived, so I only waited about a minute before the gentleman behind the counter took my order. The ordering area itself is incredibly festive—stepping inside genuinely makes you feel like you've been transported straight back to Mexico. They carve the meats and serve up your tacos in no time, and then you just follow the counter down a few steps to the cash register. That’s where you order your drinks before paying and heading out to find a seat.

The covered patio is decked out in a heavy Mexican theme, making it a great, vibrant space to sit down and eat. If it gets packed, there’s actually a second dining area tucked further back if you need some breathing room. I’m assuming they get absolutely slammed at peak hours, which explains why the setup is so practical. A very nice touch is that they have napkin dispensers scattered everywhere—the tables further out back even have their own dedicated dispensers, which is incredibly smart when you're dealing with messy street food. They also have a fully stocked salsa bar where you can grab extra garnishes and radishes to dress up your plate.

I noticed another reviewer mentioned the tacos were small, but that completely misrepresents the reality here. These tacos hold up beautifully and are incredibly substantial. The corn tortillas have a distinct, rich corn flavor and don't fall apart under the heavy meats, and every single house-made salsa tastes vibrant and fresh.

Suadero Taco: Easily one of the best suadero tacos in Oakland. The slow-cooked beef is executed flawlessly, hitting that perfect balance of a deeply savory, crispy outer bark while keeping the meat underneath incredibly tender and juicy. Topped with their coarse red salsa and a whole grilled jalapeño, the bright acidity cuts right through the rich beef fat.

Tripa Taco: I ordered this purely as an experiment to see how their kitchen handles it. I’ve actively avoided tripe for decades, but I wanted to push my palate a bit. Ultimately, the intrinsic flavor of tripe just doesn't appeal to my taste buds. That said, the kitchen's execution is flawless, and if you actually enjoy authentic offal, you won't find a single thing to complain about here.

Lengua Taco: The tongue is perfectly poached—melt-in-your-mouth tender, incredibly clean, and a fantastic contrast to the rich chew of the suadero.

All three proteins have completely distinct, defined flavors and textures. Having traveled extensively through Central and Southern Mexico, I can confidently say this is about as legitimate as street food gets on US soil.

To wash it all down, I opted for a large Mango Agua Fresca. Visually, the bright orange tropical juice looks incredible sitting next to a rustic tray of glistening tacos, but functionally, it’s a brilliant palate cleanser. The crisp, sweet acidity cuts straight through the heavy fats of the beef, instantly resetting your taste buds between bites. It’s an essential part of the meal.

Taqueria El Paisa puts on a textbook demonstration of authentic DF-style street food mechanics. Pairing the rich, savory meats with a massive fruit agua fresca is a flawless strategy. If you want a bulletproof, elite taco experience, this spot belongs at the top of your list.
The best tacos in the bay. Friendly & fast service! + they have a salsa bar. The Al Pastor & Suadero tacos were my favorite. The horchata was also veryyyy good!

Taqueria el Paisa is the spot for tacos.I had not driven to Oakland for tacos in a while because it was a turn off.Every taqueria had small,dried,minced meat looking tacos.The salsas where unfavorable and believe even if they had a good salsa that would over power the taste of the unfavorable meat that would be one thing.But my tío and tía took me here to Taqueria el Paisa Giiirrrrlllll! Let me tell you it's a whole experience.You order your tacos, burritos quesadillas tortas and they have other plate options.They have Aguas Frescas and other drinks.After you order and pay your order you move over to next line which is basically next 5 steps and you have all these guys ready to prepare your food.Tjey have a variety of meats carne asada,tripitas,buche,carnitas,suadero,chorizo,carnitas etc...The tacos are to die for they serve you so much meat like for 3 tacos.The meats have so much flavor.The tortilla is warm cooked to perfection,Its not oily or tearing apart like other places.They have a salsa bar where you have a variety of salsas.The one with avocado is spicy but it's spicy good.But beware because if you're not use to heat it will ruin your tacos.I did the mistake of putting lots couse of the avocado 🥵 and the horchata helped but the spiciness took from my experience.But I've come back all the way from Livermore for them tacos.My husband had a Burrito and he said it was delicious lots of meat not like every other taqueria that gives you a burrito of rice and beans and little meat.it was giant.Yiu can sit inside and outside.They have big screen ti's the ambience is great everyone is enjoying their food.They have parking and street parking.The service is quick and the food is delicious 😋  come check them out yourselves.This is the spot.

I was very disappointed with my burrito and tacos. The chicken was super dry and overcooked. The beef brisket was also dry and tough. The parking lot is basically Costco and inside is hectic. The staff are incredibly nice. I was looking forward to a good experience considering online reviews but the only good part was the tortilla and grilled onions. Also my burrito had a few chopped up chicken bones. It’s been a few hours now and I just feel sick. I would recommend avoiding.

Some of the best tacos in Oakland! Don't sleep on the chicken taco, my go-to is usually 2 or 3 tacos: chicken and carne Asada. Highly recommend taking a moment to enjoy the space and eating there, the food will be warm, fresh, and delicious.

reviews_snippets.content: "Quick service, excellent food, good variety and tasty spicy sauces."
"Omg this place is the bomb on there tacos and quesadillas with meat."
"My favorite taco spot that's legit and offer a great selection of options."

name: HINODEYA Ramen Union Square
address: 219 O'Farrell St, San Francisco, CA 94102, United States

top_reviews.content: We found this small popular lively ramen shop when we arrived to San Francisco in the evening.  We tried their unique clam ramen and karage. The ramen was fresh and the clam broth was light and flavorful with a refreshing beer. It was a perfect meal after a long trip. Please use the machine in front of the door to join the waitlist. Waiting on line without joining it would not get you into the que.

A delightful little ramen restaurant featuring a beautiful Japanese-style wood interior. There is seating for about 15 pairs of diners, one slightly longer table, and a few outdoor tables as well. The food is fantastic. The menu offers around three or four dishes at a time—options include vegetarian, spicy, and meat-based varieties—which can be paired with Japanese beer or sake if desired. Prices range from $20 to $30 per dish. Anyone who loves Japanese udon soup will be more than satisfied here—a fact attested to by the many Asian patrons.

After several great meals in San Francisco, this was one of the surprises of the trip. The ramen was outstanding from the first bite to the last, with a rich, flavorful broth, fresh noodles, and quality toppings that all came together perfectly.

The star of the bowl was the poached egg. I’ve eaten a lot of eggs over the years, and this was hands down the best poached egg I’ve ever had. Perfectly cooked with an unbelievably creamy yolk that made every bite even better.

The atmosphere was upbeat and energetic without feeling rushed, and the service matched the food—friendly, attentive, and genuinely welcoming. If you’re staying near Union Square and craving ramen, this is an easy recommendation. We’ll definitely be back the next time we’re in San Francisco.

This ramen shop is located right near Union Square, in a bustling area with high foot traffic.
Indoor and outdoor seating available. Outdoor area may be a little noisy (central location). Vegetarian ramen options included! The prices are very reasonable, staying on par with shops in other neighborhoods.
I was honestly shocked to learn that this place has been around since 1885. It is one of the most impressive ramen spots my family and I have ever visited in terms of flavor. My Aunt—an older Asian laddy who is quite particular about her food—really enjoyed her meal here, which says a lot.
The broth is packed with umami and perfectly seasoned. Out of all the places I've been, this ramen is hands-down my favorit
The staff are incredibly sweet and friendly. On the day of our visit, we were welcomed by a lovely girl from the Philippines.
We will definitely be coming back soon!

Paloma was a great server and provided excellent service. She checked on us so much, each time she came I had food in my mouth and couldn’t speak lol. The ramen was very good especially with this SF weather. I definitely recommend the gyoza and chicken karaage

reviews_snippets.content: "Staff is polite and food is served quick with good portion/price for the area."

top_reviews.content:
For my birthday, my wish was for Indian cuisine, and Aama’s Kitchen made it a memorable celebration. I’ve lived in the Bay Area since the 1980s and have eaten at many Indian restaurants. I discovered Aama’s Kitchen through a Google search, and its exceptionally high reviews convinced us to try it. They were well deserved.

The food, service, and atmosphere were all five-star. Sentos helped us choose dishes that matched our tastes and preferred level of spiciness, recommended a delicious wine, and was professionally attentive throughout our meal.

The balance of spices and flavors was extraordinary. We especially enjoyed the butter chicken, lamb tikka masala, Himalayan chicken momos, and butter naan. Every dish was distinctive, beautifully seasoned, and delicious.

The pièce de résistance was the pistachio kulfi, presented with a birthday candle — a lovely and completely unexpected ending to a wonderful birthday dinner.

Aama’s Kitchen is now firmly on our list of Bay Area restaurants worth returning to. Five stars without hesitation.
So far, so good. Looks clean nice vibe. Wish they had Vietnamese coffee but the spicy chai looks great. Bring your own stevia, all they have is sugar. Food is lovely.

Food was flavorful. I had the Garlic and Cheese Naan, Tandoori wrap, and Chicken Chowmein. Surprisingly their Chowmein was more flavorful than most of the Chinese restaurants where you would need to add soy sauce to bring out the flavor.

Their tandoori wrap is a little slim for the $18 price tag, but i wrapped it in a garlic naan and it filled me up. If you're a chilli head like me ask for the spicy sauce on the side. It adds another layer of flavor.

Try this place out, but with so many options around ill find it hard to go out of my way to come back.

Amazing food, fast service! I love Nepal food and have experienced many different types and this establishment is by far the best in the bay. Not only are they kind but they deliver their amazing countries cuisine so quickly! Sorry we ate it so fast so all you get is a picture of the cha!

We went there during the weekend But to my surprise being highly rated the food quality was not upto the mark. Being the vegetarian we ordered noodles, the food quality wasn’t great I would say the taste of noodles was too bad. And then we ordered dal and tandoori roti but the taste of dal was most of garlic like and we have to call server multiple times to provide dishes and all and then he did not even provide us with noodles sauces which was basic. Don’t think I will be going there again,

top_reviews.content:
Visited once for lunch and once for dinner. I like to come here for special occasions, though lunch prices are reasonable for a nice weekday meal! The food, especially seafood is really good.

I’m a big fan of the fried smelts, though they might be larger during winter/early spring season, as they were noticeably smaller when I came here in July. The octopus was very tender, and dolmades were easy to eat as well. For the main, I enjoyed the fish dish a lot more than the chicken. Chicken Souvlaki was not too substantial and felt a little flat compared to the fish.

For desserts, I’ve tried their frozen yogurt and loukoumades (donuts). Frozen yogurt texture is really interesting, stretchy like ice cream and not icy! The greek donuts were nicely crisp on the outside and soaked in spiced honey sauce.

Service is always friendly and attentive. looking forward to coming back!

Exceptional! Best meal in the city!

We loved the appetizers:
• The excellence of the zucchini cakes (kolokithokefteth) made a non-zucchini-lover eat the whole cake! Key to the success was the firmness of the zucchini slivers and adding the sauce and cucumber on top.

• The baked feta (feta tou fournou) was not salty (as often feta is) and eating it with the complimentary sourdough bread made for a great mix of flavors.

• Saghanaki did not come set on fire tableside with the “Opa!” celebrations as we’ve encountered numerous times at other restaurants, but the cheese was really delicious. (This cheese we found saltier than the baked feta.)

For the main meals: the whole sea bass tasted fresh and cooked to perfection, while the lamb was soft and flavorful. We’d recommend both.

Wish we had room for desserts, but the excellent cocktails added isn’t own sweetness.

Highly recommend!!

Kokkari Estiatorio was an easy choice when family visited from SoCal and wanted a nice dinner spot. We made a reservation about a week in advance, which I’d recommend since this place tends to stay busy. Expectations were high; one person in our group had been here before and spoke very highly of it, and it lived up to it. We were seated near the fireplace/oven, close to the bread station, which added a warm, lively touch to the overall atmosphere.

Our group of six decided to sample a bit of everything, so we ordered several mezze and salads to share, and they were all flavorful and well prepared. For entrées, we tried the salmon (Solomos), roasted chicken (Kotopoulo Souvlaki), and lamb chops; the lamb chops were easily the standout and a big hit at the table. We also shared a couple of desserts, and those were just as good as the rest of the meal. Portions are solid, and the quality is consistent across the board.

Service was excellent. Our server was attentive and handled our group, who can be a bit particular at times, very well, ensuring everyone was taken care of without feeling rushed. The dining space is fairly large and divided into sections, which helps keep the noise level manageable. One quick tip: the restrooms are downstairs and require an elevator ride, so plan ahead. Overall, it’s a great spot for a special meal, and I’d confidently recommend it in the city.

Kokkari Estiatorio: A San Francisco Masterclass

If you are looking for a "treat yourself" meal in the city, **Kokkari Estiatorio** is the gold standard. The vibe is impeccably classy—think rustic Mediterranean elegance with a warm, upscale energy that makes it perfect for a celebration.

The service truly elevated the night; our server, who introduced himself as "the prince," was phenomenal and kept the evening feeling special from start to finish.

**The Standout Mains**

**The Duck (Papia):** This is an absolute mandatory order for duck lovers. It is perfectly rendered, tender, and seasoned to highlight the rich flavor. The potatos were cooked in the duck oil that was dripping while roasting. What!

**The Pork Chop (Hirini Brizola):** This wood-grilled pork chop is legendary for a reason. The highlight is the crispy pork skin—it’s perfectly crackled and adds a salty, savory crunch that pairs beautifully with the juicy meat.

**The Sweet Finish**
We shared a beautiful spread of desserts including the airy
**Loukoumades** (Greek donuts) and the **Baklava** with vanilla-praline ice cream. They even added a "Happy Birthday" touch to the plate, which was a lovely gesture.

**​Reservations: Keep in mind that they require a $25 per person hold to secure a reservation, so be sure of your headcount when booking. This is through Open Table

**⚠️ A Quick Note on the Water**
Just a heads-up for large groups to avoid a surprise on the bill: we had a slight **miscommunication regarding the water**. One person at the table asked for carbonated water, while the rest of us specified "not carbonated." This was interpreted as a request for bottled water for the entire table. At **$10 a bottle**, we ended up with an unexpected **$90 charge for water** on the final tab. Definitely be extra clear if you just want standard tap for the table!

**Rating:** ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
**Price:** $$$$
**Perfect for:** Birthdays, anniversaries, or showing off the SF food scene to guests.

Kokkari was hands down one of the best dining experiences I had in San Francisco. From the moment we walked in, the restaurant had a warm, upscale atmosphere with incredible service that made the entire evening feel special.

We started with several appetizers, and every single one was outstanding. The Saganaki was perfectly crisp on the outside with a rich, creamy center. The Octapodaki was incredibly tender with just the right amount of char. The Kalamata—grilled olives stuffed with feta and fennel—was unlike anything I’ve had before and packed with amazing flavor. The Marithes Tiganites (crispy smelts) paired with the garlic potato skordalia was a surprise favorite, crispy, fresh, and absolutely delicious.

For our entrées, we ordered the ribeye and the lamb chops, and both were cooked to perfection. The ribeye was juicy, flavorful, and perfectly seasoned, while the lamb chops were tender, smoky, and some of the best I’ve ever had.

Everything we ordered tasted fresh, authentic, and beautifully prepared. Combined with the attentive service and inviting atmosphere, it’s easy to see why Kokkari is one of San Francisco’s most celebrated restaurants.

If you’re visiting San Francisco or looking for an unforgettable meal, Kokkari is an absolute must. I would return in a heartbeat. Highly recommend

top_reviews.content:
I've been meaning to try their BBQ since I just found out that they are the makers of the 4505 chicharrones pork rinds (great with pilsner or lager)!

Definitely would go again, tried their ribs and hot links. Links weren't too 'hot' but I didn't mind. Enjoyed them! Ribs were soft, smokey and flavorful. My rack did have a little too much fat; but It didn't take away from how good it was. Sides of potato salad and baked beans were excellent; sweet rolls were good also! Next time I'll try their brisket and other offerings!

Wish their BBQ sauces weren't so watery....maybe they were diluted? Shrug.

We had a real yen for some BBQ, and decided to try this place out.
Nice covered patio eating area, with heaters.
It's a good BBQ.... But not a great one.
The flavors just didn't wow.
And my wife and I both got mile indigestion afterwards.
On the plus side, the sweet potato fries were excellent!

This spot is a classic around here! Only outdoor seating (with heat lamps and partial roof covering) - they got drinks and burger stuff. Burgers are super yummy and juicy. They got other small plate options that are yummy but they are small and expensive. Overall this place frequently hits the spot but prob not ideal to come here a ton.

We ordered the beef brisket plate with spicy fries and beans. The beans were the surprise standout—rich and delicious. The fries had a nice kick, but the brisket itself was just okay—chewy and a bit tough, not something I’d rush back for.
The outdoor seating with wooden benches is dog-friendly, though it can get noisy with kids running around and dogs barking. I did appreciate the convenience of having a QR code with the table number to order anything extra once seated. On the bright side, the service was friendly and attentive.

The food is just phenomenal. Juicy, smoky burgers with char and toppings. Fries are crisp and salty perfection. Chill outdoor vibe, quick service, strong drinks. Pricey but worth it when you want a solid burger fix in SF, it's great!

top_reviews.content: Wonderful atmosphere, a long time San Francisco restaurant in the heart of North Beach. Espresso martini 🍸 was one of the better ones I had! The waiter was good, helped give me honest feedback of all dishes. Bread was soft (a bit harder on the sides for me) and I loved the fritto misto- everything was fresh, hot and seasoned perfectly. I got the Marry Me Farfalle and the cream sauce with sun dried tomatoes and fatty prosciutto was delicious. I wish there was more! The roasted chicken I added was too dry for me, next time I will try the prawns. I got a birthday warm vanilla butter cake and that was a highlight- I will be back for that dessert!

There was a 1 hour wait. But they immediately made room for us in the VIP room as they opened it up due to being busy for the holiday weekend. Was a beautiful deep green small cozy quiet room in the back away from all the noise. We loved the room. I think if we were seated in the main dining or even bar area it would have been way too loud for my liking in a holiday.

All our reviews: The fettuccine Alfredo was the best they’ve ever had. Grilled shrimp was great. The burger sandwich was really good, perhaps too large though. The veal parmigiana  was incredible with Ravioli in the side, again too large for one adult man. My veal piccata was good, wish I ordered it as chicken piccata instead, may have been slightly over cooked, with a side of gluten free penne pesto was incredible!

Everyone loved their dishes, everyone also took home about 1/3 of their meal, easy to say we could have all split dishes. I was not impressed by the fries or the cocktails at all, the garden basil martini wasn’t bad, but the dirty martini wasn’t good at all, I’ve have much better cocktails elsewhere.

Original Joe’s is one of those classic San Francisco spots that delivers every single time.

The standout for me is the veal piccata—and it’s done exactly how it should be. Tender, perfectly cooked veal with a bright, balanced lemon-caper sauce that cuts through beautifully without overpowering the dish. The texture is spot on, and the flavor has that clean, buttery richness you want from a traditional Italian-American preparation.

What really elevates the experience is the consistency and atmosphere. The dining room has that old-school, timeless energy—white jackets, polished service, and a buzz that makes it feel like a true institution. You can tell they’ve been doing this for decades and haven’t lost a step.

If you’re looking for a place that executes classic dishes at a high level, Original Joe’s is as reliable as it gets. The veal piccata alone is worth the visit.

To be honest, always thought that Original Joe's was a tourist trap; but after this meal, it's clear that the people behind the business care about the brand and the quality and experience that Original Joe's stands for.  Expected a busy crowd in the heart of North Beach on a pretty nice Friday afternoon... The sun was still out, but SF weather can change on a dime.... Chose to seat at an outdoor table, since there was no wait.... Assuaged by the reassurance of an overhead heating lamp.
The food was..... What one would expect from Original Joe's...hearty, more than fair portions, fresh and speedy service.  The service portion needs to catch up with the rest of the experience... As there were several long periods of time where we could not attract any personnel unless we acted and went out of our way to do so.... Prices were actually very fair for this time and age, location and quality.    A solid 7.... Maybe 7.5.

We visited Original Joe’s for a birthday celebration. The place was packed, which was great, it showed us that it must be good and even though they were busy the staff was tentative to us. they always made sure glasses were full and drinks were flowing. The food selection was great. We all got something different and we all really enjoyed our meals. We will definitely be back. It’s a San Francisco classic that’s a must try. We were able to go to a bar down the road while we waited for a table to get ready, plenty to do in the area, including a nice park just across the street. We were able to park just one street away which made for a nice stroll that was flat to the restaurant. I got the prime rib and we had a number of appetizers prior to eating. We really enjoyed ourselves. The restaurant was comfortable and well decorated and very clean.

top_reviews.content:
Wow. Zazie has been going strong for 35 years and dinner tonight was a reminder of why it’s such a beloved and busy place.

We ordered three starters to begin: the mushroom fondue, steak tartare, and the chicken liver pate. These are apps I order at restaurants everywhere and Zazie’s are the best.

The tartare was topped with a quail egg and has a bit of pickle which gave it an amazing brightness. The whole table loved it. The chicken liver pate was rich, creamy, and served on grilled toast (fabulous), and the mushroom fondue!!!

We could have stopped there but then ordered the mussels which are the best I’ve ever had. (I’m not exaggerating!). Plump, juicy, and flavorful.

My son had the burger with Gorgonzola.  Delicious!

We finished by singing Happy Birthday to my husband over a lovely crème brûlée.

I also love that there is no tipping. The restaurant is now owned by the chef and team and everyone has a living wage, health and dental insurance as well as a 401(k) plan.

Clearly this is a place that takes care of its staff as well as they take care of their customers.

I’ve been coming to Zazie since 1994 (when I was single and return with my husband and adult son).  It’s really special that they have managed to keep the culture and level of cuisine so high.

I commend this establishment for paying their employees a living wage. It was refreshing to not have to think and calculate tip!
Went for brunch.. chicken sandwich is very delicious.  French toast was great.  Overall an excellent restaurant.

Very pricey place to eat but they dont require you to tip as well. Certain style and class to the food but if you go to the back you'll walk through their kitchen and it didnt seem sanitary from what I thought but all in all food was great. I had the Florentine Eggs Benedict and even though I wasnt full from that tiny serving it was still quality food. I loved the experience in the backyard set up and thought it had  a pretty cool vibe to it.

Zazie is hands down one of our Top 5 favorite restaurants in the San Francisco Bay Area, and every visit reminds me exactly why.

As someone who’s a big, big meat eater, I rarely go for a meatless option—but the lemon ricotta ravioli here is in a league of its own. Bright, creamy, and melt-in-your-mouth delicious, it’s one of the very few vegetarian dishes that leaves me totally satisfied without even thinking about meat. That says a lot.

Of course, when I do indulge my carnivorous side, the pork chop is absolutely divine—so tender it practically falls apart, and paired with buttery potatoes and the dreamiest mac and cheese. Rich, hearty, comforting. It’s the kind of dish you crave long after the meal is over.

The escargot deserves a special shoutout—it instantly transports me back to Paris. Delicately prepared, garlicky, and served with that unmistakable French flair. It’s the real deal.

And please, whatever you do, don’t skip dessert. The Chaud is an experience. Warm, gooey chocolate topped with toasted marshmallows—it’s like being wrapped in a hug that somehow takes you straight to Brussels. Yum, yum, YUM!

This place was an awesome choice.   Yes, it's touristy, but seriously....if it has good food, good service, and a cool atmosphere....who cares!!!!

My wife ordered the coconut shrimp and I ordered the taco plate.

The coconut shrimp may have looked overcooked...but guess again.   The shrimp was perfectly cooked and was full of great coconut taste.   The dipping sauce was so good, my wife needed a second.

I ordered a mixture of tacos....fish, chicken, and a pork one (I forgot the name....ugh).   The latter two were well seasoned and cooked well.   Fully loaded with slaw and sauce.

The fish taco....OMFG, was delicious.   It was breaded pacific cod and was like butter.   Moist and flaky, perfectly crusted, and tasted like it was freshly caught.

The Maverick drink was so full of adult goodness, that a second should've been ordered.

The blood orange beer hit the spot.

The vibes and servers were great, and everything we ordered tasted good! We got the fried pickles, nachos, and drinks, and overall had a good experience. The one downside was that our fried pickles came with a surprise piece of fish. As two people who absolutely hate fish, that definitely killed our appetite a little.

My husband and I stopped in for lunch. We were seated quickly. Another table was seated about 5 minutes after us. Our server visited that table before us. Then she came and took our orders.

Someone from thr kitchen delivered our food. The food was okay. Our server never came and checked on us after we received our food or offered drink refills, which we were wanting for a while. We finished our food and sat for a long time and saw other servers around us paying their checks at the table with the servers on their tablets that they used to enter orders. We asked a guy who came to clear our dishes (still server had not come to our table) if we could get our check. The server was later seen several minutes later on her way to greet a table across from us. We waved at her and started to ask for the check and she said just a minute. She then proceeded to take the other tables order, then came to our table and handed us the check. My husband handed her his card and then she walked away with his card and her tablet. This is not what any other sever had done. My husband then got up and walked over to the corner she went to to swipe his card and then he saw what appeared to be her starting to enter a tip for herself and he stopped her. She was very rude and unprofessional. top_reviews.content:
Let me get the only minor negative out of the way: they expect everyone to purchase a bowl of ramen. I understand that, but we had two kids with us who can share. We ordered two sides (wagyu sashimi and uni/wagyu) which were more than the ramen bowls themselves so they were okay with that.

With that out of the way, the ramen was the best I ever tasted (in the States). It does rival ramen I've had in Japan. That is saying a whole lot for those who haven't been to Japan, the ramen there is top notch obviously.

The ramen noodle itself was perfect texture of chewy, smooth and aldente at the same time. It was perfect. The broth was creamy but you didn't feel it was over bearing with cream, it didn't feel heavy. Meat was buttery soft and delicious.

The wagyu sashimi was almost too smooth, there I couldn't taste any flavor. I'd honestly rather eat thick wagyu seared slightly in each side.

Overall, I'm glad we waited on the long line. That line is consistently long for a reason. A must try in SF!

Hands down the best ramen we’ve ever had.
The signature bowl is rich and deeply flavorful, while the classic is a great option if you prefer something lighter. The GKO and lamb cumin ramen bring in Chinese-inspired flavors, which is a unique and creative twist. Everything we tried was delicious—highly recommend!

The signature ramen was delicious. The matcha duck ramen was creative, but the taste was only so so. The wagyu beef sushi was good. The fried enoki was crispy and nice. The wait for not too long for a Monday evening around 6-7pm. Overall, we had a good dinner.

Hands down the best ramen I’ve ever had. The broth is incredibly rich, creamy, and packed with flavor—every spoonful feels carefully crafted. The noodles have the perfect texture, and the toppings are high quality and unique.

This isn’t your typical ramen spot—it feels elevated, almost like a Michelin-level experience in terms of technique and flavor. You can really tell there’s a lot of thought behind every element of the bowl.

If you’re into bold, intense flavors and don’t mind something a bit heavier, this place is a must-try. I’d absolutely come back

Tried Mensho Tokyo in San Francisco and it absolutely lived up to the hype.

We ordered the Spicy Lamb and the Extra Spicy GKO both were incredible. The broth is rich, thick, and almost curry-like, packed with deep, bold flavors that really stand out from typical ramen.

They’ve got a great variety of veg and non-veg options, which makes it an easy pick for mixed groups too.

Definitely one of the best ramen spots I’ve been to, highly recommend checking it out!

Japanese with Jazz!
Thanks to our friends who introduced Yoshi's to us. The meal and the concert following made for a truly memorable experience. We drove from San Jose to Oakland for it - totally worth the effort!
The package deal includes parking within the structure - unheard of! They validate - so remember to pass by the electronic validation machine on your way out.
Warm sake, sushi, and Jazz - life should be so good!

This is easily my favorite music venue in the Bay without a doubt.  My wife and I used to live in Oakland and could walk here.  And we would go once a month at least.  First of all, the food is phenomenal.  Most live music venues are not known for their food.  But the sushi, ambiance and service from this restaurant are top notch.  If you make a reservation for food before the concert, you often get priority seating too.  The music venue is in a separate room inside the restaurant.  Once you enter the music venue, it is small and close knit.  There are no bad seats in the house.  Bartenders will serve you drinks and food during concerts as well so you never have to leave your seat.  I was shocked at the list of artists that come into this place.  Artists that can probably fill up stadiums and arenas perform here.  Depending on the artists, it can turn into a party.  I’ve seen the audience get up and dance in their seats on plenty of occasions.  And the ticket prices are decent.  This place is a must try!  It’s easily what we miss the most from Oakland.

Yoshi's is a standout when it comes to authentic Japanese cuisine. From the moment you enter, you’re greeted with a warm, inviting atmosphere that sets the tone for an exceptional dining experience. The decor is sleek yet cozy, offering the perfect environment for both casual meals and special celebrations.

The menu at Yoshi’s is packed with options, but the sushi is what truly shines. The fish is always incredibly fresh, and each piece is prepared with attention to detail. Whether you're enjoying a classic California roll or a more adventurous specialty roll, you can taste the quality in every bite. For sashimi lovers, the selection is extensive and always perfectly sliced.

Aside from sushi, Yoshi's also offers a variety of other Japanese dishes, like ramen and teriyaki, that are equally impressive. The service is top-notch—attentive but never overbearing, and the staff is knowledgeable about the menu, always ready to offer recommendations.

If you're a fan of Japanese food, Yoshi's should definitely be on your radar. The combination of amazing food, great atmosphere, and excellent service makes it a must-visit spot. Whether you're a sushi aficionado or new to Japanese cuisine, you’ll leave Yoshi’s feeling satisfied and eager to return!

The courtyard is cozy and intimate with warm patio lights above. Even with the occasional breeze patio heaters keep things toasty.

The ceviche had a nice kick from the habanero in the dish. For our mains we got the persian spiced tuna and the madras curry sesame fried chicken. The fish was super savoury and the complimenting brand and peppers really complimented the dish. The chicken had the perfect fried chicken flake. So many flavours that came through nicely.

To end our meal we shared the sundae. The fruit macedoine was nicely spiced and compliment the richness of the ice cream really nicely.

I liked the atmosphere, the service was sharp and professional. Great volume and ambience, and the wine list is solid. Razor Clam was delicious and Mozzarella Pepper dish was fantastic (especially with focaccia)! Fried Chicken was not my favorite but I know it’s a popular dish. Love the daily changing menu. Highly Recommend!

I loved how fresh the food felt! Each ingredient was refreshing to taste. The atmosphere is romantic and makes for wonderful conversations. Everyone was having such a good time which adds to the jolly ambience.

Went to Foreign Cinema in San Francisco for Saturday brunch and had a great experience. Definitely recommend making a reservation—it was almost fully packed when we arrived. They offer both indoor and outdoor seating, and the overall vibe is really nice and lively.

We ordered the tuna ceviche, French omelette, and seafood sandwich. Everything was fresh and really tasty. The only small downside was the portion size, especially the ceviche, which felt a bit small for the price.

Overall, really enjoyed it and would definitely come back.

Wow

I then saw a sign that literally says "Pasta Lab" - off to a great start.

top_reviews.content:
Charming ramen place with a variety of options both from drinks, ramen dishes to other dishes and appetisers. There is something for everyone.

The ramen broth was excellent, light and balanced but flavourful and brought me back in time to when I had ramen in Japan. Beautifully done noodles and other toppings.

Service was very pleasant and quick, with very short waiting time for the food.

The ambiance is very pleasant with casual but authentic vibes throughout with a lot of seating both inside and outside. Definitely coming back on my next visit to SF

Hinodeya has been a ramen mainstay in the city for a long time, and for good reason. Their dashi-based broths are always so light and clean without sacrificing flavor, which I especially appreciate in a city where ramen often leans much richer with tonkotsu or miso as the more prevalent options.

The broth has such a deep umami character, and I especially love it in the hamaguri ramen, which comes loaded with littleneck clams. There is just something about a seafood dashi ramen that feels incredibly satisfying. On my most recent visit, I went for the seasonal Tokyo Seven Duck Ramen instead, and it was excellent in a much richer way. The chicken-based broth was the perfect foil for the perfectly cooked and sliced duck breast on top, and the thicker wavy noodles worked beautifully with the bowl. It also came with a perfectly jammy egg, and the charred negi was an underrated highlight since it added sharpness, crunch, and a little smokiness to cut through the richness.

My partner ordered the Spicy Butter Miso Butter Corn Ramen, which was even richer and more about buttery corn and miso umami than overt heat. The spice level is definitely more subtle than the name might suggest, but the bowl was still very satisfying.

It is a bit pricey for ramen, especially the duck bowl at $34, but the portions are generous and the flavors have always been there for me. That said, it is hard to make this a regular option when there are so many great options in the Bay Area.

I came to Hideyama Ramen today with my partner, and this visit was really disappointing, especially considering I’ve been coming here for years.

On a positive note, my Tokyo Duck ramen was actually very good great portion and rich, flavorful broth. We also had gyoza and hot sake, which were enjoyable.

However, my partner ordered the beef sukiyaki ramen, and when it came out, there was a thick, short, wavy hair in the bowl clearly not something that should ever be in food. This is a serious contamination issue.

We tried to get our server’s attention, and I understand it was busy, but being busy is not an excuse when it comes to food safety. Eventually, another server came over. We showed him the issue, expecting at least a proper apology or some explanation of what happened. Instead, he just took the bowl away and said a quick “I’m sorry” no explanation, no reassurance, nothing.

They brought out a new bowl of ramen, but at that point, the experience was already ruined. It’s hard to continue eating normally after something like that, it honestly just stays in your mind.

What makes this more frustrating is that I’ve been here many times before with friends, family, and coworkers, and when everything goes right, it’s great. But when something goes wrong, the response is just a simple “sorry” with no accountability or communication. Even on my last visit a few months ago, the broth was bland and the response was the same just “I’m sorry.”

At a minimum, for an issue this serious, there should be clear communication, reassurance about food safety, and a more professional response.

Because of both past and current experiences, I don’t think I’ll be coming back. I really hope they improve their service and train staff to handle serious situations like this more appropriately.

this was honestly one of the most disappointing ramen experiences I’ve had.

I ordered the duck ramen, which was nearly $40, and it was not worth the price. The duck tasted mostly like burnt seasoning, and the broth was surprisingly bland and lacked the depth and flavor you’d expect from a good bowl of ramen. The karaage was actually the best part of the meal.

The service didn’t help the experience either. After we had already been seated and settled in, we were asked to move to another table to accommodate a larger group. While we agreed, it was inconvenient and not something you expect after you’ve already gotten comfortable.

The restaurant was also extremely loud, making it difficult to enjoy the meal or conversation.

To top it off, the end of the experience felt rushed and unfriendly. The waitress came over, handed us the payment device and bill without asking how the food was or whether we needed anything else. It felt more like we were being rushed out than treated as guests.

For the price, quality of food, and overall service, I left very disappointed. Unfortunately, I won’t be returning.

top_reviews.content:
I’ve been wanting to try this storied North Beach institution for years, but always avoided it because of the notoriously long weekend lines. We came during the week instead, and got seated immediately.

Unfortunately, the experience seemed to suffer from the classic malaise of historic establishments where new ownership can't quite maintain the same level of quality as the founders.

The Food: Our table ordered a few of their specialties: the huevos rancheros, eggs florentine, and eggs benedict. Across the board, the dishes arrived cold, the breads were noticeably hard, and the overall execution fell flat. The potatoes were just okay, but nothing to write home about.

The Service: While the food came out quite fast, the staff lacked the warm, welcoming friendliness you’d typically expect from a historic mom-and-pop brunch spot.

My ultimate recommendation: come for the history and the story, but don't expect a premium meal.

Mama’s on Washington Square is truly a must-visit spot for breakfast in San Francisco. From the moment you arrive, you can feel the charm of this iconic place in North Beach. Yes, there’s usually a line—but it’s absolutely worth the wait.

The food is exceptional. Everything is made with fresh ingredients and great attention to detail. The French toast is perfectly cooked—crispy on the outside and soft inside—and the pancakes are fluffy and full of flavor. The egg dishes, especially the Benedict options, are also outstanding. Portions are generous, and every dish feels thoughtfully prepared.

The service is friendly, efficient, and well-organized, even during busy hours. The staff keeps things moving smoothly while still making you feel welcome.

The location, right by Washington Square, adds to the overall experience and makes it even more enjoyable.

Overall, an unforgettable breakfast spot with amazing food, great service, and a cozy atmosphere. Definitely a place I would come back to and highly recommend.

One of the best monte cristos I’ve ever had!

As an sf local, I have been meaning to try this place for years. I was worried it wasn’t going to live up to its hype but alas - it did and I will be back!

There is always a line but it moves fast.

Upon entering, you’ll order up front where they will give you a number and direct you to the next open table best suited for your party.

WE WERE SO LUCKY!!!  My wife and I were scooting around on Saturday morning looking for breakfast.   I've always known about Mama's but the line outside was always a deterrent.
By chance,  we passed Mama's and there was no line.   My wife jumped off and went inside.   I parked my Vespa and she came rushing out telling me that there was a table.  Awesome!!!
It was my first time eating here. I've know of it since the 90s and finally I  would be able to enter.   The restaurant is very SF and very tidy.   The staff were super nice and very attentive.   The coffee was pretty decent too.
I had the French Toast sampler and my wife had the breakfast sandwich.   Both items were excellent.
Thanks for a wonderful time this morning Mama's!

Mama’s consistently delivers a best in class dining experience with standout execution across the menu. The Montecristo sandwich is rich, perfectly balanced, and cooked to absolute perfection. The Washington Square omelette is exceptional, fluffy, flavorful, and clearly made with quality ingredients and attention to detail.
To close it out, the cake crumble is outstanding, indulgent without being overwhelming and the ideal finish to the meal.

From entrée to dessert, everything feels intentional and well curated. This place is operating at a very high level and continues to exceed expectations. Highly recommended for anyone looking to enjoy comfort food done right.

However, I tried a lot of other things in the menu and they were all quite mid in my honest opinion.

The biscuit with spicy fried chicken was really really spicy and plain and the mango habanero sandwich was missing some freshness / it was very sweet. Also the apple fritter we're good but very heavy and oily. This just wants to be a constructive feedback.

Even if the loaded fries with bacon were not bad, I think it would be nice to also have some loaded chicken fries on the menu.

The Bird always hits regardless of location. Super easy to order, food comes out fresh and tasty. Service is always friendly, and the vibes are bar none.

Recommend the buffalo bird and the wings, loaded fries also always hit (imo preferable over the tots since the tots get soggy after prolonged cheese exposure). Love that there's wet naps and paper towels at every table.

Saturday dinner:(~6.30 pm) a few times🔥

- Walked in, ordered at the counter, simple menu. Lovely place, great vibe, busy but not crowded.
Protip(s): If I may, fried chicken sandwich, tater tots, regular coke, enjoy!
If you’re picking up, drive up twin peaks view point and enjoy it with the SF view🌃and perfect weather 🥂

- Ordered Spicy Fried Chicken Sandwich(with and without cheese). Both are good, but I loved the one without cheese, it’s spicy, juicy with slaw, more meat less bun, the best kind of sandwich there is! 🤤😮‍💨🔥

- Tater tots are a good side, crispy, a lil crunchy with the hot chicken sandwich.

- The mango habenero wings are good and 🔥, perfect for ordering with a group of friends.

- Food is ready in like ~10 min. Little hard to find parking, but there’s paid street parking around, hope you get lucky.

Wow, this was a mighty fine chicken sandwich! I ordered the fried chicken sandwich, and the breading was wonderfullly crispy and herbaceous, the chicken was hot and juicy, and the slaw topping was crisp and paired perfectly with the chicken. Their curly fries were well-seasoned and crispy. Portions were very generous.

Service was friendly and fantastic! I would highly recommend a visit if you find yourself in soma in search of a quick, yummy bite!

​I ordered for pickup, and the food was fresh and ready. The chicken sandwich is a standout—the portion was huge and the flavor was spot on. I also tried the loaded tots; the green onions added a nice freshness, though the bacon had a bit of a pre-packaged (bacon bits) tast to me. Overall, it was a great experience with generous portions that left me satisfied. I’d would definitely go back and even recommend to someone.
