top_reviews.content: Was grateful to get a reservation on Valentines Day! My niece called them and they were able to seat a group of us (7) within an hour. Excellent service, and the food was great. Some highlights - the popovers of course, the clam chowder, and my fried chicken was very good. The ambience was both romantic but capable of seating multiple people. Enjoy!

Excellent food it was perfect. The portions are shareable and I really really enjoyed the mashed potato Buratta. All the portions are so big.

Service Swiss, excellent, attentive, time dwell, very friendly, everybody helped each other during service time. Definitely the highlight of this establishment is the service.

Location is great. It’s near the water near the office as well as near the hotel no issues walking there. it’s spacious a bit busy during the time when we went, otherwise we were seated fast and we were perfect in our table.

This was a pretty good place. Reminded me of an old haunted hotel vibes without the dust and cobwebs. I loved it! The food was nice. I didnt love the elote-esque deviled eggs appetizer. It had a weird texture with the corn kernels but the flavor was fine. We also got the steak and frites which was cooked beautifully but the cut of meat was a little tough. It tasted really nice though. Overall we would definitely come back and try new things.

I came across Wayfare Tavern while exploring the area on Google Maps, and I’m so glad I decided to give it a try.

The restaurant leans into elevated American comfort food, and I was honestly really impressed. I wasn’t sure how refined and flavorful comfort food could get, but the quality of the ingredients truly stood out. Every dish felt thoughtfully put together, and when paired, the flavors complemented each other so well that they elevated the entire experience.

We also had a few drinks, and the quality there was just as strong — well-balanced, well-crafted, and definitely worth it.

What really made the visit memorable though was the service. It was outstanding. I haven’t experienced that level of attentiveness and hospitality in a long time, so major credit to the entire team.

We were seated fairly quickly when we arrived, but by the time we left, there was a huge lineup outside, which says a lot about how popular this spot is. They also had their patio open, which added to the overall ambiance, beautiful space, great aesthetic, and a really enjoyable vibe.

Prices are mid to high-end depending on what you order, but in my opinion, it’s absolutely worth it for the quality, service, and overall experience. Highly recommend if you’re in San Francisco and looking for something a bit elevated but still comforting.

We visited on a Saturday for lunch. Highlights were the 1) Yorkshire pudding / popover, 2) Organic fried chicken with an amazing herb aroma (rosemary I think?) and 3) Tavern burger (on the sweeter side, but still good). Downsides were 1) slow service (took 10 mins to get water) and 2) the deviled eggs. This alone took this review down from 4 stars to 3 stars. $18 before tax and tip for the saddest eggs - we ordered it for the corn flavor and got maybe 1 piece of corn in each piece. They dumped clumps of paprika on top and it was just a sloppy app. I would come back for the burger and the chicken if I worked nearby but wouldn’t come out of my way to visit again.

A glass of beer and white wine and we had a great time for about $50.00 all in.

The staff worked hard to keep everything well organized and were friendly and attentive throughout our visit. We would definitely recommend this restaurant and would be happy to return.

Stopped here for brunch on the Saturday of Easter weekend, and it did not disappoint!  We got the fried fish tacos and the clam & fish chowder - AMAZING!  Fish tacos were seasoned beautifully and filled with avocado, an tasty sauce, and huge crispy chunks of fish.  The chowder was the best I've ever had.  The outdoor seating area was nice as well.  We'll be back for more menu items!

The food was very nice, we had Fish & Chips  and fish tacos. The service was good enough, some waiters friendlier than the other. Overall, nice place to sit at the seaside and enjoy a sunny lunch.

top_reviews.content: Great location and beautiful interior. We went for Happy Hour because we were between meals and wanted to enjoy the view. The Happy Hour options were about half of what the regular price on the menu. Initially, because were were sat in the the dining room, we were told that we could not order the happy hour, but I guess they had a private party in that area, so they allowed us to order it. I ordered their version of an Aperol spritzer and it was very tart and sour, so I asked for more soda in it, then it was fine. The most expensive thing on the menu was the crab cakes which were 3 tiny dots and not worth the $$ in my opinion. The sliders were good and we got a 2nd order of those and the beef dish was good as well. The reason I did 3 stars on food is because we ordered a salad and it was super gritty- like they had totally forgotten to wash it. I couldn't even get through one bite. They did give us some little dessert bites for our anniversary, which I thought was kind. Service was great and our waiter was very responsive. On the whole, I would give it another shot.

What a wonderful experience! We came here today to celebrate the fifth anniversary of our dental office. Paul was our server and he was fantastic. He welcomed us with a card signed by the Epic team, which was such a thoughtful gesture. Paul was friendly, attentive and just made our dinner a great experience. The food is delicious. We loved the steak, creamy mashed potatoes, the baby carrots and the strawberry short cake. The ambiance is beautiful. They have a great view of the Bay Bridge and the restaurant is lovely! We will definitely be coming back.

First time here and it did not disappoint! I will start with our exceptional server Joseph was one of those servers who just makes the experience all the more amazing. Every once on a while you get a truly amazing service this was one of those times. When you feel welcomed, taken care of at every turn and over all makes dinning there an absolutely amazing experience. Now on to the food the new York was cooked to utter perfection the best steak I've ever had hands down the gold mashed potatoes and asparagus delicious! The tiramisu was so good! The atmosphere and ambiance were a whole vibe and the view oh man the view!!!! Highly recommend coming here and ask for Joseph!!

I had made a rsv for my wife’s birthday at the restaurant. We arrived on time and they brought us to our table shortly. I had requested outdoor seating because the view is just incredible. It was a little chilly that evening but they have outdoor heating, it made our dinner very comfortable.
Our server was very attentive and informative about the menu. However he never introduced himself so we did not get his name. We tried their cocktails they were very fruity and good. We opted in for their porter house steak because it is big enough to share. We also made it a combo which includes salad or soup, the steak, appetizer and dessert.
We ordered some raw oysters they were very fresh. The jumbo shrimp was my favorite both the shrimp and the sauce goes very well with each other. I like my steak medium rare however the steak came out to rare. I did not bring this issue to my servers attention because it was bearable to me but it was too rare to my wife’s liking. The truffle mac and cheese was phenomenal. Overall the food was 5/5 to us.
I had told the restaurant that it was my wife’s birthday and they had a hand written birthday card for her which I thought it was a nice touch. The server also told us that one dessert would be on the house so we were able to pick 2 different desserts to try.
Overall epic steak is very great we would be back for special occasion if we are ever in sfo again.

Epic Steak Review

Epic Steak  yeah !

Absolutely epic in every way. The steak was cooked to perfection—juicy, tender, and full of flavor. Top-quality meat, beautifully seasoned, and served exactly how a great steak should be.
The atmosphere is upscale but relaxed, with an amazing view that makes the whole experience even better. Service was professional, attentive, and genuinely friendly.
If you’re looking for a high-end steakhouse with outstanding food and vibes, Epic Steak is a must. Worth every dollar.

top_reviews.content:
Dinner happy hour here felt like a small escape from the city noise. The space is bold, colorful, almost like stepping into a painted dream.

I kept it simple with appetizers and honestly that was more than enough to be satisfied. The papaya salad had that sharp, fresh spicy punch that wakes you up in the best way, the egg rolls were crisp and comforting (the side sauce was amazing), and the small tom kha with chicken was silky, fragrant, and just right for an early dinner.

Service stood out too, attentive without hovering, the kind of rhythm that makes you relax into the meal. It is an easy recommendation for a relaxed dinner happy hour 😋

As a new California resident, I've been loving the experience of exploring so many new restaurants across San Francisco and the Bay Area. I tried Farmhouse Kitchen Thai Cuisine for a weekend lunch, and overall, it was a great experience.

We started with Thai tea, which tasted good, but the giant ice ball added mainly for presentation was a bit of a mood killer--it looked nice but diluted the drink quickly.

The crispy egg rolls were delicious--perfectly crispy and flavorful, a great way to start the meal.

We  also ordered chicken tom kha. It was very tasty, with big pieces of chicken and vegetables, but it felt more like a stir fry than a soup. I personally wished it had a bit more soup

For the mains, we ordered the chicken red curry with blue jasmine rice. The curry itself was absolutely delightful--rich, comforting, and full of flavor. However, the blue jasmine rice didn't really add anything to the taste. It looks great for Instagram shots, but you can easily skip it and stick to regular white rice.

We also ordered the Thai fried rice, which was a total flavor bomb--so good that I actually forgot to take a photo of it!

Their Mother's Sauce deserves a special mention--it's incredibly delicious but very spicy, so be careful if you can't handle the heat.

The ambience is very cute, and the service was fast, making the overall experience enjoyable.

Definitely going back--there's still so much on the menu to try!

Awesome option for Thai in the city!

Every dish that we got was hot (temperature), flavourful, and delicious.  The drinks were also on point.  The desserts deserve a notable mention even though I don't even like desserts...

The service was fast and the bill was quite reasonable.

Well definitely be back!

I'm not in the Bay Area often (just about once or twice a year for work), but this is a classic for me. I've ordered it every time I'm in the area, and once even had it twice in one trip. For 2-3 people, you MUST get their platter (btw I think it might be takeout only, not sure, have never dined in), which comes with a ridiculous amount of food like a little sampler of everything.
The dessert platter was okay, but would not get again. Either way, their normal dinner sampler platter itself is a perfect 5 stars for me. I do, however, miss when the platter was only $100, and it is now $130-ish :(

I had lunch at Farmhouse Kitchen Thai yesterday and tried their tasting menu. Honestly, every single bite was incredible! The Pad See You with beef was perfectly balanced and rich, the samosas were crispy and packed with flavor, and the Neua Num Tok roll had such a fresh, vibrant kick. The Mieng Kum Kung was a standout, so unique and layered with textures, and even the Tom Yum soup was deeply flavorful. Everything was just so delicious. Definitely one of those meals where you’re already planning your next visit before you leave!

top_reviews.content:
We arrived at our reserved time and were seated promptly. The meal itself was a pleasure. We started with a mushroom soup that was rich and delicious, if a touch too salty. The duck was tender and flavorful, served with crisp fried zucchini and potatoes. Dessert was the highlight: a beautifully made tart paired with ice cream and hot cookies that melted in your mouth.

The service, unfortunately, was uneven. Our waiter was attentive early on, but once the restaurant filled up he seemed to vanish just as we were ready to order dessert. We tried to flag down help, yet three separate servers came and went from the tables around us without so much as a glance our way. It wasn’t until we caught the maître d’ mid-stride that things were finally sorted out. To their credit, the meal wrapped up well after that.

A word on atmosphere: the room runs loud, with an energetic, lively vibe. Worth knowing if you’re hoping for a quiet, conversational dinner.

It was nice to come here to catch up with friends. The food was pretty good, some dishes better than others. The staff is nice. They have a coat/ bag check. The space is airy and inviting. Farm to table restaurant with credits on back of menu

The warm olives were very good. They melted in my mouth and the bread was delicious. The steak was too chewy and spicy for me. The lettuces salad was also very good, crunchy lettuce and I liked the dressing. My favorite dessert was the chocolate malt ice cream, so unique and actually tastes malted! The cookies were good too and I’m glad we got both so can eat them together.

Overall nice place, a little pricey but would come back again for a special occasion

After hearing so much about the burgers at Nopa, I finally got around to trying the out, and I gotta say I was a bit disappointed. Don't get me wrong, the burgers are solid. But for $30, I would have expected a more flavorful party, or a more interesting sauce... Really anything that would have made the dish more memorable.

The fried chicken was also good but not mind blowingly amazing.

The service was great though, as was the upscale ambience with its demure hipster vibe.

Nopa didn’t quite live up to expectations. The starters were mostly good and set a promising tone, but the mains were disappointing. The burger lacked flavor and felt rather ordinary, while the pork chop, although one of the better dishes, still didn’t fully convince.

The interior of the restaurant is impressive, but the acoustics are poor, making it very loud inside. Fortunately, we were seated outside, which was just ok in terms of comfort. Service was good, but not exceptional.

Overall, a somewhat disappointing experience that didn’t meet expectations.

A transcendent dinining experience full of unique flavor firsts and service of the highest level.  Margo took us for a culinary ride suggesting the pork chop, the best ive ever had.    A few more choice suggestions had us finishing with the malted chocolate ice cream.  It’s clear why this place has stood the test of time.  Fresh local ingredients and a staff that loves what they do.  Thanks!

top_reviews.content:
My husband and I decided to come here for lunch. This is a very nice restaurant that offers indoor and outdoor seating.
We opted for indoor and we were seated with four other tables.
My husband ordered the half crab, which was disappointing because it was not cracked, it came in a sauce so if you dropped a piece, you were not given a bib or extra napkins. We constantly had to look around for someone who was working on the floor as they would serve someone and then disappear. I had the salmon which was okay.
Our server came around a couple of times to see if everything was okay, but after giving us the check, he disappeared. All the other tables were empty and there was no one to be found.
After ten minutes of waiting, we took the check and went downstairs to find someone so we could pay the check and leave.
I may go back someday if i'm in the area as it is a very nice and clean looking restaurant with very pretty views.

Came here for a work dinner recently and while we overall had an enjoyable time with a stellar atmosphere, the food itself was a bit disappointing.

The service itself was great. It’s never easy to handle a big group and our wait staff was patient and helpful. We were quickly seated outside and had a lovely view of the lake.

Atmosphere is definitely what you’re paying for when coming to this restaurant and with a lovely sunset it makes for incredible backdrop.

Now for the food. While the food itself generally looked good and the vast menu had options to support many preferences, what I actually ate left something to be desired. The rice in my dish was pretty bland overall and the slaw while flavorful didn’t have enough punch to save the dish.

Highlights were actually the drinks and dessert. The tamarind marg was delicious and the desserts, specifically the bread pudding, were a hit.

top_reviews.content:
Had some high expectations after my wife and I were told by the hostess on her birthday that the restaurant was by reservation only, regardless of being very openly vacant.

When we came by for our reservation months later, I had Tapas on my mind, and wished to savor the Spanish flavors in each bite.

While the food was yummy, I can’t say I wasn’t left disappointed by the majority of dishes. Not that they tasted bad, but that they were reaching so far into the Californian style of making dishes, that the dish ended up being diluted to %30 Spanish authenticity.

The “Spanish” Tortilla on special should be renamed Californian Spanish Tortilla, missing the essence of the rich Spanish flavors, but was still tasteful. Also, the bread with tomato was in a style seemingly foreign to Spain: the tomato was cooked and not already on the bread. My understanding it’s raw tomato ground on a plate with fresh basil.

Their quail egg “Diablo” was the perfect combo of California + Spanish flavors, and was well balanced, not just feeling like a Californian blend of ingredients in a Spanish form. Having the authenticity is special for tapas, especially those claiming to be Spanish.

Cocktails and wine were delicious, although I would have liked to receive my wine before I had finished my cold appetizers, to pair the Albariño with the white fish.

The chicken croquettes and Iberian ham croquettes were amazing, as well as the meatballs of pork&duck. The cream Catalan was very tasty, but also had an un-traditional consistency/texture.

In short, while it’s a relaxing spot, with a wonderful waterfront view, expect more of that and less of Spain and you will enough your food and drink!

Food and service were excellent, as always, except for our server Marco.

When I made the reservation to celebrate my wife's birthday,  I specifically requested a table for 3 with room for a stroller. We came at 1:15pm on a Saturday, and when we arrived the host had set up a spacious 4 top table for us with an ocean view. But as soon as the host left and we settled into our seats, Marco told us that we could not sit here and that this table was reserved (which turned out to be a lie). He instead took us to a small 2 top table. Despite the stellar food, the dishonesty left a bad taste in my mouth.

We ordered 7 dishes, including a large paella. There was little space on the table and we had to constantly stop eating to make sure our toddler didn't grab any of the dishes or silverware off the table.

Thank you to all the other servers who provided attentive friendly service, who made us feel welcome, and proactively took care of our needs.  Multiple other servers checked in with us to take our order, serve us food, refill our drinks, clear our table, bring us the check, and pack our leftover food, even including extra condiments for us to take home.

After we were sat in the main dining area, we noticed only one other party sat after us, and when we left the restaurant it was almost completely empty. And the table we were originally sat at was unused for the duration of our meal, which was how we knew that we were lied to. This was one of our favorite restaurants that we've been coming to for years, but it's hard to recommend anymore given the experience we had.

Back to SF and had yet another delicious culinary experience at Coqueta! Nice, eclectic cocktails to start, followed by a series of shared tapas - the smoked salmon (the truffle honey on it was remarkable!), the melt-in-your-mouth grilled octopus, the unique and delightful duck-and-pork meatballs, the rich poached prawns, and the inventive patatas bravas accompanied by a glass of Sangría Tinta! Attentive service in a vibrant but not noisy atmosphere… Spot on as always!

July 2026 Review:

Food: The tapas are very overpriced here. Expect to spend at least $100 per person as the portion sizes are small. The plates are not anything to write home about either.

Service: Bad! After being seated for nearly 15min, we had to remind our server to give us water at our table. We ordered cocktails - mine came nearly 20 min later (we were done with several tapas at this point) and to make matters worse, my friend’s cocktail never arrived because the kitchen forgot to make it.

Overall - there is nothing special about this place - it is an overpriced tourist trap. I recommend avoiding it all together.

Recommended by my son!
He mentioned he comes here often whenever he’s in the beach. He usually gets the poke, but since it was a bit chilly the day we visited, eating cold poke outside didn't seem like the best idea. So, we went with the Fish and Chips instead.
Because it’s attached to a seafood market, you can really tell the quality of the ingredients is good. Everything tasted so fresh and delicious! You can usually tell when a place uses low-quality ingredients or old oil just by the smell as you walk past, but everything here felt clean and fresh.
The vibe is very relaxed and laid-back—it instantly gives you that fun, "I'm on vacation" feeling. They also serve great local beers that paired perfectly with the food.
If the weather is nice, this is a fantastic spot to go for a stroll nearby and grab a drink. Highly recommended!

Meh. Not sure what the hype and long wait was for. The fish and chips were decent but as I expect fish and chips to taste, nothing exceptional. It’s just a fancier version of Wahoos or any Baja fish style place.  I think it’s more of a tourist trap, since everyone there were tourists. Get in, take your instagram photos, eat once, (standing up since all the tables are full) and move onto the next tourist time trap.
If I knew about the decent but “just ok” flavor, I would not have waited in line or for the food for an hour and a half. Would have found some other spot.

Really flaky fish and chips with a thick flavorful tartar sauce. Fries are well seasoned and on the stiff side. Loved the poke. Fresh, tender but not mushy.

The restaurant is really crowded whenever I’ve been on weekend lunches. Staff was busy but communicated the food would take 40 minutes to an hour (an accurate assessment).

Already looking forward to coming back!

First time trying this place. Went there on a Monday early evening (5pm). Little wait, but there are couple of people enjoying their food.

I orderd Fish and Chips, and it was good! Crispy batter and juicy fish. The included chips are seasoned perfectly!

Overall, I want to try them again and enjoy the atmosphere :)

Really incredible little restaurant! As the name suggests, it specializes in fish, and they make it really well. The fish tastes fresh and it's made perfectly. I also love the way they constructed the outdoor seating area; very unique and pleasing architecture. The people behind the counters were also very friendly.
I love where it's located as well. You'd expect a restaurant of this theme and quality to be in some high-end, downtown area or by the bay, but the fact that it's located in the Sunset district makes it incredibly calming to dine there.
Prices are high, of course, but it's a fantastic place to treat yourself or others for a meal.

top_reviews.content: The cajun chicken was good as well as the fries. Ordered the banh mi also but that was more like a pulled pork sandwich. Great deal for $20, sandwich and a $10 play card. Sat outside, they had a big water fountain, bean bag toss. The arcade was fun, had a little bit of everything. Win tickets to get a prize. Didn’t bowl but that was a cool option. Parking was the only hard part, parked a few blocks away but no problem for us to walk there.

Came here for a hackathon event and had a great time. It’s a fun spot to hang out with a large group, with plenty of space to socialize, play games, and unwind between sessions. The location right on the waterfront is a huge plus, and the weather was beautiful during our visit, making it even more enjoyable. Overall, a great venue for team events, meetups, or just spending time with friends. Would definitely come back!

Very nice venue,  located in Jack London Square, across from Scott's.   We had lunch early afternoon and it wasn't busy. We ordered the fish and chips and chicken salad.  Both were delicious!!  I was told the place gets packed, during sports season, and they offer many outdoor tvs for viewing.

The first couple of times I went to Plank it was fun, but expensive, so now I only go for Taco Tuesday. Not anymore. Last couple of times I went, the tacos were so disappointing and took forever. Last time I went; my order was wrong, the tacos took forever and were too chewy, overly full of onions, and service was subpar. The waitress basically told us they were out of anything we ordered except soda and water, and when she missed tacos in our order, she blamed us. Even tacos that were part of our order never arrived. We got there around 7:30 and were able to eat 3 tacos before they closed the kitchen at 8:45. Over an hour for cold and hard tacos?! To make it worse, we were some of the only people actually inside the building at the time. No one checked on us to make sure we got our food or if we needed anything, we had to get up multiple times to check on our stuff.

They were showing the World Cup match, and I ordered wings at the bar. The waiter left them by the cash register for over 20 minutes; they got cold, and he never brought them over. When we asked him about it, he was incredibly rude—he raised his voice at me and said he was busy. I had paid in advance, and I’m a customer, too. Plant is a terrible place  now. It’s not the Plant it used to be; it’s a disaster now. I had dinner at the nearby restaurant Scott's Seafood. I recommend it.

name: Marugame Udon
address: 3251 20th Ave, San Francisco, CA 94132, United States

google.name: Marugame Udon
google.address: 3251 20th Ave, San Francisco, CA 94132, United States
google.description: Hip spot where an array of udon dishes are prepared with noodles hand-pulled in an open kitchen.

top_reviews.content:
Came in for lunch just a little bit after opening on a weekend and the place was already filled with good aromas and busy staff. You order as you walk in and I had already looked at the menu and chose a large beef udon. After the person preparing the bowl added the tempura flakes and green onion I saw some fried foods in a case and grabbed a croquet and some tempura fried mushroom. A can of coke brought the total to about 23 bucks. The atmosphere is casual and modern and there's plenty of seating, probably even when it's very busy.

The udon was delicious, ample chewy noodles, fatty beef that wasn't tough and a rich hot broth. It was supremely filling and it's understandable why this is such a massive chain in Japan. The fried foods where fine, warm with a good texture, but the batter was quite bland, even accounting for the salty dipping sauce. I would probably skip those next time. The chili oil was a great addition.

Marugame Udon is perfect for a cloudy or rainy day and worth going a little out of the way for.

Marugame Udon never disappoints! The noodles were incredibly fresh, chewy, and cooked perfectly. I ordered the beef udon, and the broth was rich, flavorful, and comforting without being too heavy. The tempura was crispy, light, and made fresh, which paired perfectly with the udon. The staff was friendly, the restaurant was clean, and the service was fast even during a busy time. Great quality, generous portions, and excellent value for the price. I’ll definitely be coming back and highly recommend it to anyone looking for authentic, delicious udon!

We stopped in before heading to the crystal fair happening at Golden Gate Park. This was our first time here. Wow! Just wow!

#1 Fresh Made Udon Noodles!!!! Woooooowwwwww!!!! And Yuuuuuummmm!!!

#2 The menu looked so delightful, we had a difficult time figuring out what to order.

#3 It is a lunch line set-up. First, order your meal, then choose which toppings to add to your dish. THEN, check out the grab-ems -- deep fried seafood,  chicken and veggies -- to add to your meal tray. Then add beverages when you pay.

#4 The tables were clean and seating was ample -- both inside and outside.

#5 The food was AMAZING!!! Perfectly seasoned and cooked. Tasty!

Yuuuuuummmmmm!!!

Service with a smile.

Oh.. and one of the families that were there had more small children than adult hands so staff helped carry their food and drinks to their table. Above and beyond!

We will definitely go back.

Highly recommend.
Filling and delicious! I love the self service water and the dishes are honestly very affordable. However my noodles were pretty soggy and started splitting in half 😭

It’s been half a year since I last visited this place. They’ve replaced their Curry Soup base with Tomatama Curry, which is a mix of tomato and tamago (egg) with curry. Unfortunately, it doesn’t taste like actual curry at all. The regular-sized bowl has been reduced to a much smaller size, and even the quantity of udon noodles remains the same. However, the soup base has been limited, which is crucial for udon. It makes the udon cold very quickly and not enjoyable. The tempura sauce is also too sweet, which prevents me from dipping too much, ruining the tempura. Tempura is supposed to be dipped all the way and soaked up.

top_reviews.content: Pretty good burger. I tried the new seasonal burger that had a beef patty as well as a chicken patty and it cane protein style lettuce wrapped. It was very hard to eat it. The lettuce they use is not made for burger wraps at all. It was a wet soggy mess. I'd try this place again but will opt for a bunch next time.
I wish I had change to tip. The food was amazing. Chicken was well-cooked and seasoned. The Vegan/vegetarian patty was also yummy. Better than In-n-out in my opinion.

The burgers are good but definitely not super duper.
The chicken patty was nicely grilled with good sauce but they toasted the bun too which was not expected but not either. The lettuce was better too.
Overall, a better grilled chicken burger than BK or Macdonald.

Because the chocolate was too hot, I was offered to dip the fudge myself. . . Yes they did try and throw away two ice creams. I wish they gave me the one that is not “perfectly” dip instead of one half melted ice cream with half a small cup of chocolate fudge. . .

It’s your standard Super Duper Burgers. If you’re unfamiliar with the experience, but love burgers this place is a hit. Never skip the pickles. Personally, I’m a big fan of their pints. Love a good draft beer with lunch. Affordable. This is my go to spot for a place to sit and have a break from the bustling city life.

top_reviews.content: Best experience ever!!! Lol. Thank u to amaxing servers - Huy, George, Jaydin & Mariah. This place was the best and they took our photos bought us food everything was incredible. I didnt get a chance to film the steak because i was too busy eating it but it was so good best steakhouse ive been to

This was our fourth visit to the Emeryville location, and we've always had a great experience in the past, which is why we wanted to share our feedback. We appreciate that our request for a quiet table was accommodated for our daughter, and it worked out very well for our family.

The restaurant itself is beautiful, clean, and welcoming, and the food was excellent as always. We have no complaints about the quality of the food, the atmosphere, or the overall dining environment. Everything we ate was outstanding.

Unfortunately, the service during this visit was much slower than what we've experienced before. We repeatedly had to ask for drink refills, repeatedly request French fries for our daughter, and repeatedly ask for meat service because long periods would pass without servers coming to our table. At times, it felt like we were being overlooked. When we were ready to leave, we also had to ask multiple times for the check, and it took involvement from three different staff members before we finally received it.

We noticed staff appeared to be having a meeting during our visit, which may have contributed to the delays. We understand that every restaurant can have an off day, and based on our previous visits, we do not believe this experience reflects the usual high standard of service at this location.

We eventually had the opportunity to speak with the manager, Mr. Murmilo, who apologized for the inconvenience and graciously offered to waive the charges for our meal, requesting payment only for the beverages. We sincerely appreciate his professionalism, understanding, and willingness to make things right. He listened to our concerns and handled the situation in a way that left a positive impression.

We wanted to share this feedback because we genuinely enjoy this location and have had excellent experiences on our previous visits. The restaurant, food, and atmosphere continue to be outstanding, which is why today's service delays stood out. We appreciate Mr. Murmilo taking the time to listen and resolve the situation professionally.

Despite today's experience, we'll definitely be back. One slow day won't keep us away. The food was outstanding as always, and honestly, that amazing meat keeps calling us back. 😅🥩

Thank you for your time and for considering our feedback.

Sereene was an absolute gem of a server! Her patience and warmth while walking us through the menu made the whole experience feel so personal and unhurried — she clearly knows the menu inside and out. She was incredibly attentive and responsive to every request we had, going above and beyond without us even having to ask twice. You can tell she genuinely cares about making every guest feel welcome. Sereene is the kind of staff member who turns a great meal into a truly memorable dining experience. We’ll definitely be coming back — and hoping to be seated in her section again!

This was the first time I've gone to a Fogo de Chao and it was an amazing experience! George was attentive and considerate, he answered all our questions and made our experience one of a kind. The rest of the staff was also very attentive and got us everything we wanted.
The food was delicious and so unique. I loved every minute of it! I got to try new and interesting new cuts.
They truly make my birthday one to be remembered.

I went there for my birthday in December, and the food was so good- I was not disappointed! What truly made my night, though, was the care and attention from our server, Sidney. She was very respectful, attentive without being intrusive, and made us feel completely comfortable from the start. She took the time to explain how the experience works and checked in on us thoughtfully to make sure we had everything we needed.
If we return to Fogo, it will be not only for the food- but ultimately because of how well we were treated. I had an amazing birthday and was happy that my group had a great time trying so many different things. I loved it so much!

top_reviews.content:
I want to give a shout out to a wonderful employee at this NATION’S location
Her name is Sulba and she was very helpful when I was making a birthday purchase of pies. She went over the different flavors with me. She was very accommodating when one of my birthday coupons wasn’t going to redeem and I really enjoyed her customer service so she gets ALL THE STARS ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️Thank you so MUCH !!!!

I went out to nations with my girlfriend and her parents, and we had a lovely meal! I ordered a double cheeseburger with fries, my gf ordered a breakfast platter with ham, toast, hash browns and toast, and her parents ordered a breakfast burrito and another breakfast platter with scrambled eggs + jalapenos, sausages and pancakes. My burger was delicious, it was really big, about 5 inches in width. It came with fresh, juicy veggies and a succulent burger patty. The fries were crispy, and yummy, but I wouldn't reccomed ordering if your on a budget or don't really feel the need for fries. The fries portion was a bit small for a 3 dollar upcharge, but I would say it's worth it if you enjoy fries. The service was very nice, easy to order and they will call your order number out when they are done. It did not take long for the food to come out, maybe just 10-15 mins. They also have a soda fountain and a little area for condiments and a ketchup dispenser. Overall very much recommend this place! Yummy food for a reasonable price, and feels very American diner like.

Grew up with Nations, and this location is a good mix of nostalgic and modernized. Breakfast and burgers, good pie, what else can you ask for? Ingrid and Benjamin were so chipper and friendly for an early morning.

I recently went here for the first time and was amazed with the customer service. Nicole took my order and was kind, gave me options for what I would like, and was patient with me which I appreciated. My food was really good and I was completely satisfied. The restaurant looked neat and cleaned. 10/10 experience 🤩Will be coming
here again! Thank you Nicole for your kindness and Kytana for cooking the delicious burgers! Lastly, Shoutout to Ingrid for providing extra condiments when asked!

ONE OF MY ALL TIME FAVORITE SPOTS!!! I’m such a regular that they know my order by heart. Their food always hits the spot. This place is a go-to, especially on late nights, as they’re open 24 HOURS! Friendly service. Not super fancy inside but it’s cute! There are always fresh flowers on each table which is a nice touch. top_reviews.content: E/Z access from the freeway. Underground parking available near by. A refreshing walk to the restaurant. Seating right on the water. Service by Pearl was EXCELLENT! She made sure we had everything we needed! Food was Excellent. Great atmosphere with live piano music in the background. Very pleasant, I HIGHLY recommend.

Beautiful restaurant with a beautiful view. The food is decent, but it does not reach a top-tier or Michelin-level standard. The service is professional, but it does not go beyond a basic level of execution.
My biggest disappointment was the use of Dreyer’s commercial ice cream in the dessert presentation. For a serious steakhouse, this is not acceptable. In Oakland, with so many excellent artisanal ice cream makers nearby, the restaurant should either source a premium local product or make its own. A high-end dining experience requires attention to detail in every element, including the final course.

I had a wonderful experience at Scott’s Seafood in Oakland. I used to visit their Walnut Creek location often, so I was a bit sad when it closed—but this location definitely lived up to my expectations.

The restaurant is beautifully situated near the bay, which creates a relaxing and scenic atmosphere. The interior design is elegant and inviting, making it a great spot for both casual meals and special occasions.

The food quality was excellent—fresh, flavorful, and perfectly prepared. Everything we ordered was delicious, and you can really tell they take pride in their seafood.

What stood out the most was the service. Our server went above and beyond to make sure we were comfortable and had everything we needed. Their attention to detail and friendliness made the whole experience even better.

Overall, we had a fantastic time—honestly, a 5/5 experience. I highly recommend this location, especially if you’re looking for great seafood, a beautiful view, and outstanding service. I’ll definitely be coming back!

I've been to Scott's now for dinner and for their new Jazz Brunch and both have been nice! For dinner we had calamari, very delicious oyster Rockefeller (endorsed by my mother in law from New Orleans), seafood sautee and my husband had crab stuffed salmon with lobster sauce. Bananas foster bread pudding was also really good. We also sat by the window and had a beautiful sunset!

For brunch the selection was bigger than I expected. A nice chilled seafood section, mini bagels with lox and all the fixins, carving board, assorted composed dishes like crab cake Benedict and seafood en croute, and several sweet options including my favorite - blintzes! I took my mom there and she was thrilled. Jazz band played a lot of fun songs as well.

Overall this restaurant is perfect for a nice meal out. Tasty and scenic and well located in Jack London. Would definitely recommend!

Another excellent lunch at Scott's.  This is my family's go-to place in the Bay Area. Over the past few decades the food, service and atmosphere have remained excellent. The parking is convenient, views gorgeous and location perfect.

We look forward to many more years enjoying Scott's excellent food and service.

top_reviews.content:
While exploring Japantown in SF, we came across this authentic udon restaurant and were so happy we decided to wait. There was about a 30–40 minute wait on a Saturday, but it was well worth it. The restaurant has such a comfortable atmosphere with warm lighting and beautiful wooden features. They even have a little window where you can watch the cooks making fresh, handmade noodles, which was such a fun touch.

The service was exceptional, with helpful recommendations and great timing throughout our meal. We ordered the yuzu cocktails, mentai cream udon, and tempura udon, and everything was delicious and tasted incredibly fresh. You could really tell that a lot of care went into each dish.

We had such a great experience and will definitely be coming back. Highly recommend stopping by if you’re in Japantown and looking for a really good bowl of authentic udon.

Busy Udon restaurant in the Japan Center in Japantown SF on the 2nd floor. We put our name down on the Yelp waitlist and the wait was only about 30 minutes for Sunday during lunch.

Our waitress Jane was extremely helpful and pointed out the most popular items as well as the most popular and recommended ways to customize some dishes. Jane also checked in with us regularly to make sure everything was to our liking and made sure our water cups were always filled!

We ordered:
- Assorted Tempura: This came with shrimp, squid, broccoli, eggplant, sweet potato, and pumpkin tempura. I enjoyed their light and crispy batter, was a generous portion for 2 people.
- Mentai Cream Sauce Udon: So good, full of cream and cheese, very umami. Our waitress recommended to add a poached egg on top which made it even more rich!! Definitely would get this next time too. Perfectly cooked udon!
- Nabeyaki Udon: This had a very light broth but I felt it had too many toppings in it, wish it had less chicken pieces. But broth was good and noodles were perfect too.

Next time I would like to try the Tonkatsu Deluxe Udon or the Kitsune Udon!

Fantastic Japanese udon specialty restaurant in Japantown SF! We ordered the Mentaiko Cream Udon and the Tonkotsu Udon. I’d heard about their Mentaiko Cream Udon for the longest time, it’s one of their signature dishes and honestly, it absolutely lives up to the hype! Incredibly creamy and flavorful without feeling heavy or greasy at all. Tonkotsu Udon was okay. First impression, it was very filling with generous toppings like chashu, shrimp tempura, a soy-marinated egg and veggies. However, the broth wasn’t particularly impressive, if I’m being honest. It seems like the toppings saved the dishes, they're delicious, but that's all it offers. Next time I’ll definitely just order the Mentaiko Cream Udon. It’s absolutely scrumptious and seriously addictive!

They almost always have a waitlist, but you can join it online about 15 minutes before you arrive. I did that, and the whole dining experience was smooth and hassle-free.

Fully and wholly the best tokatsu udon I’ve ever eaten. Ideal place for family lunch or takeaway. Servers were courteous and willing to give recommendations. Highly recommend our server, Jane!

Best menu items: Takoyaki (appetizer), Tempura Curry Udon, Kitsune Udon, Katsudon Udon, and Regular Curry Udon. Great options for sake, beer, and non alcoholic drinks as well.

Food was fantastic. Great udon dishes and crispy onigiri bites (appetizer). The agedashi tofu was too big and wasn't crunchy enough; if it was half of the size, it'd have been better. Premium chashu could use some searing to enhance the flavor.

Our server, Janny, was amazing. She greeted us with enthusiasm and took time to explain the menu very well.

They were clearly appropriately staffed and were all working hard. Very refreshing after seeing so many restaurants chronically understaffed. I cannot recommend this place enough.

A well‑earned 5 stars.
This breakfast spot delivers the kind of meal that makes you pause mid‑bite. The breakfast burrito came bursting with flavour - rich, well‑seasoned, and wrapped just right. The pancakes were a standout: airy, tender, and beautifully crisp at the edges. Every plate felt thoughtful and satisfying, and the portion sizes were generous enough to keep even big appetites happy. A must‑visit for anyone chasing a memorable San Francisco meal.

Gets busy for lunch, so better to be early, before noon. Service is quick and menu has breakfast, lunch options, which can all be customized to your choice. The chicken break cutlet for the sandwich was perfect thickness and tasty, fries were also rightly salted on the lesser side to highlight their flavor, a few got stuck into bundles. Orange juice was fresh and good.

First meal in San Francisco and it set the bar high! Staff, service, food, and vibes all a 10/10! We all loved our dishes, and were very accommodating for vegan. Would and probably will go back… tomorrow haha

Great find for a Friday Brunch!! We had no wait and the staff is friendly, fast, and fantastic!!

We got the pancakes w/ fresh fruit x2, bacon (yum), and hash browns!! coffee & grand mimosa!

Everything was excellent and was a LOT of food. Nothing disappointed! The hash browns could have used a bit more s&p, but that was remedied with what was on the table!

Highly recommended and will definitely be back when we visit SF again!!

top_reviews.content:
We were invited here by good friends who spoke highly of this place and its long-standing reputation.

The staff were fantastic—friendly, approachable, and clearly skilled. Service was definitely one of the highlights of the evening.

The food, however, didn’t quite live up to the hype for us.

The famous shoestring fries were tasty, and the portion was very generous, but I didn’t find them particularly special. The aioli, on the other hand, was packed with garlic, which we absolutely loved.

The gnocchi was my favorite dish of the night—soft, creamy, with an elegant, subtle sauce and earthy mushrooms.

We also ordered the melon salad. It was fresh and fragrant, although the bresaola portion felt a little small and slightly dry.

The much-talked-about chicken was juicy and flavorful, and the stuffing underneath was delicious. The simple salad complemented it nicely. That said, while it was a very good dish, I don’t think it justified the $75 price tag.

Overall, we had an enjoyable evening thanks to the wonderful service, but the food didn’t quite match the reputation or the price.

That’s just my side of the story. 🫶🏼

Popped in to Zuni Cafe on a Thursday evening and there were plenty of tables available. The first thing I noticed was how hot the restaurant was, easily above 75 degrees so it was a bit uncomfortable.

I started with the fresh lime margarita. It was okay, nothing special and I wouldn’t recommend it. Then my caesar salad came. The croutons were incredible, lots of parm and fresh lettuce. I enjoyed it a lot!

The shoestring fries took over 25 minutes to come out. Massive portion, they were salty and the aioli was good. They charge extra for the aioli, they definitely needed it.

The service was nothing memorable, they have an automatic 20% gratuity. Overall, I could’ve skipped this restaurant on my SF trip. Decent food but at the price point there are definitely better options.

Our table for two for dinner started with excellent Acme bread and butter, olives, and the fried potatoes. I’d hoped to have the famous chicken but it was a 60–75 minute wait. We both opted for the quail instead—with lentils. This dish was tasty though hard to get all the meat off tiny bones. My friend loved the pavlova and I found the flourless chocolate cake pretty decent. Great drink selection.

This place has a lot of potential, ambience and interior are great. Staff seem good.

However, the menu sounds promising but underdelivered; the food is overpriced and mid at best. $4.50 oysters on ice cubes (not crushed ice), cold bread and butter (making it unspreadable), and the salad and entree seemed like something you could make at home with basic ingredients.

Mandatory 25% tip too which is ridiculous!

It was my first time here (but my husband’s nth time). He was raving about their chicken but we had no time to wait for it (75 minutes cooking/waiting time for this) so we ordered something else.

He ordered the olives and pizza, burger for me, and shoe string pizza for our daughter. The pizza looked good and my husband loved it. I tasted the olives but didn’t care for it. The hamburger was moist but lacked flavor (not well seasoned) - other cheaper burger options are far better than this. The highlight of the meal was surprisingly the shoestring fries - its simplicity was just great.

The service was commendable and the ambiance was that of Paris.

reviews_snippets.content: "Huge selection of tasty raw oysters, yummy shoe-string potatoes and chicken too!"
"Good coffee, good orange juice, good service, sensible prices for the quality."
"The chicken skin is crispy, salty, meat is juicy, cooked in their brick oven."

name: San Tung
address: 1031 Irving St, San Francisco, CA 94122, United States

google.name: San Tung
google.address: 1031 Irving St, San Francisco, CA 94122, United States
google.description: Famed dry fried chicken wings, handmade noodles & other Chinese eats in a no-frills setting.

top_reviews.content:
Honestly the wings are phenomenal, however bad the service was and the dirty restroom…
Had the combo fried rice and Mongolian beef very solid options. But the main reason to come here is the wings. Im not even sure if i want anything else from here other than that.
I expected the wings to be good but they really are phenomenal.. 6pc for $15 during lunch and 12pc for $20

San Tung absolutely lived up to the hype. From start to finish, the food was incredible and easily one of the best meals we had while visiting the Bay Area.

Of course we had to try the famous dry-fried wings, and they were phenomenal. Perfectly crispy, coated in that signature sweet and garlicky sauce, and packed with flavor. They truly deserve all the praise they get.

Everything else we ordered was just as impressive. The shrimp and broccoli was fresh and well-seasoned, the chow mein had great texture and flavor, and the salt and pepper shrimp and calamari were perfectly cooked with a delicious crispy coating and just the right amount of seasoning. The dry shrimp dish was also fantastic and added another bold flavor to the table.

Every dish came out hot, fresh, and full of flavor. You can really tell the kitchen takes pride in what they serve.

If you’re in the San Francisco area, San Tung is absolutely worth the visit. We came for the wings but left impressed by everything we tried. Highly recommend!

We ordered the Dry Fried Flounder Fillet, Three Deluxe Spicy Sauce Noodles, and the Famous Original Dry Fried Chicken Wings. The fish was outstanding — perfectly crispy on the outside, warm and flaky on the inside, and packed with flavor. The spicy sauce noodles were incredibly tasty and definitely something I’d order again. The chicken wings were also nicely crispy and well sauced; they were good for a one-time try, though personally they weren’t my favorite wings I’ve had.
The standout dishes for me were the noodles and fish — both were so delicious, and I’d absolutely come back to try more dishes on the menu. We did wait several hours for a table, which was tough, so next time I’d probably order takeout since the food is great but the wait wasn’t worth it. Overall, definitely worth trying!

We ordered two small soups and the fried chicken wings.

🍲 Tomato Soup and Egg Drop Soup: For a small, they were quite generous with the portion size. Definitely could have ordered one to share. Both were flavored quite well and enjoyable.

🍗 San Tung Fried Chicken: I heard the fried chicken was a must-try, but it wasn’t for me. It was far too sweet for me and just reminded me of korean fried chicken. I don’t prefer my protein on the sweet side, and these left a jarring sweet aftertaste in my mouth I did not enjoy. I will not be back for the wings but would be interested in other things.

The prices appear to be a bit more expensive for Chinese food, but the portion sizes are slightly larger than average.

The San Tung Chinese restaurant sure smacks out some amazing Char Siu Chicken, and the Potsickers were simply amazing!  This restaurant is far underrated, my old pal Albino Bob raved about it so much...I just had to go!  It was well worth the trip across the bridge!  5 ☆☆☆☆☆'s all day long!

reviews_snippets.content: "The dry fried wings are really tasty and the service was good."
"Ordered seafood tan tan noodle size is good for 2 people !"
"Food was alright but bit sweet for me and not spicy as real Chinese."

name: Beretta Valencia
address: 1199 Valencia St, San Francisco, CA 94110, United States

google.name: Beretta Valencia
google.address: 1199 Valencia St, San Francisco, CA 94110, United States
google.description: Handcrafted pizzas, small bites & unique cocktails keep this trendy spot hopping.

top_reviews.content:
A modern take on your more traditional Italian, funky-hip interior, $10 bar bites during happy hour.

* Calamari (perfectly fried, with grilled lemon wedge - nice touch!)
* Pizza Margherita (extra thin crust, chewy goodness)

Pastas are well-prepared. Linguini alle Vongole is no doubt good, served with perfectly plump manilla clams; the sofrito adds a nice herbaceous punch though may surprise a purist.

Overall, an excellent option when wanting to commune with friends or family over a simply good meal. Nice option for first date at the bar.

Four of us enjoyed a delicious dinner at Baretta's last Saturday. Although the restaurant was very busy, the manager, Raul, gave us a warm welcome and made us feel well taken care of throughout the evening.
We started by sharing a wonderful salad and olives, followed by two delicious pizzas and two excellent pasta dishes. We finished with a tasty tiramisu that was the perfect ending to the meal.
Despite how busy the restaurant was, every course arrived promptly. Raul checked in with us several times to make sure everything was to our satisfaction. He could not have been more gracious or attentive. We are excited to return. Thank you, Raul!

Went here on a date two things struck me upon arrival: this establishment is way more relaxed and unpretentious than pictures might otherwise indicate and when packed it is an overwhelming experience. I would recommend coming here during less busy hours, since there seems to be some combination of witchcraft and acoustic physics at play that allow what might be a normal conversation to break the sound barrier. Our server was very kind and able to move us a table away from our neighbors, which helped, but the issue of noise could only really be mitigated by people emptying out. Ordered the arancini, carpaccio de pulpo, and caesar salad to start, followed by the lasagna and bartenders pizza. The caesar salad was definitely the star of the entire meal, not your ordinary bed of chopped romaine hearts, they clearly put care into purchasing their produce here, and the real treat of course is that they use boquerones. I would recommend this salad to anyone in the city. The pizza was also good– actually spicy without the need for supplementary condiments or other accoutrements– but nothing to make it really stand out amongst other pizzas in the bay area. The other two appetizers were good, but not necessarily something to come running back for, just solid well-prepared food. The real letdown was the lasagna. It had been left in the broiler for too long so that the top was charred to the point of having that carbon flavor you usually only get when setting marshmallows on fire while out camping. It was quite heavy, (even for lasagna!) due to the inordinately high meat:ricotta ratio and had not rested properly so that the entire thing slid apart 3 bites in, leaving something of a mess in front of me. The bolognese was not bad, but frankly I could have made better at home, which is not a quality I look for in pasta.

First time here with a few friends. Waitress was attentive but not bothersome. Food was tasty. There are vegan options available as well. I had the summer risotto. Havent had a risotto in a while so a bit salty for my taste but im not sure if it is normally that flavorful.
The burrata walnut toast was delish.

In terms of atmosphere, lots of conversations but not excessively loud from where we were sitting.

For an app and main, expect around $40-50 after tax tip
Everything was delicious. Service was a little wonky. Drinks were delayed and inconsistent. Overall pretty good experience.

reviews_snippets.content: "A great late night Italian place with lots of small dishes and good pizza."
"The food and service as amazing and the staff was the friendliest."
"Really nice atmosphere, delicious food, and yummy drinks."

name: Il Casaro Pizzeria
address: 348 Columbus Ave, San Francisco, CA 94133, United States

google.name: Il Casaro Pizzeria
google.address: 348 Columbus Ave, San Francisco, CA 94133, United States
google.description: Pizza, Italian street food, and wine are served in a cozy space with a mozzarella bar and late-night hours.

top_reviews.content: Il Casaro Pizzeria was an absolute throwback to Napoli. From our Italian waiter’s impeccable recommendations to the vibrant, energetic neighborhood vibe, this spot checked every single box: busy, fast, fresh, and authentic. The carbonara was easily the best we’ve had since visiting Rome—finally, a kitchen that knows how to execute it properly. The Neapolitan Calabrese tasted just like what we remember from Naples, and wrapping up the meal with a classic espresso and an exceptional panna cotta was the perfect finish. Hands down one of the best pizza spots we’ve eaten at since Italy!

Everything was so good! Our waitress was super welcoming and helped us navigate the menu since it was our first time. Just a heads-up: the portions are huge. We were totally stuffed and still couldn’t finish everything—wish we had more room!
We were so hungry at first that we forgot to snap a photo of the grilled calamari, but it was amazing. It’s done in the pizza oven, so it has that perfect char without being greasy like the fried stuff.
I added the imported Burrata to my pizza, and it’s so perfect! Much better than the same thing I got from supermarket, so creamy and rich. The pizza crust was perfectly charred too, with a LOT of mushrooms and prosciutto. My partner originally said she wasn't in the mood for pizza, but she literally couldn't stop eating it lol.
The Pesto pasta she ordered was also fresh and light, which balanced out the richness of the pizza.

We ordered Tiramisu for dessert- it’s moist and light, not overly sweet (which is important) but packed with flavor.

Also, I have to mention their Calabrian chilies!! Those little peppers are salty, fiery, and have that perfect fermented tang. They remind me so much of the pickled peppers from Hunan China.

Hands down the best pizza I’ve had since moving to the United States nearly a decade ago. We ordered the Quattro Formaggi and the Diavola, and both were downright mind-blowing. Truly authentic, delicious pizza. Highly, highly recommended!

Some of the best pizza in San Francisco! My dad works with Italians and they loved this place so I had to check it out. The dough is soft but not too thick. The pizza is cooked perfectly. Thryvhave a nice selection all day but if you want the classic marinara you can get that in the happy hour menu, which is 3 to 5. My girlfriend also liked their spritzer. For dessert we got the lemon sorbet and afagado which were both expertly made.

The pizzas were absolutely amazing! The crust was fresh, the toppings were high quality, and all the flavors came together perfectly. If you're looking for an authentic Italian pizza experience, this is definitely the place to go. We also ordered the tiramisu for dessert, and it was just as incredible as the pizza. Everything was delicious, and we'll definitely be back!

reviews_snippets.content: "Fun atmosphere, fantastic pizza, lots of variety in toppings, and great service."
"Great place to enjoy food, enjoy your company, and have a relaxing night out."
"High quality ingredients, cooked to perfection and wonderful staff."

name: Gott's SF Ferry Building
address: Marketplace 1, Ferry Building, Ferry Plz Bldg 6, San Francisco, CA 94111, United States

google.name: Gott's SF Ferry Building

top_reviews.content:
Gott’s @Marketplace 1, Ferry Building, Ferry Plz Bldg #6, San Francisco, CA 94111

This newly opened branch at the San Francisco Ferry Terminal is a great addition to the area. We chose to eat here because dogs are welcome in the outdoor seating section, which is a big plus for pet owners.
The line can get long during busy hours, but ordering is simple since you can grab a menu while waiting. Prices are reasonable, and the food was excellent. We tried the burger, tacos, and French fries, and everything was fresh, flavorful, and satisfying.
The restaurant is clean and well organized. Condiments and a water refill station are conveniently located on the side. There’s also plenty of seating indoors, along with a large TV. Overall, it was a pleasant dining experience, and we’ll definitely be back to try more items on the menu. Highly recommended!

I ordered the double cheeseburger. They serve them with a little bit of pink in the middle. Most places default to well-done, but this was juicy and tasted like high-quality protein. The buns were solid and they didn’t skimp on the sauce, which I always appreciate.
We came in with a group of six, So I obviously had to wait a bit for my order. However, I think this place is usually pretty busy, so be prepared to wait for a bit. The staff was kind.
For the side, I tried the onion rings. To be fair, I’m not a huge 'onion guy' to begin with, but these tasted a bit underwhelming. If you’re like me, you might want to stick to the burger—which is clearly the star of the show anyway.
I'd be more inclined to give it a higher score if it didn't cost as much as it did. If I'm going to spend $17 for one burger ( not including fries) I need to be super impressed.
Overall, a very solid experience and a  7.8 out of 10. I’d recommend it if you’re in the area."

I honestly love the place and very satisfied with the service. I am vegetarian and I ordered Texas avocado burger with veggie Pattie and cheese fries !! I love it. I would recommend people who are vegetarian and looking for nice place to have a burger. (Although I guess they have egg bun- not sure. Just confirm your priorities before you order )

But over all, highly satisfied food quality! Even though it was busy, it was good !

I love the space, clean lines, simple, full of natural light. Classy but no frills. Bus your own table. Staff always polite and helpful. These are generous burgers, and based on how they come out I think they are cooked on what seems to be a traditional flat grill. I appreciate that you can get wine, beer, hotdogs, sweet potato fries and other things besides burgers. Great pitstop in ferry bldg before or after ferry trip.

Soft serve ice cream. Tried their Straus Vanilla and can definitely stand behind Strauss quality! Will have to come back and try some other flavors. For a little sweet treat, it is not a bad price as most places! Check it out!
Also note, they have a "Soft Serve" booth that is completely separate from the restaurant! I have not tried their burgers, but will give it a try at some point.

reviews_snippets.content: "Enjoyed the vibe, lots of burger choices and good selection of draft beer."
"The food tastes good; I ordered a hot dog and sweet potato fries."

name: Taqueria Cancun
address: 2288 Mission St, San Francisco, CA 94110, United States

top_reviews.content: Incredible breakfast burrito. Huge portions. Tortilla is chewy and the flavor and textures are great. I asked for no rice but would also get no beans next time.

We were looking for the best taco spot in SF and this place kept popping up. it was just what everyone described. The food was amazing, and they served big portions. The meat was flavorful. If you dine in they give chips and salsa while you wait for your food. I got the carne asada platillo and my gf got the alambre platillo and it came with avocado which is really rare. we also got a taco to try it and it was really good. The service was fast and the people were really nice. The vibe is 10/10 couldn’t beat it. Would definitely recommend for an authentic Mexican restaurant experience

Was on my way home and just needed something to eat. I ordered the Chicken Enchiladas and a Lime Jarritos for here. The food was ready fairly quick. It came with tortilla chips, salsa, refried beans, and rice. The chicken was overcooked, dry, and burnt. I did enjoy the rest of the meal.
Delicious, huge portions, reasonable prices. I had the loaded chicken taco. I don't usually have chicken but I was trying to be healthy. I will probably have chicken again, it really impressed.

The food is hearty and affordable, but lacks flavor a bit for me. I was planning to try this place for a while as it’s a true SF staple but was disappointed by the quesadilla I picked. Just tons of cheese and bland chicken. Barely could finish a half of it. The wet burrito had more taste thanks to the sauce so that’s probably the safe choice if you can manage to eat that huge thing. The service was very friendly though and the ambiance of a lively Mexican spot was nice.

reviews_snippets.content: "Crispy, tasty, hot burritos with a variety of fillings to choose from."
"Great service and great employees delicious food an affordable price"
"High quality, big portion food at reasonable prices with quick service."

top_reviews.content: Had a quick bite here while I was in the area. The service is good, the place is clean, and the food was great. I ordered the Super Famoso Burrito, and it was HUGE! I will probably order it without the enchilada sauce next time. For the price, this burrito is a great buy.

I was craving something fresh and spicy and convinced hubby to stop on our way back to the city. We ordered 1 aguachiles and a pitcher of lime Margarita. Because we sat directly in front of the bar,  I was able to see the bartender fixing drinks. I saw him start a pitcher using a big can of orange concentrate and never saw him use one  lime so i just figured it was someone else's order, but no. The pitcher was all canned orange juice and a wedge of fresh orange  thrown in. It tasted horrible and the taste of canned juice couldn't be masked by one wedge of orange. I instantly regretted ordering the pitcher over just a couple of margaritas at almost $40 a pitcher! They took about an hour to bring out the food, which had me worried because its just shrimp in spicy lime juice and they were not that busy(hubby kept teasing that they were unfreezing the shrimp). Finally the order comes out and again, at $38 an order I expected a little more than six shrimp cut in half (the long way). While we did enjoy the flavor it just wasnt worth it. Btw, the waitress that brought out the pitcher never returned to check on us after bringing out the drinks and we didnt get any attention til another waitress brought us the food. We were less than satisfied to say the least. We ended up paying at the counter because both waitresses never returned. Oh, we were only able to do half of the "margarita pitcher" it was pretty bad. The end result ,  $80 plus $10 tip(hubby didn't even wanna leave a tip). Yeah, we will not be returning.

My parents have brought me here since like 07, I have been going ever since. It is honestly life changing. I tell everyone about this spot. Todays burrito blew me away and it's big enough to split n half for lunch n dinner

Went for dinner this evening. Big menu which is kind of intimidating but the have everything you might want. Service was very good, polite and quick. Nice atmosphere, lots of local people around who looked like they were regulars, which is a great sign. Portions very large and very filling. Everything tasted great, we had an amazing meal. A must go place for everyone who likes Mexican food 👌.

I had the grilled chicken burrito and it was sooo good. It was my first time there. My best friend took me. I will definitely  be bk to try more. A guy was singing, I enjoyed it even though I don't speak Spanish.

top_reviews.content:
Saturday morning seemed unusually quiet, but service was very slow. I’m not sure if they were short-staffed, but our server appeared to be covering a large section on her own. Because of that, check-ins were minimal, and my coffee wasn’t refilled until I was nearly ready to leave.

As for the food, the French toast was a bit dry for my taste. The corned beef hash was the highlight of the meal, though it could have benefited from a little more seasoning.

Overall, this is a good spot if you’re looking for a no-frills, classic American-style breakfast. While the experience wasn’t exceptional this visit, it has the potential to be better with more attentive service and a few improvements in the kitchen.

I made an online order. I ordered biscuits and gravy, an extra side of gravy and some hash browns. I also asked for ketchup and condiments. I arrived and my food is just sitting out on the cabinet. There was no ketchup and condiments, and my extra side of gravy wasnt in the bag. I went back in and got my side of gravy. i got home and im missing a sausage link and the hashbrowns were extremely burned. Burned beyond eating. I would not return to this location.

Enjoyed an early breakfast here.  Excellent biscuits and gravy.  My older son tried the volcano - very good!  The younger enjoyed Mac and cheese with bacon.  I really like that they serve their entire menu all day.  Service was attentive and professional.  The decor is charming.  We enjoyed our first time at this restaurant.

Enjoyed my breakfast of the scram bowl. It was very large so I will be taking the portion pictured home. Tasty and my husbands bacon looked like it was cooked to perfection. I may have to taste some of his lol. I’ve been to one in Colorado Springs and this did not disappoint.
My chocolate chip pancakes were fluffy and sweet.  Great service.  The place looks like it was filmed in Twin Peaks.

reviews_snippets.content: "Variety of food on menu very kind waiters and waitresses."
"The waiter gave me an excuse it would take 15-20 mins to get the eggs I ordered."

name: Mel's Drive-In
address: 3355 Geary Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94118, United States

google.name: Mel's Drive-In
google.address: 3355 Geary Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94118, United States
google.description: Part of a local chain, this family-friendly 1950s-style diner serves classic American comfort fare.

top_reviews.content:
Overall 3 rating is the best I can do. There was nothing particularly wrong with the food but, there was nothing special about it either.

The service was poor as I had to wave down the server several times to get my coffee topped off after my breakfast was served. By the way, he paid more attention to his conversing with his co-workers than he paid scouting the room for his customers needing assistance.

The food is nothing to write home about. I ordered a vegetable omelet and they must’ve put a whole bell pepper in it. It would’ve been better if they’d put more than one leaf of spinach, it was dry and the egg was over cooked on one side.

My dining partners seemed to enjoy their meals. However, the turkey burger looked dry. I did enjoy sampling the onion rings as they were the best item I tasted.

We dined on Thursday June 11, 2026 at about 10:30 am. I can’t find the receipt to include the waiters name.

If I ever find myself there again, I will definitely not sit in his area and order the onion rings, only.

Coming back to this place was a real trip down memory lane. I used to come here after school (and sometimes during school 😉) back in the late ’90s, so walking in again brought back a lot of great memories.

The clam chowder was awesome—just as comforting as I remembered—and the cheesecake was excellent too. It’s great to see that the food still holds up after all these years.

The atmosphere still has that classic Mel’s diner vibe, and the staff were friendly and welcoming, which made the experience even better. More than anything, this place reminded me why Mel’s was such a staple back then—classic vibes, familiar flavors, and a timeless feel. Definitely glad I stopped by again.

I had a very frustrating and disappointing experience at this Mel's location, for multiple reasons:
1) Two food quality issues*
2) Our Groupon ($20 off a meal for two, purchased for $12.50, so it was actually a $7.50 discount) was not accepted. (We'd purchased it about an hour before coming in and it perhaps wasn't in their system yet, but we've done this at a different Mel's before without any issues.) The server, who was otherwise pleasant, charged us full price for the meal and told us we would have to get it resolved by coming back another day, when she was on shift again and would remember us. So, Mel's owed us $20. We were a little surprised that they didn't just comp $20 off the bill and call it a day, especially given the hassle that followed.
3) We came back the next day with our Groupon, which the system accepted this time, but the server couldn't retroactively reduce our bill and didn't have a manager around to fix it.
4) We then had to have a phone call the *following* day with a manager to try to fix this, and he said we could just use the Groupon on another occasion. (No we couldn't, we'd already "redeemed" it on our end for use, which sets a relatively short deadline. Also, having to pay *two* large dinner bills to get the discount is not equivalent. Thirdly, as we found out later, this was false because it had been marked in the Groupon interface as used.) We had to insist to get a measly $20 refund, which the manager granted because it was "only" $20, and which was value we *already* had given them, not a discount.
All told, it took us a few hours of our time over multiple attempts and conversations over three days to get a measly $7.50 discount on our dinner for two.

*We didn't try to bring up the food issues with the staff because things are tough for everyone these days, but man... While many of the dishes served at Mel's are tasty, their chicken soup is not. Don't get it. They had clearly taken too-old soup with disintegrating noodles and added a lot of fresh pasta to it, resulting in what was basically a wet, bland pasta dish with a number of noodles so old they had swelled to 2.5x their size and turned to mush. See photo.
I ordered the Lana Del Rey milkshake (a specialty shake with several components). It was clearly a Lana shake but had a strong flavor of banana in it, which was definitely not the recipe, so... do they clean their equipment? Did part of a banana fall in without being noticed? Good thing I'm not allergic to bananas, but some folks definitely are.
My partner ordered a burger that was reportedly delicious, which is why this is 2 stars and not 1.

Dining at Mel’s Drive-In really felt like stepping into a classic American retro diner! I tried the salmon Caesar salad, the wrap, and the fried chicken burger — every dish came in generous portions. The salmon was perfectly seared, tender inside and crisp outside, paired with fresh lettuce and cheese. The wrap with potato salad on the side was creamy and flavorful, while the fried chicken burger was crispy and juicy, complemented by golden fries that were impossible to resist. The staff were friendly, and the food arrived quickly. The whole experience was fun and nostalgic — highly recommended for anyone wanting to enjoy authentic American diner vibes!
Very\nDelicious hamburgersThe lady let us 2 seniors split a hamburger and French fries.So we can have a milkshake each. She was so nice.It was great. the price was right.
