google.description: Old-school diner open 24/7 & dishing out burgers, malts & other classic all-American fare.

top_reviews.content: Open early, open late, Orphan Andy’s is the place! Such a vibrant energy as I walked in, the decoration is fabulous. The service is top notch and everyone is so friendly. I ordered the steak and eggs with hotcakes and a freshly squeezed orange juice. The pancakes were scrumptious and the steak and eggs were just right. I want to check this place out at night time, I imagine it gets popping. I would definitely be back to try more on the menu.

This is a staple of LGBTQ+ history, and the atmosphere is incredible. The interior alone makes the experience feel memorable, especially for someone visiting the Castro for the first time.

That said, the food was decent rather than especially memorable. My partner and I had different reactions to it, so we compromised on a three-star rating. I do not work in food service, so I cannot speak to the preparation with much authority, but my partner is a professional baker and an experienced cook, and she felt that some of the ingredients tasted canned rather than fresh. I personally did not notice that as strongly, but I thought it was worth mentioning.

I would absolutely bring tourists here if they were curious about the Castro, LGBTQ+ history, or just wanted a fun and distinctive dining experience. The atmosphere is the real standout, and for a first-time visit, it is hard to beat.

After a fun adventure with the ladies in the City we were so excited to try this diner out. The first thing we did was adore all the Christmas lights and take all the pics. Then after sitting down and ordering the yummiest 24 hour diner dinner we relaxed in the jolly atmosphere until our food arrived in less than 10 minutes. Not only is this place adorable, but the service and the food are top notch.
My fiance and I were recommended this restaurant from a friend when we visited San francisco. Was not disappointed. Excellent service and great food!

Worth Every Minute of the Wait

If you’re looking for a true San Francisco classic, Orphan Andy’s delivers in every possible way. Yes, the wait on New Year’s Day was a little long—but it was absolutely worth it.

This small, no-frills diner in the heart of the Castro has all the charm you want in a neighborhood institution. The food was superb—comforting, flavorful, and cooked exactly the way diner food should be. Every bite reminded us why places like this endure.

What really sets Orphan Andy’s apart, though, is the service. Sassy, friendly, and full of personality, the staff makes you feel like part of the scene rather than just another customer. It’s warm, unapologetically authentic, and refreshingly real.

If you want great food, iconic Castro vibes, and service with attitude (in the best way), Orphan Andy’s is a must. We’ll gladly wait again.

the pasta with veggies did not really do it for me. i felt it was an overabundance of corn and veggie accoutrements, which was distracting.

pork loin was nice and tender. the seasoning for the loin was nicely done.

the olive oil cake was something special. i could taste the olive oil from the cake. nice and fluffy as well

The last five years I came here, they used to scrape the bread crumbs off the table for me. this time they did not do it even after we finished the bread and going into the entree round. they finally did it before the desserts.

overall, i applaud the use of fresh ingredients.

Delicious food and great service.  Definitely price and a special occasion kind of place.  We were pleasantly surprised with the small appetizer, dessert tea, and small candies (orange peel and chocolate covered almonds) included with the prix fixe menu!

Had lunch at the cafe -- 3.5 stars, rounded down. It was frustratingly almost great. But IMO for an $80 lunch it needs to be solidly fantastic.

My waiter took long to take my order for main and for dessert. Food wait times were very long as well. Took many minutes for my dessert to come, and it was a slice of galette with a scoop of ice cream.

Baked salmon - Almost incredible. The cook on the salmon was gorgeous. But the flavours and seasoning were just far too subtle for my taste. Apricot galette - Almost incredible. Overall it was just too tart, even with the ice cream trying to balance things out. The crust was great though.

Went there because of the recommendation and reviews. The food had good flavors. But not sure if the price justifies it. It’s a prix fixed menu in the dining area. Their cooking is a harmonious blend of simplicity and elegance, avoiding any over-the-top or flashy elements. Chez Panisse truly understands the intricacies of each ingredient and flavor, employing the most effective techniques to elevate them to their fullest potential.

top_reviews.content:
This place is a must try from the perspective of the atmosphere, style of service, and uniqueness of cuisine. It was an extremely fun experience to sit right at the bar, learn about the different dishes and watch them be made, and try them ourselves. Due to the dimsum style service, which was quite fun, don't expect to eat in any particular order.

We shared around 11 or 12 dishes across their standard menu as well as their rotating menu.

Though this is labelled as "American" cuisine, each dish seemed like a fusion of another culture, be it east Asian, south Asian, etc. For example the 7th picture was a beat based dish that tasted just like my mom's beat curry. Flavours aren't subtle in most of the dishes -- that's not necessarily a bad thing, it just depends on your taste.

Overall a fun and playful food experience!

High energy place and fun just being in the middle of the hustle and bustle - the chefs were ever moving, churning out dish after dish, the waiters were carrying plates of tapas or wheeling them around eg. Scallop crudo, potato chips with trout dip, pork belly with fish sauce, etc I really wanted to like the food but the ones I tried such as pork belly, sourdough-sourrkraut with pecorino and ricotta, black cod toast, state bird were too either too heavy or salty or hard (deep fried). The only one I liked was the scallop crudo.

Overall, fun for a try but I expected much higher standards from a one star Michelin.

I generally do not ever leave comments but this was definitely one of the worst meals i’ve paid for in SF.

To start off with dim sum style appetizers, hog island oysters with kraut was not good together. The kraut was too crunchy and too much on soft oysters which was overpowering in general. The pate is not very good, i think french butter would have been better with almond fancier. The “best” one was the handrolls and even that i didn’t understand other toppings with scallops. Just overall did not have any harmony with the ingredients.

Regarding the “main” dishes we ordered state bird and the steak. The state bird chicken seemed a little undercooked and not worth $24 for 2 pieces of average fried chicken. Also the steak was tender for sure but was so salty i couldn’t taste the numbing sensation from sichuan peppercorn.

I actually didn’t have high hopes and i genuinely felt robbed. Their drinks and water were very good.

Wow! 5 stars cannot even comprehend how wonderful this establishment was. My only complaint was not having a bigger stomach! We arrived for our reservation and was informed our table wasn’t quite ready yet, but we could step to their sister establishment next door for a quick libation while we waited. It was perfect timing for us to enjoy a quick cocktail before dinner. Upon being seated, we were quickly educated on how things would be orchestrated for dinner service. PSA - they are not exaggerating when they say they will bring round à la carte items for you to pick from in addition to the dinner menu. Wow! So many options - it was a tad overwhelming but in the best way. We opted for 4 à la carte items and 3 dinner items. A bit much for 2 people, but we just couldn’t say no. It was all outstanding. Sadly we had no room for dessert and that was one of the parts I was really looking forward to. However, we definitely had no shortage of amazing food. All our service staff was incredibly knowledgeable and professional. Thank you for a wonderful time.

Arrived at 4:40 as walk-ins and were second in line. More walk-ins started trickling in around 5 and by the time the restaurant opened at 5:30 it was bustling. Were seated quickly and there were many servers walking around so flagging down attention was easy. They were attentive of dietary restrictions, which is impressive for the serving style. The dishes we ordered a la carte at the beginning of the meal came almost at the very end of the meal by which point we were already pretty full. Although the dim sum concept was fun, I really did not like the flavor and texture profiles of almost all of the dishes. Many were way too oily such as the almond financiers, pancakes, toast, and noodles. The toast was so tough that I could barely cut through it with a knife. Some flavor combinations did not pair well at all, such as radish with szechuan peppercorn. The almond financier really overpowered the duck liver mousse and I couldn’t taste the mousse at all. Other flavor profiles were just not interesting. Toast with cheese and corn tasted exactly like you would expect. And there were texture issues, specifically with the fried beans. The outsides were the texture of popcorn kernels, not crispy, and the inside was dry. I thought the dishes overused jalapeños and too many were fried. The peach bacon cheese pancake was interesting, it tasted like a breakfast platter in a bite. The only dish that actually tasted good was whipped cheese with cherries, but the cherries weren’t pitted.

Hidden gem! This place has one of the best Ramen I’ve ever had! The flavors were on point with the perfect amount of spice! The atmosphere is perfect, open kitchen dim lights and nice decor. I would recommend it.

The noodles were also perfectly down with some but not too much chewiness.

Washing  this down with an ice-cold Sapporo beer was perfect!

Decor was simple and chic and service was good.

Great for a quick, savory and light meal.

top_reviews.content: One of the best Italian spots I’ve been to! The portions are HUGE (come hungry), and the owners are incredibly warm and welcoming — they truly treat you like family. We ordered Pasta and their specialty Roman Pizza. The dough of the Pizza takes 72hrs to rise! What an incredible experience. Ended up our night with Tiramasu 🤩Definitely coming back when in San Francisco area!

As Authentic as It Gets – An Absolute Gem in SF! 🇮🇹
As someone who was born and raised in Italy, I have a pretty high bar when it comes to Italian food outside of home. Il Piccolo Forno doesn't just meet that standard: it completely exceeds it. This place is as authentic as it gets.
From the moment you walk in, the atmosphere is warm, welcoming, and wonderfully family-oriented. The customer service is stellar across the board, and the owner, Giuseppe, is a fantastic host who makes you feel like family the second you sit down.
Now, let’s talk about the food, because it’s nothing short of incredible:
The Pasta: You can immediately tell it’s genuine homemade pasta. The texture, rich flavors, and sauce pairings in all the pasta dishes are absolute perfection.
The Pinsa: The Roman pinsa pizza is hands-down amazing. The crust has that ideal light, airy crunch that is so hard to find outside of Italy.
If you’re looking for true Italian hospitality and mind-blowing, traditional food in San Francisco, do yourself a favor and visit Il Piccolo Forno. Buon appetito 😋

A cosy restaurant serving genuinely delicious Italian fare. The meal began with complimentary bread and olive oil. The burrata arrived like a cloud - creamy, soft, and beautifully balanced with briny olives and sweet cherry tomatoes. The lobster stuffing of ravioli di aragosta was perfectly minced, and luxurious. The spaghetti alla carbonara was silky, and lifted by generous chunks of guanciale. We ended with an affogato that delivered the perfect finale - bold, sweet and beautifully comforting. The pastas did take a while to reach our table, but knowing everything was freshly prepared made the wait feel entirely worth it. The staff were warm, cheerful, and genuinely welcoming throughout our meal. This is one spot I’ll happily return to, no hesitation.

This place is everything I like about a small neighborhood Italian spot - simple, casual, and completely unpretentious.

Food - We ordered the lobster ravioli and a pasta with truffle sauce, and both were absolutely delicious. I’m honestly drooling just thinking about them again. The flavors were rich and comforting without feeling overly heavy.

Service - The staff were also very friendly, which added to the relaxed vibe of the place. The restaurant itself is very small, so it’s a good idea to make reservations beforehand.

Nothing fancy here, just really good food and a laid-back atmosphere. If you’re in the area and craving good Italian food, this spot is definitely worth a visit.

From the moment I walked into Piccolo Forno, I was greeted so warmly by the Italian servers that I immediately felt like family, even dining solo. The hospitality alone set the tone for what became one of the nicest dining experiences I’ve had.

I started with a glass of crisp Pinot Grigio and the complimentary bread basket served with absolutely incredible olive oil and balsamic, simple, authentic, and impossible to stop eating. The ambiance was vibrant and lively, like sitting in a charming Italian countryside trattoria filled with energy, conversation, and warmth.

The Caesar salad with anchovies was perfectly balanced and fresh, and the special fussili with seafood was outstanding—rich, flavorful, and cooked to perfection. Every bite tasted authentic, comforting, and deeply satisfying. Their chili oil was an absolute delight with the pasta. I almost didn’t ask for it because I didn’t want to offend anyone, but the waiter jokingly said, “Maybe you like it spicy,” and I’m so glad he did. That chili oil elevated the dish to another level. I know I will be dreaming about it.

To finish, the tiramisu was heavenly: light, creamy, and the perfect ending to an exceptional meal.

Piccolo Forno didn’t just serve amazing food — it gave me a genuine piece of Italy. From the atmosphere to the service to every course, this place is truly special.

top_reviews.content:
I honestly don't think I've ever felt this disappointed by a restaurant experience.

We were excited to find a Southern restaurant in San Francisco and ordered quite a bit—the po' boys, a chicken sandwich, shrimp and grits, and mac and cheese. Unfortunately, almost everything about the experience fell short.

The biggest red flag was how quickly the food arrived. There's simply no way that many dishes were freshly prepared in under 10 minutes, and it definitely showed.

The **mac and cheese** tasted old and seemed like it had just been reheated. It was lukewarm on top but still cold at the bottom, which is unacceptable.

The **shrimp and grits** were another major disappointment. Instead of the rich, creamy consistency you'd expect from Southern-style grits, they were so thin they resembled soup.

The **po' boy** was actually decent and the one item I didn't have much to complain about, but one good sandwich wasn't enough to save the meal.

To make matters worse, the service felt disorganized and inattentive throughout our visit.

Overall, this was a very disappointing experience, especially considering how excited we were to try it. There are far better places to enjoy Southern food, and unfortunately, I wouldn't return or recommend this one.

Had a great lunch here the other day, the staff greated us with smiles and friendly banter. Tried the fried chicken, some hush puppies and fhe muffaletta, all of which where excellent. Fried chicken was very crispy, the hush puppies were so savory and delicious and the muffaletta was so tasty. Would be happy to dine here again soon.

Im from Louisiana and stumbled across Brenda's while at painted ladies...group of 4 and we were told you have to have reservations. But idk what happened or if it was because they knew it was birthday, but they sat us at a table without reservations. I ordered the blackened fish, greens, Mac n cheese, and red beans and rice. VERY GOOD!!! THANK YOU FOR A GREAT BIRTHDAY BRUNCH!!! The large mimosa was good too.

Got the meat loaf as my main dish and Mac & cheese/garlic spinach/bacon potato hash as my 3 sides. Overall the dish was good. Also, I was a single eater so I got seated right away at the bar. Reservations for parties of 2 or more seem to fill up fast.

What stands out is the warm and friendly service and genuinely welcoming atmosphere. It is a good spot for an uncomplicated and affordable meal.

I always enjoy coming here and can definitely recommend it.

top_reviews.content: Fantastic authentic jewish and Israeli cuisine in Berkeley! Definitely recommend checking out Saul’s if you are missing your Bubbe in Brooklyn. Of course you are paying for the authenticity ($26 for a sandwich w/ side), but that feels like a given in Berkeley. It is what it is. Don’t let it stop you from coming to try Saul’s. I recommend the corned beef reuben. You can skip the deserts and the latkes (too oily for my taste).
For the real ones, this place is the closest thing to Au Coquelet (shut down years ago). Cozy seating, yummy food, immaculate vibes. A little pricey, though! Also try their flourless chocolate cake.

Large open space, clean, tidy and well-attended. Thursdays there may be a Farmer's Market out front at noon, or one (weather permitting). We happen to be here on one of those less amenable weather days.
One visit only, so no in-depth review here.
Great Bagels and Smoked Salmon.
Well worth visiting and getting to know this place.
Staff are friendly, helpful, and try to keep my modifications from costing too much. The pastry cases are hard to pass up. Rugelach and Hamentashen come in 4 flavors, maracoons 2.
I am not eating everything to report, but the one chocolate Rugelach was dreamy.

I have loved coming to Saul’s for lunch/brunch with friends and family for 10 years. And even with the ownership change, the experience and food remain top notch! The pastrami is the best I’ve had. Get the knish, French fries and pickles. Do not sleep on their Bloody Mary as it is one of the best in the East Bay. Honestly can’t wait to go back

I really wanted to love this place, but the food was sub-par, though I did have a nice and attentive waiter, and the atmosphere was fine.

At least 1/3 of my pastrami sandwich was inedible fat & gristle (see posted pic).  While I never love picking that much fat off a sandwich, I especially didn't love it when the sandwich costs $26.95.  While, I wouldn't call the meat portion skimpy, I also wouldn't call it generous and thickly stacked like, you often get in a traditional Jewish deli, so to have a third of it be inedible was really a waste of money. The flavor was fine, but I didn't pay for a "fat" sandwich.

Also I got a latke for my side (an extra $2.95), and it was very greasy + rubbery and burned (see posted pic of inedible burned portions). It also had a slight fish flavor.  Made me wonder when the last time was they changed their frying oil?

I won't be going back - too disappointing.

top_reviews.content:
Review: Street-Level Audit — Tacos Sinaloa (Fruitvale Hub)

An afternoon operational run to evaluate one of Oakland’s highest-volume street culinary hubs. Service was incredibly fast, and the covered outdoor seating plaza made it easy to sit down and analyze the payload immediately.

Everything we ordered was excellent:

The Torta: My partner had the carne asada torta and loved it. It was packed with a generous amount of steak that was flavorful but not too spicy. The bread was perfectly soft but held together much better than he expected without getting soggy or falling apart.

The Tacos: I tried three different tacos—carne asada, fish, and al pastor—and all of them were fantastic. They were well-built and easy to eat because they didn't skimp on the tortillas. The kitchen put the perfect amount of salsa on top of each one so it didn't overwhelm the flavor of the meat.

The Standout: The al pastor was hands-down my favorite. It had that perfect balance of deep seasoning and those crispy, caramelized edges you look for in great pork.

The Drink: The strawberry horchata was delicious and super refreshing in the sun. It was creamy, sweet, and the perfect counter to the savory meats.

The Verdict: Tacos Sinaloa completely defends its reputation. Fast, delicious, and pristine street-level execution.

How the mighty have fallen this place used to be spectacular. Some of the best tacos and burritos in Oakland. Really disappointed in the fact that I spent $17 for a regular burrito. Just a little bit bigger than my small iPhone. Service was good. Just sad I couldn't use the bathroom. The only thing that I could say is the same is the flavor. It is still really good but just so upset that the burrito was very small. It was much bigger before. Like everything else, prices go up and quality goes down in this case the size.

Food is good, I've really only had burritos and a few tacos. The burrito are good and filling. 25$+tax gets you a nice forearm length supper burrito. Where I come from super means cheese and sour cream, but at Sinaloa super means bigger/longer/more....I can share this with someone or have enough for a whole meal later. My only issue is when you ask for extra lemons/limes they don't want to give you any; "it's already in the bag" excuse me I said EXTRA/ MAS in Spanish, and not 1/4 of a lime cut in half for a dollar. Other than that drinks and the food are good.

Literally the best place for Mexican food! Definitely worth every penny. We ordered the carne asada super burrito, and the flavors tasted just like a homemade backyard cookout. The burrito was huge—easily big enough for two people to share! They’re also open late, which is a huge bonus. The staff is always super friendly and kind, too. This is definitely my go-to spot for Mexican food!

Disappointed with the food, drove pretty far to get here.  Surprised that they had a line...
Customer service was good.
They are apparently known for ceviche, and it was sad, it was not that cold, flavorless, and not good at all.
The tacos were okay, I've had better.

Early lunch before watching a play @ Orpheum!

We ordered the cacio e pepe pasta which was excellent while the pizza salsiccia was just ok.

I do want to point out that while I understand metal straws are environmentally friendly, I find it not suitable for public use. Popular place with great creative food!
I strongly recommend to go early, since this place fills up very quick.
Service is good, the food is great. Portion was just right.

Only one thing you should know before you go.
Automatically 5% surcharge is included in a bill. If you don’t like it, just subtract from your tip.

Came here for Saturday brunch. Started with the cauliflower. It was fresh, and the sauce had a nice saltiness to it.
Got both the margherita and funghi pizzas. The margherita was fine but was a bit flat on flavor. The funghi had a rich, earthy mushroom flavor with a great amount of oil.
Dessert was the Nutella sundae and it was genuinely one of the better desserts I’ve had in a while. Soft ice cream, sweet, and the mascarpone added the crunch. Didn’t expect much and was pleasantly surprised.
Outdoor seating was chill. Staff was attentive and friendly, kept the waters topped off.

This Restaurant serves some of the most delicious pizza around. We started with arancini and meatballs—both excellent—but the arancini truly stood out: perfectly crisp on the outside, irresistibly creamy within, and bursting with rich, comforting flavor.

For the main, the Margherita pizza was everything you’d hope for—fresh, vibrant, and beautifully balanced—while the meatballs were hearty and deeply satisfying.

The space was lively and a bit noisy, but the quality of the food and the attentive service more than made up for it.

We had a restaurant week selection for dinner, the risotto particularly was excellent, and the chicken cacciatore was good.
The salad was a nice start and both desserts were good.

The space is a bit of an awkward shape that they've done a good job with, but it's a bit loud and the lighting is bright bulbs but spaced widely making it dim and bright at once.

top_reviews.content: Please don’t listen to the reviews. Got dal makhni and pav bhaji. Pav bhaji wasn’t authentic (tasted sweet?) and dal makhni was alright. Requested the pav bhaji to be made spicy and got an uncooked green chili with it (still don’t understand why they gave it?). The service was very slow. Would not visit again

If one review can change your mind about going to this restaurant, let it be this one. All the bad reviews are there for a reason. Please don’t take a chance thinking you’ll have a better experience.

Let’s start with the customer service, which is pretty much nonexistent.

We’ve been here multiple times, and every single time, we’ve actively tried to avoid getting this particular server because he simply does not know how to take an order properly. This time was easily the worst.

We ordered 3 appetizers and 2 main dishes, and within ONE MINUTE of placing our order, they brought out one of the main dishes. That honestly made me question whether the food is even being freshly prepared. We asked them to take it back and bring the appetizers first, as we had originally requested.

Then came the appetizers. We specifically asked for only the yogurt to be served on the side. Instead, they brought every single sauce on the side. So the appetizers basically came dry, and we had to assemble our own food at the table.

And somehow, it got even worse. Despite us very clearly saying that we wanted to eat the appetizers first, they brought the rest of the main courses out at the same time as the appetizers.

The most frustrating part? There wasn’t even a genuine apology or acknowledgment that they had messed up.

As for the food the biryani was basically coated in oil and food coloring. It had almost no salt, while the shrimp itself was unbelievably salty. The chili chicken was essentially just oil and sauce. There was barely any balance or flavor to it.

And throughout all of this, our server never once asked how the food was.

To make things even more uncomfortable, my friend was watching a show on his phone while we were waiting, and the server randomly started questioning him about what he was watching, asking, “Why are you watching a cartoon?” Like… why is that any of your business? Read the room.

The entire interaction felt dismissive and disrespectful.

We came back because we genuinely liked some of the food here, but after this experience, we’re done. Bad food can happen. Mistakes can happen. But when the service is consistently careless, the staff doesn’t take responsibility for mistakes, and the food itself is this disappointing, there’s really no reason to come back.

Save yourself the money and the frustration. AVOID THIS RESTAURANT AT ANY COST.

Smoky Chicken (video attached) and Kurkure available on the extreme left of aisle or any Indian snacks including biscuits👌Good seating space, need some planning beforehand - as there people lined up waiting to take DoorDash orders. Might have some wait time in case everything is full.

We ordered chai and vada pav. The masala chai was excellent and the quantity was a lot. The vada pav were very tasty. The chutney served were good too. Staff is polite. Menu is extensive with many vegetarian options.

top_reviews.content: One of my favorite spots in San Leandro. Paradiso is an upscale fine dining restaurant with all the bells and whistles. Went there for the 1st time today,
Loved the atmosphere, loved the food.
The best part of my meal was the dessert. I think this was the Best chocolavacake I had ever eaten in my life. The gelato that it came with… omg… fabulous. I might just go back this week just for that gelato and Chocolava.
Sharing some photos

Follow on instagram- Nusky21.

Paradiso makes a strong first impression with its stylish, well thought through design. The space is divided into two main dining areas, plus a private table option, with the bar smartly placed at the center of the restaurant. It feels modern, open, and intentionally laid out rather than crowded. Bathrooms might need some attention and maybe a renovation.

Service is genuinely pleasant and attentive. Staff are consistently on the lookout for guests without being intrusive, which makes the overall experience relaxed and well-managed.

Food is a mixed bag. The calamari was unfortunately far too greasy and ended up mostly untouched. On the positive side, the beet salad with arugula stood out as light, fresh, healthy, and generously portioned. The Wagyu burger was juicy and satisfying, and it comes with a generous serving of parmesan fries that easily steal some attention. Had to take some to-go though.

Overall, Paradiso delivers on ambiance and service, with some solid food highlights, but a bit more consistency in execution would push it higher.

Paradiso is one of the nicest restaurants we have in San Leandro. It is a bit pricey, but the quality and experience always justify it. The food has been consistently good on every visit, the service is excellent, and the atmosphere is lively and comfortable.

It has become one of our family go to spots for celebrations. Even the kids love it, and the desserts are fantastic. My personal favorite is the avocado and crab salad. We have never had a bad meal here and always leave happy.

Paradiso is our preferred place for celebrating special occasions! The 3-4-5 prix fixe dinner menu option is our favorite. We find the price to be a steal for the quality of menu options they offer for this special. My go-to is the Chicken Paradiso (ask for extra bread to soak up the delicious sauce!). Short ribs were savory and the cheesy polenta sealed the deal. Not pictured - our spectacular dessert. We were so stuffed, we asked them to box our second dessert so we could enjoy later. The apple crisp was enough for me and my husband to share after our entrees but we will enjoy our molten lava cake later! The staff is what really makes this place sparkle. They are accommodating and so kind - they make connections with new patrons as well as the regulars. Pavi was our server and he was amazing. Paradiso should be in your list for your next date night!

Salads are usually so unremarkable, but I'm still thinking about the Tea Leaf Salad even a week later. I never remember a salad I've eaten but this is such a great salad. Must get!!

I love this place. The End! I came here a few months ago for the first time and got the chance to come back and bring my wife this time. We basically bought everything (including the cookbook). Had a super yummy lunch here! Tea leaf salad was unique, fresh, and delish. Mango chicken tasted like a warm hug.

Burma Love in the Mission District is the perfect sister spot to the longtime neighborhood favorite, Burma Superstar. It carries the same magic — those bold, comforting Burmese flavors — but in a fresh, modern setting.

We ordered the eggplant and daikon, fried rice, and mango chicken, and every dish was bursting with flavor and perfectly balanced. You can taste the care in the spices and textures — nothing feels heavy, just deeply satisfying. The drinks were also a highlight — strong, tasty, and thoughtfully mixed.

The space itself has a moody, intimate vibe with dim lighting and warm tones that make it feel both stylish and inviting. Whether you’re a longtime fan of Burma Superstar or new to Burmese cuisine, Burma Love is absolutely worth the visit. 🌶️🍚🍸

Visited for dinner and ordered the medium fried rice. The dish was flavorful, well-balanced, and pleasantly light—not greasy like fried rice can sometimes be. The ambiance really stood out as well. The restaurant has a vibrant, upscale atmosphere with beautiful décor and a lively energy that makes it a great spot for an evening meal. Overall, a very enjoyable dining experience and a place I’d happily return to.

Osha Thai down by the Embarcadero is a decent spot, but with so much amazing Thai food in SF, it just doesn’t really stand out from the pack. If you end up here, stick to the highlights: the kapow chicken, drunken noodles, and salmon rolls were all super tasty. You can definitely pass on the angry shrimp and the steak, they just weren't worth it. Wash it all down with their Thai tea, which really hit the spot. The service is fine, but the place gets completely packed, so be prepared to flag down the staff if you need anything.

Wow, so delicious!! We got the best roti canai I've ever had, and the service was stellar. We were there on a weekday, so the cool patio wasn't open, but the inside is beautiful too. It seems like a great place to host a business lunch, we saw several companies with multiple tables.

I tried the classic basil fried rice, very yummy. I tried all the vegetarian stuff so I don't have a lot of feedback on the other non-vegetarian food there but overall definitely a place where I can go more than once, a little on the pricier side.

top_reviews.content: Super Duper Burger@Lower FIDI is located on Mission between Spear and Steuart streets not too far from YMCA "Barcadero," according to my experience, should be regarded of one of the best out of its 10 locations in The City. Super Duper Burgers was founded in 2010 in San Francisco's Castro district by Adriano Paganini with co-founder Eddie Sarti who have a joint vision to improve both quality and service of fast-food burger in the Bay Area. The company focuses on qualitative, locally sourced, and fresh ingredients, well cooked with a mission to provide a fast-food experience with "slow food values" and the fast-food chain has since grown to numerous locations beyond The City limits across the entire Bay Area from Napa, Concord to San Ho. Lower FIDI is conveniently connected to all transit and just one block from the Ferry Building. The location is clean, spacious (indoor and outdoor seatings) and accommodated with quality food and more importantly, a super friendly service team who will greet you as soon as you walk in. 😲My favorite order off its menu is its Chicken Sandwich with Chipotle Aioli on a fresh Ciabatta Bun with a small addon of Jalapenos for just $11.50. I have (and I am confident that you would as well) have nothing to complaint except they should place a "cookie jar" at the cashier so customers could effective place their appreciation tokens as quite often orders are placed via self-ordering kiosks. PS Regrettably, Super Duper locations on Market Downtown and Metron where I used to go have declined in both food quality and service. Service is terrible to no service at all ppl constantly chatting or joking around among themselves.  Its burgers are not well cooked (pinkish and "smooshy"). The same chicken sandwich is terribly prepared and lacks proper and quality ingredients at Metron that would make Lower FIDI a five-star location. 👼

I recently visited Super Duper Burger at 98 Mission Street in San Francisco, and I have to say, the experience was fantastic! I ordered their fried chicken sandwich, a side of fries, and a strawberry milkshake, and everything exceeded my expectations. The chicken was perfectly crispy and flavorful, the fries were hot and golden, and the strawberry milkshake was rich, creamy, and bursting with real strawberry flavor. The combination made for an incredibly satisfying meal. The service was friendly and quick, making the whole experience even better. I highly recommend checking out Super Duper Burger if you're in the area!

Delicious burgers! They do t have a gluten free bun but they offer a lettuce wrap. The burger is pretty juicy though so I would recommend a fork and knife. The garlic fries were delicious but heavy on the garlic so be prepared! The home made pickles were very unique and tangy. Would recommend!

Tasty burgers and plenty of seating.

After ordering on the kiosk, I received my mini burger about five minutes later. It was warm, on a toasted bun, and cooked perfectly. If you're looking to eat without human interaction, this is a place to do it.

The interior has plenty of seating, as does the outside. You can find some art and the nice signs that are standard at every location. However, it's not the cleanest Super Duper Burgers location. Burger was moist and flavorful. Garlic fries were good as well. I wish they could have melted the cheese on the fries, but that is just my opinion. top_reviews.content: I do feel this place is overrated. The portions are tiny and overpriced. It was good, but not as amazing as expected. Had been to Flour + Water recently and definitely preferred it there. The Raviolo is one large ravioli drenched in melted butter for over $30. We also ordered the Corn Triangoli Pasta and Fiore Di Zucca Pizza. The pasta was good, the pizza was just ok. Felt we could've gotten a better meal elsewhere, but worth a try. Enjoyed the vibes at our table outside with a heated lamp, yet service was pretty slow. Difficult to get a reservation. Had to wait a while once arrived even with the reservation. Probably won't return.

We had an incredible experience at Cotogna! We arrived right at opening on a Tuesday without a reservation and were pleasantly surprised to get seats at the bar immediately.

Everything we ordered was excellent, but the pastas completely stole the show—they were easily the best part of the meal. The lamb ragù pasta was absolutely outstanding and one of the best pasta dishes we’ve ever had. The steak was cooked perfectly, the margarita pizza was fresh and delicious with an amazing crust, and the cannoli was the perfect sweet ending.

The service was just as memorable as the food. Everyone was warm, attentive, and welcoming, making the entire experience feel relaxed and enjoyable.

If you’re visiting San Francisco, Cotogna is absolutely worth a visit. We can’t wait to come back!

Exceptional Pasta & Open-Fire Cooking
Our dinner at Cotogna was a fantastic experience, highlighted by incredible technique and standout pasta dishes that absolutely stole the show.
We started with the salmon appetizer, which was a work of art. Not only was it visually stunning, but the flavors were balanced perfectly—light, bright, and the ideal way to wake up the palate and open up our appetite.
For the mains, the pastas were the undisputed champions of the night. Both dishes we tried were a massive hit, but the egg raviolo was truly outstanding. It was executed with absolute perfection—delicate, rich, and flawlessly cooked. The waiter did mention upfront that they are primarily known for their pastas, and they certainly delivered.
We also tried the funghi pizza, which unfortunately was a bit of a miss for us compared to the high bar set by the rest of the meal. On the other hand, the lamb was beautifully done. Cooked over an open fire, it had a wonderful smoky depth, and the accompanying sauces really bonded the entire dish together. While the wood-fired meat was impressive, the pasta here is so legendary that I’ll likely just stick to an all-pasta lineup next time.
Overall, Cotogna offers a beautiful atmosphere, excellent service, and some decadent pasta you can find. A must-visit!

Such a wonderful dinner at Cotogna with our family of four. We shared two appetizers and ordered three pastas, and everything was absolutely delicious. top_reviews.content: We are local, but we had friends visiting from out of town and we're going to do an Alcatraz night tour. I didn't want to go to any of the crowded touristy places in the fisherman's wharf area. Found this place online and it had good reviews, I really love this place. Really nice upscale but casual vibe, polite and friendly service, and all the food was excellent. My group had the burger, the spinach artichoke dip, a chicken sandwich, and the French dip. All was delicious! I don't think we needed our reservation, but I'm glad we had one. Definitely check this place out.

Incredible french dip and chili! This restaurant has a decidedly upscale feel and service to match. Our server (Oliver) was also the bartender and his recommendations and service were spot on!  The French dip is one of the best i have had in a long time, tender perfectly *medium rare* shaved beef with a jus that was flavorful and not overly salty. The crusty roll held up well to the dip, and the accompanying horseradish was creamy and made the sandwich complete! We also were huge fans of the chili, a rare treat to find in SFO.. and it was meaty and flavorful, served with tortilla chips.  Last but not least, the spaghetti squash with crimini mushrooms, parmesan and golden raisins was an excellent side in lieu of fries.  Dog friendly outdoors for bonus points!

Ate here for the first time yesterday and wanted to share some thoughts.

My friend was wearing a black sleeveless sweater and was approached by a manager and asked to put his jacket back on after removing it near the end of our meal. Fair enough, that's on us, we hadn't seen the policy posted on their website:

“Our attire standards benefit everyone because clothing can elevate or diminish the experience of the room. Sports and team athletic wear, including headwear or jerseys, gym style clothes, including sleeveless shirts or sweatpants, and footwear like slides or flip flops are too casual for our restaurant and not permitted. Our staff takes pride in their appearance and we appreciate your respecting our guidelines.”

But there were at least two other people at the restaurant visibly breaking this same policy: a woman in a white racerback top that looked more like a sports bra than a shirt, and another in a cami top with bra straps out. When we pointed this out, the manager said the policy is “just for gentlemen,” which is weird, and also not true, per their website.

It's an interesting choice to selectively enforce a policy, and somehow the only person affected by it is also the only Black man in sight (on Juneteenth, also). Our bill was already on the table, we were leaving. Why bring it up at that point at all?

The food itself was good, especially the emerald kale salad and the double-cut pork chop. We also loved the artichokes, but even with prices being high everywhere right now, $25 for 1.5 artichokes is kind of wild.

The staff could learn something here: enforce the policy for everyone, or don't bother.

There were three of us, and we got the ribs and two Hawaiian ribeye steaks. The ribs were burnt, so we sent them back (tasted like charcoal). We asked for medium-rare steaks, but they were more like medium-well (dry, like well-done). The starters were just okay. Artichoke dip was the dish that stood out. Honestly, the food wasn't great.

But the service? That was awesome! Super fast and cheerful, which really made up for the food. Thanks, Mr. Waiter (sorry I forgot your name).

We didn't take many pics except for the burnt ribs and dry steak, even though it doesn't really show in the photo (we tasted it though!).

Oh, almost forgot, they have no toothpicks 🤣
Excellent crab cakes. Solid French dip sandwich. Super silky key lime pie. And insane apple crisp. We would easily go here again.

top_reviews.content:
What an incredible brunch experience! Every dish we ordered was outstanding.

We started with the jook, which was rich, comforting, and full of flavor—the perfect way to begin the meal. The Umami Fried Chicken lived up to its name: crispy, juicy, and packed with flavor. The Dolsot Bibimbap was excellent, with perfectly seasoned ingredients and that delicious crispy rice at the bottom of the stone bowl. The Kimchi Fried Rice had just the right balance of spice, tanginess, and smokiness.

The quality of the ingredients, thoughtful preparation, and beautiful presentation made every dish memorable. The service was warm, attentive, welcoming, and super fast, adding to the overall experience.

This is easily one of the best Korean brunches we’ve had in the Bay Area. We’ll definitely be back to explore more of the menu. Highly recommended!

Fantastic brunch!! The patio had a great vibe and all our meals were delicious! I had the belly bap which was fantastically tender pork belly and rice with egg on top. The chicken cup bap was phenomenal - the pieces of noodle and egg mixed into the rice made it superb. The portions are generous here! The ube matcha latte was good but the ube flavor was very weak and easily overpowered by the matcha. Absolutely you must go here!

Amazing food and good portions to boot! We sat outdoors and enjoyed the shade and the well kept area. The food is so flavorful - definitely my favorite meal of our whole California trip, not to mention of SF.

Second visit after many years. The place still looks the same. It is closed to Giradheli square. We made reservation a day earlier. This restaurant used to be very busy one. When we arrived we were the only party but the other tables filled up pretty quickly. Looks like this restaurant has relation with Sweet Maple in Palo Alto as they serve similar dishes like pimped up ramen and the millionaire bacon.
We ordered couple dishes like banchan , bbq set tor 1 galbi, Korean Fried Chicken, dolsot bimbimbap snd pimped up ramen.
All are yummy especially the fried chicken. The pimped up ramen is unique and bacon is yummy. Galbi and dolsot bimbimbap are yummy too but not that special. Usually banchan is free at most of Korean restaurant but you have to pay at this restaurant and I don't think it is re fillable.
The service was great and our server was friendly.
Overall it was nice dinner and catch  up with our cousin from overseas.

I recently ate at this Korean restaurant in San Francisco and ordered their Korean fried chicken, expecting something authentic after my excellent experiences in Seoul. What I received was a massive disappointment. This so-called Korean chicken didn’t even come close to the real thing — it wasn’t even in the same league. It tasted exactly like regular KFC chicken: same overly thick, soggy breading, generic seasoning, and zero authentic Korean spice, crunch, or flavor.
After having incredibly delicious, crispy, perfectly seasoned Korean fried chicken in Seoul, this version felt like a cheap fast-food imitation. For over $30, it was a complete rip-off. At that price in San Francisco, you’d expect something special, but instead I got something that wouldn’t even stand out at a KFC drive-thru.
Honestly, if you want Korean fried chicken, skip this place entirely and just go to an actual KFC — you’ll get the same taste for a fraction of the price without the disappointment. I was genuinely shocked at how far off the mark this was, especially after knowing how amazing real Korean chicken can be.
Save your money and your expectations. This place is a hard pass.

top_reviews.content:
I go to Jollibee all the time, and it’s honestly one of my favorite fast-food places. Their fried chicken is delicious and easily one of the best fast-food fried chickens I can recommend.

However, the service at this particular location can be hit or miss. One day, I stopped by around 11 AM before going to work and ordered a chicken sandwich through the drive-thru. I ended up waiting more than 8 minutes, and it seemed like they may have forgotten about my order. When I finally received the sandwich, it was cold.

I still really like Jollibee and will continue coming back, but I hope this location can improve its service and make sure food is served fresh and hot, especially after customers have already waited that long.

Jollibee was one of my favorite chains to eat fried chicken. I'm sad to say was instead of is as my last outing to Jollibee was disappointing to say the least.
The chicken was cooked well and the crunch was excellent but the salt and seasoning were completely missing making it hard to eat. On top of it, the chicken was so oily that I didn't feel good after having it. I don't know if it has to do with this particular outlet but its created an aversion towards fried chicken to me for a while.

top_reviews.content:
Would definitely come back here. Must try.

The Pretty Hot Wings were flavorful and juicy — not your flour or breadcrumb crust, more of a skin-crusted wing, with a tangy tamarind-based sauce.

The Nam Tok Beans were a very nice surprise — something I'd never tried before. Lightly coated, deep-fried beans with great seasoning, served with lettuce leaves and cucumber so you can make little lettuce wraps. A little on the spicier side, but I loved it.

The Pad Kee Mao was the best dish of the night — perfectly seasoned flat noodles, great aroma, full of umami. Loved it.

The Masaman Curry had a huge chunk of beef with small potatoes and shallots in a rich, creamy, flavorful gravy, and the beef was perfectly cooked. Flavor was on point — though $60 for it is steep.

Sticky rice was basic and perfect.

The Black Rice Pudding dessert was something I wasn't sure about, but it was amazing — crispy puffed rice, strawberry jam, a peanuty flavor, and sesame. Very unique and great tasting.

Will definitely order the pad kee mao again.

Just had a really good bowl at Kin Khao in San Francisco while sitting outside. The presentation was beautiful rich broth, soft-boiled egg with a perfect golden yolk, tender chashu, bamboo shoots, fresh greens, nori, and sesame seeds. Everything tasted clean and well-balanced. The broth had depth without feeling heavy, and the toppings were clearly made with care.
Sitting outside made it even better, watching the city go by. Service was friendly and the whole experience felt special without trying too hard. If you’re looking for thoughtful, high-quality food in SF, this place delivers. Already thinking about coming back.

Cute, cozy, and flavorful place. The service is professional and warm. The menu has dishes that you will recognize but with a fun and exciting twist, and there are some other dishes that are their personal creations. Everything is well thought out and balanced with textures, temperatures, colors and flavors. The dishes spark your taste buds with umami, bitter, sweet, salty, and sour ingredients. Its a full experience. Their wine list is perfectly curated to dance with the menu and take it to another level.

Pretty hot wings were a pleasant surprise. Khao Yum presented an interesting combination of flavors and texture. Green curry rabbit is a venture for me, meat is tender easily separated from bones, meat balls in the curry more taste. Pork belly was very good. All dishes were well prepared. Blueberries cake was a fantastic dessert wrapped up.

This restaurant is probably the most authentic Thai restaurant that we have been to in the States. Between the three of us, we got the mushroom hor mok (highly recommend!), charred eggplant salad, yaowaraj noodle‍, and massaman nuea. All of the dishes were cooked wonderfully, and some of them had flavors we had never experienced before. Although the restaurant was way too loud at times, it was great finally being able to try Kin Khao, and I am glad it had lived up to the hype.

Hidden gem!!

Friendly staff. Felt like a family run business that appreciated you dining with them rather than a chain.

We arrived around 9.30am. Placed our name on the yellow clip board and waited for our name to be called out. Obviously a popular place with the locals and lots of people willing to wait for a table.

Just over a year ago, my family and I visited 8 AM Brunchbin for the first time, and we walked away talking about two things: how good the food was and how genuinely kind and attentive the customer service felt. That combination stuck with us so much that on this trip, we made it a point to come back—and ended up eating breakfast here two days in a row.

The food is exactly as we remembered: incredibly fresh, simply prepared, and absolutely bursting with flavor. The lox bagel was perfect, and the waffle might be one of the best I’ve ever had. We actually found ourselves debating how the cooks manage to make something so straightforward taste so exceptional.

The service is still top‑tier—friendly, patient, and welcoming in a way that makes you feel like they’re truly happy you’re there.

Highly recommended. This place has earned a permanent spot on our San Francisco must‑visit list.

Love the food. I got Thai fried rice and the chicken and egg tasted very well together. The thai iced tea had the perfect amount of sweetness!
The restaurant’s interior was really nice with painted murals and lanterns. The air-conditioning was slightly below average(I went when it was hot).
The staff were very kind and welcoming. ❤️
However, I was surprised when we were not allowed to dine in when there were almost no customers. The person I was with was already sitting and eating when we were kicked out. While I understand it may just be the store policy, staff should be more flexible when it comes to paying customers as someone who also works in food service.
Almost there guys!
Overall this restaurant is great.

I got recommended this place after the gym and it was definitely worth the 20 min walk!!

The bbq pork fried rice was super delicious, but I was still a little hungry so I then ordered the Ka Na Moo Krob (Crispy pork with chinese broccoli) and that was probably some of the best asian food I had so far from this city!!

Super delicious, the sauce was heavenly, the pork (I believe it was pork belly) super tender, and got a side of rice with it!! Definitely worth a stop but they were a little busy on Friday so be prepared for that!

It was also very affordable because the pork fried rice was $14 and the crispy pork was only $17-$18. So even when I ordered two meals the total was still under $40 which in this city is not bad at all!!

Wanted to try something in San Fran. Being a professional travel I've tried different Thai restaurants thoughtout the country from Seattle to Los Angeles, Tampa, NYC. The new Thai in San Francisco was not bad nor great, fitting in the tried category but wouldn't come back. I was greeted promptly and sat, the tables and chairs are old wooden style from the 70s not too comfortable. The decor was creative but provided a cheesy feel, it must have been me but I felt like Inwas in a decorated Garage. Nonetheless, my water an ice Thai tea was delivered, which honestly, the ice Thai tea was the best part of the visit. Very good flavor with a surprise frozen panda of yogurt on top. I ordered a stir fried beef  meal, I forget the exact name on menue. No pre snacks offered, wonton or such. The meal came with a typical scoop of bland white rice. My beef(no pun intended) was what I can only construe was hamburger beef grounded up in a chili broth with a few red an green peppers. The flavor was ok, nothing great, wasnt spicy although it was to be. Its a no frill, minimalist restaurant providing same with food. I wouldn't steer people away but I wouldn't recommend as there are many choices in the area.

The mango salad way too sweet.  The pad Thai too salty the beef curry was fine, though should have had chicken as the beef didn’t have any of the curry taste.  The chicken satay was good.  It did not did not live up to the reviews that I had read. Tried it won't come back.

The food is top tier and fast! They do get busy so lunchers beware however they are very efficient and super kind about going over details on the menu. I always recommend this place to my friends who come visit. Plus its walking distance from several landmarks if your showing off the town.

top_reviews.content:
La Note is *the* brunch spot in Berkeley for a reason. The patio is lovely, the service was great, and I’ll absolutely be back to try other menu items.

That said, I ordered the Lemon Gingerbread Pancakes with Poached Pears, and my expectations and reality had a brief disagreement.

When someone says “pancakes,” I imagine soft, tender, fluffy clouds that happily absorb maple syrup. These were more like:

* Dense
* Cakey
* Crumbly
* Heavy

The texture reminded me less of a pancake and more of a gingerbread muffin that accidentally got promoted to breakfast.

The flavors were nice, the poached pears were beautiful, but the interior texture wasn’t for me. If you love gingerbread cake, you may love these. If you’re expecting a classic fluffy pancake experience, you may be surprised.

Would I come back to La Note? Absolutely.

Would I order the Lemon Gingerbread Pancakes again?

Not unless they come with a warning label that says:

“Attention: This pancake identifies as cake.”

Really adorable French cafe. Very busy Sunday morning for breakfast, but getting a table inside worked out well for us. Definitely faster than waiting for the patio.

The service was excellent: fun, friendly and attentive.

The food was solid but not incredible. The baguette with goat cheese and honey was delicious, but the breakfast sausages (apple and spicy - I forget the actual names) were underwhelming. The Bloody Mary was spicy and good.

Pricy but good. We’d go back.

Five stars all the way. The breakfast potatoes were crispy and perfectly seasoned, finished with fragrant herbs and mellow roasted garlic that added a rich depth. The scrambled eggs had a light, creamy texture that felt comforting and well prepared. The pear and gingerbread pancakes were not my favorite choice, so next time I would try a different flavor combination with a stronger fruit presence. The atmosphere felt warm and inviting, and the service was attentive and friendly. A lovely spot to relax and enjoy a satisfying brunch experience.
It’s my first time to try French food and I like the taste. The pancake is soft and not so sweet (they provided me with syrup). The oat meal is like a bowl of light sweet porridge, which is ok.

I had eggs benedict and honestly, the highlight for me was the herb and garlic potatoes on the side—so flavorful and perfectly cooked. It’s amazing how something so simple can taste that good. The menu being in French added a nice touch, and the cozy ambiance made it even better, especially with the rainy weather outside. A really warm and satisfying experience overall.

The food was always super fresh, and flavorful. You can taste it in the shrimps, the fish, and everything you ordered here. With their top notch quality and i really mean it, their price is very fair and reasonable. My pride restaurant to take visiting friends, and family here any chance i could. Make sure you have a reservation ahead of time.

Honestly, I’m not sure it lives up to the hype as much as I’d hoped. While the vibe and decor are as bright and inviting as the welcoming staff, the quieted Cuban flavors left me wanting a bit more.

I had the fried pollo cholita plate, but the chicken thigh was overcooked and unfortunately tough and stringy. The beans and rice were excellent though, and I loved the plantains. It’s possible I just got a bad one-off with the chicken, but it still was a miss.

The cubano sandwich was much better, though after recently visiting Miami, I couldn’t help but think it could’ve stuck a better landing.

I know I’ve been here before and enjoyed the tacos, so maybe next time I’ll focus on the more Mexican-forward portions of the menu. Still, Cholita Linda brings a lot of bright energy on Telegraph which is always fun to walk by.

Always looking for great local food when I travel. This was outstanding! Ordered fish, pollo and carne asada. Wow! Juicy. Flavorful. Service was quick and easy. The space was so bright and the back seating area outdoor was perfect of enjoy the weather and food. Highly recommend

top_reviews.content:
The Speisekammer in Alameda is a delightful German restaurant that never fails to impress. I recently visited after a long break since the pandemic, and I was pleasantly surprised to find that their culinary expertise and friendly staff have remained unchanged. The food is still as delicious as ever, and the staff is more than happy to guide you through their extensive menu to find the perfect dish that suits your taste buds.

One of the standout features of The Speisekammer is its large screen TVs, making it an ideal spot to watch the World Cup soccer matches. The cocktails are equally impressive, expertly crafted and bursting with flavor.

During the fall, The Speisekammer truly comes alive with Oktoberfest celebrations. They throw an extravagant German party that is unlike any other in the East Bay. The outdoor patio is a great place to enjoy the beautiful weather and socialize with friends.

I highly recommend The Speisekammer for anyone looking for a fun and delicious German dining experience. I plan to return soon to catch some soccer matches with friends and soak in the lively atmosphere.

Good for those who drink, it's a great place to have a beer. I don't drink, but the service was excellent. I noticed the waiter seemed a little upset that my friend and I didn't drink alcohol. We had dinner, and I can say the food is formally German. I have some of the highest-rated German restaurants on my resume. I can say that Parabara is passable, but as a truly typically German restaurant, it deserves a visit. However, it does its job admirably. I won't give it a harsh review, especially since I'm comparing it to excellent quality German restaurants both here and abroad, but it's worth a visit. Because it's the only one in the area.

My wife and I were craving German food and so we checked out Speisekammer.  Wow, what amazing food!  We ordered the German salad combo which was filled with pickled veggie goodness.  This paired well with the heavier jager schnitzel and spatzel (fried chicken cutlet and dumpling style pasta) we shared. The chicken was super tender and juicy despite being a thin breaded chicken breast and the spatzel was an airy chewy mound of deliciousness.  It came with a mushroom gravy that added a lot of flavor.  I don't know what they did to those mushrooms but there was intense mushroom flavor in the gravy.  They of course had an amazing selection of German beers on tap, but what impressed me most was the full bar with cocktail options.  My favorite cocktail is a New York Sour, which is not always easy to find, and they had it as a standard cocktail on the menu.  Overall it was an awesome experience and I will definitely be returning.

Excellent food. A tremendous selection of all your German favorites. It brought back wonderful memories. I will return to eat my way through the menu. Fast and friendly service. Beer by the boot is an option for the fast drinker. Prost!

Feels like Germany! The food is consistently good. I love the vegetarian dishes and the German salad, which is basically a variety of pickled veggies. I especially like the pickled beets. We had everything from schnitzel to sausages and everything was delicious. If you are craving good German food, this hits!

top_reviews.content:
I first visited Greens in the early 2000s and was just back tonight for a second meal. While it is very expensive, the food was fantastic. My friend and I started with a bread basket, which, for $9, should’ve included at least two pieces of everything, not one, but was tasty. We skipped a “first course” and went straight to the main course. I had the Mesquite Grilled Jerk Tofu (which, while it did not include the sides described on the menu, was nonetheless delicious. My friend had the Wild Mushroom Wellington, which also had at least one subbed side but which she says was quite good. We skipped dessert as we were so full from our dinner. We each enjoyed glasses of wine (from a surprisingly short list of wines by the glass). Is Greens worth $50+ per person? From the perspective of a long-time vegetarian, it’s unusual to find such imaginative, delicious plant-based dishes, so while Greens is too expensive to make it a regular go-to, it’s a top-of-list special occasion restaurant. I hope it isn’t 20-odd years before I return.

Be sure to ask for a table next to the water, especially if you’re there near sunset.

Greens is a truly awesome place that we have been visiting for a long time. The location at Fort Mason is unbeatable, and the food is consistently high-quality and flavorful. It remains a staple for us in San Francisco. Our only minor critique is that the wine selection could be a bit more robust (though it’s possible we’ve just had some unlucky timing with the list). Still, it's a must-visit for the views and the excellent vegetarian cuisine.

My husband and I came here thanks to a gift card that I got for my birthday, so we came to splurge.

The Food: delicious and fresh. Can't recommend the Falafel Platter enough - a very generous platter. The bread plate was tasty but definitely a smaller shareable portion. Our mains were quite tasty, and for dessert, the Lemon Creme Brulee and Matcha Almond Cake were the perfect ends to the meal. While individually some of the portions were on the smaller end, when enjoying in a multi-course meal, everything was perfect. I left fully sated. One of the best meals I've had in years.

The Service: Unpretentious yet elevated. I always felt a server was available when I needed one, without feeling like they were hovering. I had clean plates for shareables throughout the meal, and our server noticed that a plate and spoon he initially set down were not perfectly clean, and swapped them out on the spot. Just much nicer service than I am used to.

Would highly recommend Greens to everyone.

This has been my go-to place in San Francisco for a great vegetarian or vegan meal in a beautiful, upscale setting. Reservations are definitely recommended, especially for dinner and special occasions. The high ceilings, the wooden sculptures at the entrance, and the views of the Golden Gate Bridge make the dining experience truly unique.

The appetizers, entrées, and specialty cocktails are all excellent. The restaurant is entirely vegetarian, and the menu clearly marks dishes that can be made vegan with a **VP (Vegan Possible)** designation.

The prices are on the higher side, but for vegetarians and vegans celebrating a special occasion, the extra cost is well worth it.

This place truly exceeded my expectations. I went for my birthday with 12 friends for the first time, and not only did they have special menu that said happy birthday, they also brought us FREE sorbet and champagne. I was floored. The staff was so nice and wanted to do anything to make it a special experience. Best part of course was everything we ate was SO good, and ALL vegan: from appetizers to entrees, this place delivers.

I had the "lobster roll" and the combination of lobster mushrooms and palm hearts was so delicious and the texture was amazing (not soggy at all and had a great mouth feel). The "something fishy" jackfruit was seasoned well and the flakey texture of the jackfruit worked perfectly for a fish alternative.

Hits the spot when you're craving vegan American food. The dishes can be heavy but that comes with the territory. Brunch is my favorite but I'm also partial to a good pancake 🥞 Sit in the back patio area for the best experience 🌞

I got the flying papadopoulos chicken gyro.  One friend got the vegan BLT.  Other friend got the vegan egg (tofu) scramble with vegan bacon.  My gyro was amazing.  Great flavor and all Vegan. And I am NOT vegan.  So good!!!
Not my friends enjoyed their food.  I tried the vegan eggs and they were delicious.  I tried the vegan bacon and that was good.  Not true bacon but it never said it tasted the same.  If you want to explore and try vegan this is a great place.  All food was fresh and delicious.  Will it be like the other stuff….no.  But is it fresh and cooked with the love of good food….HECK YA.

name: Tempest Bar & Box Kitchen
address: 2940 431 Natoma St, San Francisco, CA 94103, United States

google.name: Tempest Bar & Box Kitchen
google.address: 2940 431 Natoma St, San Francisco, CA 94103, United States
google.description: Pub grub, draft beer & cocktails are on tap at this low-key, brick-walled hangout.

top_reviews.content:
I checked out Tempest Bar & Box Kitchen on a Thursday around 10 p.m. with some friends after finding it on Google as one of the top-rated spots in the area. The photos looked great, and I was excited to try it out.

Unfortunately, our experience didn’t quite match the expectations — and to be fair, this is just based on the specific time we visited. When we arrived, there didn’t seem to be any floor staff managing the tables. Almost every open table was dirty, with leftover food, debris, and empty glasses. We genuinely couldn’t find a clean place to sit, which was a bit surprising given that the space itself looks really cool and has a great vibe.

We ended up heading to the bar where there were only two available seats for our group of four, so we made it work with two sitting and two standing. The bartender seemed friendly but was clearly very busy. Despite waiting for close to 10 minutes, we weren’t able to get service — even though the venue itself wasn’t particularly busy at the time, with only a couple of tables occupied (though the bar area was full).

At that point, we decided to leave.

That said, I do want to highlight that the aesthetic of the bar is really nice — it has a vibrant, laid-back energy that I can see being great on a different night. I’d be open to giving it another try in the future, but based on this visit, the lack of cleanliness and service made it a disappointing experience.

Solid food and a laid-back bar atmosphere. The burger and fries were the highlight—cooked just right, full of flavor, and served hot. The fries paired perfectly with the burger and made for a really satisfying meal.

One thing that really stands out is the drink selection. There are plenty of options to choose from, whether you’re into beer, cocktails, or something simple. It’s a great place to grab a drink and relax with friends or unwind after a long day.

The vibe is casual and welcoming, with a clean space and a fun, no-frills atmosphere that fits perfectly with the location. The staff were friendly and kept things moving smoothly, adding to the overall experience.

Between the great food, wide drink selection, and relaxed environment, Tempest Bar & Box Kitchen is definitely worth checking out. A solid go-to spot in San Francisco for a good burger and a drink. Highly recommend!

Stopped in this dive-y bar to watch the World Cuo. The regulars & staff were friendly and welcoming, the prices are super-reasonable, and the menu is fantastic. Had a great sandwich & can’t wait to come back & try the vegetarian chili dog.

Solid dive bar that checks all the boxes: pool table, graffiti, stickers on the walls,dark corners, interesting patrons and a jukebox that cranked metal. Surprising they had a solid kitchen with elevated variations of traditional bar food offerings
Great snacks! Cool bar! Nice staff!

google.address: 595 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94105, United States
google.description: Indoor & outdoor tables plus a colorful space keep the vibe festive at this Mexican bar & eatery.

top_reviews.content: I found this place walking down the street and it did not disappoint. You can either order at a counter or you can order via a QR code at the table and they will bring everything to you. They have happy hour with some good deals. I got a happy hour quesadilla which came with two quesadillas, sour cream and guacamole for only seven dollars. They also serve alcohol. My favorite part is that atmosphere they obviously put attention to detail into their customers. They have blankets you can use for when it’s too cold, which is such a beautiful detail. They have great service great food and a really good price. I highly recommend.

Oh man. Great prices for delicious Mexican food. We went crazy for tacos and love them. My personal favorite is the Asada. So delicious.

Friendly staff, super fast. They have a margarita bar and beers and chips and salsa. Why are you still reading ? Go!!

After dropping off Bushwacker Bob at the Ferry Building I headed straight up California to the world famous Uno Dos Tacos Restaurant for their equally famous Tacos!  Normally.. when the taco gods call to me I head down to the Mission district because of the vast variety of taquerias, but today it's going to be Uno Dos Tacos!  And...I'll tell you why!  They're perfect in every aspect from the tortillas and meats to the salsas and chips, most restaurants have multitudes of choices, and make a few of them good, but Uno Dos Tacos has a straight forward menu that includes just those items that they specialize in.  So, none are good because good isn't good enough, they've all got to be great!  Having a smaller specialized menu let's the team focus on greatness, and what you get are Amazing Tacos!  5 stars every single time!  ☆☆☆☆☆

One of my favorite Mexican spots in SF! Got the chips and guacamole, and they were so fresh and delicious! The onion and tomatoes added such flavor and the chips weren’t too salty. Also got the tinga chicken tacos which were topped with grilled onions and cilantro. The verde salsa and onions were the perfect combination on the chicken and I wanted to order more! The music was amazing and the outdoor seating was a vibe as well! Highly recommend for a quick lunch or dinner if you’re in the city!

Hands down my favorite tacos in the city (I usually get the carnitas - which are always perfectly done).  I’m not sure how, but even when the line is long at lunch, I’ve always been able to do a half-hour lunch when necessary (but have also always felt comfortable lingering for longer conversations with friends).  The inside and outside spaces are comfortable and the food is great...breakfast tacos are delicious too.  They are a super well organized machine but still friendly and with a great vibe.

top_reviews.content: Very solid and unassuming Italian restaurants! The rigatoni with pink sauce reminds me of the pasta from Aquarello, which holds two Michelin stars, but is much more balanced in flavor. Their polpo is super tender, and I have to say that their panne cotta is probably the best one I’ve ever had! Perfect balance in sweetness and texture. Will definitely come back!

Came here for a Saturday dinner date with no reservation and still was able to get outdoor seating.

The bread starter was nothing special, but the green herb sauce that came with it was good enough to keep dipping into. Also got the Tortino di Melanzane. Eggplant was watery and the sauce just tasted like normal marinara. Not worth it in my opinion.

The Tagliolini Ai Funghi E Tartufo was the move. Saucy pasta with strong mushroom and truffle flavor. Really satisfying.

Outdoor seating with dim lighting, staff was genuinely helpful with the menu, but once you order, expect to wait. Two hours from starters to dessert is too long. Price felt a bit expensive for what you get.

Amarena is one of our neighborhood favorites! We love all of the pastas which always pair well with the various vines and cocktails they offer. The apps are also amazing—we especially love the bruschetta because it is so fresh! It tastes like the tomatoes were just picked from their garden. We love their happy hour deal which is a shocking every day ordeal. The outdoor parklet is so wonderful during sunny days and the interior is quaint and cozy. The service is always top notch and everyone is always so friendly and kind. Would recommend if you are craving yummy pasta!

I had a really nice meal here. The food was cooked to perfection. The service was friendly as well. I recommend this restaurant if you love Italian cuisine. My waiter was kind of hard to communicate with though. I give them 4 stars ⭐️

I went to this restaurant with my cousins who are local to San Francisco. We really enjoyed the food and service. Cool vibes, good food and friendly staff. I was able to find a ample vegetarian options at this restaurant. I would highly recommend it. I would definitely visit again in future .

name: The Ramp Restaurant
address: 855 Terry A Francois Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94158, United States

google.name: The Ramp Restaurant
google.address: 855 Terry A Francois Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94158, United States
google.description: Casual waterfront restaurant on Mission Bay serving lunch, brunch & evening appetizers year-round.

top_reviews.content:
A respectable bar/restaurant situated at a unique waterfront corner of the Dogpatch. Their fairly limited menu contains your typical American bar fare, with a seafood twist.

The new England style clam chowder was the star of my meal - not the best I've ever had, but an all around solid offering for the portion and price.

The burger on the other hand... It was by no means bad, but it distinctly lacked cohesion and was quite disappointing for the price. I knew I wouldn't get much lobster from a single tail and would be paying a hefty premium for the novelty of it, but to not only just have it unceremoniously stacked on top of an already too tall burger, but to have it be so overcooked it was tough and chewy really ruined the novelty.

The rest of the burger toppings were all individually good, but they didn't meld at all. The avocado quickly smashed out the sides in my attempts to compress the stack to a biteable height, meanwhile the bacon was crosslinked into a network that yanked out half the sandwich. The burger itself was a bit small and had no distinct flavors of its own, simultaneously being both a bit too lean and a bit overcooked.

For a first visit novelty, the burger was only mildly disappointing as a whole, but I'm definitely not ordering it again.

The fries that came with were fine, though the seasoning made them reminiscent of public school lunches. The remoulade dipping sauce was their best feature.

Worth a visit for the ambiance, especially if going with a group for drink and appetizers, but don't expect too much from their entrees.

Lunch with my good friend julie su at the Ramp restaurant. Great location with view of bay spacious patio and by beach with kayak rentals. Cuisine and service great. Kimmy chill and comfortable 😌.  Highly recommend 👌 kimmy gives two paws 🐾

This is a historic restaurant that has been there for 30 years.  They have made improvements since I was there last ,20 years ago.
The food is average. We had a burger and a bowl of clam chowder. Plenty of clams but slightly runny.  The views of the bay are  incredible interrupted by a few rusty hulls of old boats a remnant of the past.

Enjoyed my time here, only Major issue was that they seemed to be short one bartender on Memorial Day before Valks/Giants game. Even a barback or someone who was cross trained would have been helpful to support.

Their food looked good and and kitchen was pumping it out.

I have to give props to the bartender who was doing an amazing job despite flying solo.

She did have some support in ringing folks up, which helped a little.

My previous visit was very chill. Will probably be back.

I am glad I tried something new and got to relax by the water in San Francisco. This is a new brunch spot for me and I loved the selection. The people are super friendly here and the service is great.
