google.description: Branch of a pizza chain serving both deep-dish & thin-crust pies in a room with customer artwork.

top_reviews.content: The thick crust pizza is one of the best if you like tomatoes.  It takes around 30 minutes to cook. Very flavorful and filling.

The menu has many delicious options.  Your can order just one slice or any size pizza you want with a variety of scrumptious toppings. My small mouthwatering pizza  was a hot, cheesy, saucy offering with sausage,  pepperoni,  mushrooms and spinach. There was plenty left over to take home for two more meals. The service staff are super friendly and knowledgeable. The ambiance is great. I loved the artfully pleasing wall decor. The place is super clean and that includes the bathrooms.
This was the first time I dined in because I  usually get take out. But there is spacious seating here that can accommodate any size group.

Forgot to make a review a year ago when I revisited. After a decade, I’m happy to say that the delicious taste of this deep dish pizza is still the same as before! There’s no place like Zachary’s, I highly recommend it. If there thin crust pizzas are anything like I remember, those were also really good. I also love that all locations have art pieces of Zachary’s in different media, it’s very fun and unique!

Supposedly this restaurant has been open since 1983, I’m not sure how they survived for that long if their pizzas were like what we had eaten. The place was still relatively crowded near closing, and was decorated with nostalgic memorabilia. Caesar salad was pretty good but standard and on the heavier side. The two pizzas we got were the thin style Rustic Italian and the Chicago style Zachary’s special. The Rustic Italian had pretty good flavor and I liked the whole garlic cloves, though it could be more roasted. The biggest problem was the crust; it was so granular it almost felt like it could break apart easily, and it did not have that pizza char that it could greatly benefit from. The Zachary’s special was very disappointing, it was filled with basically just canned tomato sauce with very sparse sausage (that was just steamed inside the pizza) and other toppings. The flavor was just sweet and lacked any depth. The crust was even worse on this one, and was just a chore to even finish. The prices for these were also more on the expensive side at around 25-35 dollars per 10 inch pizza. There are many other pizza places you can go to in Berkeley before even considering this one.
Even their smallest pizza good for 2-3 people. Great quality ingredients. They told us how long since some were deep dish. Six people. Everyone loved their choice.

The meat is fresh as well.

The restaurant was clean; seating was very tight (not their fault that they are popular). Each pasta was cooked to perfection, not mushy. Sauces were flavorful, and meats were fairly tender. Portions were the perfect ratios of carbs, protein, veggies. Love the roasted garlic cloves on the bread! Everyone who was with me said they would come back again.

Food isn't very high quality but it's close to the bars so its price for quantity is good value. Discount for cash and extremely packed on a Friday night so food takes a while.

I got their pesto calzone for $15. Huge, but not very good (I got sick of it after a few bites) and took over 20min for a takeout place.

The pesto was oily and a bit bland. Chicken and the thick dough tasted cold and very, very dry.  Ambiance is not nice to sit at, feels like an indoor taco truck.

This place probably isn't in my top 5 for the area because its not too good and it takes a long time, but if someone wanted to eat here I wouldn't argue against it.

Absolutely love this place! I can see why there are plenty of students here! The food here is very filling and comes with huge portions! I do have to say the salad needs a bit more dressing as there's not enough. Nonetheless it's still a 5/5.

We ordered the RED POZOLE, the Tamales, Guacamole and chips, and an Arnold Palmer.  The Pozole had a gorgeous depth of flavor, a savory, distinct, well made, balanced dish with perfect accompaniments to garnish it,  The guacamole was perfect with subtle lime notes and great texture.

We will order TO GO again soon!  Nopalito is one of the finest Mexican establishments in our fine city,  It never fails to execute delicious dishes that feast the eyes and the soul.  The men and women have passion for their culture and their food and it shows in every savory, delicious bite!

And added plus, they sell their cookbook at their take out window and looking through it makes your mouth water.

Well done to all!  So happy to have your fine restaurant in our amazing city showcasing best of class dishes.

Thank YOU! ✨✨✨✨✨
Great place to grab a Margarita and Tacos.  Quick service and attentive bartender.  Everything was delicious !!!

Im not very experienced in Mexican food, but this is one of the very best I've ever had. We started with a nice sweet nutty and creamy almond horchata. So refreshing. Then we ordered the fish tacos, quesadilla with chicharron and the birra main. The fish taco was sublime. Pun on the lime. It was so flavorful and delicious. The quesadilla was unusual. The soft taco layer was fried to a crisp shell with pulled pork and lovely chicharron overflowing. So juicy crunchy and umami. The birra was a pulled beef dish with rice. So good and filling. This is my favorite Mexican food place.

The Mexican food and drinks here are fantastic. I came with a group of friends for brunch and we all tried different dishes. Every single plate was flavorful and well prepared. The vibrant atmosphere and great service made the experience even better. I will definitely be coming back.

google.name: ROOH SF

google.description: Michelin Guide-featured Bay Area restaurant serving Indian food with an innovative spin and unique cocktails.

top_reviews.content:
Rooh is one of the finest modern Indian restaurants in San Francisco, offering a perfect blend of contemporary Indian cuisine, exceptional cocktails, and outstanding hospitality. The location is convenient, making it a great choice whether you’re a local or visiting the city.

My wife and I visited Rooh to celebrate her birthday, and it turned out to be a wonderful experience. The restaurant has a beautiful, elegant ambiance that creates the perfect setting for a special occasion. The staff was warm, attentive, and made us feel truly welcome throughout our visit.

The food was absolutely excellent, with every dish beautifully presented and full of flavor. Their cocktail menu is equally impressive and definitely worth trying.

If you’re looking for an upscale Indian restaurant in the Bay Area for a date night, celebration, or simply an exceptional dining experience, I highly recommend giving Rooh a try. It was a memorable evening, and we look forward to visiting again!

Went to Rooh in San Francisco for a weekday team dinner, and got to try a lot of their dishes. Appetizers included Dahi Puri, Chicken Malai meatballs, Octopus Balchao, and Tamarind shrimp. The chicken malaise meatballs were my favorite as it was creamy, and also surprisingly crunchy. The Dahi Puri was also really good. For the main dishes we had Kerala beef, butter chicken, and Tawa Branzino. The Kerala beef was really good with the Malabar Paratha, and the other dishes were also tasty, yet subtle enough to not be overpowering. For dessert we got the Kela Kapi Brownie and the Texture of Milk dessert (rasmalai); both were good, but the brownie was the star. The food overall was above average-to-great, a solid 4.5 out of 5 for me. Atmosphere and service were good; the main downside is related to reservations and service. During an earlier attempt to visit there was some confusion regarding reservation times, where the restaurant mistakenly put our reservation request at 5pm instead of 6pm. There was no table seating anymore, only bar seating, which was not conducive for a team dinner. The team eventually was forced to look for a different restaurant to eat in. This time worked out though through OpenTable, and we understand that they are very strict with customers and reservations. It was also a bit pricey, but delicious, and overall this gets a 4.25 out of 5.

Outstanding Indian food, the best we’ve had in San Francisco. Every dish was super creative (the dahi puri chaat was amazing), great cocktails, and super friendly waiters and waitresses. Puja especially was really
friendly and helpful.

Great spot for elevated Indian cuisine.

ROOH SF was superisingly good. Overall I enjoyed the experience more than copra because my server was the sweetest guy with great recommendations. I went with more conventional choices instead of some of the more fusion options they have. I was craving north Indian food, and so ordered mostly that, but will be back to try the other offerings.

For apps, got the malai kebab meatballs and tamarind prawn. The meatballs were well spiced and the cream sauce was tasty, the edible flowers also made for great presentation. The prawn was well cooked and tangy with some foam on top to jazz it up.

The butter chicken was spicy, and chicken was smoky and well cooked. The sauce was a great silky consistency you can only get with a seive and a kitchen aid and lots of heavy cream.

The lamb shank was fall off the bone soft with strong flavors of saffron and caramelized onions. This was the the best protein. With some biryani rice this would have been 🔥👨‍🍳😘(chefs kiss).

The daal makhani was super rich and creamy.

We got naan and onion kulcha. The naan was a little disappointing. It looked like they cooked it in an oven and then blow torched it for a little char on top, or they have a gas tandoor. I have yet to find a good naan in they bay that is crispy  and thin with the kind of blistering and smokiness you get back home from charcoal tandoors.

For desert we got the texture of milk which was inventive with the mango moose and rabri. The condensed milk or cream pour was a nice table side element. The rose petals and cardamom and crushed biscuit were good touches.

Ambience is nice and cozy and service as I said before was impeccable. 10/10 will be back.

Our experience at Rooh San Francisco was unfortunately quite underwhelming for Jain food and fell far short of what we'd expected from a Michelin-recognized fine dining restaurant.

Things got off to a disappointing start when we were seated at a wobbly table. Rather than moving us to another available table, the staff simply placed a piece of wood underneath one of the legs to stabilize it. While it solved the immediate issue, it didn't reflect the level of service you'd expect from a restaurant of this caliber.

The biggest disappointment was the ** Jain Dahi Puri**. It was probably the worst version I've ever had. The dish was almost entirely yogurt—about 95% dahi—with very little of everything else, including the puri itself. It lacked the balance of textures and flavors that make this classic chaat enjoyable.

The **Signature Paneer Pinwheel** was the highlight of the meal and was well-prepared with good flavors. However, one good entrée wasn't enough to make up for the overall experience.

Overall, the meal felt underwhelming, and neither the food nor the service delivered the memorable fine dining experience we were expecting. I had much higher expectations and left disappointed.

I love the one egger(pictured) and the PIE!!! So much food for a great price. Our waitress, Raquel, was incredibly sweet and helpful as well. Love this place!!!!

I've heard their pies are really good, so we got one for the birthday cake. My experience today at this particular nations was amazing!!! Overall the food was great. Socorro attended me very well and treated me and my family as if we were her family. Really did appreciate that!! Overall a great nations location

Such great breakfast! the place is clean, spacious and has lots of free parking. Everything on the menu is excellent. Soccoro and Christine are the nicest employees and are great cooks! One of the last affordable and still delicious spots on the Bay Area! They also have great pies, coffee and burgers- but we come for the all day breakfast!!! We love Nations Berkeley!

I had a great experience at Nations in Berkeley. The food was fresh, hot, and exactly what you expect every time — solid breakfast and great pies.

What really stood out was the service. Socorro and Araceli were both incredibly friendly, attentive, and welcoming from the moment we walked in. They made sure everything was correct with our order and checked in to see if we needed anything else. It’s always nice to see staff who genuinely care about customer service.

I’ll definitely be coming back. Thank you for the great experience!

reviews_snippets.content: "Breakfast AA egg, meat, hash browns, and toast combo makes a hearty meal."
"Pies and best burgers and chili fries omg love love that place"
"I’ve received great service from Cynthia and the food she’d cooked was delicious"

name: HINODEYA Ramen & Bar Downtown
address: 680 Clay St, San Francisco, CA 94111, United States

google.name: HINODEYA Ramen & Bar Downtown
google.address: 680 Clay St, San Francisco, CA 94111, United States

top_reviews.content:
A small coincidence on my first day in San Francisco turned into my favourite spot. I needed to check in to the hostel but it was too early, so I searched for ramen on Google Maps and found HINODEYA nearby. Good reviews, so I gave it a try. The pork katsu ramen was one of the best I have had, the umami flavour was amazing.

On my last day in San Francisco I went back, exactly two weeks later. This time I ordered the Spicy Miso, equally good. What makes this place special is the staff. Genuine, warm, and you feel seen even if you are eating alone. The kitchen staff joke around and seem to enjoy themselves, and that energy spreads through the whole room.

A nice detail: when guests arrive, the staff beat a taiko, a traditional Japanese drum with roots in festivals and temple ceremonies. Historically it was used to create energy and mark important moments, and here it becomes a personal and memorable way to welcome guests.

Two visits, same high standard both times. Highly recommended, and it has also sparked an interest in exploring more Japanese food in Japan itself.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

Such an amazing experience dining here! I was solo and sat at the bar. Had the house ramen…seriously some of the best ramen I’ve ever had, and definitely the best Chashu pork I’ve ever had in a ramen. They have little crispy’s you can add to your ramen on the table, DO IT! It elevates the dish so much. Also tried the Matcha Beer. Love matcha so had to give it a try! They whisked matcha in a ceremonial bowl and then added it to my Asahi beer. Paloma was the absolute sweetest server and was the cherry on top to an amazing lunch. She was so sweet and attentive, and made me feel like family! I can’t wait to come back here.

We came for dinner and ordered a variety of dishes. I had the Hinodeya Ramen, while we also shared chicken karaae, takoyaki, and gyoza. For drinks, we tried the Matcha Beer, Yuzu soda, and Ume soda.

The ramen was decent, but the broth wasn't particularly memorable.

The standout dish was definitely the chicken karaage. It was crispy on the outside, juicy on the inside, and incredibly tender.

As for the drinks, it was my first time trying Matcha Beer, and it had a unique and interesting flavor. The Yuzu Soda and Ume Soda were both refreshing and delicious, though they leaned toward the sweeter side.

The food came so fast and was so delicious. The perfect lunch place.

The chicken karaage as a starter was perfectly cooked. And the spicy miso soup was so flavourful. Absolutely loved every sip. The pork belly was slightly crunchy but so tasty.

This is an amazing Japanese restaurant with authentic Japanese flavors. I had the spicy miso ramen with corn and butter, along with the takoyaki, and everything was delicious!!
A special thank you to Paloma and Nobel for their excellent service. I truly had a wonderful lunch here and enjoyed every dish. Highly recommended!

reviews_snippets.content: "The tofu and crispy greens in the creamy vegan bowl was amazing."

name: Toy Soldier
address: 52 Belden Pl, San Francisco, CA 94104, United States

google.name: Toy Soldier
google.address: 52 Belden Pl, San Francisco, CA 94104, United States

top_reviews.content:
Excellent service!
The owners are Mexicans, so we asked for their recommendation and got some great tacos. We said we don't like spicy and they helped us choose the best options and even got us a sample to try first.

Omar and Alan took great care of us tonight!  Service was spot on.  Drinks were amazing! Definitely get the lamb chops or the salmon.  The only miss (and a slight one at that) was the roasted Brussels sprouts which were absolutely swimming in butter sauce. The oysters, however, were incredible! Just make sure to ask for a side of horseradish.  We will definitely return!!

Arturo was my tender this evening. He has great skills that match the amazing food. I had the clam chowder first, WOW! Absolutely delicious. Followed with house salad, which was perfect and not soaked in dressing; and my main was the pork chop, off the charts, large portion perfectly cooked. This place is a fresh delight.

Came here with a group and it was nice since they got our table ready super quickly!

Good:
- The place had so many food options
- Loved the $1 oysters and got 12 of them - super fresh and tasted like the ocean
- I liked the clam chowder soup - very big portions and tasty
- The dessert was delicious too - we got the chocolate cake
- A good place for a friends and family reunion

Bad:
- Pretty dim lighting and felt super dark
- Food took a while to get there
- It was pricey!

Overall it was a nice experience but due to price will likely not go again.

So disappointed... It took them more than 30 minutes for the waiter to TAKE the order for the drinks, and more than 1 HOUR to bring the food. the $60 for that small piece of meat was way too much, and it was not correctly cooked.

Same with the fries, calamari, etc., that are just ok; they are extremely overpriced, plus the waiting.

reviews_snippets.content: "We also enjoyed the pasta, with a really tasty cream and mushroom sauce."
"Steak cooked to perfection, friendly bartender good vibes all round."

name: Lapisara Eatery
address: 698 Post St, San Francisco, CA 94109, United States

google.name: Lapisara Eatery
google.address: 698 Post St, San Francisco, CA 94109, United States
google.description: Chic destination serving American classics for three meals a day, plus a few Thai dinner dishes.

top_reviews.content: Great brunch place if you want a fusion breakfast. Good cappuccino and iced caramel macchiato (with a sweet teddy bear floating). We had the ‘Holy Chili Bomb Basil Omelette (a fancy name for a omelette with Thai Basil ground Chicken filling), the Tom Yum Burrito (self explanatory), and the Chicken Waffle (too much of syrup). Everything was pretty good. We would’ve liked it a bit more spicy but it’s not a dealbreaker at all. Definitely a good place to go. Area is also free of homeless people (I guess being in Nob Hill 😇). Enjoy and let me know if you agree with my review if you do visit.

Great Saturday morning brunch spot! We didn’t have a reservation, but adding our name to the iPad waitlist at the door was seamless, and we were seated in just 5–10 minutes.
​The vibe was lively and nice, and the service was super quick and efficient. We tried the avocado toast, the Sweet Dream, and an ube latte—everything tasted amazing! The presentation was gorgeous with edible flowers on the plates, and the drinks came in the cutest bear cups.
​Highly recommend Lapisara for a fun and delicious brunch in SF! 🌸🐻

An overall better taste than other good brunch we tried. We ordered pacific scramble, steak and egg, and fried chicken waffle. The scramble is fresh and the shrimp is juicy and almost crunchy. Steak has a funny durian flavor, my girlfriend find it a little weird. Salad is slight marinated with lemon and honey? But it was great and has a more smooth texture. Waffle is flavored just spot on, I can’t stop eating it.

Came here on a Saturday for brunch.

I got the Holy Chili Bomb Basil Omelette. It had ground chicken and veggies inside, and the chicken and basil were the flavors that stood out. I wouldn’t call it spicy at all. The omelette felt small for the price and there wasn’t much filling inside.

It came with a side of potatoes that were really good. They had a nice crisp on the outside and were soft on the inside. I also got a regular coffee, and they do unlimited refills.

The place was busy for brunch, and I liked the bear theme. Some of the coffees came in bear-shaped glasses, and some of the lattes had a decorative bear made out of ice.

The food presentation and taste was out of this world! I loved it so so much and I would definitely recommend this restaurant to everyone I know. I ordered the Sweet Dream Belgium waffle and it was truly so delicious. I especially loved the Ube Latte not just because of the cute bear but also because it tasted like authentic Ube. The staff were really nice and accommodating as well!

reviews_snippets.content: "Cosy space Great and friendly local place Quick service Good tasting food"
"I ordered chicken and waffles, side of eggs with cheese and hot chocolate."

name: La Mission
address: 1255 University Ave, Berkeley, CA 94702, United States

google.name: La Mission
google.address: 1255 University Ave, Berkeley, CA 94702, United States
google.description: Busy joint offering burritos & tacos in small, bright digs with painted walls plus outdoor seating.

top_reviews.content:
We stopped by this restaurant late at night, around 10 PM, for dinner. I wasn’t extremely hungry, so I ordered three tacos — though I could only finish two and ended up taking one home. My friend also ordered a few tacos along with a Baja fish taco and another item.

The place has a very casual, chic, student-friendly vibe and offers a wide variety of Mexican dishes on the menu. The food felt fresh and made from scratch, which I really appreciated.

Among everything I tried, the chorizo taco was definitely the standout. It was flavorful, juicy, and perfectly seasoned. I also tried carnitas and al pastor. Usually al pastor is my all-time favorite, but this version didn’t quite match the ones I’ve had in Mexico City. Still, it wasn’t bad by any means.

They had a salsa station where you could pick your own sauces, though I noticed they didn’t offer the usual grilled onions or spring onions that many more traditional Mexican spots serve. Overall, the restaurant felt more like a California-style Mexican place with its own twist rather than a fully authentic Mexican taqueria.

That said, the freshness and quality of the food really stood out. I’d definitely go back, especially for the chorizo tacos. Overall, a really nice late-night food spot.

This is a MEXICAN restaurant. The very  kindest and nicest service. The food is just way off the high end of the charts. The atmosphere... Fantastic. 6/5. Across the board. They have a chocolate horchata that is the best I have ever had.

This place is conveniently located right on University Avenue. The staff is extremely friendly and they offer many homemade items including homemade corn bread, etc. I ordered the steak nachos and they were perfect. Wait times were non existent and the service was very quick and professional. Will be back!

Quick service and sweet staff.
However I felt the legumbres vegetarian burrito could have had more flavor.
The chocolate cake was good but the icing was maybe a touch too sweet.
Husband liked his chicken burrito.
Lovely outdoor seating area.

Great burritos and other Mexican food. They’ve got beer and wine too.
Nice outdoor patio area. It’s screened off from University Ave with plants but you can hear some traffic.
Staff here are super nice and friendly.

reviews_snippets.content: "Amazing Mexican food work a great service and super friendly staff"
"Variety of fresh food from tacos, burritos, nachos, ceviche, pan ducle."

name: Oren's Hummus
address: 71 3rd St, San Francisco, CA 94103, United States

google.name: Oren's Hummus
google.address: 71 3rd St, San Francisco, CA 94103, United States

top_reviews.content: First time dining at Oren. I had the lamb skewers and the schnitzel with hummus and fluffy pitas. The hummus was amazingly rich and smooth, that is new to me. The lamb skewers were well seasoned and no gaminess! Love it 😍. The schnitzel is well made and crunchy. Overall I thought my meal was wonderfully cooked. Definitely recommend this place. This restaurant is centrally located in downtown SF and walking distance from union square.

Oren's Hummus is one of the best Mediterranean restaurants I've been to in San Francisco! The atmosphere is warm, modern, and inviting, and the service was outstanding from start to finish. We ordered the chicken rice bowl and the kebab rice bowl, and both were incredibly fresh, flavorful, and perfectly cooked. Every bite was delicious, and the portions were generous. You can really taste the quality of the ingredients. I'll definitely be coming back the next time I'm in San Francisco. Highly recommended!

Located in the heart of Union Square, this is such a cute and cozy spot with great food. We ordered the hummus chicken, and sweet potatoes, and everything was delicious. We were visiting from NYC, were a bit jet-lagged, and celebrated our anniversary here, which made the evening even more special.

One standout was the spicy dip served with the starter—I haven’t had anything quite like it before, and it was absolutely delicious.

The only downside was the service. It was a bit slow, and we often had to call someone over, even for something as simple as getting drinking water. Other than that, we had a lovely experience and would definitely recommend giving this place a try.

I lost track of how many times I said “mmm” while eating this meal!

My server was friendly and very knowledgeable about the menu. He had great suggestions. After taking my order, he returned with a complimentary snack that was pickled red pepper and I think cabbage.

I wanted to try 2 different types of hummus, so I got the smaller side portions of the Jaffa hummus with pine nuts, and the Muhammara hummus. OMG, the Jaffa version is the best hummus I’ve ever had outside of the Carmel Market in Tel Aviv! It’s delicious and airy, and next time I will get a huge portion of just that.

I had never tried Muhammara before and it did not disappoint. It’s very flavorful with a little bit of sweet, heat, tangy & savory flavors. It came with crunchy pita strips. I ordered extra white pita bread for my dips, and highly recommend it. It was soft and also identical to what I enjoyed in Israel.

Near the floor by many tables were outlets, which made charging phones or devices easy for tourists. The meal was pricy, but worth it for me as a treat.

The food was so flavourful and delicious, absolutely recommend it.

The chicken hummus was delicious, but the main attraction was the australian lamb. Marinated in harissa, this was so delicious we loved it. Too bad there was only two pieces of roasted vegetables, I would’ve eaten a side dish only with roasted veggies from this place!!

reviews_snippets.content: "I had ordered vegetarian food: pita falafel, Babaganoush dip and Baklava."
"Service was quick, atmosphere was calm and lovely, I really enjoyed the music!"

top_reviews.content:
Came here for lunch solo. Ordered the omelette of the day which was chicken and spinach and came with hash browns and toast. Also ordered a side of salsa verde. Omelette was cooked perfectly and the chicken was flavorful. Very delicious. Only comment is that the hash browns could be a bit more crispy.

Also got an iced tea (unlimited refills). I appreciated the service there, as the lady at the front came by several times to give me a refill on iced tea.

I also loved the bathroom door covered in stickers, really unique 😀

Definitely come here if you are craving classic American diner food.

​If you’re looking for a great local spot in Emeryville, Rudy’s Cafe is it! You get that classic, cozy diner character the moment you walk in. Service was wonderfully friendly and attentive, and the food arrived fast, hot, and packed with fresh flavor. With so many choices on the menu, I’m already planning what to try on my next visit. Highly recommend!

Really disappointing, Rudy can certainly fail.

Denver omelet was just egg on a pile of undercooked vegetables and ham, no seasoning. Hashbrowns undercooked, no salt. The plates came out way too fast to cook the food properly and it showed

Still a great  place for breakfast. Not like it used to be with a server. Now you order at the entrance and then you can seat anywhere. The breakfast was still good and all the different themes were a handful of memories.
A great  place for breakfast. You order at the entrance and then you can seat anywhere. I got the Tower of Power. Really good and very filling. I also liked all the different table displays.

top_reviews.content: This place is the oldest restaurant in San Francisco. Street parking only. Outdoor and indoor seating. I highly recommend making a reservation for big groups. This place is always crowded. Get ready to wait in line. I came here for their unique cocktails and I was not disappointed. Next time, I'll try their food.

At the outskirts of San Francisco lies this historic gem! This is a great place to have a good time with friends and family. I ordered the pork adobo dish and it is a must try! Lovely presentation and the adobo was served sizzling on a hot plate. It was my first time trying fish lumpia and it was a great flavor. There are so many more dishes on the menu that I want to try. This place is great for a group and the outside patio is chill on a sunny day. I hear the desserts are lovely as well!

So grateful they could last minute accommodate our group of 20 here after our weekday hike. Don't skip out on their ube tres leches cake with fresh sliced strawberries on top!

Amazing and kind staff for a bar that is a historical roadhouse I read the articles about in the restroom. LOL

*Re: Their online ordering platform' UI doesn't make it clear there was an automatic 20% gratuity included for our large group. Not the restaurant's fault, but I had to call after to refund the extra 20% tip I added because I didn't see the auto-gratuity, but they were super kind. No questions asked, staff saw the double charge and refunded the second 20% tip.

Had an amazing time here, the food was so good. We ordered the Sisig with a side of arroz caldo, Cow palace burger, garlic fries, ube hot chocolate and mango juice. The sisig was sooo good, unfortunately it was a bit spicy for me but my partner enjoyed it a lot.

Everything else was delicious, the cow palace burger is so worth it as it can be a good meal for 2 even 3 people plus it comes with fries. It was my first time trying the ube hot chocolate and I absolutely loved it, perfect for the cold weather. We saw that some reviews mentioned the filipino food isn’t “impressive” but that honestly couldn’t be further from the truth. My partner, his family, and friends all being Filipino and having lived around this area for a long time say the food is delicious and quite homey.

They also have a DOGGY MENU, which we took full advantage of! Our dog is quite small but we were given to-go boxes to split up his dish and they also provided him with a free biscuit and a water bowl!

Great environment, it was a super cold day and we asked for the heater since we were seated outside. They set up quickly for us and even helped us adjust it to an appropriate temperature.

Thank you to Jas as well, out waitress, who was outstanding and super on top of it!

I've been a repeat offender to this establishment for a few years.   A couple times a month 2.5 yrs ago and now  that I'm back in the area,  here i come again.   Food is good,  service is excellent, bartenders are exceptional and the history of the place is interesting.  It's popular so street parking is available but, you may need to put in a few steps.  It's not the worst thing.   If you're in the area or passing through, you won't be disappointed.

reviews_snippets.content: "Down-home Bar and Grill Latin music jazz big variety of food excellent waitstaff"

name: Harborview Restaurant & Bar
address: 4 Embarcadero Center, Street Level Drumm Street &, Sacramento St, San Francisco, CA 94111, United States

google.name: Harborview Restaurant & Bar
google.address: 4 Embarcadero Center, Street Level Drumm Street &, Sacramento St, San Francisco, CA 94111, United States
google.description: Contemporary, family-style outlet serving Cantonese-style dishes with panoramic harbor views.

top_reviews.content: Our cruise had a stop in San Francisco, the restaurant was recommended by locals. We made reservations for noon, but got here around 11:45 am. Glad that we did, since the restaurant got packed quickly. Service was efficient, did not help much by way of recommendations. I suggest that you have an idea of what you want to order. Nothing disappointed as the food was excellent. Highly recommend the baked buns. It was only two of us and we could have done the full duck rather than the half portion.

The dim sum is refined, and distinctly non-greasy. While it carries a premium "FiDi price tag" compared to holes-in-the-wall in Chinatown or the Richmond, the ingredient quality and execution back it up.Cocktails were pretty good,traditional cocktails with an Asian twist. It also offers panoramic, postcard-perfect views of the historic Ferry Building and the sprawling Bay Bridge.
💓dog friendly

I had the most delicious lunch at this restaurant. The garlic chicken, jasmine rice and almond soup was amazing. The waitstaff was very friendly and the ambiance of the restaurant was awesome. I highly recommend this restaurant. Be Shure to make a reservation if you decide to come here because it is very popular and quite crowded . 5 stars!⭐️

Since we didn't have a reservation, we were seated in the bar area through a separate entrance — not sure if that mattered, but this was honestly the worst Chinese food I've had in the U.S.

Nothing tasted fresh. Every dish came out fast-food quick, like it had been pre-made and reheated. The meat in the fried rice was tiny and tough, the eggplant skin was chewy, and the fried items were all soggy. The best thing we had was the salad — dressed in what tasted like store-bought sweet chili sauce.

An 18% gratuity was automatically added for our party of three (including a small child) — no one informed us until the bill arrived.

I was really excited to try Harborview after hearing so many great things. Unfortunately, my experience was very disappointing. I was seated and ordered the Lychee Pu-er Tea Lemonade, which was excellent—refreshing, with a strong lychee flavor balanced by subtle tea notes. Unfortunately, that was the only thing I had.

After receiving my drink, I waited about 45 minutes without anyone taking my food order or checking on me. Eventually, I had to flag someone down just to pay for my drink, and then I left without ever eating. I walked in looking forward to experiencing one of San Francisco's best Cantonese restaurants, but I left hungry and disappointed. I sincerely hope this was just an off night, because based on my visit, the service did not live up to the restaurant's reputation.

reviews_snippets.content: "We ordered salt and pepper calamari, sautéed veggies, beef with peppers, etc."
"Prices not on the menu I was upset about 18% service charge for only 4 people"

name: Marlowe
address: 500 Brannan St, San Francisco, CA 94107, United States

google.name: Marlowe

google.description: Stylish & lively option serving Californian comfort food in a hip & sprawling space.

top_reviews.content: Popped in to grab a bite on a Saturday night. We were seated right away. Service was great and super attentive. I got a gin based drink (I believe it was called Karl the Fog) which was tasty and aesthetically pleasing. For food we got the lamb ribs, scallops, and sides of roasted potatoes and broccoli. Both my partner and I found the food to be quite salty. Still edible but I think we both would have enjoyed our meals a little more had there been less salt.

We were pleasantly surprised with this establishment from the outside. It doesn't look like much, but when we walked in the atmosphere was live, the service was great. The food was incredible, and yes, we will return when we are in the city of San Francisco. You guys rocked out on atmosphere and food. Everybody loved their plates. Thanks again.

The burger is overhyped in my opinion. There’s nothing wrong with it, maybe it’s slightly under seasoned if anything. It’s a very mid burger and too expensive for what it is.

The Crispy Pork Schnitzel was incredibly tender but lacked flavor.

Service was amazing though. The staff were friendly and they proactively cut our burger and our schnitzel in half when we mentioned we were sharing them. That was a nice detail that I appreciated.

We came in for brunch and everything was so tasty. We tried the heirloom tomato, egg sandwich, infamous burger, scrambled eggs, and polenta — not a single miss on the table.

My boyfriend and I often come here for date nights, and it’s just as good during the day. The food is consistently delicious, and the vibe is cozy and lively.

Pro tip: make a reservation! It gets super busy, especially on weekends. Can’t wait to come back again!

Update: Marlowe burger is still great, and the devil eggs.

We had our wedding dinner at Marlowe 7 years ago. Every once in a while we are able to stop in for a meal. Still love it many years later 😁

reviews_snippets.content: "Table and counter service available, friendly staff, high-quality dishes."
"Beautiful place with good service, but portions are quite small for the price."
"Great place for after work drinks seated the bar grade bartenders great food"

top_reviews.content: Their mutton Biryani was very good however, the rice were a little less serving. Chana dal was very authentic and pure Pakistani style. I recommend for Takeaway since the ambience of the restaurant is average.
Very tasty halal food, If you love desi then this is the must visit place for you in SFO.

We love Pakwan. I mostly order to go and I am always happy with the quality of food and the consistency. I like their chicken tikka masala with garlic naan, and also the tandoori chicken leg.
I wasn’t the fan of seekh kebab, but overall a good experience.

One of the best Pakistani food in town. Everything I had over here tasted as authentic as it can be but also has a touch of fusion from some of Pakistan's neighbor countries. Clean places, good access to tables, plenty of seating, best mango lassie in town. Food is delicious and perfectly flavored. Naan-bread is really good especially the cheese Naan. BBQ chicken and beef was amazing and the curry goat was out of this world. Finally all to be sealed with a seriously delicious veggie biryani that had the perfect spice level. Love this place and I've been coming here for the past 14 years and with every visit I find myself thinking about how soon I can be back.

We visited on December 24th after reading so many rave reviews, and Pakwan completely delivered. The consensus is right—this is some of the most flavorful food I’ve had in many years. Also, it is halal.

We ordered Goat Biryani, BBQ Chicken Legs and Breasts, Chicken Shikh Kebab, Chicken Boti Kebab, Garlic Naan, Cheese Naan, and Plain Naan. The goat biryani came in a huge portion—definitely enough for two people to share. It was incredibly aromatic, with perfectly cooked rice and tender meat. The Chicken Shikh Kebab was okay, nothing extraordinary. The Chicken Boti Kebab was good, but for me, the BBQ chicken was the star of the show: very flavorful, moist, and tender, checking all the boxes for truly great food. All the naans were fresh, fluffy, and delicious.

The service was efficient, and the food came out quickly. As many have noted, it’s a no-frills, casual spot with an average ambiance, clearly focused on fantastic food and great value. There are plenty of seating arrangements available, suitable for both small and large groups, and portions are generous for the price.

It can get very busy and loud during peak dinner hours, but that’s a testament to how good it is. This is now my go-to spot for a satisfying, flavorful meal in San Francisco.

Highly recommended!

reviews_snippets.content: "Amazing food, great portions, rapid service, very kind staff"
"Meat tasted old and tough, naan bread was undercooked with a doughy texture."
"Hard to beat this Pakwan on the combination of food, location and price."

name: Picante
address: 1328 Sixth St, Berkeley, CA 94710, United States

google.name: Picante
google.address: 1328 Sixth St, Berkeley, CA 94710, United States
google.description: Housemade tortillas & local cheeses make up the Mexican plates at this festive cafeteria-style spot.

top_reviews.content:
I hadn't been to Picante since the remodel so I was looking forward to seeing what had changed. The remodel is fine, definitely more of a modern aesthetic. I remember the food being good but pricey and I'd say now they are closer to being average and pricey. I ordered two shrimp tacos which cost $6.95 each! I was expecting a hefty portion of shrimps for that price. Each taco came with two sad looking shrimps with the rest of the taco being filled with salsa and slaw. I also had an horchata which was fine but it's hard to mess up horchata. I gave it an extra star just for the helpful staff. Overall I was very disappointed with Picante and won't be coming back for future visits with so many amazing Mexican places in Richmond and Oakland.

Recommendation: If you want the most delicious shrimp tacos go to Tacos el Tucan in Richmond, top notch.

The food is great here. The server is fast/average, but the register was is SLOW. They could probably handle a slightly faster pace.

There is a hot sauce refrigerator where you can get three different levels of "hot". Be bold, try the habanero! It doesn't hurt going in or out!

They recently completed a remodel, but unfortunately the atmosphere changed. It seems a bit too "upscale", even if it looks REALLY nice inside and out.

i’ve been coming here for many years and i went again last night with family for a lovely meal.  at first i did not care for the new renovation, and strongly preferred the original picante with red vinyl booths, papeles hanging, viewable tortilla station, etc.  i am starting to better appreciate how nice it now is though in a different way.  we enjoyed our food a lot.  this is high quality food beautifully presented. staff are always friendly and efficient. food comes out so so quick. we have not had to wait in line at the front but even if u do, the food comes out very quickly once you order.  overall id say tho we do miss the old picante we will be returning soon! thanks to the staff for always serving us a beautiful meal. shout out to Alex for his warm hospitality!

It is consistently good. During covid they went thru some changes trying to make things work and come together... They're better now than they ever were! The food is really good! The atmosphere is clean, open, indoor and outdoor seating. The service is quick and efficient. The bathrooms are maintained well. (When that changes, there's a problem).

Picante is one of the best Mexican restaurants in Berkeley. Their food is good and tasty, but it’s a bit pricey, which is why I knocked their rating down a star. Street parking is difficult during most of the day, but there is a small parking lot across the street and to the south about half a block. That often fills up too though. They have a bar and a lot of alcohol to select from and I see people drinking margaritas, but I’ve never tried them. The chips are just so so, they’re thick and a little greasy. I suspect there are some people that like them as they are not the normal chips you’d get in a Mexican place, but they’re just too greasy. The salsas are in the fridge by the door and they are pretty good. Everything else I’ve had here has been good, my favorite are the mole enchiladas, which are probably some of the best mole that I’ve had. They make good guacamole, and good salads as well. If it’s not too cold out, there’s an outdoor seating place.

reviews_snippets.content: "Loud place, but a fun, family-friendly atmosphere and table service."

top_reviews.content: I’ve been coming here for years. I went two days in a row this week for them Lion’s Mane Sliders. 10/10 I recommend. The Crispy buns with cabbage, the swamp sauce and pickles. The lion’s mane is so tender and breading has the perfect crunch. Go get that.

Disclaimer: I am NOT a vegan but wowwwww! I’ve been turned onto it because the food here is better than any southern cooking I’ve ever had. Love the ambiance, old school hip hop playing, delicious cocktails and amazing service. Highly recommend the vegan Mac and the beignets!!! Chefs kiss

100% VEGAN awesomeness!!!
What more can be said?  All the food is concocted and made right there. No beyond or impossible meat. They have their own unique menu, with unique flavors, so simply stuff you can’t find anywhere else and DELICIOUS!!Go support these people!

Souley Vegan is a great spot for comforting vegan food right near Jack London Square. The fried steak was the standout, crispy on the outside with a satisfying texture, and the mashed potatoes were rich and flavorful without feeling too heavy. Portions were filling, and the large indoor dining space made it easy to settle in.
I went in the morning and there was about a 15 to 20 minute wait with just one group ahead, which suggested they were a bit light on staff. That said, the team was friendly and welcoming throughout.
The location is especially convenient if you are coming from the ferry, making it an easy stop for a casual meal. One practical note: the app did not work for takeout orders in the morning, but calling in works since they handle to go orders all day.
Overall, a reliable option for hearty vegan comfort food, and I would definitely go back. Might be THE best in Oakland!
I’ve been a fan of Souley Vegan for many years. Some of the best vegan soul food you’ll ever have. Highly recommended!

I totally enjoyed my meal. The taco tropical with the jicama tortilla is a must try. The churros were great as well.

Great cocktail and food menu. The Taco Tropical and Chile Relleno worth go back, but the fried chicken taco I ordered was quite disappointing. The fried chicken breast were bone dry and tough to chew.

top_reviews.content:
We decided to try this place after seeing it on CBS Mornings. We thought it would be a great way to celebrate our anniversary. However, it was difficult to make a reservation, as the place is quite small and has a bar.  After checking daily, the calendar opened up.

The koshikari arancini was an absolute delight. It was so tasty and flavorful. The salsicia Bianca pizza was also a unique and delicious choice. It had a generous amount of sausage and was packed with flavor. The lamb parpadelle was another great dish. It was tender and flavorful, and the home made pasta was perfectly cooked.

For dessert, we had the chocolate espresso cake with cream topping and sea salt. It was a great ending to an amazing meal. We also had the pleasure of trying their homemade gummies flavored with earl grey, which was a nice surprise.  Not to mention, service was perfectly timed and our server was attentive and had a nice demeanor.

Overall, we had a wonderful time at Flour and Water. Thank you for making our anniversary dinner so special.

Okay let’s talk about the food and the hype. The food is good don’t get me wrong but for the hype it’s not there to be completely honest with you.

I would not order anything but the pasta dishes for your main. The other main courses are just not as good. We ordered the duck and though it was amazing it does not even compare to there pasta dishes we had which were very delicious.

The service was very nice. Our waiter was ver attentive to us and took care of us and the atmosphere was very relaxed and easy to talk to people.

So scrumptious. We ordered a la carte, and had more than enough. The portions are quite decently sized, so I would advise not overordering. We started with the Spring Lettuces salad which was flavorful and fresh. Then we shared the Patata Bianca pizza, Carrot Agnolotti pasta, and Porcini Gnocchetti Sardi. All were super tasty and unique, and we had plenty of leftovers between the three of us. The Chocolate Budino we chose for dessert was actually underwhelming, yet the main dishes and salad that we shared outshined the so-so dessert. Great dinner and recommend making reservations well in advance.

a little skeptical coming after hearing mixed reviews but flour and water surprised me in the best way possible.

service was top tier with our server providing detailed recommendations. loved the complimentary sparkling water that was specifically mentioned.

all of the filled pastas were top tier!

carrot agnolotti: reminiscent of a cozy fall, had great spices and flavors. perfectly cooked pasta.

rainbow scarpinocc: the famous signature dish was tasty but honestly expected a little more. would still recommend though

porcini gnochetti sardi: highly recommend. creamy, rich, al dente pasta

budino: don’t typically like chocolate but wasn’t too sweet and decadent.

I’ve heard so many good things about this place and I can say they live up to the expectations. Duck casoncelli and seaweed Chittara were both delicious although the pasta was more al dente that I typically like. The ricotta was ok but not the best I’ve had. Amberjack crudo was absolutely fresh and delicious. For dessert we tried strawberry pavlova and chocolate budino and they were both amazing with all the right textures

top_reviews.content:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Our server Martha was absolutely amazing! She was honestly one of the best servers I’ve ever had. She was so friendly, attentive, and welcoming from the moment we sat down. She constantly checked in to make sure everything was good without ever being overbearing, and she made sure we had everything we needed. She was very knowledgeable, patient, and genuinely made us feel taken care of. You can tell she really cares about giving her customers a great experience. Martha definitely made our visit so much better, and she deserves all the recognition! If you come here, ask for Martha you won’t be disappointed!

We were seated fast and forgotten even faster. We weren’t asked for a drink order until 20 m minutes in!  That red flag told me we need to know what we want to order when they finally make it to our table. So many times were we passed by and a total of 3 waiters working the entire restaurant at 11:40am  I hate to write a review like this but it is my honest opinion. My boneless buffalo wings were cold, to the point the sauce was thick and clumpy. It took so long to receive my appetizer I didn’t order anything else. I just left very disappointed truly. Alameda do better! The carpet in the restaurant holds such a disgusting smell also! So much food is spilled, drinks outside dirt and bacteria from shoes! Just overall should be rebuilt/remodeled and needs new management and a whole entire diverse new team. No reason alameda Applebees shouldn’t be the spot to be at on a Friday evening after bowling!

My partner placed an order through DoorDash, and after an hour of waiting we received a notification from a doordasher asking if we had already gotten our food. When we called Applebee’s, and we come to find out that they had given our order to another driver without confirming anything. They handed our $63 order to someone else for free and took no accountability for the mistake. The manager, Maria, spent the entire call defending the situation instead of resolving it, and simply told us to reorder. Very poor customer service and an unacceptable way to handle their own error.

I'll say I went to the bee's a few years ago and it was a better experience.

Came in on a Wednesday night, I'd say about a 1/3 or less full, 5-6 servers working.  Multiple staff walked by me waiting to get a table, took like 5 minutes of standing there while a server was dapping up friends at the bar and ignoring me, which started things off on an annoying note.

Took probably 15 minutes just to get water, took another 7-8 to get an iced tea.  Had to ask about the AYCE promotion because they aren't giving out menus for it like they did previously.  The food took a really long time, the follow up plates took a long time and were tiny, I'd say the only reason to do the AYCE is if you plan on getting some reading or laptop work done and want to snack while doing it.  Our server was cool like attitude wise but it just seemed like everyone working was moving underwater, just super slow and weird vibes.

The shrimp are good, the BBQ riblets are pretty good, the boneless wings are fine, I liked the chili glaze, hated the buffalo, it's a salt bomb.  Coleslaw is diabolically bad.

Overall, I've been to applebees like 6 times in the last 2-3 years and this was probably the most disappointing

Alexis is the GOAT!! Easily one of the best servers you could ask for. Great personality, always takes care of his tables, and somehow makes serving look effortless. He’s the type of server you remember after you leave because he actually makes the whole experience better. Funny, friendly, and always bringing good energy. top_reviews.content: I used to love this place before COVID, but it’s just not the same anymore. The food is still genuinely good—the sushi is fresh and the rolls hit the spot—but everything else has really gone downhill. The prices have gone up like crazy, which makes it incredibly hard to justify when the service is so lacking. Be prepared for a super long wait just to get a table, and then an equally long wait to actually get your food served once you sit down. It’s a shame because this used to be a go-to spot, but the massive price hikes and terrible wait times just ruin the experience now.

The service was quite good, and the food was decent overall. However, if you’re looking for a truly authentic Japanese dining experience, this may not be the place. I ordered a $30 bento dinner, which came with tempura, soup, salad, and rice, along with a choice of two main items. I chose tuna sashimi and yakiniku, and the portions were very generous. That said, the flavors didn’t quite feel traditionally Japanese.

The restaurant itself is fairly large, with plenty of seating and a pleasant atmosphere. We also ordered three different rolls, though I don’t remember their names. The rolls were enjoyable and tasted good, but the overall flavor profile leaned more toward a Japanese-American fusion rather than classic Japanese cuisine.

Overall, it’s a comfortable place with good service and generous portions—nice for a casual meal, just not ideal if authenticity is what you’re seeking.

Amazing sushi with a beautiful view of the bay! Everything was incredibly fresh, delicious, and very filling. The atmosphere was relaxing, and the waterfront view made the whole experience even better. We’ll definitely be coming back. Highly recommend! 🍣🌅

I’ve been a loyal customer for over 10 years, so I was disappointed by my recent experience. On 6/22/2026, my bill was $55.38, and I left a $5 cash tip. However, when I checked my card transaction, I was charged $65.38 instead.

I recommend that everyone take a photo of their receipt before leaving the restaurant and double-check the amount that posts to their account. I hope this was an honest mistake, but it’s important to review your transactions carefully.

I ordered rainbow & cherry blossom rolls.  My rainbow roll tastes ok except the fish is not as fresh as I’ve expected.
My cherry blossom roll was really bad.  I noticed when we dine in, the salmon tastes better than when I place a to go order. This place always use the salmon part that we couldn’t bite through since they have lot of white texture strings under.  We ended up throwing all the salmon on the cherry blossom rolls away.
The roll portion here is huge but the quality is going downhill!

top_reviews.content:
Too expensive for the taste / flavor. Most of the dishes I tried tasted under seasoned. The only thing that was good was their chili pepper sauce. No cheung fun (rice noodle roll) at this location.

Lotus Wrapped Sticky Rice: Felt too wet and lacked flavor. The rice wasn’t sticking to the leaf

Shrimp Har Gow: Nice and plump, but not juicy and moist. Lacks flavor

Siu Mai: nice and firm, but lacked seasoning

Egg Tart: Mediocre egg custard. Has a flaky crust

Highly recommend for the food, and any private event!

We hosted our post-wedding dim sum brunch on Yank Sing Stevenson's patio for ~45 guests. The patio is technically outdoors, but is sheltered/covered and heated.

This place came recommended by relatives — even my parents, who hadn't been to SF in years, remembered eating here decades ago, so we knew it had to be good. We even came for a delicious meal in December, and decided on the spot this was the space for us. Booking (6 months out) was smooth and responsive over email.

Day-of, Lina took incredible care of us. She checked in constantly, anticipated what we needed, and even remembered we'd already paid our deposit — something we absolutely would have forgotten in the chaos of wedding weekend.

Our patio happened to overlap with Pride parade crowds, but it was barely noticeable. Cart service dim sum is such a rare treat these days — it made the whole meal feel like an event, not just a meal.

Below Bay Area average dim sum. The items we tried are good and service is also good but 1 they don’t have a lot of the common dim sums that we wanted and 2 super expensive (>50 per person pre tip and we are not even full…) Also difficult to find parking

Yank sing has authentic and tasty dim sum while also being clean with a nice ambience.

The pork spare ribs and har gow were good.

I love the chilli oil which is mildly sweet, not spicy and has a lot of soybeans.

The fried curried shrimp wontons were light and crispy and not too oily.

The xiao long bao was a little different from the ones at other places. The broth had some additional aromats but I couldn't say which.

Service is efficient and a little brusque for the fine dining prices.

The food is good but for what you get prices are steep. Dumpling home/story is still my go-to.

It’s a clean and tasty restaurant for dim sum, though not everything was deeply impressive. The portions felt a bit small for the price, and a few of the female staff members came across a little brusque.

Considering how expensive it is compared to other dim sum places, I rated it by fine-dining standards. It’s definitely an upscale restaurant, but it doesn’t quite reach the level of the very top establishments.

As far as I know, it was only once mentioned by Michelin back in 2016.

top_reviews.content: The presentation was beautiful, the portions were generous, and the seafood tasted incredibly fresh. This place deserves so much hype. The flavors were rich but balanced, and everything paired together perfectly. Honestly, this dinner made me so happy.

Tasty and good portion. Servers are really friendly, checked in on us multiple times. Tiger wood roll is surprisingly spicy (has a good kick in a good way.) Children plate has chicken teriyaki, tempura, gyoza, rice and miso soup for ~$15.

Came here for happy hour as this is one of the only restaurants open in the area after 10 PM

Got the Katsu chicken plate and edamame and it came with a side of miso soup

The edamame was fine, but they could’ve steamed it a little bit longer

Katsu chicken was a little heavy on the breading and one piece of it was slightly undercooked, but overall decent

I pointed this out to the server who came to check in on me. He said since I ate, most of it, he couldn’t get me another order or cancel it from my tab. I said I don’t want him to do either, just would like the kitchen to know. I paid with cash, tipped and left.

Next thing I know the server is coming out with a bag chasing after me: the manager was upset that I didn’t have the best experience and sent some edamame for me to take home. It was awfully kind of them to do so, and I did not ask for this.

Will come back to try some of their rolls

It was a very nice experience overall

I love the food here, been coming here since high school and the quality is still at top tier. You can’t beat Kansai for good sushi. Shoutout to my waitress, super friendly and funny. Will definitely coming back.

Came for happy hour right after 9pm, it wasn't too busy and we were sat down right away. Server came with our water and we asked for straws and our server looked at us like we just spoke gibberish. When we were ready to order, the server said they couldnt take our order because they were training. But the order was all marked on the happy hour menu. We waited for someone else to take our order and noticed others who came in after had their orders taken before us.

When a server finally came to take our order, they informed us one of the happy hour  items we wanted, the deep fried hamachi roll, was no longer being offered. Okay, weird because its still on the regular menu, but no big deal. We ordered shrimp tempura, meat gyoza, lion king roll, and Bob roll from the happy hour menu and the Newport roll, which we've had numerous times, from the regular menu.

We received our appetizers and it was tasty.

However our baked rolls took longer than usual to come, we know to expect baked rolls to take 15-20 mins, but after more than 20 mins we were growing impatient. When the server, the same one who gave us our water, came out with a platter of orders, he passed us to serve a table that came in after us a placed their order after us. Then he came to our table and placed one roll down, started to leave our table, before realizing the rest of his items were for us, he came back and placed the rest of order down. He gestured to our items to explain which roll was which, nearly touching the rolls with his hand, he slipped up and called the lion king roll a tiger roll.

The rolls were clearly over baked. They were very crispy, stuck to the aluminum, and tasted a little burnt.

Although they were overbaked, the Newport roll, which is baked salmon in the middle, was partially raw, some of the scallops ontop were falling off, not covered in sauce, and lukewarm.

The lion king roll, which contains avocado, had bad pieces of avocado in it.

We didn't want to wait for a new order for the Newport roll. We asked the server for the check and a box. He brought our check right away, the hostess brought our box. We paid, and it was collected right away. He processed it and brought it back with great urgency.

We were so disappointed, the slow service when we arrived and the rush to close out our check made us feel unwelcome.

top_reviews.content: 5 🌟 Rating from my experience. Its so amazing to find a Pure Vegetarian Restaurant in the Heart of "San Francisco". The taste of Food is just Amazing, Price is affordable and quantity is good. Everything we ordered tasted nice and staff are very helpful. Who ever the owners are just wanted to say keep up good work and thanks for operating a Pure Vegetarian restaurant which is hard to find in other cities around US.

I was recently in San Francisco for the Snowflake Summit 2026 and ended up eating breakfast at Udupi Palace three times during my trip. Everything about this place—the food, the environment, and the reasonable prices—is absolutely superb.
I tried a variety of their tiffin items over my visits, including the Tiffin Thali, idli, puri, and pongal. Everything was incredibly delicious and fresh, but my absolute favorite was the pongal paired with their sambar—it is a must-try!
If you are looking for authentic South Indian comfort food in SF, this is the spot. I’ll definitely be back the next time I'm in town. Highly recommended!

I was visiting San Francisco from Boston and discovered a hidden gem near my daughter's apartment. This South Indian restaurant serves authentic, mouthwatering food. The rava dosa was perfectly crisp, the idli was soft and fresh, and every dish was full of authentic flavor. The cozy ambiance makes it a wonderful spot for a satisfying meal.
Our waiter was incredibly friendly and helpful. There were three of us, and we ordered four dishes based on his recommendation because the portions are very generous. He was absolutely right! We each enjoyed our own dish and shared one, leaving pleasantly full without overordering.
The food arrived quickly, which made the experience even better. Between the authentic flavors, generous portions, attentive service, and prompt delivery, this restaurant exceeded our expectations. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for outstanding South Indian cuisine in San Francisco. We will definitely be back the next time we visit!

Recently a friend and I had made lunch plans for the end of the year (we work together and we don't usually see each other again for months). She recommended Udupi Palace and I'm so glad she did- I've had Indian food before when I lived in LA but not since I moved back to the Bay. I'm pescatarian so a veggie friendly menu that is also budget friendly. WIN WIN!

We ended up inviting other colleagues and we were a group of 14 in total on a Monday afternoon. We called ahead of time to make sure they could accommodate us and it was no issue at all.

The ambience gives very casual and cozy.

The service was 10/10- Jacob was our server and although I didn't ask I almost felt like he could have been the manager or owner. He gave us full attention, made sure our water glasses were full and when I say as soon as we all ordered- the food was coming out piping hot and fresh! I was impressed.

Location: It's located in the Mission off Valencia- a short 10 minute walk from the BART station (24th/Mission). Lots of culture all around.

I took pics of everyone's food including mine:
Some our selections were the paper dosas (which is like a thin like crepe fried up)- they were huge in size...well very long. See the pics
A number of people ordered different types of dosa combos, we had veggie byrani and I had the lentil/veggie soup which was perfect on a chilly day.  One of the dosas came stuffed with potatoes and another combo had some sort of salsa on top and came with a mini fried donut of sorts. Great variety of options to choose from.

I would highly recommend checking this place out for great hospitality, good warm food served with care and a price menu that won't break the bank.

I see they have a location in DT Berkeley as well.

One other thing to mention- online it does mention if you are part of a large group (over 6 or 8)- they automatically charge gratuity. However, when our receipt came- that was not the case. We assumed it was added in and realized quickly it was not automatic so just check your receipt.

ENJOY!

We ordered thali
It was delicious with over seven different types of curries like chole, avial, bhindi with buttermilk,poriyal, kootu, curd, sweet, sambar, dal and with choice of roti/poori with rice
The owner Jacob was very welcoming and the food was served pretty quickly
Definitely a must visit place for anyone who loves South Indian cuisine. There are a number of options for dosa too!

top_reviews.content:
Shan Dong is definitely worth a visit if you’re looking for delicious Chinese food in Oakland. The food is flavorful, fresh, and packed with taste across the dishes we ordered. Service was quick and efficient, and despite the restaurant being busy, we didn’t have to wait long to be seated as a party of two.

The portions are very generous, so it’s easy to have leftovers or share a few dishes. Considering the quality, quantity, and overall experience, it offers excellent value for the money. And whatever you order, make sure you request the handmade noodles—they’re absolutely worth it and really elevate the meal.

I’d happily come back the next time I’m craving great Chinese food.

Came on a Sunday around 5:30 and waited around 40 minutes to get seated.

Loved the string beans- great flavor with a mix of chili oil and garlic, couldn’t stop eating it cause it was so addicting! I ordered the pork chow mein with the hand pulled noodles - HUGE portion (I had leftover that lasted me 2 meals) and the noodles are super thick and chewy which I love, no other place do their noodles like this place!

Note to self: make sure to mix the noodles before eating since the sauce is accumulated in the bottom to actually get the flavor!

A very delicious place in Oakland’s Chinatown. I had their shandong chicken, dry fried green beans, salt and pepper pork and chicken and they were all excellent. The shandong chicken is your typical orange chicken, but they did something to the sauce that gives it this dark toasted caramel taste to it. top_reviews.content:
Hongkong Claypot Restaurant @960 Grant Ave, San Francisco, CA 94108

The entrance is up a small staircase. The men's restroom is on the left, while the restaurant entrance is on the right, where the women's restroom is also located.
We were seated immediately upon arrival and served a free hot tea.
We ordered the fried wontons, orange chicken, pork BBQ fried rice, and the seafood claypot with mushrooms and tofu. The fried wontons were not too salty—just right for my taste. The orange chicken, pork BBQ fried rice, and seafood claypot were all incredible, flavorful, and also not overly salty. Everything was well-seasoned and delicious. The service was very fast, and the prices were reasonable.
There was only one server, but she was incredibly efficient and managed everything on her own without any delays.
The clientele was a mix of locals and tourists, as well as both younger and older diners, which created a welcoming atmosphere.
The restaurant has about 12 tables. There are five or six round tables that can comfortably seat seven or more people, while the remaining square tables are suitable for groups of two to four.
My partner said she would definitely come back, and I would recommend this restaurant as well.

When we ventured to Chinatown, decided to stop here for dinner. We were really surprised with quality of food. Chicken tofu clay pot and beef and broccoli was amazing. Staff was great and service was really quick. We ended up eating too much food.

Walked in with my wife off the street on Mother’s Day Sunday and she wanted sweet and sour chicken I wanted a beef dish .   No problems getting a window seat for 2.  75% full, great welcoming service and staff throughout our visit.  We chose banquet B which met both our tastes and swapped out wonton soup with chicken and sweet corn soup.   Very tasty and filling at reasonable price.  Couldn’t finish everything.   Will definitely recommend.

Amazing hole in the wall. Smaller portions at cheaper prices so you can try more stuff. Hard to find - go upstairs to second floor, door on the right. Plenty of indoor seating. Chicken clay pot, green beans, west lake beef soup were delicious! Perfect for two, we finished the whole thing.

Got the two person deluxe special and it was amazing. Everything they brought out was better than the last.
I keep thinking about the sweet and sour chicken, wonton soup, and Mongolian beef.
Will definitely go again next time we’re in town.

top_reviews.content: Very good food and atmosphere. The street it was located on had tons of little shops to go around, and was located right off the ocean. I got the fish tacos, but the burgers looked great as well! I would definitely come back, the service was polite and worked at a timely manner. I recommend this place to anyone in the area!

Centrally located on the main Road in Sausalito so the location is definitely good.
Pricing throughout the area is a bit inflated, in my opinion, for what you get regardless of location, so I don't totally hold that against this particular establishment.
We were a party of eight.
Many people ordered the burgers which did not come with fries for $24 I thought that was a bit pricey.
I had the fish tacos which were $26.. also did not come with anything, a few small lettuce pieces on the side that you could probably make a salad out of, but not really.
We also ordered two orders of guacamole with chips and two orders of onion rings for the table I don't recall with the total bill was but sides were definitely necessary.

Hamburgers were delicious,  good beer 🍺 and good service.  My kids and I enjoyed our time eating there.  We got a table very quickly even that we didn't have reservations.  Parking could be busy in Sausalito.
We had a great experience at Restaurant. The food was delicious especially burgers, the atmosphere was warm and welcoming, and the service was exceptional from start to finish.

Hecka good burgers here. I had the whiskey bacon burger and it was hecka yummy and cooked to perfection. The salad included was good. French fries good and our server was extremely polite and helpful. I will come back. Thank you

name: Roma Antica
address: 3242 Scott St, San Francisco, CA 94123, United States

google.name: Roma Antica
google.address: 3242 Scott St, San Francisco, CA 94123, United States
google.description: Welcoming neighborhood spot serving modern Italian eats & wine in petite digs with marble accents.

top_reviews.content:
We had an absolutely terrific lunch experience thanks to David. From the moment we sat down, the service was thoughtful, attentive, and genuinely welcoming.

We ordered a pasta dish to share, and David kindly portioned it for us without even being asked. He also brought out a little extra for the table, which perfectly captured the spirit of great hospitality—undersell and overdeliver. Small gestures like that make a big difference.

The food itself was outstanding. Fresh, beautifully prepared, and clearly made with care. The atmosphere was romantic and relaxed, making it a perfect setting for a long lunch.

Service like this is rare. David struck the perfect balance between professionalism and warmth, and he elevated the entire experience.

If I could give six stars out of five, I would. Highly recommended.

I genuinely don't understand how this restaurant has such a high rating. The entire experience was disappointing from start to finish.

The food was mediocre at best. For an Italian restaurant, the dishes lacked flavor and didn't feel worth the price.The pasta did not taste fresh, and the Grandma's Gnocchi was absolutely drowned in cheese, making the dish feel heavy and one-dimensional. Even something as simple as asking about the different sauces for the Grandma's Gnocchi seemed to annoy our waiter, who acted inconvenienced by basic questions about the menu.

On a chilly evening, my friend asked for a blanket, and instead of politely helping, a staff member practically slapped it onto their back and walked away. It came across as rude and dismissive.

To make matters worse, servers were openly yelling at each other throughout the restaurant, creating an uncomfortable and unprofessional atmosphere. Between the poor service, lackluster food, and chaotic environment, it was hard to enjoy the evening.

Overall, this was one of the most disappointing dining experiences I've had in a long time. With so many better options available, I'd recommend taking your business elsewhere.

Food was good, but the the best. Solid 7/10 for the oxtail pasta and 6/10 for the lasagna. We tried this place for the second time because they have lasagna on the menu and their sister restaurant na’pizza has the best pizza! Not sure we will be back here for these dishes, but the service was good and the vibe too!

Our first time here and we'll definitely be back! We loved the amatriciana and carbonara! Delicious, excellent service, lovely ambiance (we sat outside).

Simone - our server from Rome - was amazing!! I had some dietary restrictions and he made sure that everything was good for me to eat. He made our dining experience A+ 💯!

Absolutely phenomenal! Everything was on point. The service was excellent our waiter was charming, friendly and helpful. The food was wonderful.  I ordered pizza and others ordered lasagna. They ate it quickly so no pictures of the lasagna. We dined outside under the heaters. It was relaxing and pleasant. Definitely will be back.

top_reviews.content:
Wow—the ambiance, food, and service were incredible. I brought my friend here to celebrate her birthday, and the entire experience made her feel so special. Our server surprised her with a mini birthday cake and candle, which was such a thoughtful touch.

Everything we ordered was cooked perfectly, and the service was attentive without being intrusive. I’ll definitely be back and highly recommend it for special occasions, date nights, or simply when you want a delicious meal. A truly memorable experience.

The staff were quick and genuinely kind from the moment we walked in. A reservation will be probably needed.

The place stays busy, so service isn’t hovering-over-your-table attentive, but everything ran smoothly and we never felt neglected.

The atmosphere is lovely and modern.

The food itself is good. Not the best in the world but with some unique flavor combinations you don’t run into everywhere.

A great spot overall and one we’d happily return to.

Tried Lolinda out as a group of 6!

We had reservations, and were led upstairs and pretty quiet for the most part which was nice. (As we left for the night, it was pretty packed downstairs and a lot louder).

We ordered quite a bit of food!
-tartar de carne $15
-ceviche mixto $17
-pan de queso $10
-pulpo (octopus) $23
-milanesa napolitana (chicken thigh) $31
-seco de costilla (short rib) $38
-yuca fries $10
-gaucho (bone-in ribeye) $85
-hueso asado (bone marrow) $18

For dessert, we ordered:
-chocotorta (chocolate cake)
-churros

All desserts $11.

Overall, flavors were good. Plates are definitely tapas, so on the smaller side.

Street parking if you're lucky. Otherwise, we parked in the garage about a block down.

Went to Lolinda in SF and it’s hands down the best steakhouse I’ve been to. Ordered the ribeye and a dessert & both were amazing. The ribeye was cooked perfectly it was super tender and full of flavor. The atmosphere was really nice too, great vibe without feeling too fancy or over the top. Definitely worth it.
Really enjoyed this place. It has a lively atmosphere, the staff were nice. The steak was tasty, though I wish it had been a bit more tender. The chicken and veggie skewers were my favorite.

reviews_snippets.content: "The food is good if this is only thing people choose a restaurant to eat."
