top_reviews.content: I would give a much higher rating but I came here to see spacemoth and La Luz and the sound was terrible. The band was visibly pained by it. I had earplugs in and it was still so intense! The bass was so loud it was distorting. And this happened for both bands, so it wasn’t just the musicians’ setup. I have seen other reviews on here complaining about this. I’m not sure what needs to happen to fix this, but if the sound were better I would give five stars. spacemoth forever!!!

This was my first time at this music venue and gastropub. We were only there for the show. The interior was nice and new, though a bit bland. The menu seemed ordinary and I'm not into craft beer. I wasn't familiar with the facilities layout, but I later found that you enter the venue by going to the back of the restaurant and turning left. We only had drinks at the bar inside the venue. It was quickly served. The venue itself is a typical "black box" venue. Just the right size for standing GA shows of smaller bands and legacy acts. We didn't check out the balcony. The biggest negative was the concert started 1.5 hours (show at 8, but started at 9:30) after the scheduled time. The DJ who played during the wait time was okay, but still would have preferred to start on time.

My wife and I brought our son to see Wax, Jarv, and J Lately. We had never been to Cornerstone before so we came early and ate dinner and had a couple beers pre show. I got the Chicken Pot Pie and my wife got the BLT Salad. My son got the grilled cheese and fries. Beer was great, food was great, and Michele the hostess, waitress, runner, security person, was there to take care of us the entire night from beginning to end. She went above and beyond the call of duty for us. We felt genuinely cared for. We will be back for sure. Thank you!

It's a large venue with full bar and restaurant with many screens and projectors around. Great for sport watching, groups, casual hangouts and meetups.
There are big runs for private parties with screen in the back.
Not kids friendly on busy game days but could still be nice on regular days!
Service is great with many responsive attentive staff.
Foods are pretty good American style. I'd recommend burger, fries, sausage, tri-tips sandwich, pulled pork, etc pretty much everything is good after couple pitcher of good beer 🍻😀

First let me just say. This spot has it all. Great food. Awesome bar and socializing locations. Outdoor fire pits, indoor tables, counters, couches. And the music venue location is awesome 😎 And the staff here, is super cool. 🤘🏻😮‍💨💨

top_reviews.content: We had a year-end celebration at this newly remodeled, spacious restaurant on a bustling street in northern Alameda. The dim sum dishes and Chinese food were delicious, with generous portions. We like the salty pepper crab 🦀 and various dim sum dishes. The chrysanthemum tea was very refreshing with a flowery flavor. The staff were friendly and helpful. We shall come again.

Our first time making a reservation at East Ocean for Christmas dinner. When we arrived, there was a large walk-in crowd already waiting to be seated. The dining room is extremely spacious, nicely decorated and lit. The atmosphere was very inviting and festive which was a good start to our family holiday.

We had to wait to get our multiple dishes for our larger table but there is a reason why this restaurant is packed. Our cocktails were very yummy and nicely garnished. Every plate, both veggie and protein-based, was super delicious. We had the black mushroom and sea cucumber clay pot and it was perfectly cooked. The mu shu pork was fantastic and so was the tofu ma po. The few dim sum we ordered were gone just as soon as they hit the table. Mango pudding made with real mango and the kids loved it!

Every dish served family-style to share as the fun wheel spins around the table. It is always very exciting to have so many people to hang out with while celebrating Christmas and sharing such a nice celebration together. The service was attentive but you could tell that they were a little understaffed. We heard from the bartender that they had a few people under the weather that night. However, the servers went above and beyond, running up and down trying to cover everyone’s demand, and making a real effort that night. Kudos to those kind people who work to serve others on special holidays vs. taking the day off to enjoy at home! Thank you for a wonderful family meal, East Ocean, we will be back for more!!

Loved the service and atmosphere. Within minutes of being seated, we were already ordering plenty of food from the carts. One standout was a black shrimp dumpling that was fried — unique and my favorite of the dishes. We also enjoyed the Chinese donuts (sa young bao) and the black sesame jelly rolls. Everything came out fresh and flavorful. Would definitely come back!

We came here for the first time and overall had a great experience. Some dim sum dishes were delicious, others were just okay, but the variety is huge and definitely worth exploring. The food was fresh, the flavors were good, and I’d happily come back to try more.

Dim sum is apart of our Bay area heritage. San Francisco has the oldest chinese-american community in the country but the East Bay has always had great dim sum options.

It's exciting to see the new generation of dim sum and Chinese restaurants blossoming in Alameda as folks move away from Oakland Chinatown to nearby areas. The shumai was absolutely perfect. Giant (twice the normal size) dumplings perhaps inspired by take away counter bakeries (usually cheep with think wrappers a style that evolved to satisfy dinners on the go) with the refinement of smaller more traditional versions from great tea houses like Peony and etc

Traditional foods change slowly in order to hold on to and honor tradition. East Ocean does it their way but anyone familiar with good dim sum will agree - don't miss out on eating at East Ocean if you love dim sum!

top_reviews.content: The chicken ALWAYS hits 🌶💥 The sandwich is huge, the slaw has the right consistency and balance, added with the pickle bites on a soft roll? The sauce is really an extra benefit but crazy good nonetheless! I can't wait to try the etoufee and the b&g!

Beware the hotness scale. Medium and below is what I would go with.

I was hyped for hotboys. The fried chicken sandwich was tasty but with the price point and the seating on the road you are better off going to super duper.

The crinkle cut fries were ok. The chicken tenders were juicy but not out of this world.

The coleslaw in the sandwich was good and the pickles work well to cut the spice. The bun could have been better as well as toasted.

All in all I will probably return for a fried chicken craving.

Good food and great customer service. Outdoor seating only and one gender neutral bathroom available for patrons. Their chicken sandwich is good but I really like the loaded fries. They do NOT play with their spice levels. Take it easy if you can’t handle it. Have some milk on standby if you decide to challenge your palette. Enjoy!

This shop just screams Oakland, y’all. Between the mural, the colors, and the volume of people waiting for their orders, you know you’re somewhere good food is made. Order at the window and wait your turn. It may take around 20 minutes as they are popular and they take their time making those good eats.

The “sando” is offered with dark meat while the “chicken tender sandwich” is white meat, which is what I prefer so that’s what I’ve tried. They offer seven different spice rankings and recommend Medium + for folks who like it spicy. That’s what I chose, along with a delicious watermelon aqua fresca.

I do like heat, but I think the Medium + is a good call as an upper limit—I was crying, and that’s rare for me. Crying in a good way, of course! But there were moments when I thought I may have aimed too high . . . what I’m saying is I’m glad I resisted the Hot.

Serving coleslaw on the sandwich is key, as its creaminess has a tempering effect on the spice. The pickles add flavor, but I do think there may be too much “money sauce” squirted on top. I did appreciate the sauce’s creamy assistance in battling the spice, however! The sauce tasted like a chipotle and 1000 Island blend. The pickles were good, but the bun bread was just okay for me.

That chicken meat is tender and plentiful, which is sometimes a feat for white meat and definitely a plus.

Fresh hot chicken, straight from the oil, which keeps it very moist. They use the thigh (tender is also available and is cheaper) for their signature sando. The fries are nothing special, but you do get a generous serving of curly fries with some spice dusting, and they provide plenty of their signature sauce on the side. Outdoor seating only, which makes it dog friendly, but difficult on rainy days and/or nighttime in this sketchy neighborhood (our car got broken into only a few blocks away). The loud music playing right in your ears doesn't help. Overall, good place for a quick bite, especially when when in a rush, but nothing more.

top_reviews.content: Spruce is Michelin-Star-worthy. Absolutely fantastic in every way. My server Michael T was so kind, knowledgeable, attentive as were the other staff. The Alaska gin/yellow chartreuse/orange bitters cocktail was unique and flavorful, and I received excellent advice on choice of wines (was even allowed two half glasses of two wines with the duck since I couldn't decide after tastings!). I had the agnolotti primavera, duck two ways, and pastel de maiz if I recall correctly; on the dessert. Everything was perfectly cooked, flavorful, seasoned well, delectable. Corn infused sauce with the dessert was incredibly unique, sweet, creamy, and so tasty. Amuse Bouche, Parker rolls, chocolate tray all amazing and server kindly offered me small caviar tastes since I had mentioned interest but was worried I would get too full. Beautiful ambiance. I just had a wonderful meal and time there. Thank you Spruce team!

Looking back at my photos from a weekend brunch here in May of 2021, it stands as a really memorable snapshot of San Francisco's hybrid dining era. This visit was back when Spruce was still holding its Michelin star, and the kitchen's technical execution completely reflected that status. We sat out on the sidewalk parklet space due to the restrictions at the time—and while the temporary outdoor street setup was just okay compared to their famous, moody indoor dining room, I deeply appreciated the fact that they were able to pivot and let us dine safely.

Every single course tasted absolutely great. We started with a pastry basket of house-baked scones and muffins paired with a rich raspberry jam and sea-salted whipped butter, which set a fantastic baseline. Next was a vibrant spring pea velouté soup, which had an incredible texture and a beautiful layering of crisp radishes and croutons. For the main, the Maine Lobster Benedict served over thick, house-made English muffins with an airy hollandaise and soft quail egg yolk was a total knockout. We finished with two desserts: a remarkably precise chocolate opera cake with hazelnut crumble and dark ganache, alongside a light strawberry panna cotta ringed with white chocolate and macerated fruit. Given the sheer quality of the ingredients, the execution of the seafood, and the generous pacing of the menu, it felt like an incredibly good value at the time. A really excellent experience from start to finish.

Spruce embodies the elegance and precision of a true gourmet kitchen, making it a wonderful choice for an intimate and refined dinner.

The wine selection is impressive, and the three course menu is thoughtfully designed, allowing guests to choose their main course and dessert for a balanced dining experience. Everything arrived perfectly timed and at the ideal temperature.

The service was nice, attentive, and very professional. I especially appreciated the thoughtful recommendations and the patience in explaining the menu.

Definitely a place worth returning to.

#refinedexploring YouTube
We had great service and vibe. However, food is not impressive, at least for the three-course dinner that the three of us tried. The appetizers had some salty or fruity flavors, but not something that made us feel excited. Main entrees we chose were dry-aged duck and spare rib that was dry and frankly horrible- not to mention a $25 up charge!

We came here for the Valentine’s Day menu and overall had a lovely experience.

The cheese course was absolutely the highlight for me. It featured three different cheeses, each with an incredibly bold and intense flavor profile. It was powerful, complex, and honestly very impressive. Definitely the most memorable dish of the night.

The filet mignon was excellent — perfectly cooked and very tender. The king salmon and the Maine lobster were both very solid. Fresh, well-balanced, and thoughtfully prepared.

The chicken dish, however, felt a bit ordinary compared to the rest of the menu.

Overall, a well-executed and enjoyable meal with a few standout moments.

The staff was very friendly and nice. I like that they roll out the pasta in front of you when you enter. It gets me excited to eat Italian food!

The carbonara was excellent. It was creamy and cheesy, but not too heavy and the pesto was pretty good. It was fresh, but it’s a little more seasoning or flavor.

Nice Italian homemade pasta.
The pasta was excellent, So delicious!!! and many choices of sauces.
The staff were very friendly.

Came here with my partner Thursday. Place was pretty packed but was able to order and get the food quick.
Got the pesto and bolognese with cream (I think it’s called Pastiata?) with Lasagna to share.
Honestly lasagna was huge and we couldn’t finish but more to take home!
Everything was fresh and delicious. I really liked the pesto.

You order up ahead, but servers checked in on me and was super friendly.

Definitely will come back again and we found a new favorite spot!

The food was excellent, and the quality really stood out. Everything was fresh, flavorful, and the portions were generous, making it great value for money. The service was decent, although it’s more of a self-ordering concept, so there isn’t much table service. However, the outstanding food more than made up for that. We’d definitely come back and recommend this place to others.

If you’re looking for authentic Italian food that truly stands out, look no further than The Italian Homemade Company. From the moment we sat down, we knew we were in for something special.

The lasagna is on another level — rich, comforting, and packed with flavor in every single bite. We also tried the pesto and the pesto ravioli, and honestly, they were absolutely delicious. Every dish felt handmade with care, just like the name promises.

We paired our meal with a drink from April Street, and it was fantastic, along with the beer, which was incredibly tasty as well — the perfect complement to such a flavorful meal.

But what truly elevated the entire experience was our server, Enrique. His attentiveness and genuine hospitality made all the difference. He was incredibly helpful and turned a great meal into an unforgettable one.

top_reviews.content: We came here around 7:30pm on a Sunday in December, and sat outside under the headlamps on the covered sidewalk. I was warm enough o remove my jacket. We were waited on promptly, and opted for the absolutely amazing French onion soup--- this is a must. And I mention it first because it was our favorite. We both ordered the $20 burgers, a steal of a deal; it will fill you up! She got the salmon burger with side salad (which was huge), and I got the beef burger with the $3 cheese add on and fries. Both can on ciabatta rolls. I like that the burger came with a side of greens and caramelized onions to put on it if you like. I asked for a side of mustard, and that was tasty on the burger. The aioli is strong on the garlic, so if you enjoy that taste you'll love a side of that to dip your fries in. All in all an enjoyable dinner. Not my favorite burger but pretty darn good! Love the small crispy fries. Ambiance is cozy.
Love this cozy urban nook on the hill. It feels miles away from The Fray of San Francisco almost like a little village the food is deelish. I've never had less than attentive patient service. Yumm

Was recommended this place but it was very disappointing. First, the bread was chewy and stale and the server dropped the bread in the floor. Then came the french onion soup which was average at best. For mains, we ordered the salmon crepe, which was horrible: the crepe dough was very dry, tasted weird and there was more arugula than anything else, which just dominated the overall taste. For reference, there was more arugula inside than smoked salmon, and it was very wet, THEN there was a pile of it on top of the crepe. The only thing that was decent was the mac and cheese, and that should tell you a lot given that this was a french restaurant. Will not be back, and will not recommend to any of my friends.

Quaint little French spot that’s a must-stop when I’m in the area! The service and food are both top-notch. There is plenty of street parking around, which makes it very accessible and easy to get to. Highly recommend!

Be prepared for a wait—there’s often a long line, but it’s absolutely worth it. The food was fantastic overall. The escargot is a must-try: rich, garlicky, and perfectly cooked. The sole was incredibly tender and flavorful—definitely a highlight. The French onion soup, while comforting, was a bit too salty for my taste. I also tried the crepe, which had a great texture and was well-executed, though slightly salty as well. Despite that, everything was delicious and full of character. Would return!

Regional Review: Farmhouse Kitchen Thai

A midday stop brought my tracking to Jack London Square for a busy lunch session. The front-of-house execution was seamless; the hostess politely greeted us and offered an immediate choice between the interior or the deck. We chose the outdoor patio and secured an excellent table with a direct, unobstructed view of the waterfront. The patio layout is exceptionally pleasant and well-shaded, and they stage the tables with beautiful plates that are perfect for sharing. While we opted for the fresh air, the interior design—featuring a polished counter and well-spaced table seating—also looked highly refined and inviting.

Service pacing was sharp. The staff handled multiple table check-ins, kept waters continuously replenished, and deployed our dishes remarkably fast. It is a fantastic, high-energy atmosphere all around.

Hat Yai Fried Chicken: A definitive winner on the table. The execution on the chicken was flawless, achieving an incredibly crisp crunch while retaining a perfectly juicy interior. It pairs beautifully with the striking blue rice. The curry was delicious and well-balanced, and the accompanying roti was honestly some of the best I have ever evaluated—immensely flaky and perfectly cooked.

Pork Pad Thai: This classic baseline dish was excellent. We swapped in pork as our primary protein, and the flavor balance was spot-on. It delivered great traditional depth without veering into the common pitfall of being overly sweet.

Cocktail Flight: The aesthetic presentation on this flight of four different drinks was visually striking and well-crafted. Overall, the drinks did the job, but the flavor profiles on the palate were a bit of a mixed bag; one of the specific variants had a heavy, medicinal finish that honestly reminded me of mouthwash. Next time around, a crisp beer would likely be the better pairing.

Sharp service, rapid execution, and a fantastic view. The kitchen proves it can back up its vibrant, high-end aesthetic with genuine technical proficiency. While the food, service, and atmosphere were all undeniable 5-star caliber, the mixed note on the cocktail flight slightly tempers the overall score. I would absolutely return to explore more of the menu, and for that exceptional chicken and roti alone.

This was one of the most confusing and disappointing dining experiences I’ve had in San Francisco.

After waiting in line to order, no one explained how the restaurant worked. It’s apparently a sit-down restaurant where you order and pay up front, but nobody greeted us, walked us through the process, or offered to seat us. After paying, we were left to fend for ourselves—finding a table, getting our own water, utensils, and napkins. For first-time customers, the lack of basic hospitality was surprising.

The food didn’t justify the price either. The Dutch pancake was nearly $20 and arrived with the top noticeably burnt. It was edible, but far from something I’d order again.

The billing was the final disappointment. Before we had even sat down or received any food, the payment screen asked for a tip. Then the receipt included two separate 5% surcharges, both specifically stating they were not tips. So you’re asked to tip before receiving any service, charged additional fees that aren’t tips, and then receive essentially no service. Someone dropped off our food, and that was the extent of our interaction.

I don’t mind paying premium prices for a great experience, but this felt like a self-service café masquerading as a full-service restaurant. Between the confusing ordering process, lack of service, burnt food, and junk fees, I left wondering what exactly I was paying for.

top_reviews.content:
Dumpling Home definitely lived up to the hype. I came on a Tuesday evening with no reservation and was seated quickly. The outdoor seating was a nice bonus and made for a great dining experience in San Francisco's cool weather.

The highlight of the meal was the Numb & Spicy Pork Xiao Long Bao. The soup dumplings were fresh, juicy, packed with flavorful broth, and absolutely delicious. They also serve complimentary hot jasmine tea, which pairs really well with the meal, and the Thai iced tea was creamy and refreshing.

The Beef Brisket Noodle Soup was flavorful with tender beef and handmade noodles, although the broth was a little oilier than I personally prefer.

A tip for first-time visitors: don't skip the black vinegar and fresh ginger that come with the soup dumplings. Dip each dumpling lightly, bite a small hole first to sip the hot broth, then enjoy the rest. It really elevates the experience.

Overall, excellent food, friendly service, easy seating, and I'd definitely come back. Highly recommended if you're looking for authentic handmade dumplings in San Francisco.

overall a decent spot for Chinese dumplings. The soup dumplings were good, but if you’re used to really good Asian/Chinese food, I’d say most of the dishes were fairly average rather than exceptional.

The pan-fried dumplings, though, were amazing, easily the standout of the meal and something I’d absolutely come back for. Service was great as well. The restaurant itself is pretty casual and nothing particularly special atmosphere-wise, but you’re really here for the dumplings.

Overall, a solid meal and worth trying, especially for the pan-fried dumplings.

These are, without exaggeration, some of the best soup dumplings I've had in recent memory. Dumpling Home, tucked into a corner spot on Gough St in San Francisco's Hayes Valley, earns every bit of the hype  and the Michelin Bib Gourmand it's been awarded for good reason.

Every single thing I tried was packed with flavor. There's nothing phoned-in on this menu. The xiao long bao are the standout: thin, supple skins that hold together just long enough to deliver a spoonful of intensely flavorful broth the second you bite in. Chefs are wrapping and folding everything by hand all day, and you can taste the difference. These aren't your standard one-note pork dumplings either; they go beyond with chicken, beef, and a Sichuan-inspired numbing pork that's become a personal favorite.

This is a walk-in-only spot, so yes, there will likely be a wait, but don't let that stop you. It's worth every minute. Grab a table, order generously, and prepare to leave full and thoroughly impressed.

If you're anywhere near Hayes Valley and you haven't been, fix that immediately. Go here.

Had the Fresh cucumber with garlic sauce (just wanted to eat the whole plate, couldn’t stop eating them), pan fried dumplings (crispy on the bottom and steamed on top; different crunch profile with good flavor), soup dumplings were very good, had nice big red spoon to eat the dumplings, they a soy sauce, ginger, vinegar dipping sauce. Overall, it was amazingly good. We were able to come and had no wait for a party of 4.

Be sure to ask for the chili oil as it adds an extra zing. We ordered the numb and spicy pork xiao long bao, steamed chicken and mushroom dumplings, and the friend beef bao. The broth in the xiao long bao had the perfect tingle without being overwhelmingly spicy. The steamed dumplings we the most plain but paired well with the chili oil. The pan friend bao were piping hot and packed full of flavour. Everything was so fresh and flavourful. Worth waiting in the line

top_reviews.content: I’d been waiting to check out Thanh long for years and it didn’t disappoint. The Roast and garlic noodles were amazing!! The crab was very fresh and perfect for two people. It came out to $100 per person but both my friend and I walked out stuffed. I don’t say this a lot but it’s definitely worth the wait.

​A San Francisco Legend: The Ultimate Roast Crab & Garlic Noodle Experience 🦀✨
​If you are looking for an iconic dining experience in the Outer Sunset, Thanh Long remains the gold standard. This isn't just a meal; it’s a culinary pilgrimage for anyone who appreciates the perfect fusion of Vietnamese flavors and fresh California seafood.
​The Highlights:
​The World-Famous Roast Crab: The Dungeness crab is the undisputed star. It arrived perfectly cooked—meaty, sweet, and drenched in that legendary secret garlic sauce. The rich, savory aroma hits you the moment it reaches the table.
​Signature Garlic Noodles: You cannot visit Thanh Long without ordering these. The noodles are chewy, buttery, and packed with deep garlic umami. They are the perfect companion to the crab, soaking up every bit of the flavorful juices.
​Shaking Beef (Bo Luc Lac): The beef was incredibly tender, seared to perfection with just the right amount of char, and served over a crisp, refreshing salad.
​Appetizers: The Mussels served on toasted baguette slices were a highlight—the broth was fragrant and vibrant. The Fried Calamari was also impressive: light, crispy, and seasoned beautifully without being greasy.
​Atmosphere & Service:
​The ambiance is warm and upscale yet remains inviting and unpretentious. Despite the restaurant being busy, the service was attentive and professional. The staff knows the menu inside out and ensures the pacing of the meal is spot on.
​Verdict:
​Thanh Long continues to prove why it has been a San Francisco staple for decades. While it is a premium dining experience, the quality of the ingredients and the consistency of the flavors make it worth every penny.
​Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
Pro Tip: This place is popular for a reason—be sure to make a reservation in advance, especially on weekends!

Overall food is good but expect to pay a lot.

I’ve been really excited to try Daughter Thai Kitchen, and Christmas lunch felt like the perfect time to bring my family. The restaurant is beautifully decorated with purple wisteria at the entrance, and the courtyard feels romantic and serene. Inside, the ambiance continues—very elegant and upscale, immediately giving the impression of a fine-dining Thai restaurant.

Most dishes average around $35, including typical options like fried rice, stir-fried noodles, papaya salad, sweet and sour soup, and eggplant dishes. We ordered one of their specials, the Tsunami Lobster ($80), which was disappointingly small—not even a pound—and looked much larger in the photos. Unfortunately, it was definitely not worth the price.

Our total came out to north of $300 for 6 dishes and 2 desserts, with the lobster being the most expensive item. For that price point, the value just wasn’t there for me.

Overall, the food tasted average, similar to what you’d find at a typical Thai restaurant. The papaya salad was very basic and overly salty, and for the price I wish it included shrimp or fish. The fried rice was good, but beef is an extra charge and labeled as Wagyu—though it was really just thinly sliced beef. The soup was one of the better dishes: rich, coconut-forward, and filled with seafood. The pad kee mao noodles were just okay and lacked the wok-smoky flavor we were hoping for.

The lobster dish was the biggest disappointment. The seafood was overcooked and dry, making it far from worth the cost. For dessert, the coconut vacation was overly sweet, but the mango sticky rice was done just right.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

Raising Cane’s absolutely delivered today.

Sometimes you’re not looking for anything complicated. You just want hot, fresh, crispy chicken, ridiculously good sauce, and a team that knows how to execute the basics at a level that makes you wonder why everyone else can’t do it this well.

That’s exactly what I got here.

From the moment I walked in, the entire experience felt effortless. The staff was friendly, professional, attentive, and moving with the kind of coordination you immediately notice. There was a great energy throughout the restaurant, and it was obvious that the team takes pride in what they’re doing.

And then there’s the food.

The chicken was hot, crispy, tender, and ridiculously satisfying. The Cane’s Sauce deserves its own paragraph, its own award, and possibly its own zip code. 😂

The fries were fresh, the toast was on point, and the whole meal came together perfectly.

What I appreciate most about Raising Cane’s is the consistency. You know what you’re getting, but when the team is operating at this level, it still feels special.

There’s something to be said for a restaurant that understands its identity and executes it without overcomplicating anything.

Great food.

Great people.

Great energy.

Exceptional execution.

To the entire team working today, thank you for bringing the professionalism and hospitality. It may seem like “just chicken,” but when you take pride in what you do, customers can absolutely taste the difference.

This was six-star fast food disguised as a chicken finger restaurant.

Five stars without hesitation.

Crispy chicken, legendary sauce, and service that was as smooth as the Texas toast.

Absolutely phenomenal experience.

I came to this location today 2/13/26 and got a Canniac combo. We waited in the drive thru for 25 minutes and cars were not moving for a straight 10 minutes. Ordered, paid, then pulled up to the last window and told to wait 5 more minutes for the food. When I got my order I smelled something was burnt, I had to drive 40 minutes away, so going back was not an option. When I opened and tried my chicken, it tasted straight up burnt. Since my bread was on top of the chicken it also tasted burnt, and the cherry on top my fries were not well cooked. I could not finish my food it was so bad. How can we be told to wait and then get food that is burnt? Don’t they get the smell that it’s burnt? 30 minutes wait and 25 dollars waisted. Worst Cane’s in the area. Hayward location is better.

I ordered the Box combo.  I waited for 30 minutes around 4pm on a Thursday.  The chicken tenders seemed like they weren't fried long enough cause the breading tasted off... the flavor was bland.  The fries were ok but not warm.  The Texas toast was probably my favorite.   The Sweet tea was good.  It was not overly sweet and just the right amount of ice.  The cashier who gave me the food was sweet, great attitude and asked if I needed anything.  Service was great but the food was just not great over all.  The long wait for the food just wasn't worth ever going back.

this location is in a high crime area. Only the driver they is open. My wife and I had walked from our hotel,  and they graciously took our order while we waited outside.  The chicken is still easily my top 5 fav!

I was lucky to have a short drive through line. my bill was near 100.00 for the party pack five fries and bread. The bread was pretty decent , everything extremely disappointed more hype than good food. My drive time home was five minutes. Food was not as Crispy as fried chicken should be fries tasted really old I don’t recommend this Raising Can’s Chicken Fingers . However this could have been just a one time bad experience. Overall frozen fried chicken that you by from the store and place in the oven is better and super cheaper. I truly dislike overpriced bad food.

name: Hong Kong Lounge
address: 5322 Geary Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94121, United States

google.name: Hong Kong Lounge
google.address: 5322 Geary Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94121, United States
google.description: Bustling restaurant delivering a varied menu of dum sum faves right from the kitchen to the table.

top_reviews.content:
This is the sort of dim sum place that feels reassuringly traditional rather than unnecessarily reinvented.

The dim sum is authentic and very much in the classic Hong Kong style. The siu mai and shrimp dumplings are particularly solid, and the menu has a good range of the old favourites rather than trying too hard to make everything fashionable. Other diners also consistently mention the baked BBQ pork buns, rice noodle rolls, sticky rice and porridge among the stronger choices.

Portions are generous and, by San Francisco standards, the prices are quite reasonable. That combination probably explains why Hong Kong Lounge remains busy and has built such a loyal following. It is not trying to be elegant, theatrical or Instagram-ready. It simply serves proper dim sum, and does it well. Local discussions also regularly describe it as one of the more authentic dim sum choices in the city.

A very worthwhile stop if you enjoy traditional Cantonese dim sum. Sometimes authenticity is simply food that tastes the way you remember it should, without anyone feeling the need to put truffle on top.

This was our favorite dim sum place to visit whenever we're in town.  This time is a disappointment.   I think they changed chef.  The beef stripe tastes plain and no ginger was added.  Definitely different from before.

Came here based on high recommendation from local relatives. The food is really really good and authentic. We tried quite a few items that we’d never seen in dim sum restaurants in the US. All very good. Will definitely come back when in the area.

The food d was ok although we didn't like the desert. The "yellow tart" has a strong egg taste.
Usual chinese-American food. The setting was confortable but not fresh.
It was not noisy, just the normal chinese "sitting" restaurant.
The service is fast but not personalized.
It a good place to go if you have a chinese craving.

We had a long layover so I was looking for some decent dim sum without breaking the bank. Back in Chicago, I could always find a decent dim sum place. Reddit led me here and reviews were okay. We ordered salt and pepper tofu cubes, deep fried crab claws, almond balls filled with egg yolk lava, curry beef dumplings, dried scallop with taro dumplings, and deep fried shrimp balls.

The ones that I thought were decent to eat were salt and pepper tofu cubes, deep fried crab claws, and deep fried shrimp balls. The other ones I forced myself to finish, since the food was a bit overpriced and I hate wasting food. Food overall was pretty mediocre so 3 stars is sufficient. Nothing truly stood out for me. Service was okay, standard in most Chinese restaurants. The place was clean but initially when we walked in there were barely any Chinese people eating there. First red flag. More Chinese people came later but that still didn’t change the quality of the food. This was my second time in SF, and Chinese food here hasn’t really impressed me that much.

name: Underdogs Tres
address: 1224 9th Ave, San Francisco, CA 94122, United States

google.name: Underdogs Tres

top_reviews.content:
There are plenty of places in the area to choose from, but their menu immediately stood out. We started with the nachos, then ordered a couple of burritos along with their house margaritas. Everything was excellent. The homemade sauces actually have flavor, not just heat for the sake of being hot, and really elevate the dishes.

The wait staff was friendly and easy to deal with, even though the place was busy while we were there. If you’re in the mood for Mexican food, I highly recommend stopping here.

Loyal customer; have been coming here for years. The food is usually quite good and nice people. I order my burritos with no rice and no beans. Lately, I’ve been having trouble locating ingredients other than tortilla inside my burrito. Here’s a pic of my latest order - SF chicken burrito. Can you spot the chicken?

Ordered take-out via phone and found it peculiar that many of their burritos do not come with rice and beans, and if you want to add it on its $3+. Otherwise, the “Impossible Burrito” and it was very flavorful, and they had a generous portion of the protein that made the burrito so savory! Chips seemed fresh and came warm! My mom got the “Baja-style burrito” and reported that the fish was over-cooked and very firm/dry which was disappointing.

So ..I asked the guy where's a good place to get some tacos around here, and he said in pretty good English "Go for the 3 little dogs"  After an exhausting Google search I believe it's Underdogs Tres Mexican restaurant that he was recommending, so off I went.  I got 4 chicken tacos and they were simply amazing!  This restaurant is highly underrated, and well worth a cross-town trek! 5 ☆☆☆☆☆
Nicky’s Way tacos are the way to go - a soft taco wrapped around a crunchy taco holds a very generous filling of your choice of protein.

top_reviews.content:
Authentic Italian pizzeria with a curated list of only Italian wines. Thoughtful upcycling design that gives a bit  of nostalgia into the past, like the sewing machine table we sat at.
It gets busy around 6:30 pm. We had reservations for 5:45 pm and our table was ready. Great staff as well with full knowledge of the menu and wines.

Back in 2018, my now-husband suggested Montesacro SoMa for our first date. The pinsas are absolutely divine and it has been a favorite restaurant of ours for years now. So much so, that we reached out and asked if they'd be willing to cater our cocktail hour for 160+ guests at our June 2025 wedding in Petaluma. To our luck and surprise, they agreed and even attended our venue walkthrough to ensure they'd be able to use the on-site, outdoor brick oven. The pinsas were the highlight of the night and our guests still rave about them to this day. We worked with Chefs Anna and Mattia - both of whom were so receptive to our requests. I mean, Chef Anna was individually casing the sausage at the venue on the day-of. Need I say more?!

Lovely small space for delicious pinsas. Excellent short wine list. Old world charm. Feels so local, so Roman, so authentic of itself. Cozy old chairs and tables burnished by extended service. Not for glam, but for the glory of crispy pinsa, killer salads. Close to theaters

Delicious pizza with a special recipe dough.  It's just a little bit different, but not blatantly obviously so.  Regardless it's delicious!  Great friendly knowledgeable service.  Wildly interesting eclectic decor, especially the washroom.  The neighbourhood is a little more gritty but not dangerous by my accounts, and there are neighbourhood ambassadors around as well.

The pinsa was sooooo good! We got the artichoke and pecorina crema pinsa and the dough was exquisite. We also tried the pinsa with prosciutto, really good too. Highly recommend! Just be aware that the neighborhood isn't great.

Super nice café near Market Street, would for sure go there again!
Food was delicious, staff friendly and we waited just 5-10min for the food.
Big menu with vegetarian options, can recommend for sure:)
Many locals coming in as well!

We had breakfast here twice during our visit to San Francisco, and honestly, we’d go again tomorrow if our flight back to Maui wasn’t so early.

The coffee was delicious, and we ordered the quinoa bowl with eggs and avocado for breakfast, so good and satisfying. The staff was super kind and efficient, everything came out at a great pace, and the quality was consistently excellent.

Such a great spot to start the day.

top_reviews.content: First time to visit there. So it was not easy to find because we need to drive through the hotel parking. Their parking is small so hard to find the parking. At the restaurant, beautiful ocean view and not so noisy. I love sausage! I will try other sausage next time. Reasonable cute restaurant.

A must stop if you are traveling through Oakland on the 880. We were looking for a lunch spot and this was an easy on-easy off stop on our travels north from Monterey. This is excellent German food and we enjoyed everything we got. I chose the Bretzle & Obadzta starter because traditional pretzles are EVERYTHING. This starter came with a traditional cheese spread and pickled onions. We discovered the mustards that are provided are a great addition to dip in also. In the brown squeeze dispenser there is a stone ground mustard that packs a punch with what can only be described as horseradish. The yellow squeeze dispenser is a dijon type mustard (no Frenches here) and the red one... is of course...ketchup. For the main scourse I tried the weiner schnitzle and my partner got the avacado asparagus omlet with country potatoes. All the food was hot, timely and served with a smile. we sat on the patio and enjoyed the breeze from the bay. The patio has cool picnic style tables that you might find at Ocktober Fest and umbrellas for the sun shy among us. Overlooking the docks and water, it was perfection. On cooler days there is plenty of dining space indoors. Parking was a snap, we got there shortly after they opened at 10:50 am and it filled up while we waited for and enjoyed our selections. This is our new favorite spot in Oakland, so glad we found it on Google maps!

We went there for the Schweinhexe (pig knuckle) and it did not disappoint! Plenty of left overs too!
The Potato Dumplings with mushroom gravy were a great starter!

Decent quality German food in a cool location right by the water. We tried the Wiener Schnitzel and a snack plate. The schnitzel was good. It came with fries and a little container of applesauce. The snack plate was a pretty good option if you want to try a bunch of different things. Pickled egg and veggies with a piece of salami type cured sausage,a pate style meat, a cheese spread and their addictive spicy nuts. Oh, and a baked pretzel!
Service was pleasant and fast.
We had the schnitzel. Unfortunately the meat was beaten too flat and fried too long. The spatzel and rotkohl was good though.

The home fries especially stood out, they were absolutely delicious and exceeded my expectations. Great food, quick service, and a place I looked forward to coming back to every morning!

Food was pretty good. The syrup was the best. Drawn and kept warm so the drizzle on the toast and souffle was delightful. The place is super busy. I had to wait sometime for the syrup because I got my souffle (takes longer than other food to prepare they warned ahead of time) before the syrup came.

Oceanview Diner was a delightful dining experience from start to finish. I ordered the potato pancakes served with sour cream, house-made applesauce, and a sausage, and every bite was flavorful and satisfying. I also had the chance to sample my husband’s pancakes and my daughter’s potato salad, and everything across the table was consistently delicious.
The coffee was fresh, hot, and the perfect complement to the meal. Overall, a thoroughly enjoyable experience with comforting, well-prepared food. I would happily rate Oceanview Diner an 8 out of 10.

I found this pancake mix yesterday in a pantry of a condo in Florida. The side had an order form for merch that you cut out and mail in with payment. And while I'm excited to eat her pancakes, I think I'll wait till I'm in the area for some fresh ones.

name: Great China
address: 2190 Bancroft Way, Berkeley, CA 94704, United States

google.name: Great China
google.address: 2190 Bancroft Way, Berkeley, CA 94704, United States
google.description: Chinese restaurant with a chic, modern atmosphere & a menu that offers Peking duck & other classics.

top_reviews.content:
We’ve eaten at a few Bib Gourmands in the past and we mean it when we say it: this place deserves a star. We had a reservation and the place was so packed it had a line around the block at the opening for dinner service. The wait was about 15-20 minutes from when they opened as they were working quickly to get everyone seated and setup. We were seated at their family sized tables in the back and the service was fantastic. We ordered quite a bit of food since we had a large party so here’s a list of what we got:

Pork dumplings 8/10 - devoured in minutes within our party, everyone loved it.
Salt & pepper spare ribs 10/10 - some of, if not, the best we’ve ever had. Perfect seasoning and chew to them.
Fried rice 9/10 - just delicious, nothing special about it and yet still amazing.
Ginger scallion crab 6/10 - seafood is not really our thing to be fair, but we still did enjoy the meat, the sauce was a bit of a miss though.
Duck bone soup 9/10 - unbelievably good, the cilantro and onion pack it with flavor and the consistency is great.
Broccoli, beef, and string beans 8/10 - a classic just done right, seasoned well and broccoli with a good chew; beef perfect texture and velvety.
Chicken chow mein 10/10 - perfect chew, perfect flavor. Would’ve ordered another if we weren’t so full.
Peking duck with steamed buns and flat bread 11/10 - on this scale an 11 denotes it’s the best we’ve ever had, just in case you thought we failed 1st grade math. Crispy skin and delicious, tender meat.

Great China is undoubtedly some of the best Chinese food we’ve ever had. Add onto the fact that it’s at a better value than other places and it becomes clear that this is a special place. The food itself deserves a star but sprinkle in the service and it begs the question as to why it doesn’t have one. More on the service actually, they were incredibly patient as we ordered many dishes with different requests and were on top of everything from refilling water and tea to removing plates. When the only issue with a place is the parking situation then you know it’s good. (Side note: parking is pretty hard to find and we saw a lot of cars getting tickets for invalid parking so keep an eye out). That shouldn’t deter anyone though as this place might just be worth that fine, half kidding. Do yourself the favor and come here at all costs.

If you come to this restaurant, and I highly recommend you do, keep in mind it is very popular and there will be a wait. The only question is how long. We were expecting to wait a long time, but we got there before it opened on a Sunday, and only waited about 10 minutes. We felt very lucky! We came here in a big group, which is definitely the way to do it because you can get a variety of dishes. Everything was absolutely delicious! The Peking duck was our favorite. But we also liked many other dishes. The only dish that I would say was not fantastic was a fried rice, but that could be just my taste, because someone else actually liked it. This is a really terrific place to come with a group for delicious Chinese food. Highly, highly recommend.

Food is pretty good, though don’t expect authentic Chinese cuisine; this is more Chinese-American food.

The double skin is an interesting dish and definitely worth trying. The walnut prawns are also good, though I’ve had better versions elsewhere. The guo ta fish is a little underwhelming, as it’s just very simple steamed fish with soy sauce, but not very good quality fish.

Portions are fairly decent, but I still found the pricing a little high.

Peking duck is great with pancakes. Pricy but worthy the money. We also ordered eggplant with tofu, sadly was greasy and not impressed. Will skip this dish is possible. Overall, very authentic Peking duck.

This place has the best American Chinese food I’ve ever had anywhere.  The prices are a bit higher than other places.  But well worth it.   Everything always tastes fresh and well made and each visit provides consistency from the last.  The spring rolls are some of the best I’ve had anywhere.   And the steak dishes are always tender which is not always the case as most Chinese food establishments.  Service is quick and efficient.   I’ve never found better Chinese anywhere.  The quality is definitely worth the price.

reviews_snippets.content: "I love 2 skin appetizer, rice sizzling soup, crab meat with buns."

My husband kept saying he wasn’t nice about it. They also didn’t help to move anything over, everyone had to grab their own cups and dishes. He just walked away and didn’t help, so that was really uncomfortable and awkward. They moved my friend to end of the table away from everyone so she felt left out. Thankfully my friends moved around so she could feel included. I also tried to get some answers regarding renting a room for my party, but the lady (Nancy) wasn’t very helpful or cordial, and it took several tries to get my questions answered to which she didn’t even answer them all and I gave up renting the room. She actually didn’t answer my question about costs and menu set requirements, and she instead told me to just book a normal table, so I basically gave up on trying to book the room. She had zero customer service, just one or two word answers and no follow up on how she could help me plan this group dinner. I even said I can add more people if there’s a minimum to book the room. This interaction almost made me not want to book this place at all, but it was a big enough place for my group so I ended up booking it. Also, it was my birthday and there was no simple candle with small dessert situation and we were never asked if we wanted dessert. By that time it had been almost 2.5hrs and we hadn’t seen the waiter in awhile so we decided we may as well wrap up.

Food: food was just okay. I felt for the price it could have been a lot better executed. The good: miso cod was delicious, nigiri and sashimi platter were good (idk why the sashimi came out at the very end when I told the staff to bring the nigiri and sashimi out first? It seemed they forgot about it and put it together in the end). The not-so-great: the karaage looked and tasted more like chicken nuggets, there was no classic crackly, craggily outer skin and the color was more like a beige and not that dark reddish orange skin that I’m used to seeing. The crab fried rice had no taste, the texture was good and there was plenty of crab it was just kind of like a bland filler. The hamachi with strawberry slices tasted okay, but I couldn’t get over the fact that the puffed rice looked like maggots and the dish didn’t get finished. Also my friend who had her service dog asked if she could order a few pieces of fish for just herself and she was told no and the person was just rude to her. That is so uncalled for, please fix your customer service especially towards ADA people.

Overall, if you want a fancy looking place that has a lot of space and decent sashimi and a unique cocktail list, this could be nice, but I think it’s way overpriced for what this is. It felt like an overrated cash grab Vegas strip restaurant with a chef name behind it to afford the rent. Personally, this is not my kind of restaurant, so I doubt I’ll return.

Menu ideas and cocktails were perfect
We got the special fried rice with lobster Wagyu and bone marrow which was amazing and the duck ramen. The shrimp toast was also so crunchy and nutty at the same time. Service was so perfect with a surprise birthday dessert and overall kindness. The only missing piece is seasoning. We felt like each dish could have had more salt or pepper seasoning or maybe some other balancing flavors maybe spicier ? Something made it feel bland despite the ingredients were so fresh and menu ideas were top notch. However the sushi roles were 100% top tier. We got rainbow rolls and toro/caviar/scallop roles which were one of the top 3 in SF.

Valentine's Day Dinner — A $175/Person Disappointment

At $175 per person, you'd expect near-Michelin-level quality in both food and service. What we got instead felt like a calculated cash grab dressed up as a special occasion dinner.

Atmosphere & Seating
The moment we walked in, it was clear the restaurant had reconfigured its layout specifically for Valentine's Day — cramming in as many 2-top tables as possible to maximize covers. The result? A packed, noisy dining room where couples are elbow-to-elbow with strangers. To make it worse, the seating was wildly inconsistent — some couples were seated in large booths meant for 6, while others (like us) were stuck at tiny two-tops with zero privacy. For a "romantic" Valentine's dinner, the atmosphere was anything but.

Food
Mediocre at best. The sashimi/nigiri plate was unremarkable, and the overall menu felt deliberately simple — likely to speed up table turnover. The steak was the highlight, with a creative sauce and solid mashed potatoes, but that's a low bar for this price point.

Drinks
We paid $40 for a glass of Moët & Chandon that arrived relatively flat and was not poured tableside — despite the table next to us receiving a full tableside pour for their champagne pairing. That level of inconsistency at this price is inexcusable.

Service
This is where the experience truly fell apart. Our server checked on us exactly zero times throughout the entire meal. When our wine glasses were empty, we waited 20+ minutes just to flag someone down. The one request we made all night — asking if our wine could come out quickly so we could enjoy it with our steak — was met with our server rushing away and saying, "It'll come out when it comes out." On Valentine's Day. At $175 a head. Stunning.

To top it off, when a server accidentally dropped a plate nearby, a manager in a suit stood there, watched him clean it up, shook his head, and walked away — no apology to nearby guests, no offer to help. It was a perfect snapshot of the attitude permeating the entire staff.

The Bottom Line
This restaurant saw Valentine's Day as an opportunity: pack in as many tables as possible, charge premium prices, serve a stripped-down menu for fast turnover, and let service slide. The lack of hospitality wasn't accidental — it was the predictable result of a management team that prioritized profit over the experience they were selling. Save your money and your evening.

Each tea comes with its own kettle, and Ken even came back to refill the hot water for us.

We also tried the Sichuan Seafood Dumplings and the Iberico Pork Dumplings, both of which were delicious. One order is definitely enough to share.

top_reviews.content: This is my 1st Indian restaurant since moving to the Bay. The restaurant is beautiful inside.  The art and decor give a well-balanced feeling of deep culture and traditions. The staff were polite,  funny and very detailed in their service.  We were explained,  any dish and were able to try a wide variety of food. The food was delicious! We had varying dishes, lamb, shrimp, creamy chicken and sides (no French fries lol). My skillet was good, shrimp and peppers.  The price was unreasonably affordable! We were shocked at having a healthy portion for the price we paid per person.  I would recommend trying this restaurant and exploring some different dishes, from a unique and beautiful place.

Great lunch buffet for 17.99. Our server Navi was attentive and polite. Food was remade frequently during my visit.

Only critique I have is I wish they played some music! It was so quiet inside you can hear forks hitting your plates. I’d still visit if you’re craving Indian food and don’t mind the silence.

India Clay Oven is an absolute hidden gem on the SF Peninsula, and it made for the most precious, private, and romantic date night. The restaurant is unbelievably gorgeous on the inside, yet surprisingly, there wasn't a single soul sitting down when we went. Having that beautiful space all to ourselves made the atmosphere feel incredibly special and intimate. The Paneer Tikka Masala was absolutely amazing, and it is totally worth getting it spicy because the heat level and flavor were perfect. The garlic naan had phenomenal flavor and texture, and the rice was incredibly generous with the seasonings. It was mouth-numbingly good and paired perfectly with the curry.If you want top-tier Indian cuisine and a stunning, quiet setting for a night out, this is the spot.

This place is absolutely amazing. We've come for their lunch buffet and consistently get their takeout, both are equally delicious. But the PHENOMENAL service especially from Nabi!!!! is the true highlight every single time. They are so kind and attentive, the best food : service : atmosphere ratio you'll find in the area. We'll keep coming back :)

The lunch buffet is back!   I’ve been eating here for the last 20 years and they have been a staple in the neighborhood.  Navi and his team have provided reliably delicious Indian food in the Richmond district.

Pro tip:  a cup of chai is the perfect way to finish the meal.

reviews_snippets.content: "Really tasty food, nice atmosphere, and super friendly service! great spot"

top_reviews.content:
This was a great little spot for lunch!  The food was delicious especially the peperdelle pasta with pork, this has got to be one of the tastiest pastas.

Fun fact, they don't have pepperoni on their pizzas!!!!  The pizza was okay, and the service was fair.

Not a bad place but not the experience I was hoping for, especially given all the hype.

We had a great experience here! The meatballs were absolutely amazing, the tomato sauce was so good that we practically cleaned the plate. The pizza was delicious, and the Caesar salad was fresh and full of flavor as well.

The service was fast and attentive, and everything we ordered arrived surprisingly quickly. The atmosphere was relaxed and enjoyable, although the restaurant was very busy. We came without a reservation, but the staff still managed to find us a table. That said, I’d recommend making a reservation if you can.

The food was fine, but the service was some of the worst I’ve experienced. We sat for over 10 minutes without anyone acknowledging us—no water, no greeting, nothing—until we had to flag down a server ourselves. When someone finally came to take our order, we jokingly said we thought we’d been forgotten. Instead of an apology or even basic courtesy, the server was rude and dismissive, snapped “go ahead,” and treated us like an inconvenience. Completely unacceptable service.

Calamari was simply delicious, couldn’t stop eating it.  Loved the addition of shishitos and the lovely sauce.

White prawns and bread were nice - very lemon forward. Shrimp were sweet and cooked perfectly.

Liked the apps more than entrees.

Pizza w/fennel sausage (no pic) was par. Pasta with pork and pappardelle was tasty.

Not a huge fan of all the fees on the bill.

Good Italian restaurant in the Marina. It has a nice outdoor seating area, as well as lots of seating indoors. It's a bit cramped indoors, and most of the seating is at long tables sitting on hard stools, which aren't very comfortable. Because of the long tables, you may end up sitting right next to another group, so it's not the best place for intimate conversations.

I tried the mushroom pizza with the gluten-free crust, and it was delicious. I also had the winter salad, which was small but tasty.

Service was good, with the server walking me through the GF options on the menu. However, when we wanted to leave to catch our movie, it took a long time to pay. After a while of waiting at our table, we eventually went up to the register to pay.

top_reviews.content: Got to experience Trabocco with the entire family on our trip to the bay, searched up Italian food and were blown away by the menu, once we arrived we were met with phenomenal service from Pedro and another gentlemen who i didnt get to catch his name. The chef was very interactive and friendly with my children and wife. The food was extraordinary, i had steak, my wife had the calzone, my eldest had the squid ink kalamari, my 2nd son had the sea bass, 3rd son had a pep pizza, and our baby tasted all of it. Atmosphere was beautiful, we sat outside but had heaters for the warmth. Very luxurious experience, highly recommend for anyone visiting or who lives in town and hasnt tried it yet. Thank you Trabocco staff, we will see you again . My 2nd son said the napkin was something else 🤣

Fancy looking Italian spot close to the Alameda shores! The place is chic and oozes class. The chef quacks Italian and looks Italian. So he must be one! He greeted us and we sat at the chef's counter, which I highly recommend. You get to see how the sausage is made.

The bread arrived and it was just right. Then came the burrata. While I loved the consistency of the cheese I didn't enjoy the tomato as much. It felt a tad crisp and unripe, but that's a personal preference. The salad with lentils, beans, and quinoa looked interesting and they swapped out the anchovy dressing for something simpler, but it didn't work for me at all. It felt bland. The main course was gnocchi with butternut squash and mushrooms. The mouth feel and the chewiness was simply right but the flavor had a little more to go for me. Overall it's a great Italian spot with a couple of vegetarian options.

It’s not usual I give five stars but this place was fire.
Beautiful ambience, we sat outside on the heated patio. It had great lighting and even with a reserved party there was plenty of space to walk in and be seated immediately on a Saturday night. The reverberation was minimal and it was not too difficult to hear our own conversation as we chatted among other customers.
Food was also delicious, and service was super friendly from start to finish. It was worth every dollar and I would absolutely come back again.

This is a GREAT place. The food, the vibe, but….. Trabocco; Mikelle is really a big part of what make places like this great. Because servers like him; they are really there to make the dinning experience special.

Mikelle thanks!!

We feel welcome and just had a great time

Great food in a lovely atmosphere with that extra personal touch. We were there to celebrate my birthday. I had the seafood platter special and my husband am had the half chicken with roasted vegetables, we were both very happy with our meals. The cocktails are amazing, with interesting flavor combinations. The tiramisu dessert was perfect and the chef coming out to sing happy birthday was much appreciated. The staff are very professional, attentive, and accommodating. We will be sure to visit again.

top_reviews.content:
My wife wanted to try this place as she's a big fan of ramen. We both got a bowl of the Hakata Tonkotsu DX. But not before starting with a few appetizers, like their Marufuku bites and classic Takoyaki.
The food was filling but I liked the appetizers more. I would try their curry next time.
We tried their hot sake but it wasn't a favorite. We would try their cold ones next time.
Staff was very friendly and attentive. Kept our water glasses full and made us feel welcome.

Don't miss this! The service is quick, friendly and fun. It's a whole experience at a totally worth while price. I'd eat here again and bring my friends to enjoy it too. Loved the bar seating and the fast paced scene that lets you chill in the midst of it. Careful with the chili oil, for real 🤣🙏🏼

Bebelin was such a wonderful server. It was my first time eating at this establishment, and she gave our party the service experience of a lifetime. She was bubbly, kind, and made sure that we were taken care of throughout the duration of our stay. The food was delicious and offered in a beautiful ceramic bowl that highlighted their special attention to detail. The presentation, food quality, and waitstaff make me excited to dine here again.

One of my favorite locations of all-time and favorite restaurant for Ramen. Flavor consistency, visual presentation, and customer service is phenomenal. Amanda went above and beyond making for a great memorable experience!

I ordered 3 bowls of ramen and chicken karaage bento for a delivery. The ramen tasted more like instant noodles than restaurant-quality ramen. The chicken karaage was completely covered in a sweet-and-sour orange sauce, which wasn’t what I expected. The gyoza included in the bento also tasted like the frozen kind.
We paid $120 for three ramen, one chicken karaage bento, edamame, and an extra order of noodles. For that price, I expected freshly prepared, authentic Japanese food. Instead, it felt like we were served pre-made, low-quality meals.  I can honestly say that people in Japan would not pay more than $40 for food of this quality, and most would not accept it at all. The value simply did not match the price. Overall, it was disappointing and not worth the cost.

top_reviews.content: Absolutely amazing and authentic Mexican food. The workers are extremely helpful, and are genuinely happy to be there. Before your food is served, they welcome you with a delicious chips and homemade salsa. I highly recommend their Birria Tacos with cheese. This is an absolute hidden gem found on 26th and South Van Ness.

When I say these are the BEST birria tacos I have EVER had I am not exaggerating. The beef was cooked perfectly and was tender and juicy. Consomme had a lovely umami and rich flavor. The salsas were made in house, cold, and refreshing. My agua fresca was definitely a bit too sweet but that’s probably how it’s supposed to be. Will absolutely be back next time I’m in the Mission district.

Decided to come here and got an al pastor quesadilla since line at La taqueria was too crazy- meat was super tender and rly liked the quesadilla itself but a little too oil for my liking; parchment paper on the bottom was literally drenched in the oil. Their known for their quesabirria tacos so might come back to try that next time

Great food and service. Next time my family is in San Francisco we will definitely go back! Manager and staff are very kind. Our favorites were the birria tacos (best we’ve had) and ube flan (from OnlyFlanz).

Took BART straight from SFO to this Mission gem for a shrimp quesadilla…. crispy, cheesy, ridiculously good. Fast service, fair prices, tasted every bit as good as the hype. Worth the trip before boarding your flight home.

top_reviews.content:
🇺🇸 California Road Trip – Part 2: San Francisco & Yosemite
📅 December 2023
The next morning, we left Pismo Beach and continued our drive north toward San Francisco. After several hours on the road, we finally arrived in the late afternoon and checked into the San Francisco Marriott Fisherman's Wharf.
The following morning, we walked toward Pier 39 for brunch. Along the way, a kind local named Frank unexpectedly handed us a 15% discount coupon for Eagle Cafe. It felt like one of those little moments that make traveling so special.
The restaurant overlooked the waterfront, creating the perfect atmosphere for a relaxing brunch. Everything we ordered was delicious, and somehow the meal tasted even better because we were enjoying it in San Francisco. Maybe that's one of the gifts that travel gives us.
After brunch, we visited the Golden Gate Bridge, one of California's most iconic landmarks. Seeing it in person was even more impressive than I had imagined.
From there, we headed to the famous Lombard Street. Watching cars carefully make their way down the winding road was just as entertaining as the beautiful city views surrounding it.
Later, we rode one of San Francisco's historic cable cars to Union Square, where we took a break at Caffé Central. It was the perfect place to slow down for a while. The coffee was excellent, and after a busy day of sightseeing, it was exactly what we needed.
The next day, we left the city behind and drove into Yosemite National Park. We stayed at the historic Wawona Hotel, where time seemed to slow down.
One of the things I loved most was being away from modern distractions for a while. With limited Wi-Fi and internet access, it was refreshing to disconnect from everyday life and simply enjoy the peaceful surroundings.
That evening, we had dinner at The Winter Wawona Dinner. The warm atmosphere, delicious food, and historic setting made it one of the most memorable dining experiences of our trip. Sitting by the fireplace after dinner, surrounded by the quiet beauty of Yosemite, felt like one of the best moments of our entire California journey.
Sometimes the best memories aren't made by famous attractions alone. They're created by unexpected kindness, a wonderful meal, a quiet cup of coffee, and peaceful moments shared along the way.
Next stop: Back to Los Angeles... 🇺🇸

Stopped in for lunch on a Saturday around 12:30pm. This weekend Pier 39 was packed because there was the Pokémon Go 10th Anniversary event happening as well as the World Cup. It was busy, but we got seated right away still. Seating was tight but the service was great. Since we were so packed in the only decor I really saw were all of the military hats pinned high on the walls around the room. I thought they were cool. They weren't dusy, so either they hadn3t been there long or the restaurant takes care of dusting up there, which is nice. We were checked on frequently by the wait staff and the managers. He had the fish and chips and I had the fish tacos (cod). The food came out reasonably quick and hot. The tortillas were soft and seemed freshly made, so I appreciated that. And the fries were so crispy and airy. Our meal total was just over $50. The water was served in glass bottles but the cups they provided were very small (like kids cups). Overall, I would come back!

Really wanted to like it here because it came so highly recommended. The service was fast and the atmosphere is tops—super cool spot.

The problems that brought it down:
-The coffee tastes like it was made with hotel tap water—and water absolutely is an important ingredient for coffee.

-Bacon came out flimsy. If you like bacon that way, then it’s all good. I’d have appreciated the server asking how we wanted it so we could’ve asked for crispy.

-The toast was definitely a “great value” type of brand.

-Some of the potato wedges were crispy, but most were greasy and mushy.

-The eggs and the burrito were room temp. It was off-putting to have some hot bites mixed with cold ones. The burrito was all too cold to melt the cheese on top which probably came out of the fridge.

-Chocolate chip pancakes were about the only thoroughly successful dish this time around.

-Expensive food is to be expected here, but $7.50 for lemonade and $5.50 for coffee is good old fashioned greed. Super disappointed in that area.

Overall, we may have caught the team on a bad day. There are enough good reviews that make me think we were just unlucky. Here’s to hoping management sees these very easy fixes and implements them so they have a few more happy tourists who can recommend that others eat here.

We had the avocado toast and biscoff pancakes, the eggs were good and I liked the fact that they use sourdough bread. Very generous with the avocado and the wedges were ok. We loved the biscoff pancakes and the syrup that it came with. The pancakes were thick and yummy and the bananas on top were ripe. Perfect finisher to our meal. Good service and kind staff.

Eagle Cafe is right on Fisherman's Wharf in San Francisco. This place just oozes of the history of the area as the restaurant is almost 100 years old. On top of that, the interior is beautifully maintained despite seeing heavy traffic most days (being on the wharf).

For our breakfast, we enjoyed the scrambled eggs and Eggs Benedict. Both came with fried potato wedges. Everything was delicious, perfectly prepared, and the portion sizes were generous. The Eggs Benedict was placed on a thick slice of toast, which was a nice variation of the dish.

In addition, the service was prompt, attentive, and friendly.

If you want an authentic San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf experience, then go to Eagle Cafe. We really enjoyed our visit!

top_reviews.content: Got the Cochinita Plate, which is their signature dish. Can't say I was really impressed by it. But I felt like they deserved another try, so I came back for their al-pastor burrito. And it was fantastic! One of the best burritos I have eaten around SF! They keep the place clean and tidy, staff was helpful and quick. There are plenty of space to eat. You have the sauce counter with 3 different sauces. The mild sauce is dangerously delicious (little bit of a sweetness to it).

The 2nd and 3rd visits were as satisfying as the 1st. We tried Taqueria Los Mayas several months ago. We ordered different dishes but both had mole which was memorable. Months later, I remembered how delicious the mole was and ordered it in the burrito bowl.

The dish was aesthetically pleasing and colorful: against the dark mole were crumbles of queso surrounded by purple pickled onions, red rice, greens, black beans, and sprinkles of sesame seeds.

On the 3rd visit, I tried the breakfast burrito. The eggs were perfectly scrambled and the potatoes were comforting. My hubby ordered the tortilla soup - fitting for a cold day - and the fish tacos, which he enjoyed very much. The fish was fresh and sauteed with a slight crisp.

Almost every dish came with tortilla chips. There's a salsa bar with 3 salsas, one green (mild), one orange with mango (mild and our favorite), and one hot.

Will be back soon to have something with mole.

Amazing food! The panochos were great, the flavor of the carne asada and cochinita pibil were to die for. The torta de carne asada was phenomenal as well, and the elote loco lived up to its name in the best way!
Really tasty carne asada and very zingy guacamole. Loved the super burrito. The different salsas were all very delicious. Can’t wait to come back
Delicious food! Highly recommend the plantain burrito for fellow vegetarians. Employees were kind, service was fast, and the music and environment were lovely. Can’t wait to come back!

top_reviews.content: Great tacos and carne asada fries. We can back twice on our trip. The breakfast burritos are also delicious. The prices are good and the portions are big. The employees are friendly and quick.

Just had amazing nachos! Went for the lengua (beef tongue) as I had never tried it. It was delicious, so glad I did. The portion was massive, could easily do two people as a snack. Hope I have a chance to pop back before I leave.

Came across this restaurant when searching for non-touristy spots near Fisherman’s Wharf and so glad that we tried this restaurant! We ordered to-go so can’t speak of the dine-in experience, but even tho the restaurant looks small it’s well organized! We ordered the large nachos with shredded chicken, the sour cream and guacamole was so flavorful, we also ordered loaded grilled chicken nachos and omg the chicken was so flavorful, a 10/10 item! And finally we also ordered the Baja tacos, the fish felt a little bit dry so it’s a 7.5/10, but the nachos and grilled chicken made up for it! Will definitely try it again if we are in the area!

The reviews speak for the high quality of this restaurant.  The food was super yummy and the lady who took our order was really nice.  Food came out super quick.  If you like Mexican food make your way here.

Nice location, and the tacos tasted good, but our Taco Tuesday experience was disappointing.
We were told all tacos were $3 each, but when the bill came, the fish and shrimp tacos were charged $4.50 each. While I understand specialty tacos may cost more, the bigger issue is that we were served the smaller Taco Tuesday-sized fish and shrimp tacos instead of the regular-sized tacos we paid for.

When we asked our server, she acknowledged she had given us incorrect pricing information but never addressed why we received the smaller tacos. Paying full price would have been fine if we had received the full-size tacos. Instead, we paid $4.50 for tacos with only two shrimp each.

The food was good, but the inaccurate pricing and inconsistent portions left a bad impression.
