top_reviews.content: One of the best meals I have had in San Francisco in a while. The halibut and couscous were cooked perfectly and very well balanced. The staff were friendly and helpful. They have heaters for their outdoor seating which is nice. Before you sit take a quick scan inside and outside to avoid being near loud kids...

If you’re looking to try authentic Turkish food, Lokma is definitely a must-visit. The restaurant offers amazing Turkish food options, especially the burger and chicken bowl, both of which were flavorful and perfectly prepared. The pita bread was served fresh, warm, and soft, pairing really well with the incredibly tasty baba ganoush.

The seating inside is small and cozy, giving the place a welcoming vibe, and they also have two outdoor sheds for comfortable open-air seating. To top it all off, the baklava was perfectly crispy and delicious. Overall, a fantastic spot for anyone wanting to explore Turkish cuisine with great flavors and a cozy atmosphere.

A story about how one of my favorite spices (cinnamon) ruined brunch on a Sunday.

I love cinnamon. In pastries, in coffee, in savory chili.i just did not expect it to hijack a savory Turkish ratatouille and dominate my entire plate.

The Good:
• For a walk-in only, a short 10 minute wait was very much appreciated
•The eggs were beautifully executed - soft, fluffy, properly folded, tender inside without being runny or rubbery. You can tell the kitchen knows what they’re doing.
• Tzatziki on eggs? Unexpected and absolutely delicious. Cool, tangy, creamy against warm eggs - amazing!
• The Arnold Palmer was perfectly balanced (not too sweet, not too tea-heavy). Clean layers, refreshing, 5/5.
• Cold water served immediately upon arrival (and properly cold). It’s such a simple touch, but always appreciated.
• Ambiance is top notch - warm, inviting, great brunch energy.
• Attentive staff throughout.

The Not-So-Good:
• The Turkish ratatouille was overwhelmingly cinnamon-forward. That was the only dominant note I could taste, and it overpowered the dish to the point where I struggled to finish it. Interestingly, the server initially mentioned they don’t add cinnamon but after checking with the kitchen, confirmed that cinnamon is indeed added. It was just far too much.
• No side plate. With oranges, sauce, and potatoes sharing space, there was nowhere to rest utensils or keep citrus from soaking into the stew. Small detail, but it matters.
• No salt and pepper on the table, so there was no way to tweak seasoning.

The frustrating part is that the technical cooking - especially the eggs - was excellent. But when one spice dominates and a few small service details are overlooked, it changes the entire experience.

Cinnamon, I still love you.

Food is just okay, the portions are small, and I feel like the things we got were just okay.

Greek yogurt pancakes are solid, but not mind blowing. I think it lacked a little bit of flavor or depth. It feels like they just put some Greek yogurt and berries on pancakes. Also pretty pricey for what you get. Service and atmosphere were nice.

The food was also excellent. The chicken was extremely tender and well prepared and the freshness of the ingredients really shines through. I do wish I was able to see/understand Turkish influences a bit more clearly but we really liked this place and will be coming back again.

top_reviews.content:
Excellent service, phenomenal food, great quantity of food as well.

I came here just before July. They saw they had signs stating that they would raise prices in July. I was greeted and walked to a table. The interior was very nice.

I ordered a lunch special with galbi tang. They served me eight banchan, steamed egg, rice, and a pot of barley tea, and a cup of silhye when I went to pay. Everything was excellent. The galbitang had plenty of meat and also had rice noodles. I'll definitely be back.

Traditional Korean restaurant located in the Richmond district. Pre pandemic I would come here with my friends from out of town and I’ve been here when Korean tour busses stop by and the tours come in and out so quickly. You can do your own bbq or Ala carte. Ala carte is easy, came here during the week for lunch and there’s not usually a wait. We got hot stone bulgogi bibimbap, seafood pancake, bulgogi, pork belly, complimentary tofu soup, and comp rice tea at the end. We wanted to order another beef stew but we already had so much. They have tons of fresh and unlimited banchan. Food is fresh and we got it quickly, feels like you’re in Korea. Staff are efficient and used to working quickly through people. There’s street parking surrounding the area, you can probably find a spot circling around. Also feels homey inside and you can order soju and beer.

The menu is variety of the items. Very traditional, authentic and super delicious. The owner lady was very friendly and accommodating. She offered us some dessert sweet fermented rice drink was amazing. We will come again. Thank you

Came here for late lunch on a Friday after spending the morning in the Presidio. We were looking forward to eating off the traditional Korean grill and were not sure they had that for lunch. However they had a really good and relatively inexpensive lunch menu and we ordered several items from there. The quality of food, starting with the ban chan, were really good. We had the bimbimbap, kalbi, rice cake soup, seafood scallion pancake. Would return for dinner. Located in a quiet neighborhood in outer sunset, there was a line outside late in the afternoon - not sure how that would look like at dinner time…

The food was great—especially the Korean BBQ, which I really enjoyed. The service was good overall, but I wish we had a bit more attention from the waiter. At one point I wanted to order more food, but the waiter wasn’t around. I’d recommend ordering everything you want right away. Still, the food itself was very good and worth it.

top_reviews.content: Tried Tacolicious for the first time with a friend—we walked in without a reservation and were quickly seated at the bar, which was a nice start. We ordered the aguachile along with fish and shrimp tacos. The tacos were definitely the highlight—fresh and really tasty. The aguachile wasn’t for me since I’m not a fan of raw shrimp. Overall, it was a decent experience, but with so many great spots in the Marina, I’d probably skip it next time.

My go to place for a cheap happy hour delicious meal with drinks.

$8/margarita and $4 taco before reward member perks (which give 40% off!) is unbeatable value. Nice staff, nice atmosphere, great down to earth food.

Try this place out and guarantee you won’t be disappointed for happy hour.

Ordered the fish tacos and shrimp tacos, tasty. Served more like room temperature than hot. Two house margaritas too with tasty flavor and good salt on the rim. Nice space with bar searing made it easy to talk.
Loved sitting on the patio in the sun.  Servers were very attentive.  Homemade guacamole 🥑 was delicious and the tacos were flavorful and juicy!

We live close by and love coming here for a lunch or dinner. Tacos are really good and beer selection is diverse. If the Warriors or 49ers or Giants are playing great to sit at the bar! The staff is great and service is fast! They having dining outside on Chestnut St which is fun too! I definitely recommend coming here for all these reasons!

For the price these are a great dogs, choice of different sausages on a French baguette style bun with basic self serve condiments.
Service is dull and boarder line rude, the store has zero atmosphere, didn’t feel welcome to stand in the store and wait for my food.
Kitchen looks like it could do with a deep clean.

Top Dog is a Berkeley classic and I’m glad I found out! Quick and easy service if you’re lucky to avoid a line. Self service station for condiments was a nice touch. The hot link was amazing but the bread is what makes the dog special. They have many options for hot dogs and there is something for everyone.

I was here for memories as this is one of the places I visited a lot when I first visited CA for a long stay. It’s still there for students and the neighborhood.

Besides pork and beef, chicken ones were juicy and great. Stuff you can add on to your dog by yourself.

I just adore this place. I have their success and mural posters, and there is just something about the vibe. This place has been here since 1966 - just such a Berkeley staple. Definitely stop by and maybe you'll catch Bill Murray on their tele

Absolutely incredible, hot dogs don’t get better than this! We were on a road trip and were a tad intimidated by the long line outside. These were so worth the wait, the crispy yet chewy hot dog bun, and the flavors of the bratwurst, garlic, and the all beef frank were amazing! Best hot dog I’ve ever had!

top_reviews.content:
Went with a party of 12 and joined the waitlist early so we were able to get seated pretty quick! Our table ordered one kalbijim medium spicy with cheese and one mild kalbijim. Between the two we liked the medium spicy with cheese a lot more since we thought the mild one a little too sweet.

Meat was super tender and so were the veggies, and it paired very nicely with the purple rice! Wish they had more variety for their side dishes but rly delicious over all, just a little pricy!

This place is so good! I don’t like Korean food or waiting in lines and it was amazing! Waited an hour but worth the wait with friends
You have to get the cheese. I don’t like cheese that much and it was good. You just need to try it
So good! Great portion sizes! Helpful staff
So good

Food was great — especially the kalbijjim. Banchan were also very good.

However, on a Friday at 6:30pm we waited about two hours total (one hour online + one hour at the door, even with preorder). Then we were asked to leave after 40–50 minutes of being seated, which felt rushed.

Delicious food, but the timing and service made it a frustrating experience.

We went here on a Friday night at 7pm and waited roughly 1hr 15mins for a table of 2.

Ordered the Regular size premium Kalbijjim and it was amazing!  The portion was huge and they do not skimp out on the beef. We love that there was also stewed radish, potato, carrot and rice cakes inside. The flavour was delicious and very much worth the wait!
The banchan was good and free refill. Kimchi, radish not too spicy or salty. Service was fast and efficient give how busy they were.

The galbitang is soooo good here. I've tried their galbijjim which is also good, but if you want something light, the galbitang is great! The galbitang's broth was my favorite. I am drooling just by writing this review. The server was very nice and was very quick with refilling our side dishes! When you're in SF and you want something light good Korean food, you need to come try Daeho!

Nice place for celebrations and dates. Spacious but intimate interior gives the right feel. The service is welcoming and food was great every time I visited.
Was not a fan of their drinks (natural wine and non alcoholic drink I tried were not well balanced) But overall the place is worth coming back

Had a great lunch consisting of sandwiches , hummus and my favorite the green goddess salad. Server was friendly and on top of all
The orders .

Really enjoyed Barcha. The place has a lively Mediterranean vibe with a great atmosphere. The spicy dumplings were excellent,packed with flavour and a perfect kick of heat. Great spot for a fun dinner in San Francisco. Would happily come back!

I ordered the Turkish Spiced Lamb & Beef Shawarma with potatoes, and it was delicious! The meat was tender and perfectly seasoned. Service was a bit slow this time, and it’s on the pricier side for a sandwich and side, but the flavor made it worth it. On my prior visit, we dined inside and service was a bit faster. Pictures are from September visit--Chicken Shawarma and Grilled Steak Kabob.

top_reviews.content: After meeting up with Billy White Shoes Johnson at his flop on Webster Street we decided to have lunch before heading down to the Larry Flint Center for the Performing Arts to see the Wonderful Fantasia preform her spectacular 3 Women Lumberjack show..it's an amazing experience...but not as amazing as the fried chicken we had at the Aburaya restaurant...Now that was truly amazing!  5 ☆☆☆☆☆'s!

Aburaya is a gem. Fully gluten-free and good for folks with celiac. So many sauces and seasonings for the chicken, which was crispy and juicy. Fried tofu was also fab, and great salads. Punk rock vibe, love the stickers. No-frills on service - the staff are super chill & nice but everything is self-service. Bus your table! Will definitely be back!

Enjoyed my dinner here. Stopped by before a concert in downtown Oakland. It’s a busy spot with not enough seating inside for the crowds.
I enjoyed the chicken I got, cooked well. Was nice and juicy. I ordered their bbq sauce and it was very tangy, hard to describe. I’d definitely try out other flavors before getting bbq again. The bland salad and cabbage didn’t seem needed either.

Good option for a quick meal, and I mean quick seriously. From order till I got my food was likely less than 4 minutes. I went with the 4 piece fried chicken with side salad, splitting the flavors on the chicken between BBQ(sauce) and General Tso(dry rub). Of the two the BBQ I personally preferred more, the flavor was deeper and the slight spice to it added more, it had a slight crisp but not as significantly as the the General Tso due to the dry rub. The general Tso was good as well and had a better crisp but the flavor was as exciting. The interior of the restaurant was a bit dim which is easier on the eyes but made my pictures come out a little dark. Not much else to say, happy with good fried chicken

There was a very long line when we went there and the place was crowded/loud. Ordering online and picking it up is much easier. Since the weather was nice, we ate by the lake instead of eating indoors. Everything was delicious. I just wish there was a little more sauce on the chicken.

top_reviews.content: Creative mexican option. Delish cucumber and jicama salad - tangy and slightly spicy. Shrimp ceviche disappointing albeit very fresh. Soup excellent. Fishtacos very good.

This upscale Mexican restaurant has amazing vibes and delicious food. We sat inside, but there's a really pretty shaded outdoor bar area with heaters that looked really nice too. The service was attentive, the food was very flavorful and felt like just enough to feel satisfied, but not so much you're struggling to finish.

Had a lovely dinner there last night. Our waitress was very attentive. We had the whole roasted chicken and it came with lovely tortillas, beans and rice. Cocktails were yummy too. I liked the ceviche, though there could’ve been more shrimp. The Tlayuda was very good. Also, there were a lot of adorable children running around, which is always a plus.

Was pleasantly surprised by the atmosphere of the back area of Comal. From the front, it doesn’t really look that big but once your inside they an elegant sit down interior and then their back area has a tall ceiling and a very earthy vibe with a bar connected. The food itself is authentic. Especially their hand pressed tortillas. The prices are a bit steep but it’s worth it for a cute dinner date or elegant time with the family.  I got the cod tacos which were extremely delicious. The tortillas are super soft and surprisingly light.

To be honest, this restaurant was very disappointing. We started with the shrimp ceviche, which didn’t taste good at all. It felt more like shrimp covered in chimichurri sauce and served with cold chips than an actual ceviche.

The cod tacos didn’t taste fresh, and while the carnitas were edible, there was absolutely nothing memorable about them. I also had a margarita, which was just okay.

Overall, this was not a good dining experience. If it hadn’t been for Michelle’s recommendation, we probably wouldn’t have tried it. Even the quesadilla wasn’t very good. Unfortunately, I wouldn’t return or recommend this restaurant.

The best CUCINA ROMANA in San Francisco! 54 mint has a very cosy and inviting ambiance, with a relaxed casual vibe making it perfect for both catch up with friends over drinks as well as date night.

The team at 54 Mint couldn't be friendlier and make you feel right at home from the moment you arrive. The experience is rounded out by a menu that consistently impresses- top-notch comfort food with something for everyone, plus creative, well crafted cocktails and wine that pair perfectly with the food.

It's the kind of place that I've return to again and again. One of my favorite Italian restaurants for a reason.

A MUST VISIT FOR ANYONE WHO LOVES GREAT FOOD, COCKTAILS AND WINE!

Location is nice. Seems solo diners are just ‘dumped’ at the bar.
Do not drink the water - tastes like sea water
The pour of wine was from the bottom of the bottle and didn’t seem a full pour.
Carbonara was very salty - fine at first but gets more pronounced the more you eat.
No balsamic served with the bread and oil, no pepper offered for the pasta.
Woke at 3am with a really painful stomach having had nothing since leaving there - unsure if it’s coincidence and so haven’t rated on that, just on the few points mentioned.
Really not worth the price tag for such better experiences in the city

Very tasty boutique italian restaurant! I got an off menu item the bartender recommended which was very good and filling. It was a fettuccine noodle dish with baby shrimp and zucchini tossed is a spicy sauce (just right for me and i have high-heat tolerance). The portion was perfect for an individual. I assume their other entrees are similar size. I also ordered a basket of bread (Its appetizer plate basically; cost extra; enough for 2-3 ppl). Lastly, I ordered a smokey old fashioned. Overall,  nice lowkey restaurant. I recommend!

top_reviews.content: The first time that I ate their BLACKENED CATFISH last Friday it was very flavorful, but when I returned for a second helping yesterday, Jul 22, 2026 hoping to find some consistency I did not. The blackened catfish looked and tasted like leftovers, as did the macar& cheese. I know warmed-over food whenever I taste it. The catfish texture had no substance. Each piece (6..I purchased extra) broke apart as I tried to eat it. The macaroni, I'm certain came from the bottom of the pot. The OX TAILS that I purchased from there were so delicious that I went home and slapped my Grandma. They were fall off of the bone- superb. The muffins are not diabetic friendly at all, absolutely no corn taste. They taste like a child's birthday cake with added sugar. It could just be that the cook who was there last Saturday was not there yesterday,  and so his leftovers were sold. There us no consistency in any of the non-chain restaurants.

TLDR: great food, friendly service and sports on the tv, love it!

We got here around 7 on a weekday and had plenty of availability. I got the beef ribs in gravy and they were super tender and fall off the bone. It came with two sides and cornbread  which is plenty of food for about $25. Service was friendly and efficient, also got to watch the giants game and hangout a bit so overall great meal and a good time

Great food, Great Service, Great atmosphere.....I had the shrimp balls which were amazing. The gumbo which was absolutely delicious and the blackened catfish with Mac and cheese and potatoes and gravy! Everything was just perfect. Yummy!

ard Knox Cafe delivers a comforting, no-frills Southern dining experience that feels both nostalgic and welcoming. From the moment I walked in, the warm red tones, casual booths, and soulful décor made it feel like a neighborhood staple rather than a tourist spot. The food is hearty, generous, and clearly cooked with care this is the kind of place where comfort food truly lives up to its name. Service felt genuine and attentive without being rushed, which made the entire meal feel relaxed and enjoyable. Portions are satisfying, especially if you’re hungry or sharing dishes family-style. It’s the kind of restaurant where you linger, talk, and enjoy the atmosphere as much as the food. Overall, Hard Knox Cafe feels authentic, approachable, and deeply rooted in comfort and community.

Wasn’t impressed. The Mac and cheese had too much garlic powder in it and this isn’t catfish. Also the wrong spices for fried catfish. I’ve lived in the bay area for almost two years and I have yet to find real soul food that hits the spot. Really should open my own restaurant

top_reviews.content:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ An absolute San Francisco institution!
You can’t say you’ve truly experienced North Beach without a stop at Molinari Delicatessen. Stepping inside this legendary shop on Columbus Ave feels like being transported straight to a classic Italian deli in New York or Naples.

The Food:
The sandwiches are massive and use the highest quality meats and cheeses. The North Beach Special is a masterpiece, but you really can't go wrong with the Renzo Special or the Luciano Special.

The Bread: It’s all about the crunch! Grab your own bread from the bin at the back before heading to the counter—the Dutch Crunch and sourdough are iconic.

The Goods: Beyond sandwiches, it’s a foodie paradise stocked with imported olive oils, house-made pastas, and a deli case full of incredible cured meats.

The Vibe:
It’s bustling, chaotic in the best way, and smells like heaven (garlic and aged provolone). There's no indoor seating, so do what the locals do: grab your sub and walk a block over to Washington Square Park for the ultimate SF lunch.

Pro Tip: This place is popular for a reason. If you're visiting on a weekend, get there early to beat the rush, and remember to grab a number as soon as you walk in!

It's authentic Italian deli, market with lots of delicious stuff with variety of deli meats like prosciutto di parma aged for 18 months!
It's walk in only with looong wait line. Goes by number so pick your no as soon as step in!
Great sandwiches and breads.
Service is so delicate and despite long line they spend quality time with you to make to order your sandwich.
Parking is tough in SF and it's OK with kids as long as they can be entertained by the market stuff. Flat entry but narrow inside for accessibility. Couple small tables outside to eat in but mostly take outs.

One of the best sandwiches I've ever had. I had a porchetta sandwich on the Dutch roll. The bread was soft, the porchetta flavorful, and the fresh mozzarella was so rich. I highly recommend!

This is s bit of a wait especially on a Saturday. You also need to grab a number when you walk in, they'll call your number when they're ready!

Got the classic Italian combo. It was fine. The bread was very good. The vegetables were OK. The meats were a bit thin and overall didn’t have enough sandwich feel to it. I don’t understand why they have all pre-sliced meat stacked in the deli case that doesn’t give me the freshness that I was looking for. Also, I don’t know why those are stored next to the raw Italian sausage.

I bought 2 sandwiches a turkey basil sandwich with fresh mozzarella roasted bell pepper and sun dried tomatoes. The 2nd was a chicken cutlet with provolone cheese on a Ciabatta bread. Both sandwiches were delicious

top_reviews.content:
Ordered veggie burrito, 3 tacos and non-alcoholic aqua fresca.
-Requested to make veggie burrito wet and was accomodated for extra 4$ but there was barely any sauce specifically the green sauce was negligible.
-Tacos were mostly bland. Could have been a little more spicy and flavorful. The filling quantity was extremely less. Just one thin sheet of soft taco corn shell per taco instead of industry standard two.
-Quantity of food was very less even for non-starter items
-Aqua fresca was super diluted and tasted very basic like plain watermelon juice diluted into ice water.

Overall not a great place for food. The food is bland, very less in quantity and expensive so not worth the value. I guess the premium prices are for seemingly nice ambience which I couldn’t care less about.

Could be a good place for happy hours though. Had a long happy hour menu with reasonable pricing.

Tip: reservation required, specify inside! Fun vibes. Delicious enchiladas and tacos with classic and creative fillings (loved the cauliflower). Perfect taco shells. Wonderful service and excellent drinks. Perfect location if you are going to a show at The Masonic. Take a car service or public transportation because street parking is impossible and paid parking is wildly expensive.

I stopped by late in the evening and only ordered the churros for dessert.

The service was great—friendly, welcoming, and attentive. The staff made me feel comfortable even though I came in close to closing time, and I have nothing negative to say about the customer service.

For the churros, they were a bit disappointing. The texture suggested they may not have been freshly made. Instead of having a crisp outer layer, it was slightly soft and soggy, blending into the inside. Because of that, the texture was the biggest drawback of the dish.

However, the sugar coating was well-balanced and not overly sweet, and it paired nicely with the chocolate dipping sauce.

My wife and I used to eat here frequently when we lived here and always liked it. So on a recent visit, we made Matador our first meal. And I think it was even better than ever! We only had a small meal, but it was super tasty. The chips and salsa are fresh and the salsa was very authentic and spiced very well. The taco trio (we ordered caulifower, ground beef and chicken)  was tasty as well, the only reco would be to serve the ground beef gringo-style in a hard shell. But other than that, it's great. The people are very nice, the space is very comfortable and the tequila and wine selection is great. Go!

The atmosphere, food, & staff were amazing. I originally was going to ask to sit up front so I could watch outside passersbyers, but the hostess asked if I was interested in sitting in the back room. Curiously, I asked her to show me and decided to sit back there. It was small, quaint and beautifully decorated with Mexican art work. The female bartender / server was great.

I’ve lived in Chicago, Dallas, Austin, Irving, & Tucson, I really enjoyed the Mexican food and flavors. I loved the American authenticity of the Mexican food, it is 100 times better than TexMex, and reminded me of the Mexican food I’m used to in Chicago & Tucson.

top_reviews.content: Came for a celebration with a larger group. We were sat at the end closest to the entrance at a long table which did not feel private since everyone walks by. There was a set minimum pretax amount that was hard to hit despite buying bottles of sake and wine. Food was okay. The people who were vegetarian did need multiples of the same order to be full. There was a decent level of noise but still able to hear everyone at the table.

Absolutely exceptional experience from start to finish. Every dish felt intentional, beautifully executed, and incredibly fresh.
The nigiri was a standout. Perfectly seasoned rice with delicate, high-quality fish, topped with thoughtful touches that elevated each bite without overpowering it. The salmon dish with chili and sesame had just the right balance of heat and brightness, and the crispy rice was addictive.
The grilled shishito peppers were simple but done right, blistered with a deep, smoky flavor and finished with bonito that added a subtle umami depth. The octopus was tender and flavorful, paired with acidity and texture that made it one of the most memorable dishes of the night.
Beyond the food, the presentation was stunning across the board. Every plate felt curated, not just assembled. The atmosphere was warm and stylish, and the service was attentive without being intrusive.
This is the kind of place you go when you want sushi that feels thoughtful and elevated.
The restaurant’s interior is just stunning. We really enjoyed the ambiance here and the service was amazing! Some of the best dishes we had were the fried chicken and steak sirloin with bone marrow.
Best Japanese Steakhouse we've ever been to. From the A5 wagyu that melts like butter in your mouth, to the sushi/sashimi/nagiri and desserts - amazing menu.  Top notch service.  Will come back

pleasant atmosphere, attentive servers that are easy to get the attention of, and good food. our reservation was for 8pm and the server kindly informed us that the kitchen closed at 9 so ordering any extra food before then was acceptable. we first ordered the sashimi platter, dry aged ribeye, wagyu tartare, fresh oysters, and bone marrow. around halfway through our meal we also ordered the corn, more oysters, and a bowl of rice. the staff were very accomodating when we asked for plain rice around 9pm, didnt expect them to accept that order but they managed to fulfill it.

one issue we had was how long it took for the corn, dry aged rib eye, and bone marrow to arrive to our table. the sashimi, tartare, and oysters were quick, but the other three took much longer and didnt arrive until the 44 minute mark of the hour. otherwise, amazing service.

the oysters and bone marrow were our favorites, everything else was okay. the wasabi was textured and different from every other place we have dined at on the east and qest coast! truly wonder how roka akor prepares the wasabi.

the corn was good but what they dont tell you is that its corn on the cob halved. it's a little messy and personally i think cutting them lengthwise into quarters or thinner would ensure for a less messy experience for the customer so that customers can still use their chopsticks for the corn on the cob.

top_reviews.content: Got the 49er sandwich and it was incredible — easily one of my all-time favorite sandwiches. Packed with pastrami, brisket, and corned beef, every bite was insanely flavorful and delicious. You can really taste the quality. I’ll definitely be coming back to try the other sandwiches on the menu. Highly recommend this spot if you don’t mind splurging a bit, as it is on the pricier side for a sandwich, but absolutely worth it. Also, pro tip: come before noon because the lunch line gets long fast!

I’ve had The Deli Board saved on my Google Maps for a while, so I was excited to finally give it a try. I arrived around noon and was greeted by a line out the door. The wait ended up being about 45 minutes, but the line moved steadily and never felt frustrating.

I ordered The Bradley, which seemed similar to the 49er but without the coleslaw. The sandwich was packed with flavor and the ingredients tasted fresh and high quality. At $24, it’s definitely not a cheap lunch, but the portion size and quality helped justify the price.

One thing to note is that there’s no indoor seating, so you’ll need to find a spot nearby to eat. Even with the price and the wait, I still think The Deli Board is worth checking out. When it comes to finding one of the best burritos in town, Taqueria Guadalajara is a go-to favorite. My companion and I frequent this location often, and it never disappoints.

The Food

We ordered the chicken burritos, and as always, they were excellent. The portions are generous, the flavors bold, and each bite is loaded with tender, well-seasoned chicken. The green salsa is a standout, vibrant, flavorful, and the perfect complement to the burrito. Plus, every order comes with chips and access to the salad bar, which offers plenty of fresh options to customize your meal.

Service & Atmosphere

The staff is consistently friendly, welcoming, and quick. Whether it’s a busy lunch rush or a quieter evening, they always show up with great attitudes and efficient service. It’s the kind of place where you feel like a regular, even if it’s your first visit.

The atmosphere is simple and straightforward, nothing extravagant, but the colorful murals on the walls add a nice artistic touch that reflects the restaurant’s cultural roots. It’s a casual, no-frills spot where the focus is on good food and good vibes.

Final Thoughts

If you’re looking for consistently great burritos, friendly service, and a laid-back environment, Taqueria Guadalajara is a must-visit. The food is always fresh, flavorful, and satisfying, making it one of the best spots in town for authentic Mexican fare. Highly recommend!

Everything was so good!! Thoroughly enjoyed the meal and sitting outside. Wish they had slightly more seating and a bathroom so that's why only 3 stars for atmosphere. Potato balls were bomb!

I had the fried buttermilk chicken filet with cole slaw on French roll (fancy way to say chicken sando 🤣). The bread was fluffy with every bite, and the flavor palette works really well between the classic well-seasoned chicken patty and cole slaw combo.

To be nit picky, the proportions are a little off:
1. There was too much bread for the amount of meat and coleslaw. The cole slaw could be kept better in the sandwich if it was more finely chopped. Going from rough to fine chops allows the slaw to be more flexible (like solid to liquid) and fill out the inside volume of the sandwich instead of constantly falling out of the sandwich.
2. While the chicken was perfectly salt-and-pepper seasoned, had a nice crispy crust, and looked appetizing, it's skinnier cuts relative to the wider roll left more savoriness to be desired. Butterfly-style cuts can help produce wider chicken slabs increasing surface area-to-volume ratio enabling the display of more of its flavor.

The real thing that'd discourage me is the price and not enough seating. My friend and I paid half a benji for 2 sandwiches and potato balls that we couldn't enjoy until we got home.

Again, the above are nit picks, and wouldn't discourage me from eating here again! In fact, I'm writing this review in hopes that my feedback is valued to make the chicken sando better than it already is. :) The potato puffs are 🔥!!! And the server peeps were super friendly!

top_reviews.content:
We’ve been to Thailand more than 20 times, so we’re pretty picky when it comes to Thai food. When a restaurant gets it right, we know it immediately… and this place absolutely nailed it.

The Tom Yum soup was incredible. The aroma alone made you want to dive right in. It had that perfect balance of tangy lime, fragrant lemongrass, rich broth, and just the right amount of heat that slowly builds with every spoonful. It was one of those bowls you don’t want to end.

The Tom Kha was pure comfort. Silky, creamy coconut broth infused with galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and fresh herbs—it was rich without being heavy and so flavorful that I found myself scraping the bowl to get every last drop.

Then came the Pineapple Prawn Fried Rice… wow. Fluffy jasmine rice, sweet juicy pineapple, perfectly cooked prawns, roasted cashews, and that unmistakable smoky wok flavor. Every bite was sweet, savory, buttery, and absolutely addictive.

The Chicken Pad Thai was exactly how Pad Thai should be. Tender chicken, perfectly cooked noodles, fresh bean sprouts, peanuts, lime… and a sauce that hit every note—sweet, tangy, savory, with just enough tamarind to make every bite better than the last. We kept saying, “Just one more bite,” until suddenly the plate was empty.

The entire meal tasted incredibly fresh and authentic, and it instantly brought back memories of eating in Thailand.

On top of that, our manager, Lily, was an absolute sweetheart. She was so warm, welcoming, and genuinely kind that she made an already amazing meal even more memorable.

If you’re craving authentic Thai food that transports you straight to Thailand, do yourself a favor and eat here. We’ll definitely be back.

top_reviews.content: Sam Wo was exactly what we wanted when we were looking for a restaurant in Chinatown! The food was amazing!!! We enjoyed beef fried rice and sweet and sour chicken. Sam Wo is one of the oldest restaurants in San Francisco. Their menu has the right amount of selection and from what I’ve tasted…like their restaurant it has classic food tasting. Simple service but very attentive. Bathroom is clean with reminders how old the restaurant has been running via news clippings on the wall. It’s in SF Chinatown so you already know parking is a challenge. And yes…for traditional and classic tastes Sam Wo is a place worth coming back. 👍🏼

If you want a taste of "Old San Francisco," Sam Wo is a must-visit. Dating back to roughly 1907, it stands as one of the oldest establishments in Chinatown.

​The restaurant is split into two levels and is quite compact.
​Watch Your Head: The second floor has notably low ceilings. If you’re tall or struggle with tight spaces (claustrophobia), it’s something to keep in mind, though it adds to the quirky, historic charm.

​While the menu is smaller and more focused than your average Chinese restaurant, it hits all the nostalgic notes:
​The Legend: They are world-famous for their BBQ Pork Rice Rolls—a mandatory order. Instead of thin rice noodle rolls, this one is thick.

​You’ll find traditional staples like wonton soup, savory porridge (congee), and various noodle and vegetable dishes.
​It’s simple, no-frills, and steeped in history. Go for the rice rolls, stay for the century-old atmosphere.
Overall the foid is just ok. It is the history that make it attractive for local and tourist.
At last, don't expect a nice service.

We finally tried Sam Wo the other day!

Margherita Pizza (9/10): Outstanding work. The wood-fired crust hit a perfect baseline with beautiful, uniform leoparding. Texturally it was spot-on—not overly chewy at all. The tomato sauce was the clear star of the show, utilizing vibrant, high-quality tomatoes that balanced perfectly with the fresh basil. A textbook Neapolitan pie.

Maccaronara (8/10): A strong success. The house-made noodles had an excellent, firm al dente snap to them, holding up beautifully against a rich, properly reduced tomato sauce.

Orecchiette (6/10): A total technical failure. The quality of the base components (like the lamb sausage) was obviously high, but the kitchen completely forgot to season the dish. From the very first bite, the flavor profile was entirely flat and bland. While the noodle texture was perfectly fine, the total lack of salt or seasoning made it a chore to eat. Wound up abandoning it halfway through to go back to the pizza.

Chestnut Street has a great weekend energy right now with plenty of foot traffic. Stick strictly to the wood-fired pizza and the tomato-based pasta dishes here. Approach the alternative entrees with caution until they dial in the seasoning consistency.

Italian restaurant with a unique name.  A16 offered indoor and outdoor seating.
There’s a little courtyard behind with a few small tables. It was super busy on a Saturday night and I can tell it’s very popular.

Service was friendly and attentive. The food was good. Wine list was interesting with Californian wines.

Olives were fresh and nicely marinated in olive oil and a bit of lemon. They were very tasty and the slight touch of lemon brought out the flavours perfectly.

Burrata with prosciutto was ok. Artichoke salad was great.

Squid ink pasta with fresh crab meat was very good. Pasta was cooked al dente, chunks of crab meat and tossed with some olive oil, lemon zest.
The taste was well balanced, light on the palate with the freshness of the crab coming through.

The service was excellent and well paced. The appetiser plates were cleared before the pasta arrived. Each course was finished and cleared before the next course arrived. This attention to proper service is excellent!

It was very noisy inside the dining area. Opt for outdoor seating or the courtyard for a more quiet dining experience.

For context, I work as a host at a restaurant in the city, so I understand how reservations, walk-ins, and pacing can work. That said, this was one of the more frustrating front-of-house experiences I’ve had.

Over the course of three different evenings, I came in hoping to have dinner as a walk-in. Each time, the host immediately told me they were fully booked, but it never appeared that she actually checked availability before saying so. On one visit, I was told there may be outdoor seating available later, despite several outdoor tables being visibly open at that moment. I waited nearby for about 15 minutes to see if those tables were actually reserved, but no one arrived for them, and I also didn’t see any indoor reservations being seated during that time.

I completely understand managing flow and not overwhelming the kitchen or service staff, but from the outside it felt less like pacing and more like turning away business unnecessarily. If I were serving there, I’d be frustrated to see potential guests consistently turned away without much effort to accommodate them.

I do want to mention that one gentleman I interacted with earlier in the week was very kind and helpful. He walked me to the lounge area and explained that it was first-come, first-served, which I appreciated. Unfortunately, on the following visits when he wasn’t there, the experience was entirely different. The woman at the front offered very little information or hospitality, and each time I entered the lounge, the bartender never acknowledged me with even a simple greeting.

I’m sure the food may be excellent, but hospitality is a huge part of the dining experience. After multiple attempts, I no longer feel inclined to return to a place that made me feel unwelcome before I ever sat down.

We finished with dessert, and I was craving chocolate cake. It absolutely delivered. It was light and airy, with a melt-in-your-mouth texture that made it dangerously easy to keep eating. I honestly think I could have eaten an entire cake.

Our waiter also helped us choose a wine, and it was perfect for the meal. Overall, this was a great experience: lively atmosphere, excellent food, strong service, and a very good value for what was offered. I’ll definitely be back.
Easily one of the best stops in SF if you enjoy set menus. Exemplary service, and the food was fantastic. They wouldn't give me the recipe of the sauce for the schnitzel unfortunately.

We went here with another couple on a Friday night at 6pm. Cozy atmosphere, attentive service, great food.
One complaint is not the 36% in tax and fees (20% for service, 6% for SF health, and 10% for CA sales tax) but that the same fees apply to corkage. So the $35 corkage is actually $48. My initial thought was that the wine was diverse and reasonably priced,so bought a $109 bottle of champs off the list and brought an aged CA red from our cellar. I was surprised the alcohol tab for those 2 bottles was almost $200.
My other issue is that the space is LOUD. Maybe it was because  we were sitting next to the brick wall, or because the floors are bare and hard, or the ceiling 15-20’ high or all of the above. But I found it incredibly difficult to have a table conversation for 4. So, my recommendation is only go with one other person that you really like so you can lean in to talk to each other.

Overall, The Melt is an excellent restaurant that I would highly recommend to anyone looking for flavorful food and outstanding service. I look forward to visiting again and trying more items from their menu. It is a place that truly deserves a 5-star rating.

Just touched down in San Francisco and passed by this place! Have already been here twice for their meltburger! Love the pickle and jalapeño mix. Service is always quick and easy..staff was helpful and friendly. Food comes out fresh and hot. A very chill spot..with great people watching from every way!

The self serve condiment station was gross with globs of ketchup in the tray.

top_reviews.content: Kevin’s Noodle House is a staple in San Francisco/ Bay Area. I enjoyed a nice bowl of pho on a cloudy Tuesday afternoon. The menu is easy to read and the numbers make ordering quick. I ordered the number 1 large. The bowl arrived in less than two minutes. The service here is fast and they really mastered their process. The hot tea is a nice touch and the usually vegetables on the side dish was just right. The pho broth is is always healing and adding the spices and ingredients makes each pho bowl customizable. This is easily one of the classic Pho spots in the Bay Area.

I LOVE when pho places (or any places) have a small size option that is actually small. As someone who can never finish a full sized portion and frequently forgets to eat leftovers this was perfect.
The pho itself was also delicious, noodles were the perfect texture and soup flavor was good. Service was also super fast.

When I first tried out their pho, I remember thinking it tasted so familiar until I learned there are two other locations in Daly City, which are the ones I used to go to. So happy they also have a location in the city, so I can get my fix! Highly recommend coming early since line can be long during lunch and dinner hours. However, if you come during those busy hours, don't worry, the line moves fast here!
Grilled pork + shrimp cake + sunny side egg with rice. Absolutely delicious! Quiet for around 230-3pm. Service staff polite and attentive.

My son and I are absolute pho lovers. We'd love to cook it, we'd love to eat it, we love to buy it, we'd love to talk about it. In this pho exceeded expectations. It has hole in the wall prices, and a casual neighborhood vibe, but the inside of the restaurant is well maintained, the ingredients are high-quality, the broth is delicious, and generous with the meat which is also high-quality. And the bean sprouts and herbs are so fresh! I was shocked at the value that we got for $15 a full. At this price point you can't be the value, the taste, the quality and the experience. Five stars all the way!

top_reviews.content: Seating was limited but was given a spot at the bar immediately. Very clean and well-kept, with a calm but busy dinner ambiance. Bathroom was very clean and spacious. Best ramen experience I’ve had in SF!
The chicken thigh was packed with flavor, even inside the meat (you know when it’s seasoned just right 👌). The broth was so rich and creamy, but perfectly balanced, not too salty and not too plain either. Everything came together so well, from the texture of the noodles to the depth of the broth. I left super satisfied and already craving it again. Definitely a spot I’ll come back to!

top_reviews.content: Always love our dinners at Bix! The ambiance of the restaurant is elegantly reminiscent of a bygone era, with its dim lighting and classic jazz tunes played by a live band. It sets a perfect mood for a sophisticated dinner. The attentive and knowledgeable staff are the best! Although the specific dishes I ordered escape my memory, each course was exquisitely prepared, capturing the essence of fine dining with flavors that were both complex and satisfying. One of my favorite aspects of the evening at Bix was the seamless blend of excellent service and delightful live music! I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a special night out in San Francisco.

such a vibe! The live jazz music really sets the tone, and the cocktails are epic. Even as someone who doesn’t drink, I was impressed by how good the non-alcoholic options were.

I came for dinner with three friends, and overall it was a really fun experience. The Sakura Pork Chop was super flavorful and definitely one of the highlights on the savory side. The duck was decent—not bad, but not the standout dish.

I’d skip the market salad—it wasn’t that great and didn’t live up to the rest of the menu.

Dessert, though, completely stole the show. The Warm Chocolate Brioche Bread Pudding and the Tarte Tatin were absolutely incredible—easily my favorite part of the meal and worth coming back for alone.

Great atmosphere, great desserts, and a perfect spot for a lively night out with friends.

I just came down to check out the place and ended up on a seat at the bar sipping on two cocktails. The place has a after work vibe and generally relaxed. The staff is good at their job but customers are catching seats or disturbing other customers like a being on a local train!

We will definitely return to enjoy the live music, drinks, and seasonal fare.

top_reviews.content:
The experience was genuinely disappointing. The service was very slow from the start, and more concerning, even when it was clear the grill was burning, the staff did nothing about it, as if they didn’t care.

At one point, I called a waiter and was completely ignored, which made the experience even worse. I understand that places can get busy, but that wasn’t the case here—there were only about seven tables occupied.

Overall, the service left a lot to be desired. I’ve been to many Korean restaurants, and considering the value for the price, this experience was not good enough to make me want to come back.
We were seated pretty fast considering we went during dinner time (7pm) so that’s a plus. The menu selections were on the smaller but had the basic meats. Service was alright.

My partner and I are big Korean BBQ fans and go often back home in NYC, so we were excited to try YakiniQ for the first time. Unfortunately, it didn’t live up to expectations. The food was just okay and lacked flavor, even on the premium plate. The beef bulgogi didn’t really taste like beef, and overall, nothing stood out.

Service was also disappointing. After waiting an hour to be seated, it took another 10 minutes before anyone checked in to take our order, and the couple next to us (who arrived after) were served first. Even water took about 20 minutes to arrive….

I also didn’t realize it was self-cook, which might be fine for some, but the experience felt very “here’s your meat, good luck.” The ventilation could use improvement too; the smoke builds up quickly and makes your eyes sting.

Overall, not the experience we were hoping for.

YakiniQ has some strong points, but overall, my experience fell short. As a first timer in a Korean BBQ costumer, I’ll start with the positives: the service is truly outstanding. The waitstaff is attentive, patient with explaining the process and how it works, friendly and quick, making you feel well taken care of throughout the meal.

Now, the downsides: the food, unfortunately, lacked flavor. For a BBQ spot, I was expecting bold and exciting tastes, but it just wasn’t there. The restaurant also felt overcrowded, and with poor ventilation, the smoke from the grills clings to your clothes—definitely not ideal.

At $45 per person, there are plenty of options for prime cuts. A big issue was the automatic 18% service fee for parties of 5 or more. While this isn’t unusual, the waiters should clearly explain this policy upfront, especially before asking for an additional tip. For those like me who don’t pay close attention to the bill, this feels misleading and can leave a bad taste after an otherwise polite dining experience.

Would I go again? Probably. The service is excellent, but transparency around the service charge is a must.

Love this place. Met the manager from here, Aaron Tan, who was very welcoming and made our first experience here unforgettable. Amazing service, food, and all around great vibes! If anyone is looking for a place for some sensational Korean BBQ, this is it.

Small Thai restaurant with charm of the main strip in Inner Sunset.  Went on a weekday at 6pm and plenty of open tables.  Pad Thai had a nice charred wok flavor, but could use more sauce and flavor (definitely added some chili sauce to give it a boost).  The pad see eew was perfectly cooked and tasty.  The Thai egg rolls stole the show!  They were hot, crispy, and delicious!  We enjoyed this meal with an iced Thai tea.  So good!

We got the pad see ew and khao soi and it genuinely made me think about how much I appreciate life. Normally when I go out with my wife we eat at a decent pace and talk about things from our day but today we scarfed down our food and the only thing we talked about was how good it was. Happen to come across this joint on my way to the Giants game. If you're looking for a soul food with character, great music, and downright delicious eats, Little Skillet is a must-visit. Tucked away near Oracle Park, this hidden gem serves up Southern classics that hit all the right notes.

The biscuits? Buttery and flakey perfection served with honey butter. The blackened shrimp with grits was flavorful, and balanced. The fried shrimp with mashed potatoes? A combo that's both indulgent and deeply satisfying. And the fried chicken? Crispy, juicy, and everything you'd hope for from a true Southern kitchen.

Little Skillet delivers big on taste, with a warm and welcoming atmosphere that makes you feel right at home. Whether you're a local or just passing through, this hole-in-the-wall is worth seeking out. Highly recommend!

top_reviews.content: Friendly staff accommodated our group of five during a busy lunch hour. We ordered rainbow salad, samusas, cheesy garlic noodles with pork belly, eggplant curry, chicken fried rice (my name), and a pork and potato lunch special with tea leaf salad. To start, the lunch special served was chicken with mango, not the pork that was ordered. Fortunately, it was a happy accident because it was the best dish. The rainbow salad was good but watery. The samusas were filled with potato, which would have been good if the filling was flavorful. It was not. It tasted like boiled potatoes with little seasoning. The cheesy garlic noodles lacked savoriness, it required more salt and cheese and did not even have a hint of oyster sauce as listed on the menu. The eggplant was good but the eggplant seemed like it wasn't cooked in the curry for long of at all. Also, they charge for white rice even with a curry dish. The fried rice was enjoyed by some in our party but I found it lackluster. Overall, the experience was mediocre. If the staff were not exceptional, which they were - shout out to Chuy - I would have given this a lower rating given the cost of the fare. Sure it's expensive in Alameda but no more than comparable restaurants where we live in the DC area. FYI they're are Burmese restaurants where we live.

Yum…?

While Burma Superstar has good food, their dishes lack one thing or another.
We started off our dining experience with the tea leaf salad. While I did not eat it personally (I’m not a big fan of salads), my peers reported that it was tasty but somewhat bitter.
After that, we got the paratha and the ‘sauce’ (not sure what to call it). While the paratha was sweet, the sauce took away from the sweetness and as a result it wasn’t as sweet as I would have liked.
To follow, we got the fiery tofu. It was delicious, and spicy. (Again, according to my peers)
Then we got the coconut noodle soup. It was large, not coconut-y at all, and the soup was thick like gravy. Would not recommend.
All in all, food was good, but make sure you don’t mind a flaw or two.

Service

While they only checked on us once or twice, the staff was friendly and gave great food recommendations.

This place is noisy inside, and you get the regular traffic noise outside.

I have eaten at this place before. I came with a group of four for dinner and we waited almost an hour to get in because of the mass good reviews. It was great the first time. Nope I wonder if the first meal tasted good because of how hungry we were or it was too dark to see the plates.
Now, would I come back again… hmmm. The food did taste good. The eggplant was good quality and it literally melted before it got to my mouth. The green beans weren’t fresh. You can tell from how faded they were and the fork couldn’t get in to poke them. I think that was the only old ingredient.

After trying several other spots in the area, I keeps coming back to Burma Superstar because they truly understand flavor, texture, and value. Unlike other restaurants that serve "watered down" versions of Southeast Asian cuisine, the food here is consistently rich and intentional.
1. Tea Leaf Salad:
This is easily the best in the West Bay. The mix of fermented tea leaves, fried garlic, crunchy yellow split peas, and seeds creates an incredible depth of flavor. It’s a party of textures in your mouth, savory, salty, and a little bit of a caffeine kick. It's an experience you can't easily replicate at home.
2. Chicken Curry:
This is exactly how a curry should be. The chicken thighs are incredibly tender, and the sauce is a thick, aromatic stew of coconut milk and turmeric. It isn't "soupy" or thin; it's hearty and clings perfectly to the rice (or the platha!). You can tell the flavors have been simmering for a long time.
3. Value and Service:
Yes, it’s a popular spot and can get busy, but the quality justifies the price. You get generous portions and professional service. You never feel like you're paying a "premium" just for the aesthetic, you're paying for top-tier execution.
If you want a meal that is actually satisfying and full of authentic flavor, skip the "trendy" places and just come here. It never fails.

And shout-out to our server Timothy his services was indeed A1 during dinner rush and during the world cup no less!

top_reviews.content:
Since moving to Hayes Valley, I've been here at Papito Hayes about six or seven times for lunch, so I think I'm ready to share some thoughts about this place.

Walking in, you're greeted with a friendly atmosphere and a beautiful mural. The service is polite and chill, and they usually invite me to sit wherever I'd like at the small open tables inside. There's also a small outdoor area if you'd rather sit outside.

The staff always have a friendly buzz about them and seem to all be friends, which I like to see. It gives the place a welcoming feeling.

Compared to some of the other places nearby, this spot has slightly cheaper options, but expect to spend close to $30 per person.

By far my favorite things to order are the chicken soup and the asada enchiladas.

The way the enchiladas are served is unique and adds to the flavor of the dish. The rice and beans are placed beneath the enchiladas in a small skillet, so all the juices and sauce drip into them, which makes it a pleasure to tuck into. The asada enchiladas also come with a tasty red sauce, and the smoky bites of steak inside each enchilada make me devour them every time.

I've also tried the pork enchiladas, which are pretty good for similar reasons. The chicken enchiladas weren't for me—but that might just be because I don't really like the taste of mole.

For $9, you're served a surprisingly filling bowl of chicken soup with rice. The rice is never mushy, and the broth is really savory and moreish, probably because it's made with bone broth. It also comes with plenty of chicken and vegetables, plus a big pile of cilantro, which I really like.

I've also tried a bunch of their tacos. I wouldn't recommend the duck confit tacos, as they're a little too sweet in my opinion. However, the Baja-style fish tacos are really nice, as are the fried chicken tacos. They're not super traditional, but they're tasty and balanced with a little cilantro and salad in each.

If you ask, they'll also give you a small bottle of what seems to be homemade habanero sauce. I consider myself pretty good with spicy food, but this stuff is actually pretty hot, so be careful with it.

There was one time when they didn't really hit the mark. I ordered the chicken soup, as I always do, and it came out tasting much blander than usual, with much drier chicken. I let the staff know, and they gave me a discount, which was nice.

Overall, I really like the vibe of this place and the bright flavors they offer. Compared to Souvla nearby which I'd put in a similar bracket, I prefer to come here. I'll definitely be coming back for lunch again.

Papito Hayes is a good Mexican spot in Hayes Valley for lunch or brunch with great vibes. The food quality is solid, but honestly it lacked flavor overall. Even the habanero salsa wasn’t spicy, which was surprising. Didn’t get a chance to try their drinks, but would come back for the ambiance and give it another shot.
Solid take on Mexican favorites (don’t expect Abuelita’s cooking) and it’s a great spot for a happy hour with friends! I recommend you get a couple of apps to share, especially the guacamole!

We were lucky enough that there was bar seating when we arrived (walk ins), and we eat dinner early , yup at that stage of our lives

Sangria red: perfectly sweet and great with our meal

Highlights:
Tocino: that pork belly was so incredibly delicious and melted in my mouth

Pulpo: the best octopus I have ever had

The rest of the meal also tasty, but had to highlight those

The torta was delish but a little too sweet, the dusting of powdered sugar while pretty was not needed imo. The olive oil is a nice touch.

The food itself was good. I haven't had Spanish cuisine before, so it was new and interesting to me. Our favorites were the Colifor, Buñuelos, Hamburguesas Morunas, and Arroz Negro. The flavors were solid, though some dishes leaned on the saltier side for my personal preference. That said, paying $65 for a paella with such a small amount of protein is disappointing. Especially compared to the advertised picture of Arroz Negro.

The restaurant had a very chill, relaxed, atmosphere. A good place for a casual outing or evening date. Everything was clean and pleasant.

We had a weekday reservation at 5pm and spent a little over an hour and a half dining, during which there was almost no service at all. At least 3-5 tables were empty throughout the entirety of our meal, so it definitely wasn't due to the restaurant being overwhelmed. After placing our initial order, we didn't see our server for 45 minutes (time stamped, yes). When we wanted to order more food, we had to ask the food runner to find someone. Even then, it took another 15 minutes before someone finally came to take our order.

No one refilled our water even once, and no one checked in to see if we needed anything. We saw servers refilling water at other tables, but they never came to ours. Servers were basically nowhere to be found, to the point where when I finally saw one closing out another table, I handed her my card before she could run away because I was worried she'd disappear again and we wouldn't be able to pay for another business day.

We added a bottle of sparkling water to our bill before closing it out but it wasn't brought out until we were waiting at the door ready to leave, that was also after when we had to ask again for it.

At no point were we acknowledged for being ignored. Nothing like "It's busy tonight" or "We're short staffed". We would've understood if there were special circumstances, but we received nothing aside from what felt like attitude and impatience from the waitresses. (God bless them, hope they had a better night than I did)

The experience left us speechless. For a place where per-person spending is $100+, the service was shockingly bad (although is it really "bad" if it were nonexistent?) The menu deserved better service. Just stick to DoorDashing or takeout.

Hopefully others won't have the same experience we did.

Edit: The owner kindly reached out to us in regard to our experience. We appreciated the effort from their end to better the situation and improve their quality of service.

The Caesar was a generous portion for two and overall good, though the dressing was lighter than expected. The croutons were excellent and easily the standout of the salad. The large cioppino was the highlight. The broth looked tomato based but leaned more toward spiced flavors than tomato. It was filled with crab, crab legs, shrimp, fish, clams, and mussels, all well prepared, and bibs were provided since it can get messy. top_reviews.content: Lovely spot to eat. Our server was very attentive and professional.  The food was delicious! We split a clam chowder and it was perfect! We ordered the linguine with meatballs & fettuccine with smoked salmon in pesto sauce. Everything was perfect.

Absolutely love this place. My wife and I found this hidden gem last summer on a weekend trip to SF. So when I was in town one night for business, we made a drive intro eh city for a great dinner before our flight.

Lucky for us it was a rainy Tuesday night and we didn’t have to wait for a table.  The service here is so good! They had fresh bread (and I mean piping hot fresh sourdough straight out of the oven) on the table in a couple minutes.

I had the clam chowder and it was so friggin good! Amazing taste and chuck of clams spread out in almost every bite. Then I ordered the same thing I got last time, linguine with seafood 🍤 🍣! The pasta is done of the best homemade pasta I’ve ever eaten. They literally pack this full of clams, mussels, calamari and a giant scallop and shrimp. I love that they don’t scrimp on the seafood.

Definitely a hidden secret but my first choice for authentic Italian In little Italy 🇮🇹!

We eat at many decent restaurants and felt the seafood linguine (with 2 different sauces) was loaded with seafood and very tasty, and the classic cioppino was even a level above the linguine! The heaps of seafood were immersed in an exceptionally complex tomato-based sauce that will be remembered for a long time.

Visited with our toddler (tired and hungry). Food was brought out quickly for him (and was delicious) but he wasn’t in the mood to eat so got quite cranky. My husband took him outside to try settle him so I could eat, and the staff, or one lady at least, made us feel bad by closing the windows while my husband was outside calming my son. I appreciate people don’t want to listen to a whinging toddler, but you don’t have to be obvious about it. We weren’t even there late, has a 5pm booking, reasonable for young children. The chef as well told my son not to break wooden animal figurines left out near our table even though he wasn’t even rough playing with them, and we were watching him as well to make sure he didn’t do anything wrong. I felt a bad vibe from the staff at the restaurant, and may have been while my son didn’t settle there. We’ve been travelling a lot around the US the least week and a half and this is the least comfortable he’s been.

The food otherwise was delicious. I had the seafood linguine in the tomato cream sauce and my husband had the lobster ravioli in the tomato cream sauce. Great flavours and fresh seafood. Just a shame about the service.

A Must-Order at Betty Lou’s

Ever since we discovered the Wok Crab at Betty Lou’s, we’ve been hooked.

This casual spot in Little Italy is known for its standout seafood, and the Wok Crab is the dish that keeps us coming back. The crab is sautéed with cilantro and scallions, along with plenty of garlic and ginger, all brought together in a savory soy-based sauce that coats every bite. It’s the kind of dish where you’ll definitely want extra bread on the table—perfect for soaking up every last bit of that incredible sauce.

The atmosphere is relaxed and welcoming, and the service is consistently friendly and attentive.

A nice bonus: they allow you to bring your own bottle of wine for a $25 corkage fee, which makes the meal even more enjoyable.

Yarsa Napalese Cuisine in San Francisco offers an authentic and delightful journey for the taste buds, making it a must-visit for anyone craving high-quality South Asian flavors. Based on my recent order, everything was executed beautifully, from the rich curries to the fresh sides.
​The Stars of the Show
​Chicken Tikka Masala: This classic dish was a creamy revelation. The chicken was incredibly tender, and the sauce struck a perfect balance--rich and flavorful without being overly heavy or sweet. It's easily one of the best versions I've had in the city.
​Saag Curry Lamb: A true highlight! The lamb was cooked to perfection, falling apart with gentle pressure. The Saag (spinach) curry itself was deeply savory and earthy, seasoned masterfully to complement the meat. It had a wonderful, comforting depth of flavor.
​Sides & Bread Perfection
​Yellow Rice with Vegetables: This was a vibrant and flavorful accompaniment. The rice was perfectly cooked--fluffy and separate--and the inclusion of fresh, tender vegetables (carrots, peas, etc.) made it a substantive and refreshing side dish.
​Garlic Cheese Naan: Absolutely essential! The naan was warm, pillowy, and generously stuffed with melted cheese and fresh garlic. It wasn't greasy, and the balance of savory garlic and gooey cheese made it irresistible for dipping into the curry sauces.
​Overall Verdict
​Yarsa Napalese Cuisine delivers an exceptional dining experience. The ingredients taste fresh, the spices are complex and aromatic, and the preparation shows genuine care and expertise. If you're looking for fantastic Nepalese and Indian classics in San Francisco, look no further. This place is a gem! The service was great ! The waiter was very friendly and it was a nice vibe in. The restaurant.
​Highly Recommended Dishes: Chicken Tikka Masala and Saag Curry Lamb.

top_reviews.content: This is such a nice local hot pot restaurant. I love how many side dishes you can pick from. Every ingredient we tried was fresh. Imo food quality was similar to hidilao.

Will probably be back.

The combo 2 with Wanyu beef is amazing.
I do love their tomato and tom yum base soups.
The combo for 2 portions is big enough for 2.5 people.
But you can choose the add-on.
The self-help sauce bar is good, but they could provide extra salad, which could be better.

Near by street and garage parking are available.

I’m sharing this as a business owner who wants to see this place succeed.

Food quality was solid and the concept is strong. We enjoy hot pot often and the experience shows good potential.

This visit had a few operational gaps that are easy to fix:
•	Wait time was about 45 minutes for a party of 6
•	18% service charge is applied upfront. That sets expectations for consistent service
•	Water refills were slow. We had to signal multiple times. The manager helped when available
•	Spice station needs frequent cleaning. Spills were visible and not addressed quickly
•	Empty plates stayed on the table too long. This impacts comfort and table turnover

Simple improvements would make a big difference:
•	Assign rotation for spice station checks every 10–15 minutes
•	Add a clear system for water refills
•	Bus tables more actively during service
•	Align service level with the fixed service charge

I was going to give 4 stars, but leaving 3 to make sure this feedback gets attention. I will come back and hope to update this after improvements.

top_reviews.content:
​We stopped by Hideout Kitchen for lunch. If you're looking for a nice venue with an open atmosphere and easy parking, this spot definitely checks those boxes. The space is bright and spacious, offering the flexibility to sit either inside or outside.

​The Food
​The food here is good, but I wouldn't call it great. It's solid enough that I can't complain about the quality, but the main drawback is the pricing—everything feels quite expensive for what you get.

​The Breakfast Burrito: it comes wrapped in a vibrant red tortilla, stuffed with eggs, potatoes, and cheese, and served with a side of tater tots and dipping sauce. While it tasted perfectly fine, it has to be the most expensive breakfast burrito I've ever bought.

​The Frittata / Omelet: this dish is packed with vegetables, topped with crumbled goat cheese, and served with rustic toast, butter, fresh fruit slices, and a sweet jam or compote on the side.
​Service & Logistics

​The Service: Overall, the staff was perfectly friendly and the service was good. However, water management could be improved—I felt like I constantly had to keep asking for refills.
​Watching a Game? Keep in mind that they only have a few TVs on-site. If you are planning to head down specifically to catch a game, make sure to ask to be seated inside so you actually have a clear view of a screen.

​The Verdict
​If you want to enjoy a very nice venue and don't mind paying premium, somewhat overpriced fees for standard brunch food, Hideout Kitchen fits the bill.

The Atmosphere & Location

The ambiance here is fantastic—perfect for a date night or grabbing drinks with friends. It’s easily accessible and located in a beautiful shopping area, which is one of its strongest points.

—

The Food: Hits & Misses
• The Best Part: The Truffle Fries were excellent and a huge hit with the kids! The toast-based dishes were also very tasty, and the mashed potatoes were a highlight.

• The Risotto: Quite disappointing for the price (nearly $50). The portion was very small, and while it had a strong seafood flavor, the seasoning felt unbalanced, which slightly overshadowed the texture of the rice.

• The Mains: The fried chicken was a bit too sweet for my liking, and the burger patty lacked that "juicy" feel. The regular fries were just average.

• The Sides: The green vegetable side was quite salty and definitely needed to be eaten with the mashed potatoes to balance it out.
Value for Money

—

To be honest, I found it overpriced. We ordered five items, and the bill came to $150+ before tip. Given the small portion sizes and inconsistent flavors, you can likely find better value elsewhere at this price point.

Summary: Come for the vibe and the great location, but be prepared for a higher tab relative to the portions.

He explained what the specials were and provided great service. Unfortunately, the evening was tremendously dampened when our table was approached by a woman who didn’t introduce herself and decided that in spite of the fact that there were two empty chairs to our left and right, it was necessary to remove our coat and purse that was occupying the empty chair at our table and those items were placed in the seating beside me along the cushioned bench and she proceeded to take our chair and provide it to another table. Although we were perplexed by this we carried on with our evening. Our food was served and we ate and had the remainder boxed
to go and decided to have desert. As we sat sharing our Tiramisu and Chocolate cake, the same rude unidentified woman approached our table for the second time and rudely asked us if we were taking our deserts to go, my friend who was paying for the evening informed her that she had just given our server her card to pay and the rude woman said, “Ok, because we’re going to need this table shortly.” and sauntered off. My friends who have patronized this establishment several times were stunned and both said that they had never been approached in this manner before and needless to say, I was utterly flabbergasted. I have no intention of ever returning to this restaurant because of this so-called hostess. There’s a right way and a wrong way to do anything and the way that woman treated us was disrespectful, rude and very inconsiderate. She certainly didn’t represent this establishment in a good way and left a very bitter taste in my mouth. Aside from her terrible antics, the food was fine but she dampened an otherwise lovely evening for myself and my friends and didn’t represent the Hideout Kitchen in a good way at all. For service I rate JP a five star, however the so-called hostess’s antics makes the overall rating two stars for service and she ruined the atmosphere, so I give that a one star.

The staff was amazing, the atmosphere was amazing, and there was a line down the sidewalk waiting for the restaurant to open even though we all seemed to have reservations. Everything we ordered was great. The focaccia was soft and crisp at the same time, with strawberry cream filling inside, probably the best focaccia I have had. The pizza was the first pizza I have had that I want to finish up all the crust, it was made in sourdough, so delicious!
