Very popular, nice Italian restaurant in Divis that's a great choice for a date night or special occasion.

The restaurant is located upstairs with a rustic loft interior featuring hanging dried flowers and with a glass area with hanging meat. It's huge, with tons of tables, and was packed. We arrived at 6:30pm on a Thursday and managed to get a walk-in table for two, but every other table was full and even the bar was packed, so I wouldn't count on walking in. Despite being packed with close-knit tables, my friend and I were able to carry on a conversation without issue. This may be because we were at a booth at the back.

The menu features salads, handmade pizza, & handmade pasta. It's on the pricier side for Italian restaurants in San Francisco. The food was delicious, but the pasta & salad portions were too small (and we're two thin women!). The pizza crust was soft, fluffy, & delicious. The menu featured unique dishes with seasonal ingredients. Everything we ordered was delicious and I'd go back to try other menu items.

I'd go back here for a date night or a special night out, but it's too pricy to return to frequently.

I rarely leave negative reviews, but our experience at Che Fico was disappointing from start to finish.

We had a 9:00 PM reservation and arrived around 7:00 PM to see if there was any possibility of being seated earlier. We completely understand that restaurants can be fully booked and that accommodating an earlier table may not be possible. However, the hostess’s attitude was unnecessarily cold and dismissive when informing us that no earlier seating was available.

When we returned at 8:50 PM for our reservation, the experience only got worse. We were directed to a “waiting area” without any explanation of what it was or why we needed to wait. After standing there confused for about 10 minutes, we finally asked for clarification. We were then told that we could not be seated before 9:00 PM because our reservation was for 9:00 PM. I don't know whether that make sense.

Unfortunately, the food did not make up for the poor service. Both appetizers we ordered were overly salty and excessively acidic, lacking the balance and refinement I would expect from a restaurant recognized by the Michelin Guide. The overall dining experience fell far short of the expectations created by its reputation.

Given both the service and food quality we experienced, I don’t believe Che Fico currently delivers the level of hospitality or execution that justifies its inclusion on the Chase Sapphire Reserve Exclusive Tables list. There are many restaurants in San Francisco that provide a much warmer welcome and a significantly better dining experience.

This was an interesting experience. We wanted to try something new and Che Fico is always on every list of must try places so we thought we'd try it out. I'll start with the pros and then move into what didn't work for me.

Pros: The Giardinera Martini is really good and something you don't see every day. Personally I liked the foccacia and the stronger Fennel taste but that's just me. My pasta had a filling with nettle which also was new for me, and good.

But overall the service was all over the place. Sometimes we were rushing, sometimes there was no one. We came right at our reservation and we were told to go to the "waiting area" which is just a bar, with people super busy to take orders. Its Friday night so its going to be busy, I. get it. But tables were also empty. Also, its very pricy. I don't mind spending money when the food blows you away, and in SF there are several places that you can get that at. My experience at Che Fico just seemed like it was "dining out on its own reputation."

Still, they have been around for a while so maybe its worth trying again. Or maybe just for some drinks and a snack.

We had such an incredible meal at Che Fico. Every single thing we ordered was outstanding! Truly one of those dinners where you keep looking at each other after every bite.
Beyond the food, the atmosphere completely makes the experience. The open kitchen brings so much energy to the room.  Every table was full, music was playing, the space felt alive and somehow it still felt intimate enough to easily talk and actually hear my partner. That balance is rare and they nail it.
We sat at the chef’s counter and I absolutely loved watching the kitchen in motion. Seeing the team move and then tasting the dishes as they came out made it even more special.
The focaccia was phenomenal. The pasta with their bolognese was rich.  The pizza was my personal favorite perfectly balanced and beautifully executed. And the crostata? Eyes-rolling-to-the-back-of-my-head good.
Absolutely incredible. No notes.

top_reviews.content:
Jong Ga House is the real deal if you’re looking for an authentic Korean meal. The food was excellent, the staff was wonderful, and the entire experience felt genuine and welcoming.

We tried quite a few dishes, and there were some definite standouts. The bulgogi was amazing, tender and packed with flavor. We also really liked the spicy pork, which had a great balance of heat and flavor. The hot pot bibimbap was another hit, arriving sizzling hot with that wonderful crispy rice developing along the bottom.

The kalbi had excellent flavor, although the meat was a little chewier than I would have liked. I’m also a fan of Korean BBQ cooked over charcoal, so I would have preferred charcoal grills to the gas grills they use here. There’s just something about that smoky charcoal flavor that takes Korean BBQ to another level.

Those are relatively minor complaints, though. Overall, we had a great meal with plenty of dishes we’d happily order again. Great food, wonderful service, and an authentic experience. Definitely a place I’d return to.

Authentic Korean barbecue with bold, traditional flavors and high-quality meats. The grilling experience at the table makes it interactive and fun, and the banchan selection really completes the meal. Service was attentive, and the overall atmosphere made it a very enjoyable dining experience. I’d definitely come back.

Very delicious, authentic, and affordable Korean food! I ordered the beef stew and friend got fried fish, both of which were amazing! The service was also fast and professional. Located in a convenient location with plenty of street parking. So much variety on the menu as well! I want to come back to try the other dishes for sure.

Five of us tried Jong Ga House for the first time today. The food was delicious and we all had fun.

I'd give it 5 stars, except for the staff was not very welcoming. The boss was nice, but that was it.

The prices were reasonable considering the amount and quality of the food.

If you like hot pot (shabu-shabu), or you want a culinary adventure, then I definetely recommend you give it a try.

Extremely disappointing birthday experience

I came here to celebrate my birthday with my birthday cake and was expecting a fun Korean BBQ dinner. Instead, the way I was treated—especially by our server, Eddie—completely ruined the celebration.

I celebrate my birthday according to the Chinese lunar calendar. When I asked about the birthday discount, Eddie refused to honor it because my Chinese birthday apparently did not count as a valid birthday. I understand that restaurants can have rules for promotions, but the issue was not just the discount. It was the dismissive and indifferent attitude that came with it.

I found the whole interaction disrespectful. I had my birthday cake sitting right there, and I was clearly there to celebrate my birthday. Rather than explaining the policy with basic courtesy, Eddie made me feel like my birthday and the cultural tradition behind it were not legitimate.

As a Chinese customer, I found that especially upsetting. A Chinese lunar-calendar birthday is still a birthday. If the restaurant has a strict policy requiring a government ID or only recognizes the Gregorian calendar for its promotion, then state that clearly. There is absolutely no reason to make a customer feel belittled over a cultural difference.

The service throughout the meal also felt cold, unfriendly, and indifferent. There was no effort to make the situation better or even acknowledge how poorly it was handled. What should have been a happy birthday dinner ended with me feeling unwelcome and disrespected.

I’m not upset over a discount. I’m upset over how I was treated. There is a big difference between politely saying, “Unfortunately, our promotion only applies to the birthday listed on your ID,” and treating someone’s cultural tradition like it is not real.

Management should seriously address how Eddie and the staff handle situations like this. Customers from different cultural backgrounds deserve the same basic respect as everyone else. I would not choose this restaurant again after this experience.

top_reviews.content:
Deserving of the hype.

Every single bite was special. One of those meals where you’re talking about going back before you’ve even finished your first dish.

We started with the cold peanut eggplant (which we liked but didn’t love - bit too much peanut sauce), and then did the mapo tofu (the best we’ve ever had - spectacular), the lobster cheung fun (wow), and the pork char siu (wow). Amazing whiskey peanut cocktail.

A bit surprised to see some of the other reviews calling out service (we thought it was excellent). Obviously not cheap ($350 all in for 3 people).

Great fusion of Chinese flavors and and western dining. They don’t skimp out on their portions and the service was also great. All of the dishes were solid, and the cheung fun was my personal favorite. It was served in pasta style, but the tastes were very Chinese with that XO flavor coming through. It felt like eating a delicious plate of pasta with much easier digestion due to the rice noodles. Another favorite was the scallion milk bread - you get that amazing scallion flavor as if you’re eating Chinese scallion pancakes, but through the soft milky bread with the melted butter. The salt and pepper shrimp crackers were a great appetizer to start the meal as well.

The lamb dumplings were savory and had a sharp spicy level, so might not be food for people with low tolerance. The dirty fried rice was slightly under seasoned and I did t enjoy the stickiness of the okra as much in fried rice. But still solid and great portions.

We had an amazing dinner here, and every dish hit the mark. The Fortune cocktail was the perfect start, and the shrimp chip and salmon dip is an absolute must-try. The chopped pork and dirty rice were packed with rich flavor, perfectly balanced by the fresh crunch of the snap peas. (Pro-tip: don't skip their incredible chili sauces!)
​What made the night even better was our server, Cry, who was attentive, welcoming, and provided the best service. We’ll definitely be back!

I can see why this one star Michelin restaurant is getting mixed reviews - the signature peijing duck is dry and very hard to chew. We also ordered ma po tou fu which is good. A small cucumber starter not bad, and a lobster fry noddle which is not great. I really don’t see this place how it become Michelin starred.

Two of us opened 450$. Comparing with my other Michelin experience - not that great.

My wife and I randomly picked Mr. Jiu's from a Google search in order to experience SF's Chinatown and WOW were we impressed. The staff seated us immediately (at the bar albeit) and we were attended instantly (by three bar employees), all personnel being very hospitable and knowledgeable :) The food (shrimp chips and the strawberry dessert) did not disappoint, and the beer(s) complimented well. Personally, the playlist was the cherry on top and pushed this place to 5 stars and spurred me to take pics! The price point was listed as ~$100, but we spent way less and still left happy and satisfied...I would for sure come here to meet friends, take a date, or have a meeting! Definitely worth stopping in if you are looking for food in Chinatown and want a high-end flare to the night :)

We really enjoyed our time at Lazy Bear. We loved the origin story of the restaurant. An impressive pandemic-era parklet execution, but a return visit is required for the true experience.

I visited Lazy Bear in March of 2021 during their outdoor parklet chapter. While the safety protocols meant missing out on the energy of their true communal indoor dining room, the team did a remarkable job transitioning an elevated, high-end experience to a temporary sidewalk setup.

I must note that as someone who doesn't care for duck, this turned out to be a highly challenging menu for my personal palate, as duck heavily anchored the meal. However, looking past my subjective protein preferences, the technical execution and sheer creativity of the presentation were undeniable. Every course I was served showed precise artistry despite the outdoor environment, from the intricate visual openers to the complex, multi-layered main courses. The attention to detail, down to the custom cutlery, was notable.

Service was highly attentive, and the waitstaff did an excellent job managing the outdoor flow under tough restrictions. My only minor critique is that the interactions felt a bit overly scripted—dish descriptions and conversations sounded more rehearsed than organic—though this was entirely understandable given the rigid operational structures restaurants had to follow at the time.

It was great getting to experience Lazy Bear’s impressive resilience during that challenging period, but a return visit to finally evaluate their true indoor dining room experience is still a must.

top_reviews.content:
March, July 2021

Dining at Angler in March 2021 offered an exceptional case study in wood-fired culinary mechanics. Securing a seat with a direct view of the open-hearth fireplace is highly recommended, as it allows you to observe the kitchen’s precise temperature control firsthand. The service throughout the evening was excellent—polished, observant, and operating with a smooth, deliberate pace.

The menu landmarks demonstrate a flawless understanding of texture and salinity. The Parker House rolls arrive perfectly proofed, boasting a uniform golden glaze, paired with a remarkably deep seaweed butter. When dismantled and stuffed with their pastured chicken and pan jus, it yields an incredibly balanced, structurally rich bite. The wood-oven roasted chicken itself was spectacular—among the finest versions I have ever encountered, executed with pristine skin lacquering and served rustic style with the feet intact.

The accompanying elements maintain this high technical standard: the iconic whole radicchio salad balances bitter and sweet notes flawlessly, while the laminated potato showcases immaculate layer separation, anchored by a rich, sharp cheese sauce. Even the tabletop assets, like the heavy-duty custom knife, underscore the restaurant's sharp attention to detail.

Due to mid-pandemic protocols, the buffalo milk soft serve arrived with the warm caramel sauce on the side. Pouring the sauce independently added a compelling, interactive component to a structurally perfect dessert. Angler successfully strips away the rigid formality of fine dining without sacrificing a single drop of its technical execution. A compelling, highly recommended dining experience in San Francisco.

This restaurant was absolutely outstanding and truly lived up to its Michelin-star reputation.

We ordered the tasting menu, and every seafood dish was exceptionally fresh and well-seasoned. The flavors were thoughtful and balanced, allowing the quality of the ingredients to shine through.

The only minor drawback was the rice cake served beneath the scallop and sea urchin course. It was noticeably too salty. It seemed that the rice cake had been torched or grilled beforehand, causing moisture loss and concentrating the saltiness more than intended.

The restaurant also offers beautiful views overlooking the harbor, which made the dining experience even more enjoyable. The service was attentive, professional, and well-paced—they took great care of us without interrupting our meal too frequently.

Overall, this was an excellent dining experience, and I would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a memorable meal. We will definitely be back.

top_reviews.content:
Step inside, and you’re met with excellent food and the genuine warmth of a family-run spot. The staff are kind, welcoming, and absolutely deserving of the community’s support.

We had the thali with our choice of goat curry-beautifully balanced and authentic spread with great variety. We also tried the chicken fried rice, which was surprisingly flavorful and perfectly done, along with a sweet lassi that was creamy, refreshing, and the perfect finish to the meal.

Delicious food, fair prices, and heartfelt hospitality. Don’t let the exterior or the surrounding area near the Tenderloin put you off - Little Delhi is truly a hidden gem.

I was looking for authentic Indian foods. I’m pleased to find Little Delhi which offers delicious authentic flavour and great hospitality. The family owned restaurant provides the most affordable Thali set for $14.99 and if you prefer to order from their a wide selection of vegetarian and non vegetarian dishes from Nepal and India .

I stumbled upon Little Delhi purely out of necessity—my phone battery had completely died, and I was desperately looking for a place nearby to charge it. This spot came up just a short walk from Market Street, not too far away from Powell station near Carl.

From the very first moment, the customer service stood out. Without even asking much, the staff immediately helped me find a place to charge my phone and even lent me a charger. Brownie points right there.

Since my mum and I were already there (and feeling a little tingle in the stomach, though not starving), we decided to sit down for a light bite while the phone charged. We ordered samosa chaat and two cups of chai ($7.99 & $3.99 e.c) The prices were very reasonable, especially considering it’s right in the heart of downtown. The street itself may look a bit edgy or rough, but if you give this place a chance, you’ll be pleasantly surprised.

After tasting the samosa chaat, we couldn’t resist ordering their aloo paratha as well. It was nicely cooked, soft, and comforting. The only small thing I wished for was a side of pickle or chutney, which would have made it even better.

We also picked up rasmalai as a takeaway, and it was a perfect sweet ending to the experience.

It’s an Indo-Nepali restaurant, which I only realized after looking at the menu—and that was a nice surprise. The flavors were really good, the chaat was tasty, and the wait time wasn’t long at all. The space itself is beautifully decorated—minimalistic yet classy. It’s the kind of place where you could easily spend 2–3 hours sipping tea, reading a book, or having a good, relaxed conversation with friends.

Another thing worth mentioning: the restrooms were super clean, and even the seating area was being regularly cleaned, which really adds to the overall comfort and hygiene of the place.

The customer service remained fabulous from start to finish. Gopal, who helped us, was exceptional—attentive, kind, and genuinely welcoming. There was also another gentleman with spectacles who assisted us; special mention to him as well for being very prompt and helpful.

As a small suggestion: I’d love to see more chaat options like golgappe, or classic North Indian dishes such as chole-bhature. Maybe even a vegetarian burger with an Indian twist. With flavors this good and a name like Little Delhi, this place truly has the potential to go a long way.

Overall, a comforting spot with great service, good food, and a welcoming vibe. Definitely worth stopping by.

top_reviews.content:
BLAND FLAVORLESS NOTHING
Can't recommend this place.

Let me make this clear before I continue. The staff is great, they were totally cool with me, friendly and helpful. This has nothing to do with the staff or how they prepare the sandwiches.
The ingredients IB's is using are substandard. I've worked in the restaurant business for 35 years and I know, when substandard ingredients are being used.
The sweet peppers have no flavor at all, the cheese has no sharpness, the buns are bland and the meat is either under seasoned or just doesn't have a lot of flavor. These are the hallmarks of restaurants that source all of the ingredients from one company and the company kind of just throws them together to make a profit.
I drove 50 mi, because I had heard it was a great cheesesteak, and I am a fanatic for great cheesesteaks, and got a large one to share with my buddies, and what I got was a bland, bland, bland. No flavor, no sharpness, no cut.
You know that when a cheesesteak is properly constructed and still has no flavor, it has nothing to do with the staff, it has to do with where the owner is sourcing the ingredients from, and the ingredients suck. Okay I feel bad for the staff there, having to work with those ingredients. It's probably going to cost them in the long run, because cutting corners like that, will lessen your business in an area where people want strong flavors.
Anyway the staff was totally cool, I didn't mind the price for the gigantic sandwich, but the experience was just boring, and bland, and no flavor.
Anyway, I wish I could send a better report, I hope they do better maybe I'll give it another chance at another time, but probably not if it's going to be like this.
I'm sure the management is going to respond to this with some cookie cutter response, not taking responsibility, because people that take responsibility for their food, don't work with food like this. It looks like they've gotten in trouble with dozens of people before, and apparently the sale from the old owner has resulted in not only poor quality ingredients, but also poor quality responses.
Stitch incoming 3.2.1

There are restaurants that serve beautiful food, and then there are places that create an entire experience. Bottega manages to do both effortlessly.
Every plate felt thoughtful, balanced, and deeply comforting without losing refinement. From the pillowy gnocchi to the rich red sauce, delicate prosciutto, crisp salads, and perfectly executed seafood, every bite reminded us why simple Italian food done exceptionally well never goes out of style. Even the atmosphere carried that same warmth: relaxed, elegant, lively, and unmistakably Mission.
What stood out most was how inviting everything felt. Nothing overly complicated. Just incredible ingredients, beautiful execution, and the kind of meal that makes you slow down and enjoy the moment.
One of those places where you leave already planning your next visit.

From our very first interaction, this restaurant exceeded our expectations. We called ahead with a large party of 11 people, plus our dogs, and were greeted with such warmth and kindness. Instead of making us feel like a challenge to accommodate, they made us feel genuinely welcome.

When we arrived, we were blown away by how beautiful the restaurant was. The décor is absolutely stunning and creates an atmosphere that is both elegant and inviting. We were especially happy to find outdoor seating, which allowed our entire group—including our dogs—to enjoy the experience comfortably.

What really impressed us was how thoughtful and attentive the staff were. Not only did they welcome our dogs, but they even brought out food for them. Our dogs absolutely loved it and were just as excited about the dining experience as we were! It’s rare to find a restaurant that goes above and beyond to make every member of the family feel included.

Then the food arrived, and that’s when this place truly became unforgettable. Everything was absolutely delicious. From the fresh bread to the pasta, every bite was packed with flavor and clearly made with care and passion. It was exactly what we were hoping for and more. The quality, authenticity, and attention to detail were evident in every dish.

What started as a simple dinner turned into a truly memorable experience. Between the beautiful atmosphere, exceptional hospitality, incredible food, and the kindness they showed to our dogs, this restaurant has earned loyal customers in all of us.

If you’re looking for authentic Italian cuisine, outstanding service, and a place that genuinely makes you feel welcome, this is it. We can’t wait to return. Thank you for making our evening so special! 🇮🇹🍝🐾❤️
First time dining here and it was amazing! Luka’s service was outstanding. Food was really good and my dog even got some free meatballs which she enjoyed a lot too. Will definitely return.

I love the simplicity of fettuccine done right: garlic, cream, Parmigiano Reggiano, cracked pepper, salt. It’s one of those dishes where there’s nowhere to hide, so the execution really matters.

Unfortunately, this one didn’t land at all.

I was hungry but couldn’t finish my pasta, which says a lot. The garlic didn’t taste fresh - more like garlic powder than properly sautéed garlic. The cream sauce was broken and curdled rather than smooth and cohesive, which made the texture feel off from the first bite. It lacked that silky, emulsified quality you expect from a well-made fettuccine.

I also couldn’t taste the Parmigiano Reggiano, which is usually the highlight and what brings depth and balance to the dish. Here, it felt muted or missing entirely.

What really stood out was how the dish held up afterward. Fettuccine like this typically tastes even better the next day as the flavors settle, this didn’t. The texture and flavor didn’t improve, which reinforced that something was off in the preparation.

It’s a simple dish, but that’s exactly why it needs to be done well. This missed the mark for me, and I don’t think I’ll be coming back.

Luisa’s feels like stepping into a real old-school Italian restaurant in the best possible way. Everything about the experience felt warm, comforting, and authentic.

The gnocchi was incredible. Soft, pillowy, rich, and perfectly coated in sauce. You can immediately tell the gnocchi is made with care and tradition behind it. The chicken parmigiana was another standout… perfectly crispy with amazing marinara and melted cheese, plus classic spaghetti on the side. We also ordered the meatballs, and the meatballs were huge, tender, and packed with flavor.

One of the most special parts of the night was getting to meet Luisa herself. She’s 95 years old, and honestly, she is absolutely remarkable. Sharp, elegant, welcoming, and still personally connecting with guests at her restaurant. It made the whole evening feel incredibly meaningful. You can feel the history, love, and generations of family behind the restaurant when you talk with her. It’s rare to experience something like that anymore. Her bottled house wine was also fantastic and paired perfectly with the gnocchi, chicken parmigiana, and meatballs.

A huge thank you as well to Claudio and Luca for making the experience feel so personal and welcoming. You can tell this restaurant is built on genuine hospitality and heart.

The atmosphere was cozy, the service was wonderful, and the entire evening felt memorable from start to finish.

Final recap: absolutely order the gnocchi, chicken parmigiana, and meatballs. The gnocchi was unforgettable, the chicken parmigiana was classic comfort food done perfectly, and the meatballs were some of the best meatballs we’ve had in San Francisco.

Wonderful experience! Our wine and food choices were recommended, and they were fantastic! Lamb Shank, Gnocchi and Tiramisu. Best Gnocchi I’ve ever had, and the lamb sank melted in your mouth! Make sure to save room for some Tiramisu!

Ms. Luisa came over to greet us, and she was a standout. Her presence was radiant, her personality engaging, and you could tell she takes pride in what she has built. She even took a moment to take a picture with us, which made the experience feel even more personal.

If you’re in the area and want authentic Italian food in a welcoming setting, this is the place to go. You will not be disappointed.

The table next to us had to ask the waiter to take something back to the kitchen temporarily because they couldn’t fit it on their table. It was very odd and unexpected for a restaurant like this.

We recently had the pleasure of dining at Chutney Restaurant in San Francisco, and overall, it was a pleasant experience with room for growth. The ambiance was cozy and welcoming, though a bit more attention to lighting and decor could enhance the atmosphere.
To start, we ordered the garlic naan, which was perfectly fluffy and fragrant, with just the right amount of garlic and butter. It paired beautifully with the chicken tikka masala, which featured tender chunks of chicken bathed in a creamy, spiced tomato sauce. The flavors were robust and well-balanced, making it a highlight of the meal.
The chicken breast dish was also well-cooked, juicy, and paired with a mild sauce that complemented its natural flavors. The lamb chops were another standout: they were succulent and had a nice char, with a marinade that brought out deep, savory notes.
The biryani was aromatic, with fluffy rice and well-spiced seasoning. Each bite had a nice blend of herbs and tender meat. The beef dish was flavorful, though it could have used a bit more seasoning to elevate it further.
A lovely touch was the complimentary milk tea, which was soothing and well-prepared, offering a nice, sweet finish to the meal.
In summary, while the food at Chutney Restaurant was enjoyable and showcased some really tasty dishes, there’s definitely potential for refinement and improvement. I’m excited to see how they evolve and enhance their offerings in the future.

I went to Chutney with a friend recently and was absolutely delighted. I ordered Chicken Tikka Masala and branded biryani — the meat is perfectly marinated, the spices are bright and balanced, the portions are large, you can safely share. The atmosphere is simple and cozy, the staff is polite and fast — you can see that they are cooking according to real recipes. Excellent price/quality ratio for San Francisco, I will definitely be back.

Unfortunately, I don't want to come back here because of the environment.

top_reviews.content:
This was our first dinner at SF. We were staying at Holiday Inn Express, Fisherman’s Wharf and it was 5 mins walk. We were in time for the WC soccer, to watch Aus vs Paraguay match. We arrived late in the evening from Dallas after watching Argentina play Austria. We were tired and hungry and wanted something light.

We ordered a plate of idli, chicken soup, lemon chicken and mysore masala dosa. The order took around 15-20 mins, but came gradually as dishes got ready. All food items were good, above average - Idli sambar was stock standard, can’t go wrong. Chicken soup and lemon chicken both were quite good, though their medium spicy (like we asked) felt slightly spicier than our palate. The dosa was big, taste was average and I was a bit disappointed that it was not crispy enough.

They advertise diff types of beers, but have only Coronas, atleast that was the case when we visited for dinner. Overall a good experience, would go again if in town.

This Indian restaurant ( South Indian Style) near Fisherman’s Wharf with a solid menu of dosas, appetizers, curries, and biryanis that generally taste good. We tried the chilli chicken, curry, and chapati, and all of them turned out well with generous portions that felt worth the price. The dining area is quite large, so it’s comfortable for groups and doesn’t feel cramped.

However, the service was disappointing on our visit. The server seemed inattentive and didn’t really check in on guests. With better service this place could easily move up, but for now it’s a mixed experience—good food and value, but lacking in hospitality.

Hidden Gem for a quick bite right on the waterfront and pier 39 areas accessible by a few minutes walk and also available street parking for those visiting there by driving straight to the location. Service is excellent by attending staff Raja and Venkatesh. Their seating is very spacious and does not feel crammed for an eatery in that vicinity. Additionally they also have a separate banquet type area which can accommodate party or celebratory occasions that demand music and lighting provided. We came for a quick bite and ordered items which were prepared fresh and tasted yummy. Their choice of drinks are also straightforward with a glass window refrigerator to give you an idea of the soft drinks and alcoholic beverages (beers). Their menus and decors bring back nostalgia from the South Indian state and cities vibrantly including the south eastern coastal Marina Beach experience. Restrooms are also accessible in this restaurant which are maintained well and kept clean. Definitely going back for items I need to try but couldn't during this first visit. This gives off a nice namma Chennai vibe. Aapdi Poode. 👌👍👏👏

We came here right after our GoCar experience and were really hungry, so we decided to give this place a try. To our surprise, the food was actually really good!

They have a large seating area, which was nice. We really liked the Kothu Parotta — definitely a must-try! The Gobi Manchurian was good too, and the biryani rice was pretty tasty. We also tried the buttermilk and mango lassi, and both were good.

Overall, a nice option if you’re looking for South Indian food.

The only thing is that the service can be a little slow. They bring the dishes out one by one, so don’t expect everything to arrive at the same time. But it was manageable.

Definitely a good find, especially when you’re hungry after a day of exploring! 😊

Stopped here for lunch and had mysore masala dosa and filter coffee.
Both were really good.
Sambhar and coconut chutney were the highlight.
Seatings were also good and spacious.
Loved the fact that the refill of sambhar and chutney was free unlike other restaurants.
Dosa was also reasonably sized. Overall loved the food .

top_reviews.content: Super cool spot, great patio seating, ambiance, warm, friendly and fast service. Pancakes were a 10! The food was all excellent, will be back soon.

I recommend showing up an hour before you plan to eat. They have a sign up sheet that they don’t follow since they call parties at random. Went here today with a party of 5 to try it for the first time but after we placed our name on the list we waited for almost an hour with no communication from the hostess.

After about 45mins of waiting we noticed she was only calling parties of 3 or less but it was never communicated that they were only seating smaller parties.

We ended up leaving without eating here due to poor service.

We don't go nowhere else for breakfast. If you want it real without all the extra BS  unnecessary 'California' nonsense, This is your place. Real real: grits, cornbread done right, and the coffee is hot and strong.

The one downside with this place, is you eat outside but they made it pretty comfortable with heating and all of that so it's not as bad as you might think.

The history of this place before it became Sam's makes it even better - gambling joint and probably a whorehouse amongst other questionable business endeavors. Storied: as all the best places to eat are.

Rarely do I give five stars for anything especially if there's even one item that doesn't cut it for me which here might be the 'you have to eat outside' situation. But everything else is over the top and I get stuff and take it home so... The fifth star is for over the top and exceptional. That is Sam's.

i was bracing for this place to be super touristy but it was actually really great. the interior is so cozy and warm, like stepping into someone’s actual cabin. i ordered the fried chicken and it was perfectly crispy, not greasy at all. my freind got the cornbread and we kept stealing bites from each other becuase it was that good. the service was super friendly too, even when we had aksed a million questions they didnt rush us

i honestly didnt want to leave, we just sat there for a while soaking it all in definately coming back
Outdoor seating we a nice little treat we were not expecting. 100% worth it, if your in the area!

My friend and I visited SF for the first time a few weeks ago, and this restaurant is located in the same building as the hotel we stayed at (The Andrews Hotel). We were surprised by the great reviews on Google, so we decided to give it a try. We were very lucky to get a table even though we made the reservation on the same day. 😁

We ordered the Linguine con Rapini e Aglio, Linguine Frutti di Mare, and Calamari Fritto. The fried calamari was so good… even without the tomato sauce! The pasta portions were very generous, especially the Frutti di Mare. I have never seen a plate with that much seafood 😆

Looking forward to visiting SF again and coming back to this restaurant in the future. 👍🏻😁

I’m here for a couple weeks for work and this spot has so far been my Favorite! I sat at the bar and had amazing service from Megan! It felt like I was hanging out with a friend. So sweet and caring. The food was amazing! A must try in SF!

This is the place to go for a wonderful Italian meal! We had 7 people in our party and our server was amazing. All the food and dessert was incredible. Chef Ramsey would be impressed with how the scallops were prepared.
Thank you so to the staff and Chefs for making this a memorable evening.

A gem of a restaurant. Authentic Italian dishes served with old world charm. A delightful way to relax after a busy day. Staff is professional and attentive. The ambiance is a balance of upscale, romantic and cozy. The food is some of the best Italian food I have had and the portions are large with generous amounts of seafood. I would also recommend to single diners as the service is so gracious.  Be sure to order dessert as it is a feast for the eyes as well as the palate.

Incredible Italian restaurant with the friendliest staff. And by San Francisco standards, not that expensive.

I had the veal piccata and it was delicious and the veal was ‘fork tender ‘.  Their gnocchi was also fantastic.   Really liked the bartender.

top_reviews.content: If you want to experience a classic meal in San Francisco, Eddie’s Cafe is the place!  For 65 years this corner has been bustling. Shoutout to Ami for welcoming me in. The coffee mugs on the wall are an art piece. I ordered a hearty hot chocolate and it made me feel like a kid again. I ordered the pancakes, eggs, and hot links but I hear the hash-browns are amazing. Will have to try that next time. The memorabilia on the wall is admirable as well. The hot link had great flavor and this meal started my day on the right step. Locals love this spot, I met a retired legend that used to operate the cable cars years ago! You never know who you may run into, and Eddie’s Cafe is the place to feel the true energy of San Francisco.
A gorgeous diner run by a lovely friendly team. Service was speedy and friendly. Food was great, just what we needed after a long travel day/night

Vibes are immaculate. Super cozy. Food tastes amazing. Staff is super friendly and welcoming. It was very wholesome witnessing the regulars and the staff greet each other by name.
Bar seating seems to be very popular but the seating is very comfortable!! Food is inexpensive for San Francisco and it is delicious. I will be back!

Eddie's was a suggested breakfast spot while I waited for my Dad to recover from surgery at near by Kaiser. Once I walked in, I was immediately greeted warmly by staff who sat me right away at the bar. It truly felt like I traveled back in time to an old school San Franciscan diner. The crowd was cheerful and the food was absolutely delicious. My compliments to the cook who grilled my eggs just the way I ordered them and the bacon that was cooked to perfection. The belgian waffle was golden brown, slightly crispy sprinkled w powdered sugar, which was perfect. Thank you Eddie's for the wonderful experience which put me in a good mood.

top_reviews.content: Great bar with great food! My wife was very impressed that they were willing to cook her fries less to order. She doesn’t like them crispy. They also did a great job cooking her burger medium rare to order. Popcorn needed more salt. Onion rings were phenomenal.

Louie’s Bar is one of those places that just gets it right. From the moment you walk in, the atmosphere feels welcoming without trying too hard—lively, but still comfortable enough to settle in and enjoy your time.

Honestly, everything we tried was great, but the food is what really stood out. The burger is something you don’t want to sleep on—it’s rich, flavorful, and clearly done with intention. It’s one of those dishes that sticks with you after the meal.

The potato skins with the quail egg on top were a definite hit, especially paired with the house-made hot sauce, which brought everything together with just the right kick. The buffalo wings were also a standout—nicely spicy, but in a way that adds flavor rather than overpowering it.

If I had to point out anything, it would just be that it can get a bit busy, but that’s more a sign of how popular it is than a real downside.

Overall, Louie’s Bar delivered across the board. It’s the kind of spot you go to for great food and end up planning your next visit before you’ve even left.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Off the Charts at Louie's Place 🔥🌮
Matt and Daryl absolutely crushed it at Louie’s Place Bar and Restaurant in San Francisco. This spot is next level.
The tacos? Unreal. The flavor hits different, something about the seasoning and that tortilla shell makes every bite stand out. Not your average taco… these are must-order status.
And the onion rings? Over the top in the best way possible. Beer-battered, I think, with this subtle cheddar flavor that takes them into a whole new category. Crispy, rich, and addictive.
Pro tip: get them with the cheese sauce. Game changer. 🧀
This place delivers bold flavors, great vibes, and food you’ll be thinking about long after you leave. Matt and Daryl know what they’re doing.
Highly recommend. I’ll be back. 💯

google.name: Acqua e Farina

top_reviews.content: Excellent food and service whenever we go. The steak was cooked perfectly and our pastas were delicious. Their homemade bread is also to die for along with their cream of asparagus! The drinks are made at the bar and straight to your table. Classic old school Italian aesthetics but very clean.

Acqua e Farina (AeF) is an interesting Italian joint. First of all, you get this "mafia" style entrance where it is dark, it has a corridor to the inner dining, and a separate dining hall. It feels like a bit out of the Godfather where you are led to the room behind the room type of feel. The interior also is "classical" per se. Not sure whether they were going for the homely vibe but then you get this weird neon and holiday lights dangling (in the middle of July). The restaurant also has a unique scent which I couldn't make out what it was. Definitely not food. It could've been the cleaning detergent or some type of an air refreshner. But definitely not "Italian food" per se.

At this point, I'm getting a bit worried. I saw 4.6 stars on Google Maps and was hoping a bit more classical yet "proper" Italian joint for my business lunch. The menu also looks a bit dusty or rusty. Clearly it was getting a bit confusing as to why AeF was scored so high. I was seriously contemplating to just walk out.

But then the bread came. The warm focaccia with olive oil immediately put me back into my seat. So good. So well done. Whether they baked it fresh or bought it fresh that day and warmed it up, it didn't matter. The bread was lovely.

The bruschetta was also nicely done. Freshly chopped tomatoes and top of fresh baguette toasted to perfection. Very homely. Not pretentious. Just honest good food.

Finally, I went for the risotto special with shimp and scallops. Now I tend to not order scallops unless I can fully trust the establishment as scallops are the first thing that goes bad when ingredients are kept in the fridge for an extended period of time. The risotto was not perfect. But it was the type of risotto you would get from your mother's kitchen. It definitely could have had more mushrooms. It could've used a bit more butter. A bit more thicker. But somehow, you feel good when you eat in to the spoonful of hearty rice. And yes, the scallops were just fine, and so was the shrimp.

Unlike the facade and the interior, there is something really hearty and homely about AeF. It just feels like a restaurant you can visit week after week, time after time. No frills. No pretentions. Just go enjoy the good food.
Took the future ex husband here for Father’s Day dinner. Lovely place for Italian food. Really delicious linguine and clams and the salmon was very fresh. Delicious carpaccio too.

We made a reservation but we got there 20 minutes late due to parking. The hostess was really nice and seated us right away. The food, atmosphere, and service were excellent.  Table spacing gives a lot of privacy. Our server was very attentive and recommended a good wine to match our order. The only food that we did not like was the side polenta.

Was my very first time ever! Atmosphere was amazing! Service was extremely friendly from the moment we walked in and sat at the bar.  Cocktails were good! I had an Old Fashioned and would rate it a solid 6.5/10 I'm picky when it comes to my drink.  My girlfriend got the espresso martini and we both gave a 9/10.  From presentation to taste.  We started with an order of Bruschetta and Calamari.  Absolutely no complaints from quality to flavor 10/10 on the appetizers.  For entrée we ordered 3 because we couldn't decided.  We ordered the Gnocchi Della Casa, Fettuccine Gamberetti and Tortellini alla Panna.  Me and my girlfriend have gone back and forth on which one was better than the other and which was our least favorite.  At the end of the day although our order may be different we both agreed nothing was bad.  We ate everything or took home what little was left.  We would order everything again over in a heartbeat but also are planning to try different things next visit.  If you are looking for amazing Italian with great flavor and awesome quality and quantity you found the spot.  I look forward to our next meal

TLDR - Spacious spot with quick service and great breakfast/ lunch options. Fit for large or smaller sizer parties.

Love the house potatoes - nicely seasoned and flavored. The crepe is savory and yummy but I will warn that it might get soggy because of the juices from the spinach and capers. I also got a side of the fresh squeezed OJ - perfect weekend brunch spot.

Crepevine has a cozy, inviting vibe and a menu packed with variety—crepes, pastas, salads, and more. The food is solid and satisfying, with generous portions and fresh ingredients. I’ve tried both savory and sweet options, and everything has been consistently good.

That said, nothing really stands out as exceptional. It’s tasty, but not memorable. For the price point—often $18–25 per plate once you factor in tax and tip—it feels like you’re paying a bit more than the experience delivers. The ingredients are fresh, but the flavors are pretty straightforward, and the presentation doesn’t quite justify the upscale casual price.

Still, the service is friendly, and it’s a great spot if you’re in the mood for variety or need something crowd-pleasing. Just manage expectations—it’s more of a convenient comfort food spot than a culinary standout.

top_reviews.content: Great experience at Marugame Udon! The udon was fresh and chewy, the broth was flavorful, and the tempura topping was crispy and delicious. The drink was refreshing as well. Service was fast and friendly, and the restaurant had a clean, comfortable atmosphere. I would definitely come back again.

8/10 (this location) | 9/10 overall

How can you go wrong with Marugame Udon? Seriously. It’s one of those spots that just hits every time. This location gets an 8/10 from me—still solid, still satisfying—but overall, the brand is easily a 9/10 because it’s just sooooo good.

If you’re going for the first time (or even if you’re not), do yourself a favor and get the beef or nikutama. The broth is rich, savory, and comforting, and the noodles have that perfect chewy texture that makes every bite worth it. It’s simple food done really well.

And don’t skimp on the tempura. That’s where people mess up. Load up your tray—shrimp, sweet potato, whatever catches your eye. It’s crispy, fresh, and honestly half the experience.

Quick, casual, and consistently delicious. Hard to miss here.

Now that I’m done with UC Berkeley, I can confidently claim that this has always been a very tasty ramen restaurant. I would go here whenever I had in-person campus visits. The thick vegan noodles with carrots, broth, and cabbage are very delicious.

My son attends UC Berkeley, so I come to Berkeley at the beginning of each semester. This time, he took me to Marugame Udon, and it was such a great experience. The food was simple, fresh, and delicious, and I loved the whole concept. There’s nothing like this where I live — definitely one of the best!

It is a great spot for comforting and authentic Japanese food. The udon noodles were freshly made, thick, and perfectly chewy, and the broth was light yet very flavorful. I appreciated being able to customize the bowl with different toppings, which made the experience fun and satisfying. The service was fast and well organized, even when there was a line, and the prices were reasonable for the quality and portion size. A solid choice for a quick, delicious meal if you’re craving udon in Berkeley.

My parents and I decided to go to Buon Appetito for my dad's birthday and it's one of the best Italian restaurants in Hayward. Pretty well setup inside especially with how utensils, glasses, napkins, and plates are organized. It also looks nice inside especially at a larger dining area where there weren't anyone there when I got here. They also have a patio too, but no one goes outside since it's cold now.

The food is really delicious here. We were given normal sized plates and I'm surprised that the food seems small from the outside but volume of it says otherwise. It could be the ingredients that they used to make our meals.

I seen dishes like Fettuccine Alfredo and Spaghetti Bolognese, which are very common dishes, but I don't want either of them. So I got Fettuccine alla Friuliana. It's mostly fettuccine with Italian sausages and tomato sauce. That dish really hits the spot especially when cheese makes it more flavorful. I also tried my parents' dishes and they're as good as the one I got.

For dessert, we got tiramisu. I love how it sprinkled with cocoa powder I believe as well as topping it off with some sort of cream I think. They actually blend well with that dessert. Honestly, they should have but it in a smaller plate to match the food-to-plate ratio.

Overall, it's one of the best Italian restaurants out there. If you're looking for Italian cuisine here in Hayward, this is one of the spots I recommend coming into. You won't be missing out!

The pizza at this location is, frankly, underwhelming, especially if you’ve experienced higher-quality pizza elsewhere. A single slice ranges around $6.40, depending on the variety, but the quality doesn’t justify the price. This is the type of pizza one might reach for late at night, perhaps after a night out, when taste isn’t a primary concern.

When fully sober, the pizza’s flavor reveals an unpleasant chemical undertone that’s difficult to overlook. It’s simply not enjoyable for those seeking a satisfying, well-crafted slice.

top_reviews.content: We made a quick stop at Begoni Bistro during our visit to Chinatown after seeing the positive Google reviews, and it turned out to be a great choice. Begoni Bistro was an absolute gem in Chinatown — easily one of our favorite meals in San Francisco!

The food was incredible. The house fried rice alone could be a meal by itself — perfectly cooked, flavorful, and so satisfying. We also had the siu mai, which were delicious and fresh, and everything we ordered came out hot and full of flavor.

We tried the roast duck for the first time here — while it wasn’t our favorite dish personally, it was still a great experience to try something new, and everything else more than made up for it.

The atmosphere is exactly what you want in Chinatown: busy, lively, and casual. It was packed when we arrived, which turned out to be a great sign — clearly a place people love, and for good reason.

If you’re looking for authentic, no-frills Chinese food with amazing flavor, this place is a must-visit. We’d definitely come back!

High-quality dimsum made-to-order. All expertly made, clean tasting. Standouts include:

* Steamed Beef Tripe with Soy Sauce
* Shanghai Pork Soup Dumplings (xiaolongbao)
* Spicy Pork and Shrimp Shu Mai
* Salt and Pepper Chicken Wings
* Pea Sprouts with Chopped Garlic

I have to say, you should definitely go to this restaurant. Even though it was my first time ever trying Chinese food, especially dim sum, and I wasn’t familiar with it at all, it was amaaazing. top_reviews.content:
Quality food always!  The food comes out quick and the taste stays consistent across plates ordered.  Staff is tremendously friendly and polite.

Portions are generous, so there is plenty to share with everyone.  13+ tables available that can accommodate parties from 4-8 in a decent size room with nice lighting and easy access to restrooms.

Although parking is limited in Chinatown on the streets, Spicy King is on the corner and easy to get to from Grant.

Highly recommend the Cashew Chicken (thicker glaze sauce).  Kung Pao Chicken is a great spicy option with a nice “kick” to it.

A restaurant in San Francisco's Chinatown. On vacation I ran into this restaurant while walking around this historical part of the city. The staff were welcoming and so was the atmosphere. They have chopsticks ready to use but will provide common spoons, forks, and knives. Very accommodating. We had crab puffs and I had the General Tao's with a side of white rice. My son had the Dan Dan noodles. The General Tao's was just the right spicy and my son enjoyed the noodles. The portions were plenty. This was a great spot. Price was $50-60 for two people. Well worth it. A great place to eat and enjoy the uniqueness of the city.

When I tell you this place had some of the best Sichuan food I’ve had, I’m not exaggerating.

The spicy wontons and cucumber salad are non-negotiable. That sauce was insane. Spicy, savory, garlicky, and the kind of sauce you keep going back to even after the dish is basically gone.

The Kung Pao was stellar. The chicken chow mein had great flavor, with saucy noodles that actually hit. Mongolian beef was really good too, although definitely heavy on the onions.

Service felt super homey, which made the whole meal even better. Just one of those spots that feels warm, authentic, and worth coming back to.

The Authentic Sichuan food, If you are looking for màlà flavour, this restaurant hits the nail on head.
Cozy style atmosphere.
Friendly staff.

Dined in with 3 others. We each got a dish and 2 apps for the group. It was so much food! The food was very flavorful. I had the Kung Pao Prawns and they were spicy, I loved it. So good. So many juicy prawns. Try the crispy chicken dumplings, delicious. Price seemed fair.  It got crowded shortly after we were seated. It was a popular place. I will go back again when in San Francisco.

Tashakor, Kamdesh!
The food was delicious but meat was not tender. Quantity was less as compared to price. Service was good.

I absolutely love Kamdesh Afghan Restaurant. Every time I visit, the food is consistently delicious and full of rich, authentic flavor. You can really tell how much care they put into every dish. The service is always warm, welcoming, and attentive, which makes the whole experience even better.

top_reviews.content:
This reminds me of SS; I'm sure that was the inspiration.  The burgers don't taste like SS burgers but they're still really good.  Best ever?  No.  Definitely not better than INO.  But still, its a solid burger and it's clearly made fresh.  This reminded me more of something you'd get at a sit down restaurant, just without the wait.  Definitely juicy as advertised.

Fries were good, but not amazing.  Fountain soda is a little expensive but considering how relatively cheap the burger is for what you get, its hard to complain.  There are no real combos where you save money but I got a burger, fries and a coke for $17.  For California prices, I think that's really good.

When my Amtrak train was delayed in Emeryville, CA, I was very grateful to get a good burger, fries & a drink right across from the station. There's nothing fancy about this location, but my meal was good & the service was polite & quick. 👏🏼

This is now our favorite burger place. They are the absolute bomb. Most delicious, juicy, flavorful burgers 🍔 we have ever had. The double burgers are so big that me and my husband share a burger. The garlic fries 🍟 are really really good too. The milkshakes are creamy 😋 and delicious. Even after sharing one meal we leave stuffed.
We have only been to the one in Emeryville.

Been coming here for years now and have had beyond superb service whether ordering or picking up my food.  Today I told the counter woman she wasn’t doing a good job because she saw me waiting around, had lots of down time, had my order waiting on a high shelf the whole time and never thought to ask what I was waiting for.  Her coworkers are always aware of everything and manage that counter so well and with enthusiasm and professionalism.  The manager Laura came by and told me not to talk to her workers like I did.  More unprofessional than her worker apparently, go only lacked the innate sense of service and helpfulness with the public.  LAura took my photo and told me never to come again.  Didn’t think at all like a manager representing her owner.  Didn’t think to ask about my concern or to even try in the slightest to rise above it, rise above what she saw as my bad behavior.  Definitely not someone I’d hire to represent me if she can’t think professionally on her feet.  And while she photographed me, she scurried away when I tried to photograph her.  But I got it eventually.

Loud music drown out conversations, makes it hard to hear your number call also. Burgers are not special or standout but I appreciated how hot they arrived, still steaming hot, love it. I ordered the basic to see how well it was seasoned since they are voted to be #1 for 2 years. Good amount of salt but lack flavor. Same with the truffle burger. Garlic fries had a good amount of fresh (real)garlic butter (though I'd love to have more garlic on mine, enough to rebel vampires) topped with cheese. I prefer it to be melted more rather than just dump it on the fries. I gave 4 stars because I appreciated how hot the food was & the garlic :)

This restaurant very accommodating to food allergies, so much so that they request to report any allergies on the food menu and are very professional when it comes to handling them.

I was blown away by the summer squash pizza and mascarpone/san marzano pizza! Some of the best I have ever had. Perfectly crispy crust with very complex complimentary flavors.

Check out the bathroom when you visit as well, it's very cozy.

A small hole in the wall with plenty outdoor seating. The food is solid - a great cheese board to start for me and I loved the muni themed beer. The flour less chocolate cake was also very well done. I see why the place is so packed all the time!

One of my top choices for pizza in the city. It’s a very small cozy place. You can tell the staff is passionate about food. I like that the menu is small and simple, yet they always have specials. They also have a small wine selection with a few of them that can be purchased by the glass.

Simply delicious and fantastic service with cozy, warm setting.  I was looking for a simple, thin crust neighborhood type place in SF and saw this so giving a try.  It blown my mind with everything from the great chill relax vibe, to great nice and friendly service and the foods are simple but yet elevated to several unexpected levels.  Our server recommended the farm egg pizza and I picked the pepperoni one.  I was skeptical at first of the farm egg but surprisingly I like it more than my pepperoni (still fantastic but damn).  Who knows that eggs pizza was that fantastic and so yum!  The salad is simple but tasty and the dressing was marinated well without seeing it, just tasting.  We finished it all without stopping.  We just ate 4hrs prior so we’re are still full (just want a good pizza before we flying the next day) but the pizzas and the salad was just somehow disappeared without us knowing that we ate them all. On top of these, we ordered the passion fruit panna cotta and yup, gone just gone within 2mins.  Really want to order more but had to restrain or else we’re unable to fit into our clothes. Will be on my list to must comeback in SF for sure.  Thank you for the incredible foods and service. Just simply loving it. Oh they have inside but it’s small and tight with 6-7 table for 2-4 seatings, but they do have outdoor sitting with heat lamps and blankets.  Very romantic and cozy place for sure.

This was a really very good place. The pizzettas were fresh and made with high quality ingredients. We tried the hazelnut pizza and it was very delicious and interesting. They also offer homemade sausages, and the salads were creative and something different. The service was great. The place itself is quite tiny and small, but cozy.

Ignore all the one star reviews. This place is awesome. Sure, it feels a little cramped, but their homemade dumplings and hand pulled noodles make up for it. I highly recommend the pork and chive dumplings, the beef noodle soup, and the pea sprouts. As someone who has been to china, this food is top notch.

This was a lovely authentic place in China Town. The Orange Chicken was perfectly friend and then the sauce went on which it stayed crispy. My partner had the chow mein. top_reviews.content:
My husband and I recently had our wedding reception here. It was one of our best experiences. We're a young couple starting out and Jeremy (Manager) helped us every step of the way. He responded well to emails, gave really useful suggestions, and was really accommodating. We didn't know where to find a DJ and Jeremy recommended one that was very professional and so easy to work with.

Jeremy allowed us to visit several times to view the space and met with us on multiple occasions so he knew what we needed and gave us information that we needed to know. On the day of, our family mentioned during the set-up, time of the event, and clean up so many good things about the staff, noting how helpful and calm they were (helped calm me down because I was stressed), easy to approach, and even mentioning that they loved watching them dance and enjoy the evening with us.

The Star really made this a beautiful reception in about a month and a half. Anything we needed, Jeremy tried to make it happen, even if it was outlandish. They allowed us to bring in outside vendors like Tuckers. Our guests enjoyed the food and drinks, and whatever was packaged away for me and my husband was enjoyed as well! Guests also mentioned how the atmosphere felt so welcoming and how much they felt good being in The Star's space.

The Star has always held a special place in our hearts and probably always will because we've made so many memories there, even before the reception. Some people in our family are already trying to think of another event to have there because everything was just that good. Thank you!

If we ever move to Alameda, The Star on Park would be my favorite pizza restaurant! We were looking at homes and while walking around, came across the charming Star on Park, that used to be a bank!  Our waitress was lovely and everything we ate was delicious!
The personal deep dish pizza lunch special is probably the best deal on the island. The catch is that they take some time to cook but it's well worth the wait.

Seriously some of the best pizza I've had in quite a long time! All made fresh to order and I really wanted to try the Detroit style pizza but the family wasn't feeling adventurous but we did have the Detroit style cheesy bread which was phenomenal!

Our favorites were the chicken pesto and the carbonara! But seriously, everything was good!

Delicious pizza with crust made to perfection! Beautiful decorum, prompt and friendly service (thanks Lewis for taking such good care of us!) This was our first time here, but I'm sure we'll be back again!👌

I am generally pretty critical about Indian places in SF downtown specially if they are North Indian. Most of them are pretty meh.. They may be decent in ambience but fails to deliver in flavour.

This place is opposite - very basic in ambience but really good value of money. Food here is reasonably priced and the quantity and quality both are above average.

I have been to Raavi in last and my experience was lackluster. But my recent experience was pretty good.

I wouldn't say that flavour is top notch but for the money you are spending - I will take it anyday. I tried Karahi Panner and from the looks you can say it doesn't have the same look of Karahi Panner but it was still pretty decent.

One of the SF North Indian spot where I don't mind visiting again.

We ordered a ghost tikka masala, palak panner, 2 basmati rice & 1 original nann. Everything was so delicious and have beautiful aromatics. I normally like to eat my curry with rice but this time I really enjoyed it with nann.

The service was fast and staff is friendly. They also have complimentary chai which was a plus!!!

Raavi North Indian Cuisine absolutely impressed us. We ordered the chicken korma, garlic naan, and basmati rice, and every single dish was delicious. The korma was rich and flavorful without being heavy, the naan was perfectly soft with just the right amount of garlic, and the rice was fragrant and fluffy. You can tell everything is made with care. We’ll definitely be coming back.

We ordered chicken Tandoori, garlic naans and chicken vindaloo. The chicken tandoori and chicken in the vindaloo are so hard and undercooked. I really expected more! And when I called front desk he asked me to come over to the restaurant and speak to the manager. I expected a refund!!!
Extremely disappointed on a Doordash order. The garlic naan arrived completely charred and inedible. I’m not sure how the kitchen thought it was okay to pack this up and send it out.

top_reviews.content:
Had a birthday dinner at this special place.
Lovely food, minimal menu which we loved , but not all dishes were amazing.
This is a $$$ restaurant and as such we are looking to get more wow.

Met up with a few friends to catch up. The place was busy and the ambience and the service were nice. Seems like a convenient location near the offices for dinner or drinks. We all ordered a pasta dish and a few entree dishes to share but they are just average and forgettable. The food comes out very quickly, and the price point was decent though.

Perbacco has always been my favorite Italian restaurant in the city, and it never disappoints. From the service to the drinks to the food, everything is excellent. The only minor drawback is that the decor feels a bit dated. That said, the food is reasonably priced for the quality—delicious dishes with just the right portions.

Antipasti:
Vitello Tonnato ($19): Slow-roasted veal with capers and arugula. This was my favorite starter—beautifully presented, delicious, and a generous portion.
Heirloom Tomato Salad ($19): Mozzarella, pressed watermelon, and cucumbers with mint, basil, tarragon, and champagne-lemon vinaigrette. Fresh and flavorful.

Pasta:
Pappardelle ($31): Wide pasta ribbons with slow-cooked short rib ragu and scallion horseradish crema. This is one of their signature dishes, and it's always outstanding—never disappoints.

Secondi:
Liberty Farm Duck Breast ($40): Generous portion of perfectly cooked duck breast. Absolutely delicious.

Dessert:
Panna Cotta - they make the most delicious Panna Cotta in the world ! They often changed the fruit/sauce that accompany the Panna cotta.
This time I got The Figs Panna cotta.
I highly recommend Perbacco if you're craving authentic Italian cuisine in the city. It's a reliable favorite that consistently delivers excellent food and service.

Food: 5/5
Service: 5/5
Atmosphere: 5/5
Noise Level: moderately loud

Just about everything was perfect for this dinner. Our server Jamie was personable and efficient.

The Italian 75 and Mamma Mia cocktails were great.

The Acme bread and parmigiano butter were delicious. The butter was nice and soft, yay.

The Little Gem Salad was great, delicate and not overly dressed.

Our Tajarin and Agnolotti dishes were perfectly delicious, seasoned well. The fingerling potatoes were also great. Loved the duck fat making the potatoes very tasty. Roasted perfectly.

The Butternut Squash Budino was great. Nice sweetness from the squash. The Brutti Ma Buoni was also very good. Very light. Can make a mess and shatter if you don’t cut it right!

The atmosphere was lively, and also elegant. We had a great time here and would love to come back.

Very good experience at Perbacco. Good service from the staff. I felt the food could have been better. We ordered the roasted octopus for an appetizer and then halibut and risotto for the main course. The risotto was tasty, but the halibut was a little dry and the octopus was a bit tough. For dessert we ordered the flourless chocolate cake which was delicious.

name: Moo Bong Ri
address: 4390 Telegraph Ave Ste K, Oakland, CA 94609, United States

google.name: Moo Bong Ri
google.address: 4390 Telegraph Ave Ste K, Oakland, CA 94609, United States
google.description: Noodles, fried chicken & other Korean classics in a modest counter-serve venue set in a strip mall.

top_reviews.content:
Some restaurants simply serve food. Others create an experience. This place belongs firmly in the second category.

We arrived around 6:00 p.m. and were pleasantly surprised by the efficiency. Despite a growing crowd, the wait was only about 10 minutes before we were seated. From the moment we walked in, it was clear this restaurant runs like a well-rehearsed orchestra. Every member of the staff seemed to know exactly where they needed to be, creating a smooth, welcoming atmosphere that immediately sets the tone for the evening.

The restaurant itself is spotless, modern, and full of energy without ever feeling chaotic.

The menu is extensive—but in the best possible way. Instead of feeling overwhelming, it feels like an invitation to come back again and again because there’s simply so much worth exploring.

Every dish that arrived at our table was memorable. The pork belly was outstanding, cooked with that perfect balance of crispy edges and tender, juicy meat that almost springs back with every bite. The cheesy noodles arrived still bubbling with heat, rich, comforting, and packed with layers of flavor. What impressed me most wasn’t just how good each dish tasted, but how every ingredient held its own while contributing to the bigger picture. Nothing disappeared into the background. Every bite told its own story before coming together in perfect harmony.

A few Korean soju shots, a couple of cold beers, great company, and incredible food turned dinner into one of those evenings you don’t really want to end.

As the night went on, the restaurant filled to capacity, and after eating there, it wasn’t difficult to understand why. Great food, attentive service, fair prices, and an atmosphere that makes you want to linger a little longer.

Some restaurants leave you full. The best ones leave you planning your next visit before you’ve even paid the bill.

This is absolutely one of those places, and I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend it.

We were seated immediately for a late Monday dinner. We ordered the spicy rose rice cakes and bulgogi. The banchan was served right away after we ordered which was great. Service was good all around from start to finish. Highly recommend when you’re in the area!

I really wanted to try Blood Sausage Soup after hearing my friend who just came back from Korea, say she had it three days in a row. Luckily, I found a place tjhat serves it!

I ordered the Spicy Blood Sausage Soup, which came with blood susage, broth, offal and meats. I would say the blood sausage had a really interesting texture, chewy but soft at the same time. I don't fully get the hype around it, but the flavor was really good!

We also tried the Spicy Stir-fried Octopus & Noodle, which tasted really delicious. it came with lots of small octopus and shrimps, and the flaor was enhanced by Bonito flakes and sesame oil, giving it a really unique taste. I would highly recommend this dish!
I ordered the beef soup. I was nervous at first but this soup was bursting with flavor. Primed with kim chee and topped off with ice water. Definitely coming back.

This was my first time here the and I was looking for soup and Bossam. The Seol Leong Tang was good and tasty and the Bossam with Garlic was a huge portion, but the garlic was a bit overkill for me. The garlic tasted very mild in flavor and slightly sweet. Nor what I was expecting, so I should have ordered the regular Bossam. It was a good experience overall.

top_reviews.content:
On our way to another breakfast place when we decided to stop in here instead. What a costly mistake that was.

Unfortunately it was on a day when there was only one waitress for the whole restaurant. We were seated right away next to the front door but had to move cause of the monsoon wind blowing through every time someone walked in, especially when some one holds the door open for everyone and their mother to come in.

Waited a while for anybody to help us and for our order to be taken and couldn't even order some coffee until our waitress came. They could've served us coffee right away since it was from a carafe. The bus person was attentive and the waitress was friendly and accommodating. The hostess was not friendly at all.

We ordered the special, Steak and Eggs $27.95, Eggs Benedict $18.00, Half Order Beignets $15.50, Coffee $5.00 and Espresso $3.50.

The steak was an 8 oz. Ribeye, cooked as ordered. The eggs were ordered over medium, the yolks were hard and whites runny. The Country Potatoes were bad, they were deep fried cubes that came hard and cold, pretty bad. Only one slice of toast cut in half was served instead of the normal 2 with a breakfast. Clearly cost cutting. The black grease on the edge of the plate could've been wiped off

The Eggs Benedict were just ok. First of all I don't want any flowers on any of my food, especially my Eggs Benedict. Who puts flowers on Eggs Benedict? Hollandaise was a little broken and not very tasty. And again the deep fried Country Potatoes were just bad, cold, hard and flavorless.

The Beignets were just not good. They were not light and puffy. They were thick, hard and just warm. They didn't even puff up and were just flat pieces of fried dough. They were served with strawberries, not jam and melted chocolate they called ganache.

The theme and ambience is of a French Bistro. The management needs to pay more attention to the quality of the food and not letting a customer wait so long after being seated even when short staffed. The squirt bottles on the tables for the condiments are just tacky. The bus people or even host can serve coffee. The food was just not that good and we won't be returning. We should've gone to Nation's.

Stopped by as my mom wanted to try the place again.  In this visit we found the service to be slow.  Just like what other reviewers noted too. We had to flag down a server to check on our food.  Once they went back to the area to check on it we saw that they were carrying it out with in a minute.  This means our food was sitting ere for a while.

The place wasn't busy as there are a few open tables but we still waited for a table.  We counted the number of guess and looked at the number of workers.  They had a good ratio.  Not sure why it was so slow.

When the food arrived it looked good.  Instagram ready.  Flavors were okay.

Overall its a 3 star place, but with a 2 star service.

If you want to try out the place make sure you have extra time.

Absolutely amazing breakfast spot! I had the avocado toast and French onion soup, and both were absolutely fantastic—fresh, flavorful, and beautifully prepared. My husband ordered the vegetarian omelet, which was perfectly cooked and full of flavor. To top it all off, the matcha tea was outstanding—smooth, rich, and the best I’ve had in a long time. Highly recommend this place for anyone who loves delicious food and warm service!

Came here for breakfast with my girlfriend on a Tuesday morning and it was the perfect move. It was nice and calm during the week, and we grabbed outdoor seating to enjoy the sun. Super relaxed vibe.

The food was honestly amazing. Everything tasted fresh, portions were solid, and it came out looking just as good as it tasted. Coffee was on point too. It just felt like one of those easy, feel good breakfast spots.
I’ve seen this place get crazy busy on the weekends, so coming on a weekday was clutch. If you want a more chill experience, I’d recommend doing the same.

Definitely coming back.
Try their Matcha latte 🔥

This place was cute. Food was ok. Belini were decent priced. I like my pancake golden, the one I received was dark brown. The country potatoes seem to be old and no season and the eggs were bland. Great company with my Lil sis.
