top_reviews.content:
Belotti Ristorante e Bottega in Oakland is a must-visit destination for anyone looking for authentic Northern Italian cuisine in the East Bay. The kitchen operates with a level of precision that is rare to find, and the consistency from start to finish is excellent.

The handmade pasta is the clear highlight of the menu. Their Casoncelli, prepared Bergamo-style with beef, prosciutto, pork shoulder, and Grana Padano, is a masterclass in balance. The dough is rolled perfectly—thin and delicate, but with enough bite to stand up to the savory butter and sage sauce. The addition of chewy smoked pancetta adds just the right amount of texture to the dish.

For starters, the Uovo Asparagi e Tartufo is a standout and a great example of layering textures. The egg has a perfectly crisp exterior that yields to a rich, molten yolk, and they aren't shy with the fresh truffle shavings. It’s an earthy, savory dish that works incredibly well with the fresh asparagus and creamy, savory fonduta underneath. The Vitello Tonnato—slow-roasted, grass-fed Piedmontese beef with a delicate yellowfin tuna sauce—is equally precise, with the caper essence and lemon zest providing a bright, clean finish.

Even while dining in the outdoor parklet, the experience was great. It’s well-designed and comfortable, making the most of the natural light while keeping the atmosphere quiet and enjoyable. I also appreciated that they serve imported Italian MoleCola rather than standard sodas; it has a crisp, refreshing bite that cleanses the palate effectively between heavier courses.

Dessert service was exceptional. The Affogato al Caffe is excellent on its own, but adding a splash of Grand Marnier gives it a sophisticated, citrusy complexity that pairs perfectly with the espresso and vanilla gelato. The Bunet Piemontese was also a highlight—a rich, velvety pudding of cocoa and crushed amaretti cookies, encased in a 60% dark chocolate shell and topped with soft, unsweetened whipped cream. It is intense but not too heavy, which is exactly how a dessert like this should be.

There isn't a weak link in the experience at Belotti. It is officially one of the best spots in the East Bay for anyone seeking high-quality, authentic Italian food.

Everything was outstanding, but the Pappardelle Al Funghi was truly unforgettable – rich, earthy, and perfectly balanced. The panna cotta was divine!

top_reviews.content:
I've ordered from here several times, and this is now the second time this exact issue has happened.

Your menu lists birria as one of the taco meat options for $4 per taco, and it clearly offers the option to add cheese for $0.50 to a taco. Based on that pricing, I ordered four birria tacos with the cheese add-on, which came to $18.

When I received my order, none of the tacos had cheese, even though I was charged for it. If customers aren't actually allowed to add cheese to birria tacos, then that option shouldn't be available on the menu.

What makes this even more frustrating is that it feels like customers are being pushed into ordering quesabirrias instead, which cost $5 each. If the same portion of cheese is being added, it doesn't make sense to charge an extra $1 per taco while also advertising a $0.50 cheese add-on for regular tacos. Birria is simply one of the taco meat options, and customers should be able to add cheese for the advertised price.

This is the second time I've been charged for the cheese add-on without receiving it. At this point, it doesn't feel like an isolated mistake. If the menu is incorrect, it should be updated. If the add-on is offered, it should be honored. Customers shouldn't have to pay for something they don't receive.

I hope this issue gets addressed so future customers don't have the same experience.

Today I had the most mysterious dining experience in the Bay Area🤔 I ordered a shrimp ceviche tostada and a fish ceviche tostada and received what can only be described as “Fish/Shrimp Ghost Ceviche.”👻
After spending nearly $30 on food, a drink, and tip, I got home excited to enjoy my craving. I opened the container and found vegetables, tomatoes, onions, and cucumbers. What I didn’t find was the shrimp or the fish. I literally recorded a video digging through the entire container with a fork like I was on an archaeological expedition searching for evidence that seafood had once existed there. Spoiler alert: not a single shrimp or piece of fish was found. When I realized there was neither shrimp nor fish, and then discovered how disappointing the seasoning was, I honestly didn’t know whether to laugh or cry. If you’re looking for a completely vegan ceviche experience, this might be your place, because my order contained absolutely nothing suggesting that a shrimp or fish had ever participated in the recipe. The strangest part is that when I ordered, I was asked whether I wanted the ceviche raw (cured in lime juice) or cooked. I chose the traditional lime-cured version. However, when I tasted the Fish/Shrimp Ghost Ceviche, it didn’t taste like lime at all. It also had no salt. I actually had to add both lime juice and salt at home just to give it the basic flavor you’d expect from a ceviche. I completely understand if a restaurant is running low on ingredients or nearing the end of the day. What I don’t understand is selling shrimp and fish ceviche when what arrives is essentially a marinated vegetable salad. Eating out in the Bay Area has become increasingly expensive. For many people, it’s an occasional treat, not an everyday expense. That’s why it’s especially disappointing to spend the equivalent of about an hour’s work on a meal that doesn’t match what was advertised. If they were out of seafood, I would have appreciated a simple, honest explanation. “Sorry, we’re out of ceviche today” would have been far better than serving Fish/Shrimp Ghost Ceviche. Maybe this was an exception. Maybe this was an exception. Maybe it wasn’t. Either way, it was unacceptable.
What I do know is that after this experience, I won’t be coming back to find out.
Would I recommend this place?
Absolutely.

To my enemies.

Not to my friends.😶

Incredible quesabirria & shrimp tacos! This is my go to for the 2.5 pound kilo burrito for only $22. The staff is nice and their seating area is very well kept. I would suggest removing any valuables before parking ANYWHERE in Oakland. Give them a try!

This place was recommended by a few friends. We went on a Saturday the line and the wait to get the food was not long at all. If you are looking for Mexican style sea food this food truck has that and much more. We arrived and saw the menus on the food truck and it was mind blowing. Not only could you read what they had but you could see all the plate’s because they have photos of each plate that they make all over the food truck. So we got into ordering we had the Baja shrimp and fish tacos they were amazing we also ordered a ceviche mixto also good and súper tasty to top it off we order a quesibirria it’s a quesadilla with beef meet that was also amazing. Unfortunately our stomachs were not big enough to try more things, but we are definitely coming back. Not only they have sea food but they also have a veggie menu and a full taco truck menu with all the tacos and burritos you can imagine. I highly recommend you coming here with an empty stomach and get ready to enjoy all the amazing food they make here.

Baja Mango Habanero Fish Tacos 4/5
Steak Nachos were 4/5 (chips were stale)
birria tacos 3/5, juicy meat but salty
Wet Burrito, sauce salty and meat was salty
Regular Steak Burritos, salty

I would be back for the mango habanero fish tacos. They were not spicy like how I’d a expect a “habanero” to be, but it was sweet with a kick from the jalapeños.

Plenty of parking spaces and they have a wash station and restroom on site! Cool addition! 🤣

reviews_snippets.content: "Plenty of parking,places to sit, fast service and the food was THE BOMB!!"
"The meat om the tacos is juicy and tender and the sauce is not too salty."
"The fish taco and the shrimp taco are really good...money well spent"

top_reviews.content: We came here for a late dinner on Saturday. First, I'd like to mention that the service here is excellent. The staff was very attentive from the moment we walked in. I like the purple potato chips with lime juice that came with the meal and the food presentation. For starters, we had the Empanada Trio and the Anticuchos (grilled chicken skewers). The skewers were flavorful, and I liked the little side bitter green salad with grape tomatoes. For small plates, we had the Costillas (crispy pork spare ribs, gochujang - Inca Kola bbq sauce), and the Pulpito Parrillero (the grilled octopus was tender, and the purple mashed potatoes that came with that dish were fantastic). The Yuca Fries were great with a little bit of crispiness on the outside & well salted. The Garlic Spinach as the side dish was nice and garlicky. I also liked the decor of this well-lit 2-tier level restaurant.

Came here with friends last night and had a reservation. We were seated on what looks like an addition and was up against the wall with a large bench, which worked out well for us. Tables had a mix of tea light candles as well as some led tea lights but it was pretty well lit and didn't need those table lights but does add a bit to the ambiance.

We ordered several appetizers and small dishes that I missed taking photos of but came out pretty quick. We had ceviche (which I didn't have so not sure on quality but the table seemed to like it), Mac n cheese, yucca fries, Tequenos, pulpo,shrimp and tuna tartare. Mac n cheese was a standout and better than I expected, really creamy but not overly oily/fatty with a nice mouth feel. The octopus was nice and tender but nothing to special about it--could have used a nice sauce to pair with it and the tartare was just okay, not as fresh as I'd hoped. The shrimp was also a hit and the quinoa coating they put on it gave a nice textural contrast to the dish.

For entrees, I had the pollo, which was nice and tender and it came with fries and a salad. The salad didn't quite seem to fit well with the dish. The greens were a bit bitter and honestly a bit soggy. The seafood paella was really good, seasoned well and the seafood was cooked to perfection.

Overall an enjoyable meal but a bit on the pricey side. It's a nice date night or special occasion restaurant but a bit steep for a regular meal out.

The wait staff and bartenders are amazing. Especially Mary and Washington.  Their happy hour is amazing as well as their margaritas. They use a house made salt rim made of hibiscus, salt, and mango puree! 🔥

The service was really excellent! All of the staff like Hector and Nacho are so nice and attentive. You can’t sit outside, but I like the fact that the windows open so pretty much you’re outside. Raw Oysters were so fresh! The Pescado à la Macho had really fresh seafood esp the salmon, thought the broth was a little too creamy. Lomo is delicious. 🤤
Amazing vibes. Tall roofs. Great ambiance. Friendly staff. Ceviche and tequeños! And non alcoholic beer available

reviews_snippets.content: "My husband loved the combination of the roasted chicken, fresh salad, and fries."

top_reviews.content:
Casual but nice atmosphere. First came here to celebrate a friend’s milestone birthday in a group of 8. Been back several times for the food, location, and service. It’s one of my favorite spots to stop at on our way to San Francisco. Parking can be a little tough but you can find it (check the parking lot in the back).

The pizzas are amazing, great variety, fresh, high quality ingredients. The salads and appetizers are also great. They also have a full bar if you want to get down like that 😜

Who doesn't love pizza. This pizza joint was highly recommended in Albany. I hate the parking as it's only street parking. The restaurant is easy to find. Plenty of seats and good for groups. The restaurant is modern and nicely decorated.

We ordered two large pizza's.  One is a thin crust Chicken Pesto. It was very good but pesto is really strong. We also ordered the Detroit style All star pizza. These were pretty good. We also ordered their large Caesar salad for the family. That was pretty good even if the leaves were whole and had to cut it up. I had a sangria as well, and it was good and strong.

Service was very good. Prices are little pricey though but I enjoyed myself there. They were training a new hire but they still served us well. I think I would come back again if in the area.

i thought pizza places in albany we’re all pretty average, but then i found this spot and it totally changed my mind. the crust is that perfect chewy crispy balance and the sauce is actually tangy and fresh not just sugary syrup. already planning my next visit becuase i want to try like three other pizzas on thier menu.

Great pizza! Nice people and good beer too. Totally family friendly. They had a Kolsch that was quite refreshing. They were willing to make a pizza with just goat cheese (lactose intolerant here). Good experience overall.

The pizza and salad were great as always, but what really made the experience wonderful was our server, Kiley! Not only was she prompt and efficient, but her friendly, cheerful demeanor made us feel right at home. So kudos to Kiley and to Little Star pizza! ❤️

reviews_snippets.content: "Overall, amazing pizzas, service, decor, and atmosphere."

top_reviews.content:
I stopped by the Burger King on John Daly Boulevard in California and had an exceptional experience from start to finish. The parking lot was immaculate, and walking inside, the entire restaurant was just as spotless.
​The staff provided very friendly and remarkably quick service. I used a coupon for a free Whopper, and I have to say—Burger King is really trying to revamp the Whopper right now, and they have done an absolute stellar job. The bread was fresh and crisp, and the lettuce, tomato, and onion were wonderfully crisp and fresh as well. The Whopper itself was piping hot and absolutely delicious.
​If you are in the area, I highly recommend this location. It’s clean, fast, and the food is top-notch!

I appreciate they open on Christmas day and no music is great!  However, they told me there's no wifi.  Therefore, I give them 4 stars.  Popeyes on market has wifi.
The owner is very kind to respond back to me.  Now there's no music is even better.  I come here to write to the White House telling them todo their jobs right.

This location refused a valid coupon I received in the mail. When I called customer service, they asked for my email but never sent me an email to correct the problem. Burger King has demonstrated a lack of proper representation, luring me to their restaurant, denying me proper service, then failing to offer supportive customer service. What a big let down. I will be going to In-N-Out for now on.

They do not speak English here. It took 5 staff to fill an order because the people working the register do not speak English well enough to answer questions about the menu in English. They also call out the numbers in Spanish. I wouldn't be surprised if ice showed up soon. It wouldn't be a problem if the staff was not rude to people that don't speak Spanish.
Not a bad Burger King! My local BK is always good but some locations the food tastes off... not this one though! Same tasty food I've come to expect.

top_reviews.content: Super yummy food and a cute little classy spot. We will definitely be coming back.

We had a very nice table outside on the deck looking at all the boats. The food was really good we started with oysters and we had shrimp and everything was just what it should be. Also the wine was the house variety and it was really good. We will definitely come here again

Really enjoyed finding this spot right at sundown. The view of the San Francisco skyline being back-lit with a sunset set the tone for a good meal.
Had the spicy scallops and shrimp and my friend had a nice piece of Salmon. Each was cooked nicely and both were well seasoned. I would recommend either and found a bunch more on the menu that I want to try. Also great view of the local Alameda Harbor on one side, and a view of the Aircraft carrier on the other.

Went there with some friends over the weekend. The place is located at the Yacht dock. Nice and peaceful place. Menu was great. I enjoyed Sautéed Prawn. Started with Fresh OJ and 2 sides. Both were awesome. For starters, sauces were awesome.

Main course were fantastic and delicious. We ended the lunch with super awesome dessert.

After the heavy, we went for light walk around with view of Bay Bridge.

Service was great and fast too. Waiter was very courteous and respectful.

Highly recommend this place to try and visit.

We come here a couple times a year for various group gatherings. They make it fairly easy to host events for a fixed price. Food is fresh and tasty, service is good, they have a full bar onsite for folks who like a cocktail.
Good all around deal for group gatherings.

top_reviews.content: Found Prospect frustratingly inconsistent. The drinks were excellent. (I tried the hibiscus margarita and the lovely peachin’ to the choir.) The melon starter was good, but the burger took an unfathomable amount of time to arrive and was clearly overdone for a medium-rare order. (The fries were yummy.) Frustrating.
I walk by this restraunt a lot and it always looked somewhat stuffy. I was pleasantly surprised and thoroughly enjoyed my meal and the service! Thank you for a great eating experience!

I needed a quiet place to unwind by myself after a brutal work week and decided to give Prospect a try. Sat at the bar and the energy of the place instantly lifted my mood—it's upscale but has this lively, hip warmth to it. I ordered a cocktail recommended by the bartender and paired it with their famous pork chop. Honestly, it was cooked to absolute perfection and the portion size was incredibly generous. You can tell they put a lot of thought into the menu details. The staff was friendly and kept an eye on me without being overly intrusive, which I really appreciated for a solo dining experience. I’ll definitely be back next time I need a treating-myself night.

Can’t believe I’d never been to Prospect before! Was sooo tasty and had a fun, vibey atmosphere. I came here with a group, and it was perfect for us to lounge on the couches near the door.
The dish I had was everything I could want in a pasta. I wish I could remember the name 😩 it looks like it’s no longer on the menu unfortunately. I think it was a rigatoni  with beef ragu and truffle. What really made it was the fried rosemary - I had never seen that before, but it really elevated the dish. Paired with a glass of rosé, Prospect was the perfect evening!
Vibe is good here and food is great.   Easy to find street parking around this place too.

reviews_snippets.content: "The happy hour includes $5 glasses of wine and a good selection of bar bites."

top_reviews.content: The view was beyond beautiful and added to the coastal experience. The food was lacking in spice level but the overall flavor profile was well rounded. I loved that they have a shrimp taco that was gluten free.

We are visiting from the most southern part of California. My wife and I had their Fried Shrimp, Birria and Pork Tacos. They were delicious. My wife had the pineapple margarita. It was the best. Jairo, the Lead/Host is a stand up guy. Emily, the bartender is amazing. Lead Karla kept us entertained with some great information on San Francisco.

This is a Mexican restaurant in Ghirardelli Square in the Marina District.  There was no wait when we arrived for a late lunch.  They have both indoor and outdoor seating and the views of the Maritime Historic District are lovely.  Today was a clear day and the view of Alcatraz was fantastic.  The food is very tasty.  There is a nice array of variety with a little something for most tastes and the price point isn't awful for San Francisco.  I would recommend a nice stop over here to rest your feet and have a bit to eat or a cold drink on a hot day!

Best taco I’ve eaten and the service was spectacular 100%. Good food good beer good views and great service even on a busy night like 4th July 250 Anniversary. Thanks guys you made a great night for a couple of Aussie travellers

Everything is prepared daily on the spot. The freshest and yummiest tortillas and authentic Yucatán menu by Chef Tim & his amazing team. Excellent cocktails, with + without alcohol, and gorgeous views to boot. Don’t miss it!

reviews_snippets.content: "Excellent food, we ordered a portion of nachos that we ate well in 2 people."

top_reviews.content:
This restaurant offers an exceptional dining experience for breakfast or brunch. The culinary offerings are exceptional, particularly the fried chicken, which possesses a unique flavor profile that distinguishes it from conventional fried chicken. The menu is diverse and includes a variety of delectable dishes that are highly recommended.
While the establishment is popular, it has limited seating capacity, resulting in a considerable wait time before being seated. Additionally, the wait time for food delivery can be extended. However, the overall experience is worth the wait, and the establishment’s service could be improved. Apart from these minor shortcomings, the establishment is otherwise flawless.

Had a fantastic brunch at Cracked & Battered! The chicken and waffles were absolutely delicious—the waffle was fluffy and perfectly cooked, while the chicken was crispy, juicy, and full of flavor. Great portions and a really satisfying meal. Definitely a spot I’d happily visit again! 🍗🧇

Great food and customer service! The place is run by the loveliest family.

The food is clean, fresh and the portions are very generous.

We ordered hummus, pancakes, fried chicken, and got to try their fresh squeezed orange juice.

This is top of my list of places to checkout when in SF. Looking forward to their new and larger location coming right down the street.

Enjoyed the experience at C&B and looking forward to the next visit.

Came here for brunch and love the setup. You order and pay online before they serve you food. The food is amazing. I had a fried chicken Benedict and was super impressed by the portion and the taste. The only downside is the outdoor seating we were at was directly in front of the sun and it wasn't the most pleasant dining experience. I am okay with outdoor seating but maybe have a shed for situation like this.

Besides that, i would definitely be back to try on different menu again.

Great chicken & waffles! Waffles were crispy and freshly prepared, and so was the chicken. Wasn’t too much of a wait for the food after ordering in person. Definitely a great brunch spot to try out in the city.

top_reviews.content:
Rose’s Cafe is a lovely little brunch spot with cozy tables and genuinely friendly, accommodating service. We were a party of six on an early Monday morning and had no trouble getting seated, though there are no reservations.

The cinnamon roll and croissant were fantastic, as were both breakfast pizzas, salmon and turkey, served on thin, crunchy toasted bread with egg. The fluffy spinach soufflé and pudding-like French toast were also delicious. And the latte served in a bowl? Magnificent! Coffee was pretty good, too.

A great brunch spot in a lovely neighborhood, perfect for wandering around the shops afterward!

We’re visiting from out of town, and I came here with a friend who drove in from San Jose to spend the day with.  We went on a Saturday for brunch, and we got the breakfast pizza to share with a side of bacon and roasted potatoes.  The pizza and bacon were delicious, but the potatoes I would pass.  I think they were over cooked and bland.

Also got a cafe au lait, and it was served in bowl! Super cute.
Beautiful bistro on a picturesque street corner. Rose’s Cafe is one of the few spots in the city that serves brunch until 4 PM! And the food is 💯.

The food was good, but I wouldn’t call it one of the best brunch spots in SF, definitely not worth all the hype. The soup was actually quite good, and the breakfast pizza stood out as the best dish.

The space itself is lovely with a great vibe right on Union Street, which definitely adds to the experience. However, the service wasn’t very friendly, which took away from the overall feel.

All in all, a decent spot, just slightly above average for SF brunch standards.

Just wow!  The bread on many dishes is light, fluffy, and just a quality product.  The corner location is easily accessible and there is well over 25+ seats outside on a less than busy corner.  Accessibility is easy for all patrons.

Salmon dishes here are a top recommendation.  The Salmon Cozy is light, yet has a sweet Italian dressing taste that makes it highly desired for more with subtle watercress.  The Salmon Pizza is a unique gem that combines eggs with smoked salmon:)

There is plenty of dishes that kids will enjoy.  The pizza is again light with sauce and the dough is crunchy and holds its form well.

The Staff is the friendliest with quality service throughout your time at Rose’s.  Do not miss a stop at Rose’s when in San Francisco.

top_reviews.content: Still the best place to enjoy that fresh California vegetarian burrito and crispy fish tacos. They're doing specials (but one beer, get a second for free!) and have two TVs 📺 📺 for the world cup! People complain about the price but one is paying for the excellence, the freshness, the amazing and delicious array of salsa at the salsa bar. My opinion 😉 to me, I'm okay with enjoying an excellent meal for maybe $4-5 more but you're getting such high quality. It's worth it! It all rounds out to be about the same anyway with what's included. 👍🏼

Look, I love this place and their food is excellent and I've been eating here on and off since high school. . . buuut at this point their prices are frankly bordering on exorbitant for a taqueria. I got a regular burrito earlier today and it cost me 20 bucks. A regular, not a super burrito mind you.

TLDR: this place serves wonderful food, and the owners/staff are very nice but their prices are bonkers.

Decent Mexican food in downtown Berkeley. There isn't table service here. You order at the counter and pick up your food. You also have to bus your own tables. Despite all I felt the food is a bit in the expensive side for Mexican food. However, the portions are large. I ordered guacamole with chips as an appetizer and we received a very generous amount of guacamole!

We had a delicious burrito and chips and a margarita to share. All of it was great! The chips and the salsa of course are the star of the show. We officially like the pumpkin seed salsa. The burrito was the mole burrito, perhaps the one thing I would suggest for improvement is the amount of meat in there. The atmosphere of course is really beautiful.

I ordered a burrito and soft drink, which came to $30 before tip $35 total after adding gratuity. While the food was acceptable, I don’t believe it justified the $30 price point. The service was mediocre at best, with no complimentary refills offered on soft drinks, and the burrito itself was noticeably smaller than what I’d expect for that price.
For the same money, I can get a more generous portion at Chipotle just down the street, with free refills included. Given the combination of high prices, small portions, and lackluster service, I’ll be eating at corporate America owned Chipotle next time. The value proposition here simply doesn’t add up, especially when there are better options so readily available nearby.

top_reviews.content:
A great halal option in the heart of SF.

They have a big menu with lots of speciality pizza options. We tried the buffalo chicken, margarita, and garlic chicken.

The pizza dough, sauce, and cheese are carefully sourced and come together to make a great pie.

Plus side, everything on the menu is 100% halal which is hard to find in a pizza place.

Best part of the experience was the customer service. The employees are warm and nice.

We’ll be back again soon!

This is arguably the best pizza I’ve ever had...across the world.

The owners clearly put serious care into every detail, from the dough to the sauce, cheese, and every topping. All the meats are halal and either carefully sourced or made in-house, which really shows in the quality and flavor.

The pizza itself is incredible, with a perfect crisp in every bite and a really well-balanced taste throughout. They even recently competed in the Pizza Maker of the Year contest in Las Vegas at the Pizza Expo, which says a lot about the level they’re operating at.

10/10 pizza, and even better hospitality from the owners and staff. This is my go to spot when I'm in SF. No one does it better than Pronto Pizzeria.

Every time I come to Pronto Pizzeria, it feels like comfort, happiness, and amazing food all in one place. The food here is absolutely incredible — especially the pasta and pizza. Honestly, everything on the menu tastes fresh, flavorful, and made with care.

What I love most is that this place never disappoints. No matter what kind of day you’ve had, the food here somehow lifts your mood and satisfies every craving. The atmosphere is welcoming, the taste is consistently amazing, and you can truly feel the passion behind the food.

One of my favorite spots in San Francisco without a doubt. Highly recommended for anyone who loves great Italian food and a place that feels good to come back to again and again.

This place is a halal haven for people like me who want quality delicious food for an actually affordable price in this city.

This is my third day in a row coming back, and from their pizza slices, to sandwiches and even pasta I couldn’t get enough (talking from a guy who comes from Toronto).

Chicken buffalo pizza and Philly cheesesteak sandwich are on peak I gotta say! And service is great as well!

This place makes the most FIRE pizza! It seems like a hole-in-the-wall but don’t be fooled. They source their ingredients from Italy, all organic and natural, the food in here is absolutely peak, and the staff are incredibly friendly. Ask for something called a burrata pizza, it’s the only place in the city I know where to get it with globs of burrata cheese, basil, and a blend of Parmesan. I find myself going back there literally all the time because it's worth it. Can’t speak well enough of this place, ya’ll doing god’s work… of keeping me fed at odd times of the evening.

The salad was the worst of it all since the croutons ended up being stale and the lettuce and sauce disappointed. Luckly the server took it off the bill which I will was was great of then to do.

Okay - so the service was amazing - they checked in on is multiple times throughout our meal. Refilled our drinks, brought us more bread etc. Nice spot on the water , clean restaurant. I thought the prices were super reasonable. We got the spinache dip appetizer and I thought it was excellent. Some one got the chowder and they said it was good. One person in our party got the salmon piccata (said it was good). I got the beef short ribs and thought they were good. Nothing that I would crave and not the most amazing thing ever, but good. They had a really good menu. Lots of stuff I wanted to try. The only thing I was surprised they didn't have is chicken piccata (which is what I wanted). I think I'd try the meatloaf if I went back. Some one else in our group got a pasta dish (like raviolis with cheese but called something else). I'm definitely gonna go back there.... For sure getting the spinach dip again and then I'll try a different entre. Overall impressed with the service, the price, and menu selection.

Great location! Beautiful views! Did was good, not great. The salmon piccata was good, the salmon was great the pasta was from a box.

The Old Siam is conveniently located on the corner of Ellis and Mason streets in downtown area (two walking blocks away from Powell Street Subway Station) that is surrounded by hotels imhv should be regarded one of the few best authentic affordable Thai restaurants left in The City.
According to legendary “Chef Pam” from Bangkok authentic Thai food is indeed a marriage of Thai Chinese which is consisted of “five elements: salt, acid, spices, texture and the Maillard reaction, the chemical reaction between amino acids and reducing sugars that occur when heated.” However, there is a saying "green comes from blue, but intends to be better than blue." Signature Thai cuisine is unique which has many flavors:{ 1. sweet, 2. salty, 3. sour, 4. spicy, and 5.bitter} not overpowering one another yet robust with aromatic lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves, coconut milk, palm sugar, and red chilies 😮 😳.
My favorites at the Old Siam are ❶Lunch Specials: Combination of Catfish Prik Khing @Goong Hom Par {Fried Shrimp Rolls(2)} ❷Chef Specials: Combination Seafood or Siam Seafood ❸ Thai Noodle Soup: Thai Traditional Noodle Soup or Seafood Noodle Soup. “Gin hâi à-ròi ná!”😉Kop Jai!🙏 Nick!🫡
PS: "Siam" is the former name of Thailand,  derived from foreign terms (possibly Sanskrit for "dark/brown" also in ancient Chinese referred to based on its pronunciation as Xian [暹] or, more commonly, Xianluo [暹羅]. Thai Chinese are the largest minority group in the country and possibly the largest overseas Chinese community in the world, estimated at 10 million people accounting for 11-14% of the total population of Thailand. The Chinese traders started migrating to neighboring Siam in mid 1300s and primarily are Cantonese, Hokkien, Teochew, Hainanese, and Hakka.  Under King Rama in early 20th century law required the adoption of Thai surnames by migrants, a move which was ostensibly aimed at the Thai Chinese community. Common Chinese Surnames according to AI are in two categories:
1. "Sae": Saelee/Saeli (李), Saetang/Saetung (陳), Sae-ung (黃), Sae-ngow (吳), Sae-lim (林), Sae-wong (王).
2. Long Surnames (Teochew/Thai mix):
Limcharoen / Tancharoen (Lim/Tan - 林).
Wongsuwan / Wongsawad (Wong - 黃/王).
Jiarawanon (Chia/Ha/Xia - 謝). Tongthaworn (Tong 唐 or 湯).{Is that right, Hannah 😂}

For comparison, Night and Song market in LA, or Sticky Rice Lao street food in Orlando, FL, blows this place out of the water. It definitely does not deserve the recognition it deserves. Or perhaps its quality has changed since I visited over 10 years ago. However, we did randomly run into an old friend we haven’t seen in 25 years here, so that was super cool.

Been going to CG for years. I'm stuffed and sleepy so short review.  All the food at CG is good you can't go wrong.  Get the sampler  plate that sausage will change your life the crispy rice that's a meal and a deal. I need a nap.

5 stars for food, but giving 4 because historically their phone almost never rings properly, and their hostess told me last call was 9:45pm when I called earlier today but they actually close at 9 🤦🏻‍♀️ Their website also doesn’t work properly… so yeah amazing food but management could really use some work.

Favorites:
- Larp
- Pumpkin curry
- Pad ped pla cook (catfish)
- Rice ball salad

Everything, especially the vegetables, is literally cooked to perfection.
Great food, menu has many options, Laotian and Thai selection, the food I got was just a bit sweet for me. Lovely service and food came quick!

Pad Thai was pretty good, and big portion. Green curry was excellent. Thai iced tea also good, and they even put less ice when asked. Mango sticky rice just okay. Rice was a little dense, but coconut sauce is flavorful, and mangoes were rice. Friendly service

reviews_snippets.content: "Go to place for lunch with great flavorful food like curry and pad thai!"

top_reviews.content: Absolutely amazing experience from start to finish! The food was fresh, flavorful, and perfectly seasoned. Every dish tasted authentic and homemade, especially the grilled meats, hummus, and warm pita bread. The portions were generous, the service was friendly and attentive, and the atmosphere was cozy and welcoming. You can really tell they use high-quality ingredients and put care into every meal. Easily one of the best Mediterranean restaurants I’ve been to — highly recommend and will definitely be back!

We went for a family dinner with friends and kids and surprisingly we and one more table, were the only ones with kids. The other table sat outside.

There was no wait for a Sunday dinner.

The place has more of a formal but cozy ambience. You can dress up or be casual and both would go.

The food itself was a mix of good and okay.

They start out with some chips for the table. We had 4 vegetarians and 2 non vegetarians in the group and everyone had a good set of items to choose from.

We shared the brussel sprouts which were great, the grape leaf rice with herbs (warak inab) which was okay. The non vegetarians shared the Musakhan chicken rolls from appetizers which were great.

For main course we had the beet arugula salad (great), makhaluba with lamb (great) and mujjadara vegetarian (which was okay). We shared the baklava with ice cream dessert which was good!

Overall-
Food had some great items and others were just okay.  The overall menu is on pricier side. There is no kids menu but we never order from kids menu; and all dishes were kid friendly . So it wasn't an issue for us. But something to note as many families do look for a kids section and this place doesn't have one.

Ambience is nice and chattery but not noisy. People seemed to be having a good time

Good clean restrooms
There is outdoor seating and parking is on the street

I would definitely go again to try more dishes.

Food was very good.  5 of us were seated along with our 2 yr old. We were automatically charged the 6 or more person gratuity and taxed for the gratuity. If you will be automatically be assessed the gratuity, please provide good service. Please do not forget about us because you know you will automatically get your tip. It doesn't feel good.
The food was amazing. The ambience was lively. We had a great time. Looking forward to my next visit.

Really enjoyed a Friday night out with partner for first time dining at this lovely Mediterranean place.  Serverd by Erika, we had a great evening with her service. Explained many options on the menu, made perfect drink recommendations,  and all was with a smiling attitude.  Thats been hard to find lately.  Thank you for a great night Erika! Thank you Zaytoon. We'll be back

top_reviews.content:
Juan's Place has been proudly serving the Berkeley community since 1972, and being a customer for about 30 years makes the connection to this iconic spot even more meaningful. The restaurant’s remarkable history is rooted in a commitment to authentic Mexican cuisine and a welcoming, family-run atmosphere that has drawn generations of locals, Cal students, and visitors for over five decades.

Having been a loyal patron for around 30 years, it’s clear how special Juan’s Place is—a true staple where the flavors and traditions of Mexico are celebrated with every meal, continuing a legacy that began more than 50 years ago.

Pro's:

- Quiet place, at least for weekday lunch, no music playing, relaxing atmosphere

-Friendly staff who give you free soda refills and pretty much as much tortilla chips and salsa that you want. I believe they make their own tortilla chips and they are quite good. They will even give you a bag and little containers to take home some of the chips and salsa if you want to.

Con's:

Way too expensive for what you get! I can't say the food is bad or anything, but certainly nothing to write home about. It's simply over-priced!

Such an amazing spot to enjoy! Their super burrito is HUGE and the tacos are a very healthy serving.

The lime wine margarita was a solid drink choice. The waiters here are so kind and happy to strike up a conversation and share a laugh with you.

The prices are great, the food is great, and the parking was easy!

What an amazing, family restaurant! My wife and friends try to order from here once a week. They're always generous with their chips, salsa, and extras. Food is always fresh and you can tell by the dairy they use! The place is huge too with an under rated bar where we ate and watched the Warriors. Such an under rated restaurant in the bay!

This is a classic place that I hadn’t been to since I was in college. It hasn’t changed a bit. The decor is really cool and the food is very good. Prices are a little bit high, considering what you get. Service was good, but not great. I was surprised at how long it took for the food to get there. The servers and staff were very nice. The place is a bit off the beaten path, but if you’re in the area, it’s definitely worth checking out.

top_reviews.content: Stopped by for a quick drink and bite and also for the dog menu! The hostess was super nice and I loved the qr menu. We keep to ourselves my husband and I so it was nice to order from the qr code. We got the salmon taquitos and the egg and purple rice for our dog. They kept our water pitcher full and our drinks were so good and really nice size for the price.

This is the cutest, most dog friendly patio with tropical food and drinks.

Of all of the "puppy menu" places we have tried, this one had the most thoughtful and hearty.

Thanks for having us!

Palm House is highly recommended if you’re looking for a great spot for happy hour and small bites. The drinks are fantastic, and the staff is incredibly friendly. I tried their Palm House slushy, which was the perfect treat for a warm day in SF!

We also loved the food—all the small bites were so delicious that we ended up ordering second and third rounds because they were just too good to stop at one!

Beyond the food and drinks, the technology here is a huge plus. They use QR code ordering at the table, which makes the whole process so much faster and more convenient. You don't have to wait for a server to take your order, and you can even settle your final bill directly through the QR code. Everything came out lightning-fast.

It’s also a top-tier spot to watch sports—I recently came here to watch the one of World Cup game, and the atmosphere was great. Highly recommend!

Second time here, first time for food, what a lovely gem especially on a warm, sunny day! Love that they have a combination of staff and self-service ordering. The food was fresh and healthy while still filling. Drinks are tasty and strong. Most of all, I love that they have a dog menu option. Also looks like they have event options like bingo and a DJ several nights per week.
Great experience, food was delicious and reasonably priced. Service was very friendly and the outdoor areas was a great vibe!

reviews_snippets.content: "Very polite staff, very tasty spicy fries and jerk chicken tacos"

top_reviews.content: Barely any meat. Got a #3 - smoked turkey, brie cheese, sprouts and mustard. Basically just one thin layer of sliced turkey as you can see in the photo. Maybe 2 slices total. Not worth the 30-45 minute line/wait. Ive seen Subway sandwiches packed with thicker layers of meat
Food was made super quick and enjoyed a coffee while I ordered. The sandwiches were sooo freaking good! The #14 on ciabatta was insane. Tons of bacon and avocado, best sandwich in CA by far!

Morucci’s makes sandwiches and they are pretty good, but not life changing. If you’re in the area I’d recommend checking them out. Definitely beats lunardi’s and Ike’s. I especially liked how the bread they had was a great level of crunchy and how they had tall and skinny diet cokes in addition to the regular ones.
They have the best sandwiches- the bread the meat and freshest ingredients - tried roasted Turkey with tomato mozz and pesto was awesome and so was the roasted red pepper soup

Morucci’s Deli never disappoints! The ingredients are incredibly fresh, and they don’t skimp on the fillings. Every sandwich is packed generously with plenty of quality meats, cheeses, and fresh toppings, making it a satisfying meal from the first bite to the last.

The staff is friendly, welcoming, and incredibly quick with the service. Even when they’re busy, they keep things moving while still providing great customer service.

If you’re looking for a fresh, delicious, and generously filled sandwich, Morucci’s Deli is definitely worth a visit!

name: Kuma Sushi + Sake
address: 1040 Polk St, San Francisco, CA 94109, United States

google.name: Kuma Sushi + Sake
google.address: 1040 Polk St, San Francisco, CA 94109, United States
google.description: Minimalist neighborhood locale for nigiri, sashimi & Japanese small bites.

top_reviews.content: So it was my birthday, and I really wanted sushi.  There is no dearth of quality sushi restaurants in San Francisco, however almost all of them are omakase – and to be honest, I am not a huge omakase fan (and I speak Japanese, have lived in Japan, and have consumed sushi all over the world – omakase does not necessarily mean better). Kuma’s execution and fish quality is some of the best I have had in the US in a long time. I dined with my mother, who is a Hamachi kama fan, and she said it was one of the best she has ever had. The atmosphere is no frills, and there were only two staff working the floor, one was I believe the manager – but service was attentive. Overall, this is probably my favorite new place to have non-omakase sushi in the city. Definitely recommend, and you definitely need a reservation.

In San Francisco for one night and wanted some great sushi and we lucked out finding this gem of a place. We grabbed a reservation which I highly recommend since it was packed. We sat at the sushi bar with a great view to watch them work their magic. I got the jackalope which was recommended by our sever and it was so good and I also ordered the Fresco which was also really yummy. My husband got sashimi of all kinds and loved it all. We also got a seaweed salad which was great too.
Appetizers were good, sushi is ok. We got the hamachi crudo and tofu apps + 3 rolls. One of our friends had bones in her raw fish (see photo below). Quite pricey as well. Would not recommend.

Fantastic experience. I love salmon so my waiter helped me pick the best sashimi and sushi roll. I sat at the bar and it was so nice watching the kitchen prepping everyone's orders. At the end the almighty ice cream which I chose the pistachio flavor. The best ice cream in the city I have tried lately. Highly recommend this restaurant to all sushi lovers.

Cute atmosphere, amazing, attentive service and great food! Def some of the best sushi my fiancé and I have had yet. We aren’t from the area but came from our engagement shoot over at city hall and we loveeee sushi- we decided what better place to get fresh sushi than sf- we couldn’t be more pleased with our pick! the cinch roll and the hey girl rolls were my personal fav, but everything was so tasty. And the sake🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟we even got the sweetest little surprise at the end as a congratulations to us on our upcoming wedding🥹🫶🏻 100000/10 food + experience and can’t wait to be back!

reviews_snippets.content: "Excellent service, great food, and a perfect date night ambiance."
"The fish was soft and fresh, the appetizers were average and a bit salty."

name: Aziza
address: 5800 Geary Blvd, San Francisco, CA 94121, United States

google.name: Aziza

google.description: Innovative Moroccan cooking with Californian touches & creative cocktails in a colorful setting.

top_reviews.content:
One of the best dining experiences I’ve ever had in San Francisco.

From the moment we walked in, the service was exceptional. Our server, Vlad, was absolutely amazing—knowledgeable, attentive, and genuinely passionate about creating a memorable experience. At the bar, Brandon and Caley crafted cocktails that perfectly complemented every course and truly elevated the entire evening.

We started with the octopus, eggplant, and chicken liver appetizers, and each dish was outstanding. Every bite was packed with flavor, beautifully prepared, and unlike anything we’ve had before. For our main course, we had the lamb shank, which was incredibly tender, rich, and perfectly executed. We finished with the date cake for dessert, and it was the perfect ending to an unforgettable meal.

The food was out of this world, the cocktails were exceptional, and the hospitality made us feel incredibly welcome. Aziza delivered on every level and easily ranks as the best dinner experience we’ve had in San Francisco. We can’t wait to come back.

May very well be the best dining experience I’ve had in the Bay Area. Certainly the food cannot be beat. I’d been wanting to go for months with my partner but never quite found the time. Totally exceeded my expectations, and those were quite high! Servers were inviting, attentive, and friendly. I felt well taken care of and never rushed. Per some other reviews’ recommendations we went for the cauliflower, and it’s one of the best dishes I’ve ever had—would go back just for that! That being the standout dish, I have nothing but praise for all the food. The bread was unctuous and rich, and I was on the verge of scraping up the leftover spread with my fingers. Octopus was beautifully prepared with just the right amount of chew. My one note is for the chicken. I’m not familiar with tagine, and was expecting something a bit more saucy and strongly flavored. Those expectations aside, it was a beautifully prepared bird, one of the best pieces of chicken you can get in the city. Very rarely do I order more than I can eat, but in this case my partner and I left too stuffed for dessert (another reason to return!) with leftovers in hand. An incredible night, and I’m looking forward to going back!

Aziza was an amazing experience! The atmosphere is beautiful, serene, and upscale. We were able to get a same-day reservation. The staff was even kind enough to move us to an earlier seating time.

Our waiter was attentive, knowledgeable, and did a great job explaining the menu, particularly food allergies for our daughter. The main dishes took a little while to arrive, but our waiter explained that the cornbread is prepared that way to make it extra moist—and it was totally worth the wait! Every dish was unique and delicious. Ordered the roasted cauliflower, grilled octopus, short ribs, and buttered cornbread. The wines were perfectly chilled and crisp. Great food, excellent service, and a wonderful atmosphere. We'll definitely be back!

Aziza is a little gem out here in this part of the Richmond neighborhood. We came here for a Friday dinner night. The vibes inside are dark and intimate, good for small groups or dates, but still have the space for bigger groups.

Everything we had was so delicious. The highlights for us were definitely the appetizers. We loved the trio dip, cauliflower, grilled octopus and corn bread. The lamb shank was delicious as expected but I would opt to try other meat/fish dishes instead. Overall I would come back and try other items on the menu!

The only con we had was that the service was very slow. I’m not sure if it’s because we had a later dinner reservation or the service was intended to be like that. If you want something shorter than 2.5 hours dinner, I recommend an earlier dinner resy or letting the server know to speed up the service in case you have other commitments after.

Excellent experience from start to finish. Service was attentive without hovering. Never a long wait between courses.

We started with the bean dip, muhamara with flatbread, octopus, olives, and cauliflower. The octopus was the standout: smoky, sweet, tangy, and briny all on one plate. The dips were generous and flavorful.

We split the whole branzino for mains. Perfectly cooked and portioned well.

The atmosphere is casual but elevated. The value is better than comparable restaurants at this tier. You get real portions here, which matters when the check arrives.

Highly recommend for special occasions or a nice dinner out.

top_reviews.content:
Nice looking Italian bistro style restaurant, they ah e small bar by the entrance where you can order drinks.
We ordered 2 bottles of the Montepulciano and it was a good vino, but with the pasta it put me in a good coma for hours 🥱

The food can be hit or miss, for appetizers we got the mussels and clams in a red sauce and the beef tartare and arugula salad with pistachios and golden beets. The tartare was pretty unremarkable and didn’t have a zing in the dressing, it was quite plain and ordinary. The arugula salad was also quite ordinary but the clams and mussels were quite flavorful but a tad too salty

For mains I tried the classic spaghetti and meatballs, but the sauce and the meatballs were quite flavorless, and I sent it back. My friends enjoyed their Calabrian pasta which was the most flavorful dish in the place and the pasta was al dente to the max which added to the flavor of the dish.

For dessert we share a tiramisu and it was quite good, but not made in house.

Very cozy Italian spot - feels like old school family vibe. Food was decent, I liked the Pavarotti pasta with chicken, Illini and dried tomatoes - very tender fusilli and creamy sauce. Was not a fan of gnocchi- on a chewy side, lacking softness. But the pesto sauce was great. The service was very nice and good came fast. We definitely enjoyed the neighborhood vibes seating next to the window and watching couples and families entering the restaurant for a weekend dinner.

I always complain about how hard it is (impossible even, when it comes to sandwiches) to find comparable Italian fare in the SF bay area, coming from NY/NJ. I visited here for dinner based on others' recommendations. It's no doubt a proud joint with long history (which serves as a proof of quality itself), so obviously there's some lower bound on the food/service quality to expect.

TLDR; the food was ok. I had gnocchi and as everyone mentions this place really wants everything al dente so it was a bit too firm for my taste. I personally found the sauce (I got the creamy tomato) had two problems: (1) it was too little (barely any left to soak up with bread), and (2) it was a bit too mild in flavor. All in all I had had better gnocchi at a random Italian restaurant I dropped by on the street in NY. I also had tiramisu for dessert, but this was unfortunately absolutely mediocre. I think it was the quality of store-bought.

I did enjoy the glass of cab which was a good pick and poured generously! And the staff was exceptionally hospitable, so no problem there. I think it's still a solid option in the area, hence 4 stars. But for me the food wasn't quite hitting the level I'd have liked, especially for the very high price they charge.

Honestly so delicious! Lovely neighborhood trattoria on street corner. Host and my server, Jesus Al., were so nice, thoughtful and attentive.  I had the Polpettine (spaghetti and meatballs).  The beef and pork meatballs were so flavorful and tender, pasta perfectly cooked, and tomato sauce was so flavorful.  A side of broccoli with lemon and Parmesan was perfect accompaniment.  Nicely crafted martini.  Highly recommend !!  Oh and value was great too!

I had a great experience at this cozy Italian restaurant. The atmosphere is warm and inviting, with a charmingly rustic feel, complete with a well-stocked bar and string lights that give it a homey, comfortable vibe. The service was friendly and attentive without being overbearing, and our waiter was helpful with the menu.

The real standout of the meal, and something you can tell from the photos, is the sheer size of the portions. They don't mess around! I ordered a pasta dish topped with a generous amount of fresh basil and what looked like burrata or a similar creamy cheese. My friend's spaghetti with a huge, impressive-looking meatball was also massive, and the clams in white wine sauce were abundant and delicious. You definitely get your money's worth here, and you'll likely have leftovers.

For dessert, we had a simple but delicious bowl of vanilla ice cream with chocolate syrup. It was the perfect way to cap off a very filling meal. I highly recommend giving this place a try.

First time visiting San Francisco, and I’m so glad I found The Little Chihuahua on Divisadero! I ordered the Garlic Shrimp Bowl with an extra side of fried plantains.
The shrimp were juicy and well-seasoned, and the smoky chile salsa that came with it was packed with flavor—just a little spicy, but in the best way. It added a perfect kick to the dish. The plantains were also really good.
This spot made a great impression on me as a first-time visitor. Tasty food, chill atmosphere, and friendly staff. Definitely recommend checking it out if you're in the area!

Excellent choice for “healthier” fast-casual food. I loved the plantains being an option and the self-serve salsa bar! I experienced fresh food and pleasant service at this restaurant on a recent visit to the city.
My favorite place so far. Love their Al pastor burrito

top_reviews.content:
I called and ordered take out.  It is better to speak Cantonese when picking up the items.  We ordered House Special Fried Rice, Beef Chow Fun, Salt and Pepper Chicken Wings.  Among all 3, chicken wings are the best.  The place was busy!  Like all places, price went up and close to $50 when paid.

Update: This time we ate in the restaurant.  Four of us needed to wait about 10 minutes, and we needed to share a big table.  Despite that, food were hot and tasted excellent.  Shared the chicken wings and walnut prawns pictures.
.

During our tour of downtown San Francisco, we found ourselves extremely hungry. The recommendation of this place came from my son's friend. Despite the tight space, we ordered several entrees after my son assured me of their fried chicken's quality. Upon tasting, I was left speechless; the food is far superior to what I've experienced in Texas. It's indeed puzzling why Canton restaurants like this aren't found in Texas.

Ok, so this is Chinatown. Of course it’s busy. Of course it’s hectic. But finding this gem was the highlight. As the planner of any vacation I always need to keep in mind my picky eaters, my two kids and my wife. After having looked at photos I decided to bring the family here. My wife and kids gave it glowing reviews. The egg rolls were perfect. The broccoli beef, juicy. The pork fried rice was so good. They ate everything I put on their plate, and as any parent to small kids would know, that is the ultimate seal of approval. I’m going to recommend this place to anyone looking for food in Chinatown

😋 😋 😋

Did not wait long before food arrived!

Salt pepper wings - get this your first time! Great flavor, crispiest chicken wings I’ve had in Chinatown…and possibly rest of SF. Aria is a close contender but location is more sketchy. I like that this is not drowned in sauce like at San Tung

Fukien egg tofu - great flavor and texture, I like the contrast of super thin crispy skin with soft jiggly tofu, no chewing required, satisfying to eat

Pea shoots - fine

Green bean with pork - fine, more crunchy than I expected

Chicken chow mein - did not like the thin noodles, I prefer thicker noodles that are more chewy; too oily also

Good portion size, I suggest ordering one dish per person for no leftovers.

Loud during peak hours but nice and quiet if you go during a lull.

They take cash and credit card.

My girlfriend and I love this spot. Their salt and pepper chicken wing is our favorite and we go to sf chinatown just for this, its definitely a must try if you are in Chinatown. Overall, great food and I love the authentic casual vibe of this place.

Chicken burrito fell apart. Flavor was basic.

The place is fine, ambience is fine - maybe a little too in-your-face to appeal to a more generic demographic but I don't mind. But that doesn't mean anything if I'm taking a bite of my somewhat mediocre quesadilla (can we flavor the chicken just a *little* more please) and a black hair falls out of the chicken. Their mole amarillo was at least authentic enough. But still. I clearly bit into someone's hair. And that's an automatic one-star review.

Wow! The torta I got was delicious! I would gladly drill a few more holes in my belt to make room for more of those.
I wish I worked close by.

Highly recommend the corn and zucchini taco, I actually thought it was more flavorful than the fish taco. You pay at the front before sitting down.

Plenty of seating and the food comes out fast. There’s two bathrooms in the back.

I’ve been eating here since I was a kid and it never disappoints. The tacos are delicious and the churros are super super fresh. I love the limonata and it’s the perfect lunch spot if you’re shopping on 4th street.

The fog in the Inner Sunset doesn’t just roll in; it conducts a hostile takeover of your morale. It’s the kind of damp, bone-deep San Francisco cold that makes a man reconsider his loyalties and start confessing to crimes he only thought about committing. I was marooned on Irving Street, dodging the screech of the N-Judah and seeking a safe house. I found it at Manna. From the outside, it’s an unassuming storefront, the kind of joint that doesn’t need a neon sign to prove it knows its business. Inside, they offer a very specific, beautiful paradox: a modest, softly lit dining room that serves weaponized heat.
Before the main event, the table is populated by the banchan—small, cold side dishes of fermented defiance. Radishes with a sharp, garlicky bite, and seasoned greens that taste like they were plucked from a much brighter, more optimistic climate. They are the opening arguments, a cool, crisp misdirection before the kitchen unleashes the heavy artillery.
Then, the photographic evidence arrives. The bibimbap was delivered not on a plate, but in a black, cast-iron stone bowl hot enough to forge a counterfeit coin. This wasn't just dinner; it was a localized geological event. Look closely at the egg, resting on the summit of marinated beef and julienned vegetables like an unblinking, innocent yellow eye. It sits there, completely unaware of the searing violence about to take place. You are forced to become an accomplice, plunging your chopsticks into the center and frantically folding the raw yolk into the scorching rice before it sets. The sound is a violent, beautiful sizzle. What remains at the bottom of the bowl—the nurungji—is a structural masterpiece of caramelized desperation, a layer of scorched rice that crunches with the satisfying finality of a closed case.
To my left sat the stew. A soft tofu jjigae boiling with the sheer, unadulterated hostility of a jilted lover. It arrived actively raging in its own cauldron, spitting red, microscopic droplets of thermal warning across the table. Ordinarily, soup is meant to soothe. It is the food of convalescence. But this molten, crimson broth was a full-blown interrogation. It demanded your sweating, undivided attention. You don’t just sip it; you negotiate terms with it. Yet, beneath the fiery chili oil and the bubbling surface, the tofu itself is impossibly silken, a quiet mercy hiding in a bowl of fury.
Providing a necessary alibi to all this aggression was a plate of japchae. It’s a deceptive tangle of translucent sweet potato glass noodles, tossed with cabbage, carrots, and ribbons of beef. Slippery, slightly sweet, and aromatic with toasted sesame oil, it acts as the diplomat of the table. When your palate is exhausted from the blistering masochism of the stone bowls, the japchae pulls you back from the ledge.
Five stars. It’s an exercise in delicious, calculated trauma. In a city increasingly obsessed with foam, tweezers, and edible flowers, Manna is the only place in the neighborhood where the dinner actively, gloriously fights back.

Miss Saigon is one of those hidden gems that reminds you why family-owned restaurants are so special.

The atmosphere feels warm and authentic, with Christmas lights, religious décor, and patriotic American touches that make it feel like you're dining in someone's home rather than a commercial chain. It's a true mom-and-pop restaurant with plenty of character.

I ordered the filet mignon pho and the filet mignon bánh xèo, and both were outstanding. The pho broth was clear, rich, and full of flavor without being overly salty. The filet mignon was tender, and the fresh herbs, bean sprouts, jalapeños, onions, and lime let you customize every bowl. The bánh xèo was huge, perfectly crispy, generously filled, and served with fresh vegetables and a delicious dipping sauce.

The portions were generous, the ingredients were fresh, and the service was friendly and welcoming.

If you're looking for authentic Vietnamese comfort food in San Francisco instead of a trendy, overpriced restaurant, Miss Saigon is absolutely worth the visit. I'll definitely be back. Highly recommended! 🍜🇻🇳

Golden Era is a rare find in the plant-based dining scene. While too many vegan establishments focus on ethical and environmental benefits but serve what is essentially non-meat junk food, this restaurant takes a different approach. The food here is not only good for the planet and the animals but is also good for your health.

The extensive menu encompasses Vietnamese and Chinese specialties that can be customized to meet specific dietary needs. The service was caring and family-like, filled with helpful advice. When we requested adjustments to our dishes, they were executed perfectly. Furthermore, when we mentioned that one of our party is a fan of spicy food, the staff responded not with a single option, but with three different sources of heat—a gesture that was highly appreciated and added significant enjoyment to the meal.

The cuisine is excellent and the service is commendable, but we must point out one significant weakness: the restroom. Unfortunately, we found the entire mirror covered with rude inscriptions. For a family-friendly establishment, this is out of place, and the management would do well to clean it up promptly.

As ordinary consumers, we are not paid or compensated in any way for this review. We appreciate the healthy, high-quality food and hope the facility maintenance matches the kitchen's standards in the future.

Golden Era is a 100% vegan Vietnamese spot with delicious noodle soups. I ordered the vegan crab noodle soup (bun rieu chay) and it tasted so close to the traditional non-vegan version. The tomato-based broth was the best part of the whole bowl, a bit sour, light, comforting and full of flavor. It came with tofu, soy protein, green herbs and all the toppings went well together, super addicting!

I came around 5:30pm, so it was pretty quiet and easy to get seated. Their menu is also hugeeeeee, with everything from banh mi, noodle soups, entrees and rice plates to desserts and drinks. You’ll want to come with a group so everyone can order different dishes to share.

Highly recommend if you’re in SF and looking for a great vegan restaurant, or even if you’re not vegan and just want to explore unique twists of Vietnamese dishes!

The authenticity of the dishes wasn't there and I don't think that anybody was doing quality control in the kitchen.  Every dish show cased lots of bell pepper, onion and too much garlic. Even the simple stuff, aka the rice was off. It was dry and under cooked.   The greens with garlic was almost the highlight.  Whereas the lotus root was drowned in a garlic chilli sauce, not a bad idea but the garlic overpowered the chili and it kinda resemble a hot mess.  The cumin lamb featured more bell pepper than lamb and tasted almost the same as the Wowo Tou besides the hint of cumin.  Bummer as there aren't tons of Chinese restaurants in the Castro to start with.   Oh well let's just hope that Mama Jis finds her way back from her stroll.

Love this place. The charm. It fits perfectly in the Castro. The menu is interesting, many items which have some kick. The Hot & Numbing Fish is so unusual and amazing, we always order that. The fact they have a number of Beligum beers is amazing too. The staff are very cool, they are excited to be there. This restaurant is the best. Mama Ji!
I tried the Triple C tofu after reading reviews. It was really flavorful and delicious but just a bit too sweet for my taste. I will be going back to try other stuff!

top_reviews.content:
The restaurant is clean and spacious.  The restaurant server quickly ushered me to my table and politely asked if I would like tea, if not water. The welcome drink is then served in a paper cup.

I ordered my usual Beef Special Pho which comed with beef steak, tendon, balls and stomach, and also a hot viet coffee.

The pho comes in huge serving and lined with hugh generous portion of steak slices and other ingredients. The highlight of the pho would be the  steak slices. It was fragrant and is tasty like the steak you would have ordered at a steak house.

The Vietnamese cofffee was strong and also have a balanced taste with the amount of condensed milk and hot water combination. Highly recommended as well. Beats blue mountain and star bucks hands down. 😄

We come here ever so often and the food always hits the spot. I highly recommend their pho, rice plates, and especially the Bun Bo Hue. The portion size is great…very good broth to noodle to meat ratio.

Pho was better than most places I’ve been to. Portion size equals to portion amount. Other places give to more noodles when you order a large but the meat amount is the same as a regular size. The rice noodles doesn’t have a starchy smell, meaning they soak and rinse the rice noodles thoroughly.

Very authentic, very popular, and very tasty!
The service was fast and efficient, the Pho was a good portion, fresh, the meat was plentiful and the broth delicious, and without another thought I had eaten it all!! No photo! I can highly recommend.

We were craving for some pho as a hangover cure and found this place! We were seated quickly when we arrived, and the room was already full!

I ordered their imperial rolls, and the large #1 House special beef soup noodle, which comes with sliced lean beef, brisket, beef tendon, beef tripe, beef balls, and a side plate of bean sprouts, basil, jalopieno, and lemon.

The imperial rolls were just alright; they didn't have enough flavor, lacking the distinct white pepper taste. I would try their shrimp spring rolls next time!

The combination pho tasted delicious, the broth was fragrant, the noodles were cooked to the right texture, and it came loaded with meats.

The staff was attentive, the food came out quickly, and they served hot tea! On top of that, the prices were really reasonable. Highly recommended!

reviews_snippets.content: "Amazing food, amazing prices, and very kind and patient staff 😁 ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️"

Had a blast here for a birthday party recently! We were in a private room, which was super nice and already decorated, giving us a perfect little space to celebrate. The service was on point—everyone was attentive and kept things moving smoothly.

This place has decent food and the atmosphere is perfect for a big group. Plus, being right in the Hillsdale Shopping Mall is a huge win—it’s a great mall to walk around and do some window shopping once you're done eating

Had a great time at Pinstripes Hillsdale. The venue is spacious, modern, and has a lively atmosphere that works well for both casual outings and group gatherings. The bowling lanes were well maintained, and the staff was friendly and helpful throughout the visit. Food and drinks were enjoyable, and the overall experience felt well organized. A fun spot to spend an evening with friends or family in the Hillsdale area.

9.1 💥 Great tasting pizza, no complaints here.  Great sauce, fresh ingredients and the crust was perfect.  The atmosphere was vibrant, lots to do here, wish J could have bowled.  The staff was super friendly.  I will be back to try out other items on the menu.  👊🏽

This place is fantastic! The wings and calamari are must-tries, and the banana split is absolutely amazing. The rest of the food is great as well. Everything we’ve tried has been enjoyable. You really can’t go wrong here. Highly recommended!

Came here for the first time for my grandson's birthday celebration...Walked in and THANKFULLY this is no Bowlero.. the furnishings and the open spacing was DELUXE.  Got here early and was able to watch some of the Masters on the multiple and nicely placed big screens..  the chicken wings were fantastic..I tried the sweet chili sauce ..yummy (no pics).. the bowling was  FUN.. bumpers and ball ramps for the young ones like my 7 yr old grandson and for those who wanted them.. ya. even  as an old school bowler it allows ALL a chance to score, succeed and have an enjoyable experience!..which what the day was all about! $20/ adult $10/child under 12 for 2(two) hours of bowling! top_reviews.content:
Was staying at The Marker and they have welcomed free drink at Tratto -
might as well have dinner there! Excellent ravioli (also the squid ink pasta and the massive lasagna)! Shout out to Ms Maria Chavez for the warm service.

Italian food never disappoints. Exquisite food, phenomenal staff and all within the perfect setting to enjoy a nice dinner. We opted for the Formaggi & Affettati which was a beautiful spread to showcase their cured meats, the immaculate Sogliola Piccata and lastly the Controfiletto paired beautifully with a Frank Family Cabernet. Each dish was perfectly made and I wish we could have stayed longer for dessert but that will have to wait for next time. And I hope no one takes this as a complaint as it was a very happy surprise but their cocktails were delicious and STRONG, glad I can count on someone to make a nice cocktail with a heavy hand.
The pesto gnocchi was amazinggg! We came here for restaurant week and I would come back again for just this dish. Cocktails were great too.

Nice food and atmosphere, but very poor service.
Tratto has a pleasant environment and the food itself is good, but unfortunately the service really took away from the experience.
We first tried room service for breakfast, and it was honestly painful—the person we spoke with sounded in a very bad mood, which immediately set a negative tone.
We decided to give it another chance and went for dinner, but the experience was even worse. We sat at the bar, and while there was a large Christmas party going on, the staff seemed overwhelmed and very evasive. We ordered a glass of wine and asked to make a small change. The waiter had already poured it, then abruptly took the glass, dumped it into the sink, and appeared visibly annoyed. Eventhough, we tried several times to make eye contact or get his attention, but we were completely ignored.
If you’re looking for a relaxed date night or a pleasant dining experience, you may want to skip this place and go somewhere else. The food and setting have potential, but the service needs serious improvement.

Rustic Italian restaurant near Union Square in San Francisco. It is attached to the Marker Hotel on Geary St.
We were there early on a Monday evening, so it wasn’t very busy. It never ceases to amaze me when checking in if you have a reservation, yet the whole dining area is empty.
We ordered a beet salad for an appetizer and the entrees we had were the Spaghetti con Vongole, and the Gnocchi pesto. Both were very good.
The servings are adequate but not huge.
The service was hit and miss. We waited several minutes for the table to be cleared and we still had to ask for the check.

top_reviews.content: I know this is a historical location that is thriving with plenty of diversity. I saw peeps from all walks of life happy and ready to be served. Really good customer service and awesome variety. Everything is made to order, so you may wait a few minutes. I’ll make this a staple for Chinese food. I got carry out so haven’t had the food just yet but when I get home it’s on! Shrimp egg fo young extra green onion, vegetable fried rice with extra onions about $47, but servings are huge enough for 2-3 meals from what I can see.

Nice Peking duck served on platter with some sauce underneath the duck and that’s it. Our server recommended The Gold Medal Chop Suey as a starch to accompany the duck and it was delicious with slices of beef, chicken, pork and pieces of scallops and other tasty sea critters which I couldn’t recognize. Service is fast, maybe even curt, but that’s what it takes for them to be so fast at such a busy small place. The 9pm crowd was very diverse with a large table of loud post-clubbing guests which added to the “ambiance.”  Not for everyone but I really enjoyed this place.

We saw this restaurant was recommended by people for their hours and decent offerings. We came pretty late in the night, so there was no wait and parking was a breeze.

Food itself was OK. Their menu is pretty big with reasonable prices. We got a few things, like the BBQ pork rice platter, roast duck, congee, and wonton noodle soup. The standout was definitely the duck, while everything else was pretty average or so-so.

If you've never been to an authentic CANTONESE restaurant, the service may put you off at first. But Cantonese people and restaurants tend to be very straight forward and can seem unfriendly. I wouldn't say service was unfriendly at all, but it was more for efficiency. They do charge a service charge, but it is not unreasonable.

Overall, if you want some Cantonese comfort food this is a good place to have it, especially if it is super late at night. Maybe we just came at a time where food was more mediocre but we were happy this restaurant was open. When we left it was bordering towards midnight and the restaurant started to fill up, so looks like many people appreciate for this restaurant for their hours.

This is a locals go-to for decades. From seafood to meat dishes all your traditional Chinese dishes can be found here. Nothing is amaricanized like the panda food. You can’t go wrong with bbq duck, wontons, salt n pepper fried pork chops, chow meins, and even vegetarian options are good here. Lobster and crabs are also delicious.
Bring your friends or family here and eat an authentic Chinese meal here. It’s almost a whole in the wall so no need to dressed up.

Don’t forget to follow me on IG for more great foodie spots to try!
@Only1Christinelu

My friend and I were looking for Chinese cuisine after 10:30pm on a Friday and night and Google led us to New Gold Medal Restaurant in Oakland, at 389kk 8th St.  It clean and friendly with a large menu to choose from.  Walnut shrimp is my JAM and I was not disappointed.  The serving was hearty, the walnuts nice and sweet and the shrimp....FRESH!, as was the shrimp in the fried rice I ordered. My picky friend ordered egg-foo-young and beef and vegetable chow-mein and there were no complaints.  We had enough food for the next day; lunch and dinner. I am excited to visit this wonderful eatery again.
Great service from start to finish.
No craziness either. This restaurant is quiet and pleasing.
Open till 3am but check before you go.

This was a perfect treat and a memorable dining experience. I would highly recommend Capo’s to anyone looking for great food, excellent service, and a fantastic atmosphere. Definitely worth a visit.

top_reviews.content: Went here late afternoon. Very fun, chill hangout spot. Great beer and cocktail selection. I had the root beer old fashioned, which came with a root beer dumdum!  Service was very friendly and alert. Food was delicious. My partner and I both had burgers (patty melt and 5150). We shared the porcetta fries (por que no!).
