The fries were bomb. Definitely coming back here and bringing friends.

Quite possibly one of the best cheeseburgers I've had in a long long time. If they ask you how you'd like that meat done -- don't bother.  It's all medium.   I don't know why they ask. Still juicy though.  4 on food just because of that.  A little pink would have made that a 5

Beeryland is absolutely fantastic. I've been coming here for the star trek trivia for almost two years. The adult slushies are yummy, and so is most of the food. I don't know if the kimchi grilled cheese is still on the menu, but it's a divisive item. My friends like it but I despise it. Use caution. As you can see by the state of my AmInal Fries (yes the spelling is correct), I am one happy customer. Four stars on the atmosphere because the bathroom could use a facelift, but it is a bar. Cheers!

The burger & garlic fries here were amazing. Good beer list, lots of outdoor tables and warmers in the evening. Cool that it has a room of pinball machines. Definitely want to come back to try other items on the menu!

Hi, I went into Berryland today as it is Fourth of July and wanted some burger as well as beers from my favorite burger place. I ordered a 5150 w a side of mac and cheese, no veggies with a cider. And my partner ordered the impossible burger w lettuce only, and a dirty Shirley. We paid, and I tipped the man (who turns out to be the owner 15%). My partner sits down, and I wait for the drinks. I watch him make the Shirley and there is no alcohol placed in at all. It’s okay, I won’t make a fuss I go and sit down. Partner and I disappointed, but whatever. And then my order comes out completely wrong. It comes out as a Mac and cheese burger. My partners burger has no lettuce at all. I clarify all these issues to the waitress. She apologizes and goes back to the kitchen to correct this. She speaks to the man who took our order and he marches over. First starting by telling us that it does have vodka in it, I inform I watched him make it and there was no vodka. He takes a taste and agrees to make us a new drink. He argues and says that there is vodka in it and he can taste it and that he does not make mistakes. I then go “‘my Order was completely wrong and so was my partners” and he begins yelling at me. I walk over to the waitress to ask to speak to a manager or owner, to which I am informed it is this man. He is the owner. The owner yelled at me over him being wrong. I asked for a refund and got yelled at more. We left and will not be returning. A shame to see my favorite burger joint of the last few months ruined by the owner being a terrible person.

top_reviews.content:
We had such a great experience at Arash’s restaurant. It is truly a fantastic spot with amazing food, a beautiful interior, friendly staff, and a lovely terrace where you can sit outside and enjoy the atmosphere.

The location is perfect: easy to reach, also when you are with kids or when walking is a bit more difficult. There is parking right in front, plus a parking garage nearby, and it is located in a nice shopping street, which makes it perfect for lunch during a shopping day or for a relaxed dinner in the evening.

The food was excellent. We had pizza and a burger this time, and both were really good. We also had dinner here before, where Arash and his friend put together a mix of different dishes, a bit Italian-style with antipasti vibes. The combinations were spot on, full of flavor, and the quality was truly top-level.

It is also a great place for families, with good options for children, but at the same time it works perfectly for a nice lunch, dinner, or casual evening out.

I always tell my friends who are visiting San Francisco or anywhere nearby to also check out Walnut Creek. And when they are there, this is definitely a place I recommend for food. A really great spot, with great taste, great service, and a very welcoming vibe.

Delicious food, attentive staff, and a welcoming atmosphere! My team and I hosted a corporate holiday party for about 60 people at Main Street Kitchen earlier this month, and were highly pleased with the staff, venue, and quality of food and service.

We worked closely with Nina, who made planning and executing the event a breeze. Whether in-person, on the phone, or via email, Nina was attentive, responsive, and flexible to our needs. Food allergies and restrictions were taken into consideration, and we were able to select a wide variety of apps and desserts for our team to enjoy.

Our employees' feedback indicated this is one of the best holiday parties we've ever had, with many impressed by the food and decor—some will even return with their teams for lunch! I would definitely consider returning for another event, and 10/10 recommend it to anyone looking for a great meal!

Main Street Kitchen & Bar is an exciting addition to the brunch scene in Walnut Creek offering a tantalizing variety of dishes presented in a cozy yet trendy setting. The food is truly outstanding, with flavors that explode on your palate with every bite.

The fish and chips are incredible—made in-house with a light, flavorful batter and paired with excellent aioli. Don’t miss their custom wood-fired pizza oven, which produces delicious, fiery pies.

What truly makes this spot stand out is its fantastic outdoor seating area, perfect for soaking up the sun during a leisurely brunch. Whether you're craving classic favorites or eager to try something new, Main Street Kitchen & Bar promises an unforgettable experience that will leave you wanting more.
This place is amazing. Great experience with the Head West Coast Arts festival for Mother's Day. Fish 🐠 and chips for the win.

I’ve enjoyed breakfast at Main Street Kitchen & Bar several times now, and it has easily become a favorite spot for breakfast on a weekend morning in Walnut Creek. The Fra’Mani Ham Chilaquiles and Old Fashioned Potato Hash are both really good, you can’t go wrong with either dish. The food seems fresh, and aways satisfying. The coffee is fresh and on the strong side. I  recommend this spot for anyone looking for a great breakfast! I will have to try this place out for dinner some time soon.

Saturday night at Perry’s on Union Street is almost a San Francisco tradition going back decades. I hadn’t been there in a while and a friend wanted to have dinner there and I happily agreed. I was pleased to see they still make their onion soup so I ordered that along with the steak salad. My friend had the ribs and we shared a bottle of Cabernet that I brought with me. all the food was fine and the service was pretty good considering how busy they were.

So I've learned that Perry's is an institution. People have been coming here for years and it dates back a good ways. This place is a fantastic experience, they have a diverse menu, prices aren’t too bad and excellent service. We ordered a mix of things and there wasn’t one item that wasn’t absolutely Tasty. Everything you see here is really good so load up!

I will always crave the buticha and split peas.

Vegan options are plenty and there is no sacrifice made.
Veggie combo and an order of mushroom tibs is my go to order.

What an amazing dining experience! We first tried Ethiopian food about 10 years ago, but this was by far the most authentic Ethiopian meal we’ve ever had. Every dish was fresh, flavorful, and absolutely delicious. You can truly taste the care and tradition in every bite.

Our server was fantastic. They were incredibly knowledgeable, explained the menu, answered all of our questions, and made the experience even more enjoyable.

If you’re looking for authentic Ethiopian cuisine with outstanding service and a wonderful atmosphere, Café Colucci is a must-visit. We can’t wait to come back!

Cafe Colucci has been on our list for months so glad we had the opportunity to visit on MLK Jr. Day ❤️

Everything from the vibe, food, and service were better than we could’ve imagined. What a fun time and thanks to Damian for the hospitality🔥

The banana pudding is LOADED, the mac and cheese is smothered, and collared greens taste fresh made. Can’t go wrong with either the fish or chicken. The best meal I’ve had in ages. Made by real kind people.

First off the pictures of the food look amazing. The service behind the counter was great. The amount of food was amazing…you get what you pay for and some. Finally the taste was great for our, shrimp, wings, & catfish🙌🏽

I have been coming to JJ's fish and Chicken since I was a kid everything I used to get to this day hits the spot from the deep fried catfish to the red snapper to the jumbo shrimp or just some good ole fried chicken wings. The customer service is great. I don't remember their name but the two counter guys, one older and one younger in the front taking orders  know what they're doing they keep the line moving quick and the turnaround time from ordering your food to getting it as quick as well. Sometimes during their lunch rush hour they are pretty busy. So I'd recommend phoning your order in to give them ample time, catch up with orders as well as do yours by the time you get there. It should be ready for pickup. A trip to jj's is not complete without one of their scrumptious homemade desserts that they get delivered from the banana pudding to peach cobbler to pecan pie to sweet potato pie to all the other options of cake slices they have you can't go wrong. I got a big Sweet tooth myself and whenever I go I always end up getting multiple desserts. Their menu has a lot of options between fish and chicken as well as good sides like mac and cheese, fried okra, fried zucchini, jalapeno poppers Mac salad. Potato salad. All are good options and can't go wrong. Wash it down with an ice cold, fresh squeezed lemonade and you got yourself a whole meal. They add this for lemon salt to the chicken and the fries that make it. So addicting. You can't stop eating. Their fries are really crispy too. I think they coat them in flour and when they fry them it gives it an extra nice crisp. Their ranch is hella good too I put it up there with Wingstop Ranch. This is a pretty long review, but JJ's is definitely worth talking about. There are other locations in the Bay area. It is a chain store but this location on 3rd & Revere is my favorite parking can be a little hard at times given you're in the city, but usually there's parking on the side or half a block down the street. Whenever I'm in the area I definitely go by and grab my fix. Price is pretty good too. Definitely affordable compared to other spots in the city for seafood. They fry it crisp to perfection.

Great local spot! Hush puppies are moist and delicious. Okra was crispy and hit the spot. I also had the german chocolate cake. Great selection of cake. They have red velvet, yellow chocolate, banana pudding and more. They also have a lot of fun soda flavors. Roll up for great service and tasty food.

Solid neighborhood fish fry, serving generous portions of a wide variety of seafood, crunchy cornmeal batter. Light on salt, perfect so as not to feel heavy.

Choice of two fish and fries ($16.99) can easily feed two. Calamari and Whiting, excellent.

Though a Chicago chain, a solidly Bayview establishment.

top_reviews.content:
Located conveniently right next to the Goodwill off of International Blvd in the Fruitvale neighborhood in Oakland, this is a taco truck that you do not want to miss at all costs!

This is a local business that I stumbled upon one night when I was highly craving tacos. I love how they still have seating despite the weather, rain or shine. If you’re pulling up to this place, you’re in luck — because they have  Their taco meat—whether you go for al pastor, carne asada, carnitas, or lengua—is generously seasoned and rich, with that juicy, well-browned texture that makes each bite memorable. From what I’ve heard, Oakland locals often praise the quality and depth of the meats, and you can tell they’re working with ingredients that stand up to the hype. The corn tortillas hold up beautifully too: warm, slightly charred at the edges, and the perfect vehicle for every squeeze of lime and sprig of cilantro.
It’s laid-back street food at its best—tacos that hit hard on flavor and make you want to come back for another round. Honestly, I would be coming here to enjoy with minimal fuss, cash in hand, and a big appetite.

The tacos here are exceptional, particularly the tripitas. I've often considered sharing this feedback with the owner, but I've hesitated. The red sauce, unfortunately, has a flavor profile reminiscent of chamoy combined with a generic bottled sauce, which is quite unsatisfactory. The green sauce appears to be a simple mixture of green tomatoes and water. I strongly recommend an upgrade to the sauce offerings.

Tried the $20 super burrito 🌯 — massive portion, packed with flavor, and absolutely worth it. One burrito could easily feed two people. Fresh, filling, and satisfying from the first bite to the last. Would definitely get it again.

Their food is great! The guys are great! My brother's doctor is across the street from them in Fruitvale. We order food everytime he has an appointment. We love their carne asada burritos. To bad they don't deliver 😊
Quesabirra tacos are hella good here definitely a must try if you haven't had them before

top_reviews.content: This place has good food. It was a little more than I expected for two people but maybe that’s because mentally, I’m stuck in 2014 or something. I liked the meatballs a lot. I thought the sauce could have been a little less sweet, but the freshness counteracted and it was still good. The broccolini was exceptional, so spicy and delicious. We both thoroughly enjoyed the lasagna and bread as well. A carb lover’s dream. Service could have been a little better, but we get it, it’s a busy place for good reason. Make a reservation.

Finally, I visited to try their famous Monday for lover’s special! $60 cash only for two appetizers, one entree, one dessert, and a whole bottle of wine. Wow what a deal! We were worried at first if it would be enough food, but I felt stuffed afterwards and needed to walk it off. We got an early reservation but the place really filled up as it became prime dinner time. Highly recommend booking ahead of time if you want to come on a Monday. Staff seemed to be quite busy, and we had to get their attention a couple of times. The space is cool and had bar seating, booths, and a back patio area. They have two pin ball machines and a photo booth as well, very fun.

For food, our two appetizers were the chicken wings and the caesar salad. Both were spicy, but not that spicy. Instead of traditional croutons, they added bread crumbs on top of the little gem lettuce. I enjoyed their take on a caesar, though it felt pretty heavy, much like the rest of our meal and the menu haha. The wings were delicious and my friend and I fought for who will take the last one. Spaghetti and meatballs was a very size able portion for two to share. We ordered the grandma’s meatballs with the spaghetti and meatballs which had a different recipe, I believe crushed cashews are added. I enjoyed them, were not wowed, but very filling and hit the spot. The peach panna cotta was delightful! We savored each bite. My friend doesn’t even like peaches that much but he really enjoyed this dessert. For wine, they have two house wines to choose from, a red and a white. We chose the red to pair with our meal and we liked it! I would definitely return for this dinner special.

yummy!!!

Awesome vibes, service, and food. The FLAMINGO WATER was soooooo tasty.
We got the spaghetti with grandma meatballs, the focaccia bread, spicy Caesar salad, and cauliflower arancini. All yummy, especially like the salad and the spaghetti. Cauliflower arancini was good but note that they are much smaller than typical italian arancini and have a lighter feel because of the cauliflower.

Unknowingly a friend worked there and gave us the panna cotta - soooo delicious, light, and loved the fruit on top.

Outdoor seating looked like a completely different vibe, so peaceful, definitely coming back with my pup!

Oh and there’s a fun photo booth as well!

Busy spot, so obviously the atmosphere can get a little loud and hectic, but honestly the vibe here is really cute. 🤭 We needed a table for two and luckily they had a spot at the bar or window, so we went with the window!

The setup, decorations, and lighting are definitely a vibee. Everything feels really cool and chill, and I loved the overall trendy atmosphere.

Food was good! I got the spaghetti & meatballs… nothing mind-blowing, but a solid portion and it did the job. My friend got the shrimp Alfredo, which was also pretty good.

Overall, we had a fun time! I don’t think I’d rush back anytime soon, and it probably wouldn’t be my first choice, but I’d definitely go again if someone really wanted to. I’d try a different dish next time because I feel like I need to understand the hype. :)

First time eating here. We ordered the Italian-American Hot Wings, Spaghetti with Grandma Meatballs and Spicy Vodka Fusilli.

The wings were juicy with a mild level of spicy. The flavor’s ok but personally, I prefer a more seasoned somewhat a bit saltier wings.

I’m not really a fan of spaghetti made in other countries given that I grew up eating a sweet-spicy style spaghetti. That said, theirs is ok because it wasn’t that “sour”. The meatballs were ok (but bland), it reminded me of our local spring rolls. It could do better with a little but of salt or seasoning.

I enjoyed the spicy vodka fusilli. It had the right amount of spice and creaminess. It’s a 4 out of 5 for me and would have been a 5 if it had been cheesier.

The star of the show is our server. He was genuinely friendly and attentive to every table there is.

top_reviews.content: Got the 3 tacos, carne asada, pollo asado, and carnitas. Each was delicious in its own right and there are many options for customization with sauces, toppings, etc. Highly recommend the agua fresca (I got fresa)... Very refreshing and not overly sweet.

Ordered three meat tacos with carne asada, pollo asado and carnitas, mixed order. Went “super” with cheese, guacamole, sour cream, lettuce and tomato. Each taco was well filled, with the meats chopped and layered under the toppings. I gave them a generous squeeze of fresh lime. Added pico de gallo on the side and tortilla chips with guacamole. The pico was fresh, bright and sharp. The guacamole was chunky and avocado-forward, with visible onion and seasoning, not blended smooth. Everything tasted fresh and peppy, and I’d go back without hesitation. Great value too.

Counter service setup with large menu boards behind the line and several staff working. Ordered, picked up from the counter, found a table. In and out in about 20 minutes.

Visited on a sunny Saturday afternoon after a local recommendation. Indoor seating available, though it is geared mainly towards takeaway. Easy to spot corner location at Valencia and 17th. Bike parking right outside. I walked over from 16th St Mission in around five minutes.

Afterwards walked up to Dolores Park and took in wide open city and bay views from the higher end.

(Visited April 2022)

Authentic Mexican foods. Clean and spacious. Reasonable prices. Foods were ok. But they need to improve their service. I was there in non-peak hours weekday, and there were only 2 customers included me. I was the only one standing at the counter to wait the servers taking my orders. No greeting, no one asked me what I wanted. After 10 minutes wait, finally they took my order but the service was slow and the server was impatient when I asked them to repeat what they said.
Not sure if I would come back even though I wanted Mexican foods in Mission.

VERY affordable with INCREDIBLE food! Mild salsa was the best I've ever had, and the spicy is pretty spicy (white person on fire spicy). Great spot. Only downside is it can be pretty loud in there to hear what the staff is asking you. Lovely spot tho!

I went to this spot today for a "super" burrito & a drink, but the experience fell short in service & quality. While only one of the four staff greeted me warmly, the others seemed disinterested & acted as if serving was an inconvenience, which made the visit feel unwelcoming. The burrito itself was underwhelming dominated by rice and beans with minimal meat & overly salty seasoning. They also forgot my chips, salsa and napkins.

Food is tasty but I notice my broth was not as hot as I usually seen it at other places  ( note ) i seen other customers dishes steaming maybe I got the last of the batch anyway I didn’t like the bowl was not clean also observed floor is very dirty and chairs  I went into restroom and is dirty also

Unfortunately, after more than 10 years of being a customer, I won’t be coming back.

My wife ordered the SP11, and I noticed she was mostly just pushing the food around her plate. After trying it myself, I understood why. The beef was dry, bland, and noticeably different from what they normally use for this dish. It tasted like a cheaper cut of meat.

I really wish I had taken a picture of the food. The plate was nearly untouched and still basically full, but I was so upset and disappointed with the situation that I left without even thinking to take one.

I understand that every restaurant can have an off day, and if that were the only issue, I probably wouldn’t be writing this review. What really disappointed me was how the situation was handled. All I wanted was a refund for the SP11 while paying the rest of the bill. When I went to the cashier to explain what happened, they refused, claiming that we had eaten too much. ????

The food was barely touched and looked almost exactly like the stock photo used on the menu. I found it hard to believe they would refuse a refund when the dish was barely touched.

I’ve been coming here for over 10 years. During COVID, I made it a point to support this restaurant, I’ve recommended it to friends, and I’ve tried to come in at least a couple of times a month, sometimes more. Unfortunately, after all that, this experience was enough to make me stop coming.

Very disappointing, especially from a place I’ve supported for so long.
The pho broth is well-balanced and flavorful. Good portion for the price, and the menu has a nice variety. My favorite is #10 Pho Dac Biet (beef combination). 😋

The food was good, but the service could definitely be improved. The older woman handling the register, who I’m assuming is the owner, could have been friendlier. Not even acknowledging customers with a simple “hi” when paying is honestly sad. They took our order, but no one ever checked in afterward. I would come back for the food, but experiences like that when the owner is like that make me hesitant to continue supporting the business.

top_reviews.content:
An absolutely delightful dining experience at um.ma. ✨ The food was exceptional, with the bone marrow corn cheese being one of my favorites. Rich, indulgent, and incredibly flavorful, the marrow and cheese complemented one another in the most harmonious way.

The pork belly was beautifully seasoned, and I especially appreciated the chili served on the side..just enough to add a spicy kick according to my own tolerance.

The tteokbokki was equally impressive. I loved the pleasantly al dente texture of the rice cakes, which paired beautifully with the flavorful sauce.

Overall, my experience was nothing short of amazing. From the comforting food to the inviting ambiance, um.ma is definitely a place I would happily return to. ❤️

Food: we got bulgogi, kimchi fried rice and some vegetable dish. The bulgogi tasted good but it had a sort of grainy texture which I didn't like. The kimchi fried rice and vegetable dish was okay. Overall everything was okay but I wouldn't go out of the way to come back.

This was a great casual spot for a group of 6, although it’s easy to run out of space quickly on the picnic tables if you have a full crew! We got a widespread of food; I was the only vegetarian at the table, but for a Korean BBQ spot, they had a surprising amount of vegetarian/vegan options (even a vegetarian section on the menu). The kimchi fried rice was my favorite. The don’t have a full bar, but a good selection of soju, wine, and beer.

Felt like an authentic KBB experience. You can be seated at a table with a grill in the back patio or you can choose to not have the grill inside.
You can be at a table with a grill and not order the grill food options.
Overall good, but pricey

Chicken wings were very yummy and extremely crispy, tteokbokki was average. Overall, food was good but not life changing. Patio was warm and cozy, but indoor vibe was not great. Would recommend for a yummy casual dinner with a nice vibe and good value.

top_reviews.content: Really nice atmosphere here, way beyond you usual bar or beer garden. The owners work here, chill dude who seem to know half the guests here (at least for the World Cup). The popcorn chicken was the best I’ve had. Superior food to other bars. Also nice to be able to sit inside or outside as the bar opens up large windows. Huge beer selection of course out of a nicely designed tap system.

We stopped by before a show at the brick and mortar. Next door. A cheeseburger was $22 and a beer was about 13.  The staff was friendly enough but The vibes kind of weird like it's not an Irish pub or is it? The food was decent. Little greasy on the burger but I would stop by again before a show. I just wouldn't go out of my way otherwise.

Hands down my favorite spot in the city. I’m here literally every weekend — the beer list is always on point, the vibe is relaxed but alive, and the staff just gets it. Also, whoever curates the playlist deserves a raise — I’m Shazaming tracks almost every time I’m in. It’s the kind of place you want to gatekeep, but can’t stop telling people about. 5/5, no notes.

EDIT: Pedro is killing it with the summer menu. Tandoori Carrots 🔥🔥

EDIT Nov 2025: new season, new menu, still 🔥🔥. Try the stir fry eggplant.

The Crafty Fox Ale House was one of my favorite stops while visiting San Francisco. The space inside is cozy with plenty of seating and a great bar setup. The beers on tap were varied and had one of my favorites in the US (Allagash!). Prices were fair, service was quick, and beers cold. 100% would come back.

I've been coming to SF and I always go to this place, it feels like coming home. Good vibes and nice ambiance, I always Shazam off their playlist or recognize a niche song that
I know. The staff is always helpful and knowledgeable, but most of all, friendly and kind. Next to that, maybe the most important thing (for me): their beer list is insanely good. If you like lambics/geuze/sour beer, IPA's, or stouts. They have the best stuff on tap. The food is very good as well, nice comfort food with a beer and good variation. Go here if you love beer. While there are other spots in SF that have nice offering (liquid gold, Toronado) this one is my favorite. The range of the beer offering on tap, but the people and ambiance do it every time.

Zingari Ristorante & Jazz Bar was hands down one of the best nights we’ve had in San Francisco. The atmosphere is incredible, cozy, lively, and elevated all at once, with amazing live jazz that makes the whole place feel special from the moment you walk in.

If you’re looking for amazing Italian food, live music, creative cocktails, and a warm atmosphere with top-tier service, Zingari absolutely delivers. Already looking forward to coming back.

top_reviews.content:
(Jan 9, 2026)
My friend took me to this small traditional-looking Chinese place. The service was quick. Two of the three dishes stood out.

1. Vegetarian hand-pulled noodles -- The hand-pulled noodles are long and irregularly thick, they give a scissors to cut it. It has a nice bite to it.

2. Eggplant with Tofu -- The tofu is so soft, yet firmly fried in the exterior.
The sauce at the bottom is excellent! It is more soy-y?
My friend says it has sugar, and asks me to try it with the noodles, it is very good.

3. Vegetable Dumpling -- Normal and nothing noteworthy.

Totaled to $33.51 before tips. I do plan to come back to this place for the eggplant with tofu.

No fluff Chinese food! Remember to bring cash as this is a cash only establishment - it helps that there are a billion banks nearby.

I got the sesame beef pancakes, cow stomach, and rib noodle soup.

The soup was really clean and the noodles were so bouncy. The cow stomach was not as tender as I would have liked. And the beef rolls look handmade and remind me of ones I’ve had in China 🥹

Good place to get relatively affordable house made noodles and pancakes. Not too different from other hole in wall places. Great service and staff. I wanted to try their sesame pancake but they were out. Got their vegetable pancakes instead. Would come back again if i was in the area

This was our first time trying House of Pancakes, and let's just say--the name is definitely misleading in the best way. While you might expect a traditional breakfast spot, this cozy, mom-and-pop-style restaurant serves up hearty Northern Chinese dishes packed with flavor.

We came with a large group of extended family and were impressed with how accommodating and friendly the staff were. They even made thoughtful dish recommendations based on our group size and preferences, which made the experience even better.

We ordered quite a bit to share:

Beef Pancakes (a house specialty)
Lamb Skewers (spicy and non-spicy)
Lamb Dumplings
Pork Dumplings
Lamb Stir-Fried Hand-Pulled Noodles
Fresh Cucumber Salad

Overall, the food was delicious and flavorful. That said, if you're not a fan of lamb (like me), just be aware that the lamb skewers and dumplings can be a bit gamey. The spicy skewers helped mask it a bit, thanks to a generous sprinkle of paprika.

Surprisingly, I really enjoyed the lamb stir-fried noodles--the lamb in that dish was melt-in-your-mouth tender and tasted more like beef than lamb to me. Unfortunately, I couldn't try the beef pancakes due to dietary restrictions, but my cousins absolutely loved them and said they were a must-order.

The pork dumplings were a standout for me--juicy, flavorful, and perfectly cooked. And the cucumber salad was refreshing and balanced everything out nicely.

The restaurant has a small, casual diner vibe that gives it local charm--nothing fancy, but welcoming and perfect for sharing a flavorful meal with family or friends.

Local, low-key, friendly staff, cash only.
Good hand-pulled noodles, beef pancakes/rolls, handmade chewy dumplings.  Yes!  We want all of them.
Cash only -and you will have lots of food and change afterwards.

We stopped by on our way to see some friends in the mission and wanted something warm. Luckily we found Cha-Ya and was very pleased with that decision. Like I belonged in this space. Inspiring work, the craft of the cuisine, and good they serve their employees.

Have you ever had debris fall from the ceiling while dining at a restaurant? Unfortunately, my first experience happened at Penny Roma.

During our meal, black debris repeatedly fell from the ceiling onto our table and even into the wine glasses for the premium bottle of wine we had brought with us.

When we brought this to the manager’s attention, we were told that it was probably because “the wind caused dust to fall from the ceiling,” and we were offered another table. However, that explanation was what concerned me the most.

To me, the first priority of any restaurant is not just great food, but sanitation and food safety. Offering us another table was certainly the appropriate immediate action. However, what I expected to hear first was, “We’re truly sorry. We’ll inspect the ceiling and the facility immediately to determine the cause.” If debris is falling into guests’ food and wine, the issue is not the table—it is the facility itself.

Despite this, the food was exceptional. It was one of the most memorable Italian meals I’ve had in San Francisco, and we genuinely enjoyed every dish.

The Halibut Crudo was fresh, vibrant, and the perfect way to begin the meal. The Salmon Crudo featured a delicious sauce, although it slightly overpowered the natural flavor of the salmon.

The Ragù Mafaldine was outstanding. The wonderfully chewy mafaldine paired beautifully with the silky white sauce. The Salsiccia was also delicious, although the generous amount of cheese made it a bit too salty.

The Agnolotti was a wonderful example of a traditional interpretation. My favorite dish was the Cappelletti—the creamy corn sauce, Crescenza cheese filling, and the delicate aroma of fresh basil came together beautifully.

The desserts were equally impressive—elegant, balanced, and not overly sweet.

The service was also excellent. Our servers consistently refreshed the ice bucket for our wine, replaced our plates throughout the meal, and explained each dish with professionalism and warmth.

That is precisely why this experience was so disappointing.

When the food is this exceptional, it deserves an equally exceptional standard of sanitation. Debris falling from the ceiling into guests’ food and wine is, in my opinion, a serious food safety concern. This is not merely a service issue—it is a maintenance and sanitation issue that requires immediate investigation and corrective action.

I sincerely hope this matter will be thoroughly investigated and resolved. Penny Roma has rightfully earned its outstanding culinary reputation. I also sincerely hope that Flour + Water Hospitality Group will ensure that its standards of sanitation and facility maintenance reflect the same level of excellence as its cuisine.

Corkage is $40 per bottle, and the wine list is somewhat limited.

Had an amazing dinner at Penny Roma tonight. We started with the Arancini di Carciofi, which ended up being our favorite dish of the night, along with the focaccia — both were absolutely delicious. For pasta, we had the agnolotti dal plin and the rigatoni arrabbiata, and everything was fantastic. The staff was incredibly friendly and attentive, and we really appreciated that we never felt rushed throughout the meal. Can’t wait to come back!

top_reviews.content: I have been sneaking into this place in the afternoons before it gets too busy for many years. The magic of this informal Mexican Restaurant is its Yucatan origins. The flavors are different and highly addictive. The margaritas are made with just fresh squeezed limes. Over the years they have used different tequilas for their house margaritas, but they are always amazing, so don't miss out! The salad dressing on the house salad is so delicious one day I am going to find out how they make it. I have only tasted it in the Yucatan. Perhaps I should ask before the pitcher of house margaritas kicks in! They have a legendary tequila bar that is a cozy experience. The lights are dim, and the ceilings are low, which gives a cozy atmosphere. The staff and service seem like this place is family run, and it makes for an intimate unique experience.

We had a fun, great dinner at Tommy's. The staff was very friendly and made good recommendations on food and drinks. I had two of the house margaritas, both of which were awesome (they were strong and tasted good). I should have taken more pictures of the food, but I was too busy eating, I guess. My wife had the verde cheese enchiladas pictured here. They were really good, but the unlikely star of our meal was the simple salad they brought out as an appetizer. I'm not sure exactly what ingredients they used, but I'd go back just for that.

San Francisco’s Tommy’s Mexican Restaurant is a must-visit destination for tequila enthusiasts. This family-owned establishment is renowned globally for its extensive selection of 100% agave tequila and the iconic “Tommy’s Margarita,” crafted by Julio Bermejo, the owner and a tequila connoisseur.

Tommy’s offers a unique experience for those seeking to explore tequila, providing tastings and educational opportunities alongside traditional Mexican and Yucatecan cuisine in a lively and welcoming atmosphere.

One of my closest friends, Gary, introduced me to this exceptional establishment, and I wholeheartedly recommend it. The margaritas are exceptional, and the Camarones Al Mojo De Ajo is the best I have ever tasted. Pork Chops “Chuletas” and cheese quesadillas are also outstanding.

During my visit, I had the pleasure of meeting Julio, the owner. He is an exceptional individual, highly attentive, friendly, and exceptionally kind.

To ensure a pleasant experience, it is advisable to arrive early to secure a spot at the bar and engage in conversations with Julio. I assure you that you will not be disappointed.

Tommy's Mexican Restaurant holds a special place in my heart, and I'd like to share a brief story about it. When I moved to San Francisco around 30 years ago, a dear friend and colleague (who has since passed away) invited me to an after-work gathering for one of Tommy’s famous tequila-tasting classes. It was a wonderful opportunity to meet my new coworkers and connect with people outside the office. Over the years, I returned many times. However, as life changed and jobs shifted, I found myself away for nearly twenty years until yesterday. Being in the neighborhood reminded me of my late friend, and I decided to drop in for a bite and a drink in her memory.

I sat at the bar, where the “good stuff” (read: tequila) is on display. The current owner, Julio Bermejo, happened to be there, and we chatted for a few minutes. He shared that this year marks the restaurant’s 60th anniversary and mentioned how patron habits have evolved; younger folks don’t go out for drinks as they once did. Although bar traffic has decreased compared to the past, the restaurant is still thriving, and, yes, they continue to offer their tequila classes. That’s what makes Tommy’s special: it’s not just a restaurant; it’s a piece of San Francisco history.

Tommy’s was founded in 1965 by Tomas (“Tommy”) and Elmy Bermejo, who gradually introduced authentic dishes from their native Yucatán. This focus on Yucatecan cuisine sets Tommy’s apart. While they offer all the classic Mexican dishes, the real highlights are regional specialties like their famous Chile Rellenos, Poc Chuc, and Pollo Pibil. It’s comfort food perfected over decades.

Then came their son, Julio, who transformed the bar scene. A tequila expert, he decided early on to use only 100% agave tequila (their liquor license dates back to 1976). He created the now-famous “Tommy’s Margarita,” which replaces triple sec with pure agave nectar. It’s simple, clean, and so delicious that bartenders around the world replicate it today.

What started as a small family spot serving home-style recipes has become known as the “epicenter of tequila in the United States.” Despite its fame, it still feels like a neighborhood establishment run by a family eager to welcome you and share great food along with some of the best tequila you'll ever taste. If you get the chance, stop by before the end of the year and raise a margarita or a tequila shot to celebrate their 60th anniversary.

Our table was not cleaned well and the condiments on the table looked old and the containers looked like they needed to be cleaned, hence the reason for my 3 and 4 stars on the service and the atmosphere.
Pictures says it all: Ramen egg was served with a gigantic hole. I understand that eggs have variations but even at home if I open an egg that looks like that, I would never serve it to my guests.

Food: OK, solid for US ramen. Nice to be able to get Hakata style. Broth was solid, presentation was lacking but not terrible. As lunch, this bowl of ramen did not leave me feeling disgusted at the amount of food and oil consumed, which I think is a failing in the world of ramen. It lacks the carefully put-together excess that should be present.

Price: too high. Without adding the $4 egg, my $17 bowl of ramen was fairly simplistic and the portion size didn't feel like a serious indulgence the way ramen really should. I think this is one of the better options for ramen I've had in the bay, but as with most US ramen, the value is just not there and this value is worse than some other very solid I've had in the area.

Atmosphere and Service: Nice, clean restaurant with attentive staff. The disposable chopsticks are cheap and do fray - not the end of the world. A few hand-trucks of ingredients came through the front at about 1pm - also not a big deal, but did have to interact with that on my way out. Overall very pleased with the atmosphere and service, no strong complains or issues. The Japanese menu wall art is a nice touch.

Overall: For me personally, I probably won't come back, but if you're into the local ramen scene you'll probably enjoy this spot.

top_reviews.content: This place is an absolute gem! We just had one of the best dining experiences we’ve ever had in San Francisco at Tommaso’s, and I honestly can’t wait to go back.

From the moment we walked in, we felt genuinely welcomed. The woman who greeted us was so kind and warm — chatting with our toddler and making us feel immediately at home. She seated us, took care of us throughout the evening, and served us with such joy and hospitality.

And the food… absolutely incredible. We ordered the Burrata and Roasted Tomatoes appetizer, Pasta alla Boscaiola, Spaghetti and Meatballs, and a cheese pizza for our (picky!) little guy. Oh! And for dessert we had the best tiramisu of our lives. Everything tasted authentic, homemade, and full of history — the kind of meal that feels like it’s been perfected through generations of family recipes. You can truly taste the love and care in every dish. And somehow, our picky kiddo happily finished two whole pizza slices — which honestly says a lot!

Later in the evening, we learned that the woman taking care of us the entire time was actually the owner. She humbly shared the story of the restaurant — a 90-year-old business with its original pizza oven and decades of history behind it. Her passion for hospitality and preserving something so special shines through in every detail.

By the end of the night, she gave us a big hug and we told her we’d come back with our whole family next time. That says everything about the kind of place this is.

Amazing food, unforgettable hospitality, and the kind of experience that reminds you why family-owned, women-owned restaurants are so special. We absolutely loved it and can’t wait to return!

top_reviews.content:
An ok 3.5 / 5 experience.  Rounding up to 4 🫥

I understand that carrots and zucchinis in your taco burrito can throw people off. On the other hand if you want more veggies in your Mexican food, this place would be a blessing. I think they should do bell pepper and onion fajitas, instead of carrots and zucchini.

It had been 20 years since I was in the Bay Area, and was so happy to nothing changed.  Just delicious burritos.

I think Gordo’s secret is steaming the tortilla with the cheese.  Get it all melt.

I hope it won’t be another 20 years; but if it is Gordo’s: please don’t change. 👍👍

In response to some of the other reviews:

The pollo asado is the best I’ve ever had—perfectly cooked. If someone is afraid of, or confused by, blackness on their chicken, may I recommend Chipotle.

The moisture in the burritos is part of the excellent cooking. The beans are perfect, every time, and this means that they are perfectly moist; as is the salsa, the meat, and the rice. All perfect, every time. So, yes: you won’t get a super-dry burrito, and yes, this means that if you insist on taking it home, it may degrade slightly in structure (it will be perfect if eaten in-taqueria). My friends and I have been eating these burritos for over twenty years and have enjoyed many a one at home, just a little wetter. It’s worth it to have perfectly cooked ingredients.

Atmosphere. Let’s talk about atmosphere. This is one of the last  not Starbucked, not third-wave-coffee-housed joints left in the Bay. If you’re uncomfortable with the small space or old-school tables and chairs, then, again, allow me to recommend Chipotle. Or Taco Bell. How about Taco Bell? They keep their revolving-door A.I. market image updated every few months. You shouldn’t be bothered by any authenticity or lasting tradition there.

Bottom line: Gordo Taqueria is a Bay original. So many old authentic Bay Area eateries have been bought out, disappeared, or made unrecognizable. Please let Bay Area natives enjoy this one in peace before we flip every last space into a Tesla showroom.

I am sorry to hear about poor customer service, if it’s true; and to hear that long-timers have experienced bad food service. I hope that everything is going Ok for the owners and staff during a weird, tough time in the Bay and the world. Customers do have a right to demand civil treatment and continued quality.

I feel terrible posting this after the storm, but I had to share my experience. The place is quaint, and reservations or takeout are a must. Although I'm not a pizza fan, my kids loved it, and I enjoyed a delicious truffle pasta. The wine selection was unique but excellent.

If I can enjoy good food and wine with my family at a reasonable price... we’re in! I hope everyone is okay after the flood. See you soon!

Really delicious salad and pasta and massive portions. Super reasonable prices for the quantity and style of restaurant and apparently they have a crazy good deal where it’s 60 bucks for a salad pasta pizza and Dessert!! Will be back

I always have so much fun here from the excellent tunes to the superb brews. Top notch pasta dishes and pizza to die for. The staff go above and beyond doing everything they can to provide a unforgettable experience. Food comes out hot and portioned for two! I make reservations months in advance to ensure a smooth dining experience. I ABSOLUTELY LOVE THIS RESTAURANT.

name: Sequoia Diner
address: 3719 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland, CA 94619, United States

google.name: Sequoia Diner
google.address: 3719 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland, CA 94619, United States
google.description: Quaint, bright cafe with retro flair & a menu full of housemade sausages, breads, jams & pastries.

top_reviews.content:
Sequoia Diner is such a great spot and absolutely worth the visit. The food alone makes it stand out, and the overall vibe feels cool, laid-back, and very much like a neighborhood favorite.

When we arrived, there was about a 45-minute wait, which wasn’t surprising given how popular the place is. We decided to walk around the area while we waited, and it worked out perfectly—they actually called us before the 45-minute mark, which was a nice surprise.

Once seated, the food really delivered. Everything we ordered was great, well prepared, flavorful, and satisfying. It’s the kind of comfort food that’s done really well and leaves you glad you waited.

The staff experience was a bit mixed. Some team members were very friendly and welcoming, while others were more neutral. Overall, though, service moved efficiently and everything came out smoothly.

One quick heads-up for future diners: they do include a service charge that essentially functions as a tip. This wasn’t explained to us at the time, so we ended up tipping an additional 20% on top of the 19% service charge. Not a dealbreaker at all, just something good to know ahead of time.

I’ll definitely be back.  Great food, a cool vibe, and a well-managed wait make it a spot worth checking out just be mindful of the service charge when the bill comes.

Update March ‘26. Visited and something was off. The staff were different and the food was not the same quality. I couldn’t put my finger on it but googled it and found it was sold a few weeks ago which perhaps explains the difference. I hope they can get it back to what it was in the past:  my older review from earlier in 2026: I just love this place, I’ve been many times over the decade they’ve been open and I am never disappointed. The menu is always mouthwatering,  food is always top notch, the staff is cheerful, the atmosphere is buzzing, the interior is cute. I’m not  a vegan but I love that they have a variety vegan plate, which I often order. The potatoes here are so good. It’s always worth waiting in line for a seat at the Sequoia table!

Really loved this breakfast! It's so hard to find good biscuits and gravy on the west coast and they NAILED it. The biscuit was buttery, the gravy was savory, the greens had just enough spice.

We also loved how friendly the staff was. Our kids felt welcome and the staff were so good with them. The little ones loved the waffles, which were flaky and soft and cooked perfectly.

Seating can be tight but it's worth it.

Fantastic food and really nice staff. They have recipes I’ve never tried before, created with excellent craftsmanship. It’s not a greasy spoon for sure, but less expensive than other “high quality” diner-style restaurants nearby.

Came here after a hike. Waited about 30 minutes to get seated. Set at the bar. Food was out within about 20 minutes. The potato salad was exceptional. I loved the pickled onions in it. The Cuban sandwich was pretty good too. It was a little bit loud. It was hard to hear the person I was dining with but otherwise everything was great.

top_reviews.content: I like the retro Thai Movie decor that is around the restaurant. I started with the Thai Ice Lime Tea and that was super tasty and different from the regular Thai Iced Tea in a great way. The standout dishes for me were the Tom Yum and the Roasted Pork and Crispy Pork Belly. The Crying Tiger steak was too fatty for my liking. Great service though. Come check it out if you're in the area.

Tried a bunch of dishes here and everything was amazing and authentic!

The shrimp paste fried rice was great—super flavorful with lots of toppings (a must if you like bold flavors). The five spice pork leg, crying tiger, and salted egg yolk squid were all perfect, while the tom saap pork ribs tasted super authentic and spicy (just wished for a touch more lime). Even the wings and papaya salad were on point.

Drinks were great too—especially the Blaco Margarita (smooth and tasty without being heavy on alcohol). Overall, this place nails authentic Thai flavors with great execution. Definitely recommend if you’re into bold, spicy, and savoury dishes!

This my second time eating in this restaurant. I did not take pic of my first visit but I ordered their spring roll and pork belly rice meal. Somehow, this is a so so food. For the second time, I tried their pad thai with prawns and fried fish cake. This is good better than food i ordered in my first visit. They take order and serve food fast. The price is on the expensive side but the food quality is good. The vibes in the restaurant is very good. They have large tv with a bar. Very good for drinking and watching sports.

Food: there were several creative dishes on the menu. The food was overall good but is on the salty end. The portion also felt small relative to the price. Be careful, even medium spicy is very spicy.

Service: I was a bit disappointed with the service. Next to us was a table with 10+ people. The same server checked in with them multiple times during our 1.5 hour of meal, but never once checked in with us. We had to wait 15+ minutes just to get the server’s attention to request the check.

The food here is incredibly fresh and flavorful and authentic.
Their sweet fresh coconut was so refreshing and delicious. perfect for cooling down the flavorful dishes. Our food came out surprisingly fast, which was great because we were starving!
Everything we ordered was absolutely delicious, made with fresh ingredients and bold Thai flavors. We may have over-ordered but the food was so good that we finished every last bite. Highly recommend this spot for anyone craving authentic Thai cuisine!

reviews_snippets.content: "Would recommend the duck noodle soup and the crispy rice salad 😋"
"We ordered the fresh rolls, green curry w tofu, and pad see ew with chicken."
"In duck salad we didn't found duck, just small fried pisces, dry and fired."

name: Niku Steakhouse
address: 61 Division St, San Francisco, CA 94103, United States

google.name: Niku Steakhouse
google.address: 61 Division St, San Francisco, CA 94103, United States
google.description: Japanese-American menu of house-cut wagyu & local sides by the Omakase Group (Omakase, Dumpling Time).

top_reviews.content: This was our “treat yo self” decision for our upcoming anniversary while on vacation. We love being from Alabama, but sometimes there is just food in another state that’s worth waiting for! We arrived a bit earlier than our reservation, and were seated at the bar for a cocktail while we waited for a spot. We had upgraded our original reservation from the dining room to the chef’s table so we could watch while they cooked (my partner is my personal chef, so I requested he watch closely!) When our spots were ready, we were seated and presented with some champagne for our anniversary, as well as their version of avocado toast. I had no idea those small bites could be so delicious. We ended up ordering both the australian wagyu filet mignon as well as the tasting of japanese wagyu - a3 mother and a5 bushu so we could taste it all side-by-side. FIrst of all, it was all incredible and we truly could tell the difference…but we could’ve just had the filet and been pleased (we’re foodies, but not THAT cultured). However, it was a highly rated restaurant, our server was helpful, kind and guiding and we were there for a splurge - you only live once, you know? We also split the corn capellitti and roasted broccolini as our sides. Although we opted not to get dessert, we were handed a small bowl of sorbet and who can say no to that? It did not disappoint. All in all, this meal was everything we hoped it would be and more. Thank you for treating us so well and we truly enjoyed the conversations with all who stopped to chat with us!

Niku and our server Rueben made our anniversary dinner truly unforgettable. The team went above and beyond to make the night feel special, and the service was outstanding from start to finish.

We started with uniquely prepared and flavorful bone marrow and shishito peppers perfectly paired with anchovies aioli. For the main course, loved the recommended stone iron steak and A5 wagyu pairing, both were exceptional. Counter seating is a must to watch the chefs attention to every detail and get recommendations from the chef!

Amazing food, incredible quality, and thoughtful service. Highly recommend for a special occasion or an unforgettable dining experience.

Truly a five star experience. We dined here to celebrate a special occasion. The atmosphere is top notch. The service is friendly and attentive. We sat at the counter space and the gentleman preparing the steaks made great conversation and recommendations. He steered me towards the flat iron and it was a pleasant surprise. The food was wonderful. Our steaks (flat iron and filet) were seasoned wonderfully, tender and cooked to perfection. Our sides- the potatoes and corn- were a perfect compliment to the steaks. The dessert- brownie- was outstanding. It brownie was perfectly sweet and not overly sweet. Its texture was chewy in the best way possible. The meringue and ice cream (?) topping made it almost s’more like. This was the best meal we had in San Francisco.

For our anniversary dinner, Niku came very prepared to make it a memorable experience. Starting off with drinks, Greg was the knowledgeable and friendly face behind the counter. Niku has one of the most unique drink menus I’ve encountered in the city, and Greg broke down the various drinks and their processes, like purpose of clarifying certain drinks and how to go about making a milk punch. He satiates curiosity and really helped set the tone for our night, as the rest of the evening we felt the same level of care, attention to detail, and generosity from all the other staff. A special shout out needs to go to Avery as well, who graciously walked us through the menu and kept the vibe going! As for the food, I was thoroughly impressed with the beef tartare and bone marrow starters. Of course, you can anticipate the quality of beef as you step into a beef-centered Michelin-starred restaurant. However, the starters blew me away and I continued to be amazed with our rib eye and short rib courses. The potato au gratin is a must, a beauty in technical skill and a treat for your taste buds. Lastly, you can’t leave without trying the wagyu fat brownie. You just can’t. Thank you to Greg, Avery, and the gentleman that helped us to complimentary champagne to help us ring in our special evening. We will be back!

An amazing restaurant. The steaks and sides are delicious and the atmosphere is very good. Highly recommend eating here.

What I don't like is staff sanitation. I watched an employee multiple times pull their phone out of their pocket and then directly started working on food with both utensils and their hands and not washing in-between. That was definitely a huge turnoff.

top_reviews.content:
Just delicious! Their menu is a bit confusing as the in person menu is different from the “order online” menu, and the “order online” menu had some items listed as “out of stock” but when we asked, they were able to make the items.

We got the cilantro beef and combo chow mein. Huge portions and so so good. We eat ultra low sugar so we are always afraid dishes will be too sweet, but nothing we ordered had too much sugar. We’ll definitely be coming back.

Best Hunan food in San Francisco! I’m from Hunan and find the food here so authentic. The stir fried dishes has good wok hei, the smoky aroma from high-heat wok cooking. The wok hei turned some normal dishes into totally different tastes. Must try if you like hunan or spicy food.

This was our second time coming to this place, and I think we had tried most of the items on the menu.

We had Serrano pork, spicy pig ear, fried pig intestines with spicy sauce, stir fried bef wit hpickle pepper, cilantro beef, stir-fried with lettuce stem, cumin beef, and Stir-fried tomato and scrambled eggs.

All of these dishes taste amazing. Spicy and flavorful, and served in generous portions.

We went on the evening of the 23th. It wasn’t very crowded, but since there were only one or two servers, we still waited a short while to be seated. We were seated in a corner near the entrance, so it was a bit hard for the staff to notice us.
Most of the dishes here lean on the spicy side. We asked for very, very, very mild, but the food still had a slight kick. The shredded potato dish was a bit thick-cut and on the sour side. The fried noodles were decent, and the stir-fried beef was fine as well. Thankfully, the stir-fried pork didn’t have any unpleasant pork smell. My friend mentioned that it didn’t have as much “wok hei” as the first time she tried it.

Visited at 6 PM on a weekday when the restaurant wasn’t too busy. The ambiance was pleasant and welcoming, and the staff were friendly throughout our meal. The egg rolls made a great start — crisp and flavorful. The Kung Pao chicken was perfectly spicy and easily the best dish of the evening. Both the shrimp and chicken combo fried rice and the chow mein noodles were tasty and satisfying. Overall, a nice spot for a relaxed and delicious meal.

Colonel Sanders, Pig Candy Bacon, Cornmeal, Craft Brew, Cat Fish, Beef Ribs, Grilled Shrimp, House made Ranch, Stewed Tomatoes, Pulled Pork Beans, Okra, Baby Back Ribs, enough smoke to cook an entire ranch and stories, service, genuine kindness, originality, culinary craft, attitude, flavors, did I mention flavors 4 house made BBQ sauces from Molasses to Sweet and Spicy and stories and hospitality from the owner that elevated this experience from restaurant to Cult Classic...

Baby Blues is at entirely different level of  BBQ brought to San Francisco, living up to the Mission Street reputation as a destination for quality food, authentic experiences and downhome loving people. The reminisce of the Harley Dealership across the street blended with the owners fond memories of growing up with Colonel Sanders, the founder of Kentucky Fried Chicken, coupled with authentic Philly attitude and upbringing this long time San Francisco Pit Master has a restaurant that every BBQ lover in the Bay needs to try at least once and keep coming back for the atmosphere, Ribs, burgers, baked potatoes and authentic downhome quality touches that makes all their sauces, meats and sides exceptional. And great craft beer and conversation.

Leave your attitude at the door and come experience the down-to-earth honest food that makes culinary adventures in San Francisco worth every bite. Family BBQ joint in every way possible. Exceptional Service and Food.

We’re not local, but we were craving some good barbecue on our way home from SFO. This place really hit the spot and also had a great selection of beers. The bar was full with everyone watching the USA versus Venezuela baseball game. Very cool vibe. Great service too! Adding this spot to my list! We loved it!
Brisket and mac and cheese were delicious. The sauces they have are also amazing. Would recommend. It is a bit on the pricy side  though but worth it for that smokey flavor

I thought the food here was “ok”. The baby back ribs were a little tough and I didn’t hear my friend raving about their brisket, but there’s so much on the menu that I’d go back and try more things. My side of mac n cheese was good, but we did not are for their savory style baked beans… personal preference. The cornbread is blah but I don’t need great cornbread (but it helps).

I’d go back though, need to try more to see if anything here is crave-able.

The brisket was cut with the grain so it was extremely tough instead of fork tender. That’s how I judge a bbq place and this place failed. Fries were fine, pulled pork was fine, ribs did not fall off the bone. It’s sad that the Bay Area has such bad bbq that this stands out as good in comparison.

"Rustic place, bit grunge, bit philly...bit dive bar."

top_reviews.content: Its a small restaurant than get busy during the lunch hours. The food we ordered was overall good. We ordered the vegetable crouquette, veggie okonomiyaki, and mushroom creamy ramen. My favorite was the vegetable crouquette. It was crispy on the outside and good in the inside. The flavors were great too. The veggie okonomiyaki was also quite tasty. However, the mushroom creamy ramen was just okay for me. I felt like it was missing something, but I couldn't pinpoint what it was. But the presentation was good and I did like the crunchy noodles in it. The staff were good, but busy as we ate during lunch hours. If it's busy and you're a small party, you may have to share tables with another party, but I didnt see that as a huge problem. You are also able to reserve tables ahead of time, especially if you're a larger party, so you can try doing that if you're concerned. Prices were okay, especially for being in San Francisco. I would come again for the crouquette and to try the other dishes. There are a lot of options on the menu to try.

Food was delicious and authentic, and the service was wonderful! It was funny when the owner poured soy sauce on the radish and told me to eat it together with the mackerel haha. I had the saba, yakitori, and tonkatsu, all were really yummy and taste exactly like what I had back in Japan. I will be coming back sometime with family and friends :)

I went on July 4th and the workers were all pretty fast even though there was a wait list. They were also very friendly the entire time. As a group we ordered the spicy cheesy ramen, spicy tantan ramen, and the dynamite sushi roll to share. They give you chilli oil on the side to adjust the spiciness yourself. The spicy cheesy ramen was good, nothing extraordinary. The tantan ramen had a rich and creamy peanut flavour which I loved. But the dynamite roll was genuinely the BEST sushi I’ve ever had in my entire life. It had this kind of subtle smokey flavour and the sauce was pretty spicy but so good.

Excellent value. The combo plate is generally pretty good. Katsu was well made. I would skip the terriaki chicken. Shrimp tempura were good. The best best thing was the Crispy Chicken Chili Creamy ramen.

Such a massive menu for meat eaters and vegetarians alike! It's also picky-eater friendly! Personally I'm a very picky vegetarian, yet still feel I could eat there for breakfast, lunch and dinner two days in a row without repeating menu items! Plus it's sooooo yummy and authentic! And they have deals to make it more affordable!

top_reviews.content: I was very disappointed in the service we received yesterday. It appeared the staff and our waiter were more interested in the soccer game on TV than providing great service.  I had to remind them to give us napkins twice.  I had to remind them for a straw to drink my water twice. After my daughter and I were done with our meal, we sat with empty plates and glasses in front of us for at least 15 minutes before being acknowledged.  My daughter enjoyed her pizza, but my fish could've been better. My fish tasted as though it had been fried in old oil and was greasy. The fries were delicious.  The ambience was very nice. Not to be negative, but I came to this location back in October of 2025 and was disappointed at the customer service by the male host when we were seated. My kids were a bit upset because I chose to leave due to poor customer service, ironically enough when we returned yesterday my daughter understood explicitly why I chose to leave the first time. I believe in second chances but after two bad incidents in a row, we will not return.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️HAPPY HOUR, 9pm
I am pleased to say I gave Honor another shot at  the 9pm happy hour. Vibes were excellent in the lounge. It was very cozy with beautiful decorations and lovely Christmas music. The truffle fries were outstanding, but not on the happy hour menu and unavailable after 10pm. I would highly recommend the Mushroom and Arugula pizzetta on the happy hour menu. Ordered around 10pm and the kitchen had no problem making them quickly.
I love the cocktails/drinks of the day. They almost never miss. The espresso martinis are also not on the happy hour menu but so delicious because they brew their own espresso.
The bar tenders and servers are always very nice and we are greeted immediately and brought water.
I love when Shai is on aux because there are no ads and the music is great!
Luis is also a friendly face to have around. So kind and welcoming. Jolly vibes, good drinks…late night happy hour is the way to go.

Amazing food, service and atmosphere. The dogs love it here and are always welcomed with a big bowl of water. Honor Kirchen is an overall great place for hanging out with friends enjoying good eats. ♥︎♥︎♥︎

This place has a vibe. Just walking by makes you want to go inside. It's chic, eclectic, and homey all wrapped into one space. The food was good, but to be honest we only ordered apps. We ordered six appetizers. No disappointments on the food. However, the cocktails were a miss. The creations here didn't work for our palettes.

Horrible. Spoiled food. We came hungry, during happy hour (restaurant was closed). The hummus was spoiled to the taste and smell (Manager refused to smell it). Chicken sliders, one came out with cheese and one without. Per the menu, there’s no cheese. Food was ordered together but all came out at different times and we received the wrong food. Crab melt came out within a few minutes... too fast if you ask me. Meanwhile the pathetic slider took 15 minutes. The place was full. I guess the drinks are good. Grateful that the Americano had whipped cream. They comp'd us, but I won't be back. I draw the line at spoiled food, especially when the service is bad.

top_reviews.content:
We had such a wonderful experience celebrating my mom’s birthday here! From the moment we walked in, the atmosphere felt warm, elegant, and perfect for a special occasion.

Every dish we ordered was absolutely delicious. The pasta was rich and flavorful, the steak was cooked perfectly and paired beautifully with the cheese and sauce, and the seafood dish was fresh and well-balanced. Even the sides like the vegetables and polenta were done so well. And the desserts — especially the tiramisu and cheesecake — were the perfect ending to the meal!

What really stood out was the presentation and attention to detail. Every plate looked beautiful and tasted just as good as it looked.

The service was also excellent — attentive, friendly, and made the whole experience feel relaxed and special without being rushed.

Overall, this was the perfect place for a family celebration. My mom had a great birthday, and we’ll definitely be coming back again. Highly recommend!

My husband and I were in town for a very short weekend and were recommended Original Joe’s but when we popped in it was very loud and not the atmosphere we were looking for. So we walked up the street and stumbled upon North Beach Restaurant and from the moment we stepped inside we knew it was going to be an amazing experience. The design of the restaurant is elegant and the service was so informative and thoughtful. Our server was very knowledgeable about the wine we ordered samples of to choose from and honestly it was hard deciding between the three because they all tasted amazing. We were trying to hit many food spots within our trip and so were only popping in for a bite to eat. We settled in on the pesto gnocchi and our server gave us the option to add chicken on. He served it to us already split between two plates and the presentation still looked very intentional. It was exactly what both of us were wanting out of a mid afternoon meal and the chicken was a great addition. After we finished our food we decided to try the house made tiramisu which was absolutely divine! Overall, amazing experience and we will be back to try all the pasta options that sounded equally delicious.

First time her. Enjoyable ambiance with live singing and music. Service was attentive and nice. And the food was delicious. I got the eggplant Parmesan while others in my party got pesto gnocchi and other amazing looking dishes. Will be back here for sure to this North Beach restaurant!

North Beach Restaurant is truly the best spot in the neighborhood. I eat there all the time. Their dishes are incredible — the tortellini, the seafood pasta, the lasagna, the prosciutto with burrata — everything is outstanding. The service is exceptional. Francesco is the best host, always so attentive, and the whole team makes you feel genuinely cared for. They put so much love into every dish. I really, really recommend this place.

Nice experience on a Tuesday night. Ordered fritto misto, lasagna, tiramisu. I drank Powers, neat. They provide bread with cheap olive oil and balsamic, complimentary.

I asked for a table away from the live music but they put us right in front of it, so we had to ask to move. The table we moved to wasn't much quieter, but had more romantic lighting so we settled down there. Great portion size on the fritto misto.

Server, Nino, was good - a little anxious towards the end, he was trying to check out - but he gets a pass. The pasta is fresh, though missing an element of structure. Tiramisu was disappointing, again lacking structure and missing depth of flavor.

A decent place for a romantic dinner, though maybe not for a critic, or to bring a group to enjoy the atmosphere. The music and lighting complemented the vibe.

top_reviews.content: My friend ordered the custom Detroit style deep dish pizza, including Pepperonis and mushrooms  as a topping. The dough was pillowy soft, like biting into a dense fluffy cloud. The sauce was wonderfully seasoned, when I was eating the pizza I could even see the seasoning in the sauce, appearing to the oregano/Italian seasoning. The cheese was stretchy and warm, and had a slight cheese pull. The Pepperonis were salty and soft, and the mushrooms were pretty good. The crust had a cheese crust on it, with a good structural  integrity, which combine together to give a slight crunch, a perfect complement to the soft doughy pizza. I would highly recommend the deep dish pizza, and overall the food is very good for the price. The location is not the best location, often with homeless people outside, but the service is good and quick. Easy to order and pick up. Highly reccomed this place for cheap pizza!

I have been here many times, also I had got  it delivered to me before via DoorDash. I usually stop by when I am in need of a quick bite, when my cravings are focused for a pizza or if I just so happen to be in the area. The staffs here are welcoming, well trained, understanding and helpful where I had never encountered an issue during any of my visits. They have items that are ready for purchase and some things that are made to order which is usually what I go for since it is quality over quantity and I never mind the wait since I am a very patient person. They have promotions throughout the day which will definitely fill you up. Their menu is simple and organized where I guarantee you will find something that fits your taste. You can order in person, order online, or have it delivered to you via a delivery app. I highly recommend this place to all pizza lovers, to anyone in need of a quick bite just like me or if you just so happen to be in the area to check them out. I definitely will be back to tryout the other delicious options they have to offer.

Location is decent, people stand around waiting for their pizza so you gotta ask if anyone is in line. Pizza was good, workers were nice so I cant complain. Parking was hard bc I had to find street parking which was sketchy and packed. I survived luckily, would go again:)

I guess don’t order food too late because they literally don’t put any thought into what their preparing to send out to customers not to mention I paid for my crazy sauce and didn’t even get that. There’s no butter or Parmesan on top of this so-called cheesy bread. Isn’t that a shame?

1/4/2026: NFL Sunday! I wanted to eat some cheap pizza while watching the games. My order was ready in about 30 minutes. I like how you don't have to deal with the line if you order via their website. There's a machine where you punch in a code and the little door opens for you to get your pizza. I had their deep dish sausage $11.50 and a stuffed crazy crust $13. This was filling. Maybe not the best ingredients, but Little Caesars does the job. My mouth had a weird salty taste afterwards. Even a few beers didn't wash it away. On the stuffed crazy crust pizza, I noticed they sprinkled parmesan cheese on it. It was burnt onto the crust and tasted really salty. On the next slices, I scratched them off before I ate it.

Original review: This Little Caesars location is not bad. I've been to worst. I ordered online and my combo deep dish $15 was ready within the expected time frame. Most days, this location is busy and wait times can be about 20-30 mins after you order online. While the quality is still aren't as good as Bravo, Little Joe's or North Beach pizza in this area, it was still enjoyable for a chain pizza restaurant. These are much better than the other ones. You know which ones.

top_reviews.content: This was my first time visiting The Harlequin and I found it to be a very relaxing environment. Service was very good very polite and attentive. We ordered the steak frites and the ribeye and the chocolate molten lava cake for dessert. The ribeye steak was a little overcooked and everything could’ve used a little salt aside from that everything was delicious. Good place for anybody looking for a place to eat in SF.

My group of friends and gf were staying across the street at The Marquis, and this was just so convenient to go try out for dinner before a night out. The food was good; pizza was delicious!! (Goat cheese hits every time), the drinks were yummy and on theme. We also had a magician join us at the beginning while we waited for our food; it was a great time, funny, charismatic, and his tricks were very entertaining. I don’t leave reviews often, but this was definitely a nice place to visit.

Fantastic American-style restaurant! The atmosphere really stands out and makes it an enjoyable place to sit back and relax.

There’s a solid selection of beers, cocktails, and wines, so plenty of options no matter what you’re in the mood for. The food was great across the board, and the service matched it. The Smash Burger is one of the favourites I’ve ever had

Overall, a great experience and definitely worth a visit!

Fun friendly and low prices with very high quality drinks and food. Location is excellent and easy axis for convention folks or shoppers. Unfortunately there is no mall next door anymore to go shopping after a few drinks. The place still is relaxed and friendly and that's all you really need.

Pretty good food. Fries could have been hotter and needed more salt, but the smashburger was good. My wife’s steak was slightly undercooked and not enough sear, but it was still delicious. Not sure if the price point was worth it. $130 after 2 beers and tip.
