top_reviews.content:
We had such a great time at Goat Hill Pizza's Monday night buffet! The pizza was delicious, the atmosphere was fun, and the staff made the experience exceptional.

My boyfriend has celiac disease, and they went above and beyond to accommodate him. They remembered where we were sitting and personally brought each gluten-free pizza to our table, with lots of great options throughout the night. It made him feel so included, and we really appreciated the extra care.

If you're in Potrero Hill, the Monday night buffet is a no-brainer. Even if you're coming from another neighborhood, it's worth the drive—easy parking, amazing pizza, and some of the friendliest service we've experienced. We'll definitely be back!
The veggie pizza was tasty with fresh ingredients and great flavor. It was a little oily, but overall I still enjoyed it.

Utterly fantastic little hidden gem of a pizzeria.  The staff is beyond friendly and genuinely love their pizza and their customers.  The pizza itself is out of this world and I tried the buffet which gives you access to one hot slice after another.  This is a must do Monday only tradition.

The crust is a perfectly crisp sourdough and toppings and all ingredients are of the highest quality.

Why are you even reading this!  Go out and eat here now!

Parking is very easy.  Especially for SF.  Safe neighborhood.

Well worth the trip up Potrero Hill. This place is a city staple and the pizza is delicious. Whether dining in or takeout, it's always amazing. The atmosphere is cozy and rich San Francisco history. The staff is always friendly and inviting. Our Favorite Pizza Spot!

This is one of those places that I consider old school San Francisco, a neighborhood gem and one I wish will never go away and stay just the way it is.

I've been going to this place since the early 80's, in my college years, through working various jobs in the city and living in different neighborhoods, and now into the latter years.

Its food is good in all regards, a reliable standard, the staff friendly and the facility remains in good order after all these years. So perhaps it isn't just the food, the staff and the restaurant, but in the aspect that it also holds a lot of good memories from the past with old friends and previous dates, it's precious in that way for me.

Keep on rockin' Goat Hill Pizza, they don't make restaurants like you anymore.

top_reviews.content:
An outdoor to-go stand only. Might need luck finding parking but the order came out pretty quick.

Buttermilk Fried Chicken Sandwich ($14.60): The coleslaw salad alone was not enough. It really needed another sauce in the sandwich. Chicken wasn't moist. Very subpar.

Chicken Salad ($13.50): This is the exact same thing as the sandwich, minus the bun. No need to order both items unless you really want extra carbs. The coleslaw salad by itself was not bad though. Just didn't pair well in the sandwich. Chicken was meh, again.

Strawberry Shortcake ($8.00): Basically a deconstructed shortcake, if you like that kind of stuff. A biscuit in one corner, cream in another, then topped with strawberries. It's pretty good but not mind-blowing.

Do not underestimate the power of the local pie store in the Temescal neighborhood! If you're looking for a local business that makes the best pies, whether it be apple, blueberry, or more -- look no further than Bakesale Bettty!

They are located right off of Telegraph and 51st Street, right across from the Children's Hospital of Oakland. Though they do most of their sales outside (rain or shine), they know just how to impress the right people -- and one of those people would have to include me because their pies really took me to a different level of pie appreciation.

We went on a Friday morning (keep in mind they are closed Monday through Wednesday, so plan accordingly when you want to go buy these pies), and while the lines were a bit long, the line wasn't too bad, and they went rather quick.

Me and my friend got the banana cream pie, and the key lime pie. I love how tart the pies were -- the banana cream was so layered, made with actual banana and it was topped with another layer of cream and chocolate covering. All in all, $7 a slice for a piece of pie is not bad at all, especially if they were made by food artisans who knew their craft.

Ambiance is rather good, and not underwhelming at all. This place IS worth the hype forsure xD

I'm definitely recommending Bakesale Betty to any and all friends who want to try this :)) till we meet again!!

I don't get the hype. I've bought the chicken sandwich twice now and it's nothing special other than it's kind of big. Also why is the counter always out on the sidewalk? Everyone should take a breath and walk down to OK's Deli for their delicious sandwiches aha... Sorry guys I tried to enjoy yours - you can do better!

Bake sale Betty…… Mmmm Mmmmm DELICIOUS!  this place gets packed and busy and the operation time is limited, so if you go there, it may have a long line, but they will get the orders in and out real quick. The chicken is tender and crispy, the slaw has a little spice since it has jalapeño’s in it but it’s a nice blend. If they have the strawberry short cake… GET IT!! ITS HELLLLLLLLLAAAAAA GOOD HAHAHA.

Betty's has been around for a long time and there are numerous great reasons for that. Her chicken sandwichrs are phenomenal, gtendre, crispy fried breast with a ton of mixed saled and just the right seasoning. Her pie crust is one of the best anywhere, her crumbles delightful and the whipped cream is delicious. I miss the ironing board tables and openness, it is only take out. But the quality of the food, including the cookies makes a trip there always worthwhile, even with the sometimes long lines.

I thought the green tea was complementary as it was just in the table but I was wrong. I was charged for that. So felt a bit misleaded there.

We have been to many faux meat / vegan places but the food here was just ok.
We ordered steamed dumplings and vegetable chow mein. Dumplings were good, not super flavorful though. Chow mein was served with a big portion but was too oily. At last, we ordered spicy Ma Po Tufo which has a really thick, overly starched gravy, awful.

Staff did not seem warm and welcoming enough.

Great little vegetarian restaurant. Veggies were fresh and the flavors were strong. I would eat here again

top_reviews.content:
Very popular bar & restaurant. I joined friends here for dinner on a Saturday evening and it was fully packed. Every table was occupied and there were also a number of people standing at the back near the bar.

They don't take reservations, so you may need to plan to wait a while for a table. There is a large outdoor seating area in front off the street, as well as a reasonable amount of seating indoors.

The food was good and tasty. We all enjoyed our meals.

Service could be improved. There weren't enough servers for the number of people and I think someone only came to the table twice the whole time we were sitting there. I had to ask the hostess for a menu after waiting for a while.

Because this place is so popular, it's very loud. I had to strain to hear my friends speak just across the table. For that reason, it's not an ideal spot for deep conversation or a date.

Def a pick up spot but that’s ok if that’s what you’re looking for. The food is great and the vibe is happy and fun. Wait staff is really great! Our waitress was so sweet and on top of everything. I know they are known for their espresso martinis and literally every single person sitting at the bar had one. We had wine instead which was also yummy. Portions are also pretty huge so keep that in mind when ordering. My BLT was def enough for 2 people. They also have outside seating which is fun on nice days.

I was excited to try Balboa Café, especially since it’s known for having some of the best espresso martinis in the city. The espresso martinis were smooth and well-balanced.

Unfortunately, the food didn’t quite match the same standard. I had the salmon, which lacked flavor, and the paella was just average. Another downside was the cleanliness — the table we were seated at had a noticeably dirty tablecloth, which was disappointing and took away from the overall dining experience.

Great for drinks, but the food and attention to detail could use some improvement

Around midnight on May 24, 2026, I was subjected to an unprovoked assault by security staff at Balboa Cafe. A guard [refer to image] threw me against the exit door, causing me to strike my head, and then shoved me into oncoming traffic in the middle of the road while threatening to fight me. The assault only stopped when a second guard intervened after I threatened to call the police.

Following my online and direct reports to management, the security guard began cyberstalking and digitally harassing my wife as retaliation. He doxed her personal details online and posted disparaging remarks on her company's professional page using an anonymous account.

After discussions with Balboa Cafe's manager and PlumpJack Group's Director of Operations, the security guard has been permanently barred from the venue. However, he remains employed by the third-party security company for the time-being, so please be aware and take caution if you see him elsewhere in San Francisco.

Vibes here are great! Drinks are great!!

Burger was the driest burger I've ever had. My buddy from the UK who was joining me asked if this was normal. It is not.

top_reviews.content:
This restaurant has a different interpretation on Vietnamese food. Some people raves about it and others complain.

There’s different menus for lunch and dinner. Lunch has Pho, chicken wings, spring rolls etc.  Dinner menu omits all that’s offered at lunch, and offers more sophisticated dishes.

Tried the special of the day and it was not great. Angel hair pasta fried with seafood and topped with crab meat. It was too dry to eat!!

Service was ok. Atmosphere is ok… nothing outstanding. Food was lukewarm.

Bodega SF had been on our list for a while, especially after seeing it ranked in The Infatuation’s top 20 restaurants in San Francisco, so we were excited to finally try it. We made a reservation for a Wednesday night and were seated quickly upon arrival, while there was a noticeable line for walk ins.
The space has a trendy, lively atmosphere that sets the tone for a fun dining experience. We ordered a variety of dishes: steamed rice rolls, tiger prawns, stir fried pho noodles, mushrooms with quail eggs, and crab fat fried rice.

There were definitely some highlights. The tiger prawns and mushrooms with quail eggs were standouts, and I especially loved the stir fried pho noodles since they felt unique and creative compared to typical noodle dishes. However, not everything landed. My sister and mom found the filling in the steamed rice rolls to be a bit dry, and the crab fat fried rice did not quite work for us as a combination of flavors.

Service was the main downside of the evening. Although the restaurant was busy, our waiter passed by our table multiple times without stopping to take our order, and our food took over 20 minutes to arrive.
Overall, Bodega SF offers a stylish setting and some memorable dishes, but the experience was mixed due to inconsistent execution and service.

I haven't been able to find any Vietnamese food that i like in the city and have had my eye on this spot for a while so i booked a reservation on a weeknight for dinner to treat my sister! It really scratched the itch for the homesickness of my mom or grandma's homecooked viet food but make it a little upscale but still approachable and comforting.  I really appreciated the family style menu. Jeremy was our server and was very knowledgeable, kind, and attentive. They really hit all the marks. I could eat like forty of the banh khots. The Bo luc lac was the star of the show for my sister and is definitely a must try but the off-menu razor clams were my personal favorite! We also loved the crab fat fried rice, matcha crepe cake and hochija pannacotta! We will definitely be back.

Came on a weekday and tried out the chef's tasting menu. It was surprisingly filling. I hardly could finish the last of the entree, completely stuffed. We enjoyed the varieties of Vietnamese cuisine within the selection. A tad too similar in taste with the overuse of fish sauce in all their dressing and sauces. Vietnamese cuisine has other sauces, but they might be too pungent for the western palate.

I’m so glad we tried this spot. It is a unique and I would say elevated take on classic Vietnamese food. We had the Shaking Beef and Chimichurri Banh Mi. The spices and flavors of the Shaking Beef was really good however it did leans slightly salty. The Banh Mi came with a beef pho broth dipping sauce. This was a delicious combo and the beef broth itself was super flavorful.

Excellent food and amazing service! First time here from Houston and really enjoyed everything we ordered. The chicken 65 is the best I have ever had. Houston raves about its food here equally good if not better!

top_reviews.content: Arrived about 3:10pm, after lunch before dinner service, not a full menu available. I tried their pastrami sandwich which was really tasty and fries. Everything was good. Nothing blew my socks off though. Will be back to try dinner. Make your reservations ahead of time, the place is small, I thought it would be bigger. Some paid parking available along the street.

Food is 5 stars for flavors and presentation and the cocktails are quite tasty too. We had the potato fennel soup and Brussel sprouts to start. The soup had a surprising  kick and the sprouts had bite from the apple and acv that made them totally pop.

One of our entrees was the pork chop with seasonal veggies, a grilled peach and sausage bites. Each component on its own was a burst of flavor but when you put them all together it was a true flavor explosion. This sausage bits we amazing!

Our other entree was the half chicken with roasted potatoes, which also had great flavor and again when the components were eaten in one bite, the combination was fantastic. The sauces on both dishes did their job and brought the dishes together too.

For desert, we chose the profiteroles with seasonal fruit and ice cream and that was a great way to end the meal.

We may have caught them on an off night, but service was a bit slower than we prefer - was just over an hour from being seated to main course, but the food was worth the wait.

It was a clean restaurant too, but could use some sound baffling to make conversation a bit easier. We were seated in the center of the room and found it a bit noisy.

We will definitely be back again!

We got to the Oakland restaurant right before they opened for lunch and were greeted warmly by the staff. They gave us our choice of a table right by the window or a spot further inside the dining room. We picked the window, which turned out to be an awesome people-watching node while we looked over the lunch menu.

Our waiter was incredibly friendly and helpful. We ordered the pastrami sandwich and the hot pork sandwich, telling him we planned on splitting them. When we asked if they came with fries, he mentioned they usually come with coleslaw, but he kindly let us swap out one of the slaws so we could try the french fries too. A short time later, the kitchen went completely above and beyond—they brought our food out pre-split on four separate plates. Getting a perfect half-sandwich, fries, and slaw delivered right to each of us without us having to messily cut them at the table was a really kind, thoughtful touch of hospitality.

Starting with the sides, the fries came out piping hot, perfectly crisp, and well-seasoned. They tasted great with just standard ketchup.

As for the best pastrami sandwich in the East Bay contender? It completely delivered. The meat itself was deeply savory, perfectly cured, and piled high on a phenomenal, crusty baguette from La Farine bakery. The Dijon-horseradish dressing gave it a great, sharp kick that cut through the richness. It’s an absolute triumph and entirely worth the trip.

The hot pork sandwich, however, hit a weird bump (3/5 stars for this one). As I picked up my half, the first thing I noticed wasn't the sharp, bitter scent of broccoli rabe, but a strong smell of cooked spinach. When I took a bite, an overpowering spinach flavor totally took over the palate, completely masking the taste of the pork. My partner noticed the exact same thing. I opened up the baguette to check it out, and while there were a few actual pieces of broccoli rabe, the main culprit was a dark green, long, stringy mass. I ended up scraping most of it off. When I isolated the pulled pork by itself, it was actually delicious, tender, and beautifully seasoned, and the bread was excellent. But with that heavy cooked spinach smell and taste, I just can’t recommend the pork sandwich in its current state. It completely ruined the sandwich for me.

Overall, between the flawless service, and the great tavern atmosphere, Wood Tavern is easily one of the top places for a pastrami sandwich in Oakland.

Probably the best New American restaurant in the East Bay. Their steak never misses—perfectly cooked, delicious, and big portions. Rotating dinner menu (except steak and pork chops) and even the veggies included differ depending on what they have available. The scallops and risotto are always so good when it’s on the menu. Bonus: complimentary bread and butter.

It’s always packed and busy, even on weekdays. It’s been a local staple in the piedmont area. And it’s really the only new American restaurant that I find myself revisiting!

Wow, I didn't know this place was scheduled to close on December 31, 2026. I can remember eating here when they had a soft opening  years ago. Today I had a terrific lunch with a friend. Do try the charcuterie, so many yummy choices of cheese. Definitely add the duck, It was fantastic. Any of the sandage choices are great. The  seafood stew was superb. For dessert, we had the two scoops of ice cream/ gelato. I'm definitely going to try to squeeze in two more visits before they close. Definitely worth adding to your list if you've not been here.

top_reviews.content:
July 15, 2026

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

There are pizza nights, and then there are nights where the pizza gods themselves look down from the heavens, nod approvingly, and whisper, “Yeah… that’s the order.”

Today was one of those days.

I rolled in and ordered a 16-inch pepperoni pizza, two sides of ranch, and a pint of whatever magical liquid everyone else seems to order when they know more than I do. Sometimes the best strategy in life is trusting the professionals, and this establishment did not disappoint.

From the moment I walked in, the service was phenomenal.

The staff was friendly, welcoming, and genuinely happy to help. No attitude. No rushing. No feeling like you’re just another transaction. Just good people providing great service with the kind of effortless professionalism that makes everything feel easy.

And then the food arrived.

Let’s talk about that pizza.

Absolute top-tier.

The kind of pizza that makes you take a bite, pause for a second, and immediately start calculating how many slices you’re willing to share versus how many you’re secretly planning to protect with your life.

The pepperoni was on point.

The crust was exactly where it needed to be.

The cheese delivered that perfect combination of flavor, texture, and happiness that only great pizza can provide.

And the ranch?

Let’s just say there are dipping sauces, and then there are lifestyle choices. Those two sides of ranch were not merely condiments. They were valued members of the team.

Every bite felt like the kitchen genuinely cared about what they were sending out. There is a difference between food being made and food being crafted, and you can taste that difference immediately.

What impressed me most was how seamlessly everything came together.

Great food.

Great service.

Great atmosphere.

No drama.

No problems.

No complaints.

Just an experience that reminded me why people keep coming back.

In a world where excellence often gets overlooked, it’s worth recognizing places that consistently get it right. The team here clearly takes pride in what they do, and it shows in every interaction and every bite.

I arrived hungry.

I left happy.

And somewhere between slice number one and “I’ll save the rest for later” (a promise I absolutely did not keep), this place earned a loyal customer.

If you’re debating whether to stop by, stop debating.

Order the pizza.

Get the ranch.

Trust the process.

Your future self will thank you.

Five stars all day long. 🍕🏆

Love Philomena! The mushroom pizza and Miss piggy are delicious! But if you love pesto… there are some yum options, too.
I always keep a bottle of Phil ranch in the fridge and use it at home for all sorts of things.
Okay… and then there is the meat lasagna. I swear a little old grandma made that sauce. With cheese, garlicky toasty bread.
I usually want to eat the whole thing but try and put half in a box right away so I can savor it for lunch the next day.
They have great ice creams and gelatos with rotating flavors.
Tricia night every other Tuesday is a hit and so fun. I work as a teacher and we enjoy getting a group together every so often. It’s a great hang!

Philomena's is an absolute gem that delivers on every front!
The pizza, top tier, hands down! I ordered the Mushroom Pizza. It has persillade sauce and green onions. I added the Italian sausage, so good. Some of the best pizza ever!

Special shoutout to Rico and Kyle—these two are best in show! Their energy, kindness, and attention completely elevated the experience. It’s rare to encounter such genuine hospitality, and they made sure everything was spot-on from start to finish.

Whether you're there for the pizza, craft beer or just the atmosphere, you'll leave with a full belly and an even fuller spirit. Perfect therapeutic escape after a taxing day. Highly recommend!

Whether you just want easy takeout or a good hang with friendly locals, this is the spot. A super diverse menu for a pizza place, with seasonal veg dishes and some great desserts too. The pizza is SO good, and the wings are a go-to. Super neighborhoody vibe with exceptionally friendly staff, a superb beer selection that is constantly rotating and fresh, and excellent salads.

Plus sports! Catch a random weeknight Dubs game or spend the better part of a Sunday watching NFL and noshing on pizza and beer.

This isn't your chain pizza joint; it's a legit original, and you can tell the moment you walk in.

I normally don't leave bad reviews. So the fact that I'm bothering with this should go to stress how awful this pizza was.

A simple margherita. Shouldn't be hard to get it right, no? No char on the underside. No gluten development, crust is completely deflated. Mozzarella is overcooked and rubbery. Tomato sauce was flavorless. My partner had their mushroom pizza and it was just as bad. Both pizzas went into the trash before the third slice.

If this pizza wasn't cooked from frozen, I would be genuinely shocked. I guess that's why you're not allowed to modify the "house pizzas".

As some other reviewers pointed out, this seems to be a consistent problem with their delivery as opposed to their dine in. Which wouldn't be anywhere near as offensive if it wasn't for how overpriced the Pizza is for the quality. Imagine paying $42 for what might as well be a $10 Digiorno.

Papito in San Francisco is a cozy, welcoming spot with a menu that balances flavor, freshness, and creativity. The overall service was attentive and friendly, making the dining experience smooth from start to finish. The staff checked in often enough to make sure everything was good, but without being overbearing, which always makes a difference.
When it comes to the food, everything we tried was impressive. I had the Vegetariano, which was hearty, flavorful, and satisfying without being too heavy — a great choice for anyone looking for a tasty meat-free option. The chicken tacos were another favorite, perfectly seasoned and well-portioned, not greasy or overloaded with toppings. Their quesadillas stood out as well: they had the right amount of cheese and filling, balanced and not overly stuffed, which kept them delicious without feeling overwhelming.
The drinks complemented the food perfectly. The spicy mango drink had just the right kick of heat to balance the sweetness, making it super refreshing and unique. Along with a few beers, the overall mix kept the meal fun and flavorful.
Papito does a great job of keeping things authentic yet approachable, offering a dining experience that feels both elevated and casual. Between the good service, satisfying food, and unique drink options, it’s definitely a spot worth revisiting when craving Mexican food in the city

top_reviews.content:
If you're looking for an authentic Hong Kong–style breakfast, this is an excellent place to visit.

The wonton noodle soup was outstanding. The egg noodles had the perfect springy texture, just like you'd expect from a traditional Hong Kong noodle shop. The tea egg included with the set meal was also flavorful and perfectly cooked.

The breakfast set comes with your choice of coffee or milk tea. I chose the coffee, and it was rich, bold, and reminded me of the authentic local coffee I had in Malaysia.

Even the cucumber side dish was fresh, crisp, and well seasoned, making it a great complement to the meal.

The tables and decorations were also well organized and had a comfortable vibe. Overall, I think it is a great restaurant to visit if you’d like to try the Chinese cuisine. Note that there are limited options to whether you can adjust the ingredients of an item.

TL;DR: Legit Chinatown spot with great veggie options and serious allergy awareness. Service is on the slower side and there’s usually a line, but the food hits the spot.

Layer up for the walk because parking is non-existent.
Honestly, such a solid find in Chinatown! The vibe inside is super nice and they actually have a bunch of great options for vegetarians. Major shoutout to the staff for being so awesome with allergies too—I told them about a soy allergy and they were totally on it, recommending exactly what was safe to order.

We got the veggie dim sum, the chicken sweet corn soup, and a veggie hot and sour soup. Everything was seriously delicious.

The only catch? The service is definitely on island time. It's slow, there’s usually a line to get in, and the food takes a minute to roll out of the kitchen. Just be ready to wait a bit.

Also, trying to park in Chinatown is a total nightmare. Your best bet is to just park further away or take transit. Definitely layer up for the walk over, but honestly, cruising through Chinatown is half the fun anyway because the neighborhood is so gorgeous.

Would totally come back for the dim sum!

Hon’s Wun-Tun House is a classic Chinese comfort food spot in San Francisco, serving handmade dumplings and fresh noodles. I remember this was one of the first restaurants I visited when I first landed in San Francisco in 2024, so it brings back good memories.

Here are my thoughts on everything I tried:
Green onion pancakes: The best dish! No meat, just crispy pan-fried pancakes, but they’re incredibly addictive.
Beef brisket & beef tendon noodle soup: The broth was comforting. Honestly, the broth was everything for me.
Beef brisket over noodles: A pass. It was too oily and felt heavy.
BBQ pork: Yes! One of my favorites. So delicious.
Seafood XO sauce stir-fried vermicelli: It needed more seasoning. We ended up adding soy sauce, which helped.
Shanghai soup dumplings: Unfortunately, no. They were overcooked, and the soup leaked out as soon as I picked one up with my chopsticks (fyi, I know how to use chopsticks. I also know how to eat xiao long bao).
Pork & chive dumplings: To be honest, they seem to always overcook their dumplings (I visited a few times and they always overcooked it). Maybe it’s because they’re always busy? Even so, the filling still tasted okay.
Stir-fried baby bok choy with garlic sauce: It was okay. Nothing special, but a nice vegetable dish to balance out the meal.

Overall, the food was definitely hit or miss. Some dishes were excellent, while others could use some improvement. However it's always busy and has a waitlist. That said, this restaurant has always been, and will continue to be popular because of its legacy. And I’ll definitely come back for the memories.

top_reviews.content:
Visiting from out of town and went here with our SF friends who are locals. They couldn’t believe how good and how busy this place was.

I didn’t get a before pic but here’s the after lol

Chicken pesto pizza was great and the G-Mediterranean salad was fresh.

Great family, casual environment. Just a good ol pizza joint!

So good. Been eating here for 45+ years and it's just so good I keep coming back. Family run. Great staff. Great food. Good for kids and take out is super quick too. Two thumbs up! Oh, my favorite is the Giorgio's Special on regular crust (NY style and foldable) and antipasto salad. Great combo.
Been coming here since the 1990's and Giorgio's still has the same local feel and charm. The pizza and pasta never disappoint so we try to come by whenever we are in SF.
I live in Seattle. My stepdad has raved for years about this place from back when he lived in the SF area so I had to try it. Fantastic. I'm bringing him back a pie.

It’s been years since I last visited Giorgio’s Pizzeria, but I finally came back for lunch to meet a good friend, and I’m so glad I did. The decor has changed a bit, but the food still has that same heart and quality that made Giorgio’s an institution in San Francisco.

For those who don’t know, Giorgio’s has been around for decades. It started with the father and has now been passed down to the next generation, the sons and daughter still run the restaurant today, keeping it very much a family operation. You can feel that warmth the moment you walk in. They are the warmest family.

The pizza is still absolutely delicious. They’re generous with their toppings (no skimping here!) and what I love most is that they’ll let you do half-and-half, even on a small pizza, something most places won’t. Prices are also incredibly fair, especially for San Francisco. Honestly, I’d say they’re underrated and under charging with inflation.

We tried the shrimp appetizer in marinara sauce with crostini — so good — and a new salad they’re testing for their upcoming San Rafael location, which I heard is opening sometime before summer. I also had the chicken sausage penne pasta and one of their Everything and Corsican (veggie) half-and-half loaded with flavor. Everything tasted fresh, balanced, and made with care.

I got lucky and saw the family all there. It was nice to see the family working together, one of the siblings was making dough while the others ran the dining room. The crowd was a great mix of longtime locals and families, and it just felt… real.

They do takeouts and delivery through third party platforms but honestly, dining in has its own charm. Located right on Clement Street, Giorgio’s sits in one of the best pockets of the city — close to shops, Green Apple Books, and a few dessert spots for a post-pizza stroll.

If you grew up in San Francisco, you know Giorgio’s. And if you haven’t been yet, go. It’s one of those family-run places that reminds you why local spots matter. Just remember to feed the meter — it’s San Francisco, after all.

top_reviews.content: Stopped by Novy for lunch and had a fantastic meal! The food was delicious, and the service was refreshingly fast and attentive. It has a great, comfortable ambience that makes it a super easy spot to drop in for a quick bite or casual afternoon catch-up. Highly recommend!

We drove all the way back here from Burlingame because it is so good. I’ve spent a year all over Greece and this restaurant is one of the very few that actually rivals real Greek food. Incredible lamb burgers!

I love that this is a family-owned, women-owned local spot. That alone made me excited to try it. I met friends here for dinner and the whole experience was wonderful. The service was fantastic from start to finish and the food was truly delicious.

We ordered the seafood pasta and the pesto pasta, and both were perfectly portioned and full of flavor. Each dish felt thoughtfully prepared and very satisfying. We did not have time to try dessert since we were heading to a show, but I was happy to see they had a gluten free option on the menu, which gives me another reason to come back.

I will definitely be returning.

In the Noe Valley neighborhood of SF lies Novy, a fantastic modern Greek restaurant with a laid back vibe and delicious food. The surrounding area allows for decent parking options and the walk over no matter where you are is nice since the area itself is quaint. The interior is nice and modern although we opted to sit outside and enjoy the weather a bit. The staff was very friendly and on top of things, clearly making sure that we were happy and content with our food.

Speaking of food, it was great. We ordered appetizers of grilled halloumi and fried calamari, both of which were great but with the halloumi’s rich and savory flavor really standing out. After that we ordered the lamb bolognese, which again was fantastic. The thick noodles had a great chew and the bolognese was savory and had a great contrast to the feta sprinkled throughout. The portion was also pretty decent making sure we felt full by the time we left. We also ordered their flourless chocolate cake to go which we ate later and it was delicious. Overall, the meal was just great and the setting brought it up another notch. This is just a great restaurant flat out and we would say reckons a serious try if you’re in the surrounding area of SF.

During our visit to San Francisco last week, we celebrated New Year’s Eve with friends at NOVY in Noe Valley. This family-owned, woman-run Greek restaurant impressed us with its mix of traditional Greek cuisine and fresh California comfort food.

Arriving for Restaurant Week at 6:30 PM, we were promptly seated thanks to our reservation. The interior, though cozy, exudes a modern charm with creative touches like cheese grater lamps. The atmosphere was warm and inviting, perfect for our celebration.

Here’s what we enjoyed:
Appetizers:
•	Hummus: Creamy and flavorful, paired with fresh pita bread.
•	Fried Calamari: Lightly battered and complemented by yellow onion, tarragon, and a spicy aioli.
•	Fried Brussels Sprouts: Crispy with a delicious mix of bacon, mizithra cheese, and chili flakes.
Entrees:
•	Moussaka: A standout! Crispy on top, with rich layers of beef and eggplant, it was perfectly executed.
•	Pesto Pasta: Bucatini with tender Mary’s chicken, smoky bacon, kale, and a creamy pesto-gorgonzola sauce—a hearty and satisfying dish.
•	Chicken Apple Walnut Salad: Grilled curried chicken breast paired with crisp green apple slices, toasted walnuts, and a house-made honey mustard dressing. Fresh and flavorful.
•	Chicken Wrap: Packed with Mary’s chicken, lettuce, tomato, pickled onion, tzatziki, and salsa—a perfect balance of freshness and zest.
Desserts:
•	Galaktoboureko: Flaky and decadent, with a delightful berry sauce that tied it all together.
•	Brioche Bread Pudding: Warm and comforting, topped with vanilla ice cream and caramel.
•	Flourless Chocolate Cake: Rich, smooth, and topped with a luscious chocolate ganache.

The service was excellent—efficient and friendly, with dishes arriving quickly despite the busy evening.

NOVY offers a polished yet relaxed dining experience that’s great for fans of Greek and Mediterranean cuisine. With its rich history and thoughtful touches, it’s a must-visit spot in Noe Valley. Highly recommended!

Everything was soooo good. We came at 10pm and it closes at 11pm so it was perfect! The service was so quick and everyone was so nice and welcoming. top_reviews.content:
Dimond Slice is one of those neighborhood spots that just gets it right. Fully vegetarian and vegan, counter service on MacArthur, nothing fussy, and the pizza is genuinely great.

We got the Yukon gold potato pie, roasted potatoes, red onions, mozzarella, pepper jack, cilantro, and a garlic olive oil base. Sounds like a lot, tastes like someone actually thought it through. Crust had a good chew, cheese pull for days, and it didn't sit heavy the way a lot of pizza does. My kids demolished a couple slices before I could grab a second.

What I liked just as much is the vibe. There's a big chalkboard wall where kids can draw, and ours went straight for it and stayed busy the whole meal. Framed food photos everywhere, a couple TVs, plants in the window. Feels lived in, not staged.

They do a lot for different diets without making a thing of it. Gluten-free crust, vegan cashew cheese, salads with organic greens. If you've got a mixed group where someone can't eat this or that, this is an easy call. And the fact that the whole menu is meat-free means nobody has to ask twice.

Staff were friendly and quick, the pies came out hot, and it was reasonably priced for what you get. We'll be back. If you're anywhere near Dimond, go.

Not only was the pizza superb, but the service was outstanding as well. There was a lady there named Lily M. (I think), and she was incredibly friendly and welcoming. I really love this place! They sometimes have great specials, which is an added bonus. I’ll definitely be back, and I highly recommend giving this place a try.

Mili L. (sorry if I got the name wrong) provided excellent service and was incredibly friendly. I also noticed how warm and welcoming she was with another customer, which really stood out to me.

Both pizzas were outstanding. The flavors were in perfect harmony—like yin and yang—with neither overpowering the other. I also recommend keeping an eye out for their daily specials, as they sometimes have some great deals.

I absolutely loved the pizza and the exceptional service, and I will definitely be ordering again. What impressed me most was that Mili seemed genuinely kind and caring, not just polite because it was her job. I really appreciate that kind of authenticity.

Ok, so don't judge the book/pizza place by the cover/storefront.  It doesn't look like a fancy place, but the pizzas sure are.  Delicious vegetarian pizzas that you only get one choice of.  Yep, they only make one type of pizza per day.  Don't like it, well, I guess you're going somewhere else.  Because of this, they are able to pump out the pizza with consistency and have it ready for you in a few minutes when you order.  They do some really interesting combinations too.  Ever put corn or potatoes on your pizza?  They do!  As stated the place isn't fancy, but at least they have a huge chalk board wall that you can doodle and leave your message on.  Also get the green sauce!  It's a little spicy but delicious to dip your crust into!

Dimond Slice is one of Oakland's true gems. The pizza is outstanding (which I didn’t expect for a vegetarian pizza place) Great crust and yummy toppings! Make sure to try it with their green sauce. But I have to say even with the consistently good pizza, where they really shine is in their customer service and community that they have developed. From the first time I walked in they made me feel like family.  They always remember my family’s special dietary needs and ask about us with genuine interest. They have become our Friday tradition, and we rarely miss. Give them a try and you will find out for yourselves!

top_reviews.content:
The khaman was a big dhokla piece served with chili thecha. The thecha was really spicy but didn't taste fresh — it was red and felt packaged. The dhokla itself was fluffy and fresh. Overall pretty average, not something we'd order again.

The dahi vada was great — something different. Very crispy and crunchy, with lots of good dahi, green chutney, and tamarind chutney. We liked it so much we ordered two portions.

The dal makhani was the best thing we had all night — amazing. Not your typical Delhi-style dal makhani but in a good way; it had a really nice garlic tempering and was very flavorful and rich.

Loved the paratha — fresh and flaky. The cheese garlic naan was a little over the top with all the mozzarella (not really my thing), but it was good and went well with the dal makhani.

The one real letdown was the service. The waiters kept rushing to clear our plates — we had to tell them multiple times that we were still eating and working on our food, and they kept coming back asking to take plates. At the end of the night, when we asked to split the bill in a way other than 50/50, they first said they could only split it in half and were reluctant to accommodate us — though they eventually did. The service could definitely have been better.

The food has standout moments — the dahi vada and dal makhani are the ones to order.

Awesome food. Great ambience. We especially loved the masala mushrooms, undhiyu pie & vindaloo koftas. The dal makhani was one of best we ever tasted. The platter of pickles was novel & delicious. Cucumber gimlet was super refreshing. A must try.

My parents were in town for the weekend of Diwali and we figured we would finally try out Besharam after months of wanting to. They had a special menu which we didn't order from BUT even with a smaller a la cart menu, we had an amazing time.

The service is great, with the right amount of both follow-up and space. Its a little bit pricey but honestly, some of the uniqueness is worth it. The vibe is also very new yet old at the same time, and I found myself picking out plenty of pieces of decor that I know my grandma has, or that I know we used growing up which was a nice touch. Plus, plenty of parking.

Now the food.
They have a decent wine selection and we had a few cocktails that were very tasty but back to the food.

The drunken pani puri is a refreshing start and the puris were SO crunchy! I also added on the candy Karela which somehow is my dad's favorite vegetable and if it was made like this growing up, I also would agree, another winner.

We also had the Vindaloo Koftas, Dal Makhani, Maska Paneer and a cheesy garlic naan. Everything was very tasty and had a slightly different approach to dishes you've eaten before.

I know the menu changes so I cannot wait to go back and try more food that as a fellow Gujju, brings back memories and also let's me make new ones!

Excellent food, amazing service (our server Jake was amazing and took great care of us!) this is one we keep coming back to every couple months.  Definitely get the dahi wada and saag paneer if those are on your menu. I also like the pani puri, khichu, undhiyu wellington, dhokli, ringan oro, shrikhand cheesecake, carrot halwa. garlic naan is worth trying once but it’s too heavy for my liking, I prefer the paratha. cocktails are interesting too! chai is great.

Was super excited about dining here as they’ve had good reviews and a great story. The atmosphere is industrial chic and service was good, but the food was a let down. Nothing adventurous or exciting and pricey for what it is. Flavours seem muted by design to appeal to a certain taste but comes out just mid. Biggest let down is that the “pickle” aren’t actually pickles but just pickled chutney which at $5 a pop or $16 for four is a huge rip off. The cheeses garlic naan was the best dish. Everything else was kind of forgettable.

I had never eaten Indian food before, but my buddies showed me how to properly eat it. The Naan, along with the Rice, and the Chicken Tikka Masala: it was an explosion of flavors! It felt like an experience in my mouth, that could have only been compared to an energetic music festival. I HIGHLY recommend this place, to ANYONE: residents of SF, or just some dudes that spent the night there for fun, who are looking for food that will leave their tongues buzzed with flavor, their stomachs full with warmth, and their senses pleased beyond what they could have ever dreamed of!

Ate there May 5th 2025 (yesterday/night time)

So originally i was supposed to have a date here and the girl flaked on me, i ended up eating alone.

Before i came here i read some of the reviews saw some pics of the food and it seemed good. I was already interested in this place. Started talkin to a girl and tells me she down to go eat and i tell her about this place, tell me she's been here before and she like the place. I get there wait outside for some minutes no replies. Finally head inside and it's a 40minute wait for a table and i was already 100% sure i was eating alone. I had already decided to stick around cuz i was hungry anyways.

Im tellin this story for a reason, so anyways i got chilaquiles rojos and hell yeah they still serve eggs at night. The food was really good. The vegtables went really good with the main food. The beans were really good too. Finished it all and the food made me feel satisfied. They ended up givin me a free beer. Anyways yeah i highly recommend this place
I dont live in California and if you ever around Oakland you should check it out. Im in the area cuz of my job.

Will be back to try out other things.
Absolutely the best Mexican food in Oakland while visiting! Juan was so nice and I tried their Chile Rellano shrimp plate! Just wow like better than LA tbh!

Food here was a 6.5 not great but decent enough to comeback and try something different. Portion were ok except for the side dishes very small and over priced. Spent over $65 for 2 meals chips, salsa and guacamole.  Too expensive for non authentic Mexican food that you can find  better at a food truck for cheaper.

The dining experience at this restaurant was highly enjoyable. The food was fresh, well-prepared, and served in generous portions, making it both satisfying and good value. Each dish was thoughtfully presented, reflecting attention to detail in both preparation and plating. The overall quality of the food was consistently strong, with flavors that were well-balanced and appealing. The combination of freshness, portion size, and presentation creates a dining experience that feels both polished and approachable. This restaurant is a great option for those seeking a reliable and enjoyable meal, whether for a casual outing or a more intentional dining experience. We would gladly return and recommend it to others looking for quality food and a pleasant atmosphere.

I love this place! My parents and I have dined here multiple times and we always have a fantastic time! The service is amazing and the food is always delicious! I highly recommend ordering the molcajete and the quesabirrias - both are amazing!

Fried shrimp - 5/5 crunchy umami,  salty and sweet, creamy, not too oily, perfect with the dip! Highly recommend

We had a great meal and service at Sai’s. Our waiter was extremely friendly and made the dinner we had a truly special experience. He said he has worked at the restaurant for over 40 years (I think he and/or his family owns the restaurant). Their 5 spice chicken banh mi was truly delicious (we forgot to take a picture before we dug into it. So the picture is after we took a few bites). The bread is nice and crispy and the filling was very tasty. We also loved beef tenderloin pho. We also came back a couple of days later and once again our experience was great. I highly recommend Sai’s for a great meal and great service.

All 5s. Best Vietnamese food I’ve had ever I think. Clams were incredible in one of the best ginger bay leaf lemongrass broths imaginable. Succulent fish and squid in a wonderful seafood broth that made my taste buds quiver in relishment. Not a word no problem. Lastly, I had the clay pot. Describing the clay pot with shiitake mushrooms and tender chicken and perfectly cooked shrimp is impossible. The rice was crispy to the ideal point while the chicken and shrimp combined in land and sea pandemonium. Mmmmmm! Recommend!

Walked in during the final quarter of the NBA WCF game 7 and was able to get a table in front of the TVs. Owner was very nice and welcoming. Saw he greeted a lot of customers on their way out. Seems like there are many returning customers. The interior was clean and nice. Food was great. Love that they have us free hot tea as we felt pretty cold during that day. Love that we were able to watch the game with great warm vibes after a long day.

The best Pho Bo so far! Very nice brouth! Also there are many sauce bottles on the table, ypu can add them to make your Pho more special. I made mine more spicy. My husband ordered curry with lamb, it was awesome! Very deep and correct flavors. I wish you could add Tom Yum in menu, I've never tried a good Tom Yum in United States, to be honest. Neither in SF, nor in NYC or Sacramento. Maybe you could make the best one, since you're so skilled with soups! We will definitely come back.

top_reviews.content: Food was quick in a busy night. Everything was delicious and the wait staff was on point. I had the spicy pork bbq and it’s totally worth it! The projector above was playing very funny k pop videos. If you are in the area late night, you should swing by.

Great spot if looking for dinner late, everything was fresh, quickly served and reasonably priced. Good intimate vibe for groups and good service. Everything had a good taste but my favorite was definitely spicy chicken with cheese, bibimbap and the corn cheese

If you’re a Korean restaurant that cannot tell the difference between gyeranjjim and gyeranmari, between galbitang and ttarogukbap, then chances are you are catering to clueless K-Pop fans.
Food taste: The guk in the yukkejang and the ttarogukbap tasted the same and worse, suspiciously like it was made with ramen soup bases. Btw, the manager sent the waiter who had made a mistake (they brought galbitang instead of the ttarogukba we ordered) to suggest to us that they would spice up the galbitang to make it ttarogukbap...!!! That seems consistent with stuff tasting the same.
How do you like your eggs: We asked if they had steamed egg because this is a standard item (and because it was not listed in the menu). The waiter said they did and pointed to an item listed as “a big omelette”. I  wondered and they insisted . And then they plunked a dish of gyeran mari on the table. Oookay. But if I want my gyeran jjim that has been converted to a gyeran mari smothered in ketchup and cheese, then I will find my way to a proper Japanese joint. Leftovers - no thanks.
Banchan: Please check the banchan before you hit up a Korean restaurant. If you see measly excuses for banchan, the food cannot be far behind. We lowered our expectations after the banchan came out. That is not kimchi. It’s not about the kimchi being old or sour (although Korean restaurants worth their salt, especially in big cities will get you fresh kimchi) - this was watery and looked like it has been washed. If you are not getting a basic like kimchi right, then…But seriously, this is just an insult to Korean cuisine.The quantities are also consistent with how the managers are cuttings corners to cut cost - three kinds with a tablespoon each.
Ambience: The worst thing in the place is the noise level. You will sit cheek to jowl with what, after about 3 minutes, will feel like a bunch of howler monkeys on market day!  It felt great to conclude the meal in more ways than one.
Conclusion: We made a valiant effort with the food. A successful meal is when the rice and guk disappear.  Clearly not in this case. No worries Zzan, you do you and the K-Pop teeny boppers will go home feeling like they have scored authentic Korean food. But if you care and want to call yourself Korean, at least get your kimchi right. How hard would that be?

We have visited numerous Korean restaurants along the West Coast, including those in Hawaii. However, this was the first time we were disappointed by the food at a Korean restaurant. We ordered the SF special, cold noodles in kimchi broth, SF seafood soup in tang, and a deep fried noodle in seaweed. The cold noodles has the cube ice not shaved, the soup was bland and seemed like it was just water, and the seafood soup had little flavor. giving 2 rating  since the fried noodle was good!

The food was good, which is why we decided to come back a second night.

Last night, the service wasn’t great, but we decided to give the restaurant another chance because we really enjoyed the food. Unfortunately, tonight’s experience was even worse.

Halfway through eating my ramen, I found a strand of hair tangled in my noodles. I showed it to one of the staff members, he showed it to the lady. And the lady came and  took my bowl away. Naturally, I assumed they were making me a new one, so I waited.

After quite a while, I had to ask what was happening. That’s when I was told they had simply removed the ramen from my bill because the kitchen had already closed and couldn’t make another bowl.

I completely understand that the kitchen was closed. I wasn’t expecting the impossible. What disappointed me was that no one communicated this to me when they took my bowl away, and the lady did not even apologised. I was left sitting there hungry, waiting for food that was never coming.

I’m not someone who usually leaves negative reviews. I work in the food service industry myself, so I understand that mistakes happen. Finding a hair in food can happen anywhere. What matters is how the situation is handled, and unfortunately, this was handled very poorly.

The male staff member was polite, but the female staff member/ boss came across as dismissive and unfriendly throughout our visit, which made the experience even more unpleasant.

The food is 7/10 , but good food alone doesn’t make up for poor customer service. I hope the restaurant takes customer communication more seriously in the future. Please. 🙏🏻

Been here a few times and I love the atmosphere, but the food quality seems to be going down. The roti canai is made fresh, yet it was cold when it comes to my table and the dip wasn't even warm. The food was very good! My daughter keeps on asking when we'll go back, the atmosphere was nice and the service was pretty good. Their green curry is amazing and the restaurant is pretty big. I would 100% recommend it for your next family dinner!

top_reviews.content: One of the best cheesesteak sandwiches I have ever had in my life! It was delicious! Their garlic fries are amazing too. Customer service was great. The staff was friendly and attentive. I definitely recommend this place. It's a great little restaurant with big sandwiches.

Casual neighborhood walk-up counter right across the street from Molinari's on Broadway. Staff is chill, food is hot and tasty, no question why they're voted Best Cheesesteak in CA. Outside seating lets you enjoy the food and the pulse of the neighborhood with a view of the back end of Chinatown. Hands down my favorite spot and just about a mile up Broadway from Pier 9 for the tourists.
Also have to say that the garlic fries are fantastic and heartburn-free for me

Day and night, Buster’s is the spot for a Philly Cheesesteak in San Francisco. I ordered the Phillapeno for that extra kick. Shoutout to Danny for holding it down and helping me out with the sauce selection. The honey garlic was bussin, but Danny said it’s better on the chicken sandwich. I def wanna go back to try it next time. Overall a super friendly vibe inside to eat by the window and people watch. The outside section is smooth as well to enjoy on a sunny day. Buster’s Cheese Steak is a certified San Francisco Classic.

Very cool spot! Stopped by with one of my friends, and we were not disappointed. The sandwiches were very well cooked, and the sauce added exquisite flavor. Would highly recommend to anybody in the area!

If you’re anywhere nearby, you HAVE to come here. Every time we’re traveling through the area, we end up stopping for lunch or dinner because it’s become a must for us. The cheesesteaks are absolutely amazing, huge portions, and everything tastes incredible.

But honestly, the best part of the place is the people. Chris, who takes care of customers, is one of the nicest and friendliest guys you’ll meet, always welcoming and making everyone feel at home. And Jose is an absolute legend. The guy works nonstop, but somehow he’s always smiling and in a great mood. You can tell how hardworking he is, and it really makes the whole place special.

Seriously, you’re going to love it. Great food, great people, and an awesome atmosphere. Highly recommend.

top_reviews.content: Ordering experience was awkward because the ordering kiosk is hidden. Strawberry matcha latte was yummy. We also ordered the salmon bento and the hayashi rice. The salmon was quite unseasoned and the hayashi rice was more like a tomato stew than a gravy dish. I heard the tofu bowl is good though so I will try that one next time.

Like this spot for it’s intimate feel. Getting there in the middle of the day teleports you to a twilight zone with warm lights on and slow vibes. I liked my avocado toast. It was loaded with salmon, cream cheese and greens. The presentation was great too. My friend tried the salad and also liked it. The service was fast and we got a seat without wait during the lunch break. Overall it’s a decent place for a lunch with a friend near downtown
Their matcha is really good and unsweetened! The avocado toast has the perfect crispy texture and a nice flavor combination. I'd give it one more star if there were more food options for breakfast.

Food was very good for the most part. Thought the cod was a bit bland. The fried chicken was delicious and light, black sesame dessert was a hit and rigatoni with smoked salmon was cooked perfectly and way more delicious than you might think! Also had some of the duck and it had a great flavor to it.

Overall a fantastic meal only issues were with pacing of the plates. We sat an ordered drinks then food a few minutes later with the fried chicken supplement. Less than 10 minutes later we get the fried chicken before anything else. We did say "as it's prepared" but figured it would come after the salad. From there it was a good 40 minute wait (about an hour after we sat down) before the salads came. Rest of the food was paced fine just a weird start.

They were also out of several things, which happens but was a bit of a let down.

Would definitely come again as it was way more good than bad! Space is super cool!

I’ve had Cassava on my want to go list for some time, so when we stopped in on Friday and they had a table without reservations, we were very excited.
We decided to try to $118 tasting menu because it was suppose to be a James Beard finalist and you normally put your best dishes on a tasting menu like that.
The menu was generally very disappointing,  seemingly without any cohesion or theme. The asparagus appetizer was fine, but the crab and pea over toast was so bland that it kind of ruined the crab for me. The fish & lamb were fine but nothing special. Overall, it felt like a new chef trying their hand at a set menu, but didn’t really know what they were going for.
They also seemed to forget about us between the 2nd and 3rd course. It took over 2.5 hours to receive and eat 5 course! The server was super friendly though, so overall I still give the service 3 stars. They did remove the price of our tea ($14 total) from the final price, but they charged a 5% SF mandate and a mandatory 20% gratuity, so overall it was still over $300 for 2 people.
I wouldn’t come back again after that, which is a shame because it seems like their regular menu is pretty decent. For this price, there are many places in the city that’s much better.

top_reviews.content: I visited this restaurant specifically to try the octopus, but unfortunately, it didn’t live up to my expectations. However, I was thoroughly impressed by the rest of the food. The lively and inviting atmosphere, coupled with the incredibly friendly and attentive servers, made for a pleasant dining experience. My favorite dishes were the Kayseri Manti and the Arayes Kebab.

Wow, what a treat! This place is absolutely amazing. The location and the ambiance is difficult to compete... In the middle of Presidio, this fantastic parc. The. The food is just exceptional. I love middle eastern food, but I must say I was so impressed but those dishes I never experienced before. And of course the staff was really nice. We had a wonderful time for our family celebration.

Excellent date-night spot near the Presidio. We walked in early and sat at the bar, which ended up being perfect. The staff made us feel genuinely welcome as visitors from Brazil, and Mars took excellent care of us. She explained the whole menu from memory, gave thoughtful recommendations, and made ordering much easier.

We were looking for a lighter, lower-carb dinner and the menu worked really well for that. The octopus was a perfect starter, especially with the excellent in-house salt crackers. The oysters were fresh and beautifully served, and the duck dolma was memorable. Everything felt thoughtful, flavorful, and easy to share.

The room is beautiful without feeling overly formal, the service was great, and we finished with a very good espresso at the end. Walking back through the Presidio afterward made the night even better. Highly recommended.

Went for brunch, sat by the kitchen table. Delightful food - the pita and dips were amazing (always a fan of the muhammara and smoked yogurt), fluffy and amazing pita, great egg dishes also. Staff was warm and friendly - the chef let us try a gazpacho from the dinner tasting menu (so fresh and seasonal and every ingredient came through). Ended with a great dessert that was like a very elevated s'more.

I've also previously been here for dinner, and dinner here is even better! Such an amazing set of flavors, great seasonal ingredients, and so much care into every dish!

Presidio’s hidden gem for Modern Mediterranean dining
Dalida exceeded every expectation for our date night. The mezze spread, fresh bread, hummus, yogurt and olive spreads. set the tone perfectly, followed by a stunning octopus carpaccio and melt-in-your-mouth lamb chops over hummus with fragrant saffron rice.
The cocktails are creative and refined, don’t skip the Fig Negroni or the Saturnalia. We finished with a layered baklava and goat cheese ice cream that was simply perfect.
The open kitchen makes the whole experience feel alive and dynamic. If you’re looking for a memorable date night or special occasion restaurant in San Francisco, Dalida is the answer. Highly recommend!​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

top_reviews.content:
Located in the historic Dogpatch neighborhood, Moshi Moshi is one of my favorite restaurants in all San Francisco! Decorated with a rotating selection of artwork and serviced by kind, accommodating and friendly staff, the eating environment here is very desirable.

But the star of the show is the food. Moshi Moshi has an extensive menu with many great Japanese-inspired items! Every last detail is thought of on each dish. The fish used is never anything but extremely fresh. The rice is prepared perfectly each time, and the dishes all come out looking and tasting perfect without fail. The menu covers traditional favorites (like the tekka or negi hama maki) and cool modern creations (like the fire lizard or Akasaka nights roll).

The menu has so many cool options; I have tried much of the menu and liked pretty much everything. I love the sushi and sashimi here (the fish is just so high quality and fresh), but they have great teriyaki bowls, udon, and tonkatsu as well. I think you should try the teriyaki beef or the Tokyo kara age udon meals.

I like to come here often because it is a place beloved by friends and me, and I almost always start my meal with a nice warm miso soup. Moshi Moshi makes great miso soup (yet another detail that has not been overlooked).

I recommend you try it! The food, service, and ambiance are top-notch.

Moshi Moshi is a 38 years old legacy sushi place in Dogpatch SF. We tried a bunch of stuff and some were hits, some misses.
- Bacon wrapped mochi: We started with this. Honestly didn’t like it. Just fat and greasy, felt a bit heavy to start the meal.
- Hamachi Bomb:  Best dish of the night. There were 2 pieces only, but flavorful. The hamachi was wrapped around rice with yuzu.
- Rainbow Spider roll: A special, monster size roll. It’s got tempura soft shell crab, avocado, and cucumber then topped with a ton of sashimi and unagi sauce. Super filling.
- Red Dragon roll: Solid if you like spicy tuna and salmon. A bit sour idk why
- Haleakala Maki: My 2nd favorite. Albacore poke with the ogo seaweed and red clay salt had such a unique flavor, then top with torched albacore and spicy garlic oil. Honestly, 10/10.
For drink, I had the El Fuego de Japan. It’s margarita with jalapeño tequila and yuzu, I didn't impress much.

I've been into Moshi Moshi a few times now and I've always enjoyed my meals. There is excellent variety, fun cocktails, and the staff is always so friendly and accommodating. The bartenders are very attentive and friendly !

Solid neighborhood Japanese, with a little something for everybody — a wide selection of hot and cold appetizers, nigiri, rolls, noodle soups and classic entrees. Though maybe not a culinary destination, a fashionable local option frequented by Dogpatch regulars. Outdoor patio seating. Dog-friendly, inside and out.

Soft Shell Crab Katsu, crunchy breadcrumb deep fry served with Japanese tartar sauce — satisfying comfort. Squash Blossom Tempura — a novel seasonal specialty, the batter, more beer batter. Shrimp Dumplings — top choice. Hamachi Kama, chargrilled yellowtail collar — excellent. Chicken Udon — solid delivery.

Sun Dragon Roll, though good, the shrimp tempura batter was not as lightly crisp as hoped, the rice slightly densely packed. Inari with Wasabi special — clever and sweet. Selection of nigiri sushi, does the trick, but not life-changing.

Great as a small dish izakaya, with Japanese whiskey flights a novelty.

Would go again for sure. Touch pricey. Great service. Everything so tasty, great Cocktails. Birds and bees and hibiscus marg great, plum drop and rhubarb zinger good. Great appetizers, got the gyoza (if order again ask to make it crispy), piri ten calamari n green beans was bomb, grilled lamb chops so tasty, salmon sashimi was like butter. years and it has always been consistently awesome. ALWAYS.

Tigger shrimp ravioli is unforgettable. Rabbit ravioli is occasionally on the menu, as well, and is also delicious for a starter.

Entrees are all excellent- portions are good.

Great date place- a bit of a hideout.

I discovered L’Ardoise Bistro years ago on a crisp December evening. As I approached, the lighted tree in the window caught the part of me that loves a little romance, intimacy, storybook charm, and the kind of magic that happens when a space makes you feel both transported and completely at home. It has been more than a favorite restaurant ever since.

Dinner at L’Ardoise is one of the best ways I know to show buyer clients what living in Duboce Triangle can feel like, because words only get you so far. The restaurant somehow brings together everything I love about the neighborhood: intimacy, warmth, lack of pretension, quiet sophistication, and, especially in December, enchantment.

I often bring fellow real estate agents to L’Ardoise for dinner because there’s something fitting about discussing business inside a place that demonstrates what doing good business looks like. There are no declarations about service or hospitality on the wall. They just do it, consistently, through the food, the pacing, the atmosphere, and the way the entire experience holds together.

The kitchen’s execution is flawless every time. The coq au vin is deeply savory, wine-rich, and comforting, with the kind of depth that comes from patient, slow cooking; the Tiger prawn ravioli is decadent without being heavy; and the caramelized Apple Tarte Tatin is the perfect finish.

L’Ardoise is so special to me that I take myself there for dinner every year on my birthday.

It captures something timeless and soulful about San Francisco that is increasingly hard to manufacture and impossible to fake.

Absolutely fantastic experience! This was one of the best French restaurants I’ve been to. Every dish was outstanding from the soup and salad to the perfectly cooked steak and creamy risotto. We also ordered the chef’s special of the day, a puff pastry filled with lobster and shrimp, based on our waiter’s recommendation, and it was incredible. Everything was flavorful, fresh, and beautifully prepared.

The service was exceptional as well. Our waiter was attentive, knowledgeable, and his recommendation ended up being the highlight of the meal. The restaurant itself has a beautiful atmosphere that’s elegant yet comfortable, making it a perfect spot for a date night.

One piece of advice: definitely make a reservation before you go, as it’s a popular place. Highly recommended, and I’ll certainly be coming back!

top_reviews.content: Five stars. My son and I had the Omakase experience at Akiko's in San Francisco, and it was hands down the best sushi we've ever had. Every course was beautifully presented, incredibly fresh, and packed with flavors that exceeded our expectations. The chefs' attention to detail and craftsmanship were evident in every bite. The service was equally outstanding, warm, attentive, and perfectly paced from start to finish. The entire evening felt like a true culinary experience rather than just dinner. If you're looking for an unforgettable Omakase in San Francisco, Akiko's is absolutely worth it. Five stars. We can't wait to come back.

One of the most overpriced omakase places we’ve tried. The starting courses were okay but the nigiri lacked creativity and flavor(over sauced, sushi rice was plain, and when we asked for a little more wasabi the chef put too much to the point where we teared up). Also the chef never tried to make conversation with us, just told us the piece of fish which we could’ve just read off the menu, and she had an annoyed face the whole meal. The only dishes that stood out was the tuna and caviar over milk bread and the scallop dish. At $270 per person and we ordered 4 cocktails between my wife and I we spent over $800 total and we left hungry.

Akiko’s Restaurant is a solid omakase spot that I’ve visited twice—once at the bar and once seated at a table—and the experience does vary depending on where you sit.

The bar seating clearly stands out. Portions felt more generous, and the personal interaction with the chef made a noticeable difference. Watching each nigiri being prepared and served directly to you adds warmth and intention that elevates the meal. The table seating is more comfortable, especially for a longer dinner, but the experience feels slightly less engaging.

Some of the nigiri were truly outstanding. The coffee-cured bluefin and the chocolate-cured ocean trout were both memorable and creative without being gimmicky. The toro tuna belly was also excellent—rich, clean, and perfectly balanced.

Same-day reservations were possible on both visits, which is a big plus for an omakase of this caliber in San Francisco. Overall, Akiko’s offers high-quality sushi and a reliable experience, with the bar seating being the way to go if you want the best version of the omakase.

We had such a great experience, from the moment we walked in to when we left. We were greeted warmly when we entered, and the hostess acknowledged the special occasion we were celebrating, which was such a nice touch. We were seated exactly where we had requested, had our coats checked, and sat down at the bar where our menus were already waiting. The menu even included a note recognizing our celebration, which really made us feel welcomed.

The set omakase was excellent. We loved it all but particularly enjoyed their signature dish,and the coffee cured nigiri as well as the chocolate one. Every course was beautifully presented and tasted amazing. Our meal was well paced. The staff were friendly, knowledgeable, and easy to talk to. We also added a few pieces from the regular menu and those were just as good. The ice cream dessert was the perfect end to the meal.

What stood out as well was the service. The staff were attentive without hovering and clearly very experienced. It felt relaxed, polished, and genuinely welcoming.

Highly recommend Akiko’s if you are looking for incredible sushi and thoughtful service.

We did the Valentine’s Day set menu. The first half was a mix of different fish dishes and two of the 6 items were great. The others I could have done without. Then we had 6 different nigiris and all were amazing.

Delicious but somewhat expensive burgers in the Gourmet Ghetto that is in North Berkeley.  Barneys is a small chain of hamburger restaurants that are primarily in the Oakland Berkeley area. We didn't know, but now we do.

For perspective, a Barneys burger costs $17.50, but it's a really good burger. Burgers are cooked to order with very good quality beef. Fries, onion rings, and other sides are ordered separately. Whereas the burgers were excellent, the onion rings and fried vegetables (their version of tempura) were on the oily side. Keep this in mind.

Their menu is expansive, and they offer salads and other items. We stuck to the burgers.

Service is friendly and efficient. Parking can be challenging, but there are metered spaces about a block away near Safeway.

The restaurant is clean and well maintained. The shiny sign out front gives a slight indication of the pride they take in the establishment... or maybe we're just being too generous.

In any case, on a nice day, try to snag a table on the patio and bite into a juicy, well crafted burger..all  while soaking in the liberal elite vibe of North Berkeley  It's a nice experience.

The complimentary chips and salsa were lovely and a great into to the main courses; I got two of their fish tacos, which were quite tasty. top_reviews.content:
Alrighty so honest review time. Ive eaten before at pakistani places and back home too many times as i go for few months each year.

We came in. Nice establishment restaurant away from tenderloin side. Quran was playing and not music so thats a plus there. Menu was missing some usual stuff on there like haleem and nihari but luckily haleem was there today to order. Ordered haleem, 2 naans and 2 tikka legs.

After getting our food. First thing we noticed were the chicken legs were very small.  No wonder 2 legs came in one order but compared to other restaursnts the legs were much smaller.  They were marinated well though.

Second thing which was a shocker was the naans. They were not the usual size, they were deep naans warmed up on a tawa like stove. The deep naans you can buy frozen from any desi grocery store for 2.49 for pack of 5, they are giving you a single naan piece here for $2 each. A restaurant should atleast have a tandoor to make naans with fresh. I understand this place used to be a foodtruck, deep naans would be fine there but at a restaurant with a kitchen- deep naans is highly disappointing to say the least.

The haleem was heavy on black peoper and masala, and had more of a channe daal texture/taste than a haleem. Honestly $20 for haleem is a bit too much. Regular price is about $15-16 as well.

Chai when asked was only masala chai no regular doodh patti one.

Seating was ample and decor inside was good. Staff was friendly but food dissapointed. I hope they can improve, get bigger chicken leg quarter (try restaurant depot), for naans please get a tandoor and make them like regular traditional tandoori naans . And for haleem make it more haleem like and less daal like.  Go check out pakwan as an example for naans and haleem

I visited MashaAllah Halal Pakistani Food Restaurant with my friend, and we ordered their lunch special. The food was absolutely delicious, fresh, and full of authentic flavor. Everything we tried was super yummy, and the portions were generous. What made our visit even more special was the wonderful service. The lady was incredibly kind, welcoming, and attentive, making us feel right at home. Her warm hospitality truly stood out and added so much to our experience. I highly recommend MashaAllah Halal Pakistani Food Restaurant to anyone looking for great halal Pakistani food and excellent customer service. We will definitely be coming back inshallah!
