July 2026 Update: Returning to the Benchmark

Five years after our foundational visit, we returned to Quince yesterday to see how the benchmark holds up in 2026. The short answer: it remains an undisputed titan of fine dining, elevated even further by its stunningly reimagined physical space.

The Legend, Revisited: In my original review, I noted that I still dreamed about the caviar, panna cotta, and brioche canvas. To return yesterday and experience its evolution—an absolute masterpiece of geometric precision balancing intense, clean luxury—felt like a full-circle validation. It remains a flawless signature.

Spaghetti & Caviar: While the classic canvas holds its legendary status, the absolute triumph of the lunch was the spaghetti cooked in beets and crowned with a mountain of caviar (thoughtfully comped by the chef). The deep, earthy sweetness of the beet-infused pasta playing against the intense, briny pop of the caviar was breathtakingly brilliant.

Tableside with a Master: A truly memorable highlight of our lunch was when Chef Michael Tusk stopped by our table. Right on the heels of his well-deserved James Beard Foundation win for Best Chef, he took the time to speak intimately with us about the architectural design, philosophy, and evolving ethos of the restaurant. It highlighted the exact type of genuine, world-class hospitality that defines a true three-star house.

A Reimagined Atmosphere: The physical evolution of the dining room since our last visit is striking. It trades none of its historic brick soul while embracing a brighter, more fluid architectural sophistication that beautifully mirrors the evolution of the menu.

Everything about the lunch was fantastic. Quince has not only maintained its pristine standard; it has sharpened it. It remains firmly anchored as one of my absolute top fine dining destinations in San Francisco.

Review: Quince – A Masterclass in Three-Star Hospitality
Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

A Foundational Milestone in Our Michelin Journey
Our visit to Quince in September 2021 remains a cornerstone of our culinary journey. As one of our first three-star experiences, Chef Michael Tusk and his team set an incredibly high bar for what world-class hospitality and technical brilliance should look like. It is a memory that persists even after visiting dozens of other starred establishments globally.

The Standout Moment
The absolute highlight was the Golden Ossetra Caviar with panna cotta and brioche. Nearly five years later, I still dream about this dish—it remains one of the single best things I have ever eaten. The salty pop of the caviar against the silky panna cotta and the warm, buttery brioche was a masterclass in balance and luxury.

The Experience

Impeccable Service: The service was a seamless demonstration of professional grace. Every detail was accounted for, making us feel welcomed and valued.

Culinary Artistry: From the stunning flower-pressed pasta to the intricate snacks and the legendary bread service, the commitment to Northern California’s terroir is superlative.

Sophisticated Atmosphere: The dining room balances opulence with a warm, focused energy that feels quintessentially San Francisco.

Final Thoughts
Quince delivers on the "Three-Star Contract" completely: excellence in food, atmosphere, and professional grace. For anyone seeking the absolute best in the Bay Area, this remains an essential destination.

top_reviews.content:

We ordered quite a few dishes and started with Omakase gushi, which came with chicken breast, thigh with leek, heart, cartilage, and minced chicken.  We also ordered the oden set, sasami, tori tataki, gyu-tan, enoki bacon, and buta bara.

Evertyhing tasted pretty good, but the most impressive dish was sasami with umeboshi, which was inner bresat with umehad was the inner breast with umeboshi. It was my first time trying raw chicken, and it tasted really good. The chicken breast was really tender, with a tuna-like texture, and without any slimy or odd flavors. Ever since then, I've been telling my friends to try it. The Tori Tataki was seared chicken breast sashimi with ponzu, which tasted a bit plain compared to the sasami. So  I would highly recommended to get theeir sasami!
Wow!!! i loved this place - great food, great atmosphere- about as japanese as you can get outside of japan - wish i lived closer so i could eat here all the time!! seriously worth going to.

Ippuku (一服), which means to take a short break for a cigarette or tea during a busy day (literally meaning “one dose”), had a very nice vibe walking in. The entrance was unassuming, but the interior transported me back to Japan. They had seating areas which simulated traditional seating on zabutons and tatami maps, and also more western style sitting areas. You can immediately tell they take pride in Japanese tradition without becoming pretentious or trying too hard to be "unique".

They gave a complimentary chunk of cabbage with kewpie mayo topped with togarashi. While pretty difficult to eat since it is just a large chunk of cabbage, it was a very nice palate cleanser throughout the whole meal. We ordered four skewers: Gyutan (beef tongue), Kurobutabara (pork belly), Negima (thigh with leek), and Kawa (skin). Additionally, we got the Ikasumi chahan (squid ink fried rice) and Kani korokke (dungeness crab creme croquettes).

The squid ink fried rice, while pretty good, was the biggest disappointment. It tasted like a standard rice that can be made at home, but colored with squid ink. The squid ink felt more like a gimmick that made my tongue and lips black after eating a few bites. The crab croquettes were very solid, a nice structural integrity and creaminess one bitten in. The crab slivers were noticeable and added a nice sweetness and crabby flavor overall. The sliced cabbage under them was a good palate cleanser too.

The skewers, specifically the yakitori, was their advertised specialty. Starting with the beef tongue, it was slightly thick, but cooked perfectly. It had a nice bite whilst not being too chewy, and the charred jalapeños provided a good spice that broke up the pieces of meat. It was also seasoned nicely, without need for a sauce. The chicken skin was my least favorite of the skewers. While the outside had a good crunch, which I love in chicken skin, the inside became very soggy and chewy. I would have preferred them to not be in skewer form, and to just be fried as whole skin pieces. The chicken thigh was very impressive. With a thin coating of sauce, the chicken was succulent and juicy, very flavorful, and the leeks provided a nice textural contrast as well as a freshness. This was a very impressive skewer that I would definitely get again. The pork belly was my favorite bite of the night. It was both juicy and had nicely rendered fat. It was a very meaty taste, accentuated by the simple seasoning of just salt and letting the charcoal flavor come through. The sauce they served with it was also really unique, a mix of miso paste and doubanjiang, giving a slightly fruity note and a perfect accompaniment to the pork belly.  The server also gave complimentary matcha ice cream, which was really good too. The matcha flavor was deep and was a creamy ice cream.

Overall, it was an obvious upgrade to the last izakaya, and no dish was bad. While only a few items truly wowed me, I enjoyed how they stuck to tradition to provide an unpretentious experience that reminded me of Japan. While pricey, this is a place I could recommend to others who want to try a very solid izakaya.

Appreciated the small dishes for variety, but quality differed between dishes and I also found many of them lacked flavor.

My favorite dishes were the negima (thigh with leek), the shisho making, and the goma yogoshi (spinach in sesame paste) for their more unique tastes. I wouldn't recommend the Nama-Yuba nor the mochi wrapped in bacon or nori.

Service is good with the plates coming out in intervals to accentuate the dining experience.

Would recommend making reservations since the restaurant gets packed quite easily.

The staff? Always kind. Always attentive. The atmosphere? Casual but cozy, like your favorite local spot back home.

If you’re new to the Bay Area or just hunting for a place that gets Japanese food right, start here. Kiraku isn’t just a restaurant. It’s the kind of place that makes you want to come back before you’ve even left.

This is honestly my favorite spot in the entire SF/Bay Area — no competition, no close second. I mean it. Nothing else compares.

I first came here around 2022 and was absolutely blown away. I live far, but this is still a place I’ll happily drive an hour for, wait 40+ minutes for, and revisit 10+ times without hesitation. Zero complaints. Always worth it.

The space isn’t big, but the sticker-covered walls and posters give it so much personality. It feels like a place that’s been loved and thoughtfully run for years — a true neighborhood gem with soul.

💡 Best tip: come right at 5:30pm opening or join the Yelp waitlist in advance.

Writing this review makes me sad thinking about the day I leave the Bay Area and can’t come back here anymore.

Kiraku is absolutely a must-try in the Bay Area. Come experience it yourself — you won’t regret it!

Absolute meet cute with a cozy vibe. Came here for a late night snack at 10pm.

They have a little table out front to check in, but as I was a walking they came to get me and seated promptly.

Whole place sits maybe thirty people tops thirty five

They have a tapas style menu of small plates which is nice if you want to mix and match.

I got the toasted green tea, clam miso soup, garlic edamame, and a skewer each of the eel and lamb.

The green tea wasn’t piping hot but warm. Tasted… toasty. Didn’t think I’d like it but three cups in it grew on me. Give it a chance.

Garlic edamame was excellent. Had a coating of anchovy bits that made it unique and had me snacking my lips. Will order this everytime.

They said that the miso soup usually comes at the end, after the other courses. When asked for a preference, I deferred to them. They thought it right away.

The soup had about five clams which imparted a salty brine depth that eclipsed the expected umami of the miso. I’m not mad. Tastes great. But I do like my miso on the lighter side. Worth trying to see if it’s for you.

Lamb skewer was well seasoned and light. It’s rare to find lamb in Japanese restaurants so I make it a point to order it. Had bits of scallions grilled with it, came with a dollop of mustard. Delicious.

The eel skewer was my absolute favorite. Soft and buttery, partitions on its own and melts in your mouth. Seasoning was strong but adequate. Cane with some wasabi. Avoid the wasabi for this one. You don’t need it, as it distracts from the unagi’s natural qualities.

They had a dessert menu, but I passed on it

The restaurant’s dark wood walls are sprinkled with vintage Japanese beer ads.

The staff are attentive and very sweet. When I came in, they asked if it was my first time here and walked me through the menu. Then they proceeded to give me a warm towel as I was coming in from the rain. An absolute vibe.

top_reviews.content: Love Slice House! It is great when you don't want to order an entire pie. My favorites are their New York style and deep dish slices. Once you order, they give you a number to listen for when the pizza is warmed up and ready to go. The slices are a good size and will definitely fill you up easy. I want to really take the time to say, THANK YOU, to Slice House for its commitment to accommodating lesser known allergies like my boyfriend’s Dairy Allergy. My significant other had attempted right before  to order a pizza from a competitor (I won’t mention their name because the focus of this review is on the extraordinary job of Slice House) who had no option to edit dairy on DoorDash which I wouldn’t say is out of the ordinary honestly. What was out of the ordinary was to have a location refuse to make it without cheese even after being informed of his allergy. No reason other than they wouldn’t.

Dejected from the interaction and feeling that he ruined our dinner, I began to offer to find alternatives. His counter offer was he could pull off the cheese. I have never cooked a pizza myself, but I’d burn down my kitchen tonight trying myself before I’d let him suffer through the indignity of being charged, told he couldn’t have his pizza the way he wanted even though it may kill him and he paid for it, not being provided a refund, then pulling off cheese hoping it’s enough for his throat not to close. I begged to allow me to find an alternative and he agreed. I looked for a suitable alternative and Slice House looked like a winner. When I handed him the phone to check the menu after some coaxing I heard a loud “OMG”. That was immediately followed about enthusiasm and smiling because of what he saw. SH allows you to customize almost anything and has the most allergy alternative options I’ve ever seen from a pizza company. We had an amazing meal and will forever sing the praises of Slice House. Not because they let us decide what we wanted on the pizza we paid for, not because it is the best Pizza in SF and DoorDash, because you know you’re cared for as a customer and human even though we have never talked to a single employee or even been inside the store.

I stopped by this location at Fisherman's Wharf around 9:00 PM, and it was a surprisingly relaxing experience. Unlike many places in this highly trafficked tourist area, there was plenty of space to spread out. I ordered a cheeseburger, and the quality was excellent. You can easily tell that it was freshly made to order rather than sitting under a heat lamp. The bun was soft and toasted, the cheese was perfectly melted, and they did not skimp on the fresh toppings—it came with crisp, thick-cut slices of raw onion and tomato that gave the burger a great crunch. It is a solid, well-constructed classic burger.

While I came specifically for a burger, it's worth noting that their menu is incredibly extensive. They serve hearty breakfast plates all day, and their front counter boasts a massive, fully stocked dessert case filled with fresh-baked pies and cheesecakes (everything from Key Lime and Coconut Crème to classic Apple and Pecan).

If you are looking for a high-quality, freshly made, and satisfying meal late in the evening without having to fight through claustrophobic crowds, this spot is an absolute gem in Fisherman's Wharf. Highly recommended!

Given the popularity of this place, that’s a pretty big inconvenience. It was not busy at all only about 3 tables filled and it was dinner time. Even though the entire boulevard was crowded.

Between the average pie and the lack of basic facilities, I’m not really sure why this place gets so much buzz. It’s fine in a pinch, but didn't live up to the reputation for me.

Between the entree and a la cart wings, it was enough for me to have leftovers for lunch the next day.

They also used to have this coconut seafood veggie dish tbh at was da bomb.  Haven’t seen that years.

Dammit I’m old.  Missing the good ol days.

Haven't been in over a decade. We used to go all the time when we lived in the Bay but haven't been back after moving to Sacramento. We happen to be coming back from SJ and decide to stop for a late lunch aeound 3. It wasn't to busy so we were seated right away. Staff were friendly.

Only had the noodle soups but they’re are solid. Big chunk of noodles, couple pieces of bok choy + whatever you ordered. Broth is good, it has some real flavor not all salt. Ladies who work there are nice

As I understand, the name Daimo stems from the Cantonese term "day mouw ( floor squat)" which is short for "day mouw goohn"...an impromptu,likely illegal,  food stand without chairs or tables where you practically have to squat to eat your food. Remembered fondly by some, these places were known for good food at cheap prices.

Daimo in Richmond is a far departure from those "day mouws" in China but is nonetheless a solid choice for those looking for traditional Chinese fare.

Their go-to dishes include their beef chow fuhn, beef stew over rice, and other assorted rice plates. Prices are moderate, but for certain items, portions are quite large.
In fact, they're well known for their large portions. People seem to come from far away to take advantage of this.

Service is good, and the waitresses are friendly and  helpful. The restaurant has a lot of windows and they give the place a bright airy feel.

If you're in the area and looking for Chinese food, give Daimo a try. The food is good, traditional and you certainly won't leave hungry.

Its a little retro 90s inside, but its spacious, my table was clean, they offered a complimentary hot tea & hot oil on the table for the food.

I ordered a lunch special for $15.95, I asked for her reccomendation - she suggested the beef Xo. This came with a beverage (I chose a can of coke) & a small soup (sweet & sour). The beef xo also had a side of white rice on the plate as well - which turned out great, because although the Xo is yummy, it is quite rich and salty, the white rice cuts that richness very well. The portion was also ample for a lunch serving. I say it is for sure worth it! The beef was super tender and flavorful as well. I really didnt care for the Celery in this dish though. Next time I'd ask them to leave it out, its really nothing but a filler & not a good one at that. The snow peas were a nice addition though.

I also ordered Beef & Chive chow fun i believe it was $17.95. This is a HUGE portion, so while $17.95 sounds high to me, this can easily fill 3 people with just the chow fun alone! This price is super reasonable. As far as taste of the chow fun - the beef was great and tender, I just wish the noodles were thicker and fatter. These arent typically the kind of noodles I envision when I think chow fun... this is probably closer to a thai pad see ewe noodle, still good! But i was really wanting a fatter wider noodle. The sauce was perfect - maybe id have liked it to be a little wetter even, but the flavor was good.

For appetizers i ordered a
- BBQ pork rice roll $7 8pc (my favorite thing out of everything!)
- Shrimp & Chive Dumplings 3pc (my least favorite of everything)
- Turnip cake $6 3pc (this was interesting - texturally like a mix between fake mashed potatoes & gelatin.. I didnt hate it. The seared parts were super yummy)

The shrimp & Chive Dumplings was a bit dry. Bland & a little over burnt on the seared outside. It also didnt come with any sauce. Id never order it again

The BBQ rice roll was texturally pleasant to me - with the super soft rice roll & the addition of the BBQ pork added texture + it was laying in a sort of ponzu or soju sauce which was also yummy.

Overall I'd rate everything a 4 out of 5. The service was great. The ladies were super friendly and wiling to make suggestions. They even packed my to go leftovers them selves, & didnt charge me for my extra coke... which may or may not have been intentional - either way I added what that cost would have been to their tip so it works out.

Id definitely be back!

Not sure what’s up with the negative reviews, but I have been eating here for years and the food is still consistently good and tasty. We always order a variety of different main dishes and they are fresh and taste good. Generous portions.

* Paitan Ramen: Known for its rich, creamy, and opaque broth (often chicken-based), offering a deeply savory "umami" profile that stays smooth and balanced.
* Miso Ramen: Typically features a bolder, heartier taste due to the fermented soybean paste, which can sometimes be more assertive than the silky Paitan.

Outside the food, loved the homey feel of the restaurant and the staff were all very friendly with a smile.

This is your go to place if you want to try a delicious torta. Guac was extremely fresh, flavor was on point. Service was excellent 👌, 100% recommended

The food is comforting, addictive, and consistently outstanding. We clean our plates, scrape every last bite, and take leftovers whenever possible.

We will absolutely be back again and again and again.

top_reviews.content:
I’ve been tracking San Ho Wan for a while now, but I always seemed to remember too late, leaving only the "late evening" slots available. I finally got on the ball and scored a prime-time reservation, and the experience confirmed exactly why this place holds its Michelin Star.

The Vibe & Value:
What’s refreshing here is the casual atmosphere. In a city where some 1-star establishments are pushing the $300+ price point, San Ho Wan is a breath of fresh air. It’s accessible, yet maintains a standard of technical excellence that some luxury tasting menus miss. While S.F. has plenty of good Michelin choices on the less expensive end, this is a standout for modern Korean BBQ.

The Technical Audit:

The Gyeran-jjim (Steamed Egg): Absolute technical perfection. The rise was consistent and the texture was soufflé-light.

The Galbi / Short Rib: The Maillard reaction on the beef was lacquered perfectly. You can see the quality of the sourcing in the marbling—rich, rendered beautifully, and handled with real precision.

The Banchan & Sides: Every detail, from the vibrant ferments to the crispness of the ssam (lettuce wraps), was handled with care. The kitchen operates with a visible discipline that you can see in the cleanliness of the stone pots and the clarity of the presentation.

Pro-Tip on Access:
If you can’t snag a reservation through the system, they do have counter space for walk-ins. It’s a great fallback if you’re in the Mission and want to bypass the online calendar.

The Verdict:
If you can navigate the competitive reservation system, it’s a must-visit. It delivers a high-functioning kitchen performance without the "stiff" service often found in the Mission or SoMa fine-dining scenes.

top_reviews.content: We ate as a party of 13 friends at the China Village located at Solano Ave, Albany near Berkely yesterday night on 5/21/26. The restaurant is located conveniently by itself across the sidewalk from parking. All you need to do to get there is cross a short sidewalk. The area felt clean and safe. When we arrived and walked in, we were greeted by many nice, beautiful and hospitable ladies who were to be our waiters and led to a private "Dragon" party room near the back. In the front were standard tables and a lot of pretty Chinese decor from Gold to Dragons. There were bathrooms separated by gender and area located near the front. There was also a fish tank full of sea-life such as Crabs and Fishes and Lobsters that were on the Chinese Cuisine's Menu. It was a very laid back vibe and very quiet and peaceful and relaxing. In the back, were we were seated, the tables had comfortable chairs and a round spinning table like something you would find at Chinese Dim Sum. The atmosphere felt very relaxed and easy-going and brought us back to feeling like we were in China or Shanghai's Nightlife. The waiter's service was great, they constantly came to check in on us and were very personable and formidable and made nice small talk with us and chatted and it felt like they were close friends which each waiter should strive to be. Our table was filled with neat napkins to wipe, put on your lap and to double as a handkerchief with, silverware, a glass of fresh water not tap as well as herbal fresh tea that was simmered just right with a hint of bitterness you would expect from fresh tea with leaves. We ordered and the food was promptly brought out almost immediately with little wait time. This restaurant is known for their fresh Chinese spark of Sichuan(Spicy) and Mala(Spicy) as well as Seafood(Seafood), once again it felt like we were transported back into the luxurious city of China. This was very authentic and fresh Chinese food, not like the fake food that is AmeriChinese like Panda Express. We ordered delicious food such as clams and oysters which were paired with a lot of extra garnish to truly bring out their wonderful shelly flavor, beautiful and delicious small crustacean prawns and shrimp that tasted fresh from the sea, Spicy Mala/Sichuan Beef as well as Fish which were pretty spicy yet savory, Yangzhou Fried Rice with the perfect amount of veggies and beef, Honeybee Lobster that was golden crisp, Orange Chicken that was not as sweet as many fake Chinese places make them so these were the authentic real deal, Pork and Shrimp Dumplings which were nicely coated and didnt fall apart, Shellfish which were deliciously chewy, Scallops which were very tasty and more. The food was very clean and fresh, they had a rich savory seafood taste and aroma and tasted like the deep blue ocean, and most of the food came with a side of unique sauce that was to be best paired individually with each unique dish. The service was great, the waiters were very attentive and attentful with their service, constantly refilling our glasses and helping us make way and navigate around our big party of guests and limited spaces to make way for new dishes to glaze our table. Everyone was full, we were not rushed and came out feeling very refreshed and sleepy as the food was so so delicious. Fair price! I attached some pictures below of what I had, if anyone is in the nearby area, I encourage you to come try the food at this delicious and authentic Chinese restaurant. Even if you are not in the immediate area, this place is worth a drive as we did coming from the Solano Area all the way here just to sample this delicious food from a mutual friend's wonderful recommendations. We are sure to come back in the near future to try their delicious other menus offerings and we are confident that we will be equally if not more impressed with their offerings the second time around as well. Thank you so much to China Village for hosting our large party and be very pleasant to be around for both service and coordination of the big dinner that took place yesterday.

It's been quite a few years since I last visited this place. So much has changed since 2016, especially after the pandemic and the subsequent lockdowns in San Francisco. Our routines were drastically altered, and many places where we used to gather to have a drink and enjoy each other's company became distant memories.

A few days ago, however, I met an old friend at The Royal Exchange, just like we used to before the pandemic, and it was a grand time. It felt like things were finally getting back on track.

The Royal Exchange is still an excellent pub with a classic feel. With plenty of beer choices and great bartenders, it remains a perfect spot to meet friends and catch up. It's also easy to get to, with convenient access via public transportation and nearby parking for drivers.

The pub opened in 1972, the same year the first episode of "The Streets of San Francisco" aired. Given the timing and the pub's classic San Francisco atmosphere, it's not at all far-fetched to imagine Stone and Keller stopping by for a couple of beers after a long day of chasing bad guys.

Tasty Indian food in a low-key setting.

We tried the butter chicken, saag paneer, and baingan bharta, all of which were delicious. The garlic naan & butter naan were also good.

We came here around 9pm on a Saturday evening and it was completely empty, so no issue getting a table. A few more people trickled in while we ate.

The restaurant isn't too large and has simple on-theme atmosphere and decor.

This was my first time at this particular restaurant and it was quite interesting since it's in Japantown San Francisco. I was shocked by the amount of vegetarian as well as vegan dishes on the menu so I was able to order things with ease.
Everything we ordered tasted delicious but I think we came in just as a larger table ordered so it took us about 25 minutes to get our food. Everything tasted delicious so it all panned out, I also liked the ambience of the restaurant and it made you feel like you were actually in another country with the authentic paintings on the wall as well as music and comfortable decor.
I wouldn't mind coming here again and trying some More dishes!

Extremely disappointed with my experience at Royal Indian Cuisine on Fillmore.

The biggest issue is the food quantity, which is honestly unacceptable for the price. The portion of rice was so small that it wasn’t even enough for one child. For an Indian restaurant, serving such tiny portions is very disappointing and leaves customers feeling like they’re getting poor value for money.

The staff also failed to follow simple instructions. We gave clear requests with our order, but they were completely ignored. It felt like nobody was paying attention to what the customer actually wanted, which made the overall experience even more frustrating.

As for the taste, it was just average—nothing memorable or worth coming back for. There are many Indian restaurants that offer far better food, much better service, and significantly larger portions for the same price.

Overall, the restaurant falls short in the three things that matter most:

* Quantity: Extremely poor and not worth the price.
* Service: Staff does not pay attention to customer instructions.
* Taste: Just average and not enough to make up for the other shortcomings.

I would not recommend this restaurant based on my experience, and I certainly won’t be returning.

top_reviews.content:
I would absolutely recommend this place for anyone wanting Mexican food and balling on a budget. I got the super burrito and it was really good. Could’ve used a little more avocado sauce but other than that it was exactly what I was looking for.

Keep in mind if you get protein the price of the item may change from what’s shown on the menu. I’m not a huge fan of not knowing what those costs are before ordering, but don’t let that influence whether you go here or not — just ask ahead.

This area of town is fun. There are lots of bars nearby, and Coit Tower is just a few minutes away.

Overall, highly recommend!

Located on the Upper portion of Grant Ave. just past Chinatown above Columbus Ave.
I was recommended this place by a friend.
What I ordered:
1.) Passion Fruit drink $2.75 if you like passion fruit, you will like this.
2.) Supreme Carnitas Burrito$12.50 this tasted just ok lacked a bit of flavor.

In streets of San Francisco, flavors softly call,
But one small taco conquered and outshined them all.
Golden tripa sizzling, crisp with perfect bite,
A humble work of magic wrapped warm and tight.

Not fancy words nor silver plates could match this simple art,
Because these beef intestine tacos went straight into my heart.
Seasoned with tradition, fire, and soul so true,
One bite became a memory I never outgrew.

Some meals are quickly forgotten and quietly let go,
But these unforgettable tripa tacos deserve the world to know.
So if you’re chasing flavor that lingers long after you roam,
Please, get the tripa tacos.

El Farolito is a solid Mexican food chain in SF. It has multiple locations and some locations are cash only but this location in North Beach/Chinatown accepts card. They’re also open late and close at 2am so late nights can be filled with many drunk people but a must for some food to soak up that alcohol. I was craving a carne asada super burrito for a while now and it hit the spot, good with both red and green sauce. Their quesadillas look really filling too. And also can’t go wrong with tacos. They’re fast and efficient and they also have chips too. It’s a pretty cozy spot so there is seating inside, no outdoor seating but perfectly ok to enjoy your food out there or even take out. Huge portions for a pretty decent price. There’s street parking but it can get very busy, there are some parking garages in the area and 24 hour ones too.
Have had the bistec encebollado, Mexican Torta, SuperBurrito, Tacos, and Super Nachos here.  All were pretty good (I skipped some sides due to dietary issues).  Prices are very reasonable.

I recently tried a Hawaiian vegetarian burger, and wow,  it was incredibly delicious. The combination of pineapple and teriyaki made it one of the best burgers I’ve had so far. The sweetness of the pineapple paired perfectly with the sauce, giving it a tropical twist while still keeping that satisfying, hearty burger feel.
I also tried the Challenger turkey burger, and it was yum as well. I added Thousand Island sauce and pickles, which made it even better — tangy, creamy, and full of great flavor. Both burgers still had a nice touch of traditional burger taste, which I really enjoyed.

No special sauces here which I think is usually what makes a burger stand out, otherwise all the other toppings are pretty basic. I say the burger is OK, I just wish there was more flavors to choose from the bar.

The fries were excellent and crisp. Fountain drink is as you expect.

The self service toppings bar was different but I really enjoyed it so I could freely pick and choose not only my toppings but also the dressings to go with my burger.

Definitely recommend this spot if you’re in the area and looking for a good burger spot.

top_reviews.content:
This is one of the nicest restaurant experiences I've had in all of SF! I came here on a Thursday night as a solo diner close to when they opened and was immediately met with a very warm welcome. Everyone was friendly and the ambiance was so warm and intimate.

I sat at the bar ordered a glass of wine and two pasta dishes - the bottarga and a special that had a lamb ragu with olives. Both were excellent! The bottarga had a nice rich, salty sea flavor and the lamb ragu flavors were super balanced with a bit of savory truffle and ricotta salata. I wasn't planning on getting dessert, but I ended up getting a chocolate hazelnut panna cotta that was the perfect texture. Everything came out quickly and fresh, even when they started getting busy later in the night.

I've been trying a lot of pasta restaurants around the city, and this was one of the only places I've been to that had both interesting pasta dishes and felt authentically Italian. In a city of great pasta restaurants, it's unique since it focuses on Sardinian cuisine. I definitely hope to come back and try many more items on their delicious looking menu!

Delightful food and service. Incredibly attentive host—always had enough water and the food came out hot and fresh with clear attention to ingredients and cooking method. Highly recommend the calamari appetizer, lamb tenderloin, and gnocchietti. Lamb tenderloin was perfectly cooked! The gelato flavors were extremely unique (goat cheese and fig, and rum raisin). Thanks, Cheryl, for having us!

I rarely leave negative reviews because I understand how important positive feedback is for small businesses. However, our recent experience was disappointing.

The server’s attitude felt disrespectful from the start. He questioned whether we were comfortable with the wine prices in a way that made us feel uncomfortable. He also described a special as having a “bolognese-like sauce,” but when I referred to it as “bolognese pasta,” he abruptly stated that they did not have bolognese pasta, which was confusing given his earlier description.

What concerned me most was his behavior toward my daughter. She was quietly drawing on the back of the receipt when he took the pen from her abruptly, without asking. She was visibly embarrassed by the interaction.

We spoke with the owner, whom we like and respect, but unfortunately the experience left a negative impression. For that reason, we will not be returning.

This was an amazing place to get dinner! The gnocchi was to die for! Best gnocchi I have ever had! We also had the uni pasta, the calamari, the lamb, and some gelato and ricotta for dessert. After the gnocchi, my favorite was the calamari and from the gelato I loved the goat cheese and fig flavor. The team was also so so sweet, from the host to our amazing server Vadim, who had such great energy, to even the owner who came out to ask us about our dining experience. We had such a great time here with such friendly, warm service. Definitely recommend having dinner here. One of my favorite Italian restaurants now. We will definitely be back. Thanks to Vadim and the team!

Had been wanting to try this place for a while - the service was great and the ambiance was cozy (except for the front entrance, there was no waiting area and lots of people were crowded waiting for their tables throughout the night).

top_reviews.content: I was in the neighbourhood and wanted to try something that is local and on sweet Dutch and found this deli. The deli is really cute at the corner of the streets. My girlfriend ordered the tuna salad and when we got to the port we realized it was actually chicken salad. The was a little disappointing for her. She was also not a fan that something was a little spicy, maybe the mustard. I got the number one on their menu and it was good. Decades of Deliciousness!

I've been a customer at Freddie's Sandwiches for over twenty-five years and live just two blocks away. When I wanted to update my review, I realized that the comments from my 2016 review still hold true! So, I won't repeat that they still make the best sandwiches for the price, but I will share that I've added their Club Sandwich to my list of favorites.

Freddie's Club Sandwich comes with ham, turkey, and bacon, and you can add any combination of mustard, mayo, lettuce, tomato, pickles, and onions. The bread makes a huge difference, and if I may, I'd like to give you a hint: Go with hard sourdough bread, ask for it to be gutted out and toasted, and go light with the mayo. You will enjoy it.

Their coffee is also pretty good. It's drip coffee only, but the owner is a coffee enthusiast like myself and always has fresh, hot coffee available upfront. If coffee isn't your thing, they have plenty of non-alcoholic options to choose from. Their deli salads are made daily and can be a great companion to your sandwich.

The store is small, and there is no room to sit inside, but they have three or four small tables and chairs available outside if you and a companion or two want to have your sandwiches there.

The owner seems very serious at first, but after chatting and exchanging pleasantries, you'll find that he's actually a very nice and helpful person, as are the rest of his staff. They sometimes fill in behind the counter if he's not around.
Just a great sandwich. The veggie was fresh and had lots of bite. The small is a big portion. Filled me up for the rest of the day.

top_reviews.content:
A friend recently introduced me to Laundromat Bagel & Cafe on Balboa Street in the Outer Sunset, and I'm so glad they did.

The cafe immediately stood out thanks to the irresistible aroma of freshly baked bagels drifting onto the street. Inside, the space felt airy and inviting, with a thoughtful blend of wood and metal accents that created a warm, modern atmosphere. What impressed me just as much was the staff. Everyone was welcoming, smiling, and genuinely friendly. Their warmth made the experience feel personal and memorable.

As for the bagels, they are hands down superior to most bagels I've had in San Francisco. Even without toasting, the exterior had a satisfying crunch while the inside remained light and fluffy. The flavor was wonderfully balanced—neither sweet nor grainy, but pleasantly nutty. Most remarkable of all, the bagels weren't overly chewy, allowing their texture and flavor to shine.

The cream cheese deserves special recognition as well. The best way I can describe it is New York meets Bay Area style: dense and creamy, yet somehow light and fluffy, with just the right amount of tanginess.

I'm thrilled to have been introduced to Laundromat for its exceptional bagels. Now I have every reason to return and see what their pizza and beer are all about.

Tried both the bagels and vegan broccoli pizza and both were soo good! Pizza had a great amount of cheese and some spice and the broccoli rabe is a cool variation you don’t often see on a pizza! Will definitely order again. There can be lines on the weekend even for pick up but worth it! Staff helped me confirm if the bagel I chose was vegan and the vegan pizza is clearly labeled
Staff is really nice too!

As a bagel enthusiast, I have to agree with the claim that these are the best bagels in SF 🥯 The vegan cream cheese is delectable but 1 tub is enough for 4 bagels. Get an everything bagel if you want it fresh and hot or try a poppyseed if you wanna branch out. Plan to eat the bagels elsewhere since there's no seating; I recommend taking them to Lands End 🌁

Im someone who hates waiting in line, but I think this place is worth the 35 min wait. The staff is genuinely nice and wants you to enjoy. The pizza is the star of the show… but DONT skip the truffle honey!!! Or their very cool wine selection! Loved the ambiance & food

Bagel shop by day, pizza spot by night. We only went in the morning for bagels, but after seeing the pizzas later that day, I’ll definitely be back to try that.

The line looked long when we got there, but it moved quickly. That said, there is definitely a little pressure to have your order ready by the time you reach the laundry baskets full of bagels. Not from the staff necessarily, but very much “Soup Nazi” energy from Seinfeld where you do not want to be the person slowing the line down.

The setup is very simple. No slicing, no toasting, just grab your bagels and go. There also isn’t really anywhere to sit or dine in for the bagel service, so we ended up finding a nearby bench to eat at.

We tried the sea salt and egg bagels and both were so good that we immediately went back in for another. Highly recommend the sea salt. They sell bagels individually or by the half dozen/dozen, but schmear only comes in 8 oz tubs. I wish they offered smaller portions or per bagel options because I wanted to try multiple schmears without committing to huge tubs.

Overall though, really great bagels and I’d absolutely come back.

Ambience and food are top tier. All items were uniquely Mexican and unapologetically tasty. Classic cheese enchilada was my favorite item because of the good balance of cheese and spice. Elenas Mexican Restaurant surpasses my expectations, and I can confidently assert that it is the finest Mexican restaurant I have ever experienced in the Bay Area. The culinary offerings are exceptional, and the preparation process is meticulous. The food is freshly prepared, and I thoroughly enjoy every dish. The restaurant boasts a distinct flavor profile that sets it apart. The staff is exceptionally kind and polite, comprising the most dedicated and passionate individuals I have encountered. Unlike some restaurants where employees merely await tips, the staff at Elenas are genuinely invested in their work and deliver exceptional service. The ambiance of the restaurant is elegant and sophisticated, making it suitable for both casual and formal occasions. I highly recommend Elenas to anyone seeking authentic Mexican cuisine. I am certain that I will return to this restaurant in the future.

As soon as we walked in you smell the woodfire. The restaurant is very pretty with plants everywhere, sky lights for lots of natural light and pastel paper banners on the ceiling.  We ordered a guacamole to start. I have to say I was a bit dissapointed, it was good, but it needed a bit of salt. The rest of the meal though made up for it. The ribeye was melt in your mouth, seasoned and cooked to perfection. The halibut ceviche was ah-mazing. They served it with crackers but I used the tortilla chips because hello classic combo. We also had the shredded chicken enchiladas and it was so tender and delicious. We topped the meal off with a chocoflan, which was soo good. The chocolate part tasted almost like a brownie...soo good. We ordered cocktails that were great as well like the margarita and tres leches martini. We were there for a late lunch at around 3pm on a Wednesday afternoon so no reservations needed although they didn't have reservations available for the evening.

The Ambiance: Elena's was dubbed the hottest new Mexican restaurant in town, so I booked a table months in advance to see what the hype was about. The space is gorgeous (exactly as beautiful as it looks online) and the service is outstanding.

The Food: We ordered the chicken empanadas and the crab enchiladas (a first for me!), alongside a few other items. While the quality is good, the flavor profile just wasn't for me. This menu is designed for comfort food seekers who prefer the familiar Americanized staples: melted cheese, sour cream, flour tortillas, and mild ground beef.

The Verdict: It essentially feels like an elevated version of Chevy’s or On the Border Mexican Grill & Cantina. It’s a pleasant experience with great aesthetics, but for me, the culinary experience didn't quite live up to the hype of being the hottest new Mexican restaurant in SF

Love Elena’s! The best paper thin complimentary tortilla chips and salsa. Great for lunch, dinner, and just margaritas/cocktails at the bar. The enchiladas are delicious especially as someone who doesn’t like enchiladas. The churros were ok, but the tres leches was sadly not great and wouldn’t order again

top_reviews.content:
I only eat #2 here.  Huge portion, taste better than other shop in Oakland, good price when paying cash. However there are some Downsides:
1) the neighbourhood is scary, lots of trash & homeless problems in the back streets.  In front of the shop is filled with garbage & dirty.  This location is worst for parking as well. Watch out for your cars.
2) the male cashier (owner) is rude & looks down on customers.

First time visiting this spot, it was recommended by Gemini actually.  Weird hours but if you are nearby when it's actually open this is a must stop place.

First of all, 95% Asian customers which is what you want to see when you're getting Asian food.  Be prepared to wait.  From getting there to leaving it was about 45 minutes, I recommend getting a few things to make the trip worth it.  Waiting an hour for one sandwich is diabolical.

This place is sick.  $6-7 bahn mi, big portion, lots of pre-made meals and drinks, I will for sure come back and try more things.  I got the #2, #7 & #13.  #7 hit hard, #13 was my favorite, the meatball isn't what I'd typically go for but Gemini said it was the most popular and I see why.  Although I'll probably opt for the version without the egg next time, not really necessary for me.  Bread was good, veg was great, this is a top notch bahn mi.

Parking is tricky, it's a bad part of town but they seem to have made some efforts judging by other reviews, to clean up the space in front.  No seating, its a to go only, but it's 100% worth it.  Check this place out

As always, be careful when you’re in the area. I used to come but it’s been the first time since Covid because I thought it was worth it but this time, I got the grilled pork Bahn mi but it wasn’t slices of grilled pork, but rather, pork sausage???

Then as I was mid way through the Bahn mi, there was a plastic bit????

Suffice to say, I won’t be coming back here. Kind of creeped out.

I had been wanting to try Banh Mi Ba Le for a while, but their extremely limited hours made it tough to make happen without having to deal with an extreme wait. They're only open Friday through Sunday from 7:30 a.m. to 3 p.m., so I finally made the trip out on a Friday and arrived around 9:30 a.m. It was already fairly busy, and it only got more packed while I waited for my order so I would strongly recommend getting there before 9 a.m. or phoning your order in ahead of time.

I ordered 4 sandwiches total, and it took somewhere between 30 and 45 minutes for everything to be ready, but both the #2 Special Combo Ham and the #13 Meatball and Egg were absolutely fantastic and well worth the wait. The #2 is how I benchmark a good banh mi, and this place really delivered. The pate was out of this world, the sandwich was piled high with delicious cold cuts, loaded with perfectly pickled veggies and jalapeños, and stuffed into a roll that had the perfect balance of a crisp exterior and pillowy interior. The #13 seemed to be a popular choice as well and for good reason. It had all the same great attributes as the #2, but with the pate and cold cuts replaced by a sweet and savory crumbled meatball paired with a perfectly soft boiled egg. It was every bit as satisfying and delicious and had such a different flavor profile to the #2, which I really appreciated.

It is not in the best neighborhood and the hours are painfully tight, especially if you want to avoid a long wait, but the end product is absolutely worth it, in my opinion. And at $6 to $7 per sandwich, the value is still a good value, even if it is a far cry from the $4-6 range that it seemed to hover in for a long time.

Bánh Mì Ba Le is a must-visit spot for anyone craving an authentic and delicious Vietnamese sandwich experience. Located in the heart of the city, this casual eatery has earned a reputation for serving some of the best bánh mì in town. The sandwiches are packed with fresh, flavorful ingredients, from the perfectly crispy baguette to the savory meats like grilled pork, chicken, and even tofu for a vegetarian option.

One of the highlights of Bánh Mì Ba Le is the balance of textures and flavors — crunchy pickled vegetables, fresh cilantro, and a kick of spicy chili sauce all come together in each bite. The meats are well-seasoned and juicy, making each sandwich satisfying and filling.

The service is quick and friendly, and the prices are very reasonable for the quality of food you get. If you're a fan of Vietnamese cuisine or just looking for a tasty lunch, Bánh Mì Ba Le is a top choice!

top_reviews.content:
I visited Napizza San Francisco for dinner and had a mixed experience. It’s a nice, cozy little place with a good ambience and outdoor dining available. Since it was cold, I chose to sit inside, but I liked that they offer blankets for guests who prefer sitting outside.

The service was quick, and the staff was friendly, which made the overall experience pleasant. However, I was expecting the food to be the highlight and was a bit disappointed.

The starter bread they offered was unique and something I really enjoyed. The pasta was probably the best dish I had - I liked it, though I felt it could use a little more sauce. I ordered the Meyer Lemon pizza, and while it was a nice thin pizza, it was a bit too sour for my taste because of the amount of lemon. Btw they helped to customize it with 2 extra things I wanted on pizza. I think it needed more mozzarella balance. The pesto on the pizza was also disappointing; it looked like a very dark green sauce and didn’t have the fresh pesto flavor I was expecting.

I also tried a mocktail that was priced at $12, but I don’t think it justified that price. For dessert, I ordered the tiramisu, which was good - not amazing, but definitely a nice way to end the meal.

Overall, the place has a nice atmosphere and good service, but the food needs improvement to match the expectations that come with the experience.

We had a great meal at 'Napizza in San Francisco. We shared the La Sorrentina pizza among four people and it was excellent. The crust was perfectly crisp with nice char, and the toppings tasted fresh and well-balanced. For my main plate I ordered the Tonnarelli Tartufati, and it was delicious too. The pasta had a rich truffle flavor that worked really well.

The bread they served at the beginning was good as well. Warm, soft, and perfect for sharing. Overall a solid Italian spot with flavorful food and nice portions. We would definitely come back. 🍕🍝🥖

Wow. What can I say, other than incredible! From the service to the wine, to the food, then dessert. 5 stars!! For starters we took our server's recommendation and ordered the fried dough with the burrata. Amazing! Then we shared a sausage& black truffle cream pasta, which my fiance said it was possibly "the best pasta I've ever had". Then the pizza... the dough, the sauce, the flavors, the spicy chili oil. Perfection. To top it off we received a delicious tiramisu on the house.. we usually go to Tony's for pizza, but I'm so glad we decided to switch it up, we will definitely be back!

Not a bad spot to check out. We had the Caesar salad which was good, the pizzas we tried were tasty but the pasta was underwhelming. The prosciutto on the pizza didn’t feel very fresh, however the dough was very fluffy which is why I’m still giving this place 4 stars. The pasta was bland and lowkey tasteless, almost no salt or flavor but the overall experience was good.

The outside seating is great. The service is quick and the meals are delicious

Update — June 23rd, 2026: Back for a second visit, and the pizza is still excellent. That said, I’m dropping my service rating from 4 stars to 1. A group of three arrived later and were treated noticeably better — bread, a snack for their dog, the heater switched on. The difference was hard to miss. Sadly, not a place I’ll be returning to.

top_reviews.content:
It’s a simple, relatively small, old‑fashioned French bistro. Nothing fancy, but the atmosphere is warm, the tableware is modest yet not cheap, and the service is friendly and quick. On Saturday afternoons there’s live music on the street‑side patio, which adds charm. The lunch and dinner menus overlap quite a bit.

Boeuf Bourguignon
The beef is tender with a pleasant chew, braised in a thick, flavorful Pinot Noir sauce. The portion is generous and normally comes with carrots and fingerling potatoes. We asked for a substitution, but they only offer additions for an extra $7.

Blanquette de Veau
A creamy veal stew (velouté) with mushrooms, carrots, and pearl onions. There’s less meat than in the Bourguignon, but it’s noticeably more tender, and the sauce and mushrooms give it deeper aroma and flavor. I actually preferred the veal, even though the beef was above average. It’s usually served with steamed rice, and substitutions are also only available for an extra charge.

Crème Brûlée
A good vanilla crème brûlée, enjoyable but not above average.

Overall
A genuinely pleasant dining experience with several well‑executed classic dishes. The restaurant is recommended, though there’s still room for improvement, especially regarding flexibility with sides.

The one disappointment was the service. During the first part of our meal, the staff came across as somewhat cold and unfriendly, and it was noticeable enough that others in my party commented on it as well. To their credit, some of the staff seemed to warm up as the meal went on, which improved the experience.

Overall, the food and atmosphere were strong enough that I would gladly return when I'm in the area again. With a warmer and more welcoming service experience from the start, this place would be truly exceptional.

The service leaves much to be desired.

When the pizzas finally arrived, they were a soggy mess. The oven was apparently running so hot that the pizzas came out burnt on the outside while still containing undercooked dough inside. The vegetables had released so much water that the result was an embarrassing excuse for a pizza.

When I pointed this out, the waiter responded with excuses rather than concern. I was told that "this is a new style," that "we make it in an oven," and that I should "talk to the owner." Burnt pizza is not a style, and using an oven is not an accomplishment if the food comes out poorly cooked. I have better things to do than track down the owner to explain basic quality control.

What was most disappointing was the complete lack of accountability. Instead of apologizing and trying to make things right, the waiter seemed more interested in acting as the restaurant's lawyer. Between the excessive wait, the poor food quality, and the dismissive response, this was an experience I would not recommend.

top_reviews.content:
Square Pie Guys sits right in the heart of Old Oakland, an area that’s perfect for wandering and grazing across different shops and food spots. Inside, the vibe is casual but energetic with an open kitchen lets you watch the pizzas come to life, while a blazing blue neon sign highlights their signature square slices. There’s a steady flow of locals grabbing their boxes to go, mixed with small parties dining in. The space inside feels compact, the outside seating helps, but this location is not built for big groups. Parties larger than five or six will probably feel squeezed. It works perfectly, though, for grabbing a couple of slices with a few friends or a relaxed date night.

The staff clearly care about what they are doing. They are friendly, attentive, and genuinely knowledgeable about the menu. Even during busy stretches, while constantly pulling pies from the oven and managing orders, they stay patient and helpful. It feels like a team that enjoys the craft, not just the job.

The salads are reliably excellent: fresh ingredients, made to order, bright and satisfying. Don’t come expecting standard sodas from a fountain or domestics on tap. I like how they focus on local beers and craft soda options, so go there open to trying something new to drink.

Their Detroit-style crust hits that ideal balance of crispy edges while remaining airy inside. The “Mush-o-Roni” is a classic go to, layering classic pepperoni with mushrooms for a rich, umami-heavy bite. Whereas the “How Mush-Room” offers a creamy alternative with its white sauce that pairs well with the cheese blend to satisfy the fungi fanatics.

The lemon pepper wings deserve special mention. They are crispy on the outside, tender inside, and clearly made fresh. They are well-executed, though the seasoning could use a bit more of a punch. Pairing them with their signature lemon pepper pizza (featuring lemon ricotta cream, more of that lemon pepper chicken, and green onion) was a smart move. The sauce alone elevates the whole pie and made me glad I tried it.

The spicy pepperoni also deserves special mention. Those crispy cups of pepperoni, spicy vodka sauce both under and drizzled over the cheese for extra depth is something special. The Detroit-style crust and edges are consistently on point across all of their pies and keeps me coming back.

Square Pie Guys never lets me down. Fresh ingredients and respectful execution of Detroit style make it a strong alternative to the usual round pies. Go if you love thick, crispy-edged Detroit pizza, especially pepperoni-forward or creative combos, or if you’re a lemon pepper lover. The wings and pizza together satisfy that craving well. Ideal for small groups or casual outings. I am absolutely planning a return, probably soon. Solid 4.75/5.

Didn’t get to try the pizza but snacks and beer I had were great. Didn’t interest with staff too much but overall a good impression on service. Love all the natural lighting and color. Seems welcoming and fun.

I had been wanting to try Square Pie Guys for years. My wife and I had the day off together and we ended up in Emeryville for some errands. I decided that we should come and try Detroit style pizza. Street parking was easy to find right out front. We opted to sit outside because it was a nice day in Oakland, but it was like 1pm on a Monday so the streets and shop were pretty dead. The inside of the shop was also a little warm and stuffy from the pizza oven.

After looking over the menu I decided to order the spicy pepperoni and my wife got the ultimate plant with dairy free cheese - see photos. I also got an order of the Szechuan chicken wings - not pictured - and my wife got the chilled bowled salad - also not pictured.

First off the wings were dried fried style and has the crispiest exterior. The seasoning was a mix of salt, white pepper, and sugar; very reminiscent of Wingstop's fries with the sweet and salty combo. The cilantro lime crema dip that comes with the wings is also fantastic. Although I feel the crema is better with veggie sticks as it overpowers the wings when eaten together. By far the best wings I've ever had at a pizza place. Highly recommend.

The salad was delicious as far as salad goes but my only criticism is that it had too much dressing. I feel like they could have dialed it back a little bit. But I did love the gigante beans in the salad; very rare you come across those.

Lastly our pizzas. My spicy pepperoni was fantastic although I wished the bottom crust was a little more crispy and crunchy. The dough was nice and pillowly on top. The pepperoni was super crispy with a little bit of char. My wife loved her ultimate plant and they gave her a good mix of veggies. We both agreed that the pizza could have used a bit more sauce. For those of you who know, vegan cheese is very high in sodium. I felt like her pizza was way saltier than mine, and mine was pretty salty already. Just be aware that after two slices, you're gonna feel very bloated and dehydrated.

Overall we both loved Square Pie Guys, and are excited to go to the Walnut Creek location later this year - it's closer to us. It may not be the best Detroit pizza, but it's definitely good Detroit pizza.

We visited this restaurant to get some food for a quick dinner. My husband was always against getting Panda Express and I had never had it so I had to try it. We ended up getting two plate meals so each had 1 side and 2 entree’s. We ordered Chow Mein, Orange Chicken, Beef and Broccoli, and Honey Walnut Shrimp.

Firstly, the Chow Mein is dry and lacking flavor. The beef for the beef and broccoli was tender, however the sauce on it lacked any sort of flavor.  The beef and broccoli was a weird experience because I’ve never had such saucy tender beef that was so lacking in flavor. The broccoli had flavor but not a great flavor.

The orange chicken had a very mild spice, however it does not taste like oranges if thats what you are expecting in the dish. It also is not very crisp, it was like sauce had set on it for awhile and absorbed into the bread coating on the chicken making it no longer crisp.

The honey walnut shrimp was probably our favorite of what we ordered. It had a nice crispness to it with a sweet glaze that tasted more of coconut in flavor than walnut or honey. There were a few pieces of walnut also found amongst the shrimp. If we ever are desperate enough to go again, this would be the only thing we order.

For a side to go along with the two plate meals we got we ordered a chicken egg roll to try. This egg roll was a major disappointment. I have high expectations in egg rolls coming from an Asian family and had lowered them knowing this is a fast food chain and wanted a quick egg roll fix; it still did not meet expectations at all. The outside wrapper was a little bit doughy, almost like it were cooked from frozen. The inside was lacking in seasoning. It had some cabbage, carrot, rice noodles, lettuce, and a tiny amount of ground chicken. Chewing through the whole thing left a displeasing taste on the palate, not like old grease, but displeasing.

I’m not sure how often food is made fresh, but while we were there employees were checking the temperature of all entrees.

If you choose to go here, be careful of the 5 star reviews because there was a sign to leave a 5 star review and get a free entree.

Having previously lived in Oakland’s Laurel District prior to Jo’s opening, I was highly motivated to return to the neighborhood and check it out. I frequently tend to over-order when establishing a baseline set of dishes, and tonight was no exception—though the excess was manageable. The dining room is remarkably comfortable and pleasant, showcasing a beautifully curated interior. The bar area is visually stunning; I would certainly enjoy having a cocktail there on a future visit. The front-of-house wait staff took exceptional care of our table and were all highly pleasant and accommodating.

The Timing & Service Cadence:
We started with the Crunchy Catfish Salad and the Scallop Kanom Krok. Following these starters, the remainder of our entrée selection materialized within a remarkably short time window. This flawless service cadence was highly appreciated; many contemporary restaurants consistently struggle with timing and kitchen execution, but Jo's had their sequencing down perfectly tonight.

Course-by-Course Technical Breakdown:

Crunchy Catfish Salad (Yum Pla Duk Foo): A spectacular way to begin the meal. The flavor profile is deeply savory, salty, and incredibly tasty without delivering an overpowering catfish taste at all. Flawlessly balanced.

Scallop Kanom Krok (Savory Coconut Cakes): These savory coconut-rice pastries emerged next. While pricey, they are an absolute revelation and entirely worth a try. The briny pop of the trout roe pairs perfectly with the rich, creamy coconut custard core, yielding a highly creative and texturally elite starter.

Kang Kua Massaman Curry: This was absolutely delicious and my undisputed favorite dish of the evening. This is the exact dish I think of when I think of premium Thai food. The curry base is incredibly comforting, and Jo's version stands as one of the finest I have ever tried in the Bay Area. The accompanying jasmine rice was executed perfectly to absorb the sauce, and I loved the deep, earthy colors present in the dish.

Stir-Fried Eggplant: Flawlessly cooked to yield soft, melt-in-your-mouth pieces of tasty goodness. There is a unique affinity between eggplant and Thai cuisine that completely elevates the dish, and Jo's recommended version delivers a remarkably hearty portion size.

Smoked Brisket Drunken Noodles (Pad Kee Mao): Spicy and delicious. While you can customize the spice level of your choosing on select dishes, this noodle dish carried a spectacular extra kick. The technical execution here is elite: the deeply smoky brisket transfers its charred flavor notes directly to the noodle strands in the most perfect way. The inclusion of a fried egg on top—allowing the rich, liquid gold taste and texture of the egg yolk to bleed into the noodles—completely elevated the entire composition.

Blue Sticky Rice with Mango Gelato: I truly wasn't sure what to expect here as I am typically not a huge fan of traditional mango sticky rice, but Jo's version is exceptionally good and departs completely from your standard version. The indigo butterfly pea flower sticky rice creates a great visual bedrock, and the contrasting textures present in the dessert complement each other perfectly. The flavor profile of the mango gelato was very good, especially when matched with the generous chunks of fresh mango and crunchy toppings. I would definitely order this again, although their alternative dessert—the fried ice cream—sounded amazing.

Final Verdict:
This has easily secured its placement as my new favorite East Bay Thai restaurant, and I am incredibly grateful it is situated only 10 minutes away. Give Jo's a try. It is an elite, high-utility addition to Oakland’s Laurel District.

top_reviews.content:
Stopped in after a salon appointment in Albany and found this to be a slightly more polished version of your typical Bay Area pho spot.

Food:
The fresh spring rolls (gỏi cuốn) were fresh and well-prepared. Peanut sauce was good, nothing standout, but definitely enjoyable.

I ordered the bún bò Huế, which included traditional congealed pork blood (huyết), always a plus for authenticity. The broth had good depth of flavor, but it lacked the expected spice. This dish should have a bit of heat, and that was missing.

The side veggies leaned heavily on bean sprouts (very typical here), but I would’ve preferred more shredded cabbage for balance.

Drinks:
Vietnamese iced coffee came out almost immediately, so it’s clearly pre-made. Efficient, but you do miss the traditional drip experience.

Service & Atmosphere:
Service is very fast, everything came out within minutes. After that, it’s pretty hands-off, so you’ll need to flag someone down if you need anything.

The space itself is nicer than most pho spots, and the uniformed staff gives it a slightly more put-together feel.

Overall:
Good food, very quick service, and a clean, comfortable space. Not exceptional, but a solid, reliable option if you’re in the area. Pricing is in line with current Bay Area averages, though it feels slightly high given the quick-service, pho-house style experience.

Pricing (my order):
•	Fresh spring rolls: $10.95
•	Bún bò Huế: $17.25
•	Vietnamese iced coffee: $6.95

3.75⭐️

The food is always Incredible and quality, the home-like atmosphere and the service is top notch. My family and I used to go here pretty consistently where they would cook and laugh over a hot grill.

Now the experience that brought me to this review are complementary to FOUR SERVERS. My friend from college is visiting me to tour the wonderful city of San Francisco. Korean cuisine is something we both cherish and love as we both grew up with it. We walk through the door to a busy atmosphere and a delicious aroma filling the air and sounds of people laughing and smiling. We were immediately  greeted, a table cleaned and we were sat within 2 minutes, menus in hand. To say that our first server was wonderful is an understatement. Right before our eyes, like a close up magic trick, an array of snacking items appeared in front of us. Kimchi, seaweed, fish cakes, spicy salty dried fish, a spicy paste, lettuce, cucumber and of course rice. After some heavy discussion of what to get, ( because everything sounds so good ) we ultimately decided on kalbi and bulgolgi.  then 30 seconds later it appears in front of us. Me personally, I never do the cooking at kbbq so I'm inexperienced, and my friend isn't experienced in cooking either. The second server can somehow tell we're in a pinch of struggle and COOKS THE FIRST ROUND FOR US. endsuring the meat is cooked and flavorful and even teaches us how to do it. She made sure our plates never emptied, that we were smiling and fed, and our glasses were always full. My friend and I felt so pampered to the point we thought she was going to tuck us into bed and kiss us goodnight. Our third server is the hot coals guy. This man made sure our grill was hot and the heat was distributed evening and replaced the grill consistently too.

( I know what your thinking, the flavor on the grill!! Noooo!!!!      Listen, the flavor in the marinade is so sticky that if you don't replace it enough, you're just losing your meat to the grill and that's like 3$ you're not eating, just trust them).

The last server made sure we were content with our meal and closed us out . At the end we were stuffed, but were given a complimentary kimchi tofu soup that was so good I genuinely teared up from the love of the flavor. This was a meal of a life time and my friend and I talked about it for hours after we left. He said that it was the best first bite he had ever taken and he would come back just for seat at this lovely establishment.

Thank you so much for all that you do, your food is Cherished.

top_reviews.content: I’m rating Gioia five stars on the pizza. I love it. Love it. And I love the style which is the New York style way. You order your slices which are pre made pies. Then they heat them in the oven which makes them hot and crispy. Several topping choices to choose. No indoor seating. Other than a bench there’s really no outdoor seating either. But the pizza is so good. And it’s nice, shady outside. Decent amount of street parking.

YUM. I’m so happy to have found this spot. This is some of the best pizza I’ve ever had, and I’m a former New Yorker.

The crust is perfectly chewy and the toppings are absolutely delicious. Our favorite is the Julian, which I’m pretty sure is perfect. The cheese and sausage are so yummy and they are generous with the garlic and lacinato kale. So delicious and dare I say healthy too?

The fact that you can get most of their specialty pizzas by the slice is the cherry on top and reminds me of my days in nyc, but pizza this good was even hard to come by there.

Tucked into the side of your average street in Berkeley is the best pizza we’ve had in the Bay Area. GIOIA is serving up some VERY good pizza out of what feels like a hole in the wall. Beware that parking may be hard to find as it’s right off the street although there is a lot just down the road. The inside is very bare bones, which in this case is a good sign. The smell of the oven and dough just hits you once you step in and it’s fantastic. Ordering was quick and easy and the slices are priced a bit high but for the quality of pizza we’d say it was worth it. We got some classic slices and also their fungi slice. From ordering to eating it took about 5-10 minutes despite a few people ahead of us so it was relatively quick.

And now time to try it… man was it good. It’s clearly a good representation of NY style. The crust is firm and crunchy but the pizza has a nice flop to it. The cheese is tasty with a good sauce under it too. The fungi also popped with flavor from the mushrooms, parsley, and olive oil; just a great series of slices. The best place to eat it is probably the bench seating they have outside but it may be full as a heads up. As far as we see it, GIOIA is a must stop in Berkeley. It came very highly recommended and was devoured in less than 5 minutes. We almost wish we didn’t have plans to eat later that day because we could’ve eaten 2 more slices each then and there. This is as close to true NYC style pizza as you can get outside of NYC.

There is the original location in Berkeley and then another location in Hayes Valley in San Francisco. We passed it all the time so we thought we would come in and try it. They are crust is incredible! Nine out of 10 in that category. They have a very interesting sauce, it’s almost on the edge of a pasta sauce, but not quite. I think honestly if they slightly changed up their sauce, the pizza would be better. If you like cheese on your pizza, this is the place to go because they’re pretty heavy handed on the cheese. Overall, we liked it and we would try different slices, but it is not our absolute favorite pizza in the bay area. We tried the margarita, so we haven’t tried all of the different slices and flavors that they offer. So we’ll have to go back and see how the others compare. Thus far, we would give it a solid 7/10.

This spot has been saved on my bookmarks for a while. Luckily I had a training nearby and had a chance to try it.

The space is small with some seating right in front of this business. The lines can rack up during lunch so far ready. They're fairly quick with the order. A co-worker in front of me recommended their avacado salad and Julian pizza. Both were delicious! The total came out to -$23 plus tip, which seems to be an average for lunch these days.

The pizza had a perfectly cooked thin crust. The dough was so sparkly doughy and stretchy with the right amount of firmness on the bottom of the crust. The toppings (kale, sausage, mozerlla cheese, garlic..)Jwent well together too with a fair amount dispersed on the slice.

The salad was filling. I probably didn't need to get the pizza. It was well balanced with farro, avacado, golden raisins, and almond. The vinaigrette was also a nice balance (you don't need much).

Go check them out!

The PPQ Beef Noodle House – “Pho Phu Quoc(富国牛肉粉)”  located on north side of Irving at 19th

south and the quantity is less and less imhv. 😔 }
As seasoned San Franciscans we know quality of a bowl of Vietnamese rice noodle aka “phở bò - beef”
or “phở gà -chicken” depends on the genuineness of its rich broth from real chicken or beef bone and/or oxtail, which is rare in The City nowadays, as well as the freshness and abundance of other ingredients including premium meat and aromatics such as yellow onions, shallots, ginger, bean sprouts and  rau thơm (basil, mint, and cilantro.) My usual order at PPQ is #1 Phở Đặc Biệt which would cost me less than $17 plus a nice tip.

PPQ Phu Quoc is my pho restaurant of choice in the Sunset in comparison with others including Kevin’s across street and the other two on the east side of Irving one called Perrilla and the other I forgot the name but it sounds like a massage parlor.😂
Also, PPQ Phu Quoc seating is much more comfortable not like chow hall seating at Kevin’s or Santung or Yuanbao Jiaozi with little or no privacy.

However, I am gonna check out the other popular  pho place called Viet Quan Vietnamese Noodle House located on Taraval at the corner of 28th Avenue to write a candid review.

In sum, instead of paying almost $2 for one filthy
pork meat dumpling which is not only not filling but also can arguably entice  you for the runs. So you should seriously consider other options available in the Sunset for better portion and price.

front a popular restaurant in internet era doesn’t always equates to good quality. C'est la vie 😉

The five spice chicken garlic noodles $15.45 were great, as usual. Service was a bit lacking with the rookie.

Good job PPQ staff. My bill was $15 with tax and tip.

top_reviews.content:
Tonight, we dined at Firenze By Night, a cozy Italian gem in San Francisco's North Beach neighborhood, and it was nothing short of spectacular during our Dec 2024 visit.
* Caesar Salad: Absolutely perfect! The greens were crisp, the croutons were perfectly crunchy, and the dressing was balanced with just the right tang and creaminess.
* Alfredo Pasta with Jumbo Prawns: Creamy, rich, and indulgent. The jumbo prawns were cooked to perfection, adding a fresh and luxurious touch to the dish.
* Fettuccine Pesto with Chicken: This was, without a doubt, the best pesto I've ever tasted. The vibrant basil flavor, paired with tender chicken and perfectly cooked fettuccine, made it unforgettable.
* Gnocchi: Light, pillowy, and coated in a delicious sauce--this award-winning dish lived up to its reputation.
* Bread with Olive Oil and Olive Paste: The olive oil itself was great, but the olive paste served with it was out of this world! It added an intense, savory richness that elevated the bread to another level.

The ambiance was warm and inviting, with a classic Italian charm, and the service was friendly and attentive throughout the evening. However, the place can get loud if there are too many large parties, which might affect the overall experience for some diners.

Overall, Firenze By Night delivered an exceptional dining experience. From the unforgettable pesto to the incredible olive paste, this is a must-visit spot for authentic Italian cuisine in San Francisco. Highly recommend!

A stellar neighborhood lasangeria serving a good variety of styles at excellent an price for the portion!

Interior seating is severely limited, but there's plenty of outdoor seating and lasanga makes a great takeout dish if you live nearby.

They're also next door to deceptively massive board game store and, at least the night I went, partnered together to run food into the game shop if you wanted to dine while you played.

Drink selections are a bit limited, but there's a few wines, sodas, and a number of NA wine/beer.
