Also had salad, imported meats and cheeses, and grilled veggies.  The two lasagnas were butternut squash and abruzzo.  Some of the best I ever had.  It will be one dinner to remember!

We came to dine in. They only offer “take out style dining” so your meal comes packaged and you use plastic utensils. The lasagna I heard was good. I am lactose intolerant and asked what was best on the menu given my restriction. The only meal they can offer is the salad with no cheese. I asked if there was a simple pasta and was told “I don’t feel comfortable serving that without cheese.”  I should have just left but wanted my partner to try the lasagna as the opening hours are so strict.

My salad was just acceptable. At least the chicken came freshly grilled, but the salad dressing portion was inadequate if we were going to do take out. It was greens, tomatoes and chicken. I had to ask for additional dressing.

Surprised that they do not offer a vegan pasta option given this is San Francisco. I’m glad they are doing well in the neighborhood but I would most definitely not come back.

name: Commis
address: 3859 Piedmont Ave, Oakland, CA 94611, United States

google.name: Commis
google.address: 3859 Piedmont Ave, Oakland, CA 94611, United States
google.description: Open-kitchen experiments with unique ingredients to craft inspired New American fixed-price dinners.

top_reviews.content:
Celebrated my husband’s birthday here and it turned out to be one of the most enjoyable dinners we’ve had in a long time.

The service stood out from the moment we sat down. Fresh cutlery for every course, the table cleared and tidied between dishes, and the staff walked us through the ingredients and story behind each plate. The 20% service charge felt completely earned.

The menu blends Thai, Chinese, Japanese, and Northern California influences — Thai-style sour and spicy notes, fresh oysters and herbs, Chinese pork meatballs, duck glazed with Shaoxing wine and soy, a Japanese-inspired beef rice — all reflecting the chef’s Chinese-Thai roots. The flavors really suit an Asian palate, and the portions are generous. I thought the snapper was the grand finale, but course after course kept coming until we were completely full! The rose ice cream at the end was unforgettable — floral, light, and not too sweet.

And the plating is genuinely art. The chef loves pairing dishes with flowers: delicate blossoms over the sashimi, a dew-covered mini lotus leaf resting on the meatballs. Every dish was a feast for the eyes.

Food, plating, service — all at a Michelin two-star level, and at around $279 per person before tax it almost feels like a deal. Location is in downtown Oakland with public parking a 2-minute walk away (I’d recommend the garage over street parking). Highly recommend!

Amazing 12 course meal with 5 courses of appetizers, 4 mains, and 3 dessert courses. I was stuffed at the end. All the dishes were creative, artistic and delicious! The menu changes every month, so I hope to come again!

My only prior experience with Commis' culinary output was tracking their takeout format during the pandemic, making this my first opportunity to witness the menu executed in its native environment.

Arrived slightly behind schedule due to a minor orientation error on approach from the west. The prominent exterior 'Commis' signage is actually positioned over a secondary doorway—blocked by a rope and obscured by a black curtain—which I mistakenly flagged as the threshold. After waiting until 5:06 PM, I stepped further east down the sidewalk to discover the actual entrance. Once inside, check-in was seamless. I was engineered into a stunning table boasting an uncompromised, direct line of sight into the kitchen —an ideal vantage point for observation. For those driving, district parking is highly efficient; there is an open lot a three-minute walk away completely integrated with the ParkMobile app.

The dining room operates with high aesthetic intent. The table setting is beautifully minimalist, accented by fresh floral arrangements. Ambient audio consists of low-profile, rhythmic electronic beats without discernible tracking, allowing the focus to remain on the room’s acoustics. Notable property asset: the restroom features neatly folded, reusable linen cloths, a detail I always inspect and appreciate.

The beverage program opened strong with a well-balanced cocktail featuring a flawless, hyper-clarified ice block cleanly monogrammed with the house branding.

Plating geometry across the board was visually stunning. Certain courses were deployed using a strict three-point presentation matrix on the table, showing deliberate service choreography.

The clear peak of the engineering here is their legendary signature dish: the slow-poached egg yolk resting in a malted cream base with smoked dates and crisp alliums. It is a brilliant study in texture—velvety, rich, and profoundly comforting. This singular dish justifies the entire booking.

From an operational standpoint, the pacing of this meal was exceptional—easily ranking in the top five dining experiences I have tracked globally. The kitchen and floor staff maintained a hyper-focused, synchronized posture throughout the multi-hour window. Service movements were fluid, deliberate, and entirely free of friction.

Crucially, the clearing of empty plates was immediate, and successive courses materialized without a single dead gap. Staff check-ins were frequent but entirely non-invasive. This baseline pace never wavered, holding perfectly steady even as the dining room reached peak capacity later in the evening. A masterfully managed system.

Dined here in July 2026. Overall a decent experience, but quite underwhelming compared to the other Michelin 2 stars in the Bay Area. Not too keen on coming back unfortunately
+/- The menu was just ok. The highlight was the chef’s special—slow poached egg yolk. The white corn, pork belly, and drunken hen were also delicious. The rest was either decent or downright bad
- Added the caviar supplement, but it was a waste of stomach space—definitely wouldn’t recommend
+/- Decent service and interior decoration

The service was outstanding, thank you Israel and team. The food, pacing, and atmosphere was phenomenal. It was the best fine dining experience I have ever had. What made it the most special was the sommelier, Andrew. The wine pairings were so good, unique, flavorful, and exciting!!! I seriously was blown away. Thank you for a great evening and birthday celebration.

top_reviews.content: I am reviewing as I am finishing my meal, just in case I forget to review later. This place has phenomenal pastas, and I can’t believe the one I am eating is gluten-free, besides being completely vegan. The ambiance is nice and I would recommend this place to anyone looking for not just healthy, but tasty options. Ordered the Arnold Palmer mocktail which is good too.

**UPDATE**

The vegan pasta is fantastic: rich, comforting, with just a touch of heat. It’s exactly the kind of dish that reminds you vegan food can be every bit as satisfying as traditional comfort food.

Unfortunately, brunch was a very different experience. The vegan eggs came with potatoes, very sweet squash mixed into the scramble (squash and potatoes was a mushy texture overload) ketchup with a hint of curry, and a side salad with dressing so light I could barely tell it was there. I love eggs, and this had all the ingredients to become a favorite brunch dish, but it just didn’t come together and wasn’t a satisfying meal.

I also tried the Chimichurri Burger. The combination of grilled onions, peppers, greens, crunchy potato sticks, and chimichurri is genuinely creative and delicious. The bun, however, tasted several days old: dry, dense, and stale. Instead of absorbing the sauces and bringing everything together, it did the exact opposite.

I was going to order the French toast but decided to make it at home instead: fresh challah or brioche, vanilla bean, cinnamon, a pinch of salt, a splash of cream, maple syrup, and fresh berries. It may take more effort, but after this brunch experience I wasn’t willing to take the risk.

—————————————————————
Orecchiette with spicy sausage arrabbiata (Beyond Italian sausage, coconut parmesan, basil) was excellent - perfect level of heat. I couldn’t even tell it was chickpea pasta, and the vegan sausage didn’t cause any heaviness or heartburn.

The avocado chocolate ganache was also great. The whipped cream was light and delicious, and the berries with toasted almonds balanced the richness nicely. I probably wouldn’t order it again only because I prefer milk chocolate.

Portions are modest, set expectations accordingly.

Unfortunately my mom passed away a few years ago, but she would still frequently eat here up until she passed. My dad still comes here fairly often, as it's still pretty reasonably priced, reliable food quality and because it's easy for him to either dine in or get it to-go (he has mobility issues).

I'm a pretty boring, plain Jane kinda person in terms of my taste buds (Unfortunately 😋). So I've always been partial to getting a grilled cheese or a cheeseburger, fries and milkshake or I used to occasionally get root beer floats. I can't remember if they ever offered French dips or if I'm thinking of another diner. Their food has always maintained the same and is pretty much just a  good ole standard diner type of establishment. During all the years/decades I've been coming here I don't ever recall ever encountering any issues with the food, service or atmosphere.

In terms of atmosphere, it's pretty much looked the same for as long as I can remember. Maybe just a few small upgrades to the tables and such over the years.
So for the snooty out-of-towner Karen who was whining about it bring "dirty" ina recent review....PLEASE! 🙄 It's never, ever been a "dirty" or gross restaurant and has always been pretty well maintained. Some might consider it to be a little outdated but that's pretty typical for most diners and restaurants like the Tennessee Grill. I think that's part of the charm (and nostalgia) in most cases anyways?

The staff and service have always been very welcoming, friendly, attentive and polite! Never, ever had any issues whatsoever with both the waitresses and cook(s).

For how friggin expensive everything is these days, I was pleasantly surprised to see their prices are still fair and consistent! And I feel it's pretty fair for what you get, depending on what you order. I don't think a lot of people would still keep coming here years/decades if it wasn't an overall consistent and welcoming atmosphere.

I'm so happy it's still open and running after all these years/decades! ESPECIALLY since SO many similar rewards and diners had to close their doors during or after the pandemic.

Long live the Tennessee Grill! A true,  classic OG diner and historic SF gem!

name: Kitchen Story Oakland
address: 5422 College Ave, Oakland, CA 94618, United States

google.name: Kitchen Story Oakland

top_reviews.content:
This was a cute restaurant! The prices were reasonable (for the bay).
While I'm not a coffee drinker, my partner rather enjoyed it and described it as strong. I am a tea drinker however, and while the tea was good, I rather wished there was a better way of serving it, as the hot water in the clay tea cup made for rapidly cooling tea before it could steep :/

The service wasn't BAD persay, but could have been a bit more streamlined, as the outside tables were small. It seemed that there wasn't one food runner over seeing specific sections, so our order was initially placed on another customers table.

The bulgogi bowl was good but a bit on the sweet side. I had the Tater Tot Poutine and I feel they fell a bit short. When I think poutine, I'm thinking cheese curds. In fact, one of the reasons I chose this place was because I was very excited to see what an Asian influence on poutine looked like. Seeing my food arrive with no curds, I sent it back because I was sure something was missing. Alas, no, the cotija cheese was the cheese for this dish. I would have rather they used queso fresco instead. It doesn't have a strong flavor and would have satisfied my cheese curd craving </3 That being said, it still slapped.

The star of the show was the Millionaire's Bacon. The cuts were thick, flavorful, creamy (?) and almost melted in my mouth. I won't lie, it's heavily influencing my review.

I wish the outside tables were a bit more spaced, as I felt cramped.

I came here during a weekday for brunch. That is probably the best time to come due to street parking filling up fast.
To drink, I had the raspberry lemonade. This is easily 5/5. Perfect blend of sweetness & tartness.
For an appetizer we got the popcorn chicken & Korean FC. My favorite was the popcorn chicken it was 5/5 and I loved that they added actual popcorn. The Korean FC was okay 3/5.
The Mac N Cheese sounded very interesting, however, it fell flat. It was dry and not cheesy. I would rate it 2/5. We got the Chicken & Story Burger. The Chicken Burger 4/5 was definitely better than the Story Burger 2/5. The Story Burger was lacking in flavor. The potatoes wedges were really good though. Not pictured was the millionaire bacon 5/5. It was so good and I would love to try the BLT with millionaire bacon.
Lastly, we got the Lemon Ricotta Pancake 1/5 it was bitter and the second pancake under the first was burnt. We also got the Mascarpone Stuffed Deep Fried French Toast which was 100/5. Every bite was amazing. Would definitely come back again for that dish alone. Other than that, a lot of the dishes fell flat for me but the presentation of the food was beautiful and service was good as well.

This has easily become one of my favorite brunch spots in Oakland. I usually come with my dog, and one thing I really appreciate is how consistently warm and welcoming the manager and servers are :)

The menu has a Korean-inspired take on brunch, and I almost always order the Blackstone Benedict and the Lemon Ricotta Pancakes.

The Blackstone Benedict is probably my favorite savory dish here. The combination of bacon, asparagus, bread, and hollandaise just works, the richness from the sauce, the saltiness of the bacon, and the freshness of the asparagus are really well balanced. I will say that on a few visits, the sauce had a slightly eggy aroma that I wasn’t crazy about. It’s pretty subtle and hasn’t stopped me from ordering it :-)

As for the pancakes, I’ve tried a few of the options, and the Lemon Ricotta is easily the standout for me. The pancakes are incredibly soft and fluffy, with just enough lemon to brighten everything up without tasting overly citrusy. The ricotta adds this subtle creaminess and richness that makes them feel a little more special than your standard brunch pancakes.

Great food, genuinely kind service, and very dog-friendly, which, for me, is always a plus :-)

Phenomenal brunch flavors are worth the wait (and sore bum)!

Kitchen Story is an epic brunch spot. If you're planning a weekend visit, I definitely recommend making a reservation, or be prepared for a bit of a wait.

I met a friend here for Sunday brunch, and we ordered an assortment of plates and beverages to share. Everything was delicious and repeatable, but here's my order of personal preference for the food:

Korean FC Wings: Crispy, flavorful, and absolutely standout.

Lemon Ricotta Pancakes: Perfectly fluffy, and bright flavors on perfectly prepared pancakes.

Goji Bowl: A solid, satisfying savory option.

For beverages, the Ube Latte and the Millionaire's Bloody Mary were the stars of the show. Their house coffee and unsweetened passion fruit iced tea were good, but fairly standard.

My only suggestion for management would be to invest in more comfortable seating, but honestly, it was worth the sore bum to enjoy all those delicious flavors! I will definitely be returning and recommending to friends.

Wanted to try something different for Sunday brunch. The noodles with the egg, bacon and pork had just enough savory flavor to knock your socks off. The service was ok. The waiter forgot to process my order so I had to ask about my food after watching other people around me get seated and served before myself. He was apologetic and did comp my meal so he did make it right. Just disappointed because the food was soooo good.

top_reviews.content: I don't care where in San Fran you're staying or how you get here, but every vegan NEEDS to come and experience Cybelle's FULL plant-based menu. I had to come a second time to explore more of the menu. As a 12 year vegan, this is by far the biggest vegan menu in a undedicated restaurant I've seen. The garlic knots taste just like Domino's but without the fast food feeling or aftertaste. The mozzarella sticks are DEAD ON with Sonic's (just no cheese stretch). The texture and taste of the chicken wings are FANTASTIC. Loaded fries was jam packed with flavor. This is a must stop in San Fran!

My favorite neighborhood pizza place. If I'm by myself I order two monster slices: one Omni Delite and one Cheese ($2 cheaper) and I take home half of each for another meal./ Beignets are delicious and can come with different flavors of dipping "butter." The plain ones made with vegan cheesecake are my favorite./ The owner and wait staff are friendly and personable (ex. "How are your parents?").

Best girl dinner spot ever 💖! Very carb-heavy, cheesy, comfort food. Great for treating yourself post breakup 🫩 are there any good men in this city?!?

Anyways… the vegan golden dragon pizza is very good. It has this decadent ooeygooey 🤤 cheese that I’ve never experienced before! The impossible loaded fries had a similar flavor profile to the pizza, both had a strong bbq flavor, so stick to one! Garlic knots were amazingly huge and delicious. Would not recommend the gnocchi, it was a bit starchy 😮‍💨.

Overall, would return, but be cautious that many of the dishes are carb and oil-heavy. Order accordingly! 🤓☝️

4.5 stars. As a vegan of 9 years I have to say this is the best pepperoni pizza I’ve ever had! Really amazing. The wings are okay, not really worth it in my opinion because they are damn expensive and they’re a little too mushy and wet inside. But the flavors are great. The dipping sauces are SO yummy!
The vibe is nice here. I would come back for the pizza for sure but only to splurge once in a while because it is so expensive!

The atmosphere loved it. Service was amazing! The Food Was Top Tier! I had the deep pizza with garlic and a garlic pizza. I cant wait to return to san francisco to come back here. This place should have been packed! Weekdays I know people are working. 10/10 best garlic pizza!

top_reviews.content: Beautiful family owned restaurant with authentic dishes. In particular the kale chaat, daal, garlic naan, momos and paneer tikka masala were amazing. The service is great and reminds you of being treated like family. Highly recommend!!

The combination of cultural food here is great. Some of the best Indian food I've ever had combined with some unique items from Nepal such as dumplings that seem similar to something you would find at a dim sum restaurant. Overall, the food was outstanding, including high quality sag lamb and great naan bread too.
This is a family restaurant and clearly the people running it care very deeply about providing great service and great food.
Prices are very reasonable too. We had an appetizer, two main courses, and one drink each for a total of $68 before tip.

This is some of the best Indian food I’ve had in the Bay Area. They took our table late, right before closing even though it probably meant they had to stay a little later.  I had the apricot curry and it was amazing.  Their naan is the best I’ve ever had - even just their plain naan with butter is a reason to go. The decor and ambiance is nice, a great experience overall.  10/10 recommend!
The apricot chicken is unique and delicious! I loved all the curry-ish dishes I got to taste (curry, tikka masala or korma). Service was attentive with complimentary papadum & dips.

Started out with papadam, serves with the usual condiments.  Crispy and good, quite a few pieces.  Then we shared Chicken Korma with gluten free naan.  This was probably the best gluten free naan I've had.  Not quite the same as wheat but enjoyable non the less.  The Korma was delish. Added some Raita and couldn't ask for more.

Great, authentic food. Homemade pasta. LARGE portions--prepare to share or take some home. Only suggestion is change pop music out for Italian tracks: Perche' no? Good service. It's an order and take to table situation, self serve. Can order ahead, pick up, and eat in, if desired.

Just like the one in San Francisco, this delicious pasta shop offers a mix & match option to choose a sauce and then a type of pasta. They are fast and delicious.

Amazing beet gnocchi with mushroom sauce yesterday! Oh, baby! Gnocchi was the Perfect Consistency and the sauce? Holy Toledo, Batman! So frigging good that my mouth and stomach are still saying “thank you very much!” Today!! Price was crazy reasonable and service was great (Thank you, Tomas).
I love this place.

top_reviews.content:
Wow, exceptional taste for such a good value.

We loved all the tomato dishes.

We were seated outside and still quite warm (granted, during a "Bay Area summer").

Minus one star for lots of mix ups with our dietary restrictions and who ordered which dish, but that was easily fixed.

Looking forward to coming back!

Excellent food, great vibes, fair prices!

We did the latest Prix Fixe menu, which changes roughly monthly for seasonality.

The waiters were fun, service was fast, we got a seat for just us two on Friday night, and the food was just AWESOME.

Focaccia with olive tapenade slapped super hard, and both salad / soup we had for starters were awesome.
The braized pork in fresh pasta was unctuous and filling.
The panna cotta was my favorite dessert.

We spent $100 each for two full courses, plus scallops to share, without alcohol (but got one NA drink).

Had a fantastic anniversary dinner at MAMA Oakland. The food is fresh, flavorful and clearly made with care. While it’s Italian, it has a modern spin and beautiful presentation. We had the entire Restaurant week menu and has only led us to come back again. Its atmosphere is warm and a perfect spot for dinner with friends or a relaxed date. Staff is welcoming and attentive (big shout out to Chris - restaurant manager, terrific guy who makes you feel at home) and the whole place has that comfortable neighborhood restaurant feel. You will want to come back for more. Give it a go… and thanks for an amazing experience MAMA staff!

Setting: Outdoor Patio / Parklet Dining

The Damage: ~$43 per person (Base 3-Course Prix Fixe Menu)

The Vibe: High-energy neighborhood Italian gem with genuinely warm service.

The Starters: Comfort on a plate
House-Baked Focaccia & Accompaniments: ($6 add-on). This is an absolute must-order for a proper Bay Area restaurant review. The bread features a beautifully airy, high-hydration crumb with massive interior pockets that practically beg to sponge up olive oil. The crust delivers a loud, satisfying crunch. It's served with a velvety whipped tallow butter and a sharp, acidic caper-and-herb relish that cuts through the richness instantly.

Pork & Beef Meatballs: A total standout on the Oakland food scene. They feature an excellent outer sear that locks in an incredibly soft, moist, and loose interior grind. Pillowed under a generous snowcap of freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano, they sit in a vibrant, slow-simmered tomato marinara that achieves absolute balance. Frankly, I could pull up a chair, order just the meatballs and the focaccia, and walk away completely satisfied.

Sweet Corn Soup: Delivered with a tableside pour directly onto a layered mosaic of whole sweet corn kernels, smoky bacon lardons, and a clean swirl of crème fraîche. It’s a flawless emulsion—perfectly highlighting the natural sugars of summer corn while utilizing a sharp undercurrent of chive oil to balance the creaminess.

Summer Squash Carpaccio: Spring on a plate. Shaved mandolin-thin, the green and yellow squash discs remain ultra-fresh and crisp, showing zero signs of raw moisture weeping. Beautifully plated with fragile squash blossoms and a shower of salty ricotta salata, the entire dish is tied together by the distinct, buttery crunch of toasted pine nuts.

The Pastas: Why This Node Dominates the East Bay
Rigatoni with Mama's Sugo
Nothing in the local grid touches this long-braised meat base; it justifies a trip to Grand Avenue on its own merit for anyone hunting for the best pasta in Oakland. The house-extruded rigatoni features excellent, distinct ridges that act as a mechanical lock for the rich beef and pork sugo. The ragu is deeply comforting, rich, and consistent—the kind of pasta that forces a head-shake of absolute validation with every single bite.

Saffron Cavatelli with Calabrian Sausage
A truly spectacular plate. The hand-rolled cavatelli delivers a dense, perfectly calibrated al dente chew that frames the savory, milder pork sausage crumbles seamlessly. The addition of tender, charred broccolini on top introduces a fresh, vibrant crunch, while the residual spiced pork oil finishes the dish with spectacular depth.

The Sweet Finish
Plum Crostata with Ricotta Orange Gelato: One of the finest desserts I've encountered here. The presentation is pristine, featuring concentric layers of vibrant, tart plum slices resting on a flaky pastry base boasting a rich, buttery flavor profile. The gelato arrives at a dense, sub-zero temperature, creating a smooth, slow-melting sauce layer as it bleeds into the accompanying thyme honey.

Chocolate Devil's Food Cake: A chocolate lover's absolute dream. Slicing the sponge exposes an incredibly tender, open cell structure that retains its moisture perfectly along the lower base. The rich cocoa depth is front and center, balanced beautifully by dense chocolate buttercream and a sharp, pooling Amarena cherry glaze.

The Verdict: 5/5 Stars
At just under $43 per person for the core three courses, the price-to-value ratio at Mama Oakland is practically unmatched for East Bay fine dining. The outdoor patio layout provides plenty of space, a relaxed evening breeze, and a highly attentive, friendly service staff. It completely solidifies its status as an elite local institution for a casual date night, and being only a 10-minute drive away, I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

This may be the greatest restaurant in the entire world! You wouldn’t know it just by walking or driving by, but this Michelin star establishment has some of the best food in the entire world! And, it’s a three course meal, but it is extremely accessible in terms of price. The staff are incredible, and the environment is very welcoming and cozy. We literally go here to celebrate every major event in our lives (anniversaries, birthdays, you name it). Don’t sleep on MAMA!

top_reviews.content:
This noodle place is the real deal! The couple running the restaurant are the absolute sweetest. They were so patient with us, taking their time to explain the menu items and give great recommendations.

I ordered the #2 (wonton noodle soup) and it was absolutely delicious plus the portion size was great. I also had the Thai iced tea, which was perfection because it wasn’t overly sweet, just the way I like it. Exceptional food and even better hospitality. We will definitely be back!

Was craving some Teochew/Cambodian-style dry noodle and this place hit the spot. The owners were incredibly nice and there was a sweet elderly couple helping out around the restaurant.

Make the trip out here; it’s worth it.
My go-to noodle place in the city. Their 海记什锦 is the one. I really like their rice noodle (河粉）。It’s wide and looks homemade to me. The owner and staff are all very friendly.

I've been here several times and they are extremely consistent in taste and portion size. Prices are reasonable for the portions you get and the service is always very efficient and friendly. Sure it's messy in the TL, but the restaurant is a homey spot with lots of customers and comfortable on the inside.

Things I've ordered:
House special ho fun (soup and dry) - this is the must order here in my opinion, it is full of toppings over the noodles (shrimp, char siew, pork slices, ground pork, chicken strips, fish cakes, beef balls, bean sprouts, pork liver if you want it). I've only gotten the rice noodle version and like it dry with soup on the side. It is well seasoned on its own but you can jazz it up with pickled jalapenos and other sauces that they provide on the table. The fried garlic oil they put in it is delicious and I've never regretted ordering this.
Golden fried fish cakes - about 3 whole fishcakes in each order, cut into half and fried to golden perfection. They are a little greasy but tasty with a nice bounce, they taste great dipped in the hoisin sauce. Served with pickled vegetables on the side (cucumber and carrot) which cuts through the grease perfectly.
Wonton soup - the wontons are just ok, there's no shrimp in it that I could discern and is mostly just wrapper and ground pork. It's seasoned well and comes in the same soup that they serve with the house special noodles.
Beef stew ho fun - this was more soupy than stewy in my opinion, with a strong tomato flavor. The beef was alright and pretty chewy and tough, it would have been nice if they had stewed the meat a little longer to get it nice and soft. The rice noodles don't come with anything else except beef and bean sprouts. It's an ok option but I would opt for the house noodles over this anytime.

The crowds here seem inconsistent, I had to wait once for over 20 mins for a table and it was packed to the gills, and other times I got a table right away and there were a decent number of customers but no wait. The tables turn over quickly though since people are here to eat, not sit around for hours.
Braised Duck Leg Egg Noodle Soup(Dry) was delicious. Fast service. Homemade Soybean drink was good too.

top_reviews.content: Food was good especially the home fries.  Very crunchy. The pancakes were yummy. Good size portions. Server was friendly and always top off my coffee☺️would come here again. Spend about 35.00 per person including tax and tip.

We ordered chocolate chip pancakes, crispy home fries, & a side salad. And wow! Everything was amazing. The pancakes were pillowy soft, & buttery. The hash-browns were  perfect & the salad was way bigger than expected (in a good way!) and delicious. If you’re looking for big portions & great food this is your place!

I arrived around 10:15 a.m. on a Monday and was seated right away without any wait. By the time I left around 11:00, there was a small line forming, so arriving earlier seems like a good idea.

The service was excellent throughout my meal. My servers were friendly, attentive, and quick with everything. I especially appreciated that my coffee was refilled regularly without having to ask.

I ordered the Ube Pancakes. They came out quite quick and the portion was huge. I left stuffed and still couldn't finish the entire plate. The ube flavour came through in every bite without being overwhelming, and the grilled banana was a great addition that complemented the pancakes nicely.

Overall, it was an awesome breakfast with generous portions, great service, and delicious food.

One of if not the best breakfast/brunch spots in SF. The waitstaff here are so friendly and kind and the food is absolutely amazing. Their pancakes and breakfast options are great but the huevos rancheros and chilequiles are divine. I suggest coming on a weekday if you can as it gets crazy busy during the weekend.

A simple, small cafe located in the busy retail area of popular Noe Valley on 24th Street.  The three of us ate brunch there the day after Christmas around 10:30. We waited 10 minutes for a table, but the table looked directly into the open doorway of the kitchen and the back of the grill cook. To the credit of the two stressed yet accommodating servers, when we saw a better table open up, they relocated us at our request. Portions are generous, so we ordered two entrees for our party. The Pancake Boy Plate ($25) with Lemon Ricotta Pancakes, 2 sunny-side up eggs and pork patty and Pb’s Burger ($20) with French Fries. We noticed tables were served their food one entree at a time rather than all entrees being served together to the entire dining party resulting in diners eating in shifts. Thankfully that didn’t happen to us. The Lemon Ricotta Pancakes were five-star. The best in SF. The Burger was big but in this case bigger doesn’t make it better. It was ordinary. The French Fries looked promising. They were crispy but were not seasoned. There was no taste. We’ll definitely be back for the pancakes and the cafe offers many varieties.

top_reviews.content:
Ordered takeout from Kitava while visiting San Francisco and had a good experience overall.

As someone with celiac disease, I really appreciated having another dedicated gluten-free option available, especially one that also focuses on healthier ingredients. We ordered from the Mission Street location through a delivery app, and everything arrived correctly and packaged well.

The food itself was good, fresh, and satisfying. Nothing wildly over-the-top or extravagant, but definitely solid food that I’d happily order again. Most importantly, I didn’t get sick afterward, which always makes a huge difference when traveling with celiac.

Overall, a reliable gluten-free option that I’d absolutely keep in rotation when visiting the area again.

Warning! Not located in a great area of the city! However, the food was amazing! We had friendly and fast service. Love that everything is gluten and dairy free! Would definitely door dash next time though.

I recently dined at Kitava in San Francisco’s Mission District, and it was an absolute game-changer! I ordered the BYO bowl with Paprika Chicken and the Farmers Green Bowl, and both were bursting with fresh, vibrant flavors. The chicken was perfectly seasoned with a smoky paprika kick, tender and juicy, while the Farmers Green Bowl was a colorful mix of crisp greens. Every bite felt nourishing yet indulgent, which is hard to pull off!
What really sets Kitava apart is their commitment to clean eating—100% free of seed oils, gluten, dairy, and other common allergens, which makes it a haven for anyone with dietary restrictions or just looking for real, wholesome food. The fact that they avoid seed oils entirely is a huge plus, as it’s rare to find a spot that prioritizes such high-quality, health-conscious ingredients without sacrificing taste. The service was friendly and quick, and the casual, clean vibe of the place made it a perfect spot for a feel-good meal. I’m already looking forward to my next visit—Kitava is a must-try gem in the Mission! Five stars all the way

Holy cow! This place is delicious. I just moved from Hawaii so was looking for somewhere yummy with plantains and I’m so glad this popped up. I actually ordered three of their signature bowls and added chicken and avocado and they were all amazing!! Just found my new local staple!

For years I have had the utmost respect for Kitava for their commitment to making healthy food accessible to the community with their $7 “community bowl” and commitment to feeding the people at a fair price (especially considering they took over a McDonalds that provided unhealthy but affordable food to original neighborhood). I’ve also heard they sometimes gave food to unhoused people in need for even cheaper than $7 which is amazing. I was disappointed to be told today by the cashier that they don’t do the $7 community bowl anymore. Hopefully it was just a misunderstanding!

Update after owners reply ~ I changed my above review from 1 star to 4 stars as I do genuinely enjoy the restaurant, will
Update again when I have the chance to confirm it was just a misunderstanding and the community bowl Policy that I’ve always admired actually is still an option! Thank you

name: Hunan House

top_reviews.content:
Hunan House is one of those small Chinatown restaurants that proves you don’t need a huge dining room to deliver huge flavors.

The atmosphere has that cozy, neighborhood feel, but the food packs some serious punch. Every dish we ordered was delicious.

🔥 Spicy Chongqing Chicken – Crispy, flavorful, and loaded with the classic dried chilies that bring the heat without overpowering the chicken.

🥩 Spicy Numbing Beef Tendon – Tender, rich, and coated in that signature Sichuan mala flavor that leaves your lips tingling in the best way.

🍜 House Fried Noodles – A generous portion with great texture and plenty of flavor. The perfect dish to balance out the spicy entrées.

This is the kind of place that doesn’t need flashy decorations or a huge dining room. It lets the food do the talking, and it speaks loudly. If you’re exploring Chinatown and want authentic Hunan and Sichuan-inspired flavors, Hunan House deserves a spot on your list.

I can definitely see myself coming back to work my way through more of the menu.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

Follow, like, and share for more local food reviews and hidden gems! 🍜🥢🌶️ #HunanHouse #ChinatownEats #SichuanCuisine #Foodie #HiddenGem #SupportLocal #SpicyFood #NoodleLover

Fantastic food! It is a little place where the locals eat, and was recommended to us by a local in Chinatown. The food was delicious, they had a menu in English so we could understand it, and they even gave us a fork along with the chopsticks. The only complaint is that they don't bring the food out all together, and we didn't get it appetizer until after we received our entree. We ordered one entree for two of us to share and one plate of vegetables (yummy), plus an appetizer. First we got the entree, then a few minutes later the side of rice that goes with it. Then about 5 minutes later the appetizer, and they didn't bring our vegetables. I finally signaled a server and apparently they forgot to make it, do they did it quickly and it was all good food but I would have liked the appetizer first, and then the entree, rice, and vegetables all together. But we stuffed ourselves and had plenty of food leftover, so the portions are big, and the price was incredibly reasonable, even cheap. The bathroom is a little scary, but they had nice hot water and soap to wash your hands, so that made up for it. But if you are squeemish about a clean bathroom, you may not want to try it.

A whole cockroach was found in my takeaway food after I had already eaten half the meal.外賣的農家小炒肉裡面有蟑螂！！
The restaurant refunded my order, but that does not change the fact that I had already consumed part of the food. They even didn't say sorry to me.This was one of the most disgusting dining experiences I have ever had.

One of the best Chinese food in Chinatown. We stayed at the Hilton in financial district and was looking for a place to have dinner, and was attracted by all the different Chinese dishes (both Cantonese and Sichuan) shown in their menu. The restaurant wasn’t fancy looking, just like an average restaurant with red antique decor, but their food was excellent. I had the best tasting Cantonese roasted duck that flavorful but not overly salty and crispy delicious skin. They weee sold out of their spicy lamb chops, but the server suggested their toothpick lamb which was excellent. The restaurant doesn’t offer live seafood in tanks, but will cook them for you if you bring them in. They do offer seafood dishes, just not live off the tanks. Their wine corkage fee is also the lowest I’ve paid (under $10).

Visited January 2nd, 2026

After an amazing visit at Mark’s Hair Salon, I asked the gentleman at the salon for a Chinese restaurant recommendation, specifically one that served dumplings. He not only recommended Hunan House, but he actually walked us there. That small act of kindness set the tone for what turned out to be a wonderful dining experience.

My daughters, who are six and seven, had been craving dumplings all day, especially after patiently waiting for over two hours while I got my hair done. When we arrived, we saw that the menu offered two types of dumplings, the Shanghai dumplings and the pan fried dumplings. We ordered both for the girls, and they absolutely devoured every single one. My husband and I did not even get a taste, which honestly says everything about how much they loved them.

We also ordered chow mein noodles with just chicken and noodles for the kids, which they enjoyed very much. The portions were generous and the flavors were comforting and satisfying, exactly what they wanted.

For my husband and I, we ordered the black pepper shredded pork and the crispy fried fish with explosive chilies. Both dishes were exceptional. The flavors were bold, well balanced, and incredibly enjoyable. Every bite was delicious, and we truly appreciated the care and skill that went into preparing the food.

The service was quick, efficient, and courteous, and the food arrived hot and fresh. From the kindness of the initial recommendation to the quality of the meal itself, this experience made our day even more special. We are so grateful for this recommendation and could not be happier with our visit.

Great first experience! I was visiting San Francisco for the weekend and ordered from Hot Sauce and Panko To Go via DoorDash and was super impressed.

The Bacon Parmesan wings are the stars of the show—perfectly crispy, and the flavor was everything! I also tried the Sticky wings; they were okay, but the cheese on a wing was a bit different for me and didn’t quite beat the Bacon Parm. The wedge fries were also a win—surprisingly crispy and flavorful. Everything arrived well-packaged and sealed tight, which I really appreciated. Definitely a go-to spot for a wing craving!

These looked so good in pics I had to try it! We door-dashed it as it is a to-go place. Wings were $8 for 6 wings of each flavor so price was reasonable.

1. Fire wings (Buldak)
2. Mango habanero
3. Panko

The fire wings were my favorite, they were soo spicy yet flavorful, def keep water by your side before starting to have them! I’d say mango habanero was really good too, I think best way to describe it is it tasted exactly like Wingstop, which has a perfect balance of sweet and spicy. I was really thrown off by the panko wings since I usually don’t like dry wings but they were so crispy and the panko sauce with them was the perfect compliment. Definitely coming back here to try more flavors!

Delicious buffalo sauce, lemon pepper, and Korean buldadak wings. Waffles and wedge fries are bomb. Quick service and foods always fresh.

I would recommend to avoid on football Sundays though. Quality dips a bit.

Hot Sauce & Panko is definitely top 5 wings in the city. From the size of the wings to the crispiness and flavor options you can’t go wrong here.
Bourbon bacon wrapped is my go to always and now they have a hot version and a plain Jane bacon wrapped.
This time around I also went with the waffle & wings combo. Tried the Al pastor and they were awesomeness.
The last flavor which was basic but still perfection were the Salt and pepper wings.
15 premium wings and a waffle you can’t beat it.
Have patience or go to wingstop!

Overall, the wings at Hot Sauce and Panko are very solid. The flavors are great, but I’d personally prefer them a bit hotter. The beer was definitely my favorite—smooth and refreshing. I also tried the Korean and Al Pastor flavors. The Korean was flavorful, but the Al Pastor didn’t quite hit the mark for me. Place is pretty nice as well, it can be busy as I’ve mentioned before. If it’s busy, you can expect longer delays which tends to happen. Good for all ages.

It is always lovely to see friendly and welcoming Crystal.  She is there most times we visit and is knowledgeable and so enthusiastic telling us about new things to try, the things she loves and what's coming up next!  Many restaurants will offer vegan choices which just means it is minus something.  5 Tacos and Beers however gives us innovative and exciting new dishes full of flavor and actual vegan sour cream which adds a huge factor of deliciousness! This weekend I tried enchiladas with a tangy Verde sauce, cheese and lots of deep red beets and a side of black beans with vegan sour cream which were wonderful! The restaurant itself is a fun place with plenty of seating both indoors and out yet maintains charm.  I love that on good weather days they open up the doors to let in fresh air and a view of the passersby and outdoor diners.
If you love tacos and beers, this is a must-go. Absolutely delicious food and tasty beers. Just great. I come back every time I visit.

The ribeye taco is Hella good. I also tried the Octopus taco and that was pretty good too. Beans and rice could be a little better, but good. The service was good and we didn't wait long at all to be seated and to get all the items we ordered. I'm looking forward to visiting again, soon.

top_reviews.content: Huge portions, but for me the food smelled better than it tasted, and actually lacked enough flavor. The Warrior’s Breakfast is huge. I started coming to this restaurant when it first opened (around 1990) because of the muffin tops, menu selections, complimentary mini size bakery basket and food quality being consistently good. When the area developed (high rise apartments and Oracle Park) parking became insane.  The restaurant and area lost its charm,  so I stopped coming.  So when I happened to be in this neighborhood, I decided to try the restaurant and see what changes were made.  The only difference inside of the restaurant is that the bakery area is now replaced with a bar.  The small  pastry display looked pitiful. The pastries didn't look appealing - muffins were below the cup line topped with sugar sprinkles and the slices of cake look like it was just sitting there.  Other than that, the decor looked the same.

I was greeted by a friendly server and sat at a table with complete views of the bay.  Food was served temperature hot with a smile.  Server came frequent to see how I was doing and if I needed anything.
The Dubai chocolate pancake was absolutely delcious.  It looks awfully sweet but it wasn't.  The pancakes were fluffy with nice brown bottoms. Presentation was awesome. I definitely would order this again.

The chicken fried steak was good but needed more gravy.  The server bought me a bowl of gravy and once I had that, it was more delicious.  The gravy was homemade, creamy with bits of sausage.  The over easy eggs were cooked perfectly -  not too runny nor hard.  The hash browns were the best I had for a long time - it wasn't greasy and was crispy as I like it (I did ask for crispy hash browns) - not overcooked or dry. The muffin was too floury and dense for me. It was not what I remembered it to be - fluffy, soft insides with a semi crispy outside.  Overall, if you are in this neighborhood, give the restaurant a try.  The food is just as good as I remembered it 15 plus years ago but I would definitely would not recommend the bakery goods.

We love coming to Town’s End Brunch. They have all the usual breakfast suspects, each one tasty! Loved the place and brunch here. We ordered eggs benedict plate and sandwich along with latte. Appreciate the food as it was easily one of the most appetising food we had in SF.

Prices, food, service, portion size and location are okay with a couple of exceptions. Hashbrowns and over easy eggs were perfect. top_reviews.content: Walked in for dinner for 2 on a Thursday afternoon. There is some street parking around the area, we parked kind of far and just walked over. They have both indoor and outdoor seating and a nice little bar, it’s a cozy restaurant and it got busy. Service was also really friendly. We got the arancini to start, I think it was still a little cold and we also go bread with oil which was really good. I got the lasagna which was really big and I devoured it because I was starting. My friend got the involtini and he finished it as well. The food took some time but overall it’s a nice vibe and a cozy restaurant. They said the lasagna and ravioli porcini trifolati were popular dishes to get.

Really disappointing experience. We ordered four dishes and not a single one was done well.

The tomato burrata came with completely flavorless tomatoes. The tuna carpaccio was overly salty, drowning in dressing, with wet, salty tuna and even mayo on top—which felt completely out of place. The pasta ragu had noticeable chunks of pure pork fat, which made it hard to enjoy. The campagnola pasta was swimming in sauce and, instead of pappardelle, had random pieces of spaghetti mixed in.

Across the board, the pasta was overcooked, with strands stuck together. When we pointed it out, we were told this is “expected over time,” even though it arrived like that, and that the mixed pasta shapes were just an accident due to batch cooking.

Service was practically nonexistent. No one checked in to ask how anything tasted. Our half-eaten burrata and tuna were taken away without a single question. We interacted with at least four different people bringing plates, and even the wine was served by a busser, which made the whole experience feel disjointed and inattentive.

Overall, poor execution, questionable explanations, and not worth the price.

Inviting ambiance, absolutely delicious authentic food, and charming fantastic staff! Five stars easily, they transported me back to Italy! Let them order family style for your group so that you can enjoy all of their best dishes and drinks. Shout out Angelo, he was the best!

My friends, new to Berkeley, were telling me that they loved Italian food, so I told them that we must try Agrodolce Trattoria on Shattuck. I know that Agrodolce has roots going back to Caffe Sport in North Beach which I would go to in the 70's, and more recently Trattoria Siciliana on College which was my buddy David's favorite restaurant.
We loved it! The atmosphere was great, including projecting the classic film La Dolce Vita on the wall. The food was fantastic, my Swordfish was cooked, as the menu said" perfectly! The cocktail bar was  right out of an old movie. And the bread and dipping sauce was a signature classic.
My friends and I were able to catch up on recent trips to India, Normandy France and Budapest. It could hardly have been a better choice.
Needless to say we'll be back!

The food was variable...some dishes were very good, others were pretty mediocre.  The service was some of the worst I have experienced at a restaurant of this level for quite a long time.  Things started out fine. We ordered a second bottle of wine that took 15 minutes to arrive, by which time some of us were nearly finished with our main course.  I could see our bottle was sitting on the server's table where our server stood, joking with the other staff, for a good 5-10 minutes before I stood up, walked over, and requested that she bring the bottle to our table.  At dessert, we were handed two dessert menus for a table of six.  When we asked for a menu per person, we got quite the strange/annoyed look from the busboy.  A good 15 minutes had passed after we finished the desserts and no server came by to deliver the bill.  Not wanting to hang around longer, I went to the bar to request the bill.  It took them another 10 minutes to furnish the bill (the restaurant was not busy by then), upon which they added a mandatory 20% tip on the POST-TAX total, which I disputed but they refused to change.  We will not be returning, and given the long list of better and more professional options out there, I would caution anyone else from going.

Food was amazing and happy hour were very decent prices. I'm definitely coming back to try more, especially the beer! Service was super fast.
I had oysters and takoyaki both were so good, perfectly cooked takoyaki ❤️

Absolutely loved NARA! Everything we tried was incredibly fresh and delicious — the menu has such great variety that there’s truly something for everyone. It has been so long since I’ve had a sushi dinner this great. Every cut of fish was so fresh and tasty. The service was incredible. I loved how knowledgeable and tasteful the staff and chefs were. Our favorite sushi spot in the city. We normally partake in happy hour (calamari, hand rolls) and get an assortment of nigiri.

Thanks, Sonny, for always providing such great service!

top_reviews.content: Came here a few weeks ago for SF Restaurant Week and ordered off the prix fixe menu… $30 each for a main, two sides, and dessert. Bar and restaurant with mostly high top seating, dark and casual with games on TV. Staff was friendly. Arrived around 5pm on a Friday with no wait, though it filled up quickly after. We got the smoked pulled pork and mesquite BBQ chicken with various sides, both with nilla wafer pudding. Everything was delicious and felt like a proper hometown BBQ… portions were so generous we had leftovers. We also caught happy hour, which runs separately from restaurant week… $10 gets you a pint plus a well shot. One of the better value meals I’ve had in SF. Will be back, and with its generous portions we can probably share next time.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

Absolutely loved this BBQ spot. The food was delicious, flavorful, and honestly some of the best BBQ we’ve had in a while. Everything tasted fresh, perfectly cooked, and the portions/prices were great for the quality you get.

The staff was incredibly friendly and welcoming, which made the experience even better. What really stood out to me was how kind they were to our Golden retriever Labrador dog.. they brought him water and even gave him some BBQ rib scraps, which completely made our day. Such a thoughtful touch that you don’t see often.

Great happy hour, great service, great food, and overall just a really fun and welcoming atmosphere. We’ll definitely be back again!!

Pros: AMAZING service. Our waitress was so friendly and helpful, 11/10. The food came quickly and the selection of house made sauces were killer (my two favorites were the dill ranch and the tangy mustard). The portion of fries was extremely generous.

Cons: the meat was just… okay. We got the brisket and tri tip, and they both came out closer to room temp than warm. It honestly felt like they were made earlier in the day and had been sitting around — just was left wanting a little bit more quality for the price that we paid.
Great atmosphere. Great service. Drinks very delicious. Food was good. Ribs didnt quite fal off the bone but delicious sauce. Salad was good as well

Super awesome experience here during the Norway v England world cup match!

Good:
- Easy to get reservation
- Not packed compared to other places and ample seating
- Amazing apple pie ice cream dessert and also the mac n cheese skillet was so tasty!
- The staff were so nice - and we even got a free shot when Norway scored!
- Tons of TVs to watch the games
- Loved the cocktails - the ube and lychee were my favorite ones, very sweet and yet also strong
- Great ribeye
- Fun ambiance and good vibes, it's dim lighting and very intimate

Bad:
- The cornbread we had was bitter, but they were nice and gave us a refund for it

Overall enjoyed my experience here and would come again!

Tried this location out as I was in the area.  I normally frequent the San Leandro location on East 14th.

At this location I found my double char to be on the blan side.  The bread was toasted, but on the outside the bread was cold.

The fries were okay.  I found the service to be good.

Overall a 3 star location.

I’ve been to several Habit Burger locations since moving to the Bay Area, and I’m a big fan of their menu. I also appreciate their self-order kiosks, which make ordering quick and convenient—every location I’ve visited has them. This particular spot stood out for its cleanliness and spacious layout. The staff were consistently tidying up, which was great to see. Plus, there’s plenty of parking and easy access to nearby stores like Safeway and Target. Overall, a great experience!
I love this hamburger's different taste that the other ones they have a lot of choices to pick it's  good flavor real meat

A few months ago we went to this location and ordered burgers to go. When we got home we discovered that the burgers were fully wrong- they had the right stickers on them but completely different things on the burger. This is a bummer for me specifically because I have a tomato allergy, and the burger I got had tomato on it. I drove back and the manager was incredibly nice to me and replaced our burgers, and gave me a coupon for two free burgers in the future. I tried to use that coupon today, and they ended up just taking ten dollars off the total order. Fine, whatever, didn’t say anything, ten dollars is still cheaper so whatever. Got home just now and the burgers are ice cold (after a seven minute drive) and mine has tomato on it, as well as lettuce and so much mayo the bottom bun fell apart, none of which I ordered or were on the menu. Not worth going back again to fix, I’ll just go elsewhere in the future.

Stopped in recently to meet up with a friend who was in town for the holiday with her husband.

It was my first time at this location, but I love Habit. Their burgers, fries, and onion rings never disappoint. I wound up with a patty melt and sweet potato fries, which left me feeling satisfied.

Service was great and honestly I can't complain about much. Definitely, a bit of a noisy spot with a lot of teens hanging out outside and inside, but I mean we were all young once.

I'll definitely pop over here, when the line at In n Out is too crazy to deal with.

top_reviews.content:
Taqueria Mi Burrito is a gem for anyone craving authentic, flavorful Mexican food. From the moment you walk in, the friendly and welcoming service sets the tone for a great dining experience. The staff is attentive, efficient, and always ready with a smile, making you feel right at home.

Now, let’s talk about the star of the show—the chicken burrito. It’s an absolute delight! Packed with tender, perfectly seasoned chicken, fresh ingredients, and just the right balance of rice, beans, and salsa, every bite is a burst of flavor. The portion size is generous, making it a substantial meal that will leave you fully satisfied. Whether you’re dining in or taking it to go, the burrito holds up beautifully, with no skimping on quality or quantity.

What really stands out at Taqueria Mi Burrito is how fast the service is, especially during busy hours. Despite the quick turnaround, the food is always fresh and made to order. It’s clear that the team takes pride in what they do, and it shows in every aspect of the experience.

If you’re in Alameda and looking for a delicious, filling meal served with a side of warmth and efficiency, Taqueria Mi Burrito is a must-visit. Highly recommended!

Always fresh ingredients and yummy in my tummy.

Been going here for over 10 years. They are consistent and an Alameda institution.

Kids from nearby Alameda high crowd into this joint during lunch.

My favorite is their *Chile Verde pork super quesadilla. Crunchy and delicious. With guacamole goodness it’s so yummy. It’s a flavor explosion in your mouth.

Thank me later.

Always a great experience. Food is consistently fresh, service is quick, and the restaurant is always clean.  no frills, no greasy fingers. Perfect spot for our family when we need a delicious meal on the go. Highly recommend.

I have been going to this taqueria since the mid 90's, as a student of Alameda High School. Never have I felt so disrespected and as disappointed as today,  being addressed as a "Negra", by the owner! The tall older man making the food.( Negra meaning black girl) A business should never address a customer by their ethnicity, I felt highly disrespected.  That's like me saying, "Hey white girl" to and a respectable Caucasian adult woman, who has patronized my business for decades.   That just showed me, they didn't deserve my money. Plus I haven't been a girl for over 30 years. Then he laughed afterwards like it was a joke.  He was speaking in half Spanish and half English the entire time, knowing that I don't speak Spanish, then ended with Negra, and laughed a sinister laugh. I will never spend my money there again, and advise that any person of color, do the same.

Written by the account holder's wife

Best taqueria in Alameda! The simple ingredients they use is what makes this place so great. I’ve been coming here since 1999 and the super burrito is the GO TO! I’ve tried their tacos and quesadillas and those are also incredible but you’ll never go wrong with anything here. The staff are always super polite and they make you feel taken care of. I do frequent other Mexican restaurants in Alameda but when I want a burrito, Mi Burrito never fails!

I would recommend for vegans and any hungry diners alike. Excellent friendly staff who will go out of their staff duty calls to please dining experiences; one of my favorite Chinese restaurants.

There’s so many authentic Chinese places in San Francisco, but it’s hard to find the American-style Chinese food I grew up with in suburban Georgia. I finally found it here, this place really hits home for me. The general tso’s chicken is delicious, and so is the hot and sour soup. They have a great value lunch special, it’s $15 for the whole combo including rice, soup, and egg roll.

If you’ve been looking for good American style Chinese food in San Francisco, this is the best I have found yet. I will definitely be coming back!

Definitely an easy 5 star!
Food is amazing as always, comes with delivery, fair prices. Super authentic Chinese food! I recommend everything on the menu especially the Korean bbq wings and the general chicken. The chef knows what’s he doing hundred percent. Also the owner chino is an amazing guy, always gives back to the community- again, reason why I recommend this restaurant to everyone.

Ordered takeout and got the General Tso’s lunch special and the salt and pepper tofu. I know SF has everything from dim sum to Cantonese clay pot rice, but there’s something about American Chinese food that really hits the spot - and this was absolutely delicious.

The portion sizes were great - the lunch special came with an egg roll and hot and sour soup on the side. I highly recommend paying the extra $1 for the chow mein.

Tasty food, generous portions, and one of the best lunch specials I’ve had in the city!

I tend to rate my stars mostly for food. I Had the Mongolian beef lunch. Everything came out how I hoped with a pretty good amount. But as I'm writing this an hour later, I'm feeling very satisfied.

top_reviews.content: Delicious pork chop and swordfish. We did not have a single bad dish here and in fact, everything we had was rather excellent. Highly recommend. Reservations needed. Busy for a reason. Quality speaks for itself !

Pearl 6101 provides a small but quality selection of snacks, appetizers, pasta, entrees, and desserts.

Service was warm and welcoming, and we were able to enjoy some bread and drinks while waiting for a table. We ultimately sat at the bar, but it was comfy, and we never felt like we were waiting to be served.

Naturally, the restaurant is pricey. We ate family style and ordered hush puppies, roasted cauliflower, gnocchi, seared scallop, and chocolate panna cotta (one from each of the menu categories). They were all excellent.

The hush puppies were vaguely like falafel. The dill sauce was pleasant but maybe under-salted for my taste.

The cauliflower had a nice mix of flavors on account of the nuts, balsamic reduction, and raisins.

The seared scallop had three types of corn, making for a delicious sauce with varied texture. The scallop was buttery and soft but a little on the fishy side. My partner felt that it was a little overcooked.

The gnocchi plate was like a delicate forest floor; microgreens, truffle cheese with roasted chili peppers, shredded mint, and fluffy potato pillows made for an excellent and fresh tasting dish. I definitely appreciated the subtle spice on the rind of soft shaved cheese.

We opted for the chocolate panna cotta at the end which came with toasted cacao nibs which were like coffee chocolate crisps. This dessert definitely inspired me to make something similar as a sweet hors d'oeuvre for a potluck or party.

Overall an excellent meal, and I certainly appreciated the generous amounts of flaky salt on each dish. Pearl 6101 provided a nice little post card, so definitely a cute and memorable meal if you're visiting San Francisco.

Me and my husband had a great dining experience. The oysters were very fresh and naturally sweet, and beautifully presented. The scallops were generously sized and perfectly cooked, nicely seared on the outside while tender inside. The salad was light and refreshing, and the pistachio tiramisu was absolutely amazing!!! My husband and I both loved it. It’s the kind of dessert that makes you go “wow, this is so good” after the first bite.
The mussels themselves were flavorful, but the bread served with them was a bit over toasted, almost burnt.
The ambiance was warm and cozy, and the service was great. We would definitely come back.

Had dinner here with my family on a Thursday night and it was busy (expected for such a great neighborhood gem). Everything we ordered, from drinks to food, was really solid, and the service was great throughout the night.

The standout dishes for us were the roasted cauliflower and the pork chop, definite crowd favorites. The only downside was the noise level inside, it got pretty loud and made it a bit hard to hear each other.

Overall, a really good experience and would definitely come back!

Had a great dinner at Pearl 6101! We grabbed the chips & dip while waiting for our table — super good and tasty, definitely worth it. Then we had the Japanese sweet potato as an appetizer, which was insanely good.

For mains, we tried the Handkerchief and Crescenza Caramelle pastas — both were delicious, and you can tell the pasta is homemade. The whole vibe of the place is really cozy and fun. Make sure to get a reservation in advance as this place is always busy!

top_reviews.content: We stopped in before a show at The Paramount with no expectations other than a simple ramen fix. We ordered a few appetizers to start, followed by ramen, and everything was… fine. Not bad, just pretty average. With so many stronger options in Oakland, I’m not sure I’d return—not because of a bad experience, but because the competition is simply better.

The words that kept popping into my head when describing the food at Itani is "clean eating". The broth for the Oxtail Ramen was not fatty as anticipated and was soothing even. The Spicy Shrimp Ramen packed more of a flavor punch and was well balanced in spice. The Fried Chicken Sandwich was very juicy and flavorful. The slaw is proper spicy, so be warned. Will definitely be back to try more.

This review is based on my delivery order.

I had the Recovery Meal; includes your choice of a ramen bowl, 3 pieces veggie or pork gyoza, negi chashu mini donburi or small salad, and a non-alcoholic drink. I opted for the Veggie Ramen, veggie gyoza, salad, and Yuzu lemonade.

The veggie ramen was flavorful. The veggie gyoza with the dipping sauce, yummy! The dressing on the salad made it so delicious. I’m a huge fan of yuzu and the yuzu lemonade really hit the spot!

I appreciate restaurants that have okay-based and vegan options. I hope they expand on these options.

Vegan veggie vegetarian plant-based.
Crazy good food! This little place was so cozy and our waiter took the time to tell us about the art and the story behind it. The food was incredible and rich. Would definitely come back.

From out of town, first time here. Nice place, lots of diners which made us about comfortable trying it. The miso pork ramen was excellent. Beautiful broth, melt in your mouth pork and the egg was done perfectly. Our server Caleb was excellent too. Quick wit to him and he made us feel at home.

very tasty chicken especially after a night out of drinking. came here after midnight after visiting sool karaoke bar and was craving some good chicken and fries. was not disappointed at all, chicken was pretty juicy and all the flavors were great, would definitely come back!

top_reviews.content:
I went to visit my brother and brother in-law who lived in the surrounding area of SF. I've lived in the Bay Area growing but moved to TN. Coming to visit I miss getting the taste of the local foods. CA has the best and seem we forget that in other States, you don't get authentic foods as you do in CA.
Suggested to try this place I didn't know what to expect. Walking in to a small room with open kitchen and a singer playing his heart out to the dine in guests. Loud, yes but that's ok. I have traveled all over and had a good fair share of Mexican food but this was described as "Mexico City Cuisine." Their tortillas are AMAZING. I never had tortillas like theirs. Corn based but chewy and tasty. Their guacamole also was fantastic. Greatly displayed on the plate and presentation. Clean and full of flavor. Not too spicy and yet a kick in the mouth. Their 3 sauces for dipping shared among the table did not disappoint. Splashed with a margarita no salt, I was happy!

I've read a few reviews and some have said pricing. In this economy you have to understand the price of goods and ingredients have sky rocketed. I work in logistics for produce and provide product in the trucking industry for restaurants and you have to understand to dine out and eat, no one can afford. Gas and war has caused this not business such as these. They are trying hard to survive and to buy YOU the patrons the best ingredients to have good food and experience. So unless you want Wendy's or fast food and pay for it in the restroom, you will have to pay more to get best quality. That's anywhere you go these days no matter what. Go on a cruise to Italy and prices there are HIGH but yet you don't complain cause your happy and giddy to see Italy. Course you'll spend that money. But close to home to get food to the table, trucks are needed to delivery and restaurants need those deliveries to feed the masses!

We did have to walk since parking is public. Few of the streets was free no meters. But just around the corner there was meter parking you had to pay so look around and pay attention where you park so you don't get ticketed.
On a busy street will have to walk few blocks.

I’ve been meaning to try this place since I saw this on Adonis’ IG. This place does not disappoint. I had the enchiladas with mole and it was so good. The mole had a touch of sweetness with a spice/seasoning profile that I remember from my ex co-worker’s mole. You can tell they use fresh ingredients. Serving temperature could have been a little hotter but other than that I loved it! Will be coming back to try more dishes!

My wife and I come here whenever we’re craving truly authentic Mexican food, the kind you’d find in Mexico City. We usually split the Tacos de Tinga to start, then go for Mole con Pollo, Enchiladas, and/or Pozole Verde. We’ve tried plenty of other dishes, but these are the ones we always come back to. They are amazing!

This place is legit and I would love to live a bit closer and become a regular.  We ordered the chips and guac (the guac was fresh and bright and a large portion) and then followed up with the pork in chile verde and the mole con pollo.  Both were outstanding and showed real depth of flavor.

The staff was outstanding - they were professional and attentive, but also warm and familiar.  They had intimate knowledge of the menu and shared suggestions.  Great vibe.

I had been wanting to try this place for some time.  Score.

El Buen Comer is my favorite local spot for breakfast! Can’t speak highly enough of this place. I always get the huevos divorciados or the chilaquiles because I literally crave it, but my partner often gets the filete de pescado or puerco en mole verde and those entrees are super tasty as well.

Everything we have tried was delicious and felt like a home cooked meal. Plus the service is great, very friendly and welcoming.

I went to Gordo's with some friends while I was visiting in San Francisco. We stopped by for a quick lunch before heading to Golden Gate Park to play some Badminton.

Gordo's is a small space with not much sit down space. It's buzzy and had someone in line almost always!

The service was quick, with burritos ready for you in a matter of minutes.

I am vegetarian so got a bean and cheese super burrito with guacamole. I believe the price was around 12 dollars. On the pricier side coming from Minnesota but it was substantial -- I didn't feel hungry for the rest of the day.

The burrito itself was decent. Nothing too amazing as far as veggie burritos in SF go (would have killed for a tofu protein or veggies), but it was good nonetheless. I would have liked some more salsa as well, but that may have just been my fault for not asking for it.

Would stop by for a quick lunch but there are definitely better spots for veggie burritos in SF!

Initially the cantina wasn't too full, so I ordered a super chicken burrito to eat in. Overall, I would say that the ingredients were fresh and had good flavor. The burrito was large and filling, but was almost 50% rice. It was also more expensive than I had expected, getting close to $20 with a modest tip and no extras like a drink or chips. Service was fast, but not especially personal. While I ate, the taqureia started to fill up. Mostly the crowd was well behaved and not as noisy as some spots. # The Registry: Field Report - Kiki
The fog was rolling down the avenues, thick enough to hide a multitude of sins, but I wasn't looking for trouble. I was looking for dinner. More specifically, a joint that could satisfy a serious raw fish habit while actively tolerating the presence of the little anarchist. That’s a tall order in this town. You usually have to choose between impeccable sushi and a place that won't call the authorities when a chopstick is repurposed as a projectile weapon. Then I walked into Kiki.
The interior played it cool. High ceilings with skylights let in the fading San Francisco light, illuminating a dining room that clearly knew its business. The walls were lined with framed Studio Ghibli prints—Totoro, Chihiro, and Princess Mononoke staring down at the tables like silent, animated informants. Opposite them, a massive mural of a traditional red Japanese umbrella fanned out across the room, bold and unapologetic, right next to a towering wall of black-and-white paper lanterns. It felt like a hideout with excellent taste.
The interrogation began with the soup. A murky bowl of miso, swirling with scallions and seaweed, hiding its salty, savory secrets in the cloudy depths. Then came the heavy artillery: a massive red bowl of udon. These weren't your standard, flimsy noodles; these were thick, muscular ropes tangled up with tender chunks of chicken in a dark, brooding broth. You don't just eat a soup like this; you negotiate a truce with it.
Next up was the tuna bowl. Thick, heavy-handed slabs of bright pink, raw tuna draped gracefully over a bed of rice, accompanied by a hostile little green dab of wasabi. It was a beautiful, unadulterated hit of the good stuff, sliced with the kind of precision you usually have to pay a fixer for.
To keep the peace, a bento box arrived for the anarchist, laid out like a perfectly organized briefcase of delicious contraband: California rolls, a crisp salad with creamy dressing, and a pile of tempura battered in a golden armor thick enough to stop a .38 caliber slug.
Finally, the main event: a sprawling sushi combo. It was served on a plate so loud, abstract, and aggressively colorful it practically screamed for its lawyer. Slices of salmon, dark lacquered eel, and yellowtail were lined up alongside spicy tuna rolls like suspects in a high-stakes police lineup. Every cut was clean, and the fish was fresh enough to slap you across the face.
Five stars. Kiki is a rare breed. It’s a joint that serves serious, dead-center Japanese fare without treating a family dinner like a hostage negotiation. The fish is pristine, the udon hits like a velvet blackjack, and the animated wolves on the wall do a surprisingly good job of keeping the kids in line. Case closed.

I am so grateful to the staff at this location for their contamination FREE preparation of my sandwich. I have celiac and haven’t had a sub sandwich in years. I had no reaction to the sandwich from Ike’s and the staff assured me it would be prepared separately. The GF bread was not particularly good, but that’s par for the course with GF bread. I am just so happy to have eaten a sandwich without getting sick!

I ordered the vegetarian bacon sandwich, the Prissy Presley. The tiny amount of vegetarian bacon they put in there was terrible! They put in a couple of slices in the middle of the sandwich and then as soon as you get half way through the sandwich slice, there was one tiny layer! I also paid extra for guac and it was a tiny smear added! For the price of the sandwich, this is ridiculous and a rip off. I didn't pay all this money for bread!

On the flip side, I recently ordered the same sandwich from the Ike's that is near SFSU and the amount of vegetarian bacon they put in there was multiple slices throughout the whole sandwich. Perfect! This particular location that I am reviewing is ripping people off. See the attached photo I included with my review for proof.

The customer service here is great! Luis took me and my twin’s order and was super cool and welcoming. The sandwiches are amazing as well -  they’re super flavorful, and there is a huge variety. This was my first time at this place and I’ll definitely be coming back!
Ike’s is the best! Delicious sandwiches. Something for everyone (vegan, halal options). Fast, friendly service every time. If you love sandwiches, you’ll love Ike’s!
