name: Terra Cotta Warrior
address: 2555 Judah St, San Francisco, CA 94122, United States

google.name: Terra Cotta Warrior
google.address: 2555 Judah St, San Francisco, CA 94122, United States
google.description: Chinese restaurant serving not-commonly-seen menu items in modest but contemporary surrounds.

top_reviews.content:
Okay, I said I wasn’t going to leave reviews and would just give feedback directly to the restaurant. But I don’t think the server appreciated that. Instead, he completely ignored us and went back to his phone. So… here we are.

The food was, OMG, so bad. No flavor at all. The bean sprouts tasted old, and the mustard greens tasted like they were seriously spoiled. The noodles also had no flavor. Even the simple cucumber salad tasted like they just cut up a cucumber and poured vinegar over it.

In SF, I can’t imagine how competitive Sichuan food is, so how can this place be this bad? One review mentioned that maybe the head chef wasn’t there, so perhaps the food is just really inconsistent? I just can’t believe how bad it was considering how many good reviews this place has online.

I visited with a friend who also doesn’t eat meat, so our options are a bit smaller. The flavors are excellent, and they make a regional cuisine (Shanxi) that’s unique and difficult to find.

Two minor drawbacks: (1) the pita sandwich’s bread is a bit too bready- I was expecting a crispy texture (like a pressed panini) which is what I’m used to and (2) the tomato/egg noodle dish could use a bit more topping compared to the amount of noodles. But the noodles themselves are chewy, authentic, and absolutely delicious.

The food here was very good. Value of the food was reasonable, flavourful and decent pricing. Their cumin lamb is seasoned very well, not too salty like other places. The hot and sour wonton was on point, loved the spiciness and then you get a kick of tanginess/sour. The pigs ear was on point, not too chewy and not too tough, the flavour melded pretty well. The beef noodle soup was very good, thin slice of beef shank/flank, the noodles was perfect and the soup made it well.

Friendly staff, however, once you receive your food, the staff doesn’t care about you anymore especially when you need to refill of hot water for your tea.

Overall, excellent value for the food.

Super fair prices especially for San Francisco! Had a melody of dishes and all of them were definitely at least above average, most were delicious! The cold noodles and pig’s ears were tasty and I also liked the pork biang noodles. Service was super friendly as well, definitely come and try this hidden gem in the Sunset!

This place is located on a main street in a neighborhood. Was able to find parking in front of the restaurant on a Wednesday at 7:30 p.m.

As a first-timer, I ordered the spicy sliced beef 5/5 which reminded me of the first time I had this dish at a very well known biang biang restaurant in Xi'an, flavors were spot on and delicious! I also ordered the original Shaanxi style pork burger 3/5. It was a bit bland for me; perhaps I should have gotten the cumin lamb burger, which would have been more authentic. Lastly, the three in one biang biang noodles 5/5! This was recommended by my server and was packed with amazing flavor!

Service was great considering the restaurant was completely full. Surprisingly, every dish was very well priced, and portions were generous.  Overall, I really enjoyed the food and will be back to try several other dishes!

top_reviews.content:
Came here for dinner on a Saturday. Got the chickpea falafel. Honestly so good and flavorful. The sauce on top was amazing and really tied it together. The hummus was very creamy and not too salty. Also ordered the chicken skewer. The chicken itself was tasty and well seasoned, but the rice stood out a lot. The raisins added a nice sweetness and it came with more of that same sauce from the falafel which was amazing. We finished with the walnut baklava and it was easily some of the best baklava I’ve had. It was nutty and not overly sweet.

The staff was incredibly kind. We came in right before closing and stayed a bit past, and they never rushed us. Even cleaned up spilled rice right away without making it awkward. Only criticism with the place is that it is pretty expensive for the quantity and the quality of the food.
Delicious entrees and appetizers. I wasn’t the biggest fan of the Turkish delights but thats just personal preference. Possibly best Baklava Ive ever had.

Good but not as amazing as my expectations. The cauliflower and the eggplant toast were delicious. However the Greek scramble was a bit too doused in a red pepper or tomato flavor and we were quite unimpressed. The pita didn’t taste very store made and felt a bit stale. Everything was also undersalted. Most of the staff was abrupt/moving us along, but a couple staff waiters were very friendly. Really beautiful ambiance nonetheless. Great place for brunch with friends and family. Portions were decent but not massive.

Absolutely love this place! If you are vegetarian, their meal for 2 is a must! If meat is your preference, try the braised lamb, it’s unbelievable!

Come with an appetite because the servings are portioned perfectly for a hungry patron.

Must try:

Hummus- rich, creamy, and a great appetizer to start with. For those who want to make a meal of it, try the warmed variety with braised lamb, absolutely amazing!

Labneh- better than your Nine’s, it is a great appetizer to have with their tasty salad.

Braised Lamb shank- It’s something you just have to try. It’s one of  the best Mediterranean meat dishes out there.

Moussaka- a vegetarian delight, the moussaka didn’t lack in flavor, quality, or portion size. Loved it.

Vegetarian meal for 2- can’t describe how incredible the meal deal is. Please try it and come back and let me know how it goes.

We stopped in for brunch on a whim and found our new favorite Mediterranean place! The atmosphere was great and the staff were very nice. It looks like a popular place so I’d recommend making reservations. We were just two so they were able to seat us just fine.
The food was delicious and the portions were on the large side, at least for what we ordered. And there was a good variety of things on the brunch menu. We also had Turkish coffee which came with a delicious pistachio Turkish delight.
I highly recommend Troya and we look forward to coming back.

top_reviews.content: This is my third time dining here. Absolutely 💯 love this place and the meals are phenomenal! Great service. We had a party of 12 and everyone had an excellent meal. Staff helped us by keeping cold, then cutting, a celebration cake.

My husband and I went to Revival last night for dinner and it was an awesome experience from start to finish! Our server, Landis (sorry if I’m misspelling!), was so warm, friendly, and attentive. He made recommendations from the menu, checked on us often, and made our first time at Revival a real pleasant experience. We ordered some cocktails (Smooth Sailing and Trip to Trinidad), a half dozen oysters, and two specials (Denver wagyu steaks with chimichurri, broccoli, mashed potatoes, and pickled radish). Everything was delicious!!! We also ordered a pear and caramel sundae with candied nuts for dessert and it was to die for! Special shoutout to Manager Lucy for making it happen—turns out it was a seasonal dessert and they had actually switched to a strawberry rhubarb sundae, but she said they still had pears on hand and was able to make it for us anyway. Lucky us! My husband and I agreed it was the best meal we’ve had in a good long while! We really appreciated the amazing food and service and will definitely be back in the future!

Excellent pre-theatre restaurant. Quick and friendly service. Really tasty food, well prepared and presented. As appetizers, we had Kenebec potato chips,duck confit legs, and focaccia with three dips, all perfect to start. Then margarita pizza - sauce tasted out of a jar but really good base; little gem Caesar - good dressing but so-so croutons, and crispy pork belly -the star dish. All in all, great food and pretty good value. Great atmosphere.

The service was kind, the atmosphere delectable.

I ordered this mushroom risotto off the specials at the recommendayion of the waiter.

When I tell you it was awesome, I do it with the full weight of my thesis advisors censure on the usage of the word for anything that was less than a sign from God. For in this case it was close to a religious experience. The greens were fresh, well blanched, and tender. They perfectly offset the richness of the risotto and mediated texture via the pumpkin. Around the edges dollops of parsley-garlic muddles provided bursts of flavor that provided the dish a well-modulated method of enhancing the senses. The mushrooms, well, they are freshly foraged and treated with care by the chef.

Taken together I will say I was blown away. It reminded me of a Slovenian risotto made by a grandmother who has cooked it for decades, but with a presentation and sophistication suitable for a diplomats table.

If you are so lucky as to have this offered on the menu, do not miss the chance.

If it is not already clear, compliments to the chef. I eagerly look forward to whatever they whip up next.

I was so hungry and exhausted.  I didn't want to dine in a samll.whole.in the wall with quick food. I knew ai wanted something good. I came to the corner of the block and found Revival. I am very impressed with the presentation of the food, the warm ambiance inside. Plush seats and open space. Open bar very classy and upscale. Out server was polite, nice and informative. name: Mamahuhu
address: 517 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94118, United States

google.name: Mamahuhu

google.description: Brandon Jew's sleek, contemporary venue puts a thoughtful spin on Chinese-American classics.

top_reviews.content:
This spot is absolutely amazing—delicious, authentic Chinese-American food that feels deeply rooted in both traditions. They use traditional Chinese cooking methods but masterfully combine them with American flavors. It is a true masterpiece of culinary fusion where you get the soul of authentic Chinese flavors tailored to the American palate.
The Food:
Everything is top-tier, but I highly recommend:
• Hot and Sour Soup: Perfectly balanced and comforting.
• Fried Chicken Sandwich on a Pineapple Bun: An incredible sweet-and-savory combo you won't find anywhere else.
• Mapo Tofu (Single Rice Dish): The flavor is deep and authentic.

The Experience:
• Speed & Quality: The service is extremely fast, yet you can tell every dish is freshly stir-fried to order. Nothing sits around; the flavors are vibrant and fresh.
• Flexibility: I love that you can order individual portions for a quick meal or go family-style for a big group.
• Atmosphere: The service is amazing—very warm, family-oriented, and definitely kid-friendly.
If you're looking for a fresh, high-quality meal that bridges two cultures perfectly, this is the place. Highly recommend!

we fell for the nice decor and atmosphere except the fabric on the booth seatings are a little dirty. the food was mid, pretty overpriced. also thought the mapo tofu was the must try until it all tastes like vinegar. just go support a local traditional chinese restaurant this is indeed mamahuhu (so-so)

I got the kid sized boba tea sundae and it's alright. Ice cream was more on the icey side. The sauce tasted caramel to me - I expected brown sugar or honey syrup. Boba was good. I'm not sure if it's intentional but the rice cracker was stale to me.

This place is great.  They have excellently updated classic Chinese-American dishes.  I love their hot and sour soup, and I really like the MSG Chicken, the Tingly Spicy Chicken sandwich, and the Tomato Garlic Chow Mein.  Give this place a shot!

I have to admit I have been here a bunch of times and the only thing I have eaten is the vegetarian mapo tofu because I like it so much. There are other veggie options but I'm really here for that dish. I love the Sichuan spice and the mushrooms. If you get the meal with rice it also comes with a little vegetables side dish.

The staff have always been friendly. The atmosphere is pretty fast casual, it's a little nicer than chipotle but not like "dining". Food always comes out fast. I will be eating mapo tofu again here soon!

The lychee drink is popular but it was too sweet for me even asking for less sweet. I preferred the vietnamese coffee dalgona on milk less sweet. The dalgona on top was really tasty and strong. I also tried their Thai tea French toast (I wanted the special berry toast but it was out of stock) and even though it's one of their most popular items I felt it was just okay, the toast was a bit dry, I definitely recommend the waffle over it.

My other favorite was the Saigon steak, the steak was super tender and juicy.

Braided beef with baguette, spring rolls, egg rolls, and mango sticky rice were all standard, not bad but wouldn't go here specifically to order it.

Went on a Saturday around 1pm and it was quite busy. There was a short wait but the food was definitely worth it!

Favorites were the Saigon Steak and the Tom Yum Noodle Soup. They have fairly priced and fun drinks as well. Highly recommend!

One of my favorite brunch spots in San Francisco with Thai and Vietnamese fusion cuisine. I ordered the tom yum omelette, which comes with a side of potatoes and your choice of fruit or salad. I was pleasantly surprised, since I don't usually see this combination. The dish was bursting with flavor, with a nice balance of savory, sour, and spicy. It's also topped with pieces of sriracha bacon which has just the right kick.
The Saigon steak was incredibly flavorful and ended up being our table's favorite dish. The beef was soft and tender, cooked with a generous amount of stir-fried onions.
The restaurant uses a different type of noodle for their drunken noodles, but it's still a solid dish with peppers, basil and onions.
I recommend the iced butterfly lychee fizz. Its not too sweet, and the lychee flavor is prominent. Good morning drink if you dont want caffeine or mimosa!
The interior is nice, modern and comfortable. The servers are attentive, and it was overall a great experience.

This place deserves a big fat thumbs up for their attentiveness, taste and portions. I ordered their tomyum omelette, hainan chicken rice , salmon curry and crunchy French toast via ubereats.

Firstly, I m pleansantly surprised with the potatoes from the omelette. It survived the delivery process and was still crispy .

I asked for extra sauce for my chicken rice and they complied! Simple to do but yet so difficult for so many vendors whom don't give a damn so good job! The sauce and rice was flavourful and I enjoyed it!

I asked for extra spicy for my salmon curry and they did !! They wrote it on the box which I think was so sweet.

They packaged everything so well and I truly appreciate everything. 100 bucks well spent thank you!

Ps: thank you for the extra bokchoy!!! I'll be sure to order again everytime I'm in sfo! ❤️

My coworkers chose this place for lunch; otherwise, I would not have ever known about this restaurant. We were a party of 4. We came on a Wednesday around noon & were seated right away. The place wasn’t too small or big; in essence, you could hold an audible conversation. Our waitress was great.
The food was great and I thought the portions  were huge. We started off sharing the shrimp spring rolls. The white wrap was good and not chewy or hard. The peanut sauce was good. For drinks, I got the Dalgona coffee. It was rich and tasty.
I love breakfast/brunch and this place serves it until 3pm! I had the Eggs Florentine Benedict. Came with a side salad and potatoes. The toasted potatoes were cut really small, which is what I like; I’m not a fan of big wedge style potatoes. All of it was good. Couldn’t clean my plate off because I was so full. I took a picture of it but later found out my phone didn’t save it for some reason, so apologies for not including a pic.
Other items my coworkers got were: some type of noodles, stir fried eggplant/chicken w/sunny side egg on top of rice. This looked good and they finished it.
Overall, food, service, and place were great. The price is about $16+. Typical rates for the area; however, the quantity and quality is worth it. I would definitely come back here!

top_reviews.content:
🍱 The Food: Solidly in the Middle
When it comes to the sushi quality, my experience was very middle-of-the-road.

The "Okay" Factor: The fish was fresh enough, but it didn't quite have that "wow" factor you find at high-end omakase spots. It wasn't the best sushi I've ever had, but it definitely wasn't the worst. It’s a safe, reliable option if you aren't looking for anything too experimental or premium.

Good Variety: The happy hour selections allowed us to try a few different things, which is always a plus. It's a great way to sample the menu and find a few rolls that hit the spot for a casual dinner.

✨ Intimate Ambiance and Quality Service
Where Ace Wasabi really stands out is in its atmosphere.

Intimate Vibe: The restaurant was quiet and dimly lit, which created a really nice and intimate setting. It’s the kind of place where you can actually have a conversation without shouting over a crowd, making it perfect for a low-key date or a catch-up with a close friend.

Professional Service: I was also quite pleased with the staff. The service was good—the servers were polite, efficient, and checked in just the right amount of times. Even during the happy hour rush, we didn't feel neglected or rushed through our meal.

🏮 A Great Local "In-Between" Spot
The decor has a bit of a funky, retro-modern Japanese feel that adds character to the space. It doesn't feel like a cookie-cutter sushi joint, which I appreciated. While the food is just average, the combination of the calm environment and the friendly service makes it a pleasant place to spend an evening.

👍 Final Verdict: A Reliable Choice for a Quiet Evening
It’s a "solid okay" in terms of food, but it earns extra points for its great service and intimate atmosphere. It’s not necessarily a destination you’d cross the city for, but if you’re already in the Marina and want a quiet, dimly lit spot to enjoy some decent happy hour sushi, it’s a perfectly fine choice.

Ace Wasabi: Unbeatable Freshness and Friendly Service in the Marina
Ace Wasabi in the Marina is a fantastic choice for Japanese food in San Francisco. Our experience was thoroughly enjoyable, anchored by seriously fresh ingredients and a welcoming atmosphere.
The primary takeaway here is the quality of the seafood—the fish was incredibly fresh, which is the most important factor for any sushi or sashimi spot. Everything we ordered was delicious, proving that Ace Wasabi executes their dishes perfectly.
We were particularly impressed by how delightful even the seemingly simple items were. The Asparagus with sesame sauce, for example, sounds simple but was surprisingly delicious and perfectly prepared. It's those little details that really make the difference!
Beyond the food, the service truly enhances the experience. The servers were very friendly and attentive, making us feel right at home. It’s also a huge bonus that they offer a full bar with a lot of cocktail options, making it a great place to stop for a drink and a bite, not just a standard sushi dinner.
Ace Wasabi is highly recommended for anyone looking for fresh, quality Japanese food with excellent service and a fun bar scene.

Absolute gem! The food was fantastic and creative. Favorites were the Hamachi Serrano Sashimi, Crispy Tuna, shishito peppers, and the Spicy Samuri shake and share. The service was wonderful and the outdoor seating area is super comfy and cozy (with plenty of space as well, we had a group of 5), and the tables are well spaced so the noise isn’t overwhelming. The food was so delicious and our server was lovely and attentive but not at all overbearing! We will definitely be coming back :)
Amazing atmosphere. Came for happy hour and the wait staff was so nice to make space for us. Bingo was super fun and would highly recommend. Great vibes and great food.

Sushi is amazing, the most fun waitstaff, and their new bar program truly has top tier cocktails. Great Japanese whisky selection as well. If you want good sushi and fun vibes, Ace is hard to beat. Special shout out to the best happy hour in the Marina. Come for Bingo nights on Wednesday and Thursday for an extra good time.

So today we decided to try something new...give Oakland another chance. This was the place we decided based on the reviews.

The fried snapper was overcooked, old, frozen fish. So dry the fish itself dried up to a little strip within the overly crisp batter. It also carried that old fish smell. Like either they've been using the same oil for a minute or the fish is just been thawed for a min.

They provide a side and a corn muffin with the meal. The muffin was dry and processed. I chose the greens as a side and they were o-k. Quite honestly the greens were the best part of the meal. I also come from a long line of Black soul food cooks so standards are high. It seems like this place is trying to cook soul food but it's missing the soul.

Once again the guys at this place are super cool and just on that I've given 2 stars. The ambiance and experience you get once you visit this place is part of the appeal.

I am one who never likes to line up for food in SF due to the fact that we can get good food anywhere we turn in this city. However, this particular day, I realised
it was empty, but I found out later that I was lucky I came in a few minutes right before the lunch rush. I got myself a window seat facing the street and enjoyed the food that now, a few weeks later, I kept going back on a weekly basis a few times twice a week. Now it's like a Friday and sometimes Monday ritual to go walk around Clement St, pick up my sauce and yummy food around the area, and have something at Cafe Bunn Mi. Everything here is made to order which is just the way I like it since it is quality over quantity and I never mind the wait since I am a very patient person. As time went by, they got really busy and become a full house, also many customers came to pick up their orders and food delivery drivers came to pick up orders ready to be delivered. The staffs here are very welcoming, well trained, professional and understanding where all of my visits were a satisfying and issue free one. Lastly, this place is one of my favorite Thai spots in the city and it gets my cravings completed. I highly recommend this place to all Thai food enthusiasts, to anyone willing to try something new, if you are looking for a laid back spot to dine at, if you are in need of a quick bite or if you just so happen to be in the area to check them out. I definitely will be back to tryout the other delicious options they have to offer.

Atmosphere was the usual. Waiter didn’t speak English well enough which I’m willing to work with but not at the cost of what I’m paying for. Asked for steak quesadilla, got cheese. Then said I’ll just get a steak fajita and figured I’d just give my wife the cheese quesadilla. Dude came out with everything to go. They have multiple locations and food trucks! The food trucks are a go-to but when the trucks aren’t open we love going to the restaurants. The view and scenery at this location is super nice and the weather is always great. The food is delicious, especially the street tacos.

Second time eating here. First time I ordered meatball soup and the meat was clearly old. This time, four of us went for dinner and none of us enjoyed the food. Mine was cold (the others were hot). top_reviews.content:
This place was amazing.  The staff/owner was friendly, funny and kind.  The food was so, so good.  The only thing that didn't blow my away was the lamb skewer.  The pork dumplings, the special fried rice, the half Chicken and the pork belly skewer were phenomenal.

My only real gripe is that it was too much food.  Everywhere else in town, the portions feel more modest.  This place was generous, and I had to walk home with an extra full stomach.

Do yourself a favor and stop by, you will not be disappointed.
This food is incredible! We both agreed it was the best food we tried in SF when visiting. The beef and cheese empanada is a must!!! We also really liked their house made drinks.

This was a last minute choice for us when our other plans fell through and we are so glad that we did. The staff were attentive and friendly, and the prices were more than reasonable! I  had a hard time deciding on anything, so I ordered half the menu and every bite brought my wife and I audible excitement! Nothing was disappointing! The mini arepas were soft AND crispy, the tequeños were incredible, huge fresh shrimp in the fried rice, the brine on the chicken was delicious, and don’t sleep on the dumplings in chili sauce. We took the leftovers back to the hotel and ate on them for two days. My wife and I are legitimately sad that we will have nothing close to this back home. If we lived in San Francisco this would be a weekly stop. We ate fancy, touristy, and casual; and out of everything we ate on this trip, this was 100% our favorite, and it wasn’t even close.

I was running hungry downtown, the rain was starting to come down hard when I eyed this restaurant. It caught my attention for its interesting name including "Latin Asian", a name that was neither inaccurate nor disappointing as their menu items reflect what they advertise.

I was cold, tired, and slightly hungry- needing to leave room for a later dinner- and so wanted to pick at several appetizers with a friend, which this restaurant was perfect for. The first good sign was the steam rising, heat emanating from each dish served hot to the touch. I ordered the pork belly skewers, juicy with just enough toughness to be fun to chew, spring rolls, perfectly thin and crisp on the outside and extremely soft and flavourful on the inside, becoming a surprise highlight of my meal, and empanada, which was the size of both of my fists together and sopping in enough oil to warrant invasion by everyone's favourite stripes and stars- so much oil that it was literally drenching and dripping down my hands, delicious but maybe a little dangerous.

While pricing felt slightly expensive for some items, they were generally fair, as were portions. Staff was friendly and service was good, though initially slow to take orders and taking a bit more time than expected to serve the dishes, which maybe is a good sign that everything is cooked fresh.

Something I could crave every once in a while, and a restaurant I'm glad I know exists. 5.2/10.

The food is really flavorful. We ordered the pabellon with rice, beans and plantains, it was a big plate. The rotisserie chicken is amazing! Crispy, juicy, tender, and just perfect. The mini arepas are a must as a side dish. So glad we ended up in this place. Friendly staff and Latin music in the background was the cherry on top.

top_reviews.content: Solid cafe. Service is exceptional and food comes out fast. I had the French toast with raisins which was delicious and the potatoes are incredible; perfectly crispy with just the right amount of spices.

Had breakfast with my wife on May 4, 2026. My wife had eggs with bacon and hash browns. I had Crabby Cake Benedict with potatoes.  My eggs benedict were delicious, the best I ever had.  I have tried eggs benedict in various ways: florentine, salmon, classic.  However, these eggs benedict were much tastier than the other versions.  The crabs blended with the eggs and hollandaise sauce in a way in which none of the favors dominated over the others.  The temperatuture was the correct one and the size of the portion adequate. The potatoes needed  bit of seasoning.  The coffee was strong and above average.  Pelton Cafe is the plce to go if you are an Eggs Benedict fan!

This place is absolutely amazing. The girlfriend and I got the build your own skillet and it didn't disappoint. The potatoes were soft and tender, eggs cooked to perfection and the breakfast meat was cooked just right. We chose biscuits as our toast. They were warm, flaky and buttery. We also shared a short stack of pancakes and those were awesome. Soft fluffy center not overly dry or doughy. She loved the coffee and I love soda so I crushed a diet coke. The service was fast, friendly and professional. I highly recommend this spot for breakfast.

For a very busy restaurant, they were incredibly efficient in seating, ordering, and clean up. Likely why the wait time wasn't bad at all. They were also very accommodating for families with kids. We were a party of 4 adults, 1 toddler, and 2 infants (oof) but we never felt like an inconvenience and were all well attended to. Food, coffee, and ambiance were great. Exactly what you'd expect and what you'd want from a homey diner with a lot of character. A new fave in San Leandro! 🤗

What a great find this place was, you can tell the locals come here so the food is good. The only reason I gave a 4 out of 5 was because they don't use headlamps so the food was just warm but delicious. Service was quick and very friendly. I would recommend this place if you are in the area for a quick bite.

name: Izakaya Sozai

top_reviews.content:
I absolutely love Izakaya Sozai- this place never disappoints! Every dish is consistently delicious, but my personal favorites have to be the ramen and the cartilage (seriously, so good every time). Honestly, you can’t go wrong with anything on the menu, and my whole family always finds something they love whenever we come here.

It’s also an amazing spot to meet up with friends - the vibe is cool, casual, and welcoming, making it perfect for a fun social outing or any kind of get-together. Whether you’re a local looking for a go-to favorite or hosting out-of-town visitors, Izakaya Sozai is always a hit. Such a gem in SF! 👌🏼

Sozai has been a staple in the Sunset for over 16 years and honestly, it never gets old. The menu is carefully put together — every dish earns its place. Some have been here since the beginning and for good reason, they're that good. Not kept around out of habit, just genuinely that delicious. Love that they also switch things up with seasonal specials so there's always something new to try.

If you don't know where to start, the ramen, nankotsu, and maitake fritters are a few must-orders — dishes so good I'd gladly bring them to a deserted island. Trust me on that.

But the food is only half the story. The staff is always warm and attentive without being overbearing, and the vibe just feels like home. This is the kind of local spot that makes the neighborhood what it is — the kind San Francisco doesn't make enough of anymore. If you haven't been, go. If you have, you already know.

Fun place for small plates! Viewing their specials online/via QR code was fun, and threw a little extra flair into our considerations. The service was incredible: attentive, peppy, bustling around this small establishment. My only suggestion is the ramen broth could have been hotter.

What a hidden gem! I came here with some family and we ordered several things from across the menu, and at multiple points in the evening. Every single thing was beautifully presented, stunningly delicious, and we stuffed ourselves. They also have an exceptional collection of Japanese beers and sake that are all divine. Be aware this small place fills up every night of the week, so either plan ahead or get there early. I will absolutely be back the next time I’m in town. The agedashi tofu is the best I’ve ever had.

Now I have to say, for a small joint like Izakaya Sozai, they can sure serve up mini courses that will absolutely get your eyes wide open. Most of the dishes were very delicious and for a very decent price. Izakaya style, of course. My top favorite dishes were the Tako Wasabi, bacon wrapped enoki mushroom and mochi, and Ankimo pate. If you are a foodie like me and are adventurous, I recommend you come here to try it.

Just had dinner at Cocos Ramen. I got the Tonkotsu Ramen, Chicken Yakitori, and a Philly Roll.

The Chicken Yakitori was really good — juicy, not overcooked, super solid. The Philly Roll was about a 4/5 for me. In a few pieces it felt like there was barely any Philadelphia cheese — you can even see it in the photos — but the fish itself was great and overall the roll still tasted good.

The Tonkotsu Ramen was also a 4/5. The broth felt a little light for my taste, almost a bit watery — not in a bad way, just not as rich as I usually expect. Still tasty, just not a perfect 5 out of 5 for me this time.

But overall, really enjoyed it. Great service, super friendly staff, cozy and authentic vibe. Overall — 5/5.

The food, the vibe, and especially Tenzin the chef  were all amazing. This was more of an experience paired with a dinner as opposed to just food. The omakase was so good that I've made plans to come back in two days. The service is top-tier friendly and the energy of the place is extremely inviting. Would HIGHLY recommend you to visit. Also, the sake collection is great. This place bumped up to my favorite restaurant in the city.

It is always a pleasure to come here as I just love the taste of their Ramen.

In short, I use them as the benchmark for how I judge others. Yes, there are others better and some worse for sure, but these folks seem to match my palate the best.

I don't get to visit this place as often as I'd like, mainly because the neighborhood is congested and parking is hard to find, hardly their fault, but it's just a fact of life.

However, whenever I visit this place, it's like coming back to my Ramen home.

Pretty great little local spot! Not too crowded on a weekday (I was early and my date was late and yet the staff didn't get annoyed I was hogging a table since some were still open). Cozy Japanese decor (albeit slightly uncomfortable seating). Friendly but not harassing staff. Decent food and a wider selection of drinks than I'd expect. Amazing presentation of food. Overall a decent spot, and I hope to one day try their ramen since that's their namesake!

Overall 3/5 - Food 3; Ramen broth, noodles and toppings were good. Except our chasu was so tough I had to send it all back to the kitchen. The egg was old. Karaage was soggy. Rolls were mediocre. I ordered the roll with coconut and mango just to try something different and it was an explosion of interesting flavors in my mouth. Service 4; not outstanding but not bad. Atmosphere 3; were given paper plates to eat off of and the tea came in a paper cup. Seating is very close together. I would come back and only have vegetable ramen.

top_reviews.content:
A very nice Italian restaurant with a cozy atmosphere and a welcoming vibe. One of the highlights for me was chatting with the host in Italian, which made the experience feel even more authentic and enjoyable.

The food was solid across the board, though I did find it a bit on the pricey side for what you get. I also had the tiramisu, and while it was good, it didn't quite live up to my expectations—it was probably the only dish that left me wanting a bit more.

Overall, it's a pleasant spot for a nice Italian meal, especially if you're looking for a relaxed ambiance. I'd happily come back.

Had an absolutely amazing night here at Poesia, starting off with finding easy street parking downstairs. The immediate vibe we got walking in was artsy and cozy, and a bit of mysterious. Super good spot for meeting friends or a nice date <3

We came here with a toddler and service provided to us was amazing, not only did they have this nice toddler chair pulled out right away, they also provided option of kid pasta (pasta with butter and tomato sauce) which my toddler loved!

We really liked the Sardine Alla Griglia appetizer: Monterey Bay fresh sardines, stuffed with breadcrumbs and Romano cheese over spicy broccolini - it was quite interesting and super flavorful. I have not had this dish anywhere else before so was a nice surprise!

I also personally really liked the Agnolotti Al Plin: homage pinched pasta, veal-rabbit-pork filling, veal reduction - super rich in cheese flavors, and the pasta has this great chewy texture. The Paccheri Allo Spada in Puttanesca was also really good if you like spicy and tomato based sauce.

Overall I was super impressed with the pasta texture, and the great flavors they provide here. Wasn’t able to try the wines but I think they have really good selections cause I saw neighboring tables order by the bottles! Cocktail wise we had this old fashioned drink which was super tasty.

My biggest satisfaction was the service provided despite us having a toddler join us for the meal. The staff were accommodating and did not give us weird looks when we asked for plastic utensils etc. I will be looking to come back and dine again!

This was a fabulous restaurant with a great atmosphere, my wife loved it here and they were playing old movies (with no sound) right behind me. Each section had its own identity and we had probably the nicest table with chairs, not the best table exactly but the chairs were taller and padded was all. The table lights were cool and the staff was on top. Beautiful place to eat, highly recommend. Expect to pay a bit tho

Highly recommended authentic and traditional Italian restaurant and food. The owners and staff are Italian and very sweet (especially Bene). The food is amazing! There is great indoor moody seating and also a well protected and cozy patio round the back (likely not dog friendly though) that can support larger groups too.

Oh my goodness their pasta was phenomenal!! Sauce is sooo good. I will be back!

We had a pre-concert dinner (prior to the Castro Street Theatre since it’s walking distance) I had scallops for appetizer and pasta for dinner. I had a wonderful vodka martini. My friends also enjoyed their dishes.

It's a solid, value-driven Indian spot worth trying for its variety and welcoming vibe, even if flavors aren't always spot-on. Service and ambiance are genuine highlights, with friendly staff and a cozy setup that makes it easy for casual meals or groups.

The menu offers tons of dishes to choose from across North and South Indian styles, and portions are decently sized without feeling skimpy. Chicken momos and tandoori items delivered nicely. The Chicken 65 disappointed though; it arrived saucy rather than the expected dry, crispy version, which dulled the appeal.

Prices feel comparatively low for the quality and amount, so no worries there—great value overall

Well flavored - and if you want it, well SPICED Indian food in good sized portions and reasonable prices.  Attentive and friendly staff. I asked for spicy preparation for my chicken curry and am extremely thankful I was advised to try medium instead. Very tasty.

So delicious and affordable! Ordered the chicken Tikka Masala. The Chicken comes in huge pieces and is so tender and juicy and the sauce is just right. You can’t skip an order of the Samosas! The flavors are so vibrant and the textures are perfectly crispy and not oily at all! The sauces are also to die for! Trust me, you have to go here!
Delicious food and excellent service. Love their chicken momo, butter chicken masala and garlic naan

We liked everything! Portion sizes are good, what you’d expect for an Indian restaurant, with a great ration of sauce to protein. In terms of spice level, they offer mild, medium, spicy, very spicy. We chose medium to place on the safe side, while you could definitely taste the spice, it wasn’t in the slightest unbearable, so we would creep into the “spicy” range next time. The atmosphere is relaxed, with take-out orders being picked up frequently  - don’t be misguided by the looks on the outside, this is a bustling business rewarded for its tasty food and great service.

Why not dine in? The service is quick, thoughtful, and attentive without being in your face. The decor is clean and comfortable, with culture motifs galore (but tastefully).

7/7/2023
During my visit to Pho King in Oakland, I ordered the Bun Bo Hue, Spring Rolls, and Egg Rolls. The Bun Bo Hue consisted of Hot & Spicy Soup with Beef, Pork Blood, Pork Cake, and Vermicelli. Overall, the food tasted okay.

Such a great spot in Oakland! Everything we tried was delicious, and the menu felt really unique and different from the usual. It’s family style, which made it fun to order a bunch of dishes and share everything at the table. Every plate had so much flavor and felt really thoughtfully put together. Definitely a place I’d come back to!

5 stars across the board. The staff was very friendly and attentive. The food was amazing. They have a good variety of meat and vegetarian options, including some vegan, and the whole kitchen is gluten free, although you wouldn’t necessarily notice. The design of the space is also beautiful and joyful. Delicious cocktails and mocktails too!

We took Mom here for brunch and oh what a wonderful outing she had. Sharing items on the menu is allowed, so we ordered several dishes to get a good feel for their servings.  From the Bruselas El Prado to Arepa De Chocolo with chicken, then through Empanada De Ajiaco, and finally we had Flan De Coco dessert, it was a walk through a taste experience like I have not had before.  Their chef and the team are culinary magicians. The restaurant is decorated in what feels like an authentic Colombian restaurant, and the waiter kindly helped us figure out our meal.  I especially enjoyed the teamwork that made sure all our needs were met.  They had wonderful music playing in the background that made the vibe right.  The location is downtown so parking in the public lot next door is probably best.

🌟 Really fun, memorable dinner at Parch!

We came here around 6:45 on a Friday night for a double date and had a great experience. Parking was surprisingly easy to find, and an added bonus is that the meters stop at 6pm.

🎨 Atmosphere: The space is vibrant, lively, colorful, and really creatively decorated. I loved the tile, wallpaper, and all the little design details. It has a great energy and was perfect for a double date. The pacing of the meal was also just right—not rushed, but never dragging. I wouldn't necessarily come here for a quick bite, but it's a great place to settle in for an evening.

🍸 Cocktails: We tried several and they were excellent. The Mi Encanto and Tropiquita were both very good, but the standout for me was the El Hombre Caimán with green Chartreuse, a beautiful ice cube, and thick foam on top. It was unlike any cocktail I've had before. Highly recommend trying it if you're in the mood for something different.

🍽️ Food: We ordered a lot to share, which I think is the way to go here. The Tumaco ceviche had a delicious sauce and was a nice size for four people considering how many other dishes we ordered. The empanadas were also very good—the cornmeal exterior almost reminded me of corn dog batter in the best way, and the accompanying sauce was great.

The biggest surprise was the Arepa de las Monas with yellow corn and yuca masa and Oaxacan cheese. It was nothing like I pictured from the description—almost like a beautiful, cheesy puff pastry. Really, really delicious and probably my favorite of the smaller plates. The Chicharrón Crispitas were good as well, though pork belly can be a little rich for me.

For the larger plates, I loved the fried whole branzino. The fish itself was excellent with wonderfully crispy skin and surprisingly few bones. The accompanying rice was a little too sweet/coconut-forward for my taste, so I mostly skipped it.

The Corte Andino bone-in ribeye was probably the one dish I enjoyed less. It had a sweeter glaze, and I personally tend to prefer savory flavors. We ordered it medium rare, but I found the meat a little tough and chewy and actually wished it had been cooked a bit more.

Overall, though, the food was excellent and several dishes genuinely surprised us with how creative and delicious they were. Parch feels like the kind of restaurant where trying a bunch of different things is part of the fun. The staff was friendly, helpful and attentive. My glass was always full of water and they helped us select dishes to order. Great cocktails, beautiful atmosphere, and some really memorable food. Definitely worth checking out! 🍸✨

I recently had the extreme pleasure of dining at Sobo Ramen. I ate my meal in a mostly empty restaurant, which now seems odd to me. I drank a Sapporo and the Suntory and as far as beer goes, the Suntory Premium Malt is great for a salty meal. The Sapporo is fine, I just drank a lot of it in Japan and it just tastes regular now lol.

All in all, I want to live next to this place. Food is delicious, staff is friendly, prices are modest. If you're looking to decompress after a long day or a good spot for a date, you can find it here.

The ramen we ordered was nice, it's not salty and you can definitely enjoy the hot soup.
Karaage was good. We ordered hot house sake too.
The servers was very nice.

The food here was damn good! We wanted ramen for our last night on our business trip. We decided to try this place despite the 3.5 rating on Yelp. The place was pretty empty at 530pm. Servers were prompt and polite, answering questions and giving recommendations when asked. We ordered steamed gyoza and three ramen dishes.  I ordered the country ramen, amazing flavor and mild spice.  My coworkers ordered the Tonkotsu with Tonkatsu and Sobo ramen with chicken and spicy - way too spicy for my liking but my coworker loved it. I'd love to come again on my next trip!

My family and I love this place.  We eat here at least once a month, perhaps more during  cold season.

The broth is very good particularly the spicy black tonkotsu.  Meat is just right and the whole bowl is simple, just how ramen should be.  A simple comfort food.

My wife and I have been in many ramen places around the Bay Area that are ranked or rated high on several sites and even from TV food shows and I can honestly say that Sobo Ramen is among the best we have tasted.

I just wish there are more options for appetizers but we love it here!  We are regulars here by now and we are welcomed here like family each time we eat at Sobo Ramen.  It is SOBOlicious!!!

if you're craving legit ramen that doesn't break the bank but still feels special, Sabi--er, Sobo Ramen--is one of the best in the East Bay. Easily top-tier. 10/10 would smash again, no cap. Go get that bowl, you won't regret it!

Ambience is cozy as hell. It's got that intimate, low-key Japanese ramen shop feel--nothing fancy, but warm lighting, clean setup, and it doesn't feel cramped even when busy. Perfect for solo slurping, a quick date, or grabbing with friends. In the heart of Oakland's Chinatown/Pacific Renaissance spot, it's easy to get to and feels authentic without being stuffy.

Magnin Street Cafe is an absolute hidden gem and one of those places you almost want to keep to yourself. From the moment we walked in, we were welcomed with warm, genuine hospitality, and our server, Consuelo, made the entire experience exceptional. She was attentive, friendly, and truly went above and beyond to make us feel taken care of.
The food was fresh, beautifully prepared, and every plate that came out looked as good as it tasted. The omelet was perfectly fluffy, the Eggs Benedict was rich and delicious, and everything was paired with crisp, fresh greens and perfectly cooked sides. Even the coffee deserves a special mention because it was absolutely excellent, rich, smooth, and the perfect way to start the day.
Great food, outstanding service, wonderful coffee, and a cozy atmosphere make Magnin Street Cafe a true neighborhood treasure. We'll definitely be back, and we'll be asking for Consuelo again. Highly recommend!

What a delightful brunch experience! The café is beautifully decorated and spotlessly clean, creating a comfortable and welcoming atmosphere. The service was excellent, every staff member we met was kind, polite, and attentive. Our host was especially friendly and hospitable, making us feel valued and right at home from the moment we arrived.

As for the food, absolutely delicious. The pancakes and French toast were exceptionally soft and well-prepared. In fact, the French toast was one of the best I’ve ever had. I highly recommend this place for anyone looking for a top-notch brunch in a lovely setting.

Me and my partner came to Magnin Street Cafe & Bistro for the first time on Thursday, May 21st for breakfast, and from the moment we walked in we knew this place was special. I had the steak and eggs while my partner had the French Toast Delight. Our waitress was beyond kind, we shared so many laughs with her and she made the whole experience feel warm and welcoming. Then the food touched our taste buds and we were in love. My steak was packed with flavor and perfectly juicy, and my scrambled eggs were cooked to perfection.

From that day on, we tried to come back every single day, but unfortunately there was always a huge line just to get in, which honestly told me everyone else saw what I saw too.

We finally made it back for dinner on Sunday, May 24th, and I technically sprinted up the hill in heels just to make it in time for dinner opening at 5 PM 😂. I had the steak frites and my partner had the chicken Alfredo, and once again the food DID NOT disappoint. That was genuinely one of the best chicken Alfredos I’ve ever had. Yes, I ended up eating both our meals because it was THAT good. No to-go boxes needed lol.

We also had cheesecake for dessert, and although I’m not usually a sweets person, this cheesecake was astounding.

As I’m writing this review on Monday morning, May 25th, I’m currently sitting back in the cafe ordering the same breakfast that made me fall in love with this place, and it still does not disappoint. During dinner we met the couple who owns the cafe, and when we came back for breakfast they remembered us immediately. They welcomed us back and even joked about how I didn’t have to run up the hill this time 😂. I absolutely loved how personable and genuine they were.

10/10 place to eat and visit if you’re new to or touring San Francisco. Amazing food, amazing people, amazing atmosphere. This place will never disappoint

Everything I ordered was great, and the quality of both the food and service really stood out. I’d happily return the next time I’m in the area.

Upon entering the restaurant, there is no host or maitre'd to escort us to a table. A nonchalant waiter told us just grab a table and seat anywhere.

First time at any restaurant I usually will order an Arnold Palmer (1/2 tea, 1/2 lemonade). The beverage is to determine whether the quality of the food is delicious. In this case, the Arnold Palmer passed the test (4 star). Next up - eats.

Eats: for starter, beet salad consisting of a spring mix, diced beets, thinly sliced orange, candied walnuts, diced goat cheese, topped with a balsamic vinaigrette. (4 star). Salmon with a wine glazed sauce with roasted potatoes and mixed vegetables was on point and delicious. It was fresh and moist. (4 star).
My friend ordered the NY steak with the same sides. I'm not sure if he asked for medium well. Even though it was well-seasoned with rosemary, the texture was chewy, not tender. Was it cooked too long? Gristles? Wrong cut of meat? Then he asked for steak sauce. Waiter brought out a bottle of A1 steak sauce. My friend wanted Lea & Perrins worcestershire sauce. I know the next time my friend orders a steak he better specify the Lea & Perrins. (3 star)

No room for dessert. We were full. However, that bread pudding probably would have been great.

Inasmuch as I would like to give D Monaghans a 4 star rating, and there is no such thing as a 3.5 stars, either I round it up or round it down. In this case, it's rounded down due to lack of attentive service, parking and a steak with gristles.

Overall: it can be a hit or it can be a miss. Future visit? Might, then might not.

top_reviews.content: First time here and what a great date night at this restaurant. I looked up pet friendly restaurants in San Francisco and Blue Plate came highly recommended. The outdoor seating is also super cute so great for outdoor dining or if you wanna bring your doggie. The SHISHITO PEPPERS are a must try! (Didnt get a picture).

Fantastic happy hour deal that goes for a reasonable time (5-6pm)! I was here with some friends and the three of us had glasses wine, five plates of food, and a dessert, and it was around $30-40pp. Pretty good deal for San Francisco. The courtyard is really tranquil and sunny as it was a beautiful day yesterday. Our waitress checked on us often. Sometimes if you’re in the back, the staff forgets about you a bit but not here.

Food was overall good. Very creamy and cheesy, so be mindful of that if you are lactose. My favorite was definitely the shishito peppers. Blistered and delicious in this fruit sauce. The arancini were just okay. It could have been more truffley in my opinion. The artichoke jalapeño dip needed a bit more flavor. Up the artichoke and the jalapeños. Chopped salad was solid, we got another one because it was easy to put down. Lastly, the key lime pie was DELICIOUS! Highly recommend saving some room for dessert.

Great place. You can't beat the happy hour menu here. It's probably the best in San Francisco. You get really good calue. We love the pear/dates salad and the octopus.The crusted salmon is really delicious as well. Been here 3+ times. Great service; very attentive with filling your glass and changing out plates. And the best part, unlimited sparkling water!!

Blue Plate offers elevated American cuisine, but the overall experience was disappointing.

The chicory salad with dates was very good, with a tasty dressing and nice balance.

The charred octopus had a great, tender texture but lacked any real charred flavor and felt flat and boring.

For mains, the salmon was tasty but unremarkable. The steak was served as several pieces rather than a proper cut, ordered medium but arriving closer to medium-well to well, with some chewy parts. The salsa and potatoes were fine, but the dish did not meet expectations.

Dessert, the brownie with ice cream and whipped cream, was underwhelming. The brownie was chewy and lacked a deep soft chocolate flavor, and the ice cream and whipped cream were very standard.

Service was okay but not particularly friendly. The restaurant was very loud, the chair unstable, and the table uncomfortable due to poor legroom.

Overall, not bad, but not good either. I would probably not come back.

We’ve come here for happy hour twice. Made a reservation to make sure to be seated, was easy to get last minute reservation. Their outdoor patio is very nice when the weather is nice. They didn’t specifically tell us about happy hour when we were seated, and we had to ask about it and they explained that it was $10 appetizers, $5 beers and $8 wines.

We tried all the appetizers and our favorites were the octopus and arancini.

While food was good and happy hour selection and prices were decent, service was very slow and it’s hard to get the staff’s attention. They didn’t come by or actively check if we needed them, and we had to try to get their attention n several times without them seeing. The first time we thought it was because we were seated in the patio and there were more people, but the second time we were inside and the place was much emptier. When we finally got the waiter’s attention to order, happy hour time was over and he said he could only give us the happy hour price for drinks and not food. After explaining that we were trying to get his attention for a while he agreed to honor the happy hour price, but we didn’t feel great about needing to have this interaction. So would recommend coming earlier if you’re here for happy hour.

Their menu consists of your regular taqueria items such as tacos, burritos, quesadillas, nachos, plates, soups, breakfast plates, breakfast burritos, desserts, housemade drinks and much more to choose from. They even offer catering with a separate menu just for that option. Today we dined at Nari and chose the Chef’s Pick course at $120 per person, excluding drinks and tax. I do not say this lightly: this was one of the most disappointing tasting-menu experiences I have ever had, especially for a restaurant positioned at this level.

Let me be clear: I fully understand that “Thai-inspired” does not mean strictly authentic Thai food. A restaurant has every right to reinterpret a cuisine, modernize it, or take creative liberties with its flavor language. But when you call something Thai-inspired, there still needs to be a coherent culinary philosophy behind it. Inspiration should mean refinement, interpretation, and balance, not the abandonment of ingredient integrity.

What troubled me most throughout the meal was the kitchen’s heavy and relentless dependence on aggressive seasoning. Across multiple courses, the spices, aromatics, sauces, and condiments did not elevate the ingredients; they buried them. Good cooking, regardless of whether it is Thai, French, Japanese, or modern Californian, begins with understanding the natural character of the main ingredient and seasoning it in a way that reveals, sharpens, or complements that character. Here, the opposite happened. The seasoning was so loud and so dominating that the food lost all clarity. Instead of tasting the produce, the protein, or the craftsmanship of the ingredient itself, I felt like I was tasting layer upon layer of seasoning with no restraint and no precision.

That, in my view, is a fundamental culinary failure. Seasoning is meant to support food, not replace it. Spice should create dimension, not confusion. Sauce should carry flavor, not suffocate it. When every bite is overwhelmed, the palate becomes fatigued very quickly, and the meal stops being pleasurable. Throughout dinner, I repeatedly found myself asking: what am I actually eating? That is never a good sign in a tasting menu, where every course should have intention, structure, and a clear point of view.

By the middle of the meal, we had barely touched much of the food and ended up leaving roughly half of it unfinished. That is extremely unusual for us. In fact, we were so eager for the experience to end that we even skipped the dessert included in the set menu entirely. I cannot remember the last time I wanted a meal to be over this quickly.

The service only made things worse. From the moment we walked in to the moment we left, the man at the front counter hardly bothered to look up and speak to guests, as he seemed more occupied with his phone. First impressions matter in hospitality, and this one was cold, inattentive, and dismissive. Even more disappointing, when feedback was invited, it did not feel genuine. If a restaurant is not actually interested in hearing customer feedback, it would be better not to ask at all. Asking for input and then responding with attitude when a guest expresses dissatisfaction reflects poorly not only on service standards, but on the restaurant’s entire culture of hospitality.

Yes, the manager offered two complimentary drinks, but unfortunately those were poorly executed as well. A gesture of compensation only helps if the replacement itself shows care and quality. In this case, it did not.

For me, this dinner failed on both of the pillars that matter most in a restaurant experience: food and hospitality. Creativity without balance is not refinement. Complexity without discipline is not sophistication. And service without warmth or professionalism undermines everything happening on the plate.

We only left 10% on the total, and that was not a tip, it was simply our final statement on the experience. If Google allowed it, I would rate this place 0 stars.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Vientian Cafe is one of those neighborhood gems that’s easy to miss if you aren’t specifically looking for it. Tucked into a residential area of Oakland, it’s absolutely worth seeking out. Judging by how busy it was, the locals already know how good it is! We visited at 2 p.m. on a Friday, and the restaurant was completely full, with multiple groups dining in and a steady stream of people picking up takeout orders.

The staff was friendly and welcoming, and despite how busy they were, everything ran smoothly.

We ordered a fresh lemonade, fresh chicken spring rolls, combination fried rice, Thai-style papaya salad, and Pad Kee Mao with tofu. Every dish was fresh, flavorful, and generously portioned. The papaya salad had a great balance of sweet, sour, and spice, the Pad Kee Mao was packed with flavor, and the spring rolls were a perfect, fresh start to the meal.

Including tip, our meal came to $84, which felt like a fair price considering the quality, portion sizes, and variety of dishes we ordered. The portions were generous enough that we were able to take home enough leftovers for an entire second meal, making it an even better value.

If you’re looking for authentic, delicious Southeast Asian food in Oakland, Vientian Cafe is definitely worth adding to your list. We’ll absolutely be back to explore more of the menu.

Usually this place is pretty quiet with just a few people, but I went on a Friday night and it was packed (see photos). There were almost no seats available, so it felt like they were basically pushing takeout orders.

That said, the food is delicious. It feels about as authentic as it gets in the Bay Area—similar to some of the spots I used to go to before they changed—so I’m glad places like this still exist.

I ordered the pad Thai noodles with fried tofu, vegetarian rolls, mango sticky rice (so good), and Thai iced tea. Everything was great, but the mango sticky rice really stood out.
Got the Bun Bo Nuong Cha Gio to go, it was amazing so flavorful and it was a big portion. I also got the mango sticky rice delicious. But i had to save it cuz i was way too full.

Spontaneously found this place while traveling through Oakland. The biggest Thai coffee ever and honestly the best one - the RIGHT amount of coffee to sweet instead of overly sweet. We had spring rolls (generous amounts of cilantro) with peanut sauce, angel wings (amazingly crispy), green curry with chicken and sticky rice. I will come by again next time I go through town!

One of my ultimate favorite restaurants in the Bay Area! We come here at least once a month, and have been doing so for years. The food is so consistently on point and the service is great. Be sure to order the chx noodle soup, the nam koa, the som pak, and the green curry. 6-stars if I could… GOAT!!

The biggest issue is still the ordering process. top_reviews.content:
Really impressed with Pho 2000. I ordered the large Phở Đặc Biệt, a Vietnamese iced coffee with condensed milk, and a Thai iced tea, and everything was very good.

The pho was the highlight. The broth was flavorful and comforting, the portion was generous, and the combination of different beef cuts made it a great choice if you want to try a little bit of everything. It was also a breezy, overcast, foggy San Francisco evening in the low 60s, which made a hot bowl of pho feel absolutely perfect.

The Vietnamese coffee was strong, rich, and sweet, and the Thai iced tea was creamy and refreshing.

Overall, great food, generous portions, and a very satisfying meal. I would definitely come back to Pho 2000.

My daughter and I stopped by Pho 2000 after a show at the Orpheum Theater, and we're glad we did! The restaurant was packed when we arrived, which is always a good sign, but we were seated quickly. The staff was incredibly friendly, and the complimentary hot tea was the perfect start to the meal. The pho was absolutely delicious, and the prices were surprisingly affordable. Great food, great service, and great value. We'll definitely be back!

Pho 2000 is a no-nonsense hole-in-the-wall Vietnamese spot that is not especially fancy or polished, but it is serving up piping hot, flavorful bowls of pho that absolutely hit the spot. The staff were all super friendly and very prompt with things like water, tea, and bussing dirty plates and bowls, which I really appreciated.

I ordered the #3, the beef pho with rare steak, well-done flank, tendon, and tripe. I tried the broth on its own first and it had a nice depth of flavor before I added my usual dashes of hoisin and sriracha. I also ordered the rare steak on the side since I hate when it gets overcooked, and it was a good test of how hot the soup was when the slices started to turn that perfect light pink gradually as it continued to simmer in the broth.

I liked the pieces of tendon and tripe that were in the bowl, but honestly there could have been a lot more of both since those are some of my favorite bites of pho. The goi cuon, or shrimp and pork spring rolls, were pretty standard and decently fresh, though I'm not sure I'd order them again given the price as they were effectively 2 long rolls cut into 6 pieces for over $10.

Overall, this is a great spot if you're just looking to scratch a quick pho fix and happen to be in the neighborhood.

Whoever said this place has good bánh xèo: apologize to me, and I will take you to a better place. It was the worst bánh xèo I’ve had in my entire life. It was thick, wet, undercooked and unseasoned dough. Slimy and completely flavorless. I was genuinely confused. I’ve never had bad bánh xèo before, and I order it at every Vietnamese restaurant that serves it. How do you mess up a fried pancake?

As for the bún riêu, everything else was fine, but they used tofu that had clearly gone bad (2 out of the 4 pieces were distinctly sour, disgusting, and slimy inside). The bún bò Huế had good broth, but the amount of meat was disappointing, with very little variety in protein. I had been looking forward to coming here. I won’t be back.

I went here for the first time and it was an amazing experience. The food was incredible , especially the pho. The broth was so rich and flavorful, it really stood out.

What impressed me just as much as the food was the service. Our server carried the hot bowl of pho like it was nothing , I touched it for a second and it was really hot, so I was honestly amazed!

The staff made us feel so welcome and taken care of. Our server was very attentive, and even the manager came by to check on us, helped fix our plates, and made sure everything was perfect. That level of care made us feel really special.

Now, why only 3 stars then? The service: it’s not good. For context, we made our reservation about a month in advance and were excited because this was our first time here. About half way through eating (after only being there for 25-30 minutes) they started to try to clear the table, as in taking the food off the table that we were actively eating. That was the second weird thing. Then, as we’re finishing our meals, we asked the see a dessert menu and ordered. As they delivered dessert, they brought the check and we paid. Before we were even finished eating the dessert, they came over and said “thank you for coming, we need the table”. I shit you not, we were rushed out so fast that I literally grabbed the last bit of dessert with my bare hands so that we could eat it. Strangely, there were tables around us with patrons that had been there before us and were allowed to stay as we were being rushed out.

All together, the food was amazing. Compliments to the chef! But the service was seriously some of the worst I’ve had at any restaurant, let alone a Michelin star restaurant. What gets me is that they give you the bill before you’re done, so you pay and tip. And then the service gets even worse, so it makes you wish you could reevaluate your tip.

I wish we wanted to go back because the food was good, but honestly it’s not worth the bad experience. Oakland and SF are filled with amazing food, so no need to go somewhere with bad service.

What an absolute gem of a restaurant! I’ve wanted to dine here for years and finally made it happen. There are tons of vegan and vegetarian options and the food is phenomenal. They also have a nice mezcal selection. We had the taquitos, tamales, asparagus main, and queso. Would absolutely order everything again. Oh! And the staff is so nice and attentive—we had the pleasure of having a wonderful fellow as our main server (I hate that I didn’t catch his name!) but he was so kind and friendly, really made our dining experience even better.

If you’re here for the first time, I would recommend:
- Smoked Trout tostadas: great appetizer! Beautifully balanced.
- Spicy Carrots Misantla: this is a vegan dish but it’s so flavorful and memorable. I want them to release a cookbook so I can recreate it.
- Smoked Duck Confit: rich and delicious.

I would skip the potato flautas (unremarkable). The pollo rostizado is a generous serving; it can easily serve 4 people. But the taste of the marinade is just average, and the salsa verde is dialed down for the Piedmont and Allendale gringos.

It’s a cute place for date night.The first time I came here, the music was way too loud. They turned it down the last time.

Service during my last visit could be improved. They’re VERY pushy on the chips and salsa; we were asked 5 times if we wanted them( which are not complimentary! And with added 10.75% tax and 18% tip, will add another $11+ to your bill. Dining in Oakland is ridiculous!). Something as simple as that should be complimentary honestly, like Korean banchan.

We also were asked for refills on our cocktails and desserts multiple times by multiple staff. It felt like they were trying to add more items to our bill, despite us having 2 cocktails and 4 dishes already.

FYI, they don’t do any complimentary bday treats or wishes. I listed my reservation as a bday dinner on Resy and it didn’t seem to make a difference. A greeting would have at least been nice!

On the upside, we were seated all the way in the back near the bathroom, and Chef Dominica constantly checked in on us during our meal. She even waved when we left! That was nice of her.

top_reviews.content: I’ve had pizza all over the world, and this might actually be the best there is. I was never a fan of fusion food but this is just next level. We’ve been getting the vegetarian pizza from Zantes for more than 20 years. The spices and seasonings, and especially the sauce, are delicious.

Ordered a large paneer tikka masala pizza quoted on the menu pasted outside the door as $29.99. The guy said okay you can pay in advance 10 minutes when it’s ready. I should have insisted that I pay in advance - I’ve learned my lesson! I go up to pay and he rings me up for $47.24!! I ask for clarity on the price and he points me to a small, handwritten sign saying to add 45% to all menu prices, followed by new prices for each pizza size. I think this is  pretty sleazy. It’s not that hard to update the menu pasted outside, even with painters tape or something over the old prices. To me, this was clearly a ploy to surprise customers with higher prices at the end so they can no longer say no. I brought the pizza home to give it a fair shot before writing the review, but in my opinion it was not very good. I’ve had much better Indian pizzas. It was not very flavorful and the crust is very dry. Needless to say, I will sadly not be returning. Would have been nice to find a good Indian pizza spot in Bernal!

I remember eating here many years ago and found it interesting and refreshing. Today, with the plethora of Indian pizza joints in the Bay, Zante has sadly fallen.

The poorly lit interior with barebones decor and faded posters must invoke a cozy atmosphere, but in reality comes off a bit depressing once the food comes out. The paneer pakoras were barely salted or spiced. The spinach soup had giant pieces of ginger floating in it. The onion bhaji, while crunchy, did not elevate or transport to a good experience. It's really hard to mess up pakoras for a joint that's been around for decades, but that's the sad reality.

The pizza somewhat compensated for the experience. It was as delicious as I remembered it to be with the tikka masala sauce leading the charge. But, overall the place has lost its zing.
Best Indian pizza, highly suggest. Authentic flavors and really fresh

Some of the best breads I’ve ever tasted!  The Indian pizza was delicious!  Our waiter was really hospitable and funny.  Service was quick.  The food was amazing. If you’re a fan of pizza and have never tried Indian pizza from this place, do yourself a favor and try this place asap!  You won’t regret it.

top_reviews.content:
If you’re looking for a solid, no-fuss pizza spot in San Francisco, Happy King’s Pizza absolutely delivers. 🍕

From the moment you walk in, the vibe is casual, welcoming, and perfect for a quick bite or laid-back meal. The staff is friendly and efficient, and you can tell they take pride in what they’re serving.

The pizza itself is the real star—crispy crust, flavorful sauce, and generous toppings without being over-the-top. Every bite hits that perfect balance of cheesy, savory, and satisfying. Whether you’re grabbing a slice on the go or ordering a whole pie to share, it’s consistently good.

What I really appreciate is the value—you get great quality without breaking the bank, which is rare in the city. It’s the kind of place you find yourself coming back to again and again.

Highly recommend if you’re in the area and craving a classic, delicious slice. 🍕🔥

Trash! Never been so disappointed by a pizza spot in SF. It's not made clear by the sign but the only style of pizza by the slice is pepperoni. The pepperoni were cupped full of grease as you might be able to see in my video. The vibe inside just felt sad as nobody looked like they enjoyed life! I wasn't given or told where to get napkins but I literally looked at everyone's table which had a roll of paper towels. The only reason why I didn't give them 1 star was because it beats paying $20 for a slice of pizza inside the ballpark! The portion was good and the price was right but please tell me this was just a fluke accident.

You can feel the love coming from a family type of restaurant. Great, friendly friends who were willing to go above and beyond to cook up a fresh slice when they had run out! They were so kind, knowing that were wasn’t much food around late, so they offered to cook one on the spot. Delicious and great portion size! Gotta try the paneer tikka pizza!

terrible pizzas and the person in counter was extremely rude. plus dirty washrooms. I wonder if the other reviews are paid folks because this is the second time i found the pizzas terrible. shouldn’t have come again. Avoid this place at all costs

My 3 friends were in line to get food because I really needed to use the customer-only restroom and we were willing to eat anyway. The sole cashier, presumably the owner, followed me and raised his voice repeating “the restroom is for customers only!” I explained I was a customer intending to pay, I just urgently needed to pee first. I literally begged for mercy.. but he made a whole scene ending with “I don’t care. please leave!” If your customers are already standing in line and a girl rushes to your restroom.. do you really need to YELL and stop her when she intends to be your customer..  Quite rude and it was so musty and quiet in there too. I’m all for good food but I don’t support mean people

I’ve driven by George’s Giant Hamburger on my way to work for the past 5 years, and last week one of my clients insisted I had to try it. I’m so glad I finally did — I only wish I had gone sooner!

My daughter and I both ordered the Bulgogi Burger and it was absolutely delicious. Everything on the menu looked amazing, and we can’t wait to come back and try more burgers soon. Highly recommend! 🍔✨

Delicious food and wonderful staff! Very kind 😄 definitely one of my favorite food places the angus in house ground patty was so fresh and perfectly done per my preference and everyone was so nice and friendly. Will be back! Does not leave you feeling heavy compared to other burger places. Very reasonable prices, affordable. High quality and yummy!

Everything I had exceeded my expectation including curly fries. Bulgogi burger was intriguing but I had to try classic cheeseburger also.

Both were SO GOOD. Cheeseburger was rich, smoky, cheesy goodness with drizzling au jus just about every bite. And bulgogi burger… omg it is amazing. The sweet sautéed onion and then meaty saltiness with crunchy French roll. I took so many bites and wanted more. It’s pretty good sized burger too. I normally leave some buns when I eat burgers or sandwiches, but bun to meat ratio was on point.

Also, I couldn’t help but notice how spanking clean this place is despite looking nostalgic old school establishment. Tables, countertops, salt and pepper shakers, floor, chairs, ketchup spouts, etc all clean. No stickiness, no dust, no dried sauce.

Full of locals, attentive and personal service to everyone dining here. I’m not a local here but it’s worth coming back for.

Shimizu is our go-to for sushi when we go out to eat. The portions are great and the quality is perfect! Would 10/10 go again, great value and great service.

Our favorite sushi spot! Always delicious sushi options, excellent staff and service! We really appreciate that they have tamari as a gluten-free option for soy sauce. If you haven’t stopped by here - think of this place the next time you want sushi!

Really loved our meal here! Everything tasted fresh and vibrant,
you can tell the kitchen really cares about what they're making. The service was super quick and kind, and they were so accommodating with our toddler, which we really appreciated.
