top_reviews.content: My chicken taco salad $14.60 felt small. It only encompassed 1/3 of the container. They use to-go containers even though you are eating there. There's no dine-in option on the kiosk. It is a tremendous waste of plastic. Plus, when they close the lid, it smushed the salad. A plate would have been better. The salad needed balance and more flavors. There was only half a spoon of pico de gallo. While I ordered chicken, most of the salad was beans and rice. The taco shell bowl was good. It was flicky and tasted fresh. The chips were too hard to be edible. You can easily chip a molar. Those were thrown in the trash. At least the food came out fast. The chef didn't spend any time on it.

I ordered a regular pollo asada burrito and found it lacked the flavor I was used to. I only ate about half before deciding not to finish it due to the boring flavor.

Have the recipes or ownership changed recently? I noticed a few differences from previous visits, including guacamole being added to the regular burrito (which wasn't included before) and black beans instead of pinto beans.

Overall, I’m disappointed the burrito tasted noticeably different from what I remember.

The greatest burrito I've ever had! I got the El Norcal and it's going to give Thanksgiving a run for its money for the biggest food coma!!
Everything was hot and delicious! No skimping on these burritos! If you don't come hungry, you're going to leave with leftovers that could feed a small nation.
There's some seats inside. And a bench that hugs the building. Great place to get something to go!

This was honestly one of the most disappointing food experiences I’ve had in a long time. I walked in and stood at the counter while multiple employees looked directly at me and still didn’t acknowledge me. Not even a simple “we’ll be right with you.” Meanwhile, several people were standing around waiting for their orders with everyone glued to their phones. The entire place felt disorganized and completely indifferent to customers walking in.

Then the food came out and it was even worse. I ordered a burrito and two cans of Coke and the total came out to $18.85! which would be fine if the portion actually matched the price! The burrito I received was shockingly small, honestly, closer to something you’d give a little kid than a full meal for an adult. For that price, the portion size is borderline insulting.

The frustrating part is the flavor was actually good and the steak itself tasted great, which makes the tiny portion even more ridiculous. It feels like the place is intentionally cutting portions while still charging full prices. When customers have to pay first before seeing their food, it makes it feel like you’re getting taken advantage of if what you receive doesn’t match what you paid for.

After looking through other reviews, it’s clear I’m not the only person saying this. Multiple people mention shrinking portions and inconsistent service. That should be a major red flag for management.

If this place keeps treating customers this way ignoring people at the counter and serving undersized portions for premium prices, people in the community are going to stop coming. There are plenty of other Mexican food spots around that actually respect their customers and give you a portion that matches the price.

I won’t be coming back.

I stopped by El Burrito Express to have a quick bite. it is a small, no-frills corner eatery with an expansive burrito menu. No line or wait on a Thursday morning so service was fast. I ordered a grilled chicken burrito and I enjoyed it. It's pretty standard stuff but for the price it has great value. My favorite taquerías in the Mission has gone way too expensive these days.

top_reviews.content:
I've always wanted to try Bon Nene because many friends raved about their food. Overall, I'm not disappointed! So, my first impression was that, this restaurant was popular for sure, I came here just by its open time (at 5:35pm on a Friday), but their tables were almost filled (2 groups behind were put on a waitlist - crazy). The place was small, I think like 40 max capacity. But food was served quickly.
What I had:
Mentaiko spaghetti: I heard this is a must try, and honestly they don't lie. You may miss protein, but the spaghetti creamy sauce was just too addictive I don't mind
Marugo bowl: basically a tuna poke bowl. I need some proteins, but I don't find it too special, you can just skip it
Yuzunade: staff told me this is more popular than milk tea so I ordered it. Basically a lemonade, kinda refreshing if you took 19k steps just to save the calories for the meal like me.
They served pocky as complementary desserts! Super cuteeee! Overall, great restaurant! I will be back for the spaghetti for sure!!!

Overrated and disappointing. The place is nice and clean, but the food was not good. The $6 pickles were honestly almost funny—literally two slices of cucumber and a tiny bit of cabbage, with barely any pickled flavor. We also didn’t enjoy the chicken karaage, noodles/ spagetti, and beef rice.

The homemade drinks were disappointing too. We ordered the yuzu sake and there were actual lemon seeds floating in it??

Our bill was $94. If portions are going to be this small, the food needs to be really good. Here, the portions were small and unfortunately the flavor wasn’t there either. Definitely not worth the price. Hopefully they improve because the place has a lot of potential.

very quaint and cozy atmosphere, gets crowded quickly with a waitlist to write your name on outside. we had got there right as they opened for brunch at 12, but told they could not make about half of the items on the menu. wait time for food was overall okay, appetizers and drinks came out quickly but took a bit for us to get our entrées. many tables had received their food far before ours even though we had ordered the exact same dishes as them.

the katsu curry rice and karaage were average. the curry was well balanced, but i do wish they did something more with the sauce for the karaage as it wasn’t really adding anything extra. the mentaiko pasta was good, perfectly cooked and sauce was flavorful. the garnish of perilla/shiso leaves was perfect and added some freshness; i see why this is the most popular menu item. the drinks were also good, their royal milk tea isn’t too sweet although i do think it’s interesting to charge an extra dollar to have it as an iced drink instead of warm. their yuzu lemonade is nice and refreshing.

overall the food is good, to me it’s nothing particularly new or anything that stands out from other japanese restaurants i’ve been to. however if i’m in the area again i would like to try their other menu items given that they’re available.

no wait list, so on a friday night for 3 people at 6:30pm we waited 45 minutes to be seated

the food is french fusion and japanese and it was delicious! The rice bowls have a lottt of rice, which is exactly what they do in japan, but i do wish it had an extra slice or two of fish ><

the mentaiko spaghetti was actually way better than i thought it would be! it's a little smaller of a serving, but it's rich in flavor and very filling!

beer, dinner , an desert were all delicious. the staff was very friendly (though they never refilled our waters)

Even the Internet may not tell you but Bon, Nene’s wonderful Japanese breakfast is available from 10:00am only on Fridays and Saturdays!

I tried their breakfast on May 22, 2026.
The breakfast is beautifully presented, scrumptious and really healthy, which has many kinds of veggies.

The miso soup is packed with ingredients, which is great!

It’s fun to have a choice for a rice ball, or “onigiri.”
Since I grew up in Fukuoka prefecture in Japan, I chose “mentaiko.” It is delicious and I love the generous amount of mentaiko in it.

The typical traditional Japanese breakfast has a grilled salmon slice for breakfast. Here, it’s a thick fried salmon, which we can get more protein and I love that.

The dessert, chocolate warabi-mochi is a delicious rare treat. It’s very hard to find a Japanese restaurant that serves it.

The restaurant has plenty of natural light and the vibe is great.
The service is flawless.

I had so much fun here and I will definitely go back. Highly recommended!

It’s wow. The food absolutely delicious but not $40 per person delicious . The view is stunning.

The service is good.

Update: went back and sat at a table, the service was amazing and would be 5 stars if my previous experience wasn't so poor. The food was solid and fast.

Never got to try the food. Sat at the bar, got a drink quickly and then for the next 30 minutes the bartender never even checked on me or took my order, or asked if I needed anything else. I should have asked to move to a table where the servers seemed far more responsive. People seem to like the food and the view is cool being right on the bay. If I end up going back and I have a different experience I will change this but I ended up ordering from door dash to actually get food.

I made a reservation for next week, but after checking their wine list, I immediately canceled it.

The entire selection was focused on California wines, with nothing from France or Italy.
For a seafood restaurant that wants to offer a refined dining experience, this is a major disappointment. I have no interest in drinking sugary, over-extracted California wines with seafood.
A restaurant can have a beautiful location and maybe good food, but the wine is part of the experience. Based on the wine list alone, this was not the place for me.

reviews_snippets.content: "Great food, excellent service, tasty drinks"

"This restaurant has some of the best staff in the service industry."

top_reviews.content:
We really enjoyed our meal at Wojia Hunan! The fresh boiled spicy fish was definitely the highlight — the fish was so tender and literally melted in your mouth. The pork ribs were crispy on the outside and tender and flavorful inside.

The chow mein was also really good. It had that nice 锅气 that I really love — you can really taste that smoky, wok-fried flavor. Everything was flavorful and satisfying. Would definitely come back!

First time coming here. My friend recommended this place, so we came for Mother's Day lunch. The restaurant is kind of big and there are plenty of seats, but parking was kind of a struggle since the parking lot is pretty small and fills up fast (especially holidays or special days)

We ordered
1.Yang Chow Fried Rice  $25.95
2.Eggplant with String Beans  $25.95
3. Braised Pig Feet & Chicken Feet  $26.95
4. Glutinous Rice Balls (peanut filling)  $18.95
5. Spicy & Cumin Pork Chops  $23.95

The only downside was that they seemed pretty understaffed. We had to wait a while before anyone came to take our order. But honestly, all the food was really good. My favorite was definitely the eggplant with string beans, so flavorful and really well cooked. I also liked that you can ask for lower sodium dishes if you want. I would want to come back again to try other things on the menu.

This Hunan Restaurant offers a delicious and satisfying dining experience. The sticky rice pork ribs are tender and flavorful, while the green beans and eggplant are perfectly seasoned and rich in taste. The spicy lamb skewers are also a standout, bursting with bold flavor. Don’t miss the brown sugar ziba — it’s soft, sweet, and aromatic. The restaurant has a clean, traditional atmosphere that adds to the charm. I’ll definitely be coming back again!

Wojia is my favorite hunanese restaurant in the Bay area. Will definitely be back again and again.

The food is spicy and has good wok hei.

Farmers bowl is my favorite with mushroom, jalapenos, pork and egg.

The dan dan noodles are nice but skimp a little on the pork. The sauce is delicious tho.

The Kung Pao chicken was a tad sweet but still yummy. No cornstarch coating. No deep frying.

The water chestnut, broccoli and lilly was nice to cut the spice.

The human lamb was soft. The meat is velveted but not coated with starch which I prefer. Same with the Kung Pao chicken.

They don't have a parking lot.

D02 Chilli boiled flounder fillet was terrible.  Fish not fresh and soup tasteless.  We did not eat after first bite.  The staff discounted the original $28.95 for this fish dish by $7.50.   Other dishes were fine.

top_reviews.content: Stumbled on this spot walking through the neighborhood. Wow. Got the #5. It was fabulous and comforting. I could only eat half. Looking forward to coming back for the Vermicelli!

The two aunties working are amazing, very sweet ladies! This restaurant is a quintessential hole-in-the-wall experience with good food to boot. We enjoyed the five spice chicken, pork chops, and imperial roll. It's a small place but very cozy - although not my favorite in terms of viet food, I would 1000% come back if I'm in the area because it was such a fun experience. The aunties are very giving and there is a real cozy feeling that's hard to describe.

They take cash or venmo! There's a chase bank around the corner so you can also grab cash if you need.

I visit SF a few times a year for work and the first thing I always go get is Cordon Bleu. It is tradition. It is the best Vietnamese I’ve ever had, hands down. And a perfect cozy no frills environment. Thank you for always offering a genuine experience. Your food truly heals my soul.
This is a local classic. This place has been around for 55 years and the food is great every time. And such great prices as well! Would definitely recommend checking it out.

This little spot had some of the most delicious and affordable cooking around, which felt like a homemade meal. I ended up trying their #5 and loved it all. The chicken, the kebabs, and the imperial roll were 🧑‍🍳 chefs kiss. It is a small space, and while there were spaces when we got in, expect a tight and cozy environment.

name: Little Original Joe's
address: 393 W Portal Ave, San Francisco, CA 94127, United States

top_reviews.content:
Found this place not far from our stonestown lodging and it's been a staple during our long stay. They have a reliable and easy ordering and pickup system, it's been fairly simple to find parking for pickup, and the little market has been great too for some unique tinned fish and soft drinks. The selection of premade foods and pantry ingredients is superb as well albeit at higher end prices.

We've had a simple pepperoni pie most of the time and it's been a hit each time. Hot, savory, crispy, salty, and well balanced. The cheese baked in the crust is a treat too with such a good crunchy chew. I've had the Caesar wrap a couple times which is lovely with a good ratio of dressing, croutons, and chicken. Their potato chips are tasty but nothing mind blowing, at least not after 6 or 7 minute car ride. Don't miss the bottle of ranch for 8 bucks in the fridge either. It's top tier and worth every penny for the price (but heavy on dill flavor if that's a problem for you). The garlic bread was good too but probably best enjoyed on the spot (or tossed in the air fryer) to enjoy the thick, rich garlic spread on it.

The staff is friendly and runs a well oiled machine for the store and for pickup, which would be expected at this price point. For the quality and quantity the prices are fair however and there's a reason it's been busy every single time we've came by. Worth a stop in, even worth going a little out of your way I think.
Fantastic food and service in a great atmosphere.  Had the supreme pizza , chicken parm, and little joes ravioli.  And of course the famous Zucchini fries!  You must go here.  Long wait but worth it!

Great atmosphere and great service. The zucchini fries are amazing (but will create a mess all over the table), and will fill you up before dinner if you’re not careful. Service is great. Burger is average. Skillet cookie and ice cream is awesome. No reservations on weekends, two hour wait is not uncommon particularly during peak dinner hours.

This place is sooo popular, we were not able to get in for dinner but we miraculously got in for brunch, which was just as good.

We were here on a girls’ weekend trip and had the best time.  Radmir was our server, and he was the best.  Despite how busy it was, Radmir was very attentive to our group and checked up on us frequently.

The food is soooo good.  I would suggest going with a larger group like us (six total) so you can try different things.  Portions are pretty large but we managed to eat most and only boxed up a couple of things.  I have to say EVERYTHING we had was good from the donut apps to our entrees, to our drinks.  We passed on dessert bc we were soooo full but would definitely need to try that next time.

Overall a great experience.  If you’re looking for good service, good food and ambiance, this is your place!

I love Joe's but I will not tolerate this. For $20 I have got this sandwich and while it was expensive it was tasty and stuffed. This is half the ingredients between the bread. I am very disappointed.

reviews_snippets.content: "If you’re looking for good service, good food and ambiance, this is your place!"

address: 1438 Broadway, Oakland, CA 94612, United States

google.name: Edible Happy Pizzeria
google.address: 1438 Broadway, Oakland, CA 94612, United States

top_reviews.content:
This past weekend, I tried this place for the first time and ordered a vegan margherita pizza and fries for pickup. When I got home, I realized it was missing basil, which is a pretty key part of that style of pizza.

I called right away, and the staff was polite and offered to remake it, either that night or if I brought the pizza back within the next couple of days. I appreciated that they were willing to fix it, but having to hold onto the pizza and bring it back later felt a bit inconvenient—especially with a busy schedule. In my experience, many places are a bit more flexible and will honor a remake or refund with just a receipt or even a photo.

I did try a slice hoping it would still be decent, but unfortunately it just wasn’t good. The flavor really missed the mark, especially for a vegan option.

On a positive note, the staff was friendly and professional, which I do appreciate. I just think there’s some room for improvement in both quality (at least for the vegan margherita pizza) and how issues like this are handled for customers who can't easily return.

Not the best first experience especially after spending $45 for pizza and fries.  Customer service is very important in any restaurant business, therefore, if they can't make this right, I'm sure that was our last time ordering from there.
The shop is very clean and modern, very nice interior design and atmosphere. The pizza is amazing, owner is very friendly. I would highly recommend this pizza place, will definitely come back again

Ordered this twice on our trip. It is so good. I highly recommend. Some of the best pizza we've had. We had it delivered to our hotel. We stuck with cheese and sausage both times. Amazing. We got the 20 inch and it fed 9, 2 girls and 7 adults.

Our group thoroughly enjoyed the wide variety of pizzas offered at this restaurant. The menu features options for every preference, from classic cheese pizzas to vegetarian selections, hearty meat-lovers’ pies, and even creatively crafted Indian-inspired pizzas. Each pizza was thoughtfully prepared, with fresh ingredients and well-balanced flavors that kept everyone coming back for more. The diversity of options allowed each member of our party to find something they loved, making it an ideal choice for gatherings. The combination of quality ingredients, inventive flavor profiles, and consistently delicious execution makes this spot a standout for pizza enthusiasts. Whether you’re dining with friends, family, or colleagues, the variety and flavor ensure a satisfying and memorable experience. This restaurant is highly recommended for anyone seeking both traditional and innovative pizza options that deliver on taste and creativity.

I’m so impressed with this vegan selection pizza restaurant — everything tastes unbelievably fresh, and you can truly tell they take pride in what they do. The moment you take your first bite, you notice how thoughtfully crafted every part of the pizza is.

The standout for me is definitely the dough. The texture is perfectly chewy, soft, and so flavorful that you could honestly enjoy the bread by itself. It has that satisfying bite that you only get from dough made fresh in-house. It’s light yet still hearty, and it holds all the toppings beautifully without ever becoming soggy.

The flavors are bold, vibrant, and so unique. The Indian spices blend seamlessly with classic pizza elements, creating something comforting but exciting at the same time. Every topping tastes fresh — the vegetables are crisp, the sauces are well-balanced, and the cheese melts into everything so harmoniously. You can tell they don’t cut corners on ingredients.

Even though the shop isn’t huge, everything feels welcoming, warm, and made with care. The staff is friendly, the service is quick, and the quality is consistently excellent every time I visit. It’s the kind of place you immediately want to introduce to your friends.

If you’re looking for delicious vegan-style pizza with exceptional freshness and a crust that’s chewy, soft, and full of flavor, this spot is absolutely worth checking out. One bite and you’ll understand why so many people love it!

top_reviews.content:
Daiso, Alameda (South Shore Center)

I’ve been here many times, the staff are awesome and friendly.

This Daiso location has a lot of stuff but it’s very small, it’s a very tight squeeze when you’re trying to walk past people.

The prices for their items has gone up over the years.

Like all Daiso locations, there’s no return or exchange. All sales are final.

Highly recommend to buy school supplies and some Sanrio, Hello Kitty stuff.

Love the availability of Japanese sourced goods, but having seen the original Daiso in Japan and all the items truly for ¥100, the American version seems overpriced for the value.  The food specifically seemed limited, but, again, I’m used to the amount of choices in Japan.  The layout of the store is easy to understand and navigate, and although limited, the cute Japanese knick-knacks are plentiful.  If you’re jonesing for Japanese goody fix, then try this place.
Stil a nice store but things are not how it used to. More expensive now. And leas durable. This $6 lunch tote got torn just a month of use.

It has everything you need in your arts and crafts, household, care and beauty ❤️
On the other hand do NOT even think about returns and exchange🚫 Think twice before purchasing or come back when you definitely need them.
But seriously, i don't want to come back if that's the case.
I'm ok with not returning, but exchange should be allowed for non-food products. It takes some time to commute, gas, and planning, so plz reconsider your exchange policy Diaso!
The staff is helpful and there are plenty of duplicates of items. It can feel crowded really fast because there's not a lot of square footage.

top_reviews.content:
Hi-Way is the best SF burger spot. The cheeseburgers are perfect every time (tip: add grilled onions and get spicy ranch on the side)

They have great fries, crispy onion rings that actually keep the onion inside soft, and there’s tubs of pickles and peppers to ear on the side. The Oreo shake is exceptional, Straus’ soft serve with a ton of Oreos in it!
Wanted burgers and beeps was too far so found this little gem and it was super worth it! Definitely would come back. Quick to get my order with nice indoor seating. Big fan!

The food here is really good. I have tried the burgers, grilled chicken, and fried chicken and would recommend them all. It's a good value for the price too. I also enjoyed the garlic fries (VERY garlicky!) and onion rings. My only nitpick is that the sweet potato fries were pretty bland and I wish they had more seasoning. Definitely recommend this place if you are in the mood for burgers.

Walked by this spot often and always loved how friendly they were so I stopped in for a double cheeseburger - was honestly blown away! Solid juicy grilled patties and fresh ingredients - doesn’t leave you feeling too “greasy” after either. Went back twice! Def one of my fave burger spots!!

Another stop on my never ending journey to try all sf popular burger places. Had to trek out to Noe Valley for this spot and it was worth the commute. Good burger and fries to be found here. And they have Barqs rootbeer on fountain.

top_reviews.content: I ate at this restaurant because it is only a few blocks from my apartment and I am glad I ate here. This is really good Indian food. The best Indian food I have had so far. The fish was amazingly delicious and the soup 🍜 was really good too. I highly recommend this place. I give them 5 stars

The food says it all. I'm a meat person, but the paneer was next level. This is the best authentic Indian cuisine I've had; including in asia. I'll be back soon before I go back to my uncultured home city...
We ordered the butter chicken and chicken tikka masala. The food was delicious. They use an authentic oven for their food. Servers were very kind.

Would go again! Seated immediately for 2 on Tuesday at 12:15pm. I was in a rush, but luckily service was fast and we were out by 12:50pm. Great for a quick lunch. The interior was spacious and there's a nice mural as well.

The waiter was kind, attentive, and wanted to make sure we had a good experience. He gave us a mango lassi ($6) and gulab jamun ($5) on the house.

We ordered the chicken tikka masala ($16), lamb vindaloo ($18), regular naan ($3), and garlic naan ($5). Would recommend getting a side of rice to soak up the sauces, since there's a good amount in the masala and vindaloo. The masala was incredibly creamy and the chunks of chicken were tender, not dry. Same for the vindaloo, which also had lots of yummy spices. I thought prices were reasonable.

Decided to pop in with my partner after passing by many times as a neighborhood local.

We were overall very satisfied with the experience! The ambience was clean and cultured with an upscale touch and the menu items had all the Indian classics.

We ordered the prawn jalfrezi, garlic naan and vegetable pakora - all of which were a bit generic in flavor but very decent.

Customer service was also a 5/5 - our waiter was kind, attentive and even gave us a complimentary beer for the wait. I’d really recommend this place for a date night.

top_reviews.content:
We had a great experience here! The tuna was fresh and buttery and everything we ordered was delicious. Prices were very good for the quality.

We also tried the chef’s Japanese sushi set. Not every type of fish was our favorite but it was a great way to try a variety of unique fish we hadn’t had before!

The eel hand rolls were another highlight absolutely delicious!

We came during Happy Hour so it was an even better value. The food came out quickly!
We made a reservation in advance. When we arrived there was a tablet to check in but we were seated before we even had a chance to use it haha. Fantastic experience and we’d definitely come back!

Very delicious sushi! It was all very high quality and the special tasted amazing! The service was also phenomenal- the waitress even gave us complementary sake on the house! However I will say the sushi is very pricy so be prepared.

Nara offers one of the best sushi experience I had in San Francisco. The sashimi bites were fresh and tasty. The staff were so friendly. They made great suggestions tailored to our needs. I highly recommend the Hamachi Truffle (on the spoons), I could have 100 of those!

Nara is an excellent sushi restaurant providing quality fish. The happy hour menu from 5-7 provides a great value.

Ordered the Tai, Sake, Hamachi and Hotate and the fish was flavorful and served in a hand rolls the fish portions were generous.

Our first time here, and we loved it. It started to get hectic when we got there. They sat us immediately.  We started off with chicken karaage. Fresh and crispy. Mostly meat and not a bunch of fried breading. Whatever the white dipping sauce was. It was delicious. We asked the waitress but she wasn't too sure. I had the Jessica Alba roll. I got it without sesame seeds. It had shrimp tempura inside and tobiko. Which in most places is a topping. They put it inside the sushi roll, and it still had that delicious pop and crunch. Had some cucumber in it as well. On top was delicious fresh white tuna or shiro maguro on the menu. Topped with eel sauce. When I say it was delicious.  I mean, I ordered 2 for myself. It was that good. I did share a few pieces with 2 people who were sitting at the same table as us. They loved it. My partner had the hamachi kama with side order of sushi rice. Which I highly recommend together. It's a can soda type of place, so those refills cost more, but they do have happy hours and drink specials on alcohol. I love this place. Can't wait to come back to the bay to eat here again. Domo arigato gozaimashita.

top_reviews.content:
June’s Pizza is a hidden gem that comes to the rescue after a night of drinking and socializing. Their pepperoni and burrata pizza is a must-try. The crust is perfectly thick, with an extra sprinkle of cheese that adds a delightful crunch. You can order your pizza at the counter, and the staff brings it to you in a laid-back and friendly manner.

June’s Pizza has been serving delicious pizzas for two years now. They have their own small parking lot and are open every evening until midnight. I can’t wait to return and explore their other pizzas and slices.

⭐⭐⭐⭐☆

June’s Pizza is a welcome addition to the neighborhood, and it’s easy to see why it’s so popular. The restaurant was very busy during our visit, with pizzas constantly moving through the assembly line and coming out of the oven at a steady pace. The staff was friendly, and it’s great to have another local pizza option nearby.

We ordered a Margherita pizza to go. The pizza itself was solid, but it wasn’t my favorite, especially considering the price. It felt a bit expensive for what you get.

One thing to be aware of if you’re ordering takeout: they call your name once when your pizza is ready and then set it on the pickup counter. There’s no warmer, and they don’t call your name again, so you’ll want to pay close attention to avoid your pizza sitting out longer than necessary.

Overall, it’s a good neighborhood spot with friendly service and a lively atmosphere. While the pizza didn’t quite justify the price for me, I’d still be open to trying some of their other offerings in the future.

Popular pizza place in West Oakland. Two-item menu. Usually a busy place with long line but efficient and quick.
Pizza is OK. For me, too much tomato sauce made it acidic taste with eggplant aftertaste.
Sourdough crust with kinda wood-burning oven is great though.
Indoor searing with very limited odor tables.
Limited parking spots shared with next door bar. Free street parking available.
Good for small groups, couples and not easy with kids.

I read the reviews and finally gave this place a try.
Casual spot with table and bar counter seating by the kitchen.
Cool decor.
Friendly staff.
Service was fairly quick at about a 10-15 min wait with 6 orders ahead of me.
XL pizza only (8 large slices) and each one is a meal.
Marg and Pepp were the only options besides a 1/2 & 1/2 combo.
Pizza tastes great, good mix of sauce, cheese and basil plus pepp, if you choose.
This is a definite spot worthy of a visit!

We had such a great time at June's! I love how simple the menu is, only offering three pizzas: margherita, pepperoni, and a rotating seasonal option. The staff were friendly and efficient. They answered my questions about allergens in the dipping sauces. Hooray for tree nut-free pesto! 🎉🍻

The ambiance was pretty rad too. The space has such tall ceilings that, although the tables are pretty crammed together, it didn't feel very cramped at all. The yellow tile on the pizza oven and the overall aesthetic of the place are really lovely.

The pizza was absolutely delicious. We particularly enjoyed the seasonal option, which had zucchini, green onion, and some other tasty toppings. The star of the show, though, was the pesto dipping sauce we got on the side.

I knew it was gonna be all bad when I received my food in less than 5 minutes. The fried rice was good but my cumin beef that looked nothing like the picture had a weird texture to it like it was old. The portion of my cumin beef definitely did not reflect an almost $20 price tag without the fried rice which came to almost $40. I will not return! There are way too many great Chinese restaurants in SF to settle for mediocre Chinese food! Service was great though.

Ordered takeout at this place and got the General chicken and potstickers. I wasn't disappointed at all. The chicken was perfectly cooked and coated with a delicious sauce, the potstickers were absolutely delectable and were cooked to perfection, and the price for it was absolutely reasonable despite the place being in one of the most expensive cities to live in California. My order was also ready in a short amount of time.  Overall, I'm satisfied and happy with the food and experience I had from ordering here. I definitely recommend this place.

I visit this restaurant yesterday the food was really good i tasted chicken chaumin and sweet and saur chicken really good . The environment is really good neat and clean as well the server tim is really friendly helpful fast as well highly recommend this place every one i will back soon i came here to visit from bernal height San Francisco.
We walked in and were immediately seated. Our food was ready about 10 minutes after ordering and was delicious.

top_reviews.content: Hole in the wall pizza place, I love to try these places and be surprised by awesome pizza in a bare bones setting. This one didnt bowl me over, but the crust is very nicely baked and the pepperoni is good.  Pesto mushroom is dense with small mushroom slices, well done.  The cheese they use is standard issue, nothing remarkable, unfortunately. But overall a good quick stop pizza slice on the local bar circuit.

We started out at Molinari’s deli, but after 15 minutes and the line hardly moving, we left and came here. We’re glad we did. We got a slice of pepperoni and combination and both were very good. The pizza had a very crispy crust and a well-balanced sauce. It was a large slice for the price. The best part of the experience was meeting the owner and his wife. Our experience at this dumpling house was a mix of practical positives and some notable drawbacks.

On the plus side, the dumplings are decent, and the prices are fair. The steady stream of delivery drivers in motorcycle helmets suggests its main business is takeout. For walk-in customers like us, this meant there was no wait and plenty of available seating, which was a convenience.

However, the physical space could use some attention; it felt a bit shabby and worn. A more significant issue for us was the menu's lack of vegetarian main courses. Aside from a few appetizers, there were very limited options for anyone in our party who was vegetarian, making it a difficult choice for a group with mixed dietary needs.

In summary, this is a functional spot for a quick, affordable meal of decent dumplings, especially if you're dining in and want to avoid a wait. However, the shabby interior and the near-total lack of vegetarian entrees make it difficult to recommend for group dining or for those seeking a more polished experience.

top_reviews.content: I recently visited this place, and I have to say I was really impressed. I was very hungry when I arrived, but I was pleasantly surprised by the wide variety of dishes on the menu. The service was excellent—everything was prepared quickly, and I didn't have to wait long. I also highly recommend trying their lemonade. It's unique, refreshing, and definitely worth ordering. I would gladly come back again!
Solid food and warm atmosphere. We ordered the Kafta, Shawarma Combo Plate, and finished with a tasty dessert Knafeh. Once you sit, you can take photo of the QR code to order. Nice and efficient.

Ive been wanting to try this spot out for years. Stopped in for a late lunch and it was outstanding. The place has a great vibe with Middle Eastern music playing in the background. The crowd was a mix of business men, families, as well as moms catching up with babies - so perfect spot for all.

I ordered the mixed schwarma combo plate and it was 10/10. Meat was finely cut and flavorful. The yellow rice and hummus wede outstanding. Overall, a very well balanced and delicious meal.

I bookmarked this spot a year ago, so after a nearby walk, we finally jumped at the chance to have lunch at Mezze and Mooore!

From the moment we walked in, we were greeted by the owner, Nabil, whose million-dollar smile sets the tone for this charming corner café. We were pleasantly surprised by the prices — especially in a time when lunch fare has climbed everywhere else.

The interior is bright and welcoming, with beautiful tiled floors and plenty of windows that fill the space with natural light.

When we heard the mint lemonade was made in-house, we had to try it — and it did not disappoint. I ordered the falafel platter, which was generous enough for two meals. The falafel were crisp on the outside, perfectly green and flavorful inside. As a self-proclaimed hummus snob, I can say theirs was outstanding — smooth, rich, and creamy.

My friend ordered the lamb shawarma wrap and raved about how delicious it was. We finished with a piece of baklava, which was just the right amount of sweet and flaky.

We’ll definitely be back — this spot is a true gem!
Overall was great! Food tasts soo good and the place is clean and nice! The staff were soo nice and friendly too.

They also have a nice little beer selection as well as sodas and agua frescas.
Menu is pretty clear as what is vegetarian or and what is not and the staff is very helpful and will accommodate any dietary issue.

top_reviews.content: The Gold Mirror was one of my dad's favorite restaurants. He loved going with his buddies once a month in the 80s and 90s. Flash forward, to 2026, and we wanted to take my mom out for her birthday, who still lives near West Portal, and instead of heading to one of our regular spots in that neighborhood, I remembered that the Gold Mirror had gone through a major renovation, so we made a reservation. We had such a lovely meal from start to finish. The staff were all so friendly and competent. We liked seeing a wide range of ages, from folks in their 80s like my mom, down to young families with babies. I think every felt welcome. We ordered everything to share, starting with their calamari fritti, a caesar salad, a pasta carbonara, short rib ravioli, prawns dore, and a rib eye steak.  Our favorites were the calamari, ravioli, and rib eye. Followed up with tiramisu and panna cotta. The only miss in our mind was that the carbonara was a bit over-salty in our opinion. But we had such a great meal and the 5 of us were stuffed and very happy.  The dining room (and upstairs room!) kept the old school charm, with some really clean and modern updates. My teenage daughters couldn't stop taking pics. Our dad passed away before he got to see the renovated space, but we all agreed that he would have loved being there again! We'll be back!

Great experience all around!  Made reservations on a Friday night at 630pm.  The place was packed, so I definitely recommend reservations.  Never visited prior to the remodel, so I unfortunately can't compare it to what it used to look like. The place felt energetic, and casual.  The hostess and workers were very professional.  The place looked great!  High ceilings, nice-looking bar, tables and seats were nice, and the gold mirror on the wall was attractive.  The chandeliers were nice, and the place looks great.

Our server Joseph was attentive, genuinely nice, and very helpful.  We ordered a couple of cocktails, and had the calamari appetizer that tasted amazing 😋.  It was laid over either butter or some type of oil, and it was tender.  Joseph said their fish is brought fresh daily, and it definitely tasted as if the calamari was fresh as well.  We did order the petrale sole 🐟, and that tasted really good.  It was cooked nicely, and seasoned well.  We also had the pappardelle in a red sauce that had lamb.  That was yummy.

We definitely will have to come back to try their other dishes.  Thank you.
Fantastic food and beautifully remodeled restaurant with amazing ambience. Great place for special occasion or weekend dinner. Menu included many good options. Definitely a must go.

We made a reservation for dinner  here after its renovation.  I’m not sure how I’m the only one of the group who had never been. It’s a classic Italian restaurant in the neighborhood. We sat upstairs. We started with the calamari which was lightly dusted so you can really taste the squid. The shrimp appetizer sat on a nice bed of arugula which we also devoured. For our main, we each ordered various pasta dishes including the cannelloni and rigatoni. We capped off the night with dessert wines. What a lovely place!

Excellent food.  We had an amazing beet salad, and meatballs as appetizers.  My chicken sauté was excellent along with my wife's lasagna was the best she has ever had.  Deserts were home made and extremely good.  Pretty amazing place.  Plus, the waitress Joselyn was perfect in how she was attentive to our needs and able to connect with us during our conversations.  Give her a raise!

Another time for Mother’s Day, 2023-05-14, stairway walk in St Francis Wood and then to eat at the Gold Mirror.  Another amazing experience.  Thanks to our waiter, John.  Good job for a special day.

Plus, their smoothies are really good too. The boba and drink itself is fresh and high quality to the taste.

Although the restaurant itself isn't the prettiest, the delicious food makes up for it.

Cam Huong has been offering good Vietnamese food to the local community for decades. Their French sandwiches and spring rolls are yummy to say the least. I especially loved their taro drinks. However, it has been out of stock for several weeks recently. Please note: the price has gone up significantly during and after the pandemic. Remember: You wanna go there for their delicious food. But don't expect a friendly face or smile.

When a place serves really good food, it sucks to make a better review. I ordered 44 minutes ahead of time to prep me for the rush on my call. This spot may lack ambiance—think less “charming bistro” and more “four walls and a countertop”—but it delivers a piping hot performance esp with its stellar banh mi.This place is also my go-to spot for party-sized goodies!Awesome egg rolls and noodles. it’s the culinary equivalent of a trusty old friend—this place is a solid choice, every time

One of the best places to get a bahn mi and other Vietnamese dishes in Oakland.  The original combo bahn mi with its pretty decent price and taste is the star of this place. Props also to the artist who did all those big stop blocks outside the shop to look like popular Asian food items....i.e. Sriracha, shrimp chips,fish sauce, and etc lol.

top_reviews.content:
Grandehos Kamekyo is a good neighborhood Japanese restaurant with a spacious dining room and friendly service. We recently ordered takeout for the first time, and the order was ready in about 15–20 minutes.

We had the Rainbow Roll and a salmon teriyaki bento box with tempura. The fish in the Rainbow Roll was fresh, and the salmon teriyaki was especially good. The tempura was enjoyable, although I found the miso soup a little saltier than I liked. Overall, the food was fresh, portions were satisfying, and it was a very positive first experience. We'd happily return.

We stumbled on this little restaurant without significant expectations and left absolutely amazed.
We were visiting from the east coast and wanted a late night quick dinner. I had hoped to get some sushi, and found a place that had Bento boxes and great looking rolls. We ordered Kamekyo's Special Roll, a bento box, a fried soft shell crab and skins Saki.

Foremost, it’s one of a few times the soft shell crab was cooked perfectly. So many costal restaurants cook these and they are soggy, moist. Just ‘ok’. This was cooked perfectly crispy, and flavorful. You could hold it up, and it was golden crisp all the way around without any sogginess.

The roll, out of this world. The bento box, my wife loved it.

We ended up talking to the owner, of ~30 years. Who told us about her husband, who knew Jackie Chan! Also just about her history with the restaurant and coming to SF from South Korea. She is hands on, constantly, and you can tell she snags everything for every customer to be memorable.

This isn’t a Michelin sushi restaurant, or a James Beard meal. But it’s a family restaurant with customer service and cooking that you can’t match with awards or $100 per plate menus.

The quality, the atmosphere, and the level of exceptional food was amazing. Don’t miss out. Talk to the owner, try anything and everything. You won’t regret it.

Great Korean/Japanese restaurant just a few steps south of the Buena Vista, so glad we found it on this trip!
Excellent Original Ramen with rich broth umami.  The Lion King roll is one of the stars of the menu.
And just as enjoyable as the great food was being able to spend a few minutes talking with the restaurant’s owner, a very nice lady originally from South Korea.
Looking forward to visiting again to try the Korean part of the menu and bento box options!
The sashimi bi bim bap was amazing. The owner was super friendly and showed me how she makes the gochujang sauce from scratch. Delicious.

I randomly picked this Japanese/Korean restaurant for dinner, and my first impression wasn’t great. The menu didn’t really stand out, and I was honestly a bit surprised by how pricey some of the nigiri options were.

I ended up ordering the three-choice bento box and a hamachi nigiri (recommended by the host). Surprisingly, the hamachi toro was excellent—very fresh, soft, and full of flavor. I could taste the umami even without dipping it in soy sauce or wasabi.

When the bento box arrived, I was shocked by the portion size—it was much larger than I expected. The highlights for me were the salad and the grilled saba. The saba was cooked perfectly and, importantly, had no annoying fish bones. The salad included a mix of fruits, which added a nice sweetness and balanced out the overall meal.

The California rolls were also well made—since I’m in California, it felt appropriate to order them.

The environment was cozy and comfortable, even for a solo diner.

Nice ambience, I mostly do takeout. Their red veggie Curry is also very good and good proportions. They also have a bar and variety of cocktails. Can go with friends or a date.

top_reviews.content:
The Noodle is a fantastic Thai restaurant that brings authentic Thai food to Berkeley. It's small and casual, making it a really great place to bring your friends. It's also delicious and affordable, making the food addictive. My family and I have eaten here many times for all those reasons.

The menu at the Noodle is extensive, so much so that it is hard to pick a favorite. I've been here enough to summarize the following menu highlights. The fried spring rolls, fried calamari, and larb are the best appetizers I've had in this town. The Pad Thai and Pad Se Ew here are fresh-tasting, delicious noodles you've got to try. If you can handle a little spice, then try the Pad Kee Mao as well. If you like fried chicken, the fried rice with fried chicken and the crispy mango chicken are incredible! And I would also recommend a tase of the Massaman Gai curry before you top everything off with the fried ice cream or the sticky sweet rice with mango.

Some lesser known but still enticing menu items include the Khao Soi (which is great with their gluten free fried chicken) and the Lord of Noodles. Both of these are solid main courses you may or may not have tried elsewhere, made with the Noodle's signature Thai style. As for lesser known appetizers, try the Tom Kha soup, the Thai fish cakes, the chicken satay (which are totally addictive), and the papaya salad. These are not so famous but are very interesting choices.

This summer, they are adding Ka Na Moo Korb (pork belly with Chinese broccoli and egg) and cheesecake with Mitchell ice cream. I'm a real fan of these new options!

If you haven't tried the Noodle yet, I would definitely try it. Everything on the menu is so good. I know I'll be back for more!
A very clean place to grab lunch or dinner with 3-5 friends. Plan ahead for larger groups. Food was average but high quality dinnerware they serve in. Cleanliness top notch. Large portion size.

A wonderful find, light fresh food like Thai should be.
I looked in on the other Thai restaurants in the area but mostly looked hyped. This was the real deal which you could tell from the clientele and the footfall picking up for take out.
I always go for the Laab, as it’s a good test of authenticity and freshness, this did not disappoint. The people were lovely and the service was efficient, a superb light and very tasty meal!

No complaints about the service; they were quick and very friendly.

Unfortunately, I was not the biggest fan of the food. The green curry noodles came with vermicelli, and I wanted to try it since it’s what they recommend, but it just was not the right texture for the curry I felt. The flavor of the curry itself was not super flavorful. I felt like more coconut milk could have been added to coat the noodles more. The spring rolls were good. I enjoyed the peanut sauce. We also sat at the front by the door, and it was rather cold in that seat.

Food was great and the service was quick, efficient, and very friendly. The staff made the experience even better with their welcoming attitude. The place was clean and well-maintained, creating a comfortable environment to enjoy a meal. It’s a perfect spot whether you’re looking for a quick bite on the go or want to sit down and dine in. Overall, a solid choice for a casual and satisfying meal.

Size is for ants.

Proposition chicken has some pretty solid entree options. Their chicken strips are crispy, fresh, well spiced and cooked perfectly. The fried chicken sandwich is also crispy, juicy, filling and flavorful with a perfect slaw to balance it out. And their slow roasted rotisserie was also well cooked, fresh, balanced and tasty enough to pick the bones clean.

But my real bone to pick here is the sadly, the wings. I had enjoyed their other items so much. And figured an order of buffalo wings would be a great call. They were not. Ice cold, rubbery, watery tasteless buffalo sauce.
I was aghast. The bleu cheese couldn’t save em either, inedible.

If their wings were on par with everything else they do, this spot would be an easy five stars. But they were pretty gross. I’ll be back sometime, still lots of good stuff. but can’t recommend those wings.

My wife and I come here bc she is able to have a fried Gluten Free chicken Sando which brings her so much joy! I love that they use meat that doesn't have hormones and it is juicy and crispy.
The last time we went, our server was super friendly and answered all of our questions. We ordered 2 Sando, one with gf bread. We also ordered the honey mustard wings (which were delicious), 2 root beers, and a 12oz of their ranch dressing.

Very good all you can eat restaurant with tons of beef options.   It's kind of nice that the fans suck up the smoke, so you don't leave the restaurant smelling like a barbecue.  You are limited on some options to 3 plates per person, my recommendation would be to try those first before moving on to other choices.

We came to Gyu-Kaku for dinner with a large group. Unfortunately the experience got off to a slightly awkward start because we weren’t able to move the tables together, which meant our group had to be split across two separate tables. The staff said this was for health and safety reasons, which we understood, although it did make the dinner feel a little less like a shared group experience.
We decided to order the Ultimate set menu, but after we had already chosen it, our waiter told us we were only allowed to order appetizers for the first round. This wasn’t mentioned anywhere on the menu, so it felt confusing to have the rules changed after we had already decided what we wanted.
After that, service felt a bit inconsistent. At times the staff seemed to disappear for long stretches, and there were moments where we were waiting quite a while for the next dishes to arrive, even though the table next to us was already well into their meals. Occasionally dishes also appeared that nobody at our table remembered ordering, which was a little strange.
That said, the food itself was absolutely delicious. The quality of the meat was excellent, and there were some really standout dishes. One highlight was a sizzling beef rice dish served in a hot stone bowl (I’ve forgotten the exact name), which was fantastic. The karaage chicken was also great, and the sushi was excellent as well.
The staff were overall polite and friendly, even if the service flow wasn’t always perfectly coordinated.
Overall we still had a good experience thanks to the food quality, but the ordering process and timing of the dishes could definitely be improved to make the experience smoother.

We had such a wonderful experience and the service was excellent.

We tried the Valentine’s Day special menu. There was a great variety of meats and everything was fresh, tender, and full of flavor. Grilling at the table made the experience even more fun and special. The salad was very good and the special strawberry desert.

Thank you !

Travelled from Dallas with my sister. Our flight was delayed and they were accommodating that we arrived a few minutes late and with our luggage! So helpful and FRIENDLY! The whole staff!
We did the chef adventure menu and added on one single pancake. Our drinks were water, iced coffee and iced tea. At the very beginning we explained allergies and dislikes and they were very accommodating!
To start: Sweet potato hush puppy with a zucchini dip and
Avo toast, It has an egg eggplant dip at the bottom, spring onions, green garlic oil, and then like a shallot crunch on top of basil. Delish!
Next, Their annual hippie salad with  Mediterranean cucumbers and snap peas, a little sprouted lentils, and with Toto soy on the bottom, some pickled ramps on top Meyer lemon and then a lightly smoked wild salmon with Soy milk so a little bit of shrimp oil some pickled ginger.
They surprised us with candles on our pancake for our birthday! Such a special treat! I did not get the last two dishes but the staff said they would email me.

First off, my flight kept getting delayed but they continued to accommodate the reservation for us, which was very helpful. Everything was delicious and there was one course that we didn’t finish because it was our least favorite - the salmon crudo pictured below - because neither of us are big raw salmon people and weren’t a fan of the texture. The flavor was still amazing and the presentation was beautiful! They replaced it for us without us asking for that because “we shouldn’t have a course we didn’t enjoy”. Our waiter was awesome and super attentive, but it felt like every single person working made an effort to connect with us individually, which made us feel so welcome and comfortable. Every drink was really good, but our favorites were the peach milk tea punch and the drink your juice. Overall a perfect meal with my sister and we’ll be bringing my mom next time!

Hilda and Jesse | San Francisco, CA
September 2025

Brunch in the heart of North Beach can often feel like a tourist trap, but Hilda and Jesse is the real deal. It manages to hold onto its Michelin star while maintaining a fun, unpretentious neighborhood vibe that makes it one of the most enjoyable meals in the city.

The Atmosphere
From the moment you walk in at opening, the energy is infectious. The decor is whimsical and fun, featuring a vibrant color palette that matches the creativity of the kitchen. I particularly loved the unique selection of cups, plates, and saucers—it’s that kind of attention to detail that makes the meal feel personal rather than institutional.

The Experience
We arrived for a promptly seated opening reservation, and parking (surprisingly!) was a breeze. We decided to share everything, which is the only way to truly appreciate the range of the menu. Our waitress was incredibly kind and guided us toward their chicken dish—it was earthy, delicious, and grounded by a wonderful polenta.

The Food
Decadent Buttermilk Pancakes: These are legendary for a reason. They provide a sophisticated level of sweetness and a fluffy texture that is hard to beat.

French Toast: Equally yummy, with a beautiful caramelization that felt like a true morning indulgence.

Chicken & Polenta: This was the savory anchor of our meal. The chicken was perfectly cooked, and its earthy depth paired beautifully with the sweet notes of the pancakes and toast.

The Verdict
Hilda and Jesse proves that "High-End" doesn't have to mean "Stuffy." Kudos to the staff for maintaining their Michelin status while keeping the atmosphere welcoming and fun. It is a well-deserved star for a place that clearly values both culinary precision and the joy of a good neighborhood meal.

The Food
While exploring new and unique food in our area, my wife and I discovered Hilda and Jesse. They are a brunch and dinner space with what they called modern "funluxury" with a twist. We ordered a few of their dishes for our brunch
- Chop Salad
- Sunchokes
- Shrimp Toastie
- Pork Chop
- Glazed Beef Tongue
The dishes were all very good and tasty. The Sunchokes were quite unique to us as well. I have not tried them before. The Pork Chop and Glazed Beef Tongue were well cooked and tender, with a nice sauce to go with it.

The Miscellaneous
Hilda and Jesse is a corner store along Union, with limited street parking. The interior was quite unique, with the look of a diner, but more modernized. They have limited space and seating, but they made good use and maximized seating. The service was good and the staff were sincere and helpful. The menu was fairly straightforward, with unique selections and not overwhelming. They also have a Chef's Adventure Menu, which is a nice touch for those who cannot decide. All in all, it was a good dining experience and I would recommend paying them a visit if you want to splurge a bit.

I genuinely do not understand why this has a low four-star rating. This restaurant is exceptional! We did the brunch tasting menu and loved every bite. The staff is very friendly and seems genuinely excited and proud of the food they are putting out, as they should! This is some of the most flavorful food I have had in San Francisco. Not only that, but they presented a range of styles that we were impressed by throughout the short menu. We also added on their gayest pancakes ever--those are incredible! No matter what you get here, order those, too!! Unlike anything I've ever had before! Also, I only have three pictures because my phone died. There were more courses than that.

top_reviews.content:
We visited Fumi Japanese Curry Ramen for lunch today. The atmosphere and service were excellent and definitely the highlights of our visit. The restaurant has a great vibe, and when you walk in, you expect an amazing meal.

We ordered three different ramen bowls, including the Mushroom Lovers with chicken and one of their most popular ramen options. Unfortunately, the ramen didn’t meet our expectations. The egg was delicious, but the noodles were just average, and the broth felt a bit light and lacked the rich, deep flavor I was hoping for.

I probably wouldn’t come back specifically for the ramen, but I would be interested in trying some of their other dishes because the restaurant itself made a great impression. Overall, I’d give it 4 out of 5 stars
, the excellent atmosphere and friendly service really made up for the disappointing ramen.
Really enjoyed our meal here. Was my first time trying Japanese curry, yum. And the katsu was perfect, moist with crispy skin. I had the miso ramen but made it spicy. I will be back!

The curry had a tangy finish. Might be from the tomatoes not being simmered enough or too much Worcestershire. I tasted what it wanted to be but it just wasn’t enough. The tempura was really good though and especially the tempura sauce.

Honestly, the Chicken Katsu Curry Rice here is superb. 🍛 I went with the mild spice, and it still had a nice little kick to it that kept things interesting.

10/10 for the food, and the service is really solid to match.
Definitely a new favorite spot!
This is my 2nd time eating at this place and the food always hits close to what I used to eat at my home country. Their curry menu is the best in the house. 10/10

top_reviews.content:
A friend of ours told us to try this place, and since we were passing by, why not.
We had to wait outside for about 10 minutes since the place was already packed. Service was quick and the food came out piping hot. The menu was quite extensive. We settled for 10 dishes.
Our absolute favorites were the Snowy Baked BBQ Pork Buns, Beef Tripe, and the fresh Roll Noodle with Shrimp. Honestly, everything was delicious, but our least favorite was the Salted Fish Clay Pot Rice. The salted fish was a bit bland and the portion was rather small. It was also overpriced.
We tried the Crispy Durian Puff. If you like Durian, you'll appreciate this dish. If you don't like durian, don't sit next to the person who's eating it because you can really smell it! 🫢

We ordered a lot! Everything here is really great and I would come here all the time if I could. Ming’s Tasty dim sum is one of the best in the Bay Area. You can taste the freshness of the dishes and it really shows. Their service and turnaround is relatively quick and efficient. We ordered the black bean pork spare ribs, chicken feet, siu mai, shrimp dumplings, meat-stuffed snow bun, shrimp rice rolls, fried turnip cake, and fried stuffed meat dumplings. All of their food is pretty good, but some of the must-try dishes here are the shrimp rice rolls and the fried stuffed meat dumplings. Best to come with a larger party, so you can try it all!

Good & cheap eats for Dim Sum in the heart of downtown Oakland.
Dim Sum here always cook fresh & hot when you ordered.
The claypot rice is good but too expensive.  Only has 4 pieces of chicken & 1 piece of black mushroom, lol, for almost $16.
Downside: The menu is smaller compared to other restaurants.  The wait is very long here since it’s a small restaurant.  The restaurant is always packed, especially at lunch time, weekends, & holidays.
It’s small, packed, & very noisy. So, not recommended for relaxing or big family gatherings. The waitresses here are crazily noisy. They always screaming & yelling around, adding the extra noises to the noisy restaurant, & making the environment very intense.
Recommend: 1st time here, ✍️ your name on the wait list, while waiting for your table, get the menu & filled what you want to order right away, once you get your table, just hand the filled menu to the waitress so you can get your food ready soon.

I went last week as a recommendation after having my blood drawn just a few blocks away. I had the shrimp dumplings, wonton noodle soup and the pork bun. I thoroughly enjoyed myself. I went early (around 11am) and it was packed. I was accommodated a seat at a shared table. The service is friendly and efficient. The food was all hot tasty and affordable.  I spent less than 30 for everything.  I didn't have any trouble with parking - parked at a meter.

Favorites were the custard bun, pea sprout dumpling (not pictured), rice noodle roll with fried shrimp, and snowy baked bbq pork bun! Pork & shrimp dumpling siu mai were nice and big, a bit on the salty side!
Friendly service!

top_reviews.content:
Southshore Cafe, Alameda

This is a small, feel-good diner! There are a bunch of regular’s here and you can tell everyone seems to know everyone here.

What we ordered:
Pork Chops from the Breakfast section and Joe’s Special: Sauteed Ground Beef with Onions and Spinach. Both were delicious with big portions. The coffee’s are continually refilled!

This place feels very warm and welcoming. The staffs are always checking up to make sure things are doing great! Food was hot and delicious!

We had a great experience dining here and would come back again!

Got severe food poisoning from here. We waited a long time to get our bill processed.
As we were leaving I had to run to the bathroom (the effects from the meal were starting) . That’s when I realized the bathroom pretty much connected to the kitchen 🤢.

I had eaten half of my portion and my mom took a bite out of my food. She also ended up having a reaction not long after we ate, just not as severe as mine.

I don’t recommend this place the food was so-so and not sure if it was the hollandaise sauce or the cornbeef that was bad. Pretty sure it was the cornbeef.

Nice charming local place for brunch 😁 if you want  a simple American style brunch around Alameda, this is satisfactory! They do tend to have a line so get here early 😅

Photos are what my friends and I got!

Great little cafe that will take you back in time 50 years ago. Booth seating. Reasonably priced tasty classic American breakfast and sandwiches (comes with fries). Yummy comfort food that people of all ages keep coming back for more. Food comes out piping hot. The cooks are Thai so there is also Thai and Asian menu too.

Not too many restaurants left in Alameda that have the look and a good part of their menu that is still set in the 1960s. Go and patronize this mom and pop business. Opens 7 days a week for breakfast and lunch only. We need to keep Southshore Cafe in business.

There is wheelchair accessible specific table ♿️ close to the entrance.

The staff is so friendly and patient. The fries were perfect, crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside. They're also such a fun shape! The food lacked seasoning/flavor and yet was still pretty good. It was a little like something you would just make at home. The menu's also very diverse and confusing.

top_reviews.content:
If you are looking for authentic, deeply flavorful Indian food in San Francisco, Aaha Indian Cuisine is an absolute must-visit.
The highlight of the night was hands-down the Mutton Biryani. It is easily some of the best I’ve ever had—the rice was perfectly fragrant and separate, the spices were layered beautifully without being overwhelmingly heavy, and the mutton was incredibly tender and cooked to perfection. You can tell they don't cut corners on the slow-cooking process.
Beyond the biryani, the service was warm and attentive, and the overall ambiance made for a fantastic dining experience. Whether you’re a local or just passing through SF, do yourself a favor and check this place out. I will definitely be back for more!

Absolutely delicious! And that’s coming from someone who is very picky about south asian flavors. Anil at the restaurant was the kindest gentleman and made our experience a 10/10.
The pomfret fry, and the daal tardka are must trys!

Love this place in the mission. Got the chicken pepper fry and chicken chettinadu and chapati and chili garden naan. All was great, loved how many spiced and chopped onion are in both dish. Chili garlic naan is life changing, best naan I've ever had
By far the best chicken biryani I have had in SF. Strong flavors, perfectly cooked, all I could ask for in this dish. I am super happy to have found this restaurant!

Today I ordered Green Chicken Fry and Egg Biryani, and honestly both dishes were very disappointing. I couldn’t even finish a small portion of the food.

The Green Chicken Fry had no salt and almost no flavor at all. It looked like a proper fry item with all the ingredients and appearance, but the taste was completely missing.

As for the Egg Biryani, the gravy/sauce used in it was not tasty and gave the entire dish an unpleasant flavor.

I’ve eaten at many restaurants before, and this is the first time I’ve had such a bad experience. Spending $38 on food like this was definitely not worth it. This is one of the worst places I’ve tried.

top_reviews.content: An absolute gem in the neighborhood. The staff here define what true hospitality means—they are consistently kind, deeply respectful, and incredibly generous. It is rare to find a place that treats every visitor with such warmth and abundance. Exceptional food paired with a genuinely wonderful team. Highly recommended

I had a great experience at Bistro Mediterraneo in San Francisco! I ordered the gyro, and it was absolutely delicious—fresh, flavorful, and cooked perfectly. The portions were generous, and everything tasted authentic.
A special shoutout to Tawheed, who provided outstanding service. He was friendly, welcoming, and made sure we had everything we needed. His positive attitude really made the experience even better.

If you're looking for great Mediterranean food and excellent customer service, I definitely recommend Bistro Mediterraneo. I'll definitely be back!

Delightful Turkish Mediterranean market and deli with a few tables for dining. The falfel wrap was particularly good! Interesting selection of packaged food. The staff was quite helpfu and pleasant in discussing the menu and offering suggestions. One suggestion to management is to use a vegan mayo in the Grilled Mutabbal dish, which is otherwise vegan. There's some great vegan mayonnaises on the market and this dish looked quite interesting. An overall fun experience for a first time visit!

This place is very high quality. The gyro is thicker and juicer than other places and it balances it very well in the wrap. Even the pita that they used is fluffy, well textured and without a doubt, yummy.
This place is FOR SURE valid. The lentil soup was very warming as well, not being too salty or under seasoned. Everything on the menu looked fabulous and I will be sure to come back to try other things

The cashier I think his name was Taheed, was extremely genuine and kind, he knew a lot about the menu and even at a young age he handled everything with care.

Great place and great experience!

This is my new favorite place to grab a beef Shawarma wrap. They get the spicy just right. The food atmosphere is amazing. I love it.

And don’t forget the baklava with coconut ice cream. It’s next level.

This family is amazing. They are what make San Francisco so great.

top_reviews.content: Very small sushi spot, with a few tiny tables inside, one outside on the sidewalk, and a few seats at the counter. Mostly sashimi and nigiri (a few salads too). Mochi and cheesecakes for desserts. Everything was great, ingredients (some terrific fat fishes) and cooking. And the sake menu is one of the best I've seen in the area, including a sake flight. Not the best option for a cheap feast, but with that in mind, absolutely recommended.

Extremely authentic sushi place that doesn’t skimp. Sushi were already seasoned perfectly when they hit the table. Nigiri combo allows you do choose 7 different nigiri from their list which is amazing value, which also comes with a set of maki rolls which were great. $28. Last lunch seating is 2:00 which is strictly enforced.
Excellent value for the quality. The sashimi is very fresh and the sushi rice was perfectly seasoned. The space could be nicer, but the food makes it worth visiting. 10/10.

My partner and I had just finished playing Dave the Diver one night and got a massive sushi craving, so we looked up nearby spots and found this place. We enjoyed it so much that we came back the very next day，this time for takeout. The packaging was really nice, the prices are a great deal, and the flavors are legit. Pretty sure this is going to be our go-to sushi takeout spot from now on.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
The fish here is beyond delicious.  It’s the kind of meal you have and then wake up craving again.  Spectacularly simple but impressively memorable.

name: Côte Ouest Bistro
address: 2953 Baker St, San Francisco, CA 94123, United States

top_reviews.content:
Start to finish, dinner here was amazing.  We had reservations and were seated immediately.  They ooen at 5:30, and at 5:32, there were already 6 other tables seated.  The servers were quick with waters, taking orders, and bread.

The table bread was warm, soft, and a little toasty.  It came with some salted butter.

We started with the Mousse de Foie de Vollaile and the Heirloom Tomato Salad.  Both dishes arrived together before we finished the table bread.  The mousse has one larger slce of pain au levain, but there is way more mousse than we could put on that piece of bread.  The pain au levain is sweeter than the table bread.  The port jelly was light on flavor, amd there was a dusting of a spicy powder on the dish that went well with the mousse.  My gf's only wish was for some fruit jelly or honey to pair with the mousse.

The salad was lightly dressed with balsamic and perfect for two people.  The burrata was soft and creamy, the peaches and tomatoes were ripe and full of flavor.  It all paired well with the arugula.

I got the 12 oz ribeye medium rare, amd she got the Moules Marinieres Frites.  We both got french fries...

The onlything that could have been better was that the ribeye was cooked medium well and a little dry.  I expected a lot more from a French restaurant.  The French medium rare should be a little less cooked than the American medium rare.  It was good, but not great.

The mussels were all open and cooked well.  The sauce was full of flavor and we were dipping bread in it to finish it off.  We ultimately decided to finish the mussels, take the steak home, and order dessert.

We got the Moelleaux au Chocolat.  We were told that it takes about 8 to 10 minutes to prepare.  The cake was light and cooked through.  The crème Anglaise inside was warm and chocolatey.  With the caramel sauce and whipped cream, each bite was perfect.  We would definitely get this again.

Would give this 4.5/5 if I could. Excellent service, food was mostly a hit, but it was a bit cramped inside. Decent value for the price point.

Cauliflower al Pastor - was excellent, with a great contrast between the creamy, sharp goat cheese and citrusy orange bits. Portion on the smaller side.

Sauteed Calamari - moderately tasty, but perhaps a bit too busy, with the leafy greens not quite belonging. The taste of the squid itself was muted. Good portion size.

Duck Leg Confit - delicious, tender duck meat with a hearty, savory sauce that worked very well with the mushrooms and potatoes au gratin. Its more filling than it looks.

Coq Au Vin - this was a mixed bag. The chicken was done right, but the sweet/tart wine sauce will be polarizing. I liked it, but my partner did not. The sweet parsnip puree didn't really work and might better have been standard salty mashed potatoes to better contrast with the sauce. Good portion size.

I just got home from a fantastic lunch here at cote. The chicken sandwich filled me right up. The ambiance of this cute little restaurant is really something. The waitstaff was friendly and very polite. I give them 5 stars ⭐️. I wish I could give them 100.

I’ve lived here since 2005 and have been coming here since then.  It might be the best undiscovered gem in SF and is definitely one of the best restaurants.  In Paris I used to go to the small restaurant Le True Normand and this is better!

It’s a small restaurant, though the street patio adds some welcome breathing room. Soft background music creates a pleasant atmosphere, and the elegant tableware sets a nice tone. Warm complimentary bread with butter is a thoughtful touch. Service is fine overall, though nothing exceptional.

Escargots de Bourgogne
The escargots are very good baked in parsley and garlic butter, fragrant and flavorful. The puff pastry doesn’t add much in terms of taste, at least for me, but it does provide a pleasant textural contrast. It's a good dish even with pastry.

Xipirons a la Plancha
Perfectly cooked, tender calamari paired with sautéed serrano ham, greens, and a spicy yet manageable. The portion is generous, and the flavors come together beautifully.

Rillettes de Lapin
The rabbit rillettes are very tender, with some pleasantly chewy pieces of meat that work well alongside Dijon mustard and cornichons. The combination of mild sweetness, bitterness, and acidity is balanced and satisfying.

Île Flottante
A truly outstanding dessert — easily one of the best I’ve had in the last four years. The airy, soft meringue has a gentle sweetness that blends perfectly with the richer, creamier sweetness of the crème anglaise. Thinly sliced almonds add just the right amount of crunch. If you have a sweet tooth and live in or visit San Francisco, this is a must‑try.

Tarte Fine aux Pommes
A very good apple tart served with apple sauce and vanilla ice cream, though it inevitably feels understated next to the exceptional Île Flottante.

And there is a great dessert wine - Le Pere Jules 5 Year Pommeau de Normandie, - it’s another way to finish a dinner.

The restaurant may be small, but the food is impressive, and several dishes truly stand out. Highly recommended.
