top_reviews.content:
Growing up in Santa Fe, New Mexico, I was totally spoiled by the food — especially the green chile and red chile that you just can’t replicate anywhere else. Even though I’m a California native by birth, I spent my most formative years in New Mexico, and that shaped my palate in a permanent way.

Over the last 20 years living in the Bay Area, I’ve been on a quiet mission: every time a friend from high school or middle school in New Mexico came to visit, I’d try to find a restaurant here that could even remotely live up to what we were raised on. I’d take them to places I thought might pass muster — and every time, they were politely disappointed. So was I.

But today changed everything.

I think I may have just found the best Mexican restaurant I’ve ever experienced in California — hands down. And no, I’m not exaggerating.

🌮 Taqueria La Comales Mexican Grill in Oakland
•	🌶️ They will make it spicy if you want it — not just California-spicy, but real-deal chile heat.
•	🥑 Fresh, high-quality ingredients that taste home-cooked, not mass-produced.
•	💸 Extremely affordable — the kind of value that’s almost impossible to find in the Bay now.
•	🫓 Authentic flavor — I mean it. The chile here sings. It reminded me of home.

If you grew up on Hatch green chile and are constantly chasing that familiar, soulful flavor, this is your spot. I can’t even tell you how good it felt to finally taste something that honored where I come from.

Been going here for over 10 years now, never had a bad experience, food is always so good and tasty, and there priced haven't even raised, you get a good amount of food for a good price. The staff here is always nice and pack ur food. Pictured is a burrito bowl and the super quesadillas. Highly recommend the burritos/wet burritos here as well! 10/10

Great food I order Super Nachos and my girl order a Tongue Super Quesadilla. I recommend the nachos but my girl said the Quesadilla was bad. The place is small parking on the street is limited but parking is available.
Fast, quick and very friendly. Great menu and selection and very authentic food. Consistent, very accurate and great selection.

The most awesome Super Wet Burrito you will ever try!!! Best in the Town, hands down!!!

After eating this you might think, this is the only way to enjoy a burrito going forward!!!

top_reviews.content: We had a wonderful dinner at Uva Enoteca. Amazing refined, sophisticated, full of flavors, southern Italian cuisine. We all loved our dishes, desserts were S tier as well. Very kind service, great atmosphere, very welcoming, not too noisy. A wonderful restaurant for the discerning foodies. Wish we could come back.

Five stars for a dinner that felt like a quick trip to Puglia right in the Haight.

Uva Enoteca delivered hit after hit — the Burrata e Prosciutto vanished instantly, the Funghi e Tartufo was rich and earthy perfection, and the Orecchiette della Mamma tasted like your Italian grandmother was quietly running the kitchen.

Dessert sealed the deal: pistachio and cherry marmalade Puccia Dolce plus the Budino al Cioccolato. Conversation basically stopped after the first bites.

Service from Kat was warm, relaxed, and perfectly timed. Cozy atmosphere and fantastic pasta.

Recently went here with family and thoroughly enjoyed the Piccante Puccia Pugliese (pictured).

We’ve been here several times and the food and service is excellent.

We are also visiting Puglia in the coming months and Antonio, the owner, was kind enough to recommend several places and activities while we are there.

Wish that I lived in SF so I could visit this place more and 10/10 recommend visiting when you are in town and craving Italian.

Authentic Italian Food, Wine & Hospitality
We stumbled upon Uva Enoteca because another local spot we planned to visit was opening late. What attracted us as we approached the restaurant was the inviting design and atmosphere, and that it was an “Enoteca.” This gave us hope that we would experience the same authentic Italian ambiance we felt during our travels in Italy. We were delighted to find we were right.

We've traveled to Italy several times and love authentic Italian food and wine. If that's what you're after, this is the place. Everyone who served us clearly knew the wine, the dishes, the stories behind them, and the recipes passed down from grandparents to the owner, Antonio. We enjoyed the seasonal special pizza to start, shared Orecchiette Cime Di Rapa, which we didn’t expect to like as much as we did, and tried different pairings of sparkling, rosé, and red wines.

We sat at the bar and had great conversations with different staff members. The place is warm and inviting, just like Italy. I watched the staff and owner spend time with each customer, and we never felt rushed throughout the evening. It was so memorable that we haven’t stopped talking about it. We’re already planning our next trip back to San Fran just so we can return. It’s that good, trust someone who grew up in an Italian neighborhood and an Italian family.

Uva Enoteca is a hidden gem on haight street! The food tastes incredibly authentic, and the team takes care to use high quality ingredients, many which are imported directly from Italy. Highly recommend trying their pizza & pairing it with their amazing wine selection, and make sure to save room for dessert + espresso at the end😋
Amazing spot for group events as well, with a large tasting menu! The staff was extremely helpful & created a special experience for our group dinner

name: LIMEWOOD BAR & RESTAURANT

google.address: 41 Tunnel Rd, Berkeley, CA 94705, United States

top_reviews.content:
We arrived at 7:45 AM. Parking is accessible immediately adjacent to the entrance, eliminating long pedestrian transit from the vehicle. Note on the parking procedure: upon parking, you must scan the barcode on the sign in the parking lot and fill out your information; later, when you receive your dining receipt at the end of the meal, scanning the barcode provided on that receipt zeros out the parking fee before you exit the property. However, as we walked from the parking lot toward the hotel entrance, the outdoor fire pit and lounge areas were left in a messy state from the previous night or shift, featuring unbusied glassware, empty bottles, stray beverage containers, and rumpled throws left completely unmanaged well before opening. Inside, the Claremont maintains a classic, historic aesthetic. The restaurant entrance is located just inside the hotel on the left, and service doors opened promptly at 8:00 AM.

We were seated at a window table with a clear, elevated view of San Francisco in the distance. Water was provided immediately, and order intake followed shortly after. The latte was functional but lacked depth; an additional shot would have improved flavor balance, though it remained enjoyable.

I ordered the Signature Breakfast with scrambled eggs, country potatoes, and chicken apple sausage, alongside a side of grilled sourdough. Execution across the plates was solid: the scrambled eggs were properly cooked, the potatoes were well-prepared, and the chicken apple sausage was flavorful with a balanced, mild sweetness. The side of grilled sourdough outperformed expectations, as the char added strong structural flavor. My dining companion's order, consisting of fried eggs, potatoes, and thick, chewy bacon, was reported as excellent across all metrics.

Service ran smoothly during the initial phase, with the waitress performing a midpoint check-in, and secondary staff efficiently clearing plates. However, post-clearance follow-through lapsed toward the end of the meal, as no staff returned to the table, requiring an approximate 12-minute wait before attention could be actively flagged to request the check.

Overall, food quality sits above average, and the combination of historic room architecture and unobstructed valley views adequately justifies the pricing structure.

I visited for the first time to attend my friend’s birthday dinner, and this stunning restaurant truly impressed me! Located inside the beautiful Clairmont hotel, it offers a spectacular sunset view over the bay. The staff is friendly and attentive, and the food quality is good. The atmosphere is elegant and upscale, but there is no dress code, so guests can dress casually or more formally. We came on a Saturday evening and there were still a few parking spaces available. I recently had dinner at Fish & Farm in San Francisco and overall it was a very enjoyable experience that deserves a solid 4 stars. To start, I ordered the crab cakes, and I was pleasantly surprised by the presentation. Instead of being served alone, the crab cakes came on top of a fresh salad, which made the appetizer feel more complete and satisfying. The crab cakes themselves were flavorful and well-prepared, definitely a highlight of the meal.

For my main course, I went with the classic fish and chips. The dish was exactly what you would expect—crispy, golden batter with tender fish inside. While not the best I’ve ever had, it was certainly good and hit the spot. What stood out was the attention to detail: the server brought out malt vinegar without me having to ask, and there was plenty of tartar sauce provided, which is something many restaurants often skimp on. To finish off the meal, I tried the blueberry cheesecake, which was excellent. Rich, creamy, and bursting with blueberry flavor, it was one of the best desserts I’ve had in a while.

Service was good overall, though a little on the slow side since there was only one staff member handling the host stand, bar, and tables. Considering that, he did an impressive job keeping everything running smoothly.

top_reviews.content:
Top Hatters is the kind of neighborhood restaurant that immediately feels welcoming. This cozy fusion bar and grill has an inviting indoor dining room, a lively bar, and a well-positioned outdoor patio that makes it easy to imagine locals walking over from their homes for dinner or happy hour. It works equally well for a date night, family dinner, or even a relaxed business lunch.

One detail that really stood out to me was the restaurant's story. Top Hatters spent 65 years as a family-owned hat manufacturer in Oakland and San Leandro before being transformed into the Vietnamese fusion restaurant it is today. Keeping the original name as a tribute to the family's millinery legacy adds genuine character. I always appreciate when owners preserve a piece of local history, and that sense of pride carries over into the warm, attentive hospitality.

The Purple Peak, an ube margarita, was a fun surprise. Sweet, creamy, and balanced with just enough citrus, it was a creative twist on a classic cocktail. The grilled oysters with harissa butter were excellent and easily one of my favorite dishes. The Savory Bacon Donuts reminded me more of perfectly made hush puppies, with a lightly crisp exterior, soft interior, and prominent scallion and Parmesan flavors. The bacon was subtle rather than overpowering, which actually worked well. To finish, the Grilled Meat Lettuce Wrap Platter was outstanding, featuring flavorful marinated meats, fresh herbs, pickles, sauces, and vermicelli for a build-your-own experience that is perfect for sharing.

Top Hatters delivers an international dining experience with a genuine neighborhood feel. The thoughtful menu, creative cocktails, welcoming service, and appreciation for local history make it a restaurant worth returning to. Whether you're dining with family, friends, or enjoying a solo meal at the bar, the staff goes out of their way to make you feel at home. 4.75 out of 5 stars.

Finally walked in after years of passing by.
Rating: 5 Stars

I’ve lived about four blocks from this spot for over two decades. I’ve walked past it dozens of times, always smelling the kitchen from the sidewalk and telling myself I’d eventually eat there. Tonight, I finally followed through on a reservation, and honestly, the food totally lived up to those smells I’ve been experiencing for years.

We arrived right at opening and asked to sit on the patio instead of inside—it wasn't a problem at all. The patio is a nice little sanctuary right off the 580 freeway. We ordered through the QR system and everything came out in a timely manner. The waitstaff was very pleasant and I actually enjoyed hearing the kitchen staff calling out orders; you can tell they really know what they’re doing.

The standout dishes:

The Grilled Whole Rockfish: This was excellent. The presentation was beautiful with earthy colors, and the skeleton was incredibly easy to remove. The sauce and toppings really pulled all the flavors together.

Seared Rice Cake: Highly recommended. The outside was firm and crispy (though not a hard "crunch"), but when you combine it with the sausage and other ingredients, it’s amazing.

Meat Lettuce Wrap Platter: We did the short rib, pork, and chicken. The short rib had the most intense flavor, but all three were great. My only small note is the lettuce didn't really hold up against the fillings, so I ended up eating a lot of it like a salad, which wasn't a big deal because the meat was so good.

Lemon Ricotta Zeppole: A great way to finish, so delicious!

It’s rare to have that much buildup for a restaurant and not be disappointed. Great food, nice soundtrack, and a solid neighborhood vibe. If you’ve been walking past and smelling it like I have, just go in. It’s worth it.

The presentation is flawless although if you like to shake up your taste buds, that's not happening here - like the sizes, flavors are delicate too.

Indoor outdoor space with nice bar seating. Would most definitely come back.

top_reviews.content: This place is pretty good. I’d recommend it as the go to spot for Italian in Walnut Creek—although I haven’t tried all of them. The lamb chops were perfectly cooked and incredibly juicy, and the appetizers especially the roasted cauliflower and crispy bites—were delicious and unique. The bread with olive oil was fresh and fragrant, and paired so well with a glass of rosé.

Service was friendly and the vibe was cozy yet modern—perfect for a relaxing dinner. Definitely one of my new favorite spots in Walnut Creek. Highly recommend if you're looking for great food, great wine, and a great evening out!

After visiting Italy last year, Montesacro Pinseria feels like the next best thing when it comes to food. We’ve celebrated special occasions here, including Valentine’s Day, Father’s Day, and most recently, our anniversary. The food is crafted with remarkable quality, capturing the true essence of Italian cuisine without the heavy processing. This place has become our favorite, evoking memories of the delightful meals we enjoyed in Italy. The staff is incredibly friendly, and one of the owners consistently provides outstanding service. I’ll keep recommending this gem, hoping they maintain their genuine Italian spirit.

Had an amazing Valentines lunch here today. Anthony was our server (I think he’s also the manager?!) and he kept checking on us at all the right moments.

top_reviews.content:
Super super pho is my go-to Vietnamese spot in Berkeley/Emeryville. And so reasonably priced.

I always get the original banh no with the pate. Soo good with the freshnwss of the herbs and acidity and sweetness of the pickled carrots and diakon.

The beef pho with 3 kinds of beef is warm and hearty. Their broth is clear and so flavorful.

Will be back again and again.

This was my husband’s and my first time trying this restaurant. When you arrive, you place your order and pay at the counter first, then take a seat in the dining area to enjoy your meal.

The prices are quite reasonable, and the food was pretty good overall. For me, the broth wasn’t as rich or flavorful as I had hoped, though they do give you a generous amount of it. The staff provided decent service — not outstanding, but not bad either.

There are several pho restaurants along this street, and this was the first one we decided to try. Overall, it wasn’t bad at all and definitely worth a visit, but it’s not quite my top favorite just yet.

Self-service, order food at the front and pay after ordering. Get your own drinks. Server will bring your food out. I got the combo pho, it was very delicious. So far the best soup/pho I had. The portion is great. Totally worth the price. Hot tea is strong and tasted great too!

Ideally, I'd give this place 2.5/5.

Usually, the Yelp reviews for a restaurant are always on point, and they've never let me down in the past, but this time, it was a different story.

Super Super Pho has a great setup for a casual dining experience. The covered patio with string lights and heaters looked inviting, and the counter service with "find your own seat" was convenient. We arrived right after opening, so there was no wait and service was very fast. Perhaps a little too fast...

Our food came out within minutes of ordering, which was concerning. Especially considering we had fried chicken wings, a dish that typically takes longer to prepare. Unfortunately, the wings were the biggest letdown. They were bland and undercooked, not crispy and flavorful like you'd expect.

The pho (super pho combination) itself was a mixed bag. The portion was generous, with plenty of meat (rare steak, well-done brisket, and beef balls). However, the broth was a major disappointment. It lacked depth of flavor and really needed a lot of doctoring with the provided condiments like lemon and Sriracha. The meat itself was also unevenly cooked - some parts were dry, others undercooked.

The Thai tea was decent. It was milky (not watered down, thankfully), but it had some chalky aftertaste.

On the plus side, the staff was friendly when we did manage to flag them down. However, with only one other table occupied during our entire visit, the inattentiveness was surprising. We had to track someone down for water and takeout boxes.

Given today's rainy weather, I was really looking forward to some comforting pho, but unfortunately, this place did not deliver.

This was my first visit, and since it was a rainy day, I decided to try their pho. There’s something comforting about a warm bowl of soup on a cold, wet day. The soup had a rich, deep flavor that was enjoyable, but not remarkable. For comparison, my favorite pho spot is still Pho Vi Hoa in Palo Alto, which I feel has more balanced and complex flavors.

Ordering here was straightforward. You place your order at the counter, and the staff delivers your food to the table. The service was efficient and friendly, which added to the overall experience.

For starters, I ordered A2: Fresh Shrimp Spring Rolls. They were fresh, light, and paired well with the accompanying peanut dipping sauce. As for the main dish, I went with the Rare Steak Pho, adding extra noodles for $2. While the broth and rare steak were satisfying, I realized the portion of noodles was already quite generous without the extra. If you’re someone with a hearty appetite, you’ll likely find the regular portion sufficient.

Next time, I’ll skip the extra noodles and focus on the base dish. It’s a solid spot for a comforting bowl of pho, but I’d still rank it below my go-to pho spot in Palo Alto.

top_reviews.content: Great food great staff and lots of screens for World Cup games. Glad to have come here to enjoy the cheers and friendly atmosphere. Special shout out to Gifford for his hospitality and awesome attitude. The 36 hr slow cook brisket was worth every bite. Other dishes were solid as well. Lots of beers to choose from. Will be back for more food and matches.

Oakland finally has its sports bar back and it came back better.
The Oakland Athletic Club reopened just in time for the World Cup, and it did not miss. Walking into a packed house cheering the soccer match on any of 40 TVs with 20 independent sound zones felt like exactly what this neighborhood has been missing.
The space is cleaner and sharper than before with fresh energy. Seating covers every vibe: bar stools, booths, high tables, and a mezzanine VIP area ideal for larger groups. There isn't a bad view in the house.
The upgraded menu earns serious praise. The half chicken is a standout — juicy, well-seasoned, the kind of dish that's both satisfying and comforting in the best way. The bean and rice bowl is equally impressive: fresh, hearty, and far above what you'd expect from a sports bar. Real food.
What ties it all together is the staff and management. Genuinely welcoming from the moment you walk in, and attentive throughout, even on a packed game day. You never felt like just another table.
Whether you're coming solo, on a date, or rolling in with a big group, OAC handles it all with ease. This is Oakland's living room. It's back where it belongs. Will be back there again.

So glad this place is open again! I love that all the food is locally sourced- so I know I’m supporting local businesses and eating fresh options compared to other bars. Great sports bar with great vibes. Nice place to watch college football games, soccer, etc. Family friendly with games in the back!

I came here to watch a World Cup game and watch Norway play, and it was actually quite a good vibe. They let everyone in and we didn't have seating, but we had a really nice nook to eat at, so it actually ended up being quite nice.

Good:
- The mac and cheese here was really tasty and the prices were fair.
- I also liked the cornbread.
- Mostly it was the vibes and the huge TV screens. It was a great place to watch the game. They had like nine TVs showing the different games and everyone on the staff was super nice.

Bad:
- The portion sizes are really small on most things.
- The black beans and rice is tiny.
- Cornbread was half a portion, which I thought it was.
- It also took us over an hour for our food to get there so it takes a while. You have to be pretty patient especially if it's a busy day.

I'm just glad we found this spot that was great for the vibes of World Cup.
Cool spot! I liked the cucumber gimlet and guac. Many TVs but not too loud to talk.

For drinks, we had some Asashi, a strawberry sake, and another sake. For food, we had a sashimi plate, salmon nigiri, and a beef bowl. Food items tasted fantastic! Drinks were refreshing!

Our server was amazing! Having a little one being fussy near the end of our meal, our server was kind enough to warm up some water to dip a baby bottle to feed the nephew.

The menu has a variety of items so that everyone in the group can try something to eat.

Definitely can't wait to come back and try other delicious items.

Roam Artisan Burgers, also known as what I like to call "Yummy Town," delivers an experience that's about much more than just burgers. From the moment you arrive, you're surrounded by an atmosphere of pure opulence, positive energy, and ambition.

This is the kind of place where you're enjoying an incredible burger while overhearing conversations about multimillion-dollar deals, new ventures, and big ideas. Hit up Rome Artisan Burger for an early dinner on Saturday—practically had the place to ourselves at 4pm. Plenty of parking, which already puts them ahead of most spots.

**The Order**

Went with the chimichurri burger and their famous haystack of onions and zucchini. My fiancé grabbed the lettuce-wrapped turkey burger with sweet potato fries, plus a refresher (free with their loyalty signup—smart move).

**The Verdict**

The chimichurri burger? High-quality beef with interesting flavors, but honestly, sometimes a great burger doesn't need the fancy extras. That haystack looked Instagram-ready but arrived swimming in grease—definitely a sharing situation, not a solo mission. Should've stuck with regular fries.

My fiancé's turkey burger was a winner though, and those sweet potato fries disappeared fast. The refresher was apparently "amazing" according to her enthusiastic review.

**Bottom Line**

Counter service keeps things moving, there's nice patio seating for sunny days, and you can tell they're using quality ingredients. It's not going to blow your mind, but when you want a solid burger without the fuss, Rome Artisan delivers. Just maybe skip the haystack unless you're sharing.

Perfect for: Quality burger cravings, casual dining, patio weather
Skip if: You want mind-blowing flavors or hate counter service​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

Mama’s Boy is hands down the best pizza we’ve had in the Bay. We drove all the way from San Jose to try it and it was completely worth it. It honestly beats every place we’ve tried in NYC.

We got slices of pepperoni, cheese, burrata, and white. We also grabbed the garlic knots and the chocolate chip cookie and everything was amazing.

I ordered a sausage pizza for takeout and it was super tasty.  I was tempted to sneak a piece in the car before I brought it home because it smelled so good. My only complaint would be that the crust was a little chewy/tougher than I prefer, but that was only a minor distraction from an overall awesome pizza. They have an extra crispy option, I think I'll try that next.  One more thing, the pizzas are humongous!  One pizza could easily feed eight people or four really hungry people.

The pizza slices at Mama's Boy are an absolute standout, showcasing a slim, crisp foundation with beautifully blistered, airy edges that provide the ideal chew. The left slice pairs savory, robust meat toppings with a vibrant sauce and perfectly melted cheese, while the right slice elevates simplicity with fresh, creamy dollops of burrata, fragrant basil leaves, and a touch of chili flakes. When a pizzeria nails both hearty toppings and refined flavor combinations this perfectly, choosing just one slice is impossible, making the choice to grab both the only correct move. Best of all, the exceptional food is always paired with great service, making every single visit a fantastic experience from start to finish.
Don’t forget the ranch and peppers!!

We ordered a variety of vegetarian dishes. The highlights were the Guacamole with plantain chips, the Organic Veggie Mexican Bowl, and the fresh corn ribs, all of which were excellent. In summary, good food and ambience, but value for money is reduced by high pricing and mandatory surcharges.

We’re traveling from Visalia, CA, and I definitely hope to come back one day in the evening to see all the lights and experience how beautiful everything looks at night.

I’ve been to Xica several times for dinner with my husband, but recently had the opportunity to host a larger dinner party there—and it was absolutely incredible from start to finish!

I worked with Kristin Malotke to coordinate the evening, and she was amazing to work with. She made it so easy to accommodate a prix fixe menu with some challenging dietary restrictions and allergens, and handled every detail with such thoughtfulness and care.

The owner, Ignacio, was also there the evening of our dinner party and went above and beyond to celebrate our friend with us, including gifting our group a round of mocktails. It was such a thoughtful touch and made the evening feel even more special.

And the FOOD! Everything was incredible. You genuinely can’t tell that everything is gluten-free. The food was flavorful, creative, and satisfying without leaving me with that heavy, overly-full feeling after dinner—even after I had eaten a LOT of food! 😂 The quality and quantity were both outstanding.

From the ambiance, to the service, to the food and hospitality, everything was truly perfect. I highly recommend Xica for an intimate dinner date, but also for larger celebrations and group dinners. They made my friend’s celebration so special, and I can’t wait to come back!

The wait staff is very friendly, attentive and knowledgeable.   They also do private parties and Alcohol tastings.  I highly recommend Xica!

Gordo's Got My Grub: A Carnitas Burrito Ode (with ZERO Donkeys!)

Alright, we've got ourselves two kinds of burritos: the delicious food and the four-legged friend (in Spanish, "burrito" literally means "little donkey"). Edible burritos come in all shapes, sizes, and flavors! As a passionate eater, I gravitate towards the heftier options, but the taste is, of course, a non-negotiable requirement!

Gordo Taqueria serves up one of the tastiest and most substantial carnitas burritos I've ever had! Whenever I'm craving a quick, delicious, and filling bite, Gordo's always tops my list. The place is small, but there are a few tables if you want to dine in. The staff is consistently friendly and helpful.

Naturally, burritos aren't their only specialty! They also have delicious quesadillas, salad bowls, combo plates, and more. However, my personal favorite is the Super Carnitas with black beans, rice, hot salsa, sour cream, guacamole, and their signature crispy carnitas generously spread on top! While they don't serve alcohol, if you're grabbing a burrito, it pairs perfectly with a cold Mexican beer on a warm summer day!

The exact origin of the modern burrito might be a mystery, but whoever came up with the idea deserves a lifetime supply of burritos (or maybe even a Nobel Prize, category irrelevant)!

I ordered a club sandwich that was just right. It was just enough of everything and didn’t fall apart. My coworkers ordered a Chicken Patty Melt and Cheeseburger. They said they enjoyed them both. And that they did because they both finished.

I decided to eat the vegan torta with chorizo, and it tasted pretty good! However, I will say that it was a little heavy with vegan sour cream, and it tasted very off from real sour cream. It was almost sweet. Other than that, the torta was delicious,  flavorful, and well-cooked.

My sister decided to order the vegetarian wet burrito. Despite not being vegetarian or vegan herself, she enjoyed it a lot! So I would definitely recommend this to people coming to eat in a group of both vegans and non-vegans alike, because there truly is something for everybody.

The restaurant was pretty clean inside. Overall, the atmosphere was delightful and I could definitely see myself returning in the future to try out some other meals on their menu!

Paid $16 for the stalest vegan nachos I’ve ever eaten in my life. I usually enjoy the food here but lately the quality has gone down. Ordered the vegan super nachos and the tortilla chips were the stalest chips I've ever eaten lol | think I almost broke a tooth. These chips literally taste like chips they had before Christmas, then were closed for Christmas and then served again today.

FYI | ordered and ate this right away but the chips (as pictured) are so full of oil and so stale. So disappointing.

One of the Best Mexican Meals I’ve Ever Had!

Taco Boys completely blew me away. This was hands down one of the best Mexican meals I’ve ever had in my life—and that’s saying a lot! Everything is made fresh, so it took about 15 minutes, but it was so worth the wait.

As a vegan, I was thrilled to find a full vegan and vegetarian menu, and even better, my non-vegan friend was just as impressed. He actually said it was the best burrito he’s ever had! When both a vegan and a meat-eater leave raving about their meals, you know you’ve found a gem.

The vibe is super laid-back and casual—probably not the spot for a romantic dinner, but perfect for a chill hangout or quick bite with friends. Parking is street-only, so it can be a bit hit or miss depending on the day.

But honestly? If you love good food, especially if you’re plant-based, you have to give Taco Boys a try!

8/15/25

we had a peanut allergy in our party and they were accommodating and let us know which items to not order!
it was kind of quiet in the establishment, wish they had some music playing!

The bar was low for this place. Literally in the basement. I walked in to the smell of Fabulso and knew I was at a place that ran a shoestring business. The decor would make a Spartan proud - a few tables and chairs, a trash can, and a portable washbasin. You hear the sounds of the kitchen as you wait on your food.

I was the only diner and I felt a little concerned. But I needn't have. Because when the food came out I was blown away. The sambar, my usual first dipstick of how good a south Indian place is, was on point. The idlis were chopped up and dusted in Kandi podi. The portions were large enough where I was full right after the idly! The egg dosa came out next and had the same appeal. The chutneys and sambar were the same for all dishes, but they were well made.

My only complaint was the use of plastic for everything and as usual the filter coffee arrived without sugar. And adding it on the table never turns out as good as the original.

They have a buy 7 dosas and get one free offer. I am considering it!

Tasty Dosas in generous portions. Great place for a healthy meal in downtown Oakland. A speakeasy style cafe in the basement of the Ramada. Atmosphere is lack luster, but the food is worth it. Will return.

Good, authentic South Indian food is hard to find. Id Cafe isn’t exactly easy to find either. It’s located at the basement level of the Ramada Inn.

However, the food is fantastic. Truly South Indian sambar, great chutneys and excellent dishes. Syed, the man behind the counter had great suggestions, was sensitive to food allergies and had great energy.

I got idly sambar (large portions) and Hyderabad bandi dosa to go. Kudos to the chef.

For a place that’s only been open for 12 days, it is racking up reviews and business.

Worth multiple visits.

Delicious Dosas and very filling and flavorful!
Highly recommend, especially for vegetarians, since there’s a large selection and variety of really good Dosas and other dishes!

How have I grown up in the Bay Area without knowing about Crogan's? I was invited to attend a presentation (about cremations) and lunch was to be provided here at Crogan's. Nestled comfortably in a cute little section of shops in Montclair, it is conveniently located to public transportation, I decided not to drive and hopped on the 18 bus from downtown Oakland and it was a short 3-5 minute walk to the restaurant.

As you walk in, you instantly notice how spacious the space is.
Plenty of seating and a bar area- visually it gives me the vibe of "Cheers" and I'm waiting for Norm to walk in any minute. I arrived at 11:30 for the presentation and there were only a few people inside. Upon leaving a couple hours later, the restaurant was almost full on a Thursday afternoon.

Our party was a total of 11 including our host and we were seated in a private area in the back. So this would be perfect if you are looking for a place to rent for a special event- it could easily fit 15-20 people.

Now, on to the food- when I tell it came out piping hot and fresh! We were told that we could order anything off the menu up to $26. The menu cost range was about $6-30 so pretty affordable in this economy. I ordered the fish and chips as did a few other people. Everyone raved about how fresh their food was.

My fries were seasoned perfectly and needed no salt. The fish was cod I believe and came with (3) medium sized strips and I got a side of coleslaw. The fish wasn't really seasoned at all BUT it was so crunchy and crispy (texture) and the inside was so flaky, tender and super fresh like they caught the fish outside. I was able to eat a couple of pieces and took the rest home- NOTE: the fish doesn't reheat well in the oven so it needs to be devoured when you order.

The person to the right of me ordered the shrimp and avocado salad which looked really appetizing. A good portion of bay shrimp alongside ripe avocado, tomatoes on top of a bed of greens. The gentlemen to the left of me ordered a double portion of ribs. I wish I could've snuck a photo- the ribs were HUGE and he didn't talk the entire time which is a good sign.

Overall, this is a family friendly sit down place with great American and Seafood options. Food is prepared fresh to order- I definitely will be back to check other options on the menu!

5 more times they say ‘restaurant is closed’.  That’s fine we ate down the street, just want a drink. Then bartender adds on, bar closes in 1/2 hour. Yeah we heard, here for a drink.

It’s painfully obvious, he didn’t want to serve us. We are an inconvenience.

We left and you lost $60. We are local and do weekly dinners with 6+ people. I can assure you we will not be back. Go ahead chase customers away and when you don’t have jobs and you wonder why no one comes in, this is why.

Restaurants and bars go out of business constantly and I think this type of customer service is why.

Sidebar: A friendly guest tried to get us to stay…clearly we are the only two women in the bar. He seemed fun but we left.

The appropriate response:  Welcome in, would you like a drink, we are closing soon but can serve you for last call.

Europa – Where Comfort Meets Culinary Excellence

Europa is more than just a restaurant — it's a heartfelt experience wrapped in warmth, flavor, and community. From the moment you step inside, you're no longer just a guest; you’re part of something special. A place where food doesn’t just feed you — it moves you. A restaurant that has managed to capture the very soul of European home cooking and elevate it into a full-bodied dining experience, Europa is the kind of place you dream of stumbling upon… and once you do, you never want to leave.

Let’s be clear: Europa is awesome. There’s no other word that fits quite as well. It’s a harmonious blend of culinary art and cozy atmosphere — a place where every detail feels intentional, and every bite tastes like love.

First Impressions: A Place That Feels Like Home

Walking into Europa feels like entering the home of a dear friend. The exterior, though unpretentious, has a welcoming charm. and there’s a distinct, cozy glow that draws you in from the street.

The interior is just as inviting. think polished wood tables, soft pendant lighting, and tasteful decor that whispers rather than shouts. It’s super clean (you notice how clean it is), and it has an air of freshness without feeling sterile.

Soft music hums in the background, and the space is lively without being loud. You immediately get that “good vibes only” feel — people are smiling, staff are laughing, and there’s a pleasant buzz of conversation in the air. It’s hard not to feel instantly at ease.

Service That Shines

The service at Europa is, without exaggeration, exceptional. The staff here seem genuinely happy to be doing what they do, and it shows. From the host who greets you with a warm smile to the servers who are attentive without hovering, every member of the team goes above and beyond.

They know the menu inside out and are happy to recommend dishes based on your preferences. Allergies? Dietary restrictions? They handle it with total confidence and zero fuss. There's a balance here — professional, yet personal; friendly, but never pushy. They seem to know when to engage and when to step back, which is a rare and beautiful quality in hospitality.

from appetizers to dessert — is smooth and relaxed, never rushed, never dragging. It’s the kind of service that makes you feel taken care of.

The Food: Where Flavor Meets Heart

Now for the main event — the food. Europa doesn't just serve food; it serves experiences on a plate. Every dish is infused with the kind of care and detail you’d expect from your grandmother’s kitchen, but with the finesse of a top-tier chef.

Here’s the thing: this is home-cooked-style food, but elevated to exquisite heights. The flavors are rich, balanced, and deeply satisfying. Each bite tells a story — of tradition, of passion, of culinary craft passed down through generations.

Main Courses
The mains are where Europa truly shines. Whether you’re in the mood for hearty comfort or refined elegance, there’s something here that will make your soul sing.

I had The Baked Chicken on 🍋the lemon— fall-apart tender Cooked Chicken, slow-cooked in a reduction, paired with Rice, Cabbage and pillowy potatoes that carry just the right hint of earthiness. It’s rich, decadent, and absolutely unforgettable..

Desserts
Dessert at Europa is not optional. It’s a must.

Drinks: From European Brews to Fine Wines

The wine selection is even more impressive. Featuring diverse bottles but approachable. Ask your server for a recommendation — chances are they’ll find you the perfect pairing for your meal.

Vibes: Atmosphere That Draws You In

The vibes at Europa are impeccable. There’s a sense of warmth and welcome that goes beyond just This is Definitely a Five Star Restaurant ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

top_reviews.content: While the food here is good, the service is even better. Diego and crew are exceptional. The fried chicken was also good. The lechon kiwali was not to our liking but it is due to the triple-cooked process. So that is on us. The kabocha squash in coconut milk was tasty, as expected from kabocha squash. The eggplant omelette with banana ketchup was OK. The ketchup tasted like banana and not at all like ketchup. There is minimal street parking around the perimeter. The staff was great, they were excited about the menu and restaurant week and explained all the different options for their special restaurant week menu. The lumpia came out hot and crispy, loved the flavor. The adobo was my favorite because it reminded me of my lola's adobo and that is saying a lot! The pancit had a very unique smoky flavor to it which was a pleasant surprise. The jicama salad was very fresh and bright and complemented the savory salty dishes. The only odd thing was the one cup of rice for two people. Would definitely come back to try their full menu.

We saw FOB Kitchen on Check, Please recently and had to try it! What we wanted to try were the Vegan items as well as the other Filipino items!
I had the Longanisa Benedict for a Sunday Brunch, what a tasty meal! The vegetable Lumpia was a good appetizer and the Kabocha Squash side also very tasty.

We recently dined at FOB Kitchen, a Filipino restaurant located in Oakland's Temescal neighborhood, and overall, it was a flavorful experience.

Dishes We Tried:
* Shanghai Lumpia: Crispy, bite-sized spring rolls filled with a savory mix of pork and vegetables, paired with a tangy dipping sauce that elevated the dish. Personally, I think there should be more meat. The garlic rice was amazing!!!
* Lechon Kawali: The deep-fried pork belly was perfectly crispy on the outside while tender and juicy on the inside. The dipping sauce added just the right tang to balance the richness.
* Sticky Wings: Coated in a sweet and sticky glaze with a subtle kick of spice, these wings were indulgent and satisfying.
* Sinigang Baboy: A comforting and flavorful tamarind-based pork soup, with tender pork pieces and vegetables. The balance of sour and savory was spot on.
* Fried Chicken: While the seasoning was good and the exterior crispy, the chicken was unfortunately overly cooked, making it drier than we would have liked.
* Turon (Dessert): The turon was a delightful way to end the meal. The crispy fried wrapper encased sweet caramelized banana and jackfruit and was served with creamy ube ice cream, which paired perfectly. Requested the Ube ice cream to be served on the side.

Ambiance:
FOB Kitchen offers a vibrant, welcoming atmosphere that reflects Filipino culture. The decor is colorful and thoughtfully designed, creating a warm and lively environment.

Service:
Unfortunately, the waitstaff were not very attentive, even when the restaurant was not busy. This detracted slightly from the overall experience.

Overall Experience:
FOB Kitchen delivers authentic and flavorful Filipino cuisine in a relaxed setting. The standout dishes like the Lechon Kawali, Sinigang Baboy, and the turon dessert made the meal memorable. Despite the inattentive service and the overly cooked fried chicken, the kitchen's speed and precision stood out.

We recommend FOB Kitchen for those seeking a genuine Filipino dining experience in Oakland--just don't expect exceptional service.

FOB - Filipino Oakland Baes-  ask about this when you go.

Excellent food and crowded restaurant. The kalbichim was very good and not too sweet. Some places it could be too sweet but here it tastes just right. Even though it was very busy the waitresses were attentive and quick in cleaning the tables and waiting time was to a minimum. Highly recommend this Korean restaurant for their varied menu and their courteous service. For those who like Chapchae it is a must to try as well as their Kalbichim. The price is very reasonable and very good quantity of food per person. They are very generous with their side dishes and you always receive a pleasant surprise.

top_reviews.content: The fish taco and chicken salad were quite nice! The signature burger, though, was a little on the bland side 😂. The atmosphere overall was pleasant, even if we had a hard time spotting the staffs most of the time 😂

Stopped in before a movie and was pleasantly surprised. The server was very attentive and nice. Great beer selection. The food was good, keep in mind it’s pub food. We look forward to checking out more of the menu.

Visited around 2pm on a Saturday and was seated right away despite being busy. They have a wonderful outdoor patio with lots of seating, tvs for entertainment, great music on weekends, and they are dog friendly! The atmosphere was enjoyable. The servers are all very friendly and attentive, quick service with a smile. The menu didn't have as much variety as I'd like for chicken options. Tried the grilled chicken sandwich which was good, love the fries here especially the Cajun. The Philly cheesesteak was the winner at our table. Love the housemade lemonade and fresh brewed tea. The boneless wings with the Korean BBQ sauce is a must.   Would highly recommend and will be back!

I asked one the staff where the bathroom 🚻 was, he told me. I walk out of the restaurant around the corner where the bathrooms are for the entire complex and there's a combination lock on it. So I walk back, ask a different employee for the combination. The other employee obviously left out the information about the bathroom combination on purpose. Not sure why the games or making things difficult, but didn't find the environment friendly,  only cordial. Food was decent, beer was good, bartender friendly, but wouldn't go back. Plenty of other places with better food and service.

A group of colleagues and I chose The Fourth Bore for a recent luncheon. As there were five of us, we were seated at the large center table. It was a high table but had plenty of space.

We started off with two of the Bavarian Pretzels with beer cheese. I ordered the Fish and Chips. I really enjoyed the batter. Rather than the traditional batter on the fish, these were crusted with panko or similar breading. Very good.

Our server was attentive but not intrusive. It was a great meal and we all enjoyed our orders.

If you're in the area, give The Fourth Bore a try. The next time I go, I'd like to give their extensive beer menu a try. Thumbs Up!

top_reviews.content:
We celebrated a birthday with a group of 10 adults and 2 babies, and this restaurant truly went above and beyond from start to finish. They seated us at a long table by the fireplace and even accommodated our two strollers neatly out of the way.

We began with the East Coast Chopped Salad and the OC Baby Lettuce—both generously portioned, perfectly dressed and easily  for sharing. For mains, we ordered a variety of pizzas including the Margherita, Burrata, Funghi, Pepperoni, Salsiccia, and Vodka, the Bologna and Chitarra alla Cacio e Pepe pastas.

Even as someone who usually skips the crust, I couldn’t resist—the thin, wood-fired pizzas were delicious, and every topping was full of flavor.

They kindly cut and plated our birthday cake in the back before serving it to the table, which was such a thoughtful touch.

Ray, our waiter, and Isabella the hostess
provided exceptional,attentive service throughout, and we never felt rushed.

Food, service, ambiance—chef’s kiss! We’ll absolutely
be back again and again.
Rooftop is lovely and heated. Jeremiah is such a kind and funny server - shoutout him! The food is sooo yummy!!

Oh my god this place is fantastic. This is about the best pizza I've had in my life, and the cocktail I had (I believe it was called the Bee's Knees) was just perfection. Clearly the ingredients they use are top shelf. And the vibe is very cozy and fun, with the SF-themed wallpaper. Can't wait to go back and try some of their other pizzas.

Best place for food in Irwing street. Very good Italian food. Nice atmosphere. Fast service. I arrived before more people started to come so I could choose to seat outside.
Pizza not burnt. Only one minor point is the cream of the tiramisu - I'd appreciate it to be denser.
Definetely a good spot for dinner after a day at the park/museum there!

This place is off the charts phenomenal! They are gluten free friendly. (You can tell them that you have an allergy and they will make accommodations). Their food is not your average Italian cuisine. I had the Ricotta Cavatelli & Lamb sausage and it was delicious! I highly recommend this restaurant. It is also family friendly and the service is amazing!

Amazing spot here. The food is delicious. It’s a fixed menu; so you select a large or medium plate. Medium was plenty for lunch. There is a soup, and about 4-5 plate items. If you do not like one the plate options, you can sub that item out and get more of another!

I am not vegan; and this food was fresh, tasty, and felt homemade. We were all full, and loved our meal. I loved everything, especially the lentil and rice!!

The food was amazing, and somehow the service was even better. The woman who helped us treated us like family, and was the perfect balance of attentive and non-intrusive.

Highly reco. this spot to all. And wish them continued success! Their food is delicious, nutritious, clean, and healthy.

I love this place. Reliably tasty healthy food with just enough variety day to day to keep you coming back. I love that I don't have to order, just tell them how much I want. The moderate meal is a generous portion so I've never actually ordered the large.

So much gratitude for this place. Love the food and we're so grateful to have a quiet and peaceful place where humble, delicious, organic food is served by kind people. A true gem. Please keep doing what you do. I will be back soon.

Awesome, wholesome, healthy food. Soup is great and so tasty. Free hot tea and water help round out a perfect meal.

Order a medium-sized meal; plenty of it.

Really lovely vegan spot. Came here for lunch, perfect breeze, beautiful weather, got to enjoy the sun but also stayed in the shade. Lots of birds sounds. You pick either the moderate for $13 or full lunch for $15 and can add on kombucha or pies. We got the moderate, which were plenty of food. The flavors are rich and full bodied. Also would be a nice patio to take dogs to and enjoy a nice conversation with someone.

top_reviews.content: Delicious omakase! Really deserves to be a Michelin star again!! The ginger shoot was a cool touch and super tender. Great balance of nigiri and complementary appetizers and seared cod. Cute ambiance for our anniversary -- no reservation needed

This was the best sushi Omakase I've had. Period. It was worth all the decisions Ive made to get me into that seat eating the freshest and meatiest pieces with perfect preparation. This will haunt me until I come back a year later. I can only tell time by the anchor to this experience. What time is it? Oh just 3 days since I had the best sushi of my life. Chef was super friendly and even showed us his knife collection. Come hungry. Approx 2 hours for the full course.

It felt like a fusion because of some of the local ingredients and tastes. I can see they put thoughts on the flavors and the knife skills/cuttings are great.

I wish they put a little bit more effort on the menu description and how the server presented the dishes.

For an omakase, I expect more communications. Don’t just tell me “this is a tuna”, “this is an egg cake”. It’s obvious. I’d like a more detailed explanation of what I’m eating and why they are served.

It’s missing a human touch & interaction for an omakase experience.

We had a lovely anniversary dinner here. The omakase was very well constructed with a balance of hot and cold dishes that complemented each other really well. The sushi was clearly meticulously made and each dish was a delight to enjoy. Highly recommend the omakase and hot sake pairing!

We had such a wonderful time! The atmosphere was very friendly, and the chef was incredibly outgoing and engaging. He gave vivid, detailed explanations of each piece of sushi — including which part of the fish it came from and how it was prepared — which made the experience feel extra special and educational.

One unique touch was the in-house special drink designed to transition between the appetizer and the sushi course — such a thoughtful detail! Since it was our birthday, the restaurant even surprised us with a hand-drawn birthday card. Super cute and such a lovely gesture!

Constructive feedback:
1.	It would be great if the reservation time could be extended to 2.5 hours. Things felt a little rushed toward the end.
2.	It would also be nice to have a choice between water and hot tea as a default beverage option.

Overall, a fantastic experience — we’d definitely come back!

The food was amazing, quality was on point. I’d get everything again minus the chicken katsu. The volcano roll and Godzilla roll are incredible, the takoyaki is worth getting, and the lamb stank was phenomenal! The tuna tacos were so fresh. 10 out of 10 would recommend.
Service was also incredible, very attentive! Lastly, food came out quickly! Very impressed!

Sushi is their highlight - Avoid Ramen: The sushi was very fresh and very tasty, highly recommend you get their sushi. Now for the ramen, I got the garlic tonkatsu, the broth is delicious, id drink that out of a cup. Unfortunately the noodles were over cooked and slightly mushy, very low quality. The pork was not cooked enough, still very tough and the egg was very salty. Again, the broth was exceptional. If they adjust their ingredients for their ramen, itll be top tier. At this moment in time, I can only recommend the sushi, which is why I gave it a 5 star. I hope who ever reads this sees this as constructive feedback as I think your soup could be a winner, you have the hardest part down, the broth. Once more, definitely come here for the sushi.

Came here for Christmas with my family and we had a great time! This is our second time here and won’t be our last! We came around 5pm, we got a reservation, and we were seated right away. We first ordered from their happy hour menu and then their regular menu.

My favorite dish was their sashimi, the hamachi carpaccio, and their Inside out roll. Their sashimi is super fresh and was so delicious. The dishes came out pretty fast & service was wonderful!

This is our local gem on Ocean Ave.
We found this place during the pandemic.
Even though I love to go at happy hour time for beers, I love the specials menu a lot. It's being presented beautifully and taste fresh and yummy, most importantly, it won't break the bank.

I enjoy sitting by the window and the seat you need to remove your shoes and sit on the floor like a Japanese. That area of seats let me enjoy my meal most. Pls remember to make a reservation and try to appoint yourself to the VIP area. If they reject you, try to negotiate with them about 1 hour or less.

Always fresh and food is good. Service can be a bit slow at times, particularly when busy, but always pleasant. I imagine it's more the fault of delivery apps/volume than staff negligence.
A nice neighborhood space, reservations are encouraged on weekends. They have a rentable karaoke room for large groups.
It's always clean, the booths with the floor seating are nice, nothing to write home about, but pleasant.

top_reviews.content: I’ve randomly stopped by this place on at least two occasions now. Cocktails were fantastic, and the food is unexpectedly refined and really good. The patatas bravas are perfection, and I really enjoyed their smoked salmon crostinis as well. For being in North Beach, prices were also very reasonable. Would love the opportunity to try other dishes in the future!

TLdR: great food at reasonable prices especially for happy hour

All the food and drink was 20 or 25% off during happy hour. We really enjoyed the shrimp and the croquettes. I also liked that it has outdoor and indoor seating. Service was quick and professional, would come
Back!

Absolutely delicious from start to finish!

The burger was incredibly juicy, flavorful, and cooked perfectly. The ribs were so tender and juicy they practically fell apart, and the croquettes were amazing — crispy on the outside, creamy and full of flavor on the inside 🤤

Everything we ordered was excellent, and you can really tell care goes into the food. Great quality, generous portions, and a meal we'll definitely be thinking about for a while.

Can't wait to come back!

Red Window is such a reliable neighborhood staple. The tapas are always good and hit the spot. I definitely recommend getting the Gambas Al Ajillo and the Patatas Bravas.
The Brussels had the perfect crispy texture without tasting burnt, and a sour salty flavor.
I unfortunately did not like the Octopus. The ingredients just don’t go super well together. Maybe if you have it as a dip for slices of bread it’s better? Not sure to be honest.

Fun funky decor. Menu is a mix of Spanish and Italian (but mostly Spanish). The Albondigas (meatballs) were moist and delicious. The braised short rib was melt-in-your-mouth tender and full of flavor. We also had the Patatas Bravas appetizer, which were delicious. Layer upon layer of potato, with a delicious sauce.

They also had a very nice N/A drink menu, which we appreciated. The N/A Negroni was delicious.

top_reviews.content: So glad we discovered this gem! The food was absolutely delicious and the service was impeccable. My husband is a serious burger lover, and he was thoroughly impressed — we ordered the Traffic Jam Burger, the Fried Chicken Sandwich, and the Bacon Jam Fries, and every single item was perfectly cooked and seasoned. The portions are generous and the prices are very reasonable. This place has officially earned a spot in our regular rotation — highly recommend!

The environment is great for socializing, and the service is wonderful. The people who work there are extremely friendly and do what they can to make your time there enjoyable. It's a great place to hang out with friends and family.

The food, which is inspired by street food, is very solid. I wouldn't say it's the best or even that impressive, but it's also not bad in any way. The burgers there are everything you would expect from a typical street food burger. I'd say they were just tasty, satisfying and easy to eat that I had no real complaints. That said, the food, including the burgers, didn't really excite me either.

In other words, the food is just good enough not to ruin your dining experience with friends and family. I don't love the food, but it's not half bad and the restaurant still appeals to me as a place to socialize.

Really excellent spot, and close to the freeway if you’re just driving through the east bay and need a break.

I only got the burger and bacon jam fries, I think the burger was called the traffic jam. Really good w the cheese and fried egg, and for as messy as it was, the bun held up to the end. Fries were good, the bacon jam on the sweet dude, but also really excellent. The beer came from a brewery next door, also really good.

Service was great, staff all friendly. While I’m not often in this area, this is on a short list to revisit and try something else.

Who would have thought the combination of Dim Sum and burger could go so well together? It’s the best of both worlds, and it’s good that different people can have different food when they visit. Everything we tried was tasty (from burger to dim sum to fried rice). Would definitely return for more!

I’m so happy that we stopped in for brunch today! Another spot was busy with rude people from the moment we parked. We didn’t want anything too rich and my friend and I are Asian so I remembered that there’s always a great fusion menu here. And we’re so lucky that weekends also include DIM SUM. Everything was scrumptious. Got my kid homemade chicken tenders and fries. There’s a batch of soufflé pancakes being prepped in the back (call ahead if you want them)!

Can’t recommend this cozy spot enough. There’s no sign but the atmosphere is unmatched in the warm, friendly service and I’ve never tried anything that isn’t downright delicious.

The guy was nice and pizza taste awesome not sure how much my sister spend but worth it for sure, first time have that pizza it was amazing so worth it to go
Back will definitely suggest to my friends or if I was to do party I will buy pizza there

The new owners are doing a fantastic job bringing Bravos back! Had stopped going after many issues with the previous owners, but the new ownership is a breath of fresh air, and the pizza is much tastier!

My first meal at Bravo was back in about 1969, when I was a young child.  It was a staple restaurant for my parents to take my brother and I to when we were just toddlers.  We used to sleep on the old school bench seats while our parents finished their dinner.  Many years later and I am still eating at Bravo with my own kids who are all adults at this point.  The thing about Bravo Pizza is that I have NEVER found it's equal in all of the places I've traveled.  It's always the highlight of coming home to the City to stop for a pizza and good conversation with the crew there at a place that has literally been part of my entire life.  The pizza is the same great taste with a perfect crust and toppings that do not disappoint. There salads and entrees have always been great too.

Bravo is THE pizza place in the Excelsior/Outer Mission that needs to be on your list!

Needed something quick. First time dropping in. They had fresh cheese & pepperoni out the oven. Opted for the pepperoni slice with a Diet Coke. Great service, friendly guys behind the counter, served my meal & took it straight to my table of choice. Will def be back to try some more varieties.

Classic Bravo Pizza is off to a strong start under new ownership. One standout addition to the menu is the honey garlic chicken wings—super crispy, generously sized, and packed with flavor. The balance of sweet honey and savory garlic really hits the spot, and they easily stand out compared to competitors’ wings in the area. These are definitely a must-try and won’t let you down.

On top of that, the $12 large pepperoni pizza is an incredible deal, especially for a classic New York–style slice. It’s rare to find that kind of quality and portion at this price point.

The combo pizza was a bit thicker than my personal preference, but with the strong direction the new ownership is already showing, I’m excited to see continued refinements and improvements moving forward.

Overall, it’s great to see fresh energy at Classic Bravo Pizza while keeping the neighborhood favorite feel. Looking forward to what else the new ownership has in store. 🍕🍗🔥

top_reviews.content: This was a great place to stop by, busy, and I've never heard a single complaint. The sandwiches, sweets and shop items are pretty cool, some reasonable, others not so much. But the food was great and I highly recommend this place to anyone coming to SF. Plus Chestnut St is usually a sweet walk. My sandwich, although a little messy was still one of the best I've had since being here in SF, traditional, and easy to scarf down. Although I'm not a big fan of paying $10+ for a sandwich it wasn't so bad for the experience here. Also Lucca has a great crew, they seem to all work together very well.

Ordered via DoorDash For $24 (before fees and tips) - The Pat Burrell sandwich is underwhelmed on amount of meat, it feels like it’s all centered and layered to the middle of the sandwich to look good on the cut, but to the edges there’s no meat. The taste is basic!

****Restaurant - quality meal at home in about 15 minutes**** check out the photos of my prepared cheese ravioli.

On my last visit I picked up their refrigerated cheese ravioli along with a jar of puttanesca sauce, fresh thyme, oregano, and Parmigiano Reggiano. With a little olive oil and herbs, the result was honestly ***restaurant-level***if not better. The ravioli cook in minutes and the quality of the ingredients makes all the difference.

*** I did not see Grana Padano during my visit but they most likely carry it(?)***

Another thing Lucca absolutely excels at is sandwiches. Their deli counter is packed with great cheeses and cured meats, and they also offer desserts like fresh cannoli. I haven’t had cannoli this good anywhere else in San Francisco. The shells are very fresh and crispy, and while they source the shells, they make the cream themselves - DELICIOUS!

Overall: 10/10. I’m a permanent customer. The staff is incredibly helpful when it comes to selecting specific pasta, sauces, or cheeses, so don’t hesitate to ask questions. They’re delightfully nerdy about Italian cuisine.

Went to this shop to pick up some food for a picnic at Crissy Field - only 8 min drive away from the beach.

Ordered: Classic Turkey, Pat Burrel, and the Meatball sandwich… along with some cheese, crackers, and a prosecco. Loved that this shop had everything we needed.

Perfect day in SF with friends. Would come back to buy picnic essentials.

This meatball sandwhich tastes like nostalgia for me. It tastes of a simpler time when I lived off chestnut street with the boys and our biggest concern was choosing the perfect dinner to end a perfect day. This sandwhich tastes like family.

Came here after seeing good reviews online and ordered take out - when I got back to the hotel and opened up the food, I found a long strand of hair. I called the restaurant and asked if I could just get a new one, and he said that he was unwilling to deliver a new order, nor was he willing to give any compensation. The food was excellent,  spicy, and delicious.  The service was fast. The decore needs some attention to make the restarant more inviting.  However,  I would recommend the food.

We tried House smoked beef jerky and house special tofu. Although both looked fine, they were really lacking the flavor. I can taste some saltiness but not much more. I was actually surprised because the smoky Beef jerky didn't have actually the smoke flavor.

Suitable for a quick meal but not the nice vibe - The restaurant is small in a fast food style and not for large parties.

In business since 1974 for a reason. This restaurant is off the beaten path, but we'll worth the small detour from Grant Street.

top_reviews.content:
Walking into Gao Viet Kitchen felt like stepping into Vietnam. The decor is vibrant, thoughtfully designed, and creates a warm, immersive atmosphere from the moment you walk in.

I visited with my family for dinner, and despite having a party of seven, the staff was very accommodating and seated us comfortably. The service throughout the night was attentive and friendly.

The food was the highlight of the experience. The pho was rich, flavorful, and comforting, while every dish we ordered was delicious. The standout for me was the garlic noodles with the 3-way beef — absolutely fantastic and packed with flavor. They also offer a wide variety of beverages, which was a nice touch for the table.

Overall, my whole family had a great experience at Gao Viet. Between the atmosphere, quality of the food, and welcoming service, it’s definitely a place I would recommend.

We visited Gao Viet Kitchen & Bar for lunch on Saturday, September 5th, and honestly left already planning our next visit.

The Grass Jelly Cream Coffee was SO good! The Vietnamese coffee flavor was authentic, bold, and strong—the kind of coffee that actually tastes like Vietnamese coffee should. I also ordered the Sapa-Rita, and it was absolutely delicious. I love how creative they are with their cocktail names, taking inspiration from popular cities and destinations throughout Vietnam. Such a fun touch!

But the absolute star of my meal was the Bún Bò Huế. I’ve tried bún bò Huế at so many famous Vietnamese restaurants from Orange County to Houston, NYC, and Seattle, and I can honestly say this is the best I’ve had in the U.S. so far. The broth is incredibly rich, deep, and flavorful without being overwhelmingly heavy or salty. You can really taste and smell the lemongrass, and the overall balance is just amazing. This is the kind of bowl that makes you stop after the first few bites and think, “Wow, this is GOOD.” Definitely the best of the best for me!

My husband ordered the Bò Né, which was decent but more standard and didn’t stand out quite as much compared to the bún bò Huế and drinks.

We sat at the bar and were lucky enough to have the bartender take care of us. She was so sweet, friendly, and patient, which made the whole experience even better. The restaurant has such a fun, modern Vietnamese vibe, and I really enjoyed the combination of traditional flavors with creative cocktails and presentation.

Overall, we had a wonderful lunch and will definitely be coming back to try more of the menu. There are so many dishes and drinks I still want to try. If you’re craving Vietnamese food in San Francisco, especially if you’re a bún bò Huế lover, I highly recommend giving Gao Viet a try! ❤️🇻🇳

This is, without question, one of the most impressive Vietnamese restaurants I’ve visited, notable for both the range of its menu and the imagination behind it. Luxurious dishes and simpler, more unexpected offerings sit comfortably side by side. The two-level space is lively, and while service can feel hectic at peak hours, it remains admirably efficient.

What stands out most is the consistency of the cooking. For a restaurant with this much traffic, the level of execution is remarkable. The pork belly and duck arrived with exceptionally crisp skin and meat that was still tender, juicy and full of flavor. The roasted beef rib was cooked to the point where the bone slipped out cleanly. Every dish was carefully plated, showing real attention to presentation without veering into fussiness.

Overall, it is a restaurant of unusual quality, and one that readily invites return visits.

Gob smackingly good brunch. It might be considered a medium to high price point but it's soo worth it.

Gao seemed gimmicky from reels showing phozilla but I was pleasantly surprised. Bánh cuôn, bò né, garlic noodles 3 way were all 🔥🔥🔥.

Ambience is unique with the window shutter art.

Will definitely be going back for the pho.

★★★★★ Gao Viet Kitchen in San Francisco delivers bold, deeply satisfying Vietnamese flavors with a modern edge. The broths are rich and layered, the meats are tender and generously portioned, and each dish has a wonderful balance of savory depth, aromatics, and freshness.

What stands out is how the restaurant elevates familiar Vietnamese comfort food without losing its authenticity. Generous, flavorful, and memorable—an excellent stop for Vietnamese food in San Francisco.

top_reviews.content:
We made a reservation to try this new tapas spot and had an awesome dining experience. The restaurant was beautifully decorated with plants and art pieces, which made it feel so cozy and inviting.

We ordered the sangria and a frozen red wine drink, and both were delicious. For food, we had the garlic mushrooms, chicken skewers, mussels, and seafood paella, and everything was incredible. The paella didn’t have the crispy rice texture, but I still really enjoyed it because the sauce was so flavorful. We finished with the Madrid-style churros, which were the perfect ending to a wonderful meal. The staff was great too, and we would definitely come back again

I rarely leave negative reviews, but this experience was disappointing enough that I felt I had to.

The paella was surprisingly small for the price, and it was way too salty. The other specials we ordered were also very small in portion.

We made a reservation for three people, yet we were seated at the bar instead of a proper table, which wasn’t what we expected after booking in advance.

Service was also lacking—we repeatedly had to ask for more water instead of it being refilled proactively.

After reading all the glowing Google reviews, we came in with high expectations, but our experience was completely different. Based on our visit, the reviews simply didn’t reflect what we experienced. Unfortunately, we won’t be coming back.

Absolutely loved this Spanish restaurant! The paella was incredible—full of flavor, perfectly cooked, and one of the best I’ve had. The ingredients tasted fresh, and every bite was delicious. The atmosphere was warm and inviting, and the service was excellent. I’ll definitely be coming back. Highly recommend!

The tapas themselves are honestly pretty hit or miss. Crudo, eggplant, garlic shrimp were good. Beef skewers were extremely chewy, crispy pork belly was hard, artichoke didn't taste like much, flatbread tasted like frozen pizza from a supermarket, sangria was watery.

Our server seemed visibly upset at us throughout the meal, no such obligatory politeness. I don't really care about this but it's annoying for a place where you pay + tip so much.

The vibe of the place is nice. I personally wouldn't come back.

This was some of the best Spanish food I’ve had stateside. I’ve been to hundreds of Spanish restaurants - mostly in Spain and this place can stand up to the best of them. Excellent fundamentals - pan, bravas, and tortilla. They were even slinging rebujitos! I’ve never been happier to pay $9 for a 1906.

The real highlight is the croquetas. Thousands of croquetas, and you’d still be fortunate to try these small slices of simple perfection: Piping hot, perfect crunch , not too creamy or bready, perfectly sized jamón diced inside. I’m both offended and impressed they forced me to say I wanted socarrot, but the seafood paella was spot on - fresh, rich and great crunch.

Unpretentious atmosphere, excellent food, amazing flavor, and fair pricing for sf (~$10-$15 tapas, $30-45 2p paellas), can’t recommend destapas enough.

top_reviews.content: Very busy place (as most places in this area are) but we were able to get in as walk-in. Tonkatsu bun (instead of bread) was practically falling apart, with the bun too flimsy to hold up to something like a thick tonkatsu. Toro cakes were mediocre, and the tuna flavor wasn't balanced right on the fried rice ball. The tuna nigiri had fishy after taste. The cookie dough roll is an odd one, and nothing to write home about.

Our favourite meal in SF of my trip <3 thank you !

Came for the Cookie doll roll specifically but tried some of their popular apps and rolls. On more of the expensive side but loved how the sushi rolls had a perfect rice to fish ratio. Would def come here again if splurging

The food at Mamanoko was incredibly fresh and full of flavor. Their Miso soup is outstanding — a must-try.
We were also pleasantly surprised by the dessert. The brownie dough roll was absolutely exceptional.

Happy hour sushi dishes were delicious and well portioned for the reduced price (8 pieces). They were generous w/the ginger, but stingy with the wasabi dollops. Beer was overpriced for only for canned/bottled imports. Doesn't appear any beer was on tap at this bar. And when they switch out happy hour prices, they do it on the dot, be aware of the time when you dine. The atmosphere was crowded for a small space that was popular for a Tuesday night w/the locals. But, there isn't a lot of room andthis small interior results in noisey acoustic dining. So be warned for those hoping for a quiet atmosphere, cause the place draws in families w/loud children. When I dined Tuesday afternoon, it felt like a Sunday munch-and-shop crowd that day. And it appeared as if they were trying to get people in and out as quickly as possible, even with no waiting line present at the entry. Though the bartender was attentive and speedy with service, the front house staff appeared disengaged w/o direct eye contact. In the end, food was superb, but not worth a return visit.

The dining room is busy and loud (or maybe we're old), so there was quite a bit of "what did you say" in our conversations, but it did not diminish the experience.

The wine list provides a great selection to complement the menu without breaking the bank. Menu prices are in line with what we see these days - and the large portions make dining here a great value.

Our table ordered Pollo Scallopini, Vitello (veal) Scallopini, Melanzane (eggplant) Parmigiana, and the off-menu special Salmon Piccata. Everything was excellent. The veal was a big hit with the table.

Strongly recommend making a reservation. Looks like they do a good job with larger parties without impacting smaller tables and couples. This place is a mainstay in Walnut Creek for a reason.

I finally went to Montecatini in Walnut Creek and had such a great experience.

I don’t think I had ever been before, or maybe just not in a very long time, but I know they’ve made a lot of changes in recent years and it really shows. The restaurant has a traditional, old-school Italian feel, but in a warm and inviting way.

The food was excellent. The lasagna and carpaccio were incredible, and the risotto was wonderful as well. The staff were all lovely, including the bartender, and the service felt genuinely welcoming.

Such a good local spot and definitely worth checking out.

Had dinner at Montecatini’s last week and sat at the bar — as always, it was outstanding. Owner Terrence was filling in and cooking, and Taylor was doing what she always does: everything! I was really impressed by how Terrence stepped right into the kitchen to cover for his chef who was out. The restaurant was extremely busy, but he handled it like he was the full-time chef. He’s been part of the restaurant for so long that stepping in to cook looked like a piece of cake for him. The food came out perfectly, and everything kept running smoothly.

Bartender Angel not only makes phenomenal drinks, but also serves dinner to the people sitting at the bar while making drinks for the entire restaurant, which he does with ease. Marco was doing what he does best, running the front as maître d’. On a busy night, the restaurant can look chaotic to customers, but to them it’s just another night. Everyone works incredibly well together, and you can really see the teamwork and professionalism.

The food was awesome. We especially loved the Brussels sprouts, which are new on the menu and absolutely delicious. Terrence also cooked me a steak that was probably one of the best I’ve ever had. You really can’t go wrong at Montecatini’s. It’s simply the best.
I'm such a great time.We'll definitely be going again. So if you go, parking is an issue, but well with it.
