top_reviews.content:
If you’re looking for real, authentic pizza in San Francisco, this is it.

Gialina is not a touristy spot. It’s a true local favorite tucked away in Glen Park, and honestly, that’s what makes it special. The vibe is cozy, casual, and very neighborhood-driven.

The pizza is wood-fired and perfectly executed. The crust has that ideal balance — crispy on the outside, chewy inside. The Margherita was simple but incredibly flavorful, and you can tell they use high-quality ingredients. I also tried the Soppressata, which had a nice spicy kick and was just as impressive.

Service was friendly and relaxed, not overly formal but welcoming. It feels like a place locals come back to again and again.

Prices are reasonable by San Francisco standards, especially considering the quality.

⚠️ Be prepared for a wait during peak hours, and parking in the area isn’t the easiest.

Overall, one of the best local pizza spots in San Francisco. Definitely worth going out of your way for.

It's been years since I last tried Gialina and I'm so happy that it's still around, still cooking, still having the pizza oven red hot and delivers simple but consistent quality food.  We had only three dishes, a Caesar salad, a cucumber salad and a pie and of course a glass of wine.  I personally think that Gialina makes one of the best pizza doughs in SF. All in all a fun dinner experience.

I also with the server mentioned the drink menu and the things they different from standard.

We also ordered the Wagyu Loco Moco. The smash burger preparation was perfect. Egg was standard sunny side up done easy. The garlic fried rice was acceptable for a Filipino. The salad had some wilted sprouts.

But my meal was ruined by their “breaky sauce” I was excited because I knew it would be different but it just didn’t work for me. It was an overpowering vinaigrette that would have worked well with a choooed salad with a protein. But felt totally off with patties, rice and eggs. As a Filipino I would have rather just had a separate dish of vinegar to add that as I wanted but intend my patties were drowned in a sauce that did not work for me.

For Neltunes management. For me loose hair is a prep and hair net issue. That shouldn’t happen one let alone 3x in the same dish?!?! For your servers please have them explain the two menus and what is different from standards like Loco Moco.

If those issues are fixed next time I go back I’ll score the food at 4 stars which y’all should deserve for a local breakfast joint.

If he had checked in on us earlier to tell us why it was taking a while, we could have had the opportunity to decide if we still wanted them or not. At that point we decided that we didn't want them so I went up to him to let him know we didn't need them anymore and he barely acknowledged me. Within the next minute he dropped off the payment machine. We still had a lot of food on our plate and the way he set it was rather rude. Service is polite, prompt on requests (iced water, hot sauce, check) but hard to flag down when the restaurant is full. when we sat down for dinner, there were no menu on the tables. it was being contributed to other tables that was reserved. I had to go up to the cashier lady to ask for the menu which she brought to us. they mostly have larger tables. We were a party of 5 so we sat at the most inner left corner of restaurant which made the duration of the meal feeling very stuffy and hot.

for the dim sum, the pork liver was probably the best dish. pork liver was soft. the beef rice roll, the skin roll is a little too thick. beef ball was very soft and mild tasting. Fried pumpkin with salted egg was okay, I didn’t like the batter and not much salted egg taste but the pumpkin is soft. chicken feet was sweet. the mixed beef organ is another okay dish, not tender enough for elderly with no teeth. the fried pork dumpling didn’t have much filling. my dad did enjoy the black sesame dumpling and the pork dumpling ( I didn’t try). no condiments on the table for both dim sum and dinner so I asked for hot sauce which they promptly brought to me.

dinner, overall the dishes very sweet or too salty. crab meats with fish maw soup had barely any crab meat, soup tasted only of salt so not flavorful. the best dish is the fried squab, tender and very tasty. beef cube with mushrooms, too salty. steamed chicken with ginger green onion sauce was tender and tasty but a little over salted. big pea sprout was okay, a little tough but maybe the sprout is out of season. Combination seafood clay pot with overly salty and had a sweet taste too, walnut shrimp didn’t have much mayo and too sweet but the shrimp was cooked just right. giant clam was tender but a little bland. they gave us free dessert, green bean soup (I didn’t eat it) but my family said not too sweet which is how Asian like their dessert.

there is an automatic 18% tip added for a party of 6 but since we only a party of 5, tip was self added by us. they came to change our plate mid meal but only to two of the plates on our table.

metered and residential parking. Residential parking was easier for me. the place is fairly big but the tables arrangements is a little tight. it was noisy and there was a guy next to our table who was the loudest in the whole restaurant.,he was very obnoxious and made it unpleasant to have to hear him throughout our meal (our party and his arrived at the same time).

Everything was delicious, but getting at least one seafood dish is a must. Their salted fish and chicken fried rice is my favorite so far in SF.

The portions are generous and the staff is friendly.

top_reviews.content:
After a few weeks of travelling across the US, it was an absolute pleasure to find a place that feels like home.

We ordered pelmeni, vareniki, three bowls of borscht (yes, three!), solyanka, golubtsy, a litre of mors, and everything was absolutely delicious.

The portions were generous, the atmosphere was warm and welcoming, and every dish tasted just like it should. It’s not easy to impress people who grew up with this cuisine, but Red Tavern certainly did.

If you’re in San Francisco and craving authentic Eastern European comfort food, this place is a must-visit.

Thank you for a wonderful evening — we left happy, full, and feeling a little less far from home.

On the list of cuisines I know very little about, eastern European is one in trying to learn more. Found this little gem while looking on maps and decided to check it out.

I went in hungry and got a Ukrainian draft beer, an order of cucumber salad, an order of pelmini to start. Had the beef stroganoff for my main and the Napoleon for dessert. Everything was delicious!!

Can't wait to go again and try their other entrees and starters.

Brazinka Kamayanka the ex 1 armed Bear Wrestler for the Ringling Brothers Barnum & Bailey Circus called me and wanted me to come into the city for dinner at his favorite restaurant, the Red Tavern!  Well, it turns out he lives just feet away, so he gets everything to-go so he can watch America TV while he eats!  Tonight he got the Schnitzel dinner, and it was amazing!
5 ☆☆☆☆☆'s and worthy of a cross-town trek!

It’s one thing when a restaurant has a few weak dishes. But when almost every plate is disappointing, that really says something.

We ordered about half the menu. The best thing we had were cucumbers with sour cream, which is probably the hardest dish to mess up.

The final straw was the chicken shashlik. It wasn’t even close to real shashlik. And the buckwheat on the side was dry, no butter, no flavor, just bland and lifeless.

Service was average at best, with that classic old school “unhappy to be here” attitude.

I honestly don’t understand how this place still has a 4+ rating. Maybe it’s surviving on past reputation. As of 2026, this is a solid 2 stars at most.

Next day we went to Uzbek place near by, 10 times better food, service and price

I went to Red Tavern last year while I was attending GDC. The food is phenomenal, the atmosphere is pleasant, and the service is great.

I ordered the blintzes which have beef inside, the potato zrazy, and shared the pelmeni and Russian syrniki with others.

name: Mount Everest Restaurant
address: 2598 Telegraph Ave, Berkeley, CA 94704, United States

google.name: Mount Everest Restaurant

top_reviews.content:
This is genuinely the BEST restaurant in all of Berkeley, and I do not say that lightly. I’ve eaten at a lot of places around here, and nothing compares to this spot. Every single time I walk in, I’m greeted by the sweetest and kindest workers I’ve ever met in Berkeley. They are always so welcoming, warm, and genuinely happy to see you, which already makes the experience feel special before you even start eating.

Now the food is absolutely incredible. The chicken tikka masala is honestly one of the best dishes I’ve had anywhere. The sauce is rich, creamy, and packed with flavor, and the chicken is always perfectly cooked and tender. It’s the kind of dish where you keep saying “just one more bite” and suddenly the whole bowl is gone. The garlic naan is also amazing, soft, warm, buttery, and perfectly garlicky. It’s literally the perfect thing to scoop up the tikka masala with. I could honestly eat the naan alone and still be happy.

And you cannot leave without getting the mango lassi. It’s so refreshing and smooth, and it balances the spices from the food perfectly. It’s sweet, creamy, and honestly one of the best mango lassis I’ve ever had.

Another thing that makes this place stand out is the price and generosity. Berkeley can be pretty expensive when it comes to food, but this restaurant somehow manages to serve amazing quality food at a really good price. On top of that, they are incredibly generous, they almost always give us extra food or something for free, which is honestly so kind and makes the experience feel even more special. It feels like they truly care about their customers and want everyone to leave happy.

What I love most is that this place feels genuine and welcoming, not just another restaurant trying to rush people in and out. The workers are so friendly and kind, and the atmosphere is always warm. You can tell they take pride in their food and care about the people who come in.

If you’re anywhere near Berkeley and want amazing Nepalese food, this is the place you have to go. The chicken tikka masala, garlic naan, and mango lassi combination is absolutely unbeatable. Great food, incredible people, generous portions, and such a great experience every time. You can NOT beat the price or quality anywhere.

I honestly recommend this place to everyone I know. 10/10 — the best restaurant in Berkeley.
Excellent!!! The BEST Indian Food in Berkeley! Must try! Chicken Tikka Masala my favvvv! Lunch specials great deal too! Mango Lassi, lemonades, chai OMG SOOO GOOD!

The food is always 10/10!! This is the best Indian food in Berkeley & I guarantee you will LOVE whatever you get. Everything is so fresh & tastes amazing. The staff here is AMAZING. They are all so kind & make the experience amazing. My favorite is the butter chicken I highly recommend!!! You need to try this place for lunch they have an amazing $11 lunch special. One of my favorite spots in berkeley!
The service was amazing! It felt so homey and the food came out so fast. The kadai chicken and momos are to die for!!!

A gem hidden in plain sight !! This place has been around since I was in high
school (over a decade) and although it seems it may be receiving less foot traffic during the summer months, this is not a restaurant to miss!
I got the lunch set with lamb curry. The meat is tender, the spice perfect, the curry flavorful and delicious. It also came with a generous portion of naan and rice, plus chana on the side and a nice salad.
The rose lassi is also a refreshing choice, not too sweet :)

Service was so wonderful, warm and helpful staff. 100/10!
For under $20 it’s a great deal for lunch and a great place to visit.
Come check it out!

We hosted a team dinner for 12 at The Tailor’s Son, and it was such a fantastic experience from start to finish!
Leo was an amazing host his warm welcome and top-tier customer service really set the tone for the evening. He went above and beyond to accommodate our group on very short notice, which we truly appreciated. Our server was just as incredible super attentive, efficient, and always on top of making sure food and drinks came out quickly and smoothly.
We started off with a great variety of appetizers, including the Carpaccio di Tonno, Prosciutto di Parma, Mondeghili, House Focaccia, Little Gem alla Romana, and Insalata di Fragola everyone loved them all! My personal favorite was the gnocco fritto with gorgonzola dolcelatte absolutely delicious and a must-try.
For my main, I had the Bucatini all’Aragosta. The flavors were amazing and it tasted great, though I do wish there had been a bit more lobster for the price. That said, it didn’t take away from the overall experience.
Between the outstanding service and the delicious food, this is definitely a spot I’d come back to. Thank you to the whole team for making our dinner so memorable!

The Tailor’s Son is such a gem! Super yummy Italian food with the best vibes—perfect for a date night or even a casual night out with the girls.

The service was amazing and everything came out so fast. The meatballs were so good, and the tagliatelle bolognese was absolutely incredible—definitely ordering that again.

10/10 would recommend if you’re looking for a cute spot with great food and a fun atmosphere!

Ordered three dishes, service was a bit slow, the dishes didn't come out all together and had to wait for two of them. The buccatini pasta was really good. Lemon ricotta pancakes were dry and had no lemon or ricotta flavor. The vegetable scramble was ordinary, decent but nothing remarkable. It is a bit on the pricey side. Is better as a dinner pasta kinda place than a brunch place.

Be were lucky to get a table as a company of 5 on a Saturday early evening. The atmosphere was amazing- the place is full of light and feels very inviting. Most of the dishes we ordered were remarkably good (the bolognese, the zucca risotto, and the tiramisu were our favorites). The waiter, though professional, gave us a bit of an attitude. He did suggest that we order an extra main dish so that there is enough for everyone in a family style meal, however could let us know that appetizers like burrata and focaccia were served for four people and it was awkward to split between 5 diners (we could have ordered doubles of some of those). Otherwise it was a phenomenal meal.

Only did happy hour today ~ Amazing drink and small dishes - totally blown away by how small things can taste so good. The calamari is the best I had for a very long time.
The chocolate pudding also crazily good - not too sweet and with the special aroma of chocolate.
Will come back for dinner soon.

Quaint, unassuming Korean BBQ spot and offer all the highlights of Korean fare. They serve good portions of good quality bulgogi (not too fatty and not drenched in sauce). They also had special combos with bulgogi and spicy tofu soup served with banchan. Medium spiciness was not very spicy so it complemented the flavors rather than overpowering them. They offer Kloud and Terra beers along with soju. The food comes out very quickly!

Came in for a late lunch around 2pm and it was still pretty busy, which is always a good sign. the lady at the front was super sweet and helped us figure out the menu since it was our first time trying korean bbq. the meat was so tender and flavorful, especially the marinated beef, I almost ordered a second plate. the banchan was good but I originaly thought they brought out the wrong one, it was fine though, just a bit confusing. only thing I would change is the portion sizes on the combo are a bit small for the price, left still kinda hungry. overall a solid spot and I'll definitely be back to try more stuff id say it's worth a stop if you're in Artois.

top_reviews.content: I never knew this place existed but then again I never go out to Oakland . I went this day because I was celebrating my cousins birthday . We met at the lumpia company to watch the 49ers game and wait till the salsa gig started . I was impressed by the atmosphere and the smell of the delicious food . The Lumpia Company is a two-year old spot located in the Brooklyn Basin waterfront development. It’s a great addition to the area and a fun concept built around different varieties of lumpia.

When I visited at lunchtime, however, the place was completely deserted. I actually had to walk into the kitchen area to find someone to take my order, and the guy seemed a little surprised / annoyed to have a customer.

With lumpia the focus here, there’s an impressive lineup of flavors including two types of chicken, turkey, shrimp & pork, and even a bacon cheeseburger version. My order came out hot and crunchy, with flavorful filling and excellent dipping sauces. The sweet chili sauce was great, and their house “moo moo sauce” (made with mayo, ketchup, relish, and banana!) was especially tasty.

Even though there are places to sit, my order was handed to me in a takeout bag, which made it feel like they don’t really expect people to eat there during the day.

The food itself was very good, and the attached arcade adds a fun element to the space (though the game sounds can get pretty loud). My guess is that this place is probably much more lively during happy hour or dinner.

I was working in Oakland and decided to check this place out—and I’m so glad I did. I originally came in for lumpia, but the item I ended up ordering wasn’t even on the menu anymore. The manager was incredibly helpful, made great recommendations, and made sure I still got something amazing.

What I had was absolutely bomb—full of flavor and perfectly put together. It was so good, I came back on my day off just to get it again… and somehow it was even better the second time.

They definitely need to bring this item to the menu! Highly recommend.

Dinner at Miller & Lux with coworkers was an outstanding experience from start to finish. We started with several appetizers including the Beets & Goat Cheese Salad, Beef Noodle Soup, Wagyu Meatballs with Mezze Rigatoni, and the Poached Shrimp Cocktail with Fresno chili cocktail sauce — every dish was flavorful, fresh, and generously portioned.

For the main courses, we shared the Roasted Duroc Pork Tomahawk, which was incredibly tender and packed with flavor, the French Dover Sole Meunière finished tableside, and the Pan-Seared Hokkaido Scallops with pomme purée, peas, and petite carrots. We also ordered sides of lobster pesto risotto, asparagus, and Yukon Gold purée potatoes, all of which were delicious and perfect for sharing.

To finish the evening, we enjoyed espresso, cappuccino, a huge banana split, and the lemon blueberry tart — the perfect ending to a fantastic meal.

The service was excellent, attentive, and very detailed in explaining each dish. Overall, a great dining experience with amazing food, generous portions, and top-notch hospitality. We’ll definitely be back.

We had dinner here to celebrate my husband’s birthday. The service is impeccable. The food was great! Best Cesar salad I have EVER had especially if you like anchovies (optional). They make it at your table! My daughter enjoyed the fluffy butter and bread as well as the heap of black truffle Parmesan fries. We had the NY steak, ribeye, potato puree, truffle mac n cheese, and a choice of sauce on the side for the steaks. The dessert menu was tempting; however we were so stuffed!

Dined at Miller & Lux during our stay in San Francisco. Everything was absolutely incredible. The atmosphere and music were nice. Service was excellent and the food was delicious! We ordered steaks and the sides are very good portions easily for 2-3 people. We ordered  lobster risotto which I am not a fan of risotto but now I am, or at least for theirs! The table side Cesar was refreshing and the warm rolls they bring to each person at the table is nice and fluffy. They had quite a few deserts to choose from and I only wish I had the room to try something bigger. We ordered a small desert but the people next to us order a chocolate sundae which I will definitely have to try next time.

We had a reservation for 8:00PM MAY 16 2026 Saturday under the name Jim. We arrived around 07:55PM. They sat us at the bar downstairs saying our table was not ready. We had some drinks and we got seated at 08:30PM. This is quite unprofessional because most high-end fine dining restaurants usually are on time. But we said okay anyway. We started with some bread called “puff” and some butter. It was the best croissant like bread “puff” we ever had. It was crisp, hot and unimaginably delicious. Then, we ordered seafood tower featuring oysters, lobster and crab(can’t remember specifically). Anyway, seafood tower was good. But it didn’t have proper sauces. There was no horseradish which was understandable, we asked for it 3 times and finally there was a manageress. I had to talk a little harsh to her because asking for horseradish 3 times at a high-end place like this one is extremely unprofessional. We also waited for our 52 oz wagyu tomahawk for 2 almost hours. They brought it at around 10:20pm. But it was delicious and perfectly seasoned. We also had ceasar salad. That was really good. Some people working had language issues. They didn’t know English well so they couldn’t address some of our questions properly, which is odd for high-end restaurant like Miller & Lux. Also, We ordered 2 Bottles of different wines for $395 each. I also called wine guy to explain the wine for the second time, but he didn’t come to our table in around 20-30 minutes. I think this is normal for them to provide this kind of service because if it was just only that day they were making mistakes, they would’ve at least given us some dessert to make up for their poor service as a gesture. But no, they didn’t even try to fix the poor service. Total, we spent $2400($400 gratuity). If anyone is spending that much, i think it is only fair to expect top-notch service. Overall, the food was excellent. Ambiance was good. But, for us, service killed it all, so I am giving them 1 star. Maybe, Tyler Florence should focus on service there instead of trying to open up more spots. I had so high expectations since it was our first time. I am definitely not recommending anyone to go and definitely not coming back myself.

Fantastic food and service. They were so accommodating to my group being late (deepest apologies!). Sylvie is a fantastic, knowledgeable server and a class act! Food is top notch. Wine selection is out of this world. Wine assistant was so knowledgeable and helpful in pairings. 10/10 experience I so happened to pop in on for my best friend’s birthday! The tomahawk was to die for! In the future when I return I will be sure to do the surf and turf! The Alaskan oysters have my heart and the dessert menu is to die for! They deserve so much all the praise!

"The horseradish sauce we added gave each bite a nice cream and spicy kick."

name: Rice Roll Express
address: 1131 Stockton St, San Francisco, CA 94133, United States

google.name: Rice Roll Express

top_reviews.content: This place is as authentic as you can get. It’s a gem cause not many places serve rice rolls “肠粉”. This place is no frills - you order at the counter and pick it up there yourself. The food is served on disposable plates. There’s a wide variety of sauces provided for you to add yourself to your food. The special soya sauce is the best and most original way of eating it. I had the rice roll express special - it was alright. The wantons were decent but the soup was lukewarm and barely had any taste in it. The soy milk was freshly made in house. More effort could be invested in keeping the tables clean. Overall - this place is a gem if you’re looking for a real Chinese experience without breaking the bank.

Ordered to go #1 Rice Roll Special with cilantro and T5 Signature Shrimp and Roe Wonton in Chili Oil. The #1 Rice Roll Special includes a choice of one vegetable wrapped inside, the options are bean sprouts, lettuce, corn, scallion, or cilantro. The rice roll rice was paper thin and the meat inside was very good, a mix of beef, pork, bbq pork, and egg. It’s very light and easy to pull apart to eat, good with soy sauce. The T5 Signature Shrimp and Roe Wonton in Chili Oil was not too spicy, it’s a light spicy oil base around the wonton that you can dip your wonton in. Despite how red the chili oil looks, it’s not as daunting. The wontons were a nice size, not too small and a good portion, wrapped nicely and very juicy inside, the shrimp pieces are noticeable. Service was very fast, ordering was seamless though cash only and the food was ready soon after. The store inside is very simple and plain with plenty of menus on the walls and a simple setup of chairs and tables.

The food was absolutely delicious.  The shrimp wontons in the soup was very tasty.  The fried shrimp dumplings in chilli oil was my favorite dish and absolutely amazing.  The rice rolls were also very delicious.  It was crowded and tables were not cleaned I am assuming because of how busy.  Other than that I will be returning soon to enjoy the delicious food.

​Definitely a busy hot spot! Despite a long line and a tight dining area, service was efficient and turnover was quick, so finding a seat didn't take long. The flavors in the rice noodle rolls were great and  delicious. It turns out I don't really like the texture of rice noodles, but if you enjoy rice noodle rolls, this place executes them well.

Was there on a Friday around lunchtime, place filled up real quick for a good reason. We came particularly for the shrimp rolls and they were so good. Shrimp was cooked just right and that sweet sauce was a good companion to the warm rice rolls! 10/10 would come here again, maybe earlier though to beat the rush!

name: The Peach
address: 3257 Lakeshore Ave, Oakland, CA 94610, United States

google.name: The Peach

top_reviews.content: We had a fun time doing their bottomless mimosa brunch! I enjoy that they allow you to pour the orange juice into the champagne to control the sweetness factor. Ambiance was lovely on this sunny day and servers were super friendly.

I’m generally not a fan of mandatory gratuity, especially when the service was just ok but not particularly memorable.

As for the food, it was a bit hit or miss for me. The chicken was a little dry and saltier than I prefer. The bread pudding wasn’t quite what I was expecting, as it came across a bit watery and undercooked. On the positive side, the bacon was tasty and one of the better items we tried.

Having visited Lakeshore Cafe when it was in this location, it’s hard not to make comparisons. The overall experience didn’t quite live up to those memories, but it may appeal to others with different tastes. Even the drinks were decent, though they didn’t particularly stand out.

Overall, the experience was okay, but there are a few areas that could be improved.

My friend and I happened upon this spot one night after waiting for seating at a nearby restaurant. WELL we ended up never going to the other restaurant as The Peach’s new dinner menu gave us everything we needed! Beautiful ambiance. Cute soju-based cocktails. And a menu that was fun, creative, and a delicious fusion of Southeast Asian cuisine. Would def come back for dinner! And I would run a marathon barefoot if it meant another bite of their HONEY MISO GLAZED CORNBREAD! That’s a must-eat 🤤😩

On Sunday, July 5, 2026, I ate at The Peach for brunch.

Let me start off by saying this place is the shit and really really really good! The food was sensational! Here's what we ordered. The double stack Golden Pancakes with a side of fruit compote, the Fried Chicken and Waffles and the skillet bread pudding. The Golden Pancakes look similar to a viral restaurant in New York that has a 2 to 3 hour wait time just to get seated. I've been seeing these Golden Pancakes go viral on social media but the only restaurant that seems to have them and serve them is located in New York which is too far for me to travel to just for some pancakes 🥞. I'm so glad The Peach in Oakland serves these type of pancakes. The Golden Pancakes at The Peach are hands down the best pancakes I've ever eaten in my life! The texture of the pancakes are a hybrid mix between soft corn bread, regular pancakes and airy cake! It's the best of both or should I say all worlds! The pancakes are pretty big and on the bottom of the plate is a honey reduction type of sauce/syrup. You don't even need maple syrup because the honey infused reduction sauce has the perfect amount of natural sweetness. These pancakes are a must order when you come here. The fruit compote was really good. I drenched my pancakes in it. It almost tasted like peaches and nectarines mixed together. It was delicious on top of the pancakes! The fried chicken and waffles were good. The boneless chicken tenderloins were cooked perfectly. I liked how they used tenderloins compared to most restaurants who serve a chicken leg, thigh or bone in breast. Chicken tenderloins are easier to eat and you don't have to worry about biting into a bone. The batter held up very well on the chicken tenderloins and it was the perfect bite ratio when it came to chicken plus the waffle. I like the taste of the syrup. It was a spicy syrup but it didn't have that much heat which I liked. The skillet bread pudding was great. The bread pudding was cooked perfectly. It was nice and soft with the perfect amount of sweetness from the fresh fruits and whipped cream on top.

The vibe and atmosphere at The Peach is spot on. I liked the overall set up of the restaurant. The design and layout of the restaurant is nice. The restaurant is spacious and the colors inside really make everything inside pop. There's tons of natural lighting which I like. They even have outdoor seating available towards the back of the restaurant and upstairs they have private dining for special occasions. It's the perfect location for a restaurant and easy to find. It's located directly across from the Lakeshore Shopping Center. Parking isn't the best but that's how it is in Oakland and nowadays in the Bay Area in general.

Service was great. We didn't have to wait at all. We were seated immediately. Our waitress Kennedy was very nice. All of the staff members at The Peach were nice and professional. The bathrooms were clean which is a huge plus.

I highly recommend The Peach in Oakland to everyone who is looking for some great food and overall a fantastic brunch.

I can't wait to come back to eat their double stack of Golden Pancakes and give their dinner service a try! I'm sure their dinner items are 🔥 as well!

Best brunch spot in Oakland thus far!!!

Atmosphere is so incredibly loud, don’t expect to be able to hold conversations here. Honestly the food was incredibly over priced and quite bland. The hash browns were basically from Trader Joe’s across the street, tasted like there was a freezer burn taste.
There is a mandatory 18% gratuity for every check, regardless of party size. There were many times we had to bother the server for the items we ordered but they forgot or were too preoccupied to serve us. The service was Definitely not worth the tip, it felt like they didn’t care about actually serving. And then the server asked once we were paying with card for us to give more tip. The person paying fell victim to the peer pressure and tipped more. I do not recommend this place. The menu is very limited and the host (Jay) was quite rude in the beginning when we were trying to check if our table was ready.
Half the table left the food on our plate and didn’t even take it home because it was not good.
The egg omelette was very bland and the shrimp was rubbery and overcooked. The cheesy grits was the only thing remotely enjoyable.
Don’t come here unless you want to throw away your money for bland food.

top_reviews.content: I have been here a couple of times, I usually stop by when I am in need of a quick bite or when I am in the area where I am craving for some sushi. Upon arrival, there could be a wait, but you can join their waitlist and usually you will be called pretty quick even when they are busy. You can choose to have a table seating or be seated at the counter which faces directly to their conveyor. Your drinks and side dishes will be served to you through a robot that moves throughout the restaurant and comes directly to your table. Ordering is very simple, you can pick what you like off the conveyor or order something special or any particular dish you do not see on their conveyor through their tablet. If you do order something off their tablet you will hear a train like sound when the dish arrives on the shelf level. All the plates are disposed through a shoot that is located on the table. You can also opt in for their prize if you like. For the first 15 plates you place through the shoot you will receive a prize that comes randomly in a Easter egg, and for 25 plates placed in the shoot you will receive a second gift. Their menu consists of drinks, nigiri, special rolls, hand rolls, udon, ramen, hot appetizers, cold dishes, desserts and much more to choose from. Everything here is made to order which is always a plus for me since it is quality over quantity and I never mind the wait since I am a very patient person. The place is very laid back and a great place to hangout with some close ones or friends. The staffs here are very welcoming, well trained, professional and understanding where I have never encountered an issue and I always leave satisfied. For the payment you can pay at the screen which only takes cards or have a staff bring you the bill which they accept both cash and cards. I highly recommend this place to all sushi enthusiasts, to anyone in need of a quick bite just like me, to anyone willing to try something new or if you just so happen to be in the area to check them out. I definitely will be back to tryout the other delicious options they have to offer.

Is a great place for a night out in Stonestown: date night, girls hang out, tired of cooking.  But we eat more than we should-darn those revolving conveyor belts bringing the enticing plates.
Since each plate has about 3 pieces of
Nigiri sushi, is best to come with a party of 3 or 4 to try a variety.  We all found the scallops with Japanese mayo to be the beat of the options: rich and creamy scallop texture with a light and savory umami rice finish.  We’ve thought all the choices with green onion toppings to mask the underlying flavor of the protein.
Also, skip the udon and ramen soup bowls-these were too salty and at close to $13 we would had rather enjoyed 3
Plates of the conveyor belt sushi.
Service was great with a cheerful robot and staff
After consuming 15 plates, you would get a keychain.  After the 25th plate,
You would get another key chain.
But the kids loved the ambience and enjoyed the food.  If we could only not eat so much.

Good variety, love the ability to order the roll I want without having to wait and see if the dish has been replenished. Staff is always friendly and attentive. I do suggest downloading their app and scheduling a reservation, especially Friday through Sunday's.

Currently each sushi roll dish is about $4.99

I reserved a spot for 7:10pm, with the purpose of getting the limited time Kirby blanket. Childish, sure, but it's the reason my girlfriend and I wanted to come.

Instead what happened is that they let two huge parties go ahead of us, and we were seated 35-40 mins late. You can probably guess the next part, but they ran out of said blankets by the time we were seated.

Since it was almost closing time there were no more new sushi plates being made. All empty plates. So the dining experience was not good either. Bad, delayed service and not even a good meal. Maybe next time. Or maybe not. There's better conveyer belt sushi places.

The manager also came out to speak to us. I thought he was going to try to resolve the issue in someway, but all he did was deflect and try to pass the blame onto the second manager on shift. The manager said, and I'm paraphrasing since english is not his primary language, "I was on break 20 minutes ago, when I got back I saw there were no sushi on the conveyer belt, I'm trying to get more made. There's another manager on shift." In other words, trying to say it's not his fault. Was that supposed to make us feel better? That the buck keeps getting passed onto another person? Utter incompetence.

Baited with a cross promotion that ran out due to them delaying our reservation and they couldn't even feed us properly at the very least. Oh, and when we tried to pay and leave to have an actual meal elsewhere, their checkout system was bugging out and the server couldn't figure out why. He was actually asking what (few) dishes we had to "troubleshoot" the issue with us. That's not our job. Are we supposed to memorize the plates we chose? It took us around another 10 mins to get out of there because of their incompetence.

The biggest failure is the fact that we left hungry because there was basically no conveyer belt sushi left in a conveyer belt sushi restaurant. We ate dinner at another location instead.

I've been to the Kura in Austin, Texas and this one is similar but with worse service and food. My son and I had to wait 20 minutes to be seated inside, so we walked around until our number was called. We were seated by the waitress and started eating, but we had to flag a waiter down to get our water and wasabi. There was a poster ad for a special ramen, which I had planned to order, but I did not see it on the menu. once we got inside the restaurant. We tried the Japanese fish  & chips which were pretty good, but I really wanted the tempura shrimp, which were overpriced at close to $8. All in all we paid $50, for ok food, with subpar service. A little disappointing.

top_reviews.content:
Roger and Winnie well exceeded our expectations! This was by far the best omakase experience we’ve ever had! If you’re expecting something trendy and quick, please do not come here. This place has so much character and is a family run restaurant with the one and only Roger as the sushi chef. His wife Winnie and daughter support the front of the house.

Expect extremely fresh pieces of fish and large portions!! This is also not a set omakase menu! You tell him when you’re tapped out! He will take you on a journey of educating you about pairings of sake and beers and crazy types of fish that you’ve never tried. The omakase is not set because it’s all based on what fresh fish he can get his hands on!

Please come support him and his family. They’re lovely people!!! We snagged the 8pm reservation and left well after closing and we were the last group there. He’s 68 years old guys. He’s retiring next February so you should experience this level of omakase just once in your life if you’re a sushi lover!

Great hole in the wall sushi spot. Prices are pretty reasonable ($60-70pp when ordering à la carte). Our favorites were the chicken karage and the nine piece Nigiri. Service is great, very attentive and walked us through each dish.

Don’t think they take reservations, but there was space on Friday night

This was hands down the best omakase experience I’ve ever had. Chef Ryan coursed it out and this is the first time leaving omakase that I can say IM FULL. Every single piece of fish was extremely fresh and unique and chef Ryan taught me how to eat it like a pro. The flavors are unreal and it truly was an experience not just an amazing meal. Highly recommend checking this place out. Everyone inside the restaurant was extremely polite and overall it was such a fun experience!!

Awesome experience at the sushi bar with Roger and the rest of the staff. My water was always filled with a warm smile and roger made me a delicious meal. He is so passionate about what he does and I highly recommend coming to this spot. 23 years and running! Rare to find a place in SF open for so long, but there's good reason for this here.

I had heard good things about this place, so I was excited to try it.

We ordered three appetizers, eight pieces of nigiri, and the chicken udon.

We arrived at 5:30 p.m. They open at 5 p.m., and we were the first customers there. The place is definitely more of a hole-in-the-wall and appears to be family-run. I have nothing against hole-in-the-wall restaurants, but the restaurant was empty and extremely quiet. There was no music playing, so it was complete silence until another couple came in. Even then, I’m not a fan of restaurants that don’t play some kind of background music—the silence made the place feel even more lifeless.

Onto the food:
The grilled sea bass was good.
The seaweed cucumber salad was so-so. The mackerel that came with it tasted fishy, which could have been due to it being cured, but I just wasn’t a fan.
We also ordered the fried tofu, but it didn’t come out until near the end of our meal. I’m not sure why it took so long, especially since the kitchen wasn’t busy.

I enjoyed the scallops and kani (crab). They were sweet, and the scallops had a good texture. The hamachi was my second favorite. Unfortunately, the madai and salmon didn’t taste fresh. The toro was probably the worst piece of toro I’ve ever had—it was extremely fishy in both taste and smell. I’ve never had toro like that before. The unagi also had a slight sour taste.

The stir-fried chicken udon was good.

I was also confused by the order in which the food came out—it felt very disorganized. To make matters worse, my boyfriend has been experiencing stomach issues since last night’s dinner and is still recovering.

Overall, the cooked dishes were pretty good and decent. However, when it comes to the raw items, it may be safer to order more commonly requested dishes, as they’re more likely to be made with fresher fish.

top_reviews.content:
We decided to try this place because we had read a lot of good reviews about the restaurant. Personally, I think it was just okay.

The tables were pretty dirty. We had to sit at one of the tables that looked a little cleaner and clean it ourselves. The table next to us was never cleaned the entire time we were there either.

We ordered a michelada, which came with a straw, and when drinking it you could feel all the salt sitting at the bottom. The area where you get the sauces, lime, chile, and other sides was also really dirty.

We waited around 45 minutes for our food, which felt like a pretty long time. We got the chilaquiles and they were good. The patio area is actually really nice, but I definitely feel like they could work more on the service and especially the cleanliness of the place.

I love the free watermelon and melon slices!!! It really tops the whole amazing experience together, along with the delicious food and handmade tortillas! The horchata was made by them and I have to praise them for it. Most restaurants don’t do that. Whoever was at the front desk at around 5 pm was really patient when taking our orders. Edit: the melons are half there because I took this after I had already ate them. Also this restaurant is dog friendly!

Update 7/25/2025 Delivery: Had to try the tacos and burrito this time after a long work week. This time it was the Regular Burrito w/ Carne Asada, Tacos - Carne Asada and Pollo. Grilled just right. Not too dry or juicy. Ummm I'm weeping w/ pure joy.

7/2025 Dine-In:
Super delicious breakfast. Breakfast burrito with potatoes, eggs, cheese was fantastic. Friend had the chilaquiles. Everything was hot, fresh, reasonably priced. Extra points for the salsa bar with fruit. Can’t wait to return.
ps. I saw a super cool patio w/outside  bar

First time here. Taco Tuesday prices 2.75 a taco. They have a salsa bar and fruit plus chips.
Patio area super cool on a hot day.

We had a wonderful meal here! I got carne asada which was my favorite and queso birria which was good as well. My dad loved the shrimp tacos. The back patio is the perfect place to watch the World Cup! Absolutely keeping this place on my list of favorites! And they were exceedingly accommodating, my dad is allergic to cilantro and they accommodated him completely!

top_reviews.content:
Pearl Bay has officially reopened as of 4/23/2026 with a new menu and updated hours (9 a.m.–3 p.m. and 5 p.m.–9:30 p.m.). We arrived a little after 9 a.m. on Saturday morning, and by 10 a.m. the restaurant was completely full, with people lining up outside. To avoid the wait, it’s best to arrive before 10 a.m.
We stopped by over the weekend and were impressed! The dim sum came out hot and delicious, and the staff were experienced, efficient, and kept everything well organized. Definitely worth checking out!
The food and services are great, and the location is fantastic. I wish the restaurant was a bit larger, as it was quite crowded.

Still pretty good after the remodel. Great service including changing out our  plates twice during dim sum which I did not expect. They constantly came over and took away plates. The items I thought very average include ham sui gok too much dough and not enough filling. Shrimp dumplings and Xiao mai and chang fun were ok. The chau siu puffs, malay sponge cake, and beef organs and  offal were all excellent.

Food was good and everyone was nice except the cashier girl. The cashier girl was extremely rude and unprofessional. I took a minute to find my credit card, which was still on their counter table, hidden under the black tray after I signed the bill and tip. Then, she raised her voice at me and said “YOUR CARD IS NOT HERE. YOU ALREADY TOOK IT EARLIER.” She also yelled and raised her voice at my friend when my friend was checking if our table was ready. Unfortunately, I do not wish to come back here again.

Recently remodeled but the space between tables appear to be less than it used to be, even with the extra space it took from neighbor store. I guess that means more table and higher profit for the owner, less space for customer. Price and quality of food stay pretty much the same.

top_reviews.content: Service was good and I like that there’s a large variety to choose from and drinks are included from the fridge however the sauce station was lacking in good options tons of liquid options but would’ve preferred a better selection like other places I have been too. Also meat was too thick compared to other places as well. As for the soup base that was our biggest issue we got house spicy and spicy curry both were very bland which was such a huge disappointment and affected the over all taste and experience.

Perfect for a large group. We were a group of 10 and made a reservation for 5:45 on a Thursday night.

We had three bowls of soup. One spicy, one mild, and one half and half. We had thought the half and half was a mid point in spiciness but it was actually a pot with half spicy and half mild broth. Next time we’d just order three of the half n half.

It was easiest for one person to do all of the ordering and we got a spread of meats, noodles, and veggies. We were happy with how quickly everything came out and the broth was quickly hot enough to start cooking. Make sure you order the sesame balls!

A member of our group was in white and the staff brought out an apron to help them from staining their shirt. We all laughed when he told us his children don’t spill on themselves!

The self serve drink fridge, variety of sauces, and self serve ice cream were all great.

All you can eat and all you can drink for $45 each. We all left super full. One thing to note is they have moved locations so the photos in the red room are of the old space. Make sure you navigate to the new location!

The place might be slightly dated however, the service is awesome, the food is great, drink all you want such as sake /beer etc.    My family is from Hong Kong and all servers spoke Cantonese/English and I’m pretty sure they spoke mandarin too.  I went to little sheep first and they forgot to mentioned they only have all you can eat on Tuesday only.  Grand Hot pot lounge might is all you can eat everyday. Might not be fancy, but you’re not being charged for the extra fanciness, service was awesome, down to earth, no wait, and and they even have karaoke rooms!!!  $28 bucks a person.   A+++

Showed up for the lunch all you can eat hot pot experience and left stuffed and appeased. Plenty of seating, the service is quick and there is also a set of serving areas to get other items not offered on the menu. 18.99 for lunch all you can eat Hot Pot that opens at 11am. Loved coming here. Food was so good, the atmosphere was cozy and the drinks were fun.
I would honestly say this place beats out some of the Michelin star restaurants we've been to around the bay. Quality of food and taste were top tier.

The gnocchi with mushrooms was also very memorable. Let’s be real. I pretty much liked everything I ate.

Drinks I tried something that was supposed to remind you of nacho cheese. It was interesting for sure. Probably not the drink I would go for, but you do actually get reminders of sitting at a ballpark eating nacho cheese. Try it if you’re feeling adventurous.

The Tuna Tartare was my favorite item of the night. It had so much flavor within the first bite.

The Maude Burger was really good.

The Short Rib and Rib plate was ridiculously good. Both meats were cooked perfectly. The sauce on the ribs is pretty spicy, but if you're not into that, I'd have them put it on the side.

Never a bad meal here. Ever. Service is fantastic, ambience is perfect. Just such a slam dunk place for a wonderful meal. Take your mom! Take your spouse! Take anyone and I challenge you to have a bad time. Can’t wait to go back- a sentiment I feel as soon as I walk out the door after every meal.

top_reviews.content: Honestly the best Japanese Curry spot in the Bay Area. The curry is made with a beef base and has a deep flavor profile. You can add more spiciness you want as well. I highly recommend.
Yummy japanese curry and rice. If you're not too hungry, getting one dish and adding extra protein is perfect.  Inside of the restaurant is simple, not many decorations, can get loud when it's busy.

I got chicken katsu curry with pickles, pumpkin croquettes, and cabbage salad with sesame dressing.

The curry was very good, flavorful and not too spicy. The coating on the katsu had a crunch and the meat was moist. The pickles at a welcome acidity to the rich curry sauce.

The pumpkin croquettes (made with kabocha) had a nice crisp coating and were soft on the inside. I ordered tonkateu sauce with them, and the sauce added sweet and sour notes.

The cabbage slaw was simple, very fresh, and the message dressing was delicious. The slaw was great in between bites of curry, providing crisp freshness.

Recommended.

Came here on a cloudy, cold day in the city in May. It was about 3:00pm, so not many people were in the restaurant. I had the chicken katsu curry and it was delicious. You can add your own spice if you want it spicier. Mine was just right. Service was attentive and friendly, as well. I enjoyed the quiet atmosphere, but we came when it was off-hours. Not sure how busy they get.

I will definitely be back. Their food is delicious and the portions are good for the price.

Absolutely delicious Japanese Curry.  Had the chicken katsu.  Chicken was crispy and did not get soggy, curry was flavorful, rice was well cooked and sticky.  Great service as well.  Bonus points for the $4 Japanese IPAs (all day happy hour).  Will definitely be back!

top_reviews.content:
DragonEats is a no-frills shop with no seating that serves up a tight, focused menu of Vietnamese offerings, with a clear emphasis on banh mis and bún. I know they have salads, rolls and even pho on the menu, but I came specifically for the banh mi and went with the classic roast pork.

The banh mis here are on the pricier side at $11 to $13 depending on which one you order, especially given the location near the Tenderloin and all the other delicious, cheaper options nearby. That said, I did find the flavors to be very good. The roast pork was seasoned and cooked really well, and the sandwich was absolutely bursting with pickled vegetables, jalapeño, cilantro, and pate. Big shoutout to the team for offering extra of literally anything in the sandwich besides the protein for free, which definitely helps justify the higher price. The portion is huge as a result, and you could easily split a half sandwich and a small soup for lunch and be set.

The bread is sturdy, with a nice crust on the outside that does not cut into the roof of your mouth, while the inside is super fluffy and soaks up all the pate and sauce beautifully. I added a small side of broth, which I was expecting to be a simple clear consommé, but I was pleasantly surprised to find it loaded with kale in addition to the shallots, cilantro, and lime, which you can also get extra of at no charge.

Ultimately, it is not the best banh mi I have had, as the bread could be a bit crustier and the pate could use a bit more punch, but overall it was a very satisfying meal at a fair price point for the city.

I stopped at DragonEats for the first time after a couple of colleagues recommended it when I asked for a new lunch spot near our office. I wanted something I could take back to work, so I ordered the Chicken Breast Fresh Bowl.

The bowl came with rice noodles, celery, carrots, cilantro, and several other ingredients. It was fresh, flavorful, and filling without being too heavy—a good choice for a quick workday lunch.

My takeout order was ready in about five or six minutes, making the entire experience fast and hassle-free. Based on this first visit, DragonEats is a convenient option for a fresh, satisfying lunch in Hayes Valley.

We ordered roasted pork and roasted duck sandwiches. They both are very tasty and have signature pastes. The buns are well toasted and just have enough crunchiness. The rolls are also good,  very fresh. Highly recommended.

Very quick and delicious! Got a teriyaki tofu bowl which was YUM. If you are vegetarian make sure to ask for soy sauce as a replacement instead of fish sauce. Highly recommend!  Note: has peanuts in it in case anyone is allergic. But looked like it was just a topping so could ask for it without

Wonderful take out restaurant with a tiny space that has a few high chairs to eat on the premises. Two basic foods done extremely well; ban mi and salad bowls!! We had a 5 spiced chicken salad bowl and the spicy pork ban mi and both were exceptional and tasty. Total cost was $22! So if you want a quick and cheap bite, look no further as this is the place!

This is a 'hidden gem' Thai food option right in the heart of San Francisco.  I had walked by this restaurant several times and finally decided to eat here with a friend and it did not disappoint.  The restaurant does a terrific job of displaying their food on their menu so you know what your food will look like before ordering and it comes out looking just like the picture, at least our food choices did.  We had the fried pork, pad Thai, and Thai fried rice.  Those 3 choices were excellent, and I can't wait to go back to try other items that look tempting.  We also had sake and a beer, so that drove our bill up a bit, but we made it out of there for about $50 per person with tip.

Thai food was amazing - probably one of the best we have had! Service was also amazing. We had egg rolls, chicken pad thai & tom kha soup. So warm, hot, tons of hot sauce options and menu was easy to read as well. Street parking available and super cute and cozy on the inside!

Service was very kind, I was doing laundry nearby so I popped in - I ended up asking for my order to go and they didn't mind that I had a couple bites before rushing out. I got the Kao Pad Kark Moo and pink milk. The pink milk was unique and super refreshing! I had never had sala. The rice and pork was delicious but I wish I had received more meat for the price.

Since the restaurant is primarily a bar, we were a little concerned about whether it would be a good fit for our family with children. However, those concerns disappeared immediately. The staff went above and beyond to make us feel welcome, helping us find dishes that the kids would enjoy and making sure everyone was comfortable. The service was exceptional from start to finish, and we truly enjoyed every moment of our visit. The restaurant itself is beautiful, with a warm and inviting atmosphere.
Highly recommended! Whether you’re visiting with friends, as a couple, or with children, this place delivers an outstanding dining experience. We will definitely be coming back!✨

I first made a reservation at Bar Sprezzatura for my birthday dinner before heading to the Punch Line. I ordered the Fresh Bigoli Liberty Duck Ragù, which quickly joined the clean plate club. I also enjoyed the Sprezz Reviver cocktail with dinner, followed by an espresso to stay caffeinated for the evening. The dinner ended on a sweet note with a surprise tiramisu topped with a candle. It was a thoughtful touch!

On my second visit, I opted for Moroccan mint tea and shared appetizers with colleagues for lunch. The Caprese and Mushroom Forest Floor were favorites. Both appetizers were vegetarian-friendly and perfect for sharing with the table. The Scampi Alla Veneziana pasta was also delectable. It’s not easy to impress an entire team, but Bar Sprezzatura delivered.

My review is based solely on the bar/cocktail experience. My friend and I walked in without a resy and we were told to try our luck at the bar as they were fully booked for the night. The hostess was very kind and sweet to offer us bubbly while we set up shop in the bar area. We were acknowledged very quickly by one of the bartenders and ordered our cocktails in a very timely manner. Although we were standing with our first round of drinks, we ended up getting seats at the bar for our second. I’m a gin girlee and they def know what to do with Negronis here! My first drink was gin based and my second was mezcal based. The bartender convinced me to try it based on what I told him I like. No doubt their cocktail game is above par’ Overall vibe is very stale tech and vc feels (it look like people extended their work hours here to discuss funding and founders), but the staff and drinks totally compensate for that! Everyone we interacted with was very thoughtful and knowledgeable about the menu, we will be back!
The dinner service was perfectly paced and enjoyable, attention was always given without being intrusive. Wait staff was outstanding. Congratulations chef Joseph Offner on a delicious menu

top_reviews.content:
Al Carajo Yucatán is a fantastic spot for breakfast, lunch, or dinner. While I've heard people criticize the restaurant for its small dining area, I think the food more than makes up for any lack of seating comfort.

As someone who has tried chilaquiles all over the Bay Area, I can confidently say that the chilaquiles here rank in my top three. The standout is the sauce—a delicious medium-spicy, tomato-forward sauce with just the right amount of tanginess. It's layered over crispy tortillas and topped with eggs, queso cotija, crema fresca, and pickled red onions, creating a flavorful and well-balanced dish.

The portion size was generous, and the presentation was impressive. In fact, my lunch companions commented on the appearance, aroma, and overall abundance of the dish when it arrived at the table.

I'll definitely be returning and bringing guests with me. Between the outstanding food and convenient location, Al Carajo Yucatán has earned a spot on my list of favorite Mexican restaurants in the area.

Awesome breakfast! We had the torta chilequiles, breakfast burrito and aqua fresca watermelon. Burrito had great eggs, generous amount of protein, toasted and served with a mildly spicy salsa. Torta was fun with the chips on the toasted bun. Limited seating but service staff brought food out to us. Would highly recommend!

The Al Carajo Taqueria is about the best thing in this neighborhood, after looking around at all the barred up storefronts and windows the only thing I could think of was...this must be what it's like to be looking into a prison!
But...Let me yell you, I had about the best Tacos de Pollo con Mango Salsa I've ever had!  5 ☆☆☆☆☆'s for sure!

Tried their pork tacos —they were very tasty, but they came with a lot of sauce, which made the tortilla wet and didn’t make the experience the best. The tacos came in a portion of two (larger than usual), but I would prefer a portion of 3. Overall the taste was good, and I want to go back and try their burritos next time.

Definitely a place for the quesabirria lovers, the pizza is enough for two and is a beauty. The burrito with poc chuc was also delicious, very unique citrus flavor and crispy texture. Service was friendly and good vibes all arouns.

top_reviews.content: Yesterday was our first visit to RH Palm Court. We had a wonderful dinner to celebrate hubby’s birthday !  The service from check in at the front, to seating and to dining was impeccable. Shout out to “Cody”, our amazing server who was juggling multiple tables but still took great care of us, making us feel special. The food from appetizer, grilled shrimp and artichokes were delish. Our entrees, filet, branzino, lobster roll and salmon & desert were seasoned and cooked to perfection. The champagne, manhattan and margarita were well balanced. And the ambience ! 10 out of 5 !!! We love RH interiors ! It fits our beige/tan/light wood, comfortable luxury vibe ! This location is much more elegant and luxurious than the one in Yountville. We will def be back for special occasions with our friends ! Please support the servers, they were all hustling and working hard.. ❤️🙏🏽❤️

Great atmosphere from start to finish, everything feels intentional and elevated, with a refined, luxury setting that really stands out in SF.

Food is consistently strong, and the caviar avocado is a must, rich, balanced, and one of those standout bites you remember long after.

The interior design is beautiful and cohesive, with that signature RH aesthetic that makes the space feel more like a curated gallery than a typical restaurant.

And the rooftop lounge is the real highlight, open, airy, and relaxed but still polished, perfect for lingering over drinks or dinner with a view.

The bay view adds something special to the experience too, calm, expansive, and quietly grounding in a way that makes everything feel slower and more effortless.

Overall, it’s a place where the setting, food, and atmosphere come together seamlessly.

6 out of 5 for the team, 3 out of 5 for the management! For this level of service you need more of these hard working waiters, so they can actually provide their great service. Keep the team, upgrade your leadership.

Not a fan. The building is beautiful, but it's very one note inside. The restaurant is very loud - it's the acoustics from the cavernous interior.

The food was mediocre,  overpriced, and unoriginal. The server was oversolicitous - honestly, why interrupt guests every 5 minutes to ask if they are enjoying everything? We might be enjoying our uninterrupted conversation...

One last hypercritical thing: why have a dress code if no one follows it?

The rooftop has a nice view and comfy seats.

My family and I came to this restaurant to celebrate a sad event in our lives. And you know, the atmosphere is both sublime, pleasant, and a little antique, conducive to reflection (the statues and the noise of the fountain contribute). If it were not for such a sad moment in my life, I would come back here again. The service is excellent, the waiters are tactful and beautiful, the manager of the hall instantly changed the salad of the lady at the next table at her request, and having caught my sad look, a couple of minutes later came to our table and poured soda into our glasses - that is, everything is kept under control in the hall. Very precise work of the staff. The dishes are served quickly, elegantly. Very tasty avocado with caviar, sandwiches with lobsters. very tender and airy everything. Black caviar of excellent quality. The wine list is excellent. But there is no French vodka, which I needed in small quantities in accordance with my state of mind at that moment - here wine as an elegant drink did not suit me. If you want a fairy tale, romance, peace - this is the place for you, to this beautiful and pompous restaurant.

food was good, nothing crazy. the pea bruschetta was lovely and refreshing. calamari and risotto was just good. venison was rich and tasty.

service was a tiny bit slow but they seemed short staffed that day.

Then it took 20 minutes for someone to even come over to our table. The restaurant was nearly empty. We ordered drinks, appetizers, & food. Two people in our party needed another minute to decide so they put in their drink order & asked the waiter if it was okay if he came back in a few minutes to which he replied “I don’t care” with attitude. Our food came out relatively quickly however the other 2 people still had not had their order taken again. We hadn’t seen the waiter for nearly 15 minutes. Eventually we had to go ask the hostess if someone could take their order. They eventually got their food 30 minutes after ours had been served. Luckily the food was fantastic. The saffron risotto was so creamy & comforting. We loved the variety of the tricolor salad! The cacio e pepe was cooked to perfection. Our drinks were also really well made. Gum Kuo Restaurant, Oakland’s Chinatown

10/10 from us, and even though this isn’t San Diego this place is 100% DAYGOEATS CERTIFIED✅📋

Located right in the heart of Oakland Chinatown a beloved institution with authentic dining inside the Pacific Renaissance Plaza.
It is a classic, loud, no-frills hole-in-the-wall. The environment is cramped, lively, and unpretentious, with a steady hum of Cantonese spoken between staff and guests. It feels entirely frozen in time, capturing the nostalgic rhythm of an old-school Hong Kong diner where service here follows the traditional "Chinatown speed" model: fast, direct, and hyper-efficient.

In today's economy still affordable with generous, group-calibrated portion sizes. Most individual plates, bowls of porridge, or noodle soups run in the $10–$20 range

The easiest option is the paid underground parking garage directly beneath the Pacific Renaissance Plaza, which charges reasonable hourly rates instead of driving around in circles for over ten minutes and finding nothing.

Locals widely consider it to serve the best congee (rice porridge) in the East Bay, featuring a perfectly smooth texture. Combined with their house-roasted meats (like the crisp roast duck and char siu) and fresh, silky rice noodle rolls, it is widely considered an unmissable culinary landmark for authentic Cantonese soul food.

We also tried their BBQ Combo Dish, which included BBQ pork and roast duck bursting with flavor, thanks to the perfectly balanced marinade.

The Beef and Egg Over Rice was alright but not memorable.

To cleanse our palates, we enjoyed refreshing Lemon Tea, its citrusy zing complementing the savory dishes beautifully.

I also ordered their Beef Chow Fen for takeout, featuring wide rice noodles stir-fried with succulent beef, creating a harmonious blend of flavors and textures.

google.description: Neighborhood destination for Thai lunch & dinner served in a light, airy setting.

top_reviews.content:
My husband and I visited the Cherry Blossom festival in Japantown, but finding a place to eat was challenging due to the crowd. We decided to explore the nearby area and found this Thai restaurant with outdoor seating, which was perfect for us and our dog.

The staff was very friendly and helpful, and the menu was intriguing. We ordered the Thai spicy
egg noodle soup, green papaya salad, and Thai drunken noodles with seafood. Each dish was delicious, but the spicy noodle soup stood out as our favorite—one of the best noodle soups we’ve had in a while.

To conclude our meal, we ordered  the Thai coconut milk dessert, Ka-nom-tuay, served in a little porcelain cup. It was equally delightful. My husband and I were so impressed with the food that we’re already planning our next visit. Highly recommended!

I was a little nervous when I walked in at 1:30 and there was no one else there, but this place was fantastic. I got the hot and sour noodle soup and it was the perfect balance of flavor and spice and crunch. My Thai tea was also exactly the right level of sweetness. It got a lot busier as my meal went on, fortunately for them. It was hard to pick a restaurant in this very busy area of choices but this was a good one.

Too bad the food was just okay for the heavily decorated oldie Thai street theme. The dish I think is a waste of $37 is seafood crispy pancake. The rest were just not authentic enough. Pad Thai is off, there was no balance of fish sauce, palm sugar and tamarind tastes, but only tastes sour. I wouldn't touch any Pad Krapow that has long green bean in it. It's considered a cheap taste of the cooks who put them in Thailand. And this place isn't cheap. Somtum was a bit disappointing, bearable. Overall a disappointment.
Came for lunch. Crab fried rice and steamed veggies were awesome. Super fresh and flavorful! Thankful they didn’t hold back on the spice for the fried rice. True gem!

They offered a very good thai food. The serving is large and the price is reasonable. The staff in the restaurant are friendly and accommodating. The vibes of the restaurant is good with many ornaments showing thai traditional pop culture.

reviews_snippets.content: "The staff were very nice, the service speedy, and the prices good."
"We ordered pumpkin curry with chicken and eggplant with Thai basil and shrimp."
"Peanuts and lemon, served with a delicious homemade tamarind sauce."

top_reviews.content: The food and Thai tea were really good. Authentic, Thai-owned. Clean and nice interior. Quick service. Combo with appetizer, main, drink and salad was pretty good deal. Closed 3-4pm.

Still coming back here for the Chicken Satay and Rice.  Still amazing; our daughter is in love with both.

Added the steamed veges this time. Every restaurant should be getting training from here on how to steam veges. They are perfect for tossing back on the pan with your favorite seasonings and sesame oil.

Never doubt the reliability of their menu and they are always super friendly. Alameda is lucky to have this small mom and pop place.
This is a great little place for Thai food. The combo selection is a great deal for the price.

Love this place. Order from here all the time. I usually get the chicken yellow curry and gyoza. People sleep on this place honestly. Not sure why people don’t pack the place. (Location maybe?) super nice to go to sit down at. Super nice staff. Quick and accommodating service too. Food is absolutely fabulous. I usually order via DoorDash. When i did DoorDash and Uber Eats myself though i was always picking food up for people here! And there were usually multiple delivery drivers waiting too. (Means the place is good! 😂) Always made exactly how they describe it yet still tastes better somehow! 😂 definitely suggest! Prices are very reasonable for the quality of food too!

This place is still one of my favorite restaurant in Alameda even if one of our dishes was very spicy. I asked if they can make the eggplant dish to have no spices at all. The waitress said “Yes we can”.  The dish was very spicy and I told the manager. She responded to order mild next time. Go figure!  I’ll just stick to BBQ chicken next time. Maybe they really cannot make it non-spicy and just want to take orders.

BBQ chicken and crispy noodles were very good as usual.

I did not take a photo of the eggplant dish as it was upsetting.

top_reviews.content:
Orange chicken is the best I have ever had or will ever have. The price was $20 for a plate but I believe I will have dreams about this orange chicken. Spicy and flavorful in all the right ways but the TEXTURE is to die for. Genuinely every time I put the next piece in my mouth, I had another food-gasm.
If we were to do it again, would have gotten 2 plates of orange chicken and that’s all. Other food was good however nothing will ever compare to the orange chicken I ate here tonight.
Right in the heart of Chinatown.

Friendly service, reasonable prices, and clean facilities. My family of 5 split the 3 piece egg rolls (which were nicely pre-sliced in half for us), the kung pao chicken, the chili beef chow mein, and the squid with black bean sauce. Everything was delicious, with a wide variety of flavor, and we were stuffed by the end. The egg rolls had a buttery crunch, the best I've tasted. If you aren't planning on leftovers, two could split a single entree, especially if you get one of their delicious appetizers. This is an affordable place to get an excellent, authentic meal!
The food is not worth of the price because they give small portion of the dish with alot of rice I wish they did give me more duck and chicken with mushrooms
Soooo delicious! And friendly staff! Food was the best I love food but this dishes were amazing.

Amazing food. The Peking pork ribs was perfectly sauced and sweet and savory. The black bean fish had this great umami flavor. The vegetables were garlicky and refreshing. The staff were nice and friendly. Large portions. Definitely will come again.

take my word for it, this place is GREAT

i was skeptical to try it, but absolutely loved eating here. this is a sushi spot owned by an old couple who are so so so friendly and sweet, absolutely amazing service.

the food was expensive to be completely honest, but the rolls tasted delicious. i tried the gyozas and kara age too; they were so crispy and scrumptious

overall an experience that left me leaving with a smile. i would go again if i ever found myself in the area!

Not only the food is delicious, the preparation is beautiful. Good quality, fresh. I ordered two specialty rolls and they were so yummy! Appreciate a free side of garlic edamame. And I love that they have outdoor seating. Will definitely be back.  Very welcoming place and service.

Wago is our go-to for delicious and unfussy sushi in the neighborhood. The portions are great, artfully displayed, and fresh. But the real reason we keep coming back is the staff - the gentleman who is always there (I’m sorry I don’t know your name!) goes above and beyond every time we are there. The atmosphere is very homey and definitely an “if you know you know” vibe.

Incredible food. Even their miso soup that complimentary with most meals is a step above most I’ve had. It’s easy to overpay for quality in the Marina, but this places prices meet if not exceed their prices

Amazing attention! We had a 2 year old and two 5 year old and 3 adults.The waitress helped with the kids chopsticks and if they eat would have a present! They ate like never before! and a very important thing is that rolls, bento boxes and drinks were just so fresh and delicious! We will comeback from Davis, CA! Thank you!!! 💕🙏🏼🙏🏼🙏🏼

name: Wabi-Sabi SF at Soma
address: 246 Ritch St Apt 101, San Francisco, CA 94107, United States

google.name: Wabi-Sabi SF at Soma
google.address: 246 Ritch St Apt 101, San Francisco, CA 94107, United States

top_reviews.content:
A hidden gem, truly. This was by far the best sushi have ever had. The freshness and quality of their ingredients sets a high standard that has changed how I look at sushi restaurants.

Each roll was made with masterful precision and care. While some sushi restaurants boast a large variety of "specialty rolls", this restaurant takes a modest approach and executed it perfectly. I get the sense in the food the the chef knows the menu intimately which is reflected in the quality of the rolls. I would recommend the Wabi-Sabi roll and the nigiri sampler. Both offerings will give a great sense of the craftsmanship behind the menu.

The space is quite cozy and intimate, with very limited seating. We made a reservation, and I'm glad we did because this spot filled up instantly.

Great sushi spot close to Oracle Park. Service was decent. Food was good. Space is nice and quaint.

Ordered the chirashi and salmon belly which were of excellent quality. In particular, I love how the chirashi came in a mini bento box and looked well manicured. Everything tasted quite fresh. Pricing seemed reasonable for the price uplift.

Would recommend for smaller groups.

Very intimate little sushi place. There's only a handful of tables and the counter. We came in on Friday night at about 8:30 and were able to grab a table. We got a few different rolls and a Nigiri tasting. Perfect for a date or a very small group.

Not a good experience. Waited 10 mins before getting in, then 40mins to get our meals… and mind you they were simple - 2 salmon dons, 1 nigiri platter, 1 hamachi set. The chef is really untrained and doesn’t even feel like a chef. Felt like a random guy trying to put together a sushi or cut it.

Also, I saw the waiter pulling out a salmon from the freezer and it was frozen…. Frozen sashimi???? That’s insane.
Superb sushi! I had the 11-piece Chef's choice Nigiri - highly recommend. It is delicious, as well as great value. I will be back to this fantastic restaurant!

reviews_snippets.content: "A hole in the wall place with incredible sushi and super friendly staff."
"Great nigiri and rolls, high quality fish at a fraction of the price."
