top_reviews.content: their food was good, the experience was mid. I strongly recommend to not take food from the belt as they are highly overpriced. I feel like they’re intentionally delaying your order speed so you get hungry and take plates from the belt, so they make more. Their best item is the chicken katsu. Do either ayce or per order, do not touch the belt. Oh and did I mention they have cup cakes for $5? Crazy

This was my first time here with my girlfriend and we loved It! We can’t wait to come back!

We tried the Ayce/all you can eat sushi
And It was wonderful! A lot of the sushi were melting in our mouths. By the time we got to the desserts, i was already full and falling asleep cause i ate so much.

I don’t understand the bad reviews, if you’re looking for a top tier sushi spot or Michelin star..then obviously go to those spots. Other than that..enjoy the food and keep It moving if you don’t like the food. You’re messing with peoples livelihood.

Most importantly please be nice to the servers! They’re constantly working hard to provide a wonderful service for you.

Good quality fish, great quantity, friendly chef, nice service, and restaurant was very spacious and not too crowded. Generally, the nigiri are a good price with lots of fish. We enjoyed the salmon belly nigiri which is slightly seared. The salmon is very fatty and tasty.

The dragon ball appetizer was incredible, and the penthouse roll was good but not amazing. Happy to bump this rating up to a 5/5 if I can find myself a roll I like as much as the dragon ball appetizer. I’ll definitely be back

Edit- we went back to dine in and give it another shot and this time we went with the coconut shrimp, spicy fried California roll, and crunchy jalapeño roll. The jalapeño crunch was my favorite. The plain ramune Japanese soda was a hit too!

I’d bump this up to 4.5 stars because I loved the ambience at the restaurant and eating the food fresh definitely helped the taste. I do however feel slightly uncomfortable walking up to the restaurant because the neighborhood can feel a bit deserted and sketchy at night time

I truly have no idea how this place is so highly rated other than they purchased AI generated reviews.

Honestly, this was one of the worst all-you-can-eat sushi experiences I’ve had. From the moment we sat down, the waitress kept repeatedly reminding us about the 90-minute time limit, which made the whole meal feel rushed and uncomfortable.

To make things worse, the conveyor belt barely had any selection. We were waiting several minutes between plates, which is ridiculous for an AYCE spot. For nearly the first 45 minutes, only the cheapest plate options were coming around. We had to ask where the rest of the selection was, and only then did other options start appearing—by that point, we were already getting full.

The variety was disappointing overall, with very little fresh sushi and a strange mix of mostly cooked items and even desserts on the belt. Not what you expect when you’re paying for sushi.

The service didn’t help either. The waitress seemed stressed and kept bringing us random plates we didn’t ask for, trying to convince us to eat things we clearly didn’t want.

We left feeling rushed, unsatisfied, and honestly ripped off at $50 per person. To top it off, I ended up with a stomach ache. Definitely not worth it, and I won’t be coming back.

top_reviews.content:
This reviewer after having eaten in over a thousand burger restaurants in the East Bay and Northern California, cannot recommend this restaurant or its chain. It is a money grab operation, that serves disproportionately small portions, tiny burgers, tiny fries, and are actively working to push the workers out, and go all-kiosk for the orders. The workers were super nice, working hard and very friendly, but this business model, is not about quality, or value.
Basically their idea of a hamburger and the formula with which they present it, suck.
I recommend that everyone break the habit.

Some of the worse customer service Ive ever experienced. I ordered the steak sandwhich but the self order screens did not give me the option to choose well done as I am currently pregnant so I stepped up to the counter to ask one of the workers if the adjustment could be added to my order. I also ordered it with no BBQ sauce which I was anle to adjust on the self service screen myself. First off I was ignored for a good 5 minutes while 2 female workers walked back and forth and then when I was finally acknowledged I was just given a look no greeting whatsoever. However the worker said she would let the kitchen know so I sat down and waited for my order. Once I got my steak sandwhich i immediately saw the BBQ sauce dripping from the sandwhich I went back and waited at the counter for another 5-10 minutes while another female worker was working on online pick up orders I believe. When she finally came over to help me she literally just stared at me, turned to one of the kitchen staff and spoke in Spanish. The kitchen worker shook her head and gave me a dirty look and just shrugged. I told her it clearly says on my receipt no BBQ sauce. She took the sandwich tossed it in the trash and mumbled a new one would be made as shes physically walking away. I ended up getting a new one made but I just felt so uncomfortable at that point as the kitchen staff stared and quite obviously were talking about me. I understand everyone has bad days but this is not the first time I have heard of terrible customer service at Habit Grill. Definitely don't think I will ever return unfortunately.

We tried to order at the kiosk, but we found out you can't use a gift card. Which is what I had. We waited, at the register, for about 6 minutes before we were helped. They had a few orders. No biggie.

While waiting I noticed milk sitting out, but assumed they'd just finished using it. Relevance? We  were only there to order orange dreamsicle shakes. We were excited to try it.
What they lacked isn't my focus at the moment. Within a few minutes after finishing the shakes we both felt queasy and nauseous. Both of our stomachs were upset. We rushed home. That's when it hit me. That freaking milk. It must've been out way too long. It wasn't put up after our shakes were made. What the what Habit?
I'm writing this review the following day and our stomachs are still upset.

This location takes forever to get your food! There's nobody inside and it took over 15 minutes to get 2 cheeseburgers and 1 order of French fries. While waiting, I noticed how dirty and sticky their tables are. I guess they don't care about cleaning here. The employees all have a miserable look on their faces as if they're working at a prison. Avoid this location and find a better Habit location that cares.

A few days ago, I had a little time before we had to start working next door, so I popped in and satisfied my Habit.😊 see what I did there? 😉
It was my first time getting the mocha chocolate shake and, boy, howdy hay, it was good. The Double Char Burger was a 5⭐️ as usual, and the fries were perfectly done. Crispy and salty on the outside and mash-potatoy in the inside, and with the ketchup,😋 perfection. 👌
The bad things I could say about this visit is that there was a mess on the floor in front of the counter that wasn't cleaned up until I was just about done eating, and the ketchup dispenser wasn't working or stocked. Good thing they weren't stingy with the ketchup packets.
Overall, another great experience at the Habit.

top_reviews.content:
Worth every penny!
We came for a special occasion and this omakase delivered. The fish was incredibly fresh and every course looked almost too pretty to eat. Chef Peter clearly cares about his craft. You can taste it in how balanced each piece is, and he was happy to explain things as they came out.
Renee took great care of us. She was warm and attentive , and we felt welcome from the moment we walked in.
We're already planning our next visit. Highly recommend for anyone who wants a really special omakase. Thank you, Renee, Chef Peter and the rest of the staff!

This is my second time coming to this place and last time was in 2023. I had to say the experience is much better and the food is as good as it was. Chef George was amazing! There were only 3 groups of guests when we visited, so only 6 people needs to be served. Everyone was well taken care and everyone was happy. We were here for our first wedding anniversary, Chef George treated us with an off-menu sushi roll because we chatted about a bite that we had from 2023 was so good and it was no longer in the menu. Chef George is a very humble person and he introduce every dishes with details. He also took out the Polaroid that they had and let us take a picture with one of his giant knife for tuna.  The overall experience was just so great! Thank you Chef George for letting us having such a wonderful anniversary! It was a great memory!

This restaurant was amazing! The food was delicious, the service was excellent, and the chef was friendly and fun to talk to. I visited on my birthday, and they truly made me feel special. Everything exceeded my expectations, and the whole experience was wonderful. I highly recommend this place and would definitely come back again.

You have to try it! One of the more memorable omakase experiences I've had in SF, and honestly, a must visit, even after just coming back from Japan. This place still felt incredibly special.

The menu was thoughtful and well-paced (I'm a slow eater), with 19+ standout dishes like the monkfish with ponzu and the uni + caviar chawanmushi, both beautifully executed and full of flavor. The nigiri was consistently fresh and balanced (especially the toro and kinmedai ).

What really set it apart was how engaging and personable the experience was. Peter, our chef, guided us through each course with care, and Jackson (the owner) was just as present. Checking in, talking with us, and making sure every detail felt intentional. That level of hospitality and humor made the entire night feel warm, personal, and welcoming.

It's rare to find a place that delivers both high-level execution and genuine connection like this.

Already booked my next reservation!!!

Had such a fun Omakase experience here! The chef was not only incredibly skilled but also super funny, making the whole dinner entertaining from start to finish. Every course was fresh, beautifully presented, and full of flavor.

We even got to see the chef’s amazing sushi knives (some worth thousands!) and his hilarious cucumber 🥒 “snake” cutting skills — unforgettable moment 😂.

Great food, great vibes, and a truly memorable night. Definitely recommend if you want amazing sushi with a fun atmosphere!

I tried the fried plantain and recommend it! The plantains were perfect! I also tried the grilled veggies and soyrizo bowl - it was pretty yummy too! My partner had their pollo asado bowl and liked it - but seemed to like my bowl better.

If you’re the neighborhood, looking for a casual spot for mexican - stop by here!
I really like their quesadilla, the meat is so tasty, and it’s the best I’ve tried in SF! The service is friendly and fast, and it’s a cozy, modern Mexican restaurant with reasonable prices.

Walk by this place all the time and after a year i finally decided to try it. Wow! So glad I did.  The pozole was so good and authentic. The breakfast enchiladas also did not disappoint. Fast,.tasty and authentic great job!!

$20 bacon breakfasts burritos hella overpriced ~ By SF standards this breakfast burrito was flavourless and $5 overpriced. A decent portion is the only good thing about it About $20 for a carne asada super burrito and soda. Charged me a bag fee for the paper bag.. in a city with so many options, this place is a MISS

Big fan of this restaurant! Very friendly staff who have great recos, relaxed vibes and absolutely tasty food! We tried the fried plantain & black beans burrito, the salmon tacos and the chicken tacos. Each taco comes with 2 tortillas and there's enough filling to make two tacos for yourself! Portion sizes are huge and you can have a filling meal within $12-15 per person.

The sauces and pico de gallo are free flow - my absolute favorites were the tomatillo and salsa verde sauces! Im getting hungry for more just writing this review.

top_reviews.content:
Surprised by how good this place was, I think it’s definitely the best Nepali restaurant I’ve had here in the US.

Starting with the chicken momo, they were really tasty esp with the chilli powder on the side. Also got the veggie chow mein which was pretty decent, not salty like many other places end up being. The cashew chicken curry was tasty, along with the goat curry. As for the breads, garlic naan was good but wow this was my first time trying Tingmo and I loved it (gotta have that over the naan). Definitely coming back here!

Ambience was warm, food did take some time to come but servers were very nice and helped our group of 6 decide what to get!

The food is off the charts good! Like we wanted to come back again the next day.

The momos are delicious and spicy and so unique.
The sapna (I think) is the tofu dish and it's so delicious.

My only beef with the place is that the rice on the side is relatively small, but at least it's not too crazy expensive.

We had three appetizers, three mains and two rounds of garlic naan for 4 people and it was perfect

The chowmein is my all time favorite here. The pork ribs are absolutely tender and very flavorful. The Shapta has a very fun, spicy kick to it. The momo is very juicy too. Food here tastes delicious with layers of deep flavors. Their ambience is warm and cozy and reminds me of Nepal. The people here are very friendly and welcoming too.
Good food and great vibe. They were able to make chowmein for my jain friend as well. We ordered momos, kale chat, chowmein. Everything was good

10/10 on all fronts. Every dish actually shocked me with how balanced, thoughtful, and exciting they were. The pork dumplings were unlike any I’ve ever had before. This is going to be a go to spot when I have people visiting that I want to impress : )

The broth is amazing and rich with flavor, way better than other Ramen shop I have been too. The service is great as well and very friendly. If you come here you will love it.

Honestly, the Focaccia was one of my absolute favorites things here. I cannot say enough how wonderful the person who greeted us, the person who brought our water and bread, and our sever Laura were.

Lots of parking on a Saturday,  at 6:30pm.

Sat outdoors, heaters would come on, if needed.  We didn't need it 2 weeks ago.

My group of 3 ladies, celebrating a birthday of one of them. All food choices fresh, flavorful,  hot/ steaming. My chicken picatta, with mashed potatoes, grilled vegetables, perfect. $25. Had left overs.
My companions entrees , of salads, pizzas, enjoyable too.

Went here with my sister and brother in law on a Friday night. The food was splendid. We started with calamari and it was one of the best calamari I’ve had and it’s my go to at most restaurants. I had the fettuccine pasta with shrimp and it was delicious my brother in law had a taste and he wanted to order himself a plate. We had a mushroom pizza which was tasty and my sister had the lasagna which was also yummy. I had my first espresso martini and it was the perfect pairing for dessert!

I recently made a reservation for a large group. They were very responsive and they made the reservation very easy.

Unfortunately half of our group couldn't attend due to family matters. I felt terrible, but the staff was very understanding and accommodating. Our server was wonderful, I wish I got his name. (The evening of 12/10/23)

The cocktails are classics with an upscale twist, as well as an extensive wine list. The food is excellent. I recommend the calamari, ahi tuna salad, duck confit and tiramisu.

This was my first time here and I plan to go back on a date night or with friends sometime soon!

We've been to Italian colors a number of times now and every time it is absolutely perfect. The food is wonderful, the service is great and the atmosphere is fantastic. The live music from the guitarist is a wonderful touch. I'm so glad they're such a great restaurant for me to go to. I will always be going back to this place

top_reviews.content:
Excellent from start to finish. A very friendly bartender welcomed us and took our drink order. When our table for 8 was ready we were seated and serviced with excellence through the whole meal. I can not say enough for the amazing service staff. Food was equally excellent! It was a special family event , made even more special by a special staff.
A group picture was taken at the end by the bartender to remember our night. Many thanks ! This group definitely knew how to take care of their customers.

The first restaurant we planned to go to was fully booked, so we searched on Google Maps and found Grand Lake Kitchen — and we’re so glad we did! Parking was a bit of a challenge, but once inside, we loved the spacious setup and the lively vibe.

Our waiter was friendly, attentive, and gave great food recommendations. The Fried Chicken was especially delicious — crispy, flavorful, and perfectly cooked. Everything we ordered tasted amazing, and the staff made the experience even better with their warm service.

Highly recommend this place to everyone looking for great food and a welcoming atmosphere!

Have eaten at Grand Ave location several times and loved it. This was our first visit to the Dimond location.  Food was excellent,  service was so-so.  We had a much longer wait for food than expected.  The best deal on the menu was the Fried Half Chicken, which came with 2 large sides. I split this with my daughter,  but it could easily have fed 3 people.  The side dishes, especially Cauliflower salad, were fantastic as expected.  My wife had a great lamb sausage and polenta. She said it was fabulous.  The grands had the French toast and loved it...the side of peachs was excellent.   My son in law had  the turkey sandwich...his go to. It had lots of meat and cranberry spread on it.
This location is roomy and comfortable.
Would 100 % recommend.

This restaurant has a nice menu and friendly staff. Parking is a challenge. Worth going back to try some other menu items! I had their turkey sandwich that had delicious flavors with its cranberry sauce, Swiss cheese, avocado, pickles and lettuce!

Been here a few times usually just for food to go and just stick to the same things. Very chill, not to uptight. I finally had a night to hang out and decided to dine in and try out a couple of dishes. (We sat outside which was nice eat and people watch) Sadly I wasn't to happy with the food. But the drinks👍🏾👍🏾👍🏾 ( can't tell you what I got because it was a off menu special 😁) but I've had a few different beverages and they all have been great. Now food for me all the sandwiches don't disappoint (veggie, yadi, beef burger) And the donuts are cooked to order and are amazing. However all the entrees I feel all needed to just be cooked longer. Overall still great, and would definitely go back.

The service was triple A!  I would highly recommend this fine establishment!!!

We absolutely loved our experience, The double pepperoni pizza was perfectly crisp and flavorful. The lasagna was also a star!  It didn't feel too heavy or greasy. The tomato flavor was balanced and not overpowering. You can tell they don't cut corners with their ingredients.

And the staff who served us stood out with his awesome customer service. He made everyone (not just us) feel taken cared of.

Since we just live in the area, this might be our go to pizza place next time :))
Super friendly, quick service in a lovely setting. Delicious pizza, wings and baklava.

My honest take on dining at Marina Pizza & Pasta at SF Bay area… it's a solid Italian specialty spot. Good thing they’re open till late night, makes it easy after a long day. The host and chef are super welcoming and they have seating and dining area. They sell pizza by the slice so you can try different ones, plus salads and pastas are on point. Portions are big, prices fair – definitely feels like value for money. Worth a visit if you’re around.  Traveler Tips 🧳
- Great late‑night option, don’t worry about closing early.

I've worked in the neighborhood for years, but today was the first time I came in. The space was very clean and welcoming, the pizza was delicious, and the salad was surprisingly fresh. In my experience, salads at small pizza places usually taste like they were made with a bag of salad mix several days past its prime, but this salad was so crisp! The prices were also very reasonable, especially in the overpriced Marina/Cow Hollow district. I will definitely be back!

The staff ensured everything was perfect throughout the meal. I highly recommend this place and will definitely be coming back! Looks like they’re open for lunch on the weekends now - check it out🇬🇷🫒

Wow! This restaurant is AMAZING! The food is delicious, the atmosphere is one of a kind, and service is spectacular. This has easily become one of my most memorable dining experiences. Everything I ordered was cooked perfectly with a ton of flavor. I highly recommend coming here! You’ll love it!

I am a bit late in writing this review, but this place left such a fantastic impression that I just had to share my experience. My partner and I came here for Valentine’s Day, and the entire evening was amazing. The decorations were beautiful and set the perfect romantic mood, and the food was absolutely incredible—authentic, fresh, and cooked to perfection. You can truly tell that the team here genuinely cares about what they serve and the experience they provide to their guests. If you are looking for phenomenal Greek food and top-notch hospitality, this is the spot. We will definitely be back!

We had great food like moussaka and chicken souvlaki, salmon - everything was excellent. Welcoming pita bread with a very tasty garlic spread. unfortunately we hand no time to go for desserts. The service was efficient - maybe small remark - we’ve been offers with additional pita bread by the waitress, but finally no one brought it to the table.
Overall - absolutely worth to recommend.

Our first time at Milos Meze and we absolutely loved it! The staff was very kind, friendly, and attentive.

We tried the spicy hitipiti, saghanaki, horiatiki salad, beef souvlaki, and lavraki. The saghanaki stole the show - reminded me of an Argentine provoleta. Delicious melted cheese with lemon. We also loved the beef souvlaki - it was very tender, smoky, and perfectly cooked. For dessert we tried the baklavaki which was super yummy and very generous portion.

Very cozy, family feeling great for all ages and occasions. Cant wait to come back!

top_reviews.content:
Since eating here I'm going around telling everyone who didn't ask, about this place!!!

Such yummy food with tons of options if you're in a breakfast, lunch or dinner mood. It's true southern food in SF. And a great deal on a carafe of mimosas 🥂

The staff are attentive and kind. And the owner is very personable and chatted with us a few times & checking in on us.

Definitely one of the best creole restaurants in the bay, and probably the best one in SF in my opinion. The selection was great, I couldn’t decide what to order so I ordered everything: fried chicken plate with collard greens & mashed potatoes, chicken sandwich, soft shell crab, fried okra, and mini cornbread. The breading on everything fried was light and flavorful. I was esp surprised by how large the portion of soft shell crab, there was 3 per order! Collard greens were juicy, chicken tender, I’m already excited to go back again to try their other dishes!

What a lovely dinner! Great atmosphere and service. The staff did a fantastic job ensuring we had a wonderful night. Delicious gumbo and fish & chips. Cheesecake for a starter was a huge win. It was a work of art! Thanks again. We’ll be back for sure.

I ordered the “crab sandwich” thinking I was going to get a decent amount of “unshelled” crabs or better yet crab cakes Louisiana style. Instead I received the tiniest crab even seen (the size of 2 inches by 3 inches) that was deep fried with its shell and all, and then put on a piece of bread. I also ordered fish and chips and these two orders were delivered with just one tiny container of their house sauce. Pretty disappointing.

Poboys serves up Cajun soul food in a quaint and cozy, colorful restaurant in Potrero Hill. A warm welcome greeted me as I entered, and I sat down at one of their colorful tables surrounded by pops of color, and the aromas of deliciousness. I can’t go to a soul food restaurant without ordering okra, so I got that, and boy was I pleased. These tasty little crunchy morsels came with a side of jalapeño aioli, and I don’t normally like aioli, but this one was a hit. Next I opted for the fried chicken plate with mashed potatoes and gravy and collard greens. Whatever they batter that chicken with should be patented, it’s seriously good. The whole meal came out hot and flavorful. It’s a big plate of food so I could have split all this with another person and been satisfied. Now I have another meal to look forward to at home. Check out this spot and enjoy yourself a delicious meal.

name: Gioia Pizzeria
address: 579 Hayes St, San Francisco, CA 94102, United States

google.name: Gioia Pizzeria
google.address: 579 Hayes St, San Francisco, CA 94102, United States

top_reviews.content:
Tldr; food was great, service was attentive and pleasant, atmosphere was smoky and authentic. Try their margherita and gabagool.

My best friend never really got pizza, he liked it enough but never enough to go out of our way for it... Well that changed today thanks to Gioia!

Firstly the food was impeccable, truly some of the best slices we've ever had. The crust, perfect, the ingredients, quality, and as a person who never really picks up a saucy pizza, I wish my slices had more! I got a slice of margherita and pepperoni and tried some of the gabagool, and really wished I had ordered more, can't recommend enough.

The service was also great! I accidentally dropped my slice on the ground and the gentleman running the counter whipped me up a new slice without even a thought! He was also very attentive while we were ordering which we can't appreciate enough!

The physical location too, while small like most sf restraunts, was all appointed and decorated. The strong amazing smells and smoky interior were the reasons we decided to stop by, which in fact did not disappoint. But there are only 2 tables and very limited seating so don't expect to be able to dine in.

Can't recommend Gioia enough, try their margherita and gabagool!

From a lifetime New Yorker this is as close to a New York slice I’ve seen in any state. It’s about 60-70% there. The crust is light and delicious, but it’s still losing something. Most places are like 5–30% at best, but are always too dense or flat tasting or worse.

The pizza here tastes great and has the NYC pop.

We placed a large order with Gioia for a post-wedding celebration after our City Hall ceremony, and it was a massive hit! Hands down the best pizza in San Francisco that I’ve tried.

Everyone was raving about how delicious it was, and guests were literally still talking about how good the pizza was the next day! The ordering process was smooth, and the quality was top-tier. If you’re catering a group gathering or just looking for incredible pizza in the city, Gioia is an absolute must!
Very good crispy pizza. The kind of pizza that doesn’t make you feel gross after. Location only has one table. Efficient little spot.

I’ve ordered takeout from Gioia twice.
As a collegian on the Peninsula, I grew up on Frankie, Johnny and Luigi Too! pizza. It was my favorite for 50 years until a couple weeks ago when I ordered a delivery of Gioia. Wow.  I stayed over in The City again this past weekend and had Gioia delivered again Saturday.

I designed my own pizza with a Margherita Pizza base and then added pepperoni, Calabrian chilis, and anchovy on the side…well done/crispy.

The roasted tomatoes are key…depth of flavor, umami-heaven.

I’m a pain in the ass, so I call to make sure my pizza is made to spec. The staff, led by Kait, is unparalleled in their willingness to help. I just cannot recommend Gioia enough. I wish there were one in the 925, but Berkeley is as close to my home as a Gioia is based so far. I’ve not had a pie from Berkeley, but I believe Gioia is completely committed to maintaining the quality of their pizza. Nothing else comes close IMO.  I know there’s no zealot like a convert…but I’m not just being a fan boy.

Oh yeah…the arugula-avocado salad is YUM, and the dressing for it like crack.  DO not forget to check the box for utensils.  I did not…California is a request the utensils state…and that’s how I know how committed Gioia is to customer service:  Kait, CALLED ME today after she’d heard I was frustrated.

I can’t imagine a customer not being thrilled with Gioia.

top_reviews.content:
great service and really enjoyed the experience!!

the chefs and hosts were all extremely friendly and made sure to keep our waters full and fill our plates right when we finished eating

that atmosphere was intimate and a great place for a small birthday celebration!

the omakase itself was quiet filling and the ice cream was delicious. I have had omakase at similar price point that i enjoyed more, but overall still had a great experience due to the presentation and majority of the plates!!

Such a reasonably priced omakase! The corkage fee is only $35, which is a great deal. The taste, the portions—everything was excellent. It’s a hidden gem with no reason not to go. I’m definitely going every time I come to San Francisco. This is the second sushi spot opened in SF by the owner of Sushi Jin, and the quality is so good, it’s totally worth the money.

Food and service were excellent - some of the best nigiri I’ve had. However, we were very disappointed to not be able to sit at the bar as we drove 3 hrs for our first omakase experience. I am a sushi chef myself and was excited to watch the sushi being made and engage with the chefs.

We were seated at a table away from the bar. We made our reservation online through open table, and nowhere did it mention reserving the bar versus a table. There is only a section for “special requests” which I interpreted as a section to mention any food allergies, etc. As a result, we did not receive the full omakase experience we were expecting. This is something that should be clarified during the reservation process to avoid disappointing future customers. Maybe a specific question asking “bar” or “table” seating reservation.

We would be happy to return for another experience, and next time I will be sure to call the restaurant directly to make sure they have my reservation down to be seated at the bar.

I’ve lived in SF for almost 50 years and had never heard of this place.  Always searching for my for better sushi option, Hinata filled the bill.  Delicious prix fixe, Japanese omakase chef’s choice - very fresh, delicious items, with a contemporary spin on some traditional dishes.  Great place and am definitely going back for more ❤️

I absolutely love Hinata! Every time I’m in SF, I make sure to stop by for omakase. The fish is always incredibly fresh, the ambiance is fantastic, and they have a great selection of sake. The chefs are a lot of fun, and adding on extra pieces is always worth it. I still remember their homemade sesame ice cream—it was so delicious. I’ll keep coming back whenever I’m in San Fran!

top_reviews.content: This pizza is truly incredible… the flavors are brilliant and the execution is too good. Get yourselves a slice or the whole pie because you won’t be disappointed.

We went there for the first time and was given a warm welcome with the wonderful smile. Then we saw apart from cheese pizza , they had just one veg pizza as the veggie option . No doubt the taste of pizza was great and the best part I liked was their green chutney , I just can’t get enough of it .Also loved the ice cream scoop of the coffee flavor and I feel at the present the prices are very reasonable. Yes I am definitely going again!

Was going on the BART and saw this pizza shop. Needed some lunch and got two slices. The pizza slices were heavenly and were really good. They paint the pizza with an olive oil sauce thing and it is so good.

Can you please chill with the corn. Freaking every day, there's a corn pizza. I'm sure some people like corn on their pizza but surely even those people dont want corn every single day. Like, have you guys realized, toppings other than corn do indeed exist and you are allowed to use them. Every time I wanna grab a quick slice before catching the BART, I walk in, see corn, walk out, go literally anywhere else, as there is no other restaurant in a 25 mile radius so obsessed with corn.

Haven’t had their pizza for a while so I thought I’d give it a go.

To my surprise there was absolutely no one in the restaurant so the service was very quick. The restaurant is very clean and well appointed. Located in a busy and walkable area of Berkeley.

The pizza was ready straight away but I’ll be honest, is that a good thing when it appears they have no business? How fresh was it?!

Took it home and it was okay. I do think it’s been sitting for a wee bit but wasn’t cold or hard. So that’s a plus!  The flavor was good and their green sauce was yummy! I liked they were very generous with their sauce for no extra charge.

What I didn’t like is that the crust on about 1/4 of the pizza was so thin it was too crispy and browned.

top_reviews.content: If you're looking for an authentic Italian restaurant in San Fran, look no further. We are from the East coast and have the best Italian restaurants here  and Bocconcino would fit right in here in Boston's North End. The GNOCCHI AL GORGONZOLA was phenomenal (Homade gnocchi). We also had the POLLO ALLA PARMIGIANO, MELANZANE ALLA PARMIGIANA and the SPAGHETTI CIPOLLA E SALSICCIA which were all outstanding.  We did have a reservation and were sat right away, but did see people get turned away if they didn't as the restaurant is small inside.

The restaurant had a nice atmosphere for dinner although it could get a bit loud at times. I had the Ravioli de Pesce which was very good and had a nice flavor, and I could actually taste the fish. The Ravioli de Pesto and the Tortelini were good but nothing special. The tiramisu was good but a little bland, however the chocolate cake was executed to perfection!

I have no idea how many restaurants you can pack into such a short stretch of roadway but this part of Green Street sure has plenty of options, and today's top choice is..Bocconcini.
I had big Mable Hatley with me because she's in town from her compound up in Monte Rio with her crew, The Monte Rio Muffin Mashers, and they plan on hitting every LBG joint in the city, so be forewarned because they don't take prisoners!
I had ordered a few things, but the pasta dish was deliciously amazing!
5 ☆☆☆☆☆'s and that by itself is worthy of a trip across the bridge!

Unfortunately, we didn’t have a great experience here. The restaurant looks charming from the outside, but inside it was extremely loud—we could barely hear each other and had to raise our voices throughout dinner. Even though we had a reservation, we were asked to wait outside, and the service felt inattentive. We had to ask for everything ourselves, including the menu.

We also ordered a salad to share, but it was served first and our pasta didn’t arrive until we had finished it. We would have preferred to enjoy the salad together with our main course rather than as a separate course.

The food was just okay. Having been to Italy, we expected more from a restaurant promoting itself as authentic Italian. The pasta was quite basic, and the tiramisu tasted more like cake than a traditional tiramisu. The house wine was excellent, and one waiter kindly offered me a complimentary glass after noticing we weren’t fully satisfied, which we appreciated. Unfortunately, it wasn’t enough to make up for the overall experience.

I cannot rate this place highly enough. I was craving cacio e pepe and feeling a bit homesick, and even though it wasn’t on the menu tonight, the owner offered to make it for me himself. The best I’ve had since Europe. Truly an authentic Italian experience — come here if you want to know what it means to feel the love of food. Will come back anytime I’m in town. Gratzie

One of the best vegan meals I've ever eaten! Tea leaf kale salad, basil cumin chickpea tofu, and coconut veggie curry were all fresh and flavorful. Tamarind cooler and mango ginger lassi were a fine complement. Highly recommend!!

The staff made the experience even better—they were incredibly friendly, welcoming, and genuinely kind. Their positive attitude and excellent customer service really stood out. I felt welcomed from the moment I walked in. I’ll definitely be back and highly recommend this place to anyone looking for great food and amazing service!

Genuinely hurts my tooth on the giant stem left in the Chile  rellano burrito I ordered. Literally the only extra step  in making this dish (taking 2 seconds to cut out the singe stem) was completely ignored by the Monday night staff. Could have choked or fully broken a tooth.

Adding insult to injury (literally) the Monday night team (not the usual people) tried to charge for extra cheese twice for a pinch of shredded cheese. (One $1+  charge for extra cheese was expected, twice was improper).

Will be avoiding this convenient neighborhood place on Monday nights moving forward. In my experience the usual staff is much much better, responsibly removing the stems and charging properly according to their menu.

This place proves that simple, honest cooking can be extraordinary. La Tortilla Restaurant in The Castro delivered a fantastic dining experience from start to finish. The chile relleno was perfectly cooked with a great balance of cheese and pepper, and the mole had that deep, rich, layered flavor you only get from a truly well‑made sauce.

Each platter came with rice, our choice of beans, guacamole, sour cream, a crisp lettuce‑and‑tomato salad, and warm tortillas (corn or flour). Every component tasted fresh and thoughtfully prepared. It’s rare to find a place where every part of the plate shines, but La Tortilla pulls it off. Highly recommend for anyone craving real, delicious Mexican food in The Castro.

Almost all of the dishes had one component that failed on execution - perhaps a reflection of the timing for when we arrived (Friday evening). As a general note, each dish was salted very heavily, teetering on the line of being overly salted.

Tuna Ceviche with tortilla chips - tuna was fresh and the ceviche showed quality ingredients, however the tortilla chips had no snap at all and were chewy. A previous review called these “limp and leathery” and I would agree!

Glassy potato - the flavour of the aioli was good, the potatoes were however overly fried and crunchy. The table next to us ordered the same dish around 20 minutes later and we saw that their potatoes were less brown / crispy looking.

Rockfish with crispy rice - this was average, the fish was tepid.

Halibut on romesco - the fish and sauce were fine, the flavor profile was similar to the rockfish. The beans were lovely. The radicchio however was so charred/burnt and tasted so bad that it was inedible.

I visited Camino Alto and really liked the concept at first — order at the counter, then find your own table. The patio is pet-friendly, which is a big plus.

However, the experience quickly became frustrating. After sitting down, we had to get up and walk to the front for water. Then again for sugar when we ordered coffee. Having to repeatedly go back and forth for basic things takes away from the experience.

The food is okay — interesting flavors, but nothing memorable.

If customers are expected to self-serve water, utensils, napkins, and more, it makes you question why a tip is being charged. A simple fix would be adding a service station in the patio.

Overall, good concept, but the execution needs improvement.

The food was (of course) amazing. Delicious and fresh cuisine that is so seasonal and thoughtful and creative. The service really put the whole experience over the top. Sam was so hospitable and kind. She helped us change our reservation and her professionalism and outgoing personality made an already special night really memorable. She deserves a raise and a big pat on the back for providing such incredible service and going above and beyond to serve the clientele and make each person who eats here (me included) book the next reservation as soon as you walk out the door!

Came here last night for a birthday meal.  I appreciated all the GF and DF options.  I thought the food was fresh and creative however it was a bit pricey.  It is SF and of course I'm sure the rent and cost to run a business is high.  Enclosed back patio with lots of potted plants was cozy and warm atmosphere.  The pork very shoulder was basically Carnitas with black beans and guacamole with tortillas - thought that was pricey at $39 however I'm sure the difference is in the organic grass fed pig it came from.  The limeade with coriander seeds - needed more coriander infused flavor and needed to be a touch sweeter to my taste - tasted too healthy.  Should've asked for simple syrup.

Most of us had the rockfish / black cod / salmon.  The rockfish was delicious and beautifully cooked with a nice sauce, the crispy rice - a good change in texture however it sticks to your teeth.  The black cod portion is small with half of the plate covered in microgreens.  The beet hummus - bright and delicious.  The salmon looked good in terms of presentation and portion however I did not taste it.  The seed bread (GF) was hearty and healthy.

google.name: Vien Huong Restaurant

top_reviews.content:
We tried two dishes during my visit.

#21 - The broth was light and clean, and the ingredients tasted fresh. If you prefer a mild, simple flavor, this is a good choice.

#10 Seafood Ho Fun was disappointing. It came with only a few small pieces of squid and two shrimp, but a huge amount of noodles. The broth was extremely bland, and for the price it didn’t feel worth it.

The restaurant is cash only, and although the menu says prices include tax, the overall pricing still felt misleading. I probably wouldn’t return.

At this location, the fried garlic is served separately—a detail I truly appreciate. I also really enjoy their thin egg noodles, which strike a perfect balance between chewy and tender without becoming overly soft. However, the dish tends to be quite oily, so if you prefer lighter meals, this might not be ideal for you.

My usual order is the Number 1 without kidney, with the soup served on the side. I also always add fish cake as an appetizer. The total cost for two regular dishes plus one appetizer comes to $53.75.

What I love about this restaurant is how it evokes the authentic flavors of Thailand’s street food, especially the dry yellow egg noodles. While it doesn’t include traditional Thai-style char siu or wontons, the taste remains quite close to home.

This well-established Chinese restaurant impresses me with its surprisingly clean restrooms, likely due to my morning visits. Parking can be difficult, as only metered street parking is available. The branch tends to be busy, so clear communication with staff is important. Although there may be a short wait, the service is attentive and friendly.

Wow does this place get packed! I got the seafood ho fun, and it was aight. Like not mind blowing but it was good. I thought the lettuce was extremely weird. The place is cash only though so be prepared. Maybe I need to try this place again…
Waited about 15 minutes for lunch on Saturday. I thought the noodle was average, not sure what the hype is about. Also I think the noodle used to be cheaper but its much more expensive now.

*2/25/2024
I ordered the mixed noodles with both ho fun and rice noodles. The broth is light and clear, and it comes with lots of toppings like chili, sriracha, hoisin, vinegar, and Vien Huong's special chili sauce. There's a mix of meats in the dish—shrimp, fish balls, pork balls, pork pieces, kidney, and your choice of sliced chicken or pork—all served with your favorite type of rice noodles. The homemade chili oil and pickled jalapeños give it a spicy kick, making the flavors really pop.

1/25/2024
No. 21 Chow Jew Ho Fun is a dish featuring shrimp, fish balls, pork balls, pork bits, kidney, and your choice of sliced chicken or pork, all harmoniously paired with your preferred rice noodles.

The addition of homemade chili oil and pickled jalapeños provides a spicy burst, delivering that extra kick! The flavorful combination keeps me coming back for more.

Venturing into something new this time, I got the fried fish cake. It proved to be incredibly tasty, although the only drawback is its slightly higher price for relatively smaller portions. But, it's definitely worth a try!

*Tip: Cash only.

12/27/2023
Vien Huong's No. 21 Chow Jew Ho Fun is a monthly ritual with my friend! Their exceptional chicken broth, light and clear, is unmatched. After trying other places, I keep coming back for its distinct flavor.

What makes Vien Huong special is the thoughtful addition of kidney, setting them apart. The dish includes shrimp, fish balls, pork balls, pork bits, kidney, and your choice of sliced chicken or pork—all perfectly paired with your preferred rice noodles.

Vien Huong adds a spicy burst with homemade chili oil and pickled jalapeños, providing that extra kick! A flavorful experience that keeps me hooked!

*Tip: Cash only.

11/27/2023
No. 21 Chow Jew Ho Fun takes center stage on their menu. This time, I tried their mixed noodles with ho fun and rice noodle. The chicken broth is a light and clear base for their impressive array of condiments such as chili, sriracha, hoisin, vinegar, and Vien Huong's house-made chili sauce. The dish features a generous medley of meats—shrimp, fish balls, pork balls, pork bits, kidney, and your choice of sliced chicken or pork—all served with your preferred type of rice noodles. The homemade chili oil and pickled jalapeños add a spicy burst and extra kick, creating a delightful flavor combination.

We also tried their Sauteed Kidney with Ginger Onion, which I really enjoyed and highly recommend if you are not apprehensive about eating pork kidney. The kidney is well-seasoned and flavorful, with a crunchy but not mushy texture. The onions complement the kidney really well, even when paired with the Chow Jew Ho Fun.

*Tip: Cash only.

10/23/2023
Vien Huong Restaurant is a hidden treasure. I revisited this place, and it's just as amazing as ever.

Their No.21 Chow Jew Ho Fun takes center stage on their menu. The chicken broth is light and clear, giving you the perfect canvas to season to your liking with an impressive array of condiments. They offer chili, sriracha, hoisin, vinegar, and, of course, Vien Huong's house-made chili sauce. This dish is a generous medley of meats, including shrimp, fish balls, pork balls, pork bits, kidney, and your choice of sliced chicken or pork, all served with your preferred type of rice noodles.

Their homemade chili oil adds a spicy burst of flavor, and the pickled jalapeños give your meal an extra kick, creating a delightful flavor combination.

*Tip: This restaurant is cash-only, so be sure to come prepared. The prices are incredibly reasonable. You'll be pleasantly surprised at how affordable it is. Not to mention, the service is lightning fast; I can finish my meal in about 15 minutes and be on my way. Parking can be a bit challenging, but it's a minor inconvenience for the fantastic food.

address: 3251 20th Ave Second Floor, San Francisco, CA 94132, United States

google.name: Tang Bar

top_reviews.content:
Honestly didn’t expect much walking in. We had originally planned to go to the Vietnamese place nearby, but it was empty while Tang Bar had a line out the door. The choice made itself.

And WOW! This is genuinely some of the best malatang I’ve had, better than places I’ve eaten at back in China. I got the savory mix (dry toss with Sichuan pepper oil), which was intensely numbing and incredibly fragrant. My mom got the regular malatang and felt the same way. People around us were packing up multiple portions to take home, some even finishing every last drop of the broth lol.

The ingredient selection is wide and everything looks fresh. The setup is clean and well-maintained. The only downside is the wait, usually 15+ minutes, but the place is packed for a reason.

I used to think the malatang spot near my school was the gold standard, and I was sad when it closed. Tang Bar is my new go-to now!

I loved it!! You can pick whatever you want but be careful they go by weight. All the meats were hecka fresh and it was just an overall great experience for my first time here.  That hot and sour soup is kicking. Time to try the hot hot. Have a nice day.

Um.... Maybe don't come hungry because the price of your bowl depends on it. I wasn't really trying to restrain myself and just got what would keep me content and my order costed about $30+ dollars for a weight of 1.75lbs. I selected the fresh fish broth and it was as white and creamy as expected although I still really enjoyed it. I know for a fact that I could have easily reached $50 if I wanted to be full full. I have never been to Tang Bar and decided to give it a try. I enjoy the concept of a build-your-own hotpot, but with my appetite, an AYCE hotpot restaurant is more worth it. You're also at the mall with a bunch of eateries and dessert spots! Save your stomach and get some matcha ice cream, acai bowl or boba if you have time and isn't full. You won't leave hungry.

I love being able to choose what you want in your meal, the idea is brilliant! I love that there are different levels of spicy, I had a mild level and it was just perfect to what I expected, everything is fresh and delicious! Not to mention, how luxurious this place looks, the details are amazing! Definitely a must try 💚

It was my first time having malatang and it was an awesome experience with wide variety of meats, seafood and veggies. All ingredients were fresh and broth was full of flavor.

It didn’t feel like we were in a mall at all, they’ve done a great job with this place. Highly recommend it.

reviews_snippets.content: "Food: 3.5/5 - The selection of meats, noodles, and veggies is good."
"Large variety of meat, seafood, vegetables and carbs options."

name: El Metate
address: 2406 Bryant St, San Francisco, CA 94110, United States

google.name: El Metate
google.address: 2406 Bryant St, San Francisco, CA 94110, United States
google.description: Upbeat outfit with a colorful vibe offering burritos, fish tacos & other Mexican classics.

top_reviews.content:
Really cool spot with a unique two-room setup (one for ordering, one for sitting). The open-door vibe and Mexican inspired decor give it a great atmosphere! The food was fresh and very tasty, though the portions are a little small for the price. Still, the quality is there and I’d definitely come back when I'm in SF again.
Heads up on parking: it can get tough during school drop off/pick-up hours since there's a school right across the street.

El Metate is a fantastic neighborhood joint serving delicious Mexican food. I've had their burritos before, which are tasty, but the real stars here are definitely the plates, especially the birria. It comes out piping hot with a generous pile of stewed, glistening birria, rice, your choice of beans, escabeche, cilantro, onions, and a stack of warm corn tortillas. I always go with refried beans, and I especially appreciate the escabeche as it is a must for me.

Everything tastes fresh and delicious, and I love mixing and matching ingredients to create different bites with each taco. The birria itself is incredibly flavorful and cooked just right, tender but still holding enough of its shape so it does not just fall apart. Especially post-COVID, I really appreciate taquerias and Mexican restaurants that have kept their salsa bars open, and Metate's is great. There are several options spanning different spice levels and flavor profiles, but my favorite is the cucumber salsa because it has the perfect balance of freshness, spiciness, crunch, and acidity.

Every order also comes with a side of their house made chips, which I love because they are a mix of corn and flour, which have such a unique puffy texture and, of course, they pair perfectly with all of the aforementioned salsas. The horchata is good if standard, but still a great way to wash everything down. The staff are friendly, and the place is fully self-serve, with ordering at the register, self-serve water, salsas, and napkins, plus bussing your own table when you are done.

Got the green salsa chicken enchiladas and they were phenomenal! They have a salsa bar with about 5-6 different salsas and even a fruit salsa . There's something here for everyone. The woman at the counter was also very friendly and helpful.

There is so much to say about this place but here are some highlights:
- The decor of this place is beautiful. Down to earth yet thoughtful and colorful.
- The chips are so creative. The puffy ones are amazing with beautiful color. I usually discard most of chips but I need to hunt down for them this time.
- So much variety of salsa and sauce. It is my first time having a warm salsa as well. It is incredible! It is such a service mind to provide all accommodations for all tastebuds.
- The food itself is big and delicious. My quesadilla is packed with carnitas. I wish it can be a bit more crispy but it is also fulfilling. My friend got a seafood plate and it can feed 2 people. All dishes we got are under 20 dollars, which is a rare steal in SF.
In short, this is my new go-to spot for Mexican food in my beloved San Francisco!

The salsas and meats are excellent!  They taste fresh and falvorful.  I really liked the house red salsa and cucumber salsa, while my wife liked the tomatillo and chipotle salsas.  The interior is beautiful with nice music at a balanced volume.  The only aesthetic detractor is the AI-generated poster on the door.  Finally, the prices are high ($15.75 basic burrito and $18.75 tamales plate) plus 4% credit card fee, tip, and tax.  So it's up to you if the nice salsas and interior are worth 20-30% more than an average taqueria.

top_reviews.content:
This is a nice little spot for a solid breakfast sandwich. The menu isn't super varied but what they do have they specialize in and seem to do well. You might guess from the name: bacon.

We all got variations of breakfast sandwiches and they all did the job. Well constructed, hearty, salty, bacony.
The bacon jam is more like pork put through a blender... But that's not a bad thing in my book.
The coffee was good, not amazing but better than average.

The room itself is no frills. Minimal decoration, just there to get the job done. Unfortunately Porky, the little coin operated pig ride, seems to have been decommissioned :(

The food truck dropped by Oyster Point today. Honestly, I'm not particularly impressed. Food is average. I got the Banh Mi and the Porky Fries. The Banh Mi was supposed to have picked vegetables, they weren't. At least not in my sandwich. It was spicy, but lacked flavor. The fries were dry, meaning the pulled pork lacked moisture. There was hardly any bacon and I didn't see any pork belly. Overall, disappointed. I guess if the fries had cheese, it would help tie everything together. Ambiance, was great, but since they're a food truck they can't help with the windy location.

Love everything this place makes! The NYC bagel, the Porky Breakfast Burrito and the Porky Breakfast Sandwich are all just so good! The Porky versions add Pulled Pork which makes the burritos/sandwiches into meals. The Bagel is a good lighter-option.

However the place is really quite slow and needs more people working there. It was a single person when I was there, and that resulted in longer times.

Was visiting sf and looking for a breakfast spot and stumbled on this place. One of the best breakfast sandwiches I've ever had. The bread, the bacon, the egg, cheese, bacon jam are just excellent. The staff was especially nice and very helpful. The interior was clean and interesting. Absolute must try.

There’s a reason it’s called the best breakfast in SF!! So good, you’ll want to try everything on the menu. Classic breakfast sandwich and burrito, you can’t go wrong. Don’t be afraid of the weekend brunch rush, they are such efficient and the line is never too long.

top_reviews.content:
An absolute gem of a restaurant with plenty of seating and kind staff.

You order at the counter first and if you're indecisive, never fear! The staff will provide you with recommendations!

They have great deals for lunch specials and I'd recommend #4 but the staff will recommend #5. There's also free chai for customers and note that it is self-service, but there's plenty of seating!

(Disclosure) We enjoy Indian food but are not Indian.

This place is unique (half self serve/half sit down).  Orders are taken at the counter.  For dine in orders, you self serve the plates, utensils, water and napkins.  Dont forget the free chai.  Main dishes are served table side.  Payments are made at the cashier.

👉 Halal
👉 Very Large serving amount compared to other Indian restaurants and the Man in the photo serves the food is the most humble and very charming human being.

🍛 Authentic Indian & Pakistani Cuisine with rich, aromatic flavors.

🍗 Chicken Vindaloo: Spicy, tangy, and a fan favorite for its unique yellow curry.amount perfect

🐐 Goat Curry: Tender, flavorful, and perfectly spiced.amount perfect

🥖 Naan Varieties: Especially garlic naan — soft, fluffy, and ideal for dipping.

🌱 Vegetarian Options: Pakora is sooo crunchy Delicious .
Other tasty choices like malai kofta and chole bhature.

🏠 Casual Atmosphere: Simple dining room focused on great food, not fancy decor.

🚀 Fast & Friendly Service: Staff are very welcoming and efficient. Very Family friendly

📦 Delivery & Takeout: Available on DoorDash, Uber Eats, and local pickup.

💰 Generous Portions: Filling meals at reasonable prices.

📍 Convenient Elmwood Location: Easy to find and great for locals and visitors.

A must-try for flavorful curries and authentic South Asian dishes in Berkeley!

The flavors of this place are decent. The prices are better. The ambiance is great. There's lots of tables and seating. The customer service is really nice. I came with kids and they brought kid friendly cups of mango lassi for us. It was a great place to stop on college ave. They forgot two things from our order and I couldn't tell if they charged us but because they didnt give and itemized receipt but ..you know ... I'll be back. A great place to have lunch or dinner. The Malai kofta was such a treat. Oh apparently they have mozzarella stuffed naan lol. Yum

I love this place. I always get the keema naan for lunch. Only $8 bucks and I can eat it for two meals if I’m feeling snackish. Complimentary chai for sit down. Feels like home.

It is also in such a beautiful building…so gorgeous inside.

top_reviews.content: The food was so great, service very good people. They made sure we were taken care of. Talked to us, part of experience. Shahnoor, Gagan and Bhola Bhai (Man with Dimple) are best at their work. Blessings for all.

Found this place on Reddit after searching up “best Indian lunch buffet in east bay” and it exceeded expectations! As someone who’s always jealous of the Indian food options in South Bay, I’m so grateful that I now have a go to option in the east bay! Variety of food was perfect, each dish was flavorful, the environment and service was relaxed, and the highlight was the naan (best naan I’ve ever had)! It’s only $20 as well!! I don’t think some of the past negative reviews are relevant anymore and I’ll certainly be back.

I mean wow, how could a business this good be so under the radar? I personally was astonished at how flavorful and pure the food tasted. Every single bite felt like a masterclass in fresh ingredients and culinary care.
It is incredibly rare to find a place that prioritizes quality over hype. The flavors are vibrant, the presentation is thoughtful, and the passion behind the cooking shines through in every dish. This is hands-down the best culinary experience I have had in a long time.
Do yourself a favor and skip your usual spot tonight. This hidden gem deserves to be everyone's new obsession, and I will definitely be returning.

Absolutely amazing experience at Swad Indian Cuisine Restaurant & Full Bar! The place is very clean and hygienic, and the staff are extremely friendly and welcoming. Service was on time, and the food was served hot and fresh, full of authentic flavors. Every dish tasted wonderful, and the overall atmosphere was great. Truly a marvelous experience—a must-visit restaurant. Highly recommended!

The tandoori sizzlers were the highlight — perfectly spiced, juicy, and served sizzling hot just the way I like it. You can really taste the authentic flavors. On top of that, the service was top-notch. The staff was super friendly, welcoming, and made me feel right at home. Definitely coming back again soon!

top_reviews.content:
Shake Shack has been remarkably consistent between locations in SF and LA we have been to in both quality and speed and this one aligned well with those expectations.

I placed an order on the kiosk inside on a moderately busy weeknight. There was ample seating and we got bacon cheeseburger and a shackburger, cheese fries, fries, and a limited time chocolate toasted marshmallow shake. Forgoing to the soft drinks for ones we have at home really adds up here. The order took just a touch over 10 minutes, although I was pretty out of it after an insane week, so maybe more like 15, not remarkable compared to other shake shacks.

The burgers where hot and properly configured and the fries had that glassy crunch after a 5 or 6 minute drive. The shake hadn't melted either and had a great consistency and a discernable s'mores like marshmallow flavor. My one nitpick would be the cheese fries had woefully little sauce on them and I swear they used to just give you a little cup of it to dip...

You get what you pay for at shake shack and while the price is on the higher side I've yet to have a bad experience. I count this location among the other solid ones we've been too.

This shake shack could do better. I had to wait almost 15 minutes for my order and the lines are very long and slow. The food is good but could do a better job with the cooking. Overall I’m satisfied but this is embarrassing with the long wait for my order!!! Shake shack I should not wait long for the food!!!!!

This shake shack is just decent!!!
The chicken and fries were good but we had to wait while for the food. I had a satisfied experience. One thing i would like to be improved is the speed of the food being served.

This shake shack location has always been okay up until today. The fries are barely filled - I’m not sure if their containers are bigger or they’ve always been this way but it was a big visual difference. *see pic below*

Since when did burgers for to go orders just come in the wrapper? All the other locations always puts the food in a burger box. My chicken shack was stacked on top of my shack stack so all the sauce transferred over to the top bun. It was a mess.

I was so excited for the French onion shack stack BUT my portobello mushroom was barely cooked. The cheese was not even melted and it was just one big glob. The whole point of the shack stack is to enjoy the gooey melted cheese. I left feeling like I wasted so many calories for an expensive mediocre fast food meal.

I've eaten at this Shake Shack location several times, and unfortunately, this visit wasn't quite what I'm used to. The bun was soggy and greasy, which took away from the overall experience.

That said, this is still a great location if you're looking for a place to grab a bite. It's conveniently located at Stonewood Galleria, where there are plenty of other restaurants and things to do. If Shake Shack isn't your thing, you have lots of other dining options nearby, along with plenty of entertainment.

Overall, the location is great, but I hope the food quality is back to the standard I've experienced on my previous visits

top_reviews.content: Honest review as a Korean. I had Gan Zazang and Tang Su Yook. Both were way too salty. Tang su yook is super dry and barely has any meat. Food preparation was slow. Gan Zazang sauce is ok but very salty.

This Korean-style Chinese restaurant located in Oakland, California, offers a variety of delightful dishes such as Tangsu-yuk (sweet and sour pork), fried dumplings, Jjajang-myon (black bean paste noodles), and Jjampong (spicy seafood noodles). The fried dumplings were exceptional, boasting a crispy exterior and a succulent, well-seasoned filling of pork and vegetables. The sweet and sour pork was equally impressive, with a delightful blend of sweetness in the sauce complementing the perfectly fried pork strips. While the noodle dishes were enjoyable, the texture of the noodles did not quite meet expectations, lacking the desired hand-stretched quality. The green chili sweet potato noodles provided a tasty kick with hot chili. The service was excellent, though there is room for improvement in the restaurant's overall ambiance to elevate the dining experience.

The service was pretty standard. I wasn't really expecting this style of jajang mian maybe because this one is more Korean and not as Chinese like I'm used to, or this is the more traditional kind? The noodles were pretty chewy which was fun but the sauce was too much and I'm not sure what the flavor was but it was maybe too overwhelming with not enough substance or toppings in it.

It’s truly a gem of the bay. This is probably the best Chinese/korean food in the bay. The jjajangmyeon, jjajang and tangsuyuk is all we come for. Sadly, the last time we visited, the current owners of the restaurant are retiring and handing off the business to a new owner. I can’t say it’ll ever be the same. They’re training the current staff right now, but I don’t if it’ll ever feel the same…

Home-made style Korean Chinese dishes that are yummy and in huge portion.   I am impressed with how the family runs the restaurant with such energy and high quality.   Given the size of the dishes, I think the price is reasonable.

top_reviews.content: I was recently in downtown Oakland on business and there is a lack of decent restaurants downtown. This place is somewhat of a war zone actually especially at night. But I was lucky to find this little Chinese vegetarian restaurant in Chinatown. I ate here every day for lunch.  It’s sort of a dive which I actually liked but the food is great and the service is good and it seems clean if outdated and messy.  I would highly recommend eating here or even delivery.  It’s excellent Chinese food with a good variety of dishes and you can have a tasty meal without having to kill our innocent animal friends.

They have a very wide selection of tasty vegetarian dishes. The vegan meat, eggplant, mushrooms, and veggies were all very well prepared. Atmosphere is cozy and quiet, and pricing was very affordable too. Definitely a good place to check out around the Chinatown area.
I ordered takeout from here for my family and my mom (who eats meat) apparently couldn’t tell that the shrimp wasn’t actual shrimp. All the food was very good.

⭐️ Food 5/5
⭐️ Service 5/5
⭐️ Ambiance 5/5

I have been looking for a go-to Chinese restaurant for many years and this will definitely be my new spot!

Not only was the food absolutely delicious, the service was warm, friendly, and polite. I was happily surprised that everything that we ordered had the perfect flavor and texture. I have been vegetarian for over 10 years and I will say this has to be one of my best experiences for both vegetarian food and Chinese food.

Both of my children are meat eaters, and could not even tell the chicken wasn’t actual chicken! They have specific taste buds and this place had my kids happy and wanting more! Also, the portions and pricing is good. We had lots of leftovers even with full bellies ☺️

Thank you to the staff for your kindness and delicious food! We will definitely be back for many visits and lots more food 💗

We came here for Meatless Monday. My daughter and I often try to eat less meat whenever we can. This place is one of our favorites whenever we are in the area.

The lunch specials prices have gone up throughout the years BUT it is still a steal for the price. Since we had it many years ago, one thing I've noticed is that they keep the lunch meals simple. Their lunch specials always come with soup, egg roll, 2 scoops of rice, and the main entrée of your choice. We also got hot tea on a cold day.

What we ordered: Veggie Sesame Chicken and Veggie Mongolian Beef, both with white rice (but you can opt for brown rice). This meal came with hot and sour soup.

* My go-to are: Veggie Chicken General Tao, Veggie Pork Sweet and Sour Sauce.

Overall, both entrée were really good and we will come back for more.

reviews_snippets.content: "I wish the menu included crispy fried tofu options in the main dishes."
"Hands down no one can beat the price for the quality of the food here!"

name: Jay’s Grill
address: 1400 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94102, United States

google.name: Jay’s Grill
google.address: 1400 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94102, United States

top_reviews.content:
Stopped by after checking the positive reviews and they were all that an more.
The owner was very welcoming and helpful. Helped me decide on my dinner in a minute and brought out the soup in another 2. Thought the lentil soup was great, the star of the show was Jay's dinner plate and the kebabs.
Fresh, fragrant and delicious overall with the complimentary hummus, garlic sauce and the small salad. Will definitely be back

Visited here for lunch, ordered chicken kebab with fries and falafel plate. It also comes with side salad. You order at counter and food will be served at the table. Service was very good. Food was very tasty. Highly recommend this place.

Great discovery!!
Went on a Thursday night after a show at the Orpheum (two blocks away) around 9:45pm. Would be a great option after the Opera, Ballet and Symphony shows nearby.

We had two smoothies: strawberry mango and strawberry banana, both delicious. We also got the Blue Cheese burger to share that comes with fig jam and a decent side of fries. The burger was so tasty and flavorful. Food was so good that we devoured it without taking any pictures but now we have the perfect excuse to go back.

The place is clean, spacious and well kept. In addition, Jay was at the counter and he was very nice and kind to explain the multiple food options. Really looking forward to be back soon!

After finishing a meeting near Market and Van Ness, we were kind of hungry. My friend suggested we try some Hayes Valley restaurants, but they were all packed and noisy, not to mention too expensive. I suggested Jay's Grill because I walk past it every so often, and the menu looked good. There is a variety of Mediterranean dishes, including vegetarian and low-carb ones. Although busy, we got a nice table by the window. My friend ordered the beef kabob plate with rice, and I got a Caesar Salad with chicken. Our order was taken quickly and with courtesy. The plates were brought to our table within just a few minutes; faster than we'd expected. My salad was amazing! The dressing was on the side, and they gave me plenty of it. The chicken was tender and flavorful. This is one of the better Caesar salads I've had in San Francisco, even though it wasn't very expensive. I should also mention that it was BIG! Despite being hungry, I wasn't able to finish it. Our server brought us to-go boxes with a smile. I look forward to coming back here and trying something else from their menu. My only minor complaint is with some of the other patrons rather than the restaurant itself. One table was being especially loud. Luckily they left shortly after we got served.

I was really excited to try this spot since I love a good chicken shawarma wrap, but it ended up being a letdown. The $15 wrap was surprisingly tiny, overly greasy, and barely had any chicken. And what little chicken there was… just wasn’t good.

reviews_snippets.content: "Super friendly staff, great food, excellent service!"

top_reviews.content: Very cool place. We have nothing like this in Montana that I have seen. Thanks to the nice man working! He was very patient with us. We had no idea what we were doing and he walked us through the whole process, very informative, very pleasant. It was a great anniversary dinner!

This place is great, we came in on a Saturday around 2p, got seated fast, our broths and first serve of meats came out immediately, and we loved the variety at the self serve area. Lots of veggies, fish, seafood, sauces, etc.

The broths were tasty, the meats were nice and fresh, everything was so good, and there was a person who kept around in case we needed anything 😊
90 minutes all you can eat for $30 is not bad at all. The meat is decent quality and honestly the broths taste really good. They don’t dilute over time and honestly taste better the more you cook it.

I enjoyed the food at this hot pot restaurant. Most of the meat and vegetable items were pretty good. I also liked the individual hot pots for each person. However, the ordering process was very confusing. We thought we had to pay extra for the meat, but apparently the cost was all you can eat for everything. You just have to order the meat separately. The service was, on the one hand, good (this guy showed up and gave us some pointers on how to order), but on the other hand, not so great (they never brought our egg that we ordered). The price was affordable and a good deal. The atmosphere left a fair amount to be desired – the no back stools were uncomfortable, and the tables were jammed together.

Full bar with plenty of appetizer choices, sauce station and plenty of veges. However, the seafood selection and meat quality are not the best. Hope they can offer more decent quality meat selections in the future. Floor is sticky and little be slippery which is not really safe for a hot pot place and customers need to walk to the serving station which creates high traffic during peak hours.

reviews_snippets.content: "The broth and beef/pork/tofu ordered from seat."

top_reviews.content:
The servers and service here is lovely! They’re so patient and friendly!

This was my first time here and was seated right away for dinner on a weekday. There was a HAPPY HOUR FOOD menu and we took advantage of that and ordered the Momo’s (dumplings) and the ribs, and both were delicious!!

We got the butter chicken with rice and it was creamy and delicious 🤤!!

The restaurant has plenty of open space and restrooms were pretty clean.

The hard part was parking as street parking isn’t so easy around here and there’s no lot. Storefront parking could also be difficult during busy hours as it is a busy street.

I’d definitely come back for the food and service!!

First time trying this type of cuisine, was not disappointed. Service was great, nice atmosphere. I ordered the creamy chicken tikka masala, garlic naan. Great portions, had to save some for later. Recommend giving it a try.

This is a beautiful restaurant. From the interior to the staff, everything is excellent. I asked about their bar menu, and they told me it was crafted with the help of one of the oldest bars in town. That showed me they truly want the best for their customers. We arrived early for dinner around 5:00 p.m., and it was just beginning to fill up. By the time we left around 6:30 p.m., there were people waiting for tables. It was a great experience. I rarely leave reviews, but this restaurant is truly one of a kind.

Tasted better the next day, but flavor combo didn't work for me. Noodles were bland (lacked salt), they tasted much better with soy sauce. Chicken was OK, but not really worth it compared to other similar food options in the area.

Everest Kitchen, my go-to spot for craft cocktails, has undergone a remarkable transformation within a year of its full bar opening. It has transformed into a haven that offers authentic food and the best cocktails.

Among the exquisite creations, the Amaretto Sour and Jameson Mule stood out as my favorites. They were expertly crafted to perfection.

reviews_snippets.content: "Prices are a little higher, but food is good, rice included, plus a lentil soup!"

top_reviews.content:
Happened upon this place while I was walking alone in the neighborhood running an errand. I live in SF and hardly ever come to Oakland. (i know, terrible)

This place was DELICIOUS. Tried the “sampler dinner” (it was not actually called this, but I forget what it was called) and it was delicious!! My favorite was the chicken (spiciest), then beef, then the lamb (i would never order the lamb, wasn’t bad I just love spice).

Can’t wait to come back with friends!

OH! and i loved the people who work there, super helpful and friendly!

It was my first time trying Eritrean food and I was very surprised at the similarities to Indian cuisine. The food and service were both excellent. I would highly recommend the  vegetarian injera plate to anyone coming here. My friends and I had a great time having lunch here.

First time trying Eritrean/ Ethiopian food and really had a great experience here. Came right around early dinner and found the restaurant not too packed. Service was friendly and welcoming, and the facilities were nice. Tried what may have been most traditional- honey wine, spiced tea. We also ate the meat combo (which was great since we weren't exactly sure what we wanted) and the beef tar tar which impressed us a lot! Overall, it was really fun to just get in there and scarf it all down. I found the lamb and tar tar to be exceptional. The beef had an excellent "stew" savory taste to its finished and I only found it a bit challenging to enjoy the chicken with injera since the chicken was on the bone (which I like, but not experienced enough to take advantage of it). We ate so much food and the price/ quality was wonderful. Great eating experience and looking forward to my next!

Well-remodeled interior, dark wood finishes make for an intimate dining experience.

A wide selection of Eritrean classics — vegan, vegetarian and meat.

Manageable portions, a wonderful place to gather for an intimate meal. Traditional dining available in the back of the dining room.

This is the best Eritrean/Ethiopian restaurant. The owner is such a humble and kind person - he welcomes us every time we stop by and goes out of his way to make sure we’re comfortable. The food is ofc always delicious! I am a big fan!

reviews_snippets.content: "Place smells sweet and really nice , food was amazing and service was great ."
