top_reviews.content: Went to visit this place in the lovely Haight with my friend! We ordered the smoked salmon tartine and the prosciutto tartine, as well as strawberry lemonade and fresh orange juice, and we were blown away! It was so delicious and flavourful, and prices were so fair as well. The ambience of the outdoor seating was also amazing, and our service was so sweet and kind. 10/10 would definitely come back again!

As I was strolling along Haight-Ashbury, my hunger brought me here. The Eggs Benedict and potatoes were delicious. The side of fruit was very refreshing. My server, Eugenia, made the whole experience even better with her kindness and positive attitude. Highly recommend!

This is a really nice upscale café that had been on my list for a while, and I’m glad I finally stopped by. One of the best parts is that they serve their brunch menu all the way until 7 pm, which is perfect if you’re into breakfast style food at any time of the day.

I tried the avocado scrambled toast with salmon. The sourdough was fresh and nicely crunchy, the salmon tasted fresh without being overly salty, and the combination with eggs and avocado worked really well together. I also had the yogurt parfait, and their homemade granola stood out for not being overly sweet, which I appreciated.

The cortado was flavorful with a solid coffee profile. The space itself is spacious with a great vibe, and the server was kind and accommodating with customizations. Definitely a spot I’d come back to and explore more of the menu.
Got the Brisket Breakfast Wrap, and it was incredible. Friends got the French Toast and Eggs Benedict, both also loved their meals.

Brioche Bakery Coffee – 10/10!
Absolutely amazing experience from start to finish. I had the tomato basil soup, Royal Benedict eggs with fresh fruit, and a cappuccino — everything was top-notch and bursting with flavor. The food was fresh, beautifully presented, and simply delicious. The staff were wonderful and made the visit even better. The back patio made it very atmospheric and relaxing. Highly recommend this place for anyone who wants a perfect breakfast or brunch!

top_reviews.content:
The dim sum is decent at this restaurant located right off the Foothill Boulevard exit on 580. Steamed items like Shrimp dumplings,siu mai, beef globes, black bean spareribs are well done and generously sized. Their chow fun is pretty good too. Fried taro dumplings lacked any flavor.

Oriental tea house is in a building that used to be Jerrys Pancake Parade back in the 60s and 70s. That explains the old school diner, 60s style restaurant decor.

Prices are definitely lower than some of the newer flagship dim sum restaurants that have recently opened. I would say you get 15% more for 10% less.

Waitresses were polite and helpful.
Note that they automatically add a 15% service charge to the bill. Also they might also charge for items that they tell you "they ran out of". Basically inspect the bill closely before you pay.

They have a decent size parking lot but it might get full if the restaurant is busy.
The location is in east oakland so exercise the necessary precautions.

Overall decent value and the steamed di. Sum items are pretty good. Perhaps we went in with low expectations. It is worth a visit if you're in the area. We feel the same.

I recently visited OTH and was blown away by their delicious dim sum. Every bite was a flavor explosion in my mouth!

The menu was extensive, and I tried several dishes, but some of my favorites included the shrimp dumplings, pork buns, and egg tarts. The shrimp dumplings were perfectly steamed with a delicate wrapper that didn't overpower the juicy filling. The pork buns were fluffy and moist, with a generous amount of tender pork inside. The egg tarts were rich and creamy, with a buttery crust that crumbled in my mouth.

The service was also excellent. The waitstaff was friendly and attentive, and they helped us navigate the menu to find the best dishes. The restaurant was clean and had a pleasant atmosphere, making for a lovely dining experience.

It's clear that the chefs take pride in their craft and use only the freshest ingredients to create authentic and delicious dishes. I can't wait to go back and try more.
Tasty and flavor is 3/5 in comparison to the Chinese food of the largest Chinese population cities. Portion of the honey walnut shrimp is outrageously small. Other items are okay
Have not been to this restaurant for years. Dimsum is good but the classic steamed dishes like Siu-mai, Hargaw, Chicken Feet, Ribs are a bit pricey. They also add 15% service fee on the bill.
It's hard to find a place that does 功夫茶 (gongfu tea) and finding one nearby that also does dimsum has been a delight. The food is pretty good and very affordable for lunch.

top_reviews.content:
First time visit. We thought we'd give it a try after driving by a billion times. Your basic Chinese steam table with the added menu if you want to dine in, They have a whole bunch of dining tables for that purpose, although the food will be served to you as takeout on a tray. Not a problem. Staff is very courteous and friendly, I think they are the main asset.
The food. Lemon chicken was really lemon chicken. My God what a concept. Usually it's some horrible syrupy thing but very much lemony tasty and the chicken was tender. No chicken jerky.
Really good. Vegetable fried rice, fluffy and tasty with veggies.
String bean tofu isa little problematic. It did taste good but a third of the container was sauce. Other than that it was a nice experience. Plus a soda and a $3 tip, the whole thing came to about 42 bucks. They have four different combo plates ranging from the $9 range to $12 range, they also have two egg rolls for $1.99 If you're looking for a quick bite to grab, I would say do it.
Steam table also had some nice veggie dishes that I didn't get to, broccoli, beef and a veggie and shrimp. That'll be for next time. All in all pretty decent and we will probably return now and then. We don't usually eat much Chinese up in the San Leandro area, we're usually at Porky's or somewhere else. But this was good. Nice surprise

You definitely get your money's worth and the food is awesome.
I live in Newark. I drive about 30 minutes to get there but it's worth it. Every time I order something there it's always fresh. I've tried most of their items there, and everything is perfect. Staff is super nice and quick.

Greeting everyone. I use to eat at this place. There honey walnut chicken was delicious.  Besides never wiping down their tables and the flies circulating through the joint, the food was pretty good. The reason why I stopped eating here is because the last time I ate there, I was finishing my lunch and took my tray to their garbage (which hadn't been emptied from the night before) and a HUGE RAT jumped out of the can!!!!!!. Makes me wonder what in the HELL had I been eating all this damn time. I hope it wasn't Honey Walnut Rat.

I've only eaten here once.  It was ok... It seems like a lot of ppl like it. The chowmein was saucy and delicious.  Eating there only sucks because there's a lot of flies around, but overall, it was ok.

Came in for dinner and was greeted by the nicest most helpful lady ever. I told her I had food allergies and she made sure to ask the cook about all the ingredients to make sure I was okay. She even kept offering me samples to make sure I enjoyed what I ordered. This woman made my day, so sweet and such a great attitude which I find rare these days. Not to mention she packed that food box all she could and at a very reasonable price. Happy I came in as I hadn’t  came here since I was a kid. Not sure if she is always working but non the less she is appreciated. Glad to have this place in the community, food was delicious

Steak, egg and home fries were good. The steak had more fat than I like. My coffee cup was always full. Kim runs the front of the house and is such a wonderful person.
Absolutely perfect. The food was delicious (I had the waffle, bacon, browns, egg, and coffee; all amazing) and the staff is incredibly kind and genuinely caring. I'll definitely be coming back!

Kim and her husband are the best! This is my favorite breakfast diner in San Francisco. The food is always amazing and the service is perfection. Kim is the most kind and genuine server ever. If you're in San Francisco and want a great breakfast, lunch, a snack or an amazing mimosa come to jims on mission.
One of the best breakfast places i’ve been to! Very nice servers and fast service. The toast is especially good and great music playing. Overall a great experience!

We were a group of 6 adults plus 2 loud & restless toddlers. We were immediately greeted like family and seated in a spacious booth that allowed us to corral the kids. We quickly had coffee, ice water and orange juice (& 2 to-go cups with lids for toddler juice). Mrs. Kim knows our son who stops in frequently and was excited to meet his family. The famous green hot & garlicky sauce came out with the second pour of coffee, quickly followed by our steaming hot eggs, hash browns & various salty breakfast meats. Topped with the green sauce and a third cup of coffee, it was delish. One of us had the corned beef hash that was excellent, especially with green sauce. Did I mention how great the green sauce is?!

Had awesome chicken satay, shrimp pad thai, coconut curry with catfish. Cozy place, friendly host!

top_reviews.content: I was blown away with how tasty the food was in this restaurant. Our group ordered quite a few things on the menu. I tried everything and loved every single item. I have never had Peruvian food before so I have no point of reference for Peruvian food. But…I’ve been eating food my whole life so I am what is known as an expert eater. The food at Franco’s was objectively amazing! I’m so glad I went here and I’ll definitely be back. Highly recommended!!!

The food is fantastic! It’s a no frills local Peruvian restaurant with the classics. We got the classic ceviche which was incredibly fresh and packed a nice spicy punch. The octopus was exceptional! The lomo soltado and roast chicken were hommie and comforting! The fried chicken bites from the apps menu was a perfectly crispy and lightly breaded. Come here for the classics without expecting a ton of fanfare on decor and service. This is going to be our new go to for a meal out with the kids!
Super authentic Peruvian cuisine, we love coming here. The portions are generous. We always get the ají de gallina and lomo saltado. Also some Salvadoran food. Would recommend to anyone!

Everything was delightful, from the wonderful service to the amazing tasty food. El pollo en brasa without doubt is a dish worth trying, never tried chicken like this but definitely now it's one of my favorite dishes! :)

The food was very tasty and the portion sizes aren't too small! I hear it gets busy for dinner, but it wasn't too busy at lunchtime.

top_reviews.content: Great food. Outstanding guest service. The orange hot sauce was perfect! Me and my son walked in due to my Amtrack train being delayed. Not disappointed at all! Definitely will be back.

First time trying this spot and ordered takeout. My food was ready on time and the pick up was easy. Chips and salsa were included with my California burrito. I got the asada and it was delicious. Ambience seemed nice and there was a cantina we didn’t try so I’ll definitely be coming back.

Great casual Mexican spot! The tacos, burgers, chicken sandwich and fries are delicious, and the space is clean and bright. It's a fantastic location for a big group looking for a relaxed meal. Don't skip the fries!"

I got the California Burrito with Carnitas and everything in it. It was a very well-packed burrito. Nicely sealed tortilla and wrapped in aluminum foil. I didn’t have to rip apart layers and layers of aluminum foil since there was only one. The fries in the burrito are crinkle cut so there’s an extra nice texture to it when you bite into it. Everything we ordered yesterday was salty and a little overcooked. The atmosphere was good. The service was fair. This place is great for a Chinese quick to go option they have a steam table with chinese food just pick and choose. It is affordable and food is good for the price in my opinion. I would recommend it.

Bomb Chinese food! Great visible selection. Everything tasted relatively fresh, tons of flavor. And they pack it in good, large portions. Orange chicken and the fried wings are great. Chicken fried rice was excellent as well. I’d definitely eat here again.

As a local you should stop by and try it out.

top_reviews.content:
I've been eating at Tony's Pizza in SF, the OG GOAT location, since 2012.

This was my first time trying the Slice House in San Leandro.

We ordered the Motorhead pizza, which was really good. All of the toppings were fresh and tasty. The ricotta made the pizza pop! Super good! The dough was cooked perfectly. Nearly everything on the menu can be veganized especially with using their faux meat. There is already a lot of plant-based options available to choose from. We went with their Vegetarian Dim Sum ($13), Mock Chicken Congee ($10), Rice "Tamales" as they called them ($6 for two), and an order of their Kung Pao Faux Chicken.

The congee, cha siu bao from the dim sum platter, and their 'tamales' were all fantastic. It reminded me of what I used to eat back in the day. Their kung pao could've been a bit spicier but I appreciated being able to enjoy it with their plant-based chicken, which seems to be made from seitan.

Some of the vegan faux meat items though weren't as exciting. The Chicken Siu Mai was the biggest letdown and I wouldn't get that again, but everything else where they used the faux chicken was great.

Aside from the food, service here was incredible. Everyone was super sweet and checked up on us often.

Fun fact - they were once ranked the best restaurant in all of the U.S. by a publication and you can find their accolade proudly displayed inside.

top_reviews.content:
I really liked the pizza and the crust was just like KSA type pizza.

I enjoyed the pizza but I’ve had better Roman-style pizzas. I like my pizza without cheese and that means that the tomato sauce must be top-notch and seasoned well for the pizza to be good, but theirs was a little lacking in salt and just in general not enough on the bread. I might be wrong but they also use pre-baked bases, which is not unusual for Roman pinsa, but I personally prefer when they bake it and then add tomato sauce and ingredients immediately after baking to do the second baking (I’m from italy, I get annoying) instead of just prebaking all the bases you need for a night. With all this said, my pinsa rossa with roasted potatoes was good enough for a 4/5, but the real problem I had was with a specific part of the bathroom. The toilet brush (photo attached) was absolutely disgusting and for me that is enough to never want me to visit again.

On Sunday, August 16th, 2026, I ate at Pinsa Rosa in SF.

I had high hopes for this place but it truly fell short in so many ways.

The restaurant is located on Filmore Street. Parking was beyond difficult to find. That's not the restaurants fault but we literally parked over 5 minutes away and several blocks from the restaurant.

It really makes me question social media influencers' pallette because I saw so many great food reviews on Pinsa Rosa but in my opinion the food was mediocre and nothint special. People were saying it was the best Roman-style pizza they've ever eaten. I do believe Pinsa Rosa at one point was ranked #4 in the world which is shocking to me and I'll explain why. The pizza is supposed to be healthier for you because they use a unique sourdough blend that is fermented for 72 hours. The dough is supposed to be lighter and airier compared to traditional pizza. I'll break down my opinion below on their pizza.

Here's what we ordered. We started off with the Arancini $12 and La Porchetta $20. The La Porchetta was highly recommend by social media influencers and several of them claimed it was the best pork they've ever eaten. They are bold and super crazy for making a claim like that because the La Porchetta barely had any flavor and the pork didn't taste high quality. The burrata cheese and olive oil tasted terrible and was beyond cold. The bread served with the dish was hard and didn't taste good either. This dish was honestly not worth and it's hard pass. Do yourself a favor and don't order this dish. The Arancini was really good. The flavor was on point and the melted cheese, rice and the breading on the outside of the Arancini complemented one another very well. We also ordered the Lasagna Bolognese $22. The Lasagna was good. It wasn't the best I've ever eaten but it's worth ordering. It tasted like Stouffer's lasagna. Really basic. On to the pizzas. We ordered the Pepperoni e Sausage Pinsa $23 and the Summer Crush Pinsa $25. The Pepperoni and Sausage tasted good and had good flavor. The red sauce tasted off. It was sour. The pizza dough was really hard and difficult to chew. It literally cut up my gums and roof of my mouth. I honestly prefer regular or traditional pizza dough than Roman-style pizza dough. There was nothing special about the taste of Pinsa Rosa's pizza dough. The Summer Crush Pinsa came with peaches, nectarines, burrata cheese, prosciutto and hot honey. I wanted to like this pizza and it sounded so good especially mixing sweet and savory foods together, but it fell short as well and didn't deliver. The pizza dough was cold and the pizza overall just lacked flavor. It was average at best. And to top things off, I found an eye lash on the pizza. I told and showed our waiter and he offered to have another pizza made and the pizza was comped. But you know how it is, after seeing a hair or something like that in or on hour food, you loose your appetite.

The restaurant itself is very small. There's only one bathroom available. There's bar and outdoor seating. We choose to sit inside.

Our waiter Niti was excellent. He was very nice and down to earth. He had a great attitude and was kind.

Like I said before, I was looking forward to eating at this restaurant and wanted to like it but in all honesty, I would not recommend eating here to anyone. It's all about the food when it comes to eating at a restaurant for me. Even if the service is terrible if the food is good I'll go and eat there. There was no wow factor for any of the dishes and there are plenty of better pizza/Italian infused restaurants in SF and the Bay Area. Don't waste your time here.

The La Piccante and the Carbonara were delicious! Very light, airy, and tasty crust. The best pizza I've had in SF!

September 2026:

Super friendly seating is available outside and an upper level. Only about six spots to sit inside but I had no problem getting a spot.

Really good cheeseburger. I was pleasantly surprised by how tasty it was. Not greasy, super juicy, and the cheese is melted just right. Bun was perfectly toasted as well. Very friendly lady at the counter. They have a great lunch special deal too.

We came here by chance while waiting for my mother-in-law’s medical appointment to finish. We ordered the California Burger, 3 Wings (mild sauce) with fries and strawberry milkshake. The food was great.

It has a small seating capacity (3 small tables inside that can seat 2 per table and 2 tables outside which can seat about 4 per table).

Overall, a good place to eat.

top_reviews.content:
I’ve been here many times, and it’s one of the best Sichuan restaurants around. You can ask the staff to adjust the spice level—I always order my dishes extra spicy.

My favorite dish is the Sautéed Beef & Asparagus in Black Pepper Sauce. The beef is incredibly tender and flavorful, and it’s a must-try. I also highly recommend the Pickled Fish with live fish—the fish slices are amazingly fresh and have a great texture. The Cold Noodles with Chicken are another favorite of mine, especially when ordered extra spicy. The flavors are very authentic and remind me of restaurants in China.

The atmosphere is warm, comfortable, and welcoming, making it a great place for family dinners or meals with family friends. Highly recommend!

The service from beginning to end was phenomenal. The food itself was out of this world served on bamboo shoots the service. I cannot stress this enough. We were treated like family. Please don’t come here with your riffraff. If you come here be ready to be treated kindly and be ready to eat like king thank you.

Stumbled upon an authentic Sichuan restaurant in San Francisco — the décor feels nostalgic yet clean and cozy. The moment the pot arrived, it filled the air with incredible aroma! I ordered their signature “Boiled Fish in Chili Broth” — perfectly spicy, fragrant, and flavorful. The heat was just right, and it truly warmed me up inside. The owner and staff were super friendly, giving me that comforting feeling of dining back home ❤️

A small, cozy, but seriously high quality Sichuan spot. The owners are from Chengdu and you can tell they know how to make authentic Sichuan dishes. I came on Chinese New Year’s day today, and they hosted our large group of 12 people no problem

They were so sweet to us and even gave us a free dessert at the end. Just great service and welcoming atmosphere.

Some stand out dishes
- The chefs special vegetable combo 沸腾小炒 delicate fried taro strands with other veggies and pine nuts
- Mapo Tofu 麻婆豆腐
- Lamb in Cumin Sauce 孜然羊肉
- Eggplant in garlic sauce 鱼香茄子
- Pork shoulder special dish (had to order one day in advance)
- Osmanthus glutinous rice dessert - so fragrant and delicious

We will definitely be back!

We had visitors from Canada who loved Chinese food. We searched for a Chinese restaurant and we found Sichuan Home with good reviews, but the restaurant opens at 5pm. It was 3pm when we felt hungry for lunch. We searched more for a different Chinese restaurant. None of the others had good reviews or the type of Chinese we were looking for. So, we decided to do another activity and wait till 5pm to eat at this restaurant.
We finally sat down inside. The menu had good selection. The menu also was neatly categorized with the type of dishes. We had 4 main dishes: Lamb, chicken in Sichuan pepper, spicy fish and herb spice , and a vegetarian option called Dry mushroom.
The food came in less than 5 minutes 🤔. I honestly don’t know how they prepared it so fast. Those 4 dishes needed to cook. Most likely they were already cooked and ready to serve.

My mushroom pieces were too big and leathery. When I asked for knife to cut to smaller pieces. They said the didn’t have a knife! They ended up bringing scissors😳. I didn’t like that, but I had to let her cut the big mushroom pieces so I can hold them with the chopsticks and put them in my mouth without having a full mouth or mushroom ends dangling from my mouth!
The spicy breaded chicken was like orange chicken. We all agreed that the chicken needed salt. So we asked for salt. The waiter grabbed the dish from our table and brought it back very salty! It was not good before and not good after.
The spicy fish, which came on a gas cooktop next to our table looked delicious, but the fish was possibly frozen fish. You would think that having fish at a restaurant next to the ocean would serve fresh fish from the sea, but that was not the case.
Bottom line, the only fish that we all agreed was good, fresh, and tasty was the lamb.

They also brought sweet rice pieces on the house.
The service was very good. The waiter might also be the cook, but I’m not sure.
We were the only customer then another couple came in and finished before us.
Would I go back again? I don’t think this is the best Chinese restaurant in town. So I’ll try something else next time.

We’ve visited many Turkish restaurants across Massachusetts and New England, and honestly, Taksim sets the standard. Other Turkish restaurants should look to Taksim as an example of how authentic Turkish food, excellent service, and genuine hospitality should be done.

Thank you to the entire team for such a memorable experience. Whenever we’re back in California, Taksim will be one of our first stops. Highly recommended. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐🇹🇷❤️

Ordered a number of appetizers including the lamb carpaccio, the shrimp and the mezze trio. The appetizers were wonderful.
Ordered the branzino, dorade and chicken as entrees. The entrees tasted okay, but the quantities of the meats were rather low. I would recommend sticking to the appetizers. This is obviously a mezze centric place, and avoiding entrees would be a good call.

The pudding was average, but the donuts were good.

Go for the tasting menu to get all the flavors in a really beautiful sequence, it's so worth it and a much better value for the price. The MK55 cocktail (the green one) is incredible and the taste matches the Turkish spices perfectly.

Super attentive staff as well and sitting at the counter let's you watch the chefs as they work their magic.

If I could give more than 5 stars, I would! My husband and I went to Taksim tonight to celebrate our anniversary. First, the manager and staff paid wonderful attention to us and made sure we were comfortable and ready to celebrate. They made us feel special from the moment we sat down. We ordered two cocktails (55 t and the Galata) and the tasting menu. I feel like normally with a tasting menu there are some dishes you enjoy over others or maybe some you don’t care for at all - tonight we loved everything we tasted! A special note to the decor and the opportunity to sit at the bar and see the open kitchen crew work their magic. Run, don’t walk, next time you need a special place to eat!

top_reviews.content: I had a great breakfast here. The salmon was fresh, and they offer plenty of ingredients to customize your plate. I was also impressed by the bakery items, which tasted fresh and 'healthy' compared to other places. The natural light coming from the ceiling creates a wonderful morning ambiance. My only complaint is the beverage service—since there's no drink station, you have to request coffee and juice every time, which can be a little tedious during a busy morning.

Visited The Garden Court in Palace Hotel for an Afternoon tea. The place is very pretty, marble pillars, chandeliers and glass roof.

Coming to the tea experience, the staff were very professional and attentive. Went there so celebrate birthday and they were sweet enough to get a small cake.

The let down were the finger sandwiches which felt plain and bland. These definitely could have been much better provided the price we pay. Pastries were sweet and good enough.
Choices of tea are good and taste well.

Overall it’s been a good experience but very pricey.

My mom and I come here occasionally for breakfast, and it has quietly become one of our favorite little traditions.

The space is absolutely beautiful — the glass dome ceiling and chandeliers, with the soft morning light coming in, make the whole experience feel calm and special. It’s the kind of place where you just want to slow down, enjoy your food, and spend time together.

The breakfast buffet offers a great variety with solid quality. There are fresh fruits, yogurt, and granola, along with a nice selection of pastries, croissants, and breads. They also have smoked salmon, cold cuts, and cheeses. The hot items like eggs, bacon, sausage, and potatoes. Are classic but well done and consistently satisfying. They even offer a few dim sum options, which is a nice touch.

It’s not about overly fancy or flashy dishes, but everything is thoughtfully prepared and reliable, which makes the experience very enjoyable.

What we love most is the pace, no rush, just a relaxed morning where we can sit, eat, and talk. For us, it’s more than just breakfast; it’s a place to spend meaningful time together. We always leave feeling relaxed, and we look forward to coming back.

Min was awesome! He was so attentive! We’ve never had tea in a lovelier setting! The harp music was really lovely. They had a set of sandwiches ready ahead of time for my child’s allergies.

The sweets were amazing and the savory items, although creative, a couple of them had dry bread. Not a big deal but at this price point, I expect it to be perfect. The cream was whipped cream and not clotted cream.

You can't beat the setting—having tea under that 110-year-old stained-glass dome was amazing. That said, the food was just okay, and nothing really stood out. Service was average at best, as the staff were too busy to check on us until the end of the meal.

What an amazing expirience!! We were passing through San Francisco and decided to stop here after an Instagram review and it did not disappoint. The line was out the door but we were able to get seated within 30 minutes, considering it was Father’s Day and a Sunday this was awesome.

This Gold Nugget in the heart of San Francisco is definitely a don’t miss. Inside and outside seating with timeless favorites and unique plates for every palate on the menu bursting with flavor!

This restaurant has extensive menu,  we ordered the PJ’s Sweet Flight which truly lives up to the hype. The classic eggs Benedict was just as satisfying, with well-poached eggs and a smooth, flavorful hollandaise that brought the dish together beautifully.

Beyond the food itself, the overall experience felt effortlessly enjoyable. The atmosphere was relaxed and inviting, though a little bit noisy and everything—from the timing of the dishes to the attentiveness of the staff—came together seamlessly. It’s a spot that makes brunch feel like something to slow down and savor.

Awesome! Thank you.

Generous portions. Bring cash if you're buying something less than $20 or order something worth $20 because that's their minimum for credit cards. I got the HK noodles with pork chops for $13 (w/tax) and was not able to finish it for lunch and had to finish for dinner. Totally worth it. It's definitely for sharing and absolutely delicious typical hole in the wall Chinese fast food.

Very homestyle Chinese food spot in the city - the menu has both typical (chow mein/chow fun) and atypical dishes (salted fish fried rice for example) and a wide variety of wonton/noodle soups. I think it was definitely very authentic tasting, but I do feel like it was missing that little extra edge to give it top marks. Reasonable pricing (not cheap not expensive) but the only real downside is the space inside is *limited* and they get *busy* - from the time we asked for a table to the time we ate, it was about 45-50 minutes on a Sunday lunch day. They can’t help it, the space is small - but just be aware if you’re starving. Also the middle table is like family style so you sit with strangers next to you.

Very busy and crowded eatery. There was a queue during dinnertime, it's better to go early as the restaurant is small and closes by 7pm. Although it's a Chinese restaurant, there was a proportion of non-Chinese customers. Ordered the wonton noodle soup and mapo toufu and the noodle was simply delicious.

As someone of Asian background who eats Chinese food regularly, I can’t help but question many of the positive reviews here.

Speaking of the crispy noodles with sauce in the photo, the sauce itself was bland and unbalanced.
Judging from that, I honestly doubt that the wonton soup everyone praises could really be that good either.

The Surimi (fish) balls were undercooked, and the noodles were soggy — overall, the quality was disappointingly low.

Yoma Cafe is definitely when the satisfy. I will warn you that it is always busy because it is so good however it is worth the weight even if it's for a quick lunch. For $25, that plate could easily feed you for lunch for 3-4 days! Would highly recommend coming here any time. I for one, will definitely plan to come back.

We ordered sushi platters for an event.  The sushi platters were requested for Monday at 4:45pm.  I called the same day to confirm that they would be ready and was reassured that they would be. google.description: Compact corner cafe that offers traditional Indian chaats, curries, veggie items & Tandoor dishes.

top_reviews.content:
This place will soon turn into a template for the glorious days of 'the old' guard of Indian restaurants in the bay. In an unassuming interior painted bright with turmeric yellow you will find conventional north Indian food that you may soon long for, given the rapid evolution of the Indian food scene in the country.

I got the dahi papdi chaat and it needn't have come with the edible flowers. The chaat was good, though the tamarind date chutney could be better. I also ordered the saag channa and bature. The saag was delicious and creamy and the bature were not giant balls of dough, but a pair of oval shaped bread. They had been well leavened and were stretchy and paired great with the channa.

Overall I'd come here for comfort food on a cool night seeking warm home fare.

Came here on a Friday evening around 6 pm and was seated right away. We were promptly greeted and seated and asked whether we wanted ice in our water.

We ordered the following: Aloo Tikka Chaat Bites, Gobi Mussalam, Chicken Tikka Masala, along with Lemon Rice, Bhature, and Garlic Naan.

The stand outs for me were the Bhature - best to eat while still hot. It was so airy and delicious. I used it like a pocket to eat with the items we ordered. Their chicken tikka masala was very creamy and flavorful but not too salty. You can pick from four levels of spiciness. We picked level 2 which was not spicy at all for me.  But I can handle some spice.

I don’t think I would order the lemon rice again. The naan had the perfect amount of garlic. Next time I will just stick to the naan and Bhature.

We had plenty of leftovers as there were only two people in our party. Parking wasn’t too bad because we came on the earlier side. There was a steady flow of patrons and some purchasing take out but it never got crowded. Staff were all wearing masks.

Would definitely revisit this neighborhood restaurant.

Our favorite Indian restaurant in SF.  Consistently delicious whether we order takeout or dine in.  Rich and dynamic flavors with spice level adjusted to your preference.  Medium spice starts packing a punch. Friendly and quick service.  Their mango lassi is thick, sweet, & tangy - difficult to put down!

Been eating here basically since it opened. Used to be another Indian place that I frequented but when Tilak took over, the food took a leap up.

It's still one of the best Indian restaurants in the city. Easily. Everything is so good and flavorful... from basics like dahl and butter chicken to more unusual dishes like masala lamb racks and goan prawns. If something on the menu looks a bit unusual, that you don't recognize from other Indian places, I recommend going for it.

Tilak himself and the rest of the staff are friendly and awesome, but the food... Just great stuff all the way down the menu.

So, yeah, easily my favorite Indian place in SF and the place we've been doing our company holiday dinner for the last five or six years.

I have to say this is one of the best places in San Francisco. If you never tried Indian cuisine, my advice is to try it. I will tell it’s unbelievable unforgettable and memorable so cheers and enjoy. And the chief Tilak is a magician!

top_reviews.content: We had a wonderful experience at Celia’s by the Beach. The food was excellent, the atmosphere was great, and the service made our visit even better. Madison was absolutely amazing—friendly, attentive, and very professional. She made us feel welcome and took great care of us throughout our meal. Thank you, Madison, for your outstanding service. We will definitely be back!

5 stars should be reserved for O.G. places like this one. Being greeted by the proud and informative manager, Phil, on the way in, our party of twelve easily sat down without a wait. Immediately, with all the decor and pictures of celebrities and Celia on the wall, I recognized this place as every meaning of the label "bay area legacy".

I had the pollo con crema and only moments after having the best chips and salsa I've had in weeks. Forgive me if I overrate the salsa but it was clearly balanced with the fresh tomatoes and cilantro without having to cover the produce with spice. My entree of plump, seasoned (but not too much) chicken breast sopped up what seemed to be lightly ancho peppered cream sauce. The rice was done right, the frijoles were filling. Truly some of the best food in SF, a staple. Phil's grandmother, Celia herself, has left behind a true gem for the city!

We had a wonderful experience! Madison was incredibly friendly, attentive, and welcoming from the moment we arrived. She made us feel comfortable, checked on us regularly without being intrusive, and her recommendations were great. Her excellent service made our meal even more enjoyable. Thank you, Madison we’ll definitely be back!

Place is light and bright, good tunes. They had the warriors game on which they give free shots for every 8th 3 point shot made. They had other shot deals during Giants and 49er games as well. Food was SUPER delicious. I had the chili verde enchilada and it was on point.  The house margaritas were the best I have ever had. Fresh lime juice and the whole bit. Don't sleep on this place. 💚🤍❤️

Taco Tuesday – Arrive early if you want  a seat at the bar. I got there around 5 PM (they open at 4:30) and got the last available spot. Definitely an older crowd - I'm in my  mid-50s and was one of the youngest people there. The $5 margaritas, while made with cheap tequila and sour mix, were potent. I tried both the crunchy picadillo tacos and the soft house tacos – both were just okay.

Our new go-to for Korean food!  Love the authentic feel in this restaurant along with offering a mix of popular and not so well known traditional Korean dishes.

What we’ve tried:

* cod fish soup - first time to try ever, love it

Definitely going back here again :)

Extra busy here tonight. Yet we were still seated right away. Service was slow. We had to wait a looong time for our orders to be taken. But the food came quickly. The Short ribs was yummy. The sliced pork was yummy. The seafood pancake was yummy. The beef rib soup was different than what I was used to. Peppery and I liked it!!!  Korean restaurants tend to be more expensive but you get better quality food.

I stopped coming here before Brothers became the new owners three years ago. The previous restaurant had really grumpy servers. But the new owners hired better ones. This lady, Ester, in particular is the best. The food is good though is not much different than any other Korean restaurant. At least it didn’t knock me off my chair. I ordered the beef bibimbap that came with 8 little banchans which were very tasty. The bibimbap, however, was extremely salty. I couldn’t trace which vegetable was the source because by then I had already mixed everything together. This wasn’t a meal for someone with high blood pressure or a heart condition. If you are one of these people then think twice before you consume these Korean cured vegetables. Will I come back after this experience? Sure, but I’ll try something else.

It was my first time having Korean Food, besides Kimchi. I love Kimchi. My BFF works at Brother’s, and recommended me trying them out for my first time. I really liked all the different varieties of dishes.

It’s a place to hang out with your friends and enjoying amazing food.

I am excited to try it again when I am back in town.

I highly recommend this place.

top_reviews.content: The 45-min drive to Daly City was worth it. We had the special Prix Fixe menu as part of the 'Flavors of the Peninsula Restaurant Week' event. We did not expect such refined dishes, featuring fresh and delicate Korean ingredients prepared in a modern way. Every dish was cooked perfectly with layers of taste and textures - sulpang with sweet matcha spread, prawn with greens and house sauce, pork belly or chilean sea bass with sticky rice in lotus leaf, and black sesame cheesecake. The surprise slice of cake for my upcoming birthday was thoughtful. Service was friendly, informative and not in-your-face. The restaurant was pretty empty on a Wednesday but expect crazy crowds during the weekends. We will be back to taste the 'Chef's Recommendation' menu as well as the typical Korean dishes. We'll have to introduce Pogu to our Korean friends - we think they will approve. Compliments to Chef Tony and his staff!

OMG!
So good.

Galbi is super delicious.
Banchan (Korean side dishes) display is so pretty and you can ask for refill.
The Abalone chicken soup is good as well.
Can't believe a quality Michelin star restaurant is hiding inside the supermarket and I can eat Michelin restaurant during lunch time.

Had an excellent experience here. We are both vegan and gluten free and the staff took extra care in preparing our meal for us. We had the Vegetarian Korean BBQ dishes (grilled mushrooms and tofu) and the wild vegetables appetizer. It also came with gluten free rice-flour bread (which contained egg; only one of us is vegan) with matcha butter. We got a side of Korean rice with millet mixed in to the white rice. Everything was super flavorful.

Pogu in Jagalchi, San Francisco was a thoughtfully chosen stop during my visit, and the experience was thoroughly enjoyable.

Conveniently located in the heart of Jagalchi Market, the restaurant was easy to find and pleasant to visit while exploring the market.

The restaurant offers a refined yet comfortable atmosphere, featuring a clean open kitchen and well-executed interior design that reflects a high-end dining environment. The staff were professional, courteous, and attentive, consistently ensuring a smooth and welcoming dining experience.

The menu was clearly structured and aligned with the standards of many authentic Korean restaurants in the U.S. Each dish was well balanced and flavorful, reflecting careful preparation and the chef’s attention to detail. Presentation was polished, and the sauces complemented the dishes well without being overpowering. Every dish was enjoyable, and ordering two appetizers and two main dishes was a satisfying amount for three people, leaving us comfortably full.

From reading other reviews, it is clear that the team continues to refine the menu and make thoughtful improvements, including the development of new dishes. Overall, the visit was highly satisfying, and I would gladly recommend Pogu to anyone looking for quality Korean cuisine in San Francisco.

The dishes at Pogu were incredibly neat and refined, with meat grilled to absolute perfection. The mushrooms served on the side were a total "kick," and the black sesame cheesecake topped with dried persimmon was a unique highlight. With friendly staff and a great atmosphere, it was a truly satisfying meal.

top_reviews.content: A cute little spot that’s perfect for celebrating a special occasion. The appetizers were a standout - the focaccia was incredibly soft and fresh, the Brussels sprouts were perfectly charred and crispy, and the burrata with beets was delicious. While the mains were less memorable, we did enjoy the truffle risotto, but the other pasta dishes were a bit bland. Dessert was truly the highlight of the meal. The pistachio cake was fantastic, and the chocolate soufflé cake with vanilla ice cream and toasted sesame was great as well. Overall, we had an enjoyable dining experience

Warm and lovely food and service with a few memorable standouts and a few forgettable items.  We did the 8-course tasting menu and add on A5 dumplings.  One party member added the wine pairing.

The earlier dishes were all knockouts. We loved the fried rockfish and oyster.  The slaw was really vibrant and contrasted the crisp fry nicely.  The halibut crudo was a table wide favorite, so bright and yummy!  The uni creme brulee was unique, tasty, and generous.  The scallop and rice dish was fantastic especially the rich broth (mushroom dashi) which my husband and I both said we could just drink a bucket of.

The last two dishes were both a bit okay.  The porchini ravioli was good but felt a bit one note.  The venison plate was the biggest off note for the table.  The venison itself just lacked any game flavor which seemed to defeat the purpose over a beef cut, and the composition of the plate felt a bit off, we weren't sure which parts should be mixed because each element was like 3" apart plating wise.  The bean salad was absolutely amazing on the plate though it was two tiny bean cuts.

They brought two additional dishes, an amuse bouche I missed the description of maybe a cauliflower puree with caviar, and a Japanese milk toast with butter.  Both were fairly forgettable, especially the milk toast.

Dessert was good with the panna cotta being everyone's favorite while the chocolate hoho felt a bit too much.

Really good food, wish we'd enjoyed the second half as much as the first but personal prefer as well!

Nice & creative menu. We stayed in an Airbnb nearby & happened to stop in for a quick dinner. Thoroughly enjoyed it. Only down side is that they do not have a full bar so my husband couldn’t have his martini before dinner.

Highly recommended. A very non pretentious upscale dining restaurant. The quality was upscale (as are the prices) but it seemed very fun and casual otherwise. Approachable I would say.

I posted photos but didn't catch the menu so not quite sure what the dishes were called. The squash soup, uni creme brulee, the beef and the panna cotta were all very good.

For the price, this was a very disappointing meal. We ordered the 5 course fixed price for $98, the wine pairing for $65, and the uni crème brûlée and Foccacia add ons.

The wine pairing was the best part. We got four delicious wines, including one sparkling to start and a dessert wine to finish. The next best I can say is that most of the food was fine. The uni crème brûlée was good but not enough to make me feel glad I spent $40 on it. The pastas were tasty but I’ve had better in SF and wouldn’t go back for them. The focaccia was the same. Then the main course came out. While my partner’s steak was very tasty, my salmon was dry to the point that I wasn’t that interested in eating it. The desserts, like the rest, were good but nothing I will rave about to friends or likely even remember.

In the end, we’d spent nearly $500 on a meal that was probably the worst I had on my trip to SF. To be fair, I am comparing to some absolutely amazing meals — but I’d hoped this most expensive one would join those.

top_reviews.content: If you’re just looking for a reliably good pizza place, this spot definitely delivers. They’ve got a really nice dough, tasty cheese, and a sauce that pulls everything together into a pretty satisfying personal pizza. They also have some nice drink options and a good range of wines if that’s your thing. Overall, it’s just a really nice place to grab a good pizza.

*For context, this review is largely for vegans (3.5/5 stars).

Had a reservation on a Friday evening on the back patio. Beautiful weather for the back patio. I had emailed the restaurant in advance to check on vegan menu items, and they assured me that most of the menu items can be made vegan. There seems to be some confusion between the staff and management though since when I came to the restaurant it wasn't as vegan friendly as advertised (e.g., it turns out the gigante beans could not be made vegan). That being said, they were still able to make vegan the two pizzas I was interested in the She Wolf and the Old Faithful. They use Daiya cheese which looks great, but doesn't have the strongest taste profile and texture isn't amazing when it cools down. We asked for salt to increase the taste on the pizza, but think they could do a lot more to increase the flavor profile on both pizzas, since we've had similar pizza toppings elsewhere that were more flavorful. (Honestly, the toppings combination for both pizzas were excellent, but a little undersalted with the current vegan cheese choice.) Both pizzas were still solid though. I am bummed I missed my opportunity to try the pizza back when they used Butcher's Son cheese. There's tons of better tasting vegan supermarket cheeses out there over Daiya too (Parmela, Good Planet, Miyokos, etc.), but perhaps they use Daiya because it melts nicely/better or they haven't tried the others. Food was good but could still do better, especially knowing the strong competition for pizza, vegan and non-vegan.

Highlight:
Delicious vegan-friendly pizza in a spotless space with a patio you’ll want to linger on.

Restaurant:
This cozy Berkeley pizza spot takes pride in crafting high-quality pies with fresh ingredients and thoughtful flavor combinations. The atmosphere is relaxed yet well-kept, and the charming patio is the kind of space that makes you want to extend your meal just to soak it all in.

Service:
Service here is warm, welcoming, and attentive without feeling rushed. Staff members know their menu well and seem genuinely happy to guide you toward great choices. The care they put into the dining experience is evident from start to finish.

Food:
We enjoyed a vegan pizza topped with sausage and peppers, and it was packed with flavor—savory, well-balanced, and cooked to perfection. The vegan Caesar salad was another standout, with a creamy, flavorful dressing that didn’t feel like a compromise. Every bite spoke to the attention paid to quality and freshness.

Recommendations:
Whether you’re vegan, vegetarian, or just a pizza lover, this is a must-visit. Grab a spot on the patio if the weather’s nice, and don’t skip the vegan Caesar—it’s a pleasant surprise. The spotless dining area and even cleaner bathroom say a lot about how much the team cares. Highly recommend for anyone seeking top-notch pizza in Berkeley.

This place is so special! I am not sure if it is the size of the establishment or the taste of the exquisite pizza, but Rose is a great place to bring friends or go on a date. The ambience is loud but warm and friendly. The service and staff were extremely timely and professional. I had a great dinner here with friends, and will be back for more. Parking is a sore, but what is new in Berkeley!? 10/10!

Service: friendly and attentive
Price: Bay Area fair price for the best pizza around
I’d be happy to go back

Especially Mario (I think he was a customer also, check out the photos I took with the guitar) was very kind.   I highly recommend this place, peaceful clean, family friendly. top_reviews.content: We came here before they made changes but I wanted to leave a review about our experience.  I got a cold brew coffee with tahini and caramel and it was really good. We them ordered the toum caesar salad with halloumi, and the labneh and they were both fantastic. So much flavor in all the dishes. The knafeh pancake was my absolute favorite but we had to take most of it to go because it was too much food for 2 people. I will add the service was pretty slow on that Sunday morning because it took a long time to get our orders in, I had to remind them about the coffee a few times and then getting the check too a while too.

The food here is phenomenal. I’ve never had such creative fusion flavors that are both new and familiar. They have Mediterranean / Palestinian standards but with a twist; the flavor combos are so clever and they always taste amazing. They have slightly different menu items for dinner vs brunch so I’d really recommend trying both for the full experience. My favorites are too many to name but honestly you can’t go wrong—but the pancake is definitely top notch. Other favorites include the toum fries, the lentil soup, rotti wrap…actually you know what everything is good. I really don’t think you can go wrong. They also have vegetarian and vegan options, as well as other dietary restrictions options. Parking can be found on the street, though might be crowded during peak hours. I wish they were open more days of the week, it’s only Thursday - Sunday for now, but maybe in the future that will change…?

Was really sad to see my favorite unique + quality brunch spot in the bay change format to being fast casual. It was such an easy brunch pick to take out of towners or friends to.

Now instead, they've become easily one of the best fast-casual food in the bay. So I really can't complain.  I guess their format changed worked because I've eaten here more often than when they were full service. The value for the money you get here is pretty nuts. Still just as good ingredients & just as good preparation, all at a more approachable price point & form factor. What really gets me is I'm truly getting restaurant quality cooking for a unique cuisine I don't see very often, just a version that works better to-go. When you compare to some of the other casual lunch/dinner places in the area that have a similar format, it's really no competition. You'd be hard pressed to find a better way to spend $20-30/pp. I also love that they kept some of my favorite guilty pleasures from when they were a full service restaurant, like the knafe pancake.

Their in-house online ordering system is pretty slick and a good deal too. Works just as well as doordash without any of the bloated prices. Wouldn't mind seeing this spread around to more restaurants.

Pleasantly surprised to find that everything we had tasted just as good as it looked. Expected there to be too much focus on aesthetics and making everything pretty for photos, but all dishes were quite good.

Service was good and friendly, the atmosphere was bustling, and the new digs are cute. It's heavily brunch centric, but there are some more lunch dinner items.

Wish they had a beer and wine license, some natty skin contact would go great.

Review to be updated if experience changes.

Such a great brunch spot. The menu is full of super interesting and unique dishes. The Japanese sweet potatoes were addictive. They have super fun coffee options. The servers were very attentive and knowledgeable. The interior was super cute, bright and colorful. We were so full so we didn’t have room for desserts but they had a very intriguing spread. I would definitely come back here and recommend it to anyone looking for a beautiful, unique brunch spot. It’s located in a cute part of town too!

Also had no interest in scrambled eggs that looked like pineapple, but didn't even taste like eggs.  Perhaps my mistake for not ordering specific individual items for myself instead & having higher expectations overa especially mentioning that it was my birthday.

I was in the area with my family and decided last minute to eat here.

Food: The mixed tempura appetizer was fresh, crunchy, and nice mix of veggie and shrimp. Three item bento was very solid, got the beef teriyaki, ton katsu, and sashimi. My son really loved the miso soup, rice, and salad that was included lol. We also ordered the snow white, poke, and 49ers roll. Yes, we ordered a lot of food lol. All the fish was fresh and the portions were enough for all three of us plus left-overs!

Service: Very prompt and attentive service, all the staff was very kind and courteous. They effectively managed in-house and to-go orders seamlessly. My son was so happy to get a yogurt drink at the end.

Atmosphere: No-frills mom and pop restaurant, real community atmosphere with japanese decor and local sports memorabilia. Felt like I was invited to someone's home! Loved it. Clean too!

Overall: Pleasantly surprised, my whole family enjoyed it. Recommend to anyone new to the area or just looking for some good eats. Will come back again!

top_reviews.content:
Absolutely fantastic Italian dining experience! We started with a selection of delicious appetizers, followed by perfectly crafted pasta dishes that were rich in flavor and beautifully presented. To top it all off, we shared a panna cotta for dessert—light, creamy, and the perfect sweet finish.
A special shoutout to Nicholas, whose service was exceptional—attentive, friendly, and truly elevated the entire experience. Highly recommend!

A must! Lovely local spot filled with date nights, girls nights, locals, tourists (us) and beautiful food!
Service was perfect and the chef made their job easy. We cleaned every plate 🍽️
Well done chef 👏🏼👏🏼👏🏼👏🏼

Very annoying and disappointing experience.

We had reservations for outdoor seating at 530p and arrived on time. It was a cold, windy San Francisco evening 59F, and the restaurant had plenty of empty indoor tables, but the waitress still told us all inside tables were “reserved”, unless we finished our meal by 630p we could not be seated indoors. When we offered that we could eat quickly and finish in an hour, they then said we could only order one course, which was completely unreasonable. So we were forced to sit outside.

It took almost 20mins for them to turn on the outdoor heater properly. Meanwhile, when I checked OpenTable, I saw a 6p bar seating option and I immediately booked and received confirmation emails from both Resy and OpenTable. However after I told the waitress, I was told“their calendars aren’t synced,” which was clearly a lie.

Food was actually good: the mushroom mousse and 2 different pastas were all delicious. But the $50 black cod was kind of mediocre.

The worst part: despite us freezing thru dinner and rushing to finish by 645p, when we left, there were at least 3 empty tables inside and vacant bar seating (check my pics). It’s definitely the most frustrating and disrespectful dining experience I’ve ever had.

No matter how good the pasta was, I will not go back.

Amazing neighborhood restaurant with high quality food. The vibe is nice. We started at the bar and shared delicious olives and bread with a bottle of wine then moved to the dining room for an amazing dinner.
We definitely would go back again!

Today was my birthday, and my husband, my daughter, and I chose this restaurant to celebrate. It turned out to be the worst restaurant experience I've had in a very long time.
If you value friendly service, basic courtesy, and a welcoming atmosphere, I highly recommend choosing another restaurant.
From the moment we walked in, the man who greeted us was cold, rude, and incredibly arrogant. Instead of making guests feel welcome, he made us feel like we were an inconvenience.
After we were seated, our waiter noticed that something was wrong and kindly asked why we looked upset. He said he would speak with the staff. We genuinely thought someone would come over to apologize or at least try to improve the situation.
Instead, the waiter returned and told us that their "service" simply wasn't for us and suggested that we leave.
I've never experienced anything like that in a restaurant. Rather than taking responsibility or making even the smallest effort to resolve the situation, they chose to send paying customers away. That's not hospitality it's the complete opposite.
Ironically, they did us a favor. We left and went back to our hotel, where a wonderful waiter recommended Fino. We had an amazing birthday dinner there with excellent food and truly outstanding service. That experience reminded us what genuine hospitality actually looks like.
This restaurant made it clear that they don't care whether guests stay or ever come back. We certainly won't. There’re far too many restaurants in San Francisco that treat people with kindness and respect to waste your time here.

Spend your money somewhere you'll actually feel welcome!

top_reviews.content:
We came here for lunch and got two dishes: Pad Kee Mao (drunken noodles) and Pad Kra Prow (basil stir-fry). Let’s start with the good. When we got here at 12:30 on a Sunday for lunch, the place was nearly empty with just one family at a table. There was no wait and the service was minimal. We got our food promptly. The basil stir-fry was flavorful and decent.
But the pad kee mao was both overly spicy and bland at the same time. I have no idea how that is even possible. When it came out the color of the noodles was so pale, and as soon as I tasted it, it was so under-seasoned and basically had no flavor. Yet there is a strong spiciness that lingers in your mouth.
We ended up finishing the stirfry but leaving half the plate of pad kee mao untouched.

Their Champa Sampler is absolutely delicuous with the fried rice ball salad as a true showstopper. We also tried the Larp Lao style salad with duck, which wasn't the most interesting dish, and the Lad Na had good flavor but a little too much gravy.

Portion sizes were great for the price and the staff were very quick with providing napkins and utensils. Phenomenal service.
A nice place for Thai food. The Champa sampler is a great dish to share. Flavors are great and curry is tasty. Champa fried rice was a delicious dish too. I will definitely go again.

This is an Asian fusion restaurant that serves solid Thai and Laotian cuisine at decent prices.

The Food:
I was thrilled to see Kaow Soi on the menu. This is often my go-to dish when I go to a Thai restaurant, as I love its thick egg noodles, creamy yellow broth, and unique flavors. Unfortunately, that's not what I got when I ordered "Lue's Noodle Soup - Kaow Soy" from the menu. It had pretty much the same ingredients of the Kaow Soi I'm used to, but this had white rice noodles while the broth was more watery than creamy and more brown than yellow -- think beef noodle style rather than creamy coconut broth. Taste-wise, it was fine, but I was just disappointed it wasn't what I was expecting. Maybe this is the Laotian version?

Fortunately, the other dishes my group got was more or less solid. The Pad Se-ew was standard fare, but the fried tilapia was delicious, with a perfectly crispy exterior and moist interior. The Champa Sampler (Lao sausages, fried spring rolls, and fried rice ball salad) was good and a good dish to get for sharing. But perhaps the best order was the Mango Sticky Rice. Simply delicious.

The Service:
The entire staff was friendly, prompt, and competent. Unlike at most Asian restaurants, the servers checked in with us from time to time and refilled our waters.

The Setting:
It's a medium sized establishment that was clean and well organized. The restrooms were clean, though some parks vandalized the mirror and paper towel dispenser with graffiti.

Also, like many places in The greater San Francisco area, finding parking can be difficult. We lucked out with free street parking in front, but don't expect such lucky during peak weekend hours.

The Conclusion:
If you're looking for traditional Thai food, you might be a little disappointed. But if you enjoy trying a different take on Thai food or want the option of also having Laotian cuisine, Champa Garden can deliver the goods. It's really all about expectations. My true rating is 3.5 out of 5, but since Google doesn't allow for half stars, I'll round up to 4 because the staff was so nice.

Great neighborhood gem, family run spot serving Thai and Laotian dishes that had some unique dishes not commonly seen at a typical Thai spot. The black metal doors were a bit discrete, but it's quite spacious inside. we were a party of 3 for lunch and there was no wait. We ordered 4 dishes and the food came out at a good pace.

Would recommend: Green curry - great flavor, mild but creamy. The Champa Sampler with their Laotian sausages and fried spring rolls (skinny, cut into chunks) and some crunchy fried onion (?) or nuts on a bed of white rice. I preferred dipping their rice noodles on the side better than the rice.
Their fried appetizers were hot and crunchy - like their fresh fried rice balls. They have good flavored soup that warms the soul!

Pork belly stir fry with Chinese Broccoli was a pass - the meat was sliced not cubed and fried too hard to chew through. The greens were a bit too greasy from the meat.
Larp (Laotian salad) was a bit too watery and salty! The fish sauce fully soaked the leafy greens.

We will come back and try Padem derm (yellow curry) and Khao piak (noodle soup dish).

top_reviews.content:
I was craving a burger bad and convinced the wifey to get some takeout here. The online ordering was simple and accurate and pickup was a breeze after being warmly greeted by the friendly staff.

We got a humdinger burger (Swiss and mushroom) with an extra patty (note: you don't need to get an extra patty, their patties are huge) and an alley-oop burger (bacon and avacado), plus some fries and onion rings. We ordered the burgers medium well which in hind sight I wouldve gone with medium because they accurately cook them to order it seems and medium well was a little dry. That being said, the beef was delicious and the burgers where rich in toppings and so hearty. The fries and onion rings were hot with a great crunch even after the 10 minute drive back, plus the curly fries where nicely seasoned but with lots of slivers. The ranch unfortunately wasn't so good, it wasn't your classic pizza place homemade ranch, but also wasn't as bad as chemically kraft, just mid. The addons like cheese fries and the extra patty just aren't worth it when the regular item is well composed and well executed.

All in all for the price point I think expected something a little more exceptional and on a future visit with the right order it would be a true 5 stars versus the 4.5 I would give it if I could. Dining in would be nice too given it's casual and spacious seating. If you're in the area and want a burger it's a pretty sure shot if the simple menu of a place like In-N-Out won't satisfy your craving.

I have drove by the area many times for other reasons and you may not even notice this place without doing some research since it is located away from everything else. Finally I got the chance to give it a shot, I was hungry where I was craving for a burger and in the back of my head this place was calling for me. Upon arrival, there was a line out the door since it was during the lunch rush, but I did not mind since I knew it was going to be good. When it was my turn to order, I was greeted with a happy smile by their cashier. They offer burgers, sandwiches, many style of fries, wings, salads and much more. Everything is made to order which is always a plus for me and I never mind the wait since I am a very patient person. The staffs are very welcoming, well trained and understanding which made my visit a satisfying one. They theme of this place is inspired by sports and more importantly the Bay Area sports teams, such as the San Francisco Giants, San Francisco 49ers and the San Francisco warriors. From the service to food it was a great experience. I highly recommend this place to all burger enthusiasts, to anyone  in need of a quick bite, or if you just so happen to be in the area and want to try something new. I definitely will be back to tryout the other delicious options they have to offer.

We came stumbled upon this place on accident and decided to give it a try.  I got the chicken club and my son got a burger customized and let’s just say he said it’s one of the best burgers he’s had in his Life!  I agree!  The flavors were on point for both sandwiches I did taste his and he got the chili cheese fries and I got the onion rings for the sides omg if I lived here I would be here at least once a week 🫶. Next time we are passing through we will make sure to come here to eat for certain 💯 Great job chef!

If you're a fan of old fashioned, big fatty patty wide burger that leaves you half drowsy because of all the juicy fat you just ingested, then this is the place for you.
I have been ACHING for a burger like this for a long, looong time.
Thank you guys, you really hit it for me.

Seating? Great for a friends gathering. But it just tastes better in your car somehow.

Really wanted to enjoy this place however it was merely okay.

The burger was cooked medium-well with just a slight amount of pink, exactly how I like it which is a plus. It was a fresh thick hand made patty and the quality of the meat was on the better side.
The burger itself was rather bland, it didn’t seem to be seasoned which was disappointing.

The price is steep and it wasn’t flavorful enough to warrant a second visit. Perhaps they were having an off day or simply forgot to season the meat, but it left a not so great impression.

The fries were also just ‘okay’, nothing to write home about but not offensive; your average fries. Which again for the price that you pay the meal didn’t seem worth it.

top_reviews.content: Tiny place, that served great food! There was a bit of a wait but totally worth it. The Pad Kee Mao, green curry, ginger curry, and rolls were all excellent. Would definitely come back when I'm in the area.

Little Plearn Thai has been on our list since last year since we love festive restaurants, but what really impressed us is that the food is just as good as how pretty the space is ✨😍

What we ordered: Fresh Spring Rolls, Curry Puff, Pad Thai (SO fresh best Pad Thai I’ve had in the Bay, no debate), Panang Nua, Basil pork, Thai Yaki Soba, Duck Over Rice, Moo Dang & Crispy Pork Over Rice. They also have a limited Valentine’s drink menu 👌

The second time I ordered the Thai Suki dry noodle - smelled awful and tasted equally bad. My wife's garlic noodle is just ok, the pork meat is drier than the Sahara desert. The decor and service is nice though.

Brought my wife to this spot because we saw it on IG. I wanted to surprise her with a date night. They were showcasing their Christmas themed atmosphere. I made a reservation because it was suggested if going on the weekend. They get very packed. I made the reservation through their website. It was easy.

We got there and immediately noticed how beautifully festive it was. That was really beautiful and intentional. My wife was real happy with her surprise. We were seated immediately, so that was a plus.

Our waitress provided helpful food and drinks suggestions. We ordered chicken wings as appetizers, I ordered Pad See Eew and my wife ordered the dry glass noodles with various meats and tofu (I forgot the name). The wings should have came out 1st.. but that was not the case. My food came out 1st without my wife's. The chicken wings came out about 5 to 7 miss later and then my wife's food came out.. about 2 mins after the wings.

While we both enjoyed our entrees, the wings were undercooked. Like they seemed done, but you could tell and taste that they needed to have fried a bit longer. One of them had a little redness on the bone. Nonetheless, we ate them. Our drinks were so delicious. She had the green Christmas one and I had the blue Christmas one. We put Soju (Korean alcohol) in them both. I got mine w/o whipped cream because I'm lactose intolerant (They were fine with leaving it off)...BUT, I did have her bring me sprinkles to add because I love sprinkles.

So far, the night was actually Purdue decent minus those lil hiccups. However, when the waitress came over to check on us and asked us if we needed boxes for the leftovers, we said we did.. but I still had half a drink left. Sure then brought the boxes and check. I did not understand why because I was actually going to order more drinks. However, at that point, I felt like we were being rushed to get up from our table. I told her that I was not ready for the check and she was adamant about me placing it on my section of the seating. I had to tell her again.. that we did not ask for the check and that we were not ready to leave yet. She walked away and then less than 5 mins from when she came.. someone else brought the bill. I had to day the same thing to him to.. that we were not ready for the bill.

I did not like that at all. No one else around us was provided the bill while so having food/drinks on front of them. I watched the movements, so why did this happen to us? No one should be rushed to get up while still enjoying their meal and/or drinks.

Although this did not happen to us, I am still putting it into my review due to witnessing it. The party next to us found a small crystal that looked exactly like glass in their noodle dish. One of them actually had it in his mouth due to taking a bite of his food. He stated that it was hard and definitely not food. He reported it to the same waitress who simply said " Oh sorry, do you want me to get you a new plate of food". She did not ask him if he was alright nor did she bring any manager over too talk matters over with them. They agreed to a new plate, but after we all discussed what just happened, they decided to get the plate of food taken off the bill. Even when they attempted to do that, they were met with the food is already cooking.. so they had to push a little bit to be heard. She took it off of the bill. I disliked how that situation was met. Lack of full apology, no managerial apology nor followup, no automatically insisting to clear it from the bill without being asked by the customer and the fact that they do expected the customer to pay any bill after going through possibly eating glass. My wife and I were appalled.

Wow, the white rice is good…some of the best.  The flavors are on the stronger side, but in a clean way (the food was NOT drenched in oil).

Now for the corn.  The highlight of what I tried.  The corn was cut in a way that’s  easy to eat and prepared without being oily.

The beef and rice hot plate was the perfect balance of flavor.  I normally do not eat white rice, but I finished half of this by myself 😊.

The shredded chicken was great to eat without having to get your hands dirty.  It was stronger in salt, but still very good.

Finally, the dessert jelly was refreshing with a hint of mint.  Those are jelly cubes, not ice.  Great way to finish our meal.

Highly recommended!  This place is constantly busy, so you know their high turnover means fresh food and ingredients.  Quick, pleasant, and chill environment for a quick meal when you’re hungry.

The flavors were amazing, and the dish was cooked perfectly. The desserts were also incredibly creative and delicious. Everything exceeded my expectations, and I can’t wait to come back and try more dishes!

I ordered the beef stew & tendon with dry noodle + cold milk tea. Everything tasted well.  The beef stew and tendon is well done - tasty and tender.  The noodle is chewy and it comes with soup. some dishes were a hit and the others were a miss. there is significantly less beef in the teppan than there once was and the spaghetti tasted like ketchup.

HK style cafe with good menu selection variety. But wasn’t too impressed with their baked pork chop flavor. Was comparing a bit to the cafe on Noriega. Would still return to try their other dishes though. It was quite a wait for a Sunday lunch so be sure to factor that in when visiting.

We’ll definitely order again!

The food here is absolutely amazing and delicious! The sushi is always a hit, and the sashimi is fresh with perfect taste and texture. The staff is incredibly friendly, and our office loves ordering catering from this restaurant. Highly recommend for anyone looking for top-notch Japanese cuisine!

Been eating at this local restaurant since I was a kid & it hits the spot every time! They've been operating for 30+ years & we always feel right at home with their friendly service.

Got take out this time for a family dinner and ordered some classics along with some of their newer rolls: fried calamari rings, California Roll, Tempura Roll, Spider Roll, Lion King Roll, Aloha Roll (New!), Crustacean Roll (New!), Radiant Roll (New!) and Coral Reef Roll (New!).

Thank you to the Noriega Teriyaki team for coming through every time, I'm already drooling thinking of my next order 🤤 LOL
(also posted on Yelp)

I have been here multiple times, usually when I am craving for some sushi or when I am in the area and want to get something different. This place is a plus in the neighborhood, because there are not many sushi spots within the district. The staffs here are very welcoming, well trained and understanding where I never had an issue in any of my visits. Their menu consists of Japanese appetizers, sushi rolls, specialty rolls, sashimi, dinner sets, desserts, etc. For dine in, you can choose booth seating, bar counter or regular table seating. Everything is made to order which is just how I like it and I never mind the wait since I am a very patient person. I highly recommend this place to all sushi enthusiasts, to anyone looking for a laid back spot or if you just happen to be within the area. I definitely will be back to tryout the other delicious options they have to offer.

I came here last weekend and the last time I came here was back in 2007-2008ish! So it's been awhile. The setup obviously is now different compared to before. The prices for the sushi are very fair. We got the sushi boat, emperor's roll and one other roll but I forgot the name (it was also raw). By the end, we were so full! We definitely could have ordered one less roll.

Customer service was great and their free tea was delicious! There is no parking lot, only street parking. Luckily, parking here isn't too difficult.

Inhaled our food before we could take a picture, but be assured we’ll be back!

What an unassuming gem, such a cute authentic Italian restaraunt. Clearly family owned. Dimly lit with wooden tables and benches, red checkered table cloths. I felt so satisfied after the meal, and everyone we ate with liked their meal too. Got a glass of wine and it was filled to the brim.

We were left to talk and even after paying the bill were not rushed out.

I would definitely come here again! One of the best meals I have had in San Francisco.

Amazing place! Great value for the food and service. Their complementary bread was warm, savory and paired well with their olive oil and vinegar. The most charming and amazing little Italian dream on the corner. The owner is incredibly welcoming and friendly, the atmosphere is warm and food is exceptional! The pasta is homemade and you can taste the chefs magic in the food. Highly recommend!
