The chicken kebab here is my favorite! 10/10. It comes with a salad, avocado, and thick-cut fries at a reasonable price for what you get. Pro tip: try the kebab and onion rings with their Tzatziki sauce!

The service here is amazing, they are friendly, accommodating, and quick.

Unfortunately had a poor experience here for lunch. I rarely complain about food but this burger was just too big and not very tasty. It’s impossible to eat a burger that’s six inches tall. For some reason it had three meat patties on it, plus all the veggies and bacon, making it just too large. I didnt care much for the meat as well, the patties definitely looked premade. The fries were okay, brought out a few minutes before the burger was served which was strange. And it took like 30 minutes for my food, definitely not a fast food restaurant. I would not recommend eating here.
Finally a found the best place to get a great burger. It’s a must if you haven’t been there.  The staff is amazingly friendly and welcoming.   They will take care of you.  Thank you Ganims Market

Famous for its Fish n Chips, this neighborhood hangout also serves a decent selection of saucy burgers. A bunless version wrapped completely in lettuce — also an option. Yummy steak fries.

With strong corner store vibes, this place is far from gourmet; but still, stick-to-your bones goodness when taking a break from the diet.

Worth a try, likely to bring back nostalgic memories of the quintessential American greasy spoon.

My girlfriend and I visited Ganim's on a Thursday night. I've lived in the area for years and always drove past, but I never had the chance to go inside until recently. I wish I had visited sooner!

Walking in, it felt like a whole-in-the-wall hidden gem and you could really feel history on the walls. The owner and staff were incredibly friendly and welcoming. I ordered the two-piece fish and chips, while my girlfriend tried the cheeseburger with bacon.

The hand-battered cod was well seasoned and paired beautifully with tartar sauce, making for a delicious late-night meal. The burger was equally delicious, with the shredded lettuce and burger sauce complementing the perfectly cooked medium rare quarter-pound patty. Unlike many places, Ganim's doesn't charge extra for sauce, which is a nice touch.

I'm definitely already making plans to visit again, and if you're in the area and craving a burger, I highly recommend giving Ganim's a try!

I was telling this dude about the great lasagna I had the night before, and what wonderful service the restaurant has...and he pops off ..Hey, all I said was have you got the time, then he looks at his watch and tells me he's gotta run!  All the while a homeless gal was listening to the whole thing and tells me if I give her a dollar she'll tell me which restaurant has the best lasagna in the world...So, I give her the buck,  and she tells me it's the La Traviata Italian restaurant on Mission!
So...Now I'm having lasagna 2 days in a row!  Isn't life great!  Oh, the lasagna was pretty amazing!   5 ☆☆☆☆☆'s

The pasta was perfect 👌. I also want to mention the special request for my birthday; even though they don't usually do writing on desserts, they did it for me and made my day.
I was so happy, many thanks to all the staff.

A stellar experience -- no exaggeration whatsoever.

I took my partner out to La Traviata for his birthday, and it was incredible. I had the Veal Traviata, and my partner had the Al Tosca. I was blown away, and it was so delicious. The lights were dim, atmosphere was quiet and intimate with Italian opera playing softly, and you can't beat the impressive walls of framed photos of celebrities from back in the day. The staff treated us like family, and sang "Happy Birthday," and even brought us a plate of creme puffs for desert -- on the house.

We will certainly be back, many times. I am so grateful to La Traviata for making our night so memorable.

Very bad. I ordered pasta in a hurry. The sauce used to be very good, but today it was burnt. There were two young people working there, I think they were relatives of the owner. Bad service. I don't know what happened to them, but honestly, the food leaves much to be desired. I will never return to this restaurant. Keep your crap.

We landed at SFO from New York City at noon and friends had made a reservation at La Traviata where we had an absolutely fabulous diner later that day. We started with a delicious red wine from Italy and even before we began ordering anything, our server brought out warm bread that clearly had just been baked and our palates began to savor what we realized would be a very memorable feast. While lovely operatic music serenaded us, we enjoyed delicious appetizers followed by wonderful entrees. I had the Salmone ala Wixel:  the salmon was prepared inside a parchment paper pouch and cooked with olives, tomatoes, garlic, and pesto. John, the owner and chef, brought the salmon, still enveloped in the parchment paper and placed a  plate with carrots and Brussel sprouts in front of me and  proceeded to open the pouch and gracefully place the salmon with all the seasonings on my plate. I have never tasted any salmon as delicious as this very unusual and tasty dish. I’m lacking in the eloquence to describe the  salmon but urge you to order it and savor the salmon yourself! My wife loved the seabass and my friends loved what they ordered. We shared a few desserts that were also wonderful. While we were up at 5am to make our flight from JFK, we spent hours enjoying our dinner and felt incredibly fortunate to be dining in this gem of a restaurant!

It's a heavy lift to live up to one's childhood memories of having a muffuletta in New Orleans - taken there by my own Sicilian family, but Sandy does so and improves on it. Starting with the most important thing, the sandwich (I had 1 slice of the Meat version with a side of slaw and chips). the meat and cheese is  layered neatly and generously, the paste and juices are flavorful without being overwhelming, and the bread is the major improvement having put it through a press it is lightly crisp on the top keeping it a reasonable thickness for even the most modest mouth.

The service was friendly, accommodating and passionate about their product. You feel welcome.

The atmosphere is simple, unique and cozy. Less hole in the wall and more a comfortable spot to sit and enjoy. Unique stickers, flags, and the like give you a sense of the roots of those working there.

I noticed they sell to-go versions neatly boxed up - more stylish cannoli box than a pizza carton. I am scheming on a chance to buy a full sandwich for a party or anything.

My only want is a second shop further south on the peninsula so it'd be easy for me to eat at Sandy's regularly.

Delightful little place tucked away off San Pablo, this restaurant sets the standard for what comfort Thai restaurant experience ought to be. It took us a while to be seated, and then served, but the anticipation was worth it. The restaurant was overflowing with the aroma of galangal and lemongrass. It's one of the few restaurants that has an entire vegetarian menu, which made my decisions much harder!

The curry puffs are definitely worth it - little Thai samosas that melt in your mouth. I wish it came with a chutney or a sauce, but they held their own. We got the tempura fried yam and taro root and they didn't disappoint either. The little side salad with cucumbers and onions in a sweet sauce was top notch!

The lemongrass aroma was so overpowering I had to get the Tom Yum soup. It was good, not great. Somehow the taste didn't live up to the aroma. We got the tofu in sweet peanut sauce and it was decadent! I don't remember the last time I had a Thai dish so well balanced - sweet and just spicy enough to feel the burn. At this point I was too stuffed and even though the dessert menu looked interesting, I had to skip it.
Green curry was just the right amount of spicy w/ lots of veggies that were cooked just enough to still taste fresh. Everything was cooked perfectly and came out super quick!

Absolutely love this Thai restaurant! The flavors are so authentic — it really reminds me of what I had back in Asia. Their Hainanese chicken rice is amazing — tender chicken, flavorful sauce, and perfect rice. Cozy atmosphere, friendly staff, and definitely a place I’d love to come back to!

Our favorite Thai restaurant! The atmosphere is peaceful, service excellent, with attention to food sensitivities...so nice. We eat there a couple times a month and sometimes take-out. We are so lucky to have delicious food so close by.

I have been here many times trying new dishes because everything is authentic. Everything I have eaten here, I have also eaten in Thailand many times; each dish is so delicious and it takes me right back to Thailand with every bite.

I'm going to think about this meal for a while. The Szechuan green beans, garlic chicken, and salt and pepper pork were divine. Some of the best Chinese food I've had in a long time. The iced Hong Kong milk tea was also delicious.

I would say just ok. The food was ok/good but not stellar. Ordered the crispy chowmein with beef - would give it a 4.5 out of 5. Also had the siomai and would give it 4 out of 5 stars. We had the fried rice with veggies. It was an overload of vegetables, like 70% veggies and 30% rice. We wanted more rice. Would give it a 3 out of 5 stars.

The garlic chicken was amazing! Staff was friendly and made us feel very welcome. My wife was cold because the wind was blowing whenever the front door opened, so they moved us to a better table once one became available without us having to ask. It's family style and we ordered way too much food, but we both enjoyed our meal and would definitely go back next time we're in the area.

It was a nice place, but it smelled like mildew. Our waitress was super nice and I found sweet tea, just didn't know it was $6 a serving. Eeeh, maybe worth it since I hadn't found it in a couple days but sheesh 😳 I had the flounder, it was good...I kinda wish I had ordered the garlic chicken after I had ate a couple bites of his general tso chicken...it was so good! I first heard of this brand back in my high school days, but never gave it a shot until recently. Upon arrival, it was right before lunch and I was greeted by one of their many staff members. Since it was my first time I needed time to decide what I was going to get. Their menu is displayed on the left side of their wall as you enter. They have many things to choose from, such as salads, their specialty sandwiches, build your own sandwich is also an option, breakfast sandwiches, chips, cold drinks and much more. Everything is made to order which is always a plus for me since it is quality over quantity and I never mind the wait because I am a very patient person. Their Lou’s sauce and jalapeno spread is a must, it just makes every bite more delicious. You can dine in at one of their tables in the shop or outside dining is also available. The staffs here are welcoming, well trained and understanding where my experience was an issue free and satisfying one. You can order in person, place an order over the phone or have it delivered to you via a delivery app. I highly recommend this place to all sandwich enthusiasts, to anyone looking to try something new or if you just so happen to be in the area to check them out. I definitely will be back to tryout the other delicious options they have to offer.

This sandwich place was phenomenal! The special coating they put on the bread makes it even better. Everything tasted fresh and well made. The service was fast and easy, making the whole experience even more enjoyable. I’ll definitely be coming back!

Big yum. Delicious sandwiches. My mom and I both loved ours. I got veggie-licious, she got Roma's club. The $2.75 cookies are good too. Small place, but we snagged a seat. Big big subs at reasonable prices. (~$12.50) On-street parking only. Salads and breakfast sandwiches as well.

This is one of my husband and I's favorite lunch spots when we visit SF. Every sandwich we have gotten here has been delicious. I highly recommend Lou's if you're looking for a quality sandwich shop with plenty of options and generous portions.

top_reviews.content: OK, this is my very first Shabu experience.  I’m a little scared sometimes to try new foods.  Although I am quite a foodie and love eating all kinds of things.  This is an excellent place to go on your first Shabu journey.  The broth are delicious. The vegetables they bring you are fresh high-quality. I tried both the Ramen and the udon noodles prefer the udon.  We did the all you can eat $46 meal. It was beyond fabulous.  You get to try all the different kinds of meat.  That green sauce made with the cilantro. I swear I could put it in a glass and drink it!! we had a birthday party with 11 people, and they were so accommodating to us. They even helped us serve our cake with candles.  By the way, the meal comes with either red bean or green tea, ice cream.

We went right at open and our group of 6 were almost seated immediately. We got the all you can eat package and was pleasantly surprised by the amount of meat that was offered. While the selection was basically lamb, beef and pork, all the meats were nice and tender.

However the staff seemed to have a problem with our table. They were not as friendly to us as they were to other tables. We don’t know if it was because of all the meat that we were eating but if we got the all you can eat, we will eat all that we can eat.

At the end of the meal we were given the option for ice cream which was a pleasant and tasty surprise.

This is my go to Shabu place in Sf. The meat quality is top notch and paired with their special green sauce is amazing! That sauce is so addicting. I always get the all you can eat which you get your choices of unlimited carbs, veggies, and meat! Then your choice of ice cream if you still have room. This place never disappoints my appetite and would recommend everyone come and try it out! You won’t be disappointed.

Food was great but I can’t get over being seated at a table for four when we had a party of six! Table was very crowded with hot pots appetizer dishes! Finally Emily was nice enough to move us to a decent table but then we had to wait for all our food to be transferred to our new table. A big inconvenience for our surprise birthday guest. Besides that the spicy miso and regular miso broth were very delicious and fun to cook for my first experience at hot pot. Atmosphere was great and was very packed but does get quite hot inside after a while. They did have an all you can eat which is great for large groups.
The menu was quite limited on broth and ingredient options, but the ponzu dip and the matcha ice cream were great!

top_reviews.content:
Los Planes de Renderos is a charming, unassuming gem tucked into the corner of Mission and Persia. Despite its modest exterior, it delivers an exceptional dining experience. The pupusas are easily among the best I’ve had—perfectly executed with rich, well-balanced fillings. I ordered the revueltas (a classic combination of shredded pork and cheese), and each bite was flavorful, satisfying, and expertly prepared.

The ambiance is warm and thoughtfully decorated, adding to the restaurant’s inviting character. Equally impressive is the staff, whose attentiveness and genuine hospitality elevate the overall experience. This spot is a standout for authentic, high-quality pupusas and is well worth a visit.

I moved from Los Angeles to Santa Rosa and have not had good Pupusa in over a year. I made a drive out to the city and came across this little spot and I’m glad I did. I went during the week and parking was very easy to find. The food is made fresh so there’s a little bit of a wait, but I was happy to wait when I got my food. It was fresh and piping hot!

Atol shuco, a bit fermented hot drink that’s made with black masa flour, alguashte (ground pepitas)and whole beans, it can be an acquired taste if you never tried it before. The tamal de elote that can be prepared two ways, plain and fried, naturally sweet prepared on a corn husk and they are served with crema Salvadoreña. The pupusas are famous in the area and they are extra cheesy with the homemade quality that is hard to emulate. The platanos fritos are served with beans and sour cream. The camarones empanizados, (breaded shrimp) are served with beans and rice, salad and homemade tortillas. Tables are located on the second floor with tireless servers going up and down the stairs that provided excellent service on a busy evening.

The pollo asado (grilled chicken) plate $16 comes with rice, salad and two pupusas (flat bread.)  The lack of seasoning on the salad was refreshing. If it wasn't for the flat bread, I would have still been hungry as the single chicken thigh was not enough for dinner. They were quite busy when I came at around 8pm on a Thursday.

Wow!! so disappointed, about their service, the portions and price. I don’t mind paying $12 dollars for a full plate or even more. But they will rip you off if you don’t check your food before leaving the restaurant. Either missing food or put, half a portion for a full price plate. The food taste is good but service is horrible👎🏻👎🏻👎🏻

Will be back when visiting GGP.

The carrots are well seasoned too and it’s superb. It reminds me of another Banh Mi place I had a while back in San Jose minus a fried egg. The Thai tea was also the best I’ve ever had. It was so good we got a second one. They don’t use the powdered stuff and you can really taste it! I’ll be thinking about that Thai Iced tea for a while. FYI: Space is small! We got the lemongrass beef banh mi and the chicken fresh salad roll, they were so good, and the flavors were very strong. The staff were incredibly friendly and the service was great. Very warm atmosphere and reasonable prices for this day and age.

Food here is absolutely banging. I would go out of my way to go here.

One of my favorite Banh Mi's since moving to the bay. The Crunch Combo (Dac Biet) hits like a truck. They don't skimp on the Pate.

Review: Banh Mi Crunch (San Francisco)
​Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
​If you’re looking for a spot that nails both the food and the vibes, Banh Mi Crunch is a must-visit. It’s a cozy, smaller space, but they’ve managed to create an atmosphere that feels incredibly welcoming—perfect for a calm, chill lunch in the city.
​The Food
​Everything arrived steaming hot and noticeably fresh. Here’s the breakdown of the spread:
​BBQ Chicken Banh Mi: The star of the show. The bread had that perfect "crunch" the name promises, and the chicken was flavorful and well-marinated.
​Garlic Noodles: Savory, buttery, and exactly what you want from a comfort side.
​Fried Eggroll: Super crispy and served at the perfect temperature.
​Thai Iced Tea: The ideal sweet finish to balance out the savory spices of the meal.
​Service & Atmosphere
​The staff here are genuinely friendly and provide great customer service, which makes the small space feel even more inviting. It’s the kind of place where you can just decompress and enjoy a high-quality meal without any fuss.
​Bottom line: Fresh food, friendly faces, and a relaxed vibe. I’ll definitely be back!

top_reviews.content: We had our 25 yr high school reunion here. It was a lovely set up and all the staff was amazing. The food was yummy. I only had the vegetarian options so to be fair I asked others about the rest of the menu and they all said it was good! The scenery is gorgeous and it's a wonderful event space ✨️ the staff went above and beyond to make our night special and it was just that. We were able to have a photo booth and have a live show playing on all the televisions in the restaurant. Our DJ was great and it really was a whole vibe. The restrooms were clean and tidy ❤️ beautiful venue. I want to check them out on another occasion.

Came here for what was supposed to be an amazing event with my Sorority. We had the entire place to ourselves. This is definitely a beautiful restaurant inside and where it sits right by the water. I was beyond excited to see that we were eating here because it was my 1st time and I would be all dressed up. We were a party of about 35 or so. We had to choose our main entree when we signed up to attend. I informed them that I was allergic to a asparagus. We each paid ($95).

Our server's name was Gabe. We were serviced by a female as well, but I don't know her name.

However, most disappointment throughout the night was had. For starters, it wads reserved from 5pm to 9pm. I arrived at 6pm. They had wine on the table, bread and butter. No small plates were seen anywhere. So ppl sat around and could not nibble because of that. We were finally bright plates when requested.

Ou salad came out. I think it was Arugula and pecans. Very light dressing and some at my take received no dressing on their's. I sent mine back because I dislike Arugula. They did not offer nothing else to me to substitute.

The was the main entree was nice. I chose surf and turf.. without the asparagus. They gave me brocollini instead. First off, I was given the plate with asparagus. They dermal waitress quickly acknowledged the mistake and took it back. I got my plate, but as I looked around... those that had steaks... all had different sizes. My size was really small and it looked like Salisbury steak honestly.  I was at a table with 7 other. 6 out of the 7 had cold mashed potatoes, including me. 2, including me, had cold lobster and steak. We sent it back. They stated that we were getting new food. When the food came, it was the food we had because you can clearly see what was tasted or cut. So they put this food in the microwave. However, my plate returned with asparagus and brocollini. I had to spit it out and hope that I did not get an allergic reaction. They took my plate back. One of the others food was still cold..smh. My plate returned and it was the same for again without the asparagus. How was I going to eat it knowing the asparagus touched. That was ridiculous. I was told by Gabe that there was no more lobster and he offered me the chicken entree. I turned it down because that's not what I paid for and I did not want any chicken to eat. He then offered me a drink. I told him no thank you. He came back to me any 7 or so mins later and asked if I wanted fish. I told him yes. The fish was served on a fried hash brown (I think). It had some sort of gravy-like substance. I ate it became i was hungry. It was mediocre and unwilling. Gabe also asked me if i wanted a drunk, I chose a lemon drop. It was extremely sweet , but decent. Honestly, I was pissed with the whole ordeal.

Lastly, we had a apple turnover pastry. It was decent, but very hot on the inside.. but I ate it.

It's like they just had our food sitting out for some time and then had the audacity to serve it. Ridiculous. Even more so, that they microwaved food that they served cold. That's disgusting. Under my plate was filthy and it left the table cloth looking disgusting each time.

No one ever came to my table at any point and asked if we wanted to purchase a drink or had a need.

I went to Eve’s for Easter Sunday  brunch yesterday.  There are numerous things that I like about it and will definitely go back.
The customer service is very good; the staff, from the hostesses to the busboys are friendly and professional.  The hostess asked us if we wanted to be inside or outside; nice choice.
My only complaint is that we didn’t know who our server was and we did have to wait for our drinks; but still so nice!
The buffet is one of the best that I’ve been to; not a lot of options which I liked but the options provided were off the chart delicious.  My complaint was that I had to ask for a plate for myself and my (91 year old) cousin who was on a cane.  The food should’ve been hot but people kept leaving the chafing dishes opened; staff should’ve been monitoring the dishes and the food.  The crème brûlée French toast was INSANELY good; didn’t need butter or syrup.  Eat it just the way it is!!  The roasted potatoes were outstanding (lukewarm) can’t imagine how they would’ve tasted hot.  They were perfectly seasoned, a bit of crunch from the skins and perfectly cooked within.  The buttermilk fried chicken was a little dry and yet, it still had flavor.  My cousin raved about the string beans so much that all of us went back to the buffet for a side plate of the string beans; very good!!  The prime rib was also very good; better if it had been hot.  The shrimp and grits was also amazing better if hot.  Another cousin had the lobster mac’n’cheese; loved it.  The chef did an outstanding job of not over salting the food; everything had flavor without overpowering each dish.  By the time we would’ve had dessert, we were too full; biggest regret was not a bigger stomach because the desserts looked great.
Finally, what stood out among the 4 of us was that the restaurant was full but not loud!  We were able to converse without yelling; listen to the background music without competing with it.  The management didn’t try to see how many tables they could squeeze into their dining areas; including the patio area.  It was just a very nice environment.
I wouldn’t given this restaurant 5 stars had the food been hot.

So good! Everything is made from scratch so it's going to take a little longer. Well worth the wait. We enjoyed the Creme Brulee French toast. Delicious. The handmade pasta with the seared prawns was amazing. The chicken and waffles was also delicious. The drinks were good and we were happy. The manager/Chef is very nice and accommodating. We will be back! I wish they were open during the week for lunch! Soon I hope! Paws crossed!
Came here for the Easter buffet and wow. The food was really good and the view is great!

A lot of locals say this place has the best Hong Kong style barbecue meats in the city, that is when I had to make a visit and see for myself. Also the store is very compact, so not much people can just wait inside to crowd the whole place up. They offer roast duck, chicken, soy sauce chicken, chau siu, roast pork, wok fresh items and much more. They used to have dine in, but after Covid they removed that option and it is strictly for to go now. When it was my turn to order, I just went with my normal go to which is roast duck, because if you mess that up then no need of a revisit. The skin was semi crispy, meat was slightly warm and a lot of fat than meat ratio. To conclude people’s opinions and facts, this is definitely not the best Hong Kong barbecue shop in the city. I know where the best one is and most people agree with my option. I do have to say the staffs here were welcoming and well trained which made my visit an issue free one. What a magical place! Beautiful authentic interior, doors, walls, sofas, pillows, lamps, everything is gorgeous. Smiley and friendly stuff. We felt welcomed from the moment we entered. My husband, our son and myself visited this place for the first time, and we loved it. The price in the menu is fixed 65$/person, that’s included a dish from appetizers, main course and the dessert. Since it was 3 of us we had chance to try all three dishes from Entry, warm lentils soup, slightly spicy, but soothing. Then we had Moroccan salad, loved it, eggplants, tomatoes, carrots and cucumbers ❤️ Warm bread 🍞 And then chicken in fillo dough was unique, tender meat, crispy fillo, and a sweet touch of sugar powder I believe so?! For the second dish we took 1 big plate with all kind of meat, and seafood with couscous and veggies. Big portion for 3-4 adults. We couldn’t eat everything so got leftovers from first and second course dishes. And the dessert, my god, it’s incredible!!!!! There were 3 families, including ours, happy kids found place to play in the little corridor, so adults had time to talk. Couples had chance to spend time together. Music, thank god was at the right level so you can talk easily. It only got loud during the belly dance show. That’s a must have to see as well. Beautiful lady brought the mood to the restaurant, she engaged with visitors in a nice way, nothing vulgar, just a beauty of a woman body ❤️. Respect to her talent! Thank you EL Mansour team, for making our visit memorable ❤️

I celebrated my 48th birthday there and had a truly delightful and delicious experience. I chose it mainly for the food, since I hadn’t been to a Moroccan restaurant since my trip to Morocco in 2000, and I wasn’t particularly seeking the dancing. That said, the belly dancing was spectacular! She fun, engaging, and impressively close-up. The seating is comfortably low to the floor and bursting with vibrant colors.

We used a Groupon for two, but even at the regular price, it would have felt like a great value.

I had the best time celebrating my birthday here. It was my first Moroccan restaurant experience and it was everything I imagined! So gorgeous. The belly dancer, Lisa was so fab. My sister and I were also really happy with the vegetarian options!!! A beautiful experience, can’t wait to go back.

It was a fantastic experience with Morrocan ambience with decor,  food, and music. The belly dancing show is a must see and enchanting. It starts at 7:30 so make sure to make sure before. It's a delicious 5 course meal. Bring cash for the belly dancers to show your love!

El Mansour is a feast for the senses—rich flavors, vibrant ambiance, and unforgettable entertainment all wrapped in Moroccan elegance.

Stepping into El Mansour in San Francisco’s Outer Richmond feels like entering a different world. The restaurant’s interior is draped in authentic Moroccan textiles, lanterns, and ornate décor that instantly sets the mood for a magical evening. Whether you're celebrating a special occasion or simply craving something extraordinary, this place delivers.

🍽️ The Food
-  you’ll find equally indulgent Moroccan classics.

top_reviews.content: This restaurant has been on my list forever. But, recently, we finally had a chance to try it for the first time. It didn’t disappoint. Every item We ordered was just top-notch and flavorful. The service was phenomenal. Especially, the pesto fettuccine with chicken was heavenly. This restaurant easily turned into my favorite Italian Spot. Thanks again for the owner, the chef and waiter to take such a great care of us. Definitely going back soon!

Hands down the best meal we’ve had in San Francisco in many years. Everything was just perfection, true Italian food and hospitality at its very best. The place was packed and they had a huge birthday party of 20+ to deal with, but the manager and servers were so nice, so efficient and so welcoming. And the food! OMG delicious doesn’t even begin to describe it. We had the salmon carpaccio to start and it was so fresh and tasty. Don’t skip the amazing house made bread for sopping up all the different sauces you’ll have with every course! We got a 1/2 portion of that night’s house special pasta - something similar to rigatoni, with lots of sausage in a rich brown sauce, this was our favorite part of the meal. All pastas are house made and cooked to perfection. For our main courses we had the misto mixed seafood, with seared tuna, calamari, and shrimp. All fresh and delicious. And I had Petto Di Pollo, organic sliced chicken in a decadent butter-lemon sauce. Unbelievable. Even the sides on these two dishes - crispy rosemary potatoes and fresh organic vegetables - were so fresh and beautifully cooked, everything coming out of the kitchen is perfect. Save room for the tiramisu, it’s the most popular dessert for a reason. Also a wonderful and reasonably priced wine list.

The noise level was pretty high, mainly because of the birthday party I think, but the atmosphere is festive and fun. And it’s a great neighborhood location that clearly brings in a lot of regulars (no tourists that we could spot.) Reservations highly recommended, the place is intimate and every table was completely full by 6pm on a Saturday night. Walk-in’s weren’t turned away but had a lengthy wait out on the sidewalk. Serafina is officially at the top of our favorite restaurant list in SF. We will be back soon!

Kicking off the New Year with a meal at Serafina, perched atop Russian Hill, feels like coming home. This beloved neighborhood gem is where familiar faces gather and every dish is crafted with care. Known for its exceptional homemade pasta and decadent, house-made desserts, Serafina radiates a warmth you want to share with friends visiting from out of town. The journey up to Russian Hill—300 feet of San Francisco’s classic charm—only adds to the only in San Francisco experience. PS: One of the best gnocchi I've had outside NYC.

What a lovely locally owned gem. It’s small/quaint and the two servers are Italian men in their 50s. It’s not fussy but really focused on the food-homemade pasta and everything you need to feel like you’re like you’re in Italy.

The Tonnarelli al Nero di Seppia con Polpo was simply exceptional—easily one of the best pasta dishes I've had in San Francisco. The squid ink tonnarelli was perfectly cooked, with a wonderful texture and depth of flavor, while the octopus was tender, fresh, and expertly prepared.

Every bite reflected authentic Italian craftsmanship and a commitment to high-quality ingredients. The balance of flavors was outstanding, allowing the seafood to shine while complementing the richness of the pasta.

Beyond the incredible food, the service was warm, attentive, and professional. From start to finish, the entire dining experience was memorable.

If you're looking for outstanding Italian cuisine in San Francisco, the Tonnarelli al Nero di Seppia con Polpo is an absolute must-order. I'll definitely be back.

🍔 Truffle Burger

This burger is a masterpiece—caramelized onions and melted Jack cheese pair perfectly with the rich truffle oil that coats every bite. It's phenomenal! Also, definitely ask for some ranch on the side and pour it on before your next bite—it’s a great bite for sure.

🍟 Garlic Fries
The garlic fries are next-level, loaded with garlic and topped with six-month-aged white cheddar. Absolutely delicious!

🍴 Extras
They’ve got a self-serve soda fountain with ketchup, mustard, and spicy pickle spears. Grab a Dr Pepper or Coke and pair it with a few pickle spears—it’s a surprisingly good combo.

🍹 Refreshing End
After your meal, cool down with their iced tea. Add some lemon and sugar for the perfect finish.

Overall: This place delivers on all fronts—flavorful food, great vibes, and a solid setup. I know they are a chain but if you haven't had super duper, it's definitely worth a visit!

address: 2049 Shattuck Ave., Berkeley, CA 94704, United States

top_reviews.content:
On Saturday, June 20, 2026, I ate at Pizzeria Da Laura for my birthday.

Let me start off by saying if you don't know about Pizzeria Da Laura, you're sleeping big time on great pizza and Italian good in general.

The owner Laura, trained and worked under renowned Pizza Master Tony Gemignani. If you're from the Bay Area and don't know who Tony is, you've been asleep your entire life! Lol 😆 🤣 😂

I had high expectations for Laura's restaurant since she trained with and under Tony for years. Here's what we ordered. The Arancini which came with a red marina sauce, the Ray J New York Style Pizza 18 inch, the Grandma Style Pazzo Pizza, and the Rigatoni in Vodka cream sauce with sausage added to it. The Arancini was different compared to what I was used to. There were artichokes and a touch of lemon inside of the Arancini. It was very earthy tasting. The texture was spot on and the flavors were unique. The Ray J New York Style Pizza is some of the best pizza I've ever had. Two different types of pepperoni, fresh burrata cheese and drizzled with honey! It was such a unique and great tasting pizza. It's unlike anything I've ever had. I would highly recommend this pizza to everyone. The Pazzo Grandma style pizza was good. If you like combination pizza toppings, you'll definitely enjoy this pizza. This was my first time trying a grandma style pizza. I've tried Detroit and Sicilian style pizzas which are way thicker compared to a grandma style pizza. The grandma style pizza dough and crust was thin and very crunchy. It was served cut into an L/triangle shape. Pretty cool. I honestly was kinda upset because we wanted to try their lasagna but they ran out the night before and it wasn't available on Saturday when we are there around 4 pm. We opted for the Rigatoni pasta with Vodka cream sauce and sausage. It was beyond good! It really hit the spot! It was definitely one of the best pasta dishes I've ever eaten. The Vodka cream sauce wasn't spicy and the sausage was super flavorful. The pasta was cooked perfectly. A great dish overall!

I went with 8 people. Everyone loved the food. The atmosphere and decor/vibe of the restaurant is nice. There's a bar area and plasma screen TV's to watch a game. The restaurant is also connected a market/business right next door that sells slices of pizza from Pizzeria Da Laura, Gelato and cookies along with other Italian infused foods. Pretty cool.

Out waiter Justice was excellent! He was very attentive to details and had a great personality. Great service overall.

I took one star off because the Lasagna wasn't available. But its okay because this gives me a reason to go back and try the Lasagna.

Pizzeria Da Laura is definitely a 5 out of 5 star rating restaurant.

BTW, the owner Laura is very nice and down to earth. This was my first time meeting her. I enjoyed talking to her about Tony, various pizza/Italian infused restaurants throughout the Bay Area and just about food/pizza in general. Laura is a class act and I wish nothing but success for her restaurant and future business adventures.

Thanks again Laura and the staff at Pizzeria Da Laura for great food, great service/hospitality and a great birthday dinner!

Our first time so we ordered a crazy amount of pizza just so we could try three different styles: Sicilian, Detroit and NY. All were delicious with excellent crust and texture. The good news is that the pizza also reheats really well. We will certainly be coming back. 😋

Pizzeria da Laura in Berkeley is a fantastic spot for Italian food right in the heart of downtown, just steps from the university. The location gives it a lively downtown vibe with lots of energy from the surrounding area and nearby students.

The reservation and check-in process was very smooth. The staff were incredibly courteous, welcoming, and helpful throughout the visit. I actually arrived about 30 minutes earlier than my reservation time, and they were kind enough to seat us early, which was a really nice touch.

One thing I really like about this place is that they update their dishes a few times a year, so every visit can feel a little different and exciting. The menu has great variety, especially when it comes to pizza styles as you can choose from New York, Sicilian, Detroit, and Grandma-style pizzas, and the pricing is very straightforward for all the sizes they serve.

The pizza was perfectly cooked and tasted great. They also allow you to customize your pizza by adding or removing ingredients, which makes it very convenient for everyone to choose based on their liking. And they add toppings with open-heart.

The pasta was also excellent. We ordered the Peperoncino pasta, and it tasted amazing. The garlic flavor and breadcrumbs were really the highlight and brought out the authentic character of the spaghetti.

Another big plus is that they have plenty of vegetarian options, making it easy for different dietary preferences. The portions are generous and the prices are very reasonable for what they serve.

Food arrived quickly, and the service from the servers and staff was great throughout the visit. The restaurant also has plenty of space and handles reservations well.

The atmosphere is lively with lots of people around and students from the nearby university, which adds to the downtown Berkeley energy. A little more upbeat music could add even more charm to the place.

Overall, this is a place I would definitely recommend to anyone visiting Berkeley. It’s the kind of restaurant I’d happily come back to again and again.

Me and the lady went here, cause of Bay Area Check Please! You know? Cause that’s what we do. The evening we went it was busy, but we had little wait for our table. The homie Fernando was cool and on top of things. It Did however take a min to get the pies. But it wasn’t a crazy long wait. About the pies we got: I got the Detroit style of what’s called The Ray J which is named after Laura’s brother. I saw her make that on an episode Localish. My lady got a New York style of a “make your own”. Both were fire. The dough on the New York style was nice and slightly chewy. And on the Detroit style, the way the cheese cooked around the edges were tasty than a mug! If you know you know. The ambiance was cool. I mean, it’s a pizza place. Music was on point. Nah’mean?!?! Check it out.

Definitely one of the Top 3 Pizza restaurants I have ever been to. The food was INCREDIBLE! The service was top notch. The historic building was beautifully transformed into the perfect space of luxury. What a great experience, and I cannot wait to return to try some more of her Pizza. My wife bought her book in hopes of miraculously recreating our perfect meal! Thank you! ❤️❤️

My boyfriend and I had such a great experience here on Thursday! We originally planned to eat at another restaurant across the street, but after waiting a while without being greeted, we decided to come here instead and it turned out to be the best decision.

We went for lunch, and it was a great experience! Staff was very attentive, friendly and food came very quickly. We got the garlic beef filet, Hong Kong style beef chow mein and soup dumplings. The portions were really plentiful and the price was more than fair. Would definitely come again when we are in SF :)

Came here after a nice stroll in Golden Gate Park, and it was probably the best decision we made. We ordered the dry chicken, crispy Hong Kong–style noodles, and eggplant stir-fry. The portions were generous, and all the dishes were excellent.

A San Francisco institution at its absolute best
Chang’s Kitchen is hands down the best Chinese restaurant in San Francisco and, in my opinion, the entire Bay Area. I’ve been dining here since 1988, through multiple ownership changes, and the current ownership has truly set the bar at its highest. Owner Jenny deserves tremendous credit for preserving the soul of the restaurant while elevating standards across the board—from food quality to service.
The flavors are consistently outstanding. The Hunan Basil Shrimp is phenomenal—bold, aromatic, and perfectly balanced with just the right amount of heat. The Mongolian Beef is easily the best I’ve ever had: incredibly tender, deeply flavorful, and cooked to absolute perfection. Every dish tastes fresh, authentic, and thoughtfully prepared.
What truly elevates the experience, however, is the service. Loo is an exceptional waiter in every sense of the word—attentive, professional, warm, and genuinely invested in making each visit memorable. His service alone sets a standard that few restaurants can match. Lisa is also wonderful, adding to the welcoming, polished atmosphere that makes dining here such a pleasure.
After decades of returning, I can confidently say Chang’s Kitchen has never been better. This is more than a restaurant—it’s a true San Francisco institution. If you’re looking for top-tier Chinese cuisine paired with outstanding hospitality, this place is an absolute must-visit.
Highly recommended. ⭐️🥢

A wonderful shop offering high-quality, delicious, and fresh meat products made according to Polish recipes. I was delighted with my purchase of Ukrainian sausage today! I also enjoy buying sweets here.

The shop is clean and cozy, with a pleasant Slavic atmosphere and a good selection of products.

A special thank you to Mr. Andrzej for his excellent service today. I asked for Ukrainian sausage—specifically a lean variety without garlic—and trusted his recommendation. He made my shopping experience truly pleasant, even though he had clearly been working hard and had just helped a demanding customer before me.

I know that Mr. Andrzej speaks English, Polish, Ukrainian, and Russian, which is a great help to many customers. I have great respect for him and sincerely wish the shop continued success and prosperity. I visited on Saturday, just before closing time. The selection was smaller than usual, but the store was impeccably clean; it was nice to see that the food packaging consisted of high-quality, snow-white paper, along with extra paper for the products. top_reviews.content:
Bellanico was participating in Oakland Restaurant Week and I'd never been there, so along with a couple of friends who'd also never been there, we got an early evening reservation for their special prix fixe restaurant week menu. There was a very  generous set of choices from appetizers through dessert, a total of four choices for each diner (Cicchetti, Primi, Secondi, and Dolcini sampler, which was an extra $10) and within those choices there were three to four items to choose from, for $65 pp. + $10 for the Dolcini, plus drinks, tax, and tip.
For Cicchetti, we chose two of the 3 offerings:
Smoked King Salmon Canoli and Orange Cauliflower Fritters, both of these were simply delicious. We'd expected the cauliflower fritters to be slices of cauliflower, but instead they were pureed and fried and served like little balls or dumplings with a lovely sauce and some arugula - wonderful.

For Primi we ordered
Seared Ahi Tuna Carpaccio, Burrata, and Organic Farro Verde, which we shared amongst us: the carpaccio and the burrata were delicious, and even the non-carpaccio-eating diner tried a tiny piece and liked it! However, the sherry vinaigrette on the farro was very difficult to detect, which was a tiny bit disappointing because all the other ingredients seemed to work so well together.
For Secondi, two of us chose the salmon - one cooked medium and one cooked well, and the other dish chosen was the risotto. Everyone was very happy with their choices. I usually steer clear of both gnocchi and risotto in restaurants because frequently they are poorly executed, however the taste I had of the risotto here was absolutely delicious and I wouldn't hesitate to order it here! The salmon was seared with the skin on, which was lovely and crunchy, and served over black rice - the entire dish was lovely!
For Dolcini, we chose one of each of the offerings: goat cheese cheesecake, chocolate rosemary bread pudding, and bomboloni (very much like donut holes, who served with berries, custard, and chocolate). We were so full that we all settled for a lovely cups of decaf coffee and took our desserts home! As of this writing I haven't tried my cheesecake, but based on everything else I had last night I'm sure it will be delicious.
And our server was simply lovely, as were the couple of other employees we interacted with - everyone was friendly in a genuine way and that often makes all the difference in one's experience. We thoroughly enjoyed our dinner and we'll be back!
The quality of the food and people are awesome. Along with the plates they serve. Highly recommend for those itching for some delicious food

I love this place. Like LOVE.

The food I’ve gotten here has always been very flavorful, well cooked, and presented beautifully. They also have a good selection of wine as well if you want to drink wine. Their desserts are also delicious, I always order the doughnuts which come with a dark chocolate sauce and this white sauce.

They used to have these fish cannolis that were heavenly but unfortunately, those aren’t on the menu anymore.

Outdoor seating: yes

Nice owners and staff: yes
Price: it’s on the pricier side
Wine price: ~ $11-16 per glass

We had an outstanding dinner at Bellancio Restaurant and Wine BarWhat made our meal so remarkable? Every thing we ordered was very unique and delicious. We started with their “ Little Gems” Antipasti which consisted of “pickled butternut squash &red onion, gorgonzola, candied walnuts and dijon vinaigrette “! We also had a ravioli that was described as “ Casunzei Red beet & ricotta ravioli , butter sauce,poppy seeds and GRANA PADANO! These two dishes were unlike any I’ve ever had in an Italian or any restaurant! And both were absolutely exceptionally delicious! Maya was our server and she was wonderful too! And for dessert, we ordered an amazing selection of their favorite desserts that was perfect for the perfect for the four of us but selfishly, I would have loved to have it all for myself!

Our first dish we got was toast with cured salmon paste on it.  The toast was crispy and had a nice texture to it.  The paste was a good accompaniment and it was a nice dish to munch on.  We then were able to try the wild boar and ricotta ravioli.  I liked the ravioli though it was a pretty plain dish and did not think anything much of it.

I was also able to get the Russet potato gnocchi with gargonzola cream and toasted almonds.  This was my favorite dish here.  The almonds provide a nice texture and the gnocchi was prepared well and tasted great.

For dessert I got the goat cheese cheesecake.  This was a nice tasting cheesecake and it was not overly sweet.  It just had the right amount of minimal sweetness which I liked.

I really like the interior of this restaurant and the service was very attentive and nice.  I definitely would come back!

top_reviews.content:
They pack generous portions for all options, and their grilled edamame is fantastic, given for free with plates and 3 triangle orders.

I started ordering from them during their opening week, and I have never been let down. Not once. I have tried every type of meat, plates, small plates, and triangles. Everything is superb.

Unexpectedly ordered 3 triangles here for a late lunch and it didn’t disappoint. I ordered on the kiosk, and there was a little bit of a wait. It is a small space with only 4 seats inside. A lot of other people also in line to order and waiting for their food. I would definitely come back and try other triangles, I got the chicken teriyaki, grilled salmon and short rib. All very yummy. Heads up!  This is Americanized Onigiri (Japanese Rice Balls).  You are not getting Japanese style “rice triangles” that you would find in Japan and Hawaii in terms of quality (type of rice and seaweed) and style (fillings).  Initially the price seemed expensive because in Hawaii you can get onigiri for $2-$4, but here they are generous with the fillings and it’s a little bigger in size so the price seems fair.  It was pretty good here, but I prefer the traditional Japanese style.

It’s in a school zone so it can get busy.  I found free street parking easily so that was nice.  You order and pay with card on the device to your left when you enter.  You can follow the directions on the screen to pay cash at the register.  It was a full house, but orders were distributed efficiently and quickly.  If the cashier is busy, the chefs help pass out the food so I thought that was great teamwork.

If you want something fast and filling, head to Oori Rice Triangles!
I had spicy pork,  short ribs, and salmon. It's was very delicious. I  also have had their triangles, which are excellent.

As someone who works in customer service myself, I know how basic standards of respect, cleanliness, accuracy, and transparency should be handled and this location fell way short on every level. I will not be coming back to this location (or any Panda Express) again.

top_reviews.content:
Really enjoyed everything we ordered. Seafood pancake was super crispy and substantial (perfect to share). Kalbi was nicely grilled and tender enough. Tofu soup was full of seafood. Chapchae was also nice.

It was one of my favorite Korean spots in SF since 2021, but my recent visit earlier this month was disappointing. The food and service no longer felt authentic, and it honestly made me wonder if there’s new management. Something definitely changed from how the complimentary sides are placed (now in a single plate with partitions that look like school cafeteria) to the ambiance and food flavor. Less people too as it was packed on my first time here.

I ordered the stone pot rice, but there was barely any rice in it. Instead, it was mostly filled with sprouts, carrots, ginger, and other fillers/condiments that are usually served complimentary on the side. I asked our waitress, “Are you running low on rice?” She initially responded, “Would you like more? We can add some.” Of course, I said yes.

She went to the kitchen, and I overheard one of the cooks ask what was wrong. After she explained, I heard laughter from the kitchen. The waitress then returned and said, “Sorry, the cook said that’s how it’s prepared and we can’t add any more rice.”

First, don’t offer something if it can’t be accommodated. Second, the lack of professionalism and the ridicule I experienced were disappointing. Korean restaurants are often known for both authenticity and warm service, regardless of size, which is why this experience stood out in a negative way.

I still left a 20% gratuity, but unfortunately I won’t be returning. Not a good vibe at all.

It's a no frills restaurant with traditional Hong Kong cafe options. Most meals come with soup, veggies, rice, AND dessert! Each dish is not 10/10 crazy good but it will surely leave you satisfied.

#2

A Hong Kong café I’ve loved for a long time!
Since the pandemic, many things have changed. Some businesses have thrived, while others that used to do well have started struggling. This place is one of the latter.

In recent years, everything has become much more expensive, leading to significant changes in restaurant prices as well. This café is no exception. Once a spot where people would line up, it’s hard to find those scenes anymore.

That said, this place is still delicious, still affordable, and still serves generous portions! They have daily specials, and they even serve jello for dessert! I love their pasta, pork chops, and milk tea—it’s all so good!

#1

One place you might want to consider for a Hong Kong-style lunch cafe!!
It offers generous portions and decent flavors for the price. Enjoy your meal in Hong Kong!

Fantastic food and service from everyone there! Comfy and cozy ambience with soft and warm lighting. The staff were extremely welcoming from the beginning and answered all of our questions. The fish was extremely fresh without any hints of "fishiness". We highly recommend the "crispy rice" for appetizers and the omakase experience! 100% would come back - thanks for having us!

I went there with my wife for a special occasion. Made reservation 3 weeks prior to try their course menu. The food was fine, it was concise but effective with good quality ingredients and enough depth to each palette. The issue was how the course menu was designed and how it was served. The course menu was a most one hour experience, but we were there for nearly 2 hours. Each course had 20~25 minute wait in between without further explanation from the staff. Eventually towards the end one guy came to us and apologized for the wait due to kitchen being too busy. I understand things can get busy but this is a course menu. Any high caliber kitchen should be able to execute same quality course menu experience 10 out of 10 times. It ruined the night for us on a special day and it was utterly pissing that we were forced to pay over $50 in tips. If you value your time I would not go here. If you enjoy staring at the wall for an hour, yeah why not.

Good variety of selections. The sushi portions are not too big, and the prices are reasonable. I just wish the fish could be served slightly warmer - I understand it’s kept chilled for safety, but the strong contrast between the cool fish and warm rice slightly affects the overall enjoyment.

Still, it was a good experience overall!

the waitress is the best woman i've ever met. she is so kind and always make sure to smile at customers as well as checking on them. the food is good and the portion is more than enough for me. highly recommend and would visit again!!!!!!

top_reviews.content: My lips were properly numbed after eating my meal, which is exactly the way it should be, after a good Szechuan meal. Hahaha!  The lunch special included a delicious hot & sour soup (not pictured), a side dish of 2 vegetables (blanched but very flavorful), and the twice cooked pork.  It was ~$16 for the complete meal before tax.  Great deal!  Besides the lunch special, we also had the hot & sour noodles and the spicy stir fried chicken.  I’d order the chicken again!  Deep fried small pieces with lots of dry chili and it was mala and addictive.  I cleaned the plate.  The service was attentive and the ladies were friendly.  I’ll be back!

Was not sure to go in because it looked quiet, but….what a hidden gem. Food was amazing and inside is very clean. The menu card is not dirty and the food was fresh and tasty. The smoked duck was fantastic. The only disappointment was the whole chicken that was really small.

Stopped in for some classic Szechuan dishes and overall had a really solid experience. The food was bold, flavorful, and packed with spice, though a little on the salty side across a couple of dishes.

Highlights:
* Dan Dan Noodles - one of the best dishes of the night. Perfect chew on the noodles and a sauce that balanced spice and nuttiness really well.
* Pig Ears - surprisingly delicious! Great texture and seasoning, definitely a standout and something I'd recommend.
* Dry-Fried Green Beans - crisp, garlicky, and addictive.
* Beef with Peppers - tender slices with plenty of heat, though again a touch salty.
* Fish Fillet with Chili - tasty and fresh, but I've had stronger versions elsewhere in the city, so not my personal favorite here.

The portions were generous, the food came out quickly, and everything had that signature Szechuan punch of heat and flavor. If you like bold dishes and don't mind a little extra salt, this place is definitely worth a visit.
Food is delicious. Ordered on DoorDash and was very pleasantly pleased. Not usually a big fan of tofu but I'm hooked here. Absolutely on my list to reorder.

A flawless experience from start to finish. Copper Chimney truly stands out as one of the best Indian restaurants in San Francisco. From the moment you walk in, the atmosphere feels warm and welcoming, with a perfect blend of modern style and authentic charm.

The lunch buffet is also an amazing deal with a wide variety of options that are consistently fresh and delicious.
Service is top-notch — the staff is friendly, attentive, and makes sure you feel taken care of throughout your meal.
Whether you're dining in, grabbing a quick lunch, or ordering catering, Copper Chimney delivers quality every single time. Highly recommended for anyone craving real Indian flavors!

Would get again for the coconut chicken curry but would probably try other dishes instead of the tikka masala.

top_reviews.content:
I finally made it to Delfina, a spot I have been wanting to try for a while, and chose it to celebrate a friend’s birthday. I booked online and called ahead to add one more person to the reservation, and the staff were happy to accommodate, which set a great tone from the start.

We sat outside under the heaters, which were surprisingly effective. We stayed warm and comfortable the entire evening. The restaurant was packed for a Sunday night, but service never felt rushed and remained attentive throughout.

For food, we shared the Margherita pizza, which ended up being the standout dish of the night. It was simple, balanced, and very well executed. We also tried the beef carpaccio, which was solid, and the duck, which was just okay. My friend mentioned it was difficult to cut, which took away from the experience a bit. I ordered the beef cheek agnolotti, but unfortunately it came out quite cold, which was disappointing.

Dessert completely redeemed the meal. We ordered a hazelnut ice cream encased in a chocolate shell, and it was absolutely delicious. It was easily one of the highlights of the night.

Overall, Delfina delivered a lively atmosphere, strong service, and some standout dishes, especially the pizza and dessert. While a couple of dishes missed the mark, I would still come back, especially for those.
Great restaurant with high quality dishes. Bread with ricotta was yummy, and the salad was refreshing as well. Pasta dishes (forgot to grab pics) were delicious too. All around lovely evening

Inviting atmosphere and good service, but disappointing food.  Perplexed by the rave reviews here?!????

The environment is inviting and the wait staff was friendly and attentive, which we appreciated. Unfortunately, the food itself was overly salted and disappointing overall.
•	Grilled octopus: very small portion and extremely salty. It was only partially cleaned, leaving fatty, slimy fascia that was inedible and had to be removed at the table (see pic). The dominant flavor was salt.
•	Langherino bottone: supposed to be mushroom cheese ravioli, but the filling was watery with only a light mushroom flavor. Mostly salty, and $35 for nine ravioli felt hard to justify.
•	Margherita pizza: very sparse mozzarella, and the dough inside the crust edges lacked tenderness.
•	Smothered chard: initially very salty, but after asking for a remake it came back well-balanced and was actually very good.

Overall, the service and atmosphere were excellent, but the food quality and seasoning issues made the meal disappointing.

we had an excellent Sunday family dinner here. we were very late to our reservation time. usually i don’t know what to do when this happened. the communication with Delfina was smooth and stress free.

we didn’t order drinks but loved every dish we ordered! the duck was a little salty still very good!

the atmosphere was good and casual which i liked. i didn’t like the music though. it’s just my personal preference.

An unexpected surprise amidst the culinary chaos of our times! I wandered in with modest expectations and departed in something resembling a rapture.

The Tomatoes and Smoked Ricotta Pizza was, dare I confess, a revelation. ’It has been many years since a new pizza stirred my jaded soul to such affection, indeed, I feared myself incapable of love again until that first bite. Light as a summer whisper, balanced as a well rehearsed lie. Each ingredient performed its role with Shakespearean precision: the tomato, a tragic hero bursting with passion; the ricotta, a noble companion doomed to melt away too soon and arugula, holding it altogether like a valiant Knight.

And then, the dessert! The Buttermilk Panna Cotta arrived like a gentle epilogue after the storm. The passion fruit lent it a whisper of mischief, striking the precise note between sweet affection and savoury betrayal. One might say it tasted like love, delightful yet often, confusing.

I shall return one day, fork in hand, ready to rekindle our brief but passionate affair, provided, of course, San Francisco hasn’t sunk beneath its own rent prices by then.

top_reviews.content:
Pippal delivers one of those dining experiences where everything clicks.

From the moment we walked in, the service stood out. The atmosphere matched that energy. Clean, thoughtfully designed, and comfortable in a way that lets you settle in and enjoy the meal.

The food absolutely held its own. The beetroot kebab was the highlight. Perfectly crusted on the outside, giving way to a creamy, cheesy center, all brought together with a rich beet sauce.

The chaat was vibrant and well-balanced, hitting all the textures and flavors you hope for. And the litti chokha was a great surprise.

This is the kind of place that feels dialed in across the board. Great service, great atmosphere, and food that lives up to both. Definitely worth a visit.

We didn't realize this place is both Indian and Mediterranean food, not fusion. The menu is split with different options from each cuisine.

Overall our experience was decent, but we wouldn't return due to the high cost vs portion size. For example, the butter chicken was $26 then to add rice or naan was an additional $6 or $8. The butter chicken was good but not worth it. The naan was too thin and crunchy.
The falafel wrap was good with 5 waffle fries, not a bad price at $18. Our friend got the plate of falafel which wasn't as great and had no sauce. They did provide a tiny cup of hummus to use on one falafel. The flavors were good so it's a shame how costly it is compared to other restaurants in the same area.

It was very festive with party/club like music and busy! There was indoor and outdoor seating but it was cold outside and more of a waiting area. There’s street parking in a pretty busy main area.

We started with the Sai Aou- Pork Sausage, Thai Papaya Salad (less spicy than Lao), then ordered Panang Curry with Beef (slow cooked) I saw lots of people review this one. Everything was really good and delicious! Definitely hit the Thai food craving! Lively, colorful, and bright inside! We were able to easily split the bill and they had a handheld machine to pay.

We came on Saturday evening for dinner. I’ve never been here. We came to do a little food tasting possibly use them for catering for an event. So the moment you get there you join a waitlist to be seated. The restaurant was busy but we didn’t have to wait for too long. We waited maybe 8-10 minutes and we were seated.

The restaurant is not that big but maybe they have an area for big parties? I’m not sure. However, the ambiance is cute, cozy, and inviting. I love the accent wall, it’s picture worthy.

Now, let’s talk about the food. We didn’t just order one or two appetizers we ordered four and I highly recommend them: crispy shrimp roll, spicy chicken wings, crispy tofu over peanut sauce, and Roti bread (which I can eat all day). Everything tasted so fresh and like off the stove.

We also order a few dishes: Nam Khao lettuce wrap, crab fried rice, pumpkin curry with chicken and Pad Thai of course. I don’t know if I was hungry or what but everything was delicious. I never had Nam Khao which is a crispy rice with Chinese sausage and crispy pork. I loved it! It is like an explosion ingredients in my mouth so tasty.

The price: I was surprised we ordered so much food and we spent less than $200. We even had cocktail drinks and dessert. Mango Sticky on point! I don’t know about you but I felt like I was eating some really good food but also sort of healthy. I recommend this place  100 percent.

For example their Fried mackerel really hits the spot with its crispy exterior, soft fluffy interior, and generous side of peas and bean sprouts and comes with miso soup too. They also offer a large variety of combo trays for sushi that would easily serve and satisfy large parties. Lastly I would also recommend their dozen oysters, that come with topped with fish eggs along with optional Japanese sauce (forgot the name) and lemon.

As for the staff, the chef is always greeting and saying goodbye to everyone from his cook station near the front of house and is a very lovable man. The waiters and waitresses are extremely attentive and friendly too. I'm very glad I found this place. Would highly recommend, a true San Francisco gem.

Decided to eat at this restaurant, and was highly impressed with the serving sizes, and extremely nice staff. Ordered the chicken katsu, and loved the dish for the nice crisp, flavor, and not too salty. As aforementioned, the staff were quite personal, and frequently checking on us, attending to other patrons. Would highly recommend this place!

Nice place. Food was good. Service was fast.  My family likes the sizzling fish dishes, which are very tasty. Clam ramen is a popular dish and that was good too. All in all a good place for dinner/lunch.

Came across this place as we were going through the sunset. It was busy and for good reason! High quality fish at a fair price point. We loved everything we got! Split beers and rolls in a party of 5 and it was around 30pp. We'll be back!

top_reviews.content:
Pineapple beer or grapefruit beer- must have. It’s refreshing.

Seared toro sushi- great flavour. Recommend

Mozuku shot- too sour. I’ve had this in Okinawa before and it wasn’t like this- skip.

Pork cheek skewer- flavourful. A little fatty but it’s good.

Chicken gizzard- our favourite

Chicken heart- not our favourite. Skip. It was a bit mushier than we expected.

Hand rolls (Toro, miso trio) - both good.

Side note- their wasabi is delicious. Get it on the side and add to whatever you like to add a kick.

Rating is closer to 3.8, but I debated giving it a 4 stars because of a few reasons: food enjoyment and price affordability.

First, I experienced impeccable service. Shoutout to the lady who worked all of front-of-house, she is a boss. She was our hostess, server, ran food, and bused tables. All the while, checking in on us often and letting us know when things were on the way so we didn’t feel forgotten.

Food is all small plate shareables. Our one entree was the pork cheek fried rice. Maybe it was just what we ordered but I felt like everything was really oily/greasy. The freshest items were the negitoro roll and the potato salad they gave to us at the start for free. Yes, it’s an izakaya, but we found ourselves struggling to continue eating the plates since it felt so heavy. Sure, maybe we didn’t order the right stuff, but lots of the menu items are deep fried, stir-fried, or grilled also. We enjoyed the cumin lamb skewers and the negitoro the best! We were disappointed in the truffle poppers as each bite was more filled with fried breading than mushrooms. The dessert was beautiful and we did enjoy that.

We ended up paying like 100pp including tax and tip. There are many Japanese izakayas I can pay less for in San Francisco including a la carte at Rintaro! But anyways, shoutout to the hostess lady, she’s a boss.

We chose Chome as a makeup for a bad dinner choice the night before, and honestly this place HEALED me 😭 (not literally, but you get the idea).

We got there around 8:17 PM even though they close at 9:30, and they welcomed us in with no wait and never made us feel rushed. I would still recommend giving them a quick call to confirm if you’re planning to come this late, especially on a busier night.

Parking was actually pretty easy to find nearby, and the surrounding area felt nice to walk around, so even if you have to park a little further away, it’s not a bad walk at all.

Our server was AMAZING, super attentive, friendly, and very patient with us. It was our first time here, so naturally we had a million questions and needed lots of recommendations lol. She walked us through everything without making us feel rushed.

We also really loved the range of the menu. There are SO many options, but somehow it didn’t feel overwhelming, it actually made ordering easier because there was something for every craving. This would be such a good place to come with a group and order a bunch of things to share.

The food itself was delicious, unique, and honestly the portions were HUGE. Once everything came out, the pricing made a lot more sense. You’re definitely getting a substantial amount of food, and we left VERY full.

The drinks are also a huge bonus. We ordered 3 in total and genuinely enjoyed all 3, so definitely don’t skip the drink menu.

And for dessert, we got the fried durian. If you like durian, PLEASE get it. Crispy, warm, creamy, and honestly the best possible way to finish our dinner 😭

Overall, Chome was easily one of our best dinner choices on this trip. Great food, huge portions, fun drinks, lots of variety, and amazing service. Definitely a spot I’d recommend, especially if you’re coming with someone who likes trying and sharing different dishes.

Mediocre food, but everything else was nice.

Walked into a very cozy atmosphere, a bit chilly so we got a hot tea which was nice.

As for food,

Chutoro crispy rice sizzle thing: nice but rice and sweet sauce flavor are overpowering. The chutoro had a big tendon running through the middle making it hard to chew

Oysters: very good! Sweet and umami, clean oysters. Maybe a tad too sweet

Ocean chawanmushi "creme brulee" with crab and uni: this was was the most disappointing. Quite a small amount of egg, also tasted completely unseasoned. There was caramelized brown sugar just like creme brulee which was too much and I tried to remove, but couldn't.

Duck skewers: pretty good

Oxtail omurice: very underseasoned for me. Kind of heavy. Pretty good with some salt but not amazing.

Overall was disappointed by the food, especially the ocean chawanmushi creme brulee. Everything else was good
Cozy and delicious experience of small plates and sake. Expect a slight wait. Everything we had was perfectly executed- loved the noodle bowl. For me, a must-visit.

top_reviews.content:
I was really disappointed with my experience at Soo Fong Restaurant. The portion size was extremely small for the price, and to make matters worse, my food was cold when I got it.

I called the restaurant to politely ask if I could either get a refund or have them make it right by giving me a little more food. Instead, I was simply told, “No,” and that they would “talk to the chef.” There was no attempt to fix the situation or satisfy a paying customer.

Good customer service goes a long way, especially when there are issues with the food. Unfortunately, this experience left me feeling like my concerns didn’t matter. I won’t be returning, and I hope the restaurant improves both its portion sizes and its customer service.

Found this little gem while looking for something to eat. Been looking for a while and the reviews got me. The food is delicious and the staff are friendly. They can be busy at time so pleaae be patient. The area is kinda okay, a lot of traffic and semi drivers. Take your time.

Despite the restaurant's reputation as a reliable neighborhood spot for American-style Chinese cuisine, the actual dining experience was deeply disappointing. The dishes lacked balance and consistency, with most falling far short of the expectations set by the menu descriptions; while portions were generous, the quality failed to match the quantity. The chow mein and fried rice were lackluster, missing the expected depth of flavor, while the noodle soup was bland, lacking the richness and complexity of a high-quality broth. Items such as salt-and-pepper chicken wings, fried fish, fried calamari, and fried pork chops failed to deliver the anticipated crispiness, and the seasoning was poorly balanced; the overall flavor profile was uninspired and disjointed, lacking any memorable, vibrant taste.
Ultimately, the dining experience was a letdown."

Price is up $19 from $11 for fried rice but the portions stays the same???   Makes no damn sense!!!   Why is this place still open???  I won't be eating here anymore!!!  Theres perfectly good Chinese food restaurants in the SCO still worth your time soo fong is not one them!!!

My first time ordering from here and the food was delicious.  It definitely hit the spot on this cold and rainy day.  I had placed my order through doordash.
I  am very thankful that they took extra care by placing saran wrap on the Wonton Soup.  Lady who delivered my order didn't really handle my order with care when delivered.  The soup was very comforting and delicious wontons.
Mongolian Beef was delicious.  Generous with the fried rice.  I wished I had asked for chili hot oil.

top_reviews.content:
their rice rolls and some of their dim sums were surprisingly cheap and very well made.

the steamed lava buns were delicious. the lava yolk was perfectly sweet and not broken. the buns needed some work though — it was not soft enough.

spicy wontons with chili oil was okay to say the best. i can see this was definitely not their specialty dishes

their steamed rice rolls with soy sauce (the one i got was the crispy skin with shrimp) were exceptional! their soy sauce was well balanced and perfectly sweet. their skills when making the steamed rice rolls were soft, thin, and perfectly moist. I will definitely be getting more of these next time

their lobster with ginger scallion noodles we’re pretty good. lobster was a tad overcooked, the sauce was decent

The pan fried pork soup dumplings were decent. The exterior shell was perfectly crisp and thin, but the pork lacked flavor of freshness.

the rabbit shaped mango pudding was not good. the mango flavor was non existent. the rabbits were way too hard, and tasteless.

the turtle jelly was good. the consistency was too thick. it lacked some herbal taste. the syrup was phenomenal though.

the steamed har gow was very well done. the filling was very well seasoned, and the dumpling was perfectly thin.
Greta neighborhood spot for some dim sum. They have all the classics and the inside is very clean. It’s a bit small though so Mae a reservation ahead of time or add you bae early on the waitlist.

We were visiting SF and one thing my hubby always want is dim sum. We just didn't want to spend an arm and a leg for it.
We heard of Dim Sum Club and never tried it. So why not?

We were 2nd on the wait list and got seated within about 10 mins. Its a small cute little restaurant so no carts rolling around here. They give you a menu and pen, you mark what you want.

They took our order quickly but food took a while to come out.  Once it started coming, though, it was worth the wait, everything tasted great!

My favorite was the chives and shrimp dumplings, the skin was a perfect thick/thinness, so fresh, full of flavor. We ordered two types of tripe, spicy and soy/ginger. The radishes was crispy on the outside and soft on the outside. The stuffed eggplant was surprisingly delicious, it had a crispy skin and sweet soy glaze with a little ball of minced plumped shrimp. The chicken feet were tender and seasoned just right. And of course you can't go wrong with thr basics of ha gow and siu mai.

The food was delicious overall and not overpriced like a lot of dim sum spots in SF. Even with the slow timing, I’d still come back for the food alone.

We were in the area and decided to check out this restaurant for lunch. All the patrons were Asian so it was a good sign. Service was prompt and attentive. We ordered the usual dim sum dishes. The selection was limited. The har gow skins were perfectly cooked with a light spring to every chew. Most of the time, the dumplings at other dim sum restaurants were overcooked and mushy but not these. The chicken feet were flavorful. The price is affordable considering its location. All the foods were delicious. The wait staff cleared the empty plates quickly. It’s a great find and we will definitely return to try other dishes next time.

Came here for dim sum for the first time with my family, it was so good! We love getting the OG dishes like siu mai and har gow. I feel like if a place can get just the originals right, then everything else will taste good and I was right! I almost wanted to get another plate of siu mai but I was already so full from everything else.

Coming here on a weekend is definitely going to be really busy and may have a long wait, definitely plan ahead!
