Seriously great. The mini Riceless bowl is the best possible deal for a tasty keto meal in SF at an affordable price. Surprised at how difficult is to be low carb in this city or spend less than 18 USD when eating out but this was superb.

The Mini ($11 USD), is actually bigger than I expected, it's a proper meal portion and the price is right.

Wish I had found out about it earlier in my trip to SF.

Pictured in the image is the full size at the top and the mini at the bottom (black container). 10/10 no notes.

Ive been to this eatery a few times. This time i decided to order online from them.
When I received the order, the chicken breats was a slice, of cut-through the length chicken breast. The chicken thigh was also pretty meager. It seemed I got less than half the amount of chicken, than when I went to the place myself.
I initially liked this place, but after this experience I just dont feel respected or appreciated as a customer, and will look for another chicken rice place nearby.

I would normally eat here every day because quality and convenience is good, but the wait is too long, even for ordering ahead, and knowing when my order will be ready is unpredictable. If I go early for pickup I end up waiting longer and wasting time. If I go later after its ready it'll be cold by time I eat it.
I like it. It's low key, fast & casual counter service spot serving up tasty khao man gai, Thai Chicken and rice. Pretty affordable too!

top_reviews.content: Lots of food options ex: steak, pasta, bbq chicken,  spaghetti & garlic bread, fast service, delicious pizza, clean restaurant and restrooms. Seating inside. Parking a little challenge but overall would order again.

When I was growing up I would always get pizza at Mr. Pizza Man at my childhood location. Fast forward to 2025, me and my friend was craving for some pizza and in the back of my head I know there was a pizza spot where I have yet to give it a shot which is a Mr. pizza Man location. It was nearby so we decided to give it try and to refresh my memory. Upon arrival, it was a hot day and when we entered it felt very good with their air conditioning and fans on. There were a few people dining in, I was browsing their menu since everything looked and sound good. They offer build your own pizza, specialty pizzas, pasta, burgers, sandwiches, appetizers, salads, special offers and much more to choose from. Everything is made to order which is always a plus for me since it is quality over quantity and I never mind the wait at all because I am a very patient person. The staffs here are welcoming, well trained and understanding where my visit was a satisfying and issue free one. Also you can dine in, order for takeout or have it delivered straight to your location via a delivery app. I highly recommend this place to all pizza enthusiasts, if you are in need of a quick bite, to anyone willing to try something new, if you are looking for a laid back place to dine at or if you just so happen to be in the area. I definitely will be back to tryout the other delicious options they have to offer.

I was curious for sometime now to check out the Brazilian Pizza. I was there with a couple of my work buddies. Pizza was way below average and so was the Beef Stroganoff which was the absolute worse I ever tried. Horrendous.
If you haven't tried the special burger (Brazilian Grill) at this place yet, I honestly recommend it. Because it is WONDERFUL.

I been here both lunch and dinner times, during lunch service the price is pretty cheap with many things to choose from. For meats they offer beef bulgogi, brisket, beef belly, pork belly, marinated chicken, spicy chicken, seafood items, spicy and non-spicy meats, steak, ribs and much more to choose from.. And during dinner time they have the full menu available. The limit is four meat options per order which comes out quick when placed and serving is full size here This place is usually packed, but that does not bother me since I am a very patient person. The service here is top notch thanks to their well trained, helpful, polite and understanding staffs where I have never encountered an issue during any of my visits. All of the ingredients they use here are premium, delicious and carefully picked. I highly recommend this spot to all Korean barbecue enthusiasts, to anyone willing to try something new, if you are in need of a quick bite or if you just so happen to be in the area to check them out. I definitely will be back to tryout the other delicious options they have to offer.

We had a big group for birthday dinner on Friday. Had made a reservation two weeks ago in advance. I called a couple of times to reconfirm the reservation beforehand. To be honest, I was worried about the food quality and service after checked the reviews. Not sure about those negative reviews. Turned out all we had good KBBQ All You Can Eat! Foods were good except for shrimps, they weren’t fresh. Service was good and fast. Spacious, friendly. No cake cutting charge. I would have given 5 stars if they have improved their ventilation system.
Overall was good. Definitely would come back again for a big group dinner!
Incredible food with the nicest staff. My favorite Korean bbq in the city!!! The meat quality is excellent.

The only good thing about this place is the staff, really quick and kind. In terms of the food, I have to say a lot of meat but the quality of it left me speechless. As the other reviews say, the meat is really flavorless. I have been in many bbqs of this style but never had to leave because I just couldn’t eat it. Also not having a fan above your grill is definitely something that threw me off. (Just go to the other nearby even tho they are a bit more expensive at least u will come out satisfied I guarantee)

Overall this place is a gem and definitely nice place for a great meal. It was bit warm in there so better ventilation would be appreciated. Food quality was excellent, options were generous, it was tasty, and service was excellent. Keep up the great work.

top_reviews.content: Came here for lunch on a Saturday. Laos is one of the few Asian countries I haven’t been to so I can’t say whether it’s authentic but, damn was it good. Had the nom khao rice and the sai qua Laotian sausage . Family style and portions are huge!

I have high expectation of what the food would taste like based on an ad my Mother saw on Facebook.   We ordered four dishes, two were great and two were barely average IMO.

The crispy spring roll and a short ribs weee excellent. Our favorite was crispy spring roll and is a must-have. My son could have eaten it all by himself, he said.

Unfortunately, the same cannot be said for Rad Na and crab fried.  The Rad na was sweet and the restaurant does not have vinegar (น้ำพริกน้ำส้ม) even though they’re selling Thai food. That was a big disappointment because that is my mom’s favorite and we came here specifically to eat that.

The crab fried rice could be better with the wok being hotter. There is no “wok burn” smell, for all those that know how fried rice should be made. Uncle Roger would have given it a two out of five.

The waitresses were very nice and quick. The restaurant was clean and well decorated.

Overall, it’s an ok experience. I wish I could love it more. If the restaurant owner reads this, I suggest the rice rice you also have a green pickle, jalapeño in vinegar sauce available to serve. And make sure the wok is hot before smashing rice. That’s how a Thai person would eat Thai food.

This place now becomes my favorite place to go for a special Thai dish called Yum Nam Khao Tod (crispy rice ball salad with fermented pork). It takes the top spot in every way: the generous portion, the authentic flavor, and the freshness of the ingredients. Other dishes like papaya salad and spring rolls are also fresh and refreshing. I am so happy that my friend found this place and I would love to visit there again and again.

Everything was absolutely delicious. Highly recommend the Khao Soy soup- so comforting, fresh, and full of amazing ingredients. Service was very friendly, quick, and attentive. Will be stopping here anytime we’re back in Alameda.

We came here for an afterwork dinner gathering with a group of 12, and made a reservation ahead of time.

When we arrived, we were seated quickly. We ordered a bunch of dishes, so I'll review the ones that I remember.

I had the Pad Se Ew, Pad Thai, Angel Wings, Spicy Wings, Tom Kha, and the BMV Ultimate Papaya Platter.

Pad Se Ew, the fried flat wide rice noodles with black soy sauce, broccoli, and eggs. I really liked the flavor, and the noodle texture was to my liking.

Pad Thai, the fried thin rice noodles with tamarind sauce, tofu, eggs, and bean sprouts. Unlike Pad Se Ew, this dish felt a bit mediocre, the flavor was pretty bland.

Both Angel Wings and Spicy Wings tasted great; the crunch and seasoning were spot on.

Tom Kha, a coconut soup with lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and fresh mushrooms, chicken or shrimp. Really creamy and delicious.

The BMV Ultimate Papaya Platter came with papaya salad, pork rinds, noodles, cabbage, and sticky rice. You can choose up to 3 proteins and a type of papaya salad, like Thai or Lao. We had the Thai Papaya salad with 2 crispy pork and angel wings. The papaya salad was really fragrant and paired well with the crispy pork, which helped cleanse the palate.  The crispy pork had a strong umami flavor, with the rich fattiness of the meat itself. You could smell the roasted meat and rendered fat. aroma.

Also, their Thai Iced Green Tea and Beerlao are worth a try!

$19 adobo consisting of one scoop of rice, onions, sauce over 3 chunks of pork (see photo). Tasty enough but value ratio is needs no further comment than the photo.  Go to the Korean food place a few stalls down and order a $15 BBQ chicken bowl one day and see the dramatic difference in quality and quantity.

Man! This place is a gem. I've passed by this place often but have never gotten anything to eat here. I got the Lomito Al Jugo and it was delicious! Cooked just right and left me full. The service people here are also extremely kind and customer oriented. I can tell on the weekends that this place gets packed. Bottomless mimosas, bar and plenty of seating, I think I just found one of my new favorite places to eat 😄

Service was great, and the food was excellent. Got the whole chicken, which comes with fries and various sauces. google.name: Khao Tiew

top_reviews.content:
OMG everything is so good!
We started with the oyster mushroom - it’s that sweet and sour Thai taste, immediately opens up the appetite. Short ribs was super tender, we did medium rare but personally think it’s a bit raw, would prefer medium. Tom yum seafood hotpot is full of shrimp and squid, we got mild and it’s not spicy at all - had the sweet and sour Thai taste.
My favorite is the crab clay pot rice, it’s a must try! The portion is generous, crab rich in flavor, I definitely more rice than I should because of it.
$50 pp post tax and tip - great value!
Went on Monday, initially arrived at 3:20 and no one’s there, came back at 3:40 and was group #4. There were still some open tables till ~4:15.

Waited 2 hours to eat here. We got here around 6 PM on a Friday and added ourselves to the waitlist in person. There were 70 tables ahead of us. We didn’t get in until ~8:15 PM.

As for the food, it was good, but it’s not worth waiting 2 hours in line for. I did really like the duck curry though so I would like to order that again.

The service was also fast. We ordered and got our food relatively quickly. But since it’s very crowded, we had to share a table with another couple. But it’s honestly not so bad because the table is big.

As for parking, it doesn’t look too great. Seems like it would mostly be street parking. Though I didn’t park here because we took a rideshare here.

Next time I would try and join the waitlist earlier and then go do something for a couple hours and come back instead of waiting around the area.

By far the best Thai restaurant in the city and worth the wait! Unique dishes and high quality ingredients. Everything we had was delicious — the soft shell crab, duck curry, beef short rib fried rice, and toast dessert (and they even put the coconut ice cream on the side since my partner doesn’t like coconut).

Finally tried this place after years of hype, and serendipitously found myself here twice in the span of one week. Both times joined the waitlist at 4:45-5ish on a weekend night and was seated in about an hour.

The food was unique and different from your typical neighborhood Thai spot. I enjoyed the duck curry, tom kha hed, beef boat noodles, crab fried rice, pad see ew, and kha soi. They were good but not anything too special. I wouldn’t order the crispy papaya salad again, it just tasted like fried dough.

3/162024*
I went for the Chili Cha Cha Spicy Pan Fried Noodle. It's packed with egg noodles, duck, veggies, fresh chili, and basil. It's got a real kick to it!

9/30/2023
This time, I tried the Chili Cha Cha Spicy Pan Fried Noodle, which consists of egg noodles stir-fried with duck, mixed vegetables, fresh chili, and basil leaves. It's quite spicy. Overall, it tastes good, but the strong flavor of white pepper tends to overshadow the other ingredients, which is a bit disappointing. We also ordered their mango sticky rice for dessert, and it was delicious! I would wholeheartedly recommend their Pad See-ew.

8/7/2023
Returning for the second time to Chili Cha Cha 2, I was determined to take on their ultimate spice challenge: "very hot." Just like in my previous review, I was ready for an unforgettable experience.

Our choice for starters was the Dressed Prawn (6pcs) – fried marinated prawns enveloped in a delicate spring roll sheet, accompanied by a sensational Sriracha cream sauce. The cream sauce, in particular, was an absolute delight.

This time around, I ordered the Thai Spicy Pan Fried Noodle (PAD KEE MAO). This dish, a symphony of flat rice noodles stir-fried with an array of ingredients including mushrooms, bamboo shoots, broccoli, bell pepper, onion, and basil, was a spicy adventure I couldn't resist. I must admit, the spice level had my forehead breaking a light sweat, but oh, was it worth it! The dish was an explosion of deliciousness, with flavors that truly delighted my taste buds.

For the true spicy food enthusiasts, the "very hot" level is a must-try. It's a fiery punch that leaves a memorable impression. However, if you prefer occasional spice, I'd recommend the medium or hot level for a satisfying kick without setting your taste buds ablaze.

7/26/2023*
We had the Pad See-Ew at Chili Cha Cha 2, a dish that features pan-fried flat rice noodles with Chinese broccoli, egg, and chicken, all seasoned with black soy sauce. We opted for the "hot" level of spiciness, and it truly left a remarkable impression on us!

In terms of taste and flavor, this Pad See-Ew ranks among the top 3 I've ever had, even compared to the ones in Albany, CA, and New York. The seasoning was on point, perfectly balanced and satisfying. When the waitress brought the dish to our table, the sight of the hot steam escaping from it only added to our anticipation. (Please find the attached photo for reference!)

The dish was incredibly flavorful and delicious, with just the right amount of spiciness – a feature that I personally enjoyed the most. In fact, my partner found it so spicy that he was sweating throughout the entire meal! He even commented that it was spicier than the Pad See-Ew he had in Thailand – quite the compliment!

The attentive and accommodating service from our server was much appreciated. She consistently checked in with us, ensuring our dining experience was enjoyable.

I'm already looking forward to our next visit, where we plan to try the next spicy level, "very hot"! Overall, our experience at Chili Cha Cha 2 was fantastic, and I can confidently recommend it to anyone craving some flavorful and spicy Pad See-Ew.

top_reviews.content:
this is secretly the best sushi in the east bay. The fish is always fresh. Jin has a daily specials menu of fish that is unique and hard to find. i’ve been here so many times and have been holding back on a review for fear i will no longer be able to get a table here.
But really, wow.

Came here specifically for the Kohada and it was beyond expectations! Kohada is kinda hard to find around Bay Area and not many sushi restaurants have them. So I was super grateful to be able to find it here.

I rly enjoyed each piece of nigiri, from the sushi rice, to the amount of wasabi being applied to each piece, to the quality of the fish. Owner/taisho was from Japan, and knows the proper technique. Waiter was so nice!!! Gave us such good suggestions for picking the right fish. Owners told us fish are all overnight shipped from Japan and they will rotate based on seasonal availability to ensure the best quality, And I can def tell that from the taste!

The price is very reasonable as well. I had an amazing experience and will def come back.

We are so lucky to have this gem in our neighborhood. Jin is an incredible chef, overseeing daily fresh fish flown in from Japan, his omakase is comparable to the Michelin sushi spots in sf. … but for a neighborhood price with neighborhood feel.

Fantastic sushi place! This should easily be a Bib Gourmand place! Amazing Omakase menu, done the Japanese way! The owner/chef Jin is very friendly and really passionate about providing the best sushi and experience! You have to go there!

After more than a year of lock-down, we celebrated social liberation with a fabulous sushi dinner sitting at the sushi bar watching the sushi master preparing "Omakase" (chief's choice) assortment of the most delicious and beautifully presented succulent servings of fresh fish east of Japan, all while savoring glasses of fragrant chilled sake from a 1800 ml bottle of Konteki Tears of Dawn Daiginjo - absolutely heaven on earth!  Not cheap, but worth every penny spent!  In short, the best sushi in the Bay Area!

Bibimbap flavor was good, though spicy pork was not very spicy.  Also, it could have been more food for the price.  No free small plates like in other Korean restaurants, so an order of kimchi was extra.  However, that maybe just for barbeque places which they don't have.

name: Chīsai Sushi Club
address: 3369 Mission St, San Francisco, CA 94110, United States

top_reviews.content:
Chisai Sushi Club was rated one of the best omakase in SF and it truly was a wonderful omakase experience!

We chose The Oki which had the oysters and more nigiri than The Chisai. It was the perfect portion, leaving us satisfied and full. There were so many dishes with a variety of complex flavors that I lost track halfway through.

Every bite was crafted with unique sauces, marinade, and ingredients that complimented the fish. It took our tastebuds on a culinary adventure from the salty flavors of caviar, smoked fish, spice of ginger crystals, earthy truffle, richness of uni sauces, to a punch of sourness from the yuzu marmalade. Of course the Toro was so buttery and all of the seafood were top quality. They have craft beers as well on the menu.

The space is small and had the vibes of being in an izakaya in Japan. We got to sit close and personl with our sushi chef. A lot of other people were also there celebrating special occasions, and Chisai had a personalized card for each. At the end they also gave us some cute stickers as Chisai swag. Great service, spectacular presentation, and amazing food!

We celebrated a special occasion at Chisai Sushi Club and chose the Oki Omakase experience, which included an oyster, salad, sashimi, 12 pieces of nigiri, a temaki hand roll, and dessert. From the very first bite, it was clear we were in for something special.

Each nigiri felt like a carefully crafted progression to the next. More than once we found ourselves saying, "This is my favorite one," only to have the next piece top it. The quality of the fish, the balance of flavors, and the attention to detail were outstanding throughout the entire meal.

We sat at the bar, which made the experience feel even more personal and engaging. The staff were genuinely warm, attentive, and welcoming, creating a relaxed atmosphere that made the evening even more memorable. A perfect dinner, a wonderful celebration, and a sushi experience we'll be talking about for a long time.

Chisai Sushi Club is a small but cozy gem in San Francisco. The intimate setting makes the experience feel special, and they offer omakase-style dining at a very reasonable price. I had the Chisai course while my husband ordered the Oki, and every piece was outstanding. The fish was incredibly fresh, flavorful, and perfectly seasoned.

The chef was super friendly and took the time to introduce each dish, which made the experience even more enjoyable. The nigiri was so good that I couldn’t resist ordering extra pieces at the end.

Definitely make a reservation — it doesn’t seem like they take walk-ins. This is a new favorite spot that’s officially going into my go-to restaurant notebook. 🍣✨

This place is special. I’m so used to saying in SF, “was pretty good but paid 50% too much.”

The same cannot be said about this place. We had the Chiisai omakese and it was expertly plated and service was phenomenal.

From the plating, to the quality, to the ambiance, you can tell this place takes extreme pride.

Will be coming back!

We went to Chisai in May 2024.
It was amazing.
My wife is vegan and I was apprehensive about a sushi place doing vegan but she agrees it was amazing.
We got seating at the counter which gave us close access to the chef's who were super knowledgeable and answered any questions we had.
Food was great with the right mix of different cuts of fish alongside amazing accompaniments which helped to elevate every bite.
For the price this was back in May 2024 it was a steal and really kicked above its weight.
It is a small venue and got fairly loud, but you could still have a conversation with the person next to you.

Can't recommend it enough.

top_reviews.content:
On the better end of pho restaurants around Oakland.

Prices are very fair with the portions you get. They’ve have an extra large option we tried and it’s huge !

Broth is very good and rich. It’s deeply flavored but still clear and not murky so you can bet it’s authentic.

The noodles can be improved tho, the noodles were cold and clumped together, makes me feel noodles pre prepped and they let it sit out precooked for some time and when a customer orders, they dump it in a bowl with the broth, hence the coldness and clumping

As with any authentic Asian restaurant, service is nonexistent, so you can bet the food is on the better side.

Very delicious, loved the pho it came with a perfect amount of garnishes, the place had these really nice sweet pickles and extra spicy sambal and Sriracha. The tea was not served in a tea cup which I thought was a bit funky lol. The pho flavor had just the right amount of complexity, not overly distinct on any particular spice, just the right blend. There was a nice amount of meat served with the regular size. The restaurant gets a lot of natural light and has friendly and quick service. I liked the overall dining experience and was pretty happy with the food.

The main reason for the 3-star rating is because it's not very sanitary. Our server was a young man with a silver earring on his left side who came to work obviously sick with a cold. He kept rubbing his nose with his bare hands while serving people. I kept a close eye and he never handled our food. He was restocking utensils with his bare hands touching the mouth side of all of them. Thankfully an older gentleman brought our food. Only once I saw the young man go to the restroom and it's not clear if he washed his hands. Take a soup and go home and rest dude.

The menu is very basic. They didn't have my favorites, beef stew or ox tail. I tried the brisket, rare steak, and tendon. The broth was good, though it could have used a bit more protein. The pickled chilies at the table were a good addition for flavor and heat.

Would have given 4 stars but seeing this server with a cold touching everything made me almost lose my appetite.

Good stuff. Small little parking lot. Staff super friendly and chill and nice. Drinks and smoothies tasted good. Pork a bit dry but that's a vibe kinda. Overall food came out fast and experience was pretty standard. Thanks.

“Phở Hương Quê” basically means pho of the homeland. I’m pretty picky about Vietnamese food in the Bay, but this spot hits.

It’s a low key hole in the wall. They have a special vegetarian section of the menu with tons of options, which is nice because many Vietnamese spots are usually not vegetarian friendly.

The grilled shrimp and vegetarian vermicelli bowls are *sublime*. Vermicelli can be hit or miss since a lot of places don’t season the protein enough, but here everything is nicely marinated and perfectly charred. The fish sauce ties it all together and they give you extra if you ask for it.

Spring rolls are bomb too.

They’re on DoorDash and other delivery apps, but you’ll save a few bucks just going in, and even more if you pay cash.

Cholay bhature was very good, samosa chaat tasted nice, Gobi Manchurian was ok, pani puri is ordinary, Malai kofta was good, Paneer butter masala was garnished with mushroom, some vegetarians don't like that, but gravy tasted nice.
Parking is not free, but from the restaurant, you get 2 hours of free parking when you scan and register online.

We visited Indian Grill on a quiet Wednesday evening as a family of four and had an excellent meal.
We ordered a generous spread: Gobi Manchurian, Tandoori Soya Chaap Sizzler, Malai Kofta, Shahi Paneer, Mughlai Kadai Paneer, rice, Garlic Naan, Onion Naan, Kashmiri Naan, and Mango Lassi.
The Tandoori Soya Chaap Sizzler and Malai Kofta were the absolute stars of the evening — incredibly tasty, packed with bold flavors and beautiful layers of spices that kept every bite interesting. The Shahi Paneer and Mughlai Kadai Paneer were also very well executed and flavorful.
A special shoutout goes to the Mango Lassi — it was rich, refreshing, and one of the best we’ve had in a while.
The naans came out a bit on the crispier side for our taste, but when we mentioned it to the chef/owner Jassi, he was super friendly and told us we could simply request softer ones next time. That kind of responsiveness is always appreciated.
The restaurant itself is humble and unpretentious, but the food more than makes up for the simple setting. We’ll definitely be back — this is the kind of neighborhood spot that delivers far beyond expectations.
Overall: 9/10

Incredibly flavorful! 🍛 I absolutely love the tikka masala—I've had it with lamb, fish, and paneer, and it never disappoints. No matter the protein, the sauce is consistently rich and delicious, which keeps me coming back time and again. 🔥 And the naan? Always fresh and perfectly soft. 🫓 A go-to spot for a satisfying meal!

The customer service is amazing. The staff is always friendly, welcoming, and attentive, which makes the whole experience even better. The restaurant is very clean and well organized, and ordering is always easy and smooth.

The japchae was fresh and light, not amazing but still good. The stars of the show were definitely the bibimbap and the saucy bowl. Really recommend the spicy chicken vs the soy chicken. The portions are very generous, the eggs on the bibimbap are perfectly poached, it was an amazing combination of flavors and textures. I can’t wait to eat here again and will definitely recommend it to people in the area. I need to try their saucy fries too, they looked amazing.

Been wanting to try this place for a long time but for many reasons it never presented to be the rite times. Today was the day I wasn’t disappointed, it was actually better than I thought. A Good fast food option with a healthy touch.

top_reviews.content: First time trying this place and everything was amazing. Me and my husband shared lasagna and linguine with arrabbiata sauce, then finished with the best tiramisu I’ve had and a perfect cappuccino.

Okay listen… if you go to Luna Cocina and don’t get Deena, Zahir, and David taking care of you, I’m telling you right now you are missing OUT 😭👏🏽

Let’s start with my girl Deena, my AMAZING server!!! When I say she set the tone for the entire experience, I mean that. She was so attentive, so warm, and just locked in the whole time. We never had to look around or wait on anything. She was already there. Drinks refreshed, orders handled smoothly, everything flowing exactly how it should. And the way she carries herself? You can tell she takes real pride in what she does. That kind of service is what makes people come back and ask for you by name.

Now Zahir… he was ON IT. Supporting the table, making sure nothing was missed, keeping everything moving seamlessly. The teamwork between him and Deena was flawless. You could feel that they genuinely care about the guest experience!

And David?? Let me tell you, it’s the attention to detail for me. So kind, so quick to help, and so intentional. He brought my soft serve margarita with a huge smile on his face so I have to give him props too. He added to my amazing experience!

Now let’s get into this FOOD and DRINKS because wow 😭🔥

The queso with steak? Rich, flavorful, and done RIGHT. The corn ribs? So good, perfectly seasoned, and something you just keep going back to. And baby… even the chips and salsa deserve their own moment. The salsa tastes homemade like you can tell it was made fresh with care. That alone had me impressed.

And the margaritas??? Yeah they are not playing over here. You can choose from so many flavors like mango, peach, strawberry, coconut and more, and every single one is actually GOOD. Not watered down, not basic… flavorful and balanced.

And of course we had to try the viral soft serve margarita 🙌🏽 I got the strawberry and pineapple and it was EVERYTHING. Fun, refreshing, and honestly just a whole experience on its own.

Overall, the food was amazing, the drinks were hitting, but the SERVICE??? Next level. Deena, Zahir, and David didn’t just do their jobs, they created an experience that makes you want to come back again and again.

I took my time to write this because I want to give them ALL the recognition because they truly deserve it 👏🏽

Great little Italian restaurant with an open kitchen. Everything was fresh and homemade. Caprese salad. Sauteed greens was a big plate of kale perfectly sauteed, with whole garlic cloves. And homemade meatballs. A perfect meal!!

Went to this restaurant with my boyfriend. Ordered a salad with chicken, they charged $8.50 for 3 pieces of chicken that was tasteless. (btw just the salad was $10, so the chicken was almost as expansive as just a single salad. 3 pieces of chicken, nonsense) then we ordered lasagna and linguine with alfredo and chicken. again $8.50 for 3 pieces of chicken which we didn’t know about. lasagna seemed reheated and there was a part that was completely frozen, hard to eat. linguine was completely tasteless, not a single flavor, horrible. Service was whatever, only saw the server twice. Ended up paying more than $70 for horrible flavored meals. Never coming back.

Luca Cucina Italiana is one of those hidden West Berkeley gems that feels like a slice of Italy—at least as far as I can tell, having never been to the motherland myself. I’ve eaten at plenty of places where people swear the food is authentically Italian, and this spot has that same unmistakable flavor. The homemade pasta is the real deal, and their tortellini is absolutely bomb. If you're looking for a vegetarian option, though, be sure to ask in advance.

The lasagna and chicken marsala come up a lot in other reviews, and I get why—classic comfort food, done right. The garlic bread? Personally, not my favorite. They season it a little heavier than I’d like, leaning on the saltier side. But that’s a minor quibble when the rest of the meal delivers.

I’ll admit, I’ve had an off night or two here in th
e past, but lately, they’ve been on a streak. The last three times I’ve been, it’s really been hitting. Add in the cozy, homey vibe and friendly service, and you’ve got a spot that’s worth revisiting. It’s small, so plan ahead, but if you’re craving fresh pasta with a solid Italian pedigree, Luca Cucina Italiana is worth your time.

I recently attended a lunch celebration at Co Nam for my niece’s high school graduation, and it was a wonderful experience from beginning to end.

The food was outstanding. Every dish I tried was beautifully presented, fresh, and full of flavor. The shrimp rolls were light and refreshing, the grilled prawn citrus salad was vibrant and delicious, the garlic noodles were packed with flavor, and the roti with curry dipping sauce was impossible to stop eating. Everything that came to the table was thoughtfully prepared and beautifully presented.

What impressed me just as much as the food was the service. Our group spent hours at the restaurant enjoying the celebration, taking photos, and catching up with family. Throughout the afternoon, the staff remained warm, attentive, and accommodating. Even as we lingered well after lunch, they never made us feel rushed and continued to provide excellent service.

The atmosphere was perfect for the occasion. The restaurant felt inviting and the attention to detail throughout the space complemented the celebration beautifully.

It's easy to find a restaurant with good food. It's much harder to find one that pairs excellent food with genuine hospitality. Co Nam delivered both. I left impressed not only by the quality of the meal but by how welcome they made our entire group feel.

Thank you to the Co Nam team for helping make such a special day even more memorable.

The food was all around solid with a lot of flavor and plenty full. They also have an extensive selection of cocktails. Overall, I would give this place a visit and enjoy some really good Vietnamese food.

Delicious and simple combinations served in an aesthetic interior.

There was a choice of sauces, but they weren't really necessary in my opinion. The chicken was tender and juicy and the rice was perfectly cooked. It came in a cardboard food container and with a little cup of chicken broth to drink. I also had some Thai iced tea, which tasted as expected. My total was a bit over $20.

There's a restroom and plenty of seating, with options for people dining solo and groups. The interior is also nicely decorated if you'd like to post some photos on social media.

Gai by far is the best chicken rice in town. Not only they have authentic singaporean hainan sauce but also they offer thai sauce which is so good! The chicken rice is highly customizable with the choices of dark meat or whit meat.

One thing should be mentioned here is also the soup, which tastes superb. Last but not least, we also try the salad gai, that comes with two sauces, and tastes like authentic thai salad.

top_reviews.content:
Food was decent and had interesting flavors, but the service is really lacking for a restaurant that wants to be fine dining.

First off, we had a completely bizarre experience with the host. We were 20 minutes late for our reservation but entered a restaurant that was half empty. We were a party of 2 and there were 6 open two-tops and 6 of 8 open counter seats. Our reservation was for the counter but after staring at his ipad for 3 minutes, the host told us we could have a table if we finished eating at 7:30 (giving us an hour to dine). We ultimately took him up on the offer. We were reminded at least 3 times by our server over the course of an hour that we needed to keep things moving (first time, she came over, before she even said hi or welcomed us in, she said she was informed that we needed to vacate in an hour).

We finished paying before 7:30 and the server came over at 7:30 on the dot to let us know we needed to leave. There was nobody waiting at the front and there were still 2 open two-tops. Pretty baffling.

I am totally cool with respecting restaurant policies, but the whole process was just handled in a very crude way.

(Also after reading other reviews once I got home, I realized our mulhwe didn’t have noodles even though they are supposed to?…)

Great food. An amazing way to end an evening out in Japantown. The Soy Garlic wings were very crispy, crunchy on the outside. The meat itself was flavorful and juicy. My girlfriend said it was the best she ever had. The Galbi Steak was also great. I recommend paying the extra $5 for the lettuce wraps and samjang. Overall, I had a great time & great date with my girlfriend. I felt the food was worth the price.

Came for Valentines dinner, and they were very accommodating when we arrived early. We ordered the mulhwe noodles, Uni scallop toast, galbi, and ribs and rice cakes. The galbi was so tender and was my favorite dish of the night. The uni scallop toast and mulhwe noodles were both good but not mindblowing imo. The rice cake and ribs were a bit bland and some of the rib pieces were dry. Ended the meal with the nurungji ice cream which had a stickier texture compared to normal ice cream. Overall, a good meal but overpriced.

Food (5/5)
Each plate was amazing. I especially liked the potato pancakes, uni toast, rice cakes with beef, and the Galbi steak. The meat was tender and juicy and well-seasoned.

The rice crispy/syrup ice cream and matcha lava cake were great as well.

Service (4.2/5)
The wait time between plates were somewhat variable. First dish (quail eggs) came quickly, but there was some wait between other dishes. They also could’ve come quicker after giving us the bill. Also, since some dishes were a bit messy (eg, the potato pancakes with all its crispy toppings) it would’ve been nice if they could help wipe the tables between some dishes.

Atmosphere (4.5)
Pretty nice and elegant environment, overall. Spacious bathrooms. The section we were in were a bit echoey and loud, however (but it was better after the large parties had left).

Overrated. As someone who dines at fine-dining restaurants often and has high expectations, this experience was just okay at best.

We ordered the japchae, but the fried mushrooms on top were cold and tasted like they’d been sitting out for a while. The galbi was overly salty, though the black cod was genuinely very good. The kimchi fried rice was nothing special- just a very standard version of the dish.

The matcha lava cake was a pleasant surprise and it was an interesting and well-executed dessert.

Overall, I wouldn’t return, but I’m glad I was able to check Bansang off my list.

top_reviews.content:
We had a great experience at GangNam Jjajang!

We ordered the jajangmyeon, jjambbong, jjambbong-jajang combo, shrimp fried rice, and sweet and sour pork (small), and everything was satisfying.

The jajangmyeon had a rich and savory black bean sauce that was perfectly balanced, and the noodles were chewy and well-cooked. The jjambbong was full of flavor with a deep, spicy broth and generous seafood, making it very comforting.

The shrimp fried rice was light yet flavorful, with nicely cooked rice and plenty of shrimp. The sweet and sour pork was crispy on the outside and tender inside, with a sauce that wasn’t overly sweet, which we really appreciated.

Overall, the portions were generous, the food came out quickly, and everything tasted fresh and well-prepared. We would definitely come back again!

This is the perfect place to hit up if you’re like me and experience intense, borderline violent jajangmyeon cravings. Sometimes you just need a big, comforting bowl of chewy noodles covered in rich black bean sauce, and this spot absolutely delivers.

Their jajangmyeon is done just right. The sauce is savory, hearty, and satisfying without feeling too heavy, and the noodles have that perfect chewy texture that makes the whole dish so comforting. The portion size is also massive, so you could definitely share one order between two people—although I completely understand wanting one all to yourself.

I also tried their fried chicken, which was decent, but it wasn’t the standout for me. It was fine as a side, but compared to the noodles, it didn’t feel like something I’d go out of my way to order again. Next time, I’d probably skip the chicken and focus on what they’re clearly known for: their noodle dishes.

Overall, this is a great spot when you’re craving classic, satisfying Korean comfort food. I’d definitely come back for the jajangmyeon and would recommend it to anyone looking for a generous, flavorful bowl of noodles.

Gangnam Jajang is the real deal!!! I am used to Korean-Chinese as a Korean who used to eat jajngmyeon (black bean noodles) and tang soo yook as a kid.

I started with the iced tea with mango cubes - refreshing, not too sweet, and the large mango cubes at the top were a nice touch. They even had a frozen bear on the top.

The wool-myeon and the chili oil black bean noodles stood out. The wool myeoj noodles have a silky texture with super generous portions with fresh seafood. The chili oil black bean noodles had a savoy jajang base with a kick of heat. The chili oil adds fragrance and makes the noodles super addictive.

The tang soo yook was crispy but chewy on the inside. Definitely recommend this as an appetizer.

The portions are generous based on the price point and the servers were very attentive too!

If you’re anywhere near Oakland and craving Korean-Chinese, do yourself a favor and check it out.

I’ve been coming to Gangnam Jajang since they first opened in January 2022, and it’s been great to see how much the restaurant has evolved over the years. The food has continued to improve little by little, and I can see why it has become a spot that appeals to both Korean and non-Korean diners.

One of their newer dishes, the Spicy Chili Pork Gan-Ja-Jang, is definitely worth trying if you enjoy a little hot. It can sometimes feel quite rich, but the kick from the peppers cuts through that richness surprisingly well. The combination is savory, spicy, and nicely balanced without losing the deep flavor you want from a good fresh Jajang sauce.

I also really like that they’ve added more size options for their Tang-Soo-Yuk (sweet and sour pork). It makes it much easier to order when dining alone without committing to a huge portion. The one pictured here is a medium, which I’d say is plenty for 2-3 people to share. The coating is crisp without being overly heavy, while the pork stays tender and juicy inside. Paired with the sweet and sour sauce on the side, it has that satisfying contrast in texture that makes good tangsuyuk so addictive :-)

After coming here for years, it’s nice to see a restaurant that keeps refining its food rather than simply staying the same. Definitely a place I’ll continue coming back tho whenever I’m craving Korean-Chinese food !

Wonderful Korean food at low prices, cooked fresh to order in a friendly casual venue. Had the jajang noodles with fried chili sauce, and was immediately impressed by the chewy home made noodles and aromatic sauce. Portion was enormous. The fried pork is fluffy and comes with a unique dipping sauce, bright and acidic, keeps you eating! I highly recommend.

top_reviews.content:
I had been to Terzo multiple times before this incident — probably around 3 times just between the beginning of this year and the end of April and never expected this experience.

On April 24th, I dined there around 7:30 PM and ordered steak and asparagus. I left the restaurant around 8:40 PM. Around 11:30 PM, I started feeling unwell. Shortly after midnight, I developed diarrhea, followed by nonstop vomiting until around 4 AM. The symptoms became so severe that I had to go to the ER.

The doctor diagnosed me with food poisoning. I was given an anti-nausea injection, IV fluids for dehydration, and medication to take home. By the time I left the hospital, it was already around 6:30 AM. I felt extremely weak for the next several weeks.

My partner called the restaurant on Friday/Saturday, and we were told the manager would not be available until Monday. Later, a female manager called me back and asking detailed questions about my credit card transaction, told me the only thing they could do was issue a refund because the food poisoning “had nothing to do with the restaurant.”

I explained that I usually only eat one meal a day, and the only thing I ate that Thursday was at Terzo. Her response was that food poisoning symptoms normally appear after 12 hours, and since my symptoms started in less than 4 hours, it “must have come from somewhere else.”

What disappointed me the most was not even the refund issue — it was the complete lack of empathy or apology throughout the conversation. I was also told that they sold around 20 steaks that night and nobody else reported getting sick, implying this was somehow my own issue.

But food poisoning does not necessarily affect every single customer equally, and 20 steaks are not all cut from the exact same piece of meat under identical conditions.

I understand restaurants need to protect themselves, but the way this situation was handled felt dismissive especially toward someone who ended up in the emergency room after dining there.

The food was delicious, served at the right temperature, and beautifully presented. Its location in the marina is a big plus. Definitely a place I would recommend and come back to.

The hummus on the other hand was bland, pasty and forgettable (but our server said it’s permanently in the menu because it’s so good??) The portions were large, so if you like their food at least you’re getting a lot of it.
We sat in the little extra room in the way back. Ughhh. I hate sitting in the extra room at restaurants because it always feels like an afterthought. It was pretty loud in there and had zero ambience compared to the rest of the restaurant.
Overall didn’t hate this place, but I’m not in a rush to go back anytime soon…

It’s a perfect, versatile space that works just as well for an intimate date night as it does for a birthday celebration. Rice cake soup: also very good but I prefer Galbi Tang

Kimchi Pork Belly : really yummy. A little bit spicy and very addicted.

Chapjae : stir fried yam noodles. Very good

Pan fried Mackerel: on the dry side and too salty

I highly recommended the Galbi, pancake, beef soup and stir fried yam noodles at this place.

Despite tightening SF regulations on indoor flames, this near historic establishment thankfully grandfathered in its continued use of wood charcoal grills.

And unlike most Korean barbecues that have gone the all-you-can-eat route, this community mainstay continues to serve a la carte marinated meats, which help ensure quality.

For mains, we ordered the butter chicken and lamb curry (both medium spicy) to share, with a side of naan and two sides of rice. The butter chicken was rich and creamy, while the curry lamb had a nice balance of flavor and heat. Both were enhanced by the side of garlic naan.

Overall, a solid meal and nice ambience.

We got a chance to try this place with my family. We tried the pani puri, peach chaat (excellent), spicy wings, chicken momo, crab samosa, chicken biryani (great), butter chicken (great), smoked chicken (great), lamb chops (excellent), kashmiri kofta, plain and garlic naan (great), tamarind drink, pistachio Kulfi, kheer brûlée (great), and tres leche (great).

Wonderful experience while visiting from Las Vegas! Fast, kind and really good food! Will come here again if in town! Also thank you to the cashier that made sure my order was right, made my night!

Came here from Texas and this was the best service and food we have had around San Francisco! Everything we ordered was fantastic! Owner and his family really out do themselves to make sure everything is perfect for you!

My family ordered orange chicken, shrimp fried rice, chicken chow mein, Mongolian beef, and shrimp wonton soup. When we asked for the rice, chow mein, and soup, the lady asked what kind of meat we wanted in it — so perhaps not a very vegetarian friendly place. She brought out dishes for a family of around 3-4 to share each, these dishes are not made for one person to order but rather to be shared. The rice and orange chicken were delicious, especially the orange chicken which had a good amount of sauce and flavor but also a nice crunch. The noodles were a bit oily but they still had a good flavor. I did not try the Mongolian beef but my family said it was delicious and had a good amount of spice to it. I also did not try the soup but my family said it was a bit bland and wasn’t their favorite. Overall though, this place is good and I would recommend for Chinese food in the SF area.
For the dishes we ordered, plus a bottle of water and a can of sprite and another can of  Coke, our total was around $130. An $18 service fee was automatically added to our bill.

In san francisco for couple days, first time in san francisco, I was at target, couple blocks away. I love food, and was hungry and Chinatown was to far to walk at that moment, saw new mings on Google maps, Decided to walk over and peek in. I went in, order food, it was delicious. And the ladies were so so nice. Both mom and myself really enjoyed the flavor and friendliness. If im in san francisco again, ill definitely be back. You should try it, very good. I promise.

Nice place, nice people. It’s a bit pricey since it’s downtown, but they give generous servings. I’d recommend visiting! Ive only had the American style Chinese food here, but they have a very large menu

Amazing atmosphere. Outstanding customer service. The portion sizes were amazing. I had the salt and pepper pork chops and destroyed them. Please eat here and I'll be definitely coming here evetime I'm in town.

Tasted great! Very flavourful and authentic. The price is a bit high but for the amount of food you get it's great. We had orange chicken, fried fish, black pepper beef rice plate, and fried rice. All very good. There are a lot options there. Will definitely go back again.

top_reviews.content: Not the most glamorous looking place inside but I'll tell you what, the food and prices definitely compensate for it. Great tasting Chinese food with nice-sized portions with unbeatable prices. The Mongolian beef and salt and pepper rock cod are definitely my go-to dishes here. Living here in San Francisco almost all my life I learned the places that are not the most prettiest crank out the best foods.

I recently dined at a Golden Kim star Chinese restaurant in San Francisco, and I must say, it exceeded my expectations. The Mongolian beef was tender, flavorful, and perfectly spiced. The vegetable fried rice was equally impressive, with a great mix of fresh vegetables and well-seasoned rice that complemented the beef beautifully. The steamed dumplings were a delightful surprise, with a soft, delicate exterior and a delicious, savory filling.

What really stood out, though, were the portions. They were simply incredible—the best I've ever had at a Chinese restaurant, hands down. I left feeling more than satisfied, with enough leftovers to enjoy another meal at home. If you're looking for great Chinese food with generous servings, this place is definitely worth a visit!
We ordered take out for a quick meal. As an Asian I have to say the food is authentic! Fast, affordable and quality to its price. Will order again.

As a vegan visiting from Australia this was a great find for us this evening! Plenty of options to choose from, very generous portions, accommodating of my husband’s not-too-spicy request, and produced lovely flavoursome dishes - we had the sizzling basil tofu, Mandarin spicy eggplant with tofu and veggie fried rice (egg free). Best value in San Fran!

Food was delicious and service was friendly. First time eating here and I will definitely eat here again. Reasonable price, great taste, and abundant portions. We ordered the beef chow fun and some other dishes I forgot.

S e r v i c e was okay s

I was looking for a place to have lunch before a doctors appointment and found this online. I was intrigued by the description as I like to eat organically. It can best be described as an upscale cafeteria. The staff was really nice and accommodating and the atmosphere was open and airy. I had a soba noodle salad, which I thought was very delicious and my friend had a chicken salad sandwich. He objected to the overuse of sweet pickles in the chicken salad, however. Other than that, he thought the quality of the food was good,  as did I. Definitely a great place to eat if you are in the area. Their garden is beautiful and very well-maintained and you can eat outside and smell the herbs and flowers.

The food, which is what you first come for when you go out, was truly delicious. The Margherita and Sausage pizzas were thin, and perfectly charred on the underside. The olives were delicious. The fries were slightly garlicky and plentiful. The cheese and meat board was great. You order at the counter and food comes fast, service is attentive. The atmosphere is a bit cold and not warm so it’s not a date night kinda place (with a name like STEM, it’s not intended to be)

We visited Stem Kitchen & Garden on a Tuesday afternoon and pretty much had the place to ourselves. It’s a very nice and spacious venue with a modern sleek look. The staff were friendly, made conversation with us and made sure we enjoyed the food.

We totally enjoyed the food! We ordered the Buttermilk Friend Chicken sandwich and the Skirt Steak Sandwich. Both were amazing! The quality of the food is top notch! It’s just a whole different level from your average restaurant. We left feeling satisfied and not “weighed down.” I love the fact that the veggies are straight from their on-site garden as well!

Overall very pleased and excited to return and try more of the menu. Thank you for a great experience!

Our niece and her fiance chose well in having Stem Kitchen as their pre-wedding meet-and-greet venue. Atmosphere was casual and light. Food was tasty. Dessert was delicious. Drinks were refreshing. A henna artist was onsite for those who wanted a tattoo. Of course I had mine on my hand.

top_reviews.content:
The Benchmark Pizza was very good. Sauce, crust, all of it. Delicious.  We also ordered the chopped salad and spicy carrots and a pasta dish that I can't recall the name of.

Overall the experience was great. If you have more than two people, order a second pizza.

Benchmark continues to be one of my favorite spots when a serious pizza craving hits. Last night, I stopped in specifically hoping to try the eggplant pizza, but unfortunately they were sold out. Since the only other pie I’d previously had there was the brown butter sage — delicious, though I’ve learned lemon on pizza simply isn’t my thing — I decided to go with their classic Benchmark margherita instead. It absolutely delivered.

This is Neo-Neapolitan pizza done right: bright, fresh tomato sauce, creamy mozzarella, torn basil, and a beautifully balanced crust with a perfectly thin base, nicely charred underside, and those airy, leopard-spotted edges that make wood-fired pizza so satisfying. Simple, restrained, and incredibly well executed.

It was an unusually warm evening, so I opted to sit outside. My only real complaint is that the tables closest to the street sit noticeably on a slant, making it a bit of a challenge to keep plates and glasses from slowly sliding downhill throughout the meal. A small detail, but worth noting.

That said, the staff were genuinely lovely and welcoming, and the overall experience was exactly what I was hoping for. One final recommendation: do yourself a favor and ask for a side of olive oil for dipping the crusts. It’s the perfect finishing touch.

I’ll absolutely be back the next time the craving strikes.

This place serves the best vegan pizza I’ve ever had—worth a visit for that alone. Highly recommend! I also loved their sparkling red wine; we thoroughly enjoyed it. The lemon pizza and the sage pizza were excellent as well.

A few small suggestions as feedback: it would be great to see some vegetarian pasta options added. All the appetizers leaned on sweetness, which wasn’t quite our preference—having a few truly savory starters would be nice. Some chocolate-based dessert options would also be a welcome addition.

Overall, this is easily one of the best pizza spots around! 🍕

The crust here is hands down the best! perfectly chewy with just the right amount of crisp and char. You can really taste the quality in every bite. Their pasta is also solid, always cooked just right and full of flavor. And no visit is complete without ordering the sundae ice cream! it’s a must-have! Creamy, rich, and the perfect way to end the meal. Highly recommend this place if you’re craving great pizza and a cozy, satisfying meal.

One of best pizza spots in the east bay!  Salami and Calabrian Chili pizza was superb. The meat was out of this world. The Caesar salad was excellent. All ingredients very fresh and well cooked. Flavors well balanced for both dishes. Wish I left room for dessert!

reviews_snippets.content: "I would choose the fried sage pizza and Caesar salad as my last meal."

top_reviews.content:
Coming here for a casual lunch was a great opportunity to experience the flavors of native American foods. Located in the Fruitvale area right next to the BART station, you will need to be mindful of where you park. Since we were here on a Sunday afternoon we were able to utilize the BART lot for free. The interior is bright, simple and open space with several tables. We chose to dine outside under the giant tree covered patio. It's a nice relaxing space, and the owners do a good job of keeping the panhandlers from bothering the diners. The girls running the store on this Sunday were super sweet, attentive and helpful throughout our stay.
The four of us shared several dishes and all were really quite good. Everything was very fresh and well prepared. Know before you go... Wahpepah's Kitchen specializes in true native American cuisine. The food is simply prepared, fresh and local which means the menu may change depending upon what is available locally as the seasons change. I love that aspect, and their commitment to sourcing fresh local products.
Of all the items we ordered, I personally loved the bison frybread and bison tacos (meat eater here), the mole and the Three Sisters veggie bowl were also great.

Service was great, food was tasty and very good.  There was enough seating even tho they were a bit busy.  I ordered the bison tacos and sorry ate them so fast forgot to take a picture.  But I will be back to enjoy another tasty bite here.  Ingredients were on point and the taco shell was made fresh.  Couldn't pass on it since we are in Oakland. If you can't find this lil spot it's right across from the bart entrance

After seeing Wahpepah's on "Check, Please! Bay Area" we just had to try it out!
I thought that the Sweet Potato Hibiscus Taquitos were a delicious appetizer. I followed that with the Bison Warrior Wrap, lots of meat and a delicious combination of greens inside the tastiest wrap! I wonder if the lean Bison meat could be cooked a little less (medium rare?) to bring out more flavor? Dessert for me was the Corn Mush, WOW! This could also be a good starter for the day as well as dessert?!!
Of course do not miss the Frybread!

Amazing indigenous restaurant. Such a special place, in all of the United States there are so few indigenous restaurants and opportunities for people to have this experience. Indigenous people cultivate a majority of the world’s foods that are used today. So wonderful to be able to go back to one of the sources we had a great meal and experience in the wonderful restaurant. The owner even came and checked on us and was warm and kind.

Wahpepah’s Kitchen offers a unique and delicious experience for anyone craving authentic Indigenous cuisine. Located in Oakland, California, the restaurant is a gem that combines traditional Native American flavors with a modern twist. The owner, Wahpepah, brings her heritage and culinary skills to the table, making it a place where you can explore the rich and diverse food culture of Native American tribes.

One of the standout dishes is the frybread, a crispy, golden treat that pairs perfectly with various toppings like savory meats or sweet jams. The bison chili is also a fan favorite, offering a hearty and flavorful taste of Native American comfort food. Wahpepah’s Kitchen prides itself on using locally sourced ingredients, ensuring that each dish not only tastes fresh but also supports sustainable practices.

The atmosphere of the restaurant is warm and welcoming, with a deep respect for Native traditions and culture. The staff is friendly and knowledgeable, making the dining experience even more enjoyable.

If you’re looking for something new and flavorful, Wahpepah’s Kitchen is a must-try. It’s not just a meal; it’s a journey into Indigenous culinary traditions that you won’t soon forget. Whether you're a local or just visiting, this spot is definitely worth the visit!

top_reviews.content: Good pizza if you love thin and crispy, but for me it felt a bit overrated. The amount of oil was way more than expected, which took away from the flavour. Still, it’s decent enough - 4 stars, though that’s me being a bit generous.

To the point:
The pizza is consistently delicious, and if you have visitors or friends this is the place to bring them!

Perspective:
I have eaten pizza in just about every major city in America, most recently returning from a trip to New Haven Dave Portnoy's "Pizza capital", and I personal would place Casey's pizza at or above that caliber of pizza.

Recommendation:
Stop by Casey's enjoy a fresh pie, relax and settle into the evening. Then take a stroll along the walking path that leads to the view of the stadium. Bring a Jacket!

My wife and I often walk our dog past Casey’s Pizza, but we had never stopped in because it always seemed busy. We finally decided to give it a try last night, and I can honestly say we had been missing out. The pizza was absolutely outstanding—fresh, perfectly crisp, and made with dough that has incredible flavor.

We also had the pleasure of meeting the owner, whose customer service was exceptional. Since it was our first visit, we asked for his recommendation, and he suggested the East Coast Pie. We’re so glad we took his advice, because it was fantastic.

We will definitely be returning and would highly recommend Casey’s Pizza to anyone looking for high-quality pizza and welcoming service.

Casey's is everything I want out of my local pizza shop.

Atmosphere: Casey is behind the counter every day with a friendly team and happy to chat with you. The place is super casual and its great to see a mix of families, couples and people getting slices after work at the bar. They have weekly wine specials and a few fun spritzes as well!

Pizza: Thin, crispy, flavorful crust. I had been searching for this in a Bay Area pizza for years and was so happy to have found the ideal east coast style crust at Casey's! The variety of pizza styles on the menu are use local ingredients in familiar, yet creative, ways. I love them all but definitely get the East Coast Pie and Hot Pie most frequently.

Salads: Don't sleep on the salads to as a side to the pizza! I've had them all and everything is super fresh. My favorite is the Baby Lettuce. The fresh grapes, crunch of almond and shallot vinaigrette are a nice addition to the farm fresh greens.

We had a fantastic dinner at Casey Pizzeria! The baby salad  $17 was fresh and delicious, and the thin-crust pizza $32 was super good—crispy and flavorful without being too heavy. We paired our meal with two amazing IPAs $9 each from Fieldwork Brewing, which just made the night even better. The place is also baby-friendly! We brought our stroller inside without any issues, making the experience stress-free for our family. Highly recommend for anyone looking for great pizza, drinks, and a welcoming atmosphere.

We also had that bottarga and Meyer lemon, another amazing dish. Deep fried bottarga added texture and the aroma from Meyer lemon captured all senses.

Pizza dough can perhaps be a little more airy but the kale pizza was quite tasty despite the dough comment.

Desserts are ok and definitely not the star of the night.

Went here for happy hour today and honestly a really good deal. Arancini could have been a bit more creamy and flavorful on the inside but fried well and was good.

top_reviews.content: Jimmy made my first but not last experience at The Station a wonderful dining experience! I’m from Manhattan and my daughter was looking for a great restaurant for lunch and suggested coming to The Station! We actually arrived at 10:55 and Jimmy explained that they’d be opening at 11 . He was so friendly and sweet thst we happily sat and relaxed for a few minutes before ordering their most delicious kale salads. My daughter had hers with a beef patty and fries! Everything was delicious!

I got a double smash burger with a side of fries and the fries were probably the most perfect fries I’ve had. The smash burger was also great and definitely up there as well. When i did order it probably took five minutes before i got my food. Didn’t feel too greasy, tasted fresh, and have no complaints whatsoever. The spot is also very cozy and a homey feel. If i were to sum up the vibe, think a group of patagonia-puffer-with-chinos-with-a-toque-on corporate group Sunday brunch or somewhere i wish i went with my parents when i was maybe 7-8 years old (in a good way). I paid maybe 20 for my order+tip but i wouldn’t say the price was too crazy considering the quality of the food. I would come back again.

Food: 8.8/10 (phenomenal)
Atmosphere: 7/10 (cozy)
Service: 7/10 (nothing crazy but was quick)
Price: 5/10 (neither cheap nor too expensive)
Overall (8/10)

I've been here twice, once I purchased the Station burger, on a separate occasion the Saigon Smash chicken sandwich. Both selections were PHENOMENAL! The atmosphere is super nice, it feels like a comforting third space. The man at the register, Favi really brought the energy and made my group feel comfortable with whatever we needed, he felt like a ray of sunshine and an essential contribution to the vibe of the restaurant.

Tried this spot for dinner and the smash burgers were seriously so bomb. Easily the highlight of the meal. Super flavorful, and definitely the kind of burger that makes you want to come back. I’ll absolutely be back for another and already have my eye on the Saigon burger for next time.

The shakes, though, were a letdown. They looked good but were pretty lacking in flavor and too watery. The fries were just okay..Nothing bad, but nothing memorable.

My biggest issue was watching the employee pack the fries into the boats with his bare hands. It felt pretty unsettling and honestly unsanitary, especially handling hot, greasy fries that way. Just throw on some gloves or use tongs.

Overall, the burgers alone are worth coming back for, which is why I’m giving 4 stars. I just hope they tighten up the food handling practices a bit.

Very yummy smash burger, fries, and a chocolate shake. Trekked over here from SF to try out their burger and it’s worth the Bart/walk from rockridge. A lovely corner spot in a fancy neighborhood with outdoor seating. The line for ordering can get very very long so be patient.

I don’t go to vegan places that often, but this was definitely one of the best I’ve tried. Next time I’ll try the ramen! The potatoes were probably my favorite followed by point Rey’s roll. The mocktails were also really nice! All in all recommend.

Cozy vibe. Nigiri is currently my go-to bc I love to enjoy the purity of each vegetable/fruit.
Eggplant is my ultimate fav. Avocado nigiri is good too but this time there was no truffle salt so that’s what makes this Nigiri. Pickled mango is my new fav in addition to eggplant. Enrygii is saucy!

Currently offering happy hour menu (food & drink) between 5-6pm.

Wow! You will love this place!! It’s rare to find vegan sushi and even more rare when it’s so exceptional. The Pacifica was the perfect amount of crunch, texture, flavor, and layers! The Monterey had a smoky undertone. I wish I could have ordered the whole menu!

As a vegetarian, the sushi’s are a must have! Unbelievable that it’s all vegan. I feel like I’m cheating and eating real sushi. Omg 🤤 so good! Servers were friendly and accommodating. This will be a repeat for sure! Only minor caveat is the place is quite small not enough seating during peak hours, so reserve ahead of time.

Excellent vegan sushi place. A bit on the pricey but kind of worth the experience and ambience.

Host was nice and recommended we try a soft and a crunchy sushi so that we get to experience both varieties. We tried a few crowd favorites and liked the eggplant tempura sushi the best overall hands down.

Chill and cosy ambience. Appointment recommended as it gets pretty busy.

Bonus on the menu is a flaming sushi option

Cozy dim lit environment with authentic flavor. The cuisine is always on the richer side when it comes to flavor. top_reviews.content: We made a reservation and traveled over 1,000 miles, round trip, to try this restaurant for a birthday dinner with a group of friends.  First red flag was when I informed the “manager,” a person in a plain t-shirt, that my wife was celebrating a birthday, I was informed that they offered no birthday dessert to guests, but they were “happy to put a candle on any dessert off of our menu.”  Since this was a $500 dinner, it is the first restaurant I have experienced this in, worldwide.  The two servers at our table for six appeared to be learning, as another server was training them.  When the Pizza Puttanesca was described as a “pizza made without cheese…” but was extremely strong without it, and “extra cheese” was recommended, I was stunned.  So “extra cheese” was put on the order.  The first overwhelming taste impression was salt.  Portion size at the restaurant is petite.  The meatballs were fine, but four were served, the size of quarters.  The rigatoni was visibly blackened by the oven.  The Malfadine pasta was almost too spicy, unnecessarily, with no mention of heat in the description.  One dessert, served in a jar with chocolate and nuts, was the best item on the menu.  An expensive and unevenly balanced experience that I cannot recommend.  We will never return.

We went on a weekday night and it was still a little busy. We had to wait for 30 minutes. But the host (a really nice man), did ask if we wanted anything to drink and took our order. So I was able to have a cocktail while waiting.

Our server was very energetic and was attentive even though they were busy.

The pizza was delicious. We got the one with prosciutto, arugula and cheese. It was well cooked and season. We got the meatballs as an appetizer. The meatballs were juicy and the sauce was well seasoned.

Would go again, when we are back in Oakland.

We've been fans of Marzano for years. The pizza is great but the chicken is my absolute favorite. Just the right amount of spice. Great place for a date or for families. The staff is super friendly. Truly a jewel of the neighborhood.

If you're looking for an unforgettable dining experience, you have to check out Marzano! This amazing Italian restaurant is run by the talented Manna, an Eritrean woman who brings a unique twist to traditional Italian cuisine. The flavors are absolutely explosive—get ready for some delightful surprises as many dishes pack a spicy punch that will tantalize your taste buds!

Don't miss out on the must-try dishes: the octopus is a showstopper, the beet salads are refreshingly vibrant, and the meatballs are simply divine. And trust me, you can't go wrong with any of the white pizzas—they're all out of this world!

The atmosphere is welcoming, with servers who are not only professional but also incredibly friendly and attentive. It truly makes for a perfect spot to enjoy a night out with friends or family. I wholeheartedly recommend Marzano for a memorable culinary adventure!

Perfect pizzas with high end ingredients. Sit at the bar, sip a cocktail, chat with your neighbor, catch a (silent) game in the big screen and watch the staff make your pizza by hand before sliding it into the wood-fired oven. Warm service, kid-friendly, date-worthy gem.

top_reviews.content: This place has a special place in my heart. I stumbled on this place while having to take a detour due to the freeway closure when I used to drive Long Haul from LA to Oakland Daily. I made a mental note and came back a month later after I remembered where it was. Man, oh man, the gem this place is. I originally wanted their Pho, and it's very good Pho. But let me tell ya, their Bun Bo Hue was by far my favorite thing to have there. The depth of flavor of the beef and lemon grass in that broth had me.. and the chili sauce the owners wife makes is next level when you add it to this soup. I always ask for extra broth because why not. I know this is wrong, but I like Subbing out the Bun Bo noodle for the Pho noodle. Just clings on to the broth much better, so each bite and slurp are that much tastier.

Friendly service, lots of different food options. The nem nuong pork spring roll has crispy bits similar to Brodards in SoCal. We ordered beef short ribs pho #66, bun rieu #34, and pork spring roll #4NM. Food was good, the portion was just right without the food coma afterwards. The owner is very friendly, he speaks Cantonese, Vietnamese and English. Many locals and regulars come here, sit down and order without looking at the menu. The restaurant is located at a small strip mall with limited parking. The decor looks dated, but the food is good and hits the spot.

This place used to always be super good. Up until i started getting food poisoning from here, the last 2 times I’ve came here I immediately got food poisoning after and its so unfortunate because I love this place and the owner lots. Maybe just don’t order the grilled pork, I’ve ordered grilled pork both times and I’m not sure what’s going on in the backhouse but the meat has been a yellowish color and seem like leftover pieces mushed together. It sucks that I won’t be able to eat here anymore

I recently tried out Saigon House and really enjoyed my meal. The seating outside seemed nicely covered and cool, while the interior has a lot of personality from its classic all wood counter to the many plants hanging around the windows and sills.

The service was prompt and friendly. The owners seem to generally be taking orders or hanging around and are friendly, funny and talkative. I found that to make for a good dining experience personally as it added to the local, mom/ pop vibe present at this restaurant.

We ordered a spread of food- the pho is really good. The brother is on the lighter side and not overly savory/ aromatic with a slight sweetness, so if that fits your palette, I believe you would enjoy it. The herbs and added items were generous and I got a good amount of meat in the bowl too. The bun bo hue was equally delicious, with a good flavor though did not have the trotter or pork blood which I always love to see as an add-in.  The Korean BBQ Garlic Noodles surprised me and so I had to give them a try- the meat was perfectly cooked and flavorful, and the noodles were good, albeit slightly dried out over the course of our meal. The Vietnamese coffee here is really great, and the banh mi was also delicious and had a nice sweetness to them.

Overall, I loved eating here from the atmosphere and service to the pretty solid meal too. If you are thinking of trying out this place, I would recommend doing so.
Authentic Vietnamese. Broth is rich and full of flavour, noodles cooked perfectly! Iced coffee is strong, sweet and creamy.

Ate at this restaurant years ago when it first opened up, have always liked it. But based on my experience with the food delivery in the recent few years, I have become very disappointed with Enjoy Vegetarian Restaurant in Sunset.

One thing to note beforehand is that nobody at the restaurant ever picks up the phone, and there is no voicemail either. So if you want to make a reservation on the phone or want to talk to someone in the restaurant, good luck!

While the dishes are good in general, the quality is very inconsistent. For example, I once ordered the Braised Spareribs w/Dai Kon. It was awesomely delicious. Then, when I ordered it again the following week, it was horrible--the white radish were only half cooked, and the big chunks of carrots were so hard that I could tell they were only cooked for less than 10 minutes, both were tasteless. Maybe they have to regularly demonstrate that they only use fresh ingredients?

They used to make the tofu in-house. But nowadays, most of the tofu in various dishes taste like commercially made--dry and hard.

All in all, even if they won an award in 2017, for sure this location no longer lives up to that standard.

THIS LOCATION IS AMAZING HOLY MOLY

I had only ever gone to the Chinatown location until yesterday when I went here.

So much more friendly here, like night and day difference. The older lady at the Chinatown location is mean but here it was a young man and another lady with shorter hair and they were so nice! I had given up on the other location but am so pleased to know I can still get amazing food and with a smile not a scolding look the entire time 😅

I got the string beans and chicken w/ black bean sauce, bbq pork, and orange chicken to bring home to my girl. Everything was outstanding. First time trying black bean sauce and I loved it.

I ordered takeout and it was ready in 15 mins. We enjoyed every dish which was the house special chow mein, fatty pork, & green beans and chicken. The fatty pork was supposed to come with mustard greens and Napa cabbage but I only found cabbage. They also give complementary sesame balls for dessert, so good.

I’m not vegan/ vegetarian but my husband is pescatarian and we’re both trying to eat less meat. Enjoy Vegetarian will blow your mind with the kinds of amazing things they can do with plant products: vegetables, wheat gluten, & tofu. We recently brought visiting family to EV and our 13-year-old nephew, who had previously been asking for “meat-on-a-stick” was astounded at how real/ tasty the chicken dishes were (particularly fragrant crispy chicken & orange chicken).

Our go-tos:
Spinach & pine nut rice, Eggplant & Sea Bass, sliced fatty pork with mustard greens, Vegetarian duck, honey walnut shrimp, and their sesame balls.

They are a pretty small establishment, but what lacks in atmosphere is more than made up by the kindness, friendliness, and efficiency of their small staff.

So glad they are in the neighborhood!!

top_reviews.content: A truly wonderful meal. I opted for the #7 at the recommendation of the nice gentleman who took our order. I went there for my first time and the food was wonderful. The service was incredible, especially the mama who was taking care of me. Luv it ❤️
