Second time eating here. I really like what I got that I got it again. The duck meat is really tender that it falls off the bone. I like the soup on the side so the sauce of the duck is with the noodles and not diluted in the soup.

Both times was in a weekend and there is a wait so make sure to have someone put their name down asap! I don't remember how long the wait was but I believe it's not more than an hour from the two times I went.
They only have two tables for more than four people.

Excellent restaurant with a focus on wonton noodles with a incredible duck leg in a wonderful soup. The soup is very good with a nice complexity and can be served on the side which is recommended. The duck is extremely tender and flavorful. You can add the soup into it as you eat. The table is stocked with lots of condiments. Also you can have either hot or cold soy milk which is complementary which is also a wonderful touch especially in cooler San Francisco. We really enjoyed our meal but it can get crowded and the owner is very very nice, other servers however are a little less friendly.

My parents had a craving--no, a calling--for the kind of Vietnamese-Chinese noodle soup that could awaken old memories and warm the soul. I was determined to find the very best in the city, a place worthy of their nostalgia.

That quest led us to Thai Nghiep Ky Mi Gia, tucked away in the heart of San Francisco's Sunset District.

The moment we stepped in, the air was rich with the scent of simmering broth. We were seated instantly, greeted with a smile that felt like an old friend welcoming us home. Then came the bowls--piping hot, fragrant, and full of flavor. One sip of the broth and we were transported straight back to the bustling streets of Saigon, where time slowed and every bite was a memory reborn.

The atmosphere was laid-back yet full of life, the service warm and attentive, and every spoonful felt like an embrace from the past.

For anyone seeking not just a meal, but a journey--I wholeheartedly recommend it.

Picture this: a regular crust, generously smothered with a velvety white sauce that set the tone for the entire culinary experience. A base layer of cheese formed the perfect canvas for what was to come next.

The pepperoni, an all-time classic, brought a zesty kick, while the mushrooms added an earthy depth that perfectly complemented the other ingredients. The olives, with their distinct briny flavor, added a tangy contrast that danced harmoniously on my taste buds. Then came the diced tomatoes, offering a burst of freshness and juiciness that elevated each bite. And finally, the Italian sausage, with its savory notes, tied everything together in a savory symphony.

The amalgamation of these ingredients was a testament to Mountain Mike's mastery in crafting flavors that not only satisfy but also surprise. The contrasts and harmonies on this pizza were like a culinary work of art.

When I swung by to pick up the pizza, I was met with a warm and friendly demeanor from the lady at the counter. It's always a plus when you're greeted with a smile, especially when you're excited to dig into your order.

All in all, the Snow Alps pizza at Mountain Mike's was a delightful journey through taste and texture. Each ingredient played its part, creating a harmonious ensemble of flavors. With the friendly service adding a cherry on top, this experience left me with a satisfied palate and a craving for more. If you're looking for a pizza that goes beyond the ordinary, the Snow Alps might just be your ticket to a flavor-packed adventure.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

If comfort food had a passport, it would probably be stamped “Lucky Dragon Cafe.”

I stopped in today around 12:34 PM looking for a solid Chinese food lunch, and I walked away wondering why I hadn’t come here sooner.

From the moment I walked through the door, I was greeted with warm smiles and genuine hospitality. There was no feeling of being rushed, no pressure, and no sense that I was just another order in line. Instead, I was welcomed with the kind of effortless customer service that instantly sets the tone for a great meal.

Now let’s talk about the food.

Absolutely phenomenal.

Every plate that came out of the kitchen looked like it was prepared with pride. The portions were generous, the presentation was inviting, and the aroma alone was enough to make me impatient for the first bite.

Then came that first bite…

Game over.

Everything was hot, fresh, flavorful, and cooked exactly the way great Chinese food should be. Every ingredient tasted fresh, every sauce was balanced, and every bite reminded me why this cuisine has become one of the world’s greatest comfort foods.

This wasn’t food that was simply made.

This was food that was cared for.

There’s a difference, and you can taste it.

What impressed me most was the consistency throughout the entire experience. The dining area was clean, the restaurant had a welcoming atmosphere, and the staff worked together like a well-oiled machine. Everyone seemed to genuinely enjoy what they were doing, and that positive energy carries over into the entire experience.

I also have to give credit where it’s due—it’s refreshing to find a local restaurant that still believes in generous portions and outstanding value. You leave feeling like you received far more than what you paid for, and that’s becoming increasingly rare these days.

In a world full of restaurants competing for attention, Lucky Dragon Cafe doesn’t need flashy gimmicks.

They let the food speak.

They let the service speak.

And both have plenty to say.

To everyone working today, thank you for your hospitality, your professionalism, and the obvious pride you put into every meal that leaves the kitchen. It’s clear that you’re not just serving food—you’re creating an experience that keeps people coming back.

If you’re craving Chinese food that’s fresh, comforting, generously portioned, and served with genuine hospitality, Lucky Dragon Cafe absolutely deserves a visit.

Five stars isn’t enough.

The food is top-tier.

The service is top-tier.

The value is exceptional.

And the entire experience felt effortless from beginning to end.

I’ll definitely be back for another round.

Oakland is a unique place where you can find soul food and local cuisine nestled in the heart of the city. Unlike San Francisco or the South Bay, many people are unaware of the diverse food scene here in Oakland. One evening, I was looking for some fried rice 🍚🍛and, since I was staying nearby, I stumbled upon a charming little spot where I decided to order a combination plate.🍜

The elderly lady at the cashier was incredibly sweet and friendly, and I suspected the chef was her husband. I requested fried rice along with half chow mein, and she provided me with excellent options for that evening. When I went to pay, I noticed that I could add extra shrimp for just a dollar more; I asked her for the shrimp, and she generously gave it to me for free. She was truly delightful!

top_reviews.content:
Phat Thai, Lombard Street, SF

Lombard Street is a parking lot disguised as a landmark. The fog was working overtime, curling around the bumpers of gridlocked tourists, and I needed a sanctuary. I pushed through the doors of Phat Thai, hoping to outrun the damp chill.
The interior had the kind of deliberate, brooding shadow a guy can appreciate. Black walls, an exposed ceiling trapped behind a heavy wooden grid, and an industrial fan slowly chopping the air like a lethargic helicopter. The artwork—framed prints of Bangkok tuk-tuks and street food carts—stared back with the vibrant, mocking warmth of a city that doesn't need to wear a wool coat in May.
The menus laid out the terms of engagement. I put in an order for the chicken yellow curry and the pad see ew with shrimp, bracing myself for whatever the kitchen was going to throw at me.
The chicken yellow curry was a masterclass in deception. Refer to the evidence in the attached photos. It arrived as a placid, golden lagoon of coconut milk, carrots, and chicken, flanked by a highly disciplined mound of white rice. It tasted completely innocent for about three seconds, and then it hit you—a subtle note of spiciness. It was a quiet, simmering heat that didn’t kick the door down, but simply picked the lock and made itself at home. It was very good. The kind of curry you’d willingly confess your secrets to.
Then came the pad see ew, sprawling across the plate like a beautiful, complicated mess. Broad, flat rice noodles tangled up with shrimp and Chinese broccoli. But whoever was working the wok must have had a score to settle, because the noodles were slightly burnt. Just a little too much char on the edges, like the dish had been roughed up in a back alley before being thrown onto the table. It gave the plate a smoky, cynical attitude—flawed, sure, but it still had legs.
I’m giving it 4.5 stars. It’s a solid hideout where the yellow curry plays a flawless long game, even if the noodles spent a few seconds too long on the wrong side of the fire.

I went to this cafe hoping for some real Thai food but it was a big letdown.
The shrimp Tom Yum is supposed to be the star dish the heart of Thai cuisine. Here it was just bad. It honestly didnt even deserve the name Tom Yum. The taste was weird and flat like the ingredients were old or the broth was made wrong. No aroma no spice no balance at all just really disappointing.
The Pad Thai was also way too sour like they went crazy with the lime. It completely ruined the dish.

FOOD: EXCELLENTSERVICE: JUST OKAMBIANCE: JUST OKPARKING: TERRIBLEPRICING: Reasonable
Went for a nice Memorial Day Weekend meal on a Sunday at Itria. Excited to try a lot of the dishes I saw on social media and knew it was Michelin rated.
THE FOOD: Go for the food and tolerate everything else. This food is top-notch, reflecting SF and California cuisine. It's really good and consists mostly of crudo, salad and pasta. That combination makes for a great meal without ordering too much. We started with the Amberjack Crudo - stellar with excellent fresh fish, sweetness from passionfruit, spice (a nice little red pepper) and freshness (mint) all in one bite. Great to share between 2 people.Salad: We had the Asparagus Salad - lightly cooked and cut asparagus with a great savory butter Caesar dressing. The crispy shallot made it, topped with some nice Parmigiano-Reggiano. Again - stellar.Main Pasta: Agnolotti with Roasted Corn, Hen of the Woods (mushroom) and chive - this dish rocks. So savory with the pockets of pasta filled with cheese and the sauce of mushrooms and corn are an umami and sweet touch. Bravo. Second Pasta: Mafaldine Cacio e Pepe - BOOM! My new fav pasta. The Mafaldine noodle just really makes this dish. So different, yet so perfect for holding the amazing sauce in the ruffled edges. Cooked perfectly and they seem to know how to mix the simple ingrediants in the proper fashion to create greatness in a dish. No dessert, but I do hear the Panna Cotta is quite good.
SERVICE: Just ok to poor. Rotating staff at the door seemed busy helping inside and were not very attentive. There are typically lines at the door, and they seem to have a challenge seating people. We booked the bar and asked for a table since most tables were open when we arrived, but we were denied. Tables did fill up while we were there but a few were still open when we left. The bar experience was just okay; the bartender seemed overwhelmed serving us even though only half the place was full. Orders were entered late, and the service suffered.
AMBIANCE: This place could be stellar if the ambiance and design was fixed or updated. The front of the restaurant is all tables for 2 or 4 and a little cramped. The bar area is dark as a funeral home. Some of the bar seats will put you infront of a small refrigerator and the overall bar area is unappealing. Messy and unorganized. The rear of the house is probably the best. Far more lit because of a skylight and a view of the kitchen. Community table and some two and four tops sit in the area and it seems pleasant.
PARKING: Terrible. No Valet, no great street parking or parking garage options. Give yourself 20 minutes to find a space. Better yet - only take Uber.
PRICING: Reasonable. Two of us ate for $124 plus $10 tax and an $8 SF Mandate (whatever that is). We had a choice between this menu or the Tasting Menu (now up to $105 from $95) which probably would have been too much food for one person but would offer a good taste of all their food.
In Italian, "Itria" most famously refers to the Valle d'Itria (Itria Valley), a stunning, sun-drenched region in central Apulia (Puglia). The word has also gained popularity as a name for traditional, hand-made pasta derived from ancient Mediterranean roots.

Itria Restaurant in SF lives up to this from a food perspective. Put up with the service, ambiance and parking - the food is worth it!

Came for the $75 SF restaurant week tasting menu and loved it! We started with the crudo (scallop, amberjack, and trout) - loved the texture of the scallop but the sauce on the amberjack was so tasty! Next was the cercioni, which was a tad salty for me but hearty and savory. I also loved the texture of this pasta! Then came the mafaldine which was sooo good!! The fresh black pepper was delicious!! Ended the meal with a banana panna cotta. I’m usually not a huge fan of banana flavored items, but I loved how light this tasted! Would definitely come back!

From time to time, I visit this restaurant and I am always delighted that they remain in business.

Maybe it's because I'm a longtime San Francisco resident and this brand has been around a long time. I started eating Hunan province style Chinese food back when it was in the Chinatown/Barbary Coast locations.

They've been true to their original recipes going back decades, not succumbing to latest trends. And so, part of the allure for me regarding my fondness for this place is its continuity and consistency from the past.

Yes, the food can range from "not-hot" to raging inferno, so be careful how you order your spiciness level. Their portions are generous, but they are also on the pricey side for Chinese restaurants.

However, they are located in a section of town that's not hurting and pricing reflects that. While I do praise them for keeping consistent in their menu through all these years, they can be a bit of a hit & miss from time to time. Sometimes they're great and at times, they miss the mark, I'd have to say.

top_reviews.content:
I was waiting for the hype to die down a bit before trying Sforno, and I'm glad I finally did because it absolutely did not disappoint. I placed my pizza order online for pickup right when they opened, and when I arrived there was no line, though that could definitely be day and time dependent since I went on a weeknight. They had blocked the Pizza Portafoglio from online ordering, but it was easy enough to add on in person, which was well worth it.

This is very much a grab-and-go spot, with only a handful of 2-tops available, but there are a ton of outdoor seating options nearby, including the various bars that are all outside food friendly as well as Patricia Green just across Hayes, which makes it easy to enjoy your meal with a drink and/or soak in the weather.

In a city full of fantastic pizza options, I genuinely thought the pizza here was outstanding. The crust is airy and chewy with charred spots throughout, and while the undercarriage is not super sturdy, I think that is a feature, not a bug for Neapolitan-style pizza as it tends to have that signature "flop". That especially works for the Pizza Portafoglio, which is folded over twice and makes for the perfect compact bite on the go. It is surprisingly packed with flavor from such a simple lineup of ingredients, with the tart San Marzano red sauce, creamy cheeses, fresh basil, and the spicy, salty spianata piccante all working beautifully together. For just $11.50, or even less without the salami, it is one of the best deals in the city for a satisfying meal.

I also tried the Mortadella Speciali and loved that just as much. It had all the qualities I loved in the Pizza Portafoglio, but with the added richness of thin sliced mortadella, salty shaved parmesan, crunch from pistachios, and generous dollops of burrata throughout. I did not have room for dessert, but everything on the menu looked and sounded delicious, and I'm already planning to go back for those and to try the panozzis, especially the porchetta.

Probably a 5 star spot for those that prefer Neapolitan style + mild toppings and sauce (I prefer NY style so giving it a 4 star). Highly recommend nonetheless. Love stopping by for tacos and burritos - this place never disappoints. The carnitas and chicken is always great. Solid portions, consistently good food, and definitely a spot I keep coming back to when I want great Mexican food.

*Authentic* and delicious food with generous portions and great value. Everything we ordered was flavorful, and the service was excellent! We couldn’t finish all the food, and the leftover packing was done very thoughtfully. Highly recommend!!

The staff was very fast and helpful, and the portions were huge. And they give kimchi!

I highly recommend and have been 4 times. Green beans are perfect, potsticker wrappers are homemade, scallion pancakes are fried, and fried rice has excellent flavor and lean bits of pork. I have since had the vegetarian fried rice and it's my favorite, there were even bamboo shoots in it. We usually get sweet and sour chicken but have also had kung pao chicken. Everything is great, the servings are large enough for leftovers which are almost even better the second time around. The staff is friendly and attentive. The restaurant is clean and bright. Street parking is available every time I've been.

Thanh Ky Restaurant, Oakland

I've been coming to Thanh Ky since forever. You'll always see OG's eating here. And yes, this is a hole in the wall spot.

Thanh Ky’s Crispy Fried Shrimp Roll is so good! It’s cut up into pieces so every bite has a crunch! Just thinking about it, one order isn’t enough! 🤤

The staff are always nice and the owner is always friendly. The noodle soup always hit the spot when I'm craving for noodles! 😋

I came here years ago and I returned to be disappointed. I love to support local businesses! We had the egg noodle with the wonton and that was okay, but the chow fun flat noodles are usually 3/4” wide at other restaurants. Ours were like left over thin pieces?

We visited Thanh Ky Cafe for an early brunch to beat the lunch rush. Since it’s similar to another spot we frequent, we were confident the noodles would be good—and they did not disappoint! We ordered the #9 “House Special Ho Fun,” which includes pork kidneys. The standout surprise was the addition of fried pork skin, adding a delicious crunch and depth of flavor to the dish.

If you’re in the area, it’s worth stopping by. Just be aware that the surrounding neighborhood can feel a little sketchy—after all, it is Oakland—so take a few extra precautions. Overall, tasty food and a satisfying experience!

top_reviews.content:
🍣 The Pinnacle of Bay Area Sushi
This restaurant sets a massive benchmark for Japanese cuisine in the region, and boy, the name is true. After sampling numerous spots across the region, I can confidently say this is the BEST SUSHI I've had in the Bay Area! The kitchen displays an exceptional level of mastery, ensuring that every cut of fish is pristine, well-tempered, and presented beautifully. From traditional nigiri that melts in your mouth to innovative specialty rolls, the execution is flawless. It’s a true destination for sushi purists and casual fans alike who want top-tier quality.

🍶 Amazing Happy Hour and Fair Pricing
The value proposition here is outstanding, making it accessible without compromising on the premium nature of the ingredients.

Amazing Happy Hour: They feature an amazing happy hour that provides incredible deals on both drinks and signature bites. It’s the perfect opportunity to sample a wide variety of the menu at a fantastic price point.

Reasonable Everyday Value: What makes this spot even better is that the prices are fair even during normal times. You don't have to wait for a special promotion to get a great meal for a reasonable cost, which is a rarity for sushi of this caliber in the Bay Area.

Generous Selections: The portion sizes for the sashimi cuts and rolls are substantial, ensuring that you leave feeling entirely satisfied with the investment.

✨ Vibrant Atmosphere and Stellar Service
The front-of-house operations complement the high standards of the kitchen perfectly.

Lively Vibe: True to its name, the environment is energetic, fun, and highly welcoming. It’s an ideal spot for a fun night out with friends, a casual date, or uncoiling after a long work week.

Attentive Staff: The service team is quick, knowledgeable about the daily fish catches, and excellent at pacing the meal so you never feel rushed or neglected.

Clean and Modern: The dining room is beautifully maintained, balancing modern aesthetic touches with a comfortable, classic sushi bar feel where you can watch the chefs at work.

🍱 Final Thoughts and Recap
To recap, this is an awesome place that easily earns a flawless 5-star rating. The realization that this is the BEST SUSHI I've had in the Bay Area makes it a mandatory visit for any local foodie. Between the amazing happy hour deals and the fact that prices are fair even during normal times, it delivers unmatched value. If you want phenomenal seafood, a great drink selection, and a fantastic atmosphere, I highly recommend making this your next dinner destination!

I’ve been here many times, but unfortunately my most recent visit last week was not a good experience.

We ordered a sushi roll that came with very mushy avocado. I personally was fine with it and still ate the entire roll, but my wife did not enjoy the texture or taste.

I politely mentioned it to the waitress and made it clear that I still enjoyed the sushi and ate the entire roll. I even asked to order another round of the same roll - but politely asked if the next order could be made with firmer avocado.

Shortly after, I found out the chef was also the owner, and he unexpectedly became defensive and confrontational, insisting the avocado was fresh. I calmly explained that while it may have been fresh, my wife simply did not like the overly mushy texture because it did not feel or taste fresh to her.

Despite that, he continued giving me attitude in front of other customers, which honestly felt embarrassing and unnecessary. He eventually walked outside afterward.
What stood out most was that the waitress later apologized for his behavior and even mentioned that he can get grumpy at times and be difficult to approach. That made the situation even more uncomfortable.

The waitress herself was amazing throughout the experience, and I still tipped her well because none of this was her fault.

Unfortunately, because of the owner’s unprofessional behavior and how the situation was handled, I do not plan on returning.

Should have just went to tio chilos where they have better vibes and customer service that doesn't act like lil teenage girls . I will do a review on yelp with more details ..

For the longest time this place was cash only.  They've recently started accepting credit!

Flavorful banh mi but they don’t toast the bread so it’s very crispy.  Sometimes it’s been downright just soft.

They both contained smaller than expected amounts of shredded proteins. I’m guessing they are made from the advertised protein, but neither of these is flavorful nor even close to what I was expecting to receive. If you’re going to serve shredded proteins, you need to identify them as such on your menu.

I've had Chinese style BBQ pork and Vietnamese style BBQ chicken, both in Bahn mi previously, as they are both a very common filling.

These both failed miserably by comparison.

I would much rather pay more for a sandwich that arrives with the fillings as expected.

Sadly, I won’t be back.
Quick. Affordable. Delicious. What more could you want? The elderly couple who runs this restaurant must be two of the hardest-working people in the Bay Area food industry!

I've had better pho at half the price.

I've been wanting to come here on Sundays but found out they are closed on this day. This place was actually recommended by the owner's nephew who I know. Good thing tonight I happen to be nearby and decided to come in. The restaurant is clean and has got a good decor. Food and service is quite good. I ordered the grilled pork vermicelli. To my surprise it is not your typical Vietnamese vermicelli. I would consider it fusion Vietnamese. Instead of a bowl the meal is served on a plate. It looks like they are trying to accommodate the Western taste in every way. I was most impressed with the egg rolls. I normally don't like the standard Vietnamese egg rolls which are stuffed with some unknown mushy meat. However, the ones here are stuffed with ingredients that you can see and know what they are. Overall the food experience was good. I can't wait to find out how they serve their Pho and rice plate on my next visit.
A couple of things to watch: parking is awful around the area. It's better to come at night. During the day it's all metered parking so that will add cost to your meal. Secondly, prices at this restaurant are about 50% higher than your standard Vietnamese restaurant. I normally pay $10 somewhere else but here I paid $16 plus tips. Still a good experience.

top_reviews.content:
Fun and cozy neighborhood sushi restaurant. We loved the oysters and octopus, we got there a little late so they were out of some of the specials but you can order from their menu too if you don’t see something on the boats.

Some comments mention the boats move a little fast, it’s true but for us that was part of the fun and you get the hang of it very quickly. Service was great and all ingredients were fresh and flavorful, we loved our experience and highly recommend it.

Warakubune Sushi was exceptional. We walked in about 15 minutes before closing and still received some of the warmest hospitality I’ve experienced at a restaurant. Tiffany took incredible care of us — friendly, welcoming, and genuinely engaging. She even shared local tips, including great dim sum spots nearby, which made the experience feel personal and connected.

The vibe inside was wonderful. Most of the guests seemed like regulars who knew each other, giving the place an easy, communal feel that instantly puts you at ease. The sushi itself was fresh and delicious, and the unagi in particular was outstanding — rich, flavorful, and perfectly prepared.

Despite the late hour, the team treated us like valued guests, not an inconvenience. Highly recommend Warakubune Sushi for both the food and the atmosphere. It’s the kind of place that makes you want to come back soon.

Absolutely love this place, my favorite casual sushi spot. Everything is really fresh and well made. I like to have a lot of variety when I have sushi, so the boats are great because you get a couple pieces of a few rolls or nigiri so you can try everything you want rather than have to pick between larger rolls. Aside from what comes around on the boats, they also have a menu including non-sushi items plus if you just ask the sushi chef he will make you whatever you want. Great alternative to takeout if you just want something fast and also a great spot for dining alone - you can get in and out without the fuss of waiting on typical full-service dining. Highly recommend!

I’ve lived in the neighborhood for 16 years, and this place never fails to disappoint. Worst sushi in the area. Way too expensive for the poor quality. The rice is very dry. The tempura is heavily battered and deep fried like KFC. The unfiltered sake is crazy sweet. We had 9 pieces of sushi each (mostly California rolls), two miso soups, and two house sakes for $90. We won’t be coming back.
The sushi is great, the staff is friendly and eating is fun. So many delicious choices. The scallops and crab rolls were my favorite.

Stumbled upon this place by chance and were pleasantly surprised — the ambiance and the food were amazin. We especially loved their kombuchas; the lavender and ginger flavors were absolute standouts.

For food, the arugula salad was delicious and the pulled lamb bowl was truly out of this world. The lentil miso burger was just okay, so you might want to try some of their other options instead.

Overall, definitely a must-visit spot!

This place is truly a hidden gem! We found it by chance on Google Maps after seeing all the great reviews and decided to give this local spot a try - we’re so glad we did.
Everything was delicious, the ingredients were fresh and high quality, and the presentation was beautiful. The café itself has a cozy, stylish atmosphere that makes you want to stay longer.
The staff was incredibly friendly, the service was outstanding, and you can really tell they care about their customers.

We’re happy to support a local business like this and will definitely be coming back. Highly recommend checking this place out!

Family-run hidden gem for lunch among all the low quality and corporate options in this area. I was craving good meat and veg and Boochmania delivered. Perfectly al dente veggies with simple, tender meat. I modified the quinoa bowl which they were very nice about, and really enjoyed the blend of counter service (order everything at the register) and restaurant feel to the cozy seating. This is going to be my new go-to place every time I’m in the area for work

This was one of the best Turkish restaurants I’ve visited outside of Türkiye.

The food tasted just like it does back home. Many places abroad advertise “Turkish food,” but the flavors often end up being quite different. That definitely wasn’t the case here—everything was authentic and full of flavor.

It’s a family-run restaurant, and you can really feel the warmth and hospitality. Everyone was incredibly friendly and welcoming, making us feel at home from the moment we walked in.

The portions were generous and very filling, and the prices were more than fair considering both the quality of the food and the portion sizes.

I highly recommend this place to anyone looking for authentic Turkish cuisine. We’ll definitely be back!

Delicious food and kombucha thoughtfully made and served by a kind and passionate family. I tried the pulled lamb wrap and the currant & clove kombucha and would highly recommend both, as they were flavorful while being light. When possible, sitting upstairs is extra cozy and comes with a great street view. Looking forward to returning!

Highly, highly recommend this place for a casual night out, fine night out, or a bar buyout for the party of your dreams! We recently hosted a large themed party here, and it was absolutely fantastic! 💃🏼🥂

He went above and beyond to make the event special, helping us customize the experience—including renaming some of the drinks to match our theme, which became an excellent conversation starter among our guests! He also has a back room that can easily be setup as a photobooth!

The food was a hit too—the jalapeño poppers and vegetarian spring rolls disappeared quickly and received rave reviews from our guests. The drinks were equally excellent. A special shoutout to Victoria, our bartender, who even dressed in gold to match the theme! She and the bar back were both amazing, creating delicious drinks and helping keep the energy high all night!

The setup of the bar, TVs, and karaoke was perfect and made the whole event feel effortless and fun. You can tell Jeremy genuinely cares about creating memorable experiences, and it shows in every detail and thought he has put into the bar. Thanks to the party master Jeremy - he really knows how to put the soul in a party. At his bar you can play a slideshow of your own photos/videos, watch a game on the many TVs, play your own music!

If you're looking for a venue for a birthday, company event, networking mixer, fundraiser, or private celebration, I cannot recommend this place enough! Outstanding hospitality, great food and drinks, and a team that truly goes above and beyond. Our guests are still talking about it! 🥳

Stoked to find this little gem before a show at the Great Northern. Awesome drinks, killer local band was playing and the food was bomb. Talked with the owner Jeremy as he was working the bar and running food/ drinks. Super cool dude and you can tell his place reflects his energy. Will definitely be back again!

A super fun spot in SoMa. I've been there for Trivia night a couple times and also hosted a bar party recently! The crew is super friendly and the owner Jeremy went the extra mile to make sure we were having a good time. They had set ups for Karaoke, beer pong, and even a ring light for photos.

The drinks are some of the most reasonably priced you'll see in the city; the vibe is great on a Thursday night with a good amount of people, but plenty of space to sit and chat; and they've got some good happy hour food.

top_reviews.content: Hole in the wall but has very authentic delicious pupusas. Had the combo plate breakfast with pupusas. Price is about right for the serving had to leave review because it was soo good. Have to come back again! They take card but cash would be best.

I ordered the Desayuno and one chicharron papusa via DoorDash. The desayuno was tasty and great. The papusa was more on the dry side but still tasty. I’ve definitely had better papusas but I would still order from here again.

Was craving papusas so I went out of my way to visit. Got the $13 Papusas plate which comes with 3 Papusas (I got.mixed but your choice), cordito (Salvadorian pickled slaw - think Kimchi without the heat or strong sour fermented tang) and a non spicy red  sauce.

Their sauce and cordito were refreshing. The star was the Papusas.these were the lightest and thinest skinned Papusas I ever had. Sometimes Papusas feel like stuffed thick tortillas. These are now my favorite Papusas in NorCal: I'll take there cheese Papusas over a quesadilla anyway of the week.

This was such bad food! I ordered something off the menu based on the many pictures they had on their walls. I asked the man working behind the counter if this option was available. What I received did not match the picture at all. I was given mystery meat, some mediocre rice and beans that were NOT Gallo pinto and the plantains look soggy and tasted odd! Never going back, I tried calling the restaurant and number was not available.

My brother is Salvadoran and so my family grew up eating pupusas.  It’s become my favourite thing to try pupusas in every neighborhood I stay in while visiting the Bay Area.  These ones were exceptional.

I ordered a revueltas and a carne asada pupusa and when they were brought out they were very clearly freshly made, puffed up beautifully with a gorgeous sear on them.  I was given a very decent amount of curdito and salsa, both of which were excellent.

Everyone was so exceptionally nice and the restaurant itself was so clean and spacious. I enjoyed myself so much I actually came back an hour later and ordered more pupusas to take away for my next couple of meals.  They were just as exceptional.

You guys have created a very special place with wonderful food.  I can’t wait to come back to Oakland to dine here again :)

top_reviews.content:
What a find this little restaurant was for us. In the Sunset & Richmond districts are a plethora of Thai restaurants and today we chose to try Nakorn. Definitely a kind of a hole in the wall, which is usually my favorite kind of restaurant. The open kitchen upon us entering was nice to see, and the cooks were extremely welcoming.
We started off with our Thai iced tea, which were quite good.
We decided to each get something different so we could share. I had the red curry with vegetables and tofu. My other friend had Tom kha kai soup and the other person had a peanut curry. ALL were delicious bursting with flavor.  I’m excited to have my leftovers for dinner tonight. The prices are quite reasonable and the portions large. I would definitely return to this spot again if in the area.

I ordered pickup by phone directly from Nakorn Thai because I like supporting local and avoiding delivery apps when possible/it makes sense. I went with the #21 Kao Gra Prow with pork and added a fried egg, since it seemed like a popular choice, and the person who took my order was very nice and even helped recommend a spice level. I went with medium, and when I mentioned that I like spice, she also offered to include some of their available spicy sauces, which I appreciated.

Overall, the flavors were good, but not especially memorable for me. I was expecting a lot more of that savory punchiness I love in Thai food, but everything tasted a bit muted. The medium spice level was also very mild, so if you enjoy heat I would definitely recommend going with at least hot.

One thing that did disappoint me was the pricing. I ordered directly because I wanted to avoid the app markups, but I was still charged more than the price listed on their website. The item I ordered was shown as $18, but I was charged $21, which felt misleading. They should either keep the online menu updated or remove the prices altogether so there is no confusion.

Overall, it was a decent meal with friendly service, but between the muted flavors and the pricing issue, I'm not sure I would go back to try other items as perhaps I ordered the wrong thing.

Nakorn Thai is an absolute gem!
From the moment you step in, you’re greeted with a warm and welcoming ambience that instantly makes you feel at home – a solid 10/10. The atmosphere is inviting, with thoughtful decor and a calm, cozy vibe.
The food quality is exceptional – fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented. Every dish we ordered was cooked to perfection, easily earning a 10/10. You can tell they use high-quality ingredients and put genuine care into every meal.

Cleanliness is also top-notch – the entire restaurant, from the dining area to the restrooms, was spotless. It’s clear the staff take pride in maintaining a clean and comfortable environment. Another 10/10.

Nakorn Thai SF exceeded all expectations. It’s a place you’ll want to return to again and again. Highly recommended for anyone looking for authentic Thai cuisine served with excellence in every aspect.

Absolutely better than Marnee Thai in Irving and 9th Avenue.

First time eating here for dinner and it was very good. My Red Curry Duck was delicious. My wife had Pumpkin Red Curry with tofu and she felt it had little flavor.  We will go back to try another dish. The dining room felt a bit cool and sterile even with the afternoon sun coming in the skylight and soft lighting. But it was comfy enough for a nice evening out on our anniversary.  Not super romantic, but cozy. Also had the fish cakes app...very tasty!

My go to place for Thai in the city. Small but pleasant seating area. They always have a friendly staff. The old school fried rice with the chicken cutlet on top is still a favorite of mine from when it was part of king of thai. Their pad see you and rad na is pretty yummy. Let them know how hot (spicy) you want it! They will accommodate you.

As someone visiting from Texas, I have pretty high standards when it comes to bold, rich Mexican flavors—and Modí completely blew me away! The Italian-Mexican fusion here is absolute genius.
The Birria Lasagna is a must-order. It is incredibly rich, savory, and comforting, with perfectly tender beef and just the right amount of kick. I finished the night with the Churros, which were spectacularly crispy on the outside, pillowy on the inside, and the perfect sweet ending to the meal.
Huge shoutout to David and his entire team. The service was top-notch, the vibe was fantastic, and they’ve built something truly special here.

I had the most incredible lunch at Modí! If you haven't been yet, you are seriously missing out. Combining Mexican and Italian flavors sounds wild, but they execute it so beautifully and thoughtfully.

The vibe is wonderful, but the staff really makes the experience—they are so warm, welcoming, and friendly that you immediately want to invite them to join your party!

My absolute must-orders: You have to get the branzino and the clams. Trust me on this, order them and thank me later!

The menu is exciting, Italian and Mexican mix, with the Ravioli Elote, the Pizza Al Pastor and the Branzino being my favorites. Enjoyed a wonderful sandwich and Matzah Ball soup for lunch at Iggy’s Place. A super clean, spot to drop in for a stuffed sandwich. The special of a half sandwich and soup is an amazing value.

WHEN: Thur @4pm

I wanted to come here at opening time for a few reasons:

- PARKING: It’s downtown so not sure how parking would be.  But lucky for us, we found free parking just around the corner!  When we left around 5pm, more opened up!  I’m guessing it’s because the auto repair shop was closing.

- THE CROWD:  This place is popular and there is usually a line.  Though they have a great amount of seatings available (outdoors), but I prefer a space I don’t feel like I have to menu ear so much around.

- THE FISHWICH THAT SELLS OUT:  I was told about this special fried fish sandwich that sells out.  So in order to guarantee there will be one for me to order, gotta get there early!

It’s my first time, and here’s what I had:

THE FISHWICH - $14.50
Panko crusted rockfish, American cheese, Pickle, Shredded Cabbage, Tartar, Potato Bun.
This is a limited supply item that is only available Wed-Sat until sellout.  A friend shared it was amazing, but sadly I couldn’t agree from one reason:  This was bland.  I love the softness of the potato bun, the crispy and hot pink-crusted textures, and the generous amount of tartar sauce.  But I tasted nothing—just all sorts of texture.  I owned up top it though and finished the entire thing.  Was I satisfied?  No, but my belly is full!

THE DRIVE THRU - $10.50
American cheese, Schmalz onion, Pickle, Lettuce, tomato, Special Sauce, Sesame Bun.
Overall decent burger, and I enjoyed it.  Really can’t say more without comparing it to SCOLARI’S but it’s a solid burger.

HAND CUT FRENCH FRIES - $5.35
Blanched and Fried chipperbec potatoes.
I think I enjoyed these fries because they remind me of SCOLARI’S friends, heh.

​We got an XL CYO pie (half cheese/half sausage w/ olives, mushrooms, and green peppers). I forgot the green peppers on my DoorDash order, but when I ran next door, the staff were incredibly friendly. The place was visibly clean, even during a busy, rainy Saturday night rush! Brother’s Pizza is located on Tarvael Ave near Ocean beach in San Francisco, CA. I think this is the perfect location with a lot of foot traffic since they are near Ocean beach which is like a 5 min walk. It’s perfect for you to get some great pizza and Indian food. When I first came in, the interior had nice character and I can’t believe they were in business for 30+ years. That’s crazy and they are quite popular. Anyways, I got their half and half pesto pizza special+Indian vegetarian pizza, paneer palak, and their samoas. I have to say their Indian food and pizza were near on point!

I got their pesto pizza and Indian vegetarian pizza.When I first opened the box, they didn’t skimp out on the toppings. There were a lot in there and the pizza looked awesome. The crust was well cooked and not rubbery so I thought that was a plus! I thought their pesto pizza was great and the toppings that were on it were very nice. I tend to love pesto on pizza and this one definitely delivered very much. I also had their Indian vegetarian pizza as well. I was actually happy that they didn’t add tomato sauce and substituted it with Indian gravy. The gravy was flavorful however, I thought it was slightly oily in terms of taste and how much oil was used on the pizza. The toppings were a great size and were very plentiful but again the toppings were a bit oily. Overall the pizza was flavorful, delicious, and plentiful! I also had their paneer palak which I thought was tasty. The taste was creamy and mild which every paneer palak must have. The naan bread however wasn’t the softest and was a bit charred too much which came with the paneer palak. I would just eat the paneer palak by itself if I have to be honest. The samosas were crunchy, flavorful and perfect. The ratio of dough and filling was great and it was just a nice samosa to have.

Overall even though there were a few flaws, I would totally bookmark and recommend this great pizza place if you are ever at Ocean Beach! The staff was very nice, the food is home cooked and this spot rocks for their pizzas and Indian food! I would definitely come back to taste more of their items.

Don’t be fooled by the size of this store. It somehow manages to have just about everything a vegan, vegetarian, or meat-eater could want.

My favorite part is the impressive selection of plant-based foods. There’s an entire refrigerator dedicated to hummus (although I was sad to see they no longer carry my favorite brand).

The biggest surprise, though, is the produce section. It’s consistently some of the freshest produce I’ve found, with an incredible selection of seasonal and locally grown fruits and vegetables. If you enjoy cooking with fresh ingredients, this place is an absolute gem.

Other Avenues Grocery Cooperative – A Quiet Treasury of the Natural World

Next to Judahlicious, where we had sought nourishment of a different kind, stood Other Avenues—humble in appearance, rich in purpose. We paused not out of necessity, but curiosity, and within its doors found more than shelves and labels.

This co-op stands as a quiet defiance to the chaos of processed living. No loud branding. No gimmicks. Just carefully curated food, drinks, and essentials—organic, natural, non-GMO. One might say it’s a marketplace for those who walk with intention.

We left with Uncle Harry’s Miracle Mouthwash—not out of impulse, but alignment. It felt right. As right as mint on a morning breeze, or calm in a world that often lacks it.

This place reminds us: the good things in life are often quiet, often real, and often found when we are not looking—but simply open.

My favorite grocery store. Employee owned. Good vibes. It's a different and in my not-so-humble opinion much better way to relate to people and get the things you need than going to a corporate store. I wish there were more places like this.

I'm a native New Yorker who's been living in CA for over 20 years.  I know good pizza.  The Bay Area has some great pizza places and I like to try them all.  This place was a big let down.  If you like Domino's pizza, you might like it.  I won't be back.

This place is SUCH a perfect neighborhood gem and awesome for everything from family dinners to date nights. We have never felt so welcomed to a decent restaurant with our three very young kids in tow. And the food is always superb.

The food here was soo delicious!! We ordered the Ancient Grain Cheese Cannelloni and the Pennoni alla Norma (with Pennoni subbed for a very nice, soft Tagliatelle). The crepes in the Cannelloni were just the right amount of crispy, the Sheep milk ricotta had a very nice unique flavor, and the tomatoes were so well cooked and flavorful. Everything worked together so well! And the eggplant in the Pennoni alla Norma literally melted in your mouth leaving just the flavor of pure eggplant goodness. Paired with a very nice tomato garlicky sauce, and the very soft pasta noodles, it was also a very comforting dish. My girlfriend and I were both very impressed with both dishes! The serving sizes were also enough to leave us very filled after both dishes, and the prices were appropriate for the quality and amount of food.

Being vegetarian, I was very happy to see the wide variety of vegetarian options as main entrees on the menu. At many places, I've found that the vegetarian options are basically the non-vegetarian options with meat removed, but the vegetarian options here all felt like very complete and intentional meals designed to be had as is.

The service was also phenomenal. Our waitress was very nice and was patient in giving us recommendations. And at the end, one of the other ladies gave us a very passionate and interesting lesson on the history of Sicilian cuisine and how it is influenced by so many different cultures!

top_reviews.content:
We ordered 2 California Burritos online, and selected the “No Meat” option. We have ordered from this restaurant before and this hasn’t been an issue. This time however, both burritos contained chicken. When attempting to call and find out what happened, I was told the burritos usually contain steak and was hung up on when trying to ask follow up questions. When I tried to call back, I was hung up on again.

My husband and I love the food from here, so this experience was very disappointing and makes us not want to return.

I ordered a chile relleno combo. It was the nastiest ever. It had more layers of fried egg than cheese inside the roasted poblano pepper. It also wasn’t cooked all the way. The ride and beans had no flavor and food is very expensive. If I can give this place zero stars. I would. I definitely do not recommend this place. Please be aware of any foreign items on your food.

Food:
Having visited twice, I found the food here to be a mixed experience. On my first visit, I tried the street tacos - carne asada and al pastor - accompanied by a generous bag of chips. The chips were a highlight, fresh and crispy, complemented by two salsas: a mild salsa verde and a spicier salsa roja, both served in convenient squeeze bottles. The street tacos, priced at $3.50 each, felt somewhat pricey given their small size. The carne asada was decent, while the al pastor, though generously sauced, was overly salty.

My second visit was for the Baja-style fish tacos, which, at around $19-$20 for two, were notably expensive. The tacos came with guacamole, garlic aioli, and pico de gallo. Unfortunately, the pico de gallo and guacamole didn’t seem freshly made, impacting their quality. The fish itself was crispy and plentiful, but the overall experience didn’t justify the high price.

Service:
The service here is straightforward and efficient. You order at the counter, and the food is brought to your table. There’s nothing particularly special or noteworthy about the service, but it gets the job done.

Ambiance:
The ambiance is typical of a casual, hole-in-the-wall taqueria. There are some seats inside with paper towels on the tables and additional seating outside, which is convenient for those with pets. It’s not a place you’d go for a fancy dining experience, but it serves its purpose well for a quick, casual meal.

Overall:
Overall, this taqueria is just okay. It’s not a place I’d highly recommend, but it’s a decent option if you’re in the area and craving tacos. The prices are more reasonable compared to other nearby Mexican restaurants, though some items can still feel overpriced for the quality offered. If you’re willing to spend a bit more for a possibly better experience, you might consider other options, but for a quick taco fix without venturing too far, this spot might be your best bet.

A good evening is getting some tiki drinks from Forbidden Island, then stumbling the few blocks over here to stuff down a giant burrito.

A Mixed Bag of Great Flavors and Disappointing Service

I recently visited Il Pavone, an Italian restaurant I had been looking forward to trying for a while. The overall experience left me with very mixed feelings—while the food and ambiance were delightful, the service was unfortunately disappointing.

Let’s start with the good.
The ambiance at Il Pavone is charming. From the moment I walked in, I appreciated the tasteful decor, warm lighting, and relaxed atmosphere. It had that classic, cozy Italian restaurant feel that makes you want to settle in for a long, satisfying meal. To top it off, there was no wait time when I arrived, which was a pleasant surprise.

The food itself was fantastic. Every dish we tried was full of flavor and made with high-quality ingredients. The pasta was cooked to perfection, and the sauces were well-balanced and authentic. I had no complaints about the taste or presentation. It was, in fact, one of the best Italian meals I’ve had in the city.

But here’s where things took a turn.
Despite the restaurant being far from crowded, our server vanished after taking our initial order. We had planned to order more food, maybe a second round of appetizers or a dessert but the opportunity never came. After our dishes were served, no one came to check on us, refill water, or ask how things were. We sat waiting for quite some time, trying to flag someone down, but no one seemed to notice or care. Eventually, we gave up on ordering anything else and just left.

To make matters worse, the portion sizes were surprisingly small considering the steep prices. For a restaurant charging at this tier, I expected either more generous portions or a more upscale service experience, preferably both. Unfortunately, neither was delivered. Value for money felt way off the mark.

The most frustrating part was the server’s attitude. Not only was she inattentive, but when we did interact briefly, her tone came off as dismissive and even condescending. At one point, she tried to explain something to us about a dish in a way that sounded more like a lecture than helpful information and unfortunately, she didn’t even seem to know the correct details. It left us with a bitter taste after what could have been a lovely meal.

Final thoughts:
Il Pavone has the potential to be a standout Italian spot thanks to its food and ambiance, but it falls short due to poor service and a lack of attentiveness that makes guests feel unwelcome. I sincerely hope they work on their service training and pricing structure because otherwise, they’re wasting a great kitchen.

Until then, I’m hesitant to return or recommend it. Good food alone isn’t enough when the overall experience doesn’t make you feel like a valued customer.

top_reviews.content:
My husband and I decided to go here because the reviews seemed great. However, we regret having spent our money here.

Upon entering the restaurant, you see a cute cat neon sign on the wall. But they still had Christmas decorations in May. Not a big deal, but still indicative of lack of care.

We were greeted by a no-frills hostess who didn't seem very happy to be there. Then we were told to scan the QR code to order. We ended up ordering scallion pancakes, xiao long bao, and chicken fried rice.

The scallion pancakes were the only saving grace of this dining experience. The texture was crispy, airy, and thin, which we enjoyed. It was paired with a sweet and sour sauce which we have never seen before, so we opted out of eating it.

The xiao long bao were unfortunately flavorless and steamed for too long as it just ripped apart immediately. However we did appreciate that they seemed handmade.

The worst of this meal was the chicken fried rice. It was also flavorless and for some reason had shreds of unseasoned iceberg lettuce in it. It would have been okay, but then we found a hair after eating half of the dish 🤮 We normally don't ever let food go to waste, but we could not bring ourselves to finish the dish.

There are many better Chinese restaurants in SF, so I would recommend spending your money elsewhere.

I love dining in restaurants where you can just scan a QR code on the table and order/pay from there. There Mapo Tofu is the BEST I say the BEST one I've ever had. Would highly recommend that with a side of rice. Overall the food was delicious especially given that. Wish I can come back here again but unfortunately I live in Fullerton. Thank you.

I ordered the beef noodle soup and the 8-piece eggplant & pork boiled dumplings for dinner.

The dumplings arrived first about 10 minutes after I sent in the order. The dumplings arrived hot but cool down really fast, so dig in before they get cold and the skin hardens. I couldn’t really taste the eggplant but I did feel the consistency of it with the pork. Flavor is light but I’d like more of the meat flavor to come out. I doused the dumplings in chili oil.

The beef noodle soup came out about five minutes after the dumplings arrived. The soup was hot and fresh. The noodles were pretty good and cooked well for the most part, I did find a very small tangle of noodle that was stuck together. There were a handful of greens in the soup, which were good to give some crunch to your chews. Beef stew quality is above average (C+/B-), not too fatty but can still chew pieces of good meat. Soup base flavor is good and what I expected, no surprise spices or herbs added.

The food we ordered was not very good for the most part. Tried a variety of soup dumplings and the skin was mushy, filling was bland, and the soup was greasy instead of the flavorful broth I was hoping for on the inside. The skin on the shrimp gow was crumbly rather than springy and chewy, and the shrimp tasted old. The smashed cucumbers were probably the best thing we had there, those we enjoyed and would recommend.

Ordered takeout — went with the pork, cabbage, and onion dumplings. They traveled surprisingly well; still soft and juicy when I got home. The flavor was solid — savory filling with a nice balance between pork and cabbage — though nothing that completely blew me away.

Overall, a dependable dumpling spot if you’re craving something comforting and straightforward. Nothing fancy or over-the-top, but it definitely hits the spot. I’d order again, especially for a quick and easy meal.

Have walked by this spot several times and finally got a chance to try it. I’m so glad I did!  Everything was excellent; the giant wood fired oven adds a wonderful touch to several of the menu items. My favorite was the prosciutto and melon salad, it was salty, sweet, crunchy, and fresh.

Came here for lunch with a friend at 1 PM on a Saturday. We came 15 minutes late after our reservation because of parking and they were understanding of it. As soon as you walk in, you're hit with the smell of a campfire from the oven. The restaurant is absolutely gorgeous with an Art Deco design. The ambiance is cozy but elevated.

Benedict (buttermilk biscuit, dungeness crab cakes, marinated swiss chard & beet greens, herbed hollandaise, poached eggs & mixed greens): I'm not a huge benedict person because they can feel heavy, but this one was fantastic. I loved the textures and flavors of the crab cakes pairing with the greens and vegetables. It felt balanced and not too creamy or exhausting to eat. It definitely stands out from the run-of-the-mill brunch benedict.

Vegetable Hash (roasted sweet potatoes, garnet yams, sunchokes, cauliflower, cremini mushrooms, celery root & onion, savoy spinach & poached eggs): This was also delicious and also set itself apart from the standard brunch hash. I loved the different vegetables in it besides being just potatoes and onions. The mushrooms and root vegetables worked really well together.

Everything was well-seasoned. I'm glad we ended up choosing these dishes even though neither were my original top choices (I decided on the menu with my friend). It made me feel like you can choose anything and it'd be a banger.

We were quite full from these dishes, and we forget we also ordered beignets to come out last. They were fluffy and mostly air (but not in a bad way).

The service throughout the meal was good. We were checked on from time-to-time and our waters were refilled, although I wish the water glasses were a little bigger. One small thing to note was that we were given the check while we were still eating, even though the restaurant was still seating people despite it being close to closing time. Unsure if/why we were rushed like this.

Overall, this was a memorable brunch spots I've been to in the Bay (dare I say one of the best?). We left smelling like a campfire. I would recommend it.

We arrive around 11:30am and luckily a table for 2 was only a 20 minute wait. So we put our name down and walked around the neighboring shops before deciding to go to the flower shop right next door.

We had just finished purchasing a potted plant and some scented shower steamers when I got the text that our table was ready. The hostess sat us at a hightop communal table in the main dining room, which has a rustic warehouse feel and lots of natural light. We started with an Arnold Palmer and a fancy mocktail.

Drooling over all the delicious menu options, we decided to share a few dishes between the two of us. We ordered the skillet cornbread, the baked French toast, and a scrumptious quiche.

The food came out quickly and everything was so good that my date decided to order a second quiche to take home to her man.

The service was attentive, the noise level was mid range, and the overall vibe was hip but not pretentious. We would definitely eat here again, and based on the dishes we saw at neighboring tables, we plan to try the eggs benedict and their sandwiches next time.

I’ve had their Spicy Hog, steak with mushroom, a few Cubans, but the one that I always come back to is “The Balls” sandwich.

First off, this sandwich is massive, so be sure that you come here on an empty stomach. These beef meatballs are seasoned to perfection and bursting with flavor. The balls are covered in their red sauce with provolone and Grana Padano, which gives it that nutty and salty flavor that pairs extremely well with the meatballs and baguette. All the juices and cheese just get soaked up to perfection. The baguette bread they use is supplied by La Farine, which is just a few meters away from each other. Just putting out there that La Farine is hands down one of the best bakeries in Oakland, so it makes sense that this sandwich would be so dang good. top_reviews.content:
Dabao is easily at the top of my go-to restaurant list. Every visit feels like pure comfort. I absolutely love the Nasi Lemak with fried chicken and the Seafood Laksa — I’ve ordered them countless times, and they still make me ridiculously happy. More than once, I’ve wanted to text my friends mid-meal just to tell them how amazing the food is.

The fried chicken is perfection — crispy, juicy, and deeply satisfying. And the laksa broth? Rich, fragrant, and comforting with every single sip. If you see the seasonal chili crab on the menu, don’t miss it. It’s a must-try while it’s in season.

Beyond the incredible food, the staff are genuinely warm and welcoming, especially Nang - always with bright smile! It makes the whole experience even better!

Thank you for bringing such authentic, delicious Singaporean flavors to us. I truly hope Dabao stays around for a long, long time. I’ll definitely keep coming back.

I was tricked! This store is called Dabao Singapore, specialty includes Hainan chicken claiming to be Singapore Hawker style food. Nothing of the sort! The food is so bland. I asked for the ginger sauce and it wasn’t made of ginger at all. I just returned from Singapore and the food is definitely NOT Singapore Hainan chicken. I also had the chicken katsu and again very bland and tasteless. Yes, I am very particular about my food and I expected to taste the same if you claimed to be so. I’m so disappointed 😢. What a waste of food and money.

★★★★★ Dabao at the Metreon is a fantastic hidden gem tucked inside the food court. The food captures the bold, authentic flavors of Filipino street food—comforting, flavorful, and satisfying without trying to overcomplicate things.

Service is impressively fast, making it an easy stop even when you’re short on time. Authentic flavors, quick service, and a great find in an unexpected setting. Definitely worth seeking out!

Quick and super tasty. Great way to try food from Singapore. From the seafood soup to a vegan soup, it is fresh and flavorful. The team is super friendly and great at explaining the menu. It’s in the middle of a food court. Nice escape from the bustle outside.

It is my second time here in over a year and am happy to know that Singaporean food is still available in the building.

As a Singaporean myself living in the Bay, I know how hard it is to find food from home and one that is done well. I do have mixed feelings about the taste but I believe it’s because I know what it should taste like. I still eat it because it’s available, tastes good (enough), and appreciate the effort the owner does to bring our food abroad as authentically as possible.

For starters, I’m glad that the laksa broth tastes more flavorful this time and that there was a good amount of tofu, fishcake, prawns and of course hard boiled egg. The last time I feedback verbally that it needed a lot more salt but was told a restrained approach was taken to make it more healthy. I know from the many reviews that I was not the only one who felt salt was needed to bring out laksa’s rich flavors. Having said that, I still needed to put a little more salt myself this time but maybe it was a personal preference.

The noodles were overcooked though and I could not taste much of the coconut milk either and wondered if an alternative like evaporated milk was used instead (I hope not). The sambal was good as always. Packed with flavor and made the laksa better but since there was already a kick in the broth, I did not necessarily want to make it spicier just to get more flavor. All in all, I felt it would’ve been perfect if the flavors were deepened more cause it did feel like I was eating curry noodles with a hint of laksa leaves instead of curry laksa itself.

The black carrot cake was a nice surprise! I never thought I’d see it outside of Singapore. It is on the sweeter side which is fine until it gets cold. Unfortunately, it did feel like eating eggs with a side of carrot. It was severely lacking daikon radish so most times we were just eating sweet egg. The sambal helped but it did not taste right at all. Felt like chicken rice chilli was used to make it efficient but there was too much vinegar in the sambal. Just like the laksa, the garnish was very little.

My overall impression is that this place has a lot of potential and am sure the owner herself knows how to cook good Singaporean food. My suggestion would be to have more QC. Perhaps the people cooking & preparing don’t understand the subtle nuances that make the food taste good or excellent. A simple example would be like the amount of garnish. Someone who isn’t familiar with the cuisine would think the garnish is just for show, but in our food, it actually affects the flavour. Small things like that make a difference.

All in all, I hope the business takes my suggestion into consideration and hope to see it thrive even more. It definitely has potential.

top_reviews.content:
Late night, healthy options can be hard to come by, so I was pleasantly surprised to find Ben’s Fast Food tucked inside the SOMA Food Court near where I was staying. It actually reminded me of the Colony setup in Santa Monica with multiple food concepts operating out of one central pickup space.

I admittedly made the mistake of walking there thinking I could just order at the counter, only to realize it’s more of an online-order/pickup operation—but no big deal… who needs human interaction anyway, jk. Within minutes of ordering, my food was ready. They definitely weren’t lying about the “fast” part.

I ordered the Chicken Mixed Bowl and honestly devoured it before I even thought to take a picture, which probably says everything. For around $10, the portion was generous and filling. Mine came with brown rice, rotisserie chicken, broccoli, cucumbers, carrots, pickled onions, roasted sunflower seeds, mixed greens, and a really tasty green sauce. The sauce ramekin could’ve been filled a bit more generously, but the flavor absolutely delivered. The only thing I’d tweak is swapping some of the iceberg-heavy lettuce mix for a heartier green like kale, which would take it to another level.

This definitely isn’t a dine-in kind of place—there was a steady stream of delivery drivers and pickup orders coming through—but if you’re looking for a quick, solid, healthier option late at night in SOMA, this hits the spot. I’d absolutely try it again and explore more of the menu.

Ben’s fast food is truly a gem. Not only is their food high quality, but it’s ready fast! I’ve ordered numerously from the SF location, as well as this San Mateo location & the order is ready quickly! I hope they expand and open more locations ASAP. Until then, I’m always recommending this place to family & friends that value delicious & healthy quality meals.

My partner and I got the same things but different dressing. We were impressed by the affordability and were thoroughly satisfied by the healthy “fast food” meal. It was delicious, fulfilling, and felt good to eat. The smoothie hit the spot, as I was craving something cold and fruity—it was not too sweet and not too leafy greens-leaning, either. Damn, why didn't anyone tell me how good this food was.... look, I finally had iLava Hawaiian Barbecue for delivery and WOW--this food showed up like it had something to prove. Everything arrived hot, fresh, and smelling so good I forgot I was supposed to plate it. Straight out of the container and into my heart.

The portions are MASSIVE. Like, "this box feels heavier than my responsibilities" massive. The meat was insanely tender and flavorful, drenched in that smoky, savory goodness that somehow survived the delivery journey perfectly. Not dry. Not sad. Just thriving.

Mac salad was still creamy and delicious (delivery mac salad is risky, and this PASSED). Rice was fluffy and plentiful, clearly there to support the star of the show like a loyal sidekick.

I fully intended to save some for later. That plan lasted approximately 3 bites.

If you're ordering delivery and want food that arrives tasting like it was made just for you five seconds ago, iLava is the move. 10/10 would order again. 11/10 would fight my family over leftovers.

Absolutely amazing!!! I cant wait to try the rest of the menu items 😋

04/14/2026
**UPDATE:** I had to come back and run it back a second time… because the first time trying this place was so good I needed to make sure it wasn’t a fluke. Spoiler alert: it was NOT. If anything, it hit even harder the second time.

From the moment you walk in, the smell still hits like a warm Hawaiian slap of flavor—instant hunger activated. It’s giving laid-back island vibes without trying too hard.

The BBQ plates? Still wildly disrespectful—in portion size and flavor. The meat is juicy, tender, and grilled like somebody in the back really cares about your happiness. That smoky-char flavor? Consistent. No drop-off. No excuses.

The mac salad? Yeah… I thought I knew what to expect the second time. I was wrong. Somehow even better. It’s lowkey the side that turns into the main character when you’re not paying attention.

Rice? Still doing elite-level support work—fluffy, warm, and soaking up sauce like it’s got a purpose in life.

Customer service? Same energy: friendly, quick, and genuine. No attitude, no weird vibes—just solid people making sure you’re taken care of.

And let’s be clear… this is still NOT a light meal situation. This is “I’m taking a break halfway through and coming back stronger” type portions. Second visit confirmed: you WILL leave full, possibly plotting your next nap.

**Second visit verdict:**
🔥 Flavor: Still a 10/10 (consistency matters!)
🔥 Portions: Still outrageous—in a good way
🔥 Service: Still solid and welcoming
🔥 Vibes: Chill, no-frills, just great food

Final verdict: iLava is officially in rotation now. First visit made me a fan… second visit made it a habit.

Cozy cabin vibes. Packed after hardly strictly

This meal hits that unapologetically indulgent Chinese-American sweet spot—big flavors, bold sauces, and zero restraint. The lo mein is exactly what you expect in the best way: glossy, slightly oily, and packed with savory depth from the beef and wok-charred vegetables. It’s not trying to be refined, and honestly, that’s the point—it delivers comfort with every bite.
The eggplant dish was the standout for me. Silky, almost buttery in texture, it soaks up that garlicky, soy-heavy sauce in a way that feels borderline addictive. There’s a balance between sweet and umami that keeps it from being too heavy, even though it absolutely leans rich. It’s the kind of dish you don’t think will be your favorite, and then suddenly you’re going back for more every few minutes.
The fried chicken dishes, though, are where it gets a bit excessive. Both the chili-loaded version and the sweet glazed one bring crunch and flavor, but they blur together after a while—more about intensity than nuance. Still, if you’re leaning into a full-on comfort food moment, this spread delivers. It’s messy, loud, and satisfying—the kind of meal that doesn’t pretend to be anything other than exactly what it is.

Hidden gem in SF, they have good varieties of Chinese cuisines.

Chilly chicken is to die for, and so are other items.

Sichuan Tasty is our favorite Sichuan restaurant in SF so far. Their mapo tofu, fish fillet, and green beans are always sooo good. We always bring our out of town friends here and everyone love it. Definitely our comfort spot when we’re craving Sichuan food.

top_reviews.content:
Tried out Rigatoni's with my wife and our two kids last night. New to the area and wanting to support local spots, we went in with an open mind after seeing the post about the Dublin location closing down after 27 years.

We ordered the lasagna, chicken fettuccine Alfredo, and rigatoni bolognese, solid classic Italian comfort food. (The lasagna was my favorite of the three though my wife thought frozen lasagna from Grocery Outlet tastes better.) The self-serve bread bar was a nice touch and a hit with the kids.
The dining room had a relaxed, low-key vibe, not too crowded for a Saturday, which meant no wait and plenty of room for our family. Food was fine; nothing that especially stood out, but nothing wrong with it either. Comparable entrees all run about $19, and with self-serve water and bread bar, service felt pretty hands-off; the woman checked-in with us just once during the whole meal.

In contrast, we've also recently eaten at 88BaoBao, which is another counter-service type of restaurant but comparable entrees run about $11-$14. Despite being the "cheaper, no-frills" option, the young teen waiter/server/bus boy came by repeatedly to check in on us, refilled our water multiple times, and even noticed our daughter was cold and closed the door for us. My wife, who almost never tips extra, went back after the meal just to hand him an additional tip.

That contrast made the value gap at Rigstoni's stand out more than it might have otherwise. The restaurant itself was pleasant enough and not too crowded, which was nice for our family, but at a higher price point with more hands-off service, it didn't feel like it justified a 20% tip the way a place doing more for us did.
Still hoping Rigatoni's finds its footing, we like having good options nearby.

Tastee Lasagne with Meat Sauce. Garlic Cheese bread was good as well. Hot Fresh Food made to Order. Nice Clean Dining Room. Customer Service with a 😊😁. Kind Knowledgeable Staff. Easy to Park. Easy to Find. Take Out Available. Reasonable Prices.

They have really great service super fast delivery and if you eat here often or not they are predictable and each dish we have tried from the rigatone bolognese to the house spaghetti to the spicy chicken is fantastic. The experience is above average time and time again by ourselves (me and my daughter) or with friends (we have brought about 6 different people who have shared our enthusiasm) this restaurant is a absolutely fantastic experience. I wanna go tomorrow just thinking of it now. Highly recommend sopping by as it is one of Castro Valleys nicest little places.

We wanted to try this place out since we pass by it frequently. The staff was super helpful with questions we had on the menu. We tried 2 dishes on the house specialty section, no substitutions, and they were so good! It was extremely flavorful, and the portion size was perfect. We are definitely planning to come back and try other dishes on the menu. The cheesy garlic bread is a must-have, btw!
