top_reviews.content: Really excellent sushi for a very reasonable price. As of September 2026 they have a promotion where buying a 49ers roll gives you the option for a $10 sizzling halibut plate and both are fantastic. I also highly recommend the Cal Bears roll.

I had an incredible experience at Tazaki Sushi. Mr. Tazaki runs a wonderful, welcoming spot with fantastic sushi and a great atmosphere. The sushi was extremely fresh, beautifully prepared, and honestly some of the best I’ve had in San Francisco.

They currently have an amazing sushi special running through May 4th, and the value for the quality is outstanding. The presentation alone was impressive, and every bite tasted just as good as it looked.

What really made the visit memorable was the friendly conversation and warm hospitality. Mr. Tazaki and the staff make you feel like a regular the moment you walk in. It’s the kind of place where you want to slow down, enjoy the food, and just relax.

If you’re anywhere near the Sunset district, don’t miss this place. Great sushi, great price, and genuinely kind people. Highly recommended. 🍣

Local gem of a sushi restaurant and genuinely the best I've had across all of San Francisco. The nigiri is where they really shine, but the rolls are inventive, balanced and delicious also. Mr. Tazaki is a seasoned expert and a legend to behold. You can usually find him behind the sushi bar and ready to tell you what's in season or make you a custom roll based on your favorite fish. The staff are kind and have encouraged me to try new things which has always turned out deliciously! My absolute favorite is the tamago. Classics like sake (salmon), hamachi, and maguro are always delicious (especially in hamachi season in winter), however some other favorites of mine include the bluefin tuna, kampachi, shimaaji, and toro. The crystal maki is also so fresh and unique and delicious! This is also a beloved local gathering spot, and you can usually find friendly regulars sharing a sake at the bar or celebrating a birthday with the staff. We are so lucky to have Tazaki sushi!

I stopped here for dinner with a friend and had some ridiculously delicious sushi. The fish was wonderful and the texture of the sushi was perfect.
The restaurant itself is family-run with attentive staff, and we never felt out of place or ignored. Everyone was super friendly and kind, and it seemed like a popular neighborhood spot as they often ran out of seats! There was even a cute little room in the back for large parties that looked like its own house with the decor.
Overall I definitely recommend stopping by- I’m sad to just visit and wish I had a spot like this in my hometown!

I have lived just a block away from Tazaki Restaurant for 7 years and I have eaten here maybe 100 times during that period. The quality of the food is incredible, especially for the price. That said, there’s something special about the restaurant that I can’t quite put to words. I have taken people here that are visiting from out of town, I have eaten here by myself after a long day of work, I have made this a ceremonial place for when something is worth celebrating, and everything in between. And so it felt right to consider Tazaki Restaurant as the place that would host a reception dinner for my wife and I on our wedding night.

I had asked Chef Tazaki if this is something he would consider and he gladly accepted. He worked with us to create a unique dining experience in that the restaurant would be closed for dine-in, we’d have our own private server, a full range of incredible sushi and Japanese dishes, and a chef-selected assortment of Daiginjo sake.

Tazaki Restaurant has an authentic Japanese feel to it, one that is hard to describe, and yet it also has a characteristic to it that feels quintessential to San Francisco. You can tell that the chef takes immense pride in his craft and that the servers care deeply in ensuring that their guests enjoy their meal. My wife, myself, and our guests all had a wonderful night celebrating our marriage and can’t thank Chef Tazaki and his team enough for this experience. Thank you for everything!

P.S. These are some of our favorites: N-Judah, Cherry Blossom, Summer Love, Omakase, Toro

Good neighborhood restaurant.  Nothing fancy,  just good food and good service.  If you are in the area try it.  But, it's located in a residential area,so parking is difficult as only street parking is available.

Surprisingly great.  Food was really good. Decent prices. Waiter was so sweet. Even though it said they closed at 8pm, people would still walk in at 7:55pm and be seated. We had dinner here - classic Cantonese dishes. Would definitely come back for dim sum.

top_reviews.content:
Fabulous!!! Service was top notch. The food was balanced and well seasoned. Everything seemed fresh and full of flavour. The outside patio is very cute and the inside is cozy. Everyone in the team is friendly and kind.

This place had been for a long time in my brunch list and it exceeded my expectations.
What a charming dinner spot! I came to have dinner with a friend and we were not disappointed. I ordered the pesto pasta and it was probably my favorite ive ever had. Will definitely be coming back!

We chose The Magic Flute for our wedding reception because we wanted something intimate, charming, and uniquely San Francisco — and it was absolutely perfect. From the start, the team was so easy to work with, accommodating every detail with kindness and professionalism.

The evening itself was magical. The food and wine were incredible — our guests couldn’t stop raving about both — and the service was friendly, attentive, and fast. The restaurant’s warm lighting and beautiful ambiance made every photo glow, adding to the cozy, elegant feel we hoped for.

We wanted our guests to experience the heart of San Francisco in an intimate setting, and The Magic Flute gave us exactly that. Our night was truly special, and we’re so grateful to the entire team for making it unforgettable.

I really love the old San Francisco atmosphere here and the service is good but I have to say that the quality of the food has gone downhill. This place taught me to love salmon but the salmon on spinach that I had the other day was so salty my mouth was actually burning. It was also incredibly expensive for a meal that was a bust to put it lightly.

We came here on a cold and rainy night. The restaurant was nice and warm inside. The front room was full so we had to sit in the back.
Our waitress was extremely nice and accommodating.
They have a very simple menu.
The garlic bread was light and fluffy and very garlicky.

top_reviews.content:
Let me start by saying that my son and I found this spot by accident, and he looked it up on Google review and said it looked good! Now, living in California we tend to take Mexican food for granted but in reality it's hard to find a place that has exceptional Mexican cuisine. The menu is relatively small but what's on there really packs a punch!
The inside is light and airy giving you the feeling you could be on the coast and not in a... Well to be honest, kind of a hetchy-sketchy part of Berkeley. But I digress, the inside is very simple but upscale feeling and I love the tall ceilings and skylights. Our server Luis was extremely friendly and the service was fast but we never felt rushed. My son had the spicy pork tacos which he said were great, and I had the chicken verde enchiladas which also were phenomenal! We skipped dessert because we had started with an appetizer that was delicious but really way too much for two. What a delightful accident finding this place, I think it's safe to say we have a new favorite!
The Superb-intendent 🍀

Tasty, flavorful but not heavy Oaxaqueño food in a high ceiling elevated environment.

The drinks were lively but harmonious. The Tuna Tostado was sooo light and good. You could easily just order appetizers. But come as four people if you can so you can share. For two people it would be a romantic outing.

Service was excellent but unobtrusive.

We loved this place! So much seating and good vibes. Food was delicious! We ordered the chicken tacos, chicken enchiladas, a drink. Everything tasted fresh and was brought out very quick. For dessert we had the flan which was rich and hit the spot. We will definitely be back soon!

Had an amazing experience at Mercado 925 while visiting Berkeley. The food was excellent — incredibly authentic Mexican flavors with a modern approach that made every dish feel thoughtful and elevated. The drinks were outstanding, the music and overall vibe were perfect!

Nicole and Jose took such great care of us all night. Super sweet, attentive, and genuinely welcoming.

If you’re in Berkeley, this hidden gem is a must. We’ll absolutely be back!

Wow, just wow.  We lucked into this place...Just looking for a place to eat and found this on Google Maps.  Great venue.  Beautiful interior.  Great wait staff.  And then the food!!!  Try the tuna tostadas (ask for extra tostados).  My Al Pastor tacos were terrific!  Corn tortillas, lots of meat, Great salsa on the side.

top_reviews.content: This is a delicious Thai family owned spot in the Temescal. The food is Issan from Northwestern Thailand. Their specialty is larb - a delicious sort of ground meat (or mushroom & tofu) dish eaten with lettuce wraps and dipping sauce. We’ve also enjoyed the drunken noodles with ground chicken. They have a cool box set for $23 which is enough for two for lunch! It includes larb, choice of protein and green beans. And they have lots of curries!

I ran into this place during Covid and got hooked since. The food is exceptional, I don’t think I have tried anything I didn’t like here. The service also always friendly and attentive. My go-tos are Gai Gra Pao and Drunken Noodles. If you feel adventurous, the chicken heart skewers are delicious. If you can’t tolerate spicy, make sure to make it very clear.
I ate the best chicken wing of my life here. So crisp on the outside, so moist on the inside. Even if you go only to try the chicken wing, it'd be worth a trip.

A small Thai restaurant with a Thai street style.
The food was surprisingly delicious, even the simple papaya salad was great! Their Roti is very different, they put the topping on top instead of dipping it in sauce!

The tables are close together , maybe when it’s full house will not easy to talk with each others !

Overall the food is delicious but nothing that was phenomenal that would warrant me to go out of the way for unless I’m in the area EXCEPT that the fried chicken spring roll and Kao Ka Moo was tasty.

Chicken spring roll has outer layer that was not the usual spring roll and so it gives a nice texture to the meaty spring roll.

The Kao Ka Moo, stewed pork belly, was so tender that it just shreds and the flavor was yummy. This was the entree that we pretty much finished since it was yummy.

Pad see ew was so so. A little on the soggy side which I’m not used to and I prefer pad see ew from another location about 1 mile away that is hands down the best I’ve had.

Nam Kao was ok too.  Texture was lacking since everything was mostly soggy when I’ve like the crispy rice texture together with all the meat and vegetables.

Kao soi had good coconut milk soup but it didn’t have that spices depth to it. If it did, it would have been perfect, just as how I would remember it when I had it in Thailand.

top_reviews.content:
We had a delicious dinner here. Most of us ordered the omakase, and it was so good. The fish was very flavorful and served at the perfect temperature. The omakase starts with a plate of appetizers such as monk fish pâté, mackerel sashimi, and tamago. The presentation was beautiful. Then came the sushi served five at a time. Lastly, we ate chawanmushi topped with two slices of sashimi. We also ordered a couple of rolls, and they were delicious.

Service was great. Our server was friendly and helpful. Since we were a party of six, the gratuity already was added and our server kindly pointed that out when she brought the bill.  There is a private area in the back of the restaurant, and that's where we ate. It can seat quite a few people.

Parking in the area can be a challenge, but fortunately, the Mission Bartlett garage is only a couple of blocks away.

Definitely come for the omakase! We recommend Chef Master (yes, his name is Master). Each course made it so difficult to pick our favorites because they were all so delicious!

The service and food are great, and the omakase price is very fair here. I recommend sitting at the chef counter to get to chat with the chefs and watch them prep the courses. They have tables available otherwise. The regular menu items all sounded interesting, and the ones that I saw being served looked really good. Parking in the area is tough; so, plan ahead if you're driving in. All in all, it was a great date night experience and we'd definitely go back!

There are an abundant amount of Japanese restaurants in San Francisco to choose from, however, I took a gamble and chose Okaeri for a Saturday lunch with a colleague of mine— and it did not disappoint WHATSOEVER!

The restaurant itself has a modern decor and the noise level was very nice for a late afternoon lunch.

We started off with the Yuzu Foam Oysters which really set the bar for what was to come. The yuzu foam was intriguing to see as an offering, and it absolutely blew us away with how well it went with the oysters. Creamy and Umami— so so good!

We ordered a few rolls: Cyclone Roll, Snow Mountain Roll, Salmon Lover Roll, & the Spicy Tuna Roll. Every roll tasted fresh, a great balance and ratio of fish to rice, perfect amount of seasoning, and expertly presented. Each roll had excellent flavor. My colleague and I both agreed that we were impressed with how well each tasted!

To wrap up our meal, we ordered The Toast. This is hands down something everyone in San Francisco must try at least once… because it is unique and delicious. Uni Cream-Toro Tartare + Uni Caviar on a buttered thick toast— it was DIVINE.

I am so glad I decided to venture out across the city to try Okaeri. This place is a winner. The service was great, the restaurant looks nice, and the quality of the fish and flavor was fresh and delicious. I will definitely be coming back and I highly recommend if you appreciate authentic and delicious Japanese food!

Too expensive for what it is. Ambience is refined but oddly sterile - the fishy smell when you walk in needs fixing. The $95 omakase is fine but underwhelming for the price, with especially poor rice. You can do much better at the same cost (Okane, Nakama, Eiji). Portions are small, so we had to order extra rolls. Rolls were decent, but not for the price. Sauces were consistently good throughout. Smart-casual vibe. Overall, not recommended for the price.

Came here on my own for my birthday. Was an amazing experience.

I got the omakase menu and it was excellent. The little starting plate they gave had an assortment of little bites that each had a very interesting assortment of flavors and textures. I especially liked the tempura with (from what I remember was) a little flower shaped radish piece on it. As for the nigiri, each piece blew me away. They hit each piece with a blowtorch for just enough to slightly render the fat so every piece coats your mouth in fat and flavor and it is just delicious. I have had a lot of sushi all around the world including Japan and this is probably the best I've ever had.

The service is great, every person I spoke to was very kind, friendly, and accommodating. I was a little anxious going somewhere like this on my own for a special occasion but everyone made me feel welcome.

I highly recommend visiting Okaeri!

top_reviews.content: The food is excellent. The service was excellent. The drinks were very well paired. We had the tasting menu + wine pairings and let me just say that I'd never regularly order a pea soup. But that's the beauty of prix fixe because you'll get the chef's recommendation instead of your preference. Yo that pea soup was amazing! The layers of flavors was so impressive. At first I was disappointed because the portion size seemed really small, but it was so loaded with flavor and just heavy enough that the portion size was actually ideal. Then I had the steak. I took a bite of the steak and immediately thought of the years ago when I lived in Texas and there was always a crispy char from the grill on your meat. The taste was really impressive. We also had the salad which was a highlight and then the following courses kept getting better. We ended with cookies and milk, which was delicious but not as impressive as everything else. Our server was a doll and was so fun. The bartending staff was cool and they nailed the old fashioned we ended with. Can't wait to go back!!

Went for Spring restaurant week. Got the steak and salmon option. Started off with their salad - yummy. Next is the pea soup - also yummy. Not as grainy as some pea soups can be. Steak made well with the aoili dipping sauce. Salmon also nicely made. Kids meal has a salt & pepper option. Dessert was a lemon pound cake which was a bit disappointing. Was dense and a bit too tart for me. Rustic setting. Definitely prefer the back near the fire place.

Great meal and experience. Happy hour fried chicken sandwich with garlic fries was excellent. .As an out of towner, Bartender Jay made me feel welcome and engaged in great conversation. All the staff was very kind and friendly. Great beer on Draft too. Would definitely return.

Had dinner for the 2nd time here last night and it was divine! I got the burger last time and the salmon this time. Both were delicious but the salmon was exceptional. It was cooked perfectly. I was surprised to find parking easily both times too.

Jerome the bartender is a peach. He catered to our every whim. And we had demands.

1. we were in needs of some top notch puns, and they were expertly delivered. The orange bitters were top notch.

2. we demanded free rent for all people and that was expertly served.

3. Drink flavor sophistication previously only discovered in Narnia.

4. Golden Retrievers. number 4.

5. 5 demands? omg.

top_reviews.content: As others have mentioned, it’s still a good spot, but there’s definitely room for improvement. We ordered two cheeseburgers and Brussels sprouts. The food arrived quickly, and the server was really friendly and attentive. The food was "good" but not exceptional. We didn’t mind since we were looking for a quick bite and really enjoyed the service and ambiance, but we probably wouldn’t return specifically for the food.

Impressive building with high ceilings and comfortable seating, both inside and out. I went alone but this would definitely be a good place for group gatherings. Vegetarian options available. I had the veggie burger, which itself was great, and it came with a liberal portion of fries. Will certainly be back.

I rarely leave negative reviews, but this experience was too uncomfortable to ignore.
My friend and I (two young women) were at a table with a pitcher of beer and I went to the bar to ask for a glass. The bartender, Joey, stared at me like I was crazy before asking for my ID — which is completely fine — but his demeanor was immediately hostile. Because of how rude the interaction was, my friend calmly asked if we had done something to upset the staff. His became more aggressive and told my friend “I won’t serve you!” For the rest of the night, he made faces at us, smiling and waving sarcastically from behind the bar.

At the end of the night, when we tried to speak to another bartender about what happened, Joey aggressively yelled across the bar, “Do you have something to say to me?” It was intimidating and completely inappropriate. As we were leaving, he continued glaring and making hostile faces. The other bartenders were kind and professional, and encouraged us to leave a review. Unfortunately, the manager was dismissive.
This was openly aggressive behavior that bordered on harassment. We did nothing to warrant it, and it made us uncomfortable for the rest of the night. Completely unacceptable.
Great range of beers and cocktails, good food, the staff are really friendly and helpful, there's plenty of outdoor seating in the quad behind the main bar. But it is LOUD.

This place was solid. It's just really far out there to get to for me so I had never visited before. The wings were good but a little overpriced. The alcohol selection was good and the food had a lot of variety. The bar set up seemed awkward and a nuisance for the 1 bartender that had to go from one spot to the other to get different kinds of beer from the tap.

top_reviews.content:
Amazing deluxe omakase menu!! I ended up coming here with my mom on a whim and it was such a delightful experience. Not only was the omakase perfectly curated, beautifully plated, and delicious, but the staff was so kind and knowledgeable about all the food and sake.

I’ve had a few other omakase experiences in the bay and I feel like this one is a great value. $139 per person for 9 courses, multiple of which were 3-6 pieces per course!

The cherry on top was the complimentary strawberry layered crepe cake, which was a gift to celebrate my mom visiting from out of town:) I will definitely be celebrating another special occasion here in the future!

Gem of a Japanese restaurant on the cusp of the Irving St neighborhood....a rare combination of fresh, authentic, excellently prepared sushi and hot dishes... The chawanmushi was delicate, creamy and just firm enough to still feel fulfilling. The California roll didn't disappoint... Real snow crab meat featured on another roll
Only minus was the rice was a bit too moist tonight.  Service was excellent, friendly and fast... You can tell that the owners care.  Highly recommended.

After living on Maui, I became incredibly picky about sushi because I was spoiled by some of the freshest fish in the world. I can honestly say that Zentarou Sushi serves tuna that is every bit as good as if not better than what I had in Hawaii.

The quality of the fish is absolutely exceptional. Every piece is incredibly fresh, buttery, and melts in your mouth. The otoro nigiri is truly out of this world..rich, delicate, and one of the best bites of sushi I’ve ever had. And don’t leave without ordering the crispy rice with spicy tuna. It’s perfectly crisp, packed with flavor, and completely unforgettable.

What makes this place even more special is the people. The servers are some of the sweetest and most attentive I’ve ever met, and Bee, the owner, is the definition of hospitality. From the moment you walk in, you’re treated like family, and it’s clear how much care and love goes into every detail of the experience.

Zentarou isn’t just my favorite sushi restaurant..it’s genuinely some of the best sushi I’ve ever had anywhere. Between the incredible quality of the fish, the warm hospitality, and the welcoming atmosphere, this is a place I’ll recommend to everyone. Five stars isn’t enough.

2026-06

Came here to celebrate my birthday because the restaurant had a great review and I was not disappointed. I had to try the supreme omakase menu.

The restaurant is less than two years old and it’s very clean and tastefully designed.  The waiter, who is also a co-owner was very friendly and welcoming. We were treated very well. Will definitely come back again to celebrate a different occasion next time.

I had the pleasure of eating here and chatting with the owner a few days ago. It’s so clear that he and his sister put a lot of attention, love, and quality into this place. I had the omakase and a pot of tea and it was all fresh and delicious. I especially loved the savory egg custard - it surprised me and was sooo good. A very pleasant afternoon experience that I will hopefully redo if I’m in the city again!

One of few evening dining options in Bayview.

The pupusas taste good but very greasy , when we order the Nicaraguan food the meat tasted burnt & the rice and beans everything look greasy . If I was you guys just go to another restaurant . The old lady which clearly is the owner is arrogant and hang up on people faces .  some people can’t take criticism & that’s why they fail in their business!

Way too many chickpeas in the tamales. There was also potato in there too that wasn't cooked all the way,and the pork did not taste like much. The outside part was wet and drippy too. I would not recommend.
I had the fried fish plate. It was awesome! I left feeling upbeat and full of life from a wholesome and filling meal. And had a nice bottle of Nicaraguan beer to compliment the dish. Carry on!

I was at the hair salon, I was hungry so I went to this place, which is 20 feet away.   I wanted a taco, the lady  appeared to be the owner, told me “ you have to buy 2 tacos, we don’t sell 1 taco”

I politely said thank you and walked out.   No where on the menu, did it say I had to buy 2 tacos.

I drove a few blocks down to 3rd and Williams and had the  almost best taco ever.

The rules change depending on who’s ordering.
I will tell everyone not to spend their money here.

top_reviews.content:
My wife and I don't make it up to the City very often, but we drove up for a concert at Chase Center and needed a spot to eat and pass the time. We are so glad we skipped the usual stadium-adjacent crowds and walked a few blocks south into the Dogpatch to try Ungrafted.

From start to finish, the hospitality was top-notch. We arrived a bit early at 7:15 PM for our 7:30 PM reservation, and they sat us right away. The hostess was incredibly welcoming and highly knowledgeable. We had a few questions about the wine list, and she guided us through the selection with ease—she was so helpful and informative that we just had her take our entire order right there.

To start, my wife went with a Spanish rosé and I had a French Syrah, paired with their celery fries and garlic aioli. If you go, do not skip those fries—they were fantastic.

For the main course, my wife ordered the roasted chicken, which came served over creamy polenta and was beautifully covered with peas, onions, and fresh herbs. She absolutely loved it, pairing it with an Austrian Chardonnay that the kitchen recommended. I had the steak, which was cooked to absolute perfection.

We wrapped up the evening sharing the churros for dessert. They were excellent—subtle, perfectly sweet, and not overly heavy.
For a couple that doesn't get to San Francisco frequently, Ungrafted made us feel completely at home. Outstanding food, incredible wine expertise, and an unpretentious, warm neighborhood vibe. It was the perfect 3-hour haven while the kids were at their show. We will definitely be back the next time we venture up north!

A great neighborhood restaurant with top-quality food and custom wine pairings. We started with anchovies as an appetizer, which paired perfectly with a white wine from Croatia. The mushroom pate was incredibly tasty and unique. I wish they sold it to-go so I could try it with my wine collection (they don’t). Steak frites was cooked to perfection which paired well with a special wine from South Africa (Mullineux). Overall very happy to find a place where an outstanding custom wine pairing is offered. Definitely recommend to try out!!

Great time at Ungrafted last night! Me and my wife went for a date night, the staff were amazingly friendly and gave great wine paring recommendations. I loved the Cornish Hen! Sooo good! 😊 will definitely be going back

Glad we finally got the chance to come and enjoy the food, wine, and atmosphere of Ungrafted! Great wines selected by the sommeliers and very creative and delicious food. We didn't even intend to go entirely vegetarian, but so glad we did! Loved the mushroom parfait the most! Will definitely go back for this dish every time.

Great lunch spot! Met the owners--Chris and Rebecca who are master sommeliers and had such a variety of delicious wines! The lunch food was amazing as well--we got the celery fries (so crispy and flavorful), deviled eggs and steak tartare. Beautiful presentation and great taste--was a wonderful lunch spot!

reviews_snippets.content: "Great selection, friendly service, tasty food to go."
"We ordered the calamari, shishito peppers, cod catch of the day and beef cheeks."

name: Phở Yến Vietnamese Restaurant
address: 720 International Blvd, Oakland, CA 94606, United States

google.name: Phở Yến Vietnamese Restaurant
google.address: 720 International Blvd, Oakland, CA 94606, United States
google.description: Eatery offering Vietnamese soup & traditional noodle dishes in an informal atmosphere.

top_reviews.content: I randomly stumbled into this shop during an adventure last year, and I've already been back three times. It's the kind of place where you could close your eyes and blindly point at anything on the menu, and it'd still be amazing. You say the neighborhood's sketchy? Well, there are plenty of elderly Asian residents around, and the staff at the pastry shop and supermarket are all around 65. The fresh lemonade here is absolutely incredible—perfectly balanced between sweet and sour. It's so good that even the jackfruit smoothie and rice plates, delicious as they are, can't replicate the pinnacle of flavor this lemonade achieves in that moment. The owner and employees, unsurprisingly, are all elderly. Aside from the owner, who's cheerful and loves cracking jokes, the others may not be the talkative type, but they're all incredibly efficient. Their service is better than 90% of restaurants out there—fast, polite, and not a single one of them pulls the "respect your elders" card. You can tell the owner is a kind-hearted person with a tough exterior who genuinely works hard to run a good restaurant. As long as her younger brother is still studying at Laney, I'll keep coming back to eat.

They serve one of the best Vietnamese beef balls and all the intestines noodle soups in Oakland. However, it's a little on the pricy side. Parking is easy—many Seatings. Staffs are friendly too.
Updated on 9/18/23
The business is returning—many customers sit inside and outside during lunchtime. But the prices are also getting prohibitive high. Customers, be warned!

I was here yesterday with my wife, when I went to pay; I paid in cash. The owner of the restaurant took my order and when it was time to pay the bill came out to be $31.45. I gave her $100 bill and she gave me change only $8.55, $60 was missing and when I realized the mistake I went back to the payment counter and the owner refused to pay me back the missing amount. I asked her to check the cameras for evidence and she said she can’t. Even without checking the cameras that she should have access to she still said no. And then I asked, doesn’t she do check and balances at the end of the day to see if the tabs and the money in the register matches, she said no. I was thinking it’s only $60, why would the owner of the restaurant be so greedy against me. I have dined at this establishment ever since I was a child and to have this type of disrespect and dishonesty when given out the wrong change and not pay it back is heart wrenching. I will never return to Pho Hoa Lao.

The foods good. The spring roles are kind of hard and the sauce isn’t that good compared to other places. The regular sized noodles are pretty small, and it’s little bit on the pricy side. BUT, unfortunately it’s cash only for payment which doesn’t make sense in this day of age. Had to go to the local 7 eleven to get cash just to pay. Really disappointed. If you’re looking for good vietnamese food, recommend Ao Sen in Albany. Also FYI there is NO signs saying Only Cash. Just says “For cash- Thank you” really small on top of the cashier.

I tried the Number 1 Special combo at Phở Hòa Lão Vietnamese Restaurant, which includes a mix of ingredients like rare steak, well-done brisket, flank, tendon, tripe, and spring rolls. The pho was satisfying but not exceptional. It's a good spot to curb your pho craving. The standout was their fresh and generously portioned spring rolls, accompanied by tasty peanut sauce.

*Keep in mind, this place is cash only.

top_reviews.content: Incredibly huge portions at an extremely competitive price point! This whole container cost me maybe $14. You don’t see prices like these in SF often, especially close to FiDi where most restaurants charge an $25+ for a weekday office lunch. It’s takeout only since it’s a small counter space. The couple running this restaurant is so sweet and warm. There will definitely be a line during lunch rush, but they are fast and diligent so the wait goes by quick. I really enjoyed my chicken curry also. The carrot was so sweet and flavorful. Office lunches are a little less bleak with Yo Yo’s around.

Great place for counter service. Very friendly couple (I assume), delicious, no frills, affordable. Twelve dollar chicken curry plate with a marinated egg, potato, carrot and rice. Six piece sushi was surprisingly fresh for three dollars. Out the door total 15.25, cash or Venmo.

Our new favorite SF spot! Unbelievably delicious.  We had the beef curry and udon.  The couple who own the restaurant were so friendly and helpful.  I cannot believe we paid so little for so much savory food!  You can walk a quick block and sit in the nearby park.  We will definitely come to Yo Yo's when in town!

One of the few places that make you feel like you are eating lunch at your mum’s! The owners are extremely kind and they treat each customer so uniquely nice! Food amazing and v affordable so glad a place like this exists in sf thank you 🥰

The most amazing place to get lunch in the embarcadero area. Such amazing vegetarian options, and everything tastes so fresh. The portion was double what you see in the picture but it was so delicious that I only remembered to take one halfway through!

top_reviews.content: I always get a good meal and the staff is awesome. I recommend anything on the menu. I’ve had 85% of the dishes. Some of my favorites include the burritos, the fajita quesadilla, tortilla soup, and possibly one of THE most beautiful taco salads I’ve ever eaten. Another menu item to try is the Horchata iced coffee SO GOOD. Whether you’re dining in or taking food to go both options great. Last recommendation hit up the salsa bar the roasted tomato salsa as well as the green salsa are INCREDIBLE. Little Chihuahua is a GEM

Fresh, vibrant, very California-style Mexican food where you can really taste the quality of the ingredients.

The tostada salad is one of my favorites in the city, I get it often. It’s loaded and the dressing has the perfect spicy kick. The salsa bar is fresh, flavorful, huge plus. Also, I always judge a place by its rice and this one delivers. It’s so good I’ve ordered it on its own.

Definitely a spot worth coming back to.
We visited this place in the evening for a light snack and tried their tacos—twice! They were amazing. I’m sure the rest of their menu is just as good.
Excellent service. The food is delicious. The price is just right. I wouldn’t change anything about the restaurant.

Wonderful little Mexican casual bistro, spotlessly clean and airy, bright and cheerful. The best shrimp burrito I've ever had, so the menu definitely needs further exploration. Excellent for solo dining, takeout, or groups. Service is very quick, friendly, and efficient. A great find in this area.

top_reviews.content:
The best restaurant I’ve eaten at in San Francisco.
Sure, it’s on the pricier side, but it’s a top-notch restaurant where you’ll get more than your money’s worth.
Compared to typical prices at American dinner restaurants, it’s about average.

Even so, it offers the best value for money—it’s on par with Michelin-starred restaurants.
It actually makes you wonder why this place hasn’t received a Michelin star.
The owner is truly passionate about the ingredients. And all the staff are friendly.
Be sure to let Kate guide you through your meal with her detailed explanations of the dishes.
It’ll leave you with wonderful memories of San Francisco.

If you’ve come to San Francisco and haven’t experienced this restaurant, you haven’t truly enjoyed the city.

If you’re looking for special memories of San Francisco and an authentic Japanese restaurant, I highly recommend visiting this place.
Reservations are required.

I’ve lived in SF for 10+ years and this was the best meal I’ve ever had. Eric and his team outdid themselves. The hospitality was 11/10. The creativity and thoughtfulness added to each dish made all the difference and puts them in a new category for Japanese cuisine. Kabuto is the definition of a magical hole in the wall experience. Nestled in the heart of the Inner Richmond right on Geary, it already embodies everything a local is. If you’re a foodie this should be top on your list of must visit SF.

My girlfriend and I recently had dinner at Kabuto on Geary Street, and it was hands down one of the best dining experiences we've had in the city. We opted for the omakase, and the entire progression of the meal was absolutely amazing.
A huge shoutout to our main chef, Eric, who made the night incredibly special. His attention to detail, pacing, and passion for the craft really shone through in every bite. We were completely blown away by the creative flavor profiles and quality of the fish. A few absolute standouts: the Hamachi pear was brilliantly refreshing, the Escolar chip provided the perfect textural crunch, and the Wagyu gyoza was incredibly rich, buttery, and melted right in our mouths.
If you are looking for an intimate, top-tier sushi experience with a welcoming and personal touch, you have to visit Kabuto. Sit at the counter, say hi to Chef Eric, and his amazing wife and hostess, Sun and let them take care of you!

I visited this location with my friend after a local’s recommendation to try this restaurant had a Japanese owner. We decided to do the 8 course omakase since we wanted to try their seasonal dishes. The sashimi and nigiri were very fresh and paired nicely with the garnish. Every dish was very good. The service was very welcoming and accommodated us very well. Only note was that the sake we chose was a good palate cleanser for each dish but did not pair well with the food. It might had been better if we chose a different one. I will definitely come back to this location.

The fish was incredibly fresh, and every dish felt thoughtfully crafted. I loved the Japanese-French fusion. it was creative without losing the essence of Japanese cuisine.
Definitely worth a visit if you’re looking for something a little different!

top_reviews.content: Tastes Steam Kitchen is a good place to share a meal with a group. The shabu shabu has many options for the base broth and also the items you can cook.

Highly Recommended Hot Pot Spot – Fresh, Flavorful, and Fantastic Value!
I recently visited this hot pot restaurant and it quickly became one of my new favorites in the area. From the moment we walked in, the experience was outstanding.
The ingredients are incredibly fresh — the thinly sliced meats, vibrant vegetables, and seafood all looked and tasted top-quality, with no signs of staleness. You can really tell they source high-quality items and prepare everything daily.
The broths and flavors are delicious! Whether you prefer a rich, spicy Sichuan-style pot or a milder, savory one, the soups are perfectly balanced and packed with depth. The dipping sauces are customizable and addictive — we couldn’t stop dipping and refilling our bowls. Everything was so tasty that we kept ordering more rounds.
Hygiene is clearly a priority here. The tables, utensils, and hot pot stations were spotlessly clean, and the staff maintained excellent cleanliness throughout our meal. It felt safe and comfortable, especially for sharing a hot pot experience.
The service was excellent — attentive, friendly, and efficient. Our server was knowledgeable about the menu, helped with recommendations, and made sure our broth stayed at the right temperature and our plates were cleared promptly. The whole team made us feel welcome and well taken care of.
Best of all, the prices are very reasonable for the quality and portion sizes you get. It’s genuinely good value — you leave satisfied without breaking the bank, making it perfect for casual dinners, family gatherings, or group outings.
Overall, if you’re craving authentic and satisfying hot pot, this place delivers on every level: freshness, taste, cleanliness, service, and affordability. We’ll definitely be back soon!

I pass by this place a lot during my lunch walks and finally decided to give it a try. They offer lunch special mini hotpots, and each pot comes with a free drink, a choice of green tea or black tea.

I was seated quickly, and the server took my order right away. The service was friendly and welcoming. Since I knew what I wanted and only had an hour for lunch, I placed my order immediately, knowing it might take some time to prepare.

I had the Szechuan Spicy Pot, which came with beef, fish filet, enoki, tofu, clam, shrimp, cabbage, glass noodles, fish ball, corn, pork blood, and squid balls, and a choice of rice or noodles. The portion-wise was good, and had lots of different ingredients. But the flavor was lacking; Szechuan flavor should have the bold, numbing, and tingling sensation, but I didn't find any from this pot.

My sister got the Satay Beef Pot; the flavor was spot on. So if you are craving spicy, I would not recommend getting their Szechuan Spicy Pot.
A fun and delicious experience to share with friends.  Strongly recommended if you want to chill and hangout with good food.

It's a new find for me. Evidently, this form of steam kitchen format is very popular new form of restaurants in China. The menu is huge. We did not go for the all-you-can-eat hot pot. Instead we went for the steamed pot. The staff did all the cooking in front of our table, making sure all the lovely fresh seafood is cooked to perfection.  While some dishes come with special tasty sauces, most vegetables are steamed plainly and we go to the buffet of sauces to make our own concoction of sauce dips.

All the seafood we tried, dungeness crab, razor clams, giant clams, scallops and fish were all super fresh and wonderful.

Service was good. Only complaint was when we made reservations, we were allowed only choice of either 5:00 or 7:30.

top_reviews.content:
What I ordered:
Khao Soi Gai
Guay Tiew Kua Poo
Fried mushroom

The first bite immediately made me understand the hype! Everything was so good I could literally cry. Every dish was executed perfectly, and surprisingly, my favorite was the fried mushroom, definitely a must-try! The khao soi had a very creamy coconut base with amazing flavor and a generous portion of chicken. The soup was rich, comforting, and full of depth. The guay tiew kua poo (fried crab noodles), which was a Saturday special, was super delicious, not greasy at all, packed with crab meat, and came in a huge portion! They have a waitlist but we didn't wait too long, and as a Japanese-Thai fusion restaurant, they also have plenty of ramen dishes that I would love to try, so I saved it for next time! Overall, great restaurant, I’m so happy with this meal! 🥹

Like it; can't love it.

For the long wait and the eventually seating, and the interesting beer choices, and the decent vegetarian choices, I had high hopes. The intimate seating made me think of the day when this will be a Jiro Dreams of crispy okra rice documentary.

But this isn't it. The flavors don't add up. They either ride solo or flop hard. The crispy okra rice was average at best. The ramen was mediocre, and this is hard love is only because we live in an area where ramens are spewed from the mouths of angels in amazing restaurants. The pad thai could have been classified as a dessert. It was only sweet. The other flavors had bone spurs and sat out the war. Only the corn tempura saved the day.

I love everything about this place. And I'd say it's a perfect date night spot. But make sure you have instant ramen at home for later.

This is a little gem. It combines the best of Japanese and Thai cuisines. I tried spring rolls, which were more like spring makis with delicious basil sauce, and fried seafood udon. I added that basil sauce on top and it enhanced it. It is a very busy, small place, very cute and with Japanese charm. Definitely worth trying when in the neighborhood.

I’m a regular here as of the last two and a half years and this is my favorite place to eat. I’m surprised Nute’s hasn’t been featured on/in EATER SF! Small cozy environment and the food is incredible. Anything you order on the menu is going to impress. Yes, there can be a little bit of a wait at times but it is well worth it and the food comes quick once you are seated. I especially love the Tebiaski chicken wings (best chicken wings I’ve ever had) and the Drunken Noodles are the perfect balance of sweet and savory. Award winning food in my opinion!

I had the Chicken Khao Soi at Nute’s, and it was fantastic. The broth had just the right consistency—not too thick or too watery—making it perfectly balanced. It had a mild spiciness that kept it from being too rich, which I really enjoyed. I also ordered the Spicy Miso Ramen and Okra, and everything was delicious. Despite the restaurant being very busy, the staff remained polite and attentive. I went on a Friday at 6 PM, and the line was quite long, so I recommend visiting during off-peak hours for a shorter wait. I would definitely return when I get the chance!

top_reviews.content:
I did a side-by-side comparison of L&G vs.
Saigon. I tested an iced Vietnamese coffee and pork banh mi. I compares the price, flavor and service. L&G won in my opinion. They accept credit cards (with a fee) so it's a convenience vs. price factor. For coffee, L&G iced coffee is much stronger with much less dairy. For banh mi, the bread here is smaller for a better bread/meat ratio. There are more fresh veggies. The taste of the pork is sweeter and not overpowering, plus more mayo on the sandwich. I have other favorites in the city, but if I was in the area I'd choose L&G

I'm pretty biased since I live on the block, but this is my go-to when I'm wanted something cheap and delicious. Their prices are extremely wallet friendly, and their meat portions in the banh mi sandwiches are also very generous. I come here almost once a week simply because I can't find anything else for this price to quality ratio.

Tip: I recommend bringing cash as you do save a bit
L&G Vietnamese Sandwich was a great find. The bánh mì was fresh, packed with flavor, and the bread had the perfect crunch. Fast service, reasonable prices, and I’d definitely stop by again

Coming from SoCal up to SF, this was one of the best Banh Mi sandwiches I’ve had in a long time! It’s a small hole in the wall so it is limited seating, but it’s just perfection in every sense, great price point at only $6 a sandwich, and loaded with meat and veggies inside. Everything is so fresh and the bread is incredibly crisp yet soft. Can’t wait to come again!
Exceeds the price point. Honest hard working people. Be patient, it’s worth the wait. As good as a bahn mi gets.

10/10 place. The restaurant was pretty empty though. No idea why. If you're in SF, this place is a must visit for good meals.
The tilapia curry reminded me of home. The food was delicious although a bit more oily than preferred.

Recommend! Fantastic, very reasonably priced food. Friendly and helpful staff. Our party had an app and 4 different mains with naan- everything was delicious. My only regret is  not saving room to try a desert.
It doesn't look like much on the outside but inside it is quite nice. Nothing fancy but kind of cozy. The food was great, prices were reasonable, and the service was friendly. The naan was delicious.

I was in the area and needed a quick grab-and-go lunch, so I decided to give this place a try. I ordered the Bulgogi Sandwich, which was the first item listed on the menu.

The sandwich had a good amount of carrots and fresh vegetables, but unfortunately the marinated beef and sauce made the bread very soggy. It became quite messy to eat, with the dressing dripping everywhere. Even though I was very hungry, I couldn’t finish the sandwich because the bread had become completely soaked by the end, and my hands were covered in sauce.

Overall, it just wasn’t an enjoyable eating experience for me. I’m glad I gave it a try, but one visit was enough, and I’m not sure I’ll be back.

Really clean large area to hangout. Bathrooms were a bit of a mess.

Visually, everything was stunning. I ordered the mangonada with boba, a Thai tea with boba, and a mango tea with boba. I ordered the loaded fries with chicken and the tteokboki for snacks. The loaded fries were so good! Loved every bite from the kimchi to the green sauce drizzled on top. The tteokbokki was terrible, hence the 3 star rating.

It was so salty and the sauce had an awful taste, like over processed and extremely salty. It had these black flecks, which I wish I took a picture to demonstrate. The fried chicken bites on top were great, but the bits that touched the sauce were not so good. I had tteokbokki before—from the instant to freshly made—and this was the worst I’ve ever tasted. I couldn’t even eat it. It felt like $12 wasted.
The "Dirty Stuf" has got to be one of my favorite cookies & cream shakes. You can really taste the oreos in it.

top_reviews.content:
I had to go into work on a day where no one else was in the office and I had been wanting to try OUAD forever. It was so freakin good!! I love anything South Indian and while you can certainly get it for dinner, its not easy to find a place where you can eat it for lunch as well, at least in my experience.

The packaging is perfect for carry out with a very interesting design that keeps it all warm and separated. The dosa I got was just the regular but I added the paneer burji on the side and add the podi. The dosa itself was crispy on the outside, soft on the inside, the sambar was on point and the chutneys were also delicious. I'm getting hungry just thinking about it again!

Ordered a masala dosa from DoorDash and the dosa came in a cool and colorful box. The coolest dosa packaging I have seen so far, haha. The pockets for chutneys and sambar was great too, the sambar had gotten a little split by the time it reached me, but that’s understandable. The dosa was delicious!!

Fantastic experience at Once Upon a Dosa! I’ll break my review down into a few simple categories.

Food: very very tasty chicken keema dosa! Chai was also very nice and piping hot as it should be on a chilly day.

Service: top notch service. Friend ordered the OG roast Dosa and didn’t realize it came with no potatoes. Upon simple explanation, and at no extra charge, they gave us a serving of potatoes for his dosa to upgrade it since we had a misunderstanding.

Price: pricey by my southern standards but for SF, not bad at all especially considering the portions. Plus the drinks were not expensive at all which was icing on the cake.

Would 100% recommend for a very tasty quick bite, and excellent friendly service!

I’m one and done for visits to this spot! The dosa was mid - not crispy, not spicy (even though I paid for the add-ons), and the sambar felt old. I love supporting small businesses but at $15 per entree, they’ve got to do better.
South Indian dishes were flavorful and freshly prepared, though the masala chai was disappointing. Overall, a satisfying meal with authentic taste.

This spot serves excellent, authentic Vietnamese food that hits the mark if you are looking for genuine flavors.

The clay pot catfish is a standout, perfectly balancing sweet and savory notes. For something comforting, the hot and sour catfish soup is warm, deeply soothing, and packed with bold flavor. The shrimp and cabbage salad offers a sharp, refreshing contrast to the richer dishes.

I was looking for a quiet place to spend an hour before an appointment and this place was just the calm oasis I needed.  Glad i came.  They did a good job, and were very pleasant/ welcoming. 10/21/2025*
We went for lunch to celebrate a coworker's birthday.

This time I ordered their Special vermicelli, which comes with shrimps, beef, chicken, imperial rolls, lettuce, mint leaves, cucumber, bean sprouts, pickled carrot,  topped with green onion and peanut, and served with fish sauce.

It tasted really good and was loaded with fresh greens. The vermicelli had a great texture as well. Sometimes fish sauce can be too strong for me, but theirs tasted great; it did not have a strong, funky smell, which was a big plus for me. Their Thai tea was excellent. I prefer drinks that aren't too sweet, and they nailed the sweetness level. On top of that, the portion was really generous!

1/8/2025

The standout for me was definitely the imperial roll, it was delicious! The chicken and beef, while well-seasoned, had similar flavors and were a bit too salty for my taste. The shrimp was overcooked and quite dry. Despite this, I really enjoyed the experience of having a plate with a variety of dishes. It was a fun way to try a little bit of everything.

8/8/2024

This was an absolutely fantastic restaurant! We loved the outside seating area. We had a group dinner here and the tagliatelle bolognese was amazing, thank you so much for such delicious food.

This was easily the best meal I had on my entire trip. Service was also good. Would highly recommend!

Outstanding Italian food with generous portions and fresh, delicious flavors. It’s a very cool space tucked away in a courtyard which lends an intimate atmosphere. Fantastic wine options - the team really knows what they’re doing when it comes to wine! And don’t skip the chocolate oblivion cake, it absolutely lives up to its name.

The service was not as good as I have had previous times there - they didn’t put in one diner’s order - but the food is good and I love the atmosphere. Feels a bit like you have traveled to Italy. We were bummed because we had been lured in by an email advertising a promotional pasta and wine pairing for the month of September but it turned out to not be happening for some reason. I really liked the milkshake that came with the sfingi (doughnuts) and the polenta fries were tasty. The risotto could have used some pepper and it was perhaps a little too past peak stone fruit season for the peaches in the summer salad.

What a lucky find! My sister and I stopped in for a spontaneous lunch and were so pleasantly surprised! The eggplant parmigiana was so good, and she enjoyed the  kale salad with grilled shrimp. Tucked away in a little courtyard off of Sacramento Street—you won’t be disappointed.

I had only eaten at Sociale one previous time, sitting at their little two person bar a few years ago and had always wanted to return. I cannot fathom why I have not been back until this evening. What an exceptional night!  The pillowy little rolls with delicious butter, cream of mushroom soup, a rockshrimp pasta that was not my favorite, but I could appreciate the flavors, and then a fall off the bone short rib with turnip “risotto”.  Creative food, but still comforting and delicious.. Finished with an affogato, and throughout the meal, multiple glasses of wonderfully recommended wine. But most importantly, the service was truly exceptional. The servers, the runners, every single person treated me as though I was a regular, even though this is only my second time here. Beautiful food and beautiful people.

In a city full of flash and fusion, Umi is a masterclass in substance. This is where you go when you want to bypass the hype and get straight to the heart of what makes sushi an art form: impeccable fish quality and the quiet, focused skill of a chef who knows exactly what they are doing.
The atmosphere is authentically cozy and unpretentious, serving as the perfect backdrop for a meal where the ingredients speak for themselves.
• Exceptional Fish Quality: The focus here is strictly on quality-controlled, sustainably sourced fish, with the Hawaiian tuna frequently cited as a standout for its freshness and flavor.
• Chef’s Precision: Eschewing "glamorous" distraction, the sushi chefs demonstrate expert technique in every nigiri and sashimi cut, ensuring a perfect balance of texture and taste.
• Authentic Details: Small but vital touches, like the inclusion of real wasabi, elevate the experience and highlight the restaurant's commitment to traditional excellence.
• Welcoming Environment: Beyond the food, the staff is known for being incredibly sweet and accommodating, making the intimate space feel like a hidden neighborhood gem.

Growing up in a seaside town, I absolutely love Korean seafood dishes. However, I know that if not properly prepared, some Korean food might taste unusual to others. That’s why I’ve always hesitated to suggest the Korean marinated crab dish to my American friends. But then, I found JJamPPong, and wow, what a game-changer! My first visit there with my Korean coworkers was with zero expectations, and we were blown away by the authentic and flavorful crab marination. Today, I made my third trip to JJamPPong, driving 30 minutes just to get there, and it was totally worth it. The crab is incredibly fresh, perfectly prepared with a fragrant ginger hot sauce that is simply divine. I can’t recommend it enough for anyone who’s heard about the famous Korean marinated crab but is unsure where to find a truly worthy version. You have to try it!

We celebrated our 20th wedding anniversary at Jakson Filmore on June 10th, and it was nothing short of magical — just as it has been every special occasion we've shared here over the past two decades.

This restaurant holds a rare and irreplaceable place in our hearts. When my husband and I first discovered it, we were living in San Francisco, and it instantly transported us back to our honeymoon in Italy — the quality of the food, the warmth of the atmosphere, the charm that feels both intentional and completely effortless. That feeling has never faded.

Over the years, we've come to know some of the long-time servers who greet us like family every time we walk through the door. That continuity — that sense of being remembered and welcomed — is something you simply can't manufacture, and it means everything.

But this visit gave us something truly unexpected: the privilege of meeting Jack, the owner, who sat with us and shared stories from his remarkable life — his adventures, his philosophy, his deep and genuine passion for food. We even found ourselves getting an impromptu lesson in Daoism. We left the bar seating full in every sense of the word: well fed, inspired, and deeply grateful.

Thank you, Jakson Filmore, for twenty years of beautiful memories and for making our milestone feel so personal and so meaningful. Here's to many more.

The joint is small, unassuming, the kind of neighborhood outpost you stumble into when the city has chewed you up and you need something solid, something honest. And the pizza—by God, the pizza—stood tall. No flop, no soggy compromise. A crust with backbone, the kind Dave Portnoy would tip his cap to and call righteous.

It’s not the sort of cathedral of cuisine people pilgrimage across town to see. No, this is a bunker, a foxhole of melted cheese and red sauce. The prices sting, but that’s San Francisco—the city taxes your wallet with one hand and feeds your soul with the other.

On the wall: a convenience-store lineup of snacks, as if you might need a bag of chips or a pack of candy to soften the landing after the pie. Overhead, The Simpsons run in endless loop, Homer and Bart like patron saints of this strange corner eatery.

In the end, the arithmetic is simple. The place delivers where it counts: the pizza is good, and when the last bite is gone you’re already thinking about the next. That, in this city of smoke and mirrors, is victory enough.

I was in the mood for some BBQ and had been wanting to try Roderick's for a while, and the stars finally aligned to try them out.

I drive by here all the time, and I know this place is small and not really dine-in friendly, so I ordered online to go. Honey ordered the rib plate with yams and baked beans. I ordered the rib and link plate with mac and cheese and potato salad.
The online order (DoorDash) status said it would be 25 to 35 minutes before we could pick up our food. Coming from Hayward, that was perfect timing.

When I arrived, there was a small line. "Unc" was in the back making plates, and the young lady up front seemed a little overwhelmed, but she was doing her best. Unc came from the back with our plates and asked for the online purchase verification. I thanked him, he told me to have a good day, and I went on my way.

The food was good, pricey but good. We spent 66 dollars on the two plates ordering DoorDash.

Honey is from Texas, so she’s not a big fan of pre-sauced meat; she says it hides the true quality of the meat. The online order form doesn't let you put the sauce on the side. However, the ribs were tender, peeled off the bone easily, and were seasoned just right. The link was great; I don’t think you’ll find that kind of link in a grocery store.

The mac and cheese has a hint of garlic in it, which was surprising in a good way. The yams had the right amount of sweetness to them, not too sugary or overpowered by cinnamon and nutmeg. The beans were good too, just standard baked beans without extras. The potato salad was different; the cut of the potatoes was unique and not too soft. It was good, just not what I’m used to, so I don't think I would order that again.

Overall, Roderick’s is good BBQ. I would come back, I also want to try their fried cat fish.

name: Norcina
address: 3251 Pierce St, San Francisco, CA 94123, United States

google.name: Norcina

top_reviews.content:
An Intimate and Warm Neighborhood Setting
Finding a dining spot that successfully balances a high-end culinary experience with a truly welcoming environment can be tough, but this location gets it exactly right. The space is incredibly romantic and cozy, making it an ideal destination for a memorable date night or a relaxed evening catching up over a great meal. The interior design utilizes warm lighting, thoughtful seating arrangements, and an inviting layout that makes you want to linger at your table long after the meal is finished. It has a distinct charm that feels deeply personal, avoiding the cold, corporate vibe of many contemporary restaurants and instantly putting you at ease the moment you step through the door.

Authentic Italian Flavors and Masterful Execution
The kitchen team shows a clear respect for traditional cooking techniques, delivering a menu that feels genuinely grounded in regional heritage.

Elite Food Quality: The food was great and tasted very authentic, hitting all the right notes in terms of rich flavor profiles, freshness, and presentation.

Exceptional Pastas and Entrees: From the perfectly al dente textures of the pasta to the carefully balanced sauces, every element of the meal felt intentional and expertly prepared. You can easily tell that the kitchen relies on premium ingredients, resulting in clean, vibrant flavors that stand out.

Satisfying Balance: The menu offers an excellent mix of classic comfort dishes and refined specialties, ensuring there is something to capture your interest regardless of what you are in the mood for.

Creative Beverage Programs and Standout Highlights
Beyond the traditional food offerings, the curated beverage menu brings a highly engaging and interactive element to the dinner.

Unique Tasting Options: A major highlight of the night was the drink selection, as they had some interesting drink flights too. Being able to sample a curated variety of profiles side-by-side added a fantastic layer of discovery to the evening.

Perfect Pairings: The flights were thoughtfully organized, allowing us to see how different notes complemented the rich, savory elements of the entrees.

Attentive Service: The staff did a wonderful job of walking us through the selections, sharing helpful details about the backgrounds of the pours without ever sounding rehearsed or overly formal.

Final Thoughts and Recap
Overall, this dinner was an absolute highlight, and we enjoyed it all from the minute we sat down to the final course. It is rare to find a place where the romantic, cozy ambiance is matched so perfectly by the quality coming out of the kitchen. The realization that the food was great and tasted very authentic makes it an easy recommendation for anyone who appreciates genuine Italian cooking, while the addition of the interesting drink flights kept the night feeling unique and fun. I highly recommend checking this spot out if you are looking for an upscale yet incredibly comfortable dining experience in the city.

The pizza was a classic Italian style. The pasta was full of flavor! Brussels were top top! And the beat salad was amazing, I don’t like beets…. But you couldn’t taste them at all! Norcina is the kind of unassuming italian restaurant that reminds one of why you love SF in the first place; big enough to have a small party, but small enough to feel like a cozy nook, lively on most days, but ocassionally calm and homey. The food is anything but homey tho, deliciously consistent pizzas that balance traditional flavors with touches of creative additions, perfect sauce to cheese ratio, over roasted european style crust and tasteful drink selections. I love places like Norcina because their the kind you can keep coming back to for your favorite or mix it up with endless variations without ever overspending. It's hard to strike the balance of value, quality and mouth-watering deliciousness like this, but Norcina just does. One of my faves in SF, highly recommend.

top_reviews.content:
Street Taco is a 10 minutes walk from Chase Center if you cut through the open plaza. I would avoid this area if there is a home game. They make an OK taco salad $14.45 (called street bowl.) Right when you walk in, there's a trompo (vertical rotisserie.) That made me pick al pastor as the meat option. When the salad arrived, I was disappointed it didn't come with pico de gallo. I asked the cashier for some pico and it was free. The al pastor tasted OK. It was missing that smoky flavor and missing the caramelized edges if cooked on a trompo. Toward the bottom of the salad, it got soggy and that diluted the taste.

Service was fine for an order at the cashier type of restaurant. I was the only customer at 7pm. Tables were extra clean. Good job everyone at Street Taco.

I tried this restaurant while visiting a friend nearby. The restaurant itself is beautiful and the service is solid. I tried the Carne Asada Super Burrito. The food was very underwhelming (below average). The carne asada was very low quality. Overcooked, chewy.

Honestly, I am okay eating low quality meat (common at some taquerias), but the meat needs to be cut smaller if you are using low quality cuts of beef. Large carne asada cuts (like at Tacko) are okay only if you use high quality beef cuts.

The burrito proportions are also not ideal. You can see from the attached photo, lots of rice, little to no beans, meat or salsa. The burrito was almost entirely tortilla, rice and lettuce. Maybe the worker made a mistake. By accident or design, the burrito ingredient proportions were incorrect.

The super burrito was $17.50 (I think) and had a surcharge of $1 for beef. I honestly don’t mind paying this for a good burrito (like many other SF taquerias: La Taqueria, El Farolito, Tacko), but the burrito quality here is below average. I can’t justify the price.

Some dishes here may be better (I haven’t tried other dishes), but I will say the carne asada and the burritos here are below the SF average.

There are a lot of good Mexican restaurants in the SF Bay Area and this one is currently is falling short of average.

Great Mexico City street food - tacos, burritos, quesadillas, nachos. Fresh ingredients and quick service.

While nicely decorated, the space doesn’t feel particularly Mexican and can be quite loud, particularly as the staff starts shouting out order numbers.

I wanted to not like this place because of how it's marketed but honestly it won me over. These al pastor tacos would not be out of place in Mexico City, which is saying a lot.

Edit: wow, the second time I ate here was MUCH worse.

The good: the al pastor meat is good, straight off the trompo. The salsa is good. The chips themselves are just OK, not bad, not great.

The bad: pretty much everything else. For 2 tacos, chips and guac and a mineral water, it was $30. I get it, it's SF, but I expect better quality food. In particular the guacamole was horrific -- watery and unseasoned! and the tortillas weren't great either. As mentioned earlier the chips are ok but not great. Also for some reason they give a lemon instead of a lime for your taco.

top_reviews.content:
Truly excellent Açaí bowls and smoothie-type creations, with natural base ingredients that are delicious and feel great in tummy, with LOTS of flavor variation options and excellent fresh toppings — the produce is first rate and the sweet/crunchy/powdery add-ons first rate too.

This is a must have for Açaí/smoothie enthusiasts, curious novices and imho anything in between.  Service is friendly, but as quality is not always instant gratification, prepare for a 5 to 10 minute prep time — but SO worth it!

First time trying this out after  hearing about and how delicious the bowls and smoothies are. I ordered the Bay Berry with gluten free granola. Small was a perfect size snack!  Only a 15 minute wait, definitely recommend ordering ahead on the QR code or app! Please give them some Air-conditioning it was a little warm inside for the Awesome staff preparing the orders.

I’d come back! My favorite parts of my bowl were probably the blackberry ube flavor, blue chia layer, and select toppings (fruit, flaxseed, chia, cacao nibs). The mango flavor tasted just like mango sorbet. In fact I started wondering how close it is to actually being sorbet... I’m sure there’s a lot of sugar in it and I started to think about how healthy it actually is. I appreciated that when assembling your own bowl at the kiosk, you can select a box that says you have a nut allergy. It’s nice that you can put so many toppings on! I’d go back to test my hypothesis that if you ask for a dome lid you get more toppings because they can pile it higher in the cup.
This location has very small insides though there are a couple of benches inside and one outside. I went around 1pm on a Monday and it was very busy though thankfully I didn’t have to wait in a line.

as a huge fan of smoothies bowls , i highly recommend this place. from the base itself to the wide choice of hyper quality homemade superfood toppings nothing disappointed me. an energy bomb that makes your mind and body feel like heaven :)  massive thanks to the lovely staff as well.

I’m a regular here and I want to keep coming! The taste, quality and variety can be amazing and all the employees seem hard working! I always get the “make your own bowl” and a smoothie (“just açaí” or the avocado one).
The problem is that about 50% of the time I get an order where items are missing. Often the nut butter and at least one topping is missing (today I got a bowl with two toppings missing and no nut butter). Usually getting the actual menu items is much safer than “make your own” but last time I got the “just açaí” smoothie it tasted very different than all the previous times.
Overall good, just seems like you need to be very flexible regarding getting all the ingredients you order. I wish there was a way to make sure the nut butter is there because the added protein with almond butter is why I choose palmetto over other smoothie spots and it’s a bummer when one of the major components is just not there.

top_reviews.content: Our waiter was friendly and helpful. I honestly don’t even know where to begin. From start to finish, it was the most mind-blowing experience I’ve ever had.

We met this beautiful, joyful woman named Luka, who was so kind. She sat us down at the bar, where we enjoyed some lovely drinks. They also gave us happy hour oysters, which were, of course, delicious.

Then we were seated at our table, where we got to meet the whole team. Each person individually welcomed us and attended to all our needs. Even the head chef came out personally, greeted us, and offered us items from the menu as a gesture of kindness—which, honestly, I don’t feel we even deserved.

The food was absolutely amazing. Everything was so delicious, and the flavors never clashed. I truly don’t have a single bad word to say. I can’t wait for them to receive their first Michelin star—they all deserve it.

I will definitely be coming back. Thank you to all the wonderful people for the hard work they put in—not just in bringing the food out quickly, but in doing so with love and care.

Thank you again.

Had a fantastic solo dinner that I won't forget anytime soon. The vibe is relaxing and welcoming, the service is good, and the food was fantastic. The stuffed squash blossoms with anchovies and duck garganelli were both amazing!

Sorella in San Francisco gets a solid 4 out of 5 from me. The atmosphere is really nice and makes it a comfortable place for a meal. The food was decent overall rather than mind blowing, but there were a couple of standouts. The gnocchi was my favorite and the carne tartare was also really well done. The lasagna, on the other hand, felt a little weak compared to the other dishes. Service was ok and the prices are decent for the city. Overall, it is a good spot with a few highlights and worth trying.

I went to Sorella with friends, and it was an amazing experience from start to finish. Jason was our waiter, and he was incredibly pleasant, attentive, and helpful throughout the evening.

The restaurant itself is absolutely gorgeous, and the food was exceptional. The focaccia, calamari, Caesar salad, strangulet, New York steak, and tiramisu were the highlights of the night. Everything was beautifully prepared, perfectly cooked, and full of flavor.

Chef Fernanda is incredibly talented and was also so warm and pleasant. You can truly taste the care and passion behind every dish.

I highly recommend Sorella and sincerely hope they receive a Michelin star soon — they absolutely deserve it!

My girlfriend and I had dinner at La Connessa last Tuesday, and we were blown away by the beautiful ambiance, quality of the food, and incredible service.

Juan, our bartender, welcomed us warmly and made the entire evening special. After learning that I’m a mezcal fan, he recommended an amazing variation of a Last Word made with mezcal and a touch of spice. It was easily one of the best cocktails I’ve ever had!

We trusted Juan’s food recommendations as well, and he guided us perfectly. We started with the salmon crudo with stone fruit, followed by an incredibly creamy burrata with organic tomatoes, basil, and olio nuovo. Then came the sweet summer corn caramelle - and it was even better than we could have imagined. They kindly split it for us, and we almost licked the plates clean!

We finished our dinner with the perfectly cooked flat iron steak, followed by tiramisu and refreshing mango sorbet topped with candied citrus.

Everything was delicious, but Juan’s hospitality truly made the experience unforgettable. He guided us through the evening better than anyone before. We will definitely be back!

5/5—highly recommended!

This was such a cute place! The service was great, and the food was delicious! We got a margherita pizza for the table, which was amazing and finished very quickly. We also got fried brussel sprouts to share, and the seasoning and flavor of them was beyond what we expected. The olives still had their pits and were a fun experiment to eat as a team lol. The special for the day was a risotto with truffles, various mushrooms, shallots, and more - I got that along with chicken, and it was easily one of the best risottos I’ve ever had! We also got one of each dessert to share as a table, and the hazelnut gelato was a favorite as well as the cream covered pastry. Had such a great time here!

So it's unusual for me not to know a culinary experience since for more than a quarter of a century 5 Star Restaurant all over San Francisco but this was a very rare treat and I am thankful to my son and his girlfriend for recommending and suggesting this place to celebrate what they like to refer to as my birthday. I am usually treated like VIP and given the red carpet treatment given the positions I've held over the last 30 plus years but I have to say that Rudy just went over and above to make sure that we had a very special and very memorable experience here at La Connesa everything was top notch but especially the young man (Rudy) who made us feel like royalty. I cannot wait to come back and bring as many friends as can have a month's worth of fun and the delight at their culinary experts.

I was excited to check this place out last week with a friend and when we arrived, we got sat instantly at the bar. The bartender took care of us wonderfully. I had the squid ink pasta for $37, but it had a strange sour taste that I can’t put my finger on. The noodles were super thin, house-made but way too past the al dente point. I also hadn’t had that style of pasta before.

The sparkling rose wine was memorable, the arancini oozed a smooth cheese, but the pears in the arugula salad were rock hard, a little detail that didn’t go unnoticed especially if the salad is titled with the word pear. You can make a better one at home. 🙂

I paid over $100 for my meal alone and that included a very cakey multi-layered tiramisu, also a slight disappointment. Who is designing these “creative” takes on dishes that don’t quite land? I didn’t feel the food was worth the price and the overall experience left me a little wanting. On the other hand, the design of the space is absolutely gorgeous during golden hour. I would stick to perhaps more tried and true conventional Italian options next time but am hesitant to go back. It’s a 3.5/5 for me
