top_reviews.content: This place was a compromise destination that turned out to be excellent. The service was highly efficient and the food was beyond my expectations. The atmosphere was a plus, not noisy with tasteful decor. The restaurant wasn’t crowded, but the takeout was a constant. I was very pleased with the entire experience and the final tab was fair given the amount of food we ordered. I wholeheartedly recommend this place.

A chance encounter with this restaurant turns out to be a spectacular find. I stopped in and ordered my food to go, but instantly regretted not being able to stay and enjoy the ambiance and open-kitchen dining.  When I got the food home, the aroma piqued my whole family's interest, and what was supposed to be a two-person meal was gone in 10 minutes. I ordered the Mongolian Chicken, Basil Chicken, Crispy Veggie Rolls, and Steamed Brown Rice.  One of my favorite things to find is food that has flavors you can't figure out, and the Mongolian Chicken did just that.  It is a little spicy, but the flavors combine in culinary mastery and maybe even a little magic.
Then the Basil Chicken also peaked my satisfaction to the point where the steamed brown rice was just along for the ride.  Finally, the Veggie Rolls were just right the way I like them, highlighting the veggies rather than any overpowering sauces or flavors.  5 stars are not enough for the satisfaction I got from this meal.  I'll be back with the family soon.

Only places with great food have a waiting line. The food was just amazing! There was a smokiness to my meat that made it taste so fresh! The veggies were crunchy and well seasoned. I wanted a kick so they  made it spicy but not over spicy but perfectly balanced so I could taste all the ingredients and spices they combined on my plate. I'm totally in love with their food and I'm definitely going back.

Came here for a late lunch on Monday afternoon. We were the only customers there during that time of the day so service was prompt.

The restaurant gives off a clean and modern feel. I enjoyed the photos displayed around the restaurant.

Ordered the basil chicken and walnut shrimp, with a side of brown rice.

Food was great! Honey walnut shrimp is a dish I would consider my chinese soul food and they did a great job! Also enjoyed the basil chicken.

My brother took me here for my birthday, and it was one of the best dining experiences I’ve had in a long time! From the moment we walked in, everyone was so welcoming and made us feel right at home. The food was absolutely amazing—every bite was fresh, flavorful, and cooked to perfection. You can really tell they take pride in what they serve.

The service was outstanding, and the staff made my birthday feel extra special. The atmosphere was warm, inviting, and perfect for celebrating with family. This restaurant exceeded all of my expectations, and I can’t wait to come back. If you’re looking for delicious food, excellent service, and a great overall experience, I highly recommend this place. Thank you for making my birthday such a memorable one!

top_reviews.content:
AMAZING across the board. Food was delicious - we had joes chicken and the peanut stew with mac n cheese (extra yum). Service was attentive and very friendly.

Jazz was amazing! It really felt like we were back in 1920s. The vibe was immaculate and highly recommend. Its crazy that this place is this good and has such amazing values to support at-risk youth. The chef is also associated with the SF giants. There are photographs lining the hallway with even the current employees are pictured there.

Exceptional food and service. I especially enjoyed the live jazz band. I hope everyone gets to experience Old Skool Cafe. Highly recommend the Tongan Oto appetizer. Gumbo was also fire. The last time I came, I had the fried chicken. The food does not disappoint! Vibes were 10/10.

My boyfriend and I had a very special, romantic dinner at Old Skool Cafe! We loved the speakeasy vibe and decor. We sat in a cozy, retro red velvet booth. The staff (all youth) were attentive and professional, and the cocktails and food were delicious. The live jazz (played by talented youth) provided the perfect ambiance. We will be back for another special experience! We’ve been telling our friends about it, too.

Yes. Everything about this place. The vibe. The jazz music. The incredible food. The Zoot-suited staff. The story behind it. It’s all exceptional.

Do NOT sleep on this place. Seriously, do not.

For drinks, I highly recommend their French 75 and the Sidecar.

For starters, the flaky catfish and the brussel sprouts.

For Mains, the pork chop or the fried chicken.

And for dessert, either the date cake or the lavender cheesecake.

True gem in SF - get transported to 1920s speakeasy w live music and superb southern style menu dishes. Stunning chandeliers & decorations for a supper club experience you will not forget. Highly recommend the New Orleans style BBQ Jerk shrimp w crostini as a Starter and the fried chicken and/or short rib entrees. Staff are friendly efficient and will make you feel like part of the family. Great selection of mocktails as well as wine and cocktails menu. Will be back again soon.

Having heard about the great subs here, I finally tried it. Good grief. That Mediterranean wrap with labneh, za’atar and other ingredients is insanely delicious. Can’t wait to return.

One of the best sandwiches I've ever had! They are massive and full of fresh ingredients. You DEFINITELY get your money's worth here. If you're looking for a proper deli sandwich, I highly recommend this place!

Came to try the lemongrass chicken banh mi.   The bread was mildly crunchy, and not as airy as I like. The chicken was good with some sweetness but not very lemon-grassy.  I’m not sure it’s worth $11 but I think that is the going rate unless you drive farther out.

.

Inside seating and a street parklet.

The menu is tradition with an influence of the current community. You order at the counter and then take a #. It's self seating, front, back, and the tiny court yard. The food is so Saigon. I ate here last Saturday and ordered the beef noodle soup. The soup was clean-taste and refreshing. I looked for a clearer instead of full of spices or denser soup, so it was the right choice for me! The prices are fair and the atmosphere is very pleasant and the spirit of Oakland.

Will definitely return to try vegetarian bahn mi.

First time here. Ordered the grilled pork Vietnamese sandwich. It was ok. The pork was good but not much of it compared to the amount of veggies.

They have many drink selections from Costco. They also have cut fruits and flan cup desserts in the fridge.

They use the Louisiana hickory coffee for their Vietnamese style coffee.

We got the croissant breakfast sandwich and the shrimp spring rolls. To start the croissant was amazing if you are going to get one thing here you can not go wrong with this sandwich. The spring rolls were a miss they were not bad just had way too much mint and cilantro to be able to taste any of the other parts. The service here could definitely be improved. There were six people working but it seemed that only two had any idea about what was going on or what needed to be done.

Super great experience here! Their spicy grilled sandwich was super yummy and very sizeable especially for $10! The ingredients tasted fresh and the baguette was perfectly toasted. I would say the chicken tasted yummy and well marinated but to me it could have used a bit more spice to be called “spicy.” The mango strawberry smoothie was huge for 16oz and what a great price and tasted so yummy!! man i love fresh n best :D the banh mis huge and very fresh. I've tried juices, coffees, and smoothies and they never disappoint. i plan to come back again to try the rice bowls.

just so you know, either order ahead or come before 12:15 to save time. it gets really slow from 12:20-1 pm

top_reviews.content: Great tasting Thai food with approachable pricing.  My two favorites are the Pad Thai (great balance of sweet and savory) and red duck curry (bold flavors and great tasting duck).  Definitely worth a trip to check out.  Mostly street parking or you can find a small lot on the side of the building.

This is quite honestly the worst Thai restaurant in the Bay we’ve tried so far in terms of quality. The service wasn’t that great but it wasn’t as bad as the food. We ordered the Tom yum soup with tofu, which wasn’t at all fragrant and was severely lacking in flavor. The tofu in the soup was fried (??  not sure why tofu needs to be fried if it’s going into a soup, it would make more sense if the tofu was soft straight out of the cartridge). And the tofu was over fried to the point of tasting bitter and rubbery. Not good. Then the spicy fried rice with chicken came out and it was… soggy! Like laughably soggy. They must have run out of cold rice; nevertheless the quality could be described as something similar to a newbie making fried rice for the first time. The only things that were decent were the shrimp rolls and the Thai tea, but that’s not enough to make this place good. Big X mark for me.

Tried out their veggies options, and was delish. I liked that they can make their entrees gluten-free. Ordered the Cashew nuts and the Basil stir fry. Both were similar with the exception of the basil flavored in the later one. Not sure if they have a parking lot though. I found parking on the street.

Relaxing environment , amazing customer service and some of the yummiest Tai food dishes I've enjoyed. I Love this place. I'm a frequent visitor . Jasmine is a superstar ✨️ always welcomes me with a smile and my food perfectly ordered every time.
Unexpectedly delicious thai spot with hole in the wall but cozy! Vibes and very reasonable prices for the bay area. Will definitely come back if we're in Castro valley again.

Absolutely loved That’s Amore! Everything we tried was incredibly fresh and delicious. The pizza was definitely a highlight, perfectly baked and fresh.

Definitely one of my favorite food experiences in San Francisco. Fresh ingredients, amazing pizza, great service, and such a welcoming atmosphere. I would absolutely come back and highly recommend That’s Amore! ❤️ 🍕

I decided to try this place while I was in the area, mainly because the photos of the pizzas looked great and the reviews were very positive. Maybe that set my expectations a bit too high.

Overall, the experience was good, but not impressive. The pizza itself was decent, with okay ingredients and solid flavor, but nothing that really stood out or felt particularly memorable. The atmosphere was very basic and didn’t add much to the overall experience.

It’s a good option if you’re nearby and looking for a simple pizza, but I was expecting something a bit more authentic and distinctive based on what I had seen online.

The handmade pizzas were pretty good, and the cheese was melty and gooey. Wine bottles for water were a cute touch. 4 1/2 but bumping up to 5 because I would recommend it as a good casual spot . Not many great options for lactose intolerant people, but I suppose you can argue "just go eat somewhere else".

Just fantastic! We had that’s amore for our wedding welcome party & they were excellent. The pizza, pasta & salads were amazing. Guests raved about the food & went back for seconds. Their mobile brick oven is so nice & their quality is extremely high. I was extra impressed with their lemon chicken & shrimp pasta dishes, since I hadn’t tried them before. Their suggestion of bamboo plates etc elevated things nicely. Highly recommend.

This place is consistently SOLID! I've been frequenting That's Amore for about 4 years now and the pizza, the service, the price point is always great.  Very accommodating staff - I held a Bday party with 12+ adults and 15 kids and everything went super smooth.  Salads are delicious and the mac & cheese is the ONLY restaurant mac & cheese my daughter will eat.

Wandering around SF, we stumbled onto this little burger shop with big flavor. Delicious. The kind of burger you keep eating when you are full because it's so good. I had the Giants burger which is topped with provolone cheese, 2 crispy onion rings and bacon. BBQ sauce on the top bun. Toppings of lettuce, tomato & pickle on the side. I like the assemble it how you like option. Garlic fries were perfect: crispy and topped with fresh, minced garlic. Worth the price. Super friendly woman working behind the counter. She delivered our food to us and told me the Giants burger was also her favorite. I'm still full 9 hours later. I'll be back when I'm in the city.

Fried chicken sandwich was a huge disappointment. While I understand that the highlight is the burger, which was solid, that doesn’t mean that other menu items should be disproportionately inadequate. The friend chicken sandwich patty was tiny and cabbage slaw skimpy, for sure not worth the price. I guess if one stuck to just the burger , it would be fine, but one would not have known that the chicken sandwich would be so deficient.

We had a long day with no food in our Kelly's. We found this place on food near me and decided to try it. Food was delicious and service was excellent. We will be going back to try most of the burgers.

I think they were frozen and then fried. The milkshake I had arrived the perfect consistency and had a great flavor. Portions are well worth the price.

I’ll be back!

Delicious Vietnamese dishes made hearty and clean. Chicken broth is amazing! So does everything else, but definitely get garlic noodle, one of the best I had.

People often commend this place for its amazing Vietnamese dishes but I want to bring particular attention to the Taiwanese dishes they also serve - mainly the Taiwan popcorn chicken, the fried tofu (breaded in tapioca starch). The owner was very friendly and chatted with us a bit and made us feel welcome to dine at his wonderful restaurant. I will return!

From a sunny day late afternoon lunch or a rainy day pick me up, I feel like this place is the best option anytime for a savory chicken oriented meal. Service is world class, friendly, and makes the food all the better!

After ordering in store, it took about 10-15 minutes for our food to arrive. I view this as a HUGE positive because you know you’re getting the freshest food possible. I had the chicken steak and was surprised at how juicy (& not greasy) the inside was. Sides with broccoli & garlic noodles were a must. Spring rolls & thai tea were excellent as well.

I’ll certainly be back whether it’s in person on their great (and really clean!) outdoor seating or delivery! Thank you so much!

top_reviews.content:
I recently had a massage with Anna, and I can honestly say it was one of the most incredible experiences I’ve ever had. From the moment I walked in, she made me feel completely at ease with her warm, welcoming energy and genuine kindness. It’s rare to find someone who not only has exceptional skill, but also such an intuitive understanding of what your body needs, and Anna has both.

She seemed to know exactly where I was holding tension without me even having to explain, and her technique was absolutely perfect, relaxing, therapeutic, and deeply rejuvenating all at once. I left feeling lighter, calmer, and more refreshed than I have in a long time.

You can tell she puts her heart into her work, and it makes all the difference. I will definitely be coming back, and I recommend Anna to anyone looking for an amazing massage. You won’t be disappointed!

I’ve been to this Suchada location several times and gotten massages from Anna and Noon. Each time I leave here I feel incredible. They each found the knots and worked them through, and not just gone through some routine. It’s quite clear the staff know how to do proper healing body work!

All the staff are very friendly. And the facility is very clean and calming 😌 There’s even little dried fruit snacks and Bael Fruit/Matoom tea (served at most Thai massage places) for after the massage. Amazing.

Ek or Anthony is such a skilled therapist. I work with my hands while standing all day.
He is excellent at excavating the knots while keeping me incredibly relaxed. I’ve seen him thrice and he only gets better ! Suchada is rad I’ve been a client for years, all their therapists are pros , and very reasonable prices!

I’ve been here a couple of times over the years And have found it to be pretty solid as far as practitioners go, although I haven’t frequent enough to get any solid names that I would like to work with.

I really enjoy the Foot reflexology, and acupressure and of course, who doesn’t love getting your back, walked on tehee Having said that, I often ask for extra footwork and often don’t seem to get it and don’t realize the massage is over until it’s over and didn’t get a chance to say hey what about that extra footwork? So perhaps that’s on me

I recently had the couples special massage with my partner, and we found it relaxing and fulfilling, etc.. The sauna was hot and dry and nice and they give you a little tea and water and fresh fruit, which is very refreshing. Although pay attention to wearing the robe with a body scrub in it if you take a shower and you go to put the rug back on to go out you’ll get body scrub all over you again. Otherwise totally great experience.

Extremely disappointing experience. I booked a one-hour deep tissue massage and unfortunately left without receiving the service because of how I was treated by the receptionist.

From the moment I arrived, the receptionist was incredibly rude and dismissive. Another customer arrived after me for an appointment at the same time, but she was taken to a treatment room almost immediately while I was asked to wait another 10 minutes.

When I asked if a female therapist was available, the receptionist told me, “You don’t get to choose anything as a ClassPass customer because you choose to pay less.” I was honestly shocked by how disrespectful and condescending this comment was. I completely understand if a specific therapist is unavailable, but there is a professional way to communicate that to a customer. Telling someone they are not entitled to make a basic request simply because they booked through ClassPass is completely unacceptable.

I told her that if the spa is going to treat customers differently based on how they booked, they probably shouldn’t be on ClassPass. She simply shrugged her shoulders and said, “OK,” as if she couldn’t care less.

At that point, I no longer felt comfortable receiving a massage there, so I left.

What makes this especially disappointing is that I was actually looking for a new spa that I could visit regularly. I would have been happy to become a long-term customer if I had been treated with basic courtesy and respect.

The issue was never about not being able to accommodate my preference for a female therapist. The issue was the receptionist’s attitude, the way I was treated differently from another customer, and the incredibly disrespectful comment she made to me.

A business can have policies and limitations, but there is no excuse for making a customer feel unwelcome or inferior. Based on this experience, I unfortunately cannot recommend this spa.

I’ve been wanting to try this place for awhile and really love the idea of vegan Mexican food. I opted for the nachos for my first visit with asada. One thing I found weird is that the physical menu lists nachos+ meat as $15 pre tax, but the item was rung up as $15.25 pre tax. That’s not a huge deal, but why wouldn’t the physical menu reflect the real price?

The nachos themself were pretty good and the portion size was super generous. The chips were great and crunchy and didn’t get too soggy. Their salsas and queso taste great, especially for vegan queso. Beans were fine. I maybe wanted a little more guacamole, but I’m glad it’s included in the base item without additional charge.

However, I was disappointed by the asada. I’ve never had great luck with vegan beef, but I’m always willing to try it once. It was pretty dry and had what I can only describe as that old school vegan beef flavor, when morning star used to be the only option. I ended up pushing most of it to the side.

Overall, I enjoyed the food, but I wouldn’t get the asada again. Next time, I’ll go for something else and hopefully will enjoy that more. But, I’ll definitely go back!

We catered Venganza for a birthday party, and the food was phenomenal! We got the taco bar, so we had a sampling of all the different “meats”, and each one was delicious! Full of flavor and great texture. Plus, the handmade tortillas, pickled veggies and salsas were all so tasty! All our guests were raving about it, and were blown away that it was all vegan. The owners were great to work with - super professional and responsive! Plus, the dessert menu is incredible. We got cupcakes and they were a masterpiece - beautifully decorated (based on our party theme!) and absolutely delicious! Thank you so much!

top_reviews.content:
We had the galbi tang and spicy cold noodles with beef at Daol Tofu in Oakland.

The galbi tang was rich and comforting — the broth had deep flavor, and the short ribs were tender and satisfying.

The spicy cold noodles were refreshing with just the right kick, perfectly balanced with the sliced beef.

Service was friendly and attentive, and the food came out quickly. The vibe felt cozy and casual, a great spot for comforting Korean food in the neighborhood.

Daol has been in the neighborhood a long time. It’s often quiet, and that translates to attentive service and made to order food. We went for lunch and had the chicken bento, the mackerel, and the tofu vegetable stew. Everything deliciously spicy, plenty of rice and banchan, tea, and miso soup. All for $13.99! Highly recommend.

Very authentic and Delicious thank you so much.
Bebimbap, seafood tofu soup, bulgogi, and fish. Will come back again next time.

We had an absolutely delicious dinner at Doal Tofu & Korean BBQ on Telegraph Avenue in Oakland. I must confess that this was my first experience eating Korean but it certainly will not be my last. Our waiter was enthusiastic and very helpful explaining the different kinds of dishes and why he was putting an uncooked egg on our table.we ordered the Galbi, which is a grilled beef that was very tasty and we also ordered Yachae Sundubu, which is a tofu stew that is served so sizzling and hot that we cracked the uncooked egg and added to the stew! It cooked instantly and added a wonderful unique texture to our dish. We also ordered a veggie pancake, that was the largest scallion- type pancake i’d ever seen. It tasted wonderful. We wisely had a bottle of Cass beer that’s a delicious Korean beer. The prices were very reasonable snd I can guarantee you that once you eat here, you’ll want to return often.

We randomly found this place on Google map, and we're super happy that we found it!

With 2 adults and two young kids (6 and 3,) we ordered 7 different dishes because we were excited with the variety of dishes they have to offer. And everything tastes so good!! We spent $135 before tips, which we totally think it's worth it. The house special, Bossam is worth trying! Galbi was yummy, not overly sweet, soup and Japchae were great. The banchan was yummy! Fish and pancake were also delicious. Bibimbub was also good.

Oxtails risotto and wood oven half chicken were outstanding.
My service professional Anne well-trained from the old school with attention to detail, very attentive, and courteous.
The menu changed often.
Kids friendly!

May 2, 2026

You can enjoy a variety of excellent Italian foods in this restaurant, including honey-glazed & aromatically spiced oven-warmed olives, deep-fried, garlic drenched sourdough dusted meatballs w/parm and fresh herbs, spicy red sauce, smoked mozzarella w/grilled house-made baguette, and delicious salads.

If you want to  treat your family, guests, and yourself to possibly the best pizza east of San Francisco, the East End Restaurant is the place to go for these reasons:

•	This restaurant is owned by a family that has many years of successful business experience. Paul and Michele Manousos are dedicated to serving the finest foods and beverages available in a clean and cheerful environment.
•	Paul, who appears in the enclosed photo, and Jacob Alioto, are co-chefs. Pizzas and other foods are cooked in a wood-fired, open-hearth oven – just as they have been baked for centuries. Michele meets and greets guests, and oversees food service operations.
•	Chef Paul closely supervises the preparation of food using special recipes, and assuring high quality standards.  He makes the dough by hand daily,  with his own starter and organic flour. No commercial yeasts, extenders or preservatives of any kind are used.
•	They really care about the quality of foods served and the enjoyment of their customers in consuming culinary delights.
•	Here is an example of how customers are informed of how best to bring home pizzas: “Pro tip – Pizza boxes are very unkind to our style of pizza. For take-out pizza that is more like what you’ll get in the restaurant, we recommend asking for an uncut pizza and crisping it up in your oven directly on the rack or a pizza stone for a few minutes at 450 degrees. Highly recommended if home or meal time is more than 15 minutes away, or if reheating is your plan. Finishing ingredients will be provided separately to be added after reheating.”
•	Service provided by the staff is top-notch.  Amanda and all the servers spend time explaining the menu, answering questions, and assuring service excellence.
My family and I highly recommend this restaurant. The food and service are excellent, and the prices are reasonable and competitive. Be sure to enjoy the Char-Grilled Escarole w/creamy roasted garlic dressing shallot “candy!”

As part of my Alameda Restaurant Week exploration, I spent time at East End documenting their offerings. They maintain a friendly, changing menu that keeps things interesting. The pizzas feature great toppings, but they also serve interesting and authentic pasta and meat dishes worth trying. Paul, the owner, is an artist with food - you can see his creativity throughout the menu. The non-pizza items are definitely worth checking out. It's upscale, but in a distinctly Alameda way that remains approachable.

We came to East End on a Thursday evening. There was no wait and we were welcomed graciously.
The interior is very charming. Hard seating which isn't my favorite but I was able to endure. It's a large open space, high ceilings, and rustic decor. The tables are placed so that they aren't right next to each other and angled so that they aren't side by side. You can see the wood fired oven from your seat but the ventilation is so great you don't smell any smoke at all.
The cocktails were so well balanced you can hardly tell there's alcohol. They were very tasty and super smooth. Hats off to the mixologist, she really did a great job.

We had the warm herbed olives with honey and they were fabulous! Such a great difference from a cold olive plate. Highly recommended! The honey with the salty is a magical pair. The meatball appetizer was also great. Nice portion for an appetizer, the bread was crunchy and smokey, and the meatballs had great texture and flavor. They weren't packed with bread crumbs to dilute the flavor of the meat.
The little gem salad was nice and crisp. The fried capers were a great touch. The dressing needed a little more zing. It was nicely dressed but couldn't taste much.
The mushroom ragu pasta was creamy, al dente, and had great delicate mushroom flavor. Nicely done! My friend is from Rome and she definitely approved.
The pizza was phenomenal! We ordered the Diablita and it was probably the most simple pizza I've ever tasted but the flavors were crazy! It is definitely spicy and a perfect pizza! So good!
We also got Mr. Terranova and added arugula (even though the menu says it isn't allowed). The crispy shallots added a great texture and flavor. It was a tasty pie for sure but the Diablita stole the show. We look forward to trying the other pizzas soon!
The staff was wonderful, our main server Anne was the nicest lady. We appreciated her friendly persona and cheery smile.
We did not have room to try the dessert but imagine it would be just as great as everything else.
We highly recommend dining here. We will be back! ❤️

Local squid was super good. Our server was pleasant and cool. Foods were balanced and not over seasoned at all. Impressed. Cocktails were the same. Balanced taste of liquor and sweetness impressed us. I can’t wait to visit and try other dishes!

Review:

-Soup was pretty good. No complaints. Well, except that it is high in sodium thus inherently highly unhealthy.
-Salad - sad and disappointing. Why even serve this?
-Chicken teriyaki - edible, and I did eat it all, but not spectacular or alone worth making me repeat as a customer.
-Chicken katsu - overall very greasy and not crispy at all. Very unhealthy. Not edible, so I left it all after a bite or two.
-Tempura - tasted pretty standard. Had 2 bites but ultimately left the rest because it was so greasy and unhealthy.
-California rolls - I tried this last and by then my appetite was gone after having tried the rest of the food. Tasted like any other California roll.

Overall, I ordered all this food for me to taste all at once since it was my first time eating here and because I love tasting food. Out of all this, I did eat ALL of the chicken teriyaki because it seemed the healthier and fully edible component, as well as a couple spoonfuls of white rice, a little bit of the soup (high in sodium), took two bites of the tempura, had a piece of lettuce, ate the fried unhealthy broccoli which did taste good but it’s deeply unhealthy, and threw everything else in the garbage / trash where it belonged. I estimate I threw away ~ 85% of it.

In conclusion: I was left totally disappointed with this food. This is not a place I would ever return to as a repeat customer. The food was clearly not cooked with love nor by anyone who has any care in the quality of food they put forward.

top_reviews.content:
Come for the views, stay for the convenience.

Our group was walking through the Tunnels park and got hungry so we stopped in to Il Parco.

For a large group the cafeteria style ordering was convenient for expedited service as separate payment. I wished they had the full menu at the end of the line so that I was more prepared to order, but in the final minute I decided on one of the focaccia sandwiches.

We grabbed a big table on their patio and took in the stunning views as we enjoyed the food.

Over all we felt the pizza and sandwiches were really oily and the pastries were dry. Wasn’t great, but not a bad option for middle of the park experience.

Service was sharp so for me it’s the view and staff that really made this meal.

This is one of the more difficult places for me to review. Truth be told, if you put REALLY REALLY HIGH value on the view, the high prices for a mediocre product are justified. But considering the trash on the ground and the filthy glass wind breaks, the place can definitely be characterized as a rip-off unless you a wealthy local, used to inflated SF/Cal prices, and this is your most conveniently located neighborhood coffee shop.

Food is mediocre but at least there is variety (pizza, sandwiches, salads) as is also the case with drink selection (coffee drinks, beer, wine, sodas, etc). The main problem is that because of the location, this is a one of those places that doesn't have to try hard or lower prices to stay busy.  They are really the only option within a 15-minute walk of the Presidio Tunnel Tops. Next closest is Piccino at the Letterman Digital Arts Center but it is a sit-down restaurant about a 15 minute walk. Best deal at Il Parco in my opinion is the canned beer.

Actually now that I think about it, there is another option.  If you walk 5 or so minutes Southwest from the Tunnel Tops area where there is an expansive grass lawn area you can find one or more food trucks. The better option would be to get food there and eat on the lawn or on the picnic benches in the Tunnel Tops.
The food is hit and miss, particularly the bake goods.  The Roman style pizza is pretty tasty, but the views... the view on a sunny day is stunning from the patio.

I’m not sure why the rating on this place is so low. The coffee is great. It’s got beautiful seating with glass that blocks out the wind and there’s heaters for a cold day. The service was prompt and though I haven’t tried the food yet. It looks delicious.The food is reasonable priced. Muffins are about five bucks. Pizza is between 10 and $15 and sandwiches are $20. It’s not cheap but it’s not crazy expensive either

Server was super helpful in choosing options to share with our group. Food was delicious, prepared well, and eaten by all (even picky eaters). It was very windy and cold outside, I do wish they had warmer seating options but we may it through, the food and view was worth it.

top_reviews.content:
After reading Matt Y.'s review, I came here to try their carnitas. He is 100% right. The carnitas in my taco salad $14 were terrific! The bigger meat pieces were tender and moist. The ends were crispy with bits of crunchy strands. The rest of the taco salad wasn't bad either. They use chopped pieces of romaine lettuce on top of beans and rice. Love that fresh lettuce snap when I bite into it. As for the edible tortilla bowl, this tasted fresh and not stale like some other establishments. It was fluffy and breaks apart easily when I pulled on it. There was a good balance of guacamole, sour cream,  pico de gallo and cheese. It came with free chips & salsa.

Bring a jacket. They leave the front door open and it was freezing tonight at 8pm. This is the type of taqueria where you order and pay at the cashier. My food came out within 15 minutes.

Thank you Matt Y. for always posting useful content.

The tacos at this place tasted great! The most important thing for me was that the meat was well seasoned. Really good tacos. I especially liked the Al Pastor and the Steak.

Aside from the food, the staff were really nice also.

The place itself also looked clean and felt comfortable to dine in.

Highly recommend this place if you’re looking for a good taqueria. Will come back to try their other menu items.

100 stars out of 10! We’ve come here for over 10 years and not once has the quality or the service been less than stellar ♥️ these hardworking and kind folks offer fresh and consistent deliciousness, always with a smile on their faces. They have served their neighborhood for many more years than we’ve known them. Come here and come here often, you won’t regret it!

Amazing hearty food, and great hospitality from the owner!

Ngoe-thuk organic version +$4. She wasn't sure what the differences from one on the front page were other than being organic. Hope it's the version everyone raved about in reviews. Red Hot sauce and tamari condiments.
Great hand made noodles, broccoli, carrots, left greens, tofu, celery, scallions, pumpkin seeds, mildly spiced.
Didn't often get vegan lassi option do mango was refreshing
Normally might have fed two lite appetites if shared but this guy was hungry and polished it all off!
Bhaktsa-Marku, pasta brown sugar with butter. Whipped cream topping added! Want sure what to expect but nice tasty finishing touch. Chewy and sweet small pellets of pasta.

The food here is delicate and restorative. The service is kind.

Not to be missed.

We had the momos in mint sauce and a hand-pulled noodle dish that had delicate, subtle flavors.

Generous, reasonable portions.

We’ll be back again and again. Including in our next lives! I’d be happy to not break the cycle of rebirth to eat this food.

I feel like this Banh Mi was more “American style” in the way that it was packed with meat vs a lot of cheaper banh mi where it’ll be like a strip of meat. The place is a walk up there is no seating so I ordered (2) banh mi - one bbq pork, one chicken, (2) iced coffee, and an order of imperial rolls to go. When I picked up my order I picked up the bag that thing was heavy, we drove around the park and found parking by the beach and ate. It was really good would definitely recommend. On top of the food just being good and the banh mi being packed with meat and having really good flavor, the roll was off the hook. Flaky on the outside, yet chewy, hearty to hold the goods, but still super soft **chefs kiss** Thank you will definitely be back.

Overpriced, Undersized, and Overcooked — Save Your $18

Paid $18 for what I can only describe as a half-sandwich pretending to be a cheesesteak. When I politely asked if they could add a little more meat — because it genuinely felt like less than a small handful — the owner told me "this is a normal size, we measure all our meat" and seemed almost offended I'd ask. No offer to make it right, no flexibility whatsoever.

The garlic flatbread was just heavenly—crispy on the outside, soft and fluffy on the inside, with a wonderful blend of garlic and herbs that made it utterly addictive.

For the main course, we ordered both the margarita pizza and the pepperoni pizza, and they did not disappoint. The margarita pizza had a wonderfully tangy tomato sauce, fresh mozzarella, and a perfectly crisp crust that was both light and satisfying. The pepperoni pizza was equally impressive—loaded with perfectly spiced pepperoni and the right amount of cheese, with a nice balance of flavors in every bite. The crust on both pizzas was just the right amount of chewy, with a slight crispiness that added an extra layer of texture.

What really made the experience stand out was the staff. They were incredibly friendly and accommodating, going above and beyond to make sure we had everything we needed. The atmosphere was warm and inviting, making it the perfect spot for a casual yet delicious meal.

I highly recommend Mercato Pizzeria to anyone looking for great pizza and outstanding service. It’s definitely a five-star experience!

Went to the public market for some lunch, the public area was so crowded. So we decided to check out Pizzeria Mercato, the place is spacious!

The calamari was delicious, would order that again! The pizza and pasta were good as well, but the calamari is a must for us.  All and all, we had a relaxing lunch.

You have live seafood and authentic Cantonese steam soup.

The food quality is good, a bit on the salty side. The portion is decent. You are looking at 5 dishes for 4 people.

The average is about 40-50 per person if you don’t order alcohol.

The duck noodle soup, rich with egg noodles and plenty of duck, was the highlight. We also tried the chicken feet and pork spare ribs in black bean sauce. Both dim sum items were meatier than usual and seemed freshly steamed, though they took a bit longer to serve.

The jasmine tea, at $1.25 per person, was a delightful, albeit not free, addition.

Oh I loved it! I’m from New Jersey and this was actually my first time in CA, around the Walnut Creek area. Incredible Italian food! The Luca pizza is a must! Service was great. We sat outside to avoid a wait time and it was a chilly night but they offered a blanket! They thought of everything. It was so so delicious ❤️

top_reviews.content: Good late night restaurant in the Outer Sunset. This place is cozy and pretty lively. The food here is satisfying. I like the portion size. Enough for sharing in family style. We had the Beef Fried Rice, Whole Chicken, Pot Stickers, and Kimchi Pancake. All tasty. We were a party of three, and had some leftover to take home. Very Korean! Love coming here. Food is amazing. Seafood pancake is amazing. Kimchi fried rice is super flavorful. Love the spicy pork. Those 3 are always my go to order. On a weekend or Friday night it’ll be busy and there will be a wait around dinner time but you can put your name and phone number down. I like how they are open late as well. Service is good and I like how they have a button to call the waiter. I always recommend people to come here.

If you wanna cozy at home feeling comfort meal come to this spot! I just revisited this place over the weekend and haven’t been back in a couple of years. Came on a Saturday night around 6:15 and waited about 40 minutes or so. It gets packed on Saturday.

Their side of rice is so good! It tasted excellent with the army stew we had. The portions were huge. I maybe would skip the chicken gizzard as it was a little overdone and salty.

Decoration of this place is lovely! Almost feels like the inside of a ship, lots of wood and dark tones. And huge win for staying open late! Staff is very polite and I've heard that their drinks are good, but the food doesn't stay behind! I tried their Beef Kimchi Fried Rice, Chicken Gizzard Stir Fry, Calamari Stir Fried and Calamari Soup, they were all tasty. Honest Korean food, good servings for a decent price! And if you are coming for a late night dinner or something, parking is a breeze! I have been here a few times and will be back again!

Highly recommended, if you crave for some delicious tasty authentic Mexican food!

Needed a quick late-night bite and this was the first place that popped up on Yelp so we tried it.

Glad we strolled in bc the food was good, and service was friendly and fast.

top_reviews.content: We picked this restaurant for a celebration thinking it is authentic mediterrenean. However we found out that it is mediterrenean with India twist. The food was tasty but the spices used are closer to Indian more than mediterrenean. We ordered beet salad, octopus as appetizers, adana kebab and trout as main dishes. We enjoyed all of them. As dessert we ordered kunefe which was far from original kunefe taste. They offered us complementary apple sorbet for our celebration which we appreciated. Atmosphere is nice, especially when the weather is nice you can sit outside next to water. Couple things that surprised us 1- High prices 2-Restroom is outside in a different building.

A Disappointing Mother's Day Lunch at Alora

We came to Alora Coastal Mediterranean at Pier 3 in San Francisco for a Mother's Day lunch with the family. While the location on the water is nice, the overall experience turned out to be quite lackluster due to rigid service, small portions, and mixed food quality.

The food itself had a few high points but was ultimately a mixed bag:

The absolute highlight of the meal was the Muhammara. We ordered it along with a beef skewer and an extra bazalma bread, and this was clearly the best dish of the day.

We also had a beet salad, which was refreshing and nice.

The kids ordered the Spaghetti Chitarra and enjoyed it.

The Ladolemon Chicken dish was also quite nice, and we actually liked it enough to order a second one.
A special mention goes to the rice pilaf included with the entrees, which was very tasty.

On the negative side, the Adana Kebab plate was the biggest disappointment of the meal. The kebab was not cooked well at all; in fact, it was overcooked, burnt, and hard. We have had much better kebabs elsewhere at half the price.

Across the board, the portion sizes for the plates are quite small. While some of the food was decent, it certainly didn't live up to the premium expectations.

The real downfall of our visit was the service, which
was incredibly disappointing for a Mother's Day celebration. My son really wanted to try the lamb shank dish, which was part of their special six-course holiday menu. We asked if we could order it standard, but our server, (starts with H...will not name), was completely unaccommodating. He told us it was impossible to get the dish without ordering the entire six-course meal. When we asked if he could double-check, he wasn't even willing to speak with the manager to accommodate a customer's request.
I was honestly flabbergasted by the total lack of hospitality. It is hard to imagine running a prominent restaurant with that kind of rigid, unhelpful attitude toward guests.

Overall, this place feels heavily overpriced for the food quality and the service we received.

What a wonderful find as we walked along the Pier 3 near Ferry building. The food was smashing the cocktails fantastic and the hsot Siddhesh rocks. What a wonderful experience meeting someone from your hometown so far away. The staff is warm and friendly. Go for the Carlitos Way gin cocktail it rocks. Way to go Alora.. Kudos

I went to Alora last Friday for happy hour with friends, and it was a lovely way to start the weekend. We ordered oysters along with negronis and limoncello spritzes—everything was fresh and well done. The oysters were beautifully presented and tasted great, and the cocktails were flavorful and well balanced.
The real standout here is the ambiance. The restaurant is gorgeous, with stunning bay views that make the experience feel special, especially as the sun starts to set. Service was friendly and welcoming, and while the value is okay, you’re definitely paying more for the setting and views than for a bargain happy hour—and honestly, it’s worth it.
We had a wonderful time and would absolutely return, especially when we’re in the mood for great views, good drinks, and a relaxed, upscale atmosphere.

Pooja took great care of us and she made such a great impression that we returned again the following day for lunch.  If you are in the area on a trip, this place is well worth a visit.  Thank you to all the staff for a lovely experience.

top_reviews.content: What an experience! I loved everything about this place. The tasting menu almost had a story, and each dish was dedicated to her own mother and someone close to her I believe. The presentation was out of the ball park and such an eye candy. It’s about enjoying the marriage of different ingredients creating intricate flavors. The servers were humorous and friendly. It was my husband’s bday dinner and they gave him a card signed by the staff and a small bday desert. We both don’t drink alcohol, but they offered good selections of NA wine. I strongly recommend it.

We have visited Nightbird 13 times in the past two years; the last time being December 31st 2025. Hands-down, it is our very favorite restaurant in San Francisco for dinner (we love Foreign Cinema for lunch / brunch). The tasting menu is out-of-this-world, Chef Kim does an incredible job of crafting delicious dishes in a way that some Michelin starred restaurants cannot. There's a couple of staple dishes that always appear on the menus, despite the seasonal rotations, there's clearly a reason for that - they are expertly constructed and very tasty.

Being attached to the Linden Room Bar allows you to select from a wide-range of beverages from the with a cocktail menu as you settle into the night. Both venues have their own distinct vibe, the restaurant is the perfect place if you like a low-to-medium level of noise from other diners and background music, this allows you to have very civilized conversations over dinner without raising your voice to be heard.

The servers are on-point and so kind and friendly. We always receive the warmest of welcomes (Thank you Jordan, Mark and William. They will also suggest wines as you move through the menu to complement each dish.

Do go and try Nightbird, it's a real gem in Hayes Valley and so easy to get to from Muni and Bart. It's also super-handy if you're seeing a show at the Orpheum, which is a stones throw away.

What a night! Absolutely beautiful food, service, and location. Literally everything was rock solid.

Came with a friend for a girl's night.  Service started swiftly and the pacing was just right, unrushed, but never lingering too long.

Every dish was really unique and we had so many favorites.  The crudo was fresh and clean, the scallop was perfect and tender, the squab was just perfect, the mouse donut was bizarrely wonderful.  Dessert was clean and cool and just completely light after it all.

The staff was amazing and my friend said the wine pairing and discussion with each team (most of them being sommeliers) was great.

10/10 would gladly come again.  Best food and experience of our girls trip so far.

Absolutely stunning, inventive, and beautifully crafted dishes. It was truly a journey through spring and impeccable culinary artistry. The service and wine recommendations were outstanding as well. This place is a must visit in San Francisco, and stands apart from many other fine dining restaurants in this region.

The food was poorly executed and simply did not taste good (to any of the people in my party). The beef with charred leeks tasted like it was rolled around in an ashtray. There are well executed smoky dishes and then there is this. The menu was a list of dead chefs' names and told us nothing about the dishes at all, so you had no understanding of how many savory vs sweet courses were next.

But the key reason for the one star is the imbalanced, poor service. One member of the wait staff showered all of the attention and adoration onto one of us, while completely ignoring the rest of us in my party. Only one of us was asked whether we wanted tea or coffee. Only one of us was asked how the food was. Only one of us was asked if they wanted another drink. Peculiar that those who were ignored were people of color 🤔.

The waitress told us we were vegetarians... And then apologized when she got the wrong table. She then congratulated us for our job promotion.... And then apologized she got the wrong table.

Fine dining establishments should teach their wait staff better. This is worse than Burger King.

top_reviews.content:
Phenomenal Pupusas, but Some Entrée Pricing Missteps

Popoca just received a well-deserved Michelin Guide recommendation earlier this week, so the moment I saw a reservation open up, I grabbed it immediately. It makes for a fantastic night out in downtown Oakland (with easy parking nearby to boot) and has a beautiful dining room layout with a great vibe and welcoming service.

The food across the board is packed with flavor, starting with a brilliant seasonal strawberry salad that wasn't on their online menu. It was loaded with sweet strawberries and a dense, firm ingredient with "dragon" in the name, topped with mint, pepitas, and a refreshing green herb granita. My only critique here is that I wish I had been given a spoon to scoop up the incredible leftover cream dressing, or received a fresh plate when our pupusas arrived so the salad flavors didn't mingle.

The hand-slapped pupusas are easily some of the absolute best I have ever had. Each one delivered a totally distinct flavor profile, and the cheese tastes incredible. The pupusa de lengua (beef tongue) was my favorite—remarkably rich and tender. The bacalao y ajo verde (salt cod and green garlic) was a unique wildcard, while the pipian y loroco offered a beautifully elevated take on standard traditional flavors. I would happily order all three again.

Where the meal faltered slightly was the value positioning of the mains. The pollo en chicha was certainly fantastic—the leg and thigh were perfectly cooked, juicy, and coated in a deeply savory, complex fermented pineapple sauce—but at $36, it feels significantly overpriced for the portion size, especially when another similar restaurant across town offers a spectacular, entire whole chicken for $35.

Similarly, while the traditional sides were very tasty—the rice cooked in carrot juice had a fantastic subtle sweetness, and the refried black beans were plentiful—the $17 price tag for a plate of rice and beans is tough to justify.

We were far too full for dessert, and while Popoca is an excellent addition to the neighborhood with world-class masa work, you'll want to choose your larger plates carefully to get the best value out of the menu.

We went there on a weekday to celebrate my birthday and what a birthday it was. We loved everything we were served, so flavorful. The server and the manager, both were very graceful. They also suggested how we eat every item for the best taste. They had a seafood chowmein special that night and it was so good. We had a foodgasm after that. We couldn't finish and took it to-go but the next day it tasted even better as our server told. The drink wasn't to my taste but I was told already that it is pineapple and sweeter, I wanted to try so no points cut there. I have never had Salvadoran food before, so I don't have a reference but this was as good as my taste buds would want it to be. Everything has flavor engrained. The beef tongue as well as the lamb neck has every bit of flavor infused into it. The salpicon was our first dish and we both thought we are tasting food in culinary wars now. 10/10 this place.

Went for a birthday. The food was amazing. Ate family style so we could try a bit of everything. There wasn’t one thing I wouldn’t get again. Standouts were the pupusas and pollo en chica. The quesadilla dessert was the perfect way to end the meal. Our waiter was also great and very knowledgeable about the menu. Will be back again!

We went to Popoca for my birthday. As a photographer and visual branding expert, I’m very visual and was excited to try something new—Salvadorian cuisine. It did not disappoint. I definitely eat with my eyes first, and the food looked beautiful. The ambiance was wonderful, and the staff was super friendly.

I originally planned to try their fixed-price dinner, but after spending way too much time on Yelp trying to decide, I realized it didn't include what I was craving. I'm glad we ended up ordering à la carte.

Here's what we had:
* Pupusas (mushroom + beef tongue)
* Pollo Campero (fried chicken)
* Clam Alguashte -- my absolute favorite
* Chancho con Yuca (pork)
* Tres Leches cake
Plus a cocktail to start, though I can't remember the name.

My favorites were the pupusas and the clam dish. I wasn't crazy about the fried chicken, but my son loved it -- definitely a personal preference thing. There was another mushroom dish that looked incredible, so I may try that next time.

They surprised me with a birthday drink, which was such a sweet gesture, even if it was a bit sweet for my taste.

Highly recommend.

With the year-end approaching, I didn't want to miss out on the Chase Sapphaire Reserve  Annual Dining Credit of $300, which reimburses $150 every six months. Most eligible restaurants in the Bay Area are located in downtown San Francisco or on the peninsula. I found two restaurants in Oakland, compared them on Google, and finally chose Popoca Oakland. I made a reservation two weeks in advance for an evening slot. The restaurant opens around 5:30 PM and is only open for dinner. Located in downtown Oakland, street parking is relatively convenient, and free parking is available after 6 PM. Therefore, I recommend making a reservation after 6 PM. The restaurant had a nice atmosphere. We ordered Pollo Campero (chicken), Lengua (beef tongue), and two main courses, Chancho (pork) and Lamb. All the dishes were similar to Chinese food and could be shared. We didn't order drinks. The final bill, including a 20% tip, came to $165. There was also a $75 per person set menu on the menu, presumably for CSR reimbursement, but we didn't choose it. Overall, the food was very good, even a little surprising. My teammates and I agreed to have our year-end party here next year. The CSR reimbursement arrived two days after the meal. Suddenly, I realized that CSR's new benefits, like playing a game, require advance planning, but they still bring fun to life.

top_reviews.content: Awesome high-end Mexican. We found Cantina Los Mayas searching Yelp for highly rated restaurants walking distance from Golden Gate Park. 2 blocks north of the park, it was a 10 minute walk. Reservations are a good idea- the place started to fill quickly on a midweek evening. Roger runs the front of the house. He was helpful with menu translations and suggestions. He started us with fresh tortilla chips with 3 types of salsa from sweet to hot. For apps we each had a Mayas taco: 1 cochinita pibil & 1 fish. Both were excellent. Served piping hot with fresh veggies & sauces. For mains I had chuleta de cordera: lamb chop, medium rare, as tender as I’ve ever had, very tasty, and a side of broccolini. My wife had Empanadas de Maya with shrimp. Total for 2 with 20% tip came in under $125. Service, food, atmosphere were all excellent- we’ll be back.
Loved everything we ordered. The quesadilla was slightly under-seasoned but the meat was incredibly tender. The flan was also delicious.

Cantina Los Mayas was really good. The waiters and chef were genuinely kind, friendly, and welcoming, and the overall vibe made the experience even better. Portions are big and the prices are very budget-friendly, so it felt like great value.

We started with the ceviche—it was spicy, but super balanced with a fresh pineapple-lime flavor that made it bright and refreshing. We also ordered the queso fundido, and it was a highlight: a creamy, milky blend of cheeses with chorizo, and I loved the little candle underneath that kept it warm the whole time.

For my main dish, I got the mariscos served in a pineapple. It hit that perfect sweet-and-spicy combo, and the two roasted shrimp were honestly so delicious. I just wish it came with a few more shrimp, but overall the rest of the seafood was filling and satisfying.

The only thing I was expecting a bit more from was the salsas—I hoped for stronger flavor and more heat. That said, they were still good.

Also, the location is great and easy to find, and parking nearby was pretty easy, which made the whole night even smoother.

The food is absolutely outstanding here and very unique:

Pipián con pato - cannot be missed
Chef spicy salsa - fabulous, especially the chocolate sauce
Ceviche crudo península with salsa negra - amazing
Pollo con mole - very very good
Sikil Pak - wouldn’t get again

The molcajete also looked great.

The ambiance is great - main room totally works for a date, the back room is a bit off with the TV, but very nice.

The staff are fantastic and very helpful when ordering. I also love the Mexican wine samplers.

Will be coming back for sure.

top_reviews.content:
You’ve got to try the sandwiches and loaded fries at Crave Subs! This fun, comic-book-themed sub shop serves incredible, complex subs that are fascinating and delightful. They make sub sandwiches like you may have never seen before—thick, complex, beautiful, gooey, and oh so tasty. The many yummy layers of each sandwich stack together to become works of art in their own right.

The contrast between different textures and flavors comes in perfect harmony, creating sandwiches that are overpoweringly delicious. These are not just your typical sandwiches; instead, they are culinary masterpieces, carefully crafted for maximum deliciousness.

The sandwiches come on quality bread and are smothered in this delectable Crave Sauce and filled with fresh lettuce and tomato. You can choose from different types of bread, including gluten-free, Dutch Crunch, and more. The gluten-free bread tastes great (the lack of gluten does not translate to a lack of taste); in fact, it tastes delicious.

There’s also a nice variety of fillings available. They have vegan, vegetarian, and meat subs. It seems every sandwich is stuffed to the maximum with fillings and flavor. You cannot go wrong here, but I recommend you try: The Patrick Star, a next-level fried chicken sandwich with Korean barbecue sauce and pepperjack cheese, the Pikachu, a mouth-watering grilled chicken sub with just a bit of kick, and the Buzzlightyear, which is the ulitmate turkey-pesto combination!

Not to be overlooked are the scrumptious loaded fries. Delicious, salty curly fries come smothered in cheese, meat, and sauce to create a beautiful symphony of flavor and texture. The Wolverine and Goku Black fries are particularly satisfying, and I highly recommend them!
Been there multiple times. The food is good. The boom boom sauce, and the fries tastes great. Chicken, not so much imo. Try it.

First time trying Crave Subs in downtown Berkeley and it was an amazing experience! The sandwiches are top-tier—super fresh, flavorful, and the portions are great. I also love that they have an ice cream place right there; it's the perfect way to end the meal.
​The staff was incredibly welcoming and made me feel right at home. If you're in Berkeley, you definitely need to check this place out. 10/10!"

TLDR:
Overall: My top place to eat at Berkeley
My Order: Usually Tom & Jerry, Chicken Little, or Patrick Star - all are very good. Dutch Crunch is my go-to
Price Breakdown: Usually $16-$17 per sub. A bit pricey, but they do not skimp on the meat and the portions are huge!
Portions: One normal sized sub is so incredibly filling, I'm either stuffed or I end up with left overs.
Halal/Vegetarian Friendly: Meat is halal and they have vegetarian/vegan options.
Would get again: 100% absolutely, I have to physically restrain myself from coming here every day.

This place is absolutely phenomenal, I would eat here all the time if I could. I've already been here more timrd than I can count. Halal with so many options, and the subs are so juicy and addicting! Anytime a friend visits Berkeley, I take them here by default and each of them have begged to come back. Definitely a messy eat and a bit on the pricier side, but with the portion size and how flavorful each sub is, it is absolutely worth it. The balance of the tang, sweet, and savory is perfect every time yet varied enough that it feels like a fresh experience every visit. Will note that the wait time is usually a bit long, I either order first and then hang out at Half Price or order on snackpack abt 15 minutes before I get there. The shop itself is very vibey and uniquely comic book themed, making this such a fun spot to visit.

It was about $75 total for the meal for three.  It's a bit on the pricier side, but everything was amazing.  PLUS: There's a yummy ice cream shop that shares the same location.

I recently picked up a lunch order from Joodooboo in North Oakland, and the entire experience was fantastic from start to finish. I placed my order online a few days in advance, which was incredibly easy and stress-free. When I arrived, the pickup took literally seconds, and finding free, easy street parking right around the corner made the quick stop completely hassle-free. The clerk at the counter was also incredibly friendly and efficient.

There was a lovely neighborhood energy outside, with plenty of people enjoying their meals at the outdoor sidewalk tables, and it was bustling inside as well. Everything was carefully packaged for the ride home, keeping all the hot and cold components perfectly fresh and separated.

The meal itself is beautifully put together and highlights just how fresh and high-quality their ingredients are. The creamy tofu is exceptional—it has a delicate, crispy exterior with absolutely no oiliness, breaking away to a perfectly soft, velvety center. The seasonal banchan sides offer wonderful, clean flavors that bring a perfect balance of color and taste to the plate. It is an incredibly satisfying, complete meal that comes with the main tofu, a beautifully textured multi-grain rice, a comforting side soup, and fresh sides like the sweet corn and green salad.

Everything from the packaging to the cooking was executed beautifully. I highly recommend checking them out if you're looking for a top-tier, vegetable-forward meal in the East Bay.

I ordered the Nori Acorn Noodle Bowl and also tried the Fried Dooboo Set. I liked the acorn noodle bowl more; the chilled noodles, nori vinaigrette, kimchi, and pickled mushrooms made it super refreshing and flavorful. Their house tofu was silky, delicate, and packed with fresh soy flavor. It's a must-try. Portions are on the lighter side for the price.

The only downside was the ordering system. We came on a busy Saturday evening, and having everyone order before being seated made the front area crowded and a little chaotic. Seating was limited.

super healthy and quick casual restaurant after a long day in the winery estates. the fried tofu set was delicious, and the banchan went very well. loved the umami seaweed seasoning on the acorn noodles, they were bouncy in texture. red makgeolli paired well too!

Came for a pop-up menu they had with Bazaar Sonoma, and all the food was great. Variety of food and drinks are great and everything is on theme and authentic. Definetely will stop by again if Im in the area and if you want to buy tofu, this is the place to buy it for sure.

top_reviews.content:
Gusto is a locally owned small business that proudly brings authentic Algerian cuisine to downtown Berkeley for prices that the average person can afford. The owner is a kind man who loves his restaurant and really cares about brightening his customers' days. I am proud to support this new local business in its effort to allow Berkeley to try some fantastic Algerian food!

I think the best part is the slightly charred, carefully spiced, succulent Algerian meats. I liked the chicken and beef shawara bowls, but this was my first time trying Marguez, and I was completely blown away by the deliciousness. The chicken and beef shawarma bowls came with delightfully fresh vegetables, but the Marguez sandwich (which you've got to try) had this amazing balance between sauce, flavorful meat, fresh veggies, and the wrap it came in, plus it came with a nice portion of fries that had a bit of sauce of their own. The beef tongue sandwich was also amazing in a similar way. The Tajine plate lamb and the Joojeh Sultani are also great options, especially if you want something very substantial.

The Algerian sodas from the cooler are so enticing here. I really liked the one that tasted like carbonated lemonade, but there was also a really good one that tasted kind of like licorice. Definitely give them a try; they are so worth it!

And don't forget dessert. At the counter you pay at, you will see some amazing desserts on display. The Makrut (this pillowy doughnut-like pastry) and the baklava are delicious and a perfect way to end the meal!

The eating experience is super casual, and the ambiance is friendly and informal. It's pretty fun trying to catch a glimpse of the magic happening in the kitchen while you sit in the eating area, which is a little sparse and kind of simple but very fitting for a nice, laid-back place to eat alone or dine with family and friends. I love this place!

Its my first time trying Algerian cuisine here, and honestly it was a great experience!

We tried here the kebab plate which has lamb and chicken, both were tender, juicy,full of flavor and must important prepared fresh right infront.

also had their signature couscous pot, which was such a highlight for me. It’s a hearty, warm, and comforting dish with lamb, beef sausages, and chicken, all halal as confirmed by the owner.
It was rich, satisfying, and I can see why so many people around us were ordering the same dish.

The chicken shawarma wrap was also very good juicy, well-seasoned, and honestly stood out compared to other local shawarma spots

And I’ telling you their traditional sweets are not to be missed its absolutely delicious!
My favorite was the white one coated with a light lemon-dusted powder (I think). It was so well-balanced, fresh not overly sweet.

Overall, it’s a great addition to Berkeley. I would definitely recommend it and would revisit again

Absolutely phenomenal addition to the neighborhood serving authentic Algerian food and Persian kabobs. The owner is delightful and very passionate. The food is cooked perfectly and represents both cultures well.

top_reviews.content: The chicken is amazing! Usually I don't like fried wings because they are dry and mostly greasy, but these are so good, not greasy at all just chock full of flavor! The galbi recipe is so flavorful,and the coke slaw is hella good too! You can sit outside and enjoy the view of the Oakland hills and people watch. Enthusiastic two thumbs up!

Fantastic! Actually I suggested that they develop cheese balls at early July when ordering Uber Eats and they replied to me and they really developed it now!!! I feel deeply touched and I dined in today with my boyfriend (ordering cheese balls for sure) That’s amazing! Staff are friendly, too!

This place actually catered an event at my apartment building in Jack London, and the food was so good that my friends and I decided we had to visit the restaurant for lunch. I’m so glad we did!

We ordered the Original, Spicy Original, Honey Garlic, Gangnam Style, potstickers, and the Rose Ddeok-bokki. The Honey Garlic wings were hands down my favorite—they were perfectly crispy, flavorful, and had just the right balance of sweet and savory. The Original and Spicy Original were also really good, and the Gangnam Style didn’t disappoint either. The only thing I wouldn’t order again is the Rose Ddeok-bokki. It just wasn’t for me.

The only downside is the price. An 8-piece order of wings is about $18, which is definitely on the expensive side. That said, the quality of the food makes it worth treating yourself every now and then.

The restaurant itself is really cute, with a few outdoor tables and a small bar ledge inside if you want to dine in. The customer service has always been friendly whenever I’ve visited. Just keep in mind that the food is made fresh, so it usually takes about 20–30 minutes. Don’t go in super hungry unless you’re okay with waiting, or better yet, place your order ahead of time and take it to go.

Overall, this is a great spot if you’re craving delicious Korean fried chicken. I’ll definitely be back, especially for those Honey Garlic wings!

It's SO GOOD. We got 3 orders of wings, two bone-in and one boneless. The flavors we got were galbi, soy garlic, and gangnam style, plus regular fries and sweet potato fries.

I love Korean fried chicken and this was excellent. Light, mega crispy, flavorful sauces. Yes. When asked which was my favorite flavor, at the end of the meal, It was simply impossible to choose. I love soy sauce flavor and I love garlic and their sauc is delicious. I had expected the galbi to be insipid and oversweet, since that is not uncommon, but it was really delicious and had a very nice, unexpected smokiness to it. Would I like it to be a little bit less sweet? Yes. But would I order it next time? Also yes. The one I got was the Gangnam style, with a peppery sauce and some chilies on it. I loved the black pepper in there.

I want to particularly note that their boneless wings were surprising and wonderful. Normally when you get boneless wings, you get a nugget sized chunk of meat with bearing and sauce. There's not a strong sense of chicken to the whole thing. But these "wings" were large and a bit flat, slathered with sticky, smoky galbi sauce. First you get this burst of flavor followed quickly by layers of shatter-crisp batter and then your teeth sink into a satisfaction of tender meaty goodness. This is such a far cry from the usual boneless wing they don't even deserve to be called the same thing.

We also got an order of regular fries and an order of sweet potato fries. They were both delicious but for me the sweet potato fries were, hands down, the winner. I have a tendency to prefer sweet potato fries to regular fries anyway, though, so I'm biased, but my dinner companions very much enjoyed the regular fries and were surprised to find that they liked the sweet potato ones since they normally don't. I feel like there was a bit of cinnamon or something in them, that made them extra tasty.

I would also like to particularly note that they were unstintingly generous with their pickled radish. One of my friends is a pickled radish fiend and bemoans the limited amount she normally receives at other places. Here she was told that she could have as much as she wished, and her wishes were granted, with warm smiles and fast service.

I'm definitely going back. Lovely food, lovely service. Highly recommend.

I had a fantastic experience at bbq Chicken
in Oakland! The chicken was incredibly crispy, juicy, and packed with flavor. Every bite tasted fresh, and the sauces were absolutely delicious. The staff was friendly, welcoming, and made sure our order was prepared perfectly. The restaurant was clean, and the food was definitely worth the wait. If you’re looking for some of the best Korean fried chicken in the Bay Area, this is the place to go. I’ll definitely be coming back to try more flavors. Highly recommend!

top_reviews.content:
Michelin Recommended!!

What Chef Mark has achieved with his menu at That’s My Jam is nothing short of remarkable. I used to own a restaurant and I have brought other restaurateurs and hospitality executives to also come try the food at That’s My Jam.

Don’t take my word for it… do your self a favor and go try this lovely local San Francisco gem. I swear it’s Michelin recommended to me.

We came to the spot on March 14th around 10:30 a.m. . It was a group of three people.

We were very fortunate because when we got there we only had to wait maybe 10 minutes as three parties had left when we had arrived and they were getting the tables ready.

The space itself was very cute. There were flowers along the wall on the right hand side, the that's my jam signage near the kitchen was very well done, and I'm not going to lie the HR representative twiggy was adorable. You can find her by the restrooms if she is taking her nap.

One call out for our table they did see this towards the right near the flower wall at this round table that was meant to seat potentially for people. I call that out because if we had a fourth person they would have been seated right in the middle of the walkway and wouldn't have any room to move because the walkway isn't very large as table is right next to it.

Said differently the space near the wall can get a bit crowded so you just want to be mindful of the seating arrangement.

The items we ordered while we were there were the turmeric iced painted Lady drink, a carafe of white wine, and one of the herbal teas.  For the food itself we got the baguette breakfast sandwich, the avocado toast, and Pain Pe Du Du Jour.

For the drinks, we all did agreed that you couldn't really taste the turmeric inside of the painted Lady drink. So we did ask for another shot of turmeric to be added which did help it but even so more tumor could have been put into the drink.

For the food items both the baguette breakfast sandwich and the avocado toast were okay. The items that were in the sandwich or on the avocado toast were generally good but they weren't blending together and what we recognized was that both items didn't have enough of a salt component.  I asked for salts and put it on both of those items and then you could really taste the flavors better but still it was not combining them it just let me taste a little bit more of the egg or the avocado.

For the baguette sandwich besides salt it also needed a little bit more of a fat component, say butter on the bread or maybe a type of aioli or cream sauce, it just wasn't again melding together it felt like all the pieces were trying to have their own moment in your mouth.

The star of the show was definitely the last item Pain Perdu Du Jour.  All three of us agreed that it had the most balanced flavors and it was nice to be able to dip it within the different jams that were on the plate.

Overall the food was generally good but we were underwhelmed with the baguette sandwich and the avocado toast.
Highly recommend that’s my jam! All the dishes were created so thoughtfully and had so many unique flavors. Owners were super nice and had decent vegetarian and vegan options.

Unfortunately, the main food was quite disappointing. The steamed chicken momos were extremely oily, with a strong stale-oil smell, and the chutney wasn’t particularly impressive. We also tried pork sekuwa, which had a nice smoky, char-grilled flavor, but again, everything was excessively oily and seemed to have been cooked in old oil. Overall, we were disappointed, especially after seeing so many positive reviews. The food might have potential, but the quality of the oil completely overshadowed everything we tried and left a lingering unpleasant taste and smell. Definitely not the experience we were expecting.

What a lovely experience for a chill date night with my hubby. There was a live band lighting up the atmosphere with beautiful notes and jazzy vibes. Our server was warm and friendly, providing us with on point food recommendations and even a nice movie recommendation. I can't wait to visit again on another date night or even with my kid (since they have such a broad menu).

What a gem! We stumbled upon this place by accident, and I’m so glad we did. Everything was absolutely delicious. It was so good that I’m already planning to come back before flying home. Every dish came out looking beautiful and tasted just as amazing. Can’t wait to return!

top_reviews.content: Love the vibe at Om Sabor. We come here every so often. The food is delicious, especially the nachos and the samosa. And the desserts are pretty amazing. My wife loves the live music. Definitely recommend.

All vegan menu is a big W
We got Mac and cheese, empanada and chowder. Empanada was top notch. Others were pretty good. I’ll definitely go here to try other stuff.
I wouldn’t recommend the chai cocktail though. It was hot. It’s not for everyone.

This is a nice cute bar in SF that serves vegan food. The food is delicious though a bit expensive but probably on par with the area. I had the flautas and clam chowder and it was delicious. The server was very nice and helped me pick items as well. It is a bit loud but there's live music deeper in so I can't really say I did not expect it. I would definitely sit outside of that area if you want to speak with friends. Space is a bit tight and I saw a line forming as I left so it's definitely a popular spot. I'll definitely be back if I'm in the area.
Small portion sizes but rly good vegan food. Clam chowder was mushroomy, I liked the nachos more (jackfruit “meat” and sauces - the chips were so good)

We hit Om Sabor for happy hour and walked away seriously impressed.

The flautas were a standout right out of the gate: crispy, flavorful, and authentically done.

The barbacoa tacos were a big win for my husband. For me, the texture leaned a bit mushy, but the flavor still delivered.

Same story with the ceviche tostadas: he loved them, while I’m just not as into cold entrées, but they were undeniably fresh and authentic.

Then came dessert and wow, they absolutely knocked it out of the park with the Black Forest cheesecake. Easily the highlight. Rich, balanced, and just indulgent enough. The blueberries and strawberries paired beautifully with the cheesecake and elevated the whole dish. One small note: the microgreens on top added color, but the texture and flavor felt out of place. A different garnish could take it from great to perfect.

Friendly, attentive service tied everything together, rounding this up to a five-star experience.

top_reviews.content: If Cocobreeze is at an event, we order from them every time! Our go to is the 2 protein plate with vegan spicy jerk chicken and vegan curry chicken and a cup of the sweet sorrel.
