This restaurant is family run, Black woman owned, you can see 4 generations hard at work here.

Such an amazing spot. You feel like part of the family here. Such a friendly team Also, Their vegan options are delicious. We got the vegan fish with veggies, and jerk jackfruit. Yummy! The jackfruit was spicy, but delicious. The fish had a bbq flavor. The red beans and rice was exactly what I’ve been craving. We also got a side of greens which helped mellow out the spicyness. The sweet lady that took our order was SO incredible, she had the most amazing energy. The receipt said her name was Merissa. Also at one point the chef acknowledged us for the wait, which was so nice, and she really didn’t need to do that! Afterall Valentine’s Day is so busy, but I appreciate the thoughtfulness. Everything was absolutely amazing. I come from SJ for this perfect spot, and I plan to be back!

I was so pleased to find Chef Ann and Coco Breeze during my sister’s most recent visit from Trinidad. Authentic environment is an understatement! The pictures on the wall were the same we grew up with and the whole vibe was very Trini. Chef Ann went above and beyond to make us feel welcome. My favorite of the authentic food was the pholourie and tamarind sauce. I will be back soon.

I wanna talk about how special this mother and daughter are what they bring to the community is irreplaceable. Thank you for your dedication. Thank you for your commitment. Thank you for your delicious food and thank you for the vibes today. I attended the Caribbean heritage festival downtown at the Oak stop venue and it was fantastic. Had the best time really appreciate the opportunity. Thank you for inviting us and I wish you much success and continued success for the future.

Small spot with 3 tables, 1 indoor and 2 outside. I got take away. Two veggie patties and a seamoss drink. The drink was blended fresh on the spot for me and was very tasty! The pattie were heated and placed in foil to keep warm. Later on when I ate the patties the crust was flaky, the seasonings were plentiful, and the veggies were a good mix. As I mentioned this isn't a sit down service type of spot as there is very limited seating available. However the inside is decorated to give you the feeling of Trinidad, where the owner is from. There are plenty of vegan and vegetarian options I am looking forward to trying more in the future!

I have been going to Sushi Park for 15 years since the first month they opened. This is my go to sushi spot throughout the entire Bay Area. I've tried countless other restaurants over the years and still feel nothing else compares to Sushi Park. The quality of fish is outstanding. Each roll, sauce, and arrangement is created by the staff. The service has always been amazing as well. They come to check on you regularly to get refills of water even when they are crowded. The head sushi chef Andy is also an amazing artist. He did the two paintings on the right wall as you come in!!

I will be going to this restaurant for the rest of my life. I go there for every birthday and special occasion.

If you need recommendations for starters I highly recommend the fried calamari, tempura mushroom, or/and salmon belly.

For Rolls I recommend the Double Sake, Samurai, Firecracker Ball, and Shiki.

For Vegetarians the fried mushroom starter is amazing as well as the veggie veggie and veggie tempura rolls.

We did takeout for a large group and the order was all correct and on time for pickup. The staff was so friendly and even gave us a small treat! Everyone loved their sushi and my shioyaki was delicious and HUGE. Great experience all around and will be a regular!

I have been coming to this restaurant since they opened 16+ years ago. The food is always fresh and delicious. My whole family loves it! Abi and Andy are great hosts and the whole crew of peole working there are friendly. I wish they were open for lunch time during the week as it used to be. Still my favorite sushi place!

top_reviews.content:
Beautiful restaurant and amazing food. Each dish was very delicious.

Our favorites were the beef salad and the pumpkin slices. Surprisingly the pumpkin was the star. Very crispy and the sauce that comes with it is a nice tough. Great appetizer you should get.

Beef salad hits all the notes a Thai dish should hit. Would recommend this as well.

Vibes were great here. Great music and they have a fully stacked bar. Perfect for a weekend night

I've been wanting to try this restaurant for a while, and I finally got the chance to check it out!

I started with the Tom Yum cocktail, made with rum, apple juice, lime, chili, and lemongrass. It was refreshing, flavorful, and delicious.

For the entrées, we ordered the Avocado Green Curry and the Pad Kee Mao. We asked for spicy, and they delivered! The Pad Kee Mao was packed with flavor, and the portion was decent.

It was my first time having avocado in Thai curry, and it worked really well. The curry was rich and flavorful, and the chunks of avocado were tasty.

Overall, a fantastic meal, and I will definitely be back!

The food was AMAZING! The riceberry rice is such a unique experience. Pad sew is 1000/10, Thai Thea good but very sweet.
Pad Thai 6/10, sticky rice is perfect.

Overall decent Thai food at Yimm. Both their flat noodle to pad kee mao/drunken noodle and the side thin noodle were well cooked to give the al dente chewy texture. Another highlight was the seasoning of the pad kee mao - tasteful and right-on-spot spicy.

That being said, there's plenty of room left to be desired. Both the chicken and beef we ordered were well overcooked, dry, rubbery, and plain. While the Tom Yum soup was spicy and sour, it lacked the authentic flavor from lemongrass and other herbs. The acidity was also too pungent to be enjoyable. Also wish their staff can be more friendly than the minimum service.

Not bad, really appreciated how it was not as oily like many other Thai restaurants. Would say the curries are spicier than the usual Thai places here, which I liked.

However, the portions (especially the soups) are on the smaller side for the price. Also I saw people recommended Lord’s noodles but it was honestly kind of average, the pork belly was dry and flavorless. But the avocado green curry is really good, spicy and creamy.

top_reviews.content:
My daughter and I were glad that we decided to try out this place with authentic rice noodles, and many delicacies such as marinated pig ear, beef tripe, and marinated pig intestines, that one usually does not find on the menus of everyday conventional Asian restaurants. The atmosphere is upbeat and casual, with many local parents and grandparents bringing their children for a solid Chinese meal.

Located in the Sunset District at the intersection of 19th Street and Travaval Street, the restaurant is easy to find, and street parking is generally available. The locals of the area seem to frequent this place.

My daughter and I found our entrees succulent and healthful. We each enjoyed the cucumber salad (pictured below).

The menu offers a wide variety of options, including many marinated beef and chicken options with rice noodles.

If you’re looking for authentic Guilin rice noodles in San Francisco, this place is a gem! The broth is rich and flavourful, the noodles are perfectly chewy, and the toppings are fresh and generous. Portion sizes are very fair for the price (great value around $10–20).

The staff are friendly and quick, and even when it’s busy, service feels smooth and welcoming. The restaurant is clean and casual, making it a comfortable spot for either a quick bite or a full meal.

Definitely a place I’d come back to whenever I’m in the city.

This is our go-to for guilin style rice noodles. We get takeout here at least once a month. The dry version travels better and comes with a small side of soup. Everything is very flavorful and the noodle texture is just right it's a bit chewy and bouncy.

It is a bit expensive for a simple dish but that's the price you pay for living in the bay area.

The parking around the area is limited. We visited on a Sunday afternoon, and the waitlist was incredibly long. We ended up ordering takeout, but still had to wait 20-30 minutes. We ordered the Cucumber Salad with Minced Garlic, House Special GRN, Hot and Sour Noodle Soup, and Marinated Combination Plate.

Unfortunately, the cucumber salad was bland, and the sauce was not good either. Similarly, the combination plate was quite dry. On a positive note, the Hot and Sour Noodle Soup had a generous portion, and the flavor was authentically hot and sour. I didn't try other items from the menu, but based on what I ordered, I would say the food was decent, though not outstanding.

Our group of 5 got seated shortly before they closed. We ordered and got our food soon. You can speak Cantonese or Mandarin here I think.
The staff were really fun with us and replying to us even though we spoke lots of broken mandarin. Parking around here isn't too bad.

The portion sizes of what we ordered were all really good. Some of the stuff kinda spicy if you're bad with spice so just watch out. Meat is really good, just wish their were more!

Overall great experience. Thanks!

google.name: Pomet
google.address: 4029 Piedmont Ave, Oakland, CA 94611, United States

top_reviews.content:
An incredible farm-to-table dinner at Pomet that completely shows off why it’s a powerhouse on the East Bay dining grid. The kitchen balances pristine ingredient sourcing with serious technical execution across every course.

Seasonal House Kombucha: A fantastic way to kick off the meal. It was crisply effervescent and super refreshing, with a clean acidity that served as the perfect palate cleanser before the richer dishes arrived.

Hokkaido Milk Bread Rolls: The texture on these rolls was insanely soft and pillowy, and the flavor was spot on. That said, it does lean a bit pricey for what is ultimately a baseline bread course.

Marinated English Peas & Fava Beans: I’m typically not a big fan of goat cheese, but this dish completely won me over. The local Andante Dairy goat cheese was incredibly creamy and acted as the perfect canvas for the bright, hyper-fresh spring flavors of the peas and fava beans. An excellent starter.

Ugly Mushroom Caramelle: This dish absolutely lives up to all the local hype. The candy-wrapped pasta shapes were cooked perfectly, holding in a rich, flawless mushroom filling. The texture was incredibly satisfying, but the real star was the morel miso sauce—an amazing, umami-dense pool of deep, earthy flavors.

Squid Ink Tagliatelle: An excellent seafood dish that I absolutely loved. The jet-black squid ink ribbons had that textbook al dente bite, tossing beautifully with a very generous amount of sweet, tender chunks of fresh Dungeness crab. The lemongrass chili butter sauce was perfectly emulsified and coated every strand flawlessly.

Klingeman Farms Pork Chop: A masterclass in wood-fired cooking. Pomet serves their heritage chop pre-sliced, and the kitchen absolutely nailed the temperature. It was exceptionally juicy, uniform, and not dry at all. The seasoning on the hearth-grilled crust was amazing, giving it a deep, savory edge. This is easily one of the best pork chops I’ve had in a very long time.

Chocolate Mousse Torte: This arrived with a bit of a structural comedy of errors—as the waitress set it down, the ice cream scoop lost its traction on the ultra-sleek, glossy mirror glaze and slid right off the top into the caramel. But honestly? The dish tasted so amazing it didn't even matter. The chocolate filling had a superb, dense richness that paired beautifully with the sweet caramel pool and the earthy crunch of the cacao nib clusters.

Sticky Toffee Pudding: Absolute technical perfection. The airy sponge cake was deeply saturated with a warm, rich toffee glaze, delivering a flavor profile that tasted exactly like what you get natively in England. It was outstandingly good, incredibly comforting, and easily one of the dessert highlights of the year.

Pomet is the real deal. While the bread service is a bit premium, the absolute precision across the pasta program, the legendary pork chop, and the stellar dessert lineup make it an absolute must-visit. Perfect for high-intent diners looking for elite wood-fired cooking.

you may or may not have heard that this bar, a long-standing oakland countercultural hub, has been through a lot of trouble in the last year or two because the legitimacy of one of its past construction projects was thrown into question. well, i believe the drama regarding the dubious "patio" space at eli's exemplifies not only a problem with the bar itself (on a level worthy of impacting any review of the establishment) but one with the punk movement in general, which we should all be old enough at this point to talk about (i do know there are gen z punks, but this particular conversation is for millennials and gen x for now). here's the thing: you can't "DIY attitude" your way out of complying with local regulations that exist for the preservation of health and safety. yeah, there's a lot of bureaucratic obstacles needlessly slowing down projects, and you can fight for reform on that, but you do unfortunately need to do it through slow, boring, above-board avenues. you can't just put up potentially unsafe or improperly ventilated structures and call them "good enough" when we live in a society where a basic level of trust is assumed by anyone walking through your doors. the stubborn aloofness underlying the way this bar operates is not cool, actually, and insistence to the contrary is related to elements of what it means to be punk that people don't seem to want to talk about. it's very true and important that specific music subcultures have been at the forefront of social change across the country and particularly in oakland. but let's be real: both the aesthetic trappings and the social ideals of these movements reduce with dangerous ease into layers of self-pastiche, and over time, the parts that had value can become buried under cartoonish antisociality. at their worst, music subcultures represent a selection of maladjusted weirdos brought together by a love for particular drugs. in the case of punks, the drug in question is unquestionably nicotine. now, i will confess that i actually still have a cigarette from time to time, though i don't really know why, so it is with swiftly decreasing regularity. it's not just the potential hypocrisy that stops me from wanting to tell other people what to do with their bodies, though; i genuinely think that people should have a high degree of personal freedom and that this is what makes our country a special place. however, if you are going to build a patio to smoke on, you have to do it properly, because you do in fact need to give a damn about other human beings you are sharing this city with. what you also do need to do is have an ACTUAL patio. i'm not sure what the status is now, but last time i was here, the former patio was still mostly closed off, and instead the bar was operating an almost-entirely-enclosed space with some limited opening of the ceiling, where i basically felt like i had stepped back into the nineties when indoor smoking was still legal. i went home with stale cigarette odor permeating my jacket and gloves despite personally never touching one, and i felt disgusting. secondhand smoke is a very real health risk, and it needs to be taken seriously. people should be able to go to a bar and have a drink without being exposed to that, and anyone who thinks otherwise is clinging on to the absolute worst that counterculture has on offer. listen, i still love punks. i have had nice times at eli's. the bartenders are kind. they make ok drinks, and this is the sort of place where if they made a drink that was more than ok, that might count as a point against it. but the overall attitude of the owners needs to change significantly if this bar doesn't want to develop a reputation as an embarrassment to the scene.

Our top picks!! aka what I’d order every time. (I always take photos but totally forgot this time, I was so focused on eating)
- oyster mushroom skewers (small, not king oyster)
- pork ribs skewer 烤油边 (juicy and tender)
- fried mantou bun with condensed milk (INSAAANELY GOOD! we lost our minds. perfectly crispy outside, perfectly fluffy inside)
- sweet corn skewer (on the chewier side, similar texture to 糯玉米)
- roasted eggplant (so soft, great veg option)
- cold shredded tofu skin 凉拌豆皮丝 & smashed cucumber 凉拌黄瓜 (veg palate cleansers, comes piled high with cilantro FYI)

Spice level: by default, expect all the skewers to be coated in the same blend of aromatic spices (cumin, Sichuan/mala peppercorn, maybe five spice). Each table has extra bottles of powdered spice if you want to turn up the heat even more.

Next time I want to try the tinfoil egg tofu. The bacon-wrapped enoki is also a crowd favorite, looking around the room!

PS the service is efficient, the door signs & menus are bilingual English & Chinese, the bathrooms are well maintained, plus the music is a vibe & not too loud. I hope this restaurant will always be here!

The wrappers were cooked to the right texture, not too thick, but not too thin that they didn't break when picked up with chopsticks. The fillings were well seasoned and had a comforting, home-cooked feel, making them a great option for a quick meal.

I even bought three bags of frozen dumplings to take home. Each bag comes with 18 dumplings, which is a really good value. Highly recommended!

The dumplings were delicious, and the cold appetizers were authentic and had a wonderful homemade flavor. This is definitely a must-try spot in the East Bay!

The beef noodle soup ordered by the table next to us also looked amazing, so I’ll definitely try it next time. Highly recommended!

What's unique about this dumpling place is that the food is clean and beautifully made. Not a fancy decorating or anything, but the food is properly treated so it looks beautiful: no grease, no tough pieces, no residues on top of the soup. Even the fried dishes are so light. Given the bib gourmand, this place is not busy and it is definitely approachable. I would love to eat here again.

Best experience ever! We were visiting San Francisco on Easter Day and happened to be near Golden Gate Park, looking for something to eat. We were so happy to find this little charming place.

First of all, thank you for being open on a holiday. As a business owner myself, I truly understand how hard that can be, and it means so much.

Thank you for making our Easter Day in the park so memorable. We can’t wait to come back and try your meat lasagna!

Always a great time here! The owner, Katarina, is so funny and welcoming! Love her high energy & fun vibes! The food here absolutely smacks! All the sandwiches are deliciously crafted, and have very unique flavor profiles. I definitely reccomend  the house smoked turkey brisket sandwich, and Bill’s Spicy Pastrami. The turkey brisket is smoked perfectly. The spicy pastrami has a delicious mango habanero sauce that isn’t too overpowering or spicy, but offers a nice sweetness to the saltiness of the sandwich. They also serve salads, and pasta, but the lasagna is the winner for me! It takes 4 days to prep the lasagna to absolute perfection, and is sooo meaty. I will definitely be back for more lasagna, the other delicious menu items, and great vibes! :)

Got 3 sandwiches and spaghetti. Prices are great for how big portions are. Best sandwich I’ve had, and great to support local spots. The owner and workers are SO friendly and inviting. Would recommend to come over and over again.

Pot Stickers: 9/10 With all the good reviews on this, I had high expectations. It is still really really good. Very Crispy and good flavor, I just thought it would be better. (picture included)

Orange chicken: 10/10 My favorite out of them all, very very good. Amazing texture, so so yummy. 100000% recommend.

Mongolian beef: 9/10 Very good. Rich flavor. Definitely recommend.

Sweet and Sour pork: 7/10 Good texture but something in the sauce was a bit unexpected, although it was still overall pretty good. (picture included)

Kung Pao chicken: 7/10. Very spicy, beware.

Beef chow fun: 7/10 exactly how you’d think it would taste like

Service (7/10) was less than ideal as the one server was sitting at her desk watching shows at a loud volume. Wish she paid a tad bit more attention to a party of 9.
Salt & pepper pork was delicious and only like $12, would recommend!

Very good Chinese cuisine. The pt stickers were so good and filling. The Beef Chow Fun was so delicious and felt home cooked. The duck was so succulent, juicy, flavorful and delicious. The white rice balanced it.
Very happy to have found such good food.

I have been coming here for over 2 years and enjoyed the food and had not had an issue until today but I am very disappointed because I found a dead roach in my to go food. It was in the bottom so I had already eaten some but now I feel like throwing up. This is completely gross and unacceptable.

(I call directly so they get the whole sale.)

We went here yesterday, and for 7 plates 2 of which were combos it was about $65.  Which is a steal nowadays.

1. Tocino/longanisa combo: Both items are delicious.   If you eat a lot of rice, I would recommend getting a plate of each.  Only because for $2.50 more you can get garlic rice and egg

4.  Smoked boneless bangus (tinapang):  My dad liked this one and said it was pretty good

Overall,  food was delicious and will be back soon.  Parking is a little tough.  I do recommend calling to place your order, that way you know they're open.

Whether you want some fried pork chops, tocino, or some fish, they always have each order come with fried rice, fried garlic, and an egg. Check it out if you’re in the area, you won’t regret it.

top_reviews.content: This is a small location by Lombard Street. They have very limited seating but they have delicious Bento and matcha's. Matcha is probably their bread and butter but I came here for the food and the food die not disappoint. Very fresh fish. Full of flavor, different textures that combine really well together. Definitely worth the price.

Tuesday in July, crowded inside small fast paced eatery with less than 10 seats and lots of to go pick up or deliveries. Parking was challenging, having to circle 5 blocks. No restroom, had to walk to nearby gas stations (lady at Shell was hesitant but nice)!
Matcha and one with red beans were yummy. The strong taste of matcha was mellowed out with cream so smooth makes you keep sipping away! Duck breasts already sold out before 12 noon, tried duck leg and it was tender and delicious. Waited 20 minutes for our order.
Next, will try Ebiko sushi boxes on Montgomery.

Komeya no Bento serves matcha using Marukyu Koyamaen, and the café was super busy when I visited, which already says a lot about how popular it is.

I tried both the Cream Cheese Matcha Latte and the Strawberry Matcha Latte. Personally, I preferred the Cream Cheese one because the creamy, slightly salty flavour paired so well with the rich matcha. I also really appreciated that they allow you to adjust the sweetness level.

Highly recommend!!! This was honestly the best matcha spot I tried in San Francisco.

I’m a bit conflicted about this place! On the bright side, they have one of the best matcha drinks in the Bay. Yup, I loved it. My strawberry matcha was smooth, rich, and clearly made with high-quality matcha. They’re popular for a reason!

Now for the things I didn’t like. They were super busy around noon, and somehow they completely forgot my order. I waited about 45 minutes for my food, thinking they were just busy with delivery orders. Then I noticed two groups who arrived well after me had already gotten their food (and almost finished their bento), and it finally clicked, they had forgotten my order. As soon as I told them, my food came out within 5 minutes. Okay, rookie mistake.

But then the bento wasn’t even good. I ordered the salmon with truffle soy sauce, and the salmon portion was tiny. The vegetable sides were bland, mashed potatoes are tasteless and lacked any flavor.

I’m disappointed, but at least their matcha absolutely served! So, will I come back? For the matcha, yes. For the food? Hell nah!

I’m low key obsessed with this place. I literally make a point to come here every time I’m in SF just for the ceremonial matcha. It’s so good… super smooth, not bitter, just perfect.

The bento boxes are next level. I always get the salmon with truffle oil and I think about it way too often. Everything tastes really fresh and just really well done.

It’s tiny, barely any seating, no bathroom, and there’s almost always a line plus a ton of DoorDash orders going out. The wait can be kinda long, not gonna lie, but the staff is working nonstop and hustling the whole time. You order on an iPad and they move as fast as they can.

Not the kind of place you go to hang out, but honestly always worth it.

top_reviews.content:
A Hidden Gem That Feels Like Home
If you’re searching for the best breakfast in Oakland, look no further — this place is it, and Hanna and Alex are the heart and soul behind every single bite.

The food is absolutely delicious. Every dish is made with care and intention — the kind of breakfast that reminds you what morning meals are supposed to taste like. You can taste the love in it, which sounds cliché until you actually experience it here.
And the service? Hanna and Alex bring a personal warmth to every table. They remember your name, check in with a smile, and make you feel genuinely welcomed. Service with love is the only way to describe it.
If you find yourself in Oakland — even passing through — make the time to visit. You won’t regret it. This is the kind of place that earns a permanent spot on your list and a story you’ll tell friends.
Absolutely worth every star. Don’t miss it.

Found Nib’s while looking for local breakfast places in Oakland. The fresh vegetarian omelette was amazing and Hannah and Alex really took care of us. I used to frequent Lunchbox as they have a solid variety of food options. Unfortunately when enjoying one of their hot plates I discovered an insect in my food. This is highly disturbing and concerning from any food establishment. Food containing fruits/vegetables should be thoroughly and carefully prepared to prevent insects, which may carry harmful diseases to humans, crawling about in the food. While mistakes do happen, I’m even more disappointed with Lunchbox’s response to the incident. They asked if I wanted my money back and showed an overall lack of concern, stating ‘that sometimes happens when we don’t wash our vegetables good enough’. I’m deeply concerned if you are routinely serving customers food with insects crawling inside of it. Hopefully this message will push Lunchbox to be more attentive when preparing food - nobody wants pay money to find nasty surprises in their cuisine.
Best sandwiches in the area. Been eating there practically everyday since I found the place. Highly recommend it

top_reviews.content: Such an authentic and really good Korean food restaurant in El Cerrito. Recommend making a reservation for large parties and of any size. It gets busy here even on weeknights. We made a reservation for 4 at 6pm on a Thursday and when we were leaving so many people were waiting. They have their own private parking lot and there is also street parking. Not too far of a walk from El Cerrito bart too. You order through the kiosk and that’s how you ask for more items and refills for banchan. Their banchan is so fresh and good! They have Galbijim (braised shortribs) and we like to add cheese and watch it get torched. We also got their galbitang, bossam, seafood pancake, and I wanted to try their fried chicken (regular and soy garlic). The dishes come with either regular or purple rice, we got one set of each. Service was great! They serve hot tea and water, sodas, beer, and soju too. I can’t wait to come back and try their cold buckwheat noodles and other items on the menu we didn’t get a chance to order!

Wanted to celebrate my birthday especially after coming back from Korea. It’s a new restaurant that was recommended to me by my sister in law especially since they had their own parking lot which was a plus. We ordered: Galbijin (Short Rib) one with cheese, and no cheese, Jeon (pan cake) one with onion and other with seafood, 16 piece fried chicken,Japchae, and Rose spicy Rice cake. My favorite: Galbijiin and fried chicken. Love the rice cake but not the spicy part. For drinks: Soyu peach and kloud beer to create a beer bomb just like the dramas.:).. It was awesome tasting for me. I would definitely come back.

One of the best Korean Restaurant in town. I ate with my 2 friends, and we ordered the Rose Galbi Jim. I really liked the spices and the soup of the galbi, blended really well with the mozzarella cheese. Moreover, the texture of the tteokbokki was so soft and tasty. At the same time, the portion of the Galbi was so big, we couldn’t finish it so we took some back home.
the other best part was that you could refill the banchan. Would recommend you to ask more for the tofu and kimchi, really mouthwatering. the waiter and waitress were kind and friendly, they served you fast.
we visited the restaurant quite late in the afternoon, so we didn’t need to queue since there were plenty tables. the parking area was big too.

Came to try dinner before but it was during soft opening time. Very busy at night so not as enjoyable. This time I came for lunch and much has changed. Service was quick and we are ordering from a ordering system right at the table. Would recommend trying the combo as you can have the best of both worlds (Korean BBQ and one other famous Korean dish like cold noodle). Definitely will return to try more good food next time!

Seafood pancake was also great! Fresh ingredients. Servers were also all super nice and accommodating. Overall a great experience!

top_reviews.content: Blown away! Sitting at the chef’s bar was an outstanding experience. The chef made recommendations; he is a true artist of his craft - what a delight to watch. The nigiri/sushi is classic with no frills, relying completely on the quality of the fish and the expertise of the chef. What a local gem!

Good selection of veggie, meat, noodles, and fish.

My favorite is the mentaiko udon. The basic sushi was all very good. I would order these again: tri tip, eggplant, brussel sprouts with apples. I would not get the pork ribs - it was nothing special

Found this highly-rated spot and it was fantastic. It's a wonderful fusion of traditional Japanese sushi and creative modern tapas. I loved their philosophy, which is even stated on the menu: they 'do not appreciate: FANCY ROLLS.' That's when you know they're serious about quality.

​Everything we tried was delicious, but the absolute standout was the Mentaiko Udon. It exceeded all expectations. It was incredibly fragrant, perfectly seasoned (not too salty), and rich without being heavy at all. A must-order!

​Another must-try is the Iku-uni-himo appetizer, which is a perfect bite of uni (sea urchin), monkfish liver (ankimo), and ikura (salmon roe). They finish it with a drizzle of truffle oil at the table. For the nigiri, the Scallop was the best we had—so fresh and sweet.

​Highly recommend this place. A true gem in the city!

Tucked away in a small, unassuming corner just off Valencia, Fenikksu is a true hidden gem. My friend and I were wandering the area, struggling to decide where to eat, when a sign on the restaurant's front door caught our eye. It read something along the lines of, "We do not serve fancy American sushi rolls." That was all we needed to see--we knew we had to try it.

Arriving right at opening, we were seated immediately and opted for the omakase. Our meal was prepared and served by what I can only assume was the head sushi chef, who was both attentive and efficient. The pacing was brisk but satisfying, allowing us to fully enjoy each bite without feeling rushed. As for the price, it was right in that sweet spot--neither too expensive nor too cheap--making it well worth the experience.

If you're looking for an excellent sushi spot near Mission and Valencia, Fenikksu is a must-visit. Highly recommended!

One of our favorite dining experiences of recent memory! The atmosphere is so cozy and the food is truly exceptional. Standouts included the mentaiko udon, gyoza, asparagus, kimchee pork, and anago tempura but truly everything was amazing

Absolutely phenomenal sushi at a reasonable enough price.

The Lion King is drenched in sauce which makes it seem like it won't be anything but sauce flavor, but the cooked fish comes through and it still tastes good with soy sauce added. That said, the sauce is a bit on the high side and I would prefer more flavor from the fish, but that's a small nitpick on an otherwise very good roll.

Toro nigiri is a dessert for me whenever I can get it. It's very expensive but my goodness if you haven't had it you must. No fish melts in your mouth like Toro. 9/10 experience for sure. Will absolutely be back if I'm in the area.

This Japanese restaurant impressed me from the very first bite.
The miso soup was beautifully crafted, offering a distinctive and refined flavor I had never encountered before. The edamame and green salad were fresh, light, and perfectly prepared.
The fresh oysters were exceptional — delicately spicy and remarkably fresh. Both the sake toro and hamachi toro surpassed my expectations, showcasing outstanding quality and balance. The sake don was equally impressive, rich yet elegant in flavor.
A chilled Sapporo beer completed the experience, enhancing the authentic taste of Japan.
I will certainly return — this restaurant is a true gem of Japanese cuisine in San Francisco. ❤️

The goma-ae was simple and very bonito forward which I enjoyed. Lastly, the saba nigiri was okay, but perhaps I would get a different nigiri next time.

The service was okay, nothing standout. Given that I sat at the counter and alone, I expected more conversation but we didn’t have many exchanges.

The menu has everything you are looking for. We started with Negro Modelos and their delicioso salsa. My wife ordered a Carne Asada burrito, (loved it!) and I ordered the Chile Verde Dinner, (Chile Verde is my acid test when I go to a new restaurant) and it was excellent! The sauce was perfectly seasoned and I detected a little heat.

I then ordered something I have always shied away from, like uni sushi and steak tartare. (I am now a huge fan of both, properly done right.) I went for a Lengua Taco. Yup a tongue taco.

Rosario, (who was great!) smiled as I told her this Gringo was a little afraid. It. Was. Killer. Tender, flavourful and eradicated all of my apprehensions. Sometimes you just have to go for it. (Still not a fan of elk heart. Just sayin'.) If you have never had Lengua this is the place to push your envelope.

Bottomline, this is a tiny place serving up big flavor. When in Orinda, do yourself a favor and check it out.

The food was Delicious!  If you like spicy food, I would definitely try the "La Dorada Picante" Quesadilla. It was packed full of flavor. The owner was extremely hospitable and the environment was enjoyable.  I will definitely be going back!

top_reviews.content:
Great spot for Chinese bbq open late!

The Chinese bbq is top notch, the other food is tasty but too garlicky and flavors are not too nuanced.

That said the Chinese bbq is the best thing there IMO. I had the chicken soft bone, lamb, chicken gizzard, mantou, enoki and all were 🔥.

The Korean fried chicken was not crispy enough. It came with Korean rice cakes and was in a sweet glaze.

If you like garlic, the eggplant and grilled oyster are quite nice, but have copious amounts of garlic.

The fish and mushroom dumplings tasted like store bought dumplings. The spicy wonton soup was hearty and wontons had quite a thin skin which was a +.

The sesame cold noodles were refreshing with cool cucumber slices and soft porous tofu. The chongqing small noodles were spicy, with pickled cowpea and roasted peanuts. Guaranteed to open up the sinus.

The ambience is meh. The service was very good even though there was a single waiter and he seemed a little overwhelmed.

Overall would visit again after a night of drinking.

Everything was so good but faves were lamb, beef, gizzard and whole eggplant!

A bit pricey since we weren’t very hungry and still spent ~$80 for 2 ppl (including tax and tip).

I’ve been coming to this restaurant for over four years. When they first opened, I used to eat here about twice a month. Over time, though, the food quality and value gradually declined, so I started coming back less and less. These days, I only stop by once every few months or even once every six months. Honestly, the main reason I still come back is because they’re open late.

Unfortunately, this visit confirmed why I don’t come here often anymore. The food was average and didn’t justify the price.

What really disappointed me was the payment policy. The menu prices add up exactly to the “Cash Price” on the receipt. Only after we finished our meal did we find out that paying with a credit card costs an additional 3.68%. I understand some businesses choose to pass along credit card processing fees, but this should be clearly disclosed before customers order. The “cash price” isn’t a discount, it’s simply the advertised menu price, while card users end up paying more than expected. Just be ware!

Pretty good overall! Some skewers will be better than others. The beef was absolutely delicious! It's got a hint of sweetness to it that paired really well. They're light on the spices, which I enjoyed; I'm here to eat meat, not drink crushed peppercorn. I'd avoid the oyster and sausages.

Exceptional service, decent pricing for the amount of food. Good skewer spot!

The best in SF! And please come in the weekend not in weekday!

I have been here 3 times, the first two times on a weekday night, and it was just OK (cold days, don’t know what to eat and just decided to have some light bbq), I don’t quite understand the high rating…but then the recent visit on a Sunday night was amazing!!! Everything was so amazing! Hot and really tasteful that I actually decided to leave a review!

top_reviews.content: One of the best Chinese spots in the East Bay, imo. Food here is excellent for lunch and dinner. Huge portions. Mouth watering tasty…. One of the best Chinese restaurants in the East Bay. This legendary restaurant in Elmwood serves delicious duck, pork, chicken, and vegetarian dishes. Large and reasonably priced dishes. Friendly and attentive staff. Indoor dining or take away.

Polished Setting, Uneven Fare

King Yen enjoys an ideal location on College Avenue with a bright, well-kept dining room and attentive service. The space is clean, welcoming, and clearly well-managed.

But while the atmosphere suggests elevated dining, the food rarely rises to the occasion. The Szechuan beef, though generously portioned and paired with a flavorful sauce, suffered from tough, low-quality meat—more leathery than tender. A prawn and vegetable stir-fry was better balanced and fresher, but still overpriced at $25.

Service is generally efficient, though there’s a noticeable shift in tone during the final half-hour before closing, with staff clearly eager to wrap up—a gesture at odds with Bay Area norms.

For diners seeking standout Chinese food in the area, Dumpling Express farther down College near Safeway and Philz is a stronger bet. Their handmade dumplings are excellent, the pricing is far more reasonable, and the surrounding options for drinks or coffee complete the experience.

King Yen has its strengths, but food quality and pricing leave it trailing better neighborhood alternatives.

top_reviews.content:
For better or for worse, Mago offers up a unique fine dining experience done to a T.

Any restaurant that prioritizes fresh, local ingredients is a boon to the local scene.

Menu was fantastic with fun, unique flavors. The only downside for our tasting was the two protein dishes, the cod and duck breast, were the weakest of the bunch. Not to say they were bad! Just lacked the complexity of the other dishes.

Some fine dining restaurants make you feel like family, others offer service that is politely attentive and swift in retreat. This restaurant offers the latter. There's nothing wrong with that, it's a matter of personal preference, just something to note. The service was impeccable, friendly, and then out of the way. Cold? No. Warm? Also no.

I would definitely recommend getting the supplement, ours was by far the best dish of the night.

I would also strongly recommend the drink pairings, both alcoholic and non-alcoholic. They are deeply thoughtful and felt like an inseparable part of the menu.

This review may feel very critical for a 5 stars, but since everything was done impeccably, only imperfections stood out. Would come back in a heartbeat!

My family and I drove from more than 50 miles to dine at Mägo for my birthday. It was very well worth it. The tasting menu was well crafted, with a good combination of plates and a hint of Caribbean/South American touches. We sat at the chef's counter and had a front row seat to the kitchen, watching the orchestration that goes into delivering the dishes. Highly recommended!

After coming for some a la carte food and drinks I knew I had to come back for the tasting menu. I can say that it did not disappoint. Every bite showcased the creativeness and incredible flavors cooked up by the chefs…right in front of you in their kitchen concept.

The NA pairing was also a phenomenal selection of fun and exotic flavors including some small batch and locally sourced items.

A casual Colombian restaurant that gets serious with the tasting menu.
Fun beverage pairing that includes wine, sake, and cocktail.
Service is adequate, but they are learning and trying.
The weekday tasting menu is probably a better deal. It costs more on the weekend.
----
The mission statement on the website sounded admirable: The tasting menu is cheaper on the weekdays to make it more accessible.

We were seated at the chef's counter, which offers a direct view of the kitchen. We quickly decided on the tasting menu and the beverage pairing with an add-on Dungeness crab dish. After a relatively long period of waiting, we were presented with the food.

There are some highlights! But sometimes, I wonder if some dishes need an extra boost of flavor. First were the finger foods. We love the plantains that contrast brilliantly with charged allium. The arroz de coco brought to mind arancini but with a thin crust and coconut flavor. The tostada with amberjack brightened by the kiwi. The arepa was flavorful and puffy, but the butter beans seemed lacking. A general complaint: Please give us a wet napkin or something to wipe our fingers after finger foods!

The larger format blue shrimp was cooked to perfection, but the veins were in some pieces. The achiote ponzu was amazing, but the romanesco might be a tab overcooked.

Dungeness crab guacho, honestly, is a little disappointing. The components are done well, and it is an homage to the regional dish, but it just tasted...fine.

The fish dish was a counter-example of that. I am not sure if there is a traditional dish where it drew inspiration, but it was an elevated dish that we thoroughly enjoyed.

The cilantro and pineapple spread that came with the bread had such a bright flavor we couldn't have enough!

The grilled pork is definitely the highlight of the evening. It was carefully tended by a chef over the grill, and it was flavorful and juicy. The carrot was grilled slowly until it was almost dehydrated. The intense sweetness and texture worked very well with the pork.

The first dessert course, the banana custard, was terrific. The sweetness was counterbalanced by the subtle sweetness from the caramel. The dish was not overpowered by bananas, which so often is the case. The coconut and lime foam on the top provided a contrast and relief from the custard.

The final dessert course was a bit too sweet and heavy for us. We were told that it was inspired by mole. I like the concept.

Overall, we enjoyed the food. For a meal at this price point, maybe we expect a little more. However, I saw a kitchen with a mission that served some brilliant dishes. I saw service staff striving to be better despite some oversights. Maybe Mago needs to think about where it wants to position itself, but I am rooting for them.

First time trying Colombian cuisine so don’t have great frame of reference but I thought the flavors were strangely nostalgic! top_reviews.content: Fried Chicken Wings were legit, so was the potato salad... the candied green beans with sweet potatoes were really good and quite unique! I enjoyed the Fried Catfish + Prawns - nice batter, not at all greasy. Greens were good, no meat in them + I did like the cornbread. Really nice eats + they be showing love, I'll DEFINITELY be back 🤙.

Today was my first time visiting, and I couldn’t rave how great of a place this was. From the moment that I called the owner answered, and she was polite very knowledgeable of her food and able to answer all of my questions. I placed my order over the phone and headed over. I selected the turkey chops, smothered and gravy and into my surprise. They were amazing. They weren’t overly salty or seasoned like many people do their gravy. The batter was not falling off of the chops. It was pleasant of the ratio to sauce on the meat.  For sides, I had the mac & cheese, which had a little bit too much garlic. The classic homestyle would’ve been great with my meal as I also had garlic mashed potatoes, so the power of the garlic from both the potatoes and the mac & cheese was a little overwhelming. I was glad that I also got rice with gravy on the side as it was also really good. Now, baby, let me tell you about this cornbread. It taste just like cake. I literally stood at my counter and ate it Out of the container. I will definitely be going back as I would like to try some of her Basa fried fish and fries so I would love to go back for a lunch

Came from Kansas City Missouri to eat here, the owner is definitely a gift to everyone. Personality,  kindness , patience and just beautiful! Now the food!!!! My husband had the fish and I couldn't stop eating it! Cooked to perfection! I had the chicken wings and they were excellent! Favor, cooked perfectly! Now the banana pudding cake...you'll never find this taste any were else in the world. If you're in the area you deserve to treat yourself or you are missing out.

One of the best fried chicken in a long time. It looks dry but there's a lot of juice and flavor once you get into it. If it was delivered I don't think it would taste as good. The fried cod was good but not great because it wasn't juicy or buttery soft.

The cornbread sides were yummy. The Mac and cheese was cheeeeesy and thick and medium spicy. Collard greens were normal. Green beans were sweet and yummy. Fries were normal fries.

I asked for tap water since I didn't want a drink and the server looked surprised (and partly disgusted because I wanted faucet water?) and asked if I wanted bottled water instead. I said sure so we could end the conversation and didn't see the charge on the final receipt. I wasn't sure if the server forgot to add it or bottled water is free. Overall not a complaint but if you want to avoid drink confusion, either don't order water or bring your own lol

I’m giving 5 stars even though the spicy Mac n cheese threw me waaayy off! I will not be ordering it again. There really should be a disclaimer on the menu when food is spicy. Not everyone likes spicy. Some people’s stomachs and throats can’t handle spicy due to medical condition having what’s called GERD. It’s not a cooks decision on what’s not really spicy. I hope they consider this and put it on the menu description of the Mac n cheese. The catfish was piping hot, seasoned, and fried just right! The collards were good. The cornbread could’ve been bigger, but it was good, and the peach cobbler was good as well(also could’ve been larger portion). I would’ve preferred bigger portions of cornbread, collards and dessert, with just 3 pieces of fish instead of 7. Nonetheless, I recommend this place and I will be returning to try other dishes. Also, the service was great!

top_reviews.content:
One of the most under rated cafes in San Francisco. Have never been to a cafe that offers the rare combination of incredible donuts, lively and elegant atmosphere, warm and friendly service, coffee with beautiful latte art, and delicious food. On top of all that the even have wine and Spritz? Like seriously the Lo-fi is a hibiscus lime prosecco swirl of goodness.

The creme brulee donut was something that was unforgettable, and left me in a trance. Its crunchy caramelized top gives texture to its fluffy and airy brioche dough. The barista said its a house made vanilla bean custard on the inside which was not too sweet and balanced it perfectly. I also tried the avocado tartine with two poached eggs, which was incredible. The server who was kind enough to speak with me explained it has middle eastern spice “Za’tar” and “Lebne” yogurt. The focaccia bread was so crunchy, warm, and fresh. On top of everything the head chef came and greeted us, seemed very friendly, and asked how we enjoyed our meal.

Ive also previously tried the Dulce de Leche latte  and Chocolate cruller on my way to work, which both were fantastic. Will be recommending this spot to all my friends in the future.

I’ve been here three times over the past year. The cafe is beautiful, the food portions are generous. The Nutella donut is good. The crème brûlée looks good, but the filling wasn’t very tasty. The coffee is good, but not exceptional. The matcha and tea was just okay. Overall, the drinks were average.

It’s also self-service for napkins and utensils. I know some cafes work that way, but this doesn’t really feel like that kind of place. It would be nice if they gave you one napkin and one set of utensils with your order, and then you could grab anything extra yourself if you needed it.

The reason I’m giving 3 stars is the service. After three visits, the staff have never felt very warm or welcoming. I think a smile and a friendlier attitude would make a big difference.

First time.
Cool spot with a bit of a diner feel that is more modern.
Friendly service.
Wonderful gourmet donut options (large enough to share) along with toasts and drinks.
Booth type seating and a great spot to hang out and catch up.
Worth checking out.

This is honestly one of the best places in San Francisco. The avocado toast is absolutely delicious, and the coffee is excellent. I highly recommend this spot to anyone looking for a great breakfast or coffee experience.
The atmosphere is amazing — cozy, welcoming, and beautifully designed. I genuinely don’t understand some of the negative reviews complaining about the prices. Personally, I don’t think it’s expensive at all. The prices are very reasonable for the quality of the food, the coffee, the service, and the overall experience.
It’s a beautiful place, and it’s definitely worth paying for. I will gladly come back again and would recommend it to everyone. 5/5.

We had Dulce de Leche latte, cookie butter latte, a strawberry champagne doughnut, Nutella doughnut, a breakfast sandwich, and a chicken Panini. Everything was prepared to perfection. We were catered to our table really well by an African American gentleman who was very delightful and polite. The food is a solid 9/10 (bit pricey but worth it). They substituted the bacon from our sandwich for two eggs instead which was very considerate. The Exec. Chef Rowan also greeted our table and was very open to suggestions and was thorough about his food. Would definitely come back here again. Spent around $70+ for two people.

top_reviews.content: Snagged a wonderful booth for the World Cup game. Had Gabriel for a waiter and he was 5 ⭐️ very attentive and charming! I was kind of blown away by how good their food was, maybe I wasn’t expecting much. Our toddler loved the French fries, salmon, and tater tots. The fish sandwich was as good as they say and the salmon Caesar was delightful 🧑🏽‍🩰

I love the Tavern! Been here at least 30 times (live close by) and it’s perfect for every occasion - drinks with a friend or partner, family, or with small children. The food is always fantastic - smashburger, tots and miso salmon Caesar are my favorites. To top it all off, the owner is a kind and caring person.
This place is very nice, great atmosphere, friendly and the food rocks! I had the fish and chips, my daughter had the chowder and we shared the garlic fries. Spices cider was a nice nightcap.

The happy hour prices: very good
The wings: Good texture. They could use some more flavor/heat or ranch. No ranch available other than a very dilly dill sauce. I love the super thin veggie strips.
The tots: good but too salty
The beer selection: very limited.
I would come again for happy hour with my own ranch and hot sauce. Can’t really complain for the price.

Located at the corner of Cole and Carl Street, Cole Valley Tavern offers a unique vibe with its black-and-white checkered floors and modern yet classic bar—perfect for a great meal with good company 🍻.

Smashburger 🍔
A must-try, especially with the extra patty 🥩. The kimchi Thousand Island sauce takes it to another level, making it unforgettable.

Fish and Chips 🐟🍟
Perfectly fried with a hint of curry spice, paired with tangy tartar sauce for a savory twist.

Garlic Fries 🧄🍟
Crispy on the outside, soft on the inside, and packed with garlic flavor. A delicious side upgrade.

Clam Chowder 🥣
A brothy, seafood-packed chowder served with crispy-yet-soft sesame bread 🥖—perfect for dipping and utterly addictive.

Drinks 🍹
Top-notch cocktails and specials that never disappoint.

Soft-Serve Dessert 🍦
A sweet, creamy ending to a fantastic meal.

Cole Valley Tavern does it all—highly recommended! 🌟

She has such a warm and positive personality and genuinely makes you feel taken care of. Definitely one of the best experiences I’ve had here. If you stop by Acai R, ask for Sherry! One of the best Acai bowls in SF. The rainbow bowl is the way to go, can be customized completely to your preferences for fruit, base, add-on protein, enhancements (mango chia coconut is a must!) and fresh fruits.

Acai R has honestly become one of my favorite places. I order from them almost every morning through DoorDash, and it’s one of the highlights of my day. The quality is always amazing, the ingredients are fresh, and every bowl tastes like it was made with care.

In a world where so many places are inconsistent, Acai R gets it right every single time. Their açaí bowls are delicious, refreshing, and the perfect way to start the morning. You can tell they take pride in what they do.

Thank you for making healthy food that actually tastes incredible. You’ve earned a loyal customer, and I’ll keep coming back for a long time. Highly recommended! ❤️🥣✨

top_reviews.content: This place is as authentic as it gets! The food was amazing and packed with so much flavor, the ceviche instantly brought me right back home to South America. On top of that, the service was incredible and the food came out super fast. If you're looking for a top-tier spot to grab a fast, authentic South American lunch, I highly recommend checking them out.

This is my first time a Mariposas, and it was the first time for my friend to taste Peruvian food, the food was delicious, plate prevention was very good. We ordered Lomo Saltado, Arroz con mariscos, chichi morada, Inka Cola and Lucuma ice cream. It was a great experience and the food was delicious.

My family tried this restaurant tonight for the first time.  We are from Sacramento and it was located near our hotel. I had the Arroz con Marisol and it was delicious. Seafood wasn’t overcooked, very flavorful and serving was large. Atmosphere was so nice and staff was incredibly friendly. I would highly recommend this place.

It was late in the evening, we were hungry, and we didn’t want to move the car, so we went looking for a place to eat. Excuse me for being judgmental, but the last place I would think to go is a restaurant on the bottom floor of a parking garage. Reluctantly, we walked into Mariposa — and we were pleasantly surprised.

The food was excellent, affordable by San Francisco standards, and the service was outstanding. My wife ordered the Arroz Chaufa and wouldn’t share it, so I can’t tell you anything about it. Our guest and I had the Aji Amarillo (calamari, shrimp, mussels, etc.). The portions were large, definitely ruined my diet, but the sad truth is it’s hard to find good calamari. Bottom line: if you’re looking for good calamari, get the Aji Amarillo.

We’re in that area frequently, and I’m looking forward to trying more of their dishes. A great find. The four stars on atmosphere are only because the restaurant sits on the bottom floor of a garage. For a true San Francisco experience, it would need to be tucked into an old building in a hard‑to‑find alley with impossible parking. But then, of course, they’d have to charge more for the food.

Look.. I can tell they tried. But it just didn't land. My 1st warning should've been when we walked in and we were the ONLY customers in the place. Food was just ok and service was terrible. You'd thing being the only customers would get his full attention.  But no, we were neglected for long periods of time. FS is one of the best food cities in the country. You have to do better .

top_reviews.content:
Sweet Maple has had its Walnut Creek location open for a little while now. When it first opened, there were long lines of customers, so we decided to wait before trying it for brunch.

We ordered the Millionaire's Bacon and the Tornado Galbi Omurice. The Millionaire's Bacon consists of two thick-cut strips glazed with a sweet maple coating. It was delicious, although a bit too sweet for our taste. At $15 for two strips of bacon, it may appear somewhat overpriced to some customers.

The Tornado Galbi Omurice was an interesting fusion of Korean and Western cuisine. The dish was flavorful, and the combination of tender galbi, fluffy eggs, and seasoned rice worked very well together.

Both dishes were beautifully prepared and presented, and the service was attentive and friendly. Overall, we had a very enjoyable brunch experience and would recommend Sweet Maple if you're looking for a creative and well-executed brunch.

This one is located in Walnut Creek. There is metered street parking outside of the restaurant however, there is also a parking garage nearby which is walking distance to here.

So, it was my first time having brunch here. We came 30 mins after they opened and they’re already getting busy. But we didn’t have to wait. We were seated right away.

The food was amazing! I really loved the Tornado Galbi Omurice. But actually I loved everything we ordered. Me and my friends ordered a few things and shared everything. We also ordered the Marnier French Toast, which had a sort of brûlée topping it was crispy and sweet, I loved it. And we had the Crispy Brussels Sprouts and Millionaire’s Candy (bacon). OMG that bacon had the right amount or sweetness. Salty and crispness. It went very well with everything we ordered.

For drinks I had the Ube Latte and the other girls had Coconut Chai latte. I’m glad I ordered a latte versus a regular coffee.

Now, the ambiance; it looks very classy but not intimidating. I love the light fixtures. No complaints on customer service. Our server was really nice and move quickly. I can’t wait to come back to try other things on the menu.

Great brunch spot in walnut creek! The restaurant itself is very aesthetic and clean. The service was also good and our food came quickly. I got the vegetarian eggs Benedict and it was good. I also got the brown shaken espresso. Fyi, it is literally espresso in a cup, i ordered half and half on the side to make it this color lol

I came in very early in the morning and ordered a couple different food/drink options! The drinks were great and the food was very creative. I loved the atmosphere and clean look but the chairs are a bit dirty and the layout is a bit cramped.
Tasty food and good atmosphere, the only downsides are that I had no idea who my server was. I was serviced by multiple different people, one to bring drinks, another for my order, another for the check.

Also you don't get a bang for your buck here, portion sizes are pretty small but prices high.

Excellent food. Great atmosphere. Excellent service. There was a wait at the door, but it moved pretty quickly. I would recommend getting reservations ahead if you’re on a time crunch. Parking was somewhat limiting, but there is a parking garage about a block away. I got the Korean Fried Chicken and Short Rib Pot. It’s like an Asian Fusion of Korean bibimbap using short ribs. It was quite tasty. My spouse got the omelette, it too was excellent. Great decor inside along with plenty of outdoor spaces. Definitely worth coming back.

top_reviews.content: If you want spectacular pizza that has an magnificent crust go to Irvine Pizza. Their pizza is perfectly balanced between crust, sauce and toppings. Be forewarned, don't take your Bentley or wear your Rolex when picking up your pie (it ain't that type of neighborhood). You don't have to wear a helmet & body armor but you do want to keep your head on a swivel and take note of your surroundings. The pizza is thus far the best I have had. Plus....hold onto your hats ladies and gentlemen they offer ranch sauce in addition to marinara and pesto. We won't get into weather pineapple belongs on pizza but what ever you choose they will do it right. The lesser half and I stopped in for 2 slices after a show and ended up taking a pie home for our children (God knows they don't deserve it, but I love them nonetheless). Its that good! Give them a shot and watch your 6.

This is very average pizza which is very helpful when your drunk or desperate like I was.  $7 for the supreme slice which had the usual culprits like sausage, pepperoni, onions, olives, green peppers, etc.  Sober I probably would've hated this and the price, but for a night out drinking on Polk street it hit the spot, and likely prevented a hangover.  Friendly guy working the pizzas, zero ambience.
I got a vegetable slice to go, it was hot and delicious. Loaded with vegetables, heavy with a variety of vegetables. It really hit the spot. Lady at the counter was very very nice.

Not the best pizza in the city or anything special, but if you're in the area this is a great place to grab a slice. They almost always have plain cheese, pepperoni, pepperoni & sausage (best choice), supreme/combo, and garlic chicken w/ pesto (worst choice) pizzas on display, ready to be sold by the slice. Even so, I've never had a slice that wasn't nice and fresh.

The service is part of what sets this place apart from the other 10,000 pizza places in the area. The staff are very friendly & always have a smile. It's clear that the employees enjoy their jobs and that they have fun with the customers and each other. This does not, however, interfere with their professionalism or ability to work quickly and efficiently.

It's not the best pizza in SF, maybe not even the best tasting pizza in the TL, but their  excellent customer service, consistent  product and great prices make them a great choice for takeout, dine-in, or delivery. Not surprisingly, their whole pies tend to be the tastiest, too.

Note: They also take EBT, which is an added bonus. Don't get it twisted, though... This is the opposite of Chico's pizza in every single way. How that place stays open (with not just one, but TWO locations) is totally beyond me... But that's another review for another day.
The pizza was amazing and moderately priced. Next door is a convenience store with a sub shop and regular essentials. The crowd outside can be questionable, but hey, free entertainment 😉

top_reviews.content: My favorite restaurant. Humbowl is the go-to. It’s healthy AND incredibly delicious. Lots of options, yet so simple and easy to order. Very kind people working there. I recommend this place to my friends, family, and you.

Highly recommend Humbowl in Court in San Rafael! We had dinner there before a movie and were super impressed.
I had the Thai Curry Bowl with shrimp and my husband had the Wellness Bowl with legumes.

We are hard to please so this 5 star rating says a lot.
Flavors were balanced, not too salty, or spicy.  Lots of veggies and just the right amount of rice to complement.  The shrimp were fresh and cooked perfectly!

The water was chilled and flavored with fresh mint and lemon, incredibly refreshing on what was a warm evening and we had walked down from our home on the hill.

We were looking for a quick, healthy place to eat, and Humbowl hit the spot. The bowls were large and packed with healthy veggies. The proteins were fresh, and the sauces were really what took it to the next level. The service was friendly, but the location itself isn’t that comfortable. I would order to-go next time.

I can’t believe I haven’t left a review yet! I’ve been a consistent diner and take-outer since 2020, and they have yet to disappoint.

It’s a perfect mix of healthy and tasty - lots of freshness and flavor in every bite. My all time favs have been the Togarashi 2.0 and Thai Curry with shrimp.. honestly when I’m having a bad day, I eat one of these bowls for dinner, and it makes my day slightly less bad.

You may pass it on your way to something else in this neighborhood - the Elmwood theater, the ice cream and coffee shops, the best nail salon in town - but, you’d be missing out on an amazing, filling meal.

as a vegetarian, I love this place! I've only ever ordered food, so I can't speak on the in-person experience. I love that I can order from here directly without needing to use a third party app.

the bowls are consistently fresh, nourishing, and tasty. the sauces and seasonings are balanced, not too complex (which is sometimes exactly what I want!), and really let the quality of the ingredients shine.

All the food looks amazing! Unfortunately, a most of the fishes on the nigiri was kind of tasteless so it's hard to distinguish between the pieces. Note, I suggest looking at what you're purchasing because the fish pieces might slightly differ in size. And for the price your paying, you probably want the bigger pieces like how I would.

Who needs overpriced omakase when you can get an Ebiko spread at home.

I've been visiting Ebiko for years, and the quality is consistently amazing. This hidden gem is a sushi deli selling a small but very satisfying selection of rolls, nigiri, sashimi, chirashi, and vegetarian-friendly options, along with a handful of Japanese grocery store items.

There's also a kaisen hand roll party tray available for pre-order--it's a beautiful work of art that comes with edible flowers, but I personally prefer a la cart because I'm not a huge fan of uni and ebi. I wish they had customizable options for the party tray, but I'm already highly satisfied with the a-la-carte offerings.

My go-to's, although you really can't go wrong:
- omakase nigiri set
- salmon aburi (seared to melt-in-your goodness, my personal favorite)
- unagi nigiri (unagi is so fresh and the cuts are generous)
- California roll (ft real snow crab)

Notes:
- No seating area, but I heard that you can bring your food to eat at Tea on Piedmont across the street
- Metered street parking, not impossible to find a spot but may have to circle around
- Staff are friendly and efficient at check-out
- They don't charge extra for a bag :D (I try to bring my own, but sometimes I forget in the excitement for their sushi.

Literally the only downside is that it's closed on Sundays.

While pricese were a bit higher than I expected for the portion size, the quality was surprisingly good for take-out sushi. We spent over $60 on two omakase selections, 1 tiny uni don, 1 tiny toro don, and really small seaweed salad.

I wish they sold the scallop nigri a la carte because that was one of my favorite omakase items! Also liked one of the salmon in the omakase better than the other salmon (it looked like 2 different salmon were used). Husband raved about the toro pieces in the toro don and I enjoyed the uni don.

Had gotten this recommended online so I ordered delivery via (Uber Eats) - it’s a takeout spot so I didn’t expect much. The taste and quality was amazing. Value for the selection and choice was so unexpected.

My sister and I went on a little fridate and stumbled upon this place while looking for somewhere new to walk around and try. We’ve heard of Ebiko in SF but never had the chance to go since it’s usually packed, so we were excited to find the Oakland location with much less of a crowd. The prices were really reasonable, especially considering how fresh everything was. We absolutely fell in love with the torched salmon belly and the uni ikura bowl. This is definitely a must-try for sushi lovers, you won’t be disappointed. I’d for sure come back again with my sister when we get the chance.

top_reviews.content:
This is one of my favorite restaurants in SF when I used to live here and I still come and dine here when I visit. First, the decor has a beautiful serene green lush wooden nature vibes. The patio has beautiful views of the bay bridge and ferry building.
I always had very friendly service here.

I always order the chicken skewers, the fries, and the carrots. This place is healthy and clean eating, so I can see why some people see it as “bland” in their reviews but as someone who suffers from digestive issues, I absolutely adore this place and thank them for using sustainable and healthy ingredients whenever possible.

My only issue is they removed my favorite drink La Flor de Jamaica which was a hibiscus margarita that tasted better than a margarita more elevated and refined. And it was so gorgeous! The way the big block ice cub was infused with ingredients for the drink and the tangy rim and the color wow so beautiful. I absolutely love hibiscus drinks but most places use a syrup and hibiscus drinks really should be a dark red pink color and have that rich flavor but most bars I go to are never made like that until I came here. I mean look how pretty it looks and next to their cucumber cocktail! I asked them why they removed it and they said something about seasonal but they had it for a few years until they stopped and they continue to have the cucumber drink. You can see how passionate I’m about this drink! Also, they should bring back the flatbread which was a favorite among my family and friends!

We stayed the at hotel and ate here with a $50 breakfast credit each day.  The restaurant itself is nice and has a great view of the ferry building.  For breakfast, it's counter service only.  On a Sunday morning at 10, there were at least 15 people in line.  By the time I ordered, there were at least 25 people behind mind.  It's strange that this is not a full service restaurant at 1 Hotel.  The food is also lacking and just average.  We had the sweet potato waffle, quiche (good flavor but tiny and dry), breakfast burrito (bland) and classic 1 breakfast.  If we did it again, I would just get coffees and pastries there and go eat breakfast at a different restaurant.

top_reviews.content:
One of the best ramen spots I’ve tried!! everything was honestly sooo good. From the moment we walked in, the staff made us feel welcome. They were attentive, kind, and really added to the overall experience.

The ramen itself was the perfect bowl! the noodles had the ideal texture, and the broth was rich, flavorful, and comforting without being too heavy. You can tell a lot of care goes into every bowl.

Highly recommend

WHEN: Sat @6pm

PARKING: There is metered parking around, and is free after 6pm.  It may be a bit tricky especially around meal time, but keep circling and you’ll find a spot near by enough.

This cute little ramen shop has such perfect lighting coming through thanks to thier skylight.  We weren’t actually hungry so we shared the following:

TONKOTSU - $16.50 (Regular)
Pork Belly Chashu, Bamboo Shoots, Red Onion, Wood Ear Mushrooms, Green Onion, Ajitama Egg.

You get a choice of noodles to pick:
1.) Hakata - Thin Straight
2.) Sapporo - Medium Thick Wavy

Figured since it’s my first time here, I choose the most basic version of their bowl of ramen.  I chose Sapparo and for some reason expected it to be thicker/wider, but regardless it was still good!  The presentation of this bowl is just gorgeous, served on a small wooden platter.  The red onion is chopped, and the pork Belly is quite tender.  Regarding the egg, you get just half.  Overall this bowl of ramen is creamy, rich, and the right amount of flavor and salt.  But still make sure to drink at least a glass of water!

CREAMY CHASHU PORK CROQUETTES - $8.50
I have never seen anything like this so I must give it a try!  It actually didn’t come out piping hot, so I was able to drive in right away!  It was definitely creamy (like ramen) and had pieces of the Chasu pork, encased in a crispy and warm batter that was deep fried.  It also comes with a katsu sauce and I really enjoyed it.

The staff was friendly and didn’t make us feel bad for ordering enough of just one, but man I was so full.  Had to walk around downtown Berkeley for awhile.

By far the best Ramen I had in the Berkeley area. The two soup bases were both very rich in flavor. The toppings were very fresh. Pork and chicken cha soup both go well with the soup. One of the highlights for the meal was the matcha panna cotta. It's not too sweet so can the matcha flavor can stand out. Very balanced with the red bean and soft cream. They have a hojicha flavor one too, will try next time!

Great experience! The atmosphere feels authentic, chill and cozy. The service is awesome and the food is above all.

Food tastes fresh. Spicy is right there. Matcha classic.

Ramen quality deserved 5 stars. Atmosphere and Service - so so and there’s room for improvement.
First, please do not make people wait outside a cold alley. Invert a tablet for people to put in their phone numbers for waitlist. So you can text when your table is ready for the party. Or pay a little bit for Yelp or Google to form your waitlist.
Second, please use a QR code for customers to order food at the table. It’s fastest and it would not make any mistakes by the servers.
Third, hire more servers as they’re already busy enough.
If you claim you’re authentic Japanese Ramen, then do it more efficiently. You can turn your tables quicker that way.

One last thing, ask to take out the red onion in your ramen. It doesn’t belong in tradition noodle soup.

Being that my partner and I are interracial, we both could not think but one thing: racism.

Skip the racism and go elsewhere! Save your money to spend on a place that literally cares.

top_reviews.content:
I stumbled upon this place when my friend and I had finished eating at  Brenda’s Creole restaurant on the corner. Normally I would not find the idea of another Mexican restaurant appealing (I already have my favorites ). But something drew me in.

I loved the ambiance and friendliness of one of the owners- Leo. My friend and I decided to come back a few days later for happy hour. SO GLAD we did, as this is my new favorite for multiple reasons. The variety of food (not just standard Mexican menu ) the presentation of the food , the ambience of the restaurant especially the bar, the ample portions and the friendliness of the staff.

We had tasted  4 different tequilas and 4 different mezcal’s with the “flight “ that they have for happy hour . Highly recommend. The mezcal’s came with a Mexican delicacy - crickets. - which I was hesitant to try but they were delicious.
The only food we ordered from the happy hour menu was the nachos and they were some of the best I have ever had.

From the main  menu we ordered the beet salad which is a MUST if you like beets. I was tempted to order the butternut squash salad but since it is out of season at the moment, I went with the beet salad.

#3 - I LOVE LOVE LOVE mole and their emmoladas in the mole sauce were amazing.

If you are searching for authentic Oaxacan cuisine in Oakland, incredible handcrafted cocktails, and one of the best Mexican dining experiences in the Bay Area, Mesa Maguey absolutely delivers. This restaurant deserves more than a 5-star review for its outstanding food, amazing drinks, warm hospitality, and unforgettable atmosphere.
From the moment you walk into Mesa Maguey, you can feel the passion and authenticity behind everything they do. The restaurant has a welcoming energy, beautiful ambiance, and a true appreciation for traditional Oaxaca culture and cuisine. Every detail — from the presentation of the dishes to the expertly crafted cocktails — reflects quality and care.
Leo, the owner, is one of the best hosts and restaurateurs in Oakland. He is extremely knowledgeable about Oaxacan cuisine, mezcal, tequila, and authentic Mexican flavors. Leo takes the time to educate guests about the menu, ingredients, and agave spirits while making everyone feel like family. His passion for authentic Mexican food and exceptional customer service is what makes Mesa Maguey stand out from other Oakland Mexican restaurants.
The food is absolutely incredible. Mesa Maguey serves some of the best Oaxacan food in Oakland with rich, authentic flavors that are hard to find anywhere else in the Bay Area. Every dish tastes fresh, perfectly seasoned, and beautifully prepared. The mole dishes are deep, complex, and packed with traditional Oaxaca flavor. The tacos, birria, enchiladas, ceviche, and house specialties are all amazing. You can tell the kitchen uses high-quality ingredients and authentic recipes that honor true Mexican culinary traditions.
Their drinks and cocktail menu are equally impressive. Migel, the bartender, is exceptional and incredibly talented. The margaritas, mezcal cocktails, and tequila-based drinks are expertly balanced, creative, and made with fresh ingredients. Migel provides outstanding customer service, makes excellent recommendations, and creates a fun and welcoming atmosphere at the bar. If you appreciate craft cocktails or premium mezcal, this is easily one of the best cocktail spots in Oakland.
Mesa Maguey is perfect for date nights, birthdays, celebrations, happy hour, or simply enjoying amazing Mexican food and drinks with friends. The atmosphere is vibrant, stylish, and authentic without feeling pretentious. Great music, excellent service, beautiful presentation, and incredible flavors make this restaurant a must-visit Oakland destination.

Mesa Maguey should absolutely be at the top of your list.
Huge respect to Leo, Migel, and the entire Mesa Maguey team for consistently delivering one of the best restaurant experiences in Oakland. Incredible food, exceptional cocktails, authentic Oaxaca flavors, and genuine hospitality every single time. Highly recommended — easily a 5-star plus restaurant experience.

Food was so good! I especially love the sweet and sour fish. Quite crunchy on the outside but very tender and flavourful on the inside. My daughter who is not a fan of fish can't get enough of it!
