Classic Chinese Food that will be just right for a big hunger. Have a TSINGTAO Beer or two and enjoy your pick. A llitte hidden in the back of the building its worth every penny. Ambiente is simple but clean. Service was a bit to slow and unpersonal but its probably a order / to go place mainly.

This is honestly the best place to satisfy my craving for great Chinese food. I have visited plenty of times and have never grown tired of eating there. The broccoli chicken with steamed rice is simply the best, and the ingredients are always cooked to perfection. I clean my plate every time, down to the last grain of rice, as the portion sizes are just right. The price can't be beat. Plus the owners are super friendly. I will happily visit again!

Just wanted to say Hunan Empire has great food. I’ve been a customer since the early 2000’s . The service is great. The prices have gone up but hasn’t everything ?  They have been consistently good. Give them a try and you won’t be disappointed..

Cozy place with a friendly customer service .

top_reviews.content:
I think I just discovered my favorite restaraunt of all time in Berkeley. Though the exterior of the restaraunt is unassuming, and the building itself is quite small with limited seating, the interior is still very clean and neat, and the workers are very nice.

I placed an online order for the C Chicken Momos and the Garlic Cheese Naan, which were both phenomenal. The naan was some of the best I've ever had. It was so fluffy, thick, and pillowy soft, and was not overly charred/thin or too crispy like other naan. Just pure doughy goodness. There was also a perfect amount of cheese filling--enough that you got the subtle kick of milky acidity, but not too overpowering. The naan itself was also not too greasy, and the garlic flavor was very aromatic. You could also taste a hint of the slight tartness from (I'm assuming) the yogurt used to make the naan.

The "C" Chicken Momos came with eight large pieces, which is definitely enough to fill you up. The sauce tasted like a classic sweet-and-sour sauce with a very mild and pleasant spice. Also, because the dumplings were fried, they were crispy despite being covered in sauce, but still had a bit of the nice chew you would get from a steamed momo skin. The fillings themselves were also super flavorful. Because of the ginger, they tasted very herby and fresh, which balanced the tanginess of the sauce so the meal did not feel too heavy. The dumplings also had some warm broth in them, which is perfect for a cold day.

The prices are fair too. You can often find small discounts on Snackpass or delivery apps like GrubHub. Needless to say, I will definitely be coming back. Totally recommend!
Small restaurant with huge flavor menu. Check it out. Nice folks. Everytime I visit Berk, this is the place for me.Home cooked food feeling.

I visited this restaurant yesterday and had a disappointing experience. If you are expecting garlic naan don’t go coz they have garlic bread and they call it garlic naan, even that garlic naan was uncooked and not properly prepared.  On top of that, the service was not good staff were not attentive. Food quality and customer service both need improvement.

Absolutely amazing food! The momos were fresh, juicy, and full of authentic flavor. The chutney was perfectly spicy, and every bite was delicious. The staff was friendly, the service was quick, and the restaurant was clean and welcoming. One of the best places for Nepali momos. Highly recommended—I’ll definitely be coming back!
Me and my bfs went there after class. There prices were so reasonable it’s best for students on a budget.. and the food was delicious. Server was attentive and friendly

top_reviews.content: Found this spot randomly searching for local spots to try. I seen the previous reviews and nothing beats authenticity especially in food. Went to try as a solo diner & it was amazing. Got the green chilaquiles with a pineapple hibiscus drink & sat outside soaking the sun. The sauce of the chilaquiles was not spicy (bummer) but was still good. Luckily they had side of hot sauces available. Would like to come back & try more options.

I come here 2-3 a week because it’s close to work & also because I’m addicted. This is the best family owned Mexican restaurant that so much more elevated in taste than most places you’ll find. Plenty of options to choose from and their ceviche is to die for. My personal favorite is the pork pineapple taco. I never come here without ordering at least one.

This place offers a solid taco experience, with flavorful fillings that satisfy. The chicken pozole is a comforting and tasty option, but it would benefit from a more generous portion of chicken to truly shine. An overall great spot for a quick and satisfying meal.

Okay been here a few times now - the red chilaquiles were amazing, ceviches have been mostly misses as have most of the other seafood but chilaquiles and barbacoa were good enough to ignore that

So glad to see this area busy. I had a Barbacoa taco and Chicken - Chili Verde Tamale. Both were excellent.

name: Tio Chilo's Grill
address: 2872 24th St, San Francisco, CA 94110, United States

google.name: Tio Chilo's Grill
google.address: 2872 24th St, San Francisco, CA 94110, United States

top_reviews.content: Solid Mexican breakfast spot! I had the machaca and coffee. Service was genuinely friendly and efficient, with plenty of coffee refills. The spicy salsa was perfect with the dish. Chips were forgettable, but appreciated. The midmorning vibe was great with an open front door letting in fresh air, chatty locals, and lots of sun. Looking forward to returning to try more.

This is exactly what a real neighborhood restaurant should feel like. It has that genuine family-owned, local atmosphere, and the food is hella good. Honestly, you could probably order anything on the menu and leave happy.

What really stood out, though, was the service. Our server was incredibly kind, attentive, and welcoming. She didn’t just take our order and disappear. She had an actual conversation with us, checked whether we needed anything when the food arrived, and came back afterward to ask how everything was. We ended up having another whole conversation with her because she was just that friendly and sweet.

She made us feel less like customers and more like guests in her home, like going over to a friend’s mom’s house or your auntie’s house and being fed. That kind of warmth is rare, and it makes you immediately want to come back.

The food was excellent, the service was amazing, and the whole place felt welcoming and personal instead of just transactional. This is a great restaurant to have in the neighborhood, and there should be more places like it.

I have been going to Tio Chilo’s for the last three years and I have to say they never disappoint! The food, drinks, ambiance and service is always top notch and on point!
This little family owned restaurant is a gem therefore if you’re in the Mission District area in San Francisco you must visit this spot! Make sure to ask for Liz, the owner so she can make you her famous margarita flights!

I had the Lamb Shank, served with refried beans and rice with plenty of tortillas. The Quesabirria was cheese and served with  broth that needed to be a bit hotter. Both were flavorful and served on time. The place is very clean and the bathroom is spotless. Great attentive service all around.

We ordered to go, burrito was fine however, our chicken enchiladas order had not only BONES in the chicken but a FEW end of the bone (large nerves).
Very dangerous to have this in a chicken order where you don’t expect this chicken breast enchilada order.
We will not return to eat or order at this place, even recommend this place since this was not a pleasant delicious dinner experience!

top_reviews.content:
One star Michelin in SF, Japanese and very SF local forward menu, and super friendly staff. My friend made a reservation for us 2 for her birthday.  I didn’t really do much research or look it up prior coming, so I thought there would be more raw fish but there wasn’t which I didn’t mind. But I enjoyed the sf local spring forward menu and how everything was sf/bay inspired.

We shared the zero proof pairing and I really enjoyed it. I couldn’t compare or rank which items I ate because they were all so different. They hit you quick in the beginning with the starters then they slow down. The head chefs walked around a lot. The pastry chef is Filipino!

It did take about 3 hours but didn’t feel too long, only 1 bathroom so you had to find the right time to go like on an airplane haha.

By the time the wagyu came I was so full lol but it was good, no extra add ons or additions other than drinks.

I got lucky and found a parking spot downtown be street! Also it didn’t feel hella long but there was a steady flow and our reservation was at 6 and we got there at 545 and they sat us early before more people came in but they were still having people arrive at like 845.

Today was the start of their spring menu and we were their first zero proof spring tasting, soo good. I don’t know how I would imagine the tasting without it but I didn’t take many pics of the pairing.

Meal was like $335 per person and the pairing was $165, we did a split that was only $30 more. It was nice and cozy inside, there was a separate dining area and you can kind of see the kitchen.

Posting this review late, but I still wanted to share my experience. For me, the value was not very high for the price. Some dishes were a bit strange and were described very highly by the staff, but did not really meet expectations. There were also some charges that were not clearly explained to us in advance. During the menu introduction, the service felt a little unprepared and at times they even forgot how to describe certain dishes.

That being said, some dishes were quite tasty and the seasonal ingredients tasted fresh. However, in my opinion, this was not the best standard I would expect from a Michelin one star restaurant. I hope they continue to improve.

Ranking based on other mish 1s in the area. Food punches above it's weight! Everything was tasty, no complaints. Had their non alcoholic pairing which was phenomenal, one of the best I've had, it really elevated the food to the next level, which is rare for a non -alcohol. Plating was top notch, look at that dessert tree!  Slight markdown on service due to some delays and it took a while for beverages to arrive (after first dishes came out). Standouts: uni , unagi and Sando (see menu photo). Would go back.

Had a lovely time at this place. The service was amazing. We got there a bit early and they gave us a table at their bar next door while waiting, then brought us to the restaurant via the back door. They were attentive enough to notice I was wearing black pants, and gave me a black napkin as opposed to white to prevent lint from showing up.

The vibe was relaxed and quiet. The decor was eccentric with risqué paintings in Japanese style. It was edgy as if to signal that there would be surprises in the meal.

The meal was excellent. Many dishes were quite creative. All delicious! What I didn’t love was the lengthy explanation of each dish. While I understand the why, they took away from the experience because some felt like lectures.

Overall, we had a great time here.

Nisei, an intimate One Michelin-Starred restaurant in San Francisco. I got to experience their Winter 2025 - 13 course menu!

This is my second time coming here this year because I love the experience, service, and how the chefs make various different flavors come together cohesively, and the presentation speaks for itself.

As a photographer and creator, it is fun to have beautiful food be your muse. You will also leave here feeling satisfied and full by the end of your 13 course. And there's a story behind every dish, and all the ingredients are carefully sought out and used purposefully on each plate.

Until next time.

Good for groups, vegan/vegetarian friendly. They also serve tea, wine, and soju. Definitely an easy go-to dumpling spot.

I’ve been there once with my friend for dinner. The food was amazing and the service great.

Thank you Minh for your warmth and kindness. You made my day more beautiful.

Btw, the string beans are must to try. You’ll fall in love with them.

Also, the service was some of the best we’ve had in years!

Great food and really kind service. They accidentally made my dish spicier than I’d asked for, but the woman who helped me handled it perfectly. That kind of care makes all the difference. Would definitely come back if i wasn’t on a holiday here :(

top_reviews.content:
Vulcan Thai Cafe is the kind of neighborhood restaurant that leaves an impression well beyond the meal itself. Lily, the owner, was an exceptionally gracious host: warm, attentive, and genuinely invested in making sure the dining experience was a memorable one. She took the time to explain the menu with care and shared stories of Thai culture that gave the meal a welcome sense of place and authenticity.

I ordered the Emerald Salmon Curry, and it was excellent. The salmon was complemented by a beautifully balanced curry sauce, which was fragrant, nuanced, and seasoned with remarkable precision. The vegetables were crisp and fresh, offering just the right contrast in texture while absorbing the flavors of the curry without losing their character.

Between the quality of the food and Lily’s generous hospitality, Vulcan Thai Cafe offers far more than a good meal; it offers the sort of personal, culturally rich dining experience that makes a restaurant worth returning to.

The food was incredibly delicious, and the service was exceptionally friendly. This is a family-owned establishment, and every dish we tried had a wonderfully fresh taste. We ordered Pad Ped Pla Duke,  shrimp rolls, tom yum soup, and pad kee moh with shrimp – all of them were absolutely delightful. We plan to return for more in the future. The cozy, family-oriented atmosphere of this mom-and-pop restaurant made us feel right at home. The added bonus was their extended hours of operation from 10 am to 12 am.

Wanted to give this place a try. We tried and we’re moving on…

Ordered fried rice/pad Thai/yellow chicken curry.
Fried rice and pad Thai, was very bland. The fried rice has no eggs, no sauce and no flavor. Just rice.
The pad Thai was similar. No eggs, no tofu, and nothing more. Just noodles.

Like I said, we tried and now it’s time to move on. Good luck with you if you’re planning on ordering here.

Almost missed this little cafe, just happened to search for Pad Thai while driving up the 880. Friendly service, tasty food. Ordered the Pad Thai and the Kao Kra Proa (with chicken), looking forward to trying this place again and other items on the menu!

The food is good and prices are very reasonable. It's a casual atmosphere, hole in the wall, local spot. Pictured is shrimp pad thai, beef fried rice and mango sticky rice. It's bit off the beaten path but GPS takes you right there. My friends and I usually order food for pick up or have it delivered on an app. The people are very nice!

top_reviews.content: I would say this is an actual destination -- authentic food and true care for the customer. Breakfast of huevos con chorizo could not have been better. I wavered between eating here or taking to go, but it was so welcoming inside that I stayed -- the gentleman was thoughtful to present the meal in a to-go container for my flexibility if I had to leave before finished. The tortillas were warm and tasty, the eggs and chorizo were a perfect blend and not at all salty but simply delicious, complete with scrumptious rice and beans, and a fantastic guacamole with bits of onion and tomato. I paired it with an horchata, just like you'd want from a taqueria, with no silt at the bottom. I did finish on the road but I had a relaxing stay in a clean and rustic restaurant, thanks to the staff and proprietors. A real star in Oakland is El Paisa Taqueria!

We came to this place because it had good ratings. The people are really nice, service was great, employees were attentive. Visiting this place felt like as if you were visiting your uncle and grabbed some food. The place seems to have history, it does seem a bit old, has a lot of wear and tear on the tables/chairs/walls/utensils. Food was good, seemed a bit bland, lacking some flavor. They do not take credit cards, only cash/venmo/zelle.

Been here alot for many years and their food is good quality and price, needs more recognition!!

This place is amazing, I had a really good time with my friend last night!

We ordered bruschetta, carbonara, another pasta with penne and spicy sauce (I forgot its name), and desserts (frozen lemon sorbet, and tiramisu). Everything was so tasty, and we finished all of them!

The price was surprisingly reasonable and the service was great. I loved the chill and friendly vibe as well.

I will definitely come back :)

My palét Osparonia the Fan Dancer over at the Paloma Hights Cabaret up in Pacific Hights told me about this wonderful Italian restaurant called Luisa's Restaurant Wine Bar on Guerrero St. and hell...I've never been there!  Well, I told her her I'll pick you up at 6 and we'll go there for dinner, and let me just say this...Everything about Luisa's, the ambiance, the service, the food, the patrons were amazing! ..hell even the parking was amazing!  ~no shit 5 ☆☆☆☆☆'s !

Luisa is a nice neighborhood gem offering traditional Italian home-cooking owned by a lovely lady. We tried a few apps, pastas, and finished off with dessert. Everything was delicious and reasonably priced especially for San Francisco. Some fav dishes included the parpadelle which was house made, burrata, and tiramisu for dessert. We all left completely full.

One of the best Italian restaurants in the city and probably the best value Italian spot in the city.

Gnocchi was some of the best I’ve had in a minute. Lobster ravioli was also really good. Pizza honestly didn’t look the most amazing but man it tasted great. Tiramisu was a little underwhelming but still tasty, just a tad bitter and wish they didn’t use Hershey’s.

Would come back for sure.

Hands down, this is my favorite Italian restaurant that I've been to in San Francisco so far. I thought I have had gnocchi before but omg when I tell you this gnocchi is so good, it's better than any that I've ever had. The pasta I had was delicious and fresh as well. The sauces were CRAZY delicious and truly I'm not one to obsess over Italian food usually but it was so so yummy and memorable. The service was so kind. She let us try a few wines before deciding on the one we were going to get checked on us regularly, but not too much and it was just really really good service. Luisa her self was there as well sitting in a booth and it was really cool to see her just hanging out while I was enjoying her and her family's delicious recipes. the ambience of the restaurant was so cute and quaint and I can't wait to come back.

top_reviews.content:
Disappointing experience. To be fair we arrived later in the day so that might have contributed.

It took quite some for our order to be taken or for us to be acknowledged at all (staff were chilling in the back, it was slow).

When we got our food the induction heater wasn't working. That was noticed after ten minutes or so at which point they subbed in a gas fired one instead. That ran out of gas pretty quickly at which point we needed to ask for a replacement. The service wasn't bad when received but the lack of care and attention was noticeable.

For the food itself the soup set itself was fine but very overpriced for what you get. The karrage was an overcooked burnt and ready abomination.

We had an AMAZING time here on Christmas Eve. The food was delicious, super peaceful clean atmosphere and the staff was so kind and generous. We got the Miso (vegetarian) Nabe and the vegetarian kimchi Shabu Shabu (not listed on the menu). We also had the introduction sake flights. The menu came with a pre-selected array of veggies, mushrooms and tofu. We also added fried tofu and mochi. It was a good amount of food for two people (and we eat A LOT). Towards the end of your meal you can have one of your soups made into a porridge at the table (there is egg in this, but I think everything else so far was vegan!) We ended with the green tea ice cream. I am dreaming of my next San Fran trip when I can come back :,)
10/10 will go again!

Not a huge restaurant, but we liked the vibe. Loved trying the flight. Food was good and nicely portioned, but soups were slightly bland compared to other shabu places. Went for early dinner, and the place was not packed. But it was slow to get things in the beginning.. there seemed to be just one person taking orders and serving. Things got faster as more customers came in, and more waiters were seen. Really liked the porridge thing they did at the end.

I am suspicious that they had changed ownership. From Japanese to something else. Quality of the food is worse. The rice they used at the end to make the rice porridge is old and harden essentially staled. To me that was the best part of the meal and in fact the only difference between nabe and regular hotpot.  The server was polite but loud and it felt as if I was in a night market. Definitely not a refined experience. Very disappointed.

love this place - we eat here everytime we fly to SF
really good value, quality and service!! honestly probably my favourite restaurant in this city

top_reviews.content: I enjoyed lunch on a quiet afternoon.  The Roman-style pizza (pinza) was excellent, and cooked by the owner.  It was a pinzo basso with vegetables on a thinnish crust thick enough to support abundant toppings. See the photo.  My peanut-butter gelato was dense and flavorful. There are several salad, pizza, and pasta selections.  The service was friendly and attentive from a Berkeley local.  The restaurant decor is bright and cheery, with some outdoor tables available. There is a short wine and beer list, with mostly Italian selections.  Pasta and gelato are made on site and apparently distributed wholesale.  I will return for dinner!   Tutto a posto.

I love seating behind a table gazing at the big open kitchen where the dedicated chefs prepare salad,pasta, and pizza. People are very nice here. This place and the coffee shop have basically changed the Neighbourhood. Lovely outdoor seatings on the sidewalk.
I used to live in Turin, Italy, and I just found the best pasta spot in the SF Bay Area 🙂 If you want to taste truly authentic Italian pasta, you won’t regret it.

If you want to be delighted by flavor and enjoy a good time as well, this is the place!! We organized a lunch with my family and friends at Passione Emporio for my wedding and my daughter’s baptism and they made sure everything, and I mean everything from the food to the ambience and the service was absolutely PERFECT! We loved the menu they created for us and our guests were impressed by each plate’s execution and taste. The portions were also generous and we didn’t have to wait to get served, the timing was just right. I am thankful for the excellent customer attention as well: Fabrizio made sure we were happy and comfortable. Good job, Passione Emporio! No one should leave Berkeley without trying this spot!

Some amazing happy hour deals and these slices were very reasonably priced. Pears on pizza was new to me, but the flavors surprisingly came together well. The dough ferment was very noticeable, complemented well by the oven’s temperature. Great place to stop by for a quick bite to sit down lunch/dinner.

top_reviews.content:
Sichuan Fusion is a neighbourhood staple! I’ve been coming here regularly for dine-in and takeout since 2017 and will continue to eat here so long as I live in the Bay Area. It’s one of my favourite restaurants in the East Bay.

Every dish I’ve had here has been amazing. My must-trys are the baby lotus root with beef, Sichuan fish filet with pickled mustard soup, Chongqing chili chicken (need to get it with bone!), garlic eggplant, and Uyghur style sautéed lamb. But seriously, everything is fantastic.

Alright, It's been a year. This is one of the best  sichuan places in the bay. I have never had a bad meal here and unlike Spices 3, I am treated very nicely, no weird racial aggression.  It has a comfortable dining room  that's unpretentious and soothing. My favorite dishes are the chongqing chicken bone in, shrimp fried rice, stone pot cabbage, among many others. There are no bad dishes. I will admit dining in the quality is a bit higher, but it is still good. I am praying it stays in business and doesn't change.

I didn't expect to like this as much since I'm a little sensitive when it comes to spicy food, but I liked it!

Good:
- Really solid garlic glass noodles with shrimp - not spicy, but great flavoring and tasty noodles with just enough sauce!
- The soy milk they give out here is really good if you need something to cool the spiciness away
- The spicy noodles are tasty - chewy noodles
- The sour and spicy fish soup was really good as well - so soft and tender
- The boiled spinach was good in comparison to all of the spicy dishes
- Lotus root and beef was tasty but spicy - the beef was so tender

Bad:
- Takes some time for the food to come out
- The place is super casual ambiance wise, you have to be used to Chinese restaurants and speaking Chinese to have the best experience

Overall would come again, good authentic Chinese food.

Located inside the complex, past the 99 Ranch market in the back. We love this restaurant and often order delivery or eat in. I realized I didn't review it for years so now is a good time. They have great value for the size and quality of dishes.

We usually order Kung Pao chicken, schezuan fish soup (spicy), boiled beef (spicy), and garlic eggplant. These are our favorites however the Dan Dan noodles were good and huge - a much better price than the new soup restaurant next door. The fried rice and xiao long bao are decent. The pork dishes and fried chicken are also good. Free tea if you eat inside. We haven't had a dish we didn't like and overall enjoy every dish.

Service is quick and fine. Most dishes are around $15-20 and do not include rice. The portions are very large. I recommend going with a group to try many things.

It is spicy too- the icons on the menu are accurate! Some numbing for certain dishes.

I ordered dry pot fish, chicken chow mein,  and beef fried rice. The fish was flavored well, however the fish was too deeply fried. I had mostly fried skin and barely any actual fish meat. Noodle was extremely greasy and barely any meat. Overall, ive had better chinese food.

Our beef fried rice never came out too. So I had to cancel it. Same with the noodle. It took nearly an additional 15 minutes after I paid my bill.

The porridge was a bit plain and the beef short ribs were just ok. The chicken wings are heavily battered, not in the way that I’d like but still ok. All in all, average food but not too many actual HK breakfast dishes besides cheong fun and porridge

New establishment located on Ocean Avenue near 24 Hour gym and next to Emma's restaurant. There rice porridge/ conger is pretty good. Size is personal sized for all porridge items. Their rice noodles are really good in terms of freshness and how customizable they are.  Service was alright, slightly lacking in terms of paying more attention to customers. The interior is quite clean, but the restroom (one, unisex) can use some TLC... Heh. Prices are descent.

top_reviews.content: I'm still not sure what to think about Kibatsu. Fantastic atmosphere, and it serves some unique dishes (like shark skin), some high quality fish dishes, and some basic dishes along with some (somewhat weird...) fusion Japanese. It is very inconsistent in quality and feels like it keeps some of its true gems only available in the expensive Omakase route ($120 or $150). The regular menu is limited, and is almost entirely fish based, yet some things that are only being served as part of the Omakase menu (like the wagyu dish, or the crab soup), are true gems and would be incredible if were included in the menu. I also have to call out that this place let us know, well into the meal (so too late to change our minds) that their credit card machine is not working that evening, yet somehow they had a pre-printed paper with their owners personal venmo info available, which felt very pre-planned...

Decent omakase experience. Some of the best bites included the king crab, scallop, tiger prawn, uni fried rice and toro with caviar and uni. They also have a selection of sake to go with your food. The place is rather small but you are able to make reservations online. Be careful though because they tried to refuse payment by credit card and were only accepting Venmo or third party apps. Just seemed strange since we held our reservation with a credit card and we weren’t informed of the payment policy until after our meal. We also weren’t offered anything à la carte after the meal and I was curious about the fried ice cream dessert. Kind of ruined the experience, but the food was otherwise good, just not sure about the price point

Food-wise, the dishes were decent and fairly standard. Compared to other izakayas, there was nothing particularly outstanding, and given the price point, it felt somewhat overpriced. The dinning environment was warm and cozy, the place is nicely designed and has a pleasant atmosphere.
However, the waiter are quite adept at discriminating against customers😭🫶🏻

I was seated directly next to a ventilation outlet blowing constant hot air. Everything on the table — plates, water glass, even my phone — became hot. It was so hot that while I was eating, I started to envy the dead fish in the freezer😭😭😭There was barely space for belongings, and sitting normally meant being blasted with heat. I asked twice to change seats while other tables were available and was refused both times without explanation. This seat should not be assigned to reservation guests at all.

The service was equally disappointing. The server repeatedly pushed omakase and additional dishes despite the obvious discomfort caused by the heat. It felt like aggressive upselling rather than genuine hospitality.

What made it worse was the inconsistency in service. No one offered to hang my coat upon arrival. I only realized coat service existed when the same server immediately offered it to the white guests seated next to me. I do not make accusations lightly, but the contrast was difficult to ignore and came across as discriminatory.

I left in under 30 minutes because the situation was physically unbearable. Very poor seating management and unprofessional service.

Super nice cozy vibes, love the decor of this place! Mid to low light, great for a romantic dinner with good food! Although it is not the best sushi in town, for a little above average price you're getting some good stuff!

This was my first time here. A friend who lives in the neighborhood recommended it and I couldn’t have been more pleased. Very cute dark intimate atmosphere, unique plating, great quality flavor and really friendly staff. The chef even gifted us a tasty special piece of sushi. Highly recommend!

The skewers are delicious. We especially loved the Berkshire pork belly. The sauce for the grilled octopus is tasty but the meat is under-seasoned a bit. The Wagyu Gyutan Curry is a weekend special and is fantastic! So I definitely recommend getting that if you’re there on the weekend.

Also, we loved how the food here is the right amount of spicy: spicy enough to give the food a solid kick, but not so much that it’s overpowering.

All around the food is amazing, but the service can be slow at busy times.

On a Saturday night, we got there right before it got packed (around 6:45-7:00P). Corner neighborhood Japanese in North Beach SF. We ordered a bunch of items, but our favorite was the pork belly skewers! Soooo flavorful and succulent! We ordered a 2nd order! I also did love the crunchy chicken skin! Also ordered Agadashi (fried tofu), waygu & meatball, beef short rib, mushroom. Service is pretty fast and friendly enough. Would come back!

Due to food allergies, the staff was very accommodating and made an effort to ensure everything was safe for us, which we appreciated. However, there seemed to be some miscommunication among the staff regarding our order and what we had written down. A few items were missing, and while most were brought out once we mentioned the mix-up, some items still never arrived. There were also a few instances where items that needed to be kept separate ended up on the same plates.

The drinks were good, but they didn’t really taste like they had much alcohol in them. Overall, it was an okay experience. We appreciated the staff’s attention to our food allergies, but better communication and attention to the order details would have made the experience much better.
Best spot that I know in sf whenever I want to take my out of town friends - excellent food and the staff gives a family-friendly type of service. The lanterns are beautiful and ambience is cozy

Surprisingly not busy for a Saturday dinner time, probably should have picked up the sign on this right after walking in. Our waitress was very nice, but they added automatic 18% service fee for a party of 2 and asked for additional tips as well, didn’t appreciate this “double feature”.

address: 1919 Webster St, Alameda, CA 94501, United States

google.name: Pho Anh Dao

top_reviews.content:
Over the weekend I was looking for a bowl of soup for the soul. We had visited Ph Anh Dao once before this, on New Year’s Day and it was delightful so we thought we’d pay them another visit!

The restaurant is very spacious, so spacious that two different restaurants occupy the same building! The staff are shared as well. I will say it’s a hard to get the staff’s attention. They stand at the main register in the middle of the lobby and it’s hard for them to see you waive your hand depending on where you’re seated. But once they do see you, they’re very quick to tend to you!  It’s got a ton of natural light and endless seating. There is also a small parking lot behind the building, it’s in the same parking lot as the hotel parking spaces but the hotel spaces are marked.

I’m personally a huge fan of tripe and tendon, but I always feel like I never get enough of those when I get pho at other places. Pho Anh Dao offers a build your own pho so I got a large bowl of pho with only tripe and tendon ($14.50). I also swapped the regular noodles for Ho Fun noodles ($0.50). We also got a bowl of Garlic Noodles with Grilled Beef & Egg Rolls ($17). The garlic noodle bowl is the main reason we came back, even though soup was the main goal! And of course, we grabbed a cup of Viet iced coffee. I totally forgot to snap a picture of the drink menu, but I do remember the drinks being reasonably priced.

My bowl of pho came out super fast! They gave generous portions of both tripe and tendon, so I was super happy about that. I tried the broth on its own before adding in any veggies. I prefer a very deep and rich pho broth, this was very light/bland and honestly wasn’t hot enough. The Ho Fun noodles were slightly firm because of the broth temperature. I’m also usually not one to add sauce directly into my pho, but it needed it. Even after adding hoisin, sriracha, and toppings, the pho was just okay. I was pretty disappointed but anytime I’m given a hearty serving of food, I can be pretty forgiving.

The viet iced coffee was very well rounded. A lot less sweet than other viet iced coffees you can get in the area which I appreciate. It kind of tastes like they only use milk or cream rather than condensed milk, the coffee itself has that nice roasty/bitter flavor viet coffee is known for. I’ll have to grab the Thai iced tea next time! We had asked if could get the Thai iced tea with coffee added into it but they said they sadly couldn’t do that.

The Garlic Noodles with grilled beef and egg rolls was great! Just like the first time we had it in January. The tender beef paired with a bite of chewy noodles was the perfect mixture of sweet soy sauce and garlic. I would definitely come back a third time just for this!

This is our go-to place for local pho. Service is always friendly and accommodative, quality is good and consistent, and the bowls are huge. They have generally kept prices the same despite inflationary pressures or are the last to raise prices compared to other restaurants which is really greatly appreciated

Being out of town, I  choose this restaurant due to the great Google reviews, however I’m highly disappointed! Ordered pork rice.  Pork taste like rubber band with no flavor, rice was dried and old.    It’s a shame that such big city can offer such terrible food.  After I sorted through the food and had two bite. I stopped eating and went to sleep hungry .  I’m from a town with not a lot of Asian food, but I promise, I can randomly select any Vietnamese restaurant and the food would be 100% better - and half the price!

Stopped on a Wednesday, around 4:30pm. Was not busy. Very clean and pleasant atmosphere. The waitress was very polite and attentive. I ordered an extra large Pho Ga and shrimp spring rolls. They brought my order out in less than 5 minutes, and it was huge. Broth/Pho was excellent! The Spring Rolls were very fresh and the lettuce wraps were very crisp, flavor was excellent! Peanut sauce was perfect as well. I will definitely visit again if in the area! $14 (before tax and tip) for a bowl of Pho that large and two excellent Spring Rolls was a great price as well!
Solid 4 because the prices are very reasonable. The iced coffee wasn't good so I'd skip that..they are also a Cajun boil restaurant which was very surprising to us.

top_reviews.content:
*3/24/2024
I tried the Spicy Beef Brisket Rice Noodles, and it was an experience worth sharing! What I loved most was the interactive aspect of assembling the dish with its myriad of ingredients. The combination of corn, quail egg, chives, wood ear fungus, snow fungus, ham, bean curd stick, preserved cabbage, red onion, and lettuce made each bite diverse and exciting. The soup base, crafted from chicken and pork bone, added a rich depth of flavor that complemented the ingredients. The rice noodles, made entirely from rice flour, were delightfully chewy, adding a unique texture to the dish. The beef brisket was incredibly flavorful and tender.

10/25/2023
I finally got to eat at this restaurant, which I'd been wanting to try for a while. I ordered the R3 PICKLED CABBAGE & FISH FILLET RICE NOODLES, and it was a great meal. It came with 10 different ingredients like corn, quail egg, and more. What makes it special is the tasty soup made from chicken and pork bone, cooked for a long time. The noodles are made from 100% rice flour, so they're gluten-free.

The best part was the soup – it was full of flavor and made my taste buds happy. The fish was perfectly cooked and really tender. The noodles were just right – not too soft or too hard.

Ten Second Yunnan Noodle was the perfect meal after a night of drinking. The broth was light but really flavorful, and it was fun adding in all the toppings. Super comforting and tasty. The food came out pretty quick so that was a plus.
Good taste, friendly staff! Good price too! Love it.

Part of the ten seconds noodles chain. Food is good and like the ones in other ten seconds noodles place.

It would be great if they can allow us choose soup base+ protein. I know it’s a very American dining concept but can certain provide more flexibility.

4.5 stars! Quick service and excellent broth; and the soup comes out boiling hot too! I was a pretty big fan of this place. There's a decent amount of seating inside and the ambiance is very casual.

I definitely recommend the Original Crossing Bridge Rice Noodles. The broth is rich and creamy. Very flavorful and all the ingredients compliment the broth. I did think it was a bit strange that they give lettuce rather than napa cabbage though. I loved the tender beef and the goji berries! A plus is that everything on the menu is quite affordable! Considering the quality and the quantity, $14 is a great price point.

name: Bocanova
address: 1111 Broadway, Oakland, CA 94607, United States

google.name: Bocanova

top_reviews.content:
We had a wonderful time, we have a group of people and we're seated quickly. They have a full bar which made ordering cocktails so easy. We got mojitos, amaretto sour and cadillac margarita.
We shared shrimp and beef empanadas which were so juicy.
Do not forget to order yourself those poblano cornbread because I had to share mine and I regret it.
I was so excited to get the crispy fried whole branzino because I have been wanting a fried fish like this for so long and I was so juicy and flavorful. Will order again.
But the seafood cioppino dish was so flavorful it made the whole table wished they had ordered this.
We did try raw oyster for the first time which made the weekend oyster deal worth it.
Of course we ended with the dessert menu we got the sweet potato beignet omg I wish I order a whole plate to myself. The tres leches which was perfectly soaked and flavored. Guava cheesecake with mango sauce, this is a steam cheesecake so this just melts in your mouth.

This review is long overdue. My husband and I live within walking distance of Bocanova, and we’ve already dined here several times. I’ve also attended events here through my ceramic studio Kollektiv Clay, so I can say firsthand that both the staff and the owner are incredibly warm and welcoming.

A couple of my all-time favorite dishes—the fried mushrooms and fried polenta—weren’t on the menu during our most recent visit. I’m hoping they’re just rotating dishes seasonally, because they’re absolutely delicious and definitely worth ordering if you ever see them available.

On this visit, we came for happy hour and stayed for dinner. My husband had a michelada and a beer, and I ordered a mocktail that was excellent (though I’ve also had their cocktails before, and they’re fantastic). We started with the crab deviled eggs, which are always a must-order for me. Any of their ceviches are amazing. We also tried the fried fish sliders, which were very good, and the scallops, which were cooked perfectly. My husband ordered a dinner special—a hearty oxtail stew—and finished every bite. Other standout dishes we’ve enjoyed in the past include the fried cauliflower and their tacos.

Everything we’ve had here has been consistently delicious. I was too full for dessert this time, but I’ve had the bread pudding before and would easily call it their best dessert.

I highly recommend Bocanova. The food and drinks are excellent, the service is consistently top-notch, and the staff is genuinely friendly. It’s a place we love supporting and returning to again and again.

Stopped by for happy hour. Good times.

Drinks- got wine and mocktail. My guest said the Jamaica was super refreshing.

Food- we got shrimp sliders, fish sliders, Brussels sprouts, and guac + chips. The Brussels were my favorite, great flavor and cook. Love the cornmeal crust in the shrimp and chips were hearty and well seasoned.

Service- we interacted with the bartender, server, and manager. All were friendly, attentive, and professional. helpful to each other as well.

Space- love to high ceilings, great natural light and spacious. The place is huge. Two outdoor patios, main dining room, large bar, and casual seating area.

Really beautifully decorated space, it’s elevated yet not stuffy. I came for their happy hour and ordered the 2 Buck Shuck Oysters and Pork Tacos. Both very delicious, highly recommend. I think I’ll try the Duck Tostada and Beef empanada next time I come. The service was great, very dry attentive and they have a good sense of humor.

This is a cute spot for those wanting a bit more class during happy hour in Oakland.

The bathroom is clean as well (super important for me).

Every visit to Bocanova reminds us why it is one of Oakland’s most reliable dinner spots. The atmosphere strikes that perfect balance of lively and relaxed, where somehow everyone looks like they are having a better night than they planned.

We went on a weekday evening and the place was packed, which immediately felt like a very good sign. Started with cocktails at the bar and could have happily stayed there all night. Bonus points for having genuinely good non alcoholic options too, because sometimes you want the fun without waking up wondering why you ordered “just one more.”

The food was fantastic from start to finish. The ceviche was incredibly fresh, the Caesar salad disappeared embarrassingly fast, and the steak was so good there was a brief moment of silence at the table which rarely happens with our group. Every dish felt thoughtful, flavorful, and beautifully prepared.

What really makes Bocanova stand out is the hospitality. The staff makes you feel taken care of without ever feeling formal or stuffy. It has that rare combination of polished service and a genuinely fun energy.

At this point, Bocanova is one of those restaurants we keep coming back to “just for a quick dinner” that somehow turns into a three hour night with dessert. Every single time.

top_reviews.content:
Stopped by a friend’s spot and tried a couple of their rolls.

Presentation was clean and well put together. The shrimp roll had a nice crunch with a creamy, slightly spicy topping, and the salmon/mango roll was smooth with a balanced sweetness. Fish tasted fresh and the rice was done right.

Overall, solid quality and attention to detail. Definitely worth checking out.

Ok but mediocre place, nice service, mediocre food, They have an extensive list of unique cocktails I didn't try. An ok option for when you have an event/movie close by. The gyu don was very cartilage heavy, but flavors were ok. The sushi and omakase were meh, with the sushi falling apart as we ate. Stick with appetizers like the tsukune and wings.

Great place to grab a cocktail! I can't speak for the sushi, but the signature cocktails here are phenomenal. The owner runs the bar and makes the drinks, it's fun chatting with him about cocktails & the goings-on in SF.

If you're in the area and want to try some creative cocktails with a Japanese theme, this is the place to hit up!

Had an enjoyable experience at the bar within this restaurant, learning about how Derek(owner) creates his cocktails and plans for the future.  Had the Tomato Jalapeno(the Bloody Mary), the Blue Glico, friends had the Mango Curry, the Shangroni, the Mustard Nori and the Avocado Salad.  We thoroughly enjoyed the distinct flavours in all of them.  What a great option to have a cocktail spot that rotates drinks regularly with flavours that are infused from scratch.  We tried our best to convince him to open a spot in Canada!  We tried his other spot, the Blind Pig the night before, a speakeasy location that was equally impressive.

We stopped by after a graduation ceremony and had a wonderful experience. From the moment we walked in, we felt genuinely welcomed. The food was absolutely fabulous—flavorful, fresh, and beautifully presented. We also appreciated the selection of alcohol-free mocktails, which were creative and delicious. The atmosphere was warm, calm, and peaceful—a perfect setting to relax and celebrate. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a welcoming and serene dining experience.

top_reviews.content: I was walking down Haight Street and I noticed the sign for this restaurant. Looking over the menu, I saw numerous Vietnamese dishes which piqued my curiosity. I'm glad I decided to try this place out. The service was wonderful. The woman taking orders, cleaning the tables, and manning the register was friendly, attentive, and helpful. The wonton soup was piping hot and filled with wontons, bok choy, chicken, and a flavorful broth. My favorite was the Vietnamese fried egg rolls that came with a ton of greens, herbs, noodles, and a nuoc cham dipping sauce. It was messy but super delicious. When I am next in the Haight District, I will be sure to stop by this place again to try some other dishes.

I have been a few times now, and am on board with the mixed reviews regarding food quality and customer service.

One day I visited, and the pho was very good and above average. The next time I went, the rice was hard and the mushrooms were not cooked well.

They have good amenities and a quaint restaurant, and I always wonder why it is never more busy. After going a few times, I now understand.

I am sure I will return to sample another dish or have some soup, but it would not be a regular restaurant spot for me.

The meal was fantastic. We tried the sugar cane fried prawns, pork and shrimp egg rolls, combo pho, and dry cooked Meiji prawns, and everything was full of flavor. The order arrived quickly, the service was attentive, and the prices felt very fair. A solid five star experience.

Great atmosphere and service and menu options. I love the fact that they are willing to serve you a lunch special even after lunchtime. Many Chinese restaurants don’t do this, and I don’t understand why because they can welcome a lot more customers offering the rice plates all day. The only pet peeve that I had at this place is that a normal guy came in to use the bathroom and then when he came out the lady that runs the place sort of tried to demand him to buy something because he had to use the bathroom and he apologized and said hey, I’m sorry I just had to really go and she still demanded him to use the bathroom because he had used her water so she said it’s not fair that you get to use my water and don’t pay for anything which I think is pretty petty. But besides this little incident, the restaurant is pretty good.

Do not order the orange chicken. I love garlic but the flavour doesn’t go with orange chicken, especially when you have so much of it. The pieces of garlic were crazy big and crunchy. Good if it has been a garlic chicken, minus the orange. The chicken was also nice white meat but it was dry.

On the other hand the basil chicken was good and came with lots of veggies.

I thought the veggie spring rolls were going to be fresh but they were fried. For fried, not my favourite but they’ll hit the spot if you’re in the mood.

top_reviews.content: This was my first time eating here, footnote. I’m not from this area. Had a group that went hiking and decided on Thai food after the hike. Went with the chicken yellow curry and Jazmyne rice. Overall, it was good and the service was very friendly. At the end, they brought out some snacks for dessert that were prepackaged.

I found everything about this place perfect. The food was enormously good, and the red curry with wild rice was something I would get again. The ambience is cute but also proper, with good lighting and interior design. Very friendly and helpful staff as well. I came across it on a walk, while I was touring the neighborhood for a brief work trip.

We ordered takeout from here last night it was awesome. We had Chicken Satay, Crispy Spring Rolls, Papaya Salad, Eggplant Basil, Pad See Ew, Drunken Noodle and Green Curry, Papaya Salad and Cucumber Salad. Everything was super fresh and tasty really good flavor the cucumber salad is a super good deal it was like $4 or something if I lived close that would be my snack. Lastly we had mango sticky rice, Thai Iced Tea and a Vietnamese Coffee. All for a little over $100 takeout. Would definitely do takeout again but next time we gotta eat in. I didn’t take a picture of my food plated but I did take a pic of leftovers so you know it’s a real review lol enjoy.

wawathaifood is now one of my favorite Thai restaurants to visit in Oakland! It is such a hidden gem! 💕The artworks are so cute and welcoming.

My friends and I love eating here! Everything we order was delicious and so flavorful. The Sweet and sour Snapper, Fried Chicken & Roti and Pad Thai were some of my favorites, though the ginger salad was so refreshing!

You must order the #ขันโตก Khan Toke specials, it is food that is serve on a pedestal tray which is used as a small dining table. What a fun experience, with so many delicious little plates of food to samples. Don’t forget their Thai teas/coffee, and delicious cocktails.

Check them out when you’re in Oakland, make sure to bring all your friends so y’all can try ALL their delicious Northern Thai dishes, especially the Khan Toke.
We can’t wait to come back and try the other dishes.

Tasty Thai food in a trendy, super cute bistro. We visited for takeout and had the fresh spring rolls, green curry, and Kana Moo Krob. They were all really yummy! The green curry has a good flavor, but is a bit on the sweet side, with green beans and eggplant. The kana moo krob had crispy pork belly and spicy greens. It’s a super cute spot for a date, and roughly $20 per dish. The only thing it’s missing is some cats to keep you company 😹

Although it was a hassle getting their attention, we ended up being right since they charged us more than we ordered.

This restaurant seems to do well for ordering take-out, but the actual dining area is not well kept nor maintained.

The food and service here are excellent. Although it is takeout only, some seating is available; however, I've only seen family members using that section. The consistency in serving the tastiest food in the area is a testament to their skill in preparing meals. The chicken wings are superb.

Can’t speak for the dine in experience since I always door dash my meals from here but the food is delicious every time! I always get the pork chops, prawn fried rice, vegetable chow mein and Mongolian beef. Always a hit. If you DoorDash, you get a $5 credit applied to your order just fyi

name: Doma Sushi

google.description: Compact Japanese bistro offering soups, sushi & an omakase menu in charming neighborhood surrounds.

top_reviews.content:
Couldn’t be more disappointed. It’s a $30 level of meal, not $200. And most of that would go to ingredient costs, not cooking. I’m giving this two stars instead of one because we got a bottle of $15 sake for free, since the owner themself felt sorry, and at least the water is free.

We had an appointment at 7:30, and we arrived 10 minutes early. It seemed like the previous round (6 people) was not finished. That’s totally fine. But we were pushed away from the sushi bar and asked to be seated at an individual table far away, even though the bar was half empty. Originally, we were fine with that, but later it proved that we were totally wrong.

We were sitting there for 30 minutes without anyone reaching out. After that, we got our water and the wine list. 45 minutes after we entered the door, finally, we got three pieces of sashimi. Ice cold, and I couldn’t taste any flavor from the fish itself. My sashimi was even missing the wasabi. I am not feeling sorry for myself. I feel sorry for the fish that was ruined.

Obviously, the cook doesn’t know how to season the food properly most of the time. There was a shrimp where I could taste nothing but a sharp sourness, and there was a negitoro, minced tuna, that I remember, full of saltiness. That was the time when I was truly grateful that at least the water was free. When I tasted the fried egg roll, I almost laughed out loud. It was mushy inside, so you couldn’t figure out what the ingredient was, and the outside layer was not even crisp. It’s the same one you can get from any supermarket and cook at home. Even Panda Express can serve a better version. I still can’t believe that I had this yesterday. It’s like being invited to the White House and getting a Big Mac for dinner level of joke. Sincerely, if you don’t know how to make an egg roll, or a Chinese spring roll, I can teach you. The dessert was another Costco-level mix-up. They were not even trying. The only thing good for the entire night, in 2.5 hours, was the eel. I’m not gonna lie. It was the best eel I’ve had this year so far. Hey, but I paid $200 for that.

What else? A 22% tip is absurd. If there is a mandatory tip, include that in your price. How to reduce your tax is your problem, that’s not my business. Or maybe they already knew that I would definitely put a 0 if it were optional. Since we were sitting isolated, most of our dishes came 5–10 minutes later than the main group. I was just sitting there and seeing that the main group got their dishes, and we got nothing.

For the environment, I won’t be too harsh on the cook’s musical taste. But I’m definitely not okay with music that loud. I don’t know why they dimmed all the lights. All pictures except the sashimi one were exposed for more than one second. Appearance is an important part of the food. Unless you are trying to hide something.

Hands down one of the best omakase I've ever had! There were lots of fresh fish straight from Japan such as; hamachi (yellow tail), Toro or tune belly, uni (urchin), salmon, ebi (shrimp), scallops with uni, eel. Everything that was served melted in your mouth.

I also really appreciated the intimate setting, I was able to talk to the chef and learn about different Japanese etiquette and learn about the ingredients used.

I highly recommend this spot if you're with a date or a small group of friends.

One of the best omakase experiences and sushi’s I have had!! Cute small restaurant run by a husband and wife. Everything was delicious.

The husband / chef was funny in his own way and they made sure we were well taken care of.

Highly recommend and will come back.

The best omakase and multi-course dinner I’ve ever had. We came to celebrate our anniversary here and a great time. The atmosphere was perfect and the food/fish were literally hands down the best I’ve ever had. If you want high quality omakase where every bite is the perfect blend and diversity of textures and flavors you must go here.

Quasi-private dining experience with exquisite omakase curated with top shelf fresh seafood run by a single chef and a single waitress/hostess.  Impressive culinary arts in whimsical and small dining room.  Wagyu beef topped with caviar and gold flakes nigiri for the win.  Improvements could include more familiar Japanese beers and sake along with allowing customer to choose tip percentage based on quality of service.  (I’m not a fan of flat 20% no matter what for service fee).  All in all, great dining experience and worth revisiting!

I recommend asking for hot sauce for the tamal since it's not crazy spicy but instead brings a great smokey flavor with the right amount of heat. 🔥 Friendly staff and great prices!

Edit: the pineapple tamales are vegan and so so good!!! 🍍🫔

Fantastic tlayudas! Can't believe I hadn't tried them till now, I recommend them! They also make them vegan with pumpkin flour or huitlacoche. Their food feels carefully made, and I appreciate the subtle flavors and that they don't use excessive oil.

This meal was so delicious, I couldn't even wait to leave before writing a review. The pozole is so flavorful and perfectly served hot with all the fixing. The staff is extremely friendly, welcoming, and helpful. Make sure to order the Oaxacan Hot Chocolate - it's frothed fresh for you at your table and is so delectable that it's a perfect addition to any meal you can order here. I will be back for the soup and cocoa alone. My wife also got a tomale, tostada, and potato taco Dorado and loved everything. Must try if you're in the area!

The food is excellent—authentic, hot, and carefully prepared. I wish I could rate the service even higher, but on the night that we went, I believe they were short staffed, which caused quite a delay in service. In the end, the food was worth the wait, and we left wanting to go back again!

5/5, everything was delicious, especially the salsa de chicharron!  Will 100% be back.

Only feedback is they can really upgrade the aesthetics w/ a floor to ceiling curtain in front of the locker area. (I only mention because I want this place to stick around long term!)

top_reviews.content:
Found this restaurant when we are around this area and looking for lunch. Itvis located at Outer Sunset neighborhood specializing in authentic Teochew Chinese cuisine.
It is small and busy restaurant during lunch hours.
We ordered Sohomei signature laksa vermicelli, porridge, crispy donut stick  and steamed  rice roll.
The order was ready pretty quickly.  The dishes are unique especially the laksa and porridge. They are really yummy. The lasksa is light  The riceroll is also good.
You should give it a try if you are around the neighborhood as the dishes are unique.

Authentic Cantonese food. Delicious!
Ordered:
ChaoShan Beef Steamed Rice Roll
Chao Zhou Pan Fried Oyster Cake
Hot and Sour Lao Fun Soup

Incredible silky rice noodles, filled with ground pork, egg, cabbage, bean sprouts and a little shrimp. Probably the best rice noodles I've had, maybe even from Hong Kong.
Enough for a not-heavy meal.
Some aunties were here slurpy noodles on a weekday lunch, great vibes.

I’m writing this review while still at the restaurant- that’s how blown away I am. This was the most incredible chicken congee I’ve ever had in my life. Not only was service quick, efficient and mindful (it’s a cold rainy day here in SF, and instead of bringing me water, the waiter brought me a cup of hot tea- just what I needed!).

I came here for rice porridge and when I saw it was $18 I was a little unsure- I am a chef and know how much wholesale ingredients cost, but SF is expensive to live/operate a business in & I like to support small family businesses, so I ordered. Well- this was absolutely worth every penny! The porridge is the perfect texture; flavorful, topped with fresh fragrant herbs and big meaty pieces of chicken within. It’s a huge portion, so it is more than worth the price. I ordered fried donut sticks to dip into the congee and oh my gosh…I have perhaps passed on and gone to heaven. This is PHENOMENAL. And nothing needed to be seasoned! It came out perfect, no need to add salt or white pepper or anything. The chef and kitchen team are true masters at their craft.

If you are ever in the SF area and craving a good bowl of rice porridge, this is THE place to go. This is the kind of place that should have a line around the block. Absolutely divine.

Heard some great things about this place so I decided to give it a try with some friends. It's quite cozy and clean inside, and the staff members were welcoming and helpful, especially the owners who enthusiastically helped us navigate through the menu. After all, Chinese Chao Zhou cuisine is pretty rare in this area and new to many.

We ordered their signature Chao Zhou Pan Fried Oyster Cake, Shrimp & Pork Shantou Steamed Rice Roll, Beef Ball Soup and Shantou Duck Porridge, all served quickly and looked super appetizing. The oyster cake was crispy on the outside and chewy on the inside, and there was a generous amount of oysters which tasted fresh. The rice rolls look like semi-transparent enchiladas stuffed with shrimp, pork, eggs and wow were they good. I particularly liked the rice sheets since they were so soft, slippery and chewy, and paired well with the savory sweet sauce. The beef balls had this fine, smooth texture, almost bouncy. Last but not least, the duck porridge was quite warming and nourishing.

I think the price is fair for the quality and amount of food, as well as the great ambience and services.

All in all I'm very delighted we came across this little gem. It was money well spent and I'll FOR SURE (no puns intended) be back sooner than later!

Both were terrific! The shrimp were perfectly cooked with just the right amount of spice, while the Jambalaya had its own special kick!  We also tried the Mac n Cheese, which is one of the best that I have ever had. Very creamy and smooth with a beautiful cheese pull.  We also tried the rice and gravy, which is a staple in Louisiana.  It was so good, I honestly wanted to lick the bowl.  We were too full to try dessert, so that just means that we have to come back.  This was one of the best Louisiana meals that I have ever had outside of the state. I cannot wait to come back and try more dishes.  Do yourself a favor and check them out.

I can sympathize when a restaurant is short staffed and the food takes longer to come out. But I don't believe that should compromise the quality, especially at this price point. We did appetizers and dessert and the highlight was the dessert.

The only thing I was looking forward to having was the Shrimp and Crawfish chowder, and to my disappointment they were already out only a couple of hours after opening.

The Po'Thang Sliders were dry and chewy and looked nothing like the pictures they advertise. Nothing to write home about. The best part of the Chilean Sea Bass were the sides. The fish was cooked well but didn't have a distinct flavor.

The menu seems to be modified from what's advertised. They were serving the short ribs as a sandwich on ciabata bread with fries. The short ribs were decent, and the bread was good, but the fries left so much to be desired. There was no seasoning whatsoever in either the sweet potato or the regular fries. Also, they were not crispy and had a recently-defrosted texture. Would rather have received some greens or rice instead.

My wife had been looking forward to eating here for a while and we both were not impressed. Especially considering there is so much competition in Oakland for Southern food that's better tasting and less expensive. Now we know, I guess.

Great place for breakfast, brunch, lunch, dinner... all the above. The owner was wonderful and came to check on us in their overflow event space. She gave us the history of the family business and her vision of the building and what she wants to transform the space into. The food was wonderful and tasty and the servers were great...especially Bri. She was attentive and patient with our entire party. This is definitely a go to and I would love to collaborate using her event space for events that I throw. Thank you.

I’ve been wanting to try Willows & Pine for a while, so my family and I finally went around 5:50 pm, close to 6. The front area was already packed, so they seated us in the back. We were the first group back there, but it still felt nice. The restaurant itself is beautiful and the music was great, which set a really good tone.

There was one young woman with short hair handling everything. She was the hostess and the server, so it was necessary to be patient. She did a good job managing it all and stayed pleasant throughout.

Now the food.

The “short ribs” were not short ribs. It was clearly chuck roast. There was no bone at all and the texture was that of a pot roast. It was cooked very well and tasted good, so I did not mind it, but it should be labeled correctly. They should just add carrots, potatoes, and celery and market it as a proper pot roast dish.

We also had the smothered pork chops with rice and collard greens. Everything was really delicious, hot, and fresh. The greens especially tasted like they were cooked that same day, which I appreciated. They even had soups that were not ready because it was still cooking. Hot fresh food will win every time! They are actually COOKIN’ back dere. Real southern roots, for sure.

For starters, we had the cabbage and cornbread, which were both pretty good. We also had the sausage and chicken dish, whether it was jambalaya or étouffée. It had a strong spice level and a heavy bay leaf flavor. That bay leaf flavor really stood out. Bay leaf should add to the flavors, not overtake them.

We started with a salad as well. The salad itself was fresh, but the dressing was very sweet. It needs something acidic like vinegar or lemon to cut through that sweetness.

What I really enjoyed was the frozen rum cocktail. It was delicious and one of the highlights of the meal.

Now the part that did not work at all. The mac and cheese was not good. EEEEEEEEYYYUCKKK!!
It was soupy, very heavy on dairy flavor, like milk, not cheese, the noodles were mushy, and the sauce was broken. Even though it was clearly made fresh, the flavor was off. We ended up leaving the entire bowl on the table.

Overall, you come here for fresh, flavorful soul food and you will get that with most of the dishes. The service and atmosphere were both solid. I would come back again, but I would definitely skip the mac and cheese.

The food was delicious! The prix fixed brunch is more than enough to serve two to three people.
It was my first time visiting, I was really unsure if it was a seat yourself kind of deal when my party and I first walked in. We stood at the counter for a minute before being greeted.
The vibe was very relaxed and family oriented.
I would go back again for the food even if it was for take out.

I usually approach my reviews with a fair and understanding perspective, but my recent visit to Little Caesars in Alameda on November 24th at around 4 PM was nothing short of a letdown. As someone who appreciates good customer service, I was taken aback by the staff's attitude, particularly the individual handling our order.

Firstly, there was a glaring issue with our order. We intended to enjoy a simple meal - just one pizza to share. However, due to what seemed like a lack of attention or perhaps miscommunication, our order was incorrectly doubled, resulting in an unnecessary expense of $50.

When we attempted to address this with the staff member, his response was far from satisfactory. He refused to correct the order, stating that he had already informed the kitchen, which felt like a dismissive excuse rather than a legitimate reason. His approach lacked any semblance of kindness or understanding, which is fundamental in customer service.

Moreover, his overall demeanor was unaccommodating. He barely paid attention to what we were saying, making us feel unheard and undervalued as customers. This kind of interaction is not what one expects when stepping into an establishment known for its fast and friendly service.

In conclusion, this experience was a significant departure from the quality and service I've come to expect from Little Caesars. I hope this feedback serves as a constructive point for the team at the Alameda branch to improve their service standards and ensure no other customer has to face a similar situation.

This location is TERRIBLE! I ordered pizza online 2 hours in advance to be delivered to a high school WITH instructions to “hand deliver” pizza to the office. After waiting 20 min AFTER the specified time it was supposed to arrive, I referred to the email receipt and to my surprise, a link to Grub Hub showing that the pizza had been delivered! It had not.
I contacted the store to inquire where my order disappeared to. I was told by the employee that they NEVER received the order even though I had a receipt and “delivery” confirmation. This a-hole proceeded to tell me that not only was I not getting my order, but I also wasn’t getting a refund!
Thankfully, the email receipt had a customer service number to call. Not only did I get a refund, I was told a complaint would be filed on my behalf against the store and the Grub Hub driver who took the tip without giving me my order.
After reading these reviews, I’m happy I didn’t get that pizza. It probably would’ve been as bad as the customer service at this location. Sounds like they need to get some new staff and management.

top_reviews.content: This an awesome space in the city with great food options and a chic space for working (superior option over a lot of coffee shops in the area), gathering with friends, or events. They do a drag bingo event the first Sunday of every month and June’s was so fun!

This a nice size food hall. You can move between places and get what you need. Friendly independent folks across the board. Great example of San Francisco. Food is off the charts. The bar is chill and friendly. Popcorn machine anyone? Peace.

Love this food hall!! They have a great selection of vendors, great vibes, and friendly staff. I’ve visited Saluhall several times for lunch / brunch, and I’ve been impressed every time by the variety — there’s an option for everyone, and, if you need a post-meal walk, you can always wander around the IKEA showroom. I love how spacious the space is, and I appreciate that they give each vendor a lot of space to work. I was initially a bit surprised by how few vendors / slots they had open for such a giant two-story space, but I think the extra kitchen space allows the vendors to operate a bit more like they would in a normal restaurant and serve more complex things (vs. say, Union Market in DC, where it feels like everyone is on top of each other).

My favorite vendors (so far — I haven’t tried them all) are:
- Momo — wonderful Sichuan-style noodle shop! The noodles are spicy and numbing, have a wonderful al dente texture, and come topped with super flavorful braised tofu (or meat). I think they could make the noodles even more spicy and numbing, but I may be a bit of an edge case.

- Curry Up Now — super tasty Indian street food spot! The tikka masala paneer is absolutely delicious, and the springy, but rich cheese goes wonderfully with the curry. The curry typically comes with a healthy serving of rice — about as much as the curry — and you can add naan for an extra fee. They also give out free chai that is quite tasty; it’s a bit sweet but not overly so, and super warm and comforting.

They also have a lovely cafe that I can’t remember the name of for the life of me, but the coffee is phenomenal. It’s super rich and nutty, and you can absolutely taste the flavor of the espresso, even through the milk of, say, a latte. And, of course, you can never go wrong with the IKEA food hall.

Overall, lovely food hall with tons of amazing goodies. I can’t wait to come back and try more of their stalls!
Such a great environment for having lunch regardless of group size. It’s very clean, very open, and there’s plenty of good food options. I’d definitely recommend this place, especially Smish Smash.

I love this place for all the vegan options it has to offer. Sadly the vegan burger place on the first floor is no longer there, but there are still a lot of options on the second floor! Vegan baklava and vegan lions mane steak at Kayma (also serves non-vegan options); Vegan skewers and desserts at Casa Borinqueña (100% vegan); Tacos and burritos at La Venganza (100% vegan). Saluhall is vegans' mecca and for them to invite none vegans to try some of the best vegan creations!
