top_reviews.content:
I tried their food when they were selling it in Facebook marketplace around 2020. Their fusion of Indonesian and Texas bbq was really cool, and the first dish I tried back then was their brisket soto, which was truly amazing and creative. When I heard that they were opening a brick and mortar in 2023, I had been wanting to go, but insane hype made it nearly impossible to go to, until now.

For two people, we (I) got way too much, but also it was nice that we could try nearly all of their main items on the menu. Starting with the starters, we got their nasi goreng and the smoked ayam lumpia. Their nasi goreng was average at best, it did not have any wok hei and didn’t taste like nasi goreng that I knew and loved. The smoked ayam lumpia was pretty good, they were very generous with the meat, but it was nothing special.

Next was the bbq meats: the brisket, beef back rib. and jalapeno cheese beef sausage. These meats overall showed the biggest problem we had, it was all very salty. I am not sure whether it was just a fluke, but every meat was quite salty and we felt like we needed more rice to balance it out. The brisket had a nice flavor minus the saltiness, but we did get the flat, I think that the point would have been better for the fattiness. The beef back rib could have been more tender, it was overall too hard and needed more time in the smoker. The sausage was interesting in that it was not snappy, but felt very meaty. I did enjoy the sausage, but a little more snappiness would have been nice.

Lastly, we got their rendang plate, which contained rendang, telur balado, kerupuk, perkedel, and gulai kale. The telur was really nice and a cool westernized version, where the yolk was kept running instead of the super green yolk traditionally seen. The kerupuk was nice, but also probably a bit too much on the plate. The perkedel was good and standard. My favorite side on the plate was the gulai, it tasted exactly like the one my mom made at home, though a bit on the salty side. Lastly, the main part was the rendang. While the flavors were solid and tasted like rendang, though a bit salty, I was not a fan of the meat itself. They used parts of the brisket, feels like burnt ends, instead of meat stewed from the start. I appreciated the creativity, but using smoked meat took away from the flavors of the rendang itself, and the meat felt a bit tough. I prefer it to be more like a soft stewed meat.

Given my excitement to go here, I was slightly disappointed by this experience. I do really appreciate how they have brought Indonesian cuisine to the spotlight in this area, and I am happy for the great reception they have gotten, but also I hope that this visit was an off day on their part, because the saltiness overall was excessive. I do want to go back to try the dish that made me want to go here again, the brisket soto, and to see if it is less salty next time.

We arrived 40 minutes early on a Sunday to ensure we had good position in line. Everyone in line was treated to a delicious sample just before opening, very kind!

We ordered 2x dino ribs, brisket, beef cheek, jalapeño sausage, nasi goreng, lumpia, rendang, and a cendol. Everything was very delicious and the service was great!

Only critique is - where is the heat?! Please offer sambal or a spicy sauce. Both sauces were a bit too sweet for our taste.

Fikscue Craft BBQ is an absolute gem. The Indonesian BBQ fusion concept is unique, creative, and packed with flavor. The brisket was the highlight—beautifully smoked, tender, juicy, and full of rich flavor. You can really taste the care and craftsmanship that goes into the barbecue.

The nasi goreng was an excellent complement to the smoked meat, bringing a distinctive Indonesian touch that makes Fikscue stand out from a typical BBQ restaurant. The seasoned fries were also delicious and worked perfectly with the rest of the meal.

The portions are generous—around 2 lbs (almost 1 kg) of brisket along with the rice and fries—and everything felt well prepared and thoughtfully put together. It’s not inexpensive, but the quality of the meat, portion size, and overall experience make it feel like a special meal rather than just another BBQ dinner.

If you enjoy serious smoked brisket but want something different from traditional American BBQ, Fikscue Craft BBQ is definitely worth trying. Excellent food, distinctive flavors, and a memorable BBQ experience. Highly recommended!

I drove a long way specifically to try this halal BBQ steakhouse — and it was absolutely worth it! Finding a halal steakhouse is so rare, and this place did not disappoint.

I ordered three cuts: Brisket, Dino Ribs, and Beef Back Ribs. As a foodie with a trained palate, here’s my honest breakdown:

The Brisket was well-cooked with good flavor, but leaned a little on the lean side for my personal taste — I prefer my meat with a bit more juiciness and fat. Still solid, and great for those who prefer a leaner cut.

The Dino Ribs were the absolute star of the meal. The flavor was incredible — rich, tender, with just the right amount of natural, sticky fat. Truly outstanding. This is a must-order!

The Beef Back Ribs were also delicious and similar in texture to the Dino Ribs, but came with a sweet marinade that made them slightly sweeter in flavor.

My top pick: Dino Ribs — 10/10, no question. Highly recommend this place to anyone searching for quality halal BBQ!

We had brisket, cheeks, and beef short ribs.

The short ribs are the only thing worth getting imo.  It had the proper balance of fat, tenderness, smoke and rub.

The brisket is fine but doesn’t compare.  Part of the issue is their rub is very salty.  They need to fix this — maybe 30% less salt and it’d be bomb.  And this is coming from a guy who has a high tolerance for salt.  If you get an end piece of brisket that has more rub it can be difficult to eat for more sensitive folks.

The other issue with the brisket is — not enough smoke.  The fat cap lacked the infusion of smoke that i got from the short ribs.  Perhaps it was just an unlucky cut.  I’m reading online that they use almond wood as well, so maybe I don’t like almond wood /shrug

Finally, I really wish they posted descriptions of their Indonesian dishes on the menu.  I had to google a bunch but still couldn’t find some.

top_reviews.content:
Bir Kitchen truly feels like a taste of home away from home. The food is not just delicious — it feeds both the stomach and the soul.

Today I ordered a Thali set which has  such an amazing variety of authentic dishes — fresh basmati rice,, creamy raita , takda dal, Goat Curry , flavorful salad, so many homemade-style sides. Every item tastes fresh, balanced, and cooked with love, just like traditional Himalayan/Nepali-Indian food should be.
And the hospitality — so warm, so welcoming. They treat you like family, not just customers. You walk in hungry and walk out satisfied, happy, and thankful.

If you want food that comforts your heart and reminds you of home, Bir Kitchen is the best place at SFO downtown .

Highly recommended. Keep it up! 🙏

AMAZING and AUTHENTIC Food!!!
HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!

We ordered their veg momos, samosa, chole batura, veg thali, panipuri. Every dish was made to order by the head chef Bir thapa, food was really fresh. Taste was authentic.
Not oily at all. Even the deep fried chole batura did not feel oily.

Great vegetarian options. You can taste the freshness of food in every bite.
They make their own samosas and momos fresh everyday and do not use frozen ones like many other indian restaurants.

I will definitely visit again and agai . Highly recommend this place.
Great ambience.  Good option for date nights too.

This is the best place for all the heavy hitters.  I am so thrilled with the level of culinary skill that I want everyone who appreciates great desi food to get to experience the food here.  I started coming here a month after they opened. I've probably eaten here 5 times and ordered out 4 times.

In particular, these are my favorite things to order:

The Non-Veg platter.  It includes:
------
Tandoori Chicken:  most tender tandoori chicken I've ever had in ages.  It compared a legendary tandoori spot that I went to in the Margalla Hills in Pakistan.

Chicken Manchurian:  a classic indochinese fusion dish, it takes crispy fried chicken and tosses it in a perfectly tangy, not too spicy, savory sauce.

Chili Momo (4 pieces):  The crispy fried dumpling is filled with a juicy, herbaceous, super tasty ground chicken. It's then tossed In sauce of garlicy onions & bell peppers.

Fried fish:  perfectly fried appetizer bites of breaded fish are topped with minced fried red onions. The topping is SO GOOD.
------

Butter Chicken: you can taste the Ghee and the cream. It's so good and the chicken is tender tender tender.   It's served with fluffy basmati rice in copper dishes.

Chicken Lababdar. A Mughlai dish that you never see on most menus unless you're in South Asia. This is a MUST try. The chicken is tender and the cashew, ghee, and cream sauce is incredible. We always order this.

Naan:  The fluffy garlic naan is topped with ghee and there is whole fennel seed in the dough.  It tastes so good when it's cooked.

Chapati- 2 smaller pieces in an order. They are soft and delicious.

Gulab Jamun- served warm. It is THE BEST  with layers of flavor, made with ghee, bathed in an aromatic syrup.

Mango lassi- they use fresh mango. It's great.

All the chutneys and sauces are substantial, super fresh, and aromatic.

Tried the jhol momo, tandoor momo, palak paneer, and chicken korma at BIR Kitchen, and honestly the flavors reminded me of Hyderabad. The spice level was on point and the food had that authentic rich taste that’s hard to find. The momos were especially flavorful, and both the palak paneer and chicken korma were well balanced and comforting. If you enjoy proper Indian spice and bold flavors, this place is definitely worth trying

We had non veggie platter, naan, biryani, Paneer, curry goat. Everything was good and tasty except too spicy for us. Felt very authentic. We asked medium spicy but it was way too spicy even though we do eat spicy.

I didn’t like the quail. It was very well executed but I didn’t think it went with the meal. Quail is not used much in Korean cuisine except for the eggs, but the course didn’t utilize the eggs at all.

Overall, it was a lovely meal and I would return for a new menu.

Fantastic service. Probably one of the best in town. It was warm, delicate, yet also casual and welcoming. We never felt pressured nor anything. It was just right.

We had a wonderful time and I’ll definitely come back again. The service was truly top tier.

Will probably travel to the bay just to dine here again at some point.

We didn't eat in, but had delivery.  My partner and I were inspired to try udon after watching a tour of Japan's udon restaurants in Okinawa (side quest from playing Yakuza Kiwami).  The menu at Marugame is exactly what we saw on the show, so we decided to try it and we were incredibly satisfied beyond expectation.  We were talking about how good the meal was all night until bedtime.  We woke up today asking each other when we should have udon dinner again, which will most likely be on a weekly basis now.  It's on the boards as our favorite after just one order.  I had the Nikutama udon, and my bowl was clean in five minutes, probably the best thing I've eaten all year.  My partner had the beef tomatama and his bowl was also licked clean.  He later made dumplings and used our leftover dashi sauce, not letting a single drop go to waste.  We also ordered one of each of the tempura and every piece was delicious.  We're making it a point to try every dish on the menu for future orders.  We also now want to move to Japan.

3.1.25
Long awaited opening finally here!

Love how they've transformed this location which used to be Panera. It is now so bright and spacious, compared to the slightly tight and dim feeling that it used to be. Makes this space much more inviting. There's lots of seating indoors and outdoors.

Service was smooth and efficient. Wonder if line will get longer as people start coming throughout this week and into weekend.

Calamansi drink was refreshing! Not too sweet and not too tart.

Tempura (chicken katsu, tomagoyaki and gyoza) were all yummy. Not dripping with oil which means it was cooked when oil was sufficiently hot enough. It was definitely an improvement here compared to the Berkeley location that has become very oily that we generally forgo their tempura now.

Lastly the three different bowls of udon we had were umami! We finished three bowls completely including the soup/gravy to the last drop. Udon texture is an improvement from Berkeley, but compared to Waikiki, Oahu, still missing the slightly chewy texture that takes udon to the next level. Making noodle is an art so hopefully Alameda location can continue to improve.

We will be back now that it's 3x closer to us.

3.9.25
Decided to try their online ordering and take out today. Food was ready within 10 minutes! This is awesome.

Food tasted just like in the restaurant - delicious!

Only downside that may have been overlooked is the quantity of broth. We ordered 2 large nikutama udon and the portion of noodles and beef was good except that the broth was a little too little (see included picture with this review). So we made a little broth to go with it so that we have enough. Hopefully the restaurant can continue to improve and make sure this is resolved next time - I'll share again when I do take out.

top_reviews.content:
Souvla is always one of our favorite stops whenever we visit San Francisco. It is the perfect place for a fresh, flavorful Greek-style salad or wrap — and somehow the addition of French fries inside just makes everything even better. Simple, delicious comfort food done right.

Everything tastes fresh, balanced, and high quality, from the perfectly seasoned meats to the crisp vegetables and amazing sauces. It is one of those places that feels casual but consistently delivers every single time.

The atmosphere is always lively and welcoming, and the service is quick and friendly. We seriously wish Souvla would expand to Southern California because there is nothing quite like it down here. It has become such a treat and tradition for us whenever we are back in San Francisco.

The other day was feeling healthy and wanted to try something new so came here since luve in the neighborhood.

Unfortunately this day I took the recommendation of the waiter/host to try the seasonal trout pita wrap. It sucked so much. The trout itself was ok but was disproportionate compared to the rest of the ingredients. Veggies were bland and overall felt heavily underseasoned. The worse part of it all was the pita. It was cold and hard which made it annoyingly chewy. $23 for something I should of just invested in making myself for a third the price, more filling and tastier. I ended up drowning it in hot sauce to finish and not waste food.

I guess I'll stick to the salads as they never are a bad choice. Service was friendly and really fast. Restaurant is always clean and tidy so no complaints there.

Beautiful and cozy outpost of this SF fast casual staple! Souvla has always been a favorite, with its outstanding salads, pitas, and frozen yogurt. My go-to is their vegetarian salad, which is absolutely loaded with tons of fresh greens, cheese, olives, nuts, and roasted white sweet potato. You can also get any salad Greek style and add a solid helping of fries on top for just $1 — a great choice if you don’t want to have an entire side of fries but still want something crispy. The salads are pretty big, so they can often be multiple meals (or one meal and a snack), especially if you get them with fries :). This location is especially fun — I love how wide and open the space is, especially with their super high ceilings. The overall vibe is almost industrial chic, but they also have this really fun tree encased in glass in the center of their back wall. The team is awesome and super efficient and friendly — can’t wait to come back!
Really good lamb wrap! Although I do think it was quite small. 😅 Loved the interior of the restaurant.

As a vegetarian I left this beautiful place quite disappointed. There was one option on the menu and a special. If I was still hungry, and I was, I could got the fries. The sweet potato pita was just not up to the mark. The texture and the flavor was underwhelming. It's personal, but the element of sweet does not go well in this format. The fries were good. And I wished the egg lemon soup was vegetarian. But it was chicken based.

top_reviews.content:
Really delicious sushi with a wide and varied menu. We Got the local tofu (very yummy). Chefs nigiri tasting, sashimi tasting and zeitgeist roll.
We were split on liking the Nigiri vs Sashimi tasting better, but I liked the Nigiri. Pieces had rice+fish+a little something that really complemented the fish.
Zeitgeist roll was so rich and delicious! Like the highest quality fatty drunk food you have ever had. Shrimp Tempura+avocado+eel+fatty tuna it was so decadent.

First time coming here, sushi was really good and nigiri and sashimi offered a lot of different choices. Very convenient that the hot barley tea comes with refills, because it was honestly really good. The store was a little hard to find, as there is no sign above the door. Otherwise, one of the best sushi places I’ve ever been to! :)

Had dinner with a friend. We reserved in Resy. We ordered to local sake. We also ordered charashi Deluxe, Sashimi Special & a crudo.  We sat at the sushi bar and conversed with the sushi chef. The service was good though sometimes the waitress didn’t see us since we were at the bar. The place looks like any sushi restaurant. Clean and organized. We enjoyed all the sushi they served. They didn’t have uni in this day.

One of the Japanese restaurants I’ve never been to before, and it turned out to be really good～everything was so fresh and delicious! 🍣✨

I’m honestly not very good at picking restaurants, but luckily, someone is really good at it and is happy to pick a place. I really appreciate all the effort and consideration! ❤️

Such a good experience here~ I think I’m getting used to sitting at the bar. 😂

Seated immediately at the bar- our server was super attentive, and it was impressive watching the sushi chefs work so quickly. Fresh sashimi, great rolls (I’ll order anything with toro!), and everything came out timely. Intimate, great-value sushi spot in SF - definitely coming back. I have my eyes on the hamachi Kama + ox and tiger roll next!

top_reviews.content: Very nice couple serving tasty food and generous portions. There was a misunderstanding with our order where they served us the plate we didn't order and also refunded the money although we insisted that we want to pay because we consumed the food but they didn't take back the money. Very kind people.

This place was amazing. The food was fresh, airy and packed with flavor. The restaurant was open and had many unique tables to sit. The service was fast and we received all of our food in under 10 minutes. I ordered the beef kabob platter and it was great. The beef was very tender, I could pull it apart with my hands and it was very flavorful and paired with everything very well. The side cucumber salad was very aromatic and tangy and paired contrasted well with the rice and bread. I put everything in the pita bread and it was amazing. You could tell everything was made freshly with good ingredients. The pita chips were so good, crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. Perfect. The staff were kind and served us very fast. This place needs more hype it’s so good.

Cute and delicious!

I never had food like this when growing up, but oh wow, eating it hit the nostalgia spot, like if my mom had made it. Everything felt warm and welcoming. The food is rich and alive, you can taste the freshness an love in every bite. I had a falafel wrap, spicy hummus and a side of tabouli, everything was fenomenal. The service was perfect, its like eating at your house. Thank you for everything!
Very good and satisfying. The chicken schwarma, vegetables, rice and hummus were all a great combination. A nice healthy meal.

First time here, finding parking was the key.
It was 1:30 on a Wed. Place was empty when I arrived, but 4 other diners showed up before I left.
All the food coming out of the cooking area looked GREAT. Good presentation, more than ample and plentiful portions.
Gal at the counter was also very nice.
I had the Falafel Burger and fries - $13.99 (bargain $$)
Food came out mostly hot the the fries, were exceptional.
Only downside, inside smelled like "old grease" a bit off putting.
All the condiments on the table were greasy and dirty.
My burger bun was quite soppy and did not hold up well.
I might go back, but eat outside if it's a nice day. The old great smell was pretty overwhelming.
Should add the menu was not "overwhelming", which I appreciated.

The most kid friendly restaurant we’ve ever been to! Not only was the food yummy, but the staff was so amazing with our children. They had special cups, plates and silverware for them and welcomed them so warmly.

Bangkok Thai Cuisine: A Delicious Trip to Thailand

I recently had a fantastic meal at Bangkok Thai Cuisine, and it was a delightful trip to Thailand without leaving town! The Pad Thai was a real standout. It wasn't just delicious, it was perfectly balanced. The sweet, savory, and just a hint of spice all played together beautifully. Every bite was a flavor party in my mouth!

The veggie rolls were another winner. They were incredibly fresh and packed with flavor. The crispy lettuce gave way to a delightful filling making for a satisfying and light starter.

Overall, Bangkok Thai Cuisine impressed me. The food was fresh, flavorful, and authentic-tasting.  While I can't speak to the entire menu, both the Pad Thai and veggie rolls were fantastic.  If you're looking for a delicious and affordable Thai dining experience, I highly recommend giving them a try!

top_reviews.content: Friendly atmosphere on Solano ave, friendly staff. Customer bathroom. Avoid lunch time because school kids frequent this spot, families come mostly in the evening. The wait for your pizza is anywhere from 4-7min, so a short wait. The crust is a nice bonus, if you've got the belly gobble that crust. They have recycle and compost bins near the soda fridge. There's a slice and drink combo, I always recommend. The pizza is great for the value, portion and area, there's a deep dish pizza restaurant further down Solano if you want to spend a bit more and want the social scene and ambience. This is better than Dominoes, also further up Solano in the opposite direction, Dominoes is still good and they have a great crew. This is the healthy and affordable middle of those two. And they have indoor dining. Please clean up after yourselves, this is run by a nice family.

So we’ve been ordering from this place before and it was good, but today we ordered again and it was awful- the crust was totally different, hard and thin and flat, reminded me of a bad stale flatbread that is super hard and dry. I called to ask if they changed t he recipe and said no. So I’m really frustrated with the fact that I waited for 2 hours for this to be delivered and it was soooo bad.

On vacation in Berkley CA and found this place walking around on our first night in town. Like most places downtown, it is cozy and has that inner city vibe. Not really a sit down pizzeria but a cool place to grab a slice of tasty and thin crust, NY style, pizza. Tonight our slices were meat lovers and NY (sausage, pep and mushrooms). Pizza was tasty, enough sauce and toppings and although my crust was a burned on the edges, it wasn't enough to keep me from finishing it. There was a bit of confusion on the order and we ended up splitting a lunch special but it was enough that we will return later. Overall, I would easily recommend this place if you need a quick snack or to have a craving for NY style.

Solid slice of pizza. I tried the Long Island style pizza. They included plenty of meat in terms of toppings and I was satisfied with the value. I also liked that it was tasty even as I arrived closed to closing time.
Best thin crust I've found in east bay; close to my favorite place in NYC when I lived in Manhattan  years ago. You can't beat da deal of 2 slices AND a drink for just under 10 bucks.

top_reviews.content: PHONE ORDER AHEAD. I wasn't prepared to wait over an hour for my food and honestly I think there might have been a mistake. BUT with the reviews and willingness of other guests to wait the time suggested by the person taking orders- I had a strong feeling it would be worth it. Just before I went full on Hungry Diva mode I finally received my bag of food... and it was a heavy bag. Look. Don't come here if you are on a tight budget or tight schedule. That said, you get a TON of food fresh and literally piping hot still when I got home. I love that they didn't (couldn't) completely close the takeout containers because the steam would have made the crispy batter soft. I ordered the Pineapple Prawn plate in which you get to pick the side and opted for the Garlic Noodles. Also ordered Dry Beef Ribs. The ribs come battered and 'dry' meaning no sauce covering them. Good by itself but even better with the sweet sour sauce they provide. But the real winner is the delicious and perfectly battered prawns. Tastes great with their fire homemade pineapple sauce on the side. The garlic noodles are SO garlicy and yum. Def want to try more. As always my love for the environment - will remind businesses that you DO NOT have to include plastic utensils and shouldn't unless requested, because they go directly into the trash can.

SO FIRE!! Know that you are going to order and wait, so be patient if you want to try this bomb food! We did two 4 Way Plates ~ choice of rice or noodles, choice of chicken wings or ribs, choice of Chicken or Beef sticks & 1 egg roll. Our favorites were Beef stick, garlic noodles & egg roll!! Will be back to enjoy more! Thai tea is a MUST!

I ordered the beef sticks, chicken cha-kreung, beef salawmachu, and mama wings. Everything was delicious. The chicken cha-kreung is a flavorful ground chicken dish with hints of lemon, and the beef salawmachu is a sour soup that reminds me of Filipino sinigang. This dish was my favorite. I don’t think you can go wrong with the menu. The wings were extra crispy and unique from other fried wings I’ve tried.

I ordered there but in the future I’d order ahead to avoid the waits. But I wanted to ask about the menu and get recommendations. Most people do pickup orders but there are a few seats outside at their outdoor patio.

Been meaning to hit this place up since I got to the Bay Area, finally made it happen. Unpretentious little spot smack in the middle of a working-class Oakland neighborhood. You order through actual burglar bars and pay via Venmo or Cash App, no cash, no problem, very much my vibe as I hate carrying cash.

Food was fresh, home-made, cooked to order, you can taste the authenticity in every bite. We got the Cambodian egg rolls (9/10), the beef sticks (12/10, no notes), and the prahok with steak flank - forgot the exact name but it hit. Slight sourness from the lime, a little salty funk from the fermentation, and somehow not overpowering at all for my first time trying prahok. Steak was tender and juicy, and they're not stingy with the rice and veggies either.

10/10 across the board for its authenticity, flavor, price, and the neighborhood vibe. Honestly kind of absurd how good and how cheap this is for what you're getting, and that it's tucked into this part of Oakland makes it even better.

If you've never had Cambodian food, consider this your gateway drug. Your tastebuds will be begging to come back, guaranteed. And I'm a picky eater, so trust me on this, as I genuinely wish this was my neighborhood spot.

love to see my culture get so much love, and it’s well deserved here. Drove down from OR and knew I had to stop by. Got Steak and Prahok, garlic noodles and pineapple prawns, and 4 beef sticks. Totaled around $58 with card. They said it was gonna be a 30 min wait and they were right. Everyone there was so nice and could tell they really appreciated all their customers coming by. Community felt strong. Food was sooo good and authentic. That steak and prahok sauce was the star.  Workers were also really sweet and gave us a sparkling water just cause! Will definitely come back when I drive back down through the bay. 🙏🏼

I had the breakfast burrito and I thought it was good but it felt more like a regular burrito than a breakfast burrito. It would be nice if they offered bacon / chorizo. It was a little expensive (around $20).

I would come back here.

I popped in here for a quick bite to eat and I was pleasantly surprised! I had a yummy smoked Salmon toast and coffee and it was so good!! I love that I could order from my table.. and they brought it right over! So fast! I will be back when I am in town again!

I frequent many coffee shops, but this is the first time I’ve encountered such a strict and, frankly, unfriendly policy regarding laptop use.
While I understand that businesses want to prevent "camping" and keep seats moving, the enforcement here feels quite harsh. I visited on a Saturday morning when the shop was mostly empty with plenty of open tables. I opened my laptop just to quickly reply to a few emails, yet the owner still made a point to come over and "remind" me of their no-laptop rule for weekends.
It’s disappointing that there’s no room for common sense or basic hospitality. If the shop were packed, I would completely understand, but being policed while sitting in an empty cafe for a five-minute task felt cold and unnecessary. It’s a shame because the space itself is nice, but the vibe is definitely not welcoming to anyone who might need to glance at a screen.
The coffee is excellent, and the food is truly delicious. It's a wonderful spot to enjoy a tasty breakfast and start your morning off right. Highly recommended🤩

Went here twice in two days while staying at the Hyatt Regency. A really cute little place that opens early and closes late. Their specialty drinks are excellent. I didnt stay for a game, but it seems like a great place for a board game night with friends.

I ordered the Express Special and the Vegetarian Special, and both were absolutely delicious! You can tell the ingredients are always fresh, and everything comes out hot and perfectly prepared. The crust is amazing — full of flavor, slightly chewy, and perfectly crisp.
I never leave a bite on my plate and usually go back for another slice — it’s that good. Every time I visit San Francisco, Pizza Express on Cortland is consistent and satisfying. The flavors just work together, and it’s clear they take care with every pizza they make. Definitely a solid neighborhood spot I’d recommend to anyone looking for a reliable, tasty meal.

I have had pizza from just about every pizza place in Northern California and theirs is by far the best! Excellent customer service, great prices and did I mention the best pizza I’ve ever had! Basic cheese and their Cortland’s Special…all the stars!!

It’s great to have a casual dinner spot right in the Castro, perfect for dinner before a night out.

Went with a group of 6 and had no problem grabbing a table on a Saturday night. The service was quick, food was hot and fresh, and vibe was warm. Nothing flashy, but gets the job done.

The chicken marsala was really good, especially with the shaved Brussels sprouts and carrot — unusual, but delicious. The spaghetti con polpette is one of their signature dishes, and the meatballs are massive and filling.

My one recommendation would be to consider sharing the pastas - of the 4 people at our table who ordered pastas, none could finish them. The portions are huge!
The service was amazing, good atmosphere, nice and clean & food was delicious. Jeremias came and greeted us. Want to go back to try each dish. Highly recommended

A hidden gem of a place. The restaurant is unassuming and unfussy. Just sit down, order and enjoy your meal. The key to a good pasta place is that ingredients are fresh and it is served hot at the table.

Pasta Panino nails it. Hot, delicious, fresh. Quantities are very generous for the price you pay. Service was great.

Don’t miss out on the shaved Brussels sprouts.

top_reviews.content: It’s very cozy, clean, and in a prime location in the financial district. The service is fast and unobtrusive. I love Asian soups, but I made a bit of a mistake with my choice this time—I ordered the chicken soup, and the chicken was just like standard American chicken; it wasn't very flavorful compared to Ukrainian or Cypriot chicken. I should have gone for the beef soup. Still, it was pretty good overall. I recommend it.

No one does Northern style pho the way they do. They're back with a vengeance. The ambience is trendy, upscale, comfortable, and welcoming. Service is ALWAYS great. They're so efficient and friendly. Their new menu keeps all of the old classics. I normally order Pho Bo Dac Viet, pandan waffles, pho ga, and imperial rolls. Their bowl sizes are huge, noodles are fresh, broth comforting. Amazing place eat for lunch/dinner. They were open late night, but that moved to the Marina location, which is even better bc all of the bars are in that area 😌🙃. My husband is vegetarian, and he was so happy to see he had options on the new menu (veggie pho)!
They really take care of you here. Welcome back, TT! We missed you!!

On a chilly day off, I knew I had to go back to Turtle Tower to warm my stomach and my heart. This time I got the Beef Pho. SOOO SOO GOOD! I love their signature chicken of course, but I wanted to switch it up this time and of course, it did not disappoint. It had a lovely atmosphere with joyful patrons. The service was quick and pleasant. Everything came out piping hot, just right !

I also had their green waffle 🧇 for dessert and it was yummy! 😋

10/10 recommend! I also got one of these super cute T-shirts :)

top_reviews.content:
I had such a beautiful dinner at Admas Ethiopian in Oakland. The injera was perfectly fermented — soft with that signature tang — and every item on the platter felt thoughtfully prepared. The lentils were rich and comforting, the beets vibrant, the split peas creamy, and the collards seasoned just right.

As someone who really appreciates plant-based cuisine, I could taste the care and tradition in every bite. The space felt warm and welcoming, which made the whole experience even more special.

I’m so grateful for this meal and will absolutely be back.

Authentic East African taste reflective of expert usage of spice and availability of imported injera. High-quality ingredients (down to the use of olive oil and not seed oil) makes for an even better experience.

Quanta Firfir and Veggie Combo are both rock solid. In a city of so many East African options, Admas is a top contender.

Friendly and attentive staff. Contemporary paintings on walls from across sub-Saharan Africa.

Admas is exactly what you want in a neighborhood Ethiopian spot. Unpretentious mom and pop vibes with Ethiopian music videos playing on the big screen behind the register and some nice art on the walls. We rolled 17 deep for a friend’s birthday and the staff handled it like pros.

We went with the combination platters, and these things are massive. Beef, chicken, lamb, kale, salad, beans, lentils, all the classics spread out over a mountain of injera. Everything was well-spiced and balanced, though I wouldn’t have minded a touch more salt here and there. But honestly, that’s me being picky.

The real star here is the injera. Perfectly tart, super spongy, and we kept asking for more because we couldn’t get enough. They were happy to keep it coming, which is exactly how Ethiopian dining should be. Eating with your hands, tearing off pieces of that tangy bread to scoop up the stews and veggies, it’s as authentic as it gets.

Service was on point. They kept our waters filled, checked in regularly, and helped us navigate the menu without being pushy. The pacing was great even with our huge group.

Pro tip: take leftovers. I ate mine the next day for dinner and it was just as delicious, maybe even better after everything had time to marry together overnight.

If you’re craving Ethiopian food in Oakland, Admas delivers. Solid food, great service, and that comfortable neighborhood feel that makes you want to come back.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

My family went for Mothers Day and had a wonderful meal. The wait staff was very kind and the meal was delicious. Exactly what i was craving. The jebena coffee is great too! Its a lot of coffee, so just know that as well. Overall really pleased with our experience. They even have ful which is awesome, as an arab myself. Love seeing more restaurants open that offer non-american food. Good luck to yall!

Amazing food.

The only criticism I have is getting three Injera for the two person combo. We ran out (while also eating the food mat) and it seems like a fourth would be nice so each gets two.

Will be back a lot! 🙏

“No beets?”
Me: Yes, no beets, please.
“No beets?”
Me: Yes, correct, no beets.
Got beets as 1of3 veggies. Hate beets.

Kept it 5 stars because I still got enough food, plenty of injera for me, and I like their food. I will double check my to-go orders…

Admas: please enable comments for online ordering.

If you need a quick meal, you can sit in or take it to go, stop by and check them out. Would be great for a picnic.

The food was absolutely to die for - the salmon was perfectly cooked and the butter elevated the entire dish. We also tried the maple chive biscuits to start - not a pairing I would’ve ever conceived on my own, but quite good. The staff rounded out our meal with a fun sparkler for my birthday dessert, which was also delicious. Will definitely go back!

While documenting restaurants for Alameda Restaurant Week, I spent time at Alley & Vine photographing their standout offerings. I was impressed by their tomahawk steak - probably one of the best steak deals I've seen anywhere. The place is surprisingly family friendly despite its upscale appearance. They maintain a great wine selection that complements their menu perfectly. What's interesting is how it feels like a cross between classic Alameda and going to San Francisco - warm and cozy yet has an artistic elegance to it. The food is underrated for sure, delivering quality and presentation you might not expect.

Tell you what, if you ever decide to grab a good dessert, this might be the place. Along with the good wine selection and excellent cocktail bar displays offers a wide variety of sweet goodies to complete your dinner. I dropped by just to please our sweet tooth, and we were pleasantly surprised with multiple ice cream and cake choices. Along with that we got our favorite drinks and left as pleased as we could be.
I would gladly be back for the complete meal experience.

Update to the review from February 18, 2025

Today this place lands squarely in the middle for me. The biggest miss was the service - there was a noticeable lack of attention to customers and zero willingness to work with simple requests. Being told the espresso machine was broken, without any effort to offer an alternative or show care, set the tone early.

The design hasn’t changed and feels very standard, with nothing that really stands out. That said, the second floor in the back is actually pretty cool and easily the most interesting part of the space. By the way, please work on your Christmas decorations as they are seems like just there to be…

The appetizers were a disappointment. The calamari was over-fried served with the bowl of mayo-style dressing. The fish and chips should honestly be called fish and French fries - overworked presentation, and again, way over-fried. Not impressive.

On the positive side, the main dishes were done and presented well. The lamb chops were cooked properly, though serving them on cheesy potatoes felt unnecessary. The king salmon, however, was the standout - easily the best dish of the night.

Overall, this visit felt like a wrap for me. Decent food in parts, but weak service and forgettable execution make this my last time here.

New Management, New Menu, Not the Same Alley & Vine

My fiancée and I revisited Alley & Vine, curious about its new management and updated menu. We were the only ones there when we arrived at 4:10 PM on a Saturday, so we settled into the patio with our dog.

The service was slow, although we appreciated our server's helpfulness with my fiancée's allergies. The menu seemed basic, with typical dishes like steaks and chicken breast.

I started with three Blue Point oysters at $4 each, which were plump but flavorless. They came with cocktail sauce and lemon, which were necessary to add some taste. My non-alcoholic mockarita was too tart and surprisingly came with a sugar rim instead of salt, which thankfully made it a bit more palatable.

We shared a 16-ounce ribeye steak for $62, which was a letdown. It was overcooked, not the medium-rare we asked for, and lacked the quality one would expect for the price. The broccolini was nicely done, but the chive oil mashed potatoes and pepper jus were too salty. The shoestring fries were crispy yet needed more salt, though the ketchup was good.

Dessert was uninspiring, just like the rest of the meal, and the smaller patio space was a disappointment compared to what it used to be.

Overall, our experience was underwhelming. The previous charm of Alley & Vine seems to have been lost with the new management. We won't be returning, and it's sad to see a former community staple decline.

Recent reviews were mixed, but it was a good experience for us. The location outside below the stairs and next to the parking was actually cosy with the decorations, very atypical at night. Food was good, even if you can expect more at this price. Service was nice.

top_reviews.content: I was walking down Columbus Avenue on my way to the Athletic Club to hook up with an old friend just in from Napoli, and this old Chinese lady hits me with her cane!  Then she starts yelling at me in Chinese ...I don't understand anything she's saying, then a crowd forms, and a young guy tells me she's yelling at you because it took you 8 steps to cross her path, and 8 steps to the stop sign, the 88 steps to the Da Flora Restaurant, and she counted all of them!  Then he says the number 8 is the luckiest number in the universe, and I must go into the Fa Flora Restaurant and order the 8th item on the menu for the two of us, and then go to the Lucky 88 Market and get a lottery ticket..1 for her and 1 for me!  Well...I did just that, and the Lasagna was about the best in the city! 5 ☆☆☆☆☆'s and worth the stop!  The lotto tickets..we'll just have to wait and see.

Finally, an Italian restaurant in North Beach that serves excellent food and is not a tourist trap. We had the seared halibut and the spinach and ricotta gnudi. Both were super tasty. My son and I also ordered a butter leaf salad with strawberries and toasted almonds. The salad was nice as well. We were glad we ordered the Gorgonzola dressing on the side since it was relatively strong. The woman who served us was professional, discreet, and knew how to interact with customers. The other waitstaff were attentive throughout the meal. I really liked the atmosphere of the place, which had an old time parlor feel about it. We got to sit by a large window and watch the people walk up and down Columbus Street.

I was wandering North Beach alone, trying to decide what I was in the mood for, when this little restaurant pulled me in purely on ambience. It had that golden, intimate glow that makes you feel like you’ve stepped into someone’s home instead of a dining room.

The second I walked in, I was greeted with smiles and that rare kind of warmth that feels like an old friend you haven’t seen in years. I just knew the food would be good.

I’ll admit, I’ve been heartbroken by gnocchi before. Once it was so dense it felt like chewing clay and I swore I’d never trust again. But then I saw they’re known for their sweet potato gnocchi. Add sage and bacon? Obviously yes. Focaccia? Yes. Tiramisu? Also yes.

Everything was perfectly portioned, indulgent without being too much. I left full, happy, and oddly emotional in the best way. Dinner alone somehow turned into an evening that felt like family.

If I lived nearby, I’d be a regular. For now, I’ll keep finding my way back whenever I’m in North Beach

We happened upon Da Flora when we were heading to Cobbs Comedy club and looking for a place for a pre-show meal. The service was phenomenal and they very kindly made room for us without a reservation on a Saturday evening. We split the Caesar salad and focaccia bread and ordered the ricotta spinach dumplings in a lamb sugo and the house made sweet potato gnocchi. These entrees were some of the best Italian meals we’ve had in years (and my husband had a Nona  from Italy who cooked!) Food was cooked to perfection and the waitstaff were wonderful. They obviously have long time regulars who they knew by name and order and the atmosphere was cozy and elegant with an SF quirky vibe. Definitely coming back!
Great all around experience. Good overall food including fresh focaccia. Service was very friendly and attentive. Setting was cost and intimate. Very much worth a visit.

Crossing the bridge for food is always worth it when you find a spot like this.
I found this place on Xiaohongshu and decided to give it a try — and it ended up being such a pleasant surprise!

We got there right around opening time, but the restaurant already had quite a few tables occupied, which says a lot. The space felt warm and cozy, with lots of plants inside, and you can even see the mural across the street from your seat. I feel like the atmosphere here would be especially nice at night.

We ordered the red curry, which was pretty good, though I do think it could have come with a bit more ingredients. Also, the curry doesn’t come with rice, so you have to order that separately. The rice that day was a little on the firm side.

The real standout on the savory side was definitely the Pad See Ew — super flavorful with amazing wok hei. Absolutely worth ordering. It also came with a good amount of ingredients, not just noodles, which I appreciated.

But the real star was honestly the dessert. It looked extra and tasted amazing too.
The honey toast was baked perfectly, the ice cream wasn’t too sweet, and the mango was super ripe and sweet. Paired with the sticky rice, it was such a good combo.

If you’re ever passing through Emeryville, this place is definitely worth checking out.

Very authentic Thai food. Ate lunch here on a Monday and place wasnt crowded but restaurant is small. Everything tasted great and food came out at okay pace. Mango Sticky Rice was different than other places, rice was blue/purple and had a toasty flavor.

A feast for the senses. The decor is vibrant and fun, the food is beautiful and delicious. Service was attentive and warm. Great experience, highly recommend.

The restaurant gets really busy during rush meal hours so making reservations is highly recommended. Limited large tables so groups larger than 4 would be difficult to fit unless you make reservation in advance so that tables could be put together.

A nice restaurant with lots of live plants - some are expensive tropical plants if you know them - that means the owner takes pride in the plants and does well to take care of them.

Hat yai fried chicken was ok. Chicken was tender and crispy, going well with the sauce but the sticky rice was too dry and hard that it didn’t add well to the overall entree.

Would definitely return for the roast duck lychee curry and perhaps try their version of khao soi next time

We had an amazing experience at Galinette. We ordered the beef tartare, jambon beurre, frites, and coffee. The tartare was fresh and full of flavor, and the jambon beurre was outstanding with tender, delicious pork. The coffee was different than what my mom was used to with its more floral notes, but the food really stood out and made the meal special.

Our server Carl was warm, attentive, and kind. He explained each dish and made the experience fun and welcoming. I loved that we never felt rushed, which to me is the heart of French dining, taking time to savor each bite.

The space is beautiful with open seating, walls of wine, the French flag outside, and unique mural art throughout. Galinette captures the spirit of French food and culture, and I will definitely be doing what I can to spread the good word. The owners built a gem to the city. Thanks!

Chicken sandwich was delicious! 😋 Very tender, full of flavor! Escargots were yummy and French onion soup was rich and savory. Service was excellent. Very attentive and friendly 😊 Nice atmosphere too. The food took a long time to come out but I guess they need to savor the flavors.

top_reviews.content: Been to Alameda so times I don't know why I haven't been here! However now that I know about this wonderful spot I'll be coming here time and time again. The fish and chips were absolutely delicious, fresh and flaky cod with bay fries were top notch! The bay fries with its garlic oil, parmesan cheese, old bay, parsley were a punch full of flavor and pairee great with the fish. The drinks were great and refreshing, perfect for the weather. We got the "Life is Peachy" and the "Limoncello Spritz," which were both very good, but the favorite was the Limoncello with its fresh, cold and refreshing taste. The venue itself it cute with lots of greenery and even games like corn holes that can be played. I also thought it was very considerate of restaurant to include little green blankets for its customers since the wind can be a bit cold. The staff is super cool and accommodating. You can order food and drinks at the register or at the table by scanning the posted QR code. We had a great time at this place and will definitely be back at Saltbreaker the next time we are in town.

Fantastic restaurant in a very unexpected location.
Extremely courteous and professional staff, attentive to your needs, but not overbearingly present, and very knowledgeable about the menu.

The cast iron chicken had a wonderful seared skin on it that gave just a little bit of crunch to every bite, and the chicken was extremely moist. I might suggest they consider adding a few more accompaniments to the dish's sides. On the whole, The accompanying potatoes, carrots, and whatnot felt a little sparse for the price point.

The steak was perfectly prepared. The french fries could have been a little more crunchy, but that's a personal taste. Again, for the price point, this felt a little sparse.

Had we not had dessert, I would have definitely left feeling a little hungry.

The desserts were spectacular. The Dark Chocolate Marquise Mouse Cake was Rich yet light and sweet but not in a saccharine way.

Overall, our dining experience was superb. The staff was superb. The meal was delicious.

The service was amazing from start to finish, and the food was absolutely delicious. The cocktails were delightfully boozy and well-crafted, making them the perfect complement to the meal. Dessert was especially memorable, with multiple layers and components that came together in a unique and interesting way.

My only regret is not calling ahead for a reservation on a Friday night, as the restaurant was understandably busy. I'll definitely be planning ahead next time because I will absolutely be coming back!

The cold whipping wind threatened to derail our outdoor dining experience, but thankfully, we live in Alameda and we knew to bring jackets.

With that out of the way, we proceeded to enjoy a leisurely 2 hour dinner where every dish was expertly prepared and plated.  The staff were attentive and checked in on us periodically.

We enjoyed the caesar salad with boquerones, the octopus and bay shrimp ceviche with leche de tigre, the duck confit and the the shoestring potatoes.  We finished off the meal with a small citron tarte and some coffee.

Would recommend without reservation, but a reservation might get you seated indoors.  :)

My husband and I truly enjoyed dining at Saltbreaker! Our server, Kevin, was absolutely wonderful—friendly, attentive, and professional. The service was top-notch, and the food was delicious and perfectly prepared. We had a fantastic dining experience. Big thumbs-up and highly recommended!

top_reviews.content:
La Furia Chalaca is a lovely hidden gem on a somewhat run-down block near Jack London Square. The restaurant itself is beautifully decorated and creates a festive atmosphere, with salsa performances playing on the big-screen TV screen adding a real party vibe.

The welcome was warm and friendly, and small details like flavored water and complimentary French bread with butter are a nice touch.

The menu is extensive, though it would be helpful if the staff mentioned when certain dishes were unavailable. I initially ordered the papa relleno but was told afterward that they were out, and the suggested substitution of beef kebabs wasn’t what I had in mind and turned out to be pretty average.

But the ceviche pescado was delicious: fresh fish marinated in bright lime, served with yuca, sweet potato, and a spicy dipping sauce on the side. A great example of how refreshing and flavorful Peruvian ceviche can be.

Service timing was slightly unusual, though, as my main course arrived before the appetizer, but overall the experience was enjoyable.

This feels like a great spot for a festive meal, and I would definitely return.

The service was top notch. We told our waiter this one was our first time and he explained the menu for both food and drinks. He also opened the door for us when we exited. Service definitely gets 5 stars.

However, there’s something wrong with the price on the menu vs what you will be charged. We ordered from the lunch especial menu which says items were $ 17.99 but we were charged 20 for one item and 18 for other two dishes. And the beverages were supposed be $4 based on the menu but were charged $6. May be they updated the price and forgot to update the menu?

Anyways two of the dishes fried rice and Marinated pork dishes were very salty. The bed of pasta with fish was very good but I wished the fish was basked instead deep fried. Purple corn drink was pretty good the waiter said it will be sweet and it was. If you don’t have a sweet tooth, you don’t probably want it.

Will try again sometime in the future.

La comida authentica. The food is delicious, authentic, and the people working there put a lot of care into their drinks and dishes. For sure try the Anticuchos (beef), and the fried fish in the Jalea Bites was amazing too. It was all great. Have to check it out and will def go back.

We ordered the shrimp fritos good flavor but the shrimp was too salty and the salad that came with it was sour(too much lemon), the chicken kabob was also watoo salty it was like eating salt and tasted funny ( the chicken tasted old. Our waiter waved about their lomo saltado, it was the worst we ever had. The beef was dry and not tender.
Our cocktails were the only highlight of the meal. I love supporting local businesses but fir sure we're not coming back.
The ceviche was incredible and the chicken skewer was perfectly cooked. Exceeded our expectations!!

reviews_snippets.content: "We ordered sea food stew and fried fish with rice."
"Yummy food and drinks, awesome service!"
"The rice pudding tasted burned, and the purple corn pudding was tasteless."

name: Crazy Block Cheesecakes
address: 3355 Lakeshore Ave, Oakland, CA 94610, United States

google.name: Crazy Block Cheesecakes
google.address: 3355 Lakeshore Ave, Oakland, CA 94610, United States

top_reviews.content:
This place is like a 3-in-1. There is a cheesecake display and a section for BBQ and latkes.

To be honest,  I was a little disappointed by the food. What is pictured is what I got. The beef ribs had a tremendous amount of fat and I got a slice and a sixth of brisket. The yams felt pre-cooked and too sweet. Similarly, the meat in the beans and greens felt a little fatty so the texture was off putting. I think I would have preferred a meat free option.

The restaurant decor is hella cute and parking is towards the end of Lakeshore is not as difficult. If I were to visit again, I would consider the chicken and ask for meat-free greens.

Ordered take out last night for dinner and had the plate combo and it was fantastic! The brisket was absolutely amazing, melt in your mouth good and bursting with flavor. The side of mac and cheese with coslaw very much complemented everything. To top it all off, the mini Samoa cheesecake was a delightful finish. 10/10 would highly recommend and I will for sure be back again.

Absolutely the best brisket this side of the Pacific!  I was blown away! The bbq sauce and cheesecake was also phenomenal! I hope they rename their restaurant so more people will find out about their fantastic bbq and service!

5 STARS. FIVE. I would give it six but my phone only goes to five.
Listen. LISTEN. I have been driving up and down the state of California for YEARS — years, people — on a holy quest for brisket that didn't taste like it got smoked by a guy who learned BBQ from a YouTube video titled "BBQ for Beginners (EASY)." I had given up hope. I had made peace with my sad California brisket reality. And then I rolled into Crazy Block Cheesecakes on Lakeshore Ave and my whole understanding of the West Coast meat landscape got turned upside down and shaken out like a pinata full of bark.
This is the best brisket west of the Mojave. I am not exaggerating for effect. I am stating this as a geographic fact that should probably be on a historical plaque.
The brisket itself shows up smoky like it just walked off a campfire, bark for days, and you get to choose lean or juicy which is basically the BBQ version of choosing your own adventure novel except every ending is delicious. Pull up with the chiblam combo, throw some collard greens and that vinegar slaw on the tray, and just sit there in silence for a minute appreciating what is happening on your tongue.
AND THEN. AND THEN THERE'S THE CHEESECAKE. A BBQ joint that also makes a genuinely elite New York style cheesecake from Grandma Block's actual recipe should not exist. It is not a fair matchup for the rest of the cheesecake industry. Dense, rich, made with real local dairy, and somehow this man has 160 flavors going at once like he's running a cheesecake casino.
Owner Ben Block himself was working the line, slinging plates, vibing with customers under a wall mural of Goku powering up a slice of cheesecake, which is either the most unhinged or the most correct decor choice I have ever witnessed in a restaurant. And when I told him I'd been searching forever for real BBQ out here, he just shrugged and said better late than never.
Aye men, Ben. Aye men.
Brisket: immaculate. Cheesecake: a separate, equally immaculate occasion. Vibe: dinosaurs and Pokemon and pure unfiltered joy. Will be back. Will probably be buried here.

Crazy Block Cheese is my new favorite BBQ spot in Oakland! I love everything about this place the anime artwork is dope, and the atmosphere has great energy. The owner, Ben, was really friendly and enthusiastic. He takes time to engage with all his customers and takes pride in the fresh-made food and sauces.

My wife and I ordered the three-protein combo meal, and it was more than enough for both of us. We had the beef rib, brisket, and pulled chicken, all were juicy, flavorful, and perfectly cooked. The sauces were hella good too. For sides, we got the mac and cheese and cornbread. They accidentally gave us collard greens at first but Ben fixed it right away, no problem. The cornbread was also really good! The beef ribs and brisket is my favorite.

This is hands down the best value meal you can get. Most BBQ spots overcharge and leave you disappointed, but here you get high-quality food at a fair price. I also love that they use local ingredients. Great food, great vibe, good music, great people  perfect spot to bring friends or family.

reviews_snippets.content: "The food was phenominal- juicy brisket, crispy latkas... great menu."
"The decor is such a vibe and I also enjoyed the art on the wall."
"Love the owner who brought ENERGY and stories about his family’s recipes."

top_reviews.content: Amazing food with generous portion sizes, and amazing quality of fish. Rolls were some of the best we’ve had. Looking forward to returning!

Ariake is one of those rare neighborhood spots that gets everything right. Fresh, generous cuts of fish, rolls that are creative, fantastic udon noodles, and warm family-run service that makes you feel like a regular instantly. No frills, no pretense, just consistently delicious sushi at a reasonable price for SF. A true neighborhood gem and an easy five stars.

Best sushi in SF. Period. The quality is top notch and the amount of fish per nigiri is unmatched. Selection is amazing as well. The chef has been in business for 26 years. He knows what’s up. I’ve been a patron for over 10 years and it’s still as good as ever. If you love sushi – especially raw sushi – you gotta try this place!

We visited this place on a whim and without a doubt, the sushi from Ariake is the best sushi you can treat yourself to in the Bay Area. We try Ikura at every japanese restaurant we go to and theirs is the best I've ever had amongst all of them.

We are BIG sushi people, and have traveled the world to enjoy good sushi. We flew into SF tonight for a wedding weekend in Tomales. Originally we weren’t planning on stopping in the city but decided too on a whim and randomly chose this spot due to reviews and pics. It’s was an incredible experience and reminded me of our times in cute little Tokyo spots. We will 100% be back, but until this - I hope anyone reading this review and deciding to come here, goes. You will not regret it.

We loved the miso soup and cherry blossom roll but the absolute highlight was the Omakase so the chefs could do their thing with high quality fish!

And lastly, the staff was awesome and so kind/cute with us. And the spot was just adorbs. We will be back!

top_reviews.content: Ordered a steak burrito, and while I admit the steak was actually decent, there was no balance in the burrito. 75% of the burrito was refried beans. There was barely any steak in it, and the cheese wasn't even melted. The burrito was also not wrapped very good. I only ate about half the burrito until I realized all I was eating was beans. I opened the rest up and saw there was barely any steak anyway. If you are looking for a good burrito, this place is NOT it!

The burritos are small and was skimp on the proteins.  I didn’t like the Al pastor and carnitas tacos.  Pastor was soaked in grease that soaked the paper bag and everything else.  Also found a big piece of fat blubber with my carnitas that was not very edible.  The best was the queso chicken taco.  That would probably be the only thing I would get if I ever go back to this spot.  The salsa was not very good and bland as well.  They need a lot of improvements to hang with the upscale taquerias in and around the City.

The best Mexican food I've got in the city. We got the quesabirria and I absolutely loved it. I'm a sucker for anything Birria. I saw they have the Pizza Birria too. Once got that in Miami and that was to die for. I'm definitely coming back here, would love to try the Pizza Birria here. The service was nice and friendly. And prices are OK. I personally think it is worth the hype.

This is the closest thing to actual TJ tacos I’ve found in the area. Ordered the keto and regular asada tacos, the meat was perfectly seasoned and wasn’t burnt to a crisp like other spots. The agua fresca de piña was the star of the show, absolutely amazing and fresh, not too sweet. The price is steep, I payed a total of $20 for three tacos and an agua (not including tip), but that’s totally reasonable for the area. I can’t imagine how bad rent must be right on Market St, and honestly $20 for a whole meal including drink is not high comparatively. And they do stuff the tacos with meat, so you’re getting your money’s worth! Their outdoor seating area is clean and inviting, and great to bring a pup and enjoy the sunshine!

I recently visited El Tucan: Tijuana Street Tacos in San Francisco, and it was an outstanding experience from start to finish. As a fan of authentic Mexican cuisine, I was thrilled to find this gem in the city. The tacos were absolutely delicious, bursting with flavor and made with fresh ingredients. I tried the carne asada and al pastor tacos, and both were exceptional. The meat was perfectly seasoned and cooked to perfection. The tortillas were warm and fresh, adding to the authenticity of the meal. The atmosphere was vibrant and welcoming, capturing the essence of Tijuana street food culture. The staff were friendly and attentive, ensuring that my dining experience was enjoyable. The service was quick, and despite being busy, the staff maintained a cheerful and accommodating demeanor. One of the highlights was the variety of toppings and salsas available, allowing for a personalized and flavorful taco experience. The prices were reasonable, offering great value for such high-quality food. Overall, El Tucan: Tijuana Street Tacos exceeded my expectations. I highly recommend this spot to anyone craving authentic, mouth-watering tacos in San Francisco. I will definitely be returning for more!

top_reviews.content:
I had dinner at Le Solei tonight, and I’m still thinking about every single bite. From start to finish, the meal was absolutely outstanding.

We kicked things off with two incredible appetizers. The beef tartare was superb, but the real showstopper was the premium wagyu beef that came with it — it literally melts in your mouth. Paired with a light, airy, and intensely savory shrimp cracker, it was pure perfection. The chicken lollipops (boneless chicken wings) were just as impressive: super crunchy on the outside, juicy and flavorful on the inside.

For mains, every dish delivered a knockout punch. The miso butter mushroom was a total flavor bomb — it took simple mushrooms and turned them into something rich, decadent, and unforgettable. Then came the pho risotto with braised rib bone — the meat was slow-cooked until it fell off the bone, and the creamy risotto soaked up all that savory goodness beautifully. We also had the roasted Dungeness crab with garlic noodles — the crab was cooked just right, and the noodles were perfectly al dente. Honestly, everything was so delicious.

We somehow found room for two desserts: mango sticky rice and a scoop of ice cream. Both were the perfect sweet ending to an incredible meal. My tummy was so happy by the end.

I also have to mention the excellent service — attentive, warm, and seamless throughout the night.

I will absolutely be back to try more of the menu. If you haven’t been to Le Solei yet, go now. You won’t regret it.

Came here for a little dinner date and we split the quail, chicken lollipops, lotus root salad, and shaking beef. Every single dish was an absolute hit: meats were tender and well seasoned with, as others have reported, the chicken lollipops simply sliding off the bone. There was a lot of brightness and acidity in our dishes as well, whether that was the pickled lotus root in the salad or the lemon sauce that came with the quail. These are the types of dishes where all the ingredients feel celebrated as they combine into some very thoughtful dishes. It all went down very nicely with a cold beer. We came early for dinner so the place was relatively empty and we were able to have a nice relaxed dinner. All of the staff we interacted with were so sweet, accommodating, and outgoing, and it made the space feel very welcoming. I absolutely look forward to coming back here!

La Soleil is a great place to eat crab at a modest price point. We got the garlic dungeness crab which is $89 for 2.5lbs. it also comes with garlic noodles which are tasty but a little oily. They gave us one crab cracker per person.

The shrimp and chicken crepe was salty and crunchy with great freshness from the mint, lettuce and bean sprouts. However, it was light on the meat.

The chicken lollipop was nothing spectacular but crispy and not overly oily.

The service was very good. Our server stopped us from over ordering and was very helpful when we asked for some chilli sauce even though it's not a condiment that they usually provide.

I will be back.

Had dinner there for restaurant week.

The chicken lollipop was impressive with most of the meat pulled off the bone and fried to a light crisp and it came with a creamy savory sauce.
Papaya salad w shrimp was flavorful from pops of fresh herbs.
The fish cake was good.

I was disappointed when I saw that the sea bass arrived as battered fried chunks of fish - this wasn't mentioned in the description. Besides that, the dish was overall just ok. The sauce was 2 dimensional - tasted like a sweetened light soy sauce. I wouldn't get it again, especially not with that price tag.

I tried the matcha tiramisu for dessert. Obviously not your traditional tiramisu because of the matcha, but it also seemed like they used a light sponge cake instead of lady fingers? I would've called it a matcha cake instead of tiramisu. It was good.

My group ordered several dishes to share among ourselves. The crispy noodle and chicken lollipops were the dishes my group liked best.
We ate around 6pm and reserved our table on a Saturday. If we ate any later, we would have to wait since the restaurant filled up quite quickly.

reviews_snippets.content: "The price was decent for a lunch combo which included a small bowl of soup."

Came here by accident. There was a parking spot out front. I was hungry, so I thought I would give this place a try.
The menu has many choices but a little confusing, and enchiladas  were not shown. However, there was a small sign on the counter about enchiladas.
I got the roasted chicken plate. It came with rice and the most delicious pureed black bean which were over salted, but oh my, they were the best ever. The chicken enchilada was excellent.
I will definitely go back for more. Cute, casual, spacious Taqueria, nicely decorated and clean.
Lady waitress was very pleasant and helpful.
I recommend this restaurant!

Yummy Mexican spot in the heart of Polk street! We came here later on a Sunday when places were filled up. The veggie quesadillas were a solid portion size and had corn, which I don’t usually see!

In addition, the salsa bar in the back was great and had yummy salsas! Finally, I had cantaloupe juice for the first time which was delicious.

The Carne Asada Super Burrito for $18.74, before they asked for a to go tip, was very mid. Lacked aby kind of wow factor and the burrito itself wasn't too large portion wise. The salsas were quality, and the chip portion was too big almost. All In All, a nice. modern, clean place, that's overpriced when it comes to burritos

After visiting Greens Sports Bar on Polk St, we stumbled across this understated and down to earth Mexican Eatery, and we were so pleased we did!

The food was fresh, authentic, and delicious.

We enjoyed;
Mexican Street TACOS with Pork, Beef and Chicken
Classic Cheese Quesadila
Complimentary Chips and Dips

A very comforting, late night meal. Highly recommended if you're in the North area of San Francisco 👌

La Buena Vibra, Mal Sabor

If you’re looking for a fun atmosphere and friendly service, this spot delivers — but don’t come hungry expecting much else. The energy is lively and the staff is welcoming, which makes it all the more disappointing when the food hits the table.

My vegetarian burrito bowl was a study in minimalism gone wrong: a couple of tablespoons of rice, a scoop of beans, and what can only be described as an entire head of plain lettuce — no dressing, no seasoning, no soul. My dining companion fared no better with the carne asada quesadilla, which arrived bland and stuffed with what tasted like canned vegetables, all wrapped in an oversized flour tortilla that couldn’t hide the lack of care in the kitchen.

Mexican cuisine is built on bold spices, fresh ingredients, and layers of flavor. This kitchen seems to have missed that memo entirely. At these prices, you deserve more than cafeteria-style portions dressed up in a trendy space.

Great vibe, poor execution. Come for drinks, eat somewhere else.

top_reviews.content:
Extremely disappointing. I ordered the regular beef curry and it was basically a container of salty curry sauce and rice with three small pieces of beef.

I genuinely thought there had been a mistake, so I asked the owner about it. Apparently, three pieces of beef is the normal portion for a regular size. That’s honestly ridiculous for something being sold as “beef curry.”

The curry itself was also overly salty, so there wasn’t much redeeming the meal. If I’m paying for beef curry, I expect an actual reasonable serving of beef—not mostly rice and sauce with three token pieces of meat.

Terrible value and an incredibly stingy portion. I would not come back.

Tried their Bento-box with a pork katsu and a salmon onigiri on the side. It wasn't bad, food is decent, but nothing super special. It's a bit pricy for the amount of food. But if you don't eat much, may be a good deal.

Very yummy food at this Japanese delicatessen! The 9-piece bento box was a lovely sampler, but I do wish it had more fish. The poke was also yummy. The salmon and avocado rolls were generous portions and lovely bites, the perfect lunch! Don’t forget to grab a rice ball, they’re easy to miss but really lovely eats. Service was kind and quick.

To be exact this place is located inside the Ferry Building in San Francisco. Three stars for now. We came in to this Japanese Deli at the latter part of the afternoon so the food maybe not be as fresh as if you were to come earlier in the day. We came for dinner. They serve bento box like meals, small plates and some sushi, other stuff, and drinks.

We got some sushi, a small plate of curry beef with rice, and a potato/vegetable fry thing. The food was okay. The staff weren’t really that friendly and they seemed to not hear us well because we kept repeating our order. The potato/vegetable fry thing would have been really good if it was served hot. They didn’t offer to heat it up. There are plenty of community tables but you have to be aware of your surroundings!!!

Highly recommend stopping here if you're in the ferry building! The quality of food is incredible, service is extremely quick as you would expect from a deli, and outdoor seating is easy to come by. The Bay breeze and mountain landscape created a picturesque environment for eating. The Hijiki and Soybean Salad and Beef Ginger Onigiri were by far the best of the items I tried.

top_reviews.content:
Bua Luang is hands down the BEST Thai restaurant in the entire Bay Area, not just in Albany! I have been enjoying Thai cuisine all around the Bay for over 25 years. My family and I have Thai food at least 2-3 times a week, so we have tried many (and I mean MANY) Thai restaurants over the decades, and without a doubt we all agree that Bua Luang offers the freshest, tastiest, and most delicately prepared Thai cuisine of all. Every dish is packed with the freshest ingredients. The flavors and textures are amazing. Restaurants in Thailand don’t make a Pad Thai as delicious as the Pad Thai at Bua Luang—believe us, we have tried Pad Thai all over Thailand and we still longed for the Pad Thai at Bua Luang. The chef at this restaurant is a culinary master!

Not only are the dishes at this restaurant superb, the atmosphere is serene and delightful. The indoor space is clean, cozy, and modern with soft old-world touches and whimsical lighting. The ambiance music is very pleasant. It’s not too loud, and it’s easy to talk with and hear others in your party. If you choose to dine outside, you are greeted by the most beautiful outdoor seating area on all of Solano Avenue. The space is gorgeous and inviting. And then there is the staff: always friendly and attentive. They provide a truly exceptional dining experience all around.

This restaurant is an absolute gem. If I could give it more stars I would. Don’t walk, run to this spot!

If you look at that picture, do you see a bed of spinach? Me neither.  I bought the Cashew nut chicken because it supposedly comes on a bed of spinach.
I called them and they said all the orders that went out for Cashew nut chicken were on a bed of spinach. When I returned it, they took it back in the kitchen, brought it back out to me where they had pulled most of the food away, and there were a few small pieces of wilted spinach. Not at all what I expected. Bummer, I had high hopes.

Definitely the place to visit when you are very hungry because their portion sizes are big.

Really love the decor at the restaurant because it makes one want to dine-in peacefully.

Their teas are amazing and I was blown away by the blends they offered. It was definitely my first time, having tea that’s blue in color.

The food was well-made, with good seasoning. I had ordered the sautéed mix vegetables with fried tofu and I loved how well-prepared the vegetables were.

Definitely a place that I will visit next time I’m in Berkeley

Our favorite Thai restaurant ever. 💕 They now served Kao Mun Gai (chicken and rice) Thai style. Tasty and good price. We also had Tamarind Prawn. It’s crispy jumbo prawns topped with tamarind sauce and grilled asparagus. Yummm. Best food, service and vibes. Love this place!!! Recommended!!! ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

We've ordered from Bua Luang several times before but they seem to have gone down hill. Tonight, we paid $94 for a meal and received tiny portions that weren't enough for 2 adults and 2 kids who don't eat much. The portions were about 25-40% what you would expect to get and what we'd gotten in the past. There were a few pieces of beef and chicken in small, half-filled containers. We thought maybe there was a packing error and called them to show them how the food had arrived. They weren't open to rectifying the situation and said this is how their portions are. The food also tasted greasy and not as good as it used to.
