⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | A Local Treasure for Authentic Indian Cuisine!
If you are looking for the best Indian food in the East Bay, look no further than Phulkari. From the moment you walk in, the atmosphere is warm and inviting, but it’s the food and the service that truly set this place apart.
The Food
The flavors here are incredibly authentic and layered. We tried the Butter Chicken and the Lamb Rogan Josh, and both were cooked to perfection—tender meat and rich, vibrant sauces. The garlic naan was fresh out of the oven, and you can tell they use high-quality ingredients in every dish.
The Service
What made our night extra special was the service. Our server, Aniket, was absolutely wonderful. He was attentive, knowledgeable about the menu, and made sure we had everything we needed without being intrusive. His recommendations were spot on!
The Hospitality
It was also a pleasure to meet the owner, Aman. You can really tell he cares about his customers and takes immense pride in the restaurant. He goes out of his way to make everyone feel like a guest in his own home, which creates such a welcoming community vibe.
Phulkari is a must-visit in Castro Valley! Great food, beautiful presentation, and a team that genuinely cares. We will definitely be back soon.

One of the best dining experiences I’ve had in a long time. The food was fresh, flavorful, and served perfectly. The staff was extremely welcoming and provided outstanding service from start to finish. The restaurant has a great atmosphere and is a wonderful place to sit back, relax, and enjoy a meal with family and friends. Every detail reflects quality and care. Highly recommended, and I’ll definitely be coming back

Outstanding food, excellent service, and a wonderful atmosphere! Every dish was packed with authentic flavor and prepared with great care. The staff was friendly, professional, and made us feel truly welcome. The restaurant is clean, comfortable, and a perfect place to enjoy a great meal. A Gem in Castro Valley!

After coming so many times to eat this I felt After Hours family deserved my 5 stars. This place makes me feel at home and I can always count on leaving full and happy. Great food and atmosphere! Try the Ramen and the Tonkatsu Bowl!! 👍

top_reviews.content: Great place for Mexican food in irving! Me and my girlfriend ordered nachos to share and it filled us both up for lunch. It was 18 dollars with carne asada, but without meat, it is 10.50. it was LOADED with toppings, unlike other places which usually are more stingy with nacho toppings. Ours had sour cream, guacamole, pico de gallo, refried beans, cheese and the meat (extra cost). It was delicious and satisfied our cravings. There is a little place to grab utensils, water and napkins. The service was super quick and friendly, our nachos were done in less than 5 minutes. The seating options are also quite nice, there is a big 6 person table, and also there are single tall-seats by the window, and upstairs seating. The only difference I see is this restaurant compared to others is that this doesn't have a sauce / condiment bar. However, I personally don't think that is a necessity because the food already contained a lot of toppings and sauces, and tasted amazing. I would totally reccomed this place for an authentic Mexican - American food experience  in the Irving!

I ordered the taco plate with nopales and al pastor.

🌵 🐷 🌮 Nopales and Al Pastor Taco: The nopales was pretty yummy and had a nice roasted flavor to it. Similar with the al pastor, it was quite juicy but did not have as much of a grilled char flavor. The flavor was pretty delicious for both tacos and I appreciate the singular tortilla and already dressed tacos.

🥛Horchata: I ordered a horchata as well and was pleasantly surprised they did not default to adding ice which was quite nice.

🥔 Chips and Salsa: We also ordered the chips and salsa which was nicely larger than expected. The tomatoes were chopped quite well and tasted very fresh.

🧀 Quesadilla: We ordered a quesadilla al pastor as well which was quite a generous portion and yummy but they forgot to hold the sour cream when we requested it.

Overall, the food here was delicious but on the pricier side for tacos and quesadillas. I would come back once in a while to try their other flavors!

Ordered the taco perron and the super burrito with carne asada. Both were very delicious.
Staff is friendly and swift. Sat inside by the window with our kids and watched the street. Had fun. Will do again.

I’ve finally found a burrito that reminds of the delicious, salty, so juicy you have to eat it over a kitchen sink, super burritos you get everywhere in San Jose, but not in SF. I have been searching for that type of burrito here for years, and they’re all too dry and bland. Street Taco is the closest I’ve ever gotten. I got the carne asada super burrito with black beans and no rice. It was juicy and messy, as a burrito should be. Best burrito in SF.
Carne asada tacos were solid, as was the horchata. Fun to sit at the storefront counter and walk the people go by.

We eventually ate at the outside patio since we didn't want to disturb other customers. Got to try this spot for brunch, and we only had to wait about 5–10 minutes before being seated. Since it was our first time, the staff was super helpful and informative about the menu. I ordered the Sai Oua lava egg plate, pork jowl on the side, and khanom krok.

The sausage was good, but the pork jowl was where the meal really shined. Next time, I’d definitely get the grilled pork jowl lava egg plate instead. I can be pretty picky with pork, but this one melted in my mouth and had so much flavor.

The khanom krok was beautiful and a great dish to order if you have friends to share it with. For me, one bite was more than enough as a sweet little dessert at the end of the meal. Their jasmine Thai tea was also really tasty. :)

I’m so glad I finally got to try this spot and would definitely say it deserves all the hype!

​This was my second time dining here, and it completely solidified this restaurant as one of my absolute favorites. I would easily eat here every single week if I lived closer!
​During this visit, I had the wonderful opportunity to speak with the owner. She is incredibly smart, passionate, and empathetic, and it truly shows in every aspect of the restaurant. I love the way she pours her love for her hometown into the menu and remains unapologetically authentic to her roots.
​That dedication translates perfectly into the food—every dish feels personal, deeply flavorful, and genuinely authentic. It is rare to find a place that hits the perfect balance of amazing hospitality and outstanding, uncompromising regional flavors.
​If you haven't been yet, do yourself a favor and check it out. It is a true gem!

While the inside area was a little loud at times, it was a warm familiar feeling. Being surrounded by the plants and cool air felt amazing and refreshing. The staff were so kind and welcoming, and we could not have asked for a better server.

The food was delicious and felt so worth the price. All of the ingredients were tasted in every dish, and just overall well thought out and balanced. The Lava eggs with the tender wagyu reset my tastebuds - nothing is going to taste as good for weeks. Definitely recommend sharing the Thai Beignets and the Coconut Cakes, as well as the main dishes.

we made a reservation ahead of time and ordered the prix fixe brunch, and they customized the menu to accommodate our dietary restrictions (pescatarian). the food was delicious, the atmosphere was so sweet, and the staff was incredibly thoughtful. 100% would go back! I vomited 2 times and diarrhea 7-8 times in the last 12 hours. I have to cancel my flight for Christmas because I cannot hold myself together for a flight. This is utter ignorance of public health. I’ll report to public health authority and the food delivery platform. It pains me that my favorite place did this to me.

I have been here since it first opened it’s doors, I usually make a visit when I am craving for a different style of Chinese food or when I am in the area. The restaurant is pretty compact where lines can build up. It is a two sided interior, where you can walk through the middle of the restaurant to either side of the dining area. Their menu consists of appetizers, dumplings, entrees, noodles, noodle soups, fried rice and much more. Everything is authentic, worth trying and made to order which is always a plus for me and I do not mind the wait since I am a very patient person. Their portion size is what I call more than enough, because most of the times I have food to take home. The service here is great thanks to their very welcoming, well trained and understanding staffs where I had never encountered an issue during any of my visits. You can either dine in, order for take out, phone in an order or order through a delivery app to have it delivered to you. I highly recommend this place to all Chinese food lovers, to anyone looking to try something new or if you just so happen to be in the area. I definitely will be back to tryout the other delicious options they have to offer.

My favorite hole in the wall Chinese food I crave for when it comes to dumplings.  They do fried or boiled.

It’s about the wrapper… fresh made and ingredients inside that counts.

They do good Americanized Chinese food too… best tender kung pao chicken and Mongolian beef.

I’ve dined in a couple of time and recently did take-out a lot. My friends and I are big fans of this place!

We’ve tried their sweet and sour chicken, the black bean chicken, sesame chicken, shanghai style pork strips rice cake, honey walnut shrimp, string beans, Beijing style pork strips, pan-fried chive and pork dumplings and more. I love their sesame chicken - crispy, savory and sweet umami goodness!

Never had a problem with getting seats or parking.

They have a take-out special of 3 items for about $50, soup and white rice included! Super worth it. Check it out!!

Delicious dishes served over rice 🍚 , generous portions and prices as well (especially if you go before 5p on weekdays!) they give yummy free appetizers (salt roasted peanuts 🥜 and fermented chili cabbage 🌶️ 🥬 ) while you wait for your food to come! I could only eat half and had leftovers so I had a meal ready for home later on 😊 we came on a Tuesday afternoon and were served promptly. It was not busy at all.

Stopped by B&B and had an amazing bánh mì. The owner was super friendly and welcoming, and you can tell he really cares about both the food and his customers.

The menu not only bahn mi’s for meat and non-meat eaters as well as rice bowls too. And if you need something to wash it all down with, get yourself a boba and/or fruit tea.
Since this was my first visit, I ordered the 5-spiced chicken and the bulgogi beef. Generous portions of meat served in a fresh roll. Overall delicious sandwiches and I have return a couple of time.

It is a small store front, so standing room inside is limited and there are a couple of stools for inside seating, while waiting for your sandwich. The owner/staff is very friendly.
Support your local business and check it out!

Sandwiches are a happy place. B&B popped up on my IG feed a few months back and I saved the post but lost it. Fast fwd to a coworker bringing a bulgogi Bahn mi to work.
I could have tried it then but I wanted my own full experience and to show support for this creation.
You ever had a Bahn Mi as big as a deli sandwich? You ever wanted bulgogi on your Bahn Mi?
When you first enter you’re welcomed with smiles and a good vibe. I would suggest pre ordering as there has to be a line at times. You’re hit with a menu board and tons of options both sandwiches and drinks.
I chose the Bulgogi Bahn Mi, sandwhich was huge! The beef was so tender and hefty. Guaranteed to fill you up . The pickled veggies were fresh and well flavored. The bread! Soft but has a light crunch.

top_reviews.content: Don Blanc was absolutely amazing! The meat was incredibly tender, juicy, and full of flavor, and every dish we ordered was delicious. The quality of the food was outstanding, and the service was friendly and attentive. This is easily one of the best Korean BBQ restaurants I’ve been to. I’ll definitely be coming back—highly recommended!

Don Blanc is a place where you can enjoy top-notch service, fresh meat, and side dishes. The authentic, un-Americanized Korean food is truly delicious, and the servers are incredibly friendly. In particular, the two managers, John and Chris, never forget to provide what customers need, even though they're busy, and they always have a smile on their face, making for a comfortable and enjoyable dining experience. Their delightful sense of humor always makes me happy. If I could, I'd love to visit this place often. If you're craving authentic Korean barbecue, Korean beer, and delicious Korean side dishes, this is a restaurant I highly recommend.

The quality of the meat was outstanding. We ordered Beef Set B, and every cut was incredibly fresh, tender, and flavorful. The jumulleok was especially good, with just the right amount of seasoning and a great savory, umami flavor. We also ordered samgyeopsal (pork belly), which had the perfect meat-to-fat ratio and was delicious. As a Korean I’ve been to many Korean BBQ restaurants, including Michelin-rated K-BBQ spots, and this place is honestly right up there with them.

The owner and staff were also incredibly friendly and welcoming. The doenjang jjigae (soybean paste stew) tasted very authentic, the pork jowl‘s texture was perfect, and the naengmyeon (cold noodles) had such a great depth of flavor and umami.

Overall, it was an extremely satisfying meal, and I’ll definitely be coming back often.

GOPCHANG LOVER’S PARADISE
If you’ve been missing your Korean Gopchang/intestines you had in SoCal, this is the spot to try! The portion is decent and flavor is there! Also love that there’s potato slices in there!

Other dishes-
Cold buckwheat noodles are 9/10
Soy sauce garlic chicken 7/10 (wish they weren’t full of fried batter clumps and wanted just wings)
Pork belly single serving 9/10
Spicy tofu soup 8.5/10 (love the tofu in there!)
Side dishes 8/10

Atmosphere-
Very loud and the music just adds to the noise, have to yell across the table for my friends to hear me, vise versa…. During busy hours that is.

Ate here and ordered the beef set, a plate of beef intestine, and corn cheese. The beef quality was good, but most of the meats ended up tasting pretty similar. The side dishes were also below average compared to other Korean BBQ restaurants I’ve been to.

We had three people, but they only provided two dipping sauces, which was a bit odd. The beef intestine was especially disappointing in terms of value, $35 for a very small plate.

Overall, the restaurant felt overpriced, averaging about $83 per person, and I don’t think the quality justified the cost.

One thing to note: parking on the nearby streets can be risky. Our car was broken into while we were eating (there was nothing at all inside the car), so I’d recommend being extra cautious or choosing a more secure parking option.

That said, I’ve heard their pork is the better choice, so it might be worth trying that instead if you decide to visit.

top_reviews.content:
Excellent tacos, fresh ceviche and great margaritas near Telegraph Ave in Berkeley

We arrived in Berkeley on a Sunday and after hearing many great recommendations from local students, we decided to visit 5 Tacos & Beers. Even though the restaurant was quite busy when we arrived, the place is spacious and there were still several tables available. The hosts welcomed us with a smile and allowed us to choose our own table, which immediately created a relaxed and friendly atmosphere.

Once seated, we started with the Mix Ceviche, which was very fresh, bright, and full of flavor. The citrus marinade was perfectly balanced and paired nicely with the crisp tortilla chips served on the side.

For the main dishes we ordered Quesabirrias (one pollo and one carne) with a cup of consommé, plus an order of fish tacos, and a skinny margarita. Everything was excellent. The quesabirrias were crispy on the outside, filled with tender meat and melted cheese, and dipping them into the consommé added a deep, rich flavor. The fish tacos were light and well seasoned, with fresh toppings that complemented the fish perfectly.

Service throughout the meal was friendly and attentive. The staff checked in regularly and everything was served quickly. One thing we really enjoyed was being able to see the open kitchen and the chefs preparing dishes nonstop as orders came in.

The restaurant itself is clean, colorful, and nicely designed, with a full bar and a relaxed Berkeley vibe. Parking can be found on nearby streets, but the easiest option is using a paid garage nearby so you don’t have to worry about time limits.

After eating, it’s also great to walk around the neighborhood and explore Telegraph Avenue, which is full of interesting shops, street art, and student energy.

Overall, a great spot for tacos, ceviche, and margaritas in Berkeley. Highly recommended. 🌮🍹

There is good and there is not so good to be said about this cozy little restaurant: The French onion soup is a definite no. It is a tomato marinara sauce with a piece of toast and cheese on top. Should be called Italian Soupa..
The big dinner salad is as ok. Not super great,  neither super big,  but decent. The steak with fries is very reasonable at $39 dollars, but the seasoned butter on top of my steak tasted weird and ruined it for me. So please ask them not to put their “special butter” on top. Our bill was $150 for two, including 2 drinks, 2 soups and 2 entrees.

It's a chill place. There's two outdoor tables. Everyone's sitting at the bar.

The burger is very average. I'm pretty sure this is what i would make on the grill at home if i got a premade patty.  The fries are better than average, but they don't have a special sauce to dip it in, besides Mayo and ketchup. Mayo is pretty great with the fries though, so maybe you don't need a fancy aioli.

If you want a pretty chill environment with pretty basic bar food, go for it. It's entirely possible that the burger is not what they'd like you to order. They've got some much more interesting things on the menu.

Small business owned and and operated by San Francisco and Russian Hill owners! A true gem!

The spicy mezcal-rita is delicious - spicy and smokey. Decent selection of beers on tap, although could be better.

For food - I ordered the calamari po’boy, but was eyeing the truffle ravioli. The po’boy was a good choice, coleslaw, aioli, crisp calamari - very tasty.

The burger was cooked perfectly and generous size patty. My only complaint is that it comes plain. Everything is extra, cheese $2, mushrooms $2, fries, etc, etc. Ketchup and mustard were offered, but some additional sauces would be nice as well as some specialty burger options where you don’t have to build your own.

Parking in the neighborhood is decent. Very walkable area with lots to do.

The owners are A’s fans, so a good spot to watch them, although they’ll put on something else on request.

I stumbled upon this place on accident when looking for a drink on my way to another location. Ordered an heirloom tomato dish that had amazing flavors and paired with goat cheese. The tomatoes were so ripe they were just fantastic.

This place had a lot of charm and the family running it has a lot of pride in the work they are doing. I was surprised it wasn't more busy.

Felt like I found a nice hidden gem with great food options. I hope it doesn't feel as hidden in the future. I will be back next time I'm in town.

Best pizza slices in the entire Bay Area!

I was referred to this place by numerous people so I had to give it a try… had an excursion with my son and we wanted to grab something quick so we stopped here for a slice of Za.

First off, the store is very casual with abundant seating and second, the staff is very friendly and quick.

As for the slices, they were fantastic! The pizza dough is firm with a slight crisp to it and the toppings are all organic and top notch quality. I ordered a cheese slice for my kid and a couple Sweet Little Piggy’s for myself. The candied bacon is a fantastic touch on the sweet piggy.

Highly recommend this spot!
Super solid pizza. Even better house drinks for$9 a piece. I think I'll come here to work next time

I saw the sign as I was walking by coming back from a job that said that it's $12 for two slices of pizza and fresh lemonade. I thought man with prices these days that's a great deal. So I went inside and I got the pizza and it was hot fresh and delicious with house Maid lemonade not from concentrate. I was absolutely pleased with my pizza and the service I got as well as the facility was a little bit authentic like an old family from Italy cooking pizza right out of the kitchen. If I'm in the area again I will definitely swing by this place is a must-have for Pizza Lovers of all ages

Absolutely swinging for the fences, this small pizzeria, in  Oakland's  cemetery-adjacent Piedmont neighborhood, is now my new favorite Oakland Pizza. With a slice, perfectly calibrating flat dough crunch, with a chewy delicious after effect, sauce that is perfectly acidic and just a tad naturally sweet,  and with high temperature cheese melted perfectly in an actual pizza oven, (you'd be surprised at a lot of places don't really have a new york-style pizza oven, it's a thing) these slices are 10 out of 10 for flavor, texture, and presentation.
Cannot speak highly enough of this local Pizzeria.

Querying Jonathan, the Pizza Chef, (as I am known to do)  it was revealed to me that the dough is allowed to preferment, and is a mix of doughs, perfectly combining the flavor profile of sourdough, with that with a more neutral dough, like a New York slice.
Great pizza, great people, great atmosphere, this tiny place represents what to do right about pizza.

top_reviews.content: My husband and I wanted to try Korean fried chicken. 🍗🐔 The place is very clean and The owner was helpful and kind. 😊👍 He helped us choose a few chicken flavors. 🌶️🍯 Absolutely delicious 😋. 💯

I’m just gonna say it: it smelled weird in here. Damp, like a locker room. It wasn’t bad enough to deter us but enough to color the experience negatively — I imagine I’d probably rate this high if I had it for takeout (and, it seems like most people coming in were there for pickup).

Still, sometimes these rough-around-the-edges mom and pop shops can be surprisingly good, and that was true for the Korean fried chicken. Spicy, crispy yet super saucy, and mixed in were these lovely, chewy little rice cake tteokbokkis.

I’d pass on the bibimbap, as the bulgogi was chewier than expected and the oil was a little heavy handed.

I have a feeling I would’ve liked this more after a drunken night out, so perhaps this great Korean spoon is best saved for late nights with friends.

K Soul Chicken is the perfect place for a little Korean fried chicken and snacks pick me up! Their chicken is fried to perfection, and offer so many different flavors. Posted right along Polk St, so it is the perfect place to get the party started over a little beer & casual dinner with friends before hitting up the bars. Aside from the fried chicken, the bbq pork plate and mandu were also delicious and filling. They’ve been serving the community for 35 years, and the owner is so kind and welcoming. Definitely hit them up if you’re in the mood for some delicious KFC & Korean staples.

This place was so delicious! This place was always recommended from our friends. Finally got to try it. We had a kimchi fried rice and the fried chicken was so good. The owner was super nice and he treated us so well we will for sure. Be back our new favorite Korean spot of all time.

If you read hangul, you'll understand that this place specializes in the chicken dishes. The chicken was so tender and amazing. The mandu was homemade and delicious. The sauce for the mandu was perfect, not to much vinegar and not too little. The K dog had so much cheese pull it was astonishing. I'm so glad we chose this place. I can be critical of food from my own culture because I eat a lot of it from various places. This was better than my halmoni makes - just don't tell her I said so.

top_reviews.content: Reasonably priced tasty dinner of Shanghai Soup Dumplings, Sweet fried chicken wings, and beef stew noodle soup. Delicate XLB and juicy. Judging by its name you can't really tell what kind of Chinese food  Ark Chinese restaurant offers. I think it was probably a noodle restaurant focusing on items from northern China. However it seems that the new owners have hired a cook that can also make Cantonese dishes. As a result the menu is more extensive and there are quite a few selections to choose from.

We ordered the pan fried green onion pancake, hand pulled beef noodle soup, tomato beef chow mein, beef stew noodles and sweet sour ribs. All were fairly good but I should note that the flavors were quite intense...as in too much salt or too much sugar.  If you do pay a visit, keep that in mind. You may want to tell them to cut back on the salt and spices.

More importantly the prices are quite reasonable for a restaurant  on Park Street in Alameda. Entrees, dinner items,  generally run around 15 dollars or so.

The decor is ho-hum but the dining room is certainly quiet....perhaps too quiet , or maybe we were there too early. They could use some flowers or some paintings to liven up the place. Maybe play some K pop or something.  The wait staff are friendly and helpful though.

if you're looking for an inexpensive place to eat before you see a movie or just in the area,  give Ark Chinese restaurant a try. The food might assault your taste buds but the prices won't assault your wallet.
I had lunch there today. Such a nice place. Clean and quiet. Food and service are excellent prices are very reasonable.  Noodles are hand made.

Simple, fresh, and tasty dishes in a modest reastaurant where the emphasis is on the food. Well prepared and good service. Two dishes were the tiniest bit on the salty side but were still delicious. Reasonable pricing also a bonus. We would definitely visit again.

top_reviews.content:
The butter chicken curry with the cheesy garlic naan is hands down one of the best combinations I’ve had. Easily one of the tastiest and cleanest Indian restaurants in the city.

Indian food can sometimes upset my stomach, but I had no issues here, which says a lot about the quality and freshness of the food.

Definitely add cheese to the garlic naan. It’s worth it. The butter chicken is rich, flavorful, and pairs perfectly with the soft, cheesy naan. We also tried the pumpkin curry. It was a little on the heavier side, but still delicious with great depth of flavor.

This is a spot I’ll definitely be coming back to

This is easily the best lamb biryani I’ve had in the city so far. The spices were perfectly balanced, and the heat was no joke—in the best way possible. 🌶️ My lips were on fire, but I couldn’t stop eating. Every bite was packed with flavor, and the portion was generous too.

The samosas were also surprisingly good—crispy, fresh, and definitely worth ordering.

One tip: skip the delivery if you can. Mine took about an hour and a half to arrive, so it was cold and I had to reheat it. Even after reheating, it was still amazing, which says a lot. I can only imagine how good it is when served fresh.

Highly recommended if you love bold, spicy food! 🔥

Great food and service! The indochinese food in particular was a delight, especially the chicken chow mein! Our other dishes, the naan, chicken tikka, and saag panner were delicious with the perfect spice. The mango lassi was generous in size and super fresh. Our waitress was super attentive and kind!

New restaurant on the block! Quite unique dishes with bursting flavors! Shaam Shavera and Jackfruit cutlets were definitely the highlights of our meal! Biryani was perfectly spiced and naan was just wow!!

I think the company has to provide customer service training for all employees. I don't think I will come back to these store Little Caesars Pizza Macarthur Oakland ,CA
I would give them 0 stars if I can. They have no idea what Detroit style pizza is at all! Don’t buy it. Not using the right cheese or much of any cheese. This place is a joke!

I had a very disappointing experience with this Little Caesars location due to extremely unprofessional customer service from an employee named Jessica. I placed an order through the Little Caesars app and immediately realized I selected a cheese pizza instead of pepperoni. I called the store right away—within seconds—to politely ask if they could add pepperoni to the pizza since the price is the same.

Instead of helping, Jessica immediately cut me off and said, “First of all, that’s an online order, there’s nothing I can do,” and told me to “call DoorDash,” even though the order was made directly through the Little Caesars app, not DoorDash. She then claimed the pizzas were already made, which made no sense because I had just placed the order moments before calling.

I used to be a regular customer, but after this experience, I no longer feel comfortable ordering from this location. If customer service can’t even handle a simple request—or at least speak respectfully—there’s a bigger problem. Customers shouldn’t be treated like they’re an inconvenience

top_reviews.content: One of the better Chinese places around the block. Prices are pretty cheap with 3 main dish and rice for 39 bucks. Portions are huge, food comes out fast. Recommend!

This is our second time at Ling Ling Cuisine Restaurant and I love it! First of all it’s very clean, the service is very attentive and friendly! The food is made to order and delicious; also the portions are good! I would definitely recommend it and we will come back for sure!

There's an old saying that 'good things come in small packages' and that proves true about this small restaurant. This place has been here for a long time and in a dog eat dog world of competitive Chinese eateries in a town like San Francisco, then you just might actually "wok the talk." Sorry for my puns. :-)

I've gone to this place many a times, especially the years before the pandemic when I lived in the Bayshore area, but I've moved away since. In coming back to eat here again, I'm reminded how much I like this place, particularly for its reliably good food, reasonable prices and quick service.

Which actually disproves one of my good friend's theory that goes, "good, cheap and fast, pick two! These folks actually fulfill all three, which is actually not an easy feat to do.

No wait at 11am on a Friday. Ling Ling serves basic Chinese dishes like fried rice and chow mein. Since we had breakfast earlier, we only ordered wonton soup $12 and a BBQ pork wonton noodles $15. Both were decent sized and tasted OK. I would have preferred shrimp in the wontons. The BBQ pork was dry. Service was excellent since we were the only ones in there.

I took a friend of mine who just moved in the area for lunch here today.  It was our first time in this restaurant.  Unfortunately, we are disappointed for the most part.

Parking is horrendous so if you plan on driving, be prepared to spend time looking for a parking space on this busy street OR be prepared to park at least 6-7 blocks away into the residential area.

The place is small with about 4 tables in front and I think about the same number of tables in the back.  It wasn't too busy when we got there around 12:30ish so we got a seat in front.

And we were glad we were seated in front.  The place was really loud with customers practically yelling at each other AND the kitchen is pretty much in middle of the eating area so you hear a lot of kitchen staff shouting and banging of pots and pans.   We found that we had to raise our voices to hear each other talk.  I could imagine how much more noisy it is if we sat in the back.  If you want a quiet place to chat, this isn't the place to go to.

For the food itself, we were actually pleasantly surprised with the portion of the food.  Our lunch dishes came in big plates with a good heap of white rice.

My mongolian beef lunch dish was good/OK but I found myself looking for beef under all the onions.  I love my onions...but since it's mongolian beef, I expected more beef than onions!

I asked my friend about his beef stew with tofu lunch dish.  He only finished about 2/3 of his food.  He said that the beef was quite tough, and had to chew through it.  Like mine, he said there were twice as much more tofu than beef.

I was happy and surprised at how gigantic the pot stickers are!  But sadly, when I bit into them...it was more dough than filling.

The service staff was nice though. There were two ladies who helped us and was friendly when we asked for forks and water.  The service was quick.  So 5 stars for those two ladies!

One thing that was frustrating was trying to call the restaurant beforehand. Their AI phone system kept asking if I wanted to speak to a manager, but every time I said yes, nobody answered and it pushed me to voicemail. That part was pretty annoying and felt unnecessarily difficult for a simple question about the menu.
As for the pizza itself, it was solid overall. Not the best vegan or plant based pizza I’ve ever had, but definitely good enough that I’d consider ordering again. The pizza arrived a little messy and shifted around in the box — probably more on the DoorDash driver than the restaurant — but the flavor was still there. My wife actually liked it more than I did.
Overall: decent vegan pizza option in SF, especially late night, but clearer vegan labeling and a better phone system would improve the experience a lot.

top_reviews.content: I have been wanting to try this place for a while, and I’m so glad I finally did. The food was very fresh and delicious, and reasonably priced for the quality. The braised lamb sandwich had soft flatbread, crunchy herbs and vegetables, a tangy sauce, and perfectly tender lamb. The service was friendly, warm, and the food came out quickly. Fava is a lovely lunch spot and I would recommend it to anyone looking for a pleasant lunch in North Berkeley.

Incredibly fresh and delicious food. The spicy chicken with herbs in soft, chewy flat bread is probably one of the best "sandwiches" I have ever had. The ginger tea was like nothing I have ever had, and excellent. Healthy, affordable, and fun.

Super yummy and fresh!!! I loved the fresh homemade bread/pita. The falafel was flavorful and delicious. Everything was very herb forward. The cookie was very yummy as well!

I would probably pay 15% more to have 15% more food, but I think basically I just learned that I need a side next time I come here.

They seem to do a lot of take out.

The only downside for me was that dining there didn't include any real dishes. I would have preferred this on like an enamel plate or bowl or something with a parchment paper.

Wonderful healthy vibrant food that is well presented…especially for takeout. 🩷. The person that took my order was super friendly and efficient. The food came out quickly! Loved the lemony green juice and organic chicken. The tahini cookies are giant and tasty but would be slightly better with a bit more salt in the dough or a bit of flake salt on the top. Also tasted my friend’s soup, and it was super yummy 😋 too! Note, this is a takeaway place with a few outdoor tables. Other than wanting more salt in my cookie, I loved everything.

This is amazing food. The spicy chicken sandwich and the falafel sandwich were 10/10 with the home made pita wrap, fresh herbs, and yogurt it’s impossible to go wrong. Also tried the pumpkin pudding and wow wow wow, if you like pumpkin make sure to give it a try. Pictured is the spicy chicken sandwich that is mostly gone, because it was so good I almost forgot to snap a pic 😅

top_reviews.content: We had the tamales—chicken, pork, cheese and the sweet corn one. All of them tasted great and were pretty generously sized. The red and green salsas were all obviously hand made with some love. I also noticed that the masa used had a pleasantly light, moist quality to it—it wasn’t dense and dry. You just gotta respect the hell out of a place that can serve up a hearty, nutritious packet of goodness like this for around $3.

They made a typo. They said best tamales in the Bay area but they meant worst. These are 90% masa. Look at the picture and tell me that isn't a joke. That's the pork tamale. They couldn't have put less in if they tried.
I got cheese chicken and pork and all three are incredibly light on the filling. If I hadn't read a review saying to ask for the free salsa which they don't otherwise include, these would be too dense to even choke down.
Wife grew up in the Mission in SF and had lots of restaurant, food cart, and homemade tamales. She says these are some of her favorites!

I hear the tamales are delicious,  but everytime I go there they are either out of the vegetarian options or closed even during listed open hours. At least put up a sign on when you might open the window back up,  if the clapboard is still out.

Visiting from Texas and saw this place as I was driving, so made a U-turn to stop by.

Got a chicken and cheese Tamale. The chicken was great, a little thin but it had a good amount of meet to masa ratio. But the cheese was disappointing, it was 80% masa and had a small pepper and little cheese.

top_reviews.content:
They over-charged for the food, especially when you order the large size. They give you a larger bowl with more soup and that's it(no more noodles and meat).
The one-man-show waiter is not friendly and provides bad service. I guess/maybe because he thinks it's doesn't matter because the restaurant will charge 18% tips to the bill automatically anyway!.
They even charge for containers for the leftovers to go.
On top of that, the place doesn't look clean.
Food & service was excellent. There's nothing particularly special with the ambiance or atmosphere. It just a great place to eat at very reasonable prices!

Definitely a spot to visit if you’re craving for some Pho Ga. I been here once many years ago and now the ownership has changed, ordered the #17 large. Was just kinda disappointed that they ran out of ho fun, because that’s the only noodle that goes with Pho Ga. The portion is definitely filled and would be enough for 2 persons if one is not that hungry. They also have a big menu selection including some authentic Vietnamese dishes. Will be back next time and hope they have what I need.

The fried fish cake comes with pickled radishes and carrots. The picking is spot on with vinegar to sweetness. Nice presentation with rice noodles sprinkled with ground up peanuts and sautéed green onion. Pho is the major offering but I not sure what region is being represented here, North/South or Asian? I got the large pho ga (chicken). It came with wide white noodles and really shredded chicken pieces (skin included or home style). The broth is delicious with hints of spice in the background. Very smooth flavors and pretty clean broth. No bean sprout or basil leaves, yes I said it “no bean sprout” on the side. I think that someone forgot to tell them that bean sprouts is a super food and it keeps old men regular with their cycles. Wedge of Lime and sliced jalapeño in a small dish. I gave a double shot of sriracha and two tablespoons of hoisin sauce-senior flare. I finished the bowl which proves that old people are hungry and have something to say about a good bowl of pho. Try at your own risk of course and if you are ready to expand your pho skills. Newbies to pho, go somewhere else (with knowledgeable friends). Establishment only takes cash, no credit card or bit coin.

If you find Vietnamese Taco (this is what I call it)... it a real Vietnamese restaurant. I always look for the Taco. Every restaurant have there own name... crepe... pancake... thin cookie... it all lead to Taco.

name: The Rustic - San Francisco
address: 215 Church St, San Francisco, CA 94114, United States

google.name: The Rustic - San Francisco

top_reviews.content: We have been to The Rustic a couple time now. Located on Church and Market, a couple blocks away from the 'main' Castro Street area, they are a bit off the hustle of the Castro. Interior is simple and nice, with a large patio in the back. We always choose to be in the patio area. Service has been consistent and attentive. They have a decent variety of menu items for dinner, and the food we have ordered has been good each time. Yes, you can find some other 'specialized' cuisines elsewhere, but for consistently good dining, service and atmosphere, we have enjoyed coming here.

The Rustic is the best restaurant in San Francisco that you haven’t yet heard of. Whether you learn of it from this review or from your friends who won’t stop talking about it, you will hear about it eventually. The only question is if you will get in and try it before it’s crowded every day.

Between the staff, the ambiance, and the food, you can’t look anywhere without seeing the care and love being put into what they are building here. If you can’t see it, I’m sorry, but you’re either blind or just not looking hard enough.

Do yourself a favor and try the Porcini Ravioli. Their best dish in my opinion. Though, that is not to say the rest of their food is anything less than some of the best Italian food I’ve ever had. The fried chicken is also to die for, both of which I got tonight.

They also are happy to accommodate family style dining, which was great when I was here one Wednesday with my family. By tomorrow night (Sunday) I’ll have been here three days this week, and I have absolutely no regrets about that decision. Every moment I spend here gives me the peace I’ve been looking for in this city.

If my review can’t convince you it’s worth it to try a good thing, then nothing will.

Absolutely loved this place- everything from the vibes, food, and the staff. Loved the Orecchiete- sauce was cheesy but not overwhelming and went super well with the sausage and the bits of broccoli rabe. Also rly liked how the pasta was al dente since I don’t like it when it’s too soft/mushy. You can also get some complimentary focaccia bread as well!

Their dessert was also amazing (we ordered two and ended up ordering one more)- standout was the chocolate budino (creamy foam on top with strawberry bits and rich chocolate custard and everything balanced each other so well). Tiramisu was light and had a perfect ratio of the cream and ladyfingers! Vibes are cute too and would def come back

December 2025:
Used to come to this spot often when Chow was here. But that was a long time ago. Came here on a rainy Sunday evening for dinner.

We started with the mushroom pizza to share. People liked it. I thought the truffle oil was not right for me. Would not order that again. For main, I ordered the vegetable tanguine. Portion was large. The dish could have used some more salt and pepper. It was a little bland.

Service was good.

Came here after finding this place on Resy. It’s actually quite good, though a little on the expensive side.

We got calamari, grilled seabass (branzino), the steak and tiramisu. All were pretty good.

top_reviews.content: These are the most authentic tacos al pastor in the Bay Area! They have a proper spit roasted pork (trompo) with pineapple, just like the ones you’ll find throughout Mexico. The adobo marinated pork is sliced perfectly thin with a slice of pineapple. All of the salsas are legit, and don’t sleep on their California burrito if you’re looking for something more substantial. The handmade tortilla has amazing texture, and all ingredients are incredibly fresh. This is hands down one of the best taco trucks in the Bay Area.

When they say the best Al Pastor, they certainly weren't lying.  The tacos al pastor—the perfect mix of savory, smoky, and a little sweet from the pineapple. Every bite just hits. Make sure you come here during golden hour, so you delicious tacos while having the perfect view of ocean beach with the sun setting.

Hella Mexican here so my review is raw.

Tortillas are lame cheap white GMO tortillas. Boring with extra canola oil to give them flavor.

Asada is good
Lengua is boring
Pastor is boring and I found the reviews over rated.

You have to ask for lime, onion, cilantro, radish and salsa. It is not served on your plate.

Best thing around here? Maybe. Best thing in SF? No way!

We are staying nearby and needed a late-night snack. We ordered the burrito, three tacos (chorizo, chicken, asada/beef), and two vampiros. The staff was kind and offered us all the fixings (onions, peppers, limes, cilantro, radishes) when we picked up our order. We couldn’t wait and ate right in the covered bar area. Our favorites were the red and green salsas. We would definitely go back!

Leo’s Taco Truck serves up some of the best tacos I’ve ever had, paired perfectly with their spicy fries. The food is flavorful, fresh, and worth every bite.
The staff is friendly and welcoming, adding to the experience. Just keep in mind there aren’t any chairs—only tables to stand at—but the incredible taste more than makes up for it.

The dishes were tasty. One dish was less flavorful than the others, almost bland. But one out of 5 things ordered is excusable. I will definitely return. Thank you for the exceptional service.

We’ve always been a fan of this cozy neighborhood gem, recently we’re in the area & returned. The vibe was good, lots of regulars & a lovely bar with good cocktails. Food was delicious, fresh, and remarkably well priced we got stuffed. Family run spot with attentive service & we enjoyed sitting at a little outdoor table for dinner & dessert. Ample Street parking & clean restroom.

I tried the prawns and chicken with vegetables and rice served in a clay pot, and it was absolutely delicious. Every bite was full of flavor and perfectly cooked. For dessert, we shared the apple and strawberry crisp with vanilla ice cream it came out warm and fresh, like it had just come from the oven. Such a satisfying meal from start to finish!

Incredible experience, delicious food, fantastic atmosphere. Big thanks to the entire Vanessa’s team for making tonight’s event a special one. It couldn’t have been better!
We had a group of 20 for a birthday party. Vi created a special menu for us. From the salad to the prawns, the garlic short ribs, to the garlic crab noodles, everything was impressive. They were even able and happy to accommodate some dietary restrictions.
Again, thank you to the entire Vanessa’s team!

Visited from out of town.  Happened upon this cute restaurant when they were celebrating the owner’s and her daughter’s birthdays and they were so friendly.   They had a huge cake they shared with everyone.  Nice vibe.  Food good.  Pretty casual and affordable.

top_reviews.content:
lue Nile Ethiopian Restaurant offers an authentic and welcoming dining experience. From the moment we arrived, the staff was friendly and attentive, making us feel right at home.

The food was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully prepared. The variety of dishes provided a wonderful introduction to Ethiopian cuisine, with rich spices, tender meats, and perfectly cooked vegetables. The injera was fresh and complemented every dish perfectly.

The atmosphere was warm and inviting, making it a great place to enjoy a meal with friends or family. Portions were generous, and the communal style of dining added to the overall experience.

If you're looking for authentic Ethiopian food and genuine hospitality, Blue Nile is definitely worth a visit. I look forward to returning and trying more of their menu.

Nice murals on the walls. Kind server. Not the best Ethiopian food I've had, but not bad. Reasonable prices given that this is the Bay area. We ordered the meat and vegan platter for 4 for $75. We finished every morsel of food. $3 lemonade was not at all special, must be made from a powder, but what can you expect for $3?
Great atmosphere with very flavorful food options! For the food connoisseur! Wash and eat with your hands for the full experience!
Absolutely delicious food, friendly service, reasonable prices, easy parking. Wonderful experience!

A friend told me to try this place. I’ve been vegan for a little while now and a lot of their menu (and Ethiopian food in general from what I understand)  is either vegan or vegetarian and you can have it with meat by choice.

I took my kids so they had the meat with greens dish, one lamb, one chicken and one beef. I had two vegan plates and the appetizer I’m just forgetting the names right now (see pictures).

Everything had so much flavor and tasted super fresh. The spices and flavors were great, the owners are very nice and the environment is really chill. I will be going back here every time I’m in Oakland.

To the owners, thank you so much for the food, suggestions and the hospitality. They made it through the pandemic but people should really support this place.

google.name: CIAORIGATO

top_reviews.content:
Came to the restaurant while visiting San Francisco for the first time.
The fusion of food was truly something I had never seen before, we were so intrigued by everything in the menu. We tried the wagyu carpaccio, two rolls (the fungi and tartufo and another tuna roll). We had the ciarigatoni pasta and the hanger steak and ended with a sesame tiramisu. Everything was truly so delicious, tasty and innovative.
However, the service was not up to par. Our server (whose name I don’t know because she never introduced herself) seemed lost and all over the place. We had to flag her down a couple times to order our food and even though we gave her a card when we first arrived to avoid the check coming to the table because it was my mom’s birthday. She, however, still managed to bring the  the check to the table and  left us with the toast tablet— When we reminded her about the card, she didn’t even mind to excuse herself for the mistake.

Tony, was our busser, and if he wasn’t for him, we would have had an awful experience truly. He was so attentive to us, recommended us dishes, made conversation with us and gave us the service that our actual server did not provide.

My wife and I dined here and felt underwhelmed. The focacciapan (bread) was the best part of the dinner. The Tonno and Pesto sushi had absolutely no flavor to it, also the rice is way too thick around those rolls, something was off. The ciaorigatoni was okay, and the hanger steak tagarashi yuzu was mid. If the potatoes were crispy it would have elevated the plate a little.

The service was great, the atmosphere was nice too….Overall, it’s not a place that we would dine at again.

My pictures look great don’t they? Well, that’s NOT how the food tasted. The food was average at best. The tempura was salty, and the batter was too thick. And the Japanese curry noodles were so dry and tasteless that I felt my throat was hurting swallowing. The only thing that was acceptable was the rigatoni - but again standard Italian flavor that one can make at home. Other dishes might be better, hope you try other ones. Just not the curry noodles or the tempura. Vastly disappointing.

Staff was attentive and friendly, but the food was rather disappointing.

- Chicken yakitori: chicken tasted like water chilled; had barely any flavors and the sauces were either too sweet or too spicy
- Milk bread focaccia: overall tasty, but very small portion
- Rigatoni pasta with mushrooms: flavors were generally good, but the pasta itself tasted rubbery and we couldn’t tell if it was just store bought dry pasta…
- Meatball pizza: the chicken meatballs were very dry and didn’t quite belong to this pizza…

Overall the ambience and the services had potentials, but we were disappointed by the food

​We had an incredible experience at CIAORIGATO, but the absolute highlight of our night was our server, Oana. She provided exceptional service - attentive, warm, and truly professional. She went above and beyond to make our meal special and handled everything with such a great vibe.

​The Japanese-Italian fusion is creative and delicious, but it’s the top-tier hospitality from Oana that will definitely have us coming back. If you visit, definitely ask for her!

Wish we had this type of place near our home.  FYI - if it says spicy- it is! But again so yummy! Definitely recommend this place.

My food was so spicy my mouth hurt and I started sweating which was the only time I felt comfortable because the gale was blowing in the garage door and it was cold. So brilliant! Excellent food; excellent service; excellent atmosphere. I went to the Berkeley branch when they were about to close. But the food was still hot and delicious! The bread and the sausage were so good. Danke!

top_reviews.content:
Great location on Broadway near Jack London Square. Does not have a lot of indoor seating. What seating they have is rather eclectic. The tap selection is great. Unfortunately for me about half of the taps were empty. There had recently been a couple of nearby shows so their taps were hit pretty hard. We will definitely go back to try more of their brews.
The pizzas are delicious! Kind of Detroit and grandma style pies. They do it up proper too. The employees are pleasant, professional, and friendly. The decor is heavy metal-death metal with some satanic stuff. Very interesting and cool just be aware if that sort of thing isn't your cup of tea. 😂
They have some great pinball machines in the arcade. It is a lively location.

Heshers has so many fun pizza topping combos! I love something different and it was reallt hard to choose. We settled on the Canadian Tuxedo (blueberry, blue cheese, bacon) and the Coffin's choice (pepperoni, pineapple, bacon, jalapenos) and both were excellent and balanced. The crust itself was also really good, very crispy outside and light. They also have a great selection of beers and ciders and lots of games including pinball in the back!

We passed by Hesher's so many times heading somewhere else in Jack London, so I'm glad we finally stopped there and will be back!

We had such a great experience at Hesher’s Pizza & Taproom! While waiting on our to-go order of the Cheese Master regular pizza, we played a round of Uno from their giant game closet—literally a chest with drawers full of all kinds of games. We even finished our game right as the pizza was brought out to our table!

The atmosphere is awesome—inviting, laid-back, and fun. Between the pool table, pinball machines, and all the board games, there’s something for everyone to enjoy while hanging out.

As for the pizza? Absolutely delicious. The Cheese Master hit the spot, and I loved that they included small sealed packets of red pepper flakes, cheese, and more on the side. Fresh, flavorful, and perfectly made.

The staff was friendly, attentive, and made the whole experience even better.

Overall, 5 stars across the board. Great food, great atmosphere, and great people. Highly recommend Hesher’s if you’re looking for a fun spot to relax and enjoy top-quality pizza!

This is a cool pizza spot! Metal and pizza go so well together like PB&J, I’m surprised it took this long for someone to make it happen. That’s a compliment not a complaint!

Was there when they had 2 bands playing, and one of the bands me and my buddy went there to see Hedonist; vibe is awesome! Cool spot, and the selection of Pizza is great. They have a pool table, a little corner of arcade and pinball machines which is awesome.

Overall, this is an awesome spot, metalheads and punk rockers will love this spot, and the pizza is definitely worth the price!

I would say that the pizza was created from Satan himself. It was so good I felt like I was doing something wrong. We got the pepperoni honey pizza and it was almost like Detroit style pizza. I always knew that Detroit would be derived from hell. JK but for real this environment is super interesting and is themed on heavy metal. The beer was focused mostly on ciders and was cool that I could get a flight. I would say that if you are cool with something different and are down with metal, show face here. Pro Tip; I saw a couple bring their first date here. I would maybe not do that. Maybe just your homies and play board games. 7.3/10

So delicious. We ordered the prosciutto with burrata, the fennel salad, pork chop, and ravioli. The ravioli was amazing, I don’t know how they got the favors mixed so well, but I’m not normally a huge ravioli person but this is by far the best ravioli i had in the city.

Ordered the Rigatoni alla Bishero and Gnocchi alla Piemontese entrees and they were delicious and flavorful. Shoutout to Mr. Manzoni for taking great care of us.

Had Mother's Day dinner and it was okay. We started with two salads and the eggplant with salmon and 🐐 cheese for the table. All were very good.

For my entree, I ordered the special risotto, which included saffron, asparagus, and parmesan cheese. I was disappointed because there was not a lot of asparagus. The dish looked very nice and since it was on the special menu, I had high expectations. But it was very skimpy on the ingredients.

Overall, rating 3.5 🌟. Since 1/2 🌟 are not allowed, will post 4 🌟.

I absolutely love this restaurant as this is our go to take away Thai food! And I’m so glad they got new owners too because the last guy was so cold and super rude. really exceptional green curry, I would give it five stars for the food but they're so cheap but the papaya salad you get like a tablespoon of papaya and don't get me started on their short wine pour....
Just happened to be in the area and needed to grab lunch, so glad I stopped here; the food is amazing, the music is good, the service is fast! I could not be happier about my lunch.

We stopped here for lunch after walking around Lake Merced.  We had our dog and sat at the outdoor seating. The waitress seemed ambivalent about serving us so we just ordered from the grab and go window.

Prepackaged sandwiches and wraps were fine.

Nice lake views and we came while they were doing dragon boat racing, a nice bonus.

Cypress Grill is tucked inside Harding Park’s golf course, overlooking the serene Lake Merced. The views are stunning—majestic cypress trees and the calm shimmer of the lake make for a peaceful dining experience.

Breakfast portions are generous, pricing is fair, and the staff? Exceptionally friendly and efficient. It’s rare to find a quiet spot like this where you can truly unwind while enjoying good food and great service.

Afterward, I took a leisurely stroll along the nearby path, passing vibrant yellow night primrose, lush gardens, and spotting plenty of birds along the way. It was truly relaxing—magical, even. This place has quickly become one of my new favorite hidden gems.

It's pricey with small portions. Food quality is mediocre.

Outdoor seating available. You can order from the window and/or from a more traditional menu. They have a different breakfast menu as well. The clam chowder was so-so but the tuna sandwich was good, which I got on wheat bread instead of rye. Service was spotty.

They have desserts as well including: praline and caramel ice cream, cookies and cream ice cream, fruit sorbet, chocolate cake.

Nice view of the lake from the tables. The patio has been expanded.
Sat in the patio for a late lunch since we had our pup with us. Food was good. Server was diligent and scored bonus star for bringing out water for our puppy.

Beautiful place, good Americana food and definitely a place to enjoy the scenery and have a relaxing meal or drinks with friends and family. Prices reflect the ambiance, nothing crazy but I would only come here if I could also enjoy the atmosphere.

People need to avoid this establishment because they don’t give a single damn about their customers.

I looked on ClassPass and realized that this has been going on for three months and about a dozen people have had the exact same issue.

When I reached out to them directly, they told me that I can reach out to ClassPass for a refund, and that they “have no control over it”. In reality, they have not bothered to lift a finger to adjust their schedule online so it’s accurate and that this stops happening to people, despite a dozen reviews of people having the exact same issue.

I wasted an hour overall driving there, and they wouldn’t even offer me a courtesy gift card or anything like that, claiming that they couldn’t do anything since this was ClassPass. Getting my credits back is not going to account for the hour of time that I wasted, which could’ve easily been avoided if they had paid any attention to all of the people that I’ve complained about the same thing.

I would love to come back for a dinner when the music is playing.

The place was busy and servers overwhelmed but at least we were acknowledged and given menus! The variety of the menu was impressive which made it easy to order more than two people could eat but sampling was the best move!
Started out with cold beers with a large ceviche portion of perfectly marinated fish and other seafood served with tasty chips and a spicy sauce! I ordered a pupusa which came with a marinated onion medley and more spicy sauce. My daughter ordered fish tacos which came two per order. Delicate fried fish on a warm (could have been handmade) tortilla with tasty fresh avocado and medley of sauces. The portions of fish were entree sized a real value for the quality! A big fan of the popular Hook Fish but these fish tacos would finish first everytime in a contest!
Last but not least I had ordered slow roasted brisket tacos which came three to an order. The grilled tortillas held tender flavorful moist meat which  surprised me with savory deliciousness. My tacos came with a birria like sauce which was exceptional! So good! Obviously we took boxes to go. My leftover tacos heated in a pan the next day were even better I swear!
I don't hesitate in giving 5 stars to our surprise find! You folks in the Outer Sunset probably know about this casual place that hit every thing we ordered out of the flavor ballpark!

Peruvian with a mix of other Latin food. We had the Quesabirrias and the pork was tasty and tender, it was really good. Then we had the flourless chocolate cake that tasted really good, it was like a big truffle! Servers were really nice and kind. I think it’s a great place for a date, and also to go with the whole family. (My daughter [10yo] said it was 10/10)

The Stanyan location of North Beach Pizza is just flat out horrible, while the North Beach location is a decent place to get a quick slice for under $5.00.

If this is you, go here.

top_reviews.content:
3.5 stars - Dinner Review

Like every review, “we wanted to love sirene”.. the menu caught our eyes and the variety and experimentation of different flavors in each dish sounded so intriguing so we were so excited to dine here for dinner. Service is great, they came by often to refill our drinks and clean our tables. Dishes came out at good times.

The food is where it was inconsistent. We got the scallop crudo ($24) where it was very salted on one side and not on the other. The smoked trout dish ($15) was good and probably our favorite of the night. The shrimp chorizo pizza ($25) needed an acid so bad, it was heavy and dense that we requested lemon slices on the side and it made it so much more tasty.

Now for the star of the show, the highly raved fried chicken dish with its sauces and sides. The chicken was good but I’m not sure if I was expecting too much but at least something different whether it was the seasoning or style but it was just good fried chicken. The sauces were more like soup. Took small spoonfuls and just poured it on top of the chicken with some flavor on there but none “wow-ed” me. The kimchi octopus sauce was like a kimchi jiggae.

Overall, glad we tried it.

Dinner for 3 on the outside patio, which is best place to be. I had the chicken which I thought was  ok not great. The crust was so thick and hard I had to use a knife to get to the meat which was somewhat dry. The mash potatoes were good but over salted. My wife loved the gnocchi and our companion enjoyed her sausage. My afragoto was meh as the ice cream didn’t work with the espresso. The Gruner Veltliner was ok in price although tended for a sweeter palate than mine. Glad the restaurant is doing well. In no rush to go back.

Sirene is one of my favorite little gems because she’s living a double life ☕✨By morning, she’s a cozy café with REALLY good coffee. And listen… if I’m paying for coffee, I want the good milk lol. You can taste the difference here. The pastries are chef’s kiss every single time.

I still need to properly explore the lunch menu, but dinner?? The fish and chips keep pulling me back in like the comfort show you accidentally binge for the 5th time 😂

Also one of my favorite random things: look closely in the cracks of the brick walls. There are tiny little notes hidden from past days and people. It feels a little magical and makes you want to romanticize your life for a second. Be whimsical while you’re there.

It’s also such a cute place to work from if you can grab a table… because trust me, it gets BUSY. So if you find a seat, congratulations babe, you won 🫶

My one tiny personal note? I’m not the biggest fan of the chartreuse hand soap lol. A little intense for me personally. Besides that? 10/10.

We want to really love Sirene, and it has the makings and potential of a fantastic neighborhood gem, but certain things have kept it from fully attaining that height for us.  4 stars.

Across a couple meals, we felt service was absolutely stellar: interactive, respectful, timely, and at times very generous, it is the primary reason we have come back and will keep coming back.

The food on the other hand feels a bit inconsistent, with some dishes really hitting home runs and others falling short, especially given the high price of entry and small portions.

Scallops (as many others will also mention) are fantastic, but in contrast the abalone during one visit was flavorless and the texture tough.  Black cod entrée was cooked perfectly, but then the dumpling was difficult to distinguish from the chili oil.

Both meals had mistakes made with the desserts, and it's not the first time we've heard of this happening from friends.  However, both times the restaurant went above and beyond to rectify the situation and we still left happy; service is what brings people back in the end.

The atmosphere is very loud and bustling, it can be a bit hard to hear, but it's also energetic and has a positive, upbeat vibe.

Given the pedigree (huge fans of The Morris) and the high menu cost, I expect a bit more consistency across the dishes.  We still have yet to try the fried chicken, and we're hoping the bumps in the road were growing pains of the fairly recent opening.

We would still recommend checking out Sirene, and we will be back again.  The wine list gets a thumbs up.

Sirene is an upscale seafood and fried chicken restaurant that is popular for special occasions but is also appealing with guest chefs and happy hours for the locals. The alcohol list leans on Chartreuse, amaros, and Madeira and that's awesome. This review is from a meal in May 2026.

We started with what ended up being my favorite course: potato chips with smoked fish dip and trout roe. I wasn’t sure there’d be enough fish dip to enjoy with each chip, but my fears were wrong. The dip was creamy and appetizing in flavor, the chips had a good crunch, and the roe gave it a special touch.

My dinner entrée was not as delicious. That is not to say it was bad—every element was well-prepared, from the tuna cooked just below medium (I am not a fan of rare) to the brown rice with popping outer hulls and the vibrant red tomatillo sauce and fresh pea shoots. But they did not come together to create a complete dish, in my humble food-blogger opinion. The individual parts were good, but the whole felt uninspired, more of a “what do we have on hand tonight?” option than a truly thought-out preparation.

My companions had no complaints, and the gnocchi dish seemed excellent. Its fresh, vegetal-green, garlic nettle sauce enveloped the soft gnocchi. Ricotta dotted the dish. I could have eaten more of that, for sure. My husband’s fish and chips, made with ling cod and served with piquillo pepper aioli, also satisfied.

I opted not to try the chocolate cake with buttermilk ice cream that has earned Sirene glowing reviews, but instead went for the hazelnut tart. It was like two desserts in one, with a delicate olive oil cake sandwiched between the hazelnut cream and thick pastry. Earl grey-infused cream blossomed on top and had more flavor than most earl grey-themed desserts achieve. Each element was wonderful, but this time they also combined wonderfully.

The Drinks: This is where Sirene shined for me. I began the meal with Sirene’s Cup #2, a tiki-inspired cocktail with two types of Chartreuse, gin, pineapple, and lime. Sipping it put me straight into a festive mood, and it was a fun accompaniment to the chips and dip. For dessert, in addition to the tart, I shared a trio of Fernet-type amaros with my friend. We each enjoyed different ones the most, and the expert guidance through them by the waitstaff, from Italy to Japan, was super helpful.

I’d love to work my way through their whole list of cocktails, wines, and liqueurs by the glass, though I’m not sure if I’m brave enough to try the house wine, charged at $2 per centimeter. I’d be sweating the cost!

top_reviews.content: It's my favorite restaurant in SF with creative pescetarian menu available. We come back here to celebrate every meaningful event or just for fun. It's not just a dinner, but more of a performance where food is more like art. You come here to try something you could have never imagined and would never be able to cook at home. I've tried several Michelin star restaurants in SF, but none of them came close to Anomaly. They are not just trying to surprise you with weird combinations of ingredients, but it actually tastes great. I appreciate that they are constantly making improvements to their menu, drink selection and seating arrangement.

From the moment we walked in, the experience felt truly first class. We were welcomed with complimentary champagne that was so good I happily stuck with it throughout the evening. It immediately set a refined and elegant tone.

Sitting directly in front of the open kitchen was an incredible part of the experience. Watching the team work with such focus and precision made the evening feel immersive and intentional. It gave a real appreciation for the craft behind each dish.

The food was outstanding from start to finish. Each plate was beautifully presented and layered with flavor. Every bite was mouthwatering and thoughtfully composed. The seafood in particular was exceptional and among the best I have had in one sitting. The rockfish was incredible, the crab dish was pure indulgence, and the short rib was rich and deeply satisfying. We genuinely could not choose a favorite because every dish delivered. Not a single crumb was left behind.

They were also incredibly thoughtful in accommodating my husband’s dietary needs. We reached out ahead of time, and the team followed up to personally confirm everything, which we truly appreciated. The substitutions were just as intentional and beautifully executed as the original dishes and never felt like an afterthought. Everything was handled with care, professionalism, and ease.

A special recognition to Mike Lanham. His leadership and vision clearly shine through this new menu. You can feel the dedication of the entire team and the care that went into developing each dish.

Dessert was equally memorable. Compliments to Lauren Doggett for a new dessert that was absolutely divine and the perfect ending to the meal.

The service throughout the evening was excellent. Every staff member was knowledgeable, attentive, and genuinely engaged, taking the time to explain each dish with care and intention.

This is Michelin-level dining in its execution, attention to detail, and overall experience. We left already looking forward to our next visit and cannot wait to return.

Amazing restaurant! My girlfriend and I went for her birthday and had a great time! They play with different temperatures in their food, which was fun to experience and set them apart from a lot of other tasting menus ive experienced. Lots of great innovative and creative dishes. I decided to celebrate my birthday at Anomaly this time and it was a wonderful experience. The food was top notch with so many interesting flavors. The presentation, the ambience and friendly service made this a very memorable evening for me. They were also super accommodative of my dietary restrictions and thoughtfully prepared a substitute which turned out to be my favorite dish of the experience!!!  I was lucky to be seated near the kitchen and I could watch the chef's whip up their creations. I was also impressed by how the Head Chef took time to actually serve dishes and talk to everyone in the room. Usually fine dining places leave me a little stuffed but I didn't feel that way with Anomaly. The portions were perfectly sized and I came out feeling satiated without feeling stuffed. I am looking forward to coming back again when they change their menu and would highly recommend them to anyone who wants to try out SF fine dining. This experience should not be missed!!!

I recently celebrated my birthday at Anomaly SF and was welcomed with a glass of champagne upon seating, which was a thoughtful touch.

The food was creative and well-executed, though some dishes felt a bit rich for my personal taste. The sommelier was excellent—friendly, patient, and knowledgeable—and took the time to explain each wine pairing in detail, which I really appreciated.

The restaurant was quite busy that evening, and the service felt slightly under-paced. The overall atmosphere leaned on the quieter, more subdued side, which softened the sense of occasion for a birthday celebration.

The space is modest, with a small open kitchen to watch the chefs at work.

Overall, it was a pleasant experience and works well for a regular date night. For a more festive or celebratory atmosphere, you may want to explore other options.

LTK has been my favorite restaurant for YEARS (a title i do not use lightly) and i always look forward to dining here when i’m in town. i have tried many of their dishes over the years and every single one has been absolutely delicious. portions are large and easy to share so best to bring a group so you can try as many of their appetizers and entrees as possible. (don’t miss their thai iced tea—both the regular and the coconut milk version—and their roti desserts!) i wish i could provide recommendations but it’s impossible to choose, anything you order will be great and trust that you’re going to want to come back and try everything else.

the service is also amazing, the owner boua is so kind and friendly and never fails to brighten my day. do NOT sleep on LTK!!

This place has been a go to for YEARS (since high school). Our family has experienced both dine in and take out, and without fail, every single time, they have been reliable and consistent. The family that runs this place are the most friendly and generous people. They greet us with nice chatter during every visit, even if it’s just picking up our meal. Our family has ordered so many times, we even have the “Shane special”, which is the specific way my dad orders his curry. Our go tos include: the pad thai, pad kee mao, the many assortments of curries (which I appreciate that you can choose your own spice level), and the larb. The drinks are also delicious, especially the Thai tea. This place is so good, that it has become the standard for Thai restaurants for our family. 1000/10 would recommend.

My favorite place in the area. Specials are always fantastic (I particularly love the seafood!), as is the regular menu. High quality home cooked food that never disappoints. Friendly and fast service.

Really friendly waitress… she’s always in a great mood.
Great flavors. The pa-nang curry is amazing!!
Have gone in on Saturday nights ~6 and have never had trouble getting a table.
Take out is also large portions and packaged well.

We came here for dinner and had a great meal! We ordered the Thai iced tea to drink, the Lao sausages as an appetizer, and the pad see ew with beef, phao larb, and yellow curry with chicken as mains. Everything was good, and the service was excellent! The spice levels here are no joke, so definitely stay below levels 2-3. The owner is super nice, and she even explained the differences between Laotian and Thai cuisine to us!

top_reviews.content:
I eat a lot of burritos in the bay and throughout socal. The burritos here are very good for the east bay. I highly recommend their burritos. Flavors and ingredients are top notch. I appreciate the option to add things like jalapenos into the burrito. They put rice in their burritos but you can see from my picture that they don't use it as a massive filler. It's the appropriate amount of rice.

I'm a person where a regular burrito is slightly too much food but I always eat the whole thing because saving 20% of a burrito is pointless. I recommend getting the comelon sized burrito which is $4 more but a massive burrito. Cutting it into halves if the perfect sized burrito for two meals.

Couple issues with this place. Some ingredients are free to add but some things have cost. $0.25 for black beans. Extra money for certain salsa. I don't like this. Feels like you're being nickel and dimed and most burrito shops don't do this. The burritos themselves are also not cheap so any extra cost is on top of an already premium burrito price.

Their salsa also leaves something to desire. I much prefer the salsa at Tacos in walnut creek. The chips are also thin and weak.

Considering my issues, it is still worth it for the high quality burrito. I would technically rate this place 3.5/5 but Google reviews are fake and it's basically 5 stars or 1 star. I think this place is worth the visit to try their burritos for the high quality ingredients and good flavor.

Incredible food!! The best guac and some amazing burritos as well. Quick service and very helpful staff make it a great takeout or grab and go spot. There are some tables inside but would recommend sitting outside where there is more space or taking it to go!

Comeliness is an excellent Mexican food option in Theatre Square Orinda. Their tacos are top notch and their burritos are huge and excellent. The staff is very friendly and the whole vibe is legit quality authentic Mexican food. I highly recommend you try it out. Note that most people take their food to go as there isn’t a lot of room inside or outside for sitting (but this is some).
It’s the best Al pastor in the east bay, great trompo. Pickled carrots are fire. Solid.

Seriously, the best street tacos in town! The carnitas is our favorite and we LOVE the cabbage salad. (I wish I could order a whole side of it because it is perfect.)  Everything we've had has been delicious.
