top_reviews.content: This is really a hike in the wall! Lovely atmosphere, boutique like setting (since the max capacity is prob 25 pax?). Everything we ordered is so delicious and beautifully presented. I love the sake too. The sashimi is very fresh and I would definitely recommend that if u plan on dinning here.

Butterfish is in a league of its own—simply the single greatest sushi experience I have ever had. From the moment we walked in, the staff brought incredible warmth, authenticity, and passion to the table, taking the time to explain every single dish in rich detail.

Every item on the menu hit a home run:

Albacore Melody ($19.00): Remarkably fresh, perfectly balanced, and melted in the mouth.

Island Scallops ($19.00): Delicately sweet with an unbeatable, velvety texture.

Escolar Tapa ($15.95): Rich, buttery perfection—easily one of the standout bites of the night.

Sushi and Sashimi 12-piece ($59.00): A masterclass in knife work and quality. Every piece was exceptionally fresh and thoughtfully presented.

Kani Real Crab Handroll ($10.95): Generously stuffed with real crab that truly shone through.

Sapporo ($6.95): Crisp, cold, and the ideal pairing to round out an unforgettable meal.

I honestly never realized just how incredible a dining experience like this could be. Butterfish has officially set the bar so high that it has completely ruined sushi anywhere else for me. If you are in Berkeley, do yourself a favor and eat here!

This place is incredible in food, service, and atmosphere. Such amazing quality fish and delicious dishes.

My favorite was their hand rolls and the hirame usuzukuri (like a carpaccio). Even their green tea was made well, not bitter at all - so smooth. I dont think you could get anything wrong here.

Came here last-minute looking for a good sushi place, and it was amazing. Atmosphere was indeed omakase-esque as other reviews state, really small and intimate. Sat at the bar and watched the chef at work, which I would highly recommend. I don't think you would go wrong at all ordering anything off the menu, everything we had was delicious. Portions on the salmon avocado roll were large, and there was never any padding for space in a roll with extra rice... just more fish. A bit on the pricey side, but very much worth it and really close to the best sushi I've had.

top_reviews.content: I saw all the good reviews about the chicken sandwich and was surprised to see people love it even though it’s a cafe at a museum. I decided to try it out but place is mid tbh. This was NOT the “best ever chicken sandwich” as it’s named. Chicken was a bit hard and overcooked and the fries were hard as well. Definitely not worth it.

My friend and I had a somewhat difficult time locating the restaurant as we didn't think the directions were clear, especially with it being my first time to the museum. Mid-level? What's mid-level? There was an elevator to the upper level from the level we were on but you had to go down stairs a level to get to the restaurant. So, what level were we on when we came in?

Anyway, once we entered I noticed there was no table service so we had to decide what we wanted before we paid at the register.  The line was short and there was a tender agel child, possibly 8 yrs old or so in front of us with some adults ahead of her. I assumed she was with them and not unattended. The cashier at the second register said next customer but said her register wasn't working and Michelle Mc Queen, who was at the first register, said we had jumped the line. So we went back and Michelle told the customer behind us that the second register, where we just were could take the order if paying by credit card so all of a sudden, the register was working. Hmmm...

The food came fairly quickly. I ordered the deviled eggs, excuse me, the World Famous Deviled Eggs. To us, the filling was under seasoned. I had the fried pork chop with macaroni and chees and collard greens. The pork chop was salty and hammered. It was extremely dry. The Mac & Cheese had an ok flavor but the macaroni was mushy. The greens we good.

My friend had the Fried Chicken Sandwich with fries. He offered me a piece of his sandwich and the coleslaw on it was good and needed to offset the overly salty chicken. I didn't try the fries but my friend said they were salty.

None of the fried food was oily but it was very crispy.

Michelle saw me in passing delivering a meal to a table and wanted to know how we liked the food. I said I would speak with her after. She stopped by and I told her the pork chop was overcooked and salty and, giving her the benefit of the doubt, the macaroni perhaps had been held too long(instead of being overcooked to begin with)as the noodles were mushy. My friend and I told the chicken was salty but the coleslaw was good. She pleasantly and immediately offered to re-cook the meal but I declined. To her credit, she didn't act offended or was offensive but wanted to satisfy a customer. Her attitude alone would make me want to go back. Plus  I do understand things happen in the kitchen. The cook could have been distracted and perhaps lost time how long the pork chop had been cooking as a thin cut chop doesn't take long to overcook. If something isn't right with the food, I would go back as long as the food isn't horrible or the staff is dismissive. The food wasn't horrible and her attitude was perfect.

When first walking in, the host weren’t at the, “Wait to be seated” sign and made a smart remark when my mother was walking in. We were seated about 2-3 minutes after. I ordered two orange juices that were priced $4.5 on the menu, but was charged $5. That was one thing. My food came out in a decent amount of time, the waffles were great! But the white meat chicken I ordered with it, looked like a chunk was cut out of it, fired, and then served to me; almost like it was a scarp piece of meat. Catalina was my waitress, took my payment for the meal, and brought me back the wrong receipt. Now, I wouldn’t be that worried about it, but the receipt was an AMEX purchase of $8.00, and mine was a cash payment of $55.00. So that bothered me when I realized what the waitress had done. My food I would give a 4/5 because of the chicken with my waffles. 3/5 over all for the service.

Start to finish delicious! We used to go to her spot in the Fillmore District SF called Gussie's Chicken & Waffles. Had the Bloody Mary's Revenge and the basil ginger soda, deviled eggs, fried chicken & sweet potato waffles, and the fried chicken sandwich. You can run & tell everybody that this is the spot! DJ Mark Divita during Sunday brunch gave us the perfect musical pairings.

We came to Town Fare for the first time after finding out about the restaurant from the Bay Area KQED check please show. We were thrilled to try their chicken sandwich which came with breast meat and some coleslaw. The meat was very tender, cooked to perfection, the coleslaw had really nice flavors, and the buns were good too. The mac and cheese was also very good; the cheese had good flavor. The restaurant has a very open, clean, organic modern atmosphere. Many seating options inside and outside. The staff were nice. They have street parking around the museum and a museum parking garage. 10/10 Recommend.

top_reviews.content: My friends and I celebrated our birthdays over lunch here, and everything was delicious!  The crab & garlic noodles did not disappoint, the tiger prawns were so flavorful, and everything else we ordered was so good!  The only letdown was the short ribs, meat was kinda chewy and the sauce wasn’t as flavorful as it could have been.  Service was also very friendly and attentive.  Highly recommend!

I tried their clam soup which was cold and I wasn’t expecting that. It had good flavor but I think it would taste better warmed up. We tried the aguachile shrimp and it wasn’t what I expected. I expected more lime flavor and for the shrimp to be cooked in more lime or lemon. The shrimp was more raw than regular aguachile. We tried their garlic roasted crab and it was good. The brown butter sauce gave it a more nutty taste. It was a bit too salty but I asked for lemon and it really rounded out the flavors.

TLDR: 3.5 stars, pho was underwhelming but fish cakes were really good.

I got the lunch special for $25 which was beef pho, fish balls and Viet iced coffee. Checking in and paying with blackbird got me free fish cakes.

The fish cakes were the best part of the meal. The Vietnamese iced coffee was slow dripped in front of me which is nice.
The main event was the pho and though it was supposed to be Wagyu, I couldn’t tell. It was still a bit tough in the soup. Speaking of the soup, it was light and not super flavorful.
Normally don’t like using condiments in my pho but had to use the hoisin and sriracha.

Food: We had five dishes: the Blue Prawn Aguachile, the Quail, the Miso Butter Mushrooms, the Pho Risotto, and a Promo Bo Luc Lac which happened to be free due to an ongoing promotion. We found the food alright, a little pricey for the quantity, but were slightly disappointed with certain dishes. The Blue Prawn Aguachile was decent, but the flavor lacked depth and 4 shrimp for $24 is egregious. The quail we found quite pleasant, and the flambé was rather fun, but seemed only to be for show and nothing more. For the Miso Butter Mushrooms and Bo Luc Lac, they were both decent but had a glaring issue—both had a similar and distinct burnt flavor. It ended up overpowering the other flavors in the dish and left us very unfulfilled. Whether it was by choice or by accident, it should be noted that it is a disturbing taste and a reoccurring issue. The Bo Luc Lac was better off as the sweetness and tenderness of the meat offset some of the burnt taste. The mushrooms, on the other hand, are a complete waste of money. They lacked a miso taste and we found a piece of plastic in the mushrooms. The Pho Risotto was actually quite pleasant and the meat that comes with the dish was actually very good. Overall, the food was very lackluster and portions were kind of small, but there was one dish worth trying: the Pho Risotto.

Service: The service started off alright, but ended up getting worse throughout our night. Our server was actually very nice, and helped us with deciding on dishes to order and working through the Blackbird promo that was going on. However, we didn’t see her much throughout the night as other servers helped us with other issues, but that’s just how restaurants work and she is faultless. Issues came later. When we found a small piece of plastic in our mushrooms, we reported to another server nearby, and he got it remade for us after asking us if we wanted it remade, of which we said yes to. That was the bare minimum done. While paying, we reported the issue of the plastic in our mushrooms, as one normally does, and our server went to talk to the manager. The manager ended up coming to us and talking about things. At first she offered to comp the mushrooms, but said that she would have to un-comp the Bo Luc Lac that came with the promo as removing the mushrooms would bring the bill below the $60 threshold for the promo. That was weird; usually these issues of plastic in the food and whatnot is on the restaurant to make it up and shouldn’t cost the customer anything and it comping the mushrooms would bring the total to $69, which was above the promo threshold. No big problem right? It was probably just a mistake so we called it out. Suddenly the manager backpedaled and said that since the dish was remade, we shouldn’t get comped. That was weird because earlier she was all for giving us a refund but would remove a promotion. It didn’t sound like she wanted to resolve any issue whatsoever. We found an issue with this because she never even apologized for the plastic in our mushroom. The only server that apologized for the issue was the server that brought us a new dish we reported the issue. We found the situation to be extremely mishandled. Anyways, we didn’t want to fight so we just let it go. Then came the paying. Everything was as normal except for the tip; it was a set 22% for using blackbird to pay and was based on the total after tax and SF mandate. It was weird because we didn’t get to choose a tip and the tip was based on the total after tax and not before. Plus, they have their own toilet, which is a huge plus. You can easily wash your hands whenever you need to.

The basil beef and orange chicken were so well cooked and the quality of ingredients is very apparent. So Delicious!! The service and owners are so sweet too.

My favorite Chinese to-go spot! I have never seen so many vegetarian options at a Chinese restaurant besides actual vegan spots. I love the vegan orange chicken. The orange flavor is so strong and tangy which pairs perfectly with rice.

top_reviews.content: Quick and affordable made to order onigiri with vegan/plant based options. I like the spicy tofu triangle, the teriyaki tofu and the kimchi tofu triangles are good as well. They usually throw in complimentary edamame if you get a few, and they have other options as well. More of a grab and go atmosphere but they are fast and friendly to me, and the condiment section is loaded with good stuff like free sesame seeds, teriyaki sauce, Japanese spice, Sriracha, shoyu etc. I like this for a nice light meal for some protein and energy after a work out or so.
Fantastic flavors and a great deal. Loved the chicken teriyaki and the miso soup.

Ive been coming here for years. My favorites are the spicy tofu/ grilled salmon/ ahi tuna triangles/onigiri. They also have an ahi tuna plate (over rice) which i get as well. If you get a set of 3-4 onigiris it comes with edamame. My orders have always been made quickly and prices are affordable.

In all my travels, I look for what I call "happy food."  Happy food for me is healthy, nutritious, tasty, nicely prepared, and served by smiling people in a clean environment.  Oori exceeded all my happy food requirements and then took me for a ride through food blissfulness with each bite.  I had chicken teriyaki, grilled salmon, and spicy tuna triangles.  On the side, I complimented it with miso soup and ginger. Each flavor was distinct and made my taste buds ooh, ahh, and wow for more.  I'll be back here for more without question. I felt like I was dining at a 5-star restaurant and found the food reasonably priced.

The double unagi rice triangle features large pieces of unagi.   The short rib plate is not really short rib but small bites of beef nuggets.  I prefer edamame boiled rather than wok fry as the edamame tends to be greasy with wok fry.

We love the pizzas! They also have a great roast chicken, which makes for a delicious family dinner. Ingredients are high quality and the atmosphere is sweet.

Food and service was phenomenal. We were trying to catch a quick bite before the movies at Grand lake on a Friday night and it was just perfect and convenient. We ordered the Broccoli and beef, salt and pepper wings, and vegetable fried rice. Highly recommend. Truly a gem of a place!
A 10/10 experience. The prawns with mixed vegetables lunch special was tasty and a great value. I left satisfied, and the hostess/server/cashier was very friendly.

Food is good average Chinese American menu the interior design is minimal and sedate and very clean. My complaint is that the odor of the cleaning products they use competes with the aroma of their food. Better to pickup than stay in if you don't like Pine-sol or  whatever that smell comes from.

top_reviews.content: I wouldn’t order from this place again. The Tom Yum soup was overly tangy with a strong tomato flavor and the noddles were too oily. I wanted to give this place a try since  it is close to our neighborhood but there are tons of other good Thai restaurants around. On top of it, asking for a minimum 18% tip for the order we picked up ourselves was interesting.

Me and my friend where in the area during lunch time, where both us were in need of some food immediately. We roamed around the neighborhood for a bit before we came upon this spot. We both agreed to try this place out and look no further since our appetite expanded and hunger grew. Upon arrival, there were a few guests in house, and one of their friendly staffs seated us immediately. Everything on their menu sounded delicious and made me wanted to try it all. They offer lunch combos with one or two selections of their listed entrees that comes with steamed Jasmine white rice and salad or soup. Their menu also consists of shareable items, soup, salads, their most popular items, fried rice, stir-fried noodles, noodle soups, curry, veggies, wok fried dishes, drinks/alcoholic beverages, desserts and much more to choose from. Everything here is made to order which is always a plus for me since it is quality over quantity and I never mind the wait since I am a very patient person. Finally when our food arrived I knew we made the right choice by coming here, because their dishes were balanced with flavor compared to other Thai restaurants where it is too sweet, sour or spicy and the ingredients this place choose is very fresh and carefully selected. We thought we ordered too much, but everything was finished since it was time to feast. The staffs here are welcoming, well trained and understanding where my visit was a satisfying and issue free one. And as time grew, it got busy with more people coming in for dine in and to pick up their takeout orders. You can dine in, place an order over the phone or have it delivered to you via a food delivery app. I highly recommend this place to all Thai cuisine lovers, to anyone willing to try something new, if you need a quick bite or if you just so happen to be in the area to check them out. I definitely will be back again to tryout the other delicious options they have to offer.

Went on a weekday around 1pm. I was the only customer in the restaurant which made me wonder if it would be good. The service was great and the food came out quickly. Lunch special was under $20  I had yellow curry and green beans & tofu came with a side salad. Lime tea was pretty good too.

Service is good. The staff are Chorus and prompt. They try to accommodate your requests.

top_reviews.content:
So excited  to finally try Hana Izumi! The lunch menu starts with a Chef's Tasting Plate of seasonal small appetizers. The seasonal appetizers included chawanmushi steamed egg, inarizushi, tamagoyaki egg with daikon, and 2 other items.

The Bara Chirashi Bowl included seaweed to make hand rolls with the sashimi, ikura, diced pickled radish, ginger, etc. Each type of fish was prepared well, but the scallop was especially good.

Beyond the food, the service was wonderful. The restaurant responds quickly to calls and texts for reservations. The staff are very attentive and knowledgeable about the food. The restaurant feels classy and comfortable. It is easy to see the care they put into their business.

Can't wait to visit again for dinner!

Made dinner reservations for our anniversary. Very easy process and friendly communication. Just text the number posted online. One thing about parking, the surrounding area is always busy and hard to get good parking so take the time to get here early, parking is frustrating around the area.

I’ve been wanting to try Hana Izumi for awhile and finally made the time to. Everything was delicious. The staff are extremely professional, courteous,  and friendly. The ingredients were all incredibly fresh and flavorful. Not a single bad dish. Easy favorites were the duck (pictured in the cocktail glass) and the crab. There was also a dessert duo (not pictured) that had red bean jello and matcha mochi with fruit, also delicious. Would definitely come back.

Lovely hidden gem in Millbrae/ authentic kaiseki spot. The food is traditionally done at a high level. The atmosphere is warm/ cozy.

Favorites included the sesame tofu with uni, sashimi, crab steamed egg, duck breast, and the filet mignon. The menu changes monthly, which makes it feel worth coming back to.

The service is also great, run by a Japanese couple who make the whole experience feel personal.

Hana Izumi was an incredible lunch experience. Chef Koji, the husband and owner, prepared delicious, traditional Japanese dishes that beautifully celebrated seasonal ingredients from California. Every course was excellent, and my personal highlight was the Kobachi 3 Ways. Luna, our kaiseki server and the general manager, was attentive, friendly, and welcoming throughout the meal. It’s a small restaurant, but the food and hospitality are truly exceptional, easily up there with some of the best meals I’ve had in Japan. Thank you so much for the wonderful meal!

This place is truly amazing! Every dish wowed me right from the first bite. The flavors were incredible and everything were made from scratch! The sashimi were really delicious (chutoro literally melts in the mouth) and the wagyu steak main dish is sooo tasty! The family style restaurant is super cute and everyone is so welcoming and friendly. I recommend doing it with sake for the full experience. 12 out of 10!

We ordered the seasonal truffle pasta and it was absolutely delicious, the truffle flavor was gentle and well balanced, not overwhelming, with fresh truffles that really elevated the dish. We also tried the chicken, which was good, though slightly on the salty side but topping was so good. The desserts were also tasty and a great way to finish the meal.
The atmosphere is calm and quiet, perfect for a date night. Tables are a bit close to each other, but it never felt too loud.
Overall, I would definitely recommend it as a romantic spot with very delicious food.

I was pretty excited to try this place out since I live in the neighborhood and heard good things about the place; unfortunately quite disappointed by both the service and food.

We ordered a salad, cacio e pepe, and the lasagna. The salad came out pretty quickly; nothing surprising or special about the salad, just what you would expect. Afterwards, we waited for over 45 mins to finally get our cacio e pepe that 1) came out in a cracked dish as shown in the pic (which I think is not to be expected from a restaurant at this pricing and reputation), 2) it was super salty; I’ve tried cacio e pepe in other Italian places in SF. This one was way too salty. Not sure if it was a mistake or from sprinkling too much salt on it before giving it to us. After the cacio e pepe was served, the lasagna came out after 20 mins. We ordered a simple salad and 2 pasta dishes and the total time to get all of our dishes out was over an hr which I think is pretty ridiculous.

Next the service was not great. Our server ( I’m a bit blurry on his name) checked in on us not a single time during the entire service when I noticed he was checking in on other tables much more often. I’m not sure if it was some racism going on here because we were the only Asian ppl there, but didn’t feel welcomed and served right.

One last thing; our table was situated in a weird position where we can see and hear the guy sitting on the bar eating his dish. Sometimes crumbs will fall from the bar to our table which is a bit of a ick…

So overall, disappointed and will not go again.

Excellent experience. We started with some focaccia and olive oil; it was good. We took the waiter's recommendation and had a tomino cheese special as appetizer with some pieces of toast; it was quite succulent. For main courses, we once again chose the special, a truffle pasta. The price was hefty ($55!), but it was absolutely delicious. We also had the ricotta gnocchi, which was saucy and rich. We finished the evening with some tiramisu, which was alright.

The service was mostly fine, except for some minor hiccups. The ambience is fine too. We spent $160 for two after tax before tip.

Collina is the “little sister” of Seven Hills, and you can definitely see the same polished Italian influence in a more casual, cozy neighborhood setting. The star for me was the 50-layer lasagna — incredibly thin layers, crispy edges, rich meat sauce, and a beautiful green sauce underneath. The rosemary focaccia was also excellent: fluffy inside, golden and crisp on top, and perfect with olive oil. We finished with tiramisu, which was light, creamy, and not overly sweet.

Cozy, approachable, and a great spot for handmade Italian comfort food. I’d come back for that lasagna alone!

Service was great!

Second to NONE! My fiancé and I found this place on Resy (now on open table) when we were looking for restaurants in sf (we are visitors). Liam, our server, and Ashton, the manager, made sure our experience was enjoyable, personal, and intentional. Our favorites from the night were the blue shell crab for him and the scallops for me (see pictures attached). These were some of the best scallops I have ever had. I wish this restaurant was in our hometown so we could eat here regularly! I would definitely recommend making a reservation for this spot as it is a smaller restaurant and it fills up quick. This is a place you don’t want to miss! LOVE LOVE LOVED IT!!!!

top_reviews.content:
Came for the Wednesday Prime Rib special for $65 and made it just in time for the happy hour, which was $2-$4 off the original price, so I ordered even more items. The deviled eggs had four pieces(2 kinds), the bacon marmalade was rich and flavorful and the smoked salmon was quite salty. The calamari misto was lightly battered and I loved that it came with a mix of artichoke heart, shrimp, calamari, onions, and jalapenos. I could taste the umani of the duck fat fries. The uni pasta got the creaminess down, and the squid ink pasta was cooked well, but the uni flavor was very light and the flavors weren't as bold as I had expected. The prime rib was tender and the sides were decent. The chefs amuse bouche and the churro were the cherry on top for the prime rib special.

With everything that was ordered, I was worried that I didn't have enough table space, but all the items were spaced out enough to fit everything a the right time. The Fermentation Lab is the perfect place for a date for those that appreciate a lovely atmosphere, welcoming service, vibrant drinks and beautifully plated dishes. I probably wouldn't come for just the prime rib special, but I would love to try other items on the menu. I wasn't expecting any screens, but they had two projectors and a tv playing the USA vs Bosnia World Cup game so that was a pleasant surprise!

Cocktail bar with pretty delicious food!!! I really enjoyed my experience here overall. A beautiful interior and good vibes. Everything on the menu was priced a little high, but the quality was worth it. Every cocktail was good!

FYI - Yelp advertised that this restaurant has a "no tipping policy"... but the tablet indeed asked for a tip when we checked out. Service was great, so I didn't mind... but just a heads uo!!!

+ Uni Pasta (5/5): MY FAVORITE! Squid ink pasta was perfectly al dente and carried the creamy sauce so well. Very decadent, full of flavor, and smooth. They added a good amount of uni for the price.

+ Makgeoli Braised Bossam (4/5): Very small portion, but the pork was cooked well and was flavorful. A different take on bossam, so not very traditional.

+ Tea Leaf Salad (2/5): Lacked so much flavor. Vegetables were fresh, but the tea leaf dressing truly did not taste authentic. I would not recommend.

+ Sake Flight (5/5): SO GOOD! Bang for your buck. I loved the variety of sake and the presentation. A lot of these I've never even heard before.

Easy self seating on a Saturday afternoon for two, cocktails are solid but at market rate for this area. My matcha martini was well made and those duck fat fries were damn good! Brussel sprouts were as expected.... lots of standard bar fare and happy hour prices.  Fast service, we would definitely go back. If you love beer, there are an array of good local brewed choices.

Take this with a massive grain of salt as we came during happy hour and got the specials. So, their regular menu might be great. Everything felt like it was overcompensating. The oysters were hidden under mounds of salt. Good wet wings still have a crisp to them, but these had a "mush" to them. The calamari was good and our server was great.

May 2026:
Came here on a Sunday night and was pleasantly surprised that Happy hour was all night.

From the happy hour menu, tried the Korean chicken wings. They were tasty. Could have been crispier. Perhaps the wings were precooked.

Also tried the tea leaf salad. I liked the salad. Had tasty dressing. Liked the fried garbanzo beans.

We also shared the Korean noodle soup. We had to send it back because the first time we got it, there were at least 6 clams that didn't open up. They remade the dish and it was much better. Oddly too that the first time we got the dish, the broth was a little thick. When they remade it, the broth consistency was much better.

Service was a little slow but very friendly.

address: 160 W Juana Ave, San Leandro, CA 94577, United States

top_reviews.content:
I absolutely LOVE breakfast burritos and can confidently say this is my #1 breakfast burrito… ever.

And not just me, but even SF Chronicle tried over 100 breakfast burritos and named them #1 in Bay Area. When you first enter, the vibe is high. Everyone is super welcoming and there were already customers right when doors opened. The price is actually so good and affordable, especially in this economy.

Breakfast Burrito | 5/5: it is PACKING and I was pretty much full eating a quarter of it. The jalapeno crema sauce was the icing on the cake, because it was fire.

Tater Tots | 5/5: crispy and so tasty!

Banana Pudding Shake | 5/5: absolute fire - probably one of the best milkshakes I've had.

Fruity Pebble | 4/5: this was surprisingly really good and you can taste pieces of smashed fruity pebbles in the drink too!

First bite will steal your heart and you’ll definitely be coming back for more. I already told my friends to try this place and they absolutely loved it. 10/10!

Walked into Smack Burgers thinking I was just grabbing a quick bite… walked out questioning my entire definition of a burger.

I ordered the Hellapeño and Smack Fries, and I’m not exaggerating when I say this thing looked like it just came out of a backyard cookout hosted by someone who takes burgers personally. The patties were smashed crispy on the edges but still juicy, dripping with melted cheese like it had something to prove. Then the bacon perfectly crisp, not floppy, not burnt, just riding on top like it owned the place.

That Hellapeño hit exactly how it should: not overwhelming, but enough heat to let you know you made a bold decision. The grilled onions and jalapeños blended into this smoky, slightly sweet, slightly spicy combo that honestly had no business being that good.

And then the Smack Fries… these weren’t fries, these were a full on event. Covered in cheese, grilled onions, and sauce like they were built to ruin your diet and your self-control. Halfway through I told myself “I’ll save some for later.” That was a lie.

Also, small detail but huge impact, fries cooked in beef tallow. You can taste it. It’s richer, crispier, and just hits different.

This isn’t a clean, neat, Instagram-perfect meal. This is a “lean forward, elbows on the table, accept your fate” kind of burger.

10/10. Would absolutely come back and make the same bad (but delicious) decisions again.

Since I entered the store very good service. The guy at the front register very good and also how he greeted other customers. I also like how it took 10 mins or so for the food but it was guaranteed fresh out the grill burger, fries and milks shake.  One thing fasho like I told the guy at the front register. I’ll will be back and I will let all my peoples know back in my town which I come from San Rafael ca and also all my east bay family and friends to come to this good spot.  Good jobs on a good burger spot that worth the drive and money. Also my favorite shakes is the banana pudding and fruity pebble shake. Also the hellapeno burger with waffles fries.

If you’re looking for one of the best burger spots in San Leandro, Smack Burger is absolutely worth visiting. The burgers are incredibly flavorful, juicy, and cooked perfectly every time, and you can tell they use fresh, quality ingredients in everything from the burgers to the fries and sauces. What really stood out to me was the excellent customer service — the staff was friendly, welcoming, and attentive, making the entire experience enjoyable from start to finish. The restaurant was also very clean and well-maintained, which made the atmosphere even better. It’s hard to find a place that consistently delivers on food quality, service, and cleanliness, but Smack Burger does all three and has quickly become one of my favorite burger restaurants in San Leandro. Highly recommend for anyone craving a delicious smash burger and great food.

Visited Smack Burgers after hearing a lot of positive word-of-mouth on social media and I am happy to say I was not disappointed !

Menu items we tried this time
- 2x  Hellapeno burgers : Delicious 😋
- Onion Rings : well done and crisp
- Chocolate Milkshake
- Banana Milkshake

You order at the kiosk and pick-up the order as its prepared. The food was fresh and every thing we tried hit the spot.

The milkshakes were not too sweet and had the perfect shake consistency. Highly recommend getting them.

Overall, this is my new favorite burger joint in the Bay Area. Only complaint is that they only have one location in the Bay Area in San Leandro which is quite a drive for from South Bay. Please open more locations.

top_reviews.content:
I’ve walked Noriega street multiple times and never realized there was a good Korean restaurant here!  It is easy to miss unless you’re looking for The Crew, which is why I’m glad a friend recommended this place to me.

What I liked about eating here is that the food is served HOT.  We had the soft tofu soup, seafood pancake, stone pot bibimbap, and 1/2 serving of galbi.  The portions are generous and it fulfilled our craving for Korean food.  The banchan (small plates) is average at best, but that did not deter from the experience.  The food we did order was exceptional.

the best beef bone soup i’ve ever had, and i’ve been to plenty of korean joints. something they put in that broth… it just tasted so flavorful….. the huge bone had the meat falling off it, was so tender, and the portion sizes were great for sharing! server was great, yum yum
Food was great! Came here with some friends and got kimchi fried rice, bulgogi, army stew, seafoood pancake and fries! Service was great would recommend :)

Came on a Tuesday night at 830pm and our large group of 7 was able to be seated with no delays. Shortly after though between 9-10pm, the restaurant was pretty crowded. Fortunately we beat the rush.
The food comes out and is really yummy but for the larger entrees they actually do not seem that huge. For example the daeho kalbijim definitely way more worth it than this one. But still yummy!

Service was good. Overall great late night Korean spot here in the sunset. Enjoy!

Such a yummy Korean spot in the Sunset!
This places offers a variety of Korean food. From soups/stews, to bibimbaps, to delicious appetizers like the one we got which is their signature House wings!

They have new menu items that they just dropped which is the Matcha makgeoli, buldak omelette, tofu salad, and the watermelon hwachae. All perfect for this summer!

This is what we ordered:
- Buldak Omelette - This was such a cheesy goodness omg it was so good! They added the buldak ramyeon into an omelette and then added a bunch of cheese on top! I love that the cheese and egg slightly cuts the spicyness from the ramyeon~
- Matcha Makgeoli with honeycomb - What a fun way to drink makgeoli! I’m actually not someone who drinks alcohol but them adding matcha and honeycomb was just so intriguing! They cut up a slice of honey comb in front of you and add it to your cup, after mixing everything together you get that taste of rice wine & sweetness.
- Army Stew - Simple and delicious stew, full of ramyeon, spam, hot dog, tofu and cabbage. I got the mild and that was just right for me.
- Beef Bibimbap - This is perfect for two people to share if you’re ordering other items. This came out hot and sizzling. Mixing it all together was so beautiful to watch 😍😂
- The crew house garlic wings - We chose the garlic flavor. I love that their wings were flavorful but the garlic flavor wasn’t overpowering. It was slightly sticky as well from the sauce being glazed over the wing.

4dreams in the East Bay Area offers an incredible blend of Nepali and Indian cuisine, with each dish bursting with authentic flavors. The cozy atmosphere enhances the dining experience, making it perfect for gatherings. Definitely a must-visit for food lovers seeking something unique

WOW!  Just WOW!  We were in town for a show and this restaurant showed up with great reviews and seemed to offer some different options.  It was AWESOME.  I'm a little burnt out on curry because I've been cooking a lot myself lately and so decided to go with the Nepalese options.  Just wonderful. top_reviews.content: Located at the food court area at the Bay St. Plaza. They are very busy on a weekend with steady stream of people in and out. It’s not very big inside, so it can get a little crowded. Prices are not the cheapest for the amount of food you get, but every fast food restaurant has gotten more expensive and portions seem smaller now days. Overall, good tasting food. I wouldn’t eat here all the time, it’s nice to grab an occasional burger and shake here. There are better and healthier options to eat here in the plaza.

Order the food on the kiosk.. A double smash burger & cheesy fries & mango lemonade to drink.. Cost was around $20plus & parking wasn't free.. Let me start by saying Smash burger patty way too salty!!! Fries are way too salty!!! Mango lemonade way too sweet.. After a few bites I litterly couldn't handle the saltiness & I couldn't wash it down because the Mango lemonade was way too sweet!!!. If you don't mind salty French fries & Burgers & overly sweet lemonade its for you.. I went downstairs to buy Japanese sushi at Tokyo Central & sparkling peach water.. Never again would I go to Shake shack!!!

These burgers are delicious. Fresh tasting, light and juicy, served up hot as soon as they come off the grill. I think our bill was close to $40 for two single shack burgers, one onion ring, and two large diet sodas. Pretty pricey, but hey, this is California!

They brought the food out incredibly fast, and it was absolutely delicious! Ordering was a breeze — whether on the monitor, from my phone, or right at the counter. I loved how easy and convenient everything was! The staff was super friendly and made the whole experience even better. The place was clean, organized, and had a great vibe. I’ll definitely be coming back — highly recommended!

top_reviews.content: I finally gave it a shot and tried this place out via delivery after seeing it pop up many times on Doordash. They offer a wide variety of Chinese and Chinese American dishes, such as chow mein, fried rice, soup, appetizers entrees like orange chicken, salt and pepper chicken wings/salt and pepper pork chops, rice plates, combo meals and much more to choose from. Everything was made to order which is always a plus for me since it is quality over quantity and I never mind the wait since I am a very patient person. I hate to have to do this, I think their food is good, but food production seems to be poor since this is happening again.

Went in on a Saturday night! Partner and I got the orange chicken over rice and the green bean and chicken over rice. Food was piping, hot and fresh. not overly salted as well. There are indoor tables for seating.

top_reviews.content: Solid meal, everything we tried was pretty good, and I'm not a huge fan of Peruvian food. Some very good dishes (the beet salad and Aji de gallina were a hit, as were the ceviche and arroz con mariscos according to the rest of the table) along with some ok-ish dishes like the yuca, corn and lomo saltado. The vibe is torn between trying to be elevated dining and serving some options that you cannot possibly eat in an elegant way (trying to eat a corn rib with utensils ended up with one corn rib on the floor...). Feels like they're still figuring it out, but heading in the right direction.

Found this place while looking for a nicer brunch option near Haight-Ashbury, and the ambiance really delivers: modern but cozy design, and the outdoor yard seating was lovely. I can imagine it’s even better in the evening with the lights and bar vibe. Service was friendly and patient throughout, even though there was a bit of a language barrier.

Food was mostly very good: fish quality in the classic ceviche was very good, and the leche de tigre was good but could have more complexity and depth. My main gripe is the sweet potato on the ceviche, served in a few chunks instead of a purée, which would elevate the dish (especially at ~$30). The other dishes were tasty (eggs Benedict, stewed pork, stir-fried beef with onions and rice). Drinks were forgotten at first and arrived late, and the espresso came lukewarm in a cappuccino cup.

Very close to 5 stars with a bit more attention to the small details.

Really good, fresh and flavorful, creative food with beautiful presentation. Went with a friend to eat and we both enjoyed our meal. Had the micro seafood ceviche, beet salad and chocolate cake (Carlitos) - so yum! Awesome drinks like pisco sours, attentive service and upscale atmosphere. Nice and comfortable with booths. Would love to go back to check out patio when it’s warmer weather!

I went for Brunch on a Sunday around 12:30PM during SF restaurant week. The live music was so lovely! Our food came out fast & the dessert was tasty. Ours included a mimosa too. The server was attentive & everyone was kind! Will come back during dinner for a ceviche or lomo saltado.

We love this place. The quality of the food and service is simply the best. I can’t say enough about the food, it is Fantastic!
We like La Mar Cocina Peruana but Altamirano is right there, perhaps some entrees are even better.
My Wife and I had a wonderful time here. We highly recommend it!

top_reviews.content:
I want to preface this by saying I am NOT an expert on Indian food. I maybe get it once a year. I was looking for someplace open within walking distance and placed an order for takeout

The gentleman working there was very nice and helpful, the atmosphere was very friendly and inviting. The restaurant itself was very clean but homey. I thought the food was pretty good, I got chicken tikka masala with garlic naan and thought it was great, but I’m no expert.

Such a little gem in the Bernal Heights area. We love the bright colors outside and inside. Our server was very sweet. The food was delicious- not your standard Indian restaurant fare. It includes: a wonderful salad, naan, papadam. choice of rice and 2 curry dishes. The sauces for dipping were sensational- we especially loved (and devoured) the green curry (mint/cilantro).

Again I wish that Google would allow me to give out 1/2 stars as this place would get 4.5 stars all around.
So we have all been to either an Indian or Nepalese restaurant before, I assume, and we all know that feeling, the first few bites were very tasty and then I started to feel like a pregnant mountain duck... Well not here at 'little Nepal' .
Let me back up, I ate here just about 20 years ago for the first time.  No I have no recollection on how good the food was.  But it was the same location, same restaurant name and cuisine, that I know. 20 years fast forward, who knows how many changes in ownership and chefs I went back to try the place which opened just 5 weeks ago.
I love it , the food is light,  a great blend between Indian, Nepalese and some Californian.   The staff at first is a bit reserved and shy but opens up quickly as you talk to them.  We must have chatted with the head chef for almost an hour, going over recipes, up-bringing, mountain and restaurant names , it was a delight to say the least.
Now to the food. We worked ourselves through the menu.  Fig salad, mango chicken, coconut rice. Lemongrass chicken, curry salmon, naan... None of the dishes disappointed and we didn't feel stuffed or pregnant like a mountain duck.  I love this place and highly recommend it.  I will go back and it won't take me another 20 years.

What's rare is wonderful. And the food at this restaurant is wonderful.

We had butter chicken wings to start, they took a while to prepare but we're worth the wait. Really really tasty.

Then we had two orders of Chicken Tiki Masala. Delicious. One serving would have been enough. The sauce was not at all spicy which suited one of us. Next time I'd get mine a little spicy.

Two types of Naan Bread.

Reasonably priced and took home enough left overs for lunch tomorrow.

Food was amazing! Atomosphere was great! The seats are traditional Nepali type seats which reminded me of when I used to visit family back home. The sandwich came beautifully wrapped in paper (keeps it nice and warm!) and was perfectly constructed - a soft yet sturdy roll packed with thinly sliced, seasoned steak that was incredibly tender. $10 lunch special, a defiantly low price for San Francisco. I've gotten the pork buns here too, there isn't a single item on the menu that doesn't come at a great value. Bring cash, its possible to use card above ~15 I think but cash is king. This is a neighborhood fixture, not a tourist attraction. There is no seating, no bathroom, there is not even really an optimal place to stand or form a line, the service is not scripted, and the signage is office paper. This is not a streamlined, market-research driven customer experience. It is not a panda express. What It is, is simply a reflection of the locality it serves—a long-standing San Francisco neighborhood with a heavily Chinese heritage and enduring working class character. To eat here is to eat with the community, it's to sit at the table among neighbors and friends and share a meal. The value of the community is reflected in the value of the food, and the savings are passed on. Just a thought on what it means to have a good deal. It's not purely an economic benefit to the consumer, it often times betrays an investment into the community being served.

top_reviews.content: Good spot for a slice! The owner was really nice and even cut my slice into two pieces for me. The jalapeño poppers were solid, and they let you add any topping for 75¢. Only thing , the ranch was $1, which felt a little not friendly. But overall, a good find and worth stopping by.

We live nearby and I always take the 38 bus from the stop across the street on Geary, so we were delighted to find this local spot for pizza. The guys working when we picked up our pizza were super nice and friendly.

We got the:

Cranberry Arugula Salad
Seafood Special Pizza (regular crust)
Pesto Pizza (thick crust)
Geary St Pizza (thin crust)

The cranberry arugula salad was really refreshing, with cherry tomatoes, cherry tomatoes and feta. I just wish there were slightly more dried cranberries, but the salad was solid overall.

The Seafood Special Pizza was really delicious. They really went hard with the garlic (which I love) and shrimp, and the green onions added another layer of flavor.

The Geary St Pizza was my favorite overall. Again, super garlicky and salty (because of the cheese), in the best way possible, with the spinach providing a nice contrast to the garlic/cheeses.

The Pesto Pizza was the only one that fell short. It looked amazing and was laden with tomatoes, bell peppers, artichokes, red onions, and black olives, but was not as flavorful as we were hoping. The pesto was a bit milder than expected, and the fresh tomatoes/red onions made the pizza a little soggy (by the time we got home), because of all the excess moisture. In retrospect, that was our fault, as fresh veggies on pizza always creates more moisture than I am a fan of on a pizza.

Other than the Pesto Pizza, we really liked everything. It is really nice that they have three different crust options (thin, regular, thick) for customization. We will be back if we're looking for a quick bite of tasty pizza in the area!

When I tell you this is the BEST pizza I've ever had....!
It was made to absolute perfection!
Fresh, crisp veggies, beautiful crust,  DELICIOUS homemade sauce, tasty sausage and pepperoni...
I can't say enough! It was simply, THE BEST,  hands down.

The pizza and the salad I had were sooo good! I built my own pizza and chose the ingredients I wanted. And also had a green salad with cranberries, cheese and other veggies. Truly delicious.
I felt great right after dinner, it was the great way to end the day after a long day of walking.
The place is super clean, spotless! And people who work there are so kind! I felt welcomed and nourished. Thank you!

Jose' was so sweet and kind, made me feel welcomed and comfortable right away, and made me a couple delicious vegetarian slices. Heavy with fresh vegetables, made me feel like I was having a healthy dinner. Filling and delish. Thank you!

At first glance, Joe’s Coffee Shop doesn’t really look like a place you’d immediately walk into — it’s small, simple, and pretty unassuming from the outside. But that’s exactly what makes this family-owned spot so special. Once you step inside, it feels incredibly cozy, welcoming, and authentic.
We ended up having breakfast there twice during our stay because after our first visit, we already knew we wanted to come back the next morning. The food was delicious both times, freshly made, generous, and served with so much warmth and friendliness.
Places like this are what make a trip memorable. If you’re looking for a genuine, cozy breakfast spot in San Francisco, this is definitely one to visit.

Such a cute little diner. Barstools and two to four person tables. Got there at noon, could take a seat wherever, and from order in my food I was served 7 minutes later. My waffle with strawberries and whipped cream was delightful. Definition of a mom and pop joint - two up front, one cook in the back. There were some regulars who the owners knew and greeted by name - everyone was very friendly. If laid back classic American breakfast fare is your deal I would highly recommend.

A cute diner run by an older Chinese couple.  Feels like you’re kind of in their home and they just happen to be really good at making breakfast.  I think they do their eggs here perfectly; however you ask them, they’ll get it done just right.

Fantastic local spot! The owner is incredibly welcoming, and the food is both satisfying and affordable. It opens early, which is a huge plus. Remember to bring cash! Parking is easy most days, but grab a spot early on Saturdays.

Strawberry waffle literally tastes like a warm hug.

Got the eggs, bacon and waffle combo and added strawberries and whipped cream.
Really nice local place! Hidden gem in the city.

top_reviews.content:
I was so happy that my dinner reservations (for one) were accepted the same day! I was at the Golden Gate Bridge all day and walked over to the neighborhood location; what a great decision.

My mind was blown at how John was doing it all - getting the fresh fish from the market, prepping the food, cooking AND serving!

The food was impeccable. I have a small stomach, but I was gobbling and stuffing myself silly, because I just couldn't stop eating. My favorite was a Petrale Sole dish, with the aforementioned fresh fish! Soooo delicious and with such wonderful textures.

I also felt so blessed to get more than the dishes listed on the menu... there was also soup, mouth-watering bread, and a bonus dessert! That said, I would also say that either Google or the website didn't have the right price listed. However, WELL WORTH the price for the culinary experience!

There's some quirky decor, which amused me. Check out the apron displayed in the bathroom! It was the chef/owner's when he was a little boy! What fun.

All in all, I would definitely recommend that you consider giving this place a try!

What a great place, and why I have discovered it only now.  John is the most gracious host who made us feel extremely welcome and comfortable.  The whole place is very cozy.  It's like a private dining.  We were able to enjoy our food and talk as if we were the only people in the restaurant.  The food was also great.  I don't really like butternut squash soup, but I loved John's.  Halibut was very delicious that melted in your mouth.  The other dishes were also great and wonderfully presented.  Even the dinner rolls which they bake in the house, were also delicious.  I actually begged John, and he gave me some to take home.  I think the local patrons should chip in and buy this place a great espresso machine :).  That was the only thing missing for me in this dinner.

Had no idea what we were in for that night -- including the prix fix menu surprise. That said, our party of six had a fantastic dinner. Each course was delicious, and the chef would come out and explain them in detail. The restaurant is tiny, so make your reservations early, but the wine selection is extensive for such a small place. We didn't go with the pairing option, but next time I'd give it a try.

Exceptional food and outstanding service! From the moment we arrived, John, the owner of The Richmond, made us feel incredibly welcome. He was funny, attentive, and remarkably generous throughout the evening and surprised us with extra dinner rolls (soooooo good), treated us to an unexpected dessert, and frequently checked in to ensure we were enjoying everything (including offering wine refills and/or to sample different selections).

What truly set the experience apart was John's thoughtful approach to wine pairing. Rather than simply recommending wines that complemented each dish, he took the time to understand our personal preferences and tailored his choices accordingly. It was clear that he genuinely cared about creating the best possible dining experience and did so without being pretentious in the slightest which I appreciated.

The food itself was awesome and the portions were surprisingly generous for a fine dining restaurant. By the end of the meal, we were so full that we could barely finish the last few bites (unexpected coffee ice cream with almond brittle set us over the limit).

We will absolutely be returning and are already looking forward to seeing what appears on the menu next. That said, we sincerely hope the roasted duck never gets removed!

Note: give John a heads up if you have any food allergies!

The concept here is that the chef, John, and one waitress prepare all the food and service the tables in an intimate small space. The tasting menu is the only option! Every table has its own pocket, surrounded by curtains, to create a cozy private pocket. I loved the food, especially the ribeye. Two bonus courses. They easily accommodated a shellfish allergy, changing up one of the courses. Everything tasted fresh and was played beautifully. We also had good wine that was reasonably priced. Fantastic dining experience overall.

I can’t believe I have been living right across this restaurant for over a year and only now tried it. This unassuming restaurant is absolutely a hidden gem. I can’t wait to try all the dishes because so far, each one we have tried has been 10/10.
In terms of service, they go above and beyond. The portions are generous, packed with meats and vegetables for amazing prices. My husband is Taiwanese and he’s in love. It will be very hard to keep us away from here.

I’d always passed by this Chinese restaurant and finally decided to give it a try. When I walked in, I was greeted by a very kind older lady — she was super friendly and warm, really made me feel welcome. She even recommended a dish for me, and her kindness definitely stood out.
The place itself wasn’t great — the atmosphere was simple, and honestly, it wasn’t very clean, with a few flies around. But the food was surprisingly good, flavorful and well-cooked.
Overall, the food and her kindness were the highlights.

What Tai Chi lacks in atmosphere it makes up for in delicious, flavor packed Chinese food. My new favorite casual Chinese restaurant serving some American favorites like their Sesame Chicken and Mongolian Beef. Their soups are so comforting. You can’t go wrong. The only thing I’ve had here (so far) that was not memorable were the potstickers. If you are looking for easy and dependable Chinese food Tai Chi is the place.

I visited this quiet little spot for lunch and I really enjoyed the crab Rangoons and the Bbq pork buns. The Rangoons were sweet, creamy, and crunchy. The pork buns were fluffy like a cloud and meaty in the center.

Good Chinese Food and I would eat here again. However, I did think the bathroom was a little eh for a restaurant.
This place was so amazing! The lady who took our order was so sweet and her customer service was A1 . Food is AMAZING!! Will be back soon !

top_reviews.content:
What a great little find in Berkeley! Cali Alley is tucked away in an alley with a cool, laid-back atmosphere and some seriously good food.

We tried the Chef’s Burger, fried chicken sandwich, mac & cheese, and fries, and everything was fantastic. The Chef’s Burger was the standout for me. A juicy brisket burger piled high with hickory-smoked tri-tip, Swiss cheese, crispy onions, pepperoncini, and Thousand Island aioli. Definitely not your average burger! The combination of flavors and textures really worked. The fried chicken sandwich was crispy and flavorful, the mac & cheese was rich and creamy, and the fries were just as good.

What I really liked about Cali Alley is that they take familiar comfort food and give it their own creative twist without overcomplicating things. You can tell there’s some real thought and care behind the menu. The portions are generous, the ingredients taste fresh, and the whole place has a fun, unpretentious neighborhood feel.

Love discovering spots like this. We’ll definitely be back to explore more of the menu. Highly recommend!

Cali Alley is a fantastic spot that’s well worth checking out. One of the things I appreciated most is the variety on the menu—there are plenty of great choices for all tastes, including a solid selection of vegan and vegetarian options.

A couple of things to know before you go: there isn’t a restroom on-site. It’s not a deal breaker by any means, but it’s something to keep in mind. Also, our food took a little while to be prepared, but once it arrived, it was clear the wait was absolutely worth it.

The portions are generous—don’t be surprised if you’re taking home leftovers in a to-go box. Everything we ordered was packed with flavor and incredibly satisfying. The Chef Burger was so good it should honestly be called the “Chef’s Kiss Burger.” The Mac n Cheese is to die for, rich and comforting in all the right ways. And the Mint Limeade was the perfect refreshing complement to the meal—absolutely delicious.

Whether you choose to dine in or order delivery, you won’t be disappointed. Plus, you’re supporting a great small business that clearly takes pride in serving quality food. Highly recommended!

i’ve been going here for years! delicious food! they’ve expanded their menu a lot and i’m really enjoying it. they’ve got options for gluten free and vegetarian too. one of my favorite things about cali alley is that it’s outdoors and dog friendly. such a cute place. staff are very nice too.

i love their prawn bao buns. their mac and cheese and loco moco are also really tasty. eventually i’ll try everything on the menu!

I ordered the chicken and waffles with habanero salsa and it was exquisite. The food came out nice and hot (probably made to order by the sounds of the kitchen?) and was packed with flavor. Well seasoned, cooked beautifully, and not greasy at all. I'm excited to come back and try other offerings on their menu.

*Note that it's outdoor seating only

A cute little corner stop that's full of flavor, and you'd never guess it! This burger had it all, and then some. I'm talking about the chef's burger of course. House ranch also was a nice touch. We'll be back. Maybe tomorrow.

address: 1330 Park St, Alameda, CA 94501, United States

top_reviews.content:
Marley G’s Pizzeria was an okay experience, but it didn’t quite live up to the price or expectations.

The pizzas looked appealing, but the balance of ingredients was off. There was far too much tomato sauce and not nearly enough cheese, which left the pies tasting overly acidic. The mushrooms were surprisingly bland, and the arugula felt like an afterthought—it appeared to have simply been dumped on top after the pizza came out of the oven instead of being incorporated into the overall flavor.

The meatballs were also disappointing and didn’t taste like they were made in-house, lacking the freshness and flavor you’d expect from a pizzeria charging premium prices. Overall, the food felt overpriced for what was served.

The dining area could have used a bit more attention as well. A few tables hadn’t been fully cleaned despite the restaurant not appearing to be particularly busy.

Marley G’s isn’t a bad place, but with better ingredient balance, more attention to preparation, and improved cleanliness, it could be a much better value.

Good gawd, this is the best pizza I’ve ever had. Ordered the Sicilian, white, and pepperoni slice to try them all. When I warmed them in the microwave, they came out good like they were fresh unlike other places. The dough was still soft. I got the wings too, they were full of meat and flavor. So good!

This may seem like an odd review since we didn’t actually patronize this establishment, but being in the hospitality industry myself, I feel it us important to offer constructive criticism and fair reviews.

My family and I actually ordered food across the street at Scolari’s. They don’t have indoor seating. And seeing as it was a rainy day, he informed us that we could sit indoors at their sister location Marley G’s. He was so enthusiastic and friendly, we took him up on it.

We arrived to a near empty restaurant. We sat down, leaving our bag at the edge of the table, as it was admittedly awkward bringing outside food into a restaurant.

I hadn’t ordered a drink at Scolari’s, so I had hoped to minimize my awkwardness by ordering one here. However, no one from the establishment ever greeted us. They looked our way once or twice, but never spoke to us.

That made the experience even more awkward, so we ate quickly. My son needed to use the restroom, so I we dipped in there before leaving. It was clean and had a child changing station, which is always a plus. However, they were out of toilet seat covers and hand towels. I wanted to alert the staff, but the awkwardness was already overwhelming. As we left, a customer was just sitting down, having ordered an enormous slice of pizza. It smelled and looked delicious.

Perhaps this is a daily occurrence, with visitors eating burgers(delicious, btw!) from their sister restaurant from a rooms the street. But for us, it was out of the ordinary and as I stated, awkward.

We do want to return and try their pizza. And when we do, I’ll update this review with our experience. Fair is fair.

If you’re in Alameda and craving pizza without the commitment of a full pie, check out this classic spot. They keep it simple: Cheese, Pepperoni, and a standout White Pizza with Ricotta and Spinach. My personal favorite? Definitely the White Pizza.

The thin crust is a win, although the dough is pretty standard. What adds a unique touch is their buttermilk sauce – surprisingly good with pizza!

Service-wise, it’s efficient. Order at the counter, and they’ll heat up your slices in no time. Prices are fair, making it a good value for a quick bite.

The vibe is casual and unpretentious, much like a traditional pizza shop. Bonus: there’s a parking lot in the back, which is super convenient.

It may not be the best pizza you’ll ever have, but it’s consistently good and hits the spot when you’re nearby. A solid choice for a quick, satisfying slice.

top_reviews.content:
Stumbled upon this gem of a restaurant on a late weekend afternoon in SFO. Clean and fresh vibes, classy and soothing ambience.
Food was awesome - french crepe style dish, bruschetta and the pasta was to die for♥️
The way they play with different types of cheese is amazing. Ended with affogato and
L had a beautiful day.

MATTINA is a brilliant addition to the Fillmore district, offering a fashionable and stylish atmosphere that manages to feel both sophisticated and welcoming. The service is exceptional, warm, professional, and perfectly timed making it an ideal spot for everything from a quick coffee to a long, leisurely lunch. Speaking of lunch, their $26 Weekday Lunch Special is an absolute steal; getting a high quality, three course meal in such a chic setting is easily one of the best deals in San Francisco. The food is outstanding, featuring standout items from their wood fired pizza oven and incredibly fresh, handmade pastas like the rich mushroom truffle tagliatelle. Every detail is thoughtful, right down to the decadent homemade gelato that provides the perfect sweet finish. Whether you're there for the charcoal grilled specialties or the vibrant Cal Italian flavors, MATTINA delivers an impeccable 5-star experience that you'll want to return to again and again.

My husband and I hosted a post-baptism lunch at Mattina after the ceremony at St. Dominic's Church, and it was absolutely perfect.

From the very beginning, the experience was wonderful. We booked well in advance for a fairly large group (17 but we lost a few people day of so we were 13), and the manager was incredibly accommodating, kind, and easy to work with throughout the planning process. Organizing an event can be stressful, but they made everything seamless.

The location couldn't have been more convenient—just a short walk from St. Dominic's—which made it the perfect spot. The service was warm, attentive, and professional, and our guests felt genuinely well taken care of.

And the food... absolutely phenomenal. Every dish was fresh, beautifully prepared, and delicious. Everyone in our party commented on how fantastic the meal was.

Mattina helped make such a special family milestone even more memorable. I can't recommend them highly enough, and I can't wait to come back!

Overall pasta and tiramisu were amazing and felt worth it but would skip on the appetizers, which didn’t feel worth it.

Pasta had amazing texture and great flavors (usually I find pastas under flavored). Our group favorite was pappardelle, lamb cheek was so soft and had hint of sweetness. Tiramisu also one of the best (tho thicker texture than normal). While brussel sprouts and milk bread had good flavor, the texture was a bit hard and didn’t feel worth the price

This place is so lovely, quiet and a hidden gem. The coffee is fantastic and the food is all so tasty, not overpowering and classy. Today they accommodated our gluten free requests so thoughtfully and patiently. Our waitress was Alex (maybe? Short blonde hair) - she was fantastic! Her service was impeccable!

top_reviews.content:
I had a great experience at House of Sushi on Polk Street. It’s a true hole-in-the-wall spot with a cozy, welcoming atmosphere and limited seating. There was no wait when I arrived, but I can definitely see it getting busy quickly.

I ordered the House Roll, Dragon Roll, Spicy Tuna Roll, Super California Roll, and tuna and salmon nigiri. Everything was fresh and well-prepared, but the Dragon Roll and salmon nigiri really stood out. The service was great from start to finish, and the prices were very reasonable.

Attempted to call restaurant but phone number is deactivated.

We found plastic in our sushi. Requesting a refund. Feeling incredibly worried because we are not sure if we ate plastic. Ordered one dragon roll and one Philadelphia roll. Pretty upset with the quality as we did wait outside for take out pretty long (~35 minutes).

We popped in here after yoga on a random Monday night and it was the best decision ever. Sat at the sushi bar and got the Rainbow Roll, Spicy Tuna and some nigiri and everything was melt in your mouth delicious. Could not recommend enough, and great date spot if you’re looking for affordable sushi and good vibes. Can’t wait to come back

We were in the area and saw this place- had a good feeling about it. Had to wait 30 minutes for them to open. It was worth the wait. Everything was delicious. Dragon roll and chicken teriyaki were out of this world.

Quaint little place, the takoyaki was good, but the sushi is too large imo. They'd be better off cutting it into smaller pieces which would give the illusion of more sushi and would be much more manageable to eat. I would rate it 3.5/5.

reviews_snippets.content: "Excellent food, nice cozy restaurant serving fresh fish with good sake options."

top_reviews.content: A family friend invited me there and said, “it will be the best meal of your life”. I thought he was joking. He wasn’t. He had ordered lamb shank for us. Apparently you have to order in advance as it takes a few hours to prepare. It was truly incredible. I have lived inManhattan for a few decades and have eaten in top Michelin starred restaurants as well as hole in the wall Pakistani/Indian joints. This lamb shank was heavenly. Only thing i would change is to add option of byob. Would be awesome to be able to bring your wine to dinner here

Warm plates, warm food, warm people
Complimentary chicken hot and sour soup, complimentary tea.

Very tasty and fresh food, this restaurant does not use any frozen ingredient.

Very reasonable priced with most dishes being in $14-$20 range, given that the soup is complimentary as well as the tea, incredible value and taste at $14-$20.

The food service is quick, clean and warm - they even have a warm plate, in winter this is such a nice touch to get food in a warm plate.

The ambiance is cozy, warm home-like, clean and professional.

Very polite staff and owners.

Love that they have a balanced mix of vegetarian and meat-based dishes.

5/5
Really nice mural on the walls, good ventilation, complimentary chai & water, nice staff, the BEST NAAN I HAVE EVER HAD, and great chill music

There are very few restaurants where I find myself venture back to the very next day after trying it for the first time, but Vegan N’ Chicken had me hooked after my first bite.

I was looking for a simple comfort meal after a long day and decided to try a place. It was around 8:30 and most places in the area were closing at 9 but Vegan N’ Chicken happened to be open until 10pm!

When I walked in, I immediately was welcomed with ‘mom and pop’ restaurant vibes. It is a very casual and fairly small restaurant, but it makes for a very comforting experience. You get to seat yourself then they’ll bring you a menu. The menu is simple, but also has everything you’d need. They even have a few seafood dishes! While you wait for your food, you can help yourself to their complimentary soup & hot chai. I’ll admit I have no clue what the soup is, but it is such a great way to start the meal. Especially with some hot chai too!

On day 1 we ordered Lamb Tikka Masala ($14.99), Chana Masala ($9.99), Cheese Naan ($3.99), Rice ($2.99), and Vegetable Samosas ($4.99). The servings were very generous for the price compared to other similar restaurants in Berkeley. We did ask for medium spice level, but it wasn’t spicy enough for us so they brought us a plate of onions, peppers, and cucumbers! The Chana Masala was my favorite bite of the night. It was packed with fragrant spices & the garbanzo beans were so tender. The Lamb Tikka Masala was a little bit sweeter than I am used to, but after mixing in some rice or eating it with the cheese naan it was perfect.

On day 2, we ordered the Papadum ($2.99), Rice ($2.99), Prawn Vindaloo ($17.99), and Chana Masala ($9.99 - we added paneer to it and didn’t confirm how much it was with the paneer). This time we ordered our dishes spicy to see if it was any different. It really was still not spicy at all, but honestly it didn’t bother us. It was a great way to be able to enjoy the dishes in their entirety. The prawns in the vindaloo were fairly large and the portion was perfect for two people! They were also not overcooked & still had a nice bounce when biting into it. The Chana masala with the added paneer was a great combination as well.

Vegan N’ Chicken is honestly a great spot for the college students nearby as well. It’s affordable & could easily be split into two meals even if you just order one dish!

Next time we stop by, we’re going for the biryani!

Discovered the best Indian/Pakistani restaurant in the Berkeley area, and I couldn’t be more impressed. The restaurant was neat and clean, and the owner was incredibly professional and welcoming. He took the time to go over the menu with us and highlight some standout dishes. Our group of six ordered a variety of items, and every single dish was fantastic, with the Gobi Gosht being a particular highlight. You could tell that everything was made with fresh, high quality ingredients, which made a big difference in the flavor. The food was delicious, and the service was outstanding. I’ll definitely be returning for both the amazing food and excellent service. Five stars!

reviews_snippets.content: "Delicious food with great vegan options, good service, and welcoming atmosphere."
"Amazing food, really good price for the quantity and very friendly staff!"

top_reviews.content:
Mediocre kbbq spot in inner Richmond. As an avid Korean cuisine foodie, quality was basic for what it was.

Their interior was very poorly maintained, the uncomfortable metal stools with no backing were dirty, tables and floors were slippery with grease.

Service was spotty, we had to ask multiple waiters to refill our dipping sauces.

One plus side was the variety of side dishes, they had many sides that were decent enough for kbbq.

We ordered a bucket of alcohol as advertised in their menu and the drink came not looking like the menu photo at all. This bucket was almost $30 so we were quite annoyed it did not look like the very aesthetic photo they had on their drink menu.

All in all, not worth the very expensive price tag for what it was.

All you can eat Korean BBQ.  You cook you own meats and veggies!  Their selection of veggies and meats is not as big as other places I've been, but that's ok.  They also don't give you banchan unless you order it.  We had spicy pork belly,  beef belly,  two orders of beef brisket, zucchini, onion, cheesy corn, and two orders or rice.  The service was great.  The only thing to be aware of is that the flooring is a little slick from all of the grease, otherwise a great place to eat.

We aren't local but wanted Korean BBQ so we decided to give this place a try. It did not disappoint! Food is amazing and despite being packed their service was so fast. They changed our grill out without even having to ask and being able to order items on your phone was so convenient. I highly recommend trying the miso pork belly and the Thai BBQ pork as well as the go to staples of bulgogi and kalbi (marinated) ribs. Even the kimchi was great. For all you can eat BBQ the price is worth the experience! Will definately stop by again next time we are in S.F.

I'm very disappointment regarding the service at this restaurant. While the food quality was good, the unattentive behavior of your staff completely ruined our dining experience.
We repeatedly requested a grill change that never came. After 15 minutes of waiting, we had to personally approach the staff, who responded with visible attitude and disdain. Furthermore, our order was constantly managed poorly, several items never arrived, requiring us to input additional orders to make up for the missing food.
Most concerning was the lack of customer service we experienced. The staff made us feel entirely unwelcome, treating us with a palpable coldness that other tables did not receive. Our server explicitly ignored our burnt grill multiple times while actively taking care of surrounding guests. This severe lack of fundamental customer service skills is unacceptable. I hope management addresses this behavior.

Zajang Grill on Clement is honestly one of my new favorite spots. Their food is so good — every single item on the menu hits. The sauces are on another level, especially their ranch sauce and the corn cheese… unreal. You can tell they put a lot of care into their flavors because everything tastes fresh and well-seasoned.

The employees here are super attentive and friendly too. They check in just the right amount and make sure you have everything you need without you even asking. Overall, amazing food, amazing service — definitely a place I’ll keep coming back to!

top_reviews.content:
We made a reservation to celebrate a birthday and seated right away.
Cons:
-price... for the amount of food and taste it was pretty expensive. Spent about $250 for 4 people and my husband definitely could have eaten more.
-ambiance... Got a little loud and hard to hear each other without talking really loudly.
Pros:
-service was great, but I would suggest coming early as when it got busy it was harder to get the attention of the servers
-out of all the rolls we had maybe half were worth ordering again.
-would be odd to come here and "share" unless you are really close with your table mates.
Would we come back? Possibly... Especially now that we know what to order.

I’ve been here like 4 times in as many weeks. The hand rolls are so fresh, flavorful, and interesting. I love coming for lunch. The staff is very kind and service is great. Highly recommend the black cod with truffle butter and seared albacore with garlic aioli!

I had a reservation for one and was seated at the hightop window corner. The website stated they were booked up, but I was able to call and get a seat. It's an intimate cozy place. My server was attentive and kind, and my favorite item ended up being her recommendation, the negihama (yellowtail & green onion) The rest of the rolls were just okay. The scallop and shiso leaf roll was decent. Salmon belly/yuzu/truffle salt and spicy tuna tempura roll weren't bad, but weren't memorable. I got about 4 rolls and a drink for about $50 and left satisfied, but not overly full.

Restrooms are attached to the ramen restaurant next door.

This was a surprise dinner my friend invited me on. The hand rolls are so fresh and delicious. I had 5 amazing rolls that come out one at a time for freshness m. The server was super sweat and helped me pick out what I wanted. The menu does also have set options, but I decided to do individual rolls. I definitely recommend stopping by if you’re in the Oakland area.

Had the baller set and loved it. They were so generous with the tuna caviar and uni hand rolls (unlike other hand roll bars). The price is so much better than similar hand roll bars in sf. Will be coming back!
