top_reviews.content:
Really loved the cucumber lemonade and tacos we got. We wandered in after an event near Union square and we’ll be back again.

My husband tried 3 meat tacos- the Al Pastor was his favorite. I had the tacos as well but I got a shrimp, a nopales, and a coliflor. Loved all 3- the shrimp was my favor- so tasty, and the nopales was surprisingly good. (Nopales sometimes are not well seasoned but here they were great). The tacos were a bit oily. I might ask for light oil next time.

I asked about the agua fresca to confirm that it was just fruit and sugar- no mix, and they confirmed so I picked the cucumber lemonade. It was delicious. They also had hibiscus and strawberry horchata.

We also ordered the chips and salsa. The chips were warm and we enjoyed them while we waited for our tacos. The salsa was delicious.

The staff was friendly, efficient and seamed relaxed creating a nice vibe. The prices were good and I like that you could pop in for a quick snack of a taco if you just need a small bite.

My only complaint was that we had so many little plastic salsa containers to throw away, but this seems to be somewhat normal now days. Would be great to minimize the single use plastic if possible, especially for those dining in.

Wanted some tacos in SanFran, and I got them when I randomly stopped in to this location.
Menu takes a moment to absorb, esp. if you haven't been here before.
Ordering was simple, and staff was friendly and kept location clean. There was a decent amount of people eating here on a Sat
Tacos tasted really good and were filling and had unique flavors, so I felt I got what I wanted and my money's worth.
For sure stop in if you've got a hankerin' for tacos and want a good meal.

This place was one of the best Mexican food places I have eaten. We shared a burrito bowl that had flavored chicken, lettuce, cilantro, black beans, rice, and a red sauce.  Please give them a try. You won’t be disappointed.

When I first had Pastor Papi food truck at the table tops in the Presidio, it was a 10/10 pastor burrito. Piping hot, flavorful including pineapple bits, cheesey, balanced, a next level burrito.  So, my expectations were set but not met at his brick and mortar location.  The pastor burrito was just alright, nothing to tell others about.  Lacked much if not everything from his truck burritos.

Being a pastor connoisseur makes me a little  biased but they put some serious effort and the tacos were really good. I only had pastor, tacos without pineapple (personal preference). They use double tortilla and they give you so much meat on each taco that you can use the extra tortillas to make tacos from the fallout pastor. Worth the drive to such busy part of town. I try to hit them every time I’m in SF.

top_reviews.content: This place decor was so beautiful. The hanging plants 🪴 were a nice touch. I got here the Fried Calamari, Fried Shrimp, Chai Thai rice, and Fried Chicken wings. Also, the pad pid pao (chili bamboo), Gang ga Ree (yellow curry ) 🍛. You must give them a try. Everything was delicious 😋 & amazing customer service.

This restaurant has been on my want to go list, so I was excited to try it out!

We ordered the Pad Kee Mao (drunken noodles) and the Gang Khew-Wan (Green Curry).

The Pad Kee Mao was tasty, the flavor leaned slightly toward to a sweeter, tomato flavor side, but it was still enjoyable.

The Green curry came with generous portion and was really flavorful. I especially really liked the eggplants, the texture was great and the seasoning was on spot!

This place is phenomenal!! Best Thai in Berkeley. I chose this place because the atmosphere was warm and inviting, and beautiful, without being stuffy. I wasn’t disappointed! The food was delicious, and portions are HUGE! You absolutely get an amazing meal for a great price, and our server Theresa was so sweet and patient. I would come back to Berkeley JUST for a hot meal from here. 10/10

Food was delicious! Ordered the vegetable egg rolls, Khaknom Jin Nam Ngaio, and Pad See Yew. It was all so tasty, and there was a spice rack to kick it up. I think I would skip the egg rolls next time, in favor of trying a salad or another entree. Looking. forward to going back and trying to catch the Lunch specials!

I ordered food from this place twice. The first time, I ordered tom yum noodle soup, and it was incredibly sweet. I’ve never had tom yum soup with such a sweet flavor. The second time, I ordered the Thai noodles, which were also sweet but lacked any other distinct flavors.

I've enjoyed a few meals here and I've found their food to be delicious, flavorful, and affordable. Serving size is perfect for me. The garlic & butter pasta was very good and the steak I had last week was cooked as requested and I left nothing to take home to Buddy (poor pup). Add a cold brew and don't forget to tip!

This is the best of the best customer service you with get in the Bay hands down! Wanessa and Thais the owners are so friendly helping us host a party here! By the way they have an amazing patio upstairs with a whole restroom as well! Best Quattro Formaggio pizza I’ve had in SF for sure! We ate so much everything was a hit! Sweet Serrano, Calabresa, Frango com Catupiry, try everything! Make sure to check it out!

I had such a wonderful experience at Bernal Heights! The atmosphere is warm and inviting, perfect for enjoying a meal with friends or family. The food was absolutely impeccable – every bite was full of flavor and clearly made with care. On top of that, the service was outstanding; the staff was attentive, friendly, and made us feel truly welcome. Definitely a place I’ll be coming back to again and again!

The food here is just incredible!
We had so many delicious appetizers!!!
The Brazilian options are a must-try, and the pizza is to die for, I highly recommend the calabresa one!

Had to go back for brunch and was sooo impressed! It’s a must!

Also the people couldn’t be nicer; you always feel welcome the moment you walk in.
I’ll definitely keep coming back again and again! 🍕❤️

top_reviews.content: I’ll be dreaming about this sandwich for a while… I got the chicken sandwich and it was AMAZING! I sat in the corner and they have these cute bread pillows. The sandwich was a lot more food than it looked, I ended up saving the other half and they wrapped it up for me to go. The owner / employees are super nice and down to earth. 10/10 recommend.

We ordered the Q's Benedict Sandwich (fka Q's Special) and it was amazing. The ciabatta was baked perfectly, nice crust with a soft bite. Bits of cooked bacon instead of the strip made for great texture. Eggs were perfect and it was the right size to split between my wife and I. We also shared the Morning Boost smoothie and it was so delicious. Perfectly balanced and not too sweet.

Q’s is a go-to spot for my husband and I. The food is amazing. I get the chicken sandwich every time and all of the ingredients are so fresh and delicious. The service is also unbeatable. After being there only twice a few weeks apart, the owner recognized me, told me it was nice to see me again, and even remembered my exact order. Customer service like that is hard to come by these days. Go to Q’s — you won’t regret it!
10 out of 10! Absolutely delicious! Made fresh and seasoned perfectly! I got the Cubano! People working there are very pleasant and giving! - signed, a tourist visiting from Colorado

I can’t say enough positive things about Q’s Sandwich Shop. Beyond making incredible sandwiches (my favorite is definitely the turkey pesto, but I’ve learned you can’t go wrong and they are happy to make recommendations!), they offer wonderful service - the owner will always greet you with a smile, knows his regulars, and makes sure to pay every person who comes by special attention. This place should be on the SF best sandwich list radar - no question. They are also always innovating - trying out new sandwich ideas and new sides, so every time you go back, you can discover something new!

Admittedly, I’ve been coming here for years, but I always eat my sandwiches so quickly that I forget to take a picture…
Love this place.

address: 2170 Mission St, San Francisco, CA 94110, United States

top_reviews.content:
We started with the Luo Buo Gao (turnip cake) chop salad and the shoyu ogo pickles. The crispy turnip cake was the standout here. Honestly, crispy turnip cake in a salad should replace croutons everywhere. It adds so much more texture and flavor.

For the mains, we ordered the pork cutlet sando, ginger scallion cheese bread, and crispy pork belly. While everything was solid, the crispy pork belly easily stole the show. Whatever seasoning they used on the skin was absolutely addictive. It had the perfect crunch and kept me going back for another bite.

To finish, we shared the breakfast sundae, which was a fun and creative dessert that fit perfectly with the restaurant’s playful approach to familiar flavors.

Overall, Piglet & Co. is worth visiting for its unique takes on classic dishes and creative Taiwanese-inspired menu. My only gripe is the price point relative to the portion sizes. The food is delicious, but you may find yourself wishing there was just a little more on the plate.

Unique and well-prepared Taiwanese small plate menu, reminiscent of dim sum meets upscale Polynesian tiki. Ambiance is richly colored, dimly lit setting — reds, charcoal and cherry wood finishes.

* Honey Walnut Shrimp & Pork Toast, near life-changing — a perfectly light crisp, well-balanced sweet-to-savory.

* Szechuan Honey Chicken Wings, an all-around crowd-pleaser — maintaining a perfect balance of subtle mala tingly.

* Chao Shao Pork Belly Ssam, an excellent Korean-Chinese fusion complete with fragrant perilla / red leaf lettuce wraps.

* Mala BBQ Pork Ribs, are fall-off-the-bone tender, a true lip-smacking, finger-licker.

Easily on the list of Top 10 Modern Asian restaurants in SF.  Every item tried was beyond enjoyable, causing moments to pause and simply savor in silence.

Perfect for an intimate date or business meeting.

Pretty mediocre experience, menu has pork cooked in many different ways, but lack vegetable selection making the whole meal very heavy. Meat in the donburi is quite hard to chew, pork ribs tastes sour and salty (in a bad way).
The pork and shrimp toast was pretty good, maybe a bit too sweet.
Went on a work day dinner and the restaurant was pretty empty.
Fantastic modern Taiwanese cuisine! My boyfriend loved the tasting menu, and the staff made a vegetarian version for me and accommodated my other dietary preferences. We’ll definitely be back!

Came here for a weeknight dinner with a friend after work and was able to make a same-day reservation online for 2 at the bar. Glad we made a reservation - while it was fairly empty when we first arrived, it soon filled up and the place was bustling with a full dining room! Staff was so friendly and highly attentive. This was our first time at this restaurant and they walked us through the menu and recommended dishes to us. Everything was SO. DELICIOUS! We highly recommend Piglet & Co!!! Here's what we ordered:
- Honey Walnut Shrimp & Pork Toast (our favorite)
- Mushroom Party (my second favorite!)
- Szechuan Honey Chicken Wings
- side of Furikake Rice
- Pickle Party (we couldn't decide which pickles to try...so why not all of them)
- Dessert was soooo good and I think called "Donut Sundae" or something like that...it was like a sweet donut bread with a floral/citrus yuzu kind of ice cream...regardless, I'm glad we ordered it!!

top_reviews.content:
I recently visited La Société Bar & Café and had a wonderful experience. The venue offers a sophisticated yet welcoming atmosphere, making it an excellent place for everything from a casual coffee to an evening meal with friends. The staff was attentive, friendly, and professional, creating a positive impression from the moment I arrived.

The food and drinks were beautifully presented and prepared with high-quality ingredients. The menu offers a good variety of options, including selections that can accommodate different dietary preferences. Everything was fresh, flavorful, and served promptly, reflecting the attention to detail that sets this place apart.

The café was clean, stylish, and well maintained, providing a comfortable environment to relax and enjoy the experience. Combined with the excellent service and inviting ambiance, the overall visit exceeded expectations. I would gladly return and highly recommend La Société Bar & Café to anyone looking for great food, quality drinks, and outstanding hospitality.
The Bar and Cafe located in the SF Hyatt,  hosted LE PETIT CHEF 4 corse meal food experience.   It was entertaining and the food was equally delicious!  Im thinking of going again round the holidays.

We came in at exactly 5PM when the restaurant opened.  Our sever Roger gave us a very detailed description of the menu.  We decided to order the the salad, steak with fries and dessert from the pre fixed menu.  Additionally, we also ordered the Berkshire pork chop.  Desserts came after the entree.  The food was amazingly delicious and beautifully presented.

I can only speak of the dinner here, as I haven't tried the breakfast. The food I tried was all pretty mediocre, at best. The cod was incredibly fishy, and the flavor took over the entire dish (the beans were ok, could not really taste any tomato which is a shame since they're in season). I requested a medium rare steak, and got a medium with incredibly dry (even burnt) edges. The frites were good, as were the deviled ouefs (we tried one with caviar and one without). We also tried their zero proof cocktails and found them underwhelming as well. Can't say this place is worth the price for me.

Food and service were incredible! I have tried almost every French bistro in SF as it is my favorite cuisine and almost everywhere has disappointed compared to French bistros I've tried elsewhere. I can barely get a decent cup of French Onion Soup in the city.

When La Societe opened I had to try it and I was not disappointed. Everything was flavorful and cooked to perfection. The French onion soup came with a bone marrow which was so unique (I love bone marrow!) And the meats were cooked to a juicy tender temperature.

The service was impeccable. Plates were taken away when empty. Water cups were filled when empty. But it never felt like they were hovering. Just very attentive.

Only stopped by this place for a quick drink, but it definitely left a great impression. Looking forward to coming back and trying more from the menu next time. The drink menu features plenty of options including those from Japan.

The edamame ended up being the highlight of our visit, which was done really well!

Service was great throughout, and we really enjoyed the overall vibe of the place. It had a relaxed atmosphere that made it easy to settle in, even for a short stop.

Would definitely return and recommend checking it out!

The skewer flavor is mostly subtle but some like the wagyu have a unique twist added. Chicken skewer is lean and more burnt than I would like. Skewers are fairly expensive and can leave one wanting for more.

Absolutely amazing. Mango salad was the best thing we ordered. Food was delivered fast and our waitress was very kind and helpful.

What an amazing place for sushi. I was town and a local suggested this place an I was not let down. I started with the spicy garlic edemame which he's a great kick of spice. I them had akani red tuma dashing and a flame roll. The sushi was perfect and the spice of the flame roll was squelch with my Nigerian sake! I could eat at the this place daily.

top_reviews.content: Great little spot if you're looking for something more casual than Belotti in Rockridge but with the same excellent taste and high quality! We stopped by Belotti Bottega to look at their fresh pastas and authentic italian offerings. To our delight, we discovered they also prepare warm meals on-site, so we decided to stay and enjoy the experience. We ordered a couple of pasta dishes along with drinks and settled into their outdoor seating on a cool yet sunny winter afternoon.

The service was exceptionally friendly and welcoming, making us feel right at home. The food? Absolutely authentic and rich in flavor. We tried the Agnolotti di Lidia and Casoncelli Bergamaschi, and both were outstanding. The pork shoulder and prosciutto in the Casoncelli were especially delicious, while the beef shank-stuffed pasta of the Agnolotti di Lidia left us with clean plates all around.

Belotti Bottega is a gem for anyone craving genuine Italian flavors paired with warm hospitality. Highly recommended for a cozy yet elevated dining experience.

Hands down the best fresh pasta in the East Bay! The quality is incredible, and I love that you can either grab uncooked noodles to make at home or stay for a quick, delicious meal. The staff is also incredibly welcoming and helpful. You have to try the Pappardelle with mushroom and beef reduction, it’s absolutely divine!

Absolute best handmade pasta far and wide, and I’ve had my share of of pastas across Italy. The agnolotti is out of this world good; not something you’re just finding anywhere.

The sidewalk vibes are perfect and easygoing if you dine in, and taking home a package of pasta to cook at home makes for the perfect date night! I’m thrilled to hear another Oakland location is coming!

top_reviews.content: The Monk’s Kettle is my new favorite restaurant in Oakland. This is definitely a hidden gem, and a MUST. We came here to eat the Lamb Shank we once tried and that stuck in our memory forever. And yesterday we realized it was even better than we could remember. The lamb shank was so tender that it could separate from the bone effortless, we did even need to chew it. It was laid on a bed of marinated pickles (pickles with pickled onion or shallots, and black and green olives), and feta cheese with a vinaigrette. On top of the lamb, a tasteful meat Demi-glaze that went along with the vinaigrette and the pickles exquisitely. The demi- glaze is to drink it on its own. It’s simply a genius combination: the acidity of the pickled veggies pairs so good with the fat on the lamb, it helps you clean your palate from the small amount of fat left in the lamb, just genius. But that was not the only good thing in the menu: the mac & cheese was the best we’ve ever tried, and the steak frites was cooked to perfection: pink in the inside, and with a little crust on the outside, simply perfect. The beer selection was also extensive, and the menu included the explanation of every type of beer they have . We will be back soon for sure. In my top list of restaurants in the area.

Unsuspecting from the outside but full of charm inside.

From the old wood bar/tables to the glasses behind the bar, you'll feel welcome.

They have cute kettles sprinkles throughout.

Seating is first come.

Did I mention they have a lot of veggie options and piny the elder on tap?

Server was patient with our group of 5.

Recommend for a spot with brews n food.

What?
Go to Oakland, to a gastro pub, for a lunch with an old friend?
YES - go here, it's fantastic.
1. Parking. Noon on a Thursday afternoon I lucked out and parked on College Ave., just 50 feet from the front door.
2. Service. Greeted as I walked in by a friendly staff person (who was also our waitperson). She was knowledgeable and patient and took our order (2 to stay, and 1 to go) by memory and got it all correct.
3. Food. My buddy and I got the same thing: Pub burger (medium) on brioche bun with gruyere cheese and grilled onions along with a side of kale salad (also could have had chips or fries). Excellent burger although I removed the top bun and ate the burger with a knife and fork. The shocker was the kale salad - no stems, mixed with root vegetables, and dressed with an interesting umami-ish vinaigrette: fantastic. So good, a ordered a full size kale salad to go for dinner later.
4. Dessert. Out of curiosity, I asked for a black coffee, and "do you have any cookies?" thinking maybe some big Costco oatmeal monsters. But, no - they have an in-house cookie plate (a long wooden cutting board with three hand-made cookies: gingerbread chocolate chip, light lemon bar, and a snicker doodle. Hand made by a staff person off premises - wow, really good, fresh, and perfect with robust black coffee.
My buddy and I had a beautiful lunch and sat for awhile talking and enjoying an Arnold Palmer, a black coffee, and cookies - a great mid-day break.
5. Summary: I haven't been to Oakland since the the G.S. Warriors left, but Monk's Kettle is a perfect reason to go back.

Legend has it that the carved wood encasing the shelves behind the bar once framed a (pretty spectacular) fireplace.

A remarkably dynamic selection of beers, foreign and domestic, are served in complementary glassware.  If you enjoy your beer as much as I do, you'll appreciate this level of, well...  appreciation.  🤔

I think none of the dishes were mind-blowing, but just exactly what you'd expect, done right. I'd come again!

This place is my go-to spot whenever my sister stops by my work since it’s so close to the area. The service was pretty good, and the portions were generous, each order could easily be shared by two people. Since my sister and I like trying different dishes, we decided to order three items.

First, we got the Soy Garlic Ollei Chicken Wings. They were flavorful, crispy, and perfectly coated with sauce. Next was the Beef Bibimbap. The beef was well-marinated, and it came with a good amount of veggies and rice, making it a really satisfying and well-balanced dish.

Lastly and definitely the star of our lunch was the Creamy Ttok & Pasta. We originally expected something like a regular creamy carbonara, but we were pleasantly surprised! It was incredibly creamy with a nice kick of spice without being too overwhelming, and it had a delicious drizzle of bacon on top that made it even better!

I would absolutely order the Creamy Ttok & Pasta again, and honestly, I’d recommend trying all three dishes. Everything we had was delicious!

Ollei is a fantastic neighborhood find that brings a warm, welcoming vibe and top tier Korean comfort food to the bustling Russian Hill area. The atmosphere is cozy and character filled, making it a perfect spot for everything from a casual dinner to a late night craving. The service is consistently praised for being friendly and attentive, with thoughtful touches like hand drawn happy faces on takeout orders that show they truly care about their guests. The menu is packed with standouts: the Army Stew (Budae Jjigae) and Seafood Pancakes are absolute must orders for their rich flavors and generous portions, while the Soft Tofu Soup and Bulgogi consistently hit the mark for quality and authenticity. Don't miss the Ollei Chicken Wings perfectly crunchy and available with a delicious soy garlic or spicy glaze or the inventive Creamy Ttok & Pasta for a unique fusion twist. top_reviews.content:
Milos Taverna is the best Greek restaurant in the city. I’ve previously said this about their sister restaurant, Milos Meze, and to be honest, the food here is just as amazing; but Milos Taverna has a nicer ambiance. It’s spacious, especially for a spot in the Marina. There’s plenty of room between tables so you can actually hear your guests comfortably. The chairs are cozy, and the general vibe is fantastic. Tonight I came in with my mom and sister because I knew it’d be a hit, but I’ll definitely be back for date nights and nights out with friends. The service really matches the great vibe, too; the staff was fast and incredibly attentive, constantly keeping our table clear of empty plates and making sure our water glasses stayed full all night.

Pro-tip: Don’t fill up on the delicious pita bread, and ask for extra tzatziki. The tzatziki is made in-house, super fresh, and lightly drizzled with authentic Greek kalamata olive oil.
We started by sharing the saganaki (flaming cheese) and dolmades (stuffed grape leaves), and both appetizers were best-in-class. The saganaki comes with the spectacle of a mini fire show. It’s so exciting to watch the staff walk out with swagger, pour the ouzo, and light it up. The cheese was crispy on the outside but creamy on the inside; perfect with the pita bread and a dab of tzatziki. This is a must-order if it’s your first time here. The dolmades were exactly as they should be: very large, made with fresh leaves, and neither too vinegary nor soggy. They come in a set of three per serving.

For the next course, we chose the horiatiki salad, which featured a beautiful mix of fresh tomatoes (cherry, heirloom, etc.), bell peppers, and a generous block of feta. It was incredibly crisp and bright, serving as a perfect, refreshing palate cleanser to prep us for the heavy main course.

For our entrée, we ordered the lamb shank with orzo and a side of potatoes. The lamb was so well prepared it literally fell off the bone. The meat melted in my mouth, and combining a bite of that with a forkful of orzo rounded out the meal perfectly.
To bookend the night, we had baklava and revani. The baklava was super flaky, drizzled with honey, and exceptional. The revani was something entirely new to me. I was so full I could only muster one bite, but that decadent slice of creamy citrus was the best final bite I could’ve taken.

By the end of the night, we had plenty of leftovers for lunch the next day. We all brought an appetite, but sharing this feast between the three of us still wasn’t enough to finish it all. This place is an absolute treasure. It’s the best meal you can have in the Marina, and the best Greek food in the entirety of the Bay.

I briefly considered the Classic Szechuan Spicy Soup… then chose self-preservation and left that level of bravery to the spice pros.

Perfect for a cozy, build-your-own situation when you want something warm, customizable, and very satisfying.

I really enjoyed the food, I got a spicy Sichuan base with some vegetables, rice noodles, ramen, and sliced pork. At first the only
"complaint" I initially had was being so full from eating some healing food. But the thing that makes this a 1 star review is that | got sick right after. Not the usual sickness from spice, but a really terrible sickness where I was feeling all the symptoms of a quote on quote food poisoning. I should've known the signs from the meat being displayed with the lack of refrigeration. Choose at your own risk!

If you’re craving authentic Chinese malatang, this is the place to go!
The broth is rich, flavorful, and perfectly balanced ，spicy but not overwhelming. Every ingredient tastes fresh, from the vegetables to the meats and seafood. I would Highly recommend if you want real flavor and real comfort food!

This is hands down my favorite spot for Malatang in San Francisco. They’ve got tons of options, and the broth choices are amazing. I’m hooked on the Sichuan spicy broth — super flavorful and seriously satisfying. Just a tip: if you don’t eat a lot of spicy food, check with the staff before ordering because it can get pretty hot. But if you love spice, this is the place to go.

Ordering is easy, the selection of meats and veggies is huge, and it’s perfect for nights when I don’t feel like cooking. The staff are always friendly, the vibe is calm and relaxed, and the prices are very reasonable.

In a busy city like San Francisco, it’s rare to find somewhere that’s both quiet and delicious — this place checks all the boxes.

Excellent ingredients, great broth, spotless everywhere, free drinks an unexpected bonus.

I decided to finally visit this restaurant after seeing it a few times and it did not disappoint. If you don't know what malatang is, you choose a bunch of ingredients and a soup and the staff cooks it for you. Everything looked pretty fresh, but I mostly had beef and lamb with ramen noodles in pork bone broth.

After paying a little under $15, I was on my way to the sauce station when I saw that they also offered water, jasmine tea, and some kind of grapefruit juice drink for free. The tea was hot and not too strong. For the sauce, I chose to mix soy sauce with sesame paste and garlic because it's a reliable combination that works with anything.

My order was brought out about five minutes after I paid. Everything was cooked well. The broccoli had a slight crunch, the fried tofu wasn't soggy, and the ramen was still a little chewy. The meats were all tender. I decided to try the broth and it had a rich flavor on its own.

I finished feeling full and went to the restroom, where I was delighted to see it squeaky clean and smelling fresh.

This is an excellent place to get malatang and the price ($14.99/lb) is comparable to other spots in the city. I'm sure their menu items are good too.

top_reviews.content:
Love this authentic little spot in Japan town. The soba was very earthy and delicate. The tempuras are fried with a gluten-free powder that gave a interesting texture. The dipping sauce was perfectly complementary to the chilled soba. You can add your preferred amount to wasabi and spring onions in the sauce. I love the fried the scallop tempura, and all of the vegetable tempura. This is the ultimate comfort food on a rainy day.

I came around 5pm and left as round 6pm on a Tuesday There was space for singles/couples but harder to find table for 4 given the space. No wait for table and I got my food in 15 minutes.

Great value and love this spot for a simple, authentic and nuanced dinner.

I also tried the soba warabimochi, a gelatin chewy rectangular pieces of dessert dusted in sesame powder. It was solid but the soba is the winner here. I would love to come back to try the hot soba as well.

I got here at 1:30 p.m. on Friday and got in at 2:30 p.m. and got the place to put my order.

Good:
I really liked the tamago dish, and I got the hot soba soup with a bunch of tempura. The tempura ended up being too oily, so I didn't finish it, but I did really like the soba soup. It was quite tasty and savory. Also got to sit next to the lucky Buddha, and I rubbed the feet, so that was actually quite a nice blessing. The chef is really, really nice. Even though he was being swarmed, he was very nice to me and taught me how everything worked.

Bad:
The soba noodles themselves were just okay. They didn't have much flavor, and they didn't taste that great to me. It's also pretty expensive to get just an appetizer and a soba dish. It was over $40.

Overall, I'm glad I came and tried out this super unique and special place in SF. I had a day off, so it was worth the wait. If I weren't coming on a day off, it would be harder to justify the wait.

Soba restaurant at Japanese town in San Francisco. It is  small restaurant at corner street and it is specialized in authentic and freshly made Japanese l soba noidle  . It was busy and people in line when we arrived and the restaurant is not opened yet. We missed the first seating as It only have 11 seats in the restaurant with some are bar style seat. The wait time was about 45 to more than an hour. The  best to line up before it opens.
Once you are find a  seat, you can order from the touch screen ordering The menu is simple , first you can choose hot or cold soba,  and for tenzaru and tenkake set you choose either tempura or kaikage. There is also other lr soba choices. For small bites it has chicken tenders, braised pork, and and mochi for dessert.
We ordered tenzaru and tenkske with shrimp  kaikage. We also ordered kakesoba,  chicken tender and mochi.
Both cold and hot soba are unique and yummy. I like soba texture and yhe broth cold and hot are yummy.  The kaikage is unique as it is a bit chewy. The chicken tender is ok. Mochi is yummy.
Looks like one of the worker is the owner and he was friendly. Overall it was a good lunch. You have to be patient if you want to have a meal here. Parking is on the street and the restaurant has one restroom.
In the restaurant you kind of feel you are in of of the restaurant in Japan as it is small and pack.

I arrived right at opening and was still looking at about an hour wait, which honestly seems pretty standard for this place. If you're hoping to minimize the line, I'd recommend getting there at least 30 minutes to an hour before they open. The shop itself is very small and cozy, maybe 10 to 15 seats total, which gives it an intimate, almost old-school Japan feel that I really appreciated.

I ordered the cold soba, while others in my group tried both the cold and hot versions. You can absolutely tell the noodles are homemade; the texture and freshness really stand out. That said, while the cold soba was very good, it didn't quite live up to the hype for me. When I order cold soba, I expect something that really pops in flavor and simplicity. This came close, but not quite all the way there. The hot soba, on the other hand, seemed to shine a bit more and was the preferred choice overall.

The owner was incredibly friendly and welcoming, which added a lot to the experience. My only real gripe is the wait process. Having to stand outside for so long feels unnecessary, and a remote waitlist or reservation system would be a huge improvement.

Overall, I don't think this spot fully lives up to the hype, but it's still a solid meal with great craftsmanship behind the noodles. If the line is short, it's definitely worth stopping by. Just don't expect to have your socks knocked off.

Very uniquely Japanese, you look at menu, choose and pay for thr items you want, then wait for a seat to become available, and by that time, you be able to sit and enjoy your bowl of perfectly temp noodles... 😍.

I do understand about what others stated about the waiting situation. However, you have to see each placendifferently and why it took longer for you to be seated here than other spots inside Japantown. Smaller more intimate location equals to limited seating. People still come because the food quality and taste are excellent. Then if you all didn't know, the owner and chef is also the owner of Belly Good Cafe & Crepe's! First time I came here and i was like, wait, that's and i immediately recognized him. And I said to myself, no wonder i haven't seen him for a long time! Me and my now wife have gotten Crepe's from him a long long time and everytime, he greets with a smile and just makes you feel very welcomed! He carries that same energy here, just different cuisine and clientele.  I would recommend you go here and try his food, you can literally see him and the other chef concentrating in the quality and craft when they are preparing your food. I have  to say, if your in the area, you have to try Sobakatsu! Thank you!

My only advice is to order early because popular items sell out quickly. If you're looking for high-quality takeout sushi in San Francisco, Aji Kiji is absolutely worth trying.

One of the best takeout sushi experiences I’ve had. The freshness of the ingredients really stands out—everything tastes clean, precise, and high quality, from the fish to the rice. You can tell there’s real attention to detail in how each piece is prepared.

The packaging is also impeccable. Everything arrives neatly organized, secure, and thoughtfully presented, which makes a big difference for takeout. Nothing feels rushed or sloppy—it’s clear they care about the full experience, not just the food itself.

Overall, it’s a place I keep coming back to because it’s reliable, fresh, and consistently well executed. The only small note is that it would be great to see takeout orders prioritized a bit more during busy times, as that would make an already excellent experience even smoother.

Loved the freshness of the fish and the seasoning was perfect. The pickles/tsukemono are an absolute delight with just the right amount of crunch. The futomaki and sushi are going to be my takeout staples in SF, and the brilliant service from the staff there made my day. Will be back soon!

top_reviews.content:
I love to eat at Kura Revolving Sushi Bar in Berkeley! I come frequently, as it is definitely a favorite for me, my friends, and my family.

It’s a fun, modern place to eat. The dining area is clean and sunny (with big windows letting the Berkeley sunshine stream in), and I find the conveyor belt that carries the sushi plates and the robot that brings the water and wasabi to the table so cute!

I like how you order by the plate (most plates are $4.10), which means you can have as much or as little as you can afford or feel hungry for. I’ve come here for just a plate or two before, and I’ve also come with friends and accumulated tall stacks of plates. (If you order enough plates, you might even win cute prizes that are dispensed from above the ordering console at every table!)

The environment and concept are wonderful, but the food here speaks for itself. When it comes to sushi, there’s a variety of choices that range from traditional to modern. The fish and meat are always fresh, the rice is always perfectly sticky and well-seasoned, and the nori is always crisp—especially if you order on the console because then it will come straight to your table from the kitchen on a conveyor belt. I particularly recommend the tekkamkai and the negitoro gunkan; I try these two plates almost every time I come, and I come a lot. The wasabi, soy sauce, and ginger are free and high-quality. I love to use plenty of them with my sushi.

There’s also plenty of great non-sushi items, including ramen, udon, and even fries. The miso soup here is warm and soothing, a perfect appetizer, and the beef udon is also a favorite of mine. (I love the slurpy, chewy noodles and the warm broth with the tender beef).

They take dessert as seriously as the main course. You can’t go wrong here, but for dessert, I recommend the warabi mochi, the sesame balls, and the gooey butter cake. Personally, I often find it hard to choose just one.

The menu is not set in stone, and they frequently circulate exciting specials on and off the menu, so it’s usually worth it to browse the entire menu before ordering. I think my favorite special item that’s ever been on the menu is the negitoro maki roll. (Maybe they'll bring it back, but I don't know.)

They also change out their cute prizes, if you’re into that. I have some cute key chains from when we ordered a bunch of plates a while back.

I downloaded their app, so I can receive discounts/coupons from time to time.

Eating here is always a treat!

I had some bad experiences at other Kura locations, so I was a little hesitant to eat over here, but it all turned out great!

I had a reservation and checked in with the staff when we arrived at the restaurant. We still had to wait about another 15 min for our table to be ready. It's not too bad, but I'm not sure what the purpose of making a reservation is if there's still a wait.

All of the sushi tasted better than I expected. The sushi rice held together well, not too gummy, mushy, or overcooked. And the rice was glossy, hydrated, but not too wet or soggy. The ingredients tasted fresh, and I didn't have any stomach discomfort after getting home. Highly recommended!

Made my kids happy with the conveyor and prize experience. I did like the plate disposal experience. Overall, I was disappointed with food, with ramen being the biggest disappointment. The pork slices were not fresh, very chewy, and didn’t taste right. Overall not the best value for portion sizes. If you like gimmicks, this is the place for you!
Super chill spot to eat at. The food is delicious and the desserts are as well! The gooey butter cake for dessert is a winner. ALOHA!

My swedish cousin says you never put powdered sugar on swedish pancakes, but what does he know? He's never made them for me.

It was good! The service was amazing, super fast and attentive staff. Very cozy place. The price and portions are good. But, the food looked better than it tasted. I got the Marti’s special omelet with potatoes. It was ok. The coffee was not strong and tasted  instant made. I wish you could customize your own omelet, it would be great!

Inedible eggs, but worse still really rude service.

I asked for sunny side up and got a plate with the whites completely liquid. I hate returning food but it was inedible so I asked if they could cook it a bit more to set the whites. The person I asked was fine with it, but then our other waiter came up to me and was incredibly hostile and condescending? “You said you wanted sunny side up. You want over easy? Over medium?” I just wanted the egg whites set? She made me question if maybe sunny side up means runny whites so I figured over easy because I did want the yolks to be runny - but the whites set. I thought they’d just flip it onto the griddle for the three seconds it would take to accomplish that.

Instead I was given “over easy” eggs that were even more raw than the sunny side up ones, and no follow up.

I really have to stress that I hate confrontation so I was extremely nice during both interactions, even saying “this is my bad, but can you please…” etc.

Anyway, the whole point of this spot is supposed to be warm service, right? Instead I felt like I was in the twilight zone and even googled to see if I’m wrong and runny whites are acceptable for either sunny side up or over easy eggs. They’re not.

Small local spot in the sunset serving flavorful Thai food that’s great for dining in or take out. Would recommend this place for a casual date night, lunch with friends, or a dinner in.

Loved: chicken satay (cucumber salad was a nice touch and so crunchy and delicious) and the fried rice with chicken and shrimp.

Sometimes Thai food at places can be heavy, greasy, or too sweet or saucy. Theirs was delicious, well balanced, flavorful, and on the lighter side sauce-wise, which I appreciate being someone who loves flavor but doesn’t want her food swimming in sauce.

My favorite Thai spot in the Sunset and one of my favorites in the city. <3
Obsessed with their Tom Kha soup w/ seafood, their duck fried rice is delicious & never too fatty. I typically avoid Pad Thai in America- but I really enjoy the Pad Thai here. Not greasy and not too sweet. Highly recommend!

The service is always friendly and warm, their space is cozy and lovely. Been bringing friends, family, and myself here for 10 years-  I've never had a bad meal or experience.

I’ve lived in this neighborhood for two years and go to Thai Cottage at least once a week. I’m finally getting around to writing a review because this is, hands down, the most underrated restaurant I’ve ever been to. The food is consistently fantastic—I don’t have just one go-to dish because everything I try is a hit.

It’s a family-owned spot, and the owner, Sabrina, has become a friend over time. She cares so deeply about the food and the craft. Just last night she explained to me how they make their fish cakes, carefully pounding the fish by hand—there’s so much love and skill behind every dish.

Thai Cottage is cozy, understated, and truly a neighborhood gem, but the food is good enough that you’d be thrilled to find it at a high-end restaurant downtown (and pay double). Instead, we’re lucky to enjoy that same quality right here in the outer sunset, no reservations needed.
Great find! Green curry with chicken was amazing.  But real winner was the deep fried codfish! Host was very friendly and got us a table quickly!!

Incredibly fresh and delicious dishes every time! We eat here as often as we can - we especially love the green curry, pumpkin curry, noodles, & mango desserts...we've never had a bad meal here. Sabrina and her family are so kind and welcoming- this is one of our favorite restaurants in San Francisco ❤️

First time in and we loved it! The staff were efficient and super friendly, the location and atmosphere were ideal and the food was delicious! If you’re nearby, do yourself a favor and stop in!

Standout dishes were: French Style Black Pepper Beef, BBQ Pork Chop, Beef Rib Pho.

Would not recommend this place to non pork eaters.

To be fair I probably should have looked at their menu beforehand, but I eat at korean restaurants often and never have trouble finding dishes I can eat.

However, they only have 2 dishes that are non pork, and both are soups/noodle dishes.

We ordered the Beef Short Rib Soup and the Kalguksu. I really liked the noodles in the Kalguksu, and really liked the Beef short rib in the soup. However, both soups were very simple and not that flavorful.

Their other dishes looked good, but none could be made without pork. I wanted to order the kimchi pancake, but they said that pork is included in the batter so they could not accommodate us.

I'm sure this place would be more delicious for other people, but as non pork eaters we just couldn't have many dishes. I'm used to most restaurants being very accommodating to this so it's just odd that they are very strict to this considering they are a michelin guide restaurant.

We did not get a reservation, we called ahead and were able to get a table but had to wait 45min.

The location is also not the best as it's deep in the tenderloin, and walking to the restaurant was very unsafe and unpleasant.

Food: Menu was limited, likely focused on their specialties. I ordered the pork bone soup and kimchi pancake. The soup was hot and flavorful. Quite filling. This soup is good as a full meal. It comes with a side of white rice so you should think it through if you’re getting another dish in addition.
The fried kimchi was not memorable. The edges were a bit burnt. Probably ok as a street food, not so much as an appetizer.
Drinks: the drinks were priced at city prices. Their makgeolli drink was exorbitant at $16 for a 750 ml plastic bottle. Not recommended.
Service:  It was a slow Monday night. The dinner crowd was thin so I got a lot of attention. The server was helpful and pleasant.
Location and facilities: The restaurant was cozy with a modern vibe. The place was clean and you’re not overwhelmed by the odor of food or smoke from the cooking. That’s a plus. The staff were dressed professionally and looked quite competent.
That said, this restaurant is in the heart of the tenderloin. The immediate perimeter did not exude sophistication and cleanliness, let alone a feeling of safety. I don’t recommend lingering in this area late at night or do what I did, walking from Union Square to this restaurant. Not a good idea. Parking can also be a safety issue so probably best to do ride-share.

Overall: Flavorful Korean food, cozy venue, good enough for a night out. I would’ve added another star if there were more options and if you can ignore the surroundings.

There are places you eat, and then there are places that feel like home—La Hacienda on MacArthur in Oakland is the latter. No pretension, no gimmicks, just damn good food served with warmth and a sense of place.

The carnitas burrito? A masterpiece—crispy-edged pork, rich and juicy, wrapped in a tortilla that actually holds its own. The fajitas sizzle and smoke like they mean business, every bite a reminder that sometimes, simple done right is all you need. And then there’s the bean dip, an unassuming little gift at the start of the meal, creamy and savory enough to make you wonder why more places don’t do this.

But the real magic? The people. The owner steps out, chats like an old friend, and suddenly, you’re not just eating—you’re part of something. A family-run spot that understands hospitality in a way that corporate joints never will. This isn’t just a recommendation; it’s a command. Go. Eat. Feel at home.

The restaurant was always packed with customers, and you had to wait over an hour for takeout orders. If I'm paying that much for a smoothie I shouldn't have so much ice if any. It should be all frozen fruits. My smoothie was icy and chunky, not smooth at all. I was pretty disappointed with it.

Love love love! The bowls here are super fresh tasting and such a good breakfast or pick me up rain or shine. I order ahead online so I can pick it up super quick and then go people watch at the lake while eating my bowl. Love that they also serve La Colombe coffee, which makes it a nice one stop cafe.

I ordered the summit bowl on DoorDash right at opening time. I was in a rush and the staff prioritized my order and made it for me even though it hadn’t come through on their system yet. GREATLY appreciated. And the bowl was delicious (added almond butter and strawberries on top).

I highly, HIGHLY recommend this place. The bowls here are not only incredibly fresh but also absolutely beautiful to look at, which makes the experience even better. They offer a great variety of bowls, including endurance, destination, and wellness bowls, so there’s always something that fits whatever I’m in the mood for. I love coming here after a workout to grab a bowl and add some  protein, but sometimes I’ll stop by just for a dessert-style bowl—it really just depends on how I’m feeling. I love being able to customize and create different variations of bowls. I’ve been coming here off and on since they opened and have always had great experiences.

The staff is very welcoming and helpful with suggestions if you’re unsure what to order. I also really love their rewards program, where you earn points on every purchase and sometimes receive coupons—it honestly feels like getting cash back and definitely makes me want to come back more often. I was even able to find and apply coupons to my order. Shoutout to Johnathan, John, and Kirsten for providing great customer service—they’re always friendly, go above and beyond, and very patient. I love the music choice as well. The only thing I’d hope for in the future is slightly extended hours, but overall this place is a favorite of mine.

I came in for some water and a quick slice to enjoy in the park, and left with a beaming smile :D. The pizza is delicious, and Hassan’s hospitality was unmatched! If you’re looking for a high-quality pizza and a friendly face in the neighborhood (bonus!!), Gabriella’s is the place to go!
Best pizza in oakland near lakeshore / cleveland heights area. They are great for late night pies and slices!

Found this late night pizza spot after we saw the other pizza places in town had such long lines. And it was a super delicious greasy NYC pizza with chicken/beef pepperoni. Hit the spot. The group of us who shared it all agreed this place needs more recognition.

name: Utzutzu
address: 1428 Park St, Alameda, CA 94501, United States

google.name: Utzutzu
google.address: 1428 Park St, Alameda, CA 94501, United States
google.description: Stylish, diminutive destination that offers highbrow sushi & Japanese fare at cozy counter seats.

top_reviews.content: The small unassuming entry way will make you think you’re breaking into someone’s house but it’s perfect for that intimate feeling as well.  Once you find the right door it’s a super chill vibe in a small space.  The chef was preparing everything as we walked in and the server sat us down.  The food was super fresh and the chef was very kind.  There were 13 different sashimis served along with 6 additional courses of non sashimi items.  Very nice service and amazing meal, left full and happy!

At Utzutzu, you can find a top-notch omakase experience. We’ve visited this restaurant four times, and every visit has been exceptional. The service is always warm and attentive, and the sashimi is incredibly fresh and beautifully prepared. We have never been disappointed. Highly recommended for anyone looking for an unforgettable omakase experience!

This omakase spot is tucked upstairs in a small sushi bar with around 8 seats. The chef is Japanese, so the style feels more traditional, and the fish was fresh. But overall, the flavors were flat and leaned overly salty, especially the soy sauce, which masked a lot of the natural taste.

The chef was working alone for the entire room, which made the pacing feel rushed, and the plating lacked detail. The side dishes were honestly forgettable. The service felt uneven. The hostess was friendly, but the guy at the front seemed untrained and didn’t leave the best impression.

The chef also gave off a bit of a tense vibe. He kept smiling and talking, but it felt like he was quietly venting or muttering under his breath. I couldn’t understand what he was saying, but I later noticed other reviewers mentioned the same thing, so it might be a recurring issue.

We paid about $450 for two people, with one drink each and a small add-on. For that price, I expected a more polished and balanced experience. If you’re new to omakase, it might be a decent intro but if you’ve had more refined ones, this may fall short.

The Food
I have only visited a handful of omakase places. But a friend was able to get a reservation at Utzutzu, so I wanted to give this place a try. Once we settled in our seats, the chef presented us with the fish that he will be preparing for the night. Few friends and I decided to try out their Sake of the day, which was the Nagurayama "Gekkyu". They presented the Sake in an aesthetic glass, it was not bad, though I prefer some of the sweeter sake. As the courses began, they were as follows...

- Kinpira Gobo (braised burdock root), with asparagus topped with saffron
- Nanbanzuke (marinated fish, with a slight citrus taste)

Nigiri
-  Isaki (伊佐木 / Chicken Grunt, soft and have a slight crunch)
- Shima-aji (縞鯵 / Striped Jack, hint of lime zest)
- Ishigakidai (Knifejaw, smooth with a slight chew)
- Horse Snake Mackerel
- Golden Eye (Deep Sea) Snapper (hint of roast flavor, not overdone)
- Black Seabream (almost melt in mouth)
- Maguro (leaner cut but still fresh)
- Amberjack (balanced with yuzu kosho)
- Saba (topped with sweet kelp)
- Ocean Trout

- Sumiso-ae (miso and vinegar dressed with cucumber and octopus, sweet and refreshing, octopus have a slight chew, but not tough)
- Uni Chawanmushi (steamed egg custard, topped with Hokkaido uni, along with shitake, spinach, and ginkgo nut)

Nigiri
- Scallop, Torched (slight burnt bitterness)
- Shrimp From Canada (fresh, almost melt in mouth)
- Otoro (delicious)
- Toro Hand Roll
- Tamagoyaki (the right sweetness)

- Akadashi (miso soup with zucchini, mushroom, and tofu skin)
- Peach Jelly (slight sweetness, not overpowering)

The Miscellaneous
The Utzutzu restaurant is a bit tucked away. There is no sign other than a door number, and you will know you are in the right place once you go up the stairs. The inside greets the guests with a small lounge area while they wait for their reservation. They have a sushi bar that just seats 7 people. It gives a more personal experience with the chef I believe. The service and staff were good. You know they put attention to detail when they fold the clean wipe so it is easy to use. The menu has a good variety of dishes to keep it interesting. Reservations open around 1 month in advance, it's still hard to get seating, so reserve early. All in all, the food was delicious, and quite the array of selections. Would recommend and would also want to return again.
So disappointing the chef's hands did not look healthy and he did not wear gloves. The service was great, but I was grossed out and the food was just okay.

reviews_snippets.content: "Nonetheless overall I enjoyed this omakase place as an edomae choice in SF area."
"Beautifully presented top grade sushi and dishes served in a great space."

Dropped by this location during the week. The area is a bit sketchy due to the homeless population in the area.  And some that were just acting strange.

We were seated quickly as there was alot of open tables.   The restaurant it left is quite large.  Seating shouldn't be a problem.   Finding parking close by is the problem.  Again, its due to the sketchy area as mentioned above.

The food was a bit salty but tasted okay.  The service was okay.

Overall a solid 3 star place.  1 star for the area.

The big bone pho has a lot of fat, probably about 50% of the rib is fatty. However, the owner was kind and informed me that I can request a remake for the next time if there’s too much fatty attached.

Super solid pho place! Huge portions and noodle to soup ratio. The beef rib pho came with a giant piece of rib with tender meat that fall off the bone. My favorite thing about the restaurant is being able to substitute pho noodle for my Bun bo hue!

The service isn’t the most attentive. Especially on busy days, they are super understaffed and you can be at your table waiting for a while. But you get free desserts and sometimes free pandan waffles!

Great food and portion, worker was also very attentive and somehow knew I wouldn’t want the tea and gave me ice water before I even asked. Unlucky about the exploitation of the workers as they are great, hopefully they get their fair share from the trial since they deserve it

Edit: DO NOT GO HERE!! They have fraudulently changed the tip amount before this place is horrible and dangerous!
Edit: Be careful with takeout, once got disgusting meat balls and raw beef. And the spicy selection is EXTREMELY oily. The drinks are great but the food is VERY hit or miss. The dine in experience was good but take out is iffy. Review changed from 5 to 3 stars. Pho An Hoa is another San Leandro pho restaurant and they're extremely consistent and have very good food.
Original review:
The food was shockingly good! Genuinely one of the best restaurants i've ever been to! The service was very good and the servers were helpful with the menu and made sure we got everything we needed.
Best Thai Tea i've ever had.

top_reviews.content: Really great spot for some Egyptian food. The restaurant is tiny and has an authentic feel to it but is fine for take way for very small group dining. We tried the shawarma and it was amazing. One of the best shawarma I've ever had. Very unique. The sauces and the veggies really make it but the chicken itself is very tasty too.

This place saved me & my two friends on our 11 pm post-concert food hunt. Got the Shawarma Arabic, Chicken Gyro, and Beef Shawarma plate. It was a 6/5 for all of us. Served with tzatziki and red chili flake oil + 2 banana peppers.... super flavorful, affordable, chill staff. Beyond worth it. Some cool Egyptian decorations. Only downside is sparse seating close to the door, but that's the norm for east bay. first eats in oakland!! loved it!

Its a pretty casual spot where you order at the counter so I wouldn't expect fine dining level service. I gave 5 stars for service because everyone had a smile and was friendly even though it was super busy when my partner and I went.

As far as the food, I was very, very happy with the experience. My partner and I shared mixed loaded fries. The fries were really nicely seasoned and topped with a generous portion of mixed meats. Sometimes when you get loaded fries you end up eating the layer with toppings first and have bland soggy fries at the bottom. This was the opposite! They had a really delicious tahini and chili sauce on the side as well.

When we went I had been certain that anything still open at 11pm would be mediocre but this place was just what the doctor ordered and such a pleasant surprise. If you're going to a show at the Fox or bar hopping downtown, definitely check this place out for a quick bite.

We went on First Friday, August 1 2025 and this place was hopping at 2am. I can recommended the chicken shawarma. I want to try their desserts, which by the time my group of intrepid Oaklanders made it there was sold out.

If you are inebriated or high. This us the place to get some bomb dot com Egyptian style middle eastern food. The ambiance is cool too. Highly recommend, and we will be back.

Chicken gyro was delicious and loaded with yummy chicken and veggies, white sauce and hot sauce were on point. Chips were also crispy. Service was quick and easy, very kind people. $14 exactly for the gyro ONLY. Looks small but it’s actually a good portion. Definitely will be back here to try other dishes.

We ordered late night wings and ordered a few flavors. Lemon pepper, peanut butter, spicy, and I think the Saigon one. The wings were pretty good and tasted really good. This place is made a pretty good dinner for us.

Calvin is the man ! He convinced me and my friends to try new flavors and boy was I so happy he did. Don’t sleep on the peanut butter wings yall !! He had great customer service and he made our quick little dinner into a great memory from being so genuine. Thanks again Calvin !

They changed their fry vendor and the new plain fries they use are flavorless, not crispy, and disgusting. Also I ordered extra crispy wings and got soggy wings. The store smelled like dirty mop water.

Don’t go! Save your money! The tiny sandwich cost 7$ they’ve been making them smaller lately but this is ridiculous. They told me it’ll take twenty minutes to make the order. I went to check they hadn’t even starter, I didn’t get mad I just ask “okay how much longer then” 15 minutes. I checked again still haven’t started on my order. It took 50 minutes to get my order done.

I’ve never wanted to write a bad review about a A business because I haven’t had an experience so bad that made me want to write a bad review but I can say with 100% certainty that I have never had an experience this bad.

Total cost of everything was $60. Was not even worth $16. Fries were so soggy sandwich was burnt and wings were cooked too long and dry. Save your money I never thought I’d say this about a wing spot, but you’d have a better experience at the frozen freezer Isle of your grocery store.

top_reviews.content: Ordered the Single Meat Combo for $33. Definitely felt like eating two plates as shown in the photos. Worth to also try the winter melon lemonade for your drink option. Each individual gets their own pot for themselves. Definitely helps when individuals have their own preference or dining style. Abundant choices in topings and sauces to pair with your food. Come in hungry you won't regret it!

Delicious hotpot with good quality ingredients & generous portions. Here’s what I learned:
- we arrived around 7 pm and waited around 5-10 mins for a table which is great! I did notice that groups that arrived after 8 pm had much longer wait times, so keep that in mind for your dinner time planning
- sukiyaki soup base was the best, I’d order it for everyone at the table. didn’t like the mushroom broth that much
- sides we ordered: tiger shrimp, fish balls, and shrimp balls. Fish balls were our favourite!
- we got the Classic standard package with 3 meats and just ordered the 3 halal meat options. The best meats are the Beef’s (Australian & Wagyu). We didn’t like the lamb as much tbh, I wouldn’t order lamb again
- cooking times: hotpot advice is usually to cook meats for 10-15 sec. We found that cooking lamb for 1.5 minutes and cooking the beef until the fat is melting (1-2 minutes) makes the meat taste better. I would encourage people to just experiment and try different cooking times!
- dips: best sauces were the sweet soy sauce, as well as all the spicy sauces and chilli oil. Mushroom sauce was also decent
- noodles: we tried Udon and Ramen, next time I’d order multiple Udon and only Udon!

Anyways hopefully this information helps people!
Final advice: we ordered the classic package as 2 people and we almost exploded from fullness. Still recovering the next day. Definitely go with a group of 3 at minimum 😂 also you can take the leftover broth home, it tastes so good!

Most importantly: HAVE FUN and mashikeh mogo!

Mumu Hot Pot is such a great addition to the SFSU community. Usually I get pretty overwhelmed by hot pot choices and tend to over order but I love that they offer meal sets for 2 which comes with 3 meat, 2 choice of noodles and tons of veggies for $68. There's a big selection of sauces and toppings to choose from too. It doesn't look like a lot but trust me, by the time you finish everything, you'll probably have to unbuckle your pants. Everything tasted very fresh and high quality especially the meat. I loved how flavorful the soup base is. My favorite is definitely their Tom Yum soup base. Service is great! They're attentive and efficient. Seating is spacious. Street parking is available outside. Overall, solid hot pot spot and would be back!

Nice atmosphere to hang out with friends. We were there for a couple of hours as we haven't seen each others for a while. The waitresses/waiters there were so nice and patient. There are plenty of seats so we didn't feel pressured as well.

I went there for a friends meet up. I’ve been to their San Mateo location before and this one is entirely new. I believe they opened just a couple months ago and the environment is brand new and fresh.Their service was very fast and they have two sauce bar for the guests. The seats weren’t too crowded and the hot pot tastes really good and authentic. I thought the portion was little, but I got very full at the end. The price was also very fair in the city. The staff were very nice. I would recommend here.

top_reviews.content:
The garlic noodles are middle of the road at Pho Day. My order was a grilled beef garlic noodles $20. The prices on the menu are wrong. It is listed as $19. The garlic noodles were buttery but has no visible garlic pieces. It only has a hint of a garlic taste. The beef had a sweet glaze on it and a small bit of smokey flavor. Beef slices were thin. Since I sat near the kitchen, I can hear the chefs speaking Toisan. (Not that there's anything wrong with that. A lot of good Vietnamese restaurants in the city are of mixed heritage.) The restaurant is too clean to be a true Vietnamese restaurant. I'm more used to seeing an auntie wrapping egg rolls in the middle of the dining room, some sort of loud Vietnamese music video playing on a screen and the restrooms are also used as a stockroom for cleaning supplies. None of that could be seen at Pho Day.

Service was excellent as there weren't that people at 7pm.

When I left, I realized I was still hungry. That's not good. I had to walk to another restaurant get an appetizer. Not a fan of small portions.

Pro tip, if they want more business, just add a number after the restaurant's name. All the great LA pho places do it.

So glad my friend suggest to go that place. I like the portion they give to us. Food and service were excellent. I had pho and Vietnamese coffee it was so good I do suggest this spot. It was good timing and not much people
My beef pho arrived via door dash without beef. I physically went to the restaurant because I live one block away and they called me a liar. Never eating here again.

April 2023:
Stopped by for the chicken pho. They give you a little minced ginger to add to the soup. I thought it enhanced the flavor 👍. I would probably get the chicken pho again.

August 2022:
Came here for lunch and tried the pho. It was pretty good. I asked for the beef on the side so I could cook it to a medium rare state. Soup wasn't hot enough at the end. But that is my fault for ordering it on the side.

The dry noodles were tasty too. One complaint was that the dish had a lot of noodles and not enough ingredients.

I love going to the Mission district in SF.   Remembered when I would go down that way when a KFC still existed and Valencia St. was not yet known to be hipster.  You went there to get your fixing for a super fat burrito and nothing else!  Or you would pop your head in and wait in line at  Mitchell's for some coconut or ube ice cream or sundae!  Pho Day is a casual Vietnamese restaurant opened not too long ago.  The imperial rolls were Amazing!!!  Loved the crisp and crunch.  The vermicelli w/ shrimp was a solid choice w/ good sized prawns.  The pho was good and had a clean taste. Wished they would put more noodles and meat!  I'm glad that the Mission/Bernal Heights now has another spot for Pho.  You can get some Mitchell's ice cream for dessert right after your meal!  Service was efficient. Parking is horrible!

top_reviews.content:
Came in Sunday for dinner. The moment we walked in, a waiter (or food runner?) greeted us with a blunt “no slices, only whole pizza” - no hello, no apology, no questions about our party. Problem is, slices are listed right on their menu even if we wanted slices. When we asked if we could still order, he just told us to go to the bartender and walked off to chat with his coworkers.

At the bar, we asked about the slices again since we were confused. The bartender explained they typically sell out of slices by 5–6pm. So why is it still on the menu with no disclaimer if you can’t sell slices all night long? It felt a bit deceptive given there’s no additional note on the menu.

We ended up ordering a whole pizza to-go and waited 30 minutes. When the same rude waiter handed it over, I asked for chili flakes. He rolled his eyes, trudged three feet to grab a packet, then sarcastically asked “that’s all you want?” and immediately walked back to his corner - after we’d just spent $55 on a single pizza.

The pizza itself was good and the slices are generously sized. But no food is good enough to excuse this kind of service. I won’t be back, and I won’t be recommending this place. Honestly, you’re better off going somewhere else down the street, or even Domino’s, where they’re at least happy to see you and give you chili flakes

Pizza was pretty good especially if you like a nice thin dough. Small selection of flavors BUT you can get it by the slice. Great crust and great cider selection. The cider selection was actually more diverse than the pizza selection which was liiiiit. And you can get it in a pitcher. Only downside was it was supper expensive and you even have to pay for the sauces on the side.

Hands down the best pizza spot I’ve tried so far. It feels super fancy without the crazy price tag. Every bite is packed with amazing flavors, the ingredients taste premium, and the quality is on another level.

Loved this place. The spicy vodka pizza was SO good, perfect amount of heat, amazing crust, and just really, really delicious. The music was great too and gave the whole place such a fun vibe.

What really stood out was how welcoming everyone was. The owner came over to check on us a couple of times, which was such a nice touch and made the place feel genuinely friendly and neighborhood-y.

Great pizza, great music, great people. Definitely a new SF favorite. We’ll be back!
Super cool place, Aran was super friendly & attentive! Got the vodka sauce pizza and it was tasty! Lots of drink options along with really good nonalcoholic options! Great NY style pies.

reviews_snippets.content: "Such a great selection of beer and wine paired with great pizza and service."

top_reviews.content: My friend and I heard that there are many fine restaurants on Piedmont Drive. Infinite Thai Eatery looked good so I read some reviews, and they were all five star. I chose a dish with vegetables and peanut sauce. It was DELICIOUS. I also ordered the brown rice to come with it, and it was like no rice I’ve had before. It was so flavorful. If I lived in Oakland, this would be a place that I came to regularly. The food was wholesome, delicious, and nutritious. The woman that served us was so attentive and polite.

The dining experience was truly delightful; each dish was bursting with flavor and left us craving more. While the dishes were delicious, a greater variety and quantity of vegetables would have added depth to the meal. The Thai tea was a delightful complement, and the charming flower arrangement as a centerpiece added a lovely touch to the ambiance. Additionally, the cleanliness of the establishment and the availability of street parking contributed to a pleasant overall experience. Will absolutely be back.

I’ve been coming here for a few years and I’ve never had a single bad experience. The food is always good and the owners are incredibly warm, kind people.

I particularly like all of their curries - the pumpkin curry being my favorite - but I also love their eggplant in spicy basil sauce 😍

I enjoy sitting inside or outside right on the beautiful Piedmont Avenue, and it’s also great for taking home in a pinch. Thank you for the great meals and warm interactions!
This was my first time coming. The server was very kind and attentive. Plenty of great vegetarian options. I absolutely loved the drunken noodle and the Thai fried rice, very yummy 😋

My new favorite Thai spot in Oakland! Stopped in after work to get a take out meal. Staff was friendly and didn’t have to wait too long. My drunken noodles were some of the best I’ve ever had, tofu was perfect, veg was fresh and the flavors were amazing. Already saved this in my maps and cannot wait to return!

reviews_snippets.content: "Super tasty dishes, generous portions, fair prices, nice people, good service!"

top_reviews.content:
Coming from the San Gabriel Valley, which has plenty of Sichuan food, I’m always on the hunt for good Sichuan places in East Bay. Of which, there aren’t that many.

I was pleasantly surprised by the food at Mr. Liu Noodle House.

The noodles in the Beef Noodle Soup were bouncy, and the broth was wonderfully fragrant and savory. It had just the right amount of flavor and salt.

Their chengdu dumplings are delicious as well. Nice homemade wrappers with a chew to them, in a fragrant balanced chili oil. Just the right amount of Sichuan peppercorn.

The blistered green beans had a nice wok hei to them, and packed a salty punch from the pickled vegetable (“sui mi ya cai”)

Service was lovely. The boss lady 老闆娘 refilled our water multiple times.

the wontons were super delicious and filled with a really good amount of meat. the spicy oil they used tasted amazing and added a lot of flavor.

the noodles were really good too. my only complaint is they were extremely greasy, but that might just be how the dish is cooked. overall still very tasty.

My go to combination is the chongqing style special noodles and the chengdu special dumpling. Highly recommended if you can eat spicy. A clean environment and the staff is friendly. My only wish is if they would serve hot tea in non-plastic cups.

It was my first time at Mr. Liu noodle house and I was searching for some truly authentic Chinese noodles in Oakland. I found this place and ordered their beef brisket noodles (原汤牛腩面）, and the flavors instantly transported me back to China! I would highly recommend coming here.
My server was also really kind and helpful, and I liked the cozy interior. If I had any complaints, the prices might be a little high but hey what can you do about the price of food these days.

This noodle spot is truly authentic! The flavors are perfectly balanced—not overly salty like many fast-food places—making it really enjoyable to eat. The shredded chicken in chili oil is especially impressive, with rich, layered flavors that are fragrant without being greasy. Definitely a hidden gem in the area. I’ll be coming back often and recommending it to friends!

reviews_snippets.content: "Good food, good service, good place , I love it!"

The drink menu is accomplished and sophisticated but a bit on the expensive side.
Thank you rabbit hole, what a cute name. You lived up to the reputation.

top_reviews.content:
My review is for the dinner tasting menu. At $89/person you get a full course Korean inspired meal. Each dish was fresh, light and had hit the tongue palate in all the right spots.

Beef tartare was light and perfectly seasoned. The main galbijjim steak with rice and chimichurri was buttery soft with hint of sweet aftertaste .

My friends and I could not stop eating! We were a larger group of 9 and the host did so well explaining each dish. She even gave tips on how to get the photos ! Atmosphere inside at night was modern and trendy. I can imagine it as a good date spot as well.

My first visit and I really loved this place. Decided to get both of the sandwiches, along with the black sesame latte. Really enjoyed both sandos, but the egg sando is a yummy scrambled egg filling with sriracha mayo, and not like an egg salad filling. Was still great but worth mentioning! I preferred the ribeye/galbi bc the meat was so tender and flavorful. I’ll definitely be back to try some of the rice bowls and desserts.

I’ve been wanting to try this place for months and finally made it in last Friday with my cousin and sister. We ordered the honey butter potatoes, beef tartare, clams, soondubu with the seafood add-on, fried Wagyu beef, cucumber salad, and the salt bread churros. Overall, the food was decent, but most of the dishes didn’t quite meet our expectations. That said, the drinks were a standout, phenomenal and easily the highlight of the experience.

I visited this place with my sister during one of our outings in San Francisco. We got there around 2:30 pm on a Saturday and the place was pretty full. But lucky for us, there was people leaving right when we got there so we immediately got a table and head to the counter to place our order.

What we ordered:

☕ Black Sesame Latte • 9/10
A very well-made Black Sesame Latte. Not too sweet and comforting. Will definitely order again next time.

🍹 Raspberry Omija Soda • 9/10
Very refreshing drink. The cream on top was delicious—not too thick and sweet—and complimented the raspberry soda really well. Could probably have that cream with any other drinks if I’m being honest.

🥪 Umami Kimchi Panini • 9.5/10
This was our first time having a Kimchi Panini and we both agreed it was really good. Bursts of Korean flavors in every bite and super flavorful. It was very well executed, delicious and the portion was pretty generous too. Although maybe worth mentioning, it was a tad spicy for me who can’t really eat spicy food (that kimchi really had a pretty spicy kick for me) but it was fine for my sister who can.

Also, met the owner, Esther, during our visit and she was super nice and friendly and helped us with menu recommendations. If you’re looking for a dessert cafe in San Francisco/Hayes Valley area with unique Korean flavors, this place is definitely worth trying.

Came for a solo lunch on a weekday. The octopus rice bowl was a slightly awkward pairing of ingredients, with shaved Parm and slightly overcooked rice.
And the salt bread was way less buttery than expected, compared to Tano salt bread. Tasty but maybe not worth the price tag?
Service was friendly, vibes were a little evening-oriented but still nice.
