top_reviews.content:
Unpretentious authenticity, a Mexican breakfast-lunch with Guatemalan twist.

In addition to taqueria standards, Central American style fried chicken and grab-and-go crispy specials available: empanadas, flautas. A brothy soup of the day also available upon request.

Indoor and outdoor seating.
Good food. Not the most stylish place but they try hard and make the did with love.

This isn't just a restaurant, it's a cultural hub. My mom is central American, and our culture is somewhat different than Mexican culture. This place opens at 4:30a.m., that means they're serving full meals at that time. Its where working men go to get their coffees, sweetbread, and any kind of breakfast they need to get through their day. Its home style home cooked comida Centro Americana...as authentic as it gets.
Our people WORK! its what we do... From the day we arrive in this country, we help each other as much as we can. Marthitas is that place where working men and women congregate for their morning cafesitos con pan dulcé...and long may it continue to be so. If you want the real deal, this is the place. There is no shi shi anything here, there's long tables and everyone sits together. This is a woman run establishment, because without our women, we are nothing.
Try the chicharones con huevitos y frijoles con crema...get a side of platanitos... It comes with fresh handmade tortillas. Have a coffee and a piece of sweet bread....this food is made with love. And is literally as close to what my grandma used to feed me, when I would come knocking on her door, my mom was at work, and I got hungry, all those years ago...
Marthitas, is basically a place where a Mama got up early to cook so she could feed the men, and her sons, before they went to work for the day, that turned into a restaurant...because more and more men came for that taste of home, and to be with their people...
If you want authentic, show up here before the sun rises, have some breakfast with the real workers of America...
Viva California!! Y Viva nuestra Raza!!

Delicious mexican dishes that all taste like they’re cooked from scratch. We both got the huevos rancheros, which was a more basic style than is served at most restaurants, but was still some of the best we’ve had. Phenomenal homemade salsas, and really great fresh coffee. This restaurant also had very friendly staff, a cute outdoor patio area, and very good value.

top_reviews.content: I wanted to love it. The staff and food were good & my server was great. The setup is awful. My meal began with ordering on a shared tablet. The food came out too quickly. The restaurant has little to no control over that, so no stars off for obnoxious other guests. The TVs ruined the vibe. It's so cute inside, why ruin it with screens everywhere???? Paper menus, ask the mall to move the piano, ditch the TVs and it could be a really great place. Still good food and workers. Not sure if I'll go back soon.
I really enjoyed the fresh sushi and the vibe of the restaurant! Nigiri was fresh and delicious. The jack roll with the black rice was insane. Loved the probiotic drink at the end of our meal!

Misleading Rewards Policy - Beware‼️

I’ve been a loyal customer at Kaoru Sushi and have been collecting stamps on their rewards card (10 stamps = 1 free house specialty roll).
The card clearly states it’s redeemable for a free roll with no mention that a purchase is required.

When I finally completed my card and went to redeem it, I was told by a staff member named Johnathan that I couldn’t get the free roll unless I bought something. They told me that the owner Yoyo and co-owner John are not good at english so that could be the case why it wasn’t mentioned on the stamp card. When I received the stamp card this condition was never mentioned by the server who gave it to me and anywhere on the card. It feels misleading and unfair.

I asked about it but instead of honoring the card, they insisted on the extra purchase. It’s disappointing, especially when customers spend time and money to earn rewards in good faith.

If you’re collecting stamps here, be aware that the “free roll” apparently isn’t really free. It’s a bait.

My wife says it's her all time favorite.

I popped in again for a late lunch. Got my new regular, salmon Sashimi, among other things. It was delicious, as always. I really love the decor, and the service was right on it. Not the cheapest sushi in the area, but well worth it!

top_reviews.content: I discovered this spot on TikTok and was drawn to the story behind it. Plus, the sandwiches looked incredible! I ordered their most popular sandwich, the 'Call Me Serge,' along with a chocolate chip cookie, and both exceeded my expectations. The sandwich is served hot on fresh Acme focaccia and features a Calabrian chili orange jam that adds a sweet-and-spicy kick to the rich, cheesy flavors. The cookie was absolutely amazing, with the ideal balance of chocolate and buttery flavors. It is definitely worth the hype! I arrived at noon on a Saturday and only waited about 5 minutes in line to order and another 10 minutes for my food. I’ll be back to try more of their creative sandwiches.

Wow!! Incredible sandwiches and sitting outside on the patio was the icing on top.
We ordered a Lebanese Caprese and Call Me Serge for late lunch after playing in the park for a couple of hours. Perfectly toasted and easily top 10 sandwich ever had.
Came during a school kid rush, which felt like my youth. Rush of kids, backpacks left at door, long - but fast - line, and then silence returned. Helpful and friendly staff. 5/5!
Super nice service and a delicious sandwich. A few seats in the shade along the sidewalk, but also a quick walk to Dolores park

During my first visit I ordered Timmy Tim - the brand-new toaster oven was clearly still experimenting with its creative direction. The sandwich came out dry :)

Came back to try the Ode to Barbar and this sandwich completely reset my sandwich standards.

• Rotisserie chicken – thick-cut, incredibly tender, seasoned just enough to let the texture come through

• Greens - sautéed until soft and silky so they literally melt into the chicken

• Toum - a Lebanese garlic sauce with a hint of lemon that ties everything together.

• Lebanese pickles - brighter and cleaner than the German kosher pickles I usually swear by. Crisp, lightly acidic (they cut the richness perfectly!)

• Crispy potatoes – add amazing salty crunch.

• Acme green onion slab bread – great choice for this sandwich

You can tell Ramzi puts real thought and care into these sandwiches. The balance of flavors is intentional, and it shows in the lunchtime crowd - people clearly come from all over the city for his sandwiches.

I also had the Turkish coffee brownie- I was advised to eat it cold and I did have one cold bite. I accidentally “tenderized” the rest of my brownie and turned it into a molten lava cake - STILL DELICIOUS! This place is on my permanent rotation list. 10/10 stars ✨

Really cute small corner store nestled in Dolores that's known for their specialty sandwiches. I came in around 1pm on a weekend so they were very busy! Expect wait times to be about 30-45 minutes after ordering. I got the Call me Serge which is one of their signatures, they also had a large variety of creative seasonal sandwiches that all sounded delicious. My sandwich came out super crispy and the flavors came together very well. Definitely hits the spot especially if you take it out to eat at Dolores park!

If you think poke is all the same… this place will reset your standards.

I got a half salmon / half tuna bowl with half sushi rice and half brown rice, and everything about it just hit. The fish was insanely fresh (and I’ve fished over 30 fish before), like that clean, melt-in-your-mouth kind of fresh where you can actually taste the quality, not just the sauce. The balance between the sushi rice and brown rice was perfect too… you get that comfort + a bit of texture, which I didn’t expect to matter as much as it did.

And I’ve been to a lot of poke spots (easily 15+), so I don’t say this lightly, this is one of the few places where you can tell they really care about what they’re serving. Nothing felt rushed or generic.

Service-wise, just as impressive. Everyone was friendly, fast, and actually attentive, which is rare. And Michael (the owner) stands out - super welcoming, clearly passionate, and you can feel that energy in the whole place. It’s the kind of spot where the owner being great actually translates into a better experience.

Overall, this is one of those places you go once and immediately know you’ll be back. If you’re even slightly into poke, don’t overthink it — just go.

top_reviews.content:
Homeroom always serves up the ultimate comfort food for every occasion!

I frequent Homeroom for takeout, yet I never get bored because they have such a wide variety of flavors to try from. When I’m feeling something simple but aromatic, I go for the Gilroy Garlic. When I’m wanting something a little more refreshing, the Elote Mac or the Garden Pesto Mac hit the spot. And sometimes, when I really just need something to warm my tummy and my soul, the Kogi Mac is what I reach for.

Also, how could I forget? The sides! If you’re not quite in to Mac and cheese, at least come try their Bacon Brussels & Buttery Garlic Green Beans! The Brussels can also be ordered without bacon. I am definitely guilty of just getting an order of Brussels sprouts and taking it home to eat with a hot bowl of rice. Since it’s such a crowd pleaser, you could even bring it to a potluck!

I have yet to dine in at the Berkeley location. But I’ve waited in the lobby for my takeout. It’s spacious, modern, and sleek. There’s also a play area for the little ones! Perfect spot for a family dinner.

I do also want to mention the Vegan Mac! Even though I don’t have a picture of it, I still think about it often. When Trader Joe’s doesn’t have their butternut Mac and cheese in season, the Vegan Mac here is a great dupe! Smooth and creamy without the dairy.

Came here knowing it’s famous for mac and cheese. We ordered the mac and cheese as well as a burger and fries. The mac and cheese was good, portions were generous, and we couldn’t even finish it.

The burger and fries were awesome too, juicy and satisfying. Very kid friendly place, which makes it a great spot for families. Would come back again.

I didn’t know we had something like this nearby! We had the Elote mac, the Patty Melt, Garlic parmesan fries, and Cheddar bacon ranch fries and EVERYTHING WAS SO GOOD!!! The workers are all super nice and we had an amazing time, 110% recommend❤️

3/6/2026*
We were craving mac n cheese and came back to try some of their other flavors.

This time we ordered the Kogi Short Rib Mac and the Garlicky Bacon Mac.

Both were delicious. The kogi short rib mac had a sweet flavor from the kogi bbq sauce, along with Gouda, pecorino, scallions, garlic butter, and sriracha. If you like a little kick of heat, this is your go-to.

The garlicky bacon mac came with lots of bacon, garlic gouda, and pecorino. It tasted cheesier compared to the short rib mac. If you are a bacon lover, this is your go-to.

10/14/2024
We discovered Homeroom through a podcast interview with founder, and was surprised to find they're based in the East Bay, so we decided to check it out. We ordered an elote bowl as a starter and the seasonal special BBQ pulled pork mac and cheese. Unfortunately, the elote bowl arrived after the mac and cheese. The corn was soft and sweet, with delicious cheese and pepper powder that added a great kick to the flavor. The BBQ pulled pork mac and cheese was equally impressive—nice and cheesy, with surprisingly juicy pulled pork.

Our new favorite spot in the bay for a mac&cheese craving, which is way too often lately. Unbeatable prices and the creamiest mac. Vegetarian options galore and so many flavours, it’s impossible to choose.
Luckily they have a mac&cheese trio- great for sharing and date nights. That and a glass of wine? Score and score.

Staff and GM Erick are all so friendly and caring, we just wanted to hang out with them! Can’t wait to come back for one of their event nights- what an amazing spot.

top_reviews.content:
Ceviche: Very flavorful and refreshing
Cabrito a la Norteña (goat special): The meat was tender, juicy, and absolutely delicious
Mazamorra (rice pudding with pineapple and purple corn): Very tasty and perfectly balanced and not overly sweet

Everything was made fresh. The staff were also very friendly and helpful with the order. Will definitely come back to try more dishes again!

The food was AMAZING. As a Peruvian, this food is authentic and the staff was incredibly kind and helpful. Tasted just like my grandma used to make. This place is such a gem! Highly recommend to anyone passing by the area or who live here

This place is low-key the best Peruvian food in Oakland. It's a hole-in-the-wall place and the dishes punch well above their weight. We got the ceviche and the goat and both were definitely $45 plates selling for half that!

I went in for lunch and I’m not sure what the issue was, but the service was pretty much nonexistent. At the 45-minute mark, we still hadn’t received a glass of water. The people at the table next to us told us it had taken 1 hour and 45 minutes to get their food, and we also noticed a 20-minute lag between serving two patrons their dishes at the same table.

I was super thirsty, and the people around us were warning us about the long wait. We told the server we were going to head out and to cancel our order, and the server said nothing.

I was under the impression they were understaffed and maybe the server didn’t usually work front of house? There’s no way this restaurant would be in business, let alone expanding, based on the experience we had, so maybe it was just a fluke. We ended up walking to another restaurant, and I was honestly so relieved when they handed me a glass of water.

I live really close by, love Peruvian food, and was so excited to give this place a try. I plan on giving it a second chance and actually trying the food, and hopefully I can update my review then. I’m always rooting for local restaurants, but the service was just so terrible and slow.

This hidden gem offers many exceptional Peruvian ceviches -

Lomo Saltado is as tasty and soft leather-tough as you’d get in Peru at your boyfriend’s grandma’s casa.

top_reviews.content:
Oakland’s street food scene did not disappoint on my first visit. I tried the Brussels sprouts with aioli sauce, and they were absolutely awesome. The portion size was generous for the price, making it feel like a great deal.

What really stood out was the texture—they were perfectly crunchy, which made every bite satisfying. The aioli added a nice creamy contrast, though I do wish there had been a bit more of it. Still, the flavor was spot on, especially considering the dish was healthy and didn’t rely on added salt.

One tip: eat them right away to fully enjoy that crispness. Overall, a simple yet delicious street food find that I’d definitely recommend.

I would definitely come back and try some garlic wings

I’m kind of disappointed in myself for never trying this place before. So far, it has my favorite garlic noodles in the Bay, the food tastes so good, and the Hawaiian shrimp tastes extremely good. I’ll definitely become a regular. Also, the service was great.

Five stars across the board for this establishment. I've been eating at this restaurant for years now, and I'm never disappointed. I've tried everything on the menu with the exception of the vegetarian options, and I am always a happy customer. All their sauces or dressings rare housemade.

When ordering takeout your food isn't soggy or wilted when it arrives because of the way they pack your food. Fries stay crispy, tacos stay crispy.

Staff is extremely friendly, and accommodating for anything you ask for. Parking can be a little challenging because its downtown unless you pay for parking.

Quality food, made with love! I highly recommend trying and promise you will become a regular patron.

Very neat and chill indoors but also has great outdoor seatings too, this restaurant has delicious lunch and quick bites to enjoy.  I had their garlic shrimp and rice and it was devoured up quickly.  I love how much garlic they put in it,I can eat the garlic sauce they have with the rice alone.  The order came out fast and the staff was super friendly .  Definitely will swing on by again and check out the other items on the menu.

Myself, and two other people were dining in on a rainy night. One of us was vegetarian, and there were options for her. Portions were a decent but not huge size.

Dishes we got:
Hawaiian shrimp and garlic noodles (amazing!)
Fried fish taco
Brussel sprouts
Vegan taco

Their server/person who took our order at the counter was kind and helpful. They had some seating but all were high tables and bar stools. It was chilly due to the weather and doors being partially open. Their bathroom door lock was broken, but getting fixed soon. It definitely felt like a better place to order takeout from.

Overall the food and service was great. Atmosphere alright.

top_reviews.content: Left Door is an absolutely beautiful and sophisticated space. The atmosphere feels intimate and special, and the service was excellent from beginning to end. The caviar service was a standout, beautifully presented and delicious, and the other snacks were equally enjoyable. It is a wonderful destination for cocktails, small bites, and an elegant night out.

Wow wow wowza! Cannot give this place a high enough rating for ambiance, vibe, staff, food, drinks. One of the only bars that gets it in SF. The perfect level of feeling elevated but cozy and just the right music to bop or vibe too. Incredible food and drinks menu. Like YASSSSS🙌💗👌 the caviar shots😘👌chefs kiss😚

Had my impromptu birthday here and 50+ people showed up unplanned! And Billie, Emma, Cali and Joe literally were a CLASS ACT. Fantastic bartenders as well!

I highly recommend throwing a closed event here because they did the most amazing job and this was a free for all. Can only imagine if it was reserved.

I also highly reccomend this spot for a happy hour, date night…. Post dinner night cap…legit all the THINGS. It is JUSTT RIGHT. In ALL THE RIGHT ways. Been dying to find a place of this quality level coming from NYC, LA. Thank you left door for making SF that much better.

I will be back and spread the word and love always 😘🌸😘🌸💗 you guys are IT!

My friends and I were leaving and waitress with tattoos and bangs told us “that wasn’t very nice”, and we were confused at what wasn’t nice so we asked her what she was talking about and she literally would not tell us??? We were genuinely confused, the only thing I can think of is we left our two cups on a table? Did not know that was an issue. Deadass would not tell us what was “not very nice”. Very weird and entitled environment. Just trying to get drinks and felt judged the whole time. Cool vibe tho I’ll give them that

Everything was perfect. Friendly and super knowledgeable bartender who made us some of the best cocktails I've ever had. The food was really special too - fine dining in a relaxed atmosphere, with every detail carefully attended to, and yet with no pretentiousness.

This is my first Google review because I have never felt so inclined to write a review. I just want to say how utterly disappointed I am in this place and the experience my friends and I had yesterday. We were all so excited to try the drinks and indulge in the caviar service to celebrate the 4th in the city, but we were practically turned away through no fault of our own.

My friend had our reservation set for the evening of July 4th, and yet, through no fault of our own, Left Door’s reservation system magically had it set for July 5! Genuinely, what? Our email confirmation clearly showed that we did not make the booking error and that it was their system error. Their idea of making up for it was offering to let us hang out at the bar. Mind you, there were 7 of us and there was one seat left at the bar. I’m sorry, do you expect us to split that one remaining seat 7 ways? 🤣

We were so excited to try this place out because we had heard such good things. However, even though this reservation mix-up was their system error, no effort was made to find an alternative, and no offer to make up for the mistake was extended. My friends and I had made our 4th of July plans days in advance around coming to Left Door, and this mix-up left us scrambling to find food when every restaurant in the city had at least an hour-and-a-half wait time (god bless Walgreens). I expected more from an establishment that has earned a reputation for stellar customer service. I understand that mistakes happen, but it was so annoying to have them try to make up for theirs with a simple “Sorry, ladies.”

I would recommend that you double- and triple-check your reservation before going to this place, because their system will just happen to move you around to a different date, and they will “Sorry ladies” you out of the place😭

top_reviews.content:
We’ve moved to the area and have been looking for a local sushi spot that’s in east bay and would definitely recommend this place.

We made a reservation and were seated right away. The restaurant was not busy when we went ( 6pm) but as the evening progressed it filled up ( it’s a cozy spot, so seating is limited) but never felt cramped.

We ordered the shishito peppers that were probably some of the best I’ve had, ever albite spicy! The tangy, citrus, roasted goodness topped with generous lashings of bonito… YES PLEASE!

We order 4 types of sashimi, 5 pcs each.
Kampachi, toro, yellowtail and salmon. All super fresh, and well cut for the portions.

Ordered 5 rolls ( 4 pictured)
Lion king
Warrior roll
Kakui/ Naruto roll ( not on menu)
Spicy tuna
Cali roll.

The outstanding rolls were the Lion king, warrior and kakui.

Service was quick, the head sushi chef knew what he was doing, and the service was on point!

Definitely recommend!

The food was just okay and definitely not worth the price. We waited about 15 minutes before anyone came to take our order, which already made the experience frustrating.

We ordered the premium omakase ($64 for 10 pieces of sashimi), but it was not even cut in proper sashimi style, which was very disappointing. At that price point, you would expect much better quality and presentation.

We also ordered the beef short rib, which was very salty and quite tough.

For a group of three, the total came close to $200, and none of us are big eaters. The portions were small and the taste overall was nothing impressive.

Overall, the experience did not live up to expectations. There are definitely better options for the same price.

This is my new favorite japanese spot. It’s on the nicer side, great for a date night or a celebration. The food is delicious, from appetizers to mains and rolls to desserts. We’ll be coming back for sure!
Friendly service. Tasty sashimi with good oil flavors. The miso dashi fries was surprisingly addictive. Good relaxing atmosphere.
Great atmosphere and we really enjoyed the rolls. My favorite was the Four Seasons, but my wife really enjoyed the no-rice fresh taste of the Kakui roll.

top_reviews.content: I’ve been to this restaurant quite a few times and I always order the fish. This time I got the Branzino, and it was spectacular! The portion is HUGE, and honestly, they always have the best fish in SF. Simply grilled, perfectly cooked, and absolutely delicious. We’re always treated so well, too. We love coming here and will definitely keep coming back. 10/10! ⭐️ :)

Brought friends who weren't from SF here! Walked in without a reservation and got a table right away. Strange bathroom set up: two separate just-a-toilet rooms and the sink outside.

Food was good! My favorite dish was the bottom right in the photo (something with black truffle). Was hoping for something more revolutionary for the price, but it was overall very tasty.

Service was okay. Waiters were a little aggressive with refilling our waters (splashed all over the tables and me) but it was busy so understandable. They did accommodate us for a non-alcoholic mojito, which wasn't on the menu which was kind. Overall a good experience. Probably wouldn't come again until $30 pasta isn't a big personal expense.
Very good Italian pasta! We had appetizers and two different past and desserts and honestly I can’t pick which one was better!

Romantic, trendy spot on Valencia. I’m surprised at how easy it was to get a Saturday night reservation the day-off, but it was to my benefit — would definitely come back for dinner with friends before a night out.

Great wine list, excellent pastas and the market fish was super filling. My personal favorite was salty, rich mushroom ravioli, but others really liked the red sauce.

Barberio Osteria has been on my "want to try" list for a while, so I was excited to see them on the Restaurant Week lineup. My husband and I decided to go and noticed there was plenty of reservation availability online, so we opted to walk in. We were seated right away, although next time I might book ahead since it looked like reservations offered more options (e.g., counter vs. standard seating). No big deal though - it was fun watching the hustle and bustle of the open kitchen (even if it got a little warm near the wood-burning grill).

Since there were two of us, we were able to try almost everything on the RW menu (everything except the cappelletti), while also getting glimpses of other dishes being prepped in the kitchen. As a pasta fan, I was especially excited for the pappardelle with bolognese, and it did not disappoint. Everything we tried was delicious — shoutout to the tonno e fagioli too!

Even though it was a busy night, the staff were attentive and quick to respond. I'm looking forward to coming back soon and trying some of their non-RW items!

Comfort food. No frills, but cooked well. Friendly staff.

Several friends suggested we dine their due to the low cost and decent food.  Interior was pretty old school. They also have a Chef Specials: Choice of 3 items for $39.99. Prices have gone up but less than other spots. 3.8 on Yelp, 4.1 on google.

top_reviews.content: I had a fabulous experience overall. Ken is attentive and entertaining without being overwhelming, the staff were pleasant and overall service was excellent. The space is clean with minimal aesthetics, and intimate sitting at the beautiful raw wood counter. The starter Tsukidashi was absolutely fabulous, and there were some memorable and impeccable cuts of fish like Hamo, Shimaaji, Isaki etc. Snow Crab Ankake chawanmushi was so comforting and umami perfectly balanced. Ken is a super talented chef and I look forward to returning to dine there.

We recently celebrated my partners birthday at KEN and had the most phenomenal night. We had a lot of interaction with all the staff which made the experience memorable and far from boring. The food from start to finish was out of this world and every flavor profile was *chefs kiss*. There were details throughout from the bites, to the dishes, to the sake pairing... couldn't have asked for a better evening. I had asked if we'd be having Uni because it is my absolute favorite and not only did Ken deliver, I think it was the most wonderful bite of Uni my mouth has ever tasted. Would definitely go back in the future for another celebration and have already recommended it to several friends!

P.S. the drink coasters are all handmade + gorgeous and I really wanted to buy it but they are 110% not for sale.

KEN is a hidden gem in San Francisco and absolutely worth the effort to book. I used to work in SF before the pandemic and was a regular at Kusakabe, where Chef Ken previously worked, so I was excited to finally visit his own restaurant.

The restaurant itself is very intimate, with only a 7-seat counter, which gives it a warm, homey feel. Chef Ken’s hospitality truly stands out. He took the time to introduce every fish, explain how each piece was cured, and recommend the best way to enjoy it. He was also incredibly patient and accommodating with allergies and preferences, and somehow managed to make all seven guests at the counter feel equally cared for throughout the evening.

As a Hong Kong native, I especially appreciated that Chef Ken was happy to chat with me in Cantonese, which made the experience feel even more personal.

The quality of the food was outstanding. Some of the highlights for me were the Hokkaido scallop sashimi, the otoro nigiri, and especially the nodoguro add-on at the end, which was unforgettable. Every course reflected the passion and attention to detail Chef Ken puts into his cuisine.

Because of the small size of the restaurant, reservations can be difficult to secure, but it is absolutely worth planning ahead. Parking in the area is also limited, so I would recommend taking a rideshare or using Muni, which conveniently drops you off right at the corner.

The best way to describe Ken is like having a good friend, who is also a chef, prepare a exceptional food experience for you. The space is beautiful and intimate. The staff were very attentive and kind. The menu was expertly crafted. I appreciated how there were warm dishes interspersed with the cool sushi and sashimi, as the weather is cold at this time. Makes me wonder what menu chef would come up with for spring as the weather changes.
It was an amazing experience, one you'll be thinking about for a while after. Absolutely recommend.

Dinner at KEN was one of those rare experiences where everything is considered, not just the fish, but the rhythm, the temperature, the ceramics, the space, and the human touch behind it all.

Each course felt perfectly calibrated: cool against warm, delicate against rich, flavors building intentionally. The fish itself was exceptional, pristine and expressive, but what stayed with me was the balance, nothing  felt rushed.

The setting is intimate in the best way. Friendly, welcoming, and deeply personal, without ever feeling performative. You feel cared for, guided, and included. The attention to detail extends beyond the food to the vessels it arrives in; beautiful, tactile pieces that elevate each bite and make the entire experience feel composed and intentional.

The sake also deserves special mention. Thoughtful throughout, and the dessert sake is an absolute must, unexpected, rich, and the perfect closing note.

This is the kind of meal you keep thinking about days/months/years later. A meal that lingers in memory, not just on the palate. Thank you, Ken I’ll be thinking about this fabulous evening for a long time to come.

Mela Bistro is something special. This is the kind of place that reminds you what a gift it is when food, hospitality, and tradition come together so effortlessly.

The soup was nothing special—it lacked the depth and richness I expect from a good Korean stew. It ended up tasting pretty one-note.

Service was fine, but food-wise, nothing really stood out enough to make me want to come back soon.

top_reviews.content: Used to be my favorite Indian place. The curry was so thick and flavorful, but something changed recently. Overall, it’s a nice spot with friendly service and a good location, but the food and drinks left something to be desired.

top_reviews.content: Went on a rainy Saturday and there was several spaces of parking in the lot adjacent to restaurant. It did not come with hominy sadly, and I suppose with the highest price I've ever paid for a bowl, I might have reconsidered my order. The tripe in the Menudo was just slightly more soft than I prefer but objectively, this was the bowl of flavorful Menudo that my cravings desired. The Lengua (beef tongue) burrito was huge! That said there was more rice than beans in the burrito and I wouldn't be mad if it had more beans instead. The lengua was cooked perfectly and was seasoned well. I can't believe I'm saying this but in a tongue burrito, I think less cheese works the best. Corn tortillas included in my order and salsas were delicious. Overall, I enjoyed the food. Review for walk-ins only. great food, but this place is essentially ghost kitchen. It took them 40 minutes to make our meal in an empty restaurant on a Friday, because they are flooded with delivery orders. It would have taken an hour if I hadn’t bugged them about jumping our in-person order in front of six more delivery orders.

I wish they’d warn customers before they sit down about the wait, or just close dinner service during peak delivery hours.

DO NOT COME HERE unless you want to wait 2 hrs for your food. I came in on Friday at 7pm and there were 3 other tables seated. We ordered and it took 2 hrs for our food to come. I also had to ask for hot tea 3 separate times.

There was a grand opening sign outside. Perhaps they have new owners, but the service has really gone done. You’re better off going to a different location.

We absolutely LOVED the fish selection. Every piece was delicious and fresh. The fish to rice ratio was fantastic and presentation was on point. The quality did not diminish due to it being packaged to go. Great price of $38 for 10 pieces. We called in our order on a Sunday at 1pm and it was ready within 20 minutes

We have been ordering here weekly for the last 5 years and have seriously spent more than $20k since living in the area. Since they reopened, it has been abysmal how bad they’ve gotten at timing pickup orders. We’ll regularly place an order, be told a time to pick it up, and then have to wait 30+ minutes after arriving.

What finally broke us is that the past 10 times we’ve ordered, we’ve tried to prepare by calling an hour ahead and still ended up waiting 1hr+ after the time they told us the order would be ready. Mind you this is weeknights at 5-6, not just on busy weekends or holidays.

At a minimum, they should know how to better manage expectations and timing at this point, especially since nearly every customer who comes in while we’re waiting seems to be complaining about the same thing.

Good sushi, but the pickup experience has become unacceptable.

Everything is made to order here which is always a plus for me since it is quality over quantity and I never mind the wait since I am a very patient person. top_reviews.content: I have taken 20+ classes with Truffle Shuffle since May 2020 and I can’t recommend them highly enough! Truffle Shuffle was our "go to" during COVID for a place to have fun and virtually learn to cook Michelin quality meals with high quality ingredients.  We then fell in love with all of the different chefs - now it feels like a family.  We attend one or more classes a month and absolutely love them.  If you calculate out what it would cost you to purchase the ingredients and make the dish on your own w/out guidance OR eat out at a Michelin star restaurant, you will quickly find that the prices are amazing.  I love these guys and I love the food and cocktails that we make!

It is a little expensive, but the VALUE is WORTH IT! Chefs are fantastic, ingredients are high quality, and the results are delicious!.  And, with shipping included, it is such a great deal! The classes are engaging, fun, and the energy coming through the screen from Tyler, Jason, and Sarah are so wonderful!  We need good energy and love in these crazy times. Food brings us all together.  Their mission of giving back to their community is phenomenal. Thanks so much, Truffle Shuffle!  Can't wait for things to calm down, so we can come visit in person! (Some of the pics include things we added for our meal)

Have done private events and joined in on several Sunday cooking sessions and our dishes are AMAZING every time. Truffle Shuffle has been one of my favorite parts of quarantine! A friend hosted a small group class for us where we made truffle mac and cheese, and I was hooked. I NEVER cook – like go to the grocery store a handful of times a year and live on delivery – but had a blast! They made it so easy to cook these gourmet dishes with the simple box of ingredients and clear instructions with the online classes. And the final dishes taste INCREDIBLE! I've felt so much more empowered to try getting into cooking and it's been a really fun at-home date night. I've also loved the creative cocktail pairings – we made a classic penicilin with their truffle honey that may be my new favorite drink. The vibe of the classes is really relaxed, social, and fun. Also big props to their customer support; I only had a snafu with an order once (I'm on my fourth class), and the team had such excellent service! This has truly been one of my highlights during such a crazy time, and I look forward to cooking with Truffle Shuffle on the weekends.

top_reviews.content:
Located on the Bay Street Plaza in Emeryville, on the second floor next to Barnes and Nobles. Saucy Asian is a Korean fusion restaurant. It’s a trendy place and is pretty busy all the way to closing time. We came in today after shopping at the new Tokyo Central across the street for a late dinner. We ordered at 7:58pm and did not receive our food until 8:26pm which was quite long wait for what we ordered. There is some indoor seating as well as outdoor seating.

As for food we ordered:
- Saucy Asian Bowl
- Saucy Asian Fries
- Island Style Poke Bowl (combo: half tuna/half Salmon)

All the food were good, have no complaints, but have had better elsewhere. Overall, if we’re in the mood for their food, we would come back.

I ordered the Saucy Aisan Poke with a mixed green base, salmon and tuna. It came with spicy marinatade, carrots, slaws, white onions, kimchi gochujang aioli. The fish tasted good, but the overall flavor was a bit too overwhelming. I could mostly taste the sauce in my poke. The portion was also a little for me, so it didn't feel very filling.

I also tried their sweet and spicy chicken wings, which were really delicious, it was juicy and flavorful. I highly recommended getting their fried chicken!

It was easy to place an order, you can either order in person or use the kiosk machine. The staff were really friendly and attentive.

I finally decided to give Saucey Asian a try, and it definitely lived up to the hype!

The food came out fresh, hot, and packed with flavor. Every dish we ordered was well-seasoned, the portions were generous, and you can tell they don’t skimp on quality. It’s one of those places where everything on the table makes you want “just one more bite.”

The atmosphere was casual, fun, and perfect for grabbing dinner with friends or family. The staff was friendly, welcoming, and made sure we had everything we needed throughout our meal.

If you’re in the Emeryville area and craving flavorful Asian comfort food, I definitely recommend checking this spot out. Great food, generous portions, and a great overall experience. I’ll definitely be back!

I got the Bulgogi Bowl and Island Poke Bowl. I personally found the bulgogi a little too salty. The Island Poke Bowl had quite a bit of rice, and the rice was a little mushy for my preference. Overall, it was an okay meal, but there’s definitely some room for improvement.
Even better than I expected. Very saucy yet feels healthy at the same time. Great fusion-style Korean food. I want to come back to dine in and enjoy some soju with the food.

top_reviews.content: What a discovery! The service is beyond impeccable. Very attentive, making sure the diners' needs are met without being intrusive. The servers are engaging and explain all dishes. Every bite of each dish was delicious! Well prepared and presentation is beautiful. I highly recommend all the dishes we enjoyed. However, the Spicy Tuna Crispy Rice is an ABSOLUTE MUST! I was hesitant about the Corn Tempura, but it was an unexpected treat. The restaurant is quite small so I highly recommend making a reservation.

My husband and I had dinner here tonight, and overall it was a really memorable experience. We’ve traveled quite a bit and tried sushi in many different cities, including around the Los Angeles area where we live and have our favorite spots. So when we visit a sushi restaurant, we tend to evaluate everything as a whole — price, quality, service, and of course the flavors.

For dinner we ordered the Mango Tuna Roll (which was our first time trying a mango-style sushi roll), the 8-piece Omakase Nigiri, a Double Toro Roll, two pieces of Otoro, and a hot sake. With a 20% tip included, the total for the two of us came to $163.50, which honestly falls within the average range of what we usually spend for a sushi dinner like this. Normally we might pay around $120–$130 depending on the place, sometimes a little more if we add an extra item or two.

The portion sizes were pretty standard. Not unusually large, but not small either — similar to what we’ve experienced at many other sushi restaurants.

Where this place really stood out was the depth of flavor. The quality and balance of the ingredients were excellent. At one point I actually caught myself closing my eyes just to focus on the taste, which is something I almost never do. The preparation felt very refined and the flavors were elevated, rich, and memorable. I would describe it as delicate portions with very elevated flavors.

Because of that, I’m giving this place 5 out of 5 stars.

This is the kind of restaurant that works perfectly for a nice dinner with your partner. It’s not necessarily a place where you go wild ordering everything on the menu like at a taco spot. Instead, it’s better to be thoughtful with what you choose and enjoy a few well-crafted dishes. You can easily have a special, enjoyable dinner here without going overboard.

Definitely worth visiting if you’re in the area and want a quality sushi experience with refined flavors.

The only thing I felt was missing was a small welcome miso soup. In some sushi restaurants we’ve visited, they serve a tiny cup of miso with a couple pieces of tofu as a warm welcome. It’s a very small gesture, but it creates a nice first impression and adds a sense of hospitality to the experience. Considering the quality and pricing of the menu here, a simple welcome miso soup would fit perfectly with the overall dining experience.

Food is amazing. Service is fast.
I like that you can see the one preparing our sushi and rolls, you know that it is prepared clean and properly. The Japanese-inspired ambiance ties it all together. On the expensive side.
Foods were tasty, ingredients were fresh. Service was friendly and attentive. Dinning area not really big.  Recommend make reservation on their website first. Nigiri order by pieces.

This spot is truly a hidden gem in the San Bruno neighborhood! The vibe is warm and welcoming, making it perfect for a casual dinner or a special night out. The sushi is fresh and flavorful, with a solid variety of traditional rolls and appetizers. If you’re into omakase, they offer that as well—an excellent option for those who want to sit back and enjoy the chef’s selections. Definitely worth a visit if you’re in the area!

top_reviews.content:
I craved for Japanese food so I thought I give Shokudou a try.  Well that place could make a name for itself but not for a Japanese restaurant. The few things that were Japanese, the Asahi beer which was very good, sitting at the bar and watching the sushi chef preparing the food and maybe the Japanese cartoon characters on the wall.  The chef is trying to make the food Japanese but certainly has a long way to go.  From the top
The Agedashi Tofu, the tofu was alright but the soy sauce was so salty that it over toned the tofu completely. Also the bonito flakes were rather old and didn't crumble on the hot tofu.
The miso soup, was bland and lacked flavor, almost they should use some of the tofu sauce and it to the miso soup to balance both out.
Now to the rolls and maki, I stayed away from the nigiri.
I tried the Spicy scallop, negi sake maki, hamachi avocado naki, spider roll and the golden dragon roll.
The only thing that worked was the spicy scallop, it was well rounded yet light.  The spider roll wasn't crunchy, the golden dragon roll could be alright but the slice of lemon again overtones the salmon.
On the service, complete lack of attention of detail, all dishes came out at once , which is strange. Only one of the dishes had ginger, nobody picked up empty dishes, no followup, no attention to detail.  And that makes it everything but a Japanese experience.

The food here was definitely the highlight. Everything tasted pretty fresh and flavorful, and overall I would rate the food about 4/5. The ingredients seemed good quality and the dishes were enjoyable.

However, the service was a bit disappointing. The staff did their job, but they didn’t feel very welcoming or friendly. There wasn’t much interaction beyond the basics, and with the price point here, I expected a more warm and attentive experience.

The atmosphere was also just okay. It wasn’t fancy or fine dining, but it also didn’t really give a strong Japanese vibe either. The environment felt a bit mixed and not very memorable.

Overall, I’m giving 4 stars mainly because the food was good. If I rated the experience as a whole (food + service + atmosphere), it would probably be closer to 3/5. Still worth trying if you care mostly about the food.

It’s a good stable family restaurant that serves the Bernal height resident. I wouldn’t consider it as an izakaya though, they are lack of that vibe. It’s kids friendly and the day we went, there are 7 kids inside the restaurant. Be prepared for a lot of screams and avoid dinning hour/Friday night if you are scared of kids. The food is decent, not the best I had in town but it is alright. We ordered cheesecake and they gave us ice cream on the house, so that was really nice :)

Overpriced sushi for not fresh or flavorful nigiri. $43 special for one of each of eight special nigiri, each not fresh, almost warm for some reason, and overall nowhere near worth the price tag. Servers were nice but service was very slow, when the restaurant was not packed.

With smartly decorated interior, this Bernal Heights Japanese izakaya / sushi bar / yakitori-ya is a welcome option on Cortland. The menu however lacks focus, reflected in the generally mediocre delivery on dishes.

While agedashi tofu came well-crisped (a feat), the sauce too salty. The chicken karaage, far from bite-sized as it should be and smothered in an odd tapioca-like batter — sticky on the inside. The spider (soft shell crab) roll, had an odd funk — not sweet, but more attune to gym socks.

Unfortunately, a place I very much wanted to love, but left a bit disappointed.

I’ve been talking about these tacos nonstop ever since my first visit because, honestly, it has been very difficult to find tacos as amazing as these anywhere else. These are truly some of the best tacos I’ve ever had in my life. I'm talking a variety of tacos as well-birra, carne asada & chicken tacos. The crispy tacos were also incredible.

Terrific Mexican food. Carnitas were some of the best I've had in years. Chile Relleno had tons of flavor. Enchiladas were very tasty, highly recommend while being extremely affordable!

If you’re craving an authentic Mexican dining experience, look no further. From the moment you step in, you’re greeted with warm hospitality and a cozy atmosphere that immediately makes you feel at home.

The star of the show for me was the tilapia — absolutely incredible. Perfectly seasoned with a blend of zesty, smoky spices, it was cooked to perfection: flaky on the inside, crisp on the outside, and bursting with flavor. Paired with the rice, which was light and aromatic with just the right amount of seasoning, it was a meal that felt both satisfying and refreshing. It’s clear the kitchen uses fresh, high-quality ingredients, and the dish balanced bold flavors with subtle nuances that made each bite exciting.

The rest of the menu looks just as tempting, but after this tilapia experience, I’ll be hard-pressed to try anything else next time! The drinks are refreshing, and the vibe is lively yet relaxed, making it perfect for a night out or a casual dinner.

If you haven’t been here yet, you’re missing out. This place takes Mexican cuisine to a whole new level — I can’t wait to return and explore more of the menu!

I don’t think I could’ve asked for a better experience at State Flour Pizza Co, and that includes the 30 minute wait time for a table. This is the kind of place that hires the neighborhood teens in the summers while still taking the time to source all fresh ingredients.

Consensus for favorite was split between the mushroom-sausage and green goddess pizzas, but the margherita and hot honey pepperoni were almost as good. Apple salad gave some much needed freshness to the table.

This pizza place is as perfect for a family dinner as it is for a first date, and is just as likely to have a table of college friends as it is a post-conference debrief. That’s because it’s designed for the community, so it attracts the community.

The state flour salad was beautifully done too!

All in all, we were extremely impressed and would wholeheartedly recommend this place. 🍕

Come for the Vibe, Stay for the Spectacular Duck Tacos

Tucked away as a charming hole-in-the-wall, Frank Grizzly’s is the kind of accidental discovery that reminds you why exploring a new neighborhood is so rewarding. The atmosphere hits the perfect note of casual comfort—boasting ample seating, a nostalgic soundtrack of '90s hip-hop and R&B, and an incredibly warm, hospitable energy driven by the father-daughter duo at the helm.

While the menu anchors itself in classic comforting staples like burritos and nachos, the execution is where the kitchen truly shines. A sweep of the taco menu—spanning chicken, traditional birria, and a decadent cheese birria—reveals a masterclass in flavor. Each tortilla arrives packed with remarkably savory, juicy, and vibrant fillings. However, the absolute crown jewel of the meal is the duck taco. Rich, perfectly rendered, and intensely flavorful, it is a standout dish worth traveling for. While the pricing sits at a slight premium, the caliber of the ingredients and the sheer execution make it entirely worth the splurge. Frank Grizzly's comes highly recommended.

We dined in and got 3 of our go-tos to test the food first:
1. Steamed soup dumplings (aka xiao long bao aka siu long bao aka XLB)
2. Pan fried buns (aka shen jian bao aka san jin bao)
3. Shanghai style stir-fried rice cakes (aka Shanghai chow nin go)

Everything was too sweet for our tastes, and we found a hair in one of our dishes (CNG). Not expecting anything but an argument for a complaint at a restaurant of our people, we removed the chunk with the hair in it and said nothing. We just won't be back.

The XLB were juicy but sweet and too gingery. The ginger is supposed to be julienned into the vinegar dipping sauce, where you can control the amount, not inside the meat where you can't.

The SJB were so sweet that they were still sweet microwaved the next day, which usually removes the sweet taste from too-sweet SJB in my experience.

The CNG, aside from also being sweet and hairy (a description I like to hear about dogs and cats, not food), were a little too soft and not chewy enough. I was disappointed but not surprised there were no shiitake mushrooms in it, which is a staple ingredient in this dish in Asia and in New York and Las Vegas Chinatowns, but for some reason is either missing or skimped on in California (Bay area, LA/San Gabriel Valley, San Diego). The hair was not only not the right length or texture (and in one case, color) to be one of ours, it was also buried enough that it couldn't have landed on the dish while at our table or even while being brought to our table. It had to have happened in the kitchen or hitched a ride in an ingredient.

The pancake was crispy and excellent, with a side of old-fashioned hot sauce that complemented it very well. The veggie dumplings had unique fillings and tasted a little peppery, but very well made. The buns were delicious and the skin was fluffy, although I wouldn’t mind it being a more chewy. Service was good and they give you a big kettle of hot tea when you sit down, so I appreciated that. This has been consistently the best BBQ restaurant in San Francisco for me.  Possibly best in the Bay Area but can’t confirm until waymo extends its service area.  My favorite items are the pork ribs, hot links, half chicken, and the corn bread.  The seasoning on the pork ribs is INCREDIBLY flavorful and perfectly spiced.  The half chicken is juicy and tender, falls right off the bone and has a great balanced flavor.

When I’m doing chores around my property—closing the window or buzzing in the Amazon driver—I like to set pork ribs in a circle around the brim of my cowboy hat for storage, reaching up to grab one whenever I’m ready to eat, just like they do in Texas.

This spot fully earns its stars.  The pricing is very fair, and the service is friendly, quick, and reliable.  They’ve brought a much needed upgrade to the local BBQ scene.

This was my first time ordering from this restaurant after seeing it on a show “ Check Please Bay Area”. so I had high expectations. Unfortunately, the experience was very disappointing.

The biggest problem is that the Signature Overnight Smoked Brisket (the main item I ordered) was completely missing from my order. That was the main reason I placed the order, and not receiving it was extremely frustrating.

The ribs that did arrive were cold and not properly cooked. I’ve had BBQ ribs many times, and honestly these were below average.

The potato salad was just okay. The cornbread was actually pretty good and probably the only highlight of the meal.

Overall, this was a very disappointing first experience. Missing the main dish and receiving cold ribs is unacceptable, especially for a place that gets attention on TV.

The barbecue pulled pork was absolutely outstanding—tender, juicy, and packed with rich, smoky flavor that melts in your mouth with every bite. The meat was perfectly seasoned and slow-cooked to perfection, striking a great balance between savory depth and a hint of sweetness from the sauce.

What really elevated the dish, though, were the pickles and pickled red onions. Their bright, tangy crunch cut through the richness of the pork beautifully, adding a refreshing contrast that kept each bite exciting and well-balanced. The acidity wasn’t overpowering—it complemented the meat instead of competing with it.

Altogether, it’s a thoughtfully crafted combination of flavors and textures that feels both comforting and refined. Easily one of the most satisfying barbecue dishes I’ve had.

top_reviews.content:
NoodlePanda is a low key new-ish (I believe they just crossed the one year mark) spot off the corner of Taraval and 21st Ave, a location that always seems to struggle to keep a steady business. Given that, I hope more people give it a try because the food and service were both good overall. Ordering is done through a QR code at each table, and payment is handled in person at the end, though worth noting they have a 2 card maximum for splitting bills in case that mattered.

The menu is mostly centered around noodles, in both soup and dry form, along with several popular side dishes and appetizers like lamb skewers, dry braised string beans, and garlic cucumber salad. I ordered the spicy beef tripe dry noodles, and while the bowl was packed with tripe and the mala flavor was definitely there, I wish I had been able to swap in a different noodle. Something about the thin, round noodles just did not quite work for me. I think a flatter or wider noodle would have soaked up the sauce better, or even the knife cut noodle they are known for, which I did try in another dish and thought was much better.

The garlic cucumber salad was a standout for me. It was rough chopped into big chunks, super flavorful, refreshing, and a pretty generous portion, even as part of the Traditional Hand Pulled Beef Noodle Combo. The dry braised string beans were a miss for me since they had very little sauce and not much char, so while there was a good snap it lacked both flavor and the wok hei I was hoping for. The lamb skewers were also not my favorite, as the meat tasted a bit overcooked and were way too heavily seasoned with the same dry rub I find most Chinese restaurants used for skewers regardless of protein, but it could certainly just be a matter of preference.

That said, the staff were friendly and the food was good enough that I would definitely give it another shot, though I think I would just stick to a more specific subset of their noodle soups on any future visits.

top_reviews.content: ...so glad we finally tried this place. seriously, i walked in not expecting much and walked out already planning my next visit. i had the lasagna and it was amazing, so chessey and rich but not heavy at all. my freind got the chicken parm and she couldnt stop talking about it. honestly, even the bread they bring out is bomb, we had to ask for more. the service was really sweet too, the lady at the counter even remembed my coffee order from the first time i came in. its authentic italian food made by people who actualy care.

For the third consecutive year, I pre-ordered my Thanksgiving meal from C’era Una Volta Kitchen & Catering, and once again, it did not disappoint. The entire process, from ordering to dining, was seamless.

I picked up my meal the afternoon before Thanksgiving. Everything was securely packed in easy-to-heat containers, making the holiday cooking process entirely stress-free.

Every dish was flavorful and thoughtfully prepared:
Portobello Tart with Puff Pastry & Brie: A truly delicious start to the morning. The combination of crispy pastry, flavorful mushrooms, and brie was a definite highlight.
Turkey Breast "Imporchettato": The main course was a tender turkey breast beautifully wrapped around sausage. This hearty portion was generous enough for two people. It came with classic, well-executed sides, including mashed potatoes and gravy, sweet potatoes, mushroom stuffing, and fresh focaccia.
Bourbon Pumpkin Cheesecake: A delicious conclusion to the feast, providing the perfect holiday flavor profile.

I highly recommend C’era Una Volta. Not only do they make holidays easy and flavorful, but their consistent quality is worth visiting throughout the entire year.

I had an incredible experience with C’era Una Volta.  My family and I were out of options on Thanksgiving and stumbled on this gem.  It was incredible and one of the best Thanksgiving dinners I’ve ever had! The owners were so nice and welcoming and I will absolutely come back in the future.

If I could give C'Era Una Volta Kitchen & Catering 10 stars, I would without hesitation! From the moment I walked in, I was welcomed with the kind of warmth and hospitality that only a true Italian gentleman like Rudy, the owner, can provide. Meeting Rudy was a highlight in itself—he's not just passionate about his craft, but also genuinely cares about his customers' experience.

But let’s talk about the food because it’s nothing short of spectacular. I put my trust in Rudy and let him choose my lunch, and it was one of the best decisions I’ve ever made. He crafted a salad with toast points
that were both fresh and flavorful with fresh Mozzarella and tomatoes with a balsamic dressing that was amazing, setting the stage for the main event: ravioli with a meat sauce that was simply out of this world. Every bite was a testament to Rudy’s dedication to authentic, high-quality Italian cuisine.

The service was impeccable, the atmosphere cozy and inviting, and the food—oh, the food! Rudy is an absolute gem, and his restaurant is a must-visit for anyone who loves great food and an even greater dining experience. This place is an instant favorite, and I can't wait to return! It's a small space for dining in but worth the out-of-the-box experience.

We haven't patronized C'Era Una Volta for over a decade, for good reason. We have high expectations with Italian food and unfortunately they did not improve with time.    The best part of the meal was probably the bread, served with a warm, mustardy aioli that was both smooth and pungent, creamy but not spicy.  The beet salad was so uninspiring, we could have done better putting a few pkgs from Trader Joes in a bowl and assembling something ourselves. Our daughter's kids' sausage pizza was served with mushrooms (wasn't mentioned on the menu), husband's melanzane Parmigiana was decent, but my Tagliolini alla Senese was a let-down. There was a giant clump of uncooked, unseparated noodles, and the sauce was supposed to be a chianti beef sauce but all I could get was tons of herbaceousness from a heavy hand (I forgot if it was thyme or rosemary, it wasn't pleasant). The service was very lackluster (took a while to take our order, arms reaching across the table instead of going around to serve/clear, no one checked on us after our main courses were delivered). I truly wish they would improve because I would throw my money at a good Italian reataurant without a second thought (yes, we've been to Italy, from Roma up to Venezia) but it isn't this place.

Best carne asada and lengua (tongue) burritos in the whole east bay. Lengua is not easy to make but Beatrice knows how to perfect it. I’ve been coming here since I was 13 which is 19 years in 2025. I remember when the burritos were 5 bucks! The recipe has never changed. They also have the best green hot sauce that go great with the burrito. They also have really good menudo. The ribs plate with red sauce is also one of my favorites. I’d say everything on the menu won’t disappoint. She makes everything homemade, even the tortillas.

This place is a hidden gem. I have been going here years and the staff are always great. They communicate with you well and serve you in a timely manner. The food has always been consistently great. They have the best carne asada burritos in Oakland hands down.

Vegetarian burrito here was at the bottom of the taste scale we have experienced so far: All ingredients tasted at least day-old, the lettuce was yellow and dry, rice-beans-cheese were mushed together beyond recognition, and the salsa was way too spicy (we had asked for something mild, like pico de gallo). In addition, they had no black beans, just pinto or refried, and my son ended up with stomach cramps all evening.
Minor irritants were that it took comparatively long for the burrito to be done (especially since no other guests were waiting to be served at the time); the outdoor table at which we waited was sticky with food leftovers (the server had cleaned other customers' table earlier - why not this one?); the burrito then arrived so piping hot that we had to take it home instead of eating it on the spot; and it was way overpriced, at $14 for a blech basic burrito and a small agua fresca.
Speaking of which, that "agua fresca" came in a styrofoam cup (not a green business practice) and had very little strawberry in it, just some artificial-tasting flavor in lots of water. Hm.
Not at all what we would have expected from a place with otherwise good reviews, in a Latinx neighborhood. Quite disappointing!

Sitting in the parking lot at 7:30 in a Tuesday and they are closed. No note on the door, nothing online about why they are closed. What a waste of time.

Nice job guys, won’t be back.

Won't be going back.

top_reviews.content: The first time I been here was when I was picking up for a delivery and I knew I had to come back to try this place out. Finally I got the chance to come here and give it a shot. Upon arrival, the place was filled with great aroma coming from their sandwiches which in fact made my appetite grew even more. At the moment the staffs were busy preparing existing orders, but was still nice enough to take my order. They offer breakfast sandwiches, paninis, regular sandwiches, specialty sandwiches, salads, a kids menu and much more to choose from. Everything here is made to order which is always a plus for me since it is quality over quantity and I never mind the wait because I am a very patient person. You can dine in, order for takeout, place an order by giving them a call or order for delivery via a delivery app. I chose to eat there because I was really hungry, and I got to enjoy the air conditioning along with watching T.V. The staffs here are very welcoming, well trained, and understanding where it made my visit a satisfying and issue free one. I highly recommend this place to all sandwich lovers, if you are in need of a quick bite, to anyone willing to try something new or if you just so happen to be in the area to check them out. I definitely will be back to tryout the other delicious options they have to offer.

I had an amazing experience at this place for the second time. The salads were incredibly fresh, with a wide variety of toppings and dressings to choose from, making it easy to customize exactly what I wanted. Each ingredient was crisp, flavorful, and obviously high quality, from the vibrant greens to the perfectly ripe avocados.

The service was just as impressive as the food. The staff was friendly, attentive, and genuinely enthusiastic about helping customers make the best choices. They took the time to explain the menu and made great recommendations, which really made the experience enjoyable. I’ll definitely be back to try more of their creative combinations. Highly recommend this place to anyone looking for a healthy, delicious meal with top-notch service!

2025 update. No line today at lunchtime. My salad was a Chef's Salad, one scoop of chicken salad and tuna salad with turkey, ham & cheese $17. This tasted OK. I usually get the pesto salad but I didn't see it. The scope of chicken salad was surprisingly good. I was a bit hungry still after eating this. Luckily I got a crepe down the block as a back-up in case I was still hungry.

Original review: The Salad Place makes good salads/sandwiches. They aren't as good as the other places in the city but this is Outer Mission. Healthy options are limited. For lunch I had their turkey sandwich on dutch crunch $12 + avocado $2.50 and a ceviche $9. Everything tasted fresh. On the sandwich, I would have preferred more avocado, other than iceberg lettuce and some sort of garlic or pesto sauce. This was good, but tasted plain. The ceviche was also good. I like how they use bigger shrimps. Service was excellent. Good job staff at The Salad Place.
Really cute little spot with delicious sandwiches, salads, juices and coffee. The service is wonderful and easy to order. Had a great experience and will definitely be back.

top_reviews.content: Brunch just how I like it. Great cafe for brunch. The pancakes were cooked just how I like them, fluffy and full of flavor. Not stingy with the chocolate chips 😀. Loved the country fried steak. I like my sunny side up eggs runny and am sure they would have been, but unfortunately they placed the steak on top of the eggs which  cooked the yolk. My daughter's Mass chicken sandwich was good, chicken slightly on the chewy sode. Fries were crispy and seasoned well. Definitely coming back to try other plates😁.

I love this place.  It's a solid corner spot for good eats and it's great for breakfast and brunch, especially when you have guests that a visiting.  It's a great place to bring them. My picky daughter loves the chicken nuggets there.

Glen Park in San Francisco was recently highlighted nationally as one of the coolest neighborhoods in America. The commercial core is small, with long‑time independent shops, cafes and a tight‑knit community, often referred to locally as “the Village.”

One of my favorites is Glen Park Cafe. It just has a great vibe all around. And the food is pretty awesome for sure. It seems like they have the "it" factor.

It's right on the corner with enough windows and exposure to the morning sun to make it feel "breakfast-sy" cheery. Or is it the playful menu they have, or the coolness of the patrons, essentially the next-door neighbors you'll have for the next 45 minutes or so, ones you actually enjoy.

You'll love the food and I've no doubt you'll come back. Maybe next time, you'll be my neighbor at the next table.

See you there soon!
Just happened upon this delightful cafe today while visiting the area. Highly recommend it. Great food, excellent service, very clean, nice area.

Call me Goldilocks because this restaurant was "just right". The   size of the cafe was not too big and loud, very quaint and perfect for a relaxing breakfast. The menu was nice standard American fare with items that you don't normally see like Banana Pudding French toast. The price was very fair for the quality of food; which is a nice surprise when dining out in today's prices. The service was excellent. This is a great local spot close to the Bart station that I will definitely make a habit.

top_reviews.content: We were in the area visiting relatives and it was our anniversary, so we wanted to find somewhere nice, and the reviews were right. It's a beautiful building, the service by Tony, our waiter, was wonderful, and the food was delicious. I started with the Escarole Salad, which had apples, grapes and more, it was a nice start. My wife had the shrimp cocktail, which came with 8 shrimp (she loved it). My entree was the Rack of Lamb, with 2 double-chops, sauteed kale and navy beans. It was very good, albeit a little more well-done than I prefer. My wife had the Caprese Pappardelle Pasta, which was delicious. And we finished with the poached pear dessert (which came with a candle for our anniversary). The prices were very reasonable for the quality.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
I can’t recommend Julia‘s Restaurant enough! The food is absolutely wonderful, the service is top-notch, and the atmosphere is wonderfully private — perfect for a date night or a quiet catch-up with friends. Every dish feels carefully prepared, and the staff truly knows how to take care of you. This place is a gem. I’ll definitely be back!

Overall, it was a great experience. The restaurant is inside of a historic hotel and the overall vibe is peaceful. I went by myself and the staff were very attentive.

For my dinner I ordered the corn soup as an appetizer and the mushroom risotto as my main dish. I also ordered the chocolate bread pudding as a dessert. The corn soup needed more seasoning. It was a little bland for liking. The risotto was flavorful and yummy. I will order it again. Their bread pudding was good, however it was a little hard. Overall I give the food, four stars, and the atmosphere and service, five stars.

This was our second time dining here and it was just as good as the first time. Classic French cuisine, nice cocktails, and wonderful service. We were lucky enough to have Tony as our server again this time and he's an absolute gem of a man.

My friend was in town visiting from Tokyo again and specifically requested to dine here, after I took him here last year.

If you're looking for a pleasant spot for a date or to catch up with a long-time friend, this is a lovely place for that purpose. You'll be able to have an actual conversation because it isn't a loud venue and the architecture is lovely.

This review is a bit tardy.  My wife and I had a wonderful anniversary dinner at Julia’s Restaurant in the Berkeley City Club in August.  From the beautiful ambience to the excellent service to the scrumptious food, we give Julia’s high praise.

We went early and enjoyed walking around the historic building “ooh’ing and ahh’ing” over the stunning architecture and ornate detailing everywhere.  Morgan’s Bar & Lounge has the most gorgeous stained glass Tiffany lamps (see photo) that fit the decor well.

Our waiter, Adrian, was friendly, attentive, knowledgeable about the menu, and fun.  The food was beyond amazing.  We both had filet mignon (perfectly cooked medium rare) with bearnaise sauce; it was tender and succulent (see photo).  The accompaniments, sweet potatoes and spinach, were all delicious.

We had never been to Julia’s before and now look forward to going there again for another great, special meal.

top_reviews.content: This banh mi was delicious. The crust was light and crispy, not tough to bite into like the bread at some other places. The cold cuts were tender and flavorful; the pickled veggies added just the right amount of crunch and tang to balance the meats; the sauce brought everything together without turning it soggy over time. The portion was also excellent for the price. Would eat again!

This is hands down the best bánh mì I’ve had in San Francisco.

The meat-to-bread ratio is incredible — the sandwich is generously packed with beef and super satisfying. The flavors are beautifully balanced: a little sweet, a little spicy, with a bright tangy kick. As you keep eating, you can even notice the fresh aroma of lemongrass. Absolutely delicious.

I’m very particular about bánh mì baguettes — they shouldn’t be too thick. I like them light, airy, and shatteringly crisp on the outside. The bread here is exactly how it should be, and it even looks beautiful. Everything just works. I’ll definitely be coming back.

What a surprise from this spot. One of the best bahn mis I've had in months. I eat a lot of bahn mi.

top_reviews.content: I stumbled upon this spot randomly for dinner on a Sunday night, which is arguably one of the best nights to come. It has a cool vibe and was my first time having Japanese bbq, which apparently comes from Korean bbq. On Friday-Sun they have a set menu, and weekdays à la carte.   This is one of my new favorite restaurants. The owner Andy Chiang cares deeply about the food and provided and exceptional experience for his diners. Every dish was delicious and the sake selection was also great. Easily one of the best meals of all time, and I've dined at multiple 3 Michelin star restaurants and this is my 8th year as a yelp elite member.

Simply the best. The staff were incredibly friendly and made the whole experience feel so special. My friend and I had such a great night here. You can really tell they care about the quality of the meat, and they shared so much knowledge about how everything is grilled and prepared. Amazing food, amazing service, and such a memorable experience.

Dining at Yakiniku Shodai was an outstanding experience from start to finish, seamlessly blending top-tier Wagyu cuts with thoughtfully crafted side courses. The curated tasting menu progressed beautifully, featuring highlights like delicate Australian Wagyu beef tongue topped with scallions, heavily marbled Japanese A5 Wagyu paired with fresh wasabi and kelp, and standout creative dishes like a rich Wagyu chawanmushi and a perfectly seared scallop over crisp nori. Paired with chilled Masumi sake, the exceptional meat quality, artful presentation, and well-paced menu make Yakiniku Shodai a top-tier destination for Japanese BBQ lovers. Definitely a must try.

This place truly exceeded our expectations! The food was outstanding, perfectly seasoned, beautifully plated, and bursting with flavor. You can tell the ingredients are fresh and thoughtfully prepared.

The service was just as impressive. Circle our chef was warm, attentive, and made sure we had everything we needed without ever feeling rushed. The atmosphere was inviting and comfortable, making the whole experience even more enjoyable.

Highly recommend to anyone looking for excellent food and top-notch service. We’ll definitely be returning!

Glad I chose this spot for my birthday night with my girls. We got the reservation a few days ahead. It seems to be quiet popular. The chef and the host gave us such an impressive experience. The food and service are what I would expect from an authentic upscale Yakiniku place. I also enjoyed the conversation with the chefs and the host.

The chefs here cook the meat in front of you and serve to you directly. All the meats are cooked to perfection with just the right amount of seasonings.

I’m glad they don't over season the meat nor over complicate it like other American upscale Japanese restaurants.(I enjoy food creativity if they taste good and if the complexity makes sense but sadly a lot of upscale restaurants failed to make it makes sense to me.)

Reading some other reviews on the bbq smell got me a bit surprised. I wouldn’t mind if the upscale bbq restaurant smells like a bbq place, so I am surprised ppl complained about the smoky smell in this kind of restaurant.

Thank you Chris and Circle for the fun experience!

Mediocre overpriced Gyros at this food court stand.  Good service. Small wait time for food. Bustling food court environment. Not recommended.

Jayna Gyro is inside one of the best 'food courts' in the Bay Area.  The food was really tasty and fresh.   I had the Gyro: The pita was soft, ingredients were piled high so I used a fork to get it manageable enough to then eat holding the pita.  Their version of fries (more like potato pieces) were delish...garlic & feta.  Wife really liked the falafel wrap.  My only knock's were things likely out of there control: 1) the prices have gone way up in.  In 2021 price for the Gyro was $10 and in 2025 it's $15.50...but to be fair most of the places in the food court were $15-$20 for a meal; and 2) the table we were at was 'sticky', like it was 'cleaned' with wet rag that hadn't been washed in days.  We tried another table, same result.  These are large shared tables that the whole food court uses, so it's not a knock on Jayna, but maybe they can lean on Public Market.

I really loved eating at Jayna! The people working are always so friendly, helpful, and the food is delicious, light, and fast. Many options to choose from. Flavors are amazing, too! This is my favorite spot at the Public Market.

This location offers mediterranean food, and gosh, it tastes good. Really good. As someone from around that area, I can say that I’ve been here multiple times, and each visit never fails to impress my tastebuds. (Being located in the Public Market, it can be pretty loud though.)

I went to check out Jayna Gyro in Emeryville because I love Tarla’s in Napa, CA.  Jayna Gyro is located in The Public Market which has a common food hall/court.  Public parking was free and easy to find a spot.  There are a variety of cuisine options.  Nestled amongst them all is Jayna Gyro.  It was quiet when I arrived and I did not have to wait in line.  I ordered the Beef & Lamb Gyro.  The gyro was beautiful and snuggled up inside the box.  I love the idea that there is something for everyone at this local spot!
