I was craving Teo Chew noodles, so I placed a take-out order. I got the dry mixed Original Teo Chew noodles with vermicelli noodles. It came with prawns, fish meatballs, pork meatballs, chicken, pork slices, minced pork, and pork kidney. Oddly, the noodles were not fragrant, but the other ingredients tasted great, especially the pork kidney, which was very tender. However, the pork meatballs were a letdown; they were dry with a hard texture.

12/30/24
I've been a frequent visitor to the Teo Chew noodle place in Oakland, so I was really curious to try Mi. I had the original Teo Chew noodle soup, which comes with prawns, fish meatballs, pork meatballs, chicken, pork slices, minced pork, and pork kidney with vermicelli. We also tried their Pork Kidney noodle soup.

The soup base is clear and rich in flavor, and the texture of the noodles is spot on. The pork kidney was not overcooked and had a great texture. One notable difference compared to the place in Oakland Chinatown is that Mi adds fried minced garlic on top of the noodle soup, which I really liked as it brought an extra layer of flavor to the dish.

However, I understand why some people think it's a bit pricey. They are cash-only, and two bowls of noodle soup came to around $40 before tipping.
New management helmed by the second generation improved everything!  I crave the Teo Chew Style noodles weekly and this place now holds the crown for best in the bay!

If I come back, I would try the soup noodles.

Visited for the first time last week. Was excited to get an Italian sandwich with cold cuts but was disappointed with the experience. There were only two people working, and at times only one, because the other would be dealing with the phone or delivery people who would come in. So it was an overwhelming environment with a bit of a wait since there were many people ordering and waiting for their food at once. We ordered two sandwiches, and one was completely different from what I ordered. I didn't make a fuss about it because the two workers there seemed swamped and I did not notice until I went outside to eat, plus I ate all the items in the incorrect sandwich so it was fine. I was a bit disappointed at how thick the cold cuts were sliced. I've had many Italian sandwiches and generally feel like authentic sandwiches should be sliced thin.

The thing that really bothered me though, however, was that the sandwiches were being made without gloves on. I understand the area is likely sanitized, but there were other things being touched, like the tablets, etc., so I feel like doing other things while making the sandwiches shouldn't happen, nor should handling food without gloves.

I only wish the deli itself lived up to the promise of the canopy — inside and out, it feels more like a warehouse where sandwiches are assembled. A few more tables, some chairs, and a more welcoming setup would make a big difference for anyone hoping to sit comfortably.

We stopped by Shaka Shack for breakfast and had such a nice experience! The food was delicious, comforting, and had that wonderful homemade, homey feel that makes you want to stay awhile.

We tried Da Kine, Kimchi Cucumber, Kalua Pork, and Kai’s Plate with Beef Ribs Kalbi—everything was flavorful and satisfying. The Kalua Pork was especially delicious, with that tender, savory taste that pairs perfectly with a hearty breakfast. The Beef Ribs Kalbi were also a favorite—tender, flavorful, and packed with that delicious Korean-Hawaiian flair.

The Kimchi Cucumber added a refreshing, tangy crunch that balanced out the richer dishes perfectly.

The atmosphere at Shaka Shack is relaxed and welcoming, with a cozy, homey feel that makes it a really pleasant spot for a morning meal. It feels like the kind of place where you can enjoy good food without feeling rushed.

Delicious food, comforting flavors, and a laid-back Hawaiian feel—Shaka Shack is definitely worth a visit for breakfast! 🌴🍳🤙

Sad they got rid of the witch legs 😆
Had to try this new place, and had my hopes up high. The ube wasn't ube'ing, it was very purple but the flavor was minimal in the waffle and the cream topping in the matcha ube iced latte (it tasted like butter).

I had a side of sausage with over easy eggs, and the ube waffle plate with the latte, grand total $35. A little pricey. The sauce on the waffle was good, and the fruit pieces were really good and tasty (especially with the waffle topping sauce).

Cute little “shack” spot in the corner. They only have 13 tables. 5 inside and 7 outside in their patio. Make sure to find a table first then order inside. Entrance is on the sidewalk side. I accidentally almost entered through the back where the parking lot is lol. We shared the big kahuna loco moco which is perfect for two. I wanted to try alittle bit of each meat options they had and knew I wouldn’t be able to finish it all. The hamburger patty and kalua pork was really tasty and good. I think the sausages were kinda overcooked though. My ube matcha latte looked nothing like the picture but was still very good. The ube Malasada was just ok. It could’ve used more filling. Overall it was pretty good and I’d most likely come back to try other stuff!

3.5 stars

Sat inside, simple decor. No music no tv, no ambient sound.. just cooks and staff chatting/flirting. Wasn't terrible, just weird.

Food was good, but expensive for actual quality of ingredients.

Waffles themselves are boring, but toppings make it. Cobb salad is a very weirdly composed dish, but still good.

Moco locos are obviously a well executed dish.

Little House was great but also kinda weird, and keeping Alameda weird is wonderful.

The food here is legit. Tastes like you would find in Hawaii, and good.
Staff is very engaging and they have a good selection of items.

The restaurant itself is very small. A couple of tables indoors, outdoor seating when it's available and a modest parking lot. Just be aware it might be better too to get takeout and try to sit if it's crowded.

top_reviews.content:
Visited from Oregon, stumbled upon this place looking for a spot to each lunch at.

Pictures: Tacos de lengua, caldo de camarón, & mojarra (fried fish)

Everything was delicious!!! Amazing authentic Mexican flavor, filling portions!

Would highly recommend eating here! Bonus:  clean place & Friendly staff💕

Burritos of heaven!! Toasted outsides with every ingredient FRESH and full of many colors of flavors. Fresh, fresh, fresh! Green and red salsas and fresh chips so good. Horchata yum. New favorite burrito place in SF.

What a delicious lunch we enjoyed here today. The manager, Tino, is so nice & made sure our meal was scrumptious.
Both the Baja Shrimp & Baja Cauliflower tacos were superb and my friend loved all the veggies in her veggie burrito.  Hands down some of the best housemade chips & salsa- we went through two orders!
I loved how colorful the interior and exterior of the restaurant was.  Will definitely return here.

I have been here multiple times since I moved into the neighborhood a couple years ago, but unfortunately I can no longer recommend El Jacal.

Twice I have been charged more than the listed menu price. When it happened previously I thought perhaps I had misinterpreted something but today I called them on it and pointed out the very obvious discrepancy. The cashier went to talk with someone else and then refused to honor the menu price saying it included tax, which was completely wrong and very obvious. They just shrugged it off and we walked out as a result.

It’s too bad because the food is solid, although expensive relative to the local competition, however they didn’t seem to care about their price accuracy and making things right with us. Therefore we won’t be going back.

There are so many Taquerias in San Francisco, it's rather difficult to try them all.  So I stumbled upon El Jacal while strolling through the Bernal village.  If I see lengua on the menu then I need to try it.  To me lengua is some of the best tender meat (if done right) one can eat.  Yes if done wrong you will get jaw muscle cramps before even swallowing one bite.  Well El Jacal knows how to make their lengua and it melted on my tongue.  Interesting thought that tongue could melt on your tongue...
We tried their tacos and quesadilla and there was plenty of food to share.  Their quesadilla is rather huge yet super tasty.  The tacos don't lag behind, they reminded me of the quality I'd get in Mexico City.  Thumbs up to this place I'd go back.

We loved this place! Did outdoor dining and tried the vegan roti with peanut curry sauce and vegan Malaysian stir fry noodles. Food was so good! The stir fry had a great mix of noodles and veggies and the spicy sauce was delicious.

If you’re in Alameda and looking for a spot that combines creative cocktails and small bites, Lemon Drop is worth a peek—especially on Taco Tuesday!

The tacos are fresh, flavorful, and generously topped with vibrant ingredients. Paired with one of their cocktails, it works!

The bar staff is nice and the ambiance is vibey, making it a perfect spot for grabbing a bite with friends, unwinding after work or watching a sporting event.

Highly recommend stopping by, especially for Taco Tuesday—and they have a cute fire pit!

Tasty and strong cocktails. I came on an empty stomach and I’m 194 lbs and was buzzed of of one cocktail.

Loved the Shrimp and Chicken Tacos. The lamb was not bad. The shrimps was done perfectly and I loved the heat from the sauce.

The cocktails are also repeats. If you like a smoky misquote scented bitter cocktail balanced budget perfectly by citrus do try the kingsman. Their Lemon Drop is what you would expect.

Nice R&B & Hip Hop music plays in the background but still quite enough for good conversations. Great service too. for a Thu night the place was popping.

We had a great time at Lemon Drop celebrating our friends’ birthdays! I contacted them ahead of time to reserve a table, and they were incredibly prepared and accommodating for our large group. The atmosphere, service, and thoughtful accommodations made the celebration feel extra special. The food, drinks, and Monday night crew were all amazing! Big thanks to everyone at Lemon Drop for such a special evening — especially Brandon and the woman who greeted us and got everything set up for our group earlier in the evening!

I love this spot. It's not quite a hole in the wall but definitely a neighborhood staple. The food and the drinks are always delicious. The service, not so much. It's not bad but it could be much better. Definitely not a hindrance to me coming back again and again

top_reviews.content: Delicious hot pot! Three of us ordered the Lau Pork Bone Marrow hot pot and really enjoyed it! Had plenty of pork and all the other offerings were delicious. We all took home leftovers. A friend ordered sangria loved it. Our server Kiet (Kevin) was kind, attentive, and so personable. He offered great insight into the menu and vietnamese hot pot.

Bacogai always hits the spot when I’m looking for a cozy meal that I can enjoy while catching up with friends or family. They serve traditional Viet food but they’re known for their Viet Hotpot!

I’ve been able to try all of their broths except the vegan broth. My go to is their Lau Oxtail because you get little bits of bone marrow in each oxtail piece! Each hotpot comes with a pre-set veggie & add-ins plate but the staff are always so nice and have let me substitute the ramen noodles for udon noodles before. I always appreciate how plentiful the mushrooms are and that they will replace the Sterno (heating mechanism) if it runs out. You can also get a broth refill! Usually the first one is complimentary but I’m not super clear on that policy.

Make sure you use the sauces they provide for each table! It’s a fun way to mix up the flavor profile of your hotpot. I always mean to ask what each one is… but I forget every time. Maybe it’s better that way—keeps a little mystery and makes me appreciate them all the more.

If you’re looking for something other than hotpot, you should try their variety of Banh Hoi (woven noodles served with mushrooms or meat and lettuce wraps) and Duck Goi-Slaw Salad! The salad is very refreshing and has that classic Nuoc Cham (Vietnamese fish sauce dipping sauce) flavor with the perfect balance of sweet and savory. When I first tried it, I was worried that the roasted duck would be too greasy for the delicate profile of the dish, but the fat was cooked out just enough to where the meat was still juicy and the skin was still light + crispy.

On my most recent visit, we placed a takeout order too—we got the beef luc lac garlic noodles and summer rolls. They were out of pork for the rolls, so they doubled up the shrimp. I do hope to try it the original way next time. The peanut sauce was a bit too sweet for my taste, but a little sriracha toned it down. The beef luc lac noodles were fantastic: super tender beef, perfectly cooked noodles, and an even coating of garlicky sauce.

I also have to say, the staff always make the experience memorable. They’re incredibly attentive and make sure everyone feels taken care of. The layout helps with that too—low barriers between tables mean they can see the whole dining area from the main counter. The space feels open but still cozy, kind of like being at a big family gathering.

Looks like they recently added clay pot dishes to the menu—I’ll definitely be back to try one soon!

Overall I liked the food here. Actually I was surprised by how much I liked their 2 appetizers. The duck salad was super refreshing and the shrimp crackers added a nice contrast in texture. It didn't have that much duck, but that made it taste lighter since duck is quite heavy. The spring rolls were crispy and tasty with the sauce. The 2 hot pots we got were good too. If you like sour flavors like my friend you would enjoy the seafood one (I really really liked the catfish in this one, the sour flavor cut the fishyness really well, and it was super tender!!), but I liked the oxtail soup too. The beef I ordered on the side was good but it was quite expensive. Very melt in your mouth.

My friend loves this restaurant and said their hot pot was really good so I came here with her.
Service was pretty good and the restaurant looks nice. I like the decor.

For food, we ordered lau ox tail (beef hot pot) and lau canh chua (sweet and sour hot pot). My friend said the beef hot pot was good, personally, I thought it was okay because I usually don't eat this hot pot flavor so don't quote me on this. As for sweet and sour hot pot, it has good flavor but not exactly excellent so I'm not sure if I'd order it again. We also ordered fried banana and a Vietnamese coffee. Fried banana batter has good flavor but it was quite hard. The good thing about it is it's not too greasy. Vietnamese coffee is just okay.

Overall, it's not bad but I think it's too expensive for an okay experience.

The flavors of the hot pot and the appetizers were good. They are individual pots, but for those of us who have smaller stomach so we can share, some people ate their own. The hot pots 🥘 come with their own set of vegetables to put in to the broth, but you can add on as much as you like.

I shared a pork hot pot with Lamb add-on. We also had shaken beef that my friend really loves but she said it was different here as it was not cubed and with rice. Another friend really loved the wrapped beef logs. He said it should come with more herbs, but otherwise enjoyed it.

Some people ordered wine and beer. Surprisingly, they also have sangria which one friend enjoyed two of.

Had to ask for chilies and they brought a condiment set of three. Thai chilies 🌶️always enhances all my meals.

We went with eight people. Made a reservation in advance. There was plenty of seating on a Thursday night.

All the ingredients were fresh and everybody enjoy the flavors although the price was a little higher than we are used to paying for Asian type of food. So best for special occasions, or people who really love hot pot.

Bathrooms are to the back on the right.  Plenty of parking 🚗 as it’s a strip mall Kind of situation.

Great spot for great roti. The coconut curry is very tasty, and the roti is nice and fresh. Coffee is also very nice. Vibe has a modern cafe feel. Very good place to grab a bite+drink and chat.

Aman Cafe is a cool place to go when you want a modern yet international breakfast or lunch in a hip location.   First of all they are a first class coffee shop serving an excellent brew, but they also serve Indian style Roti served American style with savory or sweet toppings, much as you might enjoy a crepe in an upscale American / French breakfast joint.

They also serve a delicious garlic noodle lunch, with your choice of chicken, tofu or shrimp.  The noodles are delicious with just the perfect texture.  You can accompany this with a Mango Lassi or from a choice of other smoothie type drinks.

The interior is impeccable and modern with progressive music featuring catchy beats.  The service is also excellent, friendly and prompt.  They have a good Internet connection and is a good place to settle down to do some work.

I was excited to find this interesting and unique location and highly recommend giving the place a try.
Vegan heaven! And my non-vegan adult children also enjoyed their roti’s cooked with butter. Fruit roti also delicious. Latte with any kind of milk including oat - yum. Delicious all around.
Ma sha Allah! Very tasty food! Eggs, sauted vegetables & paratha was very good. If you are in the neighborhood, definitely stop by. It’s very filling I couldn’t finish it all.

Got a turkey sandwich.  Although the pic shows a good sandwich, it’s really not that.  The sandwich was very loosely made.  A very messy, fall apart sandwich.  The turkey isn’t like boar’s head meat.  It was highly processed and slimy like the ones you buy packaged at the grocery store.  Very disappointing.

This is my 31st sandwich review (according to another app). Snack Sensei put Grand 7 on my radar (again), I’ve been hearing about it since I moved back from Hawaii in 2019. My apologies to the community because I truly did not understand how fire this place is.

It has officially taken my top sandwich spot. Sorry, Gherkin’s.

My partner’s job ordered catering, and lucky for me there was still an Italian on Dutch crunch at the end of the event. He snagged it for me. And let me just say: some might say a sandwich is a sandwich. Wrong.

The way the fresh ingredients and flavors marry together is just perfect. The bread to sandwich ratio is perfect and that catering order must have extra protein. The quality of the meat is far superior. And the mayo? Listen… if you know anything about Hawaii, you know we are serious about our mayonnaise.

The best part: I had half fresh on Wednesday and saved the other half for a field trip with my class on Friday and it was just as good. TWO days later.

Now I just need to find time to get there in person (limited hours!) because my friend swears they have the best chopped cheese he has ever had better than New York. If you’re looking for the best sandwich in the Bay Area, get here now.

This is the spot for a sandwich. Fresh, Clean, Quick and delicious. Staff is friendly and professional. This place must crank out hundreds of sandwiches every day. Highly recommend you give this place a try. Oh and Thursdays only they have there special tri tip sandwich which is also a must try.

The sandwiches are great here for the price and they use fresh ingredients. The Service is good but there is no real explanation for some of the menu items. First time here i asked a few questions and the answer were not clear. But the sandwich was great ill be back for sure.

He loved the atmosphere and Top Notch Friendly Service, and he noted how people seemed to genuinely enjoy having lunch there, from Longshoremen to a diverse crowd. You’ve made us fans of your family business, and we support great Mom & Pop establishments vs Franchise establishments. KUDOS TO HAVING A GREAT PLACE!

top_reviews.content:
The Presidio is gorgeous, Piccino Presidio’s patio is gorgeous, the indoor seating is gorgeous. Honestly, the whole place looks like it was designed by someone who really wanted you to Instagram it before you tasted anything.
We went big on the order — mushroom pizza, a burger with fries, a veggie scramble, and focaccia for the table — hoping the food would match the scenery. It did not get the memo.

The mushroom pizza was exactly what it sounds like: mushrooms, on bread, with feelings. One note, played very confidently. A little cheese diversity — anything beyond “the supporting cast to the mushrooms” — could’ve turned this from “fine” to “actually good.” Instead it just tasted like mushrooms had unionized and demanded top billing.

The burger clocked in at “acceptable,” which is a nice way of saying it didn’t offend anyone but also didn’t inspire anyone. The fries, unfortunately, showed up to the party, stood in the corner, and left early — a genuine miss.

The veggie scramble was the biggest gut-punch, because it tasted like something I already make at home for free, except here I had to put on real pants for it. The potatoes were as bland as they looked, and they looked like they’d already given up before hitting the plate.

Overall: beautiful room, sleepy food. This felt like a one-and-done tourist stop.

We recently visited Piccino in the presidio on Thursday night and had an impeccable dining experience. The coconut aguachili crudo with plums was the perfect balance Spice and sweet, the heirloom tomato salad was to die for.  My wife loved the roasted chicken while I thoroughly enjoyed the halibut with summer squash. We finished with a classic zeppole dessert.  Brandon did an an amazing job helping us make our choices!

Good ambience, friendly service, good options for vegetarians although the menu is comparatively small. The salads were very good especially the snap pea. Only 4 stars because of the slightly undercooked(close to aldante but not) pasta the bucatini also the focaccia was very salty (even for a salt sprinkled focaccia) Parking on the street is what we did and got lucky as it was a weekday.
They have indoor and outdoor seating.

Wasn’t expecting much but really enjoyed brunch here!! The fennel salad is a must try and exceptional!! We also got the focaccia and salsiccia pizza which were good. The banana muffin was a nice treat to end off on!

The vibes outside were so lovely and the decor inside was very nice. Service was good. Would definitely come back if I’m in the area. A great spot to enjoy the park after.

We had a great dinner here!  I got the Chiocciole pasta dish, which was fantastic -- perfectly done shells, tasty sausage, and the kale added a nice bitter kick.  My wife got the Funghi pizza, which was overflowing with savory mushroom and garlic, and the crust was nicely crispy and chewy.  Service was impeccable (our waiter was spot on with her recommendations), and the atmosphere is warm and inviting.  There's a big patio for outdoor dining, which must be great for brunch.  The location is awesome, on the edge of the Presidio.  Prices were what I would expect from this level of restaurant.  We will definitely come again!

I stopped by Hamburguesa Bar last night and had a pretty mixed experience.

On the plus side, getting seated was quick and easy. I only waited a minute or two before grabbing a spot at the bar. The service was easily the highlight of the night. The waiter was attentive without being overbearing, got my order in quickly, and handled everything smoothly from start to finish.

The ambiance is definitely what this place leans into. It has a retro, almost 70s inspired vibe with dim lighting and a nostalgic feel that is honestly pretty cool. You can tell that is where a lot of the appeal and hype comes from.

As for the food, it did not really live up to that same level. I ordered the chile hatch burger with regular fries and a Ghost IPA. Nothing was bad, but nothing stood out either. The burger was just okay, the fries were fine, and overall it felt pretty average. Mid is probably the most accurate way to describe it. Perfectly edible, just not memorable.

In the end, it feels like a place where the atmosphere carries the experience more than the food. If you are going for the vibe and a casual drink, it works. But if you are expecting a standout burger, this probably is not it. I am not sure I would go out of my way to come back.

top_reviews.content:
Aiso is a 100% queer-owned, vegan tapas restaurant on Castro. The vibe alone makes it worth a visit. Their playlist are all 2000-2010s hits. If you are millennials you will know all songs!! I was literally singing along the whole time 😍

The inside interior was beautiful, cozy with many plants and cool decors. I tried a few dishes and enjoyed everything:
- Oyster mushroom skewers: My most favorite, super flavorful, tender and perfect as a bar snack. No wonder everyone ordered them
- Jerk sliders: Tasty and surprisingly meaty but I felt a little burnt. My 2nd favorite and I also recommend you should order this!
- Beet tartare: This dish was exactly what I needed to balance things out. It was fresh, light, and refreshing
- Happy hour: Weekdays from 5-6:30pm, I grabbed a mini marteeni for only $6, very strong and paired so well with the heavy food

Overall, I was so full and left satisfied with both food and the experience. I could recommend this place more!!!!!

Nice atmosphere and kind staff. If you are planning to go at night, keep in mind that the kitchen might close earlier than the bar does.

WILL. BE. BACK. WOW!!! Truly an incredible experience. The service, the atmosphere and the ambience, the food, the cocktails we’re all exquisite. If I had the money, I would try everything on the menu in one sitting. But I will be back to try everything in increments. It was so lovely there and my friend and I just really enjoyed ourselves in that space. I can’t wait to try the udon and the peach dessert. I forget our waiter’s name, but he had a mustache and he was so above and beyond, and deserves all of the tips that you could ever think of. Pretty much all the staff deserves all the tips and handshakes and blessings that you could give them because they all were so nice and welcoming and great at their jobs. I really do love this place and hope it lasts for a very long time. Thank you Aiso!!!!!

An incredibly creative chef. This was genuinely some of the best food I’ve ever tasted. Every dish was a symphony of flavors, beautifully balanced and unforgettable. The food and the mocktails were both exceptional. I recommend this place to absolutely everyone, vegan or not. It’s truly a standout experience.

For more tips/plans on soulful exploration of places and plant-based/vegan food including in SFO please follow or DM me on @to.live.soulfully on Instagram. Happy to help!

The service and ambience were also great.

Aíso in the Castro District was absolutely incredible. ✨

San Francisco continues to raise the bar for plant-based dining, and Aíso is a perfect example of how elevated, thoughtful, and exciting vegan cuisine can be.

From the moment we sat down in the warm candlelit space, it felt intimate and intentional — rustic wood tables, beautiful plating, and a menu that celebrates bold flavors and texture.

The roasted cauliflower over silky purée with bright pickled accents was comforting yet refined.
The sautéed mushrooms with fresh herbs and lime were deeply savory and beautifully balanced.
And that golden soup topped with seeds, chili flakes, and fresh greens? Pure warmth with layers of spice and crunch.

Every dish felt crafted — not just “vegan,” but creative, soulful, and memorable.

If you’re in the Castro and looking for a plant-based experience that truly delivers, Aíso is a must.

San Francisco magic at its best. 🌿🍷

top_reviews.content:
The facility itself is beautiful and very aesthetic, but unfortunately the massages did not meet expectations.

I came here twice during their soft opening promotion for 20% off and tried both the traditional Thai massage and the deep tissue massage. For the traditional Thai massage, I had a male therapist, and it honestly felt like he did not really know what he was doing. The massage felt random and inconsistent. At one point, he moved my arm off the table and did not put it back, so there were moments where I felt awkwardly contorted on the table rather than properly positioned or supported.

Oddly, the traditional Thai massage still felt deeper than the deep tissue massage, but the experience was uneven. One side of my body would be worked on, but the same techniques were not repeated on the other side.

For the deep tissue massage, I had a female therapist. I requested medium to heavy pressure, but it felt more like light rubbing than a true deep tissue massage. There was nothing deep about it.

I could also clearly hear noise from the room next door, including another client fussing, which made it difficult to fully relax.

Overall, I do not plan on returning. My main feedback is that the quality and consistency of the massages need improvement. I recently had a Thai massage at a small hole-in-the-wall spa in LA for $60 that was far better than what I experienced here for $100–$130.

top_reviews.content: There has been a change of ownership and it is better than Cheung Hing. I'm not sure when they changed ownership but my neighbor told me about the food so I decided to try. The roast Duck is good, roast pork is standard and "white cut" chicken is okay... ask for extra ginger scallion sauce. I'd probably still go to Ming Kee or Lam Hoa Thuan for roast duck before I come here but if I'm in the area, I wouldn't be opposed to this spot.

TLDR: quality items at reasonable prices, under new ownership

We love their full soy sauce chicken, it is so moist and delicious. The red tofu with pork was also tasty with a nice gravy that goes well with white rice. The garlic pea sprouts had plenty of flavor and not too oily. I would highly recommend the chicken !!

Our duck and chicken rice plates were quite greasy. It seems like mostly regulars who speak Cantonese come here. My first time ordering in store and it was hard to know how to line up to order take out especially since there’s a row of chairs where people are sitting at randomly, so I got cut in line by a few older ladies, but finally after ordering, we waited around 30 minutes before we finally decided to go finish walking our dog first while I stayed to wait. Good thing we decided that because we waited around 40 minutes total! All we got were rice plates where the meat is what they’re chopping up by the front window, not anything that needs to be cooked up in the back so not sure what the wait was for. Was a bit too oily for my liking too.

The roast duck hanging in the window is definitely not the same one that was cut for you. The counter is very high, so you couldn't see which one he cut for you at all. The roast duck I got was smelly and not fresh. I don't recommend this place. If I really wanted to eat good food, I would definitely go to the one in Noriaga.

I’ve been looking for proper Peking duck in San Francisco for a long time, and Win’s Restaurant absolutely delivers. This place is legit.

The duck is fantastic — expertly prepared, beautifully roasted, crisp skin, tender meat, and done the way it’s supposed to be. No shortcuts, no gimmicks, just excellent execution. Exactly what I was hoping to find.

Service was equally impressive: attentive, friendly, and professional without being intrusive. You can tell they take pride in both the food and the experience.

We also ordered the beef organ soup, which was outstanding — rich, comforting, deeply flavorful, and clearly made with care. Not something you see done well everywhere, and they nailed it.

If you’re serious about Chinese cuisine and have been searching for a place that does things above board, this is it. Couldn’t recommend it more. I’ll absolutely be back.

top_reviews.content: Excellent dim sum!  Food is fresh, the Gai Lan was cooked perfectly!  The sea bass dumpling was excellent full of flavor. First time here and did not disappoint.  Will be back!

We recommend this restaurant wholeheartedly as it surprisingly has something different to offer to SF's Chinese restaurant scene. EVERYONE IN SF SHOULD COME AND TRY THEIR FOOD.

On top of that, the service is warm, attentive, and genuine. The owners are incredibly kind and clearly passionate about what they’re creating here, which just adds to the charm and heart behind every dish.

Maya Flor is a hidden gem, but it won't be hidden for long. Whether you’re a local or someone who appreciates great food and doesn’t mind making a bit of a trip, come here. Run, don’t walk.

The Kabuli Naan was like a nice potato stuffed and well flavored taste, great to eat just by itself too, but I definitely preferred the garlic naan.

top_reviews.content: This small cafe is on the alley directly across from the hall of justice and has four tables and another dozen seats along a wall. The menu is limited but the food is good and the quantity is large. There’s free water with glass containers you can bring to your seat. We ordered two bulgabi bowls, one a mini and the other the regular.  Both had broccoli, chap chai, brown rice and a lot of beef. It came with sauces as well. The food was good and a mini would’ve been enough for both of us. Service was friendly but the beef was a bit tough to chew. The place is large but spartan but clean.

Both got the cupbap. A decent portion of food but super average taste-wise, no sauce in it so pretty flavorless, atmosphere is so weird. Combination of Mexican Hawaiian Korean. None of the bowls come with kimchi which is crazy for a place called kiss my Seoul. Bulgogi just tastes and looks like beef teriyaki. Don’t think I’d ever come again and shocked at the other ratings.

Excellent food, portion, and service. Was in the area for a meeting and the price to portion ratio was excellent. The restaurant included a side of chicken because they accidentally input it wrong, even though I said it was okay.

Both the chicken and the beef bulgogi are excellent and I'd highly recommend them! Was fast to order and prepare!

Excellent cupbap with generous portion, taco was not great.

I had the regular size bulgogi cupbap ($16) and a single chicken taco ($5) just to try it. I've been meaning to visit this restaurant for years but it just wasn't convenient for me until today.

The cupbap container was filled to the brim and food inside was packed in. I didn't have breakfast today, so I was pretty hungry when I came here for lunch, but I still didn't fully finish it. I recommend ordering the mini size if you're not that hungry and you don't want to have leftovers.

Inside the paper bowl, there was plenty of bulgogi on top of broccoli, zucchini, carrot, cauliflower, glass noodles, and white rice mixed with a little bit of black rice — this dyed the rice purple-ish. It was garnished with green onion and sesame. Everything seemed to be seasoned with black pepper. The bulgogi was tender with some browning and tasted perfect. The glass noodles seemed to have been stir-fried with a sweet soy sauce. The vegetables still retained a bit of a crunch. The rice was a little mushy like it was just slightly overcooked, but I guess that's to fully cook the black rice.

I don't recommend getting a taco. There was a single tortilla. It was slightly toasted but still got pretty soggy from the salsa and chicken juices. The flavors didn't pair well. The chicken tasted like bulgogi and it just didn't work work well with salsa. The salsa verde and salsa roja were also a bit bland. You can get much better tacos in the Mission for less money.

There are plenty of seats here. There's also a small area with packaged Korean snacks like Turtle Chips.

Maybe the other dishes are good, but the smash burger was a huge disappointment. I saw a couple specks of red pepper in the aioli, I assume that’s the “kimchi.” Just a regular burger, not at ALL with any kind of discernible Korean influence.

top_reviews.content: I’m from the east coast, Philadelphia.. Been eating phó my entire life and let me tell you.. I have NEVER had a bowl of phó as good as the one I got here. As the kids say  "10/10.  No notes."

Great portions with excellent homemade taste! Staff is friendly and helpful. The chicken broth soup really hit the spot on a chilly day. Had chicken spring roll and grilled pork Banh Mi. Everything tasted great. They have indoor and outdoor seating. Perfect for a quick meal or hangout with friends and family. I would love to come back to try their pho.

The food is top-notch! Served in real fancy ceramic bowls with good quality ingredients. There is also a lovely Buddha statue made out of marble. We spoke to the parent of the owner for about five’s minutes and really liked them. I would return in a heartbeat. 💓

I love this place. Best banh mi hands down. Generous fillings, and attention to detail - even the carrots are amazing! They make their own mayo and paté as well. The bread is specially baked for them, and is the perfect soft-on-the-inside/crispy-on-the-outside loaf that a proper banh mi commands.

My second love there is the "fried egg rolls wrapped in spring rolls." Pure genius of texture and flavor that is the best of both worlds. Oh, that egg roll crunch combined with crisp cucumber and herby goodness, all dipped in a savory sauce! I could eat those every day.

And don't get me started on the pho! I don't get it too often because I end up finishing it all, and it's sleepy time for me about an hour later!

I recommend anything with grilled fish. I'm mainly a pescatarian, so this is what I've tried. My omnivore friends profess their love for the other things on the menu. I've told many friends to go there, and now some of them go sometimes two days in a row!

There is street parking right outside (metered), and you can find free parking around the corner in the residential streets off Gilman. There are both indoor and outdoor seating, the latter an enclosed patio with transparent roofing.

Portions are generous, and there is attention to detail in every ingredient. This is very intentional. I enjoy their posts on social media, too. The only downside to PhoSho is realizing you've taken the last bite!

The guys here that run the place are fantastic! They are really trying to do something special there, and are succeeding at it. When you're there, have a look around at the art - full wall and ceiling murals representing Vietnamese and Asian culture surround you. I feel so at home there!

top_reviews.content: A true local’s gem serving up the very best of Vietnamese cuisine. Piping hot soup to warm your soul, delightfully crispy banh mi, and other classic eats. Come enjoy and don’t tell your friends 🤫😉

If you're scanning for a Vietnamese spot in the Richmond that balances bold flavors with comforting familiarity, Y & Y has quietly been doing its thing.

I recently visited and ordered their satay noodles, and it turned out to be one of those meals you linger over, slowing down to savor every spoonful.

What I Loved
* Depth in the broth. The satay base had a rich, nutty backbone layered with spice -- not just heat, but complexity. You could taste peanut undercurrents melding with lemongrass, garlic, and chili in a way that felt warming and bold rather than aggressive.
* Spice done right. It hit the sweet spot -- spicy enough to awaken your senses without obliterating them. And the heat built rather than dominated, which encouraged you to keep sipping.
* Noodle + texture play. The strands soaked up the broth beautifully -- slippery but not mushy. Added onions, herbs, and bits of protein gave contrast and a freshness that kept the bowl from feeling heavy.

Little Joe's is the sleeper neighborhood restaurant. A very unassuming sliver of what appears to be your run-of-the-mill greasy Chinese spoon establishment actually turns out some fantastic Cantonese cuisine.

With a 5 year old, our standard test Chinese fare (to see where this particular restaurant falls on our scale) is fairly, well, standard,  but they are executed well here.

The house special fried rice comes with diced bbq pork, sections of chicken thigh meat, slices of beef, and 3 or 4 large prawns. The dish isn't too greasy, didn't taste of stale cooking oil, and doesn't leave a pool of oil on the plate, which means the chef is cooking with high heat and a swift hand.

Cashew nut chicken and broccoli beef are our other yardstick dishes, and Little Joe's are served with satisfyingly fresh ingredients. The cashew chicken had evenly cooked vibrant zucchini, celery, and a few button mushroom halves. No old, yellowed celery stems or squishy squash past it's prime, and a very generous scattering of cashews that didn't force us to ration each scoop.

The beef with broccoli had tons of fresh, crisp broccoli (almost too crisp, could have used 30 seconds more cooking time!) And thankfully, slices of tender beef that hadn't been given the usual Cantonese treatment of  baking soda to puff it up. I'm not a fan of pillowy puffy beef so they win points for leaving the beef and chicken unadulterated!

The establishment is small and very bare-bones; we ate under a flourescent light with a tv showing a sportsball game so the gemütlichkeit, or ambiance was not supreme, but the food was done very well and we knew what to expect. ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ 5 Stars – A Hidden Gem Worth Every Bite!

We had an incredible Omakase experience at this unassuming gem in Castro Valley, and it truly exceeded all expectations. The service was a perfect 10/10 — the host was extremely attentive, warm, and made us feel genuinely taken care of throughout the evening.

The food was exceptional — fresh, beautifully composed, and full of thoughtful flavors that worked harmoniously together. Each course felt intentional and elevated, showcasing top-notch quality without the pretentiousness.

And the dessert? Unforgettable. The Hojicha panna cotta was an absolute standout — silky, flavorful, and the perfect ending to a phenomenal meal.

Overall, this place easily gets 100 out of 100 from us. If you’re looking for amazing food, impeccable service, and a truly memorable dining experience, this is the spot. A must-visit in Castro Valley! 🍣✨

We recently dined here for the omakase experience and sat at the chef’s table, which was definitely the highlight of the evening. The space itself has been beautifully remodeled and has a calm, intimate ambiance that makes the experience feel special. Watching Chef Jeffrey work was genuinely entertaining and impressive — his knife work, deboning, removing impurities, and meticulous fish preparation showed incredible attention to detail and craftsmanship. From a technical perspective, it was superb.

Unfortunately, while the presentation and preparation were beautiful, the food itself was disappointing for me overall.

The first dish, miniature squid served over seaweed with yuzu sauce, was already placed when we arrived. It was very cold, noticeably fishy, and lacked flavor. The yuzu sauce also didn’t provide enough acidity or citrus brightness to balance or cut through the fishiness. I tried soaking the squid in the sauce to give it another chance, but I still couldn’t finish it.

The nigiri were visually well-prepared, but many pieces lacked flavor and impact. The rice appeared to have soy sauce mixed into it due to its brown tint, and although additional sauce was brushed onto the fish, the flavors still felt muted. I requested extra wasabi, but I honestly couldn’t detect much difference.

Texture was another issue for me. Several sashimi pieces felt too soft and mushy rather than firm and clean like very fresh fish should. The uni tasting plate was especially disappointing — instead of being creamy, sweet, and savory, the uni tasted overly fishy.

The chawanmushi and custard dessert also ended up feeling too similar in texture, and both leaned heavily eggy. The castella cake unfortunately suffered from the same issue: overly egg-forward, deflated, and collapsed. The best castella I’ve had in Japan was soft yet still firm, bouncy, and structured, which this lacked.

Overall, the experience felt uneven. The ambiance, chef interaction, and attention to presentation were excellent, but the food itself did not live up to the level of execution I observed behind the counter. While I appreciated the craftsmanship and enjoyed watching the preparation process, the flavors, textures, and overall dining experience fell short of expectations.

If you’re worried about the price point, please don’t. It is well worth it and more for this absolutely lovely experience.

I’m adding photos to help explain how great it all was, but I took them for my self because I’m trying really hard to learn and remember delicious food that is new to me. So I’m not apologizing for the photo quality lol you’ll have to just go and take better pics yourself.

top_reviews.content:
Fantastic Saturday lunch at Amarin Thai Cuisine! We walked by and saw their lunch special sign and were sold. Take a look for yourself with our photos.

The lunch special is 3 courses for $20. You may decide to pay to update items if you wish. We did on a couple items.

The crab Rangoon won tons were really good. The hot and sour soup hit the spot. And our main courses were yellow curry chicken and stir fried eggplant and chicken. The stir fried chicken was a little dry so I took a start off for that, but in truth we dunked out in the yellow curry and it was amazing. The yellow curry was like soup to me; I nearly drank the entire bowl as of it was!

Very friendly service and a welcoming and spacious decor.

Great service, food nicely prepared and presented, clean and inviting atmosphere, friendly and courteous staff. We shared fresh veggie rolls, and had Pad Thai with chicken and Pra Ram with chicken and rice. We’d heard about it from friends and glad we checked it out.

They renovated under new management and reopened at the beginning of Feb 2025.  I didn't go there before the update, however I think their rating will definitely go up as I was pleasantly surprised at the quality, taste, and presentation of all the dishes we ordered.  Had the Pad Thai with Fresh Spring Rolls.  The rolls were so delicious that I had to share (I didn't want to, but wanted to let others know how good it was).  The Pad Thai was just a wonderful.  Brother ordered the Basil Chicken with Fried Spring Rolls.  He raved as well.  Place was clean and the service was prompt.

This Thai restaurant truly delivers an authentic taste, making you feel like you're dining in Thailand itself. The ambiance is relaxed, with beautifully designed decor that enhances the experience. My partner and I ordered the crispy fried fish with herbs and the shrimp in tamarind sauce—both were outstanding. The service was exceptional, with attentive and friendly staff ensuring a great dining experience. If you're looking for a Thai restaurant that captures the essence of Bangkok's flavors, this place is highly recommended.

What a wonderful place to share a meal with friends! The portions are large enough to share and can be ordered plant-based. We ordered larb tofu, massaman curry, tofu satay, pad seeew, som tum (papaya salad), and, of course mango with sticky rice. Having spent time in Bangkok, we felt it was an authentic Thai experience. We ate family style (which makes it an affordable feast). We sat outside and enjoyed the lovely spring weather. ขอบคุณสําหรับค่ําคืนที่แสนวิเศษ!

top_reviews.content:
On our recent visit last week, we saw they have updated their prices and very economical for families.
Have you ever had really high quality 80's Cantonese cuisine in Hong Kong or the old San Francisco Chinatown/Peninsula before the Loma Prieta earthquake?  This restaurant is that gold standard quality.  They can cook up a storm!...if you've seen Stephen Chow's movie, "The God of Cookery"?  You get a tear after a bite like that ending scene with that judge because you remember how good food is supposed to taste like.  This restaurant has an incredible chef with cutting skills like that movie.  Ask Paul the new owner to order you the banquet style sliced ham perfectly cut chicken dish and you will know what I mean about this chef' s cuttery skills as in like "The God of Cookery".  Just to be clear I'm not a cook nor in the restaurant biz; I was a biopharma R&D Chemist, then Forensic Scientist, then Pharma Quality Management.  I'm a tough critic when it comes to Hk-Canto food of being quality or not.  I can't stand bad food. This restaurant from the first to the last dish on both dinner occasions we visited were superb; just like the golden era days of the past.  Jackie Chan, Sammo Hung, Jet Li movies.  Ingredients procurement to preparation were all A++.  They have a lot of celebrities that frequent here too to taste traditional authentic HK/Canto-food.

S & E Cafe recently reopened for indoor dining about one month ago. Hooray! I'm happy to see we've turned a corner as they were closed for indoor dining for over two years. Regulars will notice there are slight changes to the menu. I had the runny egg seafood crispy noodles $17 and a ice milk tea $3.50. With fish pieces, runny egg, scallops and shrimps, this was great. The crispy noodles stayed crispy because the chef didn't put too much gravy. Good job everyone at S & E Cafe.
Solid HK Cafe comfort food. Nothing too glam or glits about this place. Hits the spot though. Their beef Chow fun was pretty good though I feel like the portions can be slightly larger.
Came here for the hong kong tea which was absolutely delicious! The staff was so welcoming, it warmed my heart!♥️

Real deal Hong Kong style food. We ordered off the menu items like sautéed gailan, black bean garlic ginger leek crab, yu choi, and hk style beef ho fun. Good clear broth house soup and taro tapioca dessert in hot coconut soup on the house like the house soup. The crab was live swimming in tank minutes before served to us!

top_reviews.content: Nice clean place with counter seats only inside. They have a Parker with tables and chairs outside. It has an old timey feel (retro modern) interior with lots of stainless and chrome and feels very comfortable. We had the clam chowder and the tomato soups plus the cheese sandwich. The clam chowder was good but a bit watery and slightly bland while the tomato soup was just excellent and recommended. We both got the cheese sandwiches, one with kimchi and the other without. The one without was good again but a bit dry while the kimchi cheese sandwich was great!! They should just have it as a regular option instead of paying extra to make it great!! Service was ok, everything is self serve with utensils and water on the table including to go boxes which was highly convenient.

We came here for Sunday lunch, and there was a short line to order. Apparently the schmelty was their signature sandwich, so we waited another 20 min to get that, and sipped on soups in the meantime. The soups were alright, but the schmelty was definitely the star of the show and was super cheesy and crispy. I ate it with hot sauce and it was great.

A nice spot for a quick lunch. The small, focused menu made it easy to choose. Their take on clam chowder was unique and refreshingly light, with a nice clam flavor, though the bowl portion was a bit smaller than expected. The sandwich we got was also nicely composed.

The food was such a disappointment following such good service. We ordered clam chowder and tomato soup. The clams chowder had no flavor and the base was more chicken noodle soup.  The tomato soup was watery while also lacking flavor. It tasted like it came from a can with no added flavors.

I also found it odd that while lots of space, an invidivaul told someone to move to the Andy's side due to having a coffee.

I came here with my son and my favorite local group, Outer Sunset Neighbors, and I had the best grilled cheese and tomato bisque of my life.

Fresh ingredients, real technique, and the kind of careful prep you can taste. Simplicity at the highest high level.

John, the owner, is clearly serious about what he’s doing. I’ve talked with him a couple of times, and he comes across as grounded, thoughtful, and genuinely invested in the neighborhood.

The kitchen is open and spotless, which shows confidence and discipline.

It's a real local business built by someone who cares deeply about quality and about doing things the right way.

I’ll definitely be back.

top_reviews.content:
A family place with good food and comfortable setting. As sick, the service was a bit slow but I’m sure the kitchen was doing the best they could. We all quite enjoyed the food and it gave us time to chat anyway.

Open faced crab sandwich and fries.. yum! If you want a cold crab sandwich, you can get that also, but closed with two slices of bread.

Eggs and corned beef hash didn’t disappoint.

They know how to cook hash browns among the best of them! Crispy and yummy! They also know how to make soft eggs when you order them “wet”.

Update Oct 2022 with molcajete photo. Fun and looks quite dramatic.

My favorite here is still the short ribs. Apparently I start eating as soon as they arrive and forget to take a photo 😂

——-

Updated 8/19/2021 with two more pictures —of the chicken sandwich on focaccia and the salmon. Both delish. Salmon was perfect—rich and tender.  Also churro with ice cream was great.

——-

Delicious food, beautifully presented, great service.

They have expanded their Mexican offerings and so we tried the Chile Relleno Plate.  I enjoyed the grilled fish tacos on their original menu and knew it would be good -- and it was!  Was surprised by the tomatoey sauce on top of the chile but it was a great addition.

They offer their amazing breakfast dishes all day. I always love Eggs Benedict so I ordered it with smoked salmon. Yumm and perfectly cooked, as you can see in the photo after I sliced into the egg.

Other great dishes I've had here - the braised short ribs melt in your mouth. Prime rib, not on the menu right now, was huge and fabulous. Fried chicken and waffle was a bit too healthy for me, ha ha, because of the white meat chicken.

I'm always surprised that this place isn't more crowded. I think it may be because this place offers a wide variety of cuisines and people are suspicious when you can get American style burgers, Asian dishes, and Mexican dishes on one menu -- they expect only one cuisine per restaurant for authenticity. But Duo Grill prepares everything very well and always presents every plate beautifully. Especially when there are different tastes and opinions in your group, this is an excellent choice.

Still one of the top breakfast spots under the radar in the area, excellent presentation really delicious breakfast menu, well made espresso drinks, and super friendly and attentive service.
Also nice, and quiet, and a welcome change from the bustling local breakfast scene.

A mellow spot with friendly and attentive service every time. They have a great classic menu with American staples like Cobb salad, burgers, sandwiches, and pasta dishes. They also have a very tasty Mexican menu with dishes like enchiladas, tacos, nachos, burritos, and Chile rellenos. The Chile Verde is flavorful and juicy. I've also come for breakfast and they have a solid lineup, if you're brunching, try the tater tot dish it's delicious.
The french fries are skinny and cooked perfectly, the margaritas are tasty and not overly sweet. They have a happy hour with a drink special wed-sat. Right now there's a sweet parklet to eat at outside with umbrellas and lights.

Been to this spot a few times and always enjoy the food and prompt service. Street parking is almost always easy. This is one if my gotos for brunch fare for sure! There isn't a bad choice on the menu...try EVERYTHING 😋

top_reviews.content: Delicious burritos and tacos. Second time this week since we ordered out the first time.  I can highly recommend the burrito as well as a soft and large hard tacos. Absolutely delicious chicken burrito with black beans! The chicken was exceptional quality, maybe the best I've ever had in a burrito! Green salsa also delicious. My family enjoyed their chorizo con papas and vegetarian burritos, and fish tacos. This is my new go to place!

It was great! I ordered the carnitas and it was crispy and delicious. My son got the grilled fish taco and, unlike another review, he thought it was excellent! The service was very good! We ordered and it came out very quickly! The horchata was delicious 🤤 you can actually taste the cinnamon! Five stars! ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
The food was delicious. I had green pozole and my husband had a mole nopales burrito! Both were flavorful and the perfect amount of spice. We will definitely be back!

I usually stick to local taco trucks, but I wanted to support a local business so I decided to give this place a try.

Let's start positive- the customer service was good.

(I forgot to take pictures)
I ordered a carne asada taco, a Baja fish taco, and rice and beans. Unfortunately, everything was disappointing. The carne asada taco was tiny, with a tiny sprinkles of meat, and definitely not worth $6.50. The Baja taco looked bigger than it was because it was mostly piled high with coleslaw. The rice and beans were barely warm and lacked flavor.

I paid over $20 for two tacos and rice and beans, and it definitely wasn't worth the price.
The food seemed like it was toned down for a broader audience, so if you're looking for bold, authentic Mexican flavors, this may not be the place for you.
Next time, I'll be sticking with the local taco trucks.

top_reviews.content: Decent Mediterranean spot in Montclair for a quick bite. They have some seating inside. I got a Philly and falafel for about $25. Portions are huge and took me a meal and a half to finish. No toum (garlic sauce). Nice staff. Will likely try a plate next time.

I stopped by this Mediterranean fast food spot the other day, and I was honestly so impressed. The food tasted fresh and full of flavor — the shawarma was juicy, the rice was perfectly cooked, and the sauces tied everything together so well. You can really taste the quality in every bite.

The service was quick and friendly, which made the whole experience even better. It’s such a great place when I’m craving something filling but still flavorful and fresh. Definitely one of my go-to spots now! 🥙✨

Falafel Corner in Montclair is such a solid spot. I got the gyro platter and it was 🔥—fresh, flavorful, and super satisfying. The portions were great and everything tasted well-seasoned and made with care.
What I really love is the variety on the menu too—they’ve got options like a halal bacon cheeseburger and a spicy chicken sandwich, so there’s something for everyone. Always appreciate finding a place where everything is halal without compromising on taste.
It’s located in a really cute Montclair neighborhood with street metered parking and surrounded by charming mom-and-pop shops, which makes the whole experience even better. Definitely worth stopping by if you’re in the area!
The food here is absolutely delicious! Every dish we tried was bursting with flavor and cooked to perfection.

They had amazing food, and everyone working there was just so nice. They even gave us tea with free refills, and they had friendly prices, amazing service, and the mood was great too. Overall, amazing place that is a must-try!

top_reviews.content: Very sweet owners who make the food with love! Very generous portions! Garlic bread was the best ever!

One thing that makes Deja Vu stand out is even the slices are made to order. No heat lamps or oily  slices withering under a glass case here. A single order slice is actually two normal slices in one. I ordered the San Francisco slice which is like an everything slice with pepperoni, sausage, peppers, mushrooms. It was tasty and filling as it came right out of the oven and into my hands. The owners are super nice and kind. Definitely check these folks out if you are slice hunting in the neighborhood.
Hands down, best pizza and pasta in San Francisco. And yes, it is better than italian in north beach

Came here as a middle schooler and now I brought my daughter 19 years later…. Prices are to par with this economy, pizza slice is huge! And very cheesy….im not sure what cheese they use but even cold it taste bomb! Cold because I took a slice home and ate it here after..my daughter enjoyed her slice!! Dough is really fluffy and soft inside, my daughter hates pizza crust but enjoyed this one!!

Don’t judge a book by its cover. They might not look flash but this is THE hidden gem of SF pizza. Vu has been serving up slices for over 20 years now, so you know he’s doing something right. Seriously, he nails all the key points of pizza, the dough, the crust, the sauce and cheese ratio without being too greasy. Check them out next time you need a slice!

top_reviews.content: We were headed to see the Valkyries at Chase Center.  We were able to sit outside a perfect day.  Staff very attentive.  The food amazing.  We ordered fried tofu and it was a little bit too dry for our taste.  Loved the bread, side curry, chicken and more.  Will definitely stop by here again.  Thank you!

This is my second dinner at Kayah (both with a party of 60!) and it always such a pleasure dining at Kayah. Both experiences wre wonderful! The team is AMAZING (shoutout to general manager, Jude) and is so easy to work with! Coordinating a dinner for such a large group can be challenging, but Jude and the entire team make everything feel seamless and easy. I have several vegan, gluten free, vegetarian guests and Kayah has always been incredibly accommodating. Everyone is able to enjoy the meal without feeling like an afterthought. The food is served family style and always comes out fresh, hot, and perfectly cooked!  It’s impressive how consistently they deliver such great food and service for a group of this size.

Fantastic food, outstanding service, and an amazing team. I would absolutely recommend Kayah, especially for large group dinners and events. We’ll definitely be back!

One small request I would make is to have overhead heaters at the patio. It does get quite chilly after the sun goes down.

This was a really good spot that felt upscale and lively, perfect for the Chase Center area. The interiors were modern and inviting. We started with the platha with dip and the famous tea leaf salad, both of which were excellent. For the mains, we got the nan gyi dok, mango chicken, and Fieri tofu with vegetables - all flavorful and delicious. The service was professional and attentive, making the experience even better.

I went to Kayah by Burma Love at the Chase Center — their newly opened location was already bustling!
I’ve always enjoyed Burmese cuisine, and their menu here delivers the same flavors I love from their other spots. Prices are about average — not cheap, but consistent across their locations.
The servers were attentive and gave us great recommendations 💛 The environment is stylish and inviting — definitely the kind of place you want to linger.

I like their curry chicken. The portion was really big. The pork belly was also really good and I definitely recommend dipping into the sauce. I also never have pineapple salad before so that was pretty good.

Next time, I’m 100% checking out their bar! 🍹

Don’t usually leave negative reviews, but felt this experience was worth sharing in hopes it helps the restaurant improve. We paid $25 for the tea leaf salad, which unfortunately was mostly lettuce with very little flavor or dressing.

After sharing this concern with the staff, it wasn’t replaced or adjusted, which was disappointing. The green curry also fell short and was difficult to enjoy.

On a positive note, the salt and pepper tofu was excellent (5/5), and the LePhat skewers were also quite good.

There’s definitely potential here, but the restaurant could improve both the consistency and flavor of the dishes, as well as how the staff handles feedback. Overall, we left disappointed, especially given the high price point.

top_reviews.content:
I ordered the Tonkotsu Ramen and the Fried Shrimp. While it was a bit pricey, the food was actually quite good. The fried shrimp was crispy and the flavors were solid, though the ramen didn't have enough broth for my liking.
As someone who eats ramen very often, I can tell this isn't strictly "authentic," but I can appreciate the effort—it feels like they are trying hard to move in the right direction.
The biggest issues were the long wait time and the restaurant layout. The space isn't very well-designed for larger groups or gatherings; I can see the vibe they are going for, but the sense of space needs improvement. If they can work on the service speed and kitchen efficiency, it would be a much better choice.

I came by to shop in the area on a Sunday night where I was hungry and in need of food. I looked around and noticed this spot on the second floor and I decided to give it a shot. Upon arrival, it was close to dinner time and the place was almost fully packed, but luckily I was seated almost immediately. They offer small bites, rice plates, specialty items, ramen, non-alcoholic beverages, alcohol drinks and much more to choose from. At the moment I had a big appetite and everything sounded like I needed to order it. Everything here is made to order which is always a plus for me since it is quality over quantity and I never mind the wait since I am a very patient person. When the food arrived, everything was up to standard, from freshness to taste to the ingredients they use. The staffs here are very welcoming, well trained and understanding where my visit was a satisfying and issue free one. I highly recommend this place to all ramen enthusiasts, if you need a quick bite, to anyone willing to try something new, if you can not decide what to eat or if you just so happen to be in the area to check them out. I definitely will be back to tryout the other delicious options they have to offer.

To start off the appetizers were amazing.  I went when I was really hungry so I couldn't wait to eat so I got served panko shrimp right away.  Enough to at my appetite but not too much to fill me up.  I always loved watching my favorite anime character eat Ramen in Naruto and this brought me back to my childhood.  The freshly made ramen was super good!   Gonna come back here again next time I'm around. It does get packed pretty fast so if your comfortable sitting at a bar they even have hangers to put all your shopping bags off the floor.
Wish they don’t provide junk drink, just realize the soda is 48g sugar added, or just mention it in the menu so people can aware of it when ordering it.

This was my very first time having real Japanese ramen, and I was honestly so scared! I even told the server, Darrel, that I’d never had anything except Top Ramen, and he was SO nice about it. He took the time to explain everything, from the different broths to the toppings, and helped me pick the perfect bowl.

The ramen was incredible!! so rich, flavorful, and comforting. But beyond the food, what really made this experience amazing was the welcoming atmosphere and Darrel’s kindness. I had such a fun and great experience, and I will definitely be back!

Updated review 10/24/2022: Pho #1's garlic noodles $14 are only OK. The last time I was here, the waitress said their version of garlic noodles are better than the ones at PPQ. It is not. Pho #1's version is greasy without a good garlic burn and came with sliced onions. PPQ's version has grated parsley with a hint of butter plus a thing of lettuce and pickled sliced carrots on the side giving it a contrast between the carbs and the meat. The beef at Pho #1 had good wok flavor. Other than that, this is just chow mein without the characteristics of Vietnamese garlic noodles. I hope they survive because I was the only customer dining indoors on a Monday at dinner time, 6pm. You kind of start worrying about a restaurant when the employees outnumber the guests. The people here are nice.

Original review: During the lock down in 2020, Pho #1 was all boarded up. I remember getting take-out across the street at the now defunct Wing Hing and looking at their sad store front. Fast forward to 2022 and they are opened for indoor dining. I came here a few times before today for take-out and remembered they had decent vermicelli dishes. Tonight I got their black pepper beef noodles $14. It had a pleasing black pepper taste with good wok flavors. The chef did a good job. Service was fine as there were only one other party in the restaurant.

I usually came here several times a year when I’m in the neighborhood. Their food is fine: hot, edible, and clean. Their service is minimal— waitress brought glasses of water and food to the table. No refills offered and she doesn’t check up on you. All the utensils are self-service and napkin dispensers are on the table too. Prices are competitive. Portion sizes standard.

Unfortunately I had a bad experience. We had 5 people and the waitress automatically added her tip to my bill. She refused to give us a breakdown of the subtotal, taxes, and her tip amount. She kept saying the total is $89 with tip and walked away. When I asked for more clarification, she just read off the name of the items ordered and said, “what don’t you understand. That’s what you ordered” and walked away again as she spoke. See attached photo of the “bill”.

In the past, I’ve had 6 people at the table and I was allowed to determine the tip amount. I’m unsure if there was a change in ownership. There was absolutely no miscommunication since we spoke in her language.

If the waitress was transparent and wasn’t so curt, then I would have actually given her my normal tip percentage which is actually a lot more than what she demanded.

I recommend the food here, but I do not recommend the dine-in experience.

Decent, but nothing-to-write-home-about pho. One benefit is being open at 10am for those eager to get a fill before lunch time.

Seafood Pho — basic, but lacked a depth of flavor in broth. Noodles were slightly overcooked.

★★★★★

If you're passing through the area, I highly recommend stopping in. Parking is easy, with plenty of nearby options, including a public garage right across the street. This is the kind of family-run restaurant that's well worth supporting.

The food itself is what really shines. The scallion pancakes were crispy and delicious, a perfect appetizer. But the real stars of the show were the main dishes. The spicy wontons were mouthwateringly good, with a perfect balance of heat and flavor. The large bowl of beef noodle soup was incredibly rich and hearty, loaded with tender beef, fresh bok choy, and plenty of cilantro. It tasted incredibly authentic, reminding me of the food I've had in China.

it's not a place for a fancy dinner, but for an authentic, delicious, and convenient meal, especially since they're open late, it's a solid choice. It's a lifesaver when you need a great meal long after other places have closed.

I had dinner with my family at Chef Xiong Kitchen yesterday and we ordered several dishes: green peppercorn stewed fish, stir-fried potatoes, pig feet and chicken skewers, cold spicy noodles, beef noodle soup, and stir-fried green beans. top_reviews.content: As a Brit… Okay so my review will be a little skewed as I’ll be comparing this to some seriously excellent Indian food.. The CTM actually tasted pretty good albeit very different to the UK original, the meat was a little unimpressive and lacked the freshness I was hoping for. The naan, if slightly thin and crispy in places, tasted pretty good and the whole affair was washed down with a bottle of Taj Magal - Decent! top_reviews.content:
If you’re looking for a new staple on Geary, Rice & Shine is it. I stumbled in here for the first time just a few weeks ago, and it has already earned a permanent spot in my rotation.

The Food
On my first visit, the staff steered me toward the crispy pork and rice, and "unbelievable" is an understatement. The crunch and flavor were spot on. Since then, I’ve been back multiple times, and their recommendations haven't missed once.
Today was one of those freezing San Francisco afternoons, and they suggested the duck soup. It was exactly what I needed - deeply flavorful, incredibly warming, and clearly made with care.

The Service
What really sets this place apart, though, is the hospitality. Despite only coming here for a few weeks, the staff already remembers me. They treat you like a regular from day one, always ready with a personalized suggestion for something new to try.

Bottom Line: Amazing food, even better people. Whether you're craving that crispy pork or need to escape the cold with a bowl of soup, you can’t go wrong here.

The food was actually shockingly poor, the service disorganized and sloppy, but the prices are premium. To be specific, the tonkatsu was so thin that some pieces were just breading on less than a whisper of pork, yet it still managed to be very tough, the mixed tempura, rather than light and crispy, was a soggy, oily mess almost without flavor, the edamame were undercooked and undersalted, the california roll was a scant 6 piece portion instead of the typical 8, and the greatest offense was the plain rice. It carried a distinct, strong, and revolting aroma of perfume, perhaps from hand soap not sufficiently washed off when washing the rice, or someone walking by the prepared rice while spraying perfume. Regardless, it was inedible. The server seemed disorganized and unable to easily track the contents of a fairly simple order, in spite of the restaurant being quite empty, which is not surprising as the last time I ordered from them, about a year ago, they managed to forget an item entirely, in spite of my having paid for it.

In short, it's a terrible spot. I am mystified by the positive reviews, as the shortfalls were so many, and so serious, that this is unlikely to be a one off mishap.

One of the most disappointing sandwiches I think I’ve ever had. The bread was stale and I do think that a ciabatta roll is a questionable bread for a French cheese/sandwich shop to begin with. What’s wrong with using French baguette that is actually crispy? Moving on to the toppings… everything was just sad. The cornichons were chopped up so fine (and were barely there) that you couldn’t tasted them in a single bite. The butter tasted stale and old, like butter left in your fridge for a couple of weeks where the fat takes on the odors of everything around it. The cheese was not freshly cut which is disappointing for a French cheese shop. The Gruyère tasted staler than cheese you buy at Trader Joe’s or Costco. The ham was ok… but the flavor of it didn’t shine compared to anything else in the sandwich. I’m attaching pictures of my sandwich and then the sandwich they have posted online for their online ordering for reference. I also asked for something from their “charcuterie” section and asked for the ham to be thinly sliced. The shop worker brought a box of pre cut ham and just took thick slices from there. It wasn’t vacuumed sealed or anything so I question the freshness of taste. Disappointing for ham they charge $30 dollars a pound for. I wouldn’t recommend their sandwiches or charcuterie items. Maybe the cheeses that they actually cut fresh are good.

Wow is an understatement! This concept really intrigued me and I'm so happy we gave Pochys a try! Had the opportunity to connect with the owner when we visited and his passion and mission were undeniable. He told us all of the masalas (spice blends) were roasted and blended in house, something that truly makes a difference. The food was amazing, extremely flavorful and fresh; you can tell it's made upon order because everything comes out piping hot! My favorite was the chicken Kathi/rolls which were bursting with flavor and the texture of the chicken was fall apart. Everything we tried was delicious and we will definitely be back! PS: they are dog friendly and also have an outdoor patio.

I recently visited Pochys for the second time, and it did not disappoint! This time, I tried their Chicken Tenali Kura Roll and Curry, and both were absolutely outstanding. The flavors were rich and vibrant, and the dishes had that comforting, home-cooked quality—like something my mom would make. It’s clear that they use fresh, quality ingredients and take a lot of care in their preparation.

What really sets Pochys apart, though, is the owner. He’s incredibly kind and generous, making sure every guest feels welcomed and well taken care of. It’s rare to find such genuine hospitality these days, and it really adds to the overall experience.

I truly wish Pochys continued success because it deserves to thrive. I’ll definitely be back soon to try more of their amazing dishes! Highly recommend.

First time coming here after the place opened. The staff and owner are very friendly and helpful. I ordered the butter masala, which was excellent and despite a small-ish potion, it was filling. I appreciated the owner telling us about their handmade spices and Michelin star style cooking, making everything from scratch.
A couple pointers to improve the atmosphere and overall experience:
- Replace the AI art with real art (though the giraffe was quite charming)
- Keep the storage shelf in the men’s closed, it gave me an odd feeling
- Either lower the tables or replace the chairs, the tables are a little too tall
- The velvet chairs are comfortable, but I think they’ll get stained easily
Congratulations on your opening!

We were vegetarian for the day so I decided to try the lunch special which was spicy basil tofu with rice and my husband ordered the kung pao tofu. Both the dishes were so good! We polished off the good sized portions. So glad we discovered this little gem in the financial district.

One of the few spots in SF that nails “sup chow aw hor” (beef chow fun with gravy). The portion is generous — easily feeds two or makes for a solid lunch with leftovers. At $19.95, the price is actually pretty reasonable, especially for the FiDi. Flavor, portion, and value all hit the mark.

There is an unspoken culinary rule: the smaller the restaurant, the larger the portions. And it definitely holds true here.

This is a small and simple Asian restaurant, serving, as the name implies, Chinese and Vietnamese food. There's both tables and window-facing tall chairs, and the place can get surprisingly busy for lunch.

I tried the spicy beef Pho, and it was a solid choice. Nice presentation, fresh vegetables, textbook Pho. I was slightly surprised by the portion size: thankfully I hadn't had breakfast, otherwise I wouldn't have been able to finish it in one sitting!

Prices are alright, especially for the location by the financial district. Solid lunch choice.
