First, they were out of a few items I wanted. This was Saturday lunchtime. Specifically, all the mini pan-fried buns. He told us after seating and ordering. Bummer but ok. Then we ordered. I won’t go into the details.

He tells us up front they are short staffed in the kitchen and we MUST take our entire order at one time. Okaaay. Well that’s pretty normal I think. So we ordered 5 items. Keep in mind there are three of us so that’s a sizable order I think. And it’s not cheap here.

After 15 minutes one item comes. Ok no sweat, I’m sure it’ll all be out shortly. Nope. 15 minutes later we all what’s up and he says they are short staffed in the kitchen. He’ll check. He brings out second dish. Two dishes in 30 minutes. Still three to go.

Now I’m noticing other tables have been getting their food. And they ordered after us. I’m like, what? I ask the guy again to check. Takes him 8 more minutes to come back. In the meantime I see even more people get their food. Finally he’s back: “I’m sorry, there was an error in the order printing machine”. I’ll make your food now.

It’s 45 minutes since ordering and almost an hour since sitting. I’m like, no thanks we can’t wait longer, we’ll just pay for what we had. He rolls his eyes and said he has to try and back it out, or something like that, like I’m really inconveniencing him. Another 5 minutes for that.

Don’t like the way it happened. Don’t like the customer service or the attitude. My few months cooling off period didn’t help I guess.

I will say the food we did get was good.

I got the vegan chik-n parm sub here and it was AMAZING! They 100% nailed it, zero compromises on flavor or texture. When I was a kid I loved chicken parmesan, but after going vegan, I never thought I'd get to taste something like that again. Guess I was wrong! 😁

Everything about the sub was perfect, from the cheese (which actually pulls apart - I think the brand they used is Violife), to the ample amount of sauce that melts into the breading of the chik-n, to the soft texture of the chik'n itself. Halfway to Homeownership, All the Way to Happy Hour

After a long day of house hunting in San Francisco—aka the Hunger Games with realtors—I needed a break. I Googled “restaurants near me” and like a gift from the Zillow gods, The Halfway Club popped up. One review promised amazing food and drinks. Skeptical but starving, I decided to give it a shot.

First impressions? The place isn’t big, but it’s got personality. The bar seats maybe 8, or 10 if everyone skips leg day. The front has some classic tables and chairs, and out back there’s a larger space with a big screen showing the game. Beyond that? A sunny outdoor patio perfect for day drinking or pretending you’re not 12 tabs deep in Redfin.

The vibe is a mash-up of dive bar nostalgia and stylish clutter. There are old concert posters, a jukebox that seems more like a prop (no records, no labels), and liquor bottles that range from “standard pour” to “what is that?” Bonus points for the mini-library of cocktail history next to the register. I love a place where your hangover can learn something.

Now, let’s talk food and drink. I ordered the Wisconsin Old Fashioned—made with brandy and a cherry/orange cordial—and it was smooth, sweet, and strong enough to lower your rent expectations. For food, I tried the BLT Dog, which is exactly what it sounds like and somehow even better. Crispy bacon, amazing tomatos (get it and you'll understand! ), a killer sauce,  and a solid snap on the dog—served with waffle fries that were perfect, and definitely not from a freezer bag.

The menu has fun curveballs too. Next time, I’ve got my eye on the Crab Rangoon Deviled Eggs (because why choose between appetizers when you can combine them?) and the Alaska Cocktail, which sounds like something James Bond would drink on PTO.

Service was friendly, fast, and chill—no fake smiles, just real hospitality. It’s the kind of place where they learn your name, not because you’re famous, but because you came back twice in a week.

Even if I don’t buy a house nearby, I’ll definitely be returning to The Halfway Club. Sometimes, the best finds aren’t on Zillow—they’re behind a bar with a jukebox that doesn’t work.

🍣 High-Quality Sushi with "Ezpz" Convenience
Finding a spot that balances speed with actual high-quality fish can be a challenge in the city, but this place hits the mark perfectly. It is a fantastic grab-and-go for lunch, offering a level of freshness that usually requires a much longer sit-down experience. The entire system is designed for efficiency; you can walk in, grab a pristine box of sushi, and be back on your way in minutes. It makes the mid-day lunch rush feel completely stress-free and "ezpz."

🍱 Freshness and Selection That Surprises
Even though it’s a takeout-focused model, the quality of the sushi is top-tier.

Freshness First: You can tell the fish is handled with care. The cuts are clean, and the flavor is bright and fresh—never that "refrigerated" taste you sometimes get with pre-packaged sushi.

The Omakase Box: Their daily omakase nigiri sets are a great way to get a variety of high-end pieces, like fatty tuna or seared salmon, at a very reasonable price point.

Japanese Snacks: They also have a great selection of imported Japanese snacks and drinks, which is a fun bonus if you want to round out your lunch with something extra.

✨ Friendly Staff and Great Energy
One of the highlights of the visit was the service. Despite how busy the lunch rush can get, the staff were friendly and attentive.

Welcoming Environment: Sometimes these high-speed grab-and-go spots can feel a bit mechanical, but the team here is warm and makes you feel like a valued regular from your first visit.

Seamless Process: They keep the line moving quickly and the display cases fully stocked, so you never feel like you're digging through leftovers.

🍱 Final Thoughts and Recap
To recap, this is a good sushi destination that provides a fresh and ezpz lunch solution for anyone in the area. The combination of friendly staff and exceptional fish quality at a fair price makes it a standout. It’s a rare find where you don't have to choose between a fast lunch and a gourmet one. I’ll definitely be making this a regular stop whenever I’m looking for a quick, healthy, and delicious meal!

Pho Ga is such a comforting stop when you’re craving a hearty bowl of chicken pho. We ordered both the classic pho ga and the curry pho ga, along with an order of egg rolls to share.

The regular pho ga had a clean, soothing broth — light but still flavorful, with tender slices of chicken and noodles that were soft and easy to slurp. It’s the kind of bowl that feels nourishing without being overly salty or greasy. The curry pho ga, on the other hand, was the standout for me. The broth was golden, aromatic, and layered with a subtle richness from the curry — something you don’t often find at most pho shops. It’s hearty and unique but still maintains that pho comfort factor.

Egg rolls came out hot and crispy, perfect with the dipping sauce and pickled veggies on the side. Service was quick and efficient, even though the restaurant was buzzing during lunch.

Overall, a reliable spot for chicken pho lovers, and the curry pho is absolutely worth a try if you’re looking for something a little different. Solid 4/5 in my book — satisfying, flavorful, and a place I’d happily revisit when the craving strikes.

top_reviews.content: The sushi and sashimi here were so incredibly tender -- the fish would literally melt in my mouth! We got a tasty soup-based main dish as well, and I'd recommend getting it with the sushi if you're very hungry. The service was fantastic, and our waitress was very kind and generous. If you're craving a good mix of sushi and korean food, this place is definitely worth it!

I really wanted to like Yasijang since it is close to where I live and run by some genuinely nice Korean folks, both in the kitchen and front of house. Unfortunately, most of the dishes fell pretty flat for me.

Here’s a breakdown of everything we tried:

Mini Jeon - This came out as a set of three mini pancakes, and while they were fried expertly with a nice crisp exterior, I did not really get much of the ingredient flavors at all, which was supposed to have an array of vegetables and seafood.

Truffle Bosot Fry - These were fantastic. Each enoki was fried so the stems were splayed out and then dusted in truffle salt. It was clear the chef has a deft hand at the fryer, as both of the first two starters had an amazing crunch to them.

Spicy Tuna Tower - This seemed like a popular item, but it was really disappointing. It felt like a quantity over quality dish, with the spicy tuna indeed piled high, but very clumpy, as if it had just been scooped straight out of the fridge, and not a pleasant texture. There was not much flavor or spice to it and the kappa maki rolls that the tuna sat atop were unfortunately not made well, as most of them fell apart just from picking them up with chopsticks.

K-Fried Chicken - Pretty good value since you get 8 decently sized pieces for $20, or $22 if you want to add a sauce. It was curious that they do not let you do half and half, since the sauces are likely pre-made and that is such a common option at most other KFC spots. The bigger issue was the fry on the chicken as huge pieces of batter were missing from every piece, and it did not have that signature shattering crunch I expect, which suggested the oil was not hot enough and that they did not double fry the chicken. The soy and garlic flavor was actually pretty good, so it was doubly disappointing that the chicken was not fried properly.

Hwe-Muchim. - This dish was an absolute disaster. The cubes of fish and salad were absolutely drowning in cho-jang, and it was really unbalanced, so all you tasted was gochujang. The lettuce was so wilted under the sheer amount of liquid that it made the dish difficult to eat. I actually took this home, drained most of the liquid, rinsed off the fish, added fresh greens and a homemade dressing, and it tasted much better.

The staff were friendly enough, but this place is clearly targeting a drinking or late-night crowd so I would avoid if your main goal is to enjoy the food itself.  Seems like a fun enough place if you were just wanting to stop in and have some snacks with your drinks or as an end of night stop as the 4-cha or 5-cha (IYKYK).

Overall, it’s a Korean pocha (gastropub) with a great vibe. The prices are pretty affordable compared to other places in the area. The service is decent, but the food falls a bit short. I do recommend the Buldak (fire chicken), though.

I came for dinner (made a reservation)  before the symphony (about 1.5 block walk from Herbst theatre).  From the restaurant's website, I imagined the restaurant to be much larger.  Instead, it was small - probably sits 25 (tightly) without the bar and maybe 20 with the bar.  My table was next to the bar - felt cramped sitting in the corner - that's why it is a 4 star rating.  Food was served temperature hot with kindness.  Flavors, smell and presentation were good.  I would recommend the sausage basket, a variety of different sausages, for an appetizer.  It's a good segue into your main entrees which are small shared plates.

They have a bar challenge - filling up a vase with empty bottle caps.  Thought that was fun and an incentive/motivation for returning.  The restaurant definitely would be a good bar place to hang out and simply have fun.

Service was excellent - orders kept coming out as well as for deliveries.  The wait staff always had a smile and kept asking if we are okay or if we need anything else.  I thought the restaurant stools were unusual.   Since there is no space to put your coat, purse, bags, etc., the stools open up for storage.  I thought this was cleaver.
Perfect Korean fare, served by extremely courteous owners. Great spot that feels very authentic.  I did not try the sushi but assume that is great too.

The restaurant’s interior layout and seating situation inside is a little chaotic. The line runs through the middle of the restaurant, and the trash cans are by the front of the line/restaurant rather than close to the doors for on your way out. It was absolutely packed on a Saturday around 6p, and I had to squeeze past people after ordering and picking up my food. I waited 30 minutes in line and 15 minutes for my food.

It would be great if the restaurant set aside some tables for people who have at least ordered, if not received their order, to better facilitate people saving tables while waiting in the long lines/cold and ensuring people with their food have a place to sit. The outside area gets packed quickly as well. Moving the line to be flush to the wall, rather than through the middle (hot dog style), would also improve the amount of every-way foot traffic.

A great Cantonese restaurant in the food desert known as Lamorinda. All dishes are good but I highly recommend their salt and pepper spareribs, Hong Kong style chow Mein and whatever is on their daily special menu.

Yes. 95% of the time, I’m a happy camper! There’s been a few slight hiccups here and there but I appreciate this spot.

top_reviews.content:
Dining at Via Aurelia feels like stepping into the world of fine dining you see on Netflix’s The Chef’s Table.

Every detail is handled with care. The table settings are precisely aligned down to the 1/32th of an inch, our glasses were never left empty for long, and the staff was attentive and genuinely caring throughout the meal.

Panzanella: A bright green pea salad with edible flowers was one of the most visually striking dishes I’ve had, with a perfect crunch from the croutons.

Anatra (dry-aged duck) was exceptional. The tender meat, rich duck fat, rhubarb, and white asparagus came together beautifully and was a standout of the evening.

Maiale (pork chop) was the most pleasant surprise. Originally recommended as a generous portion for the kids, the adults ended up eating most of it. It was wonderfully juicy with perfectly crispy skin, and the roasted carrots were excellent.

The mugellani, salmon and crudo were also very good.

Lastly, be sure not to miss the cookie dessert. We initially wondered how special a cookie could be, but it turned out to be excellent (with a scoop of ice cream)

We’re definitely planning to return soon.

Villa Aurelia commands a prime waterfront spot in the newly developed Mission Rock neighborhood, directly across from Oracle Park. Arriving at opening on a gorgeous evening, the post-game Giants crowd energy spilled beautifully into the room, cementing its status as one of the best new restaurants in SF.

The initial check-in exposed an immediate operational friction point. The host had me pause at the reception counter to check if my table was ready, then paused me again mid-stride on the floor. Pacing-wise, you shouldn't march a guest out until front-of-house communication confirms the station is fully primed. It felt clumsy for a restaurant aiming for a Michelin-caliber standard.

Once inside, the sprawling, spacious architecture is a total victory, complemented by a manicured outdoor terrace perfect for outdoor dining in San Francisco. I loved that my seating area featured local art by Isadora Gullov-Singh—a fantastic touch that roots the upscale space into the neighborhood fabric. The atmosphere is anchored by an outstanding classic rock soundtrack (Santana, Doobie Brothers, Hall & Oates). Throwing in some Grateful Dead for the local Deadhead community would make it perfect.

The service team on the floor is remarkably kind and affable. My waiter expertly steered me toward their special Sunday Meal tasting menu ($55) with the premium sea scallop supplement ($48). It was an exceptional recommendation.

The meal kicked off with a great bread service—thick sourdough with a deeply caramelized, crunchy crust served with molded compound butter and artisan olive oil on marble. The Insalata del Mercato starter was a rustic and tasty salad, though the larger greens were clumsy to cut and a few wide leaves were under-dressed.

The absolute triumph of this San Francisco fine dining experience was the Pici Alle Funghi. Per my waiter, it features exactly six continuous, thick, hand-formed long noodles. This is elite handmade pasta. The kitchen hits a flawless, elastic al dente snap. Tossed in a brilliant, earthy cream reduction of Sierra morel mushrooms, pastis, and blood orange, it's topped with toasted breadcrumbs and parmesan for a sharp crunch. Texturally brilliant and flat-out delicious—I’m already planning a return sweep just for these noodles.

The hot line executed the Capesante (scallop) supplement with absolute precision—carrying a hard uniform crust and a sweet, pearlescent medium-rare core. Combining the scallop, its amazing burnt pear purée, and the briny pop of Tsar Nicoulai Golden Osetra caviar on one fork created an impeccable flavor harmony that easily justifies the $48 luxury add-on. For dessert, the sourdough gelato was rich and satisfying, though it sat in a noticeable pool of melted liquid, indicating it over-tempered on the line.

Hospitality touchpoints remained strong; toward the end of the meal, the host did a thoughtful, professional tableside check-in. A stellar chocolate-covered almond on cacao nibs arrived with the bill. Even the facilities held up: clean unisex stalls with a communal washing station that uses folded textile linens instead of wasting paper towels.

Villa Aurelia enters the SF dining grid with an impressive balance of visual drama, refined hospitality, and elite Italian mechanics. Despite the minor front-of-house pacing hiccups at the door, the kitchen is running a tight, high-caliber operation.

We stumbled upon this place after Giants game, located right on China Basin. Beautiful location. We didn’t have a reservation but fortunately they had available seats at the bar, which we prefer for casual dining. From cocktails to dessert, Via Aurelia exceeded our expectations. The place is very classy, the service top notch, very attentive wait staff and of course the bartender/server was excellent!

We definitely will be returning. I don’t know if I will reserve a table for two but if we have a group, I will definitely reserve one and experience that with friends or family.

Excellent tasting food with aesthetic presentation. Ambiance was very nice! However, the portions were too small and too expensive. The servers were overly attentive to the point where they tried multiple times to clear food and drink we were still consuming and we had to ask them to wait.

We came to Via Aurelia to celebrate our wedding anniversary and had a really lovely experience. We brought our 8 month old daughter and the staff was so kind and accommodating, which we truly appreciated. Service felt warm and genuine, and we loved the cozy, stylish interior. The Pegasus and Sazerac cocktails were both solid and the complimentary bread to start was a nice touch. We ordered the scallops, wild boar ragu, salmon, and dry aged duck breast and while everything was good, nothing particularly stood out as memorable. Even though we passed on dessert, they surprised us with complimentary sorbets, which felt really thoughtful and made the night feel extra special.

top_reviews.content:
Belly is a quiet little spot on College Ave right off the Rockridge BART station. We came around noon on a weekday and were pretty much the only patrons there for the duration of our meal outside of a handful of takeout orders.

Service was a little rough since there was only one person working, so we had to flag them down whenever we needed anything. That said, I completely sympathize with how tough it is to run a restaurant in the current environment, and I appreciated the effort.

We started with the kimchi arancini balls, which were excellent. They were fried nicely, the filling was ooey gooey and cheesy, and the kimchi aioli added a great cooling balance to the dish. For my main, I went with the 2 taco platter, which comes with a small salad and chips, and it was more than enough food. I tried one steak, egg, and cheese taco and one surf taco, and both had great flavor. The steak was cooked perfectly, the fried egg added a really nice richness and creaminess, and I loved the fries inside, which reminded me a lot of the Cali style you usually associate with San Diego.

The only real miss for me was the panko batter on the fish taco, since I prefer a lighter, more delicate tempura style batter. The flavor was still solid, just not something I’d order again. My bigger hesitation overall is the price, since the tacos are pretty steep at nearly $8 each and over $20 for the 2 taco platter, which makes it hard to imagine coming back frequently even though I did enjoy the overall flavors.

We just finished eating here for Restaurant week / Date night. Let me start off by saying the food is so packed with Flavor. We had the Kimchi appetizer balls it has Cheese Risotto and Kimchi. We had the Asian salad. It was light and crunchy and perfectly balanced. The Miso Butter Spaghetti was rich and full of flavor I added grilled chicken to it and that was a perfect combo. My wife had the Silk road spaghetti and added Salmon. It was tangy and spicy but not too spicy.  We will definitely be back here soon.       🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥

Been living in Rockridge for awhile and finally got out to try this cute Asian-Mexican fusion joint!

Belly has a darling blue storefront, and the cute aesthetic continues throughout the dining area. Service was really friendly and the vibe is casual but inviting.

I ordered three tacos (Korean Hot Chicken, Cali, and Pork Belly) and enjoyed them all — fresh ingredients and packed full. I do wish they had a bit more flavor, particularly in the Korean Hot Chicken.

The salad was a nice surprise to have included and the vinaigrette was really refreshing! It might have been my favorite part of the platter.

Came to Belly with a belly empty; left Belly with a belly full! Pretty happy about that.

Solid food with really nice staff in a really cute restaurant. My girlfriend and I stopped into Belly for the first time around a week ago and were pretty impressed with our food. My pork belly burrito was big and tasty and her Korean Hot Chicken bowl was pretty great (but probably could have used a bit more of the aioli sauce from the get go, but our server was really friendly and brought more of the kimchi aioli over which was really nice). Also, the habanero salsa I had with my burrito was incredible -- pretty spicy, but also super flavorful. Overall I like the concept of Belly and think their food and service is pretty great.

Belly in San Francisco is a bold, flavor-forward spot that blends comfort food with creative, Asian-inspired twists. The menu is indulgent and unapologetic, focusing on rich textures, layered flavors, and generous portions that feel both satisfying and intentional. From the moment you step inside, the atmosphere feels lively and modern, matching the playful energy of the food itself. Dishes are thoughtfully composed, balancing sweetness, spice, and umami without feeling overwhelming. Service is efficient and friendly, keeping the experience smooth even during busy hours.

top_reviews.content: The food here is pretty terrible.  I tried the puffy taco with pollo asado.  The puffy taco part - a fried, puffy tortilla - was kind of cool even though it was a bit salty.  However, the “pollo asado” was not real food! No atmosphere to speak of, just a hole in the wall.  The person who took my order was not a good communicator but she got the job done.

I had the Birria Ramen, a good portion of savory meaty birria broth served on a bowl with onions and salsa on the side. Small place, you order before you seat at the cashier’s stand, when your order is ready the attendant takes the food to your table, not much interaction after that. 24th Street and Mission,  Bart station. The area is very sketchy, lots of people participating in illicit transactions steps away from the entrance.

Nestled between a bodega and a frutería on the always vibrant Mission Street, you'll find the unassuming Casa de la Condesa. The air is thick with the dramatic tones of a Mexican soap opera blaring from the TV, and I'm the only gringo in sight—a sure sign I've made the right choice for my inaugural taco birria experience.

Yes, I admit it: this is my first time eating taco birria. But if you're going to lose your birria virginity, this is the place to do it. The consommé hits first, a robust, beefy broth spiked with raw onion and cilantro, a punch of flavor that wakes up your senses.

The taco itself is a marvel of simplicity and indulgence. Soft, shredded beef piled generously inside a tortilla that's been lightly fried to perfection—crispy on the outside, yet soft and inviting within. The raw onions add a sharp counterpoint to the savory, salty meat. And the salsa roja is probably the best I’ve had. I’ll be sure to add vinegar to my personal recipe.

Crispy puffy tacos. Perfect balance of meats & veggies. Always happy after a meal here. The restaurant is small with minimal-none decor, but always clean & the foods are delicious. The foods are best to eat right away so highly recommend dine-in.

top_reviews.content: I have been going to Bianca’s since attending St.Mary’s College in 2001.  The food is very very good and the portions are very generous. I have overheard some of the dumbest questions while waiting in line and I have seen people spend 20 minutes in line just to not be ready when it was their time to order. The owners have experienced that for decades and maybe their tolerance is just gone now.  Time is money for small deli’s and not being prepared after 20 minutes of waiting is very irritating.  That doesn’t excuse the owners attitudes because they should push through it and still provide a positive experience, but it does help me understand them a little more.  At the end of the day people are going there for food not friendship, and the food is VERY good and fresh. top_reviews.content: Eagle pizzeria is an old school spot that has great retro charm and a fun, talkative owner who will keep you entertained! The pizza is great, with a nice crust and crispy base but soft interior with a plentitude of toppings. Prices are fairly reasonable and service is quick and efficient, stop by and support a local business

My extended family comes to this reasonably-priced, neighborhood family-style restaurant for birthdays, in particular my uncle who loves pizza and is wheelchair-bound. Eagle Pizzeria has my family sit against the wall on the right with all the photos and mementos. It's easy to roll my uncle in and out and can easily sit 16 of us comfortably at one long table.

We are big eaters. We usually start with double orders of the antipasto salad, garlic bread and for some in my family bowls of minestrone, spaghetti and meatballs to share, and 4 - 5 larges or extra-larges (Eagle Special, Amy "E," Meat Lovers, Hawaiian and the Margherita), with pitchers of root beer.

Eagle's pizza is on the thick crust side with more of a tomato base sauce and not heavy cheese, Toppings are plentiful, but not overly generous. The pizzas are not heavy pies or will reach your table super burning hot. We eat gluten, so have not tried their gluten-free crust. No one is hungry after we eat and usually there is a few slices left for those who want the leftovers.

Service is efficient, but you do have to wait for the pizza. I think the wait is longer for us because of the quantity we order, the size of our party and if the place gets busy with after baseball/kid sport parties. We also start around 5:30 pm to 6 pm on Sunday nights so it's usually less crowded. Parking is also easier too without paying the meter.

Eagle does allow us to bring our own birthday cake and does not add an additional cake cutting fee per person to our final bill. They are also generous by letting us stay and linger to talk after dessert. We usually stay between 2 - 3 hrs for dinner.

6/3/2017 Update: Very kid-friendly. Has high chairs (3), serves milk and apple juice beverage options and has a diaper changing table in their unisex restroom.

top_reviews.content:
If you are planning a trip to the Bay Area, experiencing San Francisco’s legendary seafood scene is non-negotiable. At the heart of this culinary tradition stands the iconic crustacean destination that locals and travelers adore, and it has just elevated its experience with a breathtaking move to a brand-new home.
The restaurant’s latest location redefines waterfront elegance. Stepping inside reveals a striking, chic interior design that brilliantly fuses vibrant pop art elements with sleek, understated luxury. Think bold, playful color palettes paired with plush seating, ambient lighting, and high-end finishes that make every visit feel like an exclusive celebration.
Fortunately, while the atmosphere has received a stunning modern upgrade, the legendary kitchen remains gloriously unchanged. The signature Dungeness crab and world-famous garlic noodles are still absolute masterpieces, delivering the rich, aromatic flavors that put this establishment on the global map. To maximize your culinary indulgence, ordering the de-shelled crab is an essential move—allowing you to savor every single tender, succulent bite of sweet crab meat drenched in their secret garlic butter sauce with zero effort.
A trip to San Francisco is simply incomplete without a night here.

The atmosphere here is fantastic, and every course was beautifully presented and cooked to perfection. We ordered the shrimp and lobster dumplings, salt and pepper calamari, Chilean sea bass, and the lobster garlic noodles. Every dish was packed with flavor, and the ingredients complemented each other seamlessly.

The only downside was a minor service slip when the server accidentally dipped a finger into the sauce while setting down a dish, which was a bit off-putting. Still, given how exceptional the rest of the meal was, we left genuinely impressed with the overall experience.

We’ve been enjoying the amazing cuisine at Crustacean for about 30 nears now. Everything has always been spectacular and cooked to perfection. Family favorites are AN’s Famous Garlic Roasted Dungeness Crab, Tiger Prawns with AN’s Famous Garlic Noodles, and Tuna Cigars.

We were saddened to see the removal of the Papaya Salad from menu.

The new, larger, upscale location with beautiful full bar is a huge plus. The attentive staff completes the perfection of Crustacean!

top_reviews.content:
Arrived right at opening on a Sunday afternoon at 1130am.
We had 3 ppl.
The house made spicy sauce is SO good! I highly recommend getting it!
I got the ninniku tonkatsu ramen. The broth is SOOOO good too! Very flavorful.

This is officially my new go-to ramen spot! The interior design is nice, with great decorations that create such a welcoming and cozy atmosphere. The staff were incredibly friendly and attentive, which made the whole experience even better.

The portion sizes are very reasonable, especially with their free noodle refill policy. I’ve tried ramen from many different places, and this one was seasoned perfectly. It was rich in flavor without being overly salty like so many other ramen shops tend to be. It was honestly one of the best bowls I’ve had. The gyoza was also juicy and delicious. One thing to note: the ramen doesn’t come with an egg, so definitely order one on the side if you want one.

I will definitely be coming back!

Interesting experience at Ramen Kameko.

When we arrived, the restaurant was quiet with only one other table occupied. We ordered two miso ramens and an order of yakitori. The yakitori was decent, though it arrived warm rather than hot, which surprised us given how the restaurant wasn’t busy.

The miso ramen wasn’t what we expected. The broth was quite thick and rich, with visible fat throughout. After reading more about regional Japanese ramen styles through the other comments, I understand this is intentional and traditional for certain types of miso ramen, it just simply wasn’t to our taste. We politely asked if it would be possible to switch to the shoyu ramen, knowing it would be a thinner broth instead.

Unfortunately, the interaction that followed left us feeling uncomfortable. The server repeatedly questioned why we wanted to make the change and there was confusion about whether we would be charged for the original bowls. Eventually, the bowls were taken back, but the exchange felt tense and awkward. When our replacement ramen arrived, there was little communication, which added to the feeling that our request had been an inconvenience.

On a positive note, the shoyu ramen was much more to our liking.

Overall, the food was average to good, but the service experience is what ultimately led to my 3-star rating. While I appreciate that the miso ramen was prepared in a traditional style, I left feeling rather awkward, and that a simple request to switch dishes could have been handled with more hospitality and understanding.

* Edit: After reading the owner’s response, I wanted to clarify a few details to ensure my review is accurate.

The staff member who assisted us did not explain the differences between the ramen styles. We mentioned that the broth seemed unusually thick to us and that there was visible fat throughout the bowl. His response was simply, “I know,” repeated several times. At no point was it explained that this was a traditional style of miso ramen from a particular region of Japan. Had that explanation been given, I would not have described the interaction the way I did.

I also felt the handling of our request to switch dishes was unnecessarily uncomfortable. There was confusion about whether we would be charged for the original bowls, and after the uneaten ramen was taken away, the bowls were discarded very loudly in the back. Whether intentional or not, the overall interaction left us feeling unwelcome.

I understand the challenges that come with running a newer, smaller restaurant, which is why I initially kept many of these details out of my review. However, since the owner’s response characterized the interaction differently than I experienced it, I felt it was important to provide additional context and accurately reflect what occurred during our visit.

First time here and it's nice to have a different ramen spot here in the neighborhood. We ordered the Ninniku Tonkotsu Ramen and it's really good. We also got a kids meal and honestly it looked so good. It was a whole set and it came with a juice box for the kiddo.

The noodle itself was really good. Broth was very savory and thick. They didn't include an egg but it's not a deal breaker for us. What I did like that was they offer free one time noodle refill if you're up for more. It's really nice that they offer it as well since sometimes if you want extra noodles you don't need to order it and they'll refill it for you.

10/10 would come here again.

The bluefin was exceptionally fresh and delicious, with different cuts served sashimi-style as well as incorporated into rolls, allowing us to experience the variety of flavors and textures throughout the fish. What really elevated the evening was the attentiveness and care of the staff—you could genuinely feel how invested they were in making sure every guest had an unforgettable experience. As a bonus, I even won the raffle and was able to take more tuna home!

An exceptional and truly special experience. I will absolutely be returning to dine here again!

This Japanese restaurant is a true gem in the city. Authenticity is unmatched anywhere else in the US. top_reviews.content:
Finding myself in San Francisco's Mission District before an evening meeting, I realized there is no shortage of spots to grab a quick happy hour drink. I decided to step into Salt & Sangria, and the space immediately sets a welcoming mood. Looking straight at the bar setup, it is clear from the craft spirits and curated setup that they take their mixology program seriously. The energy in the room makes it the exact kind of local spot where people pop in to unwind over a couple of drinks and share a few small plates.

The bar team was friendly, attentive, and quick to hand over a happy hour menu right after I sat down. The menu itself features an impressive, wide selection of great-looking tapas that makes narrowing down an order tough. The service moves at a comfortable pace, making it easy to relax without feeling rushed.

I started with the garlic and herb fried yuca served alongside an aioli. The garlic flavor comes through strong on the yuca, complemented by a very prominent, pleasant rosemary note. While the accompanying aioli is a nice touch to round out the dish, it stays fairly standard. Next, I tried the jerk chicken tacos. The chicken itself arrived wonderfully tender and flavorful, though the creamy sauce on top and the pickled cabbage lacked the punchy flavor I was hoping for.

To finish, I ordered the Cha Cha Cha, one of their signature craft cocktails. It arrives topped with a sweet berry smoke bubble that adds a fun bit of tableside flare. The drink blends mezcal, coconut, lime, blue curacao, and pineapple, though the mezcal, curacao, and lime are the dominant notes that shine through on the palate.

Salt & Sangria delivers a solid happy hour experience with an accessible price point that makes it well worth stepping through the door. While a few elements on the happy hour food menu could use a touch more flavor, the bar team and ambiance carry the venue nicely. It is a solid 4 out of 5 star happy hour stop, and I would certainly return to sample their full dinner menu, larger entrees, and broader craft cocktail list to give it a more complete review.

Was hesitant to try the very well reviewed $17 OMG sandwich due to its exorbitant price. But it is aptly named, OMG I spent $17($21+with tip) on this sandwich. This is roughly six inches with very sparse amount of meat or ingredients listed on the menu. The bread is pretty good but not anything to rave about. This is half a sandwich not a full sandwich.

While I love a great sandwich, great sandwiches are far and few in-between.  Heroic Italian is a place where you can find a great sandwich.  I tried the signature "OMG" and it did not disappoint.  The real hero of the sandwich is the bread.   It's light, airy and crispy so you don't feel bloated with carbs.  But the bread's real super-power is letting the flavors of the imported Italian meats and assorted toppings shine through.  I had mine spicy which wasn't really hot but definitely added a touch of flavorful heat.  I'll be going back to try their other sandwiches as well as another aptly named, "OMG."

El Tacostao literally sits in someone’s backyard , which is turned into a patio/terrace on weekends. I initially thought Google Maps had messed up the directions when it instructed me to turn into a driveway , where the lawn doubles up as a makeshift parking lot.

Yelp says that this place is closed, but it absolutely isn't. Definitely go check it out.

Even though the tortillas are small, they do use two. I tried the birria, cabeza, and surtido tacos. I give them a 4 on taste for the fact they could use more salt. I know they don't fry their tortillas, but if they were, I would think they could retain a better flavor profile. On the other hand, the horchata was definitely a 5 for the legit flavor. I definitely recommend coming by and trying this place.

If you love Italian food as much as I do, y'all need to check out Heroic Italian! Everything was so fresh and light. It's simply delicioso!

OMG! OMG! The OMG sandwich was light, airy, crispy, and delicious; while the Chicken Tetrazzini Rotini pasta was light, creamy, and tasty, it was perfect with the glass of white wine.

Ps. There’s a parking lot next door, and it cost the same as the street parking meter.

I recently visited Al-Masri Egyptian Restaurant in San Francisco’s Outer Richmond neighborhood, located along Balboa Street just a short distance from Ocean Beach. The area is known for its diverse collection of small international restaurants, and Al-Masri stands out as one of the few places in the city focused specifically on Egyptian cuisine.

The atmosphere feels intimate and welcoming, similar to many family-run restaurants found throughout the Middle East. The dining space is modest and comfortable, with décor that hints at Egyptian culture through artwork and decorative accents. Rather than feeling commercial or overly polished, the restaurant carries the charm of a neighborhood spot where the focus is clearly on the food and hospitality.

The menu highlights traditional Egyptian dishes that showcase the country’s distinctive flavors within the broader Middle Eastern culinary tradition. Plates such as koshari, grilled kebabs, falafel, and slow-cooked stews reflect the hearty and spice-driven cooking style that defines Egyptian cuisine. The dishes tend to emphasize ingredients like lentils, rice, chickpeas, herbs, and well-seasoned meats, creating meals that are both satisfying and deeply flavorful.

Service during the visit felt warm and personal. Staff were attentive and happy to explain menu items, which is helpful for diners who may be encountering Egyptian dishes for the first time.

From a global travel perspective, the experience reminded me of the small local restaurants I have encountered throughout Cairo and Alexandria where hospitality, comfort food, and generous portions define the dining culture.

January 2026:

Had the chicken pho and the soup was very tasty 😋. Good combo of noodles and chicken.

Also had the chicken cabbage salad and thought it was delicious. Would order that again.

Also tasted the papaya shrimp salad and the tofu banh mi. Both were good. Will definitely come back again. Will try dining in next time.

Either Pho Star lost its star on its way from New York, or it never had a star, I ordered the wrong dishes or the chef took a leave of absence.  I didn't try their pho as it takes work and great ingredients to start with and only samples their appetizer and non pho main dishes.
I'm so disappointed, all of the dishes were blend didn't resemble anything like I recall from Vietnamese cuisine. The garlic noodles weren't bad but the grilled pork was blend .
Sorry guys but you have work to do, dust off your old recipes, take a trip back to Vietnam and rediscover the fantastic cuisine that country has to offer.

top_reviews.content:
Few places in the US are able to evoke the same feeling of being back in the old country — not only in terms of flavor, but also the decor, atmosphere. A meal at Selam Restaurant is like stepping back into East Africa — from the basic interior, the cable TV, the tablecloths.

Quanta Firfir is bold in spiciness, full-flavored, savory, cooked tomato tangy sauce. Ask for the habesha injera flown in from East Africa for the real-deal; though adding a few dollars to the price, it is well-worth it.

The tidy kitchen has nothing to hide — with diners regularly chatting with the cook as she prepares your meal at the stove. The ultimate cozy feel.

Open from 6am-11pm, catering to the long and late hours often kept by recent immigrants to America. A true gem.
a real hole in the wall. i walked under multiple freeways to get here. super yummy food, it feels like you walked into someone’s home kitchen.

Spices were flavorful, and experience felt genuine. Wasn’t provided utensils but was expected to use bread to scoop and eat. Ended up being delicious enough to take home. Didn’t like the bread taste though, could be just a personal preference, since the person I came with enjoyed it.
Very delicious lamb, and they gave me a big portion for one person that came out to $22! A good amount of outdoor seating by the street.
Salem has best veggie combo I've ever had, and there is gluten free injera. I go here at least once a week

top_reviews.content: The delightful disposition of the workers is what made us stay in and eat. Best ribs in San Francisco, and the links... oh they're the reason I'm righting a review, my wife loves them and we all know happy wife happy life. Mo the owner is great and we thank her for the hospitality and great food

If you're craving an authentic, no-frills barbecue experience, Let’s Eat BBQ and more in San Francisco which has reopened after years of closure is the place to be. From the moment you step onto the block, the intoxicating aroma of smoky goodness welcomes you—an unmistakable sign of top-tier barbecue. The menu offers classic staples like barbecue chicken, smoked brisket, house-made sausages, and world-class pork ribs.  I’ve only had the ribs and links which are executed flawlessly.

What stood out for me was the mixed greens, which were exceptional. The balance between earthy tangy collard greens and the peppery kick of mustard greens shows that this kitchen knows its craft. Definitely don’t pass on the potato salad either.

Unlike the trend-driven California barbecue scene, Let’s Eat BBQ feels like a return to tradition. It’s a family-owned gem where you roll up, order a barbecue plate and a cold beer, and walk away smiling, knowing you’ve just had an amazing meal made with love and patience—all at a fair price. This is barbecue as it should be.

If you can save some room for dessert. A friend was raving about the banana pudding. I’ve heard great things about the peach cobbler and can’t wait to try it for myself. Highly recommended!
The real deal … best bbq spot by miles. You get a ton of meat - bbq pork ribs and sauce is killer - melt in your mouth brisket, and just lovely friendly people.

Go. To. Tarocco. You. Will. Love. It. Everything is healthy and delicious, but in an indulgent way that doesn't compromise on flavor. And the daily salads are always a home run. Because the salads are already composed, and you order at the counter, service is immediate. They also have delicious coffee and tea beverages, as well as a daily agua fresca and some really delicious-looking desserts (one a day). I'm vegan, and they have yet to offer vegan desserts, but they always have at least 3 vegan salads available. This is my go-to spot to bring out-of-towners or to go with a girlfriend for a lovely lunch in a beautiful environment. [NOTE: Only open for lunch on weekdays. My adult daughter and I had tickets to see Beauty and the Beast, so we decided to have dinner at Thai Curry beforehand. It was hands down the best decision we could have made!
We started with appetizers. I ordered the Crispy Shrimp Rolls, and my daughter had the Chicken Satay. The shrimp rolls were fried to absolute perfection...crispy on the outside with tender, sweet shrimp inside. Paired with the sweet chili sauce, they were incredible. The Chicken Satay was equally impressive. They were perfectly seasoned, juicy, and tender. The creamy peanut sauce and refreshing cucumber relish took it to another level.
For our entrées, I ordered the Eggplant Basil with beef, and my daughter chose the Crispy Pork with Chinese Broccoli. OMG...both dishes were phenomenal! The crispy pork with sautéed Chinese broccoli in a savory garlic sauce was pure perfection in every bite. My Eggplant Basil was just as delicious, and adding the beef was definitely the right choice. It was tender, flavorful, and complemented the dish beautifully.
We also couldn't pass up their special of two Jell-O shots for $5. They were the biggest Jell-O shots I've ever seen! We chose cherry, and they were the perfect fun treat to finish off our meal.
From the outstanding food to the attentive staff, excellent service, and warm, inviting ambiance, everything exceeded our expectations. This restaurant easily earns a 10/10 from me. We absolutely loved our experience and will definitely be back!

It was my father’s 70th birthday, and it was our first time dining at Lula’s Eritrean Restaurant.

From the moment we walked in, we were captivated by the restaurant’s vibrant colors, elegant décor, and the warm golden glow that filled the space. The air carried the inviting scent of fragrant spices and freshly prepared dishes, creating an immediate sense of comfort and anticipation. Soft conversations and the gentle hum of activity blended seamlessly with the welcoming ambiance, making the atmosphere feel both festive and intimate—the perfect setting to celebrate such a special milestone. The service was exceptional from start to finish—we barely had time to settle into our seats before attentive staff greeted us with genuine smiles and made us feel like honored guests throughout the evening.

As someone who doesn’t regularly eat traditional Eritrean food, other than my mother’s, I wasn’t sure what to expect, but this turned out to be one of the most memorable dining experiences I’ve ever had. The aromas alone were incredible, with notes of warm berbere spices, savory stews, and freshly baked injera filling the table with anticipation as each dish arrived. Every bite revealed layers of flavor—rich, vibrant, and perfectly balanced without feeling overly heavy. Tangy, spongy injera soaked up deeply seasoned sauces, while the blend of spices delivered a satisfying warmth that lingered pleasantly on the palate. The textures and seasonings complemented one another beautifully, from tender, slow-cooked dishes to fresh accompaniments that added brightness and contrast. The presentation was stunning, with colorful platters arranged artfully, transforming the meal into a feast for both the eyes and the palate.

What made the evening even more special was sharing these new flavors with my family while celebrating my father’s milestone birthday. There was a genuine sense of joy and togetherness that made the experience unforgettable. Surrounded by the restaurant’s warm hospitality and the lingering aroma of spices, we found ourselves savoring not only the food but also the moment itself. Everything exceeded our expectations, from the food and service to the welcoming atmosphere. We left feeling grateful, satisfied, and excited to return to explore more of the menu. I highly recommend this restaurant and can’t say enough wonderful things about it and the owner.

—

at some point, someone told me all their beans are cooked in lard, so i can't order any of the burritos anymore, because i don't eat pork. not to be hyperbolic, but this lowkey ruined my life. for years i had been deliberately electing not to ask because i didn't want to know that. it was a sad day. it's been a couple more years and i'm almost over it now, though; the tacos and quesadillas are still transcendental. this is the real deal; it's exactly what you want out of a taco truck: a slightly-too-long wait, workers who get stuff a little wrong sometimes because they can't quite hear you from up in a small enclosed space full of kitchen noise, likely a level of compliance with health code that is questionable at best, and at the end of the day? street food at the absolute zenith of the medium's potential. both salsas are a powerfully smooth blend of flavors, and both the grilled veggies and the meats themselves have the perfect degree of char & texture. people say if you want a real burrito, go to los angeles, and if you want a real taco, go to tijuana. i'm sure they're right, but this has to be close enough. you can get this one day & an equally out-of-this-world representation of some other cuisine the next without going very far, and that's what is so special about the bay. chile bravo does a commendable job of showing off why oakland is magical, and i think that makes it certifiably iconic. by the way, i'm sure they cook everything on the same grill, and there's probably nothing the lard doesn't touch. i can't emphasize enough how much i DON'T! What makes it unique is the ability to customize your bowl with a wide variety of toppings, from spicy peanuts and chickpeas to paneer, fruits, nuts, and pickles, so every visit can be a little different.

The concept is refreshingly humble: take a beloved South Indian home-style dish and elevate it with fresh ingredients and thoughtful combinations.

top_reviews.content:
Great staff and good food!

The flan was absolutely fantastic!! One of the best one I have had.

great little spot in Noe Valley. eclectic menu with something for everyone. i had the pork chop cooked to perfection and the accompaniments balanced the salt and fat. had the cauliflower appetizer - a little under cooked which i like but may not be other people’s preference. salmon was cooked perfectly as well. good portions and the flan was the icing on the cake. the atmosphere was cool - local art and the menu reflects the owners memento around the world hence the little influences to their menu decisions.

We went to Memento for a pre-Valentine’s dinner, and it was such a lovely experience.

The servers were warm and attentive, and the food was excellent. As a vegetarian, I’ve never really had the chance to enjoy paella but their vegetarian paella was outstanding, and honestly worth returning for on its own. My partner had the pork chop and absolutely loved it as well.

To finish, we ordered what might truly be the world’s best caramel flan which was rich, silky, and unforgettable. The ambiance was chic and romantic, and they also have a really solid wine selection.

The only small note: the suggested tip on the bill was calculated on the post-tax amount rather than pre-tax. Aside from that, everything was wonderful.

Highly recommend for date night or a relaxed evening out with friends. We had a fantastic time and will definitely be back.

Foods are on the very salty side, both appetizer and main dishes. The price is definitely on a higher end, which we personally feel like it’s overpriced. The atmosphere is good though! Very cute place to have a quality time with friends, family or the significant other.

Outstanding Anniversary Dinner!

We celebrated our anniversary at Memento in San Francisco’s Noe Valley and had an absolutely incredible experience! From the moment we walked in, we were impressed by the casual elegant atmosphere and beautiful artwork throughout the restaurant.

Rafael, the owner, personally greeted and served us all evening. The thoughtful touches really stood out - there was an anniversary card waiting at our table and we were surprised with complimentary champagne to toast. This level of personal attention made the night feel truly special.

Cocktails were exceptional:

Defying Gravity (jalapeño tequila with passion fruit) - perfectly balanced with just the right amount of spice. Island In The Sun - like a refined piña colada with thyme, completely transparent thanks to their 4-day infusion process that Rafael explained.

Food highlights:

Truffle fries with truffle aioli - crispy and perfectly seasoned.
Beef empanadas - crispy dough, flavorful filling, great carrot purée accompaniment.
Millionaire Beef Tacos on blue corn tortillas - tender beef tenderloin, beautifully presented.
Mussels with coconut curry sauce - this sauce was absolutely incredible, we took some home!
The flan for dessert was the best I've ever had - thick custard texture with rich caramel.

Everything was beautifully presented with pansy flowers that Rafael told us come from their own backyard. The meatball stroganoff was the only dish that didn't quite hit the mark for us - the sauce could have used more flavor. However, this could be that the garlic and truffle from the Truffle fries, affected my ability to taste well.

As a special anniversary surprise, Rafael gifted us a slice of New York cheesecake that was absolutely perfect. His dessert wine pairing recommendation was also spot-on.

We felt like royalty the entire evening. The combination of creative cocktails, mostly outstanding food, beautiful atmosphere, and exceptional personal service from Rafael made this an unforgettable anniversary dinner. We're already planning our next visit and will definitely be recommending Memento to friends and family!

Thanks to everyone for making it a delightful stop in.  12/20/25!

Poor food quality, poor service.

Food: My party ordered 5 entrees (grilled vegetable panini, fish and chips, short rib burger,  quinoa salad, and fish tacos) and one appetizer (baby back BBQ pork ribs). The grilled vegetable panini was very salty such that it was difficult to eat. The fish and chips were likely double fried such that the batter was almost inedible because it was hard and burned. The temperature of the pork rib appetizer was luke warm, and the meat was tough, like a leftover heated up in a microwave. The fish tacos were fair but not particularly good. The short rib burger was done well, and the quinoa salad was fresh tasty.

Service: Our server was was very insistent on selling us more items even when it was clear we knew what we wanted. He kept pushing us, which was uncomfortable. One of our water glasses was dirty and we asked for a new one, and the server did not hide his annoyance. Then he brought a new glass with warm tap water, sending a clear message.

Atmosphere: the dining room was pleasant and clean. We wanted to watch the a World Cup game and it was available on a TV in the dining room.

The menu is not too extensive. I appreciated the outdoor seating, reasonably priced cider and the mellow music. To be honest, the service was slow, the burger was dry and there were raisins in the coleslaw. I would return to take advantage of the street parking and outdoor dining.  (I ordered a Nepalese appetizer, fish and chips [nuggets?] and a kids meal.)

Best patio in Berkeley!  The service is always friendly and nice.  The food is prepared fresh and always so good.  Best momos in town!   My husband and I will come for wine, apps and sun.  Their brunch is really good too.   Dog friendly too

Dined here for brunch and enjoyed it quite a bit. They have a nice menu combination of breakfast and lunch items. I chose both! The steak sandwich and a waffle. I know, gluttony.

The steak sando was on ciabatta bread and cooked perfectly. I asked for medium and that’s how it came. Steak fries usually not my thing but these were crispy and seasoned enough.

The waffle loses points because it was soft and had no crispness at all. And the syrup was the fake maple. They improve that and it’s a winner.

The last dish was the Mom’s eggs Benedict which comes with ham. Hash browns were thin and crispy… perfect.

And the atmosphere of this little tavern is great. Natural light. Woody. And a bar. Makes me want to come here to watch a Cal game.

Service was a little spotty. Nice enough but kind of slow and didn’t quite get my order right.

top_reviews.content: We saw this restaurant on our way back home and had to try it the next day. As soon as we looked at the menu, we knew this spot was different from other Americanized Thai restaurants in the city. Everything we tried was so good. I could eat their lemongrass catfish and drunken noodles everyday. The curry was good too but since sf has so many good Indian restaurants, I probably wouldn’t order this again. Cloud ring (shrimp paste donuts) was good, but I don’t think I’d order it again. I cannot wait to go back and try other dishes! I love spicy food and found their medium level to be pretty spicy!

I really, really love Sawaan and am so happy I got to experience this beautiful restaurant as many times as I did this summer. As someone who was born in Thailand and accustomed to an intense level of spice, they never disappointed. I often have the issue of food lacking spice, but I still remember my second visit when I was given a large bowl of Thai chillis. The service is so spectacular, and the food is delicious. We love the Purple Wok, and I love the Spicy Drunken Heaven noodles, but honestly, you can't miss here. I can't say enough nice things about this place, considering my recent bad experience at another renowned Thai place deemed the best in SF. I disagree. It has to be Sawaan first!

We are a family (8) from Thailand born and raised there stumbled upon this new Thai restaurant while we're waiting for a pizza place next door, and decided to give them a chance.

Mind oh mind the first best decision in 2026! Everything was super delicious that we didn't want to write a review because we're afraid that they'd become so popular, and we have to wait in line next time.

The food quality is 10 out of 10. The portion was perfect for 4 adults to share on each dish. Most dishes are even more delicious than what we could get in Thailand!

The presentation on each dish was very thoughtful and detailed oriented. Our kids (7-13) were super grateful they got to eat the food the same quality they used to taste in Thailand.

Oh, they also have the best Thai iced tea, not the sugar and color only kind. It tasted like the real deal.

Also, be mindful not to order extra spicy because as Thais who eat spicy food, we were suffering when we ordered the soup extra spicy!

Definitely going back to try the rest on the menu!

They were very creative with their menu. Our favorite was the fried shrimp rings. They were perfectly crispy on the outside and bouncy on the inside. Although there was a minor error in our order, they promptly rectified it for us. We truly appreciate their attention to detail and customer service!

I visited Sawaan a couple months ago now and I still remember the fondness I felt after leaving the meal. They are a new modern Thai restaurant with a fresh take on a thai cuisine menu and trendy decor. The staff here are so sweet and considerate.

We ordered the tofu cloud, spicy drunken heaven, and the lemongrass catfish. The tofu cloud came with this thick and sweet peanut sauce. I enjoyed the aromatics in the drunken noodles. Our favorite was definitely the catfish. Make sure to eat everything while it is hot! You can taste the freshness in the catfish.

Food is most important at a restaurant, yet I’d like to highlight how well decorated Sawaan is. They put a lot of effort in the design choices from the ceramics to the light fixtures to the menu.

As I get closer to the Working Girls' Cafe my imagination starts going into hyper drive mode and I see myself digging into this flavorful bowl of goodness, my taste buds wake up, my heart starts beating faster and faster and by the time I am at the counter and my now good friends at the other side of the counter ask me if I want the "regular" I automatically respond affirmative!! What is in it? Well it's got Chicken Breast, Avocado, Bacon, Gorgonzola Cheese, Hard boiled Egg, Cucumber, Tomato, and Red Onions and it is all served on a bed of Organic Kale and Organic Quinoa,with Balsamic Vinaigrette on the side.

Aside from the California Cobb Bowl, the sandwiches here are to die for! Take the California Melt sandwich which I had last time I was there. It is delicious! The vibe was equally disappointing. Instead of the welcoming energy you’d hope for in a café, it felt rushed, careless, and uninspired. There are so many great spots in the city for coffee and a quick bite — this place just isn’t one of them.

Bottom line: If you want burnt-tasting coffee and a forgettable experience, this might be your spot. Otherwise, do yourself a favor and go literally anywhere else.

A Satisfying Stop at Le Regency Deli

We were returning to the office from a quick errand when we spotted Le Regency Deli and, feeling hungry, decided to share a breakfast sandwich. When we entered, we saw two men inside behind the counter. One, who I presume was the owner, was on the phone, so the grill man approached and took our order of ham and egg on a bagel. While waiting, I surveyed the space. It's long and narrow. As you enter, you'll find the counter displaying food on your left, with refrigerators containing canned and bottled soft drinks on the right. The dining area, with about 15 tables, and the restroom are located at the end.

A few years ago, before COVID hit, this place bustled with the Financial District breakfast and lunch crowd, often having a line out the door. They even had outdoor seating. However, today, there were only a few patrons during our visit.

The grill man prepared our breakfast bagel and handed it to us in a compostable box. It was generously layered with ham and topped with an egg. We strolled back to the office, took a bite of our respective halves, and both gave it a thumbs-up.

top_reviews.content:
My husband and I were recently recommended to try Dolly’s restaurant and we’re so glad we did. From the moment we walked in, the whole experience felt relaxed and welcoming. The hosts and owners were incredibly warm and friendly.

The food was delicious. We loved the cheese wheel pasta, the bread and tomato salad, and they also had a really good wine selection. As a small business owner myself, I always appreciate supporting local family-owned spots that truly care about good food and good service. Dolly’s is definitely one of those places. We’ll absolutely be back.

We came here because of the 4.8 star rating and I’m still trying to figure out how that happened. We spent nearly $100 for fast-food quality (or worse) pasta and slow service. I ordered the Alfredo in the Parmesan wheel with smoked salmon. The sauce was incredibly watery and seemed like it was just jarred sauce boiling in a vat. It didn’t even seem like the place had a stove. The pasta was precooked and warmed up before being mixed with the watery sauce and tossed in the cheese wheel. Then they put a whole package of smoked salmon on top, not cut up or mixed in or anything. The only upside was that the servers were very nice! They kept offering us free wine. I’m not sure if they knew it was an off night or if that is the norm there. Based on the kitchen they seem to have I’m not sure how it could be much better.

What do you get when you take a young Sri Lankan chef, (Dolly) who studied under a master of Italian cuisine, (Ruggero Milano, of Milano ristorante in Tiburon), an obsession with fresh pastas, imported desserts and gelatos and add one of the best wine lists in the East Bay and a giant authentic Permesano Regiano cheese wheel?

You get my new favorite Italian place in the Bay Area.
In an out of the way location, one block from the Rialto theaters in El cerrito, this area is mostly known for its Asian cuisine which I have covered extensively, but lo and behold! An authentic Italian ristorante, with a real trained Italian chef, and a casual laid-back setting and unassuming vibe.

Following my patented strategy of emulating success, I asked the guy next to me, (Who turned out to be a baseball scout, and looked super happy with what he was eating) what to order, and he recommended the Smoked salmon Fettuccine Alfredo.
I ordered it and I watched the careful preparation of perfect pasta ending with a generous toss in a Parmesan cheese wheel, and a glass of Daou Cabernet.
Dolly really knows what she's doing, and has set a new standard for my fettuccine enjoyment, and while the dish was so rich I felt guilty eating it alone, she still gave me a spoonful of REAL Italian spumoni, flown in recently.
This place is a kind of restaurant we need more of in the East Bay. Unassuming, friendly, homey, first class Italian food for the people. I cannot recommend this place highly enough if you want to have an actual Italian food experience but need to stick close to the east bay.
And by real Italian I don't mean some shishi spot that's going to charge you $100 to bring out three olives and a single slice of veal, I'm talking about real, hearty, delicious Italian food for the people.
Thanks Dolly.
Strategy: go see a movie at the Rialto, one block away, and arrange to have some Italian food afterwards. You'll be glad you did

I went there with my partner, and the wheel cheese is amazing! They have a balanced style, very soft, chewy, and milky at the same time. The owner is so nice! We had a wonderful time! Definitely will go back!

A lovely, cozy place in El Cerrito. Family owned. Friendly service and friendly customers!  And a Fettuccine Alfredo to die for! Great salads as well and imported Italian desserts. My friend and I split the Mozzerella Fresca and the Fettucine Alfredo and it was plenty. We didn’t have room for a dessert, but we will be back!

top_reviews.content: My husband and I have been going here almost weekly since their soft opening 3 years ago. We are regular customers. We eat out a lot and like to try restaurants all over. This is one of my favorite places to go to for Bun Bo Hue, Vietnamese Rice Dish, and Pho. We occasionally cook pho and bun Bo hue at home, but it’s very time consuming. So we like to go here when we are tired to cook and craving their dishes. Would definitely recommend this restaurant!

I’ve been looking for a great Vietnamese spot like this, and I’m so glad I found it. The grilled pork chop plate and fresh shrimp spring rolls were both delicious and definitely worth coming back for, and it beats driving all the way to San Jose!

What really stood out was how thoughtful and accommodating they were with my toddler. Without me even asking, they brought a bowl, plastic spoon, and scissors to help with the meal. Such a kind touch.

Super nice family-owned spot with great food and warm service. We’ll definitely be coming back!

This is my to go place for pho Hanoi.

I have tried pretty much everything on the menu.  Today, I had #17, pho tai with fresh wide noodles.  Make sure to order clear broth if you do not want too much oil.  I always have the cooked bean sprouts too. I usually order 17, my go to order.

The broth is very tasty and generally do not need to add hoisin sauce.  Just a fresh squeezed lemon.

This place is not that busy on the weekdays.
Last week I had bun bo hue, spicy noodles soup with a large beef rib. This place bun bo hue is ok only.  However, their northern dish of bun cha Hanoi is really good, must try.

The broth seems different from most pho places I have been to. I think the secret is more garlic.

Prices can be a little high, but the food is good. I paid over $30 for a bowl of standard pho and an appetizer with no drink. The pho bowl was very big, though.

Service wasn't bad, but it also wasn't great. Maybe they were a bit tired since it was close to 9 pm.

Dropped by for dinner.  The place wasn't busy, so we were able to get a seat right away.

They took a bit longer to bring out the food than we thought.  We ordered a vermicelli bowl and a broken rice plate.  The flavors were okay, but the broken rice plate was cold by the time I got to it.  The prices were  a bit high for the type of food.

The service was okay.  They checked on us often.

Overall, it's a decent Vietnamese place when compared to other places in the area.

top_reviews.content: Good sandwiches here. What took me here was I needed to deposit some money at the bank next door. The line was hella long at the bank on a Saturday. Luckily I didn't need to see a teller and used the ATM. With over 25 minutes left on my meter, I wanted to try Ocean Subs after seeing it on my feed for so long. They were open at 11am. My Original Sub $14 was excellent. There were a few people ahead of me and my sandwich was ready in 10 minutes. Good job Ocean Subs. What a good lunch.

Stopped by Ocean Subs in SF and ordered the Atomic Sub on soft French with Swiss. It was loaded and super satisfying.

The bread was soft but still held everything together, and the meats had that nice kick without being overwhelming.

Also, their Tsunami sauce is sooo good--definitely ask for extra (like heavy extra lol). It really makes the sandwich. Super garlicky, lemony and tangy!

Nothing fancy, just a really solid sandwich that hits when you're hungry. I'd definitely come back when I'm craving a classic sub.

Wonderful experience at Ocean Subs. I ordered a Dutch crunch with salami, mortadella, provolone, and all the toppings. The mortadella and salami are a salty, slightly fatty contrast to the mound of lettuce they add into the sandwich, a pleasant mouthful experience. Half a sandwich is enough for a light meal, and a full one left me absolutely stuffed. All the toppings provided for  a crunchy contrast to the salty, pliable meat, and the volume of meat and toppings were amazing, the sandwich was about 3 inches in height.  Service was great, ordering process was quick and simple, and the food came within 10 minutes. I'm a big fan of the chairs inside, they remind me of a coin, having a circular surface. Interior is quite small, with 3-4 tables inside. Great experience, friendly staff, highly recommend for sub sandwich lovers!

This little sub shop lives up to the recent hype. Entering the top 25 restaurants in SF list I had to try it out. A simple menu with just four options, I devoured the Atomic Sub in one quick sitting. Just one guy behind the counter wrapping up delicious sandwiches on fresh Dutch crunch bread that left my mouth raw it was so crunchy! If it was closer to me, I’d go weekly, thankfully it isn’t too far to support a few times a year.

First time trying Ocean Subs today. Delicious! We ordered the original and the atomic w/cheddar toasted on Dutch crunch. Meat to bread to veggie ratio was perfect.  Bread was tasty and had a satisfying cronch. Service was great and staff so nice! 10/10 recommend. Understand exactly why they have earned so many awards. Only nega
tive thing I can say is parking can be challenging to find. However that’s SF and not the shops fault lol.

Tokyo Express, back in the early 2010's, used to be really popular with a line during lunchtime. Some of my old co-workers used to enjoy coming here. Business has sure when downhill since the pandemic. There was only one other table occupied at lunch time on a Wednesday. The staff was really busy however packing up to-go orders. I had their Wednesday special, the tonkatsu $13. The pork fillet was a bit dry and not juicy, tender and properly cooked. The panko had a nice crunch. It did come with an alright tonkatsu sauce. With this dish, it should come with shredded cabbage served with a miso-ginger dressing or Japanese sesame dressing, but it didn't come with it. Since this is not an authentic Japanese restaurant, I didn't knock off stars for that. Service was non-existent as this is an order at the counter style restaurant and no tea or water was served. There was a free cup of miso soup and my food came out in a reasonable amount of time.

I came to this location as their other locations in the city have all closed, and this is presumably the original or only place of theirs left as of April 2021. I often had the chicken udon on Mondays (the day it is a discounted special) at their Stonestown location with my late grandmother, who passed the day before I visited and wrote this review today.

The cashier working today's service was personable and pleasant to interact with, and was empathetic with my story of frequenting a Tokyo Express location in the past with my grandmother. The chicken udon I usually go for on Mondays from the daily special discount was consistently good as it's always been, whether compared to at Stonestown or the Metreon, or compared to years back.

Indoor dining service was offered and they assign a table after ordering, after that they bring the food to your table like the other locations.

Update early 2022: After reopening on the first Monday of the new year, some of their prices have gone up a bit. In the months since I've been visiting regularly, I've noticed senior customers come and sit for traditional waiter service where they are given menus and their orders are taken at the table rather than the register, so either of these dining options are available. The staff also recognize me when I try to come on a weekly basis so I'm glad to have been recognized as a regular.

top_reviews.content: I had to stay in a hotel in Alameda for 10 days because my apartment was infested with mold. Little did I know I would stumble upon this amazing gem of a restaurant. I went here five times during my stay and every single item was so delicious. The food is abundant, incredibly fresh, super flavorful, and very reasonably priced. Sadly my stay here ends tomorrow but I'll definitely be back!

A lot of people had been raving about Mango & Mint. I finally made it there yesterday for the first time and ... it was even better than my expectations!
I ordered the spring rolls. They were so fresh and so tasty! 👍The flan is also a must eat! 🙂The waitress double checked on the ingredients of the sauce to confirm if it was GF or not.
I loved the food so much I returned today for more spring rolls and flan. The waitress greeted as if I was a regular as she recognized me from yesterday. 😉😊
Check them out; they offer much more than what I opted for.

From the outside I was unsure about this place. Looked too bougie and fancy to be legit.

But the moment I walked in, I saw and heard 4 Vietnamese ladies behind the counter all shouting at each other in Vietnamese, and then saw all the printed-out signed taped everywhere advertising additional menu items, and it was then that I knew that it was actually going to be *very* legit.

I was not wrong. I ordered the char siu banh mi and it was excellent. It was also the size of a large burrito. The char siu was awesome and the veggie-to-meat ratio was perfect. My only small gripe was that the roll was not quite as crusty as I prefer, but that's a minor thing overall.

I do a delivery route on Alameda every Friday, so I will *definitely* be back. Probably try the pork vermicelli bowl next time, I saw them preparing some while I was waiting and they looked fantastic.

We tried Mango and Mint in Alameda for the first time on a Sunday afternoon, and it was such a pleasant surprise! The portion size was amazing for the price huge and definitely worth it, especially I love veggies! I ordered the grilled lemongrass pork chop with rice, and it was flavorful. Few seating capacity but that is totally fine since it it kinda quick service set-up.

The Thai milk tea was just how I like it  rich with tea flavor, not overly sweet. We also had the pineapple coconut smoothie, and you could really taste the mint and kale  refreshing and fun!

Service was great & the staff was friendly, and the menu is simple, with plenty of drink options. Overall, it’s such a wonderful local find a true underrated spot in Alameda.

I just hope the serving sizes stay consistent because everything we ordered tasted great. We’ll definitely be back!

Mango & Mint is such a great little Vietnamese spot on Webster in Alameda.
It's one of those places you’re lucky to have in your neighborhood.
Their bánh mì is easily one of the best I’ve had—fresh, flavorful, and perfectly put together. The chicken salad was also a standout. It's light, well-balanced, and really satisfying.
Everything here feels thoughtfully made, and you can tell they take pride in their food. It’s a bit more on the premium side, but absolutely worth it for the quality you’re getting.
They’re always busy (which says a lot), and for good reason.
I love that I can walk here from home, it’s definitely become a go-to.
