top_reviews.content:
Yokohama Iekei Ramen is a solid, no frills ramen spot that keeps things simple.

The staff was very friendly and welcoming, and it felt like the kind of place that might be run by the owners themselves, which adds a nice personal touch.

The ramen comes out hearty and filling, with portions that lean on the large side. It is definitely the kind of bowl that sticks with you. That said, the overall flavor landed somewhere in the middle. Good enough to enjoy, but not especially memorable.

Parking is a bit of a trade off. You can park for free in the garage next door, which is a big plus since street parking is almost nonexistent. The only catch is the short walk, which feels just a little longer than expected when all you want is a hot bowl of ramen.

It is a comfortable spot with kind service and a filling meal, even if the ramen itself does not quite stand out.

Pretty good ramen but small portions for the price.

I stopped by here for lunch before my movie and thought it’d be worth a try considering it was right next to the theater.

They have a good amount of options for food and also let you customize things like broth richness, spice level, and noodle firmness.

I got the Black Garlic Ramen and it came very quickly. It comes with an ok amount of noodles, a soy sauce egg, two small pieces of chashu, and some toppings, though for almost $20 I expected more of the non-protein toppings.

Broth was pretty flavorful and the noodles had a nice texture. Not the most exceptional bowl I had, but perfectly passable as a neighborhood choice.

Good Ramen, more expensive than it’s probably worth, but still enjoyable.

We wanted a good, quick bowl of ramen and that’s just what we got here at Yokohama Iekei . Parking is very convenient as there’s a big lot just steps away from the restaurant and the interior is simple and cozy with great service. They offer some decent variety in bowls although we opted for their classic tonkotsu and shio ramens. The bowls are priced a bit higher but the food is certainly good which offsets that a bit.

Our bowls came very quick, we’re talking about just over 5 min or so for a party of 4 which was impressive. The food itself was pretty good considering the quick preparation. The tonkotsu broth is rich and deep with above average chashu that brings the bowl a little pop of flavor. The shio ramen is also nice and savory and comes with thick noodles unlike the tonkotsu’s thin noodles. The thick noodles are definitely better with a better chew so opt for those if you come in. The toppings are good, specifically the bamboo shoot but two areas they could improve on is the soft boiled egg, it felt a bit lacking in seasoning, and the setting. The price of the bowl was a bit high considering it felt like a very casual place to dine at. It’s by no means a bad setting, it’s just at that price point it didn’t feel like it aligned. Still, Yokohama Iekei is a good ramen place that’s more on the casual side, probably better suited for a casual date or hangout than any dinner or special night.

This place serves the best ramen in the area. Each of the different soup bases is uniquely flavored and served at the perfect temperature. I tried the black garlic ramen and fried oyster. They were so good! Thank you 🙏

We definitely come back here..

While I was waiting, the waiter gave me a free lemon iced tea. What a nice surprise. I tipped accordingly as I didn't see the other customers get a free iced tea. The pork chops tasted OK. It had a smokey baked flavor. The sauce contained actual tomatoes. As for the crust, it was missing that traditional crusted layer. An increased in cooking time would have infused more flavor to the spaghetti. It was a good lunch today.

Original review: This is my first time back to Orchids Cafe since they re-opened for indoor dining a year and a half ago. For the longest time, I saw they were only opened for take-out when I drove by. The food here is delicious with authentic HK flavors. My iced milked tea was very good. They are now added to my rotation of restaurants to eat at for lunch. (Usually I go to 21 Taste House, Chase Luck, Dots, Fate Tea House, GoGo 7, Jojo's or Pakwan.) Today, I only had 30 mins for lunch because of the loading parking meter limit and opted for the curry pork chop spaghetti instead of the longer prep time baked pork chop spaghetti (takes 20 mins.) To my surprise, pork chopS came out. On the menu, it only listed a singular "pork chop." What a pleasant surprise! That and they were huge. The chef did a great job. They put the curry on the side so that the crunchy tonkatsu don't get soft. The breading on the pork chops were on point. Service was excellent as there was only one other party dining during lunch. Great job everyone at Orchids Cafe. I felt at home with the soft Cantonese music playing in the background.

Ordered a brisket with rice, but they gave me a Japanese style base, even though it’s a Hong Kong Cha-Chaan-Teng. The Brisket Tendon that comes with 咖喱牛腩 was also clearly not stewed, was rather tough and hard, when it should be soft and break apart. Hot Milk tea was not smooth — it was rather watery. Service was really nice, but I’m not sure about authenticity of the food itself.

Respectfully, for the price, I don’t believe it was worth.

top_reviews.content: Nice and quiet Burmese restaurant located at the top of the hill in Daly City, there is some street parking and it might be hard to find parking in the neighborhood. It’s a nice spot to have dinner and catch up with friends, service is good you either get hot tea or water. And it’s not too busy. We got their tea leaf salad, coconut chicken noodle soup, chicken and potato curry with roti, and pan fried egg noodle with chicken (reminded me of Filipino pancit). The portions were pretty good and the food was fresh. I wasn’t that big of a fan of their tea leaf salad. It was nice and spacious inside too and we didn’t feel rushed.

Haven’t been to Myanmar but the flavor offered by the food gave an authentic experience unique to Burma. There’s
some essence of southeast asian cuisine. Flavor was pretty string and I still enjoyed the culinary experience even after stepping outside the restaurant. ambience felt homy and culturally rich. Service was good. I tried the Khouk Swe Thoke noodle. I good balance of ingredients but the flavor of dried shrimp seemed too strong for me. I recommend Faluda, somewhat has similarity to Philippines’ Halo-halo but this one is rich and creamy with tasty egg pudding! i loved every bite of it. Perfect to end the night with a delicious dessert. Highly recommended!!

Highly rated Burmese restaurant in Daly City. Has a simple interior and decor and feels like a no frills family-run restaurant.

I love Burmese food but didn't like this place nearly as much as other Burmese places in the Bay Area, like Burma Superstar and Burma Love. We ordered the chicken curry and the chicken curry with potatoes and platha. Both were okay, but not what I was expecting. They were similar, the curry broth was thin like soup, and the chicken had bones on it that you had to eat around. The platha was greasy but tasty.

Perhaps we should have ordered something else and would have better enjoyed different dishes. Regardless, the next time I'm craving Burmese, I'll go back to Burma Love instead.

A quaint, cozy restaurant with a TV playing Burmese music videos.

Went in for a quick solo dinner about an hour after opening. About half the tables were occupied but not many tables overall. Service was just 1 main server so it took a few minutes to get orders, etc.

Tea leaf salad was ok, didn't like that it was with cabbage so it wasn't as fresh and crispy as other places.

Mohinga (fish soup) was good, I like that it had the thin rice noodles and that it was cut smaller for easier consumption. Missed out on red chili pepper on the side but could've been requested.

Sour leaf with bamboo shoots dish was great, I don't often see it on the menu for Burmese restaurants but it's a good dish to have with rice.

Burmese style fried rice was good but didn't seem to be anything special. I was expecting something close to biryani but it didn't have any Burmese spices.

Rice noodle salad (Nyangyi thoke) was spicier than expected but tasty overall. Originally wanted to try the other Burmese noodle salad but they were out of it so this was my replacement.

Wouldn't mind going back and trying some of the other dishes with more people. The only downside was the parking, I did have to drive around a few minutes to find parking but street parking and nearby municipal parking lot should be available after 6pm.

As a Burmese who born and raised in Burma (Myanmar) grew up eating home cooked Burmese foods, I can tell you that every single items at Burma Silver are very authentic, super delicious and full of flavors which close to home. Portions are quite big even though the price is very fair compared to other hit Burmese restaurants in San Francisco. The owner/chef Mr. Soe has been the sweetest and most accommodating. Totally recommend the restaurant.

Had a nice meal at Noregia Cafe and tried several dishes. Overall, the food was enjoyable and there was a good variety on menu items.

Upon arrival, the place was pretty much full since it was dinner time and I was greeted by their friendly staffs and seated almost immediately. This place offer many authentic Chinese dishes, they have a lot of things to choose from for a cafe. The menu consists of appetizers, noodles, rice dishes, a la carte items, porridge, soup, chef specialties, vegetables, even party trays are available and much more to choose from. Everything here is made to order which is always a plus for me and I do not mind the wait for the arrival of my food since I am a very patient person. As time went by, the place became fully packed and many customers arrived to pick up their takeout orders. The staffs here are well trained, helpful, polite and professional where my visit was a satisfying and issue free one. You can dine in, order for pick up or have it delivered to you via a delivery app. They accept both cash and card for payments. highly recommend this place to all Chinese food enthusiasts, to anyone willing to try something new, if you are in need of a quick bite or if you just so happen to be in the area to check them out. I definitely will be back to tryout the other delicious options they have to offer.

I waited too long to get my food and spent more time than I had expected in there, causing a line to form by the time I left.

I thought I’d at least get the fried calamari rings first since it was an appetizer, but it came together with my rice bowl so it became a side dish instead I guess.

The teriyaki beef don was okay. I worried I didn’t have enough beef to go with the rice but the rice was flavored with seaweed so I at least didn’t have bites of plain white rice. The fried calamari was too salty and really needed the sauce to balance the saltiness.

⭐⭐⭐☆☆

We stopped by Waterfront Deli for lunch and ordered the Mediterranean Plate, the Kimchi Fried Rice, a water, and a soda. The total came to about $40 for two people, which felt reasonable for the location.

The service was quick, our food was brought out to our table, and there was plenty of seating both inside and outside. The outdoor patio has nice views of the marina, and there’s also a nearby grassy area if you’d rather grab your food to go and enjoy a picnic.

Unfortunately, the food itself was pretty underwhelming. The Kimchi Fried Rice was extremely oily, and the chicken tasted like it wasn’t very fresh. The kimchi itself, however, had great flavor and was easily the best part of that dish.

The Mediterranean Plate was a mixed bag. The hummus was very bland and could have used garlic or more seasoning. The pita was quite tough, and the pickled eggplant was just okay. The standout on the plate was the “Greek salad”—marinated cucumbers, tomatoes, and feta—which had excellent flavor and was definitely my favorite part of the meal.

Overall, the location and service were the highlights of our visit, but the food needs more seasoning and better execution before I’d be excited to return.

One of my favorite places to grab a sandwich. Everything made fresh and comes out tasting delicious. 10/10 recommend!

The waterfront location of Waterfront Deli not only provides a scenic setting but also offers opportunities for a leisurely stroll along the shoreline before or after your meal. Whether you choose to explore nearby parks, take in the sunset, or simply soak in the calming atmosphere, the location adds an extra touch of magic to your time at the deli.

In summary, Waterfront Deli's prime waterfront location elevates the entire dining experience. From enjoying their delectable Turkey and Swiss Cheese sandwich to immersing yourself in the natural beauty surrounding the deli, it's a truly captivating destination that combines exceptional food with picturesque vistas. Whether you're a local seeking a hidden gem or a traveler in search of a memorable dining spot, Waterfront Deli delivers both culinary delights and a scenic feast for the senses.

The food is just as memorable. Spotted this place on a top new restaurant in SF list and immediately saved it. Came in on a Saturday close to their break time and expected to get turned around. But despite the ratings, it was nearly empty around 2PM, so we walked right in. Got the Yukhoe, Yukjeon, and the Spicy Galbijjim, and everything was fantastic.

Yukhoe - Flavor-wise nothing crazy, the classic combo with Korean pear and egg yolk. But what got us was the temperature of the beef. Most yukhoe I've had in the US come out icy, almost numbing. Here it was at the perfect temp. Don't know if they thawed it just right or used fresh beef but we could actually appreciate the natural beef flavor without the brain freeze killing it.

Yukjeon - Fried wrapped in rice paper instead of the usual egg batter, and low-key looked like little briskets. Extra crunchy too. Rice paper doesn't soak up grease the way egg batter does, so the aftertaste was clean.

Spicy Galbijjim - We did level 2 (they said it's around Shin Ramyun heat, but it was a bit hotter than that tbh). Meat was super tender without much fat, and the sauce was what we loved the most. None of that syrupy sweetness most places go for to offset the heat. Just clean spice, and all those radish cubes kept the finish crisp. Most people seem to add cheese on top, but I'd personally go without.

Highly recommend their galbi-jjim! It's quite spicy when you get to the highest level. Also highly recommend their stews, some of the best seolleong-tang I've had (not pictured). The large size was enough for 4 people, and we had leftovers too.

Very disappointing. The short ribs were mostly bones, fat, and tough pieces with barely any actual meat. For the price, I expected much better quality. The service was also not welcoming. Would not recommend.

The only time I ever had Galbi-Jjim was at Daeho and was excited to try this restaurant for the first time! We ordered the Braised Beef Short Ribs and made it an L for four of us & the Crispy Yuk Jeon (never had this before). Service was decent and we sort of had to flag someone to come over when we need water refills, etc.

The Jeon was delicious and the best way to describe - a very thin beef patty wrapped in rice paper. The Galbi-Jjim was huge and the meat was SO tender, literally like the beef melting in your mouth. The only thing I wish I knew was to order more rice cakes as an extra. They had probably less than 8 rice cakes and I kept looking for them lol

Overall, a tasty upscale casual restaurant with good portions at a decent price that I'd definitely revisit to try more of their menu.
+ The beef tartare bibimbap ($26) was tasty and more filling that I imagined, and was visually stunning.
+ The galbi tang soup ($24)  was pipping hot and flavorful, with tender meat and chewy glass noodles.
± The banchan is tasty and varied, but not that much for two people & costs extra ($5) to refill.

top_reviews.content: It was a beautiful Friday in the peak of spring. A friend from college had invited me to Kappo Yuji to experience his favorite omakase, and boy did it live up to the expectations. Though it was a little hard to find(you have to go upstairs with minimal signage outside), however once seated you find yourself in a super cozy setting with only 8 seats available. Then we began our meal. Chef Yuji started us out with the first of a number of dishes and his recommended sake. Throughout the courses, I was blown away by how simple, but balanced everything was. According to my party, this place is the most authentic to Japanese in the US, so with my limited knowledge, I took absolutely everything in. We were taken on a journey of flavor and technique which culminated in a fantastic dessert. The whole place was a complete vibe and Chef Yuji is definitely the X factor in this restaurant. His energy guides you and helps you understand everything. I really enjoyed my time here, and though I may not have left completely full in my stomach, my heart and brain were full nonetheless.

A true hidden gem for traditional Japanese course dining that deserves more attention.

Unlike many omakase spots that focus primarily on nigiri, Yuji delivers a well-rounded experience with a strong emphasis on expertly crafted cooked dishes.

Some standout highlights from our meal:
•	Eggplant with sea urchin – Perfectly balanced, with savory uni adding richness to the soft eggplant.
•	Grilled black cod – Lightly marinated, flaky, and beautifully textured.
•	Kagoshima Wagyu sukiyaki – High-quality, authentic beef served with a flavorful and unique egg dipping sauce.
•	Sweetfish tempura – Tender, with a perfectly crisp batter that preserves the delicate skin.
•	Sesame cold noodles – Rich, creamy sauce paired with springy noodles. A satisfying finish.

All of this was part of an incredible tasting menu priced at just $160.

Another thing I truly appreciated was the seasonal rotation of the menu — something rarely seen in omakase-style restaurants. They adapt the menu monthly based on ingredient availability, which keeps each visit exciting.

Seasonal crab specials to watch for:
•	July–August: Hairy crab season
•	Mid-November–December: Premium snow crab from Japan

We’re already planning to return during crab season. Can’t wait to see what the next menu has in store!

This is my second time here.  The first time was 2022.  This time, was abysmal.  We chose the sake pairing as well.

The food is nothing special, in fact down right common for the price .  The service is by a seemingly overweight bored chef.  Meaning the service was lackluster.

There were 3 late comers to the 9 bar seats.  The chef was distracted, trying to accommodate the new guests but meanwhile forgetting about SAKE pairing .

You felt you were eating at a bad diner.

And as the chef was drinking alcohol with one of the guest, his food quality slid along with his hospitality.

The food actually was disturbingly bland even before his drinking (maybe he drank already for inspiration ?)

And because the restaurant only has 9 seats, you felt compelled to celebrate this chef for his participation of being a "chef" that he was still standing and serving.

He seriously forgot we had sake pairing.

We had to remind him.

And he would seemingly wake up and drag some bottle out and claim it was from his home town, then the next bottle was near his home town, then the third tasting  was sorta near his home town (how does that relate to the food?🎈  Remember, pairing?!).

Sake pairing not sake near where your home town is.

[We also know our sake, he gave us sake we routinely buy to cook with or drink casually]

Worse was he seriously forgot we had the pairing.  Out of 9 dishes, we got 4 drinks out of mini sake glasses.  DON'T do the pairing.

Suffice it to say, not worth $800 for 2 people + the sake pairing 4 drinks out of mini sake glasses each. And mandatory 20% gratuity.

And the food, well neither of us got dysentery: that's a plus. Yay!

Would I recommend.  NO.  BUT WAIT'. Well, I'm sure they would take $800 of of you for 2 people.

But we won't ever be back. Fool me once....

It was my first omakase experience, and Yuji made it very wonderful and special. Every course had its own unique flavor, and the chef gave an introduction to every course when he served them. My personal favorite was the grilled black cod. The soft yuzu taste blended so well with the taste of the cod. I was planning on getting dessert after, but the matcha tiramisu served at the end was so good and I didn't need to go get separate dessert after.

Overall, it was a very solid experience. I do think it's a bit cramped there, but it is cool inside and there is enough space to enjoy the meal.

One of my favorite dining experiences in the city that has flown below the radar for far too long.

Kappo yuji is an intimate traditional Japanese restaurant that serves an array of dishes cooked in different ways: raw, fried, grilled, etc. If you like omakase but want to take a detour and still have that same quality of ingredients, this is a great place to go to.

I’ve been here around 3x and the menu has changed seasonally. Some of my favorite dishes that I’ve had include the seiko kani, which is a delicacy basically a female Japanese snow crab with a lot of roe, their grilled sea bass, and an uni soba dish.

Yuji has never failed to impress me, and get me rather full. Every time I’ve underestimated the set menu and always order extras and end up stuffed.

It is also a set menu worth the price at around $160, quite comparable to most set menus in sf, but in my opinion more worth it due to the intimate small seating setting and quality ingredients used.

Conveniently located in Japantown but easily missed in a humble no sign entryway. Parking is easy in the japantown plaza lot.

Their mandus are huge and tasty; the soup and rice cake parts were seasoned and cooked just right. If you want comfort rice cake soup, this will be it.  2. Bibim naengmyeon. The bibim naengmyeon noodles and not-too-spicy sauce were perfect.   3. Bossam: Served with lettuce and special sauces, but I feel like I was missing one more side that usually comes with the Bossam dish, which is spicy radish that you add inside the Bossam. 4. Chive pancake. I thought it was a tad thicker than I wanted, but my children loved it.   Their side dishes were nicely presented and fresh, especially the fresh Kimchi (geot-jeori). Side dishes are refillable. Overall, this will be the only Korean restaurant I'd visit whenever I'm in Oakland.

top_reviews.content:
We found ourselves in Japan town one night and was waiting in line to be seated at one of the more popular places. My husband was so hungry and impatient, we saw Sora and ended up waiting for a table with a much shorter line.
I’m not sorry we stumbled upon Sora.
The attention to detail is impeccable. They have a very simple menu focusing mainly on Soba. Noodles are made fresh daily.
Staff are very accommodating and polite.
There were no desserts offered on the menu and I’m glad we asked. My husband who does NOT eat asian food gobbled up everything on sight!
We were quite happy with the dessert as well (red bean with mochi ice cream)
Place is clean and though it was a busy saturday night, none of the staff ever made us feel hurried. They were very pleasant with menu questions.
Loved their tea decanter that filters the tea from the cover. Even i asked about where they got that! Would definitely come back next time i’m in the area!

Food was fast and service was great. I got hot soba this time and it was very tasty. I wasn't too impressed with the soba texture but I do want to compliment the soup. I had the duck soba and meat flavor was good. The duck slices on the side somehow wasn't pinky like the pictures but idk if that would differ the flavor otherwise 😅 Tamago appetizer chicken bites: 8/10 they were okay, not very impressive either.
I love how they offer hot broth at the end of your cold soba meal. That was detail-oriented and classy.

What a fantastic soba food option for Japan town San Francisco.
I ordered the combination cold soba with tempura as well as a special egg appetizer.

The soba noodles were perfectly prepared. The right texture, flavor, and temperature. The broth was also terrific with the right temperature, umami, and saltiness.

The tempura was also a highlight, perfectly battered and fried with generous portions of shrimp, squid, and vegetables. They even provided a Matcha salt, that I have never experienced before, that offered a wonderful additional taste to the tempura profile.

To top it all off, the restaurant is run efficiently with polite service. You can easily eat solo or have a party up to four people comfortably. The space is modern, clean, bright, and pleasant to sit in. The music is laid-back, jazz and classical music so that you can easily have a conversation with your dining party or just enjoy the food on your own.

All in all, highly recommended and well worth the price of admission!!

Food:

Sukui Tofu- 5/5
The cold tofu was silky, creamy and slightly nutty from the sesame seed topping.

Ten zaru- 3/5 & assorted tempura (4/5)
Decent soba with assorted tempura. We got some scallop, shrimp, Brussel sprouts, tomatoes, and king oyster mushroom.

Kashiwa Tamago- 4/5

Umami rich broth on a cooler afternoon really hit the spot. However, it got slightly saltier with each bite. The fluffy eggs were the star of the dish!

Service- 5/5
The staff is friendly and welcoming. There was a bit of line (~10-15 min wait) but once we were seated, got our appetizers and dishes right away.

Atmosphere- 5/5
Clean, cozy, and no frills.

Delicious dinner with fresh ingredients leaving us full yet not heavy. Everything I ordered felt light, even the karaage chicken which is fried and usually is seen as heavy, but the lemon and thin fry was just right for me. I enjoyed the matcha beer and was pleasantly surprised to have them prepare it in front of me. I thought it was going to be the bottled kyoto matcha beer, but they actually whisk fresh matcha into the house beer. Soba noodles were great quality, including the duck which was carefully prepared.

I do think prices are a bit steep. Our two sobas, a karaage, and beer with tax and tip added up to a $100+ dinner. There was also a long line to get in, I think we waited around 15/20 minutes. Because of the wait and popularity, you don’t really get a lot of time to dine once you get in since they really try to move things along. I enjoyed the food, but not sure realistically if I will return often.

Came here yesterday and there was a concert at Chase. Was told 45 minute wait for a party of 2. Sounds fair. Hung around the corner overlooking the very cool view of Bayfront Park.

Order only the pizza here. Everything else we got sucked. The calamari was the worse I've ever had. Tiny pathetic squid and the ratio of jalapeño and lemon to the squid was like 3:1. No value and frankly a waste of money and just horrible this is on the menu. Our garlic knots were also bad. Super chewy and not fresh tasting. These appetizers came out like within 5 minutes after ordering.

The disparity between serving the appetizers and our pizza was long and wild. No flow between the two and we just sat there for a while talking and got checked on once.

The pizza here is fantastic though. Very good but idk why it took kinda long, pizzas cook rather quickly. I wouldnt add the anchovies next time. I should of asked but they are just ones from a jar or tin. I thought they would be fresh for some reason. Oops should of researched.

Closed the bill and left. No goodbye or gratitude to the customer. Super awkward and for the price paid didnt match with the product and service. Unsure if short staffed or what but all the teams and individuals working lacked cohesion.

top_reviews.content:
When:
Friday evening, 5:45pm, restaurant was pretty empty except some occasional food takeouts. By 6:30, more people coming in to eat in. But it was not full throughout the time we were at the restaurants.

Experience:
Food came out pretty fast and it was hot(!). Overall, service was good and they checked in on us a few times to make sure all is good.

Food:
- Nam Khao was fantastic. Crispy rice, the mixed minced vegetables, and the cooked sausage. Together with the lime that you can squeeze to preference, it was delicious! Haven't had Nam Khao this delicious in a while!
- Pad See Ew with pork was alright. It was cooked well and a little on the sweeter side rather than savory, but missing the smoky flavor "wok hei" that would take this to the next level that I love.
- Fried Sweet Fish was alright too. Fish is fried with a very thin batter but it had black pepper which my kids doesn't want as they're sensitive to anything spicy. The fish had a light fishy taste to it (fresh water fish) which would be better if they even use a little ginger to cut the fishy taste for a better taste.
- Guay Tiew is very similar to Pad See Ew with the exception that it had a fried egg on the top and had seafood (shrimp and squid).
- Vientiane Crispy Roll is different from regular egg rolls. Made with rice paper roll so it was crispy but also chewy, which is different and may not be what everyone is used to.

Will return to try out other dishes.

A Hidden Gem!

I was initially hesitant to come here because, at the time of writing, this place had fewer than 100 reviews. But I’m so glad I gave it a chance!

This place is genuinely good and definitely worth revisiting. My only criticism is that the chicken in the tom yum soup was a little dry, which honestly isn’t shocking. A lot of places dry out their chicken, and getting it right is hard!

But the Thai papaya salad and beef Laab Seen were excellent. Bright, spicy, flavorful, and absolutely worth ordering. This place deserves more attention!

Rose Garden Uptown is a Laotian & Thai restaurant, featuring many dishes common to that region but also Californian ingredients. They offer table service, but the most business was to-go orders while we dined.

From that interior, you can view their mix of modern-day Instagram aesthetics and architecture with more traditional decorated woven trays on the walls and pictures of the menu items that’s nostalgic of many older Asian restaurants: an appealing combination of new and old to me, just like the menu and ingredients. And the pretty sharing plates also brightened my mood.

We started with the Laotian spring rolls, filled with avocado, carrots, rice noodles, and lettuce. The two sauces—one peanut and one mildly sweet and spicy—provided the most flavor for the dish.

Next came the sweet corn salad with carrots, tomatoes, peanuts, green beans, garlic, lime juice, and a mild chili. I love corn, so I expected to love this dish … and I did! Typically, I go for “hot” when asked for a spice level choice, but my friend was right to go with mild here. That added just enough of a kick to complement the corn’s sweetness. The ingredients had a satisfying variety of flavors, textures, and crunch.

We aimed for Rose Garden Uptown’s Laotian specialties for our second dish, settling on the mok pa. That’s catfish steamed in a banana leaf with herbs. It was my first mok pa, and I did not know if I was supposed to treat the lettuce as lettuce wraps, so I went ahead and did so. I scooped catfish into the small leaves, added cilantro and onions, and really enjoyed those flavors and textures all together. The catfish was soft and soothing, and the herbs cooked with it imparted a wonderful freshness. I will definitely order mok pa again.

Would love to try one of their four types of laab another time!

This place is pretty unassuming from the outside, but don’t let that fool you, the food is excellent and full of flavor. The fresh rolls came with both a sweet and sour sauce and a peanut sauce with crushed peanuts, and both were really good.

The Thai fried rice was delicious too, but my favorite was definitely the sweet chicken. It had just the right amount of sweetness without being overpowering, and the flavor was amazing. It’s nothing like the sweet chicken from Panda Express or PF Chang’s, where it’s mostly just sweet.

The service was friendly and attentive, and the whole experience was great. I’d definitely come back and recommend giving this place a try!

We discovered this place two or three weeks ago, and have now ordered from them 4 times. We LOVE the depth and complexity in the flavors, while also being very balanced.

I've had the Kao Poon, Massaman Curry (my current obession), Green Curry, Pad Thai, and Pad Kee Mao, and all have been winners. This has quickly become my favorite Thai place in Oakland, even beating out Pintoh and Attraros.

top_reviews.content: Loved my experience at Chandni Chowk! The food was absolutely delicious, especially the Goat Nihari. We had a wonderful dining experience at this Indian restaurant. The atmosphere was warm, inviting, and beautifully maintained, making it a great place to relax and enjoy a meal. The food was absolutely delicious, with authentic flavors and perfectly prepared dishes. Loved their chicken mandi rice, chat and Hakka noodles. What truly stood out was the exceptional service—the staff were very friendly, attentive, and welcoming throughout our visit. We felt genuinely cared for from start to finish. Highly recommended, and we look forward to coming back again!

The chaat at Chandni Chowk was amazing! 😍 It was fresh, flavorful, and had the perfect mix of spicy, tangy, sweet, and crunchy flavors. Everything tasted so good and authentic. The portion was great, the presentation was nice, and the place was clean. Loved the food and the friendly service. Definitely a great spot for chaat lovers! 🌶️❤️

I recently visited Chandni Chowk and had an amazing dining experience. From the moment I walked in, the atmosphere felt vibrant and welcoming, capturing the lively spirit of Indian street food culture while still being comfortable for a relaxed meal.

I started with the Tikki Chaat, and it was outstanding. The tikki was perfectly crisp on the outside and soft inside, topped with flavorful chutneys, yogurt, and spices that created a great balance of sweet, tangy, and savory flavors. Every bite was packed with authenticity and reminded me of the chaat stalls back in India.

For the main course, I ordered the Goat Nihari along with Garlic Naan. The nihari was rich, aromatic, and slow-cooked to perfection. The goat was tender and full of flavor, while the gravy had the perfect blend of spices without being overpowering. It tasted homemade and authentic, which is hard to find.

The Garlic Naan was fresh, soft, and beautifully baked with just the right amount of garlic and butter. It paired perfectly with the nihari, making every bite even more enjoyable. The portion sizes were generous, and the quality of the food exceeded my expectations.

The customer service was also amazing they were keep checking on us and the food took no time to reach our tables hot and nice.

Overall, Chandni Chowk delivered an authentic and memorable dining experience. The food was flavorful, fresh, and clearly prepared with care. If you’re looking for delicious Indian cuisine with authentic flavors, I highly recommend trying the Tikki Chaat, Goat Nihari, and Garlic Naan. I’ll definitely be returning to explore more of the menu.

I was told this is where you go to experience what hummus should REALLY taste like, and it did not disappoint.

Very fresh, delicious flavors that taste like they were made by the Middle Eastern grandma and a host of aunties I never had.

Abba's Hummus isn't fancy, but every one of their fillings and toppings are full of flavor and on point. It was my first time trying baba ghanoush, and I found it very yummy.

I particularly liked having my pita spread with a bit of the "spicy" red sauce, which wasn't so hot as much as it was flavorful.

P.S. They also carry a variety of groceries in the back, if you wanted to get anything from Middle Eastern cookies or juices, to cleaning supplies. No fresh produce, though.

I had guests visiting from out of town for Pride, one of which is celiac. She has really struggled with it in her life and lives in a part of the country that does not have options in restaurants. The pizza was better than most in the city! The crust was tasty and crunchy and the toppings were well designed. To see the looks on my friends face as she ate the best gluten free breads she ever had was so incredibly rewarding.

This restaurant is very special and is a truly perfect option for anyone, dietary restriction or not, to go. Thank you so much for enabling this experience for us! top_reviews.content:
Latte Express a local family-owned small business located on Kearny Street [between Clay and Commercial near Chinatown and Commercial District] is a popular lunch spot for top-notch Bánh mì, a/k/a “Baguette Vietnamien.” (means "wand, rod, or baton" in French which could also refer to “chopsticks” or “drumsticks.”)  The Vietnamese sandwich albeit arguably originated from French baguette during the colonialization era in the 19th and 20th centuries has its own distinctive characterizations, i.e., incorporating the mixture of rice flour, a variety of their own ingredients, such as pickled vegetables (turnip and carrots), fresh cucumber, jalapeno and cilantro, as well as various meats (pork, chicken, or beef).
Unlike many other Bánh mì sandwich shops in the City, Latte has my thumbs up 👍:1) freshly baked bread (baguet), crunch but not mushy {❌watch out for outdated bread that likely thrown out by bakeries or sold at discounted prices served at other places❌}; 2) fresh clean ingredients (see pictures) including pickled vegetables, fresh jalapenos and cilantros, as well as quality real MEAT (beef, pork, chicken not just pâté which is quite disgusting); and 3) inexpensive around $12-14 (my choice is #7 combo for $12.) Bon appétit! Cảm ơn!
Great place if you are new or visiting SF and want the best bang for your buck

top_reviews.content: My daughter and I passed by Zamboni's Pizza many times when we were in Orinda shopping at Safeway, which is across the street, in the Shopping Center. I always wanted to find out how Zamboni's Pizza tasted, but we never had the extra time to stop by till now, and I must say that it is the most tasty Pizza ever. My daughter asked me if I wanted a slice or if I wanted the traditional large pizza or a personal pizza. I chose to sample the pizza, so I opted for the personal Pizza. They offered a variety of Pizza on the menu, but I told my daughter that I felt like having the simplest one possible. So, she ordered me the regular cheese  personal Pizza. The crust wasn't deep dish, but it wasn't thin either, it was puffy, it was not salty, and the cheese was not salty at all, which is what I loved about this pizza. For those who have blood pressure can definitely drop by Zamboni's Pizza, which I definitely  recommend. My daughter, to whom I offered a piece, loved it too. So, we're definitely ready to order the large size Margherita Pizza on our next visit. Street parking is available or one can park in the Safeway parking lot and cross the street to Zamboni's Pizza. That's what my daughter and I did. We stopped at Safeway to buy our fruits and veggies and then dropped in at Zamboni's. Orinda is beautiful. The drive to Orinda is so relaxing. There is traffic in the mornings before working hours and in the evenings after work. I have taken photos for you to view.

We're a fan of deep dish so my review will be necessarily slanted. That said, the regular crust would have only gotten a single star more.

The primary issue is that the deep dish is regularly burnt, creating bitter cheese (see picture) and is pretty inconsistent with the crust crunchyness and the cheese level. Sometimes it's soggy and sometimes it's a breadbow. I tried to return a particularly burnt one, and they gave me such a hard time that I have given up.

Two of the reasons why deep dish pizza comes with the sauce on top is to prevent the cheese from burning during the longer cook time and to prevent the sauce from making the thicker crust soggy.

Interestingly, on their website the sauce is on top and it's correctly proportioned. Unfortunately that does not happen on the real pizza.

I guess the fourth strike is definitely out with this place.

I ordered the Spicy Beef Noodle Soup, which was similar to Bun Bo Hue in spirit but much more simplified. The sate had a nice lemongrass aroma, a good amount of heat and  elevated the pho broth. Broth was on the sweeter side, but worked with the strong flavors of the sate.

We were in the area so we stopped by for lunch. We found parking a couple blocks away. Service was fast. Iced Vietnamese coffee was good. I appreciate the portion sizes. Garlic noodles were great. Shrimp was grilled well.

A Must-Visit East Bay Gem for Spectacular Vietnamese Comfort Food!
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
If you are looking for perfectly executed, deeply flavorful Vietnamese classics, Monsoon in Piedmont is an absolute must-visit. The ambiance is welcoming, but it’s the kitchen’s mastery over crunch, seasoning, and texture that will make you a regular.
On my latest visit, a few standout dishes completely stole the show:
The Standouts
• The Egg Rolls: Hands down some of the best around. They arrive piping hot, shattering into a crisp, flaky crunch with every bite. The filling is perfectly seasoned, savory, and dense without being greasy. Wrap them in fresh lettuce with a dip of nước chấm, and it’s pure perfection.
• The Fried Chicken Wings: Absolute perfection. They hit that elusive sweet spot—shatteringly crisp on the outside while remaining incredibly juicy and tender on the inside. The garlic and savory glaze coats them beautifully without making them soggy. They are addictive.
• The Pork Chop: This is the ultimate test of a great Vietnamese spot, and Monsoon nails it. The pork chop is beautifully marinated with distinct notes of lemongrass and garlic, boasting a gorgeous char from the grill. It’s incredibly tender, packed with smoky flavor, and avoids the dryness you find at lesser spots. Pair it with broken rice, and you have a flawless meal.

Monsoon delivers massive flavor, excellent execution, and fantastic consistency. Whether you're dropping in for a casual weeknight dinner or grabbing takeout, the quality is always top-tier.
Do not skip the wings as an appetizer, and make sure someone at your table orders the pork chop. I’ll definitely be back to work my way through the rest of the menu!

I’m a big fan of Thai food and this is my new favorite spot in SF. They specialize in food from the Issan region of Thailand, the only restaurant I’ve found in SF that does so.

The pork larb is just phenomenal, as are their papaya salads. They also have wonderful little known dishes like bamboo shoot salad (so delicious) and Thai sun dried beef (it’s marinated, dried and then deep fried, trust me, a bit of the beef with sticky rice is last meal worthy). And the sticky rice, the staple of this cuisine, was perfectly cooked.

I will be returning many, many times (the pork larb is worth returning for alone). I’m so happy that SF finally has a restaurant specializing in Issan food, and that the food is so incredibly good.

Oh the service was very good too and the food was presented beautifully. Highly, highly recommend this new spot.

Edit: I have eaten here three times now and am even more impressed than I was initially. Every dish I’ve tried has been just phenomenal. The pad kana moo krob was amazing, and the Issan style steamed bamboo shoots were so great with sticky rice. And their glass noodle sausage is so, so good. It’s fermented in-house and is like a glorious Thai salami that you eat wrapped into a perfect bite with cabbage and add peanuts, ginger, shallot, and cilantro.

Bill was $90 including drinks probably won’t come back came around 3pm and there were 2 other groups sitting with us

I’m no food critic or food expert, but I can tell you that I believe the food I recieved was cooked in rancid vegetable oil. Every one of the four dishes reeked of rancid oil with a sour, off smell and flavor, and the entire fifty-eight-dollar meal went straight into the trash. Based on this experience, I think this place should be checked by the health department. Do yourself a favor and skip this place, but if you need more detail, read on.

Even while they were cooking in the back, the food gave off a malodorous smell, like mop water mixed with something sour and spoiled, but by then I had already paid and tried to convince myself that maybe my stress-heightened nose was overreacting. It was not. The first bite confirmed that something was seriously wrong.

The orange chicken was definitely orange and might have been chicken, but that is where the praise ends. Instead of any orange, chili, or savory flavor, it tasted flat and foul, with that same rancid oil note overwhelming everything.

The Mushu pork, with its chopped cabbage and vegetables, should have been light and comforting, but it carried the same off-putting smell, slimmy texture, and rancid taste.

Even the chicken fried rice, which looked like it might be the “safe” choice, was laced with the same rancid oil and stale, off smell.

After a long day of waiting for my father to be discharged from surgery, I had brought home what I hoped would be an easy, comforting family meal. Instead, I was still hungry, nearly in tears at the wasted money, and had to cook for my family anyway.

This place is really cute. I was very impressed with how clean it was. The car ride home smelled so good! Unfortunately it wasn't for us. The sweet and sour chicken,  the sweet and sour sauce is good. The chicken was over cooked and besides the flavor the sauce was dry. Same for the general chicken. Dry chicken and overall dry even with the sauce. But the flavor was so bad. It tasted like salt and pepper, and too much of both. The chow fun wasnt what I expected, thats my fault, I thought it was angel hair noodles. We werent a fan of them, but this could be specific to us. The noodles where the last thing we ate. I think the heat from them being in the box longer caused them to be overcooked. They were a bit soggy and stuck together in clumps. The flavor wasnt the worst but it wasnt good either. The crab wonton were also a no. My Daughter complained a lot about no filling inside just a thin swipe. Should be noted that we're from IL where food standards are higher. Overall food is too expensive these days for it not to be great. This meal that we really couldn't eat and won't touch the leftovers came in just under $57.

Fantastic food. Nice large servings. Friendly people. Atmosphere.. I think it's probably what you'd expect for the area and a little mom and pop shop.    If it isn't, change your expectations. My favorite is the war wonton soup.

top_reviews.content: Stopped in for a take away order. Fabulous bahn mi! Our server was really nice and welcoming. Wish we could have stayed and eaten in the restaurant. Calm and welcoming. You gotta try this spot! I’m Vietnamese, and born in Orange County Little Saigon and they have dishes I grew up on that you can’t find in SF unless you go to the Richmond.

Bun Cha Ha Noi comes in small, medium large sizes which is perfect if you want to eat solo or share with a group!

Their vermicelli bowls were super yummy too!

It definitely meets my cravings for solid comfort Vietnamese food

The dining room is modern and airy, I especially love it as a lunch spot

Finally a Vietnamese snail spot that is affordable and not in San Jose! Tried their Canadian sea snails in garlic sauce, which was ~$20. Portions are sizable and the snails are massive and meaty! Excited to come back and order a spread to try more.

If I had to describe this place with a simple statement that encompasses it all then I'd would say 'Somewhere in the middle'
The food is not bad but also not great. Over the years I had plenty of outstanding Vietnamese food which I can compare with.  Here at Hem, each of the three dishes had hints of what they could be but tasted like they were catering with an American taste bud in mind.  The best of three dishes was the mango salad.  I wish they made the dressing bolder and the spicier.  The Bo Luc Lac could use a better quality of beef and certainly a higher heat to sear the meat quicker.  Also don't forget the lemon pepper dip ....

The place it self is inviting while modern with quick and friendly service.  I see lots of potential and hope the chef and kitchen staff embrace their Vietnamese roots to their full potential and let them shine through their dishes.

Embarcadero Center Gem: Unwrapping the Delicious Secret of 5th Avenue Deli & Market

I was looking for something new to try when I got hungry, so I asked my colleague for a recommendation. She suggested 5th Avenue Deli & Market, a small, hidden gem tucked away in the Embarcadero Center near the corner of Clay and Drumm streets.

They offer a large selection of sandwiches, non-alcoholic drinks, and chips to accompany their creations. Since I'm not a picky eater, I asked the friendly cashier what their most popular sandwich was. Without hesitation, he declared, "SanFranPsycho!"

This sandwich features honey turkey, bacon, Gouda cheese, garlic butter, pesto, and Cajun mayo, all piled high on your choice of bread. I went with sourdough, gutted out and toasted with everything. While 5th Avenue has no indoor seating available, there are benches outside in the Embarcadero Center. I took it back to the office, and with the first bite, I was in love!

The sandwich was perfect - the bread was fresh and perfectly toasted, the flavors exploded in my mouth, and it was incredibly filling. I'm officially a fan! If you work nearby and have a sandwich craving, check out 5th Avenue Deli & Market. This is one sandwich experience you won't regret!

While they offer all the classic favorites, they also cook the comforting country-style dishes our parents grew up loving — from salty fish entrées to lamb in Sichuan chili oil, bitter melon spare ribs with gravy over noodles, crispy fried fish, and so much more.

Come here for that warm, family-style feel and enjoy delicious Chinese food paired with friendly service.

The container also leaked all over since for whatever reason they didn’t think to use one that seals fully.

top_reviews.content:
One of my favorite places in Oakland to grab some dim sum to go.  It's usually a busy place, but the lines move nicely.  There's 2 lines in there so make sure to line up in the right area.  One line is to buy the roasted meats hanging in the front window of the store and the other line is for dim sum.  There's one long table with a few chairs along the wall if you would like to rest a bit and chow down on what you just purchased.

We always try to order the siu mai,chicken feet,tofu skin roll,baked char siu bao,and a few of the fried dumplings when we go.  All of those are so flavorful and tasty.  You don't need any sauces to go with any of those since they themselves are so delicious already,they're not too salty nor too oily or fatty.  The baked char siu baos are a thing of beauty here.  If you don't grab any dim sum then please grab yourselves the baos. The filling is plenty and the ratio of bun to meat is pretty good if you compare it to other places.

I don't really care for the roasted meats myself(the roasted duck,soy sauce chicken,roast pork,etc) because I find them not as good as the other places. I don't necessarily like their seasoning and flavor.  Stick with their dim sum and you should be good but of course this is just my opinion and maybe you would like their roasted offerings.

The workers there are always helpful and friendly.   There's usually 2 or 3 people to serve each line.

this mooncake changes my life, it's just the best I have ever tried, also highly recommended to try the Sesame balls

really nice place :)

The dim sum here are decent. Depending on what you order, some are good and some are just ok. The sign says $3.80 for 4 pieces of dumplings. $2.50 for the rice crepe roll. They sell other roasted meats here also.  There's a sign for the dim sum line to the right of the door, but when I got here at 9am on Saturday, there was no line at all. The shrimp dumpling, bbq pastry puff, taro puff and the shrimp crepe roll are pretty good.  The other stuff has too thick of a dough around them. So they were ok.
Roast Duck is too fatty. Charlie is over grilled. Dim sums okay in a pinch. If u can walk across to FS Center, U'll do better there at either of the two.

My sister-in-law recommended Big Dish to me. It is located in the heartvof Oakland Chinatown, across the street from the East West Bank.

Specialties: Roast duck, chicken, pork, bbq pork, assortment of dim sum pastries. Menu board of the dim sum is mounted on the wall. Trays of pastries are in their display case.

Food is mainly for take out. There are a few tables and chairs for dining indoors.

Purpose of visit: to buy the chicken cage pastries (gai loong). They do sell out fast because it is a very popular item among us elderly Chinese people. The cost for 6 of them is $6.60. I have also purchased 3 sesame balls and 3 savory dumplings.

top_reviews.content: SO SO GOOD. Truly the best Italian place in the city. Every single dish was incredible and so authentic. (The owners are from Italy and have brought a little slice of Friuli to SF). I brought my work team here and they all were drooling.

Absolutely phenomenal. This place opened up a couple weeks ago and serves very regional Italian food. Everything was amazing and the staff were very passionate about their food. We live a couple blocks away and will be coming back regularly but I would travel across the city for this place.

BEST PASTA OUTSIDE OF ITALY!!!

This place should be on everyone’s list. It’s a cute (newish) neighborhood spot in San Francisco that is serving up northern Italian cuisine. Think more polenta, butter and cheese and potatoes and less burrata and olive oil.

The owner is so welcoming. They gave us a Chardonnay champagne to try at the beginning of the meal, and it was one of the most interesting wines I’ve ever had.

Every single dish was sooooo flavorful. All the vegetable dishes were so hearty. The carrots were sweet and the asparagus with the breadcrumbs and brown butter topped with prosciutto was salty, earthy and sweet from the butter. Flavor bombs.

We tried over 8 dishes, including dessert and while we loved all of them, the real standout was the egg noodle with sausage. It was so simple yet so insanely amazing. It’s the best pasta I’ve had outside of Italy. Our second standout was the frico (a cheeee and potatoes pie). I could literally eat that all day, everyday.

Run don walk to this new spot. You won’t regret it. They are gonna treat you like family and you’ll have one of best meals of your life.

Finally, a true regional Italian cuisine in San Francisco! This restaurant is a beautiful discovery of Friulian food and culture. Everything feels 100% genuine, from the kitchen to the hospitality, with a Friulian chef, manager, and owner who make the experience feel authentic and warm.

We highly recommend asking for suggestions from the staff, but we especially loved the frico, the polenta, and the gnocchi. The wines were excellent, and the strudel for dessert was absolutely delicious.

What made the evening even more special was the owner’s warm hospitality: you can really feel the passion and pride behind this place. A wonderful addition to San Francisco’s food scene!

Got to try this spot on opening day and it was delicious! The texture of the pasta stood out to me and found out they made everything in house!

My top dishes: Blecs (buckwheat pasta w mushrooms) Frico (potato cheese onion w side snap peas), & the creamy polenta!

Bonus that the staff was super kind and fun :’)))

Solid Indian cuisine that’s open til 10pm. Carry out orders are ready in 15min. I got the chicken tikka masala and malai kofta with one garlic naan. It was well made albeit a touch salty. Edit July 2026 - finally went in to try their lunch buffet

Selection is limited, and I felt some of the dishes were just fillers

The saag paneer could definitely use some more paneer. The chicken tikka masala was good but was a little watery. Could be thicker.

Garlic naan was one of the best I’ve had in some time. Memorable.

Dishes are still a touch salty.

No desert, and tea is not included in the buffet. No sugar free sweeteners with the tea.

Tandoor chicken was cooked well but tad underpriced

No bowls with the plates. Which is not the best experience when you have multiple curries at the same time.

For $20 a person it’ll do in an otherwise expensive and competitive area.

I think I’ll stick with take out or dine in à la carte.

Too much bread, not much filling/meat

There is nothing more exciting in the morning than freshly baked French rolls, Vietnamese coffee, and a Banh mi for lunch.  This is one of those gems where the rolls used in its Banh mi’s are baked fresh daily.
These are some of the best Bain mi’s in town.  I’ve tried them all with my favorite being the combo pork and lemongrass pork.  If I had more time, I would love to sit on the outside table watching traffic go by while enjoying my meal here.
The best part is you can get 5 Banh mi’s or 4 Banh mi’s + 1 drink for $36.

Nothing fancy, but good food and local ambience. Enjoy!

Tried Banh Mi & Rolls for the first time and it seriously hit the spot. I got the veggie banh mi and the lemongrass pork—both were loaded with flavor. The veggie one was crisp and fresh, and the lemongrass pork was tender, juicy, and packed with that savory-sweet lemongrass kick.

We also had the Thai matcha green tea and an iced coffee. The matcha was creamy and just the right amount of sweet, and the iced coffee was bold and super smooth. Totally worth the caffeine overload.

Great prices, fast service, freshly made  rolls, large portions, and everything tasted super fresh.

Definitely adding this to my regular lunch rotation!

The packaging is shockingly rugged, but don't let that fool you—the taste is surprisingly good for the price. Plus, they have a 'buy 4, get 1 free' deal. If you care more about flavor than fancy presentation, this place is an absolute steal.

The plain banh mi rolls here are great. The service, however, is not.

I came in around 1 PM on a Wednesday to ask for 5 plain loaves. There was one customer before me who was served banh mi. I was told that there was no more bread at the moment, so it was recommended that I come back in an hour. I told them that I would come back, and they said, “Okay.”

Fast forward, I come back after an hour around 2 PM. There were two customers before me who were served their banh mi. I clearly saw them receiving their orders. I asked about the plain loaves and the same person told me that there was no more. She kept shaking her head, implying that they were sold out for the day or something. Mind you, they close later in the day at 5 PM and they are a banh mi speciality shop.

I understand that the bread is baked fresh (as I could see them doing so in the back), but this was a complete waste of time. Why could I not receive plain loaves even while others were still getting their orders? The online menu was still open for orders as well. They should not have promised something they could not deliver.

I got the large to share two ways, which included a lentil soup, salad, cooked squash and other root vegetables, leafy greens, rice, and adzuki beans…honestly a great amount of food for $21. I also got a side of momo ($9 for 6), which were delicious. It was all very good! Having the feel of a healthy, home-cooked meal, not too heavy, and offering a nice complement to restaurants that go heavy on flavor but probably aren’t the best for you if eaten too often. All the food is vegan and organic, with a Tibetan emphasis. I’m not vegan, but there was really nothing unusual among the menu items that I wouldn’t normally be very happy to eat. The ambiance inside is beautiful, so I’d definitely like to come back sometime and have dinner in person.

I visited Casa Sofia for the first time with some friends on a weekday evening after walking by it a few times to and from nearby Oracle Park. We were able to snag a same-day reservation and felt fortunate to be seated in a spacious booth facing the bar. It gave us a comfortable spot to hang out in while taking in the colourful ambiance and decor. The restaurant was busy enough for a Tuesday evening, but not so busy that it felt overwhelming. I can imagine it gets much busier (and perhaps a bit more chaotic) on game/event days.

The cocktails were delicious - well-balanced, just the right amount of strong, and not too sweet. My favourite was the pisco sour. The only downside is that they don't appear to offer happy hour or any other food or drink specials or have plans to.

The food was spectacular! We shared everything family-style:
- Stone fruit salad and ceviche (both vibrant and refreshing)
- Grilled octopus (I almost missed this on the menu, but thankfully my friend spotted it. It ended up being one of my fave dishes and was cooked perfectly.)
- Pork chop (I'd heard great things about this before visiting, so it was a must-order for us. It  lived up to the hype - well-cooked and delicious.)
- Arroz con mariscos (think paella, but with its own distinct flavors)
- Crullers (freshly made and  lighter than expected)

Beyond the excellent food and drinks, the staff really elevated the experience. Everyone we interacted with was friendly, attentive, and conversational.

The only thing I didn't get to try this time was the platano frito, which is usually one of my fave add-ons. I guess that just means we'll have to come back again soon ;)

Delicious food.  Ceviche was fresh and spicy, octopus was very tender, and so were halibut tacos.  Lomo saltado had the most tender meat.  Arroz de mariscos was also very flavorful.  The only thing I did not like were the donuts for desert.  It was sprinkled with lavender and this is probably not my thing.  Our waiter, Max, was very helpful and made us feel welcome.

We had a wonderful experience! The portions are very generous and we were able to try several dishes from the menu, all of them were excellent, perfectly seasoned, with some nice spicy options for those who enjoy a bit of heat. The service was truly exceptional, attentive from start to finish. I also loved learning that they offer private rooms for events, which makes the space even more special.

Highly recommend! And they also have a fantastic vegan drink option.

Casa Sofia is such a beautiful addition to the area. From the moment we walked in, everything felt elevated — the decor is absolutely gorgeous, warm, stylish, and thoughtfully designed without feeling overdone.

The food was delicious across the board, with every dish feeling fresh, flavorful, and very well executed. But what really made the experience stand out was the service. Everyone on the team was incredibly welcoming, attentive, and clearly very well trained.

A special thank you to Facundo, who was truly the best. He made the entire experience feel special with the perfect balance of professionalism, warmth, and attention to detail. You can tell the team genuinely cares about hospitality here.

Can’t wait to come back — Casa Sofia is already off to an amazing start.

I first visited Casa Sophia during their grand opening a couple of weeks ago and was blown away by both the atmosphere and the food. I loved it so much that I insisted my husband and friends come back with me so we could experience the full menu—not just the delicious party bites from opening night.

I'm happy to report that it exceeded my expectations.

San Francisco is known for incredible food, and people will happily travel across the city—or across the Bay—for a memorable meal. That's why I'm especially excited to have a restaurant of this caliber right here in the neighborhood. Honestly, the food rivals many of the best restaurants I've visited anywhere in the country.

We enjoyed the ceviche, tuna tartare, fresh halibut, broccolini, divine cruller donuts, excellent cocktails, and a wonderful wine selection. Every dish was beautifully prepared and absolutely delicious.

Our server, Colton, was fantastic, and the entire support staff was warm, attentive, and professional. They made us feel genuinely welcome from start to finish.

I can't wait to go back again and again. Wishing the entire Casa Sophia team tremendous success. Being across from the ballpark may make reservations a little tougher during baseball season, but if I can't get a table, I suppose I'll just have to order delivery!

top_reviews.content:
Saam, a Thai restaurant with its own unique character.

The flavors are delicious,
and the presentation of each dish has such a beautiful sense of style.

The interior is just as impressive.
The lighting is beautiful, with warm brown and neutral tones that work perfectly together.

For drinks, the focus is mostly on a carefully selected wine list.
No cocktails though, sadly 🥲

I had the chance to try one of their wines,
and it paired beautifully with the food.
Thank you for the wine 🙂

As for the price…

Ouchhh 😂

The service was okay overall.
One area that could make the experience even better would be more polished and knowledgeable service throughout the meal.

With food presented at this level, I would love to hear the staff explain each dish with more confidence and detail, including the ingredients, flavors, and the chef’s inspiration behind it. I think that extra touch would help guests appreciate the food even more and elevate the overall dining experience.

But overall, I really loved the atmosphere here.
It’s a great choice for a special occasion, especially if you’re looking for somewhere intimate, stylish, and a little elevated.

The whole time I was thinking,
“I really want to photograph this restaurant.” 😂

As a Thai, this is probably the closest thing to fine dining from home that I’ve had in SF.

I’ve been following Chef Ton for years, so when I found out he was opening Saam in San Francisco, I literally counted down the days. I came on opening day and somehow ended up ordering… basically the whole menu. 😂

Every single dish surprised me. Chef Ton, Chef Tee, and Chef Ty took Thai flavors I grew up with and turned them into something completely different while still feeling so Thai. There were so many combinations I would’ve never expected, but they just worked.

The food was incredible, but honestly the whole experience was. The space is beautiful, service was super warm (not stuffy at all), and the drink pairings were on point.

You can tell there’s so much thought behind every dish, from the ingredients to the presentation to the story it tells.

If you’re looking for your typical pad thai or green curry… this isn’t that. This is Thai cuisine on another level, and I’m so happy SF finally has a restaurant like this.

Already planning my next visit. ❤️

The dishes are very special! Beautiful setup.
Just hoping to try cocktails next time when we return. (It’s their first day so not everything is on the menu is ready.)

Dessert is a bit overpriced tbh, but mango & sticky rice is my all time favorite.

My dining experience at SAAM last week
exceeded expectations, blending a gorgeous atmosphere with stellar hospitality and bold, vibrant flavors.

From the moment we walked in, the hospitality stood out. The host at the front greeted us immediately and led us to our table. He even noticed that other servers were tied up with nearby tables and thoughtfully poured our water himself—a small touch of proactive care that set the tone for the night.

The interior ambiance is beautiful, creating a warm and inviting setting. However, the absolute highlight of our evening was our server, Best. Incredibly attentive, hospitable, and full of great energy, Best completely livened up our dinner experience and made us feel genuinely welcome.

Menu Highlights
•    Som Tum Peaches (Appetizer): A fantastic way to start the meal. It carried a bit more heat than expected, but the sweetness of the fresh peaches provided a wonderful balance. I would definitely order this again.
•    Gaeng Kua Beef Curry: When the clam curry we originally wanted sold out, Best proposed substituting it with beef. That pivot turned out to be one of the stars of the night. While also on the spicier side, the curry featured incredible depth of flavor and was exceptionally good.
•    Khao Soi Haeng Seafood: Although we initially expected a traditional soupy noodle dish, this arrived as a dry version. Despite the surprise, it was intensely flavorful, packed with seafood, and easily tied with the curry as our favorite dish of the evening.
•    Mango Sticky Rice Meringue: We finished the night on a high note with this dessert. The mango was exceptionally juicy and sweet, and the meringue topping added a creative and delightful texture.

Because a few items like the pla phao were sold out by the time we ordered, we already have plenty of reasons to return and explore the rest of the menu. Between the stunning interior, Best’s top-tier service, and the phenomenal food, we are eagerly looking forward to our next visit.

I had such a lovely experience at SAAM! Everything was so beautiful and delicious, My favorite dish was the duck curry, the first bite reminded me of the curry my mom used to make at home—it brought back so many wonderful memories. It had that authentic, comforting Thai flavor I grew up with, but presented in such a beautiful and elegant way. It was truly the perfect balance of tradition and refinement. Everyone was so kind and welcoming, and you can really feel the passion behind every dish. I can’t wait to come back and try more of the menu. Thank you for such a wonderful meal!

On the food

Best sushi place in Noe, probably best in SF, I might even say best in California. The food here is always top tier, and the service is outstanding. There is limited space in front so call ahead to make sure they have room. They also have a back room for private parties or on busy days. The head chef Danny, his side chef Lu, and the head waitress Iris have always treated me very well and I have always been pleased with my experiences here.

COVID Update: Thank goodness that Oki is still doing take out and delivery, both on the phone and through DoorDash. I would not make it through the pandemic without them. Slightly different hours, maybe like 4-9 now, but still there top quality nigiri.

SO glad this place finally opened! The location has been empty for 10 months or so after the previous restaurant moved out. Sushi is our thing (literally every Sunday) and we couldn't be happier to have a new favorite spot right around the corner! We had miso soup, the bacon enoki skewer special, the salmon skin roll, the jalapeño roll, the beauty and the beast roll, and the TNT roll - all were so delicious I almost forgot to take pictures before we finished them! The fish is fresh, our server was sweet, the restaurant is nicely decorated, and the bathrooms are super clean. What more can you ask for! Can't wait to go back to try the whole grilled squid.

Good Sushi, Terrible Atmosphere

The sushi itself was good — fresh fish and nicely prepared — but everything else about the experience made us want to leave.

From the moment we walked in, the atmosphere was uncomfortable. The waitress looked confused (and almost annoyed) that we were there, with no greeting or welcome. The music was some sort of loud Disney-style soundtrack that made it hard to relax, and the space itself felt cold and uninviting.

The miso soup came out cold, and while the beer was fine, it could have been much colder. Overall, the food is decent, but this is definitely a place better suited for takeout than dining in.

top_reviews.content: Great food, lovely owners. The veggie platter was a great value for the price and everything was super flavorful and delicious. We walked in and ordered, the food came out in about 10 minutes. This is the only Indian takeout spot I need to go to now :)

Munch India operates with quiet rigor from a compact storefront just off Shattuck. There is no dining room, only a kitchen. The entire floor plan is devoted to the hotline and prep station. There is no freezer, only refrigeration. Ingredients are purchased daily, mostly from Berkeley Bowl a few blocks away. Orders are placed online each morning before noon; cooking begins after.

The daily walk-in menu is limited, changes daily, and is prepared to order. The results are consistently superb. Spicing is precise, textures are balanced, and the dishes—drawn from across India—reflect deep training and care. The chefs, Diana Afroza and Nick Ahmed, have cooked professionally since the early 1990s, with backgrounds in Boston, Europe, and India.

Prices are extremely reasonable given the quality and labor involved. They are searching for a larger, dine-in location. If they find one, their costs—and likely their prices—will rise. For now, this is high-level regional Indian cooking, offered at below-market prices. It smells wonderful inside and the people you’ll meet are awesome. Order while you can.

THE BEST! delicious, sophisticated Indian food with burst of flavors in every bite. This is my one and only go to spot in the east bay. The owners are kind and genuine people who knows how to cook with high quality foods! They are super conscious of the ingredients used making it a truly authentic experience everything i order. My taste buds thank you munch india!

top_reviews.content:
Joshua’s Gulfport Seafood on Fruitvale has been open for years, and it’s truly one of those longtime Oakland gems that deserves recognition. They’ve been serving the community for decades, and the quality has always stayed consistent.

The food is always fresh, flavorful, and perfectly seasoned. The portions are huge for the price, which is hard to find nowadays, and everything tastes homemade with care. You can tell they take pride in what they serve.

Jay is always welcoming and kind, and knowing his grandfather originally opened the place makes the experience feel even more special and family-oriented. It’s rare to find a spot that still has that genuine neighborhood feel while serving amazing seafood at affordable prices. Definitely worth supporting! This is my second day in a row eating here this week and it's very delicious!

So glad I got to try this spot! Got the 2 piece special and it was amazing. Fresh, hot, seasoned to perfection and the portion size was great. Excellent customer service and the wait was not that long. Also had potato salad which was excellent as well! Will definitely be returning!! Got some potato bread on the side that made for a BOMB fish sandwich. Came with hot sauce and tartar sauce as well. 😋😋😋

I’ve been here a couple times and the food is consistently amazing. The catfish and fries are a must—REAL catfish, super crispy, perfectly seasoned, fresh, and hot, served with two fluffy slices of bread. The homemade potato salad is also so good.
I also tried the catfish and red snapper, and both were delicious with nice-sized portions and great flavor. Definitely a great value for the quality.

The service is great also. If you want crispy, well-seasoned seafood, this is the spot!

I’m going to tell you why I love this place so much. It reminds me of food in the past when it came to buying fish you would order the fish and you would get potato salad or french fries and sliced white bread. Now if anybody is a little upper age, they understand me when I talk about the white bread nothing like it with fried fish. I’ll tell you a little hot sauce and for those who like it, tartar sauce too. It’s a very small place. There’s only a few seats where you could wait for your food but it’s definitely a takeout place you go in you order your food and you wait approximately 15 minutes if that and you’re gone. Now let’s talk about the fish crispy seasoned just right and nice portions. The french fries are good and the potato salad is pretty close to mine and that is saying a lot y’all.
The owner is a jewel. He is very kind and respectful and that is unfortunately rare, but he has it and he deserves a nice tip every time I go because I appreciate him taking the time and making sure his fish is fresh and that is cooked right and that it taste right thank you so much, sir for a good lunch every time I go. Now, if you folks are coming from out of town, you got a hotel and you trying to find some quick try his business. I don’t know how late things open but if you can catch it for lunch man, I’m telling you you will not be sorry. I’m gonna show you a picture of what old-fashioned fish orders look like my bag is all torn open because I was hungry so forgive the mess but look, that fish was good.

The fish is very good but those fries SUCK! They are light brown bricks and I even asked about them before I ordered and he said “I make them fresh”… Sir, get a new brand/type all together. People may not think fries are important but fish and fries go hand and hand and they fries were so bad, I don’t want to come back for the fish. And it’s a large tray of those bricks too.
