So decided to go on a lunch date with the Mrs. And I knew this place had just recently opened up and thought to check it out. We went on a Monday a little after 12:30. Parking is small for the area but accessible.
Place was empty. I jokingly told the Mrs that I rented the whole restaurant so we can have it to ourselves. There was one table that had used plates and silverware. I didn’t see anyone leave so I am not sure how long it’s been sitting. The server was more relaxed than I would have liked, I mean it was just us in the restaurant. Utensils weren’t given, we had to ask. And when dishes were offered they asked if we wanted an extra plate. Not 2 plates, just one. Keep in mind there was 2 of us and a good amount of food was being ordered. I would like to see service and servers be more proactive.
And now the food. We had ordered the mozzarella sticks and bruschetta as an appetizer. The bruschetta never arrived. And I was told they didn’t hear me order it. The mozzarella sticks took almost 15 minutes to come out. Followed by the Cesar salad then the chicken carbonara at about the 25 minute mark. Lastly the pizza. Which was the first item to finish cooking. We noticed our pizza sitting on  the counter and it definitely cooled down to where my first bite didn’t have that nice cheese pull. If they gave me the pizza when it first finished I’d rate this place at 4 stars. The Caesar salad and chicken carbonara stood out in my opinion. Pizza again was good. I just wish they gave it to me when it came out of the oven.
I’ll revisit this place again in a couple months. Maybe they can shake off the grand opening jitters

We placed our order online with their app and waited in the store for more than 40 minutes. Turns out they were busy and only had 1 cook working today.  When we asked how much longer, we were told just a few more minutes. And then again. And then ten more minutes, the order is in the oven, supposedly.

Ten minutes later, someone else's order was finished, ours was still not done. This was already 40 minutes. Another reviewer mentioned waiting for this long as well and the quality was poor. I ended asking for a refund before the poor quality food would be completed (that is - if it was even started to begin with 🤔).

If you ask for a refund, make sure you get a receipt.

EDIT - My response to the restaurant's reply -

Here is my suggestion to avoid creating another disaster like the one yesterday - if your restaurant is clearly backed up and you cannot complete orders by the promised time on the app, allow your staff to temporarily disable online ordering. This will encourage your potential customers to physically visit the store or call the location to get a more accurate wait time.

Second, it's incredibly frustrating when your staff recycles the excuse that the "order is in the oven" or "just ten more minutes." Because I was watching the oven carefully and the pizzas that came out were for other people's orders, not mine. So I grew increasingly suspect that the order was never touched to begin with.

Thank you, but no thank you for the small pizza. I will not take the risk and wait another 40 minutes to an hour for a pizza. Please take this review as a sincere teachable moment.

Thoroughly mediocre chicken shop/specialty grocer.

Stopped in for 1/2 rotisserie chicken box. Found they had a decent selection of sodas, non-alc bevs, wines, prepared sausages, specialty goods. May stop back in for these other things.

The half chicken, at almost $20, came packed in the box atop chicken schmaltz roasted potatoes. It was paired with hot olives and roasted garlic. An assortment of sauces (aioli some kind of green sauce and some kind of red sauce) were provided.

The chicken was aggressively seasoned and moist. Unfortunately none of the flavor had penetrated the skin which meant that if the piece was without skin, you’re left with the bland flesh. The sauces were all meh. Potatoes, perfect. Olives, nicely varied. My guess is that the bird could have been cooked a little longer and seasoned a little further in advance. (And also checked for feathers.)

I also had a slice of the key lime pie. The beauty of key lime pie is the sharp acidity of these limes (which are in season right now) and the intense floral profile of the oils in the rind. This pie was all oil and not sharp at all. Which is a shame because otherwise, it was great. Not cloyingly sweet, not too much cream on the palate. Oh well.

Hands down the best rotisserie chicken I ever had! The potatoes are cooked with chicken schmaltz and very addicting. They have so many other amazing selections from handmade sausages to their daily sandwiches. I always highly recommend this place to all of my family and friends and now I’m telling you to go and try it out, you won’t be disappointed!

I have 3 chilhood perfect food experience that became aldult obsessions. Tiramisu, croque monsieur, and panini. I have been searching for yeaaars for a panini that could live up to the one from my childhood sandwich shop in southeast france, and literally ordered paninis all over the US.

The closest came from Elysee Bakery near UCLA (too far), and 2nd place was Alexander Patisserie's old paninis before they removed them from the menu, then changed the bread when they brought them back.

By the time I just happened to walk by this place, I basically gave up virtually trying every places with paninis in the menu within the vicinity of my outings or even actively searching. I remembered searching years ago for all places with paninis in their menu around Union Square. But having been disappointed so many times within the bay, I didn't have much faith in anything being different in SF and never tried further. And it's been months since I've stopped searching.

So even though I paused in my steps when walked by and I saw that the pics looked somewhat similar to my childhood panini, I just resumed walking past the shop for half a block.

Somehow, something stopped me in my tracks, and I begrudgingly used my precious data to look at the review pictures to check that their display pics were not deceiving. Then, looked at their menu to see if they had an option that at least could potentially recreate the elusive taste of that chilhood panini.

They didn't have what I wanted, but they had a prosciutto option, which was the bare minimum ingredient I wanted. Being obsessed still with recreating that taste, now that I knew about this faint potential, I had to try. At worst, it's still a panini! You can't go wrong with a panini.

OH. EM. Freaking geeee!!! I can't freaking believe it. I went in fully expecting to be disappointed, again. Boy am I shocked. And thankful to whatever made me give this a try. It wasn't the exact taste (my childhood panini was more elaborate with sliced tomatoes and pulled mozzarella), but the taste of the prosciutto was so so close, if not identical. And how the bread was done is exactly the style I'm chasing after. This just made my freaking entire last month of the year.

But what makes me take the unusual effort write a review was not the panini, but the gentleman (owner?) who took in my order. His manners and courtesy were impeccable. Made me feel like he truly valued my patronage.

So even though the panini experience here is unique to me and less relevant to others, I still want to write this review and contribute to the 5 stars because I wanted to reward his conduct which made me feel welcomed.

I'm also writing this review because I can still, despite nostalgia driving my own preference, recommend this place with high confidence:

They claim on their display that their philosophy for a good sandwich is simple but best quality ingredients. I believe them. I tasted quality. So many places prosciutto taste stale, but not this one. And they include quite a generous amount of it! Loved that the bite felt substantial.

So based on that, I feel fairly confident that you can try any options on their menu that suits your own taste (rather than my specific choice) and still come up with a satisfying delish sandwich.
If you ever want to support a place who value their customers, clearly prioritizes on creating quality, uses quality ingredients and are generous with their meat, and try as a bonus what a panini that uses baguette as bread (doughy flavourful inside, satisfyingly crunchy exterior!), give this place a try!

For my part, I'm sad there's no option to add tomatoes or mozzarella (they have halloumi instead), because I'd have been so close to succeeding in recreating my childhood panini then.
But I know I'll definitely come back here every time I'm in SF. I added-on cheddar this time, so I'll try the halloumi next!

top_reviews.content:
I stopped by for lunch not long after opening and as soon as I come in the lobby of the medical building Banh Mi Love is located in i was met with so many savory fresh smells... Some of the meats, the fresh bread and spices.

The place seems to be ran by a mother/daughter combo, or at least a similar age difference and they're very warm and friendly taking my order and offering the jalepeno option. Initially I got a combo pork banh mi, and a  passionfruit lemonade. After I paid (cash and cards are fine) I noticed the Vietnamese lays and got a bag of fried crab flavored chips. The spicy hot pot looked good too but I wasn't feeling spicy that day.

The sandwich was absolutely lovely. I could taste the individual pork, pickled veg, and vinegary tang of the sauce, all coming together to be more than the sum of their parts. The bread is a standout being crispy and flaky, but not dry, although I do like it a little chewier. Close to classic Vietnamese baguette. The lemonade was sublime and would get again even at 4.50. the pate was a little moved to one side, but I got a ton of perfect bites with all the meats and shallot and carrot. The chips tasted like imitation crab that was fried in potato chips and tempura batter, really enjoyed their unique taste. All this was just about 20 bucks, but with my own water and skipping the chips I could get an amazing lunch for 10 bucks.

The parking garage is free and the door into the lobby from the first floor of the garage is like 10 feet from the restaurant. I would go out of my way to come here, or even better walk over from the galleria for a yummy treat. Please come try this place.

I have not been here in person yet, but had ordered here and got it delivered via DoorDash many times. They specialize in Banh-Mi (Vietnamese sandwich), their menu consists of traditional Banh-Mi, Vietnamese snacks, housemade drinks and much more to choose from. Everything is made to order here which is always a plus for me since it is quality over quantity and I never mind the wait since I am a very patient person. The ingredients they use here are fresh, premium and refreshing. I highly recommend this place to all Banh-Mi enthusiasts, if you are in need of a quick bite, to anyone willing to try something new or if you just so happen to be in the area to check them out. I definitely will have to make a visit here and continue to order from here via DoorDash in the future.

Ordered the combo pork with pate,fancy pork,head cheese,ham,mayo,pickled carrot and onion. I also added jalapeño. The combination of the toasted bread and generous pate made the sandwich crunchy and moist. Meats and veggie were very tasty with the pickled carrots. Price is right and sandwich are very good. I will come back for more.

The veggie seared tofu sandwich is alright, if a bit flavorless. They don’t put enough aioli for it to lend much flavor, and the tofu is bland. That said, the ingredients are fresh and the price is great. I was disappointed because this place has great reviews, but maybe the flavor in the other sandwiches comes from the meat. I would give this three and a half stars if I could.

I’m always on the hunt for an amazing banh mi, and today, I hit the jackpot. I went with the beef brisket, and it was absolutely phenomenal. The bun was perfection: fresh, soft, yet perfectly crisp on the outside. It paired beautifully with the tangy pickled carrots and fresh cilantro, creating the perfect balance of flavors. The beef was tender, generously portioned, and packed with flavor. And that dipping sauce? A sweet, spicy, and tangy masterpiece that elevated every bite. Honestly, I was tempted to order a second one right then and there!

I visited this weekend with a friend, and this is a lovely place.  They have nice loose leaf tea for sale, as well as coffee, tea, and food to order. Wow, why did it take me so long to try this place out. Will definitely be my go to coffee spot during my breaks. I got a nitrogen coffee delicious, workers were super friendly, and vibes immaculate. It was a great way to start my day and week here.

What a great addition to the neighborhood... Perfect little spot to grab some chow or some brew to wake you up.  Gave this place a try for lunch and tried their tuna melt.  I like their take on the tuna melt. It's light, the bread is crunchy and soft , the salad is a nice add on to compliment the dish.
I like the decor, the vibe is very chill and kicked back with a touch of modern.
The staff aka the owners are super sweet with a ton of attention to details. Well done this will be my new lunch place when I get to step away from my desk.

This place is my new favorite neighborhood spot. The staff is extremely welcoming and so helpful to provide recommendations if you’re unsure what to order. I’ve really enjoyed my past few experiences there just chatting it up with the staff and other patrons. Everyone is so friendly and the food and drinks are great. They have a wide variety of teas and other breakfast and lunch food specials that I can’t wait to go back and try.

top_reviews.content: We came in on a Wednesday night and we were able to sit wherever we liked. My favorite dishes here were the hamachi Kama and the agedashi tofu. Rolls were good too. We didn’t try their nigiri’s or sashimi but I’d come back to this restaurant if I was in the area craving sushi. Prices are average here for sushi in SF, 4 items for $66. They also happy hour but we didn’t come in time for that.

Just had an amazing meal at Au Sushi and everything was outstanding. The fish was incredibly fresh, and you can really tell they care about quality.

Sara, the owner, provided exceptional service—warm, attentive, and made us feel truly welcome. The sushi chef Andy is extremely talented; his sashimi was absolutely top-notch, beautifully prepared, and full of flavor.

Highly recommend Au Sushi if you’re looking for great food and genuine hospitality. I’ll definitely be coming back!

Fast, friendly service. Stopped in with a large group of adults and kiddos after playing at the playground next door. We were pleasantly surprised! Everything we had was great! The Gyoza were epic! Chicken udon was also a standout (sadly not pictured…). The waitress was very accommodating to our group and especially attentive to our kiddos’ needs. We will definitely be back!

Come support local family-owned business! Owner, Sara, is a super hardworking chef. She gets up early in the morning to the seafood wholesale market to get the daily fresh fishes. I ordered Chirashi Special, Saka Sashimi, and Lion King Roll. See photos attached. They are so fresh and delicious! When I had my first bite, and I was speechless!! So good!! Come try!! I saw they have many party trays for great value and I wil try that next time. 2 Thumbs UP!!! 5 Stars Quality!!!!
Friends and I came for dinner on a Friday night, I’m glad we made a reservation since it was pretty busy. Bento boxes are well portioned, and sushi was fresh and delicious. Will be back again!

top_reviews.content: If you’re looking for a great burger, this is the place. Everything was fresh, flavorful, and served quickly. The staff made us feel welcome from the moment we walked in. Five stars all the way!
Food was good overall but a little pricey for what it was. $10 for a milkshake seemed a little high to me. We were happy with our meal and there was a lot of seating. Restroom is for customers only.

I stopped by this place during my trip and decided to give it a try. I found out they had just recently opened and I'm honored to be the first person to leave a review. The smash burger was absolutely phenomenal. It was fresh full of flavor and cooked perfectly. The prices are fair and the atmosphere is warm and welcoming. The customer service was excellent. I honestly wish this place was closer because I would eat here every day. Wishing the owners lots of luck and success. Keep the quality this high and you'll have no problem building a loyal customer base. I highly recommend giving this place a try.

Checked out the newly opened hamburger place on Haight. They offer a handful of smash burger options, chicken sandwiches, fries and onion rings, wings, shakes, and ice cream. I tried a Double Chester and the Duke's Original, with an order of wings. The Original is a solid smash burger, comparable to the standard orders at Hamburger Project and other popular spots. The wings are fried, and they were really good.

The Chester, on the other hand, is my new favorite burger in SF. I think it works so well for me because I love a good grilled cheese, and the Chester is essentially a grilled cheese with a smash burger patty and onions inside. If that sounds good to you, it's worth checking out.

My girlfriend and I came here last night, and we both loved it! The burger was incredible, and the fried chicken was crispy, juicy, and full of flavor. So glad this place opened—it’s definitely our new favorite spot. We’ll be back for sure. Highly recommend! 🤩

top_reviews.content: Congrats to Chuck’s Takeaway on bringing refinement to the humble banh mi sandwich!  I was happy to see they were open on Presidents’ Day and stopped by early afternoon.  It was a small but friendly storefront with a small counter to eat in.  I ordered the #3, a peanut butter cookie, and an iced coffee.  What struck me immediately was the fresh herbs and veggies and the bold clean flavors of the pork and pate.  This was all encapsulated by a crisp flaky baguette that had a soft interior.  You could tell that the employees took pride in working for the business.  They were friendly and answered questions.  I’m looking forward to trying something else on the menu on my next visit!

Great sandwiches. Got the CP’s #3 and the Veggie Wurster Hall. Bread is excellent - light and airy, but with a shell-thin crust that crackles with every bite. Filling is generous, and you can tell that the pâté and pork cha are made in-house; they’re fresh and flavourful. The bunches of fresh herbs cut the richness perfectly, as do the pickled veggies that come on the side, though I wonder why they aren’t just inside the sandwich so that every bite is perfect.

Also got a gombo-ppang, a Korean streusel bun, a relative of the family of pastries which includes bolo bao, melon pan, and concha. This was filled with a very delicious peanut butter cream.

Service is warm, professional, and kind. Vietnamese iced coffee is great. Be sure to check out their selection of home goods. I got a chili oil which I’m excited to try.

The banh mi is dense, the sauce is flavorful, the baguette is crispy. The baguette is a little on the smaller side so for hungry people you might want to grab 2 banh mi.

However the service is so slow. I bought 5 banh mi and it took 25 minutes. That’s 5 min/banh mi. I’m sorry but that’s unacceptable for speed.

The space is spacious, easy to find, parking could be difficult on a busy day. Everyone is courteous and nice.

So come here if you’re not pressed for time, not too hungry. Otherwise pass.

Ordered the OG#3 and crispy pork belly. Seems like the $20 sandwich is becoming a thing (looking at you flour + water).

The pork maintains its crispy skin but the portion I got was quite oversalted. The sliced cucumber does little to balance that out, there's a lack of acidity. The pork is not dry, but not juicy either.

OG#3 was more balanced, at least a bit of acidity. The mayo and maybe pate was nice too- there was richness but I say maybe pate because you don't really taste liver or umami. The cold cuts seemed fresh and were on the lighter side. There's something pickled in here thankfully. Milder sandwich than the pork belly.

Sandwiches are reasonably sized for a healthy portion, which means maybe undersized for $20. The bread is very airy and squishes down, but the outside crust does seem to require some tearing through, it doesn't bite through easily. I respect the approach to modernize and perhaps bring higher quality ingredients to the table, oddly the execution of individual components seems to be mostly fine but the actual balance of the recipes is lacking.

TLDR: service is good and quick, sandwich is lacking something and I don’t like having a forced 15% service charge for just takeaway.

Was helped quickly and ordered the crispy pork belly sandwich and a Vietnamese coffee. Only when i saw the total at almost $29 for $23 of sandwich and coffee did i see the 15% auto service charge which rubbed me the wrong way, especially for only having takeout. The food came quickly and digging in, the pork belly is definitely on point with crispy skin and tender meat. However the rest of the sandwich is lacking. A ton of cilantro with regular cucumber and jalapeño doesn’t add the acidity that pickled veggies would in a regular banh-mi. The bread had a nice crunchy exterior but it tasted one note. All in all, nothing was horrible about the sandwich but it all tasted one note to me

top_reviews.content: Yummm. Not the best Vietnamese food I’ve ever had, but very solid. Got the Bun Bo Hue, Bi Cuon, and my friend had the mini shrimp crepe. Bi Cuon was spot on! The sauce for it too as superb. Bun Bo Hue Soup had a ton of flavor too. Thanks for a great meal!

Like stepping into a Vietnamese grandmother’s living room, together the warm hospitality and snug interior make the home-style cooking taste even homier.

The menu is near encyclopedic — with a section exclusive to Hue culinary specialties. Rice plates, seafood stir-frys, porridges, crepe/pancakes, dry noodle bowls and noodle soups galore.

#117 Canh Chua Tom (Vietnamese Sweet Sour Shrimp Soup) with egg noodle add-on was all that it says — plump and savory shrimp boiled in rejuvenating tamarind broth with tomatoes, eggplant and okra.

#54 Bun Heo Xao Sa gets the basic elements of grilled lemongrass pork right, but the iceberg lettuce and bland tomato toppings fall short of the refreshing crunch one would want.

#1 Bun Bo Hue, a signature noodle soup comes in well-spiced and lemongrass-fragrant broth. Three different cuts of pork plus blood cube makes for an interesting play on textures.

An excellent choice for a tasty lunch or family weekend brunch.

It was my first experience here yesterday after seeing some mean reviews about them. The place was boutique but was so welcoming and spotless inside. I felt at home as I sat down at the table. It would not be fair to say all of their dishes were great as I only got to try 2 yesterday, the bun bo hue and banh khoai. They were both great. They were like home meals by moms. Not big on the look but comforting and yummy. I would definitely come back with friends and family to show them what it is like dining in a restaurant in Vietnam at this restaurant.

In an area with many Vietnamese restaurants, this is definitely a hole in the wall where you can enjoy homemade Vietnamese cuisine. We tried several dishes including their Bun Bo Hue and they were all decent. Anything better you would need to go to San Jose.

A nice place to have Vietnamese food! Small family run restaurant that makes you feel you are in a mini Vietnam when visiting this place to eat. Definitely try their Bun Bo Hue and the Banh Uot #13. The Vietnamese iced coffee here is legit and tasted great. The coffee was in a cup and you can smell the nice aroma from it. Overall, service, food, and cleanliness is good. Highly recommend!

top_reviews.content: I was up on the North side boppin around with a group of Jamaican Astro Physicists showing them what a typical Berkeley hipster dofus looks like, and I'll tell you they were not impressed!  This group of intellects even snubbed their noses at the freelanders at the people's park, and our walk up Telegraph Ave didn't even raise an eyebrow..they told me the people in Berkeley don't know how to be layed back, and cool like an island breeze.  We settled in at Bongo Burgers up in Northside because they liked the name, it seams the group also has a band back on the island that is made up mostly bongo drums and steel drums!  Everybody in the group had an amazing lunch and as soon as they were finished, the leader, Bogart passed out Ganja..(weed) to everyone, and the had a group high out on the sidewalk!  I had the chicken sando and rings...it was amazing! 5 ☆☆☆☆☆'s

Bongo Burger in Berkeley is hands down one of my favorite spots! The food is always amazing and consistently delicious every single time. The Persian Burger is by far the BEST burger on the menu — packed with flavor and absolutely unforgettable.

The owner is also incredibly kind and welcoming, which makes the experience even better. Anyone visiting or living in Berkeley needs to stop by and try this place. Highly recommend!

Really enjoyed Bongo Burger! The Persian burger was delicious—great flavor and cooked really well. The fries were crispy and tasty, and the kabob wraps were also really good. Solid spot if you’re craving burgers or Persian-style comfort food. Will definitely be back!

Bongo Burger is still the best burger in the Bay.

What makes it so good is the style. It’s not a massive, overloaded burger… it’s light (but filling), balanced, and somehow they manage to make a thin patty that’s still cooked medium-rare, juicy, and perfectly pink in the center. That’s surprisingly hard to find.

The grilled onions have are so good on the burger, really make it a signature. Add fresh chopped lettuce, ripe tomato, and the classic Bongo Burger bun, and it’s just a perfect combo. Also the use of two different color cheeses really makes it visually appetizing.

The fries are equally impressive. They’re crispy on the outside but somehow stay soft, fluffy, and full of actual potato on the inside instead of drying out.

The cooks are talented clearly.

On top of all that, the prices are incredibly reasonable, the staff is always friendly, and the vibe feels like old Berkeley in the best possible way.

The Euclid location is my favorite. I grew up eating there in the ‘90s, and I’m amazed that the quality is still just as good today. Places like this are rare. I hope Bongo Burger is around forever.

I decided to try this place after seeing a recommendation. While I always enjoy exploring new burger spots, I have to say that my favorite burger is still In-N-Out, especially when factoring in cost.

I arrived early and was the first customer of the day, which gave me the opportunity to observe how the restaurant prepared their food. One thing that stood out to me—but not in a good way—was how they handled the grilled onions and bacon. Rather than cooking fresh ingredients in the morning, they simply reheated leftover onions and bacon from the previous day and used them for my burger. That was disappointing because I expected everything to be freshly prepared, especially for the first order of the day.

That said, there were some positives. The onion rings were excellent—crispy, and cooked perfectly. I really enjoyed them. The burger itself was just okay. One detail I found odd was the cheese. Instead of a traditional slice of cheese, they sprinkled cheese particles on the patty, which didn’t quite give the same melt-in-your-mouth experience.

As for the drink, the Coke (Pepsi) was fine—nothing to complain about, but nothing remarkable either.

Overall, it wasn’t a bad experience, but I wouldn’t go out of my way to return.

top_reviews.content: Came by on a whim. Didn't think much at first, but liked the sound of the Prescott Bowl with Blackened Shrimp so gave it a try! Impressively good! Very good mix of flavor and textures. The farro combines really well with the black beans, the cream creates a juicy saucy experience, while the leaves and roasted vegetables add a nice complexity of flavors. The shrimps top it all out giving more of a bite and seasoning to stand out. The lady that helped me at the register was also very friendly and happy to assist with my food indecision, recommending their best sellers and providing guidance through the available options. Super recommend this place! Legit hidden gem!

Came to visit my oldest daughter and tried this spot since it’s in the neighborhood and wanted to support our own. After a bit of a mix up in the order (we were given a 20% discount for the extra wait) I brought it back to my hotel to eat. FIRE!🔥 The shrimp was plump, well seasoned and not over cooked, which happens too often in my opinion so greatly pleased when they done right. Never had farro before but I see why people like it; with the right flavors, which is definitely right here,  the grain makes the meal hearty and filling. And they habenaro hot sauce was just my kinda spicy.🌶️
A little pricey but not unreasonably so cuz you get a good portion. And the food is 💣 so it’s worth it.

Hubby and I are in culinary heaven! Stopped into this Oakland gem inside the Prescott Market. He had the sweet potato pancakes with berry compote , fresh made whipped cream and …wait for it….toasted hazelnuts. I had the andouille shrimp & grits. Ya’ll know that’s my go to meal. Their version was definitely like none I’ve ever had. The grits are imported from Carolina. The texture was amazing. Just the right ratio (cause I’m a math girl) of shrimp, sausage and sauce. And with just the right amount of kick. Will definitely be a regular stop every time we are in town. You’ve gotta go check out this husband & wife team. Tell Marissa that Michelle from Riverside sent you.

Went there for lunch. The owner was friendly, engaged, warm, lively and helpful. The shrimp taco salad was one of the best salads the 3 of us have ever had. The blueberry lemonade was delicious also. We can’t wait to go back!

The ricotta donuts at Cafe Noir are an absolute standout. Light, fluffy, and fried to perfection, they have that dreamy texture that only ricotta can give. A subtle hit of lemon keeps them bright and balanced, making each bite feel indulgent without being heavy.

They’re served with both chocolate and caramel sauce, but the caramel combo is downright decadent—rich, buttery, and the perfect match for the warm donuts. It’s the kind of dessert you keep thinking about long after the plate is gone.

top_reviews.content:
The Dry Fried Diced Chicken was really good. I came here off a recommendation from a friend and that’s what she recommended. The outside is crispy while the inside is juicy, the glaze on it is sweet and sour and the green onions balances it all.

I also had the Shrimp Dumplings and the shrimp inside tasted really high quality.

The atmosphere inside was very cozy and the waitress served us like we were a part of their family.

I’ll definitely be coming back here again.

If you're looking for a hidden gem, Tenglong is absolutely worth a visit. It's a small, family-run Chinese restaurant with a warm, welcoming atmosphere that makes you feel at home the moment you walk in. One of the highlights of every visit is the wonderful owner, who is so incredibly kind, attentive, and genuinely cares about every customer. It's clear that the restaurant is a labor of love, and I’ve felt valued as a customer for the past ten years my family has been coming here.
The food is consistently excellent. The sizzling rice soup is a must—the rich, flavorful broth and vegetables paired with the crackle of the crispy rice makes it comforting and fun to eat. The potstickers are perfectly pan-fried with crispy bottoms, tender wrappers, and a juicy, savory filling. Another standout is the pork and green beans, which are cooked to perfection. The pork is tender and well-seasoned, while the green beans stay crisp and fresh, creating a simple but incredibly flavorful dish.
Highly recommend!!
Absolutely fantastic chinese food. Authentic catonese noodles, great dim sum, highly recommend. Family owned, Christina (the restaurant mom) is awesome. Definitely stop by!

This place is authentic and delicious. My partner is Chinese and he absolutely loves the place. It’s family run. The service is fast and friendly and they always get our order right. The Szechuan dry fried chicken is my favorite and it keeps me coming back for more!

Great options for vegans. Had the sesame meatless chicken, savory and delicious. Green beans and tofu were tasty as well. Very nice and helpful waiter. Very clean and chill atmosphere. Will definitely come back!

top_reviews.content: I remember the last time I got complementary soup and hot tea is back in my country which kind of makes me homesick a lil bit. It seems to be a very quiet restaurant normally, the noice in the video is due to the road construction. The lady serving me was very kind and chill. The sizzling clay pot is so delicious and I order a random dish from their today’s recommended menu, which is also very delicious. The portion is very filling!

We got the yellow eel claypot rice and the salted fish and preserved meat claypot rice. Both were delicious and the eel rice was full of eel, the restaurant does not skimp out on meat. Portion size was excellent! Highly recommend this gem of a restaurant and will definitely be returning.

Had Christmas Eve dinner here and definitely 5 stars! Their clay pots are delicious and amazingly cheap for SF in 2025. Put this on the delicious cheap eats of 2026 list! They start at $13 for a lot of options and come out hot and well portioned with plenty of protein on top. Let it sit for a bit and you get that crispy rice that cracks loudly when you bite into it. We had the chicken and sausage claypot and the traditional yellow eel one. Generous portions of meats. We also tried the lamb with tofu skin which had a rich lamb flavor and huge chunks of lamb for $15. Some of the lamb pieces have a good chunk of fat but lamb is like that. The sauce is delicious on that dish so I recommend to try something with lamb for sure. We also got the Chinese broccoli (well cooked and good portion) and pork intestines which were delicious and great texture. Final dish was the salt and pepper fish which was light and crispy on the outside and soft and piping hot on the inside. If you get takeout, throw some of those fish fillets on some Hawaiian rolls with some tartar sauce and have some awesome Fillet o Fish sliders! First page of the menu is all the clay pots (crispy rice!). This is a mom and pop place with basic decor but great food and shockingly low prices, especially for the portion sizes and quality. Please come here and support this business so they stay open so I can keep coming here. You won't regret it.

Came here for a late lunch and there were plenty of tables available. They had a tv showing a Chinese cooking show. Service was fast. Clay pots had a very nice crisp to all the edges. The rice was well flavored from the ones we ordered. Spare ribs was standard. Lamb was really good. Definitely more than a person serving each.

So delicious! Definitely one of the best Chinese spots in all of SF. It’s super underrated and every time I’ve been it’s been very empty, and I just cannot understand why.
The Mapo Tofu is out of this world - spicy, cilantro-y, tangy, and savory. The green beans were done perfectly, and clay pot rice is so reasonably priced and crackly at the edges. All together a must visit! I will certainly be coming back much more in the future 🥰🥰
The service is kind and sweet and it seems to be staffed by a family, but English is not their first language. Regardless they were lovely and very helpful.
The prices are insane. For huge portions, each dish is only in 10-15$ range, which is fantastic given that each dish can easily feed 2 and more. We ordered 3 things between 2 people, and the leftovers are more than enough for dinner too.

Haven’t been here in two years, and still just as impressed. This deli is a hidden gem. The chicken sandwich is nothing short of amazing. As we waited Saturday, Rutily was nice enough to give us some of her homemade hummus, for free. Ive never had homemade hummus, but it was amazing. I would go out of my way to stop here again in a heartbeat.

Everyone was so friendly and helpful! The store is spotless and the ability to customize my sandwich was helpful - especially since my little one is a purest with meat and cheese. The portions were very generous, which means your dollar goes the extra mile. Great selection of fresh produce too.

Rutily's is our favorite local market, and we're so glad they're in our neighborhood! Gus, Georgina and their sons are so kind, and genuinely care about their customers. They have a nice product selection and take great care in choosing the items they stock in their store. The made-to-order sandwiches and prepared items in the deli case are outstanding... We tried the half soy garlic / half hot sauce chicken (8 pieces), beef bulgogi kimbab, and seafood ramen — and everything was excellent. This place is incredible. They have the best sushi in the Richmond. Also, the service is fantastic. Huge shout out to Kyle. He was very attentive and friendly. I highly recommend the Daigo Shot and Sashimi omakase.

top_reviews.content: Fantastic kimbap, very satisfying. Particularly loved the fried shrimp kimbap! The soup that came with was light and refreshing, and the tteokbokki was delicious. I saw this restaurant a few weeks ago but it was closed. Today, attended an event nearby and decided to try this place out for dinner. After entering the restaurant, I saw that the interior was bright and had wooden panels. A video of a park in Seoul was projected on a wall that also had small achromatic paintings of some dishes. I could tell from the steel beams that the building isn't modern, but this business has done a great job with making the place feel up to date.

I approached the person working and asked to see the menu and was directed to a QR code to scan, which was a little annoying. It would be great if they had a screen near the counter with some of their recommended items or a brief menu. The menu online had a lot of items available, so I needed a few minutes to scroll through. I wanted to try their fried seaweed roll (4pcs for $5) and also ordered bulgogi kimbap ($15), a safe choice for my first visit.

The worker brought over some sweet chili dipping sauce and utensils, and a few minutes later, the food I ordered plus a complimentary bowl of broth. The fried seaweed roll had sweet potato glass noodles, the kind for japchae, in seaweed that had been battered and fried. It was simple but delicious with the dipping sauce. The kimbap came in a long serving container that spanned across my table. Wang kimbap (giant kimbap) is a relatively new thing that looks good for social media but is a bit uncomfortable to eat. Each piece fully filled my mouth and took like 30 seconds to fully chew. But least it was a good amount of food for the price. I wish they sold normal sized kimbap as well though.

While I was eating, I noticed a small fly buzzing around. It eventually landed in my sauce, got stuck, and died in it. Luckily I was already done with the fried seaweed rolls. I asked the worker to take the sauce away and he did it immediately, and he also later apologized for the fly even though it wasn't his fault.

I feel like some of the items' prices were a little high, like $5 for barley tea when some Korean restaurants give that for free, $23 for simple rice plates, or $14 for instant ramyeon, but the kimbap was fair value considering that it's freshly made to order and huge. There is a large selection of noodles, fried chicken, and street food in addition to kimbap.

I noticed that there was a step up from the street to the restaurant level so it might not be wheelchair accessible. The Tenderloin has a lot of people with disabilities who live or access services in the neighborhood. There is one restroom in the back.

We had a great time at Kimbap Heaven! We originally had plans to eat at a brunch spot nearby, but got overwhelmed by the crowd, so we decided to pop in. The restaurant is small, but very clean and well-kept. We had the bulgogi kimbap, the ssam kimbap, and the soy garlic fried chicken, which were all delicious! The kimbap comes with a side of soup for each person, which was very nice. The owner was incredibly kind, and came to check on us every so often (granted, we were the only ones dining in, however we saw several delivery drivers come in to pick up orders).

so happy they got their own brick and mortar store location!!! order ahead for pick up using toast app and it’s so easy. their kimbap is double the size of usual traditional size so the price isn’t so bad at all considering that. i feel lucky to have them nearby. absolutely love their food!

top_reviews.content: Don’t come here expecting authentic Taiwanese flavors. Nothing we ordered came close. The hot pot tasted artificial, almost chemical, and the ingredients didn’t match the price point. The deep fried stinky tofu was disappointing, and all the fried appetizers were plain, underwhelming, greasy, and served in small portions. The only decent dish was the deep fried pork chop with braised pork rice, which was just okay. We left almost angry, given the quality of food we received compared to the amount of cash we paid. Their dessert was fine.

It’s a pretty good weeknight comfort food option. I got the black garlic oil ramen. It is a reasonable portion with plenty of ingredients. The pork is well cooked and sliced thin. Next time, I will try the hot pot.

Came here for dinner on a recent Friday evening. Our party of three ordered a stinky tofu hot pot, an herbal soup hot pot, and a fried pork chop rice plate.

The portion size for each order was very good and service was fast and efficient. The two hot pots were okay, nothing spectacular. Their blood cake was very mushy, the pickled veggies very bland, and there were very few intestines. Also, my stinky tofu was not good at all. It wasn't much different than regular tofu. Their dipping sauces were not very tasty either. The three sauces, Chinese BBQ, garlic soy sauce, and hot chili oil were all very disappointing. The sauces were very sour and lacked flavor and had a very watery consistency. Thankfully the pork chop was delicious.

Having lived in Southern California, I've been spoiled by Boiling Point and other local independent spots. I guess this is decent for the area, but I won't be going back.

Not many Taiwanese restaurants nearby. Good addition to the Alameda noodle selection that isn't a one-stop-shop of all ethnic asian cuisines (although they do have Korean and Japanese things on the menu, but maybe avoid these?). I can see how they would dial down the tofu stankiness to cater to the American taste buds, but I still enjoyed mine. Lamb skewers and rice dish were great. Taiwanese desserts in general are delicious bc they aren't the sugary diabetes-inducing level at most places.

Will be back next time I need a quick fix at the last minute with family.

In the bay area, you can find a lot similar or franchise, but this one is unique in Alameda so far.
Street parking only, but public parking is plenty in the area.

top_reviews.content: I have not had brunch in a long time and Tur was a great entry back into this favored pastime. The food was great and light! Tur
1 West Portal
San Francisco

Breakfast and Brunch, Asian Fusion, Coffee and Tea

Opened 8 am - 2 pm Daily
Closed  on Tuesdays

Every once in a while, a new restaurant comes along that makes your jaw drop in amazement. Tur, from the same team behind the popular Khao Tiew, is exactly that kind of place.

Open for 2 weeks, Tur took over the prime corner location on West Portal where Squat and Gobble location used to be and delivers an incredible dining experience with stunning plating, creative flavor combinations, and dishes so beautiful that every plate feels Instagram-worthy.

We ordered:

* Softie Benedict - using Shokupan bread instead of an English muffin was so much better
* Honey Walnut Shrimp & Waffle
* Garden Benedict - Kale and mushrooms so crispy
* Berry Shot
* Creamy Lemonade- with raspberry foam, best I ever had

Everything was excellent and house made - waffles, shrimp cake, sauces….. but my personal favorites were the Garden Benedict and the Creamy Lemonade— the lemonade was so refreshing and delicious that I could happily drink it all day long.

Despite a 20–30 minute wait, service was outstanding. Mew kept everyone informed, was enthusiastic and friendly, and made sure guests felt welcomed, even as she was heading off for her break.

What really sets Tur apart is the attention to detail. From the thoughtful décor and napkins to the adorable turtle-shaped salt and pepper holders, every element feels carefully curated. The restaurant’s name, Tur, translates to “You,” and that philosophy shines through in every part of the experience—it truly feels like everything is centered around “YOU’, the  guest’s enjoyment.

This is a definite repeat visit for me. If you’re looking for one of the most exciting new brunch spots around, put Tur at the top of your list. 🥂🐢✨

I came here twice in the last few days because I really enjoyed the brunch with my friend last weekend so I wanted to come back on one of the weekdays. When we came around 9 am on Sunday , luckily we took the last table and we saw so many people came after us making the lines outside.   I came back today, Wed around noon and the wait was pretty short , about 5 min.

Based off of my own experiences here, I would rate Tur somewhere between 3.5 to 4 stars. This was actually my second time trying the food here and I am quite glad I gave them another try because the first time I went the experience was quite a bit underwhelming.

I wanted to note that both times I went to Tur, the service after being seated is quite slow. They do get quite busy but it also does take them about 15 - 25 minutes to check up on you.

To give a bit of a breakdown about the food, the first time I came here I tried their Pla Jook (fish congee) and Tonkatsu Jook (pork cutlet congee). More recently, I tried their more popular items, which are the Kai Moo (scrambled egg with pork chashu over toast), Karaage Jook (fried chicken congee), and Passionfruit & Mango Sticky Rice French Toast.

So, Pla Jook is not something I would expect for foreigners to typically order. However, the reason why I wanted to try this dish is because I really enjoyed a similar but different dish called Khao Tom Pla (a rice soup with fish) when I visited Thailand. It is interesting that Tur uses grass fish for their Pla Jook. Steaming the fish gives it a bouncy almost cartilage like texture. Personally, I am more used to and much rather prefer fried grass fish, which gives the fish a more flaky and meatier texture. While steaming the fish is certainly healthier, I had a hard time finishing the dish. I would much have rather they steamed a flaky fish like snapper or fried the grass fish to offer texture contrast. I think it comes down to personal preference but I think I had expected more from the dish and was left underwhelmed with how it was prepared.

The Tonkatsu Jook was better but the pork cutlet as a whole is a bit dry due to it being overcooked. It does help when you dip your cutlet in the congee to mask the dry texture.

Moving onto their popular dishes, the Kai Moo is quite good. The scrambled eggs are light and fluffy and the slow cooked pork chashu is both fatty and juicy.

The Karaage Jook is also more well cooked as they are smaller cuts of fried chicken.

The Passionfruit & Mango Sticky Rice French Toast is quite tasty as well. I am personally not a huge fan of crust (again, personal preference) but the toast is overall quite fluffy and soft. It goes well with the sweet and ever so slightly tart passionfruit.

I had wanted to wait before leaving an official review for Tur because my first impression of the food was quite poor. Overall, I think that if they make small improvements to their service and recipe, there will be a very visible difference.

Checked out Tur this weekend and really enjoyed it. The space is beautiful and the service was friendly.

We ordered three dishes and all of them were hitters. The Passionfruit and Mango Sticky Rice French Toast was the standout. I'd order it for the table every single time.

The only downside was the wait. We were quoted 20-30 minutes but ended up waiting a little over an hour and a half, that's not too surprising for a brand-new spot.

Food-wise, everything was really good, but a couple dishes could've used a little more seasoning.  I think a little heat or a house hot sauce option would take some of the dishes to the next level.

Take It Easy Thai Cuisine has been around for more than 8 years! I used to come here when my daughter went to the high school around the corner and came by often to get lunch.
I usually get the Pad See Ew, Pad Thai noodles, or the coconut curries. Today, I wanted to try something different, which was the Beef Jungle Curry. top_reviews.content:
This is a local South Indian restaurant chain with locations across the Bay Area, and this Berkeley location is a smaller one. We stopped by on the weekend for a quick filter coffee and a plate of masala/dal vada.

The vada was a little on the dry side, perhaps because it had been sitting for a while, although thankfully it wasn’t greasy. The filter coffee was pretty standard for the chain, and I especially like to have it with a spoonful of jaggery.

Overall, a quick and decent stop for South Indian coffee and snacks.

Very good place! Good deal on the combo in terms of price, only $11 for a dosa, medhu, and idly, and everything was delicious. The chai was very well balanced and they had jaggery to put in which was good and felt special.

In the south Indian desert that is Oakland it is very refreshing to see a stalwart take root in Berkeley. Everything Idly Express touches is savory gold. If you haven't spent time in Madras this will give you a good simulation - the music, the heavy smell of filter coffee in the air, the coffee itself....it all adds towards the small hustling and bustling vegetarian "hotels" one finds in Madras.

The food is unapologetically spicy and that's good. It keeps the flavors and the textures close the source. The soaked idlis were decadent as were the crunchy vadas. The korma had that sharpness to it and the benne dosa's life force ran all over my palm as I devoured it like a mild-mannered Bakasura at the local village.

The place is small and very functional. It's not date night material unless your date is an adventurous eater whose idea of Indian food is all the stereotypical north indian fare. Then, this place is the beginning of an adventure.

Beware, travel with a bottle of lassi, for the road is spicy ahead.

We've eaten at the restaurant 4-5 times since it's opening. Service is always speedy and the food arrives within 5-10 mins consistently. The staff are friendly  & attentive. Nice to have tasty South Indian food in Berkeley. Our favorites are the ghee podi idly, medhu vadai and masala dosa. The thali is great to share with someone if you aren't too hungry. The curd rice in the thali is creamy and delicious. The chai and filter coffee are must haves!

Bonus tip: The dosa batter in the takeout fridges make crispy golden brown dosas. Highly recommend!

I'm fortunate to live in a region of the Bay Area where there are a lot of Filipino restaurants and each of them do so much to sustain the cultural significance of the Philippine population of the area.

For years in having this restaurant as part of my rotation of Filipino cuisine, one of their superpowers is their consistency for delivering good tasting food. Time and time again, I find their offerings to be as good or better than their competitors.

Their service is great and you can count on being warmly greeted by the staff. I also feel that their portions are more generous than their counterparts. So if it's good food you're after, I highly recommend them.

And as is typical of a lot of Filipino joints, decor, atmosphere and aesthetics aren't their thing. As you'll see in the accompanying pictures, this place is about as basic, utilitarian and modest as a place can be, as stripped down as an apartment of newlyweds. But then again, you don't come here for the furniture and art on the walls did you? If you did, you'd be richly disappointed.

CASH ONLY. Great place for your Filipino food cravings. A star above your usualhole in wall place!  Spacious place with lots tables, chairs and TV for people to eat. They not only serve the usual breakfast 'silog' items but have desserts and entrees. They do catering too! Nice portion of food except had only 3 pieces of bones attached with small pcs of beef. Will not get these ever even though it was warmed in no microwave!

Mekeni Restaurant & Karaoke Bar is your typical turo-turo Filipino restaurant in Daly City. In addition to the steam table operation it also has an all-day made to order breakfast menu (Silog). Unlike other turo-turo places Mekeni is a decent sized restaurant. I've been here about half a dozen times for lunch and each time have found it to be about half full which I've taken as a good sign. It is located on Mission in an area where finding parking would be impossible during weekdays but it's not too difficult to find a spot in the lot just ahead of the restaurant on weekends.

The dishes in the steam table operation rotate but they always seem to have at-least one Chicken item (adobo, caldereta etc.) so I stick to getting a one item combo to-go ($5). They always try to push the chicken BBQ when I ask for chicken but unlike Fil-Am where you can see them freshly grill the BBQ behind the counter, I'm not sure of the freshness of the BBQ at Mekeni so I generally avoid that.

The taste of the food can be described as authentic, which means that it comes certified to give you a heart attack at 60 if you eat this every day, but its fine for once a week that I restrict myself to. Price-wise it's about 10% more expensive than Fil-Am the other turo-turo place that I generally rotate with Mekeni. I like the food here better but pick Mekeni for the freshly grilled BBQ. The only drawback that I can think of is that they don't seem to have any beef items on the weekends but that is a minor problem that will not prevent me from coming back periodically.

top_reviews.content:
Really good Vietnamese food with extensive menu.  I like that their veggies include fresh mint.

While waiting for my to go order by the door, the female staff gave me a cup of hot tea. That was really nice of her. The tea was very fragrant like pandan tea served in Vietnam.

Dining area is pretty big. Plenty of 4 person dining and big group dining tables.

One con is parking. Very hard to find parking in the mission and residential area. Went on weekday afternoon took about 15 mins circling around.  Otherwise, I think this is a good go-to spot for Vietnamese food in SF.

Very good pho.  Flavorful broth and large chunks of meat (I ordered tendon and it was full or large chunks).  Noodles were qiu-qiu and service was warm and friendly.   The spring rolls were good but I think they could have had a little more flavor to it.  Took a little bit of time to get our order in because I think they do quite a bit of takeout and delivery but all in all, was a good experience and good pho.

Very disappointing experience. I ordered the chicken curry and the soup was warm, but the chicken inside was literally cold. It felt like the kitchen just took a piece of refrigerated chicken and dropped it into the curry without bothering to reheat it properly. Biting into cold chicken in a supposedly hot dish was extremely unpleasant.

To make it worse, the dish came with a whole chicken leg with skin instead of properly cut pieces. It was awkward to eat and the texture was terrible, especially since the meat inside was still cold.

For a simple dish like chicken curry, serving cold chicken in soup is really unacceptable. This felt careless and poorly prepared. And the service is like none.

Definitely won’t go again.

When I came in, I was blasted with a feeling of comforting vibes, for a homey sit down meal. I was unsure what to order, and the kind waiter helped me chose. I chose the combination pho, ($18), and it came out very quickly, less than a 10 minute wait. The food was delicious, a typical pho, with bean spourts, Thai basil, lemon, and jalapeno as "toppings". The interior utilizes darker colors, with tawny walls and deep wooden tables and chairs. When you come in, just chose a table and sit down!  A lot of 4 seat tables, but if you have more or less, they are able to accomdate that for you. The service was very kind and efficient.

The paying system at this restaurant was a bit different compared to others I've visited, after you finish your meal, you go up to the register to pay for your meal (instead of the traditional method where they come to your table and hand you the bill). There was not a option for tip, which is extremely shocking and almost blasphemous in America. The server just handed me a receipt  of what I had eaten, and didn't include any automatic gratuity or pressure customers into tipping. There was no annoying tip option on the screen, just pay for what you ate. (Card is $15 minimum!). Although this was not a huge act, this won me over in being a returning customer. Not being pressured to tip felt like a newfound experience, like taking a breath of air after being submerged in toxic waters. By the paying register, there are the nostalgic guava candies (little green things), and a cup full of toothpicks. The tiny touch of the guava candies and even having a cute fishtank by the register (was not able to photograph:( goes to show the amount of attention that went to this restaurant and their dedication to make their customers dining experience pleasurable. I don't particlarly recall, but I dont remember this place having a bathroom so plan ahead! Although the pho didn't extremely stand out to me, it was a very solid pho, the other aspects of this restaurant won me over.

TDLR: pretty good pho! No tip, (but ofc I would reccomed you ask to tip the waiter, great service), guava candies and cozy tawny interior vibe!

* $15 minimum on cards *

Beef Banh mi for $12 is solid, the qualiry of the meat could definitely be higher for this price point.

Solid Chicken Pho, Good Broth, Average SF pricing. Comes out to $21 roughly

If you're  in Oakland, Primavera is a must-visit. I always go for the "Mother Earth" sandwich, and it never disappoints. Packed with turkey, ham, bacon, cheese, avocado, mayo, honey mustard, tomato, lettuce, and cucumber, it’s a deliciously satisfying meal that hits the spot every time.

What makes Primavera special is its welcoming atmosphere. As a small family-owned business, the staff always greet you with kindness and a smile, making you feel right at home. The prices are also quite reasonable, especially considering the quality of the sandwiches and drinks.

If you’re in the area, stop by.

What Primavera does really well that lots of other sandwich shops overlook is their bread - it's fantastic here. The portions are generous and good selection, including delicious veggie options.

This isn't a fancy sandwich shop, it's a real-deal simple, satisfying meal at a fair price. Evidenced by the droves of students that frequent it. Support family owned businesses!

What really stood out to me was their extensive drink menu. The craft beer selection was impressive, featuring both local and artisanal brews. The staff was incredibly knowledgeable and helped me choose the perfect pairing for my meal.

top_reviews.content:
First time eating in this restaurant and it didn’t disappoint. We had the steamed dumplings with crab, garlic fried rice, whole branzino with fish sauce and green beans with mushrooms and half half purple rice and jasmine rice. They were all delicious.
The steamed dumplings came out right away but we had to wait awhile for the next dish. Then the green beans and mushrooms came out which were perfectly crispy and in an oyster/fish garlic sauce. The next dish didn’t come out for a long time. We were so hungry that we essentially ate the entire side before our second two dishes came out.
It was obviously not our server’s fault. The kitchen could have timed it better.
We did not have any beverages nor dessert. The bill to $148 with an above average tip. We will be back but it’s not going to be a regular thing due to the price.

Food here was delicious, although priced for the neighborhood for sure. Really enjoyed the pork jowl fried rice, Pad Thai, and Nam Tok in particular. Great vibe inside with some really cool art on the walls, and love the circular windows on the side of the building as well.

Would have been 5 stars but we were very abruptly told we essentially had 5 minutes to wrap up our meal, pay, and leave the table less than 1.5 hours after our reservation time, for another party's upcoming reservation. For a table of 6 with 2 small kids that we were managing throughout the meal, this was quite unexpected and we didn't even get a chance to try dessert, which we'd been excited for. The reservation confirmation specifically mentions that the table is reserved for 2.5 hours for parties of 6, and we weren't told of the upcoming reservation when we arrived, so this was a really unpleasant end to what was otherwise a great meal.

Pork jowl fried rice is 🔥 We will be back for that and the fried chicken wings. The cod was delicious as well. Definitely hoping to try the pad Thai and duck curry next time.

The logistics are a bit tricky; leave 10-15 minutes for parking and expect to navigate some narrow and uneven roads. I would also not rely on the restaurant to respond to calls or texts very quickly. Changing a reservation within 48 hours is allowed by policy but not easy.

If there is one restaurant that has defined my 2025/2026 dining experiences, it is Payakk in Oakland. This isn't just a place to eat; it’s a place where food, storytelling, and pure creativity converge to create something truly stand-out and unique.
​You can feel the immense love and passion that the chef-owner pours into every single detail. Each dish feels intentional, carrying a narrative that elevates the meal beyond just "delicious."
​The curries are easily my personal favorite—rich, complex, and deeply comforting. However, the absolute "must-order" is the Pad Thai Chai Ya. It is a stunning example of their creativity and a dish I haven't stopped thinking about since my first bite.
​While it is a bit of a trek from the city (SF), I can personally guarantee that it is well worth the trip. If you appreciate high-quality ingredients used with a creative spirit and a lot of heart, Payakk is the destination you've been looking for.

Second time eating dinner here and organized a team dinner for six people on a Thursday evening.
(Note: My first review praised the swordfish... But not sure what happened to the review on Google maps.)

We started with the calamari and focaccia. Both were very tasty. For mains, we shared the cacio e pepe, crab gnocchi, wild boar paccheri, the porterhouse steak for 2, the brussel sprouts and the roasted broccoli 🥦.

Service was friendly and attentive. Would definitely come back again.

I’ve followed Chef Ryan for nearly 10 years, dating back to his days at Bellota SF and the restaurants that followed. Every now and then you come across a chef whose passion is unmistakable—you can see it in every menu, every dish, and every detail. Ryan is one of those people.

We celebrated a friend’s birthday at Bosco SF, and it exceeded every expectation. Every dish was thoughtful, beautifully executed, and absolutely delicious. The produce and ingredients felt incredibly fresh and unique, and you can tell there’s a real commitment to sourcing seasonal ingredients, working with local farmers, and constantly experimenting with what’s at its peak.

It was genuinely one of the best dining experiences we’ve had in San Francisco in a long time, and that’s saying something. The pasta and steak were sooooo good! And the avocados and produce in general tasted straight from the farm.

Whether you’re celebrating a graduation, birthday, anniversary, planning a date night, or simply treating yourself, Bosco is a place I’d wholeheartedly recommend. The space is beautiful, the hospitality was exceptional, and the entire experience felt special from start to finish.

Congratulations to Chef Ryan and the entire Bosco team. We’ll definitely be back, and I’ll be recommending it to everyone.

So happy to finally come to this new restaurant! every bite from the appetizer to dessert didn’t disappoint. loved the focaccia bread, swordfish, and the arancini rice ball the most. the steak 🥩 could’ve been a lot juicier but we felt that the pomegranate sauce made up for it in some ways. the ambience was incredible and staffs were so nice! the only caveat is their bathroom wasn’t in the restaurant (still in the same building though!).

will definitely come back and bring my family along with me next time - congrats again for the recent opening!

Bosco is an easy recommendation if you get the chance. It’s perfect for a slightly fancier night out, date night, or a fun spot to bring a group of friends.

We started with the Sourdough Focaccia and the Bosco Caesar. The focaccia is an absolute must-have; perfectly salted, lightly oiled, and has a clean feel. Not overlly filling as normal bread apps leave you.

The Caesar was also excellent, with a fresh spin that reminded me of the anchovy-parmesan broccolini at NOPA, but reimagined as a salad. Both are dishes I’d happily order again.

The Smoked Potato Polpette seemed to be on nearly every table, and it’s easy to see why. The Calabrian chili bomba sauce really makes the dish. The crunch of the fried potato against the smooth, warm sauce is one of those perfect contrasts that makes it a quick cleanup around the table.

For my main, I had the Pork Ribs Agrodolce, which turned out to be the biggest surprise of the night. I’ve paid double the price for ribs in Carmel that were almost as good. When you get a fattier cut, it melts in your mouth, and the peach pairing adds just the right touch of sweetness. It was easily a highlight of the meal.

Serving sizes are generous. I would recommend sharing an item or two start as you'll still probably have something to take home. And if the food isn’t enough, the drinks alone are worth the visit. The cocktails are high quality without the inflated price tag. You’re essentially paying dive-bar prices for something far better crafted. The atmosphere is bustling but welcoming, with décor that makes it feel lively without being over the top.

I don’t usually leave reviews, but Bosco deserved one. Definitely worth a try; especially if you’re planning a date night.

top_reviews.content:
Came here with a few college friends and left seriously impressed, easily one of the best taquerias in Oakland. Walking in, the smell of fresh tortillas and grilled meat immediately got us excited. We tried the pollo and carne asada tacos, and both were perfectly seasoned, juicy, and loaded with fresh cilantro and onion. The salsa bar is a highlight on its own, the salsa verde had just the right amount of heat.

Service was quick and friendly, prices are very reasonable, and the portions are generous. You can tell they use fresh, quality ingredients and genuinely care about the food. This is authentic, no-frills Mexican food at its best, the kind of place you keep going back to. Highly recommend, 10/10!

The meats were well seasoned, and the salsa had a nice kick without being overwhelming. Service was friendly and the place had a relaxed vibe. Definitely a spot I'd come back to when I'm in the area.

The business is very bright and clean with very visually pleasing art pieces on the walls. Their menu is easily read and extensive. The staff was very kind and warm when I entered and greeted me. The food was amazing as well! Make sure to check it out!

An amazing gem (not so hidden) in the Fruitvale neighborhood of Oakland, CA.

With SO MUCH great Latin cuisine in the Fruitvale area it was hard to choose. Taqueria Zocalo was recommended to me by a co-worker while on-site so I gave it a shot.

I’m glad I did!

Upon entering, the business is bright and clean with colorful murals and other artistic pieces strategically placed. They have their menu on a screen if you’re waiting in line as well as the traditional written menus.

Their menu has all the classics so I went for the tried and proven to see how their flavors compare with some of my other favorites places. I ordered a taco plate with 1 Al Pastor and 1 Carne Asada. It can with rice and black beans. Every dimension of this plate had great flavor, texture and looked super appetizing!

Lastly, when I got to order the manager greeted me warmly and confirmed all my order (since I was bringing some stuff back to the shop). She also brought the order out and followed up too. I didn’t expect that.

In closing I HIGHLY recommend Taqueria Zocalo and will bring friends and family there when I’m the area.

Pro tip: it’s next to a high school so keep that in mind if going Monday - Friday.

​I recently visited Emeryville for a business trip and brought my family along. Our accommodation was close to the Emeryville Public Market, so we ended up trying a bunch of different places there. The food hall has a great variety of options—the burger place was excellent, and so was the sushi spot.

​While all the food was good, Nabi Q was my favorite. I've attached a photo of the delicious meal we had there. If you're looking for a casual place with lots of great food options that cater to families, I highly recommend checking out the Public Market food hall!

Hubby and I were attending the opening of the Emeryville Art Exhibition and popped over to the Public Market for a bite to eat. I was hungry but nothing really grabbed me, so after circling twice I ended up at NabiQ and ordered the bibimbap with spicy pork and egg on top while he went to a different food stall. It was a generous portion, enough for two. The food looked appealing but the meat was too sweet for my taste even after mixing the whole thing together. It came with a small cup of kimchi and gochujang sauce. I picked at it the food but left quite a bit uneaten, didn't want to take it home. Price was over $22, including tip.

The person who took my order was friendly and polite. Food came fairly quickly. The kitchen area was clean and tidy, no complaints there.

I'll be back for sure.

SO GOOD!! I am so excited to have such a good dumpling place nearby. We got lots of food to share - our favorites were the string beans, firecracker chicken, and the shrimp wonton soup with rice noodles. Everything tasted delicious and came out so fast. Will definitely be returning!

top_reviews.content:
I had a craving for shrimp and grits and wanted it to taste authentic. The pictures alone sold me so I found myself in Bayview for brunch😋.

The people there are really kind and the place itself is really familiar/homely to me. You can tell they put a lot of intention into making their guests feel like they're coming to their "professional chef aunt's house" to eat.

The fried chicken was perfectly seasoned, the waffle was light and fluffy (the cinnamon butter was really unique and yummy!) and the GRITS!

GET. THE. GRITS.

Just a really, really good place to get soul food. Most certainly, the best in the city.

Yummy Southern eatery on Third Street serving classics like fried chicken, sautéed shrimp and sausage as well as the standard sides that make soul food so famous.

The fried chicken is lightly battered and spiced. Smoke Soul Salad (with fried chicken breast) is tasty with a citrusy house vinaigrette, berries and crumbled blue cheese served over a bed of kale.

A friendly neighborhood spot, with personable service.

Was looking for a good breakfast spot and this popped up. This little joint packs a lot of flavor in every bite. I do believe this place has the best chicken and waffles in the city. The off the porch cocktail was dangerously delicious, and I'm saying that as someone who generally never drinks alcohol, but it was incredible. We ordered the sweet creme pancake, chicken and waffles, beingets, cocktail and hash brown on the side. Everything with tip set me back a pretty penny (75$) but it was honestly worth every cent, and today's meal was definitely a splurge (without the beignets and cocktail, I would have saved myself $20).
Considering they offer $22 by steak and eggs, I think that's the cheapest I've seen it anywhere, so please, get what you can afford here, as you won't be sorry.
Fried chicken was drippingly moist, tender and well seasoned. Waffles were fluffy and went perfect with the maple butter. Pancake tasted like a slice of fresh cake, fried eggs and bacon were on point, and hash browns didn't even need ketchup as they were perfectly fluffy and crispy, just needed a touch of salt and pepper. My chicken and waffles came out last and a little longer than everything else, but it was worth the wait, as the chicken was clearly fresh from the fryer.
Service is more help yourself: for the coffee they gave us a mug to go grab our own from an airpot (slightly sour, which suggested a lighter roast; not bad, but not great 'diner' coffee, but palatable with our meal enough for a free refill). You order at the front and help yourself to cutlery and water at the back. There's a bathroom (single room, air dryer, gender neutral), the walls are beautifully painted with a proudly black woman theme, and the tables are  primarily benches or metal garden furniture seating. All tables accommodate 4-6 adults, but table sharing seems okay here too. If driving here, parking can be a little difficult, but coming on a Sunday meant no payment which was nice, and we found a spot relatively fast and nearby on the main street. Otherwise, plenty of public transit options are very close.
If you're looking for a giant fluffy PANcake, an amazing chicken and waffles, or just looking for a great cocktail, stop by this place and you won't regret it. Splurge if you can, too, cus the sides are all incredibly worth it.

There's a reason that good gatherings end up mostly in the kitchen.

I've had Southern a number of places, including where I was first introduced to it on Duke St in Baltimore, MD back in the 80s. Smoke Soul is the first place I've been that beats that experience.

The red beans and rice are spiced perfectly, and the biscuit they serve is the perfect compliment to get every drop out of the bowl.  The chicken and waffles shows other places just how it's done, with a crisp, fluffy waffle, perfectly seasoned and juicy full chicken wings, and a brown butter that'll leave you craving more.

The folk there are family and they definitely welcome you in too. The shop is immaculate with tables for all sizes of groups.

Parking is a bit tight (hey, it's San Francisco), but you can find spots, or just do the easy thing and take the T line down to Kirkwood station and you're a block and a half away. It's absolutely worth the trip.
Amazing food! We shared the shrimp and grits, crème pancakes and chicken waffles. Brown butter and maple syrup chef kiss. Sangrias also a hit. Much success to you!

Also the service was amazing, super friendly, gave great recs, and gave me live updates on my table readiness 😘 do come here!

Great new spot! We really enjoyed the bread and caesar salad, chicken, and steak! Food came out slightly lukewarm though. Wines and strawberry dessert were delicious too.

Lively atmosphere, and expect to be on the waitlist for 1-2 hours.

I would definitely come back, though with such a small menu you’d likely get the same dish each time, curious if they’ll rotate their menu over time.
Esme is a great new addition to the neighborhood and serves as an ideal date night spot. The halloumi, steak frites, and strawberry dessert were all delicious!

top_reviews.content: Great place to get a quality sandwich for lunch. They pressed the sandwiches in a panini press so they're warm but not too toasted. Just right! They also have a very secluded feeling outdoor seating area or front, but no indoor seating.

Joe Flimflam was at the Alimentari Aurora, and I was right across the street at the bookstore hoping to see the signed copy of the Magna Carta they've got on display, and all the sudden the hunger pains hit, and they hit hard!  Well, a person can always see an original King John signed document from 1215 ...But not everyone can nab a perfect sandwich from Alimentari Aurora!  ☆☆☆☆☆

This is a cute little gem that I discovered on a stroll through the Potrero Hill neighborhood. I ended up walking in and talking to the people working. They recommended some new cheeses for me to try. The cheeses were so yummy and a great combination of what I described liking. I ended up buying both cheeses and made a Charcuterie plate for dinner with the cheeses and some stuff I had at home. Very happy. Definitely check out! I know I will be back :)

This is a cute little deli and Italian grocery store tucked in Potrero Hill. You can enjoy the daily kitchen specials in the park-let or get takeout to enjoy at home.

This is one of my favorite spots for satisfying focaccia cravings. What makes it special is Chef Dario’s obsession with quality ingredients and no shortcuts. The sourdough has a beautiful sour taste that’s a result of a 3 day fermentation process - I don’t know of any other focaccias that are proofer, rested and allowed to ferment for 72+ hours, except some mad scientist home bakers. I find this better than Liguria bakery, the OG of San Francisco focaccia, and that speaks to the quality and flavors that Chef Dario is able to create.

The sourdough focaccia is thick and satisfying but not dense. It’s usually served during the weekend, for dinner, and comes in 3 different types: herbed, pizza and one with meat (fine Italian speck). I order it online on their website and probably commit blasphemy by toasting it for a couple minutes.

For lunch they serve 2 kinds of paninis: one meaty and another veggie. I haven’t tried the panini yet but that’s my next quest. It looked delicious in the Yelp pics.

I was fortunate to sample some excellent funky cheese that they sell in the store along with charcuterie, Calabrian chili oil, olives and many other curated specialty items.

Chef Dario is the nicest guy and knows his tradecraft. I was impressed when he mentioned the gelato and pizza places I loved in Bologna. Ask him for some recommendations or from his excellent staff, who recommended the most unique cheese that I have ever sampled.

I hope their oven gets repaired soon as I am craving my weekly fix of sourdough focaccia. Be warned it’s very very very addictive, and I don’t use my very’s very often.

I’ve never seen tuna spread this thin and still called a sandwich for $16.29.
