top_reviews.content: Best dinner experience I’ve had in a while. We came here for a Mother’s Day dinner and ordered the short ribs, ahi carpaccio, octopus, carrot appetizer, and drinks. They have a great corner for the business and should be busy all the time. When we came in during the afternoon to reserve a table for dinner, the inside and outside were packed. Great sign!  When we returned in the early evening the crowd had thinned out a bit, but it was still going strong. Our greeter was super friendly and energetic. She was awesome. So was Jacob and the bartender inside. We had made the reservation for inside, but the weather was holding out so we opted for a table out on the patio. Glass panels along the outer wall allow you to watch the activity on the street while still being shielded from the wind (for the most part anyway). They have indoor dining and the bar, (my cocktail was perfect), or be out on the patio with, you got it, parasol umbrellas, and then there are a couple picnic benches on the side street.
Our server was brand new (literally) as another server was giving him instructions on how to take an order, right in front of us. BOO... don't do that.  He was nice enough throughout the evening, but clearly needs to practice and get his confidence up to speed. I won't knock anyone down for learning. And besides, the other staff members here made the evening fun.
For food, we enjoyed the gnocchi dish and the braised short rib with pearl cous cous and spinach. All were good and well prepared.  Everyone here on this night were laughing and having a great time. That is always a good sign.

Parasol just opened and they are still settling into their rhythm. I look forward to returning after their grand opening in June or July.

top_reviews.content:
Super fresh banh mi with organic tofu! (4/5 Green Stars)
I wish I had tried this place earlier! I had the banh mi with organic tofu for lunch and the total cost, including tax and a 20% tip was $10.50! I was ravenous and had some concerns that it may not be enough – or come fast enough! However, the lady who took my order prepped the sandwich in as much time as it took me to take a few photos. Also, there was really a lot of tofu in the sandwich – two thick layers of it – so in the end it was pretty darn filling.

There were several memorable things about the sandwich, which I ate without any distraction even though I would normally read while eating. The bread was at a perfect state of crispiness – like a proper French roll – very light and also lightly toasted. The crunchy veggies – the daikon in particular, added a freshness to it that counterbalanced the umami of soy and tofu. I’ve only had a couple of banh mi sandwiches in my time but this one was not only the best so far but has also set a pretty high bar to measure others against.

I’m giving the Sidewalk Street Food 4/5 Green Stars for social and environmental impact. It’s a woman-owned and run business that offers affordable food in a fairly unaffordable neighborhood. Every dish option – banh mi, salad bowl, pho, and spring rolls all had a tofu option. Some of the other options – chicken and pork – are among the more sustainable choices for meat eaters. However, beef and shrimp are among the worst options Sidewalk loses a star for that. My sandwich was pretty much zero-waste in that it was wrapped in a sheet of paper and delivered in a reusable basket.
I love coming to this place for my lunch. I either get the pho with only broth and noodles or spring rolls (shrimp).

top_reviews.content:
We’ve been to Peak Alameda many times, and it never disappoints! The vibe is great, the food comes out fast and fresh, and the service is always top-notch. The staff are attentive and thoughtful, always making sure we have everything we need and checking on us throughout the meal without being intrusive. My personal favorites are the Tom Yum Reduction, Uncle Sam Fried Rice, Basil Crispy Pork Belly, Milo Thai Toast, and honestly, all of their dessert toasts are a must-try! 😍 They also offer a 2-hour bottomless mimosa experience, which makes it even better for brunch with friends.

Whether you’re craving delicious Thai food or looking for a fun brunch spot, Peak Alameda is definitely worth a visit. Highly recommend! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

We went for brunch on a Saturday. No line or wait for a table. Menu looked promising and food was decent. The tom yum egg shrimp was flavorful. Broth was very tasty. The panda brioche toast was very pretty and the panda cream was tasty, but it was just brioche toast with cream on it. My bad for thinking it was going to be like a french toast - a little more substantial of a meal. I left still hungry and grabbed 2 tacos down the block at the taqueria.

Aesthetically Good but the serving and quality difficult to compare to other Asian Restaurants in Alameda.

I had high expectations for Peak, but unfortunately, the experience was disappointing. For a place that feels "exclusive" with its reservation-only system, the food and value simply do not match the premium price point.
1. The Main Course (Pad Krapow):
This was a major letdown. Unlike the traditional dry, aromatic stir-fry you find at most Thai restaurants, this version was incredibly soupy. The meat was swimming in liquid, making it feel more like a stew than a sautéed dish. It was so off-putting that I couldn't even finish my meal. The plating was also strange, as the meat wasn't even served on top of the rice as is standard.
2. Portions (Tom Kha):
The flavor of the Tom Kha was okay, but the serving size was very small. Compared to the generous portions at other Thai spots in the East Bay, this felt like poor value for the cost.
3. The Dessert ($15 Pandan Toast):
The biggest disappointment was the Pandan Toast. Charging $15 for a single slice of brioche, a scoop of ice cream, and some shredded coconut is excessive. It felt like a simple assembly job that anyone could put together at home in five minutes. While it looked nice, there was no complexity or "wow factor" to justify such a high price.
Final Verdict:
The gap between the high prices and the actual quality of the food is too wide. There are much better Thai options nearby that offer more authentic flavors and better portions for your money. I won't be returning.

top_reviews.content: What an amazing experience. Some of the best sushi we’ve ever had. Everything was so tender, flavorful and carefully prepared. I would highly recommend to anyone looking for an omakaze!

Cozy and relaxed restaurant where the food takes center stage. We enjoyed our 18-piece omakase experience. The variety was very diverse.  Aji, Tai, Tako, Ikura, Bonito, White Tuna, Amberjack, Scallop, and Uni to name a few.

The quality of the ingredients really shined. My wife and I used very little soy sauce. In fact, we only used a small amount when instructed by our wonderful hostess, Coco. The flavors were clean and subtle. Not overpowering at all.

Also, the service was outstanding. Coco walked us through each piece and told us how Chef Kenji prepared the dish.

I highly recommend giving Hanazen a try if you enjoy omakase. However, this is not the place for you if you're looking for rolls, anything seared, or sushi covered in heavy sauce.

Each bite （almost）has its distinct texture and flavor. Standouts include the tako nigiri, smoked salmon with yuzu jelly, fluke seasoned with cherry blossom salt, nodoguro, negitoro hand roll, uni/squid hand roll, and more. They have inventive flavors and deliver a wow factor. I highly recommend sitting at the counter to talk with the chef. He is knowledgeable and kind.

Went to Japan and can never eat sushi in America anymore… except for here. The quality of fish is phenomenal, the presentation is amazing, the service is impeccable and I love the wife and husband partnership, the setting is also beautiful right across OCC and surrounded by trees and greenery. I would recommend this place 10/10 all the time, any day, any special occasion!!!!!

Best sushi ever! Such a hidden gem in Orinda. Since we moved to the area last year we've been searching for our go-to sushi place. We tried walking in once and were told to make a reservation. A year later we finally made a reservation and did the omikase, chef's choice tasting menu. OMG, was it delicious. It's a small two-person operation - literally just the sushi chef and the hostess. It's too pricey to come weekly, so I used my friends' birthdays to come back and they both loved it as well. All the fish is so fresh, delicious, and imported from Japan. You will not be getting California rolls and unagi here! All types of nigiri of fish I've never had before and not a single one that any of us disliked. Even the sushi rice is extra delicious.

--
Update - been coming back for 10 years now. It's pricey so we keep it to birthday or anniversary celebrations. We even got take out during the pandemic. I went around **10:30 AM** and was pleasantly surprised that there was no line, and parking was surprisingly easy too. Definitely coming back!

Look, if this were any other city I'd give it a heavy 5, but Oakland folks hold their food, and pizzas, to lofty standards. And while likes the pizzas and will be back again I didn't fully surrender and love it like the way I know I can.

It took a few bites before I longed to eat another one. There was some thought process that happened as the pesto and cheese bedan their relationship on my tongue and that's why I had to ding a star. At a five star place there would be no thought. Just sensory delight.

But I'll be back for the other pizzas.

It was fairly easy to find parking on a Thursday at 11:30AM and there was a few people already waiting before it opened! When we got inside, the interior and atmosphere is super nice: high ceiling, color aesthetics are dope, and I love that it gives a modern look. It is open seating and you order at the front. Staff was lovely and everyone was super accommodating and nice.

I already had some high expectations since there are some dope spots in East Bay, and I was excited to give the food a try (never been to the SF location either).

1. Margherita Pizza - 3/5 - I mean it's solid, but there was so much olive oil that when you pick up a slice, you can see the oil just hella dripping. Not sure if that played a role on the pizza also being super floppy. I do wish they had a bit more cheese and basil on it though!
2. Meatza Pizza - 4/5 - This was good and had chunks of meat on the pizza, which I'm sure all the protein lovers enjoy!
3. Mozzarella Sticks - 5/5  - These were SO solid and the cheese pull was so beautiful. Dipping it into hot marinara was the perfect bite.

Overall, it's a dope spot, and the vibes are good. Personally, not my favorite pizza in East Bay, but that's just my preference.

I had the Conrad and Meatza - both I’ve tried at the SF location before. The Conrad was soggy, salty, and the toppings weren’t distributed evenly. The Meatza was overcooked, making the crust hard as a rock. If you come here expecting the same quality as the SF pizzeria (with the same prices), then I suggest going to one of the other many pizza places in Oakland.

This location in Oakland is pretty new and their staff are super helpful and kind. The atmosphere was also really nice to where you could sit inside where you could see them making the pizzas or sit outside. The pizza itself is a mixture of New York style crust and Neapolitan style, meaning everything is a 13 inch pizza. The crust was phenomenal, true to form for New York style. We wished there was just a little bit more flavor in the sauce, especially for the margarita pizza. But one thing that they do very well are the nontraditional pizzas, such as the Hawaiian pizza that we got. This was phenomenal! Service was quick. Food was delicious. We definitely will be coming back.

top_reviews.content:
Scolari's food truck serves up seriously tasty burgers with a couple of quirks that keep it from perfection.

The classic cheeseburger hits all the right notes - perfectly toasted bun, quality cheese, sharp red onions, and fresh ingredients throughout. The execution is spot-on, but here's the catch: this thing is so impossibly tall you'll need to perform burger compression surgery just to take a bite. Not exactly the smooth eating experience you want.

The fries are the real MVP here - golden, crispy, and seasoned just right. They stay crunchy even as they cool, which is no small feat.

Now for the reality check: $7 for fries feels like food truck highway robbery, and the burger prices match that premium tier. Sure, limited competition in the area probably drives these prices, but it stings when you're calculating cost per bite.

Bottom line - the food quality is genuinely impressive with fresh ingredients and solid technique. Just wish they'd make their burgers human-mouth compatible and ease up on the wallet damage. Tasty? Absolutely. Worth the premium? That depends on how much you value convenience over value.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

Wow so many bad reviews! I have another bad experience to report. The fries were$10 and were total burnt trash. More than half the fries were less than an inch long and burned. I asked for a replacement and they said no since I ate a few of the fries. Why almanac lets them sell here is baffling.

Burnt fries, burnt chicken. Do yourself a favor and hit up in-n-out before coming here. At the very least they have better and consistently high quality food. Cashier also cancel my reciept before I had a chance to request it - trash service

I visited Scolari's Good Eats on February 13, 2024, and found their burgers to be very good, though they leaned a little toward the pricier side. The flavors and quality ingredients made each bite worthwhile, leaving a positive impression overall.

The food truck is situated at the Almanac Beer Co., which is a great location to enjoy a meal with drinks. However, it was quite busy when we went for dinner, so it was lucky we snagged a spot at the bar. Despite the bustling atmosphere, the energy added to the experience, making it a lively and enjoyable evening.

For those looking for a quality burger and a vibrant setting to pair it with a good beer, Scolari's Good Eats at the Almanac Beer Co. is worth checking out, just be prepared for a crowd during peak hours.

We stopped by Scolari’s Food Truck while enjoying drinks at Almanac Brewery and ordered a full-size fries and an order of chicken tenders. Unfortunately, they gave us a half-size fries instead of the full size we requested—an honest mistake but one that could’ve been avoided if they’d repeated our order back to us.

As for the chicken tenders, we were floored when we saw that the $16 price tag got us just three tenders. While the quality was good—crispy, juicy, and flavorful—it’s hard to ignore how overpriced they were. The fries were solid too, but again, the cost-to-portion ratio left us feeling ripped off.

It feels like Scolari’s is taking advantage of being the sole food vendor at Almanac, monopolizing the options on the island. While the food is decent, the pricing is outrageous and lacks value for what you’re getting. At these prices, it’s hard to justify another visit unless they reconsider their portions or pricing.

If you’re planning to order, double-check everything to avoid mix-ups, and prepare your wallet—you’ll need it.

top_reviews.content:
Ben Tre Vietnamese was one of my first meals after moving to San Francisco, and it did not disappoint.

I ordered the 2-Meat Combo Garlic Noodles and the Deluxe Pho (Pho Dac Biet) through Uber Eats. Everything arrived hot, fresh, and packaged really well. The pho had a rich, flavorful broth with generous portions of rare beef, tripe, beef meatballs, and plenty of fresh herbs, bean sprouts, onions, and jalapeños. The garlic noodles were packed with flavor, and the roasted meats were tender and perfectly cooked.

The portions were generous, the ingredients tasted fresh, and it was easy to see why this place has so many loyal customers.

San Francisco has one of the best Asian food scenes in the country, and Ben Tre is a great example of why. If you're looking for authentic Vietnamese food, this is definitely worth trying.

I'll definitely be ordering from here again.

Incredible. The chicken was truly some of the best chicken I've had in the Bay Area across all cuisines. I also loved the pho, pork, and their BBQ beef was nothing short of incredible. I can't wait to come back!!

Also, the location used to be a US Bank before Ben Tre took over and the authentic old bank vault is the centerpiece of the bar. Pretty cool looking aesthetic and the inside is really elegant.

Dim The Way is a daughter and father team. The food was OK. The beef stew lo mein $13 had OK flavors. That sauce they used made it OK. The noodles were too soft. Good lo mein noodles tend to be more chewy and bouncier. The chef cut the beef stew onto smaller than usual pieces. Four were meat pieces and the rest were tendons. The minced pork cheung fun $6.80 was a plain dish. The young daughter waitress will ask if you want chopped green onion with your rice roll. The soy sauce they used weren't the sweet ones normally found at dim sum restaurants. My suggestion is to add more flavor by using a sweet soy sauce with sesame oil to add some aroma to this dish.

Things I loved about Dim The Way are: No annoying music. Food came out fast. Simple menu. Free hot tea was fragrant. Clean. Genuinely nice people. Chef speaks Cantonese and Mandarin. House branded plates. Good job team at Dim The Way.

The rice rolls I got were so so good. The rice roll itself wasn’t too thick, and they gave me a lot of filling. The meal was also huge! You cannot beat the price; I paid less than $10 for my meal. I would definitely come back. The service is also great, and the food was done incredibly quick. Please support them!!

Firetrail Pizza: A Blazing Success at SPARK Social
Firetrail Pizza, nestled within the vibrant SPARK Social food truck park in Mission Bay, San Francisco, has quickly become a local favorite. Their wood-fired pizzas, crafted with fresh, high-quality ingredients, deliver a flavorful punch that's hard to beat.
What to Expect:
* Authentic Napoletna-style: The pizzas are cooked in a traditional wood-fired oven, resulting in a crispy crust with a chewy center.
* Casual Atmosphere: The food truck park setting provides a relaxed and enjoyable dining experience, perfect for a casual outing with friends or family.
Must-Try:
* The Sun dried and BBQ chicken that we tried were delicious
Their other offerings are great too -
* The Meat Lover: A pizza piled high with your favorite meats, perfect for carnivores.
* The Vegetarian: A flavorful medley of roasted vegetables and cheese.
Overall:
Firetrail Pizza is a must-visit for anyone seeking a delicious and satisfying meal in Mission Bay. With its exceptional quality, flavorful toppings, and inviting atmosphere, it's no wonder why this spot has become a local gem.

Another Tuesday (6/17) Giants home game and another food truck to try at Spark Social! Today’s adventure was Firetrail Pizza!
I got the pizza of the day Prosciutto Arugula - the menu shows what’s on it - I wasn’t sure what to expect, when I got it I was like okay that’s a lot of arugula, I needed a fork to help pull the slice out and reload it but it was very well balanced. The lemon dressing was definitely flavorful, the parmesean was really good, paired well with the prosciutto, just wish there was more meat. I ate a slice and took the rest into the game. My buddy got the bbq chicken he ate it all on one sitting. I tried a piece of chicken and it was tasty.
I will say, it travelled surprisingly well, I took Bart home and the box was sideways in my purse, but when I got home and opened the box it was in near perfect condition and I ate my leftovers the next day (removed the arugula before reheating obviously) My total (with Diet Coke) was $25.61 (with small tip). I feel it was more expensive than expected for what I got, but hey, cost of big city food and, however I could have got a slice of Tony’s in the ballpark for cheaper but wouldn’t have had leftovers.

Preferred the mushroom & sausage pizza over the prosciutto, pear & gorgonzola pizza. You could taste both the mushroom & sausage well. It was served hot and didn't take too long to cook. Pizzas are 10" and a good amount of food for one hungry person, $16 each. Is located in an outdoor food park area that has outdoor seating. Although it could get busy at times, it is doable to wear mask and then find a seating location that isn't too crowded, but the whole area has a certain level of back ground music which I felt was just a little louder than I prefer. There are several different seating options in the food park, with casual outdoor dining.
Pizza was delicious. Friendly staff, quick service but please note it’s a Food truck but plenty of seating available next to it.

We finished with the Brown Butter Banana Toast, which was so good with the melting vanilla ice cream. The staff was super friendly and attentive. Such a lovely experience - I’ll definitely be back

Came here with friends and really enjoyed it. The food was fresh, flavorful, and everything looked beautiful when it came to the table.

My favorite was the crispy mushroom appetizer—it was super crispy and went really well with the dipping sauce. The spicy seafood cha cha were also delicious, and the glory salad was fresh with a nice balance of flavors. We ended up ordering dessert too, and it was definitely worth it.

The atmosphere was cozy and relaxing, making it a great spot for a date or a nice meal with friends. I’ll definitely be coming back with my boyfriend next time. Highly recommend!

Great Thai food in a cozy intimate setting.

A lot of thai restaurants tend to shy away from bold flavors and stick with a safe sweet and salty palette. Glom makes a statement with spices, vegetables, and umami reminiscent of street food from Bangkok or Chiangmai. Their Khao Soi is an outstanding example of this.

Another favorite of mine is the morning glory salad — a dish that’s practically impossible to find elsewhere. The crispness of the morning glory combined with the refreshing salad dressing makes it unforgettable.

I’ve been back a few times since their opening and will keep coming back for more! (oh yea, don’t forget to book in advance, the spots fill up fast)

I really loved the crispy fried mushrooms and the glass noodle larb with Chicken this dishe was so fresh, flavorful, and had just the right balance of lime, making them taste bright and refreshing.

The Pla Lui Suan (fried fish with Thai herbs) came with a very generous amount of herbs and toppings. Personally, it was a little too much for me, but I can see why others would enjoy it.

Overall, the food tasted authentically Thai, the service was friendly, and the atmosphere was perfect for a date night. I would definitely come back to try more dishes.
Best Thai food I’ve had! Everything was delicious, full of flavor, and tasted authentic. Great service too. Definitely coming back!

top_reviews.content: The owner is super sweet! Did you know they've been here 20 years? I know what their secret is. It's authentically yummy Vietnamese street style food! Everything from banh mi, fresh spring rolls, boba tea, to crepes. This is my favorite quick stop when I'm in the neighborhood.
Cute snack stop. My person favorites are the fruit smoothies and the egg waffle with red beans, but their crepes are also incredibly crispy and light and their boba is good.

Little hole in the wall Cafe that serves what essentially is asian street food. They have vietnamese sandwiches, Boba drinks,  sweet ginger tofu, crepes, egg buble waffle, and some other sweet and savory offerings.  You can easily find this shop by following the loud techno/club/dance music they play on the speakers.  The workers are really nice and explain what they have to offer and what it is if you don't know.  It can get a bit overwhelming if there are lots of people waiting since the menu is so diverse.  The entire shop looks like someone just crammed lots of signage and decorations in the tiny space to make it look busier and fuller.  I don't even know how the people that work there get behind the counter. Haha.

When we came for a weekend late night snack/dessert run at close to 8:40pm there wasn't too many people but within 5 to 10 minutes more people started to come by to buy stuff.  We ordered a crepe that had fresh mango pieces, ice cream and whip cream;  a crepe with fresh strawberry pieces, ice cream and whip cream; thai iced tea with Boba;  and a warm silken tofu with ginger syrup.  The mango crepe was delicious and not too sweet. The strawberry crepe was too sweet since they used strawberry jam while the mango crepe had a drizzle of mango syrup.  I couldn't taste the Thai ice tea until we got home and ate something salty to counter all that sweet stuff we ate.  I didn't even attempt to try the warm silken tofu since I was eating the crepe and I wouldn't have tasted anything anyways.  We will be back to try the other stuff they have.  Everything looks delicious.

Update 10/15/23. Came here for a little treat because of my son's birthday. We noticed that they had signs advertising 20th anniversary buy 2 get 1 free deal. Honestly I don't remember them being there for 20 years but whatever... We ordered Thai teas, fish curry balls, and bubble egg waffles. The Thai teas were good, the curry balls were pretty flavorful and firm with a bit of chewiness but I had to take them off the stick in order to coat them in the curry sauce at the bottom of the tray. The waffles were hot with a good vanilla flavor. They were crunchy on the outside with a chewy mochi like interior.

Update 3/9/24. Came here for an after dinner treat and got ourselves some crepes. Super yummy as always and friendly owner.  They still have a special buy two get one free deal.  We ordered three crepes, and the third was free.

Hong Kong Donuts fit for Jackie Chan! Not to sweet, makes a Perfect Treat! 😉 😜  Also Awesome Avocado Smootie with Fruit sliced Jellies, ,owner Amazing guy, 20yrs in Business,  children almost out of the nest 🪹 🐦 Small Hole-in-the-Mall shop space.
Awesome Oriental Stored Throughout the 99 Ranch , Upstairs Massage also. Maybe later...

top_reviews.content:
We’ve had regular date nights here since opening, and had our first dinner here after we got engaged. The staff, food, bar, and vibes are always immaculate and exceptional. We just knew that we had to have our wedding here!

We had no idea where to start, considering we were doing this without a planner or coordinator. Mike brought so many ideas to life for us, many of which we didn’t even think of, including custom drinks!

On the day of, Levi took amazing care of our entire party and went above and beyond to make sure we, the bride and groom, had the perfect day.

The kitchen crew is phenomenal. The food was so delicious and all of our guests had something positive to say. Crowd favorite was the kimchi pork belly sliders. The servers and bartenders were incredibly attentive and friendly.

When not eating or drinking, the games, of course were a hit, and everybody loved the Photo Booth. The overall aesthetics here are stunning. I mean, I don’t think I’ve ever seen a prettier bathroom set up in my life, or a more fun secret party room… but overall the craftsmanship of this place is gorgeous, and there’s so many fine little details that I wouldn’t ever have thought of, that make this place so photogenic.

Parking is readily available (and validated) in the blue parking structure attached to the same building.

Wonderful place just for easy date night, catching up with friends, or even for a private event such as a WEDDING!

The drinks are generally so good!! I tried two different types and neither disappoint all the bartenders are super attentive shout out to kammy and levi! I highly recommended as a chill vibe but beautiful bar with delicious drinks!

I’ve been to Golden Eye Social about 5 times now and this review is long overdue. I’ve had a great experience every time. My latest visit was for my birthday and it was a blast. As a baseline, the food and drink are all excellent quality and the darts are incredibly fun for both small and large groups. The staff are also super friendly and professional here. We were able to get two lanes right next to each other so our larger group could stay together. And when there was an issue with one of our lanes starting earlier than intended, we were given some extra play time to make up for it. The staff and the manager (whose name I’ll have to get next time I’m there) really do everything they can to make sure you have a great time. I’ll for sure be coming back.

This place is absolutely amazing. The food is off the hook at the kimchi pork belly sliders, the dirty dog and the smoked trout dip. Mike was our server and bartender off the hook. Lily was an amazing!

Golden Eye Social truly saved the day for NPANA (Northwest Perianesthesia Nursing Association). After another venue unexpectedly canceled our reservation for a work event, we were left scrambling—but their team stepped in without hesitation and turned a stressful situation into something seamless.

They accommodated our group for a private party on short notice and made the entire experience feel intentional and well put together. The space was perfect, the atmosphere was elevated without feeling stiff, and the staff went out of their way to make sure everything ran smoothly.

What stood out most was how supportive and responsive they were throughout the process. It honestly meant a lot to see a business show up the way they did for a group of nurses—people who spend their days taking care of others. That level of understanding and support didn’t go unnoticed.

It made a huge difference for our group, and we were actually able to enjoy the night instead of worrying about logistics. Highly recommend Golden Eye Social for any group event or private gathering—they show up when it matters.

top_reviews.content:
La Esquina Taqueria (located in East Oakland, Ca) is the epitome of a hidden gem Mexican restaurant. If you're craving authentic Mexican cuisine that is simply divine, then this is the place to go. Service is top notch and the ambiance is pretty cool.

We decided to try the Camerones A la Diabla, a regular burrito, sope, and tacos. Let me tell you, they were all absolutely incredible.

The Camerones a la diabla had a delightful freshness to it, with a mouthwatering red sauce. The shrimp was cooked to perfection, and the rice and beans were out of this world.

We indulged in two tacos, one with tender chicken (pollo) and the other with flavorful al pastor pork. Both were heavenly, especially with the combination of onions, cilantro, and salsa.

Trying the sope for the first time was a revelation. The combination of the crispy masa base, onions, tomatoes, and al pastor meat was absolutely heavenly.

As for the burrito, we opted for the asada meat. Our daughters couldn't get enough of the burritos and thoroughly enjoyed them.

This place is truly amazing and a must-visit Mexican restaurant if you find yourself in the Oakland Area.

First time here and I was impressed. Every time I try a New Mexican spot, I always judge based on a simple asada super burrito. It was the perfect tasting burrito. Simple balance of ingredients (not too much rice, beans, etc), The perfect size, and everything held well. Green and red sauce was perfect. Staff took my order and were polite. I decided to eat in the restaurant and the atmosphere here is great and clean. Highly recommend this place
Excellent tacos, and for $3 ea., they are a steal. I will definitely be back next time I’m in the neighborhood.

Food is fantastic. They were very kind and accommodating of our dietary restrictions and let me put a bunch of stuff on the side so I could share my food with my partner. Portions were quite generous. I got an egg burrito for about $15 that I will be finishing tomorrow for lunch. I hope more people visit this place!

Atmosphere is a 3 just because it's a bit dark inside. They have one table outside so we ate there.

I am really picky about my taquerias. I like that they’re not flashy, are great at what they do, and charge a reasonable price consistent with their amazing food quality.

My philosophy is that restaurants should serve what they think is excellent, not what you expect. These guys deliver both. Plenty of appropriate sides, excellent salsa, amazing homemade tortillas, and personal service.

If this was in LA, it would compete with the likes of Leo’s tacos, Sonoratown , and Yucas.

We came to check this place out after seeing it on Instagram. We were drawn by the aesthetics and the energy that was presented. If you are looking for a place for kids and want some wine and ice cream then this place might be for you. Otherwise this place is disappointing.

The look of the place is fun and wild. There was definitely a vision for this place and it made it fun. Atmosphere wise.. it was a mess. We came around 8-8:30pm and there were kids and their parents running and screaming everywhere. There wasn’t much seating as families took up the tables. If that isn’t your vibe don’t come here. We tried their “boujee nachos” which were $27!! Nothing boujee about it. A complete ripoff. Cheap ingredients, small portions, and the meat was cold. The pretzel bites were no better.

We had our daughter’s 9th birthday party here, and it was like a fever dream in the best way possible!  The decor is over the top, girly-pop. Daisy and her staff made everything completely turnkey for us; handling all the planning of plentiful food & cute drinks, down to the optional gift bags & slime activity.

Thank you Ruby Lou's team for making this such a memorable and easy birthday party for us to enjoy!  added pics from when toured the space.

We had such a fun time at RubyLou's! Walking in honestly felt like stepping into a girly, pink, magical version of Disneyland. The decor is absolutely amazing -- every corner is picture-worthy and so thoughtfully designed. It's such a fun spot for photos and just soaking in the vibe.

The claw machines were a blast, and the ice cream was super fun too. It really feels like an experience, not just a place to eat.

We've heard they're working on expanding and improving their unique cocktail menu so stay tuned and perhaps stick to the wine and beer for the time being.

That said, it's such a unique and exciting spot that we'll definitely be back once it's been running a little more smoothly. Overall, such a cute and magical place to visit! Daisy the owner is an absolute gem!

After reading a couple of recent reviews, I felt like I had to share my experience, because it was completely different.
Ruby Lou’s is amazing. The vibe is colorful, upbeat, and genuinely fun without feeling out of control. It’s lively in the best way, and the whole concept feels creative and well thought out.
The owner was there and was incredibly welcoming, and the staff was friendly, attentive, and on top of everything. You can tell there’s real care behind what’s being built there.
We had a great time, the energy felt positive, and everything felt organized and intentional.
I’d encourage people to experience it for themselves instead of relying on a few opinions. We’ll absolutely be back.

Wow, what a fun and welcoming place! I attended a birthday party here today, and our group had a great experience. The ambiance is playful and the staff made sure we were all taken care of. This place needs a "current review".
Like many I had a break between appointments and was starving.
While I was reading the menu a fellow pointed out the "3 Tacos for $7.00" and showed me how big they were. Well folks, he was not kidding. They were huge, hot, overstuffed with goodness (not skimping on meat at all) simple w/onions, cilantro and I added a bit of sour cream and cheese. $3.00 more. Though they were not hot enough to melt the cheese (which I may skip next time) they were delicious. I could only eat 2 and saved 1 for dinner. Double shells and now I see why. 1 shell would not have been able to handle all this goodness.
I had 2 separate porks and 1 chicken.
They required 2 hands, a fork and multiple napkins.
Service was fast and with a smile.
While the other places had huge lines (think Panda Express) this place was moving right along.
Heck I may even take the bus up there on my day off to have a repeat of this delicious meal. More than satisfying and all for under $10.
Try it, I believe you will like it, especially the tacos.

I work at UCSF and Carmelita's is located next door inside the food court. My coworkers love this place and it never disappoints. This was my second time ordering from here in the last couple of years. It serves fresh food (think quesadillas, burritos, tacos and a la carte plates. As long as the lines get here, the flow moves really fast so you're not really waiting long. Price points are between $8-14.

Today, I got the shrimp quesadilla with sour cream, guacamole and Pico de Gallo on the side. It was so DAMN good.... the portions are big enough that I split it between two meals. The food was soooooo good! The bread for the sandwich was so delicious and the empanada dough also! Made fresh in house and you can tell!!! And the blue corn drink was unique and delish!

top_reviews.content: I believe the restaurant's catch phrase is "one bute, so juicy" and they're right. This place was delicious; they had a such a wide variety of dumplings, skewers, salad, and traditional Chinese dishes. We got a little bit of everything and it was all so tasty. We got seaweed salad, 1 beef skewer (lol), shrimp leek and egg dumplings, pan fried juicy pork buns (they're like the ones you take a bite out of and the juice shoots out), and the fried glutinous rice with brown sugar.

Our second time at this newly opened dumpling restaurant  at Berkeley.  We tried mostly the stir fry dishes during our first visit and mostly dumplings during our second visit. Both times were very delicious!

Handmade boas, wontons and dumplings with a variety of fillings of pork, fish, vegetables and available with steamed, water boiled and pan fried.  Frozen dumplings are also available to take home.  The handmade wrapper was very good and the mini pan fried boas were fantastic!

In addition, they served various noodles and rice noodles, authentic dry pots, skewed meats, Hunan as well as Northern and Southern Chinese cuisines.

The price is reasonable and the portion generous.  Both times we had enough tasty leftovers for another meal at home.

Dumpling Day would be our new go-to Chinese restaurant when we visit Berkeley!

Wonderful service! Food was 10/10. I tried the pork xiao long bao, mini pan fried pork bun, and the special sauce with beef and shrimp chow mein.

I didn’t get a picture of everything, but was able to split everything between the two of us. I spent $50 and left feeling very satisfied. No complaints!
Amazing food - so fresh and delish! They make the dumplings right there where you can see them. Excellent service! Must go to for fresh dumplings

Had an amazing dinner at Dumpling Day in Berkeley! Despite the name, this place serves much more than dumplings — authentic Sichuan and Hunan dishes plus barbecue, and everything we ordered was packed with bold, mouthwatering flavor.
We had the tea tree mushrooms — savory, smoky, and loaded with chilies and Sichuan peppercorns. The mushrooms had the perfect texture. We also got the lotus root, which was fresh and crisp, along with several other dishes that all came out hot, fragrant, and beautifully spicy. If you love real, fiery Sichuan and Hunan cooking, this is the place. Generous portions, great for sharing with a group. We'll definitely be back!

Anh Hong holds a special place in San Francisco’s food scene — and in my heart? I can say it’s the best Vietnamese restaurant! With over 30 years of history (originally on Geary Street in the Tenderloin), this Vietnamese gem is now nestled in the Outer Richmond.

What keeps me coming back is their warm hospitality and fresh, flavorful dishes. I especially love the DIY spring rolls — there’s something so fun and satisfying about assembling your own with fresh herbs, vermicelli, and grilled meats (lamb chops, beef rolls, sausages )or shrimp. One of my favorites is the Grilled Shrimp on Sugarcane (Chạo Tôm) — juicy, sweet, and perfectly grilled.

top_reviews.content: The best vegan dim sum in SF. Everything is delicious! I order too many things for takeout every quarter or so. There’s takeout/delivery on the Imperial Garden Seafood App but also on Uber Eats. I’m glad this is in an accessible spot but I wish they were available for more hours!

Amazing! Highly highly recommend you come here. Everything was vegan - loved everything we got: siu mai, xiao long bao, beef rice noodles, and porc bun (not pictured but was my favorite). We will be back!

We love the variety of options for vegan dim sum, we ordered 9 dishes. The only dish I did not enjoy was the bao, it is slimey inside, I'll stick to Loving Hut for that dish. I wish the eggless tarts and baked bbq were available, we'd have ordered those too. Only took off a star for service because it took awhile to get our bill and a lot of smoke was coming into the restaurant, we were in the farthest corner away from door but the smoke was still very strong.
Faves were pan fried porc bun, pan fried noodles with mushroom, shu mai and so many more. Will definitely be back to try more of the menu!!

Love, love, love this place! Wish I could come more often, but vegan dim sum/yum cha is a very special occasion. As a young vegetarian->vegan, going out to eat with my mom and friends meant generally only having a handful of choices, that almost always being Buddha's delight, or gai lan, steamed veggies, with plain rice. Sassy Foods has brought me back to my childhood with delights I haven't had in years, but my omni friends and family have agreed that it still tastes great, and has the spirit of authentic dim sum in each dish. One time, we even got these pear-shaped things and my mom said she hardly sees them outside of HK.

Pictured and thoughts upon...

Lo mai gai/sticky rice: The gold flake makes this feel so fancy and elevated. This was my absolute favorite dim sum morsel hands down as a kid, pre-veg. And this vegan lo mai gai is cooked just right, when steamed in the lotus leaf it becomes a very aromatic and unique flavor. I just wish it had some vegan yolk of sorts, because that is the best part, but very hard to replicate.

Har gow/shrimp dumplings:
The yellow wrapper has a nice chewy quality to it, a little thicker than I remember har gow to be, but this balances well with the vegan shrimp. There is a gentle flavor here that is captured very well, but I will admit myself, this one tastes the most obviously vegan. I like that because I'm vegan, but if you're hesitant on mock meats, this may not be the one for you.

Chiu chow dumplings/peanut chive:
The purple wrapper is super cute! These ones did not survive for a picture, but they are the most beautiful cute things ever. Taste wise, very fresh while still savory. The texture is very interesting, crunchy and soft at the same time.

Siu mai/pork dumplings:
I love these but my mom thinks they're salty.

Cheung fun/rice noodle roll: these are a must have! There are different filling options for whatever suits your preferences. We got the Chinese donut one this time but other ones we tried before have been great too.

Xiao long bao/soup dumplings: Not the restaurants fault I burnt my tongue, too delicious to not let it continue to burn my tongue further. Worth every second of flavor. Nice thin wrapper, good amount of soup, and the filling wasn't mushy.

Taro cake: I LOVE when taro cake is prepared this way! This is not a sweet dish! Have it with chili oil and a splash of soy, or use any extra rice noodle roll sauce.

Everything I've tried here is delicious, the level of "dim sum theatre" here is just right in my humble AB-half-C opinion. No frills, but you'll get what you want hot and fresh, you just have to know how to order.

I really wish they had the egg tarts a little more available, as I've been here a handful of times but they've been sold out/not available every time. No free red bean soup either but it's okay because we never have room after all the delicious stuff!

I came here on a Thursday evening with a party of 3. We added our name to the waitlist at around 8 p.m. and had an estimated wait time of 20-25 minutes. We stood outside and waited and got the text message at 8:30 p.m. that our table was ready. Upon showing one of the servers the text message, he told us that it would be another 10-15 minutes before we would get seated. We waited until 8:50 p.m. before we got seated.

Even though we were ready to order within minutes of being seated, the servers never came by until we finally asked if we could still order. It was 9 p.m. by the time we were able to order our food.

We ordered the following:
2x Braised Beef Noodle Soup non-spicy
1x Braised Beef Noodle Soup mild spicy
1x Popcorn Chicken w/ house mala cream sauce

All the food came out at different times, was lukewarm, and the server who took our order even forgot the mild spicy bowl of Braised Beef Noodle Soup. It wasn’t until much later when we had to tell them that we were still missing one bowl of Noodle Soup that one of the servers went to the kitchen and came back with it, and it was still made wrong.

I would describe the Braised Beef Noodle Soup as bland and salty. The soup base looked and tasted like Chinese soy sauce mixed with water. The noodle texture was very flat and mushy, it wasn’t chewy at all. The mild spicy Braised Beef Noodle Soup came with 5 huge globs of mala spice, and it was so spicy and overdone that it tasted disgustingly spicy and salty. You couldn’t taste anything else from it, and the heavy amount of mala spice ruined the dish. The Popcorn Chicken was also very bland and underseasoned, and the house mala sauce it came with was alright, nothing special.

Overall, this place was a HUGE disappointment, and the long wait time was not worth it. I would not recommend this place at all. The only reason I’m giving it 2 stars instead of 1 is because the servers were apologetic towards us.

top_reviews.content:
Google declared them some of the best garlic noodles in San Francisco. The internet rarely agrees on anything these days, so that alone was enough to make me curious. ;)

So on a lazy sunny Sunday afternoon, my friend Liza and I finally drove over to the truck to investigate. It’s located at Spark Social SF, a food truck park in the Mission Bay, and it’s a fun casual place to meet friends, grab a drink and eat food especially in a beautiful sunny SF day.

Ok so I’m happy to report, the internet fans were not exaggerating!

The noodles somehow manage to be rich without being heavy, garlicky without punching you in the face, buttery, savory, and just… ridiculously satisfying. The parmesan is the perfect finishing touch, and before you know it, you’re twirling another forkful while pretending you’re just “having one more bite.”

We also ordered the fried shrimp, fish, mac salad, and slaw because apparently we believe in thorough research! lol The nicely crispy shrimp disappeared first (always a good sign), the fish was also beautifully crisp, and the slaw was fresh enough to make us feel marginally virtuous.

It wasn’t until afterward that I learned the chef, Rudy Mihal, had lived and worked in Italy and had also cooked in some seriously respected kitchens, including Gramercy Tavern in New York. Suddenly, those garlic noodles made even more sense. They have that rare quality of feeling both deeply comforting and incredibly well executed. Nothing flashy. Just someone who clearly knows exactly what they’re doing.

The garlic noodles are famous for a reason, and I can’t wait to come back for more!

Food was absolutely amazing! The chicken was big and juicy, perfect crispiness and perfectly cooked!

There’s plenty of options near the area but no need to look around. Just go straight here and you won’t regret it

I stopped by WH42 food truck while watching a world cup soccer match at spark social. I ordered the wings and fries and the garlic noodles and shrimp.

The wings had a nice crisp and amazing flavor. It wa a sweet and spicy sticky sauce that mixed well with the chicken. The fries stayed crispy and never went soggy. Which I liked.

The shrimp was really good. Lightly breaded with a hint of garlic, but the star of the show had to be the garlic noodles. Nice thick noodles, parmesan cheese, and a delicious sauce that coated the noodles well.

I can't wait to come back.

WOW! My taste buds are in heaven!
I’d heard the food at WH42 in SPARK Social SF, Mission Bay, was good, but it exceeded every expectation. The tuna, shrimp, and garlic noodles were outstanding, and the garlic noodles were so good I had to order another portion to take home.
If you’re in the area, don’t miss this place. Highly recommended!

Hands down best garlic noodles I ever had. Tried other places in the city like crustaceans and Thanh long, PPQ, and they’re good, but not THIS GOOD. And the chicken wings, they give San Tung a real run for their money because these wings are SOOOOO GOOD. Coming from a food truck, you’re getting a 5 star restaurant meal right in front of you. It makes my review seem crazy when All these big names come into play but all I can say is go try it for yourself. You’ll be leaving the same review I am. Great job WH42, you’re now my go to spot even for a date night !

I've passed by this spot many times during my lunch walks and finally got a chance to try it! I usually get Guilin rice noodles from other places in the area, so I was excited to see another option.

I ordered the A1 House Special Pot-Roasted Guilin Rice Noodles with marinated beef, beef tripe, and crispy pork. I really enjoyed it, the flavors were great, the portion size was generous (I could probably split it into two meals), and the price was very affordable.

The only downside is that the dish was a bit greasy, but I appreciated the bowl of clear broth they provided to balance it out.

An acquired taste that diverges from the standard Chinese-American kitchen, Guilin Rice Noodles serves authentic dry noodle, noodle soups and side dishes.

Hot and Sour Guilin Rice Noodles sings of spiciness and a taste of fermentation from pickled vegetables. A healthy, and refreshing option especially when in need of a hangover cure. Liver and intestine toppings for those more adventurous. Smoked peanuts make for a wonderfully savory topping.

Open from breakfast to dinner times in Oakland Chinatown.

It was my first time trying this classic guilin dish. The crispy pork and beef tripe toppings were my favorite. I wish they added more pickled green beans, as they added a nice refreshing taste.

1 portion doesn't look big but it's actually quite filling. I couldn't finish all the noodles. The meal came with a complimentary drink. I asked what it was and it turned out to be a monk fruit drink - very interesting sweetness that only hits you after swallowing, with a slight medicinal lingering taste. I'm not used to that flavor, but it was very interesting to try.

My hubby ordered A1 dry noodle and I ordered B2, hot and sour noodle soup. It was definitely very hot (temperature hot) and sour from the bamboo shoots. We both enjoyed our food, but what I'm still thinking about is the sauteed lettuce with garlic sauce. It sounds so simple, but absolutely delicious - I ended up scarfing it down.

As someone from Guilin working far away from home, tasting such authentic flavors here literally brought tears to my eyes. I swear my "Guilin rice noodle DNA" has taken full control of me because I come here at least once a week!

⚠️ Just a quick heads-up for everyone: For some reason, the operating hours listed on Google Maps are incorrect. They are actually only closed on Tuesdays. Keep this in mind so you don't make a wasted trip. Highly recommended!

top_reviews.content: Everything tasted fresh here. Friendly staff Khanh explained the ingredients and differences in their Vietnamese cuisine. Mon Superette is a wonderful vignette into Vietnamese cuisine in the format of a charming convini-styled restaurant where you can get great quality and delicious food to-go or even enjoy in the window-side nook if you’re lucky to be in the area. The crab sandwiches are divine as they’re crispy, have great fresh flavor, and the bread is perfectly fluffy. Also, the owner Khánh was so informative and engaging as she shared the ethnic roots of her family’s cooking behind the food. Of particular note, if you have been to Japan and have enjoyed the wonders of the aforementioned convini-lifestyle (or other Asian countries for that matter) then you will be pleased to know these egg sandwiches are probably the best American option I’ve had to this date. They’re wonderfully light and have that perfect egg-to-mayo ratio that I’ve missed since returning from Tokyo. Apparently Khánh brought together the influence of having lived in Japan to this setup and it’s such a refreshing take on grab-and-go eateries. The garlic noodles and vermicelli salad (Bún) are must haves. Seriously. You need to try these. I think this is probably my favorite garlic noodles to date as they’re not overpowering or oily but just perfectly balanced for that satisfying savory flavor. They have hot food options in addition to the cold fridge grab-and-go so if you’re there, try everything out. I know I have enjoyed it and will be back to do just that.

Really love this place! The fried banana has me in a chokehold. I crave it weekly and it’s reminiscent of something you’d eat at a night market is SE Asia.

This now "corporate" chain is a far cry from it's humble beginnings. The portions have been significantly reduced, and I expect more for a $15 sando. I can hit other places for less $ and a better offering.

There are two things/"policies" that don't sit well with me: 1) they have no paper menus to take away. I'm sure the are being environmentally conscientious (they COULD use recycled paper) or they mistakenly assume that EC's older population is tech savvy enough to deal. 2) I paid cash, and did not have any $1 bills to use for the tipping bucket. I asked to change a $5,and was flatly told "we don't give change". Shocked, I begrudgingly dropped a $5 in the bucket.

These may seem like trivial things, but to me seem like a lack of customer focus.

top_reviews.content:
I stopped by Primavera at the Embarcadero Ferry Building Farmers Market (weekend 4/25 menu) and tried the chilaquiles, beef flautas, and pork tamales.

It’s honestly not an exaggeration to say these were the best chilaquiles I’ve ever had and I grew up in LA. The salsa had so many layers of flavor, and the texture hit that perfect balance of crispy and slightly softened. Easily a 10/10.

The beef flautas were also excellent. The escabeche was well balanced, not too sour or spicy, and adding their homemade salsa really took it to the next level.

The pork tamale was good, though a bit on the dry side. To be fair, I ordered close to closing time, so that may have affected it.

Overall, this is a must try spot when visiting the Ferry Building Farmers Market.

The queue started forming after I got my food (see photo), so you want to get there early if you don't want to spend time in the queue. The purple hibiscus drink is pretty intense for me. It tastes more like syrup than a drink. Fortunately I bought some bottles of plain water along and diluted it with a 1 to 1 ratio and it was so much better.

My favorite Mexican joint in a city overflowing with delicious MX food.  I loved the Shrimp and Snapper Ceviche Tostadas, the Bohemian Beer Battered Fish Tacos, the Chilaquiles “Verdes,” the Chilaquiles “Merida,” and the Tamales Plate (I got one Maurilia Pork Tamale and one Butternut Squash and Cheese Tamale).  Later I tried the Tamales Plate with one Chicken Mole Tamale and one Tamale Brazo de Reina (with chard pumpkinseed pesto, eggs, and salsa habanero).  These were also good, but the first two tamales were best.  My favorite item of all time might be the Niman Ranch Beef Brisket Tacos Quesabirria.  The only items I have not liked as much were the Crispy Chicken Tacos with Guacamole, which were flavorful but dry, and the Crispy Shrimp Tacos, which were tasty but skimped on the shrimp.  Service is competent and efficient.  Portions are generous.  Bring a healthy appetite.

The Phad Kee Mao was so so. Lacking the overall flavor of what it should taste like and I prefer fried noodles to have some smoky taste to it when it is cooked at high heat.

Param sauce was flavorful, and the steamed vegetables had a good variety to it. The downside of it was that the meat (pork) was on the not so tender side and a little overcooked.

Mekong absolutely delivered an incredible dining experience for our family! We shared a few dishes, and every single one was a hit. The sticky wings were delicious—definitely get a side of sticky rice to soak up every last drop of that amazing sauce. The salt & pepper wings had the perfect crunch, and the curry puffs were so flaky and flavorful. I always get a side of peanut sauce with them (because that’s the best way to eat them—unless you’re allergic, of course!).

Now, let’s talk about the nam khao—hands down, the best I’ve ever had. Every bite was crispy, tangy, and full of flavor. And even though we almost skipped the mango sticky rice (thinking mango was out of season), we are so glad we ordered it. The mango was perfectly ripe, sweet, and juicy—pure dessert bliss!

The drinks were just as fantastic. I’m a huge hibiscus fan, so I had to try their hibiscus drink—it was slightly sweet, slightly bitter, and absolutely delicious. Their Thai coffee was also incredible—rich, smooth, and just the right amount of sweet.

To top it all off, the service was exceptional. Our server was so sweet, fun to talk to, and made our experience even better. Oh, and if you love a good deal, their happy hour from 5 to 7 is amazing—20% off selected dishes and BOGO on selected drinks!

Overall, this dinner was a total success. We had a great time enjoying incredible food together, and we’ll definitely be back for more!

Had a wonderful lunch here. The medium heat chicken larb is perfectly executed: spices well balanced, meat perfectly seasoned and cooked with cold lettuce and cucumber slices that provide a good contrast against the building heat from chilis. A little tingle to the mouth for about 20 minutes after the meal.

Service was prompt, polite and attentive.

The atmosphere of the space is very nice, tables are well set with all the things you need from cutlery to hot sauces and tamarind dry powder
Every dish we tried was full of flavor and served hot/fresh! Cannot wait to go back and try more dishes 🤤

New spot and it’s so good! Their grilled pork is amazing and very tender. Perfect in the broken rice plates and vermicelli bowls. Will definitely be a regular here!

Best pho tai I have had in a long time.  (<  That was my sincere original review in the dining room.)  EDIT:  I ordered take out today, $100+ order. Completely opposite from the dining room experience. All I can say was that what we received was insulting.  They put broccoli in pho ga (unforgivable), and I could detect only two microscopic slivers of onion in it.  They ignored my noodle choice.  The Bun Bo Hue was not that at all.  There was no sate, no shrimp paste, not seasoned.  The egg meatloaf (chả trứng hấp) was dry, hard, salty, and colorless.  We threw it out.  There was an OK banh mi. Had a great bowl of pho to start the day the other day. The pho broth has a nice complex flavor- I could taste a good amount of star anise in the bowl and I was a fan of the wonderful plate of garnishes. The thai basil in particular was so happy and fresh, whoever they get it from take a lot of care of these plants! The serving size was excellent I felt happily full and enjoyed this bowl quite a bit.

Came in to pick up a couple banh mis to-go for lunch and I am so glad I did. GF ordered the BBQ Pork and I ordered the BBQ Chicken with extra pate. These were some of the best banh mis I've had in Oakland. The proteins on both sandwiches were so flavorful and juicy. These sandwiches may cost a few dollars more than some of the other spots around here but you're paying for quality and generous portions. Staff was really nice and helpful too. I will definitely be back soon.

top_reviews.content: I've seen the truck while coming out of the gym. We're so glad we stopped by. We only ordered tacos and my favorites from best to good go: 1) Asada, 2) cabeza, 3) Chorizo, 4) Al pastor. It's all flavorful and distinct. Next time I'll have a chorizo burrito, Asada quesadilla, and more cabeza tacos. Pro tip: ask for the extra spicy salsa.

Great Taco truck. Had burrito El pastor with everything - rice, pinto beans, onions, cilantro, sour cream, salsa. Delicious. Can eat it while holding in one hand. Next time I probably order no sour cream and add avocado, it was a little too wet for me.

Warning: This is a taco truck located in Oakland. Please do not leave your car unattended, as there’s a high risk of break-ins in the area.

That said, Tacos El Melón is absolutely worth a visit for their awesome tacos and burritos! We tried the carne asada burrito, and it was fantastic—the meat was flavorful, tender, and they didn’t skimp on it (unlike other places that overload with rice and beans). The salsas were excellent, adding the perfect kick to every bite. On top of that, the people running the truck are super nice and make the experience even better. Highly recommend this spot for authentic and satisfying Mexican food—just take precautions with your vehicle!

The food and service here was fire!!!! We visited SF for the week (i know this isn't actually located in SF but still) it was the best food we ate. Everything else we ate during our trip seemed touristied-up and not truly authentic and/original. I just wished I didn't have to eat it in my car. I would had been content sitting on public benches. SO good. We’re back in the area for a short visit and oh my how we missed the Bay Area Mexican tacos and burritos. Tacos El Melón was so delicious and they were extremely friendly. Muchas gracias!!

top_reviews.content:
The staffs were nice. We were greeted and offered seats right away.

What we ordered:

Donkatsu- The pork was good and portion was good for the price.

Pork Belly BBQ- It was a tab dry and a bit bland. Wasn’t my favorite.

Would come again if I’m in the area and try something different.

I have been a dedicated regular at both Tang Jib (formerly Korean BBQ Bowl) and Ohgane in Alameda since April 2006, dining at both establishments at least once a week for two decades. Over the years, I have left numerous positive reviews, but the steep decline in food quality, kitchen execution, and staff morale across both locations can no longer be ignored. Both restaurants are suffering from a severe lack of hands-on leadership. The current manager, who previously ran the much smaller Spoon restaurant in Berkeley, is entirely out of his depth. Running high-volume restaurants requires a floor presence and attention to service details, yet he remains hidden in the office. Without active supervision, staff morale is low, and kitchen training has evaporated. The food has devolved from exceptional to barely edible and wildly inconsistent. At Tang Jib, a recent seafood pancake came out burnt, greasy with old oil, and entirely disintegrated on the plate. To make matters worse, after sending it back, the kitchen kept me waiting for 30 minutes before the waitress admitted they simply couldn't prepare it any better. At both locations, staple dishes like Galbitang fluctuate wildly—rubbery and impossible to cut on one day, and perfectly tender on another. When confronted with tough meat, management's solution was to hand me a pair of scissors and claim "that's just how it's cooked. Owners Micha and Michael Oh need to take immediate action. Both Tang Jib and Ohgane urgently need a replacement of the uncommunicative kitchen staff and the hiring of experienced, visible floor managers who understand high-volume hospitality.

I always come here whenever I feel eating Korean food. My favorite here is the cold noodles which I always excited about. I hope they keep this on their menu! It might look weird eating cold noodles, but it is the most delicious soup that I had. When it comes to service, some of server aren’t approachable, how they approach me doesn’t feel welcoming for me. They tend to ignore me most of the time because I usually eat alone. I don’t really mind but it still nice if server is a bit friendly to customers. Overall, food is the best 100/10 always.

Tried Tang Jip recently with my girlfriend and honestly… the food was pretty good. Everything came out hot and flavorful, and you can tell it’s made fresh. The soups hit, the meat was cooked perfectly, and the banchan kept the table interesting the whole time. Definitely one of those spots where you leave full and happy.

The vibe inside is nice too. Clean, cozy, not crazy loud, you can actually enjoy your meal and have a conversation. Love the lighting they have up on the ceiling.

Customer service was great. Super friendly and attentive without being over the top.

Restrooms were okay, one door stall toilet and a shared sink.

Also the bar didn’t seem fully up and running when we went, so drink options were a little limited. Not a huge deal though. Still got a soju

Overall, really solid experience. I’d definitely come back.

top_reviews.content: I took food to go. Huge portions of tandoori chicken, a large portion of rice, delicious flatbread. Tandoori chicken takes 30 minutes!!

But when we were told the tandoori chicken takes 30 minutes, we suddenly got really busy! So, what should we order instead?? After asking around, we ended up ordering a few things, but two of them were a miss...
If you really want the tandoori chicken, just order it! The other dishes don't come out that quickly either!

I do not think it's safe to eat from this establishment when you have to worry about eating metal. If I didn't happen to feel it in my mouth, I would've swallowed it or cut my gums. We had to throw the rest of the food out as we didn't want to risk eating metal.

We did takeout for dinner and it was overall pretty good.
We didn’t do the Curry Pizza which seems to be their specialty, but we had a mix of curries and rice. They were generous with the portions, however everything was spicy

Beware of the owners of this restaurant. Their old Five Rivers Indian Cuisine location in Westlake Shopping Center was forced to close by the landlord because of long term rodent infestation issues. That stated, my food orders from Five Rivers Indian Cuisine have been delicious. With only one order that had a piece of steel wire inside an order of naan . Guessing that steel wire thread was used to kleen the cooking equipment the naan is made on. But was missed during the cleaning. Otherwise Five Rivers Indian Cuisine has been very good.

Don't expect outstanding service here. But it's solid and relatively quick if you are eating in or taking out.

Suggest giving them a try.

top_reviews.content: At around 8pm, there aren't a lot of choices for Korean food. My urge for some Korean tofu soup brought me to Kukje Market Restaurant. My order was the #3, soft tofu soup combo, beef, clams and shrimps $20. This was a small soup served on boiling hot stoneware. It took about 15 minutes of waiting before I was able to enjoy this without burning my mouth.  The highlight for me was the little Korean banchan side dishes and how it goes well with the bowl of rice. In terms of service, the waiter was more interested in talking to his co-workers and doom scrolling on his phone as it was the end of the day. At least the food came out fast.

I have been a many times, usually when I am craving for some Korean food or just want something easy. It is located at the right side when you enter the supermarket, most of the times there is not a wait. Their menu consists of appetizers, authentic Korean dishes, specialty wings, soups, beverages, etc. I have never encountered an issue here thanks to their welcoming, well trained and understanding staffs. Everything is pretty much made to order which is always a plus for me and I never mind the wait since I am a very patient person. I recommend this place to anyone looking for a Korean spot, if you want to try something new or if you want a laid back spot to dine at. I definitely will be back to tryout the other delicious options they have to offer.

I've been going here for years, and I'm happy to report that nothing much has changed.  I think nowadays we mostly just do take-out and eat at home.  While we wait, we do some shopping.  Depending on what you order, some things are pricy, so we only come here occasionally.  This time around, I ate here with my family.
Once you walk in, you're seated right away.  It doesn't really give a welcoming vibe, but it's pretty chill.  They have plenty of seating, and it's minimally decorated.  If you look to your left, you can see some people prepping the grab and go lunches/meals in the store.  The food is always made fresh and made to order,  so be patient.  They bring everything out as it's done.  They also provide you with hot tea right away.

We ordered:

1.  Lunch kal bi - May seem pricey, but I feel it's standard for any Korean restaurant.  It comes out sizzling when they place it on the table.  The meat was very tender and flavorful.  It comes with a scoop of rice and 4 side dishes.

2.  Pork soft tofu - This is one of my brothers' go-to dishes.  It is nice and hot during this cold winter morning we've been having.  Place the raw egg on top, and it cooks right away.  Vey good comfort food.

3.  Sushi regular - The sushi was fresh and rice perfectly cooked.   I loved the variety they provide as well.

4.  Original mixed chicken wings - I think you can't go here without ordering it.   This time around, we ordered mixed, which is wings, drumettes, and boneless.  This takes a little while. It was the last to arrive, actually.  It was definitely piping hot, cooked perfectly, and so crunchy.

5. Kimchi fried rice - I ordered this to go for my husband, and it was a huge portion.  It had the perfect amount of spice that just kept you wanting to eat more.

Overall, it was a good experience.  We beat the lunch rush, so it was pretty quiet.

This place is inside the Korean market. Limited parking and limited pay street parking. Cleanness is about average. Seats are also limited maybe about 10 tables.
Foods:
Side dishes are good and good favor, but very small portions, no refill or have to pay extra for refills.
Tofu soup: ordered combination tofu soup but it's a little plain and it's not hot enough to cook the raw egg. Fish egg one is flavorful and good temperature. I would say tofu soups are 3.5 stars.
Delicious Korean restaurant tucked inside a Korean supermarket. Fast, friendly service and reasonably priced. Everything we’ve tried is great! Our go-to Korean spot.

👎Chicken Tenders - Bburinkle :  Crispy, definity, crispy to almost dry, as tenders are all white meat. Not much flavor with this bburinkle by itself, you must pay extra for a dip to make it tasty.

😑Their slogan is "Tasty, Crispy, Juicy" ... unfortunately 2 out of these 3 selling points are not the case for these white meat chicken tenders. Not tasty, not juicy. Disappointing.

🆗️Cheese Balls : Deep fried,  crispy mochi dough filled with melted cheese. However, especially jalapeño cheese poppers lovers be aware, these cheese tastes sweet, kind of like those in a cheese danish. It's just funky...

📌Chicken wings have to be way better, otherwise Idk how their high ratings come from... unless people trust social media influencers...

My friend who just came back from Seoul said the menu here is truncated. It is missing some flavors and the whole chicken option. The chicken here is good and we enjoyed it. The batter wasn't thick like Bonchon's. The hot Bburinkle is better than the regular Bburinkle flavor because we like hot wings. If you are dining in, they don't have plates. The guy did give me an extra empty box for me to put the bones in. When we went at 6:20pm, there was a horde of people waiting. Wait was 20 minutes. They could benefit from a better pick-up system. google.name: Thai Power Restaurant
google.address: 6057 Mission St #2007, Daly City, CA 94014, United States
google.description: Straightforward, informal spot for traditional Thai & Asian dishes, with karaoke & late-night eats.

top_reviews.content: Let's put it this way, you might be walking down the street thinking to yourself "I need a drink and also I want karaoke, but every place is packed." Well fret not, friend. Thai power will not be packed. And it WILL have karaoke. And it will be amazing.

This restaurant is misrepresenting themselves and overcharging customers.

To All the potential people wanting to eat at this restaurant: Beware:

My husband and I came to this restaurant on 3/3/16 around 8 pm. We used Google search to find a Thai Restaurant close to where my husband works, and found the restaurant Thai Power.

When we arrived, we noticed they had Karaoke and it was very loud. We noticed the restaurant was filled with patrons. When we sat down, we waited a long time to get serviced, but no one really came to our table. I had to go to the bar to ask for menus. The lady behind the bar gave us 2 menus and we went back to our table. As I looked at the menu, I noticed that it was Filipino food and some of the menu was in the language of Tagalog. I got up to give the menus back to the bartender, and explained that I thought this was a Thai Restaurant, and that I wanted Thai Menus. She took the menus back and gave us 2 different menus and this time, they were in English and it was Thai food. Here is where we have problems with this whole situation.

After the female bartender gave me the menus, she immediately said, "I want to let you know that these menus (Thai) are old. We don't have the ability to make some of the items on this menu and the prices are incorrect. We haven't received the new menus yet, but we will have to charge you at least $1 or more more for any of the items that you order providing you order something that we make"

I was surprised to actually hear this from her. I went back to the table with my husband, and we made a decision not to eat in the restaurant anymore. We gave the menus back and we walked out.

I feel that we should have not been treated this way.

Although we don't have a problem with Filipinos or their food, it is not why we came to the restaurant, to eat Filipino food. If you give a Thai menu, the restaurant should be cooking all of the Thai Food in addition to Filipino food.

Finally, we should feel welcome in the restaurant and not be told that we have to pay $1 more per item because the menus are old.

Please note***
Other people have written poor reviews similar to ours in Yelp Revews

very expensive and not very good customer service. There were no customers dining in and my wife and I still had to wait 30 min for our food. A tofu pad thai cost the same as a shrimp. One bottle of Corona cost 6.00. Save your money and go to a better Thai Dine in.

You have to understand what "Thai Power" is really all about and yes, I realize, it is a bit confusing. Thai Power is owned by a Thai lady. The exterior is Thai. It nominally serves Thai food (IMO the Tom Yum is the best Thai dish on the menu). Yes, the prices on the menu are outdated. Inside, however, it is a Thai owned establishment with a primarily Filipino clientele. They don't call Daly City "Little Manila" for nuthin'. Counterintuitively some of the Filipino dishes they serve are very good. Adobong Kambing (Spanish style Goat Stew) is delicious IF you like goat. As with Lamb it isn't everybody's cup of tea. Lots of Black Pepper, Bay Leaf, and Dark Soy. Mixed Pancit (Bihon, Canton, Shrimp, Chicken, Fish Balls, Lemon Wedges etc.) can also be very tasty. Not for the faint of heart, but a dish I dearly love, is the Crispy Pata a deep fried whole pig's foot. Crispy, greasy, fatty DELICIOUS! It comes with a soy, vinegar, and chopped onion dipping sauce to cut through the fat. Do not order this dish to go. Deep Fried Pig's Foot does not travel well, it must be eaten fresh out of the fryer. Thai Power is, first and foremost, a Filipino FOB karaoke spot although all are certainly welcome to partake. You have to "get it". It makes me feel like I'm back in Asia. These types of joints are all over the place in Southeast Asia. In Thailand, in the Philippines, wherever. Asia loves karaoke bars, working class Filipinos in particular love to sing and dance. Remember the line from The Beatles' song A Little Help From My Friends "what would you do if I sang out of tune, would you stand up and walk out on me?". Remember those words and you just might appreciate Thai Power for the simple, humble, unpretentious cultural mashup that it is.
Came here for quick late-night thai food and ended up staying for two hours singing karaoke and dancing. Fun vibes from some regulars and good food
