Lobalita is a new Mexican spot in the Marina that took over the old Tipsy Pig space, so the interior is naturally very spacious and comes with the added bonus of a large, sunny back patio. Seating is self-serve, so we grabbed a table outside to enjoy the nice weather, and our server was prompt with menus, water, and service throughout the meal.  Overall this is more of a 3.5 out of 5 but rounding up for the friendly staff and ambience provided by the lovely back patio.

Their cocktail menu looked pretty interesting, and the drinks we ordered were all tasty, clean, and beautifully presented with really vibrant colors. We also started with the seven layer dip, which had a good overall combination of flavors, though I found the bottom layer of pimiento cheese a little strange and not very easy to scoop from the bottom. The chips were crunchy and tasty, but the ratio of chips to dip felt a bit off.

We also shared a couple appetizers. The shrimp aguachile was a big miss for me since it had none of the acidity or spice I associate with aguachile and was instead drowning in an overly sweet mango salsa. The cochinita cakes were more interesting, though I was surprised by the texture since the menu made it sound like a crispy rice patty, but it was actually more like an arancini with its soft, creamy rice center fried into a cake shape. The flavors were pretty good though likewise not something I would order again.

For mains, our table ordered a variety of tacos and enchiladas. The shells in the crispy tacos had an excellent crunch, and the halibut in the Baja taco was flaky, moist, and encased in a really flavorful, well-seasoned batter. The duck carnitas in the patito was tasty and slightly smoky, though I did not enjoy the fig jam pairing since it pushed the dish too far into sweet territory for my taste.  It definitely needed to dial down the sweetness and add some acid to better balance the flavors.

We finished with the churros, which were absolutely a highlight. They were fried to perfection with a great balance of salt and sugar, and the  coffee crema and caramel dipping sauces were absolutely delicious.

Overall, this is a fun place to hang out, enjoy the weather, and have a few drinks and bites with friends. I would not necessarily seek it out for a serious meal, since the execution is a bit hit or miss and the menu leans pretty heavily into sweetness with very little spice or acid, which was a little disappointing given how those are hallmark flavors to Mexican food.

So excited that Yumee Katsu has opened a location here in San Francisco! If you are a fan of ultra-crispy, perfectly fried cutlets and comforting noodles, this spot is an absolute game-changer. I dropped by to check out the menu and tried a wide spread of their staples. Here is the breakdown:
Udon: My absolute favorite of the bunch! It features a comforting, hearty bowl of thick noodles in a deeply savory, flavorful broth that hits the spot every single time and serves as the perfect match for the rich cutlets.
Cheese Katsu: Easily a standout. The pork cutlet is stuffed with a generous amount of gooey, melted cheese that stretches with every bite while staying remarkably crisp on the outside.
Chicken Katsu: Fried to golden perfection with a light, shatteringly crisp panko crust. Because they don't use frozen meat, the cutlet stays exceptionally tender and juicy, completely avoiding any heaviness or greasiness.
Topokki Katsu: The ultimate fusion dish combining spicy, chewy Korean rice cakes with a top-tier crispy pork cutlet. It soaks up that delicious, sweet-and-spicy sauce wonderfully.
Soba: Clean, refreshing, and ice-cold buckwheat noodles that provide a fantastic, light contrast to the heavier fried dishes.
Portions here are just right, and everything comes out piping hot and fresh. A huge shoutout to the cabbage salad served on the side—the refreshing yuzu dressing is bright and zesty, cutting through the richness and keeping every bite feeling light and completely non-greasy. Will definitely be back on regular rotation!

top_reviews.content: I had an excellent experience at Russamee Traditional Thai Massage! The space is exceptionally clean, tidy, and comfortable, creating a truly relaxing atmosphere. I especially loved the beautiful oil paintings on the walls. A huge thank you to Penny, my therapist, who was incredibly warm, patient, and skilled—her technique was fantastic. Highly recommended!

Have been searching for a massage place near me, and this is it. Welcoming front room. Professional thai massages, clean, and dedicated staff. Loved how I was able to book something on the same day and my deep tissue. My only regret is not doing a longer massage! Highly recommend.

The place is nice and the massage was fine. Unfortunately there were a number of issues that came up for me that make me reluctant to go back. First, the website invites questions, but no one answered mine after a couple of weeks. I wanted to have a massage from the owner because she had the best reviews, and she wasn’t listed for bookings. Not hearing back,  I made a reservation with another person who was well liked in the reviews, that said she checked in with people and paid attention to their responses. They gave me someone else, however and said she was not there.
Id asked for a strong massage, thinking it was a woman, but got a man.
All of the Thai people were very nice, but their English was imperfect. I was worried because I had a leg injury. I’d had 2 massages in Thailand— one was fabulous, the other damaging. I felt that the language barrier prevented me from communicating well w the 2nd person and/or she was less experienced.
I did not expect that to be a problem here in Oakland, but it was. The massage started off too strong for me and I wasn’t relaxed because I was worried about my leg. The massage was fine — it hurt a lot. Mostly I felt that was a good hurt for my tense muscles. But it was not good for my leg which still hurts days later. Unfortunately I was unable to get the good attn to the sore leg cause I had to stop the roughness.
The man at the front desk was unhelpful and rude. E.g. when I asked for the name of my therapist (to give a tip) and mentioned that I did not get the therapist I requested he said I had to “put it in the notes,” they have a different system. I said I requested the person on the website, and he kept repeating that about putting it in the notes in an irritable tone, No idea what that meant. Why ask people to request a therapist if you’re not going to honor the request? He had trouble getting change and I had to ask twice for a tip envelope. He complained that he was very busy. Maybe he was, but it didn’t seem like it-/ I was the only one at the front then. And, more importantly, he was not nice.
I was offered a drink, but the tea never came. I decided just to get out of there.
The weirdest thing was that when I got home I got an email saying that my massage had been rescheduled for 15 minutes later and had a different therapist listed. It was sent 50 minutes later than my massage appt, during my massage! This from a place that requires advance rescheduling, or you face a steep penalty. Ridiculous!
I like traditional Thai massage and would like to try again, but I’m afraid to.

My wife and I would typically do a dinner for our anniversary but this night we really wanted a relaxing massage. We are very familiar with Thai massages as we always do it while on vacation. Well where do you find one that's in town that's reputable? There's a lot of places with high reviews so it can be overwhelming. We tested our luck here and really like the atmosphere and the people. Very accommodating and very nice. The whole thing felt very soothing. I like very hard strong massages and my wife likes medium to soft. She said that was probably one of the best massages she's had. I think next time I go I want to go even stronger. The only thing I don't like about this place is that it's not private rooms it's just curtains that divide us. It still felt very private but if there's any conversations going especially with couples massages you might hear your neighbor. We were the only people during this time but again it was very comfortable in soothing. Pricing was reasonable. Will be coming back in the future.

This was the best massage that I have ever had in my life.

When you walk in the door their is a beautiful painting of Thai goddesses dancing in front of a temple. I studied it during the short wait for my massage and commented about it to Penny, the owner, before I left. It turns out she painted it.

The place is very peaceful. When one enters one feels at peace. The massage menu has many options and price ranges. I opted for a full body deep tissue Thai massage that ended up being amazing.

My preference for massage is a lot of pressure, almost to the point of pain, which is hard to find. My masseuse was named Mimi. She was very professional and gave me a strong, very enjoyable massage.

Elements of yoga are part of the massage. She would twist my body, walk on me, and work out tightness stored in my body.

After the massage I felt like I was floating. When you go to pay you are offered delicious tea.

The whole experience was wonderful and I will be going there regularly from now on.

I can see this becoming a town staple real quick. Food was top notch. The Cali Ceviche was one of the best I’ve had, so good that I practically drank the sauce out of the bottom of the dish. We also had the grilled chicken which was amazingly juicy and ha a perfectly grilled skin. Drinks were on point which isn’t to surprising since the wonderful crew of Luka’s which reined from the early 2000s to post Covid on Broadway opened up Skula an anagram of Lukas.

Service was quick and personable. The theme is under the waters of Lake Merritt with some incredible murals, paper mache and photos of some of Lake Merritt’s critters.

My new obsession. I brought my friend who's visiting from out of town, so this was our first time here. We immediately loved the atmosphere, and the service and people are so nice and attentive. The food is so tasty, and the flavors are so uniquely delicious. There are some dining experiences where you leave thinking, "I paid all that and could've made it at home," or, "this tastes like so many other places I've been to." For us, most of the dishes we ordered felt special to this restaurant.

Highly recommend!

Oh the years we spent at Lukas’s. Both of our kids went to OSA and Luka’s was on the regular Friday night rotation for sure since it was so close. I would call this an upgraded redo, for sure. The space is casual enough and yet definitely feels like an elevated night out. A very warm welcome at the door and service was friendly and on top of it all night. The crowd was quintessentially Oakland. There were mostly young, fun – looking Oaklanders. But there were a few of us elders, holding things down. The tables on either side of us turned while we were there so we didn’t really talk with the first patrons in those tables, but the second set on each side were super fun. Of course, when one side came in looking like they just did a thru-hike on the PCT with their backpack gear and hiking clothes I had to inquire. Turns out they had gone over to Stern Grove for the Public Enemy concert and just made their way back. Brilliant. So, atmosphere= A+. Food: As a pescatarian, the fact that I could eat 3/4 of the menu items was thrilling. I had the trout, which is from Lassen County and the street corn. Hubby had a steak. The trout was very flavorful and the sauce, which wasn’t a sauce per se, but more of an au jus,, was just right. The street corn was 1000% delicious. We also started with cocktails and moved onto red wine – all were very good. We will definitely return and would probably also enjoy sitting at the bar to eat our meal, as their bar looked fun.

I am so excited about this spot! 10/10  decor, food, drinks, service. The desert heat cocktail was one of the best I’ve had recently and all the sauces were so flavorful and unique. Amazing new oakland mainstay

The muscles were fat and high quality and the lemony broth a perfect accompaniment.  Fideos con queso was a very satisfying side, great caesar salad and finger licking churros with chocolate.  Wait staff were the right amount of attentive and the place had a lively buzz. We will be back as regulars!

top_reviews.content:
A true hidden gem in Oakland — deserves 10 stars!

I tried this Jordanian–Iraqi restaurant today, and wow… absolutely outstanding. The lady working there is incredibly kind and treats you with genuine hospitality. I ordered green bean stew and okra stew, and the flavors instantly took me back home — it tasted exactly like something my mother would make.

The food is clean, the portions are generous, and the prices are very competitive. Everything felt authentic, warm, and made with love.

If you’re looking for real Middle Eastern comfort food, this place is a must-try. Highly, highly recommended!

"I recently tried the chicken Mandi at this Iraqi restaurant, and it was excellent. The rice was flavorful and perfectly cooked, the chicken was tender and juicy, and the spices were balanced just right. The portion size was generous, and the dish tasted authentic and fresh. I highly recommend this place if you’re looking for delicious Middle Eastern food.”
Best smash burgers and wings out there

The food is very well prepared, with skilfully balanced seasonings, spices, and sauces.  It does take a little while after ordering before the food arrives, as other reviewers indicated.

Nice attention to detail in preparation: for instance, even the "white rice" served with entrees isn't just plain rice, but delicately seasoned with cloves and possibly something like nutmeg (?), giving it a nice and fairly "unique" (vs. other cuisine styles) taste and flavor.  The complementary "hot black tea" isn't just plain tea, but also flavored with spices - and served in beautiful little tea glasses toward the end of the meal, almost like a digestif.  Every dish we tried, tasted great and left at least an impression of some kind of authenticity; so for our party who weren't familiar with Yemeni-style quisine going in, this was also a nice (and enjoyable) learning experience.  Food presentation generally isn't particularly fancy, but above-average I'd say.

Atmosphere-wise, the place has artful Arabic-themed (but fictional), expansive landscape painting "decals" spanning the full width of the walls, and floor-to-ceiling.  This gives the room an interesting vibe, and almost makes it feel larger on the inside than it really is (it also makes staring at the walls quite a bit more enjoyable than usual... 😅).  Tables and chairs and floor/ceiling are fairly basic, as are the menu format and eating utensils.  Ambient sound is unobtrusive and not unwelcome.

Service is friendly and welcoming, though again as other reviewers had mentioned, the person taking orders isn't always at the counter (keeping busy in the kitchen, presumably) - and in that case needs to either be actively called on or waited for, and food orders must be made at the counter as well - as there is no dedicated person to go around taking orders at the tables, or regularly checking up on how the patrons are doing or if they'd like to order anything else (such as dessert...)
What a beautiful hole in the wall. The authentic flavors were comforting to the soul. Simple yet refined to the palate of the “other”. Welcoming to everyone that enters the space. Thank you.

top_reviews.content:
What a gem! In the courtyard of the Anthropology Museum, you’ll find this charming oasis. Everything from the furniture, landscape, menu, and soundtrack are all thoughtfully procured. Afternoon tea consisted of 3 refreshing flavors of tea and 3 sweet dishes. The chia seed porridge was a generous portion with a delicious flavor profile as well as texture. The toasted hazelnuts added a tasty crunch. Blackberries and gooseberries were a nice palate cleanser, and the chia seed flour brownie bites were addictive! The black walnuts and coarse East Bay salt were a perfect combination! I’m thankful they don’t sell these individually otherwise I would be eating them daily. In bulk.
Not only was the meal unique and delicious, we also learned some Ohlone history and words as well as heard some lovely songs and spoken word that were pre-recorded. It’s such a nice experience and so much more than just food and drinks!

Truly magical find.

In addition to rare local foods, they treated us to games, stories, and song.

It's difficult to find behind the bookstore, but well worth the unique and private experience.

The decor of acorns, nuts, abalone, and cattails was really lovely.

Also, they provide lovely serapes for the chill.

BE HERE

Tucked behind University Press Books is a transformative place that allows you to turn back time. The lovingly gathered and carefully prepared foods are nothing like any foods typically eaten today. Instead, these foods are the mainstay foods that allowed the Ohlone people to live in peace and in harmony with their environment for thousands of years. The two indigenous men who have created this incredible space and menu come from an unbroken line of people who have lived in the East Bay for thousands of years. The foods they are offering take a tremendous amount of time and labor, but they are not offering them in a simple format. The foods are rich and complex and take freshness to an entirely new level. Be prepared to sit outside, dress warmly. Be prepared to learn. There will be abundant information given about each course. Be prepared to ask questions. They want to start conversations that feed your soul as well as your body. Be prepared for adventure. This is an incredible opportunity to explore foods you may not otherwise taste. This is fine dining at its very best.

This place is a MUST. Deliciously fanciful, natural, clean & exquisitely flavorful dishes from our Bay Areas very own indigenous Ohlone tribe. The experience has been well thought out, and you can truly see the intentions that are full of LOVE here. This is as LOCAL and NATIVE as it gets!! Not enough stars for how happy this place makes me & how fulfilling the tastes!!

The great thing about this place is it is done for awareness of ohlone that are still indigenous to the east bay. They have not moved from here ever. Hopefully this place can raise awareness that they are much alive and well as a culture. I was concerned I might not liie some of the food for the snacks and tea on tuesday night but it was delicious and very natural to the nearby land. The experience is great as it is communal at picnic tables, preceeded by prayer, and the food is explained. Very spiritual and tasty. It was an overall great experience. Highly recommended!

top_reviews.content: We recently had our baby shower at the Yard and they did an amazing job! Great to work with the team and create the menu, seating, and set up for our 50 person party. They were extremely accommodating, easy to work with, the service was excellent too. Thank you Adam and team!

I’m really bummed writing this because Saltbreaker used to be one of our favorite spots in Alameda. We used to come here for happy hour and dinner, and I’ve told anyone who would listen that they had the best burger in Alameda. When they opened “The Yard” outside a few months ago and got rid of happy hour inside Saltbreaker, it already felt like a money grab — quantity over quality.

We were hesitant to try The Yard because photos of the burger didn’t look the same, but we were next door at Humble Sea and decided to give it a shot. I even asked our waitress if it was still the same burger as the old Saltbreaker one — she said yes, same chef. Unfortunately, that wasn’t true.

The burger was dry, overcooked, noticeably smaller, and just not constructed well. Honestly, it tasted like a fast-food burger from Jack in the Box — and more expensive than the old Saltbreaker burger. My girlfriend got the chopped cheese, and the Dutch crunch bread was very dense. Just didn’t go well with the beef.

To be fair, it looks like Saltbreaker inside now serves a different truffle burger, so maybe that’s better — but this experience at The Yard wasn’t a vote of confidence. Feels like they’re trying to push volume over quality, which is sad to see. At least mark down your prices if that’s what you’re going for. If they ever bring back their original double smash burger, I’ll be first in line. Attaching a photo of today’s burger vs. the old one for reference.

We also had a hamburger and a clam chowder bread bowl. Both of those got really strong reviews from my wife and daughters.

Ah, Il Porcellino Grasso deli in San Francisco, you know, that place is like a little slice of Italy right in the heart of the city. When I walked in, I felt like I'd stepped into one of those old-school Italian joints where wise guys meet to discuss business – and by business, I mean sandwiches.

The atmosphere, oh, it's something else. They got those meats hanging in the fridge like works of art, and right next to the counter, there's a meat slicer, a real beaut even if it's just for show. It adds that authentic touch that makes you feel like you're in the thick of things.

Now, I ordered The Don – a panini on focaccia bread. Let me tell you, it was more than tasty; it was a flavor explosion! The ingredients were fresh, and the flavors, well, they hit you like a message from the big boss himself.

And the prices, they're as reasonable as a favor among friends. Just $14 for a sandwich, hot or cold, that's the kind of deal that won't make you an offer you can refuse. They've got plenty of other options too, like soup and salad, if you're in the mood for something lighter. So, next time you're in San Francisco, be sure to pay a visit to Il Porcellino Grasso – it's an offer you won't want to miss.

It is with a heavy heart that I write this review about our post-funeral gathering at Hermitage Banquet Hall. During such a difficult time of loss, I had hoped for understanding and compassion, but unfortunately, we did not receive that.

The dinner itself was fine, but not everyone got a chance to try all the dishes. One side of the table had noticeably more food than the other, but I chose to let it go to keep the peace. Before the event, my mom and I provided the exact number of attendees. Later, my mom was asked to go upstairs to settle the bill, and at that point, she was told there were more guests than we had originally confirmed. By then, many people had already left, so we couldn’t prove otherwise. Given the circumstances, we had no choice but to pay for two additional guests.

When we received the final bill, my mom recalculated it and found that the total was much higher than what had been originally agreed upon. Only after my mom’s recalculation did the owner quickly adjust the amount, but in the end, the final total still exceeded what was originally agreed on.

I write this review to ensure others don’t encounter the same injustice. Initially, the owner seemed kind and understanding, but when it came down to the bill, it became clear that their priority was profit over honesty. No one should have to feel taken advantage of during such a vulnerable time.

The food is Ok. Be very careful with what you are promised by the owner and what you get. She doesn't keep her word and changes things as convenient to her last minute, when you do not have another option for your party already. Music is pretty bad and they only play for tips. Unfortunately San Francisco doesn't have a lot of options for Russian parties. i will NEVER go back to Hermitage to celebrate anything.

Things became more disappointing when I asked for a side of hot sauce or salsa and was told I'd have to purchase an entire bottle instead. Considering the relatively high prices and modest portion sizes, it seemed unreasonable that a small side of salsa or hot sauce wasn't available. The food itself was fresh and well prepared, but it lacked flavor and felt dry without any sauce or cheese.

The final straw came as we were leaving. After finishing our meal, we were scolded for not bussing our own table. It wasn't obvious that customers were expected to do this, and the interaction felt awkward and unnecessary. It also felt strange that no one checked on us during the meal or refilled our water, yet someone was quick to point out that we hadn't cleared our table.

The table next to us also appeared to have a frustrating experience. The cashier missed part of their order, and when they brought it to the staff's attention, the missing item wasn't prioritized. They ended up waiting long after everyone else at their table had finished eating. When they asked if the order could be expedited, they were essentially told no.

I would have gladly paid the higher prices for better service, more thoughtful vegan options, and a dining experience that didn't feel like I was being nickel-and-dimed at every turn. I really wanted to love this place, but unfortunately I won't be back.

The Pho tasted like plain broth injected with powder with no aromas of beef bone, ginger, anise, cloves, cinnamon sticks, coriander seeds, cardamom pods, and fennel seeds, etc.; however, its ingredients are sufficiently included from beef steak slices, tendons, meatballs along with herb leaves, bean sprouts, jalapeno and limon. Me So Hungry Too is located inside Hometown Bowl. There's some street parking in the residential area. I love the Count Burger and garlic parmesan fries. You get to choose how you want the patty cooked to your liking. The burger is so juicy and fresh and goes so well with the side of fries!

First off I wanna say that I appreciate that everyone on staff was wearing a mask when taking orders AND making the food. Me So Hungry Too is located inside of Hometown Bowl in the same spot as Love Burn Chicken, so with these kinds of close quarters it is so important to take extra precautions and wear proper PPO for their sake and the customers’ sake. I also just so happened to show up when they were working on a huge catering order so they were extremely busy but I was still greeted promptly and very kindly by Jerry and a few other staff members!

I wasn’t sure what to order so I asked Jerry to make me what he recommends and I believe he went with the Frankenstein cheeseburger. It came with bacon, a 100% grass-fed beef patty, cheddar cheese, lettuce, tomato, onion, and he added in some of the Me So BBQ sauce which is their hoisin based bbq sauce. My first impression of the burger was “damn, this is HUGE.” Genuinely speaking, that burger could feed two people or one person for two meals. I split it with my friend and we were more than stuffed. I asked for my patty to be cooked medium rare and that thick, juicy patty was cooked to perfection. The bacon was super crispy which was the perfect texture to be added to that burger. It added a fun textural element aside from the smoky bacon flavor. I’ve never had anything like the Me So BBQ Sauce before and I gotta admit that I was obsessed with it. Usually BBQ sauce is a bit too sweet for me but this was made so well and it wasn’t covering up the flavor of the bacon or patty either. Personally, this is now my favorite burger spot in the Bay Area.

Moving on to the fries… don’t even get me started. Those French fries were so addicting. You cannot go to Me So Hungry Too without getting 1 or 2 orders of their fries. They were fried perfectly and the inside was nice and fluffy while the outside was so delicately crispy that it was extremely satisfying to eat and hear the crunch. There was a garlic Parmesan topping on the fries that wasn’t overly salty and even if you stuffed some of the topping and the fries inside the burger it still worked so damn well together. We were eating on my car in front of someone’s house and they could hear us enjoying our food so thoroughly that they literally asked where we got our food and we watched them walk in and back out with their own burger and fries. I definitely recommend you to ask for a side of the Me So BBQ Sauce so you can dip your fries in it too!

The last thing we had was the 5pc mini churros with a caramel dipping sauce. Usually when I have dessert with a meal I like to be able to save some of the savory or salty food to help me balance the sweet flavor in my mouth but the churros were already perfectly balanced on their own. Not too sweet and the perfect texture, a bit chewy on the inside but super crunchy on the outside. Definitely grab a burger and fries combo if you’re in the area!

A bit on the pricey side for lunch but it is definitely worth it. Huge portions too I couldn't finish my plate!! I will definitely keep up with his posts to the next pop-up to try something new because if these two plates were this tasty I can't wait to see what else Rome's Kitchen has to offer. Keep up the great work!!

3-26-25 Came out to Romes Kitchen to try his supreme smoked chicken loaded nachos. They were hella good, the chicken was tender and moist and had a great smoky flavor. Chips were regular corn tortilla chips and Doritos nacho cheese chips I've never had nachos with Doritos before. I don't think I'll eat nachos any other way going forward. The bowl was a great portion I had trouble trying to finish my plate. Once again Rome's Kitchen outdid themselves and blew me away with the flavors of this dish. I look forward to trying more of Romes food on the next pop up event.

Wow I don't think I've been satisfied with dining out since Rome's Kitchen. His BBQ Hot Link Sandwich I ordered was delicious and one of a kind. Definitely will be returning and highly recommend everyone to give it a try. Rome Kitchen's made me feel like I was in my own mothers kitchen with his hospitality, cooking skills, and service he provided.

OMG, the seasoning on the fried fish was so good!! I ate up all of the cabbage because it was full of flavor. And the candied yams were just perfect. These guys know what they're doing! They're in a food truck in the parking lot of the Hunter's Point Speakeasy.

I've seen Rome's truck around my 'hood for a while & finally tried it. I had the Salmon & Italian Alfredo meal, & it hits! Salmon was cooked perfectly, with crispy edges & soft inside. The pasta was seasoned well, with herbs & pepper -- sooo good. Plus, Rome & Kenlious are super friendly. Go eat there on Wednesdays & Fridays by the old Speakeasy on Evans & Keith, unless they're busy doing private catering gigs. You won't leave hungry or sorry!

top_reviews.content: Newly opened cafe near Park Street, came and got Tofu Fried Rice plus Thai Iced Tea. Looking for a quiet place to eat and enjoy some hearty Thai food or even tasty pork porridge? Here’s the place to go.

We usually go for late brunch, just before lunch hours and it tends to be quiet - both for our sake and also for other diners since we have two rambunctious toddlers.

Their Khao Thom, pork porridge, is delicious. Our toddlers like this every time we go. Heart warming, tasty, and good amount of protein - minced pork and hard boiled eggs (which we would smash up). Only thing lacking is vegetables for it to be a well rounded meal.

Tried yellow curry with chicken today. It was good though could improve as the potato was a little on the hard side. Maybe since it was early, it was still cooking? Hopefully better next time.

We enjoyed our brunch at this cute and friendly mom & pop style Lao and Thai place! Great savory/spicy breakfast alternative to western sweet breakfast places! Loved the old school chinatown-style decor and the karaoke style covers of pop songs playing 🎤🌻

Maya the owner took our orders and was super sweet with our toddler 😊

We ordered and really loved the Khao Thom (rice porridge with ground chicken/bone broth and egg), Pad Grapow Chicken (Krapow Gai) and our kid got two pancakes (syrup and jelly at the table- wish it came with butter though!).

Also at the table were 4 types of homemade chili oil / spicy vinegars!

They’re in the process of finding what hours work best, so currently they’re open from 10a-6pm M-Th, 9am to 8pm Fri-Sat, closed Sunday. They also will occasionally close from 4 to 5pm for dinner prep!
Food was delicious, service was fast and  friendly, tried the Thai tea and it was tasty and it wasn't expensive to our party of 4 🤙🏻

BEWARE, they will overcharge you and you wouldn’t know.
I had to ask for a detailed receipt, wait 5 min while they figure out how their system works in order to find that I was charged extra without that info being on the menu. When I told them that it wasn’t on the menu, that I shouldn’t be charged this, she got mad and started acting all mad that it was beef and it is extra. I would have left it as ‘tip’ if she was apologetic and actually owned up to their mistakes and tried hard to fix it.

Food: Ok, very salty and sauce is overdone on pad thai. Not tasty

Charge: Price on the menu was 15.95$ for pad thai and pad see ew. No additional price ANYWHERE on the page or menu. I was charged 18.95$ for ‘beef’.

Never again

I was at a tiny function and the organizer had a few sandwiches laid out on a tray for visitors. I would learn that they were from Weslow's. The sandwich was delicious with an abundance of flavors and freshness. The bread was still crisp despite probably having sat on the table for an hour. The "meat" was fantastic, and the avocado added a rich creaminess. The sauce was reminiscent of chimichuri. I'd later find out that the meat was plant based and the entire sandwich vegan. Overall a fantastic sandwich and will check out the shop sometime in the future.

I Love Love Love their sandwiches and drinks! Their bread and ingredients are so fresh. I tried the BttLA, Wentino, and the Weslo and I am addicted to their Thai Tea. They actually brew loose tea leaves for all their teas instead of powder or those cheap tea bags that some other places use. Their Viet coffee is pretty good as well as their ribena lemonade. Oh and there's a free parking lot!

We tried Weslos Sandwiches and loved it! You would never realize it is there but it is attached to the Loards ice cream.  Staff was so friendly! We had both the Weslos and the Willows sandwiches, and it was tasty; even my picky kiddos loved it. I noticed they use bread from Acme Bread Company, and the herb bread I tried was absolutely delicious. I also had the HK coffee which was smooth and flavorful.  Prices are reasonable. Super convenient there is a Loards ice cream in the same complex. Definitely coming back!

This sandwich shop was hard to find at first, but once you know, you'll never forget it. This shop shares its space with the Loards ice cream shop. I ordered their Hot Butt sandwich which was unique and tasty! I do wish they could offer sourdough rolls as a bread choice. As far as their service, they were super friendly and helpful and the shop was clean and bright. I'd come back to try their other creative sandwich choices!

top_reviews.content:
Sister shop of Noodle Dynasty right next door. I actually prefer this one maybe bc I’m just pickier with my noodles lol. The nutrition here feels way more balanced; instead of just meat and noodles, you actually get a good mix of protein, veggies, and an egg. The lotus leaf rice was steamed perfectly, with every grain of rice staying distinct and fluffy.

The Black Pepper Beef Ribs Rice was a bit salty, but the beef itself was tender and the black pepper flavor was definitely there. My friend and I both preferred the Char Siu Pork & Chicken Combo Rice; it was a bit lighter and the two types of meat made for a better variety. It also came with a ginger-scallion sauce, which felt very authentic.

Portions are huge. We had about 20-30% left over to take home. If you have a smaller appetite, one order could easily be two meals. Also, a shoutout for the eco-friendly, two-compartment to-go boxes; such a thoughtful detail!

Service was great. They gave us some complimentary soup to start, which was light but clearly a slow-cooked bone broth. The staff were very friendly and didn't rush us at all, even though we hung out for a while. That said, it wasn’t very crowded for a weekday lunch, and there were plenty of open seats.

Giving 4 stars for the food as it was actually quite tasty. Sadly, the service was a bit of a letdown. Between the long wait and the server asking us to box our food before we were done, we felt unwelcome and rushed. Hopefully, they can improve the pacing and hospitality

My favorite spot near campus. Everything is so good food, service, all of it.
Highly recommend the beef tomato lotus leaf rice, it has this super subtle lotus fragrance that makes it stand out.
Honestly you can’t go wrong with anything on the menu. 10/10.

Oh my goodness!  I could go back for the yogurt alone and just eat that, which was just a dish they brought me as a side.  The yogurt is made fresh daily.  You just can't get anything like that anywhere in the city.  It would have to be home made by your grandma or something.  Everything is so fresh that it tastes like heaven.  This is a husband and wife vegetarian restaurant and the food is so enjoyable to eat and so satisfying you'll just keep coming back.

The rice was perfect!  And the rice pudding was just lovely.

I haven't even gotten to the lentils, subtle but at the same time packed with flavor, perfectly cooked to perfection.  I kept thinking about how hard it is to cook a steak perfectly; well, that kind of perfection went into the lentils––perfect texture, beautiful flavor.

If that's not enough, the owners are delightful.  They are not only skilled cooks, you just taste the love in the food--truly something special.  And they make you feel like home, such warmth and kindness.  Support them now while they just opened.  You'll be so happy you did, and you'll keep coming back.  I know I will.

top_reviews.content:
Az SF True Light Church egy keresztény gyülekezet San Franciscóban, amely közvetlenül az előzőleg bemutatott fizioterápiás központtal szemben, a 401 Dewey Blvd szám alatt található. Az épület a Twin Peaks negyed lábánál, a Mount Davidson és a Forest Hill övezetek találkozásánál fekszik.

1. Elhelyezkedés és építészet
- A gyülekezet épülete egy kellemes, fákkal övezett, kertvárosias lakóövezetben található. A templom letisztult, modern és családias építészeti stílust képvisel, amely harmonikusan illeszkedik a környező domboldalak San Franciscó-i házai közé.

2. Közösségi és hitélet
- Az SF True Light Church egy szoros, befogadó és multikulturális hívőközösség otthona. A gyülekezet kiemelt célja, hogy támogassa a helyi családokat, és egy olyan barátságos környezetet biztosítson, ahol a különböző generációk együtt gyakorolhatják hitüket. A közösség aktívan szervez jótékonysági programokat, bibliaköröket és fiataloknak szóló délutáni foglalkozásokat is.

3. Istentiszteletek és látogatás
- Időpont: A templom kapui elsősorban a vasárnapi napokon állnak nyitva a nagyközönség és a hívek előtt. A központi vasárnapi istentiszteleteket délelőtt tartják (jellemzően 10:00 és 14:00 között).
- Hétköznapok: Hétfőtől szombatig a templomépület általában zárva tart, a hétközi programokat (például a kisebb imacsoportokat vagy megbeszéléseket) egyedi időpontokban vagy online szervezik meg.

⭐️ 1 star (and that’s being generous)

The fries were cold, maybe because they didn’t bring them on time or because they just dumped them in oil with chopped garlic and chili trying to fake a “chimichurri” or something. The cardboard tray had a literal oil puddle at the bottom. Total mess.

Then I ordered the tomato soup, which turned out to be the most orange and sugary “tomato soup” I’ve ever seen. Honestly, I doubt it was even made from tomatoes. The croutons were just as disgusting.
⚠️ Don’t order this unless your taste buds are dead.

Next came the Bacon Barbecue Double Burger. To be fair, the burger was tasty 🍔.
But it took forever. When it finally came, an older lady brought it—very kind, unlike the younger girl working there, who has zero empathy, no motivation, and probably some racial bias issues.
I asked if the burger was hot, she looked confused, said it was left aside and they’d make a new one. Three minutes later it was back on my table. Yeah right—they didn’t make a new one, they just reheated it. Inside was hot, bun was cold.

I had also asked for a side of pickles, and they just threw half a cold pickle on the tray paper. No care at all.
The place looks fine, but it’s empty—and now I know why 😑.
Checked Google Maps while eating and saw it has 2.8 stars, which honestly feels too generous.

About the beer 🍺:
•	The Pilsner is terrible.
•	The Mexican lager Agua Santa is decent, not amazing, but way better than the Pilsner.

💬 Bottom line: I do not recommend this place at all.

The air is filled with the scent of freshly made tortillas, traditional salsas, and a vibrant mix of meats, spices, and toppings that awaken the senses. Every bite is crafted with care - a tribute to the heart of Mexican cuisine. These tacos are more than just a meal—they're a love letter to flavor, the very best tacos in San Francisco.

My favorite is the Lu Rou Fan, which is a Taiwanese comfort food consisting of braised, chopped pork belly served over rice.  It's savory/sweet pork matches perfectly with the rice and is hearty and filling and reminds me of home.

The Kimchi Fried Rice is also excellent and provides a bold spicy flavor that I think many will enjoy.  Both of these options are great rice dishes that have strong personalities.

The Chicken Croffle is also a great addition with the southern inspired contemporary signature dish that blends sweet and savory.  You can enjoy the chicken and the croffle seperately or stacked together, you can't go wrong.

I haven't tried the drinks yet, but I will definately be back to try them.

Their menu is simple that offers panuchos, tacos, tamales, salbutes, empanadas, tortas, hamburgers, burritos and much more to choose from. They are open everyday from eleven in the morning until nine at night. As time went by where I was waiting for my order, more and more customers showed up to place their orders. This place is definitely a plus in the area since there is little to none food spots in the area. I highly recommend this place to all Spanish food enthusiasts, if you are in need of a quick bite, to anyone willing to try something new or if you just so happen to be in the area to check them out. top_reviews.content:
This restaurant signals precision in contemporary hand roll preparation.

The rice establishes the standard. Hydration is exact. Seasoning is balanced. Grain separation remains intact. Texture registers as light, aromatic, and structurally supportive rather than dense. The rice operates as architecture.

Seafood quality confirms control. Scallop and yellowtail present with clarity and freshness. Mouthfeel remains cool and aqueous. A roll incorporating a Japanese leaf anchors the experience in cultural specificity and restraint. Originality emerges through reduction.

Torch application modifies surface chemistry without disrupting internal structure. Even the A5 wagyu expresses sweetness, tenderness, and balance.

Iced green tea functions as a deliberate palate reset. Sensory acuity remains stable across courses.

The environment supports ease and a shared atmosphere of attentiveness and enjoyment.

A meaningful addition to the Bay Area’s Japanese dining landscape.

Right outside the new Tokyo Central, Waka Sakura offers fresh hand-rolls made in front of you.

Currently in its opening phase, the restaurant features a counter-top seating 6, with more seats coming for the dining area.

The rolls are nice, although the menu is still fairly limited, mainly just traditional types of tuna and salmon. The most expensive option is the uni roll, which for $15 is a bit steep for the amount you get.

That being said, it’s a nice spot to grab a bite, the rolls taste solid, although you may find there are more options within Tokyo Central itself.

They offered take out. I helped quickly and I got my order quickly. I shopped at Tokyo central and bought some onigiri. After eating them both side by side, I highly recommended the hand rolls by Waka Sakura. The seaweed was crispy, the rice was not soggy and had a good bite and mouthfeel. The tuna was buttery and melt in your mouth. Our order was prepared fresh and was way better than the prepared onigiri at Tokyo central. Best of all there was no line to order or sit down.

The overall experience was very disappointing. The hand rolls were basically just rice and sashimi, with very small portions and nothing special to justify the price. Definitely not worth it. I would rather get sushi elsewhere.

Service was also poor. The staff did not greet us or even ask if we were dining in until I walked up myself, even though there were plenty of seats available. On top of that, both restrooms in the restaurant were unavailable and customers had to use the supermarket next door, which is unacceptable. Before I even finished my hand roll, they immediately brought the bill. Overall bad service, and not recommended.

top_reviews.content: After 2 years of eating all the banh mi at different restaurants within a 1 mile radius of my office…I FINALLY found a decent banh mi!!! Thank the kitchen gods!!! This sandwich is 9/10! I love their bread-mice and crusty and not doughy at all. I always order the social cold cut combo at every place I go. The traditional cold cut combo includes steam pork, ham, and head cheese. Here, they had steam pork, pork belly, and ham. I wish they had head cheese. That would make this 10/10!!! Flavor is perfect. Veggies crunchy and the pickled daikon and carrots were tangy and lightly sweet, just as it should be. Pate is creamy with a nice bold taste. Everything was delicious and I look forward to coming back here often for banh mi. It’s the highlight of my work day.

A new take-out spot in the Financial District, perfect for an office lunch. The food is consistently great, service is fast and friendly, and kitchen looks clean. Highly recommend their Banh Mi, Spring Rolls, and Vermicelli Bowls. They also just added Beef Brisket Pho and it has a really nice herbal flavor.

My new go to lunch spot. Lots of veggie options and very fast. It's a perfect lunch to still have mental energy afterwards with plenty of fresh crunch. I've been doing the tofu bowl - full of umami flavor on the tofu. The place is slightly hard to find, with the window facing south, not directly open on first.

Finally tried DragonEats and really enjoyed my banh mi and overall experience!! With the prices, portions, flavors, and location, it's an amazing option for lunch when working in FiDi.

Walking in, it's a super small, takeaway-only joint. There's a little standing area where you could eat when it's not busy, but, for the most part, it's a takeout spot. The staff was super warm, kind, and helpful, which is always lovely.

The menu is straightforward but also extensive. It consists simply of banh mi, fresh bowls, and fresh rolls, and each choice has its own selection of proteins. The banh mi in particular has so many amazing-sounding options, including beef brisket, roasted duck, garlic butter chicken, and more! I'm not sure how long they'll have this, but they also had a beef brisket pho offering, which looked so good!

This time around, I kept it simple and got a 5-Spice Chicken Banh Mi. With tax and a small tip, it came out to $13.50, which is a solid lunch price in FiDi, where things typically are $20+.

It came out quickly, and it was much larger than expected! If you aren't too hungry, you could definitely get two meals out of this. Now, the most important part: it was so good!!! There was a good amount of both the chicken and the veggies. The bread was great, the veggies were fresh, and the chicken was tender and not dry at all. The best part was the sauce. I don't know what they are putting in that sauce, but they need to keep putting it in that sauce!!!

Oh my goodness, it had this crazy amazing salty, savory flavor that went so, so well with the chicken and slightly sweet pickled veggies. It also kept the sandwich the right level of moist. I usually like to warm up sandwiches because of the moisture issue, but there was no need here. That said, the sauce makes things a little slippy, so just have napkins nearby and ideally a plate underneath. No pictures, unfortunately, because I gobbled it up!

I hope more people check out DragonEats! I certainly will bring it into my rotation. It's awesome, and I'm excited to make my way through the menu :)

top_reviews.content:
Fine-dining meal for $19!!

This is a wonderful little restaurant, on the fourth floor of Burk Hall, that's only open on Tuesdays and Wednesdays currently. You should make a reservation on Yelp, but I think they allow walk-ins. There's a prix fix option, which is just under $20.50 after tax. You get to choose an appetizer, entree, and dessert, and drinks. Only cash or checks are accepted.

The bread provided was foccacia cut into diamond-shaped pieces. The bread that they first brought out was hard and dry, so I told them it was hard. More bread was brought out promptly and it was softer, but still dry. I didn't tell them it was dry because I didn't want to be difficult. I had some lemonade to drink, and it was pretty good. I also had tea at the end, but it was piping hot and I didn't get a chance to drink much. It was fine.

I chose to have the house green salad for my appetizer. It was a good mix of leafy-greens covered in vinaigrette. It wasn't special, but good. I decided to have the pasta of the week for my entree. It was penne pasta salad with feta cheese, capers, and cooked grape tomatoes. It was absolutely delicious and I basically inhaled it. For dessert, I chose the pumpkin bundt cake. It was fantastic. It was moist, soft, a little misshapen, but still delicious. The créme anglaise was like melted ice cream, and I loved it.

The waiters were students and had more to learn. Service was very good, despite mistakes. The person who seemed like an instructor was great. You won't be able to find a three-course fine-dining meal anywhere else in San Francisco for the same price. The portions are good sizes and you'll leave feeling fed, but not stuffed. I highly recommend checking this place out.

Run by hospitality students from SF State. Good food and service. You’ve got the option to choose from fixed price menu which includes one appetizer one entree and one desert plus a drink. I think $17 is pretty steep for lunch. But good place :)

It was a good deal, $15 for about 14-15 different wine tastings from a different winery each time. It also comes with small bites such as 3 different types of cheese, crackers, bread, fruits, and meats. And best of all is you can purchase the wine you like there or place an order. They never push you to buy. I look forward to go again.

top_reviews.content: An unforgettable omakase experience. Every course was beautifully crafted, showcasing impeccable technique, creativity, and the freshest ingredients. The chef’s passion, precision, and attention to detail transformed each bite into something memorable. Beyond the exceptional food, the warm hospitality and personal touch made the evening truly special. Easily one of the best dining experiences I've had, and a chef whose talent shines in every dish.

I must say I had high hopes for this new restaurant. I've been in this neighborhood for 50 years and loved Uzen. Well, I love Japanese food in general and was excited to try a new place. However, I was quite disappointed in Gamsa's nigiri. THEY DRENCH EACH NIGIRI WITH SOY SAUCE!!!!!!! You don't taste the fish. You just taste SALT!!! Ikura is usually a rich orange color. Because they use soy sauce after making each nigiri, their ikura is BROWN!! I kid you not! ALL their sushi was way too salty, even the barracuda when I asked them to make it without soy sauce. They claim the fish is salty. I consider myself a sushi connoisseur  and I have NEVER tasted salty fish in sushi. To be fair, the chiwanmushi was good (although salty also!) The rainbow roll  was NOT drenched in soy sauce, but the crab inside tasted salty. They only serve full bottles of sake, not glasses. (maybe later?) The service was great, as well as the atmosphere. Very cozy and comfortable. I will give it a second chance and order the sashimi salad, chicken karaagi, and udon and see if they are salty. If so, I'm never going back!

Anyways, the food. I got the black fungus with chili sauce, boiling beef with house spicy broth, and shrimp fried rice. The shrimp fried rice seemed as if the rice was thrown into a bowl, drenched with soy sauce, and called it a day. It was tasty, so I will likely order again. The black fungus mushrooms smelled slightly rancid, and eating a bite tasted like they used all vinegar in the chili sauce.... I'm not sure if there was any chili sauce

The boiling beef with house spicy broth was exactly what I was looking for, with the perfect amount of numbing oil and sichuan peppercorn. Aside from the random cuts of cucumber, I actually really enjoyed this dish.

So while I don't know if I would order from "them" in the day time when places like Chengdu Style or Mama Ji's are open, this would definitely be a good late night delivery spot for me.

top_reviews.content: I want to give Nora and her amazing team all the stars in the sky. They are truly some of the most talented, warm, fun, patient humans I've had the pleasure of meeting. They went above and beyond for our wedding weekend, fulfilling our every dream as well as including unique touches and surprises! Much of the food was locally sourced, all of it was incredibly fresh. It was CRAVEABLE, we haven't stopped thinking about some of the amazing dishes they so artfully and skillfully prepared. All of our guests were blown away, saying that they had never experienced such incredibly tasty and beautiful food. Their demeanor was grounded, patient, funny and warm. We could never have dreamed the experience would be as good as it was and we are eternally grateful for Nora and her team and will continue to recommend and support them for many years to come. Thank you Nora, we love you so much!

Meals from Just Eat It are a wonder. It's like having a personal chef for professional-grade home cooking that's either ready-to-eat (tiramisu!), ready-to-heat (spanakopita!), or freezer-bound for when those run out and I need a quick meal (black bean veggie burgers!). A delivery is a joy to receive and I can never decide what to dig into first. The weekly menu is always a different theme that I look forward to selecting from. Order as much or as little as you like, but speaking from experience: I recommend ordering twice as many cookies as you think you want.

Whether you need a full holiday meal or just some delish mains and sides for a busy week, Nora's woman owned kitchen comes through. Add one of herspecial breads too. I love to send bone broth or gift card to friends in need.

Yesis, Diego, and their two girls have created an amazing pop up at the Stonestown Farmers Market every Sunday from 9am to 1pm.
